Name: The Charm of Robots
Introduction: This course is open to all students in the school and provides a comprehensive introduction to the basic knowledge, development overview, research hot spots and trends of robotics technology and robotics competitions. Through explanations, pictures, videos, practical demonstrations and other links, students can deepen their knowledge and understanding of robotics technology, popularize the scientific knowledge of robots, and cultivate their interest in scientific research on robots.

Name: Introduction to Earthquakes
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course is a quality education general course for all students in the school and has the characteristics of a typical natural science course. It briefly introduces the basic concepts of seismology and research methods, including the history of seismology, seismometer principles and seismograms, seismic wave propagation theory, the internal structure of the earth, exploration seismology, earthquake prediction, earthquake preparedness measures and the latest advances in seismology. Through the study of this course, students' quality in natural sciences can be improved, students' awareness of earthquake resistance and disaster reduction can be enhanced, and students' ability to escape from earthquakes can be improved.

Name: Chinese Spoken Language and Oral Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course is based on the introduction and reading of the most important documents of the "four rhythms (melody, meter, rhythm, and rhythm)" of traditional Chinese audio culture. It uses basic knowledge of phonetics, acoustics, and sound perception as its methodology to expound and explain the origin and evolution of language pronunciation organs, and poetic rhythm. The acoustic model and psychological perception basis of rhyme, the acoustic basis of traditional Chinese music rhythm, the physiological acoustic principles of vocalization and tuning of traditional operas and original folk songs, and the corresponding perceptual basis, so as to examine the scientific basis and shortcomings of traditional Chinese sound culture from a scientific perspective.

Name: Modern Chinese History
Introduction: This course is based on a large number of original materials and combined with the latest research trends in the academic world to systematically teach the dramatic changes in China's politics, economy, military, diplomacy, education, legal system and other aspects from around 1840 to 1919. The purpose is to enable students to have an accurate grasp of the development context and basic knowledge of this period of history, to deepen students' understanding of this period of history, and to lay a solid foundation for further research on modern Chinese history in the future. The course content includes ten parts, namely: China before modern times, the Sino-British Opium War, the Taiping Revolution, the Second Opium War, the Westernization Movement, the border crisis, the frenzy of partition and national salvation efforts, the New Deal in the last ten years of the late Qing Dynasty, the Revolution of 1911 and the establishment of the Republic of China, and the rule of the Beiyang warlords. Classes are held through a combination of lectures and discussions.

Name: History of Chinese Historiography
Introduction: This course is a required course for undergraduate majors in the Department of History. Its contents range from the pre-Qin period to the first half of the 20th century. Through the study of this course, students can have a basic understanding of the development process and laws of Chinese historiography, representative historians, historical achievements and their characteristics, the evolution of historiography, the development of historical thought, the relationship between history and other academic and cultural fields, etc., so as to have a relatively comprehensive understanding of Chinese historiography.

Name: History of the Americas
Introduction: The course covers the history of the new continent from Columbus to contemporary America. The course is divided into two main parts: the first is Latin American history, which is based on the background of the colonization and modernization of the world, the evolution of the Latin American position in the world system, the exploration of the path of modernization by Latin American countries, the theory of representation in the process of modernization in Latin America and the historical trends towards modernization in the third world region. The second part, on American history, focused on how the United States emerged from 13 former British colonies from the early 17th to the 1970s as a super-Power, in particular the process of constitutional building and democracy within the United States, social reform within the United States, and the relationship between the United States and the outside world, and sought to reveal the value and significance of its experience. In addition, the course will address the relationship between the United States and Latin America in order to capture the historical processes of the American continent as a whole.

Name: Introduction to Mental Health
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the knowledge and methods of psychology, mental hygiene and some psychiatric medicine, so that students can comprehensively understand the basic knowledge of mental health and initially master the basic methods of mental health through the study of this course; they can relieve general psychological pressure and promote mental health in daily life.

Name: Football
Introduction:
Football is a collective confrontational sport that focuses on controlling the ball with the feet. Known as the "No. 1 sport in the world", it is deeply loved by people from all over the world. Football has strong exercise and appreciation value. Regular participation can enhance physical fitness, develop athletic ability, and cultivate the ideological qualities of bravery, tenacity, wit, decisiveness, unity and cooperation, and can be used as a means to promote the development of exercise habits. _x000D_
The teaching content includes basic knowledge, basic techniques and basic tactics. On the premise of mastering basic football skills, it focuses on guiding the game to improve students' practical ability, understand football knowledge and rules, and be able to appreciate high-level football matches. _x000D_

Name: A Brief History of Western Opera and Appreciation of Masterworks
Introduction:
Teach the history of opera development from the birth of opera at the end of the 16th century to the 20th century. And selected classic opera works of more than a dozen famous composers from different periods and musical styles in the history of Western music for appreciation. Aiming at the perspective of ordinary college students' acceptance of music, the course introduces the content, composer, historical background, dramatic factors and musical methods of opera in more detail. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Historiography
Prerequisite: Chinese general history, world general history, Chinese history, foreign history.
Introduction: This course uses a combination of lectures, readings, class reports and discussions to systematically introduce various theories and important views on history at home and abroad, sort out different historical concepts such as traditional history, classic history, new history and post-modern history, explain various debates on the nature and significance of historical knowledge in the history of history, discuss various issues in the formation process of historical knowledge, and introduce the basic memory of historical writing to help students understand the basic issues of historical theory and become familiar with the basic memory of historical writing.

Name: Social Survey and Historical Research
Introduction: The course was originally targeted at third-year undergraduates in the Department of History. However, considering that third-year undergraduates are in summer vacation and may face various preparations for further studies, employment, and going abroad, and have limited energy, the course was moved forward to target second-year undergraduates. The purpose is to basically master the methods and characteristics of social investigation through the course, grasp the relationship between fieldwork and document research in historical research, and provide necessary training and preparation for social practice activities. On the one hand, it broadens the knowledge field of historical learning and research, and on the other hand, it strengthens the ability to understand society and practice hands-on practice. In the past ten years, the theories, methods and fields of historical research have undergone major changes. Among them, going out of the study room to conduct on-the-spot fieldwork, through empirical, regional, and case-by-case dynamic descriptions of historical development, can further accurately explain history and give full play to the social function of history. It has become an important method of historical research and teaching. Therefore, it is necessary to open a more systematic course, and it also has a certain foundation. The course content involves social investigation methods, oral history methods, and case analysis of social development and historical research from issues in various fields of social development. Students are required to carefully read relevant reference works, combine lectures, and read literature to propose feasible research outlines and investigation design arguments to lay a good foundation for summer social practice. The course results are composed of classroom performance, teaching visit reflections or reading notes, social survey topic design and argumentation (the above accounted for 60%), oral examination or open-book written examination (accounting for 40%), with the topic design and argumentation as the main component.

Name: History of Modern Sino-Russian Relations
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to cultivate and improve undergraduate students’ understanding of the history of Sino-Russian and Sino-Soviet relations. Through the research of teaching materials, historical materials and new archival materials, we will gain an in-depth understanding of the development of Sino-Soviet relations after the October 1917 Revolution in the Soviet Union. Specifically, the attitudes of the governments of the north and the south of China towards the October Revolution, the Eastern Qing Railway Incident (1929), the Soviet Union’s attitude towards the September 18th Incident, the formation of the Soviet Union and the Anti-Japanese United Front, the Soviet Union’s entry into the Northeast after World War II, the Soviet Union’s attitude towards the Kuomintang and the Communist Party during China’s Liberation War and its changes, The process and significance of the signing of the Sino-Soviet Mutual Assistance Alliance Treaty after the founding of the People's Republic of China, the Soviet Union's assistance to the economic construction of New China after the founding of the People's Republic of China, and the role of the Soviet Union during China's intervention in the Korean War, etc., to better grasp the status of Sino-Soviet relations in the historical development of Northeast Asia and the world after the October Revolution. The books I read were mainly textbooks such as "History of Sino-Soviet Relations during the Republic of China I II III", supplemented by "Outline of the History of Sino-Soviet Relations", "Middle East Railway Guards and the Political Situation in the Northeast Frontier", "History of Soviet Foreign Policy", "Data Collection on Sino-Soviet Relations (32 volumes in total)" and reference to first-hand materials or archives from the United States, Russia and China.

Name: General Survey of Korean History
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the history of Korea from ancient times to the present, focusing on political history, taking into account socio-economic history and ideological and cultural history. The contents include the origin of human civilization on the Korean Peninsula, the origin of the country, the origin of the Tangun myth and Jija legend, and the evolution of Tangun and Jija beliefs; the founding and unification of Silla, the bone system and the official system; the founding of Goryeo and the establishment of aristocratic society, the establishment and decline of the warrior regime, the relationship between Goryeo and the Yuan Dynasty, and the introduction of Neo-Confucianism And the formation of the emerging class of scholar-bureaucrats; the establishment of the Joseon Dynasty, the bureaucracy and social system, economic and cultural development of the Joseon Dynasty, the relationship between the Joseon Dynasty and China; the civilized enlightenment and anti-evil and orthodox movements in modern times, Japanese colonial rule; the division of North and South after liberation and the Korean War, the process of modernization and democratization, etc.

Name: Bodybuilding
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
Bodybuilding is a sport that uses bare hands or various equipment exercises to develop muscles, enhance physical strength, improve body shape and cultivate sentiment. _x000D_
This course mainly focuses on learning the basic theoretical knowledge and correct practice methods of bodybuilding, learning to formulate targeted bodybuilding exercise prescriptions, developing muscles, enhancing physical strength, sculpting and losing fat, and cultivating students' ability to appreciate beauty, pursue beauty, and create beauty, as well as the excellent qualities of perseverance, courage to challenge, and self-defeat. _x000D_
Course requirements:_x000D_
1. You need to wear sportswear and sneakers in class. Do not wear clothes that are too tight to avoid affecting your exercise. _x000D_
2． Take good care of the equipment and put it back to its original place after practicing to keep the venue clean. 3. When practicing with equipment, students should protect each other to avoid injuries. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students' physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, as well as the ideology of "health first". _x000D_
2． Improve students' health, enhance their physical fitness, and cultivate the habit of physical exercise_x000D_
3. Get a preliminary understanding of the basic theories and practice methods of bodybuilding. _x000D_
4. Initial understanding of bodybuilding rules and refereeing methods. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Art
Introduction: Peking University's art quality education general elective course "History of Chinese Art" is based on the order of historical development, from the origin of Chinese art to the Ming and Qing Dynasties. While appreciating rich works, it introduces the overview of ancient Chinese art history, including various art categories, art schools, representative figures, classic works and other important knowledge points.

Name: General History of Chinese Music
Introduction:
Music history is the study, explanation and understanding of historical music phenomena and facts related to music. Study the totality of musical works, events, characters and various human activity facts related to music produced during the development of human society, and make scientific summaries and inductions from them. The history of Chinese music is a historical process of development and evolution of Chinese music that lasts for thousands of years. According to the chronological order of development, it can be basically divided into music before the Qin and Han Dynasties; music of the Han and Tang Dynasties; music of the Song and Yuan Dynasties; music of the Ming and Qing Dynasties; modern Chinese music and modern Chinese music. China is a multi-ethnic country. In the long years from ancient times to modern times, people of all ethnic groups have jointly created the superior music culture of the motherland. _x000D_
This course is taught for one semester, 2 hours per week, 16 weeks. Chapter 1 Ancient Chinese Music requires students to have a systematic understanding of the temperament, singing and dancing, ritual and music systems of ancient Chinese music, musical works from the north and south, as well as musical instruments and instrumental music of this period, music treatises, music aesthetics, etc. Chapter 2 Chinese Medieval Music requires students to have a more systematic understanding of medieval music institutions, song and dance music, musical instruments and instrumental music, temperament and notation, and musical aesthetics. Chapter 3 Modern Chinese Music requires students to have a more systematic understanding of songs, musical instruments and instrumental music, rap music, opera music, temperament, music treatises, etc. in modern times. Chapter 4: Modern Chinese Music requires students to have a more systematic understanding of school music, authors, and the development of Peking Opera in modern times. Chapter 5: Modern Chinese Music requires students to have a systematic understanding of the creation of modern Chinese music, the establishment of a music education system, the creation of song and dance dramas, operas and film music, as well as music treatises and music aesthetics. Chapter 6 Chinese Contemporary Music requires students to have a systematic understanding of the creation, inheritance and development of Chinese contemporary music. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Cinema
Introduction:
"Chinese Film History" takes the 100-year development history of Chinese films as a clue, and tells the story of Zheng Zhengqiu, Shi Dongshan, and Cai Chu_x000D_
The image pursuit, spiritual exploration and cultural significance of six generations of Chinese filmmakers such as Sheng, Xie Jin, Zhang Yimou and Jia Zhangke_x000D_
As the main narrative content, it combines "Labor's Love", "Sister Flowers", "Yuguang Song", "Yijiangdongshui_x000D_"
"Flowing East", "Red Detachment of Women", "Shining Red Star", "Yellow Earth", "Red Sorghum", "Overlord_x000D_
A relatively comprehensive and in-depth exploration of the textual interpretation of films such as "Farewell My Concubine", "Xiao Wu", and "Seventeen-Year-Old Bicycle"_x000D_
Discuss the specific situation of Chinese film development and its experiences and lessons. _x000D_
  This course adopts a teaching method that combines classroom lectures, video viewing and focused discussions.

Name: Introduction to Chinese Art
Introduction: Course introduction (in order to facilitate students to choose courses, please be no less than 200 words, and you can attach an additional page) Course nature and objectives: The "Introduction to Chinese Art" course introduces the main types, techniques, works, masters and achievements, and artistic concepts of Chinese art from the shallower to the deeper, and outlines a concise, clear and complete outline of the long and rich Chinese art. In the process of describing the characteristics of Chinese art and the methods of appreciating art works, it guides students to enter the door of Chinese art, appreciate its mystery, style and charm, and thus have a deeper understanding of Chinese culture. The arrangement and presentation methods of the course have the following three basic characteristics: 1. View from all aspects. Breaking the general convention of following the order of historical eras, instead giving special introductions according to the type of art theme and form, such as landscape painting, Chinese sculpture, Chinese color, Chinese contemporary art, etc. Each lecture is a special topic, so that students can focus on mastering a certain aspect of knowledge and thinking about a certain type of problem; 2. Comparative perspective. Adopt the method of comparing Chinese and foreign art to highlight the Chinese characteristics of art knowledge; 3. Cultural outlook. Highlight cultural concepts in the interpretation of artistic forms of art works, understand the reasons why authors painted this way instead of painting (or carving) that way, reduce technical obstacles in art majors, and enhance the depth of thought and culture. Please see the attached syllabus for the specific content of the course. Teaching methods: Mainly based on classroom lectures, each course is supplemented by a large number of exquisite original pictures to observe, and the visual works are the center of the teaching. At the same time, there are classroom discussions, writing book reports and short reviews, and visiting art exhibitions and other activities.

Name: Topics in Computing for the Humanities
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Human beings have entered the information society, and computers, networks, multimedia and information processing have become indispensable tools in people's economic activities, social interactions and daily life. The awareness and basic skills of using computers, the ability to use computers to achieve information acquisition, representation, storage, transmission, processing, control and application, and the ability to solve practical problems have become one of the important indicators of a person's cultural quality. The teaching goal of liberal arts computer basic courses is to cultivate and improve college students' information awareness and improve their ability to apply computers to solve specific problems. _x000D_
The teaching of liberal arts computer basics is divided into two levels:_x000D_
The first level is computer basics. It consists of modules such as basic computer knowledge, computer operating system and its use, multimedia knowledge and application foundation, graphics and image production and processing foundation, office software application, computer network foundation, Internet basic application, and information retrieval and utilization foundation. This level of teaching content is studied by students of all liberal arts majors. _x000D_
The second level is computer basic special courses, including modules such as programming and its applications, multimedia technology and its applications, web design basics, database basics and its applications, etc. This part of teaching determines, to a greater extent, students' ability and level of applying computers to solve problems in their majors. Students can choose to study a certain module based on their professional needs and interests. _x000D_

Name: The Charm of Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Charming Chemistry is a chemistry course offered to all undergraduates in the school. By introducing the great contribution of chemistry to modern civilization, it reveals the meaning of chemistry as a core science, and demonstrates the supporting role of chemistry in modern industry and related disciplines such as energy, physics, materials, biology, information, etc. It uses simple and lively language and teaching methods to review major events in the development of chemistry, explore challenging topics in today's frontier fields of chemistry, and look forward to the future role of chemistry in promoting the development of human civilization and society. The course is presented in the form of special lectures, with detailed lectures by long-term researchers in related fields, combined with classroom discussions, to expand students' basic knowledge of chemistry and improve students' ability to understand, understand, and apply chemistry.

Name: Introduction to Advertising
Introduction:
"Introduction to Advertising" is a basic course for advertising majors. The purpose of the course is to introduce and discuss the development process, overall overview and future trends of the advertising industry, so as to lay a foundation for further learning and research. _x000D_
The course will combine cases and study the development models of the advertising industry at different stages, the service models, and business models of advertising service companies to help students gradually form an overall analytical framework and thinking method for advertising issues. _x000D_
The course places special emphasis on the analysis of the development of the advertising industry in the Chinese environment, as well as the analysis of the challenges and changes brought about by the Internet, in the hope that the course learning can be better aligned with the actual development of the advertising industry. _x000D_
During the course, industry experts will be arranged to participate in lectures and visit advertising service companies, hoping to enhance students' understanding of the advertising operation process and make up for the lack of theoretical learning.

Name: History of Foreign Historiography
Introduction: This course is a required course for history majors. Its main content teaches the formation and development process of various countries in the world, especially Western history from ancient times to the present. Including the major historians of the Greek and Roman era and their writings, as well as the principles and traditions of narration and compilation of Western historiography formed thereby; the main characteristics of Western historiography in the Middle Ages and the Christian view of historical development; the emergence of modern rationalist historiography, romantic historiography, positivist historiography and objectivist historiography. Historical background, school characteristics, major historians and writings, and the impact of various academic schools on the development of Western history; the impact of Marxist history on the development of Western history; modern Western historical philosophy; the development and changes of Western historiography in the 20th century; new trends in the development of contemporary Western historiography, etc. This course highlights the introduction of historical thinking and historical methods.

Name: General Survey of World History
Introduction: This course is a basic course for world history majors for undergraduates in the Department of History at Peking University. It aims to help students understand as much basic information about the subject of "world history" as widely as possible, learn basic theories and methods for macroscopic examination of human history, cultivate the ability to independently construct an understanding framework of overall human history, and lay the foundation for future professional studies. The basic contents include: 1) Explanation of the concept of "world history" (origin and evolution; the significance of learning world history; the construction process of the Chinese world history discipline; the main traditions of the Western world history discipline); 2) the basic situation of modern Western macro-world history (from the perspective of cultural unity) On the transformation to cultural pluralism, the major schools of contemporary global history or history of civilization); 3. The basic viewpoint of the Peking University version of "History of World Civilizations" ("World History" should be understood as the history of world civilizations evolving in interactions - explained in conjunction with the basic processes of world history).

Name: Social and Historical Survey
Prerequisite: General history of China, social studies and history studies
Introduction:
The course is mainly targeted at second-year undergraduates in the Department of History. The purpose is to provide undergraduates with an opportunity to understand society, understand society, and conduct investigation and research on related topics in conjunction with professional studies, so as to combine on-campus classroom learning with social practice activities, improve their ability to understand and solve problems, and enhance their awareness of real-life care and social service. _x000D_
Before the summer vacation, students should first complete the "Social Investigation and Historical Research" course offered by the Department of History, basically master the methods and characteristics of social investigation, grasp the relationship between fieldwork and document research in historical research, and form a group of one to three people to complete the feasibility demonstration of topics related to summer social practice. After the start of the summer, each group will conduct social surveys at various social practice locations based on feasibility studies on relevant topics and indoor literature collection and reading. The survey content includes: local archives, literature collection, visits to relevant government departments, social groups, government agencies, enterprises and villages, oral interviews and questionnaires, on-site observations and experiences, etc. The survey generally lasts about 10 days. _x000D_
After the on-site field investigation is completed, a social investigation report needs to be written in groups based on the survey data, which will be revised and submitted after returning to school as the basis for determining course grades. Scores are based on a hundred-point system, and those who pass will receive one credit. _x000D_

Name: Medieval European History
Introduction: There are at least two important reasons for studying and researching medieval history. One is to understand medieval history itself, and the other is to understand and understand the foundation of modern European and even Western history and culture. This course hopes to familiarize students with relevant historical figures and events and understand the historical changes and characteristics of this period through an introduction to medieval politics, economy, society, religion and culture. At the same time, this course expects students to have an understanding of the history and current situation of Western medieval European history research, and to be able to critically absorb the theories and methods of Western historiography to a certain extent.

Name: African History
Introduction: As the birthplace of human history, Africa is not only a geographical term, but also represents a civilization. What its history shows is a unique development process of human society and culture. To study this process from a historical perspective, the first thing involved is the periodization of African history. On this basis, we need to understand several important stages in its historical process in order to better understand Africa today. Secondly, it is emphasized that as an important part of world history, Africa has made its own contribution. We cannot only see the shortcomings of her existence today due to lack of historical perspective. Third, we should pay attention to the history and current situation of China-Africa relations, because this is a subject worth studying. For students, they can compare the history of China and Africa; for scholars, their research on this topic has certain advantages over Western scholars. Furthermore, international media coverage of China-China relations has increased rapidly in recent years. This requires us to make our own judgment on the current situation by studying the history of China-Africa relations.

Name: Eastern Literature
Introduction: In the context of the history of the development of world literature, this course defines the origins and value orientations of Eastern and Western civilization, culture, and literature, macroscopically examines the history of the evolution and displacement, conflict, and integration of Eastern and Western literary centers, and macroscopically sorts out the relationship between Eastern and Western literature and the brief history of the development of Eastern literary concepts from a multi-dimensional perspective. It also focuses on studying classic works of Eastern literature, conducting case analysis from the perspectives of myths, epics, stories, poems, novels, dramas, etc., and examining the facts of exchanges, influences, and communication in the development process of Eastern and Western literature. This course hopes that students will have an overall impression of the development process of oriental literature, carefully read key classic works, and then think about how to construct a theoretical system of world literature that reflects the true development process of world literature.

Name: Tai Chi
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
Tai Chi is a soft, slow, and agile boxing technique. It uses tent, stroke, squeeze, press, pick, line, elbow, lean, advance, retreat, look, hope, and concentration as the basic postures (commonly known as the eight methods and five steps). The movements are soft and round, with clear definition of reality and reality, with arcs everywhere. The movement is continuous and the momentum is continuous. _x000D_
This course mainly studies "Twenty-Four Postures of Tai Chi", also called "Simplified Tai Chi". Its content is concise, the movements are standardized, the quantity is reasonable, it is easy to learn and practice, and it can fully reflect the movement characteristics of Tai Chi. Through practice, externally it can benefit the joints, strengthen the muscles and bones, and strengthen the body; internally, it can regulate the internal organs, unblock the muscles and meridians, and regulate the spirit. It is very useful for regulating the balance of the internal environment, regulating qi and blood, relieving physical and mental fatigue, improving human body functions, and enhancing physical fitness. _x000D_
Course requirements:_x000D_
1. In principle, students are not allowed to skip classes. _x000D_
2. Teachers and students should give each other a fist salute when entering and leaving class. _x000D_
3. No drinking, overeating or fasting before class. Smoking, chewing gum or eating snacks is not allowed during class. _x000D_
4. If students have physical discomfort or past medical history, they should report to the teacher before class and consider arranging the activity content and amount of exercise according to the specific situation. _x000D_
5. You must wear sportswear and sneakers in class, and place your schoolbags, clothes, etc. neatly as required by the teacher. _x000D_
6. Take good care of the equipment. During class, do not carry any hard objects that may harm yourself or others. Such as: pens, mobile phones, knives, keys and key chains, etc. _x000D_
7. You are not allowed to use mobile phones, send text messages, or listen to Walkmans during class. _x000D_
8. During the practice, you should act within your ability according to your own physical fitness. Do not move too hard or move too wide due to temporary excitement, which may lead to physical accidents and injuries. _x000D_
9. When students are required to practice together, listen carefully to the explanation and strictly follow the teacher's instructions. Extreme personal behaviors such as laughing, playing, taking risks, etc. are not allowed. A practice atmosphere of unity, friendship, carefulness, tacit cooperation, and mutual help must be created to ensure the safety and effectiveness of the practice. _x000D_
10. Do not bring valuables to class to avoid loss. _x000D_
11. Practice seriously, and then learn certain sports skills while developing in an all-round way to improve your physical fitness and achieve the purpose of strengthening your physique. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students’ physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, as well as the ideology of “health first”. _x000D_
2. Improve health, enhance physical fitness, and comprehensively improve students' physical and psychological qualities. _x000D_
3. Master the basic theory, basic techniques and full set of movements of Twenty-Four Tai Chi. _x000D_

Name: Olympic Culture
Introduction:
The Olympic Movement is the highest form of modern sports and the concentrated expression of human culture. _x000D_
Beijing successfully bid for the Olympics in 2008, and the slogans of "Humanistic Olympics," "Green Olympics," and "Technological Olympics" revealed the intricate relationship between the Olympic movement and many issues such as science and technology, environmental protection, and human development. _x000D_
Looking at the history of the Olympic movement, modern sports are closely related to the development, change and continuation of human culture. International and domestic political, economic and social developments in different periods directly or indirectly affect the bid, organization and participation of each Olympic Games; people's attitudes and understanding of the Olympics can be reflected in the value orientation, aesthetic taste and ethical norms of different nations and periods. _x000D_
The Olympic Movement has made it a unique global cultural phenomenon through its charter, purpose, organizational structure, activity forms, etc. _x000D_
The "Olympic Culture" course is a new theoretical course that integrates physical education, history, human culture and sociology. _x000D_
We will discuss the development, change and continuation of culture from the historical process of the Olympic Movement, teach the influence and role of different national cultures on the Olympic Movement and the impact of the Olympic Games on architecture, music, dance, art, etc., and introduce the development of the Olympic Movement in our country, the basic pattern of today's international sports, the organization and future direction of the Olympic Games, etc.

Name: The Evolution of Chinese Popular Music
Introduction:

Overview of popular music Tracing the origins of popular music (popular music after 1900)_x000D_
An introduction to the first generation of musicians in the 20th century _x000D_

Popular music works and musicians from the early 20th century to the 1920s_x000D_

The original generation of pop music, movie interludes in the 1930s and 1940s, the first generation of urban pop music and singers, singing forms, performance modes_x000D_

Mass songs of the 1950s, movie interludes, new folk songs, new generation singers_x000D_

"The East is Red" song and dance, 1960s movie interludes, national operas, mass-created songs_x000D_
Chapter 6_x000D_
Mass-created songs, eight model operas, singers trained by the academy_x000D_

The infiltration of Hong Kong and Taiwan pop music in the 1980s, the influence of American country music, songs sung by Hong Kong, Taiwan, Japan and other singers, singing forms, performance modes_x000D_
Chapter 8_x000D_

Name: Comparative Study of Chinese and Foreign Art Creation
Introduction: As an important part of world art history, Chinese art has its own unique tradition. However, for a long time, due to the great differences in the creation of Chinese and foreign art, it has caused obstacles for the two to appreciate, understand and learn from each other. The first part of this course is the technique part. It starts from the perspective of comparing Chinese and foreign art creation techniques, focusing on the research of art creation rules, art creation methods, methods and factors that affect art creation. It analyzes and compares many painting factors such as composition, lines, colors, shapes, etc., and combines it with the experience gained from thirty years of painting creation and trying to organically combine Chinese and Western painting methods, so that students can have a comprehensive understanding of Chinese and Western art in terms of creative techniques. The second part focuses on the works, analyzing and comparing the painting creations of Chinese and Western artists, so that students can quickly understand the different and same aesthetic expression methods of Chinese and Western art, master the main creative rules of Chinese and foreign art, and quickly improve their appreciation and judgment of a work.  This course involves art works from the four cultural circles of ancient China, Japan, Russia and Europe. From different perspectives, we understand the fundamental differences between the most representative art works in these four cultural circles and the possibility of mutual communication and learning.   This course is not only suitable for general art education for Chinese undergraduate students, but also suitable for helping foreign students understand Chinese art from the art works of their own culture. At the same time, it can also help inspire graduate students in the fields of art history, aesthetics, art studies, cultural history and other fields with a certain research foundation to understand art from a comparative perspective.

Name: Chinese Women's History and Traditional Culture
Introduction: This course is offered to undergraduate history students at Peking University. From the perspective of reinterpretation of traditional culture, we use the theory of gender and difference to teach several topics in the history of women in ancient China. We will reinterpret ancient Chinese women's history from multiple dimensions such as politics, economy, thought, law, culture (female education, etc.), customs (foot binding, topless clothing, etc.); and we will guide students to re-examine traditional mainstream historical materials and texts, paying attention to marginal historical materials that were ignored in the past; and guide students how to use gender theory, the most important theory in the study of women's issues today, to guide their thinking. We hope that through this course, we will not only introduce students to the history of women in ancient China, but also enable students to gain something from theoretical and perspective perspectives.

Name: Modern Chinese History
Introduction:
This course is one of the required courses in the "General History of China" series for undergraduates in the Department of History. It is planned to continue teaching "Modern History of China" (1919-) after "Modern History of China" (1840--). This course will take 1949 as the boundary and be divided into upper and lower sections, respectively teaching the "History of the Republic of China" from 1919 to 1949 and the "History of the People's Republic of China" after 1949. _x000D_
This course will follow the "general history" teaching model, distinguishing periods and stages, focusing on the content of modern Chinese political history, and taking into account economic, military, diplomatic, social, cultural and ideological history and other aspects. _x000D_
This course will use classroom lectures as the main teaching method, supplemented by reading reports, seminars, visits, lectures, etc. The focus is on assessing students' mastery of basic knowledge of modern Chinese history as well as their personal thinking abilities and academic insights. _x000D_
The teaching purpose of this course is to lay an academic foundation for students to continue studying various special courses in modern Chinese history. _x000D_

Name: History of Ancient Sino-Foreign Relations
Introduction:
Before China was invaded by foreign powers and kicked off modern history, ancient China had continuous interactions with the outside world, and its historical picture was also rich and colorful. The nomadic people-mediated exchanges in the pre-Qin period, Zhang Qian’s passage to the Western Regions created direct connections between China and the West, the Silk Road trade between the Han and Tang dynasties and the large number of Central Asians settling in China, the influence of the barbarians and “Huhua” on the society of the Sui and Tang dynasties, the opening of the Maritime Silk Road in the Song and Yuan Dynasties, the arrival of the Jesuits from the Ming and Qing dynasties and the spread of Chinese culture to the west. These are all important chapters in the history of Sino-foreign relations that we already know. _x000D_
	This course is mainly based on the research results of the teachers in recent years. It describes some special research results on the history of Sino-foreign relations during the Han and Tang Dynasties, and how to use documents, unearthed documents, archeology, images and other materials to study some difficult issues in the history of Sino-foreign relations. It guides students to use relevant materials to study certain issues on their own. According to the interests and research orientations of students of different grades, the content taught each semester is different. Sometimes it may focus on the history of cultural exchanges between China and the West, and sometimes it may focus on the history of Sino-foreign relations after the Jesuits came to China, so as to help students develop their own strengths. _x000D_

Name: Political History of the Qin, Han, Wei, Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties
Introduction: This course is suitable for undergraduate students who are beginners in ancient Chinese history. The Qin and Han Dynasties were the beginning of the two thousand years of imperialism. The centralized bureaucratic political system laid the foundation, and politics, economy and culture fully developed and reached their peak. During the Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties, it experienced turmoil and division, gentry politics, minority dominance and ethnic conflicts, but it gradually came out of its trough in the late Southern and Northern Dynasties. This course will describe the main events in the history of the Qin, Han, Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties, explain the clues of political development in each period, analyze relevant major issues, elaborate on the process of the Chinese empire from its foundation to its peak, the development of the centralized bureaucracy, the ups and downs of various political forces, and the corresponding changes in the economy and culture; understand the reasons for the decline of the imperial system in the medieval period. This enables students to understand the basic development outline of Chinese politics in the early imperial period, stimulate historical thinking, and initially master relevant historical research results and historical analysis methods.

Name: Comparison of Chinese and Western Cultures
Introduction:
This course is mainly a theoretical comparison of several important aspects of Western and Central culture. First of all, it draws on the interlocking effects and constraints of western and central cultures, and then compares the differences and differences between the Chinese and western languages (Chinese and Indo-European languages, especially English), then expands the theoretical differences in the focus between the 10 disciplines of philosophy, aesthetics, law, ethics, literature, economics, science and technology, medicine, religion and education, and identifies regularities that will enable participants to grasp the essence of western and central culture in general macros and provide them with a number of guiding macro-level knowledge for their future micro-studies in a particular subject. In our country, comparative cultural science is still an emerging subject, which is particularly important and necessary for contemporary students, who have the advantage of foreign languages and have the ability to read relevant Western language literature to varying degrees directly, thus providing the most favourable conditions for the smooth running of the course. On the other hand, since in recent decades all our universities have paid little attention to the general macro-knowledge transfer of Western and Central culture in their curricula, which has led to the development of students of certain classes as mere tools, a relative lack of basic macro-level cultural knowledge and theoretical literacy, and the difficulty of becoming generalists and masters, despite their ability to be locally useful, the subject as an experiment is of great relevance in providing some kind of ablaze for future masters and masters.
The course was reviewed by experts from the University Quality Education Research Branch of the Chinese Society of Higher Education and was awarded a National Certificate of Honour in April 2014 for the “Quality Education Qualifications of the University”.

Name: Twentieth-Century Western Music
Introduction:
Although "Western Music in the 20th Century" is a chronological history of the "General History of Western Music", it has become an independent discipline in the field of global Western music history research because it is close to the present and all-inclusive. Due to historical reasons, China’s teaching of Western music history has long had a “braised middle” phenomenon, that is, it only teaches the two stylistic periods of Classicism and Romanticism (1750-1900). The previous Baroque, Renaissance, Middle Ages, Ancient Greece and Ancient Rome periods, and the subsequent 20th century were rarely covered, hence the reputation. In recent years, this situation has greatly improved, and the level has also improved rapidly. Since the teacher studied for a doctorate in this subject at the Central Conservatory of Music from 2000 to 2004, he has taught this course many times for students in the musicology teacher training courses of his alma mater and Chinese universities. After teaching at Peking University in 2007, it was offered as a public elective course in the second semester of 2008, the first semester of 2009, and the second semester of 2010. It was established as a general elective course in 2011. _x000D_
_x000D_
"20th Century Western Music" is an independent course covering three major research topics, namely art music (classical music in a broad sense), folk music and commercial music (popular music). On the premise of following the three major topics, the course content has different emphasis in different semesters and is not the same. For example, in 2010, it was "Special Topic on Western Piano Music in the 20th Century", in 2011 it was "Special Topic on Art Music", in 2012 it was "Special Topic on Popular Music", etc.

Name: Topics in the History of the People's Republic of China
Prerequisite: Students must have basic knowledge of the history of the People ' s Republic of China.
Introduction: The history of the People ' s Republic of China, as an emerging discipline, has received increasing attention. This is the history that we have shared with our generations and is highly relevant. Learning from this recent history helps to provide a scientific and comprehensive understanding of the winds and winds that the Chinese nation has experienced for more than 50 years, an understanding of the imperatives of reform and openness and an understanding of the challenges of the new century. Name: History of Everyday Life in Ancient China
Prerequisite: There is no mandatory requirement for the students ' first course, and it is hoped that the students ' secondary schools will have studied Chinese history, read the basic Chinese history books and are interested in the ancient Chinese history.
Introduction: The history of daily life is an important branch in current historical research. It is a new historical school that emerged from the West in the 1970s. The rise of this school of thought is actually the product of self-reflection and self-criticism of modern Western historiography. The main trend in the development of Western history in the last century was "social scientificization", which means viewing human history as a purely objective existence and being keen on statistics, drawing charts, outlining development curves, building macro frameworks, and creating social development models. According to such a "social science view of history", historical research should have a long-term, long-span macroscopic vision, focus on "big structures, big processes, and big comparisons" and strive to explain the laws of progress of human society as a whole. Scholars of daily life history have questioned this "macro" history. They believe that the biggest drawback of "scientific" history is that it "sees things but not people". Without the core of "people", no social phenomenon can be correctly explained. Scholars of the history of daily life believe that in real life, individuals are far away from "behemoths" such as "structure" and "system", but family members, neighbors, and even conversation partners can have a huge impact on people's behavior. In this sense, interpersonal communication is far better than "structure" in explaining the driving force of social development. Therefore, the history of daily life studies "daily behaviors" and explores the motivations of history at the level of small groups. This school of thought believes that historical pictures are drawn by specific people in specific life practices. Their focus is on food, clothing, housing, transportation, weddings, funerals, social interactions, etc. The content and teaching of this course are based on the above theory. This course hopes to enable students to understand the vivid daily life of ancient Chinese people through teaching topics that are specific and nuanced and closely related to the daily life of ancient Chinese people, and to see the interaction between family and country, between people and society, and the operation of social gender. This course will use the theory of daily life history, based on three levels of daily consumption, daily interactions, and daily concepts, and take multiple aspects such as clothing, food, housing, transportation, childhood, marriage, childbirth, elderly care, medical care, and funerals as the entry point to show the daily life of ancient Chinese people, and thereby observe the relationship between the country, society, individuals, and men and women.

Name: The Official Rank System of Ancient China
Introduction: Ancient China developed a complex and thorough official rank system. Its function was to organize the administrative levels and manage the taste of bureaucrats based on the position structure and personnel structure of the bureaucracy. Research on the traditional official hierarchy can reveal many important laws and characteristics of ancient administration, politics, society and even culture. This course will systematically describe the grades of various eras, and elaborate on the basic methods, theoretical framework and related major issues of the study of official hierarchy. Name: History of Modern Chinese Thought
Introduction: Modern China is a great era of conflict and integration between China and the West, traditional and modern cultures. This era produced a number of influential thinkers. They stood at the commanding heights of the times and re-examined the history of national culture, explored the future of China and mankind, and constructed a new ideological and theoretical system, which provided new cultural nourishment for the survival and development of the Chinese nation. This course systematically reviews famous thinkers in modern China, mainly including Kang Youwei, Yan Fu, Tan Sitong, Zhang Taiyan, Sun Yat-sen, Wang Guowei, Cai Yuanpei, Chen Duxiu, Hu Shi, Li Dazhao, Liang Shuming, Feng Youlan, Mao Zedong, etc. It explores the formation process of their thoughts, compares the similarities and differences of their thoughts, and highlights their ideological characteristics, so that students can have a clearer outline of modern Chinese thinkers, schools of thought, and ideological development trends.

Name: Archaeology of the Silk Road
Introduction:
This course will systematically describe the history of cultural exchanges between China and the West, especially the new archaeological discoveries along the Silk Road from the Bronze Age to the era of Zheng He’s voyages to the West (1405-1433). The opening of the Silk Road was directly related to Zhang Qian's expedition to the Western Regions in the 2nd century BC. A large number of reports about Zhang Qian's expedition to the Western Regions were included in Sima Qian's "Historical Records". According to Zhang Qian's report, he visited the Dawan Kingdom in Fergana, Kangju (Sogdia) in Uzbekistan, the Yuezhi in the Hezhong region, and Bactria (Bactria) in northern Afghanistan. During his second mission to the Western Regions, Zhang Qian visited the Wusun tribe of the Ili River (the so-called "Isetonians" by the Greek writer Herodotus). At the same time, he sent deputy envoys to visit Shendu (now Pakistan) and other countries in West Asia, such as Parthia (Parthia) on the Iranian plateau, Tiochi (Antioch) in northern Syria, and Amcha (Alan people) on the east coast of the Black Sea. _x000D_
The name of the Silk Road is translated from the German Seidenstra?e and named by the geographer Richthofen. According to the German scholar's definition, the Silk Road was an ancient international trade route that started from Zhang Qian and led to the Western Regions, from Chang'an City, through the Central Asian desert, to the Eastern Province of the Roman Empire (today's northern Syria). However, historical records and archaeological discoveries show that the Silk Road also had two important branch routes, called the "Prairie Road" and the "Sea Road". _x000D_
The Steppe Road runs from north China to the west and ends at the Black Sea. This road was pioneered by nomads from the Central Asian steppes in the 7th century BC. Scythian merchants played an important role in opening up the steppe road. From 1207 to 1360, the expansion of the Mongols in the Asian continent helped to rebuild the grassland road (via the capital of the Mongol Empire, Harakhorin). After the Mongols took control of international trade routes, the Silk Road prospered like never before. Around the same time, the Venetian merchant Marco Polo became the first European to enter China via the desert road. His travels to the East, "The World" (or "Marco Polo's Travels"), opened up Westerners' perspective on the customs and customs of the Far East. _x000D_
According to Chinese historical data, the monarch of Qi in Shandong Peninsula was addicted to the elixir of life, so a large number of alchemists went to the sea to seek immortality. Persian silverware and glass beads unearthed from ancient tombs in Qi in recent years prove the credibility of this theory. In other words, maritime traffic between the Shandong Peninsula and the Persian Gulf began at least in the 3rd century BC. Maritime trade between China and Persia continued to develop during the Han and Tang dynasties. In 1998, a medieval shipwreck was discovered off the coast of Belitung Island in Indonesia. It was a Persian dhow that sailed between the Middle East and China. It sank around 830 AD. During the Song Dynasty, there was still large-scale maritime trade between China and the Arabian Peninsula and East Africa. This historical fact is also proved by the discovery of Song Dynasty shipwrecks in the South China Sea and the Indian Ocean. During the Yongle and Xuande years of the Ming Dynasty, the Ming court organized seven maritime expeditions, known in history as "Zheng He's voyages to the West". Zheng He's fleet visited Southeast Asia, India, East Africa, the Persian Gulf, and the Arabian Peninsula, distributing gifts of gold, silver, porcelain, silk, etc. along the way, and accepting tributes from Middle Eastern and Eastern countries, such as ostriches, zebras, camels, ivories, and giraffes. In 1511, the Portuguese occupied Malacca, cutting off the traditional links between China and the Indian Ocean countries, and the Silk Road, which had a history of thousands of years of civilization, completely declined. _x000D_

Introduction:
The importance of innovation and entrepreneurship to China's economic development and transformation has become increasingly significant, providing unprecedented opportunities for industrial and commercial enterprises and entrepreneurs. It also requires business managers and entrepreneurs to master the basic theories and skills of innovation and entrepreneurship management. This course is one of the responses to the requirements of this new situation in basic business education. This course is divided into the following four modules: _x000D_

Name: Pricing Management
Introduction:
This course combines Western pricing theory and my own 1P price theory to provide a systematic theoretical analysis framework, strategies and techniques for pricing decision-making and price management. Through the study of this course, students are required to understand the formulation of pricing strategies and techniques, the period of price adjustment, the extent of price adjustment, and the direction of price adjustment; understand how to find a third party to share costs for the enterprise and share prices with customers, so that the price can still be lower than the average cost. Profit; understand how to resolve the opposition and contradiction between price strategy (1P) and product strategy, channel strategy, and promotion strategy (3P); understand how to convey price adjustment information to the inside and outside of the enterprise, the role of pricing in marketing innovation, and the process of controlling pricing. _x000D_

Name: Brand Management
Introduction: This course starts from the basic concept of brand, and from the perspective of combining theory and practice, it specifically and in-depth explains the basic process for enterprises to create and manage brands, and continuously improve brand equity. Specifically including: brand overview, brand positioning and brand creation, as well as brand development and brand extension, etc.

Name: Operations and Information Management
Introduction: The course is divided into two parts: the Operational Management and Management Information System, the main component of which is the collection, processing and analysis of data and information generated from business management using mathematical and computer tools to enable managers to make scientific decisions. The operational management component focuses on the basic elements of operational preparation, namely the application of quantitative analysis, the integration of human, material and financial resources in economic management systems and the search for optimal decision-making options for the most effective management. Preparatory education is a core course in management science and an essential tool for students in the various disciplines of the Institute of Management. In the information age, the use of preparatory science in management has become increasingly widespread and important. The management information system component focuses on the application of information systems in enterprises. Management information systems are being given widespread attention and are increasingly being used in a wide range of industries as competition increases and enterprises are increasingly demanding levels of work efficiency, process control, management and decision-making. In large and medium-sized enterprises, in particular, the products, processes and management controls of enterprises can be effective productivity for enterprises only if they are realized in MI systems, so many of them use enterprise information systems as an expression of their core competitiveness. Since the business environment is changing and business management is constantly seeking to optimize, improvements in management information systems are an endless process. It is precisely because of the role played by MIS in the management of business operations and the features of continuous improvement that the course has received widespread attention in virtually all well-known universities in the various professions involved in business management, and has been made compulsory. The teaching content of MI systems consists of an organic combination of basic theory and basic skills of a multidisciplinary nature, covering almost all computer-related technologies, applications of management science in information systems development, experience in business management, etc., and is a course with a higher level of study, knowledge point and complexity in undergraduate teaching programmes.

Name: Topics in Marketing
Introduction: This course is a required professional course for senior undergraduate students majoring in marketing and is taught by teachers from the marketing department. In the form of special lectures, this course introduces new developments in marketing theories, methods and practices to expand students' knowledge. At the same time, it allows students to have a certain understanding of the main research areas of marketing and the research interests and expertise of the lecturer, laying a solid foundation for the selection of graduation thesis topics. The specific format of the course is: each teacher in the Marketing Department introduces research or practice in related fields based on his or her own interests and research expertise, and shares his or her own experience and insights.

Name: Production and Operations Management
Introduction: Operations management is the study of how a business manages its production or service processes. Effective operations management is the key for enterprises to remain competitive. At the same time, operations management is also the link between other functional departments within an enterprise (such as finance, marketing, human resources, etc.). Operations management is a comprehensive management discipline that requires students to master certain basic knowledge of operations research, mathematical statistics, managerial economics, accounting, human resources and other disciplines, and to be able to comprehensively apply them in the study of this course.

Name: Growth of Entrepreneurial Ventures
Introduction: This course is designed for students who are interested in running and managing entrepreneurial growth-stage enterprises. In the course, we will combine on-site visits and special class discussions to train students to comprehensively analyze core entrepreneurial management issues such as business models, strategies, markets, financing, human resources, organizational structure, corporate culture, and business environment of growth-stage enterprises from a comprehensive perspective.

Name: Entrepreneurship and Innovation Practicum
Introduction: This course is designed for dual-major undergraduate students in innovation and entrepreneurship management who have a passion for innovation and entrepreneurship. Through the "Entrepreneurship Assistant" program and innovation and entrepreneurship case writing, students can directly participate in innovation and entrepreneurship practice, experience the actual innovation and entrepreneurship process, and accumulate relevant experience.

Name: New Marketing Models in the Internet Age
Introduction: We are living in and will live in the Internet era in the future. Internet marketing is becoming an important factor affecting businesses and individuals. Internet marketing always affects a person's destiny in the Internet era. This course mainly introduces what new marketing models are in the Internet era and how to apply them in the business field, especially how companies use Internet marketing thinking to creatively innovate, new product development processes, consumer preferences, new product promotion techniques, and related business model innovation and changes.

Name: Life Planning and Career Development
Introduction: The course will focus on stimulating students' passion for establishing career ideals and forming an attitude of rational pursuit of career goals, so as to actively exercise and self-cultivate their practical abilities. By introducing career planning methods and resources, this course guides students to establish the concept of proactive life and career planning, discover personal career tendencies and potentials, learn how to communicate effectively and establish interpersonal networks, market themselves appropriately, master interview skills, understand normative behaviors in the workplace, and strengthen their understanding of professional ethics and ethics.

Name: New Media Marketing and Targeted Advertising
Introduction:
In today's era of the Internet, social networks and mobile phones, marketers face many new opportunities and challenges in customer communication, customer acquisition, advertising, etc. Traditional print media such as newspapers and magazines have declined sharply, television has been gradually replaced by streaming video websites, and the rise of the Internet and mobile terminals are all new issues for traditional marketing channels. In addition to new marketing channels, in the era of big data, individual user data is becoming more and more available, providing marketers with new perspectives and opportunities. How to use this data to classify users and accurately advertise, thereby improving the effectiveness of advertising, is of very practical significance. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course explores these issues in three parts. The first part aims to establish a conceptual framework to understand and quantify advertising effectiveness using return on investment (ROI). We introduce controlled experiments and natural experiment methods to measure ROI, and demonstrate common mistakes in practical work in the form of cases. In the second part, we introduce different advertising platforms and channels, including digital media advertising, search engine advertising, display advertising, online video platform advertising, social network advertising, and mobile advertising. We highlight the unique features of different media, how to use them, and how to measure their effectiveness. In the third part, students choose a case that is happening in the Chinese market and use the framework in class to present the case. It can be a reference to the advertising model currently underway in China, or some new creative ideas. _x000D_

Name: Marketing Research Methods
Introduction:
Facing the ever-changing market and fierce competitive environment, how to collect timely, accurate and useful information, obtain profound marketing insights, and serve marketing decisions is an important task for marketing managers. Marketing research methods is an important professional basic course for marketing majors. It is also a commonly required course for marketing majors in domestic and foreign management schools. _x000D_
This course combines the current status and development trends of domestic and foreign market research, tracks the latest progress of current online research and big data applications, systematically introduces and discusses the main steps, related theories, methods and applications in the marketing research process, and cultivates students' comprehensive quality and practical ability to discover, analyze and solve marketing problems. _x000D_

With the rapid development of the national economy, the security of energy and mineral resources has increasingly become one of the important prerequisites for my country's sustainable development. Name: Economics
Introduction: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students to the basic principles of economics. The first half of the course focuses on microeconomics, that is, the decisions and choices made by the basic individuals (households and businesses) in the economy. The second half of the course focuses on macroeconomic issues, that is, the basic problems faced by society as a whole (such as unemployment, inflation, monetary policy, international trade, etc.).

Name: Innovation Management
Introduction: Through case study, students can better understand the impact of innovation on the survival and development of enterprises in real business environments, deepen their understanding of opportunities and supporting conditions for enterprise development, and initially master knowledge about innovation models and processes, strategies, processes, organizations and technologies that support innovation, so that enterprises can gain sustainable advantages through innovation in global competition.

Name: Sustainable Entrepreneurship
Introduction:
The issue of sustainable development of enterprises is first of all the issue of "whose development" the enterprise continues. An enterprise must first sustain its development. The escalating sustainability issues and challenges in the natural environment and related social fields require traditional industrial and commercial enterprises to adopt forward-looking and innovative strategies and actions to strive for sustained competitive advantage; at the same time, it also provides entrepreneurs with unprecedented entrepreneurial missions and opportunities. Therefore, this course aims to learn "sustainable development-oriented industrial and commercial innovation and entrepreneurship" by reviewing existing literature, analyzing cases and participating in corporate practice. The main contents covered in the course include:_x000D_
_x000D_
? How to use new technologies and new business models to improve the ecological environment and protect human health to start a business or company, such as new energy and waste recycling; _x000D_
? How to promote sustainability-oriented innovation and entrepreneurship in the transformation of traditional industries, such as green manufacturing, environmentally friendly materials, organic agriculture, energy efficiency management, and circular economy business cases; _x000D_

The course emphasizes the importance of integrated marketing dissemination in upgrading brand assets and embraces all aspects of integrated marketing dissemination projects: advertising, promotion, packaging, brand strategy, public relations, reputational dissemination, event and motivational sponsorship. The combination of theory and actual cases not only enhances students ' in-depth and comprehensive knowledge of the content of the theory, but also develops students ' mentalities and abilities to use integrated communication.

Name: Channel Management
Introduction: Channel management is one of the four important strategies of marketing management. It mainly provides end customers with some services that manufacturers cannot provide. However, distribution channels are not just a way for enterprises to serve end customers. In fact, they are also customers of enterprises, and distribution channels also have their own needs. At the same time, channels not only sell the company's products, but also sell products of competing brands, and sometimes produce their own products. Therefore, channel members integrate the roles of channels, customers, and competitors. Understanding their motivations and strategies is one of the goals of this course.

Name: Market Data Analysis
Introduction: This course is designed to enable students to obtain more and more correct information from market data. This course will discuss common data sources, commonly used data analysis methods, and how to correctly draw useful conclusions for business decisions from data analysis.

Name: New Product Development and Management
Introduction: This course mainly introduces how enterprises develop and manage existing products and new products/services. During the period, it will cover how companies should creatively carry out product innovation and management, new product development process, determination of consumer preferences, introduction of market forecast models, and new product promotion strategies. Through the analysis and discussion of relevant cases, students can develop their ability to discover, analyze and solve problems. The goal of this course is to provide students with an overall understanding of existing product and new product/service development and management. Provides basic skills and knowledge for students interested in careers in marketing, product/service management, project management, brand management and consulting.

The course focuses on basic knowledge of vector mechanics (including Newton mechanics, narrow relativism). These include:

At the same time, as the first physics course for undergraduate students in physics, students will be helped to complete the transition from secondary to university learning and develop the right learning methods.

Name: College English (II) (2)
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
The teaching of College English Level 2 is aimed at students who are classified as Level 2 in the College English Placement Examination. The second-level teaching will gradually improve students' comprehensive ability to use English through the training of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation skills, and lay a certain foundation for the third and fourth levels of English learning. Through Level 2 learning, students will gradually adapt to English teaching, be able to use short questions and answers and retell in English, increase their vocabulary by 600-700, and be able to translate English articles that are less difficult than the text. _x000D_
_x000D_
Comprehensive tutorials are designed to guide students through in-depth study of texts and practice language practice in reading, writing, and translation from the perspectives of words, sentences, and discourse, focusing on cultivating students' language and comprehensive application abilities. (Especially the ability to use vocabulary and phrases, as well as the ability to understand text and translate words and sentences). _x000D_

Reading tutorials provide students with more systematic and colorful reading materials, aiming to cultivate students' reading skills and improve students' reading levels, help students expand their knowledge and vocabulary, and thereby enhance students' understanding and appreciation of articles on various themes and genres. _x000D_
