The listening and speaking tutorial aims to help students enhance their understanding of English texts through a large amount of listening materials, improve students' ability to analyze, summarize, judge and reason about what they listen to, and continuously cultivate and strengthen students' oral expression skills on the basis of training and improving students' listening skills.

Name: Ideological and Moral Cultivation and Fundamentals of Law
Introduction: This course is one of the required courses for the whole school. It is an ideological and political theory course set in accordance with the national "05" education plan. The Ideological and Moral Cultivation Course of Peking University won the title of Beijing Excellent Course in 2006 and the National Excellent Course in 2007. It is currently one of the core courses of quality education at Peking University. This course educates college students on the correct outlook on life, values, and moral values ​​through the analysis and discussion of life theory and practical issues such as life, ideals, and morality. Through course study, college students can further understand the general characteristics of university study, understand the basic requirements for college students' ideological and moral cultivation, grasp the general rules for healthy growth of college students, clarify the responsibilities and missions that college students must bear in the great cause of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and consciously cultivate good moral qualities.

Name: Introduction to Computation (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: How to carry out basic computer education among newly admitted college students has always been a problem faced in curriculum design in colleges and universities. Generally speaking, the introductory foundation of computer science includes two parts: Introduction to Computing and Programming Foundation. At the high school level, many students have received basic computer education, including basic computer knowledge, such as software, hardware, computer networks, binary, word processing, and basic operating systems and database operations, as well as some basic programming training. Of course, due to reasons such as further education and other aspects, different students have different foundations. Some know little about basic computer knowledge, some have learned basic computer operations and applications, some can write programs, and some have mastered better programming skills. But few students truly understand the nature of computing. Considering these circumstances, this course integrates the connotation of computing and the basics of programming in its content, allowing students to master the principles and methods of programming based on understanding the nature of computing, and then master the ability to solve practical problems. At the same time, we design different teaching classes according to the different levels of students to meet the different needs of students, and strive to enable each student to maintain "fresh" learning in this course, avoiding phenomena such as "not keeping up", "chewing on cold rice", and "slow progress".

Name: Military Theory
College: Student Affairs Department, People's Armed Forces Department
Introduction: The military theory course is a compulsory course for first-year undergraduates at Peking University in accordance with the "Military Theory Course Syllabus for General Universities" and is organized by the Ministry of People's Armed Forces. Classes are held in the first and second semesters of each academic year, with 4-6 teaching classes held each semester. The main teaching content is: my country's national defense, military thought, military situation, military high technology, service and arms knowledge, high-tech warfare, etc. 14-15 topics, mainly taught by teachers from the National Defense University of the Chinese People's Liberation Army.

Name: Electromagnetism
Introduction: Electromagnetism is part of classical physics. This course explains the basic experimental laws of electromagnetic interaction, and based on this, gradually reveals the objective characteristics, properties, internal connections and motion change rules of the electromagnetic field, a special form. Due to the ubiquity of electromagnetic phenomena and its wide range of technical applications, electromagnetism has become an important foundation for physics, other natural sciences, and technical sciences. The main contents of electromagnetism are: experimental laws of charge interaction, properties of electrostatic fields, conductors and dielectrics in electrostatic fields, basic laws of DC circuits and their applications, experimental laws of current interaction, properties of constant magnetic fields, movement of charged particles in magnetic fields, transformation of electromagnetic fields between different reference systems, electromagnetic induction and transient processes, magnetic media, basic laws of AC circuits and their applications, Maxwell's electromagnetic field theory and electromagnetic waves, and the electromagnetic unit system.

Name: Electromagnetism Problem Session
Introduction: Questions in conjunction with Electromagnetics.

Name: Basic Astronomy
Introduction: "Basic Astronomy" is an elective course in the School of Physics and a required course for undergraduate majors in the Department of Astronomy. It mainly introduces the basic concepts of astronomical observation such as astronomical telescopes, celestial spheres and celestial coordinate systems, time and calendar, motion and distance of celestial bodies, as well as basic knowledge of planets, solar systems, stars, Milky Ways, extragalactic galaxies and the structure and evolution of the universe. It also introduces the main research methods and results of astronomy, laying the foundation for subsequent professional courses.

Name: Introduction to Philosophy
Introduction: This course is a special discussion on the principles of philosophy. Its content consists of three parts: general introduction, basic principles and history of philosophy. In accordance with the principle of dividing theoretical philosophy and practical philosophy, the main part discusses the four most basic philosophical principles in turn, including metaphysics, theory of knowledge, ethics, and aesthetics. The general part discusses four major issues, including the concept of philosophy, the field of philosophy, the relationship between philosophy and language, and the value of philosophy. The history of philosophy part mainly introduces the basic clues of the history of Western philosophy and the most important schools of contemporary philosophy. The speaker hopes that through such a panoramic description, he can help students gain objective, comprehensive and in-depth systematic knowledge about Western philosophy.

Name: Outline of Modern Chinese History
Introduction:
The subject “Outlines for China's near modern history” is a compulsory subject of ideological and political theory for undergraduate students in our general higher education institutions, as mandated by the Ministries of Education and China. The course focused on the recent history of China ' s resistance to foreign aggression, struggle for national independence, overthrowing reactionary rule and achieving the liberation of its people. It helped students to understand the country ' s history, national circumstances and the historical processes and inherent patterns of the development of social development and revolution in China in the near-modern period.
Beijing University began this course in September 2006 and was accredited as Beijing City and National Quality in 2008. Credits: 2 credits, academic system: 2 hours a week, all year round. Level: Specialization of first grade students.
The course is taught by a combination of teaching groups, divided into four teaching groups, and by a “four-person” approach to the management of teaching by course facilitators, classroom supervisors, keynote teachers and assistant teachers. Classrooms are taught, supplemented by other practical segments, including the broadcasting of documentaries or films, writing with sensitivity, organization of classroom discussions, visits to exhibitions or museums, etc. Adopt a flexible and liberal approach to appraisal. Accomplishments of 40 per cent, including classroom discussion of small papers, and final examinations of 60 per cent (opening).

Name: Kendo
Introduction:

1. The birthplace of kendo is China, but as a sport and fitness method, kendo is booming in China. _x000D_
Kendo is a sport that emphasizes intelligence. How to train people to adapt and predict changes on the field with wisdom, strategy, and methods has become a new topic for world-class players and kendo training. Although the characteristic of modern kendo is that the offensive and defensive confrontations are becoming increasingly fierce, it is difficult for players to win if they enter the intelligent fighting system without using their skills. _x000D_
Kendo is a sport that requires clear thinking, strong explosiveness, quick movements, and sufficient physical strength. As far as its tactics are concerned, it is a more complex confrontational sport that requires practitioners to make agile reactions immediately in a very short period of time. This sport not only requires people to improve their physical fitness, but also has high exercise value for their psychology and spirit. Summarizing the actual combat and theory, it can be roughly summarized into the following points:_x000D_
(1) Cultivate a sound sense of personality and values_x000D_
(2) Establish a fair attitude towards life_x000D_
(3) Improve learning understanding_x000D_
(4) Learn how to treat failure and setbacks_x000D_
(5) Physical exercise effect_x000D_
(6) Enhance self-defense skills_x000D_

(1) Wearing kendo-specific kendo uniforms, kendo hakama, and kendo protective gear (including masks, gauntlets, armor, and waist hangings)_x000D_
(2) Arrange an environmental administrator to inspect the venue before class. _x000D_
(3) Arrange the bamboo sword administrator to inspect the bamboo sword before class. _x000D_
(4) Pay attention to the safety of yourself and your classmates during class. If you have chest tightness, palpitation, dizziness or other physical fatigue, please report it to the teacher, who will arrange it according to the situation. _x000D_

1. Briefly introduce the basics of kendo, dojo precepts; clothing and protective gear; related etiquette; entry and exit rules and safety guidance. _x000D_

_x000D_
"College Chinese" is the most basic course for quality education for college students and the most basic way to cultivate students' humanistic qualities and Chinese writing and expression abilities. This course will focus on the training objectives to systematically cultivate and train students in the areas of appreciation and reading of Chinese and foreign literary works, Chinese language expression and writing skills, and eloquence. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Philosophy
Introduction: The Greek meaning of "philosophy" is "love of wisdom". For more than a thousand years in ancient times, the Middle Ages and modern times in the West, philosophy has been regarded as the source and foundation of all scientific knowledge. To this day, philosophy still plays a central role in university humanities education. This course mainly explains Western classic philosophical texts such as Plato's dialogues, so that students can understand the way philosophers explore world order and the inherent tension of philosophical life.

Name: Introduction to Logic
Introduction:
This course attempts to impart to students the general concepts of logic, the overall image of the development of logic so far, some of the most basic logic techniques and techniques, and the ideas and spirit hidden behind logic techniques. Mainly teaches propositional logic, lexical logic and predicate logic, as well as inductive logic and informal logic. _x000D_
This course belongs to the Peking University general elective course series. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Religious Studies
Introduction:
This semester's "Introduction to Religious Studies" will be divided into three parts, examining the three forms of treatment of religion in Chinese and Western civilizations. The first part focuses on ancient Western religions, that is, political religions in city-states; the second part focuses on Christianity and modern Western religions, that is, spiritual religions in society; the third part focuses on traditional Chinese religions, that is, ethical religions; the core idea running through the three parts is Shinto teachings. _x000D_
This course hopes to help students have a preliminary understanding of the ideological traditions and general research methods of religious studies, learn to look at religious issues comprehensively, objectively, and academically, master the relevant knowledge of Chinese and Western civilizations more systematically, and gradually find ways to resolve various life problems through reading classics. _x000D_

Name: Complexity Science and Philosophy

Name: Confucius and Laozi
Introduction: Laozi and Confucius are the founders of Chinese philosophy and thought, with far-reaching influence. This course is intended to be problem-centered and introduce the thoughts of Laozi and Confucius in an ideological dialogue to present different theoretical systems within the Chinese philosophical tradition and different ideas for solving problems.

Name: Microeconomics
Introduction: This course is an undergraduate course in microeconomics, covering classic microeconomic theory. This course starts by analyzing the decision-making motivations of microeconomic entities such as consumers and producers, and discusses the interaction between individual decision-making and the market, market structure, market failure and other issues. The course also covers cutting-edge theoretical developments including game theory, information economics and behavioral economics. The course teaching will start from the basic rational person assumption, focusing on the application of the basic economic method of utility maximization in individual decision-making, as well as the limitations of some traditional assumptions in certain applications. The course will involve some mathematical methods, but more will use charts and graphs, striving to be both accurate and intuitive.

Name: Introduction to Chinese Literary Classics
Introduction: The main content of this course: Lecture 1: Overview of Chinese classics; Lecture 2: Classics and the selection of classics; Lecture 3: Classics classics; Lecture 4: History classics; Lecture 5: Zibu classics; Lecture 6: Jibu classics; Lecture 7: Series and category books and others; Lecture 8: Modern classics.

Name: Introduction to the Basic Principles of Marxism
Introduction: The teaching of ideological and political theory courses in colleges and universities is the most direct and basic way to provide ideological and political education to college students, and "Introduction to the Basic Principles of Marxism" is one of the basic courses. Marxism is the science of the proletariat and human liberation. Studying the liberation of the proletariat and all mankind is the theme and core of the entire Marxism, and is the main thread that runs through the basic content of Marxism. Marxist philosophy, Marxist political economics and scientific socialism, as the main contents of Marxist theory, embody and penetrate the essence of Marxism and serve the essence of Marxism. The overall tasks of classroom teaching will focus on three aspects: "strengthening students' knowledge and understanding of the integrity of Marxism", "strengthening students' Marxist beliefs", and "enabling students to master the basic theoretical points of Marxism".

Name: Thermal Physics
Introduction: Thermal science is a course that enables physics students to systematically study and deal with the thermophysical properties of systems (gas, liquid, solid) composed of a large number of microscopic particles. Through the introduction and analysis of some basic physical phenomena, this course explains that following statistical laws is a basic characteristic of a system composed of a large number of particles. The course systematically and comprehensively introduces the basic concepts and the microscopic methods of applying statistical methods to deal with multi-particle systems. The course also introduces the macroscopic methods of summarizing the basic laws and basic concepts of thermodynamics through experimental observations. The main contents of the thermal science course include: equilibrium state and equation of state, the zero law of thermodynamics and temperature, the first law of thermodynamics, the second law of thermodynamics and its relationship with the development of modern science (such as cosmology), transport processes and main laws in gases, microscopic models of ideal gases, wheat Maxwell's speed and rate distribution law, particle distribution according to height and Boltzmann distribution, energy equipartition theorem according to degrees of freedom, statistical interpretation of the second law of thermodynamics and entropy, microscopic explanation of gas transport properties, vapor-liquid phase change, first and second type phase changes, molecular forces and non-ideal gases, etc.

Name: Theoretical Mechanics
Introduction: This course starts from analytical mechanics and systematically introduces the basic contents of kinematics and dynamics of mechanical systems. It mainly includes: constraints of motion, generalized coordinates, degrees of freedom, and the principle of virtual work; for the fixed-point motion of rigid bodies, the Euler angles and Euler kinematic equations that describe motion are introduced; the plane-parallel motion, fixed-axis motion and general motion of rigid bodies are further discussed; the equations of motion in non-inertial systems and their applications are introduced; Lagrangian quantities and Lagrangian equations are introduced, and used to deal with forces such as centered motion and small vibrations with multiple degrees of freedom. scientific system; introduce the concepts of the center of mass and the center-of-mass system of the particle group, discuss the mechanical laws satisfied by the dynamic quantities of the overall motion of the particle group, and use these laws to solve practical mechanical problems; regarding rigid body dynamics, introduce the inertia tensor and Euler's dynamic equations; starting from the Lagrange equation, derive regular equations and discuss the conserved quantities of the mechanical system; introduce Poisson brackets, Hamilton's principle, and Hamilton's Jacobian equation.

Name: Physics for Non-Majors
Introduction:
This is a general physics course for all majors in university arts and sciences. _x000D_
_x000D_
After hundreds of years of development from Galileo to today, physics has become a very mature science. Its results have also been widely used in different scientific and technological fields. However, the ideas, theories, and methods of physics have not yet become an integral part of domestic higher education. Physics courses for non-physics science and engineering majors focus on specific applications in the subject, and physics courses for liberal arts majors do not break away from the university physics textbook system (such as the national quality course textbook: "Physics and Human Civilization" co-edited by Professors Sheng Zhengmao and Ye Gaoxiang of Zhejiang University). _x000D_
_x000D_
With the increasing development of science and technology, physics and its results have an increasing impact on the development of the country and the daily life of the public. Especially in the fields of energy, environment, global climate change, space development and other fields, it has attracted more and more public attention. After the publication of the lecture notes of "Physics for Future Presidents", a course offered by Professor Muller of the Department of Physics at Berkeley, it immediately became a bestseller and was translated into various languages, illustrating the importance of a physics course that teaches public concern in general higher education. Of course, the name of this course is "Physics for General Public" - "Public Physics" (or "Popular Physics") is more appropriate. (While preparing this application, the nuclear leakage accident caused by Japan's earthquake disaster caused widespread public attention and uneasiness, and the opinions of many so-called "experts" showed that not only the public, but also many scientists and engineering and technical personnel had a very confused understanding of nuclear science and nuclear safety. And the introduction of major issues of public concern is an important part of this course.)_x000D_
_x000D_
This course is for students from various university departments with a high school diploma. It does not require advanced mathematical tools, but focuses on describing the ideas and methods of physics, and using these ideas, methods and conclusions that have been obtained to analyze issues of public concern in daily life, especially major issues such as safety, energy, environment and so on. The course applicant has tried to offer relevant lectures for undergraduates in some domestic universities and feels that it is necessary to offer a similar course in China. _x000D_
_x000D_
Preliminary consideration, the course consists of the following parts:_x000D_
_x000D_
First, we introduce the basic ideas of physics—how physicists “see” the world (Chapter 2: Basic laws of the physical world) and methods—that is, how physicists “measure” the world (Chapter 3: Space-time scales of the physical world). Then we teach how to use physics theories and methods to analyze some basic processes in the objective world (especially human society) (Chapter 4 and 5: Physical processes and social processes). Finally, we discuss major issues of public concern (Chapter 6: Physics in issues of public concern). _x000D_

Name: Optics
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory basic course for physics and microelectronics majors. _x000D_
Mainly introduces the geometric optics and wave theory of light wave propagation - including Fermat's principle, light equation, Huygens-Fresnel principle, Fresnel-Kirchhoff diffraction integral, reflection and refraction of light waves on the interface, and the propagation of light in anisotropic media; the statistical properties of light fields - including the temporal coherence and spatial coherence of light fields , Polarization state; optical instruments and devices—including spherical mirrors, thin lenses, ideal imaging systems, microscopes, telescopes, wavefront interference devices, Fabry-Perot interferometers, grating spectrometers, Leo filters, optical information processing systems, phase contrast microscopes, holographic principles; basics of photometry and colorimetry; quantum properties of light. _x000D_

Name: Equilibrium Statistical Physics
Introduction: Equilibrium statistical physics is one of the basic courses for undergraduates in the School of Physics. The content involves: review of basic theories of thermodynamics, statistical ensemble, quantum ideal gas, classical fluid, second-order phase transition mean field theory, etc.

Name: Equilibrium Statistical Physics Seminar
Introduction: Equilibrium statistical physics is one of the basic courses for undergraduates in the School of Physics. The content involves: review of basic theories of thermodynamics, statistical ensemble, quantum ideal gas, classical fluid, second-order phase transition mean field theory, etc.

Name: General Physics Laboratory (1)
Introduction:
_x000D_
"General Physics Experiment" is based on general physics and is open to sophomore undergraduates majoring in physics. It is offered in two semesters: the general physics experiment (I) starts in the autumn semester; the general physics experiment (II) starts in the Spring Festival semester, with 4 credit hours per week and 16 weeks in each semester. The purpose of the course is to guide students to learn basic knowledge of physics and basic methods and experimental techniques of physics research through experimental methods, and to cultivate students' physical experimental abilities. _x000D_
General physics experiment (1) includes an introductory course, three preparatory experiments, one error theory experiment and eleven basic experiments. In each experiment, teachers guide students to complete the prescribed experimental content. The teacher must comprehensively evaluate each student's preview, experiment, and experiment report for each experiment and give a grade. The grade of the course is comprehensively evaluated by the grade of each experiment. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Finance
Introduction: As an introductory course, Introduction to Finance introduces basic financial knowledge to non-business major undergraduates in an interesting and relaxed way, and cultivates sensitivity to financial issues. The course will combine the latest developments in the financial industry and teach the scope of finance, financial institutions and markets, investment science, corporate finance and derivatives. The course provides a comprehensive but preliminary understanding of finance.

Name: Current Affairs and Policy
Introduction: The "Situation and Policy" course is a required course for students in higher education institutions stipulated by the superior department. Its teaching purpose is to closely integrate the reality of China's socialist construction and educate students on domestic and international situations and the party's line, principles and policies based on the hot issues and ideological characteristics that concern them. The classroom focuses on teaching the current international situation and international relations, development trends, my country's foreign policy, major world events and the principled stance of the Chinese government.

Name: General Physics Laboratory (2)
Introduction:
"General Physics Experiment" is based on the experimental content of general physics and is open to sophomore undergraduates majoring in physics. It is offered in two semesters: the general physics experiment (I) starts in the autumn semester; the general physics experiment (II) starts in the Spring Festival semester, with 4 credit hours per week and 16 weeks in each semester. The purpose of the course is to guide students to learn basic knowledge of physics and basic methods and experimental techniques of physics research through experimental methods, and to cultivate students' physical experimental abilities. _x000D_
   Ordinary Physics Experiment (2) is the continuation of Ordinary Physics Experiment (1), with a total of fifteen basic experiments. In each experiment, teachers guide students to complete the prescribed experimental content. The teacher must comprehensively evaluate each student's preview, experiment, and experiment report for each experiment and give a grade. The grade of the course is comprehensively evaluated by the grade of each experiment. _x000D_
   Compared with ordinary physics experiment (1), ordinary physics experiment (2) has richer physical content, more designed and comprehensive experiments, and more difficult experimental techniques. _x000D_

Name: Swimming
Introduction:
(Junior class)_x000D_
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
Swimming is a sport performed in a specific environment of water. It has strong practical value. It is a unique physical education project of Peking University and is also an exercise and survival skill that every student is required to master. _x000D_
Through swimming exercise, you can improve your aerobic metabolic capacity, improve your cardiopulmonary function, cultivate the excellent qualities of challenging yourself, defeating yourself, moving forward courageously, and perseverance, and promote the overall development of physical and mental quality. _x000D_
Swimming classes mainly teach basic special skills and knowledge, so that students can master the basic skills of breaststroke, learn starting, turning, treading water and other techniques, and have the ability to reach the 200-meter standard. _x000D_
(1) Swimming course requirements_x000D_
1. Safety precautions for swimming lessons_x000D_
(1) Establish the idea of safety first. _x000D_
(2) A physical examination should be performed before swimming. People with heart disease, high blood pressure, epilepsy, active tuberculosis, infectious hepatitis, skin diseases, pink eye, mental illness, otitis media, fever, and open wounds should not enter the water. _x000D_
(3) Students are prohibited from entering the water without permission if the teacher is not present. _x000D_
(4) After class is announced, students are prohibited from returning to the swimming pool to swim. _x000D_
(5) It is not advisable to enter the water after drinking alcohol, after eating a full meal, being hungry or overtired. _x000D_
(6) It is prohibited to start diving in shallow water areas. _x000D_
(7) Prolonged breath-holding diving is prohibited. _x000D_
(8) Chasing or fighting on the slippery poolside and in the locker room is prohibited. _x000D_
(9) If you experience dizziness, headache, nausea or vomiting during swimming, you should get out of the water immediately and inform the teacher. _x000D_
(10) If students ignore classroom disciplines, violate the above safety management regulations, and cause injury to themselves or others, they will be held responsible for the accident. _x000D_
2． Equipment you should prepare for swimming lessons_x000D_
(1) Well-fitting dark swimsuit bottoms. _x000D_
(2) Suitable swimming cap. Beginners should choose a suitable nylon swimming cap that is easy to wear. _x000D_
(3) Swimming goggles. It can prevent eye diseases and help beginner swimmers open their eyes in the water, which is of great help in overcoming their fear of water. _x000D_
(4) Bath towels and slippers. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students' physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, as well as the ideology of "health first". _x000D_
2． Improve health, enhance physical fitness, and comprehensively improve students' physical and psychological qualities. _x000D_
3. Master the basic techniques and related theories of breaststroke, enhance physical fitness, and improve athletic ability. _x000D_
4. In practice, we promote the comprehensive development of students' physical and mental qualities and establish the concept of lifelong sports. _x000D_

Name: Appreciation of Chinese and Foreign Musical Masterpieces
Introduction:
This course is divided into two parts: Chinese works and foreign works. It mainly introduces Chinese and foreign small and medium-sized instrumental music and vocal music works. _x000D_
The music includes: instrumental solos, ensembles, orchestral pieces, concertos, songs, and dance drama excerpts. Vocal works include_x000D_
: Art songs, folk songs, opera selections, etc. This course brings together the essence of Chinese and foreign famous songs, which people love to hear_x000D_
, an enduring and popular song. This lesson analyzes musical works one by one and introduces the era of the works_x000D_
Background, creative intention, ideological content, structural characteristics, and the life of the author, etc., and use audio and video materials to teach_x000D_
Learning, so that students can fully appreciate and appreciate music.

Name: Probability and Statistics (B)
Introduction: Probability theory is a mathematical discipline that studies the objective regularity of random phenomena, while mathematical statistics is a discipline that studies random phenomena using limited data with random effects. Through the teaching of this course, students can master the basic concepts of probability theory and mathematical statistics, understand their basic theories and methods, so that students can initially master the basic ideas and methods of dealing with random phenomena, and cultivate students' ability to use probability and statistics methods to analyze and solve practical problems.

Name: Introduction to Atmospheric Sciences
Introduction: The course is mainly for undergraduate students in the lower grades of the School of Physics and the Institute of Pedagogical Studies, and is open to students in the fields of geology and environment. The course is currently run by four teachers, Zhang Qinghong, Zhao Chunsheng, Hu Yongyun and Xue Wen, and is open every semester. The development of new sources of energy, such as global climate change, high-temperature natural disasters such as floods and droughts, atmospheric pollution and solar wind and hydropower, is having a wide and profound impact on human economic and social life. Atmospheric science, with the Earth ' s atmosphere as its main object of study, is a theoretical and appliedly compatible science, based on understanding the physical, chemical and dynamic nature of the atmosphere, including its state, phenomena and changes, and thus predicting and influencing the atmospheric environment and physical processes in the atmosphere. In addition, atmospheric science includes interactions between the atmosphere and the terrestrial, marine and biosphere, and is widely applied in such areas as the environment, oceans, new energy sciences, human activities and daily life. Global climate change, catastrophic weather forecasting, air pollution monitoring, etc. are currently the focus of research in atmospheric science. This course, which is an introductory course in atmospheric science and an optional course in the physical basics, largely omits complex mathematical reasoning and provides a concise introduction to the basic concepts of atmospheric science, as well as the content and methods of research. Through this course of study, the students of the chosen class are taught the basic theory and methodology of atmospheric science and the basis is laid for flexible application to further professional studies and daily life. The elements include: 1. The Earth and its atmosphere 2. Atmospheric radiation and greenhouse effects 3. Atmospheric thermodynamics Cloud physics and precipitation 5. Atmospheric chemistry in air pollution 6. Atmospheric boundary layer Fundamentals of atmospheric movements 8. Front and cyclones 9. Thunderstorms, typhoons and tornados 10. Atmospheric and ocean circulation 11. Climate system and global warming 12. Weather forecasting 13. Planetary atmosphere

Name: Introduction to Mao Zedong Thought and the Theoretical System of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics
Introduction: This course takes the Sinicization of Marxism as its theme, takes the historical process of the Sinicization of Marxism as its main line, and focuses on socialism with Chinese characteristics. It reveals the historical process of the Communist Party of China integrating the basic principles of Marxism with China's reality from the unity of theory and practice, history and logic, and accurately explains the theoretical results of the Sinicization of Marxism, namely Mao Zedong Thought and the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, etc., so that students can correctly understand the theoretical results of the Sinicization of Marxism in guiding China's revolution, construction, and The important historical position and role in the reform, grasp the basic theory and spiritual essence of Marxism in China, establish correct beliefs and common ideals of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and enhance the consciousness and firmness of implementing the party's basic line and basic program, so that contemporary college students can deeply understand the importance of adhering to the guiding position of Marxism, strengthen college students' ideals and beliefs in taking the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics under the leadership of the party, and make their due contributions to building a moderately prosperous society in an all-round way and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Name: Atomic Physics
Prerequisite: General physics mechanics, thermals, electromagnetics and opticals, advanced mathematics, linear algebras, etc.
Introduction:
Atomic physics is an introductory course for students from physics and related disciplines to systematically study the properties and laws of the microscopic world. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will gradually reveal a series of characteristics and laws that distinguish the microscopic world from the macroscopic world, providing the necessary foundation for further in-depth study of modern physics. Its main contents include: the failure of classical physics and the establishment of basic concepts of quantum physics, the composition and nuclear structure of atoms, Bohr's atomic structure model, preliminary quantum mechanics, the spin and spin-orbit coupling of microscopic particles, the energy levels and transitions of atoms, the shell structure of atoms, Atoms in the external field, X-rays and Usher electrons, electron capture, molecular spectrum and molecular structure, basic properties of atomic nuclei, radioactive decay of nuclei, basic properties of nuclear forces, nuclear structure models and preliminary nuclear reactions, nuclear fission and fusion and nuclear energy development, preliminary particle physics, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course particularly focuses on experimental foundations and phenomena as well as basic principles. _x000D_
_x000D_
The basic credit hours are 51 hours, and courses are offered in both spring and autumn semesters.

Name: Atomic Physics Problem Session
Introduction: Atom physics study

Name: Introduction to Ethics
Introduction: This course selects three works: Aristotle's Nicomachean Ethics, Augustine's Confessions, and Kant's Foundations of the Metaphysics of Morals, hoping to present the classic form of Western ethics in the context of classical, medieval, and modern philosophical history. We will focus on explaining the ethical ideas of these three philosophers, as well as the intrinsic connection between their propositions and Greece, Christianity, and modern views of human nature and nature.

Name: Data Structures and Algorithms (B)
Introduction:
1. Introduce commonly used data structures and basic methods of algorithm analysis from the perspective of ADT. It enables students to master commonly used data structures such as linear tables, stacks, queues, strings, arrays, trees, and graphs from the aspects of the logical structure of the data structure, the corresponding set of basic operations, implementation, and evaluation of the implementation, and have a certain ability to analyze the time and space complexity of the algorithm. _x000D_
2． Introducing sorting techniques. Enable students to master common sorting algorithms such as insertion sort, selection sort, exchange sort, radix sort, merge sort, etc., and discuss their time and space overhead. _x000D_
3. Through the study of this course, students will master the design and analysis methods of commonly used data structures and algorithms, improve their programming capabilities, and choose reasonable data structures to solve simple problems.

Name: Fundamentals of Modern Electronic Circuits and Laboratory (I)
Introduction: This course is a basic course of modern electronics and information science, and is a main basic course for students majoring in non-electrical sciences. Three basics are emphasized in the teaching of this course: basic concepts, basic principles and basic circuit analysis methods; at the same time, the practical application of circuits is highlighted, and theory is combined with practical teaching, so that students can master a solid foundation of modern electronics and information science, understand the way of thinking in electronic engineering, establish the concept of electronic systems, and lay the foundation for the correct application of electronic technologies and methods in future scientific research.

Name: Optics
Introduction: This course focuses on the wave characteristics of light in optics. Based on Huygens' principle, it gradually explains in depth the interference of light waves, diffraction, Fourier optics, polarization and other contents. From the shallower to the deeper, it strives to provide an in-depth and solid foundation of wave optics for students who are initially involved in wave optics. The course also takes into account certain optical cutting-edge introductions and shows the latest applications of wave optics. The course also includes an optical demonstration component.

Name: Optics Problem Session
Introduction: Accompanies the subject of optical studies. Non-independent courses do not require separate courses.

Name: Modern Physics
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, linear algebra, mechanics, thermal, electromagnetic, optical (compatible)
Introduction: Introduce the main content of modern physics, show the progress and mystery of modern physics, and provide the conceptual foundation and basic knowledge for subsequent learning. The target is students at the end of the general physics stage, usually 2nd level or 2nd level. For students who subsequently continue to study physics, it plays a role in guiding interest and broadening their horizons; for students who subsequently study other majors, it plays a role in understanding and being able to initially apply modern physics knowledge. Each section begins with an important question. Focus on speculation, experimentation and images. Each section contains questions, examples, and discussions. The exercises in each chapter are divided into three levels, and students can choose from the designated range. Use English teaching materials and try to use bilingual teaching.

Name: Methods of Mathematical Physics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge of mathematical physics methods required for learning physical theory courses. On the basis of advanced mathematics and general physics, it mainly teaches commonly used methods in classical mathematical physics, including analytic functions and integral transformations, Γ functions and δ functions, basic solutions to second-order linear partial differential equations (separation of variables, integral transformation, Green function method, conformal transformation and variational method, etc.), as well as the main properties and applications of basic special functions.

Name: Theoretical Mechanics (A)
Prerequisite:
General physical mechanics, advanced mathematics (microcentrism, linear algebra)
Mathematics Physical Methods (reconversion function part, also optional class)
Introduction: Theoretical Mechanics (A) is a theoretical course for physics students in the School of Physics after general physics. For most undergraduates majoring in physics, it is the first theoretical physics course they encounter, and it is also the basis for many subsequent theoretical physics courses. The course focuses primarily on the teaching of analytical mechanics methods (Lagrangian, Hamiltonian). And apply the methods of analytical mechanics to a wide range of dynamic systems, including simple particles, constrained multi-degree-of-freedom systems and rigid bodies. At the same time, mechanical systems with continuous distribution will also be briefly introduced, such as continuum classical mechanics and classical field systems, etc., which will lay a certain foundation for subsequent courses (such as fluid mechanics, classical electrodynamics, etc.).

Name: Modern Physics Laboratory (I)
Prerequisite:
General physics experiments, atomic physics.
It can be read at the same time as quantum mechanics, solid physics, nuclear physics and particle physics introductory.
Introduction:
Modern Physics Experiment is a comprehensive experimental course for senior students majoring in physics. It is divided into two parts: Modern Physics Experiment I and Modern Physics Experiment II, which are mainly taught in the spring semester and autumn semester respectively. The content covers independent experimental projects and open research frontier physics experimental projects in the fields of atomic and molecular physics, nuclear detection technology and applications, lasers and modern optics, vacuum and thin film preparation, X-ray electron diffraction and structural analysis, magnetic resonance, microwave, low temperature and superconductivity, semiconductor physics, nonlinear physics, etc. Many of the experiments were Nobel Prize-winning experiments that played a milestone role in the development of modern physics. They are representative in terms of experimental methods and techniques. They also absorb the scientific research results of our school teachers. In recent years, large-scale scientific research-level instruments and equipment have been introduced, and experiments that reflect the cutting-edge of physical science have been added. In terms of experimental arrangements, students are exposed to technologies commonly used in modern physical experiments such as spectroscopy, vacuum, nuclear detection, low temperature, scanning probes, and weak signal detection. Each experiment also has certain physical content to improve students' ability to integrate theory with practice and solve practical problems. Students do seven independent experimental projects in different fields each semester. In the second semester, students with excellent grades in the first semester are allowed to choose open research-based cutting-edge physics experimental projects. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Advances in Nanotechnology
Introduction: Nanotechnology has become a highly interdisciplinary subject, a field that deeply integrates physics, chemistry, materials, information, biological sciences, etc. When selecting teaching content, we focus on selecting some basic issues, clarifying the organic connections and differences between nanoscience and traditional science, and focusing on discussing new issues arising at the nanoscale related to basic physics. We will select some cutting-edge issues in the progress of nanotechnology that are closely integrated with physics for special discussion. We will discuss which issues have been solved, and more importantly, what challenging issues can be solved or need to be solved urgently. Through classroom teaching, intensive literature reading, and seminars, students are aroused to be interested in the infinite mysteries of nanoscience. At the same time, students are fully aware that physics, chemistry, information technology, biotechnology, and materials science have different paths to the same destination at the nanoscale. Multidisciplinary interdisciplinary research is the natural and inevitable destination. It is at this intersection that nanotechnology will become the focus of future scientific disciplines coming together

Name: Laser Laboratory
Introduction: Lasers and their applications are the foundation and core of the development of micro-nano integrated photonics technology and an important driving force for the realization of ultra-high-speed all-optical information processing. This course carries out the most representative typical laser experiments, including basic laser parameter measurement, laser mechanism research, laser technology and laser applications. Specifically, it includes mode analysis of helium-neon lasers, acousto-optic modulation mode-locked lasers, semiconductor laser spectral characteristic measurements, frequency doubling and sum frequency effect measurements in nonlinear crystals, pump detection principles, Z-scan measurement principles, etc. This course focuses on the close integration of basic knowledge and cutting-edge research, helping students become familiar with laser principles and master basic experimental skills, laying a certain foundation for future scientific research work.

Name: Computational Physics (A)
Prerequisite: 1. "Linear Algebra"; 2. "Advanced Mathematics"; 3. "Methods of Mathematical Physics"; 4. It is best to complete "Theoretical Mechanics", "Electrodynamics", and "Quantum Mechanics", but it is not required.
Introduction: Computational physics is a discipline that uses computers to solve physical problems, and its core foundation is numerical analysis. This course focuses on teaching basic processing methods for various common numerical problems in computational physics, covering basic contents such as numerical solutions to linear and nonlinear equations, numerical differentiation and integration, interpolation and polynomial approximation, boundary value problems, initial value problems, numerical solutions to partial differential equations, signal processing methods such as Fourier transform, and processing and fitting of random numbers and data. Although the class focuses on teaching algorithms for basic problems, students will be required to use the knowledge they have learned through several major assignments to design appropriate algorithms based on specific problems and program to solve actual physical problems.

Name: Computational Physics Problem Session
Prerequisite: Linear Algebra, Advanced Mathematics, Math Physics.
Introduction:
After 2-3 years of teaching practice in "Computational Physics", we strive to implement the following teaching ideas of this course: (1) By teaching basic algorithms of numerical analysis in the classroom, the content is very comprehensive and extensive, covering everything from solving linear equations, matrix eigenvalue problems, root finding and optimization of nonlinear equations, to numerical solutions of ordinary differential equations and partial differential equations, etc. (2) After several large assignments (60%), teachers usually assign most of them to physics-related assignments, which require the use of classroom knowledge to write large programs to solve. (3) Final closed-book written examination (40%), which examines the basic theory of numerical analysis and error analysis, etc. _x000D_
However, many students reported that there is a relatively large gap between algorithm implementation and solving real physical problems. They hope to fill this gap through the practice classes of teaching assistants, so that students can not only firmly grasp the basic algorithm theory, but also conduct numerical experiments to solve practical problems.

Name: Fundamentals of Modern Electronic Circuits and Laboratory (II)
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, modern electronic circuit infrastructure and experiments (i)
Introduction:
This experimental course is intended for science undergraduates in the School of Physics (non-electronic information majors). It is a follow-up course to the "Modern Electronic Circuit Basics and Experiments (1)" in the theoretical course. It condenses and synthesizes the basic content of analog circuits, digital circuits, and circuit analysis principle experiments in the electronic major of the School of Information. It also includes the most basic content of electronic measurement technology and instrument use, electronic circuit EDA experiments, and virtual instrument experiments. _x000D_
The course strives to use the least amount of time to enable students to deepen their understanding of the content of various theoretical courses on electronic circuits, and focuses on cultivating the practical ability of electronic circuit experiments for science talents, laying a solid foundation for future scientific research in experimental physics or research and development in the electronic information industry. The experimental content is novel and closely follows the development trend of the times. The teaching arrangement is based on reducing academic burden, improving learning efficiency, and cultivating interest and practical ability. _x000D_

Name: Quantum Mechanics Seminar
Prerequisite: General physics, advanced mathematics, mathematical physics
Introduction: This course is a workshop on quantum mechanics. Students who choose to study at the Quantum Mechanicals College may choose to take classes to discuss them.

Name: Quantum Mechanics (A)
Prerequisite: General physics, advanced mathematics, mathematical physics
Introduction:
This course is non-relativistic quantum mechanics, which systematically introduces the laws of motion of microscopic particles. The content includes the basic concepts of quantum mechanics: wave function, state superposition principle, Schrödinger equation, operator representation and representation transformation of mechanical quantities, symmetry and conserved quantities, uncertainty relations and spin. The course also introduces the specific applications, processing techniques and approximate equations of microscopic particle motion laws, including stationary perturbation theory, quantum transitions, scattering and many-body problems. Through the study of this course, students can comprehensively grasp the characteristics of microscopic particle motion, especially the understanding of the duality of waves and particles; and comprehensively master the skills and methods of handling microscopic particle motion. _x000D_
    _x000D_
        The birth of quantum mechanics: including the maturity and crisis of physics at the end of the 19th century. The analysis of the crisis led to the idea of quantum theory, and successfully explained the photoelectric effect, blackbody radiation, and the energy levels of atoms. On this basis, it gradually developed into a perfect theoretical system of quantum mechanics. The specific content of the explanation is: a brief history of quantum theory; wave function and Schrödinger's equation. Including the statistical interpretation of wave functions, the introduction of quantization and operators, the description of coordinate space and momentum space states and the representation of operators, the introduction of the Schrödinger equation, etc.; one-dimensional stationary state problems and their solutions; operator representation and representation transformation of mechanical quantities; the evolution of mechanical quantities over time; Central force field problem; particle motion in electromagnetic field; description of spin; algebraic method of quantum mechanics; quantum perturbation theory and non-perturbation theory method; quantum jump; scattering problem; hydrogen molecular structure, etc.

Name: Introduction to Cloud Physics
Introduction: Because of the important effects of clouds on the radiation and water cycle of the terrestrial gas system, current climate studies have become a focus. The course focuses on the microphysical processes of clouds, including cloud droplets and ice crystal particle formation, condensation (condensation) growth, touch and process, and deposition. The course will also teach the macro-dynamic processes that form clouds and the macro-micro characteristics of clouds. The cloud physics knowledge taught in this course is the basis for future studies on the climate effects of clouds and weather forecasting. Finally, cloud observation methods and numerical simulations are presented.

Name: Frontiers of Nuclear Science Lecture Series
Introduction: This course plans to invite scholars (mainly domestic experts) who are active in cutting-edge research fields related to nuclear science to introduce the latest developments in the frontiers of nuclear science to undergraduates in the form of lectures, so as to stimulate students' interest in nuclear science and deepen their understanding of the field of nuclear science. The nuclear science-related fields here specifically include high-energy physics, nuclear physics, nuclear technology, nuclear physics applications, accelerator physics, nuclear energy, etc.

Name: Advanced English Listening and Speaking
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is based on cultivating students' English listening and speaking abilities at an advanced stage. This course carefully selects teaching materials and auxiliary teaching materials with authentic, authentic and diverse language. The selected topics focus on students' interests and practical news, involving life, study, leisure and entertainment, and social hot issues. At the same time, a wealth of language practice activities are designed, including two-person dialogues, group discussions, class reports, etc. In order to train each student's language expression ability and posture, a special speech was also designed that counts towards the final grade. While providing students with audio-visual material support, students are encouraged to independently search for relevant information online, organize it in writing, and then present it in class. _x000D_
In terms of learning methods, this course advocates and implements a combination of cooperative learning and independent learning inside and outside the classroom. Students are randomly divided into pairs and groups, and the group and pair activities are monitored through teaching reports. At the same time, a large number of supplementary listening and classic recitation materials are also posted online on the teaching platform, requiring students to study independently and conduct spot checks in class, which will be included in their daily grades. _x000D_
In the listening part of the course, in addition to the listening exercises in the listening and speaking textbook, CNN audio-visual and other listening materials have been added, compound dictation exercises have been compiled, and exercises and quizzes for writing outlines and summaries have been designed as an advanced listening training part to satisfy students' desire to further improve their listening and at the same time cultivate the ability to effectively extract and organize information. _x000D_
In short, through a variety of listening and speaking exercises and tests, the vocabulary has been expanded and writing practice has been achieved to a certain extent. More importantly, students' listening and speaking abilities have been intensively trained and improved.

Name: Global Environment and Climate Change
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic scientific knowledge related to the global atmospheric environment and climate change, discusses the latest progress, hot spots and difficulties in this field, and stimulates students' enthusiasm to participate in solving environmental problems. The content involves the biogeochemical cycle of pollutants, ozone holes, near-surface ozone and aerosol pollution, acid deposition, pollution source analysis, pollution control, climate change, climate prediction, climate change response measures, geoengineering, renewable energy, etc.

Name: Materials Physics
Introduction: This course aims to enable students to understand the basic outline of materials physics and condensed matter physics research, as well as the cutting-edge trends in the field of materials physics, guide students to move from books to real research, and learn how specific research work is carried out through learning.

Name: History of China's Foreign Relations in the Twentieth Century
Introduction:
The course, which is intended to be of 1949 and covers the first half of the twentieth century (1900-1949) and the second half of the twentieth (1949-1999), is devoted to the history of relations between China and foreign countries over 50 years.
This course, which will focus primarily on teachers, will be complemented by a combination of self-study and research by students, and will focus on the analysis of major events in external relations and important diplomatic strategies during the period of the late Qing government, the Government of the North, the Government of the National Party and the Government of the Republic, while clarifying the history and development of relations in the mid-twentieth century.
The purpose of the course is to enable students to develop a historical understanding of the complexities and distortions of the relationship between China and the world in the twentieth century, based on an analysis and comparison of the evolution of relations between China and the world in the mid-twentieth century, as well as the trajectories and inevitable trajectories of modern China towards the world, in order to think about and look at China ' s relations with the world at the beginning of the twenty-first century.

Name: Human Development and Environmental Change
Introduction: Environmental history is an interdisciplinary field of study that studies the interactions between humans and other parts of the environment throughout history. The time frame of this course is from the Big Bang to the present, and the space scope covers the entire Earth. This course pays special attention to the comparison of different time periods and different regions, and unifies diachrony and synchrony in the comparison. By studying this course, students can develop their ability to analyze and solve real-life problems from a historical perspective.

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (I)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
"Introduction to Earth Science" covers the basic knowledge of each secondary discipline in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is a basic course to guide students into the door of earth science. It is also a required course for all majors in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. The main purpose of the course teaching can be summarized as the following three points:_x000D_
Through lectures and in-class internships (including field internships), students can master basic earth science concepts such as space and the planet Earth, the earth's structure, the earth's material composition, the earth's internal and external dynamic processes, the earth's basic physical characteristics, and earth observation technology. _x000D_
Earth science is characterized by its vast research objects and long history, but students lack an overall understanding of earth science in middle school. Therefore, it is necessary to teach students "Introduction to Earth Science" to initially establish the concepts of time and space in earth science, understand the thinking characteristics of earth science, learn to use standardized earth science language, and lay a good foundation for the study of subsequent courses in earth science. _x000D_
It enables students to have an understanding of the overall picture of earth science and adjacent disciplines and the cutting-edge research trends of the disciplines, to have a preliminary understanding of the basic content of the subsequent courses of each major, to understand the connections between the majors and subsequent courses, to grasp the connotation of earth science from a macro perspective, and to lay the foundation for cross-research among various branches of disciplines.

Name: Basketball
Introduction:
_x000D_
