1. Basketball is a collective confrontation event that combines running, jumping and throwing. Regularly engaging in basketball can effectively promote the overall development of physical fitness and is conducive to the improvement and improvement of cardiopulmonary function. Through learning and sports practice, you can experience the enterprising spirit of bravery, tenacity, competition and hard work, and cultivate a good team style. _x000D_
This course focuses on learning basic basketball knowledge, basic techniques, and basic tactics, introducing basic rules, and focusing on actual combat experience. Combine exercise with fun to achieve the purpose of improving health. _x000D_
2. Safety precautions: Students with congenital diseases need to apply for explanation from the teacher and obtain the teacher's consent before they can choose classes; strictly follow classroom routines, do not wear items unrelated to sports such as keys, glasses, etc., abide by classroom disciplines and follow the teacher's instructions. _x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Through the teaching of basketball classes, we establish the guiding ideology of "health first" and cultivate students' collective spirit of unity and cooperation and their tenacious will quality. _x000D_
2. Master the basic knowledge, basic techniques, basic skills and methods of basketball, cultivate the habit of physical exercise, and lay the foundation for lifelong sports. _x000D_
3. Improve health, enhance physical fitness, improve students' physical fitness and adaptability to the environment, and promote their overall physical and mental development. _x000D_
4. Understand the rules and refereeing methods, and improve the ability to appreciate high-level competitions. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (II)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
"Introduction to Earth Science" covers the basic knowledge of each secondary discipline in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is a basic course to guide students into the door of earth science. It is also a required course for all majors in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. The main purpose of the course teaching can be summarized as the following three points: _x000D_
Through lectures and in-class internships (including field internships), students can master basic earth science concepts such as space and the planet Earth, the earth's structure, the earth's material composition, the earth's internal and external dynamic processes, the earth's basic physical characteristics, and earth observation technology. _x000D_
Earth science is characterized by its vast research objects and long history, but students lack an overall understanding of earth science in middle school. Therefore, it is necessary to teach students "Introduction to Earth Science" to initially establish the concepts of time and space in earth science, understand the thinking characteristics of earth science, learn to use standardized earth science language, and lay a good foundation for the study of subsequent courses in earth science. _x000D_
It enables students to have an understanding of the overall picture of earth science and adjacent disciplines and the cutting-edge research trends of the disciplines, to have a preliminary understanding of the basic content of the subsequent courses of each major, to understand the connections between the majors and subsequent courses, to grasp the connotation of earth science from a macro perspective, and to lay the foundation for cross-research among various branches of disciplines.

Name: Frontiers of Earth Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course takes the form of lectures and mainly introduces the cutting-edge results achieved in earth and space science in recent years and scientific issues for further research. The lectures will be delivered by 6 academicians of the Chinese Academy of Sciences who work in our institute, once for each person (see the following content). Starting from several different sub-disciplines, they focused on introducing the main research methods, main achievements and existing problems of earth and space science, in order to understand the cutting-edge fields of today's earth and space science research and guide students' interest in earth and space science.

Name: General Geology Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course is a follow-up course to "Introduction to Earth Science (2)". It is a practical teaching content designed to deepen the understanding of the relevant content of the course. Therefore, if you participate in the study of this course, you must first complete the study of "Introduction to Earth Science".
Introduction:
Guided by modern geological theory and based on the geology of the Beijing area, this course closely focuses on the course content of "General Geology" and "Introduction to Earth Science", and consolidates the classroom teaching content of general geology through the introduction and understanding of typical field geological phenomena, deepens the understanding of relevant course content, conducts basic field skills training, cultivates the ability to observe geological phenomena, and lays a foundation for subsequent professional courses. _x000D_
      This course is a geological enlightenment education for first-year students in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is an important cognitive internship, emphasizing basic geological concepts, basic knowledge and basic skill training. During the internship, you will learn the most basic field work methods for geological work, such as the fixation and description of geological points, the use of compasses and topographic maps; recognize the three representative rock types seen in the internship, and learn to distinguish them; understand basic geological phenomena, such as strata, folds, faults, etc.; initially establish the development sequence and characteristics of the strata observed during the internship; learn to use induction and analysis methods to initially establish a geological thinking model, and prepare a simple internship report based on various geological phenomena observed. Through internships, students can cultivate their love for nature, cultivate their sentiments, and increase their interest in geological scientific research; at the same time, they can fully realize the importance of geological practice to geological science. _x000D_

Name: Cross-Cultural Course Series: Assessing and Developing International Leadership
Introduction:
Global leadership is a relatively new concept. It was established in the 1980s. With the increasingly strong trend of international cooperation in the fields of business, education, tourism and other fields, as well as the rapid development of the information industry, people have noticed that in the complex and ever-changing global environment, the adaptability and leadership of organizations and individuals have become an unavoidable and important factor in career development and success. More and more human resources departments of multinational companies, international cooperation organizations and institutions have regarded global leadership as one of the focus of enterprise and personnel training and one of the evaluation criteria for recruitment. _x000D_
This real environment brings opportunities and challenges not only to countries and organizations, but also to individual development. On the one hand, when the status of countries and cultures is increasing in the international society, the accumulation of international experience and the cultivation of cross-cultural abilities are urgent needs for personal survival and development; on the other hand, individuals using global leadership in transnational, cross-regional and cross-cultural organizations to have a positive impact on teams or groups is an inevitable requirement for organizational development in a globalized environment. _x000D_
Since the 1990s, Western countries have conducted more and more research on successful leaders and their abilities. The United States, due to its domestic multicultural social environment and its multi-faceted international cooperation, has matured in the development of research and assessment tools in this area, which is very worthy of our reference. This course is designed to be divided into three parts: First, we will introduce in detail some cutting-edge research results, especially those specific leadership abilities and their cultivation methods that are very important to our personal lives and careers, such as personal leadership, global awareness and vision, stress resistance, flexibility, problem-solving abilities, multicultural team management abilities, etc.; on the other hand, we have also seen that a certain leadership method that works in one country fails in another country, and a big reason is cultural differences. Therefore, in the second part, we will compare the consensus and differences between different cultures on leadership issues, and discover the training methods and goals that suit our own needs from many true, interesting but profound stories. The development of any ability must start with understanding oneself. To this end, in the third part, students will have the opportunity to measure their personal abilities, understand their current level, and try to formulate a corresponding personal development plan. _x000D_
In short, the concept of global leadership is important not only for leaders, but also for everyone's survival and development in a globalized society. Therefore, while introducing concepts, rich teaching activities such as classroom debates, challenge simulations, case observations, etc. will help you understand the knowledge learned and how to apply it. _x000D_

Name: Basic Music Theory and Fundamentals of Orchestral Music
Introduction: This course systematically teaches basic music theory, including musical sound system, temperament, notation, rhythm and beat, intervals, chords, modes, modulations, basic forms of music, preliminary harmony and polyphony, and modern music theory. It focuses on integrating theory with practice, analyzing works while introducing the functional characteristics of orchestras and various musical instruments, and combining music reading and simple electronic piano playing.

Name: Cartography
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Cartography is one of the basic disciplines of earth information science. This course includes the basic concepts of maps, the earth and its coordinate system, map projection, geographic information synthesis, map graphic design, symbolization of geographical features, map production process and technology, map evaluation and use, etc. In addition to classroom teaching, three assignments/practices are also designed: map projection establishment and deformation analysis, statistical map drawing, and topographic map reading and analysis. Through the systematic study and practice of this course, students are expected to master the basic theories, techniques and map analysis methods of map drawing, and develop their spatial data processing and spatial cognition abilities as well as the basic skills of making maps.

Name: Environmental and Ecological Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Course Objective: This course is for second-year students, focusing on the basic concepts and theories of ecology, current ecological and environmental issues of concern, and the role of GNSS, GIS and earth observation technology in ecological environment monitoring, evaluation and management. After one year of college study, students who choose this course have a strong foundation in geoscience, computers, remote sensing and geographical information systems. On this basis, through the study of basic knowledge of environment and ecology and the introduction of application examples, students' creative abilities are inspired and lay the foundation for students to choose their graduation thesis. _x000D_
    Summary of content: A relatively comprehensive introduction to the basic theories of environmental and ecological science, urban ecology and urban environment, wetland ecosystems, oasis ecosystems, the role and application examples of remote sensing inversion of ecological parameters, ecological environment assessment and management decision-making. In addition, the course also arranges three computer-based homework projects, and the data used come from scientific research projects funded by the Ministry of Science and Technology. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Surveying
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course is offered to students in the second year of undergraduate studies and requires only advanced mathematics, linear algebra.
Introduction:
The current development of surveying and mapping covers the entire field of spatial information, and the English concept has changed from survey to Geomatics. Introduction to Surveying and Mapping briefly describes the basic theories and technologies involved in the field of spatial information. It is a course that must be mastered by majors related to the field of spatial information. _x000D_
    Surveying and mapping is a science that studies the acquisition, processing, description and application of spatial information. Its contents include: studying the determination and description of the earth's shape, size, gravity field, surface morphology and their various changes, determining the spatial location and attributes of natural and artificial objects and artificial facilities, making various maps (including topographic maps) and establishing related information systems. The development of contemporary surveying and mapping has expanded to the fields of aerospace and interstellar space. _x000D_
    The application scope of surveying and mapping is very wide, including urban and rural construction planning, rational utilization of land resources, development of agriculture, forestry, animal husbandry and fishery, environmental protection, cadastral management, geological exploration, mineral development, water conservancy, transportation and other national economic construction, which must be carried out in geodetic survey, engineering survey, control survey, mine survey, line survey, map drawing and so on. In addition, in national defense construction, in addition to providing military maps for military operations, it is also necessary to provide accurate geocentric coordinates and accurate earth gravity field data to ensure the rapid positioning of artillery fire and the accuracy of missile and other weapon launches. In terms of studying the earth's motion status, surveying and mapping provide geometric information on tectonic movements and geodynamics, and combine with geophysical research results to solve problems on the earth's internal motion mechanism. _x000D_
    In the process of its development, surveying and mapping has formed sub-disciplines such as geodesy, photogrammetry, engineering surveying, marine surveying and cartography, and error assessment theory and methods. Geodesy is the theory and method of studying and determining the shape, size and gravity field of the earth, as well as the geometric position of ground points. Photogrammetry studies the theory and method of using cameras or other sensors to collect image information of measured objects, processing and analyzing it to determine the shape, size and position of the measured object, and to judge its properties. To survey and map large areas of land surface morphology, aerial photogrammetry is mainly used. Engineering surveying studies the theory, technology and methods of measurement work at all stages of design, construction and management of engineering construction. Provide accurate measurement data and large-scale maps for project construction to ensure reasonable project site selection, construction according to design and effective management. Ocean mapping studies the theory and techniques of measuring and mapping ocean water bodies and seafloor. Provide guarantee for ship navigation safety and marine engineering construction. Cartography studies the theories and methods of maps and their preparation. _x000D_
    This course mainly briefly explains the principles, technologies and application methods of the above aspects, and combines actual surveying and mapping internships and visits to allow students to fully understand and basically master the basic theories and methods in the field of integrated spatial information.

Name: Human Sexuality, Reproduction and Health
Introduction: The course is based on biology, physiology and medicine, combined with sociology and psychology, and tells scientific knowledge in several aspects such as "what is sex", "sex and reproduction", "sex and health" and "sexual issues" from multiple disciplines and perspectives. The lecture content starts from the significance of this course, the historical changes in sexual concepts, the biological significance of sexual differentiation and human reproductive models, and briefly describes the characteristics and evolution of human sexual behavior, and then explains in detail the basic structure and function of male and female reproductive organs, the biological and physiological basis of gonadal function and its regulatory control, human fertilization, embryonic development, fertility, sexual development and differentiation, and the biological and physiological knowledge and problems of adolescence. It also introduces basic knowledge of human genetic diseases, sexual hygiene, and the prevention and control of sexually transmitted diseases (including AIDS). The content of the lectures extensively covers the sexual confusions and problems of college students and is close to the lives of college students. At the same time, it focuses on cultivating college students' correct sexual attitudes, sexual concepts and sexual health awareness, thereby positively guiding college students to engage in healthy sexual behavior. The course pays special attention to cultivating female college students’ correct sexual attitudes and self-protection awareness.

Name: Introduction to Remote Sensing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: The elective course requires a professional foundation in higher mathematics, university physics and geology.
Introduction:
Purpose: Through the teaching of "Introduction to Remote Sensing", students can systematically master the basic theories, methods and application technologies of remote sensing, understand the latest progress in the development of remote sensing, and have basic skills in remote sensing image processing, interpretation and application analysis. _x000D_
	Main content: basic concepts of remote sensing, remote sensing imaging mechanism, acquisition of remote sensing images, processing and interpretation of remote sensing images, remote sensing applications, etc. _x000D_
	Course Features:_x000D_
	(1) Highlight the advancement and foresight: fully draw on the teaching system and content of this course at home and abroad, and pay attention to reflecting the latest progress in the field of remote sensing; _x000D_
	(2) Maintain systematicness and scientificity: basic knowledge is introduced step by step, and teaching content is connected before and after; _x000D_
	(3) Strengthen the foundation and practicality: focus on the close integration of remote sensing imaging mechanisms with image processing, interpretation methods and remote sensing applications. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Databases
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Course Purpose: Through the study of this course, students are required to understand the basic theories, technologies and methods of databases, master database programming languages, be able to independently conduct database modeling, design and application development, and understand the new developments of database technology. _x000D_
Course content: (1) Basic concepts and principles of databases; (2) Database language; (3) Database design; (4) Implementation of database systems; (5) New database technologies.

Name: Introduction to Intelligent Transportation Systems
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
An overview of intelligent transport systems
The course is divided into nine chapters, with in-depth analysis and discussion from concepts of intelligent transport systems, systems frameworks, key technologies of intelligent transport systems, planning and design of intelligent transport systems, urban traffic signal control systems, advanced traffic management systems, traffic information services systems, advanced vehicle systems, advanced cargo management systems, etc. (b) Strict adherence to the national ITS framework arrangements for lectures, which fully reflect the core elements of the framework and focus on norms and standards for relevant elements such as terminology, definitions and so forth. At the pedagogical level, the teaching staff are able to follow up on recent international scientific and technological developments and research in the field of ITS, but are also able to provide a more informative account of the research carried out by ITS in developed countries, the current state of application, the typical system of use and the results and success stories of our country in recent years. The course will provide for a vehicle navigation vehicle demonstration experiment to visit the Beijing City Command and Control Centre or the Beijing City Traffic Control Command Centre.

Name: Principles of Geographic Information Systems
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Geography, computing, computer program design language, algorithms and data structure, cartography
Introduction: This course enables students to have a comprehensive and complete understanding of the basic concepts, data structures, technical systems and application methods of geographic information systems, and to initially master the operating skills of GIS software. The main contents of the basic theory and knowledge taught include: the basic concepts, composition, subject content and development history of GIS, GIS data model and data structure, GIS system structure and main functions, GIS spatial analysis model, GIS application methods, application examples and development prospects. It also includes appropriate GIS programming and software operation content. The former enables students to have a more intuitive understanding of the underlying GIS through some preliminary data structure coding and establishes the concept of graphics programming. The latter focuses on cultivating students' basic GIS operation skills from input, database construction, query, analysis to output.

Name: Urban and Regional Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The main task of the course is to impart basic theories of urban and regional science. This course is a precursor to the 3S course section for undergraduate teaching, and is also a basic course for digital areas and digital cities. _x000D_
This course requires students to master the subject attributes and basic categories of economic geography, urban geography and regional planning, master the basic principles of geographical location theory, urban spatial structure, regional industrial structure, etc., comprehensively master the research methods of economic geography and regional planning, principles of location selection, principles of cities and urbanization, regional industrial structure and economic growth principles, etc. It also guides students to understand and pay attention to hot issues such as sustainable development, Chinese cities and regional development, and think about the relationship between this course and the geographic information system major. Understand the development status and existing problems of regions and cities as well as the development of my country's regional development strategies, and guide students to understand and pay attention to cutting-edge issues in urban and regional scientific research. _x000D_

Name: Basketball (Advanced)
Introduction:
_x000D_
Basketball is a collective confrontation event that combines running, jumping and throwing. Regularly engaging in basketball can effectively promote the overall development of physical fitness and is conducive to the improvement and improvement of cardiopulmonary function. Through learning and sports practice, you can experience the enterprising spirit of bravery, tenacity, competition and hard work, and cultivate a good team style. _x000D_
This course focuses on learning basic basketball knowledge, basic techniques, and basic tactics, introducing basic rules, and focusing on actual combat experience. Combine exercise with fun to achieve the purpose of improving health. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Buddhism
Introduction:
This course introduces the basic knowledge of Buddhism, which has an important influence on the development of world culture. The course focuses on explaining the origin, spread history, literature, precepts, meditation, philosophical thoughts, etc. of Buddhism. The entire course is divided into eight lectures, each of which introduces an important aspect or important content of Buddhist knowledge. The basic knowledge of Buddhism discussed in this course is mainly Indian Buddhism and Chinese Buddhism. The main content involved is mainly the history and teachings of Buddhism, including important figures, schools, theories, events, cultural characteristics, etc. The purpose of teaching is to enable students to have a general understanding of Buddhism and grasp the core content and essence of Buddhist culture. To lay the foundation for further understanding or research of Buddhism and improve the humanistic quality of students attending classes. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Discrete Mathematics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Discrete mathematics is a basic subject of computer science and information technology. The basic knowledge of discrete structures and the formalization of logical thinking are basic skills for information technology students. The basic concepts of discrete mathematics are an important foundation for students majoring in GIS to study information courses. Through classroom lectures and extracurricular assignments, this course introduces the concepts and ideological methods of the theoretical basis of computer science and information technology, introduces the basic concepts of various discrete mathematics branches such as mathematical logic, set theory, graph theory, abstract algebra, formal language and automata, introduces the connection and combination between the basic concepts of discrete mathematics and spatial information technology, and cultivates students' ability to understand and master the basic concepts of discrete mathematics, use formal methods to analyze problems, and be able to consciously use logical analysis, structural level analysis, isomorphic analogy and other ideological methods to solve problems.

Name: The Earth and Human Civilization
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The Earth and Human Civilization course is based on the interaction between the Earth and human civilization. It studies how various geological phenomena and environmental factors since the formation of the Earth have promoted the evolution of life, the emergence of wisdom, and the formation of human civilization, and affected the evolution and development direction of human civilization; explore the impact of human civilization on the earth in turn; and think about the harmonious way for human civilization and the earth to develop together. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course uses classroom explanations, reading discussions, extracurricular assignments, indoor experiments and field internships, combined with various experimental teaching technologies such as virtual reality, human-computer interaction, and intelligent mobile computing, to show the evolution of the earth and the development of human civilization; students are encouraged to combine their professional knowledge and actively engage in multi-angle thinking and communication; thus cultivating students to understand and master the basic logic between the evolution of the earth and human civilization. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Computer Graphics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Since geographic information systems involve a large number of various principles and algorithms in graphics calculation analysis, rendering and optimization, it is very necessary to master the basic principles and common algorithms of computer graphics to promote the understanding and application of geographic information system principles and methods. _x000D_
This course requires students to understand the basic principles and algorithms of computer graphics and be able to express principles and implement algorithms through computer language. _x000D_
The course mainly teaches the basic principles and algorithm implementation of computer graphics generation, display, modeling, transformation and computer animation. Enhance students' understanding of principles, concepts and algorithms and improve students' practical abilities by completing programming assignments.

Name: Network Fundamentals and WebGIS
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Computer network is one of the core courses of computer majors. WebGIS is the product of the combination of GIS technology and Internet technology, and is a new trend in GIS development. Through the study of this course, students are required to master the basic knowledge of computer networks, Internet, Web and network programming; on this basis, understand the basic concepts, structures, technologies, methods and applications of WebGIS; master the design and application development of WebGIS applications; understand the role of standards in networks and interoperability, and master the development of WebGIS platform software.

Name: Principles of Remote Sensing Digital Image Processing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Cartography, probability theory and mathematical statistics, linear algebras, computational mathematics, program design, remote sensing overview.
Introduction: Digital image processing is an important means of expressing spatial remote sensing information and a direct and objective expression of ground geographical information. Remote sensing digital image processing includes basic understanding of image processing system software and hardware, digital expression of optical phenomena, mathematical transformation, enhancement, restoration, grayscale and binary processing of images, true and false color discrimination and utilization, image compression and decompression, image analysis, etc. On the basis of the above theory, basic image software is used to flexibly apply relevant processing technologies to achieve basic discrimination and analysis of remote sensing images. Features: Provide basic skills for analyzing problems using image processing methods in this field in the future.

Name: GIS Laboratory
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Through the study and use of commonly used software in the GIS field, students can further deepen their understanding of the basic principles and methods of geographic information systems, enable them to master the operation and use of GIS software, and understand the current development trends in the GIS field. The course will combine typical GIS application cases to help students gradually master independent analysis and thinking methods, and cultivate their ability to use GIS software to solve practical problems.

Name: Innovative Applications and Practice of Virtual Simulation
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Virtual simulation techniques, with virtual realities, enhanced realities and simulations as their content, have become the hotspots of innovation in recent years, known as the year 2016 as the year of VR (Virtual reality), with a convergence of VR hardware and systems, and a virtual reality that will destabilize many industries over the next 5 to 10 years. Virtual simulations can be applied to a wide range of areas of national livelihood, such as academic research, education and training, leisure tourism, urban planning and emergency preparedness.
The course provides an overview of the innovative applications of virtual simulations in various industries from the technology, products and market chain, building on the Virtual Simulation Experimental Teaching Centre of the Institute, with a focus on strengthening the teaching of practice and enhancing the innovation, practical and employment capacities of students.

Name: GIS Design and Applications
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
(1) One programming language
(2) Computer Graphics
(3) Data structure
4) GIS doctrine
Introduction: From the two aspects of design, development and application methods, students can master the development ideas and development methods of GIS, clarify the logical and physical structure of GIS, and develop the technical route and main technical methods of GIS from the bottom. This will lay a better theoretical foundation and master application methods for students to implement geographic information system engineering in the future. Cultivate their thinking and practical abilities on how to apply geographic information systems.

Name: Integrated 3S Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: GIS General; Remote Sensing General; Introduction to Earth Sciences
Introduction:
Through comprehensive field internships in typical areas, students can understand the basic methods of comprehensive practical application of 3S, cultivate students' practical ability, and help them deeply understand and master the theoretical knowledge they have learned:_x000D_
    It is a process of walking out of school and being in nature to verify the basic knowledge of cartography, physical geography and 3S basic theories learned in the classroom. _x000D_
    Apply various methods and theories learned in remote sensing, geographic information systems, and global positioning systems to practical work to deepen your understanding of basic theoretical knowledge. _x000D_
    Master the basic skills of physical geography field investigation, and cultivate and exercise students' hands-on and independent working abilities. _x000D_
    Master the basic methods and techniques of comprehensively utilizing remote sensing, geographic information systems and global positioning systems to conduct regional field surveys and thematic remote sensing interpretation work. _x000D_

Name: Programming Languages
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: "Programming Languages" is a basic computer course. It is the second stage course for undergraduates after studying "Introduction to Computing" and other pilot courses. Its main goal is to cultivate students' ability to use programming languages ​​to operate computers to solve specific problems. The course uses high-level language programming as an example to teach the basic concepts, principles, methods and techniques of programming. Through computer internships, students can master the ability to actually apply the knowledge they have learned, develop a good programming style, and lay a solid foundation for them to study subsequent professional courses and participate in related scientific research practices. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Geomorphology and Physical Geography
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The content of this course is the basic knowledge of physical geography and geomorphology that undergraduate students in geographic information systems, remote sensing and other related majors must master. Compared with the undergraduate course of physical geography, this course makes necessary adjustments to the teaching content according to the characteristics of GIS and RS majors, highlighting the basic principles, basic issues, basic research methods of physical geography and geomorphology, as well as related basic on-site inspection, analysis, description and data acquisition methods. The course content plays a very important role in correctly explaining and solving many geographical and geomorphological problems encountered in practical work and life. _x000D_
	The main teaching purpose of this course is to cultivate students' skills in analyzing geography and geomorphology issues using the basic principles of natural science through classroom lectures and subsequent field practice, understand the basic knowledge of physical geography and geomorphology, understand the mechanisms of the generation and development of various common geography and geomorphology natural phenomena, and lay a solid foundation for the study of professional knowledge and scientific research in related disciplines.

Name: Introduction to Internet of Things Technology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Introduction to Internet of Things Technology_x000D_
 The Internet of Things involves many technologies and is a new interdisciplinary subject. Current research on the Internet of Things is gradually moving out of the laboratory, and popular Internet of Things applications are beginning to penetrate into people's daily lives. This course focuses on a comprehensive explanation and summary of the concept, basic structure, system framework, key technologies and development trends of IoT technology of the Internet of Things dominated by Electronic Product Code (EPC). This course is divided into eight chapters. The main contents include: Overview of the Internet of Things, working principle and composition of the Internet of Things, radio frequency identification system, middleware, object name resolution service, entity markup language, new Internet of Things services, Internet of Things management and the construction of the Internet of Things in my country. _x000D_
    In order to satisfy the professional teaching of Internet of Things technology and the understanding of new information network technologies from all walks of life, it is planned to apply for the establishment of an undergraduate general elective course "Introduction to Internet of Things Technology". By permeating the content of the framework system in the teaching stage, teachers can not only track the latest scientific and technological trends and research results in the field of international Internet of Things technology, but also introduce in detail the research and application status of the Internet of Things in developed countries, typical application systems, and teach some of my country's achievements and successful cases in recent years.

Name: Fundamentals of Quantitative Remote Sensing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Course Necessity:_x000D_
  Quantitative remote sensing is currently the main development and research hotspot of remote sensing. Multi-source remote sensing satellites and networks covering the full spectrum have been developed at home and abroad. Various land surface, sea surface and atmospheric parameters have been estimated from remote sensing data, and are used in global change, regional energy balance, farmland ecology, urban environment and resource detection. Field observation experiments play an important role in quantitative remote sensing research. They are an important way to test the accuracy of remote sensing data and products, and are also an important means to discover various patterns of reflected radiation or self-radiation of ground objects. The course "Fundamentals of Quantitative Remote Sensing" will be aimed at third-year undergraduates who have accumulated a certain amount of remote sensing knowledge. It will focus on explaining the basic principles and various application topics of quantitative remote sensing based on field observation experiments, thereby providing the necessary preliminary knowledge reserves for undergraduates to further carry out quantitative remote sensing research at the graduate level. _x000D_
Main content of the course:_x000D_
  It focuses on introducing the current satellite remote sensing platform, the basic ideas of remote sensing retrieval of surface parameters (leaf area index, vegetation coverage, photosynthetically active radiation, albedo, surface temperature, etc.) and atmospheric parameters (water vapor content, aerosol optical thickness, etc.), as well as ground verification methods of remote sensing products. It also introduces field experiment program design, measurement specifications, instrument operation methods, algorithm principles, and software development and implementation. _x000D_

Name: Canadian History and Culture
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is intended to present the historical, geographical and social background of Canada. The aim is to help students become familiar with Canada. Once students have mastery of the curriculum, they will be able to:
• Enumerating basic facts of Canadian history and geography
• Explain the similarities and differences between Canada and the United States
• Describe the factors that have influenced Canadian history, past and present
• Analysis of the forces that changed Canada in the twenty-first century

Name: Principles of Operating Systems
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
Algorithms and data structure, program design language.
Students are required to have a certain base of software development and are familiar with the codes of advanced languages such as C, C++ or C#/Java.
Introduction:
The operating system is the core software of the computer system, the basis for all other software operations and the basic platform for the development of the computer system. The operating system provides a bridge between computer users and computer hardware, through which computer users use computer resources more easily and computer hardware more efficiently. The special position of operating systems in computer systems has made the OSE course an important address in computer science learning, which is the basic course in the computer science system. Learning about the working mechanisms and working methods of operating the system, and thus designing and implementing it, is an essential knowledge and skills of the information science class, including the GIS professional orientation.
The course focuses on the design methods and techniques of operating systems and teaches the essence of the design of numerous operating systems. The Operational System Doctrine course is a summary of people ' s practical experience in engineering in the design of the operating system, and its content is technology-oriented rather than a specific product. Course learners study and learn how to realize an operating system from the perspective of an operating system designer, not just an operating system user.
The main elements of the course include: the concept of operating systems, the basis of co-processing design, thread management, processor management, memory management, equipment management and documentation systems.

Name: Principles of Software Engineering
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
Algorithms and data structure, programming language, database overview.
Students are required to have a certain development base and are familiar with the use of advanced programming languages C++ or C#/Java.
Introduction:
Software engineering is an engineering discipline that studies and guides software development and maintenance. It is guided by the theories of computer science and other related disciplines, and uses engineering concepts, principles, specifications, technologies and methods to develop and maintain software engineering projects. It combines management measures proven to be correct in practice with the best technical methods currently available to obtain high-quality software products at a lower cost. After more than 40 years of hard work, software engineering has gradually developed into a mature professional discipline. "Software Engineering Principles" is also a necessary professional foundation for students in information science (including GIS majors). _x000D_
    This course mainly introduces the concepts, technologies and methods of software engineering, including software development models, software project management, software quality measurement, feasibility analysis, requirements analysis, software design, coding, testing and maintenance; data flow-oriented analysis and design methods, data structure-oriented analysis and design methods, object-oriented analysis and design methods; software testing and quality control methods; and allows students to participate in a small software engineering project in groups to improve software development collaboration capabilities and master software engineering implementation specifications. It aims to cultivate students' ability to analyze and design actual software systems, as well as their ability to skillfully use various popular software technologies to solve practical problems and control software quality. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Digital Earth
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
This course is an elective course for undergraduate students majoring in geographic information science. From the perspective of earth information science, the course focuses on the basic theory, construction and application technology of digital earth. It lays a good theoretical foundation for students to engage in related research, so that students have an overall understanding and mastery of the digital earth. This course mainly introduces the concept and development history of digital earth, basic theory of digital earth, digital earth information acquisition technology system, digital earth information transmission technology system, high-performance computing technology system of digital earth information, virtual geographical environment and visualization technology, digital global earth observation system, new generation digital earth, etc. This course attempts to comprehensively reflect the latest technology, latest development strategic goals and research plans in the field of Digital Earth, and guide students to understand and pay attention to cutting-edge issues in Digital Earth research. _x000D_
   Students are required to master the basic theory of Digital Earth, including the framework content of Digital Earth, key technologies of Digital Earth, applications of Digital Earth, and the future development of Digital Earth. _x000D_

Name: Remote Sensing Image Processing Laboratory
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
Introduction to Remote Sensing
Remote Sensing Digital Image Processing
Introduction:
ENVI (The Environment for Visualizing Images) is a complete remote sensing image processing platform. Its software processing technology covers image data input/output, image calibration, image enhancement, correction, orthorectification, mosaic, data fusion and various transformations, information extraction, image classification, knowledge-based decision tree classification, integration with GIS, DEM and terrain information extraction, radar data processing, and three-dimensional display analysis. ENVI is developed based on the powerful secondary development language IDL and is seamlessly integrated with IDL. Therefore, it can make full use of the powerful function library, graphics library, scientific computing and cross-platform features provided by the IDL language to develop a professional remote sensing analysis system. _x000D_
    The course uses ENVI as the teaching software, uses actual remote sensing data, and systematically teaches remote sensing image enhancement, geometric correction, orthorectification, image mosaic and fusion, image classification, change monitoring, and remote sensing special application through application examples. Through learning, students can correctly master the basic methods and experimental skills of remote sensing image processing, and at the same time deepen their understanding of the principles of digital image processing, have the ability to apply remote sensing images to process, analyze and solve practical problems, and adapt to scientific research or teaching work in related fields. _x000D_

Name: History of Christian Civilization
Introduction:
This course deals with the emergence and evolution of Christian civilization through slavery, feudal society and wealth.
The history of this monotheistic society, nearly 2,000 years ago, saw political, social and cultural changes as leading to Christian teachings.
and the basis for changes in the church system. Main elements include the emergence of Christianity, the Roman Church, and medieval Christianity.
Topics such as conferences, Renaissance Churches, the European Movement for Religious Reform and recent Christianity, and
Religions, Calvinism, People ' s Religious Reforms led by Pencer, German Peasant War, Religion and Capitalism,
Recent Christian characteristics, etc.

Name: Psychology, Behavior and Culture
Introduction: This course is based on the psychological anthropology theory of Chinese-American psychological anthropologist Xu Yangguang, and constructs a theoretical system for comparative study of four large-scale civilized societies in China, India, the United States, and Japan. The course proposes the concept of "basic interpersonal status" and uses it as a basic unit for comparative study of civilized societies. It elaborates on the basic interpersonal status of several large-scale civilized societies, the characteristics of kinship systems, attention to secondary groups and their principles of conclusion, psychological and cultural orientations, human socialization patterns (parenting methods), etc. It puts forward views on culture and civilization from a new perspective. The course combines a large number of practical examples to explore cultural differences in a simple and easy-to-understand way.

Name: The Botany of Food
Introduction: "Food is the first necessity of the people" is a saying we have all heard since childhood. But do you know what our food is? How did our food evolve during the long development of human civilization? How to ensure nutritious, safe and stable food supply for all humans on earth in the future? The answers to these questions lie in the delicious and magical world of plants. Plants are the primary producers supporting the earth's biosphere and the most important source of human food. For thousands of years, the roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds of plants have provided all seven nutrients needed by humans: water, protein, oil, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. The domestication of wild crops and vegetables is the beginning of all ancient civilizations, including the Chinese civilization. In recent centuries, the observation and study of plant life activities have greatly promoted the development of life sciences and natural sciences. More importantly, as the world's population grows and natural resources become increasingly stretched, each of us is a stakeholder in modern agriculture, because agriculture is related to personal health, social progress, and how humans can coexist harmoniously with nature and develop sustainably. This course will comprehensively demonstrate and explain knowledge related to food nutrition and safety from multiple aspects such as nutritional composition, plant classification and development, crop domestication, biotechnology, and agricultural big data. Plants are our wonderful neighbors and close partners, condensing our history and nurturing our future. If you love life and care about nature, you are welcome to take "Botany on the Tip of the Tongue" as an elective!

Name: Introduction to Lidar Remote Sensing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Light Defense And Rangeing, LiDAR is an active optical detection technology system that collects laser ranging, global navigation satellite systems and inertial measurement techniques that can be used directly to obtain three-dimensional space information. Laser radar remote sensing is the active remote sensing technology based on laser radar, which has developed rapidly internationally in recent years and which, together with imaging spectral, synthetic aperture radar, is listed as the central focus of the Earth Observation System of Systems (Earth Observation System of Systems, EOS) project for information acquisition and processing technology, as well as the core foundation for the realization of technology, such as exploration projects, in our medium- and long-term scientific and technological development plans. On the other hand, in particular from the professional standpoint of disciplines, laser radar remote sensing is the third stage of the development of traditional mapping and photogrammetry techniques for space-related three-dimensional information measurement, which will be mainstreamed into future applications in relevant industry areas. As an optional subject for undergraduate students, the course will systematically describe to students the relevant technologies of laser radar remote sensing, including basic principles, measurement methods, data processing methods, potential applications, etc., which will provide a good professional basis for their future work practices or scientific research.

Name: Principles of Natural Resource Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Focusing on the coupling relationship between natural resources and human development, this course is divided into four parts. The first part systematically explains the nature of natural resources, the international and domestic situation of natural resource scarcity and conflict, academic debates on natural resource scarcity, and the nature of natural resource scarcity. The second part focuses on the principles of natural resource ecology, including natural resource ecological processes, natural resources and human ecology, and the ecological impact of natural resource utilization and its evaluation. The third part discusses the economic principles of natural resources from the aspects of the relationship between natural resources and economic society, basic issues of natural resource economics, natural resource allocation and value reconstruction; the fourth part discusses the principles of natural resource management from the perspective of users, including natural resource evaluation, input-output relationship of resource utilization, natural resource development decision-making, natural resource protection and sustainable management of natural resources.

Name: Australian History and Culture through Film and Television
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The course “The theme of Australian history and cultural video” is part of the intercultural communication module B. A special subject in English. The subject is the interpretation of history and multiculturalism through eight films. First, the classroom film shows the history of Australia. Australia is a unique country. From a historical point of view, the original people were born here more than 60,000 years ago, so Australia is an old country. The film Rabbit Proof Fence and the former Prime Minister's Video Documentary (An Apology to Indigenous Australians for the Stolen Generals) describe Australia's ancient history of original authors. Australia ' s colonial history began in 1788 when the British entered Australia and was only 200 years old. In 1901, Australia emerged from British rule, declared independence and established a federation. Since its establishment in 1901, the country has been a young nation for more than 100 years. The films Gallipoli and Kokoda reflect the rise of Australia's history and national spirit as a young nation. The second classroom film shows the multicultural part of Australia. The unique nature of Australia ' s history determines its cultural specificity. Australian culture includes white cultures dominated by white people of Anglo-Celtic descent; post-Second World War immigration cultures; and the earliest settler indigenous cultures on Australian mainland. Today, Australian immigrants or descendants of immigrants are made up of more than 200 countries and peoples in the world. It has become a multicultural, multilingual and multicultural country in the world. Australian culture is also one of the most diverse cultures in the world. The film Crocodile Dundee, "Looking for Albrandi " , "Scriptly Ballroom " and "The Castle" in the classroom describe Australia ' s experiences over the past 100 years of interdependencies and tolerance among different cultures, which shape today ' s prosperous and stable diverse sociocultural patterns. Third, the course “The theme of Australian history and culture video” is conducted twice a week, with a total of two credits, all in English. The aims include, first, improving the language skills of students through the audio-visual art window, and, second, helping students to understand the diverse socio-cultural patterns prevailing in Australia today, broadening cultural horizons and building on them a multicultural identity and understanding. As a country with a multicultural policy, Australia recognizes such a country and is an integral part of the interdisciplinary knowledge framework for young students in the twenty-first century.

Name: General Chemistry Problem Session
Introduction:
General Chemistry is the backbone basic course for chemistry majors. It is an introductory course before entering the professional basic courses and is open to first-year students in the School of Chemistry. _x000D_
    The general chemistry course mainly introduces the basic concepts and methods of chemistry. The main contents include: basic laws of gases and liquids, chemical thermodynamics and direction of chemical reactions, chemical equilibrium, chemical kinetics and reaction rate equations, several corollaries of atomic structure and quantum theory, molecular structure and theory, crystal structure, coordination compounds and element chemistry. _x000D_

Name: General Chemistry (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
"General Chemistry B" is a course for undergraduates. This course mainly introduces basic knowledge such as chemical principles and elemental chemistry, enabling students to master the basic laws and characteristics of chemistry, and cultivating students' ability to apply this knowledge to solve chemical problems. _x000D_
    The chemical principles section includes: gases, liquids and solutions; directions and limits of chemical reactions; four equilibria in solutions and the basis of electrochemistry; atomic and molecular structures. In the elaboration of the principles, emphasis will be placed on the systematicness of the theory and the accuracy of the concepts, emphasizing that scientific experiments are the basis and premise of the theory. The element part is based on the periodic table of elements and structural chemistry. According to the characteristics of the electronic structure, the elements are divided into s and ds regions, p regions, and d regions. Pay attention to the close integration with the theoretical part, the relationship between trace elements and human health, etc. _x000D_
    The whole course consists of 64 hours, which is completed through classroom lectures, after-class exercises and Q&A, discussions and exercise classes using the teaching network platform. Performance evaluation includes: 10% of daily grades (homework, etc.), 30% of midterm exam, and 60% of final exam.

Name: General Chemistry Laboratory (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
"General Chemistry Experiment B" is a main basic course offered by the School of Chemistry to all undergraduates majoring in science and non-chemistry majors. Course starts in autumn semester, total credit hours: 60, weekly credit hours: 4, credits: 2. Small class teaching takes the form of instructor teaching, students completing experiments independently (or cooperatively), teacher guidance, group discussion, literature review, report exchange and other forms. Classroom teaching is the mainstay, supplemented by online courses, providing diversified teaching models. _x000D_
The main tasks of the course are to help students correctly master the basic methods and skills of chemical experiments through the explanation of experimental principles, training in basic operations, recording, analysis, reasoning, induction, summary and refinement of experimental phenomena and data; to establish a serious, realistic scientific attitude and good experimental style; to cultivate students' ability to ask, analyze and solve problems and scientific thinking; to strengthen students' awareness and ability of safety and self-protection. Utilize the time and space advantages of online teaching and adopt diversified teaching models to improve students' ability to learn actively and innovatively. Explore students' potential in all aspects and improve their overall quality. Lay a solid foundation for subsequent chemistry experiment classes. _x000D_
The biggest feature of the course is that it is basic and broad, covering multiple second-level chemistry subjects. The course content includes basic operations of chemical experiments, chemical constant determination experiments, quantitative analysis experiments, qualitative analysis experiments, chemical equilibrium experiments, element properties experiments and inorganic compound preparation experiments. _x000D_

Name: College English (I) (2)
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The teaching of College English Level 1 is for students who are classified as Level 1 in the College English Placement Examination. The teaching of college English in this category aims to implement the spirit and guiding principles of the "College English Course Teaching Requirements" promulgated by the Ministry of Education in 2003 and vigorously cultivate students' comprehensive English application ability. Give full play to the leading role of teachers in language teaching, strengthen the circulation of language content, pay attention to listening and speaking to drive reading and writing, and use semantics to drive the acquisition of language forms. In teaching, we must also make full use of the online version of textbooks and electronic courseware to explore students' independent learning abilities as language learning subjects and effectively cultivate students' practical English application abilities. There are three parts: "intensive reading", "extensive reading" and "listening and listening".

Name: Table Tennis
Introduction:
1. Table tennis is a ball game in which two or two pairs of players take turns hitting the ball with rackets at both ends of the net. Ping Pong_x000D_
Ball is a confrontational event across the net. There is no direct collision with the body. It is relatively safe and is a sport suitable for all ages.
