Name: General Physics Problem Session
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: The subject of general physics for the Department of the College of Physics Classes

Name: General Physics (B) (I)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The two-semester general physics course includes mechanics, heat, electromagnetism, optics and modern physics. This course places great emphasis on the introduction of fundamental concepts and principles common to both classical and quantum physics. In order to deepen the understanding of physics knowledge, this course includes many applications of physics knowledge in engineering, technology, biomedicine and everyday familiar phenomena. We encourage classroom teachers to choose teaching materials based on their own interests and student situations, and to include as much knowledge of relativity and quantum physics as possible.

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (II)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
"Introduction to Earth Science" covers the basic knowledge of each secondary discipline in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is a basic course to guide students into the door of earth science. It is also a required course for all majors in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. The main purpose of the course teaching can be summarized as the following three points: _x000D_
Through lectures and in-class internships (including field internships), students can master basic earth science concepts such as space and the planet Earth, the earth's structure, the earth's material composition, the earth's internal and external dynamic processes, the earth's basic physical characteristics, and earth observation technology. _x000D_
Earth science is characterized by its vast research objects and long history, but students lack an overall understanding of earth science in middle school. Therefore, it is necessary to teach students "Introduction to Earth Science" to initially establish the concepts of time and space in earth science, understand the thinking characteristics of earth science, learn to use standardized earth science language, and lay a good foundation for the study of subsequent courses in earth science. _x000D_
It enables students to have an understanding of the overall picture of earth science and adjacent disciplines and the cutting-edge research trends of the disciplines, to have a preliminary understanding of the basic content of the subsequent courses of each major, to understand the connections between the majors and subsequent courses, to grasp the connotation of earth science from a macro perspective, and to lay the foundation for cross-research among various branches of disciplines.

Name: Crystallography and Mineralogy
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Minerals are crystalline natural compounds or simple substances formed by geological processes. They are also the smallest independent units that constitute the earth's crust or celestial bodies. The formation, existence, evolution and demise of all geological bodies or celestial bodies are closely related to minerals. Mineralogy is a science that studies the chemical composition, internal structure, appearance, origin, occurrence and relationship of minerals. Since minerals exist in crystalline form, crystallography and mineralogy complement each other and form an inseparable whole. "Crystallography and Mineralogy" is one of the most basic courses in geological science, and it is also a precursor to other geoscience courses, such as petrology, mineral deposits, geochemistry, structural geology, stratigraphic paleontology, gemology, geomorphology, etc. Some basic knowledge in this course, such as the expression and analysis of crystal structures, is also necessary basic knowledge for related disciplines such as solid-state chemistry, solid-state physics, and materials science. _x000D_
_x000D_
    The main content of this course includes: the concept of crystals and crystal morphological characteristics, the basic concepts of the internal structure of crystals, mineral crystal chemistry, basic concepts of physical properties, the main characteristics of various types of minerals, and the composition, structure, physical properties, and origin of common mineral species. Some main contents, such as 47 types of simplexes, 32 types of point groups, 14 types of Bravais lattices, etc., can be taught using multimedia visualization, and the structure of crystalline substances can also be expressed in real time in three-dimensional ways.

Name: General Geology Field Practicum A
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This field teaching internship is a geological enlightenment education for first-year students majoring in geology and geochemistry in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is an important cognitive internship, focusing on basic geological concepts, basic knowledge and basic skill training. Through short-term field practice, students can have a relatively comprehensive and general understanding of the main content and characteristics of geological research; through field practice, they can consolidate the classroom teaching content of the geology part of "Introduction to Earth Science" and deepen their understanding of the relevant content of the course; during the internship, they can learn to locate and describe geological points, compasses The most basic field work methods for geological work such as the use of topographic maps; understand basic geological bodies and geological phenomena, learn to describe these geological bodies and geological phenomena, analyze the geological processes that formed them, comprehensively analyze the geological processes in the Beijing area, understand the geological evolution history of the Beijing area, and prepare a simple internship report. Through internships, students can cultivate their love for nature, cultivate their sentiments, and increase their interest in geological scientific research; at the same time, they can fully realize the importance of geological practice to geological science.

Name: General Physics (B) (II)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The two-semester general physics course includes mechanics, heat, electromagnetism, optics and modern physics. This course places great emphasis on the introduction of fundamental concepts and principles common to both classical and quantum physics. In order to deepen the understanding of physics knowledge, this course includes many applications of physics knowledge in engineering, technology, biomedicine and everyday familiar phenomena. We encourage classroom teachers to choose teaching materials based on their own interests and student situations, and to include as much knowledge of relativity and quantum physics as possible.

Name: Basic Physics Laboratory
Introduction: "Basic Physics Experiment" is based on the experimental content of general physics and is open to sophomore undergraduates who are not majoring in physics. It is offered repeatedly in the fall and spring semesters, with 4 hours per week for a total of 16 weeks. The purpose of the course is to guide students to learn basic knowledge of physics and basic methods and experimental techniques of physics research through experimental methods, and to cultivate students' physical experimental abilities. The course includes an introductory class, three preparatory experiments, one error theory experiment and eleven basic experiments. In each experiment, teachers guide students to complete the prescribed experimental content. The teacher must comprehensively evaluate each student's preview, experiment, and experiment report for each experiment and give a grade. The grade of the course is comprehensively evaluated by the grade of each experiment.

Name: Physical Chemistry (B)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Physical chemistry is an important branch of chemistry. It is a discipline that starts from studying the interconnections between chemical phenomena and physical phenomena to explore the universal basic laws of chemical motion. _x000D_
    The main teaching purpose of the "Physical Chemistry (B)" course at the School of Chemistry at Peking University is to enable students to systematically master the basic knowledge and basic principles of physical chemistry through learning, and to deepen their understanding of the nature of natural phenomena. These knowledge and principles are not only the theoretical basis of chemistry, but also the basis for the development of other technical sciences related to chemistry. Enable students to learn the scientific thinking methods of physical chemistry, cultivate students' ability to ask questions, research problems, and analyze problems, and cultivate their ability to acquire knowledge and use it to solve practical problems. _x000D_

Name: Paleontology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: General Petrology (I)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Before choosing crystallography and optical minerals, students should choose crystallography and minerals.
Introduction: "Crystal Optics" mainly studies the basic principles and methods of identifying minerals under polarizing microscopes. "Photomineralogy" is the study of the characteristics of the crystal structure and chemical composition of rock-forming minerals based on various optical phenomena produced when visible light passes through transparent crystals. Crystal optics and optical mineralogy are not only important foundations of petrology, but are also widely used in ceramics, castings, building materials, etc. Magmatic petrology is about the classification and classification principles of magmatic rocks, the basic characteristics of various rock types (including ultrabasic rocks, basic rocks, neutral rocks, and acidic rocks), rock types, mineral combinations, structural structures, and chemical composition characteristics, as well as the petrogenesis theory of each rock type and the geotectonic environment in which it was formed. The course also introduces basic experimental petrology theory and its explanation of the origin of rocks; the relationship between magmatism and plate tectonics and mantle plume structure, the process of crust-mantle interaction, and the significance of magmatism in the formation of continental crust.

Name: Historical Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Basic courses in geology in Earth science generals, mineral science, sedimentary rock science, paleontology and tectonic geology
Introduction:
"Geohistory" is a comprehensive geological subject that requires students to learn and master the basic principles and methods of applied geology such as petrology, paleobiostratigraphy, sedimentology, and historical tectonics, and to reconstruct the history of the evolution and development of the earth through comprehensive analysis of geological records such as minerals, rocks, and biological fossils preserved in rock formations, as well as deformation. _x000D_
The main content includes the basic concepts, theoretical principles and research methods of geohistory, as well as the basic characteristics of geological development and a brief history of evolution in each geological historical stage of my country. Taking the broad outline of the earth's evolutionary history and the formation and evolution of the earth system as the main line, this article introduces the formation, development process and evolution rules of the earth's surface layers (lithosphere, biosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere). Through learning, students can understand the evolutionary history of the earth (history of biological evolution, history of sedimentary development, history of tectonic movements), the basic laws of movement, master the basic characteristics of the new earth view, basically grasp the characteristics and features of different periods of earth evolution, and major geological events that have occurred, and understand the role and significance of each major geological event in the history of earth evolution. _x000D_

Name: General Petrology (II)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The sedimentary rock part mainly introduces the basic concepts, principles and research methods related to sedimentary diagenesis, so that students can master the formation rules of sedimentary rocks and the characteristics of common sedimentary rocks through the study of this course. The metamorphic rock section mainly introduces the basic concepts, principles and research methods of metamorphism, masters common metamorphic rock types, mineral composition and structural characteristics, and understands the origin of various metamorphic rocks and their relationship with the geotectonic environment, laying the foundation for further discussion of metamorphism and crustal evolution.

Name: Structural Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General geology, rockology, solid mechanics base
Introduction: Structural geology is one of the important basic courses for earth science majors. It mainly introduces the deformation mechanism, behavior and process of rocks in the lithosphere under the action of geological stress, as well as the various geological structural phenomena formed. Based on the theory of rock deformation mechanics and deformation mechanisms, the course focuses on important structural types such as foliation, lineation, folds, fissures, joints, faults, extensional structures, thrust-nappe structures, strike-slip faults, and ductile shear zones. Based on the ideas of geometry-kinematics-formation mechanism-evolution process, the course will introduce the geometric forms and combination methods of the above-mentioned structural types, discuss their kinematic methods and kinematic discrimination, explain the physical conditions and deformation mechanism of their formation, and explore the mechanical action mode, geological environment and dynamic process of their formation. At the same time, the course will also introduce some basic methods and basic skills in structural geology research, such as geological cartography, geometric projection, quantitative and qualitative analysis of stress and strain, case geological analysis, etc. The characteristic of this course lies in the organic combination of geometry-kinematics-genetic mechanism, and focuses on the combination of foundation and frontier.

Name: Introduction to Natural Resources
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The theory of sustainable development of natural resources is taught in the form of special topics, focusing on the sustainable development of water resources, mineral resources, especially petroleum resources and low-carbon economic issues, including petroleum economics.

Name: Fundamentals of Solid Mechanics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The geological process is to a large extent a mechanical process. In recent years, more and more mechanical analysis content has been included in structural geology research. However, in the past, traditional geologists had many misunderstandings in the application of mechanical concepts. This course describes the basic concepts, principles and methods of solid mechanics required to analyze geological structural phenomena, and provides the necessary mechanical foundation for studying geomechanics, structural dynamics and other courses, especially for studying tectonic stress fields. This course also provides a preliminary introduction to solid mechanics experiments and finite element analysis methods.

Name: Regional Geology Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: (1) Introduction to Earth sciences; (2) Geological principles; (3) Minerals, Rocks (crystalmography, sedimentary geology); (4) tectonic geology (strutcural geology); (5) Quaternary geological and geomorphology.

Name: Regional Geology Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Basic courses in mineralology, rockology, tectonic geology, palaeontology, geohistorics, geomorphology and fourth-class geology; first general geological internship.
Introduction: Geology is not only a self-contained theoretical discipline, but also a highly practical discipline. Regional geological survey practice is a core link in undergraduate teaching. Through teaching activities that combine theory and practice, students can initially master the basic knowledge, basic methods and basic skills necessary for systematic field geological surveys. At the same time, they can also understand and train new ideas, new theories, new methods and new technologies in the development of modern earth science and technology to a certain extent. Mainly include: (1) Professional skills: The focus of field practical teaching is to cultivate students' observation and reading ability, practical ability, theory-to-practice ability, geological thinking ability, ability to use geological survey equipment, and strengthen training of their language-text-graphic expression ability; (2) Professional thinking: to cultivate students' pioneering, innovative and scientific abilities. Research awareness, deepen the understanding of basic geological theories learned, and lay a solid foundation for subsequent course teaching, senior professional internships and graduation thesis internships; (3) Professional quality: Field teaching internships should reflect the tradition and characteristics of the school, cultivate students' diligent and rigorous, realistic and innovative spirit, unity and cooperation, and improve students' overall quality.

Name: Fundamentals of Geophysics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Geology, if it has a general physics base, is better.
Introduction:
It mainly introduces the basic concepts, scientific principles and technical methods in various branches of geophysics, including natural seismology, exploration seismology, gravity, geomagnetism, geoelectricity, geothermal science and seismic tomography technology. It focuses on the combination of geophysical methods and geology and its application in the detection of the earth's internal structure, energy and resource exploration, as well as the main scientific results achieved in geophysics in the past 100 years. _x000D_
This course is based on the teaching reform for the 21st century, emphasizing the importance of foundation, striving to correctly introduce physical concepts and principles, focusing on the elaboration of physical content and the revelation of the essence of physics. Adopting original mainstream textbooks from the same majors in Europe and the United States, the course uses a large number of high-simulation supporting graphics, cartoons and animations to intuitively show the connection between geological units, stratigraphic sections and structural backgrounds and geophysical methods, evidence and results to students. It strives to enable students to master the basic knowledge of geophysics while also understanding the role of geophysical methods in the exploration of the earth's interior and geological research, correctly using geophysical methods and data, and laying a good foundation for further solving practical problems encountered in earth science research. _x000D_
This lesson plan takes into account the needs of undergraduate students majoring in geology and geophysics. Through the study of this course, students majoring in geology will have a comprehensive understanding of the role, basic principles and processes of geophysical technical methods in detecting and determining the deep and shallow structures of the earth. Similarly, for students majoring in geophysics, through the study of this course, they can better understand the prerequisites for the use of geophysical technical methods and their interrelationship with specific geological environments and structural backgrounds. The explanation emphasizes the connection and comparison of relevant knowledge points in geophysics and geology, avoids complicated and lengthy mathematical derivation while introducing necessary mathematical tools, and helps students establish clear physical images and systematic earth science knowledge systems. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Sedimentology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General geology, ordinary rock science, etc.
Introduction:
Introduction to sedimentology is an important theoretical basis for sedimentology. It is a basic means for restoring the paleoenvironment, studying the sequence structure of sedimentary strata, interpreting seismic facies, conducting basin analysis, and reconstructing paleogeography. It is of great significance for the general survey, exploration, and development of energy sources such as oil, natural gas, coal, and many non-metallic mineral resources. By understanding the changes in the natural environment, the human living environment can be more effectively protected and improved. The learning purpose of this course is to master the theoretical basis of sedimentary physical processes and sedimentary facies analysis, use the principles of realism to restore the ancient sedimentary environment, explore the natural conditions for the formation of sedimentary rock layers in geological periods, and reveal the evolution laws of paleogeography. _x000D_
	This course mainly introduces the physical effects, basic concepts and research methods in the formation process of sediments (rocks), common depositional environments and characteristics in ancient strata, and sedimentary basin filling sequences and methods. Specifically, it includes three parts: First, the basic principles of fluid mechanics and hydraulics for sediment transport, traction flow and sediment gravity flow, waves and wave theory, bottom shape and flow form, operating forces for sediment transport and deposition, sediment deformation and denudation structures, and the physical process of sediment formation. The second is to focus on the introduction of clastic depositional environments and facies models, including alluvial fans, rivers, aeolian environments, deltas, coasts, continental shelves, slopes and turbidite fans, etc. Bioherms and ash mounds; carbonate platform and carbonate basin sediments. The principles of sedimentary environment and facies analysis; The third is to introduce the filling and stratigraphic accumulation patterns of sedimentary basins, and use experimental stratigraphy methods to study the sediment filling process of basins.

Name: Environmental Mineralogy
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Crystallology and mineralology, rockology, mineral deposits, geochemistry and general chemistry.
Introduction: Environmental Mineralogy is an elective course for undergraduate students majoring in geology and geochemistry. The main purpose is to enable students to master the general principles and application status of environmental mineralogy, become familiar with the basic concepts, theories and research methods of mineral environmental properties, introduce the natural self-purification function of inorganic minerals to effectively control environmental pollution, understand the system and principles of natural self-purification that exist in nature jointly constructed by inorganic minerals and organic organisms, understand new methods and technologies for environmental pollution control and environmental quality restoration, and understand the characteristics of interdisciplinary research between mineralogy, environmental science, life science and other disciplines.

Name: Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course of study requires some basic knowledge of geology, inorganic chemistry, physicochemistry, mineralology and rock science.
Introduction: Geochemistry is a science that studies the chemical composition, chemical reactions and chemical evolution of the earth based on chemical science. Geochemistry has achieved rapid development in the past decade, and it has played an important role in the research of many fields such as geology (such as minerals, rocks, deposits, structures, paleontology), energy (such as oil, natural gas, etc.), human living environment, and agriculture. Geochemistry is the backbone science in earth science that studies the composition of matter. It takes elements, isotopes, their chemical effects and chemical evolution as the research objects. It is one of the basic courses of earth science majors. The purpose of the course is to organically combine the geochemical behavior of elements with geological processes based on the properties of elements and isotopes, focusing on the distribution, migration, evolution and other laws of elements and isotopes in celestial bodies, the earth and geological bodies, as well as the physical and chemical environment when they were formed. It also introduces the importance and latest research progress of geochemical processes in earth evolution, mineral resources, human living environment and national economy. The course includes geochemical analysis experimental teaching. Under the guidance of the teacher, students can do it themselves in the laboratory and strictly control the chemical process and instrument operation. The teaching focuses on the analysis of geochemical components, cultivating students' basic skills in geochemical experiments, and understanding that geochemical analysis is by no means a simple chemical analysis test. Through teaching, students can master the subject nature, basic principles and research methods of geochemistry, understand the research status and development trends of geochemistry in various fields, and initially establish geochemical thinking.

Name: General Physics (I)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: The two-semester general physics course includes mechanics, heat, electromagnetism, optics and modern physics. This course places great emphasis on the introduction of fundamental concepts and principles common to both classical and quantum physics. In order to deepen the understanding of physics knowledge, this course includes many applications of physics knowledge in engineering, technology, biomedicine and everyday familiar phenomena. We encourage classroom teachers to choose teaching materials based on their own interests and student situations, and to include as much knowledge of relativity and quantum physics as possible.

Name: Marine Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Basic courses such as Earth Science General.
Introduction:
Marine geology is a relatively new discipline. It only became independent as a branch of geology and a branch of oceanography in the 1930s and 1940s. Marine geology focuses on the current range of oceans, including coasts and beaches, continental shelves and slopes, and the vast deep ocean floor. The study of the structure and evolutionary history of the seafloor crust is the key to solving the major issue of global tectonics; the vast ocean is a natural laboratory for ongoing sedimentation. Now, the ocean has become the focus of international scientific research. All coastal countries have carried out the investigation, development and utilization of marine resources, as well as research on the marine environment. _x000D_
This teaching first establishes an overall knowledge framework of ocean interactions, including plate tectonics theory, physical ocean foundations (waves, ocean currents, tides, storms, etc.), ocean geochemistry and ocean sedimentation, and then classifies and discusses specific ocean systems such as coastal environments and continental margins. Finally, it introduces marine resources and environmental issues that are closely related to us. This course focuses on consolidating students' mastery of key knowledge through homework design, focusing on training students to complete reading reports with good paper standards, and focusing on improving students' academic presentation skills. It is suitable for students in the second grade and above. _x000D_

Name: Gemology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Candidates should have basic knowledge of crystallization and mineral science
Introduction: Through teaching, practice, and discussion on the basic concepts of jewelry and jade, main varieties and characteristics, evaluation and identification, this course enables students to master the basic theoretical knowledge of jewelry and jade, the main types and their main characteristics, processing technology, evaluation and identification methods, etc., and at the same time master the basic skills of identifying the authenticity of common gemstones. This course is mainly conducted through lectures and internships, focusing on the training of practical skills to improve students' jewelry appraisal abilities.

Name: Frontiers of Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Crystallology and Minerals, Physical Chemistry, Geochemistry
Introduction: This course is intended for senior undergraduates who are interested in geochemical science, in order to further deepen their knowledge and understanding of experimental geochemistry and isotope geochemistry, and understand the cutting-edge fields and development trends of experimental geochemistry and isotope geochemistry research.

Name: Principles and Applications of Stable Isotope Fractionation
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: Integrated Geology Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: tectonics, rockology, mineralology, Chinese geology, general geology, general geology
Introduction: "Comprehensive Geological Internship" is a field internship course, which aims to improve students' basic knowledge structure of geology, cultivate students' ability to comprehensively observe, analyze and solve geological science problems, and enhance students' scientific research capabilities and innovation consciousness. On the basis of completing the main courses in geology, students will go to areas with representative geological sections and geological phenomena in my country to conduct field geological observation, measurement, analysis and other comprehensive geological research ability training. The internship area spans the Wutai Mountains in the North China Plate and the Three Gorges in the Yangtze Plate. The content covers various geoscience fields such as structural geology, mineralogy and petrology, paleontology and geohistory, sedimentology, and disaster geology. Wutaishan Comprehensive Geological Practice Base (jointly established with the local government) and the Three Gorges Comprehensive Geological Practice Base have been established.

Name: General Physics (II)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: The two-semester general physics course includes mechanics, heat, electromagnetism, optics and modern physics. This course places great emphasis on the introduction of fundamental concepts and principles common to both classical and quantum physics. In order to deepen the understanding of physics knowledge, this course includes many applications of physics knowledge in engineering, technology, biomedicine and everyday familiar phenomena. We encourage classroom teachers to choose teaching materials based on their own interests and student situations, and to include as much knowledge of relativity and quantum physics as possible.

Name: Geotectonics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
"Geotectonics" is an important basic theoretical course for various majors in earth science. Since the creation of the plate tectonics theory, this theory has become the theoretical basis for guiding research in various branches of earth science. "It has become a central topic in the research activities of many earth scientists." Therefore, it is very necessary to teach "Tectonics" centered on the plate tectonics theory in various majors. The course mainly includes: the birth process and key events of plate tectonic theory; basic concepts and theoretical systems of continental drift, seafloor spreading and plate tectonics; orogenic belts and continental tectonics; basic characteristics of plate tectonics in China, etc. _x000D_
The main purposes of teaching "Geotectonics" are: ① Through systematic learning, students can initially establish a scientific view of the earth and understand the basic laws and history of global tectonic evolution; ② To enable students to initially master the thinking and basic methods of geotectonic research, and cultivate students' ability to discover, ask questions, analyze problems and solve problems; ③ To inspire students to initially use basic geological data and various related knowledge to discuss geotectonic issues; ④ Lay a theoretical foundation for subsequent course learning and scientific research. _x000D_
The teaching process uses multimedia as the main means, focusing on explaining through a large number of animations, pictures, and specific examples. Encourage students to actively participate in class discussions and guide students to express different views on issues of interest. _x000D_

Name: Frontier Theory and Methods in Petrology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
On the basis of the courses of mineralogy, petrology and geochemistry that have been learned, master the current theories and research methods of some frontiers of magmatic rocks and metamorphic rocks, understand the geotectonic background of rock production, and use geochemical data to establish the causal connection between petrology and geotectonic structures. In particular, learn to use computers to process, analyze and interpret rock geochemistry and mineralogy data. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course selection target: third- and fourth-year undergraduate students

Name: Crystallography and Mineralogy
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Minerals are crystalline natural compounds or simple substances formed by geological processes. They are also the smallest independent units that constitute the earth's crust or celestial bodies. The formation, existence, evolution and demise of all geological bodies or celestial bodies are closely related to minerals. Mineralogy is a science that studies the chemical composition, internal structure, appearance, origin, occurrence and relationship of minerals. Since minerals exist in crystalline form, crystallography and mineralogy complement each other and form an inseparable whole. "Crystallography and Mineralogy" is one of the most basic courses in geological science, and it is also a precursor to other geoscience courses, such as petrology, mineral deposits, geochemistry, structural geology, stratigraphic paleontology, gemology, geomorphology, etc. Some basic knowledge in this course, such as the expression and analysis of crystal structures, is also necessary basic knowledge for related disciplines such as solid-state chemistry, solid-state physics, and materials science.

Name: Badminton
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Badminton is a flexible, fast and changeable net-attacking sport. The movements are easy to master, the equipment is simple, suitable for all ages, full of fun, and deeply loved by students. Participating in badminton can develop students' agility and coordination, is conducive to the improvement and improvement of cardiopulmonary function, and can cultivate students' tenacious, calm and decisive will qualities. This course mainly teaches basic badminton serving, hitting, and moving techniques, singles and doubles tactics, and basic rules. _x000D_
Badminton is taught in the gym. From the perspective of safety and physical education requirements, students are required to wear badminton-specific sports shoes and sportswear, and bring their own rackets and badmintons. 4. Understand the basic tactics of badminton and the rules and refereeing methods of badminton. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Sequence Stratigraphy
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Sequence stratigraphy is a science that studies sedimentary system tracts within a geological time frame. Its theoretical basis is that changes in sea level are cyclical in geological history. This cyclicity results in the rhythm and predictability of sedimentary sequences. Since its formation in the 1980s, this branch of science that combines stratigraphy and sedimentology has rapidly developed into an important research hotspot in the field of basic geology. It not only has important guiding significance in energy exploration, but also attracts the attention of more and more geologists in conducting regional geological comparisons, continental margin geology, and theoretical research on stratigraphy and sedimentology. _x000D_
This course will start by introducing the classic Exxon clastic rock model, elaborate on the core theory of sequence stratigraphy, explore the relationship between sedimentary superposition and accommodating space, introduce important sequence interfaces, such as sequence interface, maximum flooding surface and other concepts, and on this basis, introduce the sedimentary system tract. During the course, relevant data from seismic, well logging, and field outcrop observations will be closely combined to cultivate students' ability to comprehensively apply geological data. In addition, this course will introduce the sequence stratigraphic framework of fluvial, neritic, deltaic, bathyal, and carbonate platform facies. Finally, this course will conduct field practice. Students will try to establish a sequence stratigraphy model through measured profiles and combined with course theory. _x000D_
This course refers to domestic and foreign undergraduate syllabuses and is taught in English. It emphasizes teaching interaction and student participation, including group classroom discussions, exercises, experiments, profile measurements and reports, aiming to improve students' ability to comprehensively utilize geological knowledge, hands-on and oral expression skills and teamwork spirit_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course provides a more comprehensive introduction to psychology, psychological methods, major fields of study such as sensory perception, learning, memory, language and thinking, consciousness, intelligence, personality, emotions, motivations, psychological disorders and treatment, social awareness, interpersonal processes, etc. This course is intended for non-psychological students and is intended to be comprehensive and non-exhaustive and to be informative. Through teaching and learning, students need to master the basic concepts and theories of psychology and the correct methodology. Another objective of the course is to foster student interest in psychology and provide a solid foundation for further learning and research into psychological theory and practical issues. The curriculum should be one of the first courses for non-psychological students to learn about psychology.

Name: Social History of Medieval Western Europe
Introduction: This course teaches the social history of Western Europe in the Middle Ages (approximately 500 AD to 1500 AD). Called social history, many issues in medieval Western European society will be introduced and analyzed in this course. Social problems can always be attributed to political problems, so the history of political formation and development in France, Britain, Germany, Italy and other countries should be elaborated; society is composed of various strata or classes, and the status of nobles, knights, priests, monks, farmers, craftsmen, etc. must be discussed; although men have always ruled the world, women cannot be forgotten, so it is obviously useful to discuss gender and society Its historical and even practical significance; the Middle Ages is an era of faith, so it is necessary to understand the Bible, Christ, Christianity, monasteries, Crusaders, heresies, witchcraft, etc.; faith does not exclude knowledge and learning, and the Middle Ages is not as dark as people imagine. Appreciating the thoughts and lives of those masters will not only enlighten our hearts. People form society, social production organizations and systems. The unique organizations and systems of Western Europe in the Middle Ages had a significant and far-reaching impact on Western European society at that time and even for hundreds of years thereafter, such as the vassal system, the knight system, the manor system, the serf system, the guild system, the parliamentary system, etc. We will briefly analyze and introduce these systems.

Name: History and Figures of Late Qing Foreign Relations
Introduction:
The study of China’s foreign relations in the late Qing Dynasty is an important window for analyzing China’s move toward the world. The term "Late Qing" contains endless academic potential because the development of contemporary China is still within the basic discourse situation defined by Sino-foreign relations in modern times: Where does traditional national culture go? Is modernity universally adaptable in China? How to break through the modern complex faced by China's development? How do contemporary Chinese people look at themselves while looking at the outside world? Faced with the discourse hegemony of Western Sinology, how can Chinese people consolidate their subjectivity in China-centered historical analysis? Is the transition from "Chinese body with Western application" to "Chinese characteristics" inevitable or a helpless choice? Many questions require us to think seriously, and the study of the history and characters of the late Qing Dynasty can help us get closer to the real answers to these questions. _x000D_
The late Qing Dynasty is an unforgettable memory in the hearts of many Chinese people, and its charm has even developed into spiritual torture for many people. However, for a long time, our memories of this period of our foreign exchanges have been confused by the transcendental illusions of the collective unconscious and restricted by some transcendental logic and concepts created for one purpose or another, making it impossible to break through this complex. The main purpose of this course is to reorganize the foreign relations of the late Qing Dynasty and clarify key issues. In the analysis of the characters, we can get closer to ourselves by getting closer to their psychology. _x000D_

Name: Anglo-American Culture in Film and Television
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: "British and American Culture in Film and Television" selects film and television as a perspective to observe and analyze British and American culture, and uses after-school movie viewing and joint appreciation and discussion in class as a teaching model. It explores British culture from five aspects: "royalty and class", "literary classics", "pastoral and gentleman", "conservatism and humor" and "love and family". It also studies American culture from six aspects: "individualism and heroism", "American dream", "campus", "politics", "melting pot" and "love and family". This course selects the most representative film and television works, and lists more works for each cultural sub-category. It aims to help students strengthen their understanding and analysis ability of British and American culture through relatively extensive exposure to and focused analysis of British and American film and television works. At the same time, they can improve their English listening skills through watching movies, and strengthen their oral English expression skills through classroom speeches and discussions.

Name: General Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: High school physics, high school chemistry (science)
Introduction: As an introductory course in chemistry, “general chemistry” mainly describes the basic concepts, principles, methods and processes of development of chemistry. The curriculum covers a wide range of basic knowledge of physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, inorganic chemistry and even organic chemistry, all of which will be taught in the future. As a result, common chemistry presents the most basic and common chemical principles around the form of the substance, its changes, its structure and the nature of the substance. The main elements are the basic laws of gases and liquids, chemical thermal and chemical balance, chemical dynamics and reaction rate equations, atomic structure and quantum chemistry base, molecular structure and theory, crystal structure, formulation compounds and elemental chemistry. Through general chemistry, students can learn not only about the basics of chemistry, but also about the history and current state of chemistry, the relationship between chemistry and society, and gradually acquire the basic methods and techniques of thinking and solving problems, developing the capacity to think and solve problems independently and laying a good foundation for future learning.

Name: General Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
General chemistry experiment is the first compulsory experimental course for chemistry and near-chemistry undergraduates. It is a course that seems simple but is actually challenging. It is not only an independent course, but also cooperates with the corresponding theoretical course "General Chemistry". It is also a bridge connecting high school and university chemistry experimental courses. _x000D_
    This course mainly focuses on qualitative experiments, with a small amount of quantitative experiments. The main purpose is to enable students to understand the importance of "conditions" and "quantity" of experiments. During the experiment, in addition to the cultivation of basic knowledge and basic experimental skills, this course also focuses on the cultivation of critical thinking. Students are allowed and encouraged to question the content and procedures of existing experiments, raise questions, and redesign experiments through discussions with teachers, teaching assistants, and classmates to solve problems. In this course, by cultivating students' abilities to observe phenomena, analyze problems, practice hands-on practice, and analyze and summarize, students will gradually learn to use basic chemical principles to solve practical problems in the experimental process. _x000D_
    General chemistry experimental classes are taught in small classes. Every 16 to 18 students conduct experiments in the same laboratory, with a teaching assistant to guide the experimental process. There are usually two lead teachers patrolling between laboratories when students are experimenting. Each experimental class includes three links: teacher's pre-class explanation, students' practical operation, and class discussion. Each class has about 30 to 40 minutes of teacher explanation time, mainly explaining the basic principles, basic operations, precautions, safety issues involved in the experiment, and problems that existed in the previous experiment. For the basic operations that appear for the first time, the teacher will explain and perform standardized demonstrations at the same time. The actual operation time for students is about 3 hours. During the experiment, there will be teaching assistants and lecturers to guide and help students. After the students' experiment, the teaching assistant organized a class discussion of about one hour for the students. The content of the discussion was mainly the discussion questions after the experiment and the problems discovered during the experiment. _x000D_
    The general chemistry experiment class includes 13 to 14 experiments. There is a mid-term operational examination and a final written examination during the teaching process. This course mainly tests students from aspects such as experimental preview, experimental process, experimental report and classroom discussion. Before the experiment, students need to complete the pre-study report and pre-study thinking questions, and after the experiment, they need to complete the experimental report and discussion questions. _x000D_
    General chemistry experiments are prerequisite courses for other experimental courses in the School of Chemistry. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Issues
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering

Environmental science is an integrated “problem-oriented” discipline that emerges as an opportunity for global and national environmental problems to develop as human societies develop. Name: General Physics
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
This course is a 64-hour classic physics course designed to meet the basic teaching needs of non-physics majors and undergraduates. It includes four parts: mechanics, heat, electromagnetism and optics. The main content of the course is to describe basic concepts and basic laws, with the main line of physics research methods for understanding typical phenomena and summarizing the laws of the material world. It aims to establish physical images and initially master physics research methods. It provides students with a certain degree of basic training in analyzing and solving problems. On this basis, students will have a certain understanding of the history and current situation of the development of physics. _x000D_
 This course is mainly based on classroom lectures, supplemented by experimental demonstrations and exercises. It not only lays a solid and reliable foundation for students' future study and work, but also cultivates students' scientific qualities while imparting physical knowledge. _x000D_

Name: Quantitative Analysis
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Analytical Chemistry I (Quantitative Chemical Analysis) is one of the main basic courses for students majoring in chemistry. Together with Analytical Chemistry II (Instrumental Analysis), it forms a complete analytical chemistry course. Its theories and methods are not only the foundation of the analytical chemistry major, but also the foundation of all other chemistry-related courses and majors. While teaching students the basic principles and methods of analytical chemistry, we also enable students to establish a strict concept of "quantity", cultivate their ability to engage in theoretical research and practical work, and develop a rigorous scientific style. _x000D_
The course is mainly targeted at first-year university students majoring in chemistry. It provides both Chinese and English teaching. Students can choose the teaching language class according to their needs and interests. The content of the course includes introduction, data statistics and analysis methods, volumetric titration methods, gravimetric analysis methods, molecular spectroscopic analysis methods (including UV-visible spectrophotometry, molecular fluorescence spectrophotometry, infrared spectroscopy, and an introduction to Raman spectroscopy), and preparation methods for analytical samples. _x000D_

Name: Quantitative Analysis Laboratory
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
This course is a basic basic course in the discipline of chemistry, and is intended for first-year (second-year) undergraduate students in Peking University’s School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, School of Environmental Science and Engineering, School of Urban and Environmental Sciences, Yuanpei College, and School of Archeology and Museology. The course content includes chemical analysis methods and techniques commonly used in analytical chemistry (volume analysis, precipitation gravimetric analysis) and potentiometric titration and visible light spectrophotometry. _x000D_
   This course requires general chemistry and general chemistry experiments as prerequisites for this course. This course has one experiment per week, 6-8 hours each time, for a total of 8 weeks; a total of 60 hours, 2 credits. _x000D_
   Students who elect this course must take the analytical chemistry theory course in the same semester. _x000D_

Name: Integrated Environmental Practicum I
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: The internships were organized in the wake of the Environment course and gave students a preliminary understanding of the concept of environmental protection for sustainable development.
Introduction:
This course is a cognitive internship, which is the first systematic and comprehensive practical link for undergraduate students majoring in environmental science and engineering. _x000D_
This internship is arranged after the "Environmental Issues" course, and students have a preliminary understanding of the concept of environmental protection for sustainable development. Through on-site visits, interviews and other links, students are guided to understand the origins of environmental problems and the measures taken to deal with them in practice, understand the mutual influence and interdependence between human activities and environmental changes, and understand the importance and necessity of sustainable development. By understanding the importance of environmental protection work, you can deepen your understanding of this major and enhance your interest in learning. _x000D_
This internship link is based on the Southeast Coast High-tech Zone, with Zhuhai as the center to establish an internship base. With environmental protection, ecological diversity protection, urban sustainable development and environmental protection as the main lines, students will be organized to conduct a comprehensive inspection of the natural ecological environment and urban environment, including rivers, lakes, reservoirs and other water body environments, from water supply to drainage. The overall process, from atmospheric environment background to urban regional air environment quality monitoring, from waste generation to storage, transportation, and disposal of the entire process supervision, from government supervision to corporate participation in environmental protection, from urban and rural construction to economic and ecological win-win, on-site understanding of the significance and value of environmental protection, environmental monitoring, pollution disposal, and urban and rural construction work. _x000D_
The content of the internship is connected by thematic lines, and the internship process is carried out through observation, explanation, interview and discussion. Based on the principle of "thinking while doing and learning", students "see" environmental problems during the inspection, "think" about the root causes and solutions to environmental problems, "learn" the professional knowledge of environmental science and engineering contained in it, and understand the importance and necessity of environmental protection and sustainable development. _x000D_

Name: Basic Physics Laboratory
Prerequisite: Higher Mathematics, PHY-0-5x or PHY-0-4x series
Introduction: "Basic Physics Experiment" is based on the experimental content of general physics and is open to sophomore undergraduates who are not majoring in physics. It is offered repeatedly in the fall and spring semesters, with 4 hours per week for a total of 16 weeks. The purpose of the course is to guide students to learn basic knowledge of physics and basic methods and experimental techniques of physics research through experimental methods, and to cultivate students' physical experimental abilities. The course includes an introductory class, three preparatory experiments, one error theory experiment and eleven basic experiments. In each experiment, teachers guide students to complete the prescribed experimental content. The teacher must comprehensively evaluate each student's preview, experiment, and experiment report for each experiment and give a grade. The grade of the course is comprehensively evaluated by the grade of each experiment.

Name: Environmental Science
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: As the backbone of the environmental science profession, the course, while presenting the underlying concepts and theories of environmental science, emphasizes the essence of environmental science, that is, from the perspective of discovery, problem solving to prediction, prevention, to prepare students to systematically master the research methods of environmental science, including the analysis and diagnosis of the problem, the intrinsic logic of cross-science, and the means of proposing solutions.

Name: Contemporary National Defense
College: Student Affairs Department, People's Armed Forces Department
Introduction:
The "Contemporary National Defense" course is a comprehensive course that systematically introduces my country's contemporary national defense construction thoughts, military development strategies, military high technologies, the development of the world's new military revolution, and recent hot issues in local wars. Topic 15: Modern Joint Operations

Name: Jurisprudence
Introduction:
This course is a required professional course for undergraduates at Peking University Law School. This course focuses on the issues of the rule of law and the construction of order. It discusses the pluralist legal concept, the construction of sovereignty and global order, the problems that lawyers must face in modern society, and the spiritual foundation of a country ruled by law. It trains legal people's legal thinking methods, as well as their thinking and judgment on modern political and legal issues, and on this basis reflects on modern rule of law issues. _x000D_
The course adopts a teaching method of large class lectures and small class discussions, which mainly consists of pre-class reading, book report writing, classroom lectures, and after-class discussions. It has formed a relatively complete jurisprudence course teaching system, allowing students to improve their literature reading ability, writing ability and expression ability, master the ability of legal reasoning, and have the ability to think deeply about social and political issues during the course learning process. _x000D_
Course grades consist of daily assignments, group discussions and final closed-book exams. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Culture
Prerequisite: University undergraduate degree, or equivalent to university undergraduate degree.
Introduction:
"Chinese Cultural History" - the first batch of general elective courses included in the quality education of Peking University. _x000D_
     This course is a basic course that comprehensively and systematically reflects Chinese traditional culture. She reveals the background, characteristics and significance of traditional culture, vertically reproduces the splendid cultural trajectory of China for thousands of years, and spans basic knowledge at a general level in many fields of humanities, social sciences, and natural sciences. _x000D_
     This course covers a wide range of topics, with many knowledge points and high gold content. Applicable to students majoring in arts, science, and language. By studying this course, you can gain a more comprehensive and systematic appreciation of the profoundness of Chinese traditional culture, broaden your knowledge horizons, improve your personal knowledge structure, and provide the necessary cultural accomplishment and basic knowledge for further development in specific fields in the future. _x000D_
In order to cooperate with the teaching activities of Chinese cultural history, the teachers of this course set up a project at Peking University and developed the CAI courseware "Chinese Cultural History", which directly serves teaching practice. This courseware plays an important role in teaching interaction and further improving the learning environment through pictures, readings, music, knowledge unit retrieval, and links to relevant academic lectures. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Monitoring
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The course addresses the monitoring of major pollutants in environmental media and environmental pollution, teaching basic principles and analytical techniques for the various components of environmental monitoring, quality assurance in environmental monitoring and recent advances in environmental monitoring techniques. These include guidelines, water body pollution monitoring, atmospheric environmental monitoring, soil and solid waste monitoring, noise and radioactive pollution monitoring, emergency monitoring, and quality assurance and quality control for environmental monitoring. This course highlights the characteristics of environmental monitoring (sampling, placement, testing methods, data processing and quality assurance, etc.), focuses on basic theoretical learning and scientific practice, closely aligning the monitoring needs of our environmental pollution with the use of new instruments, methods and technologies in conventional and modern monitoring methods. The course seeks to provide students with an understanding of the underlying theory of environmental science involved in environmental monitoring, an understanding of trends in environmental change and methods of monitoring and evaluation of environmental quality, a capacity for routine environmental monitoring and data analysis, and an exploratory approach to environmental monitoring and research.

Name: Environmental Monitoring Laboratory
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite:
Environmental monitoring
Environmental chemistry
Analytic chemistry
Introduction: This course aims at the monitoring needs of environmental media and major pollutants in environmental pollution problems, and provides sampling and analysis technology training in all aspects of environmental monitoring. In conjunction with the environmental monitoring theory course, this course provides training in analytical techniques for monitoring pollutants in the atmosphere, indoor air, water, soil, and sediment, covering the entire process of experimental design, sampling, sample processing, instrument operation, data collection and analysis, and experimental quality assurance. Fully relying on the monitoring and analysis capabilities of the Experimental Teaching Center of the School of Environmental Science and Engineering, the State Key Laboratory of Environmental Simulation and Pollution Control, and the Urban Atmosphere Positioning Observation Station, we provide independent operation training for advanced monitoring and analysis instruments, such as automatic atmospheric monitors, ion chromatography, GC-MS, and instruments independently developed by Peking University. Through the study of this course, students will be familiar with and master the operation and use of conventional instruments and equipment in the field of environmental monitoring, the methods of collecting and pre-processing samples of atmosphere, water, sediment, soil, etc., the instrument analysis methods and data processing methods of important chemical components such as heavy metals, organic matter, ions, etc., and cultivate the basic quality and ability of students to participate in scientific research work.

Name: Environmental Engineering II
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
"Environmental Engineering (2)" is a required course for undergraduate majors in the first-level disciplines of environmental science and engineering. It is also a science platform course for the whole school. In undergraduate professional teaching, it plays an important role in transforming theoretical knowledge into engineering applications. The specific content of "Environmental Engineering (2)" is water quality purification and water pollution control engineering. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course was designed with full consideration of the knowledge needs of science students, and selected basic concepts, water quality management indicators and standards, process principles, and technology development trends in the field of water environment engineering to form the main content, along with the practical application of processes and technologies and the introduction of current research hotspots. The teaching method is mainly classroom lectures, supplemented by course website interaction, homework assignments, recommended reading materials and bibliographies, etc. The assessment method is closed-book examination. _x000D_
_x000D_
By mastering the basic theoretical knowledge of the subject, students who choose the course can establish the knowledge framework, way of thinking and independent vision of engineering; students who are interested in learning can further start exploratory thinking on new theories and discoveries, popular processes and technologies, water treatment problems, etc., which will be beneficial to their future professional choice and development. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Engineering I
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: Inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, environmental microbiology, (chemical principles, chemical mapping, mechanical mapping)
Introduction: This course system describes the basic theory, pollution prevention techniques and control engineering in the field of current environmental engineering disciplines, and trends. The basic theory and methodology of pollution control engineering techniques are taught to students.

Name: Integrated Environmental Practicum II
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
This course is positioned as field environmental monitoring operation practice, cultivating students' ideas and methods for researching environmental chemistry issues, understanding and mastering the monitoring, analysis methods and data analysis methods of the generation and change process of environmental pollution, deepening their understanding of environmental scientific research and environmental protection, and improving students' ability to analyze and solve problems. _x000D_
This course is designed to cover the practical content of two major sections: atmospheric chemistry and climate monitoring and interactive monitoring of water and soil environment. It covers the research on the changes of environmental parameters such as atmosphere, water, soil and biological environment. It involves the principles and methods of regional background atmospheric environment quality research, instrument operation, data analysis, the research principles and methods of vegetation ecology and natural source VOCs emissions, instrument operation, data analysis, the detection principles and methods of lake water quality parameters, instrument operation, data analysis, the detection principles and methods of soil environment parameters, instrument operation, data analysis, and the study of lake ecological change mechanism and process. _x000D_
This course is centered on the Saihanba Environmental and Ecological Practice Base of Peking University and carries out extensive environmental research, monitoring, and sampling activities in surrounding lakes, woodlands, grasslands, etc. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, we strive to cultivate students' environmental protection concepts of sustainable development, strengthen the field operation ability training of environmental parameter monitoring technology, cultivate scientific research capabilities, enhance and deepen their interest in environmental science and engineering subjects, cultivate students' ability to connect theory with practice, guide students to correct research ideas, and learn the ability to write normative internship reports. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Research Methods
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Environmental problems are the mirror image of economic and social development. Solving environmental problems requires an in-depth scientific understanding of the problem and an understanding of the social and economic reasons behind it. The research methods course is designed to fully consider the characteristics of environmental issues and systematically introduce scientific thinking in environmental research. From a methodological perspective, it mainly focuses on logical reasoning methods, research design methods, data collection, analysis and display methods. From a disciplinary perspective, this article systematically introduces commonly used basic model research. In the process of narrating, some basic research methods in environmental science, anthropology, sociology and economics are used as examples to conduct an in-depth analysis of various methods. The course aims to cultivate students' ability to engage in actual environmental research and gain training in logical thinking, research design, and data analysis and presentation abilities; have a preliminary understanding of basic research methods in the environmental field; and through practical teaching, learn to apply these methods in practical problems to understand and solve environmental problems. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Microbiology
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
Environmental Microbiology_x000D_
_x000D_

Teaching purpose:_x000D_

_x000D_
