Name: Environmental Microbiology Laboratory
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: "Environmental Microbiology Experiment" is an experimental course for environmental microbiology that is highly practical and applicable. The teaching target is undergraduate students in the first semester of their junior year. It is planned to have 6 hours per week and a total of 96 hours. The course content mainly covers aseptic operation methods in microbiology laboratories, observation methods of microbial characteristics, isolation and purification methods of environmental microorganisms, basic methods of microbial metabolism and biochemical analysis, environmental microbial diversity analysis methods, and nucleic acid molecular probe technology. The teaching goal is to improve students' ability to analyze and solve problems. According to the characteristics of this subject, they will know how to study microorganisms in the environment and analyze and solve problems that arise during the research. Through the study of this course, we strive to enable students to master the basic operational skills of environmental microbiology research and lay a good foundation for their ability to work independently and do scientific research in related fields in the future.

Name: Engineering Drawing
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Engineering Cartography is a basic course in engineering technology for the study of theory and methodology for projecting and solving space geometry problems using projectivity. Engineering maps are an important technical resource in engineering technology and an indispensable tool for technology exchange. The main elements include painting geometry, mapping base, mechanical mapping and computer mapping. In addition to technical students, the course is also compulsory for students in the environmental and physical fields.

Name: Water Treatment Engineering (Part 1)
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: Environmental monitoring, physical chemistry, chemical principles, inorganic chemistry (or common chemistry)
Introduction: This course is one of the main professional courses in the environmental engineering major. This course aims at water quality purification and focuses on treatment methods. It mainly teaches the basic principles and characteristics of water and wastewater physical and chemical treatment technology units, the basic calculation methods and application scope of the process, the composition and operating characteristics of the main components, typical water and wastewater treatment processes, and the latest domestic and foreign research progress in related technologies, including: coagulation, sedimentation and clarification, air flotation, filtration, disinfection, redox, membrane separation, softening and desalination, etc. Through the study of this course, students will deepen their understanding of the theory of physical and chemical treatment of water and wastewater, and improve their ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Soil and Groundwater
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: On the basis of introducing the basic characteristics, distribution rules and groundwater movement of soil and groundwater, it explains the sources of soil and rainwater pollution, main pollutants and pollution pathways; and then introduces the migration and transformation rules of pollutants in soil and groundwater, basic methods of soil and groundwater pollution investigation and monitoring, and evaluation and prediction of pollution conditions. On this basis, we focus on introducing the control and remediation measures of soil and groundwater pollution.

Name: Appreciation of Classical Kunqu Opera
Introduction: How to appreciate the Quinquoise art, focusing on its cultural significance in the twenty-first century. And the modern legacy of Quincy.

Name: Environmental Chemistry
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
With China's economic and social development, attention to environmental issues is increasing day by day. The discipline of environmental chemistry continues to develop in the process of solving environmental problems and gradually grows up among many basic chemistry disciplines. The independence of the discipline is further enhanced. At the same time, the theoretical and technological development of related disciplines also provides strong support for the system improvement of the environmental chemistry discipline. Environmental chemistry is no longer an extension of simple chemical analysis, but is closely integrated with the discussion of scientific issues such as ecological impacts, health hazards, climate change, and environmental chemical mechanisms. Environmental chemistry has become a booming and comprehensive subject. _x000D_
Environmental chemistry is an emerging research field. In the process of solving many environmental problems, profound scientific principles are hidden. Further exploration is underway. Environmental chemistry will be a booming scientific and technological field. This course hopes to provide some basic knowledge preparation for students who care about environmental issues and are interested in participating in environmental chemistry exploration, and serve as a small gateway into the vast space of environmental chemistry. _x000D_
This course focuses on elaborating the migration, transformation and effects of chemical substances in various environmental media such as atmosphere, water, soil, and organisms. It comprehensively and in-depth discusses the mechanisms and laws of these processes. It also focuses on reflecting the latest research results and progress in the fields of environmental chemistry and engineering, and provides guidance for students majoring in environmental science to initially get involved in the field of environmental chemistry. The course is narrated according to circles and topics, covering atmospheric environmental chemistry, water environmental chemistry, soil environmental chemistry, biological environmental chemistry, industrial ecology, element cycles in each circle, and the behavior and effects of typical chemical pollutants in various environmental media. _x000D_
Course teaching is arranged in 16 teaching weeks, totaling 48 credit hours. The specific arrangement is 2 credit hours for course introduction and introduction, 14 credit hours for atmospheric environmental chemistry, 2 credit hours for microenvironmental air pollution, 10 credit hours for water environmental chemistry, 6 credit hours for soil environmental chemistry, and 6-8 credit hours for other environmental chemistry topics, with time reserved for special discussions. _x000D_
Multimedia teaching is used, mainly classroom lectures, supplemented by special discussions. Class lectures account for approximately 80%, and topic discussions account for 20%. _x000D_
The performance evaluation of the course consists of three parts: Final examination: closed book, all teaching content, especially the highlighted content. Discussion class: Each topic section provides reflection questions, which you can review by yourself. In the discussion class, you randomly select topics to speak, and answer questions from classmates and teachers. All students (50%) and teachers (50%) will score jointly. Quiz: A sample test of the aforementioned course content. _x000D_
The specific methods of performance evaluation include: discussion of environmental chemistry issues, 5 minutes/person, open book, accounting for 30%; in-class quizzes, 10 minutes/time, 4-5 times, closed book or open book, accounting for 20%; final exam, 2 class hours, closed book, accounting for 50%. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Indoor Air Pollution
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: The course is open to undergraduate and graduate students.
Introduction:
With the formation of megacities, air pollution has become an important environmental problem worldwide, such as the frequent occurrence of haze in recent years. Research by the World Health Organization indicates that an average of 7 million people die each year from air pollution. Through infiltration, atmospheric pollution also affects indoor air to a large extent. In addition to being affected by atmospheric pollution, indoor air pollutants have special sources of pollution, such as chemical and biological pollution. On average, humans spend more than 90 per cent of their time in the room each day, and indoor air quality is very important for physical and mental health.

The course provides lectures on, and analyses of, the main indoor pollutants, including chemical, biological types, sources and methods of detection, as well as updates on recent national and international scientific developments. In addition, the course examines the health effects of indoor pollutants, including possible diseases, pathogenicity and protective measures. In addition to lectures on chemical pollutants such as VOC, PAH, one of the main points of this course is the description of biological components in air such as bacteria, viruses, fungi and allergies, and their health effects include infections, allergies, and associated baseline values and testing methods. The course also includes learning about relevant instruments for biological testing and some public health knowledge.

Through this course, students can have a more systematic knowledge and understanding of indoor air pollution, including sources of pollution, detection methods, health hazards, and can learn about related instruments. This course covers a wide range of fields, including highly cross-cutting science and technology such as biology, chemistry, physics, mechanics, medicine, etc., and can lay the groundwork for students to adapt to the cross-cutting needs of different disciplines. The theoretical knowledge acquired can help to capture national demand and research hot spots, both in future choices for research related to air pollution and in future business work.

Name: Water Treatment Engineering (Part 2)
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: On the basis of analyzing the sources, characteristics, and physical and chemical properties of wastewater, the basic principles and application cases of wastewater treatment technology are introduced. Guide students to get in touch with cutting-edge scientific issues and technology research and development hotspots in wastewater. The guiding ideology of this course is to use basic principles as guidance, combine theory with practice, and have engineering applications as the background, focusing on cultivating students' ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Environmental Engineering Laboratory (I)
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: "Environmental Engineering Experiment (1)" is a practical course and a required course for undergraduates majoring in environmental engineering. In "Environmental Engineering Experiment (1)", a representative water treatment unit or process is selected for simulation experiment. Students are required to complete the water treatment unit or process simulation operation and experimental data analysis and discussion on the basis of understanding the purpose and basic principles of the experiment.

Name: Control of Physical Pollution
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: "Physical Pollution Control" is the main professional course for junior undergraduate students in the School of Environmental Science and Engineering. This course focuses on the impact of noise, vibration, electromagnetic radiation, light, heat and other physical elements of pollution that are closely related to human production and life on human beings, as well as treatment and prevention technical measures; it introduces the latest scientific research trends in the utilization of physical pollution, which has certain theoretical value and strong practicality. Through the study of this course, students will have a systematic understanding of the above contents, achieve a comprehensive understanding and mastery of the generation, control and treatment technology of environmental physical pollution, and lay a foundation for engaging in environmental engineering scientific research. Guide students to get in touch with cutting-edge scientific issues and technology research and development hotspots of physical pollution. The guiding ideology of this course is to use basic principles as guidance, combine theory with practice, and have engineering applications as the background, focusing on cultivating students' ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Environmental Quality Assessment
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The teaching content includes the basic theory of environmental quality assessment, the origin and development of the environmental impact assessment system, system construction, government regulations and implementation procedures, etc., technical methods and case analysis of environmental impact prediction and assessment of various environmental factors such as water environment, atmospheric environment, acoustic environment and ecology. Through this course, students can master the basic theories of environmental assessment and relevant government regulations, become familiar with the content and methods of impact prediction and assessment of various industrial factors, and understand the cutting-edge developments in this field such as strategic environmental assessment and planning environmental impact assessment.

Name: Fundamentals of Environmental Engineering Design
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the basic knowledge and basic procedures of environmental engineering design, including engineering project operation procedures, principles of engineering project site selection, process flow selection and design, reactor design calculations, pipeline layout design, selection and application of environmental protection equipment, engineering design technical and economic analysis, etc. Taking environmental engineering project design and construction procedures as the main line, combined with case simulation training, it focuses on cultivating and improving students' comprehensive application ability of knowledge.

Name: Fundamentals of Solid Waste Disposal and Resource Recovery
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Based on the analysis of the sources, characteristics, and physical and chemical properties of solid waste, this article introduces the entire process management system of solid waste as well as the basic principles of landfill, composting, incineration, and major resource utilization technologies, and briefly introduces the main cases of solid waste treatment and disposal.

Name: Practical English Lexicology
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
The teaching purpose is firstly based on the introduction of the history of English vocabulary development, including Latin and Greek roots. The historical study of vocabulary development and the memory of root words will help students learn to master the language. Secondly, the purpose of teaching is to understand the morphological structure of English vocabulary and master the rules of word formation, which will help expand vocabulary. The third teaching purpose is based on the concept that vocabulary is a network system. The course always runs through and embodies the important ideological viewpoints of contemporary linguistics, allowing students to feel the positive influence of linguistic methodology in the process of learning English vocabulary knowledge. These thoughts and viewpoints are systematic thoughts and relational thoughts, such as diachronic, synchronic and panchronic thoughts, binary opposition thoughts, vertical and horizontal relationships, relational thoughts (relationships between vocabulary and semantics), deep surface thoughts, etc. The understanding of these ideas and relationships is to master the meaning of words in reading and to use vocabulary more accurately. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Atmospheric Aerosol Measurement Techniques and Laboratory
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite:
Common chemistry
Analytic chemistry
Environmental monitoring
Environmental science
Introduction: This course aims at the technical needs of atmospheric aerosol measurement and analysis, and provides training on the principles and main techniques of atmospheric aerosol measurement in current research. This course teaches the principles of offline and online measurement instruments for atmospheric aerosols, and combines theory with practice. Through theoretical study and experimental operations, students can gain an in-depth understanding of the current methods and progress of aerosol measurement at home and abroad. It also fully relies on the support of the monitoring and analysis capabilities of the Experimental Teaching Center of the School of Environmental Science and Engineering, the National Key Laboratory of Environmental Simulation and Pollution Control, and the Urban Atmosphere Positioning Observation Station to provide advanced monitoring and analysis instruments, such as atmospheric particle film samplers, ion chromatography, GC-MS, and Peking University's independently developed instruments. Through the study of this course, students will be familiar with and master the principles and operating methods of the main instruments and equipment for measuring the physical and chemical properties of atmospheric aerosols, and cultivate students' basic qualities and abilities to participate in scientific research work.

Name: Fundamentals of Environmental Remote Sensing
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Teaching basic knowledge of the physical, technical and mathematical foundations of remote sensing technology; teaching of the environmental foundations of remote sensing technology applications through theoretical and practical teaching, characteristics, uses of common remote sensing data, radiation correction of remote sensing images, geometric correction and mosaicing, integration of remote sensing data from different sources, thematic classification of remote sensing images and cartographic output, etc.

Name: Case Studies in Environmental Decision Making
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: Environmental issues, environmental science, environmental engineering, environmental management
Introduction: The environmental decision-making case analysis course is the last required course in the undergraduate teaching system of the college, guiding students to use previously learned theoretical knowledge such as environmental science, environmental management and environmental engineering to integrate and solve environmental problems. It is characterized by openness, integration and practicality. Its goal is to integrate the dispersed knowledge that students have learned at the university level into a unified whole, and provide students with experience and practical participation opportunities before entering high-level research studies or work.

Name: Environmental Engineering Laboratory (II)
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: (ii) The environmental engineering experiment (ii) focuses on the technical principles of artificial wetlands, bio-facilators, heterogenesis rehabilitation and the methods of operation of their installations; experiments on the treatment process of artificial wetlands and bio-facility; experiments on the technical principles of solid waste disposal, disposal and resourceization and on the methods of operation of their installations; experiments on the technical principles of safe drinking water and the methods of operation of their installations; and experiments on the technical methods of securing the pre-treatment of drinking water. Experiment I: Experiments on sewage manual wetland treatment, understanding the technical principles of manual sewage treatment at the horizontal, vertical or tidal currents, mastering the operating methods of experimental sewage treatment devices for artificial wetlands, testing the water purification effects of different functional areas of artificial wetlands, examining the evolution of COD, ammonia, TN and total phosphorus under different conditions of operation of artificial wetlands and evaluating the effectiveness of sewage treatment in artificial wetlands. Experiment II: Experiments in the treatment of sewage biofiltration tanks, understanding of the technical principles for the treatment of sewage from biological quick-filtration tanks, mastering of the operation of experimental devices for the treatment of sewage from biological fast-filtration tanks, testing of water purification effects in different functional areas of biological fast-filtration tanks, examination of trends in the evolution of COD, ammonia, TN and total phosphorus under different operating conditions of artificial wetlands, and evaluation of the effectiveness of sewage treatment from biological fast-filtries. Experiment III: Experiments for the rehabilitation of contaminated soil by heterogeneity, understanding of the technical principles of heterogeneity, mastering of the operating methods of the experiment, testing of the effects of the remediation of contaminated soil by heterogeneity, and examining the evolution of contaminants following the process under different operating conditions. Experiment IV: Solid waste disposal and disposal experiments, understanding of the technical principles of solid waste disposal and disposal, mastering of the operating methods of solid waste disposal and disposal experimental devices, testing of the parameters of solid waste disposal processes and examination of the effectiveness of solid waste disposal under different operating conditions. Experiment V: Experiments on the resourceization of solid waste, understanding the technical principles of resourceization of solid waste, mastering the operating methods of solid waste resourceization experimental devices, testing the parameters of solid resourceization processes and examining the performance of solid waste resourceization products under different operating conditions. Experiment VI: Experiment in Physico-Chemical Pre-treatment of Drinking Water, understanding the technical principles of Physico-Chemical Pre-treatment of Drinking Water, mastering the operating methods of Physico-Chemical Pre-treatment Devices of Drinking Water, testing the parameters of Physico-Chemical Pre-treatment Processes of Drinking Water, and examining the effectiveness of pre-treatment under different operating conditions. Experiment VII: Experiments on biopre-treatment of contaminated water sources, understanding of the technical principles of biopre-treatment of drinking water sources, mastering of the operating methods of experimental devices for biopre-treatment of drinking water sources, testing of the parameters of biopre-treatment processes of drinking water sources, examination of the effectiveness of pre-treatment under different operating conditions.

Name: Environmental Engineering Cost Estimation
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: General overview of advanced mathematics, environmental engineering
Introduction: Technical and economic analysis and budget estimation during the entire process of environmental engineering project construction are important means and inevitable choices for rationally raising, saving and controlling project investment, and improving project investment efficiency. They are also essential knowledge for environmental engineering technicians and managers. This course combines the knowledge of engineering budget estimates with environmental engineering bill of quantities, and systematically teaches the basic knowledge, basic principles and methods of environmental engineering budget estimates and economic analysis. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Management
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Environmental management is the most important foundation and core course of environmental and social science in the field of environmental and social sciences in the undergraduate field of environmental science, through the teaching of basic theoretical and applied knowledge of public management and public policy and environmental management; technical support and assurance systems and technical approaches to environmental management; institutional arrangements and policy instruments for environmental management; specific management theories and practices for various elements, enterprises/industry, regional and global environmental management; basic theories and basic methods of public management; a framework for environmental management research and key theories and methodologies for understanding the state of environmental management and the main theories and methods of progress; familiarity with and mastery of common environmental management tools and methods; and improved capacity to apply the relevant knowledge acquired to analyse and address practical environmental problems.

Name: History of Modern Sino-Japanese Relations
Introduction:
This course intends to systematically describe the history of state-to-state relations between China and Japan in modern times (1840-2015); it is divided into three periods: the late Qing government, the Republic of China government, and the Republic of China government, and will be discussed separately. _x000D_
This course will focus on the period of the Kuomintang government and the Republic of China government, the Chinese government's relations with Japan as the focus, and the political and diplomatic history as the main content, as well as other topics. _x000D_
The teaching method of this course is mainly classroom lectures, supplemented by readings, seminars, lectures, visits, etc. _x000D_

Name: Social Psychology
Introduction: Social psychology includes how individuals interact with individuals and groups, and how groups interact with each other. This interaction is a two-way, complex mutual influence. Social psychology systematically applies basic psychological principles to human behavior. This course will cover important theories and concepts in mainstream social psychology, including: how individuals view themselves and others, how they view and think about social phenomena, the formation of attitudes and their impact on behavior, how attitudes change, why individuals are affected by others, and the behavioral performance and characteristics of people in group situations, etc. In addition, this course will analyze the application of social psychology knowledge in social life, including the formation and maintenance of interpersonal relationships, principles of interpersonal communication and conflict resolution, smooth teamwork, and effective negotiation, etc. Moreover, this course will also introduce the current international cutting-edge psychological research progress, such as research and exploration on happiness. The biggest feature of this course will be the organizational and cultural perspectives as the core, expounding the application of social psychology theory in organizations, and paying attention to the in-depth research of contemporary scholars on human psychology and behavior under different cultural backgrounds.

Name: Market Research
Introduction:
The collection of timely, accurate and useful information for marketing decision-making is an important task for marketing managers in the face of changing markets and intense competitive environments. Market research is an important basic subject in the marketing profession and a general compulsory subject in the marketing profession at the National and International Management Colleges.
The course systematically introduces and discusses the entire process of marketing research and its associated theories and methods, taking into account the progress of domestic and foreign market research and the real problems faced by domestic enterprises, and builds the practical capacity of students to identify, analyse and solve marketing problems.

Name: Science and Technology in World Civilizations
Introduction:
This course focuses on the transformation of the World Centre for Science and Technology Activities, highlighting the history of ancient Greece.
The emergence and decline of centres of scientific and technological activity in the history of the world, and to the extent possible, the processes that led to them Medium
Social causes of rise or decline. To inform students about the main processes of development of the world ' s science and technology civilization,
and the impact of the development of science and technology on the rise of large nations, as a means of broadening students' awareness and raising their awareness
Their comprehensive cultural literacy.

Name: Management Science
Introduction:
In the process of enterprise operation and development, data, models and decision-making play a vital role. The teaching purposes of this course are to: (1) enable students to master the basic principles and methods of management science related to data, models and decision-making; (2) cultivate the thinking ability of scientific management, (3) be proficient in using computers to manage data and solve models, and (4) have the ability to solve decision-making problems that are often faced in business management. _x000D_
The main contents include:_x000D_
Part One: Management Methods of Data Information_x000D_
Data information and enterprise operations, database systems, computer language OOP models, data mining platform construction_x000D_
Part 2 Planning Theory_x000D_
Linear Programming: The focus of this section. Graphical method, simplex method, modeling, and computer problem solving. Dual planning: the focus of this section. The concept of dual programming, shadow prices. Integer Programming: Learn to model and use computers to solve problems. Introduction to nonlinear programming. Classroom explanation and discussion, case analysis and computer internship_x000D_
Part 3: Graph and Network Analysis_x000D_
Introduction to minimum spanning tree, shortest path, maximum flow, minimum cost maximum flow, traveling salesman problem and Chinese postman problem. Establish the corresponding linear programming model and solve it using a computer. Classroom explanation and discussion, case analysis and computer internship_x000D_
Part 4: Decision Theory_x000D_
Decision rules, risk decision-making, decision trees, utility functions and decision-making. Case analysis and computer solution. _x000D_

Name: American Short Stories and Film
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
"American Short Stories and Films" is a special college English course for non-English major undergraduate students. Current language teaching requires multimedia to be both a teaching method and teaching content. This course combines two texts, short stories and films, to teach English through the dual art forms of literature and multimedia. The course selects classic short stories in the history of American literature and their adapted movies. Each short story is 10-20 pages long, and each movie is 30-50 minutes long. It is more suitable for modern multimedia classroom teaching. _x000D_
The teaching of this course includes literary background knowledge, introduction to writers' works, analysis and criticism of short stories, after-class discussion and Q&A, film adaptation and appreciation, etc. With the help of modern multimedia teaching methods, this course is committed to improving students' comprehensive level of English listening, speaking, reading and writing, and enhancing their cultural awareness, literary accomplishment and dual text reading and writing abilities in the information age, so as to achieve the ultimate goal of our English teaching.

Name: Management
Introduction:
Management is the basic human capacity. Management is a basic course for the management profession, for the non-management profession
This is an extended course. The curriculum is based on managers, moving from self-management of people to management of others, from
The experience goes up to the rule of law and goes back from the rule of law to a purposeful simulation of the environment and in real conditions.
To examine practical issues. By reading classics and simulations,
Understand the cycle of management, manage the mechanisms of management, and in turn train students in management structure competencies and analysis of problem solving
Capacity to provide the necessary management for follow-up management studies, or for undertaking management practices or post-graduation employment
Pre-eminence of concepts, rules, mechanisms, capacities, etc.

Name: Chinese Society and Business Culture
Introduction: This course examines the fundamental characteristics of Chinese society and their impact on business culture. The course first analyses the structural differences and their social, economic and cultural manifestations in Western and Central China from the perspective of cross-cultural comparisons and then explores the Chinese business culture that is currently being developed, such as retail and consumer behaviour, employment relations and regulation, commercial negotiation and cooperation. The course highlighted three aspects: first, contemporary Chinese social phenomena; second, observation based on real society; and third, comparison with Western society and culture.

Name: Safety Education and Self-Defense
Introduction:
With the development of society, the progress of the times, the rapid growth of GDP, the take-off of the economy, the rapid development of the knowledge economy and information society, and the diversified international situation, while people enjoy the conveniences and civilizational achievements of modern society, they also have to be affected by various non-traditional safety factors. Frequent traffic accidents, stampedes, and violent crimes emerge in endlessly. Research data proves that crime rate and GDP growth are directly proportional. Strengthening safety education, establishing safety awareness, and cultivating college students' adaptability and self-rescue ability in emergencies are not only related to college students' personal and property safety, physical and mental health, and career planning, but also an important way and means for our country to improve national quality and moral quality of citizens. It is related to the implementation of the strategy of strengthening the country through talents, the establishment of a harmonious society, and the realization of the "Chinese Dream." _x000D_
The Indian poet Rabindranath Tagore once said: "The purpose of education should be to convey the breath of life to people." The "education" of education should start with respect for life, respect for people, and reverence for the universe. The most basic principle is to respect the existence of life and understand the non-repeatability of life. When facing these factors that threaten life safety, how to save ourselves and how to save others are the most direct and important issues we can think of. Therefore, establishing a strong awareness of life safety and mastering correct self-defense methods should become the basic qualities we must possess to respect our own lives. The temptations faced by college students are increasing day by day, and there are more and more dangerous factors around them. However, due to the lack of social experience and common sense in life, they often appear at a loss when facing danger, causing heavy losses to themselves. ? _x000D_
? In the teaching process of safety education and self-defense, a combination of theory and practice will be used to analyze various cases to improve students' prevention abilities, problem-solving abilities, alertness and psychological preparation for fighting. In actual combat teaching, decomposed movements and combined attacks will be combined to improve students' fighting skills and fighting abilities. _x000D_
The combat content of the safety education and self-defense class is a practical combination of boxing, martial arts, Sanda, wrestling, judo, taekwondo, karate, grappling and fighting. Through one semester of study, students can initially master self-defense fighting techniques, tactics, skills and strategies in practice, and improve their self-confidence and fighting experience during practice. While improving the comprehensive ability of self-defense, improve physical fitness. _x000D_
Through the study of safety education and self-defense courses, students can theoretically improve their safety and self-defense awareness, prevention capabilities and on-the-spot response capabilities, understand various safety knowledge, and be mentally prepared. After studying this course, students will be able to apply the strategies, tactics and techniques they have learned in their life, study and work to protect the safety of life, property and family. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Financial Risk and Management
Introduction: The purpose of the course is to build the capacity of students to assess and manage risks. Financial risk will be the focus of the course. Comprehensive enterprise risk management will be a cross-cutting theme of the course. At the end of the course, students will have a visual understanding of how to assess and manage the overall risks of financial institutions. The course begins with an introduction to the reasons why risk management contributes to the value of the enterprise and then proposes an overall framework for using risk management to improve the value of the enterprise. Based on this framework, the course will describe how to assess and manage market risk, cash flow risk, interest rate risk, credit risk and business risk. After students become familiar with the risks, the course will turn to the assessment and management of overall corporate risks. Evaluation of performance and corporate decision-making using an enterprise-wide risk management approach is the subject of this process. Finally, the course discusses current matters related to risk management.

Name: Identification and Analysis of Entrepreneurial Opportunities
Introduction:
This course is offered for MBA students who want to start a business, or participate in entrepreneurial enterprises, or want to engage in entrepreneurial management activities. Its goals are: to help students initially master the basic principles of identifying and analyzing entrepreneurial opportunities through topic lectures; to improve students' ability to identify and analyze entrepreneurial opportunities through case analysis and guest comments; to expand students' horizons through lectures and exchanges with entrepreneurial entrepreneurs and venture capitalists, and help students build more entrepreneurial networks. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is positioned at the front end of the entrepreneurship series: identification and analysis of entrepreneurial opportunities. The entrepreneurial process is a process of discovering and creating opportunities + realizing them. Successful entrepreneurs are those who can effectively discover and create opportunities, and turn entrepreneurial opportunities into valuable products and services. Many people contribute their talents to companies and organizations founded by others. However, there are also more and more people who are creative and are not satisfied with the status quo. They rely on their own technology and innovation to establish new companies and organizations, which not only achieve completely different pursuits in life, but also benefit society. This course is about how to discover and create opportunities, as well as realize opportunities and start new enterprises. _x000D_
_x000D_
The learning objectives of this course are: fully understand the complexity, uncertainty and creativity of the entrepreneurial process and master the analysis methods of entrepreneurial opportunities. At the same time, prepare for the follow-up content of the entrepreneurship series, including courses on business plans and entrepreneurial enterprise growth. _x000D_

Name: Business War Simulation
Introduction: "Business War Simulation" is a course that uses management knowledge to learn to run a business and solve various management problems in a simulated market environment. Under the guidance of teachers, students form the top management team of a virtual enterprise. In the market environment simulated by computer software, they face the ever-changing competitive situation and evaluate the performance of the enterprise through multi-period business decisions. The purpose is to allow students to learn knowledge, apply knowledge, and grow their talents in simulated business management practices.

Name: Financial Economics
Introduction: The financial economics course is aimed at the training objectives of financial economics majors and provides a more in-depth introduction to investors' optimal savings and asset portfolio decisions, asset pricing models (CAPM, APT, AD no arbitrage, AD equilibrium, martingale pricing, macro finance), behavioral finance, etc.

Name: Socialist Political Economy
Introduction: This course, which is based on the pattern of the socialist market economy, focuses on the five main aspects of the functioning of the national economy, the economic activities of enterprises, individual economic behaviour, macroeconomic and microeconomic coordination, social norms and individual behaviour. The relationship between the various variables in the socialist economy was first explained at the decision-making level of the national economy, the enterprise and the individual, and the role of market mechanisms and government regulation in macroeconomic and microeconomic coordination, the analysis of the relationship between the national interest, the collective interest and the individual interest, and finally the position of the human being in the socialist society from the point of view of the socialist economic and social development goals.

Name: Social Impact Marketing
Introduction: This course is designed to help students understand how marketing can help businesses, governments and the third sector to increase social influence. In the course, students will gain insight into social enterprises (and type B enterprises) as well as social entrepreneurship, consumer psychology and decision-making mechanisms, and social marketing to promote public policy formulation and impact. Students will focus on how new forms of enterprise (social and type B) can achieve the creation of shared values (the organic combination of economic objectives and social values). While learning about it, students will choose a practical business project to explore and practice their own solutions.

Name: The Middle East: Politics, Society and Culture
Introduction:

_x000D_
By focusing on the politics and society of the Middle East, we explore the history and culture of the Middle East and look forward to the development and future of the Middle East. _x000D_

Through a series of simple exercises, the course will provide students with a clear and effective way of expressing their language and performing it on stage. The focus is on how to use Shakespeare's brilliant and challenging language on stage, thereby giving students a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding of Shakespeare's drama. The course included two Shakespeare plays, King Lear and Storm, as well as some other play clips.

Name: Principles of Economics
Introduction: An overview of economic principles, including macroeconomics and microeconomics. Consumption theory, firm theory, general equilibrium, monopolistic competition, industry, inflation, economic growth, government role, monetary policy, fiscal policy, etc. Understand and master the most basic concepts of modern economics, understand the basic structure and analytical logic of this discipline, and be able to use economic principles to observe, analyze and explain relatively simple and typical economic phenomena and problems in real life.

It also appropriately introduces new developments in recent years, laying the foundation for in-depth study of physical theories and related mathematical methods.

Name: Introduction to Sociology
Introduction: Through the study of this course, students can master the basic concepts and theories of sociology, and understand the perspectives and methods of sociology in viewing and analyzing problems; enable students to understand the main issues of sociological research in my country and the cutting-edge issues of sociology, enhance students' professional identity; and enhance students' sense of social responsibility.

Teach French pronunciation, common vocabulary, and spend one year teaching basic French grammar to help students master basic sentence patterns and common expressions, while focusing on cultivating students' ability to learn independently.

Introduction: This course mainly provides students who are not majoring in German with the opportunity to learn and be exposed to German. Through the study of the first and second semesters, students will basically reach the level of German General (non-major) Level 4. At the same time, the basic situation of German society, culture and history is properly taken into account in the course arrangement, so that students can have a basic understanding of the national conditions of German-speaking countries while learning the language.

Name: Mechanical Drawing
Introduction:
"Mechanical Drawing" is a basic engineering course that uses the projection method to study the drawing of "engineering drawings". It mainly includes four parts: drawing geometry, drawing basics, mechanical drawing and computer drawing. _x000D_

It is an indispensable and important technical data in the engineering and technical circles for technical exchanges and equipment maintenance and transformation. "Mechanical Drawing" is one of the required courses for all majors in engineering colleges and related majors in science colleges.

Introduction: This course is taught by foreign teachers and aims to improve students' oral English application ability in real life through various activities such as classroom discussions, group activities, and oral communication. This course not only creates a good oral communication environment for students, but also enriches students' cultural experience, allowing students to fully exercise their English conversation and communicative skills in various scenarios.

Name: Health Physics
Introduction:
The content of this course consists of ten chapters. Health physics is an interdisciplinary subject involving nuclear physics, radiation dosimetry, radiobiology, radiation toxicology, radiation hygiene and other disciplines. It is also a highly applied subject. _x000D_
The course is conducted using multimedia teaching methods. According to the characteristics of this course, which has strong practical application significance, it strives to integrate theory with practice, vividly teach the specific application of health physics theory in different practices through specific scenarios and examples, and introduce the latest cutting-edge actual situations in various countries. We strive to enable students to correctly understand the biological effects of ionizing radiation, understand the national regulatory system and laws and regulations while learning professional knowledge about radioactive protection, and not be afraid of or despise the hazards of ionizing radiation, so as to lay a good foundation for the application of radioisotopes and nuclear technology in future study and scientific research. _x000D_

Name: Frontiers of Astrophysics
Prerequisite: Introduction to Astrophysics; overview of cosmology. It's better to have sex.
Introduction: This course invites domestic first-class astrophysicists to introduce students to the main research topics and latest research progress in the frontier research field of astrophysics. The purpose is to guide students to understand basic knowledge and cutting-edge topics in related fields, so that students can have a clearer understanding of the main research fields of astrophysics, build up interest in research, and at the same time increase communication between scholars and students and eliminate students' sense of mystery about astrophysics research.

Name: Electrodynamics (A)
Introduction:
Electrodynamics is an important basic theoretical course for all physics majors. The course systematically explains the basic laws of electromagnetic motion, the basic properties of electromagnetic fields and their interaction with charged matter. The course also includes an introduction to the special theory of relativity. The main contents include: the momentum and energy of the electromagnetic field; the motion law of the electromagnetic field is described by Maxwell's equation and the Lorentz force formula; the application of the separation variable method, the electrostatic image method and the Green's function method in electrostatics and magnetostatics is introduced; the introduction of gauge transformation and gauge invariance in the electromagnetic field The concept of relativity clarifies the physical meaning of deferred solutions, discusses the propagation and radiation of electromagnetic waves, discusses the interaction between moving charged particles and electromagnetic fields, and explains the historical background and practical basis of the special theory of relativity, the basic theory of relativity, the Lorentz transformation, and the space-time theory of relativity. The propagation, dispersion and dissipation of electromagnetic fields in media are discussed. _x000D_
_x000D_
Main teaching reference books: Guo Shuohong's "Electrodynamics" People's Education Press 1979; Yu Yunqiang's "A Concise Tutorial on Electrodynamics", Jackson's "Classic Electrodynamics".

Name: Quantum Mechanics (B)
Introduction:
This course is non-relativistic quantum mechanics, which introduces the laws of motion of microscopic particles. The content includes the basic concepts of quantum mechanics, namely wave function and state superposition principle, Schrödinger equation, operator representation of mechanical quantities, uncertainty relation and spin. The course also introduces some methods for dealing with typical problems, including non-degenerate stationary perturbation theory, calculus of variations, quantum transitions, etc. Through this course, electrostatics, magnetostatics, time-varying electromagnetic fields, propagation of electromagnetic fields, special relativity, electromagnetic radiation from moving charged bodies (including radiation from harmonic currents, electromagnetic fields from moving point charges), and the interaction between electromagnetic fields and charged particles. _x000D_
      This book includes seven chapters: introduction, wave function and Schrödinger's equation, mechanical quantities in quantum mechanics, representation theory of states and mechanical quantities, perturbation theory, scattering, spin and identical particles. When elaborating on the basis of representation theory, the book introduces the modern Dirac symbol, which is commonly used in modern times, and also introduces the possession number representation through the example of linear resonators.

Name: College Student Mental Health
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: The content of this course includes the following aspects: the standards for mental health of college students, ways to maintain mental health, how to adapt to the new environment, how to establish coordinated interpersonal relationships, how to deal with academic difficulties, how to make career planning, how to regulate emotions, how to deal with stress, how to correctly handle love and psychological problems, how to improve oneself and realize one's own ideals and goals in life, as well as the relevant concepts of psychological disorders and ways to seek help.

Name: Chinese Rhetoric
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Modern Chinese, ancient Chinese, Chinese ancient literature, Chinese contemporary literature
Introduction: It is taught to undergraduate students in the Chinese Department, hoping to improve students' practical ability in language use and appreciation of language arts in literary works. Teach basic methods of analyzing Chinese rhetorical phenomena and several theoretical issues in studying Chinese rhetoric. The content includes: rhetorical activities and the nature and tasks of rhetoric (2 credit hours), contradictions in language communication and principles of rhetoric (2 credit hours), research objects and research methods of rhetoric (2 credit hours), rhetoric and synonymous expression means (4 credit hours), rhetoric and meaning (2 credit hours), rhetoric and voice (2 credit hours), rhetoric and the structure of discourse (2 credit hours) 2 credit hours), balance of discourse expression forms (4 credit hours), changes in discourse expression (2 credit hours), focus of discourse expression (2 credit hours), connections in discourse expression (2 credit hours), rhetoric and stylistic style (2 credit hours), rhetoric and expression style (2 credit hours), and the role of rhetorical knowledge in literary creation and appreciation (2 credit hours).

Name: Modern Chinese Literature (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly studies and teaches the emergence, development and evolution of new literature in the historical stage from around the May Fourth Movement to the founding of the Republic in 1949. It examines the historical content of "literary modernization" that is compatible with China's social changes, including the transformation and transformation of traditional literature by new literature, the special role it plays in promoting "human modernization", and the changes in language forms and aesthetic concepts. The focus is on the analysis and evaluation of major literary historical phenomena and representative writers' works, as well as the combing of the formation of modern literary traditions.

Through the teaching of teachers, the course combines language structure, functionality and culture with oral expression training using audio recording, video, classroom sessions and discussions. Through the course, the following objectives have been achieved: a high degree of speech and communication in Chinese, a sound tone, a normal speed of speech, a clear, accurate and appropriate expression, a written language, and the ability to express one ' s views and opinions on general social topics.

Name: Ancient Chinese History (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is the first part of the basic course of "Ancient Chinese History" for undergraduate students in the Department of History. It mainly teaches the history from the Pre-Qin Dynasty to the Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties. The content is divided into four parts: Pre-Qin part, Qin and Han part, Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties part, and institutional history part. The purpose of teaching is to enable students to understand the basic historical facts, main clues and major issues of this period of history through systematic study, and to understand the general situation of politics, economy, system, culture, nation, etc.; to learn the basic methods of historical research in this period, to understand important academic works, researchers and the latest academic trends, and to cultivate professional awareness. This lays the foundation for further study of the second half of ancient Chinese history, as well as various chronological and specialized history courses, and for writing historical papers.

Name: Lectures on the Pre-Qin Philosophers
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly studies Confucius and "The Analects", "Mencius" and "Xunzi" of Confucianism, "Laozi" and "Zhuangzi" of Taoism, "Mozi" of Mohism, and "Han Feizi" of Legalism, etc., and guides students to reflect on their thoughts, art and modern value.

Name: Introduction to Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This is a general elective course for students from various departments who love literature and want to know more about literature. The course will be discussed in connection with excellent literary works from both ancient and modern times at home and abroad. The discussion will involve basic issues such as literature and people, literature and beauty, literature and language, literature and society, the composition of literary works, and analysis of literary reading. It strives to guide course candidates to shorten the distance from literature from both perceptual and rational levels, thereby improving their own literary literacy. The course will be a combination of lecture and discussion.

Name: Modern Chinese (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course learns the introductory knowledge of modern Chinese phonetics, vocabulary, and philology to lay the foundation for subsequent courses. The "Modern Chinese" course is a basic course in Chinese language and philology and is divided into two parts: upper and lower. The teaching content of "Modern Chinese (Part 1)" includes four parts: introduction, pronunciation, text and vocabulary.

Through this course, the following objectives are achieved: to have a high degree of speech and communication in Chinese, to use appropriate and rich language, to use complex phrases, to have a full language, to have a good basis in Chinese for the different topics of social life, to express their views and opinions correctly, in an appropriate manner, and in good manner.

Name: Selected Readings in Classical Chinese
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The "Selected Readings of Ancient Chinese" course is a preliminary course for overseas undergraduates in the Chinese Department to learn ancient Chinese. Its purpose is to allow international students to develop a certain ability to read ancient books by studying a certain number of ancient classic works, and to lay a foundation for the study of ancient Chinese courses in the future.

Name: Ancient Chinese History (Part 2)
Introduction: Through relatively systematic teaching, this course will help students grasp the basic clues of changes and major issues in ancient China from the Sui Dynasty to the Opium War of more than 1,200 years, as well as the necessary historical knowledge in politics, economy, institutions, culture, ethnicity, etc. during this period; help students learn the basic methods of Chinese historical research, understand important academic works, researchers, and the latest academic trends; cultivate professional awareness, and lay a foundation for further study of various chronological history and specialized history courses, and entry into research and practice in this subject area. Through various interactive forms such as lectures, homework and discussions, students' humanistic spirit and innovative ability are comprehensively cultivated.

Name: Studies in Chinese Mythology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The 10 chapters of this course, which are devoted to the subject of “Generalism”, “The Myths of Monuments”, “The Myths of Women”, “The Myths of Volodymies”, “The Myths of the Yellow Emperor”, “The Myths of the Great Flood”, “The Myths of Great Flood”, “The Myths of the Greatness”, etc., provide an overview of the basics of the ancient myths of China and give students a more comprehensive understanding of the ancient myths. On this basis, each chapter provides a detailed description and analysis of the origin of each myth and the mutation of each myth, and describes, as far as possible, the context of each myth, thus deepening students' understanding and understanding of the ancient myths.

Among them, the teaching content of "Modern Chinese (Part 2)" is mainly the grammar part. This course systematically teaches the basic knowledge of modern Chinese grammar, including grammatical units, grammatical classification of words, analytic hierarchy process, syntactic structure, sentence ambiguity and detection methods of common language disorders.

Name: Classical Chinese (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for all majors in the Chinese Department (including Chinese students and international students); it is an elective course for students in other departments. This course is a basic course and a tool course in language. The basic purpose of teaching is to cultivate and improve students' ability to read ancient documents through the study of ancient languages, lay the necessary foundation for further study and research of ancient Chinese language, literature, history, philosophy and other aspects of knowledge, and to better inherit the excellent culture of the motherland.

Name: Ancient Chinese Literature (I)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is one of the main basic courses "History of Ancient Chinese Literature" in the Chinese Department. It first introduces the subject nature of literary history and the basic characteristics and learning objectives of Chinese literary history, and outlines the general trend of literary development from Pre-Qin to Han Dynasty. Then the following content will be introduced in sequence: myths and ancient ballads, "The Book of Songs", prose by various scholars in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, historical biography prose, Chu Ci, Ci and Fu of the Han Dynasty, prose of the Han Dynasty, Yuefu poetry of the Han Dynasty and literati poetry of the late Han Dynasty.

Name: Reading and Writing (Intermediate, Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Improved reading and writing skills for undergraduate students.

Name: Selected Readings in Twentieth-Century Chinese Women's Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: The history of modern Chinese literature, the history of contemporary Chinese literature.
Introduction: This course selects representative works of Chinese women's literature in the 20th century as the object of analysis. It attempts to analyze the complex connotations of these novels within the overall pattern of Chinese literary and cultural history in the 20th century, and at the same time roughly outlines the historical development of modern Chinese women's literature/culture. The course is organized in the form of a special topic and is divided into 12 lectures. Each lecture analyzes a representative work (or uses 2-3 related works to discuss an important issue), and analyzes the literary historical positioning, narrative form, gender consciousness, and femin(ism) cultural connotations of these works that have had historical impact.

College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a deepening of the vocabulary part of the "Modern Chinese" course. The teaching purpose is to enable students to have a better understanding of the appearance of modern vocabulary and its research status, to teach students the ideas and methods for thinking and analyzing modern Chinese vocabulary issues, and to cultivate students' certain analytical abilities.

College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

The focus is on the analysis and evaluation of major literary historical phenomena and representative writers' works, as well as the combing of the formation of modern literary traditions.

Name: Chinese Folk Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Undergraduate studies. The course begins with a systematic introduction of the basic theory of folklore, which will be analysed in detail in terms of its characteristics, functions, classification and relationship to author literature. On this basis, the main forms of folklore are presented on a case-by-case basis, with China ' s most representative work as an example of a general course and a choice of work. Considering that the performance of rap literature and folk plays is too strong and varied, it is difficult to achieve better results in classroom teaching, so it is not intended to introduce more than one video, with a focus on the two categories of folk songs and folk stories, along with more multimedia presentations.

Introduction: Wei Jinh-DPo was the conscious age of our literary spirit and the age when our ancient literature began to be dominated by humanities. The period of literary development has been characterized by a clear stage, often divided into subjects such as Jai An literature, original literature, Xinjin literature, Dongjin literature, Liu Song literature and Qi Liang Chen literature, North Korean literature and Qianxi literature.

Name: Human Geography of China
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course "Chinese Human Geography" aims to explore the distribution, change and diffusion of various human phenomena in China as well as the spatial differentiation laws of human activities from a regional perspective. Through the study of this course, international students can more systematically understand and master the natural foundation of China's human geography, population, folk customs, ethnicity, religion, language, cultural geography knowledge and Chinese cultural heritage protection, and have a further macro understanding of Chinese culture and Chinese social development.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Grammar

Introduction: Based on the first-year "Modern Chinese" course, this course focuses on teaching some important results of modern Chinese grammar research by topic, and requires students to do certain exercises, so that students can specifically understand some of the current results in modern Chinese grammar research. More importantly, students can learn and master the methods of researching modern Chinese grammar, especially syntactic analysis methods, and improve students' ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Topics in Taiwanese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects representative novelists from different periods of Taiwanese literature as research objects, from the Japanese writers Lu Heruo and Long Yingzong during the colonial period; the post-war novelist Zheng Qingwen, to the new generation writers Huang Fan, Zhang Dachun, and female writers Li Ang, Zhu Tianwen, etc., and explains their writing characteristics and influence on the history of novels. It also focuses on the combination of text analysis and cultural interpretation to highlight the spiritual temperament and artistic characteristics of Taiwanese novels.

Name: Close Reading of Film
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course plans to use 10-12 famous films from around the world in recent years as examples to teach the basic characteristics of film art. The course intends to introduce the audio-visual language and narrative methods of film, and also discuss the composition of film representation and film culture. The course will discuss the industrial and commercial character of film and the many influences that the transnational cultural industrial system has had on film. On this basis, the course will further discuss the many social issues presented by movies, especially how movies, an art that is always connected with different countries, different national cultures, and has a global nature, present the drastic changes in today's world and try to respond, criticize, and construct them.

Name: Ancient Chinese Literature (III)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The development achievements of literature in the Song Dynasty are multifaceted. Song poetry created a new generation of poetry after Tang poetry. The style of poetry developed to its peak in the Song Dynasty, becoming the most important contribution of Song Dynasty literature to the history of literature. In addition, classical Chinese novels, story-telling novels, and operas also developed greatly in the Song Dynasty. From a time perspective, this section is divided into two parts: Northern Song Dynasty literature and Southern Song Dynasty literature.

Name: Foundations of Ancient Chinese Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The courses are intended to be presented in a face-to-face manner on topics that best reflect China ' s ancient cultural and radiant instruments; through specific cultural phenomena such as age celebrations, marriage and marriage, eating structure, indoor gardening, dress and clothing, the unique culture of China ' s ancient culture will help students to learn about and grasp the core content and spirit of Chinese ancient culture, become familiar with cultural commons and deepen their understanding of Chinese ancient society.

Name: Probability and Statistics (B)
Introduction: Probability theory and mathematical statistics are a branch of mathematics that studies the regularity of a large number of random phenomena in nature, human society and technological processes. Probability theory abstracts random phenomena into random variables to study its general regularity. Mathematical statistics starts from collecting, sorting and analyzing random data in practical problems to make inferences, predictions and decisions about problems. To a large extent, probability theory is the basis of mathematical statistics. Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory and has greatly promoted the research of probability theory. With the rapid development of modern science and technology, this discipline has developed vigorously and has more and more applications in many fields such as natural sciences, economics, humanities, management, engineering technology, etc. Especially in modern economics, probability statistics is an important research tool. Probability theory and mathematical statistics is an important basic course. This course focuses on introducing its basic concepts, theories and methods and providing necessary basic training.

Name: Saussurean Linguistic Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course focuses on the theoretical principles of Sogor ' s language and the important findings of experts studying Sogor at home and abroad, on the basis of a well-known book called Sogor ' s General Language Curriculum.

Name: Japanese Sinology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the background, formation process and various schools of the discipline "Japanese China Studies" that was formed at the end of the 19th century, and its impact on Japanese academic circles, Chinese academic circles and international Chinese academic circles.

Name: The Art of the Novel
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The long-term neglect of attention and research on the art of novels has made China's novel creations seriously inadequate in terms of artistry. This course aims to change this reading and research pattern and lead the listeners back to texts, literature, and the art of novels.

Name: The Languages of the World
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course aims to guide students to gain a comprehensive and multifaceted understanding of the world's languages. Students will understand the "family history" (genealogy) of the world's languages, their geographical distribution, and their respective phonetic and grammatical characteristics. In addition to covering the development history of language itself (including several theoretical hypotheses about the origin of language), the course also introduces cases in which language plays an important role in human history. Many of the world's languages ​​are very ancient and have a long history of evolution, but there are also emerging languages, and even languages ​​deliberately created by humans. These will be systematically introduced in this course. In addition, some questions that people often have in the application of language in daily life will also be discussed.

Name: Works of Contemporary Chinese Literature (Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: China's ancient literature, Chinese history of modern literature, art theory
Introduction: A relatively systematic introduction to the development process of Chinese literature, works of important writers and literary phenomena since 1949, with the purpose of enhancing students' knowledge of literary history and guiding them to have an in-depth understanding of important literary works and literary phenomena.

Name: Taekwondo
Introduction: Taekwondo is a confrontational sport that uses fists and kicks to fight. It mainly uses kicks, fists and feet are used together. Breaking is used as a means to test one's skills. It emphasizes momentum, uses voice to display power, begins and ends with rituals, uses strength to control strength, and goes straight. It is deeply loved by young people and is known as "the world's number one combat sport". Participating in this sport enables practitioners to enhance their physical fitness, master techniques and tactics, and cultivate perseverance and perseverance. This course mainly teaches the basic theoretical knowledge, techniques, tactics, skills and competition rules of Taekwondo, and introduces the latest developments and trends in the international and domestic development of Taekwondo.

Name: Introduction to New Structural Economics
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic principles and applications of new structural economics systematically. The teaching content of the basic principles of new structural economics includes: principles of structural change, principles of structural transformation, and principles of the role of government in structural change. The teaching contents of the applied part of new structural economics include: industrial structure, financial structure, human capital structure, regional structure, open structure, cyclical structure, institutional structure, environmental structure and other structural analysis in the economic development process.

Name: Topics in China's Reform
Introduction: Based on many years of first-hand investigation and research on China's reform experience, we systematically review China's reform experience in agriculture, enterprises, markets, regulation, and urban-rural relations, explore the tasks of comprehensive reform China faces, and attempt to provide theoretical explanations.

Name: Intermediate Microeconomics
Introduction: This course teaches at an intermediate level basic knowledge about economic decision-making by micro-agents and the role of markets in resource allocation. This course first discusses the decision-making issues of consumers and manufacturers under perfectly competitive market conditions. Then the general equilibrium theory and the welfare economics significance of competitive equilibrium are introduced. Finally, we turn to discuss several situations in which market mechanisms cannot lead to effective resource allocation, namely: imperfectly competitive market structures, the existence of externalities, the supply of public goods, and information asymmetry in economic transactions. This course is an important required course for economics majors. _x000D_

Name: Late Qing Literature and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course will give an overview of various literary phenomena and trends of thought in the late Qing Dynasty from the perspective of cultural history. According to the broader scope of "literature", it will revisit the changes in printing, publishing, reading, and writing culture during this period, and present the inner texture of the development of various types of literature such as poetry, essays, novels, and images. At the same time, the course will try to explore the interactive relationship between "literacy culture" represented by literature and modern China's political and educational system, social structure, cultural space and other external environments. _x000D_
The "Late Qing Dynasty" covered in this course refers to the fifty years from 1860 to 1911, that is, from the "Tongzhi Zhongsheng" to the New Culture Movement, when the traditional Chinese political and religious system was impacted by external forces and began to undergo a difficult transformation into a modern nation. Liang Qichao once called it the "transitional era". However, the significance of "late Qing literature" goes beyond serving as a transition from ancient literature to modern literature. The literature and culture of this period was not only an era when Chinese classical poetry, novels, drama, stylistics, and poetry criticism traditions were integrated, but also a period when these literary traditions accepted external influences, stimulated inner vitality, and triggered self-reflection. It was also a period when literary concepts, literary disciplines, and literary education were established in the modern sense. From the perspective of cultural history, late Qing literature is neither the bleak end of classical literature nor the early sprout of modern literature. The literature of the late Qing Dynasty had its own character, and it gave birth to a multi-style pattern of both elegance and vulgarity. The coexistence of various reading and writing experiences in ancient and modern times, China and the West, makes it a special era in the history of Chinese literature. _x000D_
The subjects of this course include Zeng Guofan, Liang Qichao, Zhang Taiyan, Liu Shipei and other figures who have had a significant impact on the experience of "literary" speech and writing, as well as important stylistic schools in literary history such as Tongcheng-Xiangxiang School, Tongguang Style, and New Wen Style. In addition, with the establishment of publishing networks, newspaper media, urban spaces and new educational spaces, literary phenomena such as vernacular genres, translated literature, image texts, and travel texts are also within the scope of investigation. _x000D_

Name: Works of Contemporary Chinese Literature (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: A relatively systematic introduction to the development process of Chinese literature, works of important writers and literary phenomena since 1949, with the purpose of enhancing students' knowledge of literary history and guiding them to have an in-depth understanding of important literary works and literary phenomena.

Name: Intermediate Macroeconomics
Introduction: Emphasis is placed on mastering contemporary macroeconomic analysis tools. Discuss issues related to China's macroeconomic policies and current situation.
