Including the determination of national income, output, employment and price levels, it also discusses economic models such as neoclassical, Keynesian, and monetarist, and requires a basic knowledge of calculus. The topics discussed will mainly include: economic growth, business fluctuations, inflation, and the interaction between the real and monetary aspects, etc. _x000D_

Name: Econometrics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic theories and methods of econometrics and aims to cultivate the ability to use corresponding theories and methods in empirical research. Students are required to not only master the relevant theories of econometrics, but also be able to use econometric software to carry out empirical analysis of actual economic problems by the end of the course.

Name: Financial Econometrics
Prerequisite: Economics principles, intermediate microeconomics, middle macroeconomics, econometrics
Introduction: Research on finance naturally has a strong empirical component. In order to rigorously answer interesting financial questions and validate financial theories and models, we need rigorous statistical/econometric analysis methods. Financial econometrics is the study of financial issues through model-based statistical inference. In this course, we will introduce econometric tools for conducting financial data analysis and testing market models. We will review some financial theories, focus on empirical analysis tools commonly used in finance, and analyze actual financial data. We will select some topics from asset return predictability, market microstructure, event analysis, capital asset pricing model, factor model, consumption-based asset pricing model, volatility, term structure of bond returns, high-frequency data and other topics for focused discussion.

Name: Ten Taiwanese Novelists
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects ten representative novelists from different periods of Taiwanese literature as research objects, from the Japanese writers Lu Heruo and Long Yingzong during the colonial period; to the post-war novelist Zheng Qingwen, to the new generation writers Huang Fan, Zhang Dachun, and female writers Li Ang and Zhu Tianwen. Each of them explains their writing characteristics and influence on the history of novels. It also focuses on the combination of text analysis and cultural interpretation to highlight the spiritual temperament and artistic characteristics of Taiwanese novels.

Name: Chinese Calligraphy
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Further improvement of the lingua franca for students

Name: Appreciation of Western Music
Introduction:
Although this course is titled "Western Music Appreciation", it is actually a series of courses that work together and are accumulated over a long period of time. There are five predecessors: first, in 2009, the summer school course, "Western Music Appreciation"; second, in 2010, the whole school's public elective course, "Music and Culture Series Special Topic Research·Interdisciplinary Study of Chinese and Western Music"; third, in 2011, the whole school's public elective course, "Music and Culture Series Special Topic" Fourth, in 2012, the school-wide elective course, "Music and Culture Series - Hearing Sharpening and Music Appreciation"; fifth, in 2013, the school-wide elective course, "Music and Culture Series - Western Music Appreciation: Before the 20th Century". _x000D_
_x000D_
The above-mentioned courses always focus on the basics, emphasize methods, adjust content for students, accumulate experience, and explore depth. In 2014, the course entered its final period. In 2015, after extensive exchanges and mutual verification with famous scholars and colleagues in the field of "Music Listening and Music Appreciation" at many comprehensive universities in Europe and the United States, in 2016, "Western Music Appreciation" was opened again. In 2017, he was invited by China Higher Education Press to write teaching materials. _x000D_
_x000D_
After the above five stages of exploration, horizontal expansion, integration, slimming, and finalization, and nearly ten rounds of teaching and exploration, the current appearance of "Western Music Appreciation" has five new aspects: _x000D_
_x000D_
First, it focuses on the overall weakness of pre-college music education that is common among Chinese college students, emphasizing listening methods, cultivating appreciation abilities, correcting the source, and checking for omissions; _x000D_
_x000D_
Secondly, focusing on the first-level knowledge that has been agreed upon by Western academic circles, removing too much personalization in the past, allowing Chinese students to synchronize with Western students in the basic knowledge of this course within a limited time, improving their artistic general level, laying a solid foundation and avoiding detours; _x000D_
_x000D_
Thirdly, focusing on the summary of the experience and lessons of the history and current situation of similar courses in China, inheriting Mr. Zhu Guangqian’s academic tradition of “mutual support between China and the West” of Peking University, highlighting the penetration and intersection of multiple disciplines, so that students can develop their aesthetic experience, aesthetic thinking and integration of aesthetic life while acquiring cutting-edge information in related fields; _x000D_
_x000D_
Fourth, focus on the intensive listening and interpretation of core works, educate through entertainment, have a clear system, highlight the key points, learn from the essence and use it broadly, explain the profound things in simple terms, take "how to listen to songs - how to listen to music" as the two major technical fulcrums, and "vocal tone - instrumental tone" as the two major pillars of knowledge. According to the changes in the style of the times, students are guided to master listening and appreciation tips, and are stratified according to knowledge classification to cultivate students' ability to use relevant terminology and literature; _x000D_
_x000D_
Fifth, we focus on modernity, rely on tradition, face the West, and base ourselves on China. We use MOOCs, multimedia classes, and lectures and concerts to give the course current significance, so that students can understand themselves, China, the West, and the world more comprehensively on the premise of combining rationality and sensibility, advancing listening and appreciating, and integrating aesthetics and creation.

Name: Topics in the Chinese Economy
Introduction: The course, which will focus on “Institutional change-driven economic development”, will introduce and analyse topics related to the Chinese economy, focusing in particular on its achievements and challenges since the reform and opening up of the economy. This course requires students who have chosen to have a contours of the Chinese economy and, on that basis, a deeper understanding and understanding of certain aspects of the Chinese economy. The teacher wishes to present his vision of the economic phenomenon in China to his classmates for their information, discussion and criticism, as well as to present their own observations and views, and to work together to enhance interest and analytical capacity in China ' s economic problems.

Name: Financial Accounting
Introduction: Accounting information is the basis for corporate decision-making, so accounting courses have always been core basic courses in business schools. For students majoring in economics, they can better understand enterprises and deepen their understanding of microeconomic foundations through the study of accounting. Financial accounting is a basic course for accounting majors. It mainly teaches the accounting processing of the main economic business of the enterprise and the preparation of financial statements.

Name: International Trade
Introduction: The course presents the micro-section of international economics, international merchandise trade and factor flows. The main elements include the causes of international trade and factor flows and their impact on national production, consumption and social welfare; trade patterns under different conditions; international trade policy and industrial policy analysis; and major practical issues in the international economy.

Name: Taiwanese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: As this course is a popular one, no advance courses are offered.
Introduction:
This course takes Taiwanese literature and culture since the 20th century as its basic content, and also analyzes current social and historical issues in Taiwan. The outstanding achievements of Taiwan's new literature constitute a unique part of Chinese literature. Due to colonial rule and cross-strait division, Taiwanese society and literature have developed characteristics that are both connected with and different from the mainland. The understanding of this particularity directly affects the understanding of Taiwanese culture and society, as well as cross-strait exchanges and communication. This course will explain the many phenomena and characteristics of Taiwanese literature and culture, starting from the interpretation of historical documents, social phenomena and literary texts, combined with cultural studies theory and text analysis, so that students can deepen their knowledge and understanding of Taiwanese literature and culture, broaden their horizons, understand the impact of different regions and different social situations on cultural phenomena and literature, and gain a more comprehensive understanding of Chinese literature and cultural diversity. The course is not only the analysis of literary phenomena and the teaching of literary knowledge, but also a way to understand Taiwan through literature. _x000D_
      The course content includes the interpretation and analysis of Taiwanese culture and Taiwanese literature. Taking Taiwan's new literature in the 20th century as the focus of investigation, and taking Taiwan's social culture as the basic analysis background, it focuses on exploring: Taiwan's unique historical destiny and realistic situation and the resulting special style of literature; the cultural character, writer's identity and literary imagination of Taiwanese society during the colonial period; Taiwan's literary writing, literary trends and literary production in the post-colonial period, and specifically examines the rise and significance of Taiwan's modern poetry. , important poetry schools and poets, and the significance of Taiwanese modern poetry in the development of new poetry; the group of writers and representative writers of "Modern Literature" and "Literary Quarterly" that influenced Taiwanese literature from the 1950s to the 1970s; the trends and prospects of Taiwanese literature since the end of the 20th century; the production and dissemination of Taiwanese literature; the particularity of Taiwanese literature in Chinese literature, the relationship between cross-strait literature; analysis of classic writers' works and literary hot spots, etc.

Name: Topics in Ancient Chinese Poetic Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course has chosen the most national features of China's ancient poetry theory, such as “binging”, “words and meanings”, “twilight and vision”, “mixing”, “hotness” and “ideology”, to explore in depth their historical aspects, to reveal their underlying theoretical values and to reflect on their possibilities of extending to modern times.

Name: Classics of Ancient Chinese Literature (I)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course focuses on the classic works of various genres of literature from the Pre-Qin Dynasty to the Tang Dynasty, and combines the appreciation of the works with an appropriate introduction to the historical development, stylistic knowledge and appreciation methods of ancient literature, highlighting the objective existence and positive role of literary heritage in the construction of contemporary spiritual culture.

Name: Studies in the Novel since the 1990s
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects Chen Zhongshi's "White Deer Plain", Jia Pingwa's "Abandoned Capital", Mo Yan's "Big Breasts and Wide Hips", Yan Lianke's "Shouhuo", Liu Zhenyun's "One Sentence is Worth Ten Thousand Sentences", Tien Ning's "Stupid Flower", Su Tong's "River Bank", Zhang Wei's "Remembering Aya" and other works to study and discuss. Have an overall understanding of the literary trend since the 1990s and the achievements of Chinese literature.

Name: The Origin and Development of Human Communication
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course advocates interdisciplinary research and explores the occurrence and development of human communication methods from the perspective of linguistics, psychology, and paleontology. The course introduces the various communication methods and basic characteristics of animals. It mainly compares the differences between orangutan communication methods and human communication methods, and explores the path to the emergence of human vocal language as well as the reasons for its full development and its future. On the other hand, issues related to the development of human institutions and language development are explored from an evolutionary perspective. This course hopes to help students in the Department of Chinese, Department of Psychology, Department of Archeology, Department of Biology and other related disciplines broaden their research horizons and choose cutting-edge international topics.

Name: Literature and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Explore the relationship between Chinese literature and Confucianism, Taoism, Buddhism, classics, history, philosophy, calligraphy, painting, music, martial arts, country, society, era, region, readers, etc., to enrich students' understanding of people and people in various fields of literature and culture, and understand that the understanding of literature is not just about authors and works.

Name: Studies in The Scholars
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will systematically introduce the relevant situation of "The Scholars": including the author's life, novel version, novel's theme and artistic features, etc. In particular, the original appearance of this novel will be discussed in conjunction with the research history of this book.

Name: Introduction to Classic Ancient Chinese Novels
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: There are no prior course requirements for this course, but the choice of other literary subjects, particularly in ancient Chinese literature, will facilitate the study of the course.
Introduction: This course focuses on the classics of ancient novels such as "Romance of the Three Kingdoms", "Water Margin", "Journey to the West", "Jin Ping Mei", "Three Words and Two Patterns", "Strange Stories from a Chinese Studio", "The Scholars" and "Dream of Red Mansions". These masterpieces not only represent the most important novel styles of ancient China, such as classical Chinese novels, story novels and chapter novels, and have lasting artistic appeal; but also demonstrate the novelist's profound grasp of life experience with their eclectic narratives and descriptions; and their rich spiritual heritage reflect the evolution of ancient Chinese culture, politics, society and other aspects. This course will combine the characteristics of different classics, highlight the ideological connotation and artistic value of these works, and discuss their role in contemporary cultural life and construction, thereby improving the elective's literary appreciation ability and enhancing their perceptual understanding of ancient society and traditional culture.

Name: Religions of India
Introduction: India is a country where religions are prevalent. The three major religions in the world are found in India. In addition, there are Hinduism, Sikhism, Jainism, Jainism, etc. But it is Hinduism that dominates. Therefore, this course mainly teaches the brief history and current situation of Hinduism, which has the most followers today, as well as Islam, Sikhism, and Buddhism, which played an important role in ancient times. It also briefly introduces the situation of other religions, with the purpose of giving students a more comprehensive understanding of Indian religions.

Name: Golf
Introduction:
Golf is a ball game played on outdoor venues with unique landscapes. The basic rule is to use a number of clubs to hit the holes in the order of the holes on a grass course that usually has eighteen holes. The player with the lowest total score wins the game. _x000D_
Golf originated in Scotland, England, six hundred years ago. It has a high status in the world and is a gentleman's sport with great cultural connotations. The sport attaches great importance to the cultivation and etiquette of participants. Integrity, self-discipline, and consideration for others are the most important spiritual cores of golf. _x000D_
The word golf is composed of the first letters of four English words: green, oxygen, light, and friendship. It reflects the golf realm of walking on green grass with fresh air and sunshine, hitting balls and making friends. Social interaction is an important function of golf. _x000D_
This course mainly teaches golf etiquette and culture, basic golf techniques and tactics, golf rules, etc. This course is an introductory course, mainly for students with no basic knowledge. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Law
Introduction:
Introduction to Law is a general elective basic course offered to all non-law major undergraduates in the school. The guiding ideology and purpose of this course are: to provide students with an introductory guide to law, to help students master the basic concepts, principles and knowledge of law, to cultivate legal awareness, to practice legal thinking, to master legal skills, and to be able to analyze, explain and solve legal practice problems based on the legal theoretical knowledge they have learned. _x000D_
This course strives to comprehensively enhance students' legal literacy and improve students' ability to solve practical problems through law on the basis of introducing basic legal knowledge and closely integrating major legal issues in real life.

Name: Selected Readings in Chinese History (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is "Ancient Chinese" in the Department of History. It is a compulsory language tools course for undergraduate students in the Department of History. The purpose of teaching is mainly to cultivate and improve students' ability to read ancient historical documents. The teaching content is divided into two parts: literary anthology and ancient Chinese knowledge, with the anthology as the main part. The anthology is prefaced by five documents: Jing, Shi, Zi, Ji, and Archaeology, and knowledge of ancient Chinese is interspersed between the anthologies. In teaching, we implement the principle of integrating theory with practice and teach selected works, with equal emphasis on literature and history. Teaching ancient Chinese knowledge is to systematize and deepen the vocabulary and grammatical knowledge that students have learned in the selected works. The entire teaching activity focuses on three links: classroom lectures, homework assignments, and paragraph summaries: through classroom lectures, ancient Chinese knowledge and historical and cultural knowledge are taught to students; through homework assignments and paragraph summaries, classroom teaching effects are consolidated, and students’ practical language abilities are cultivated and improved.

Name: Traditional Chinese Decorative Art and Aesthetic Culture
Introduction: This course takes the decorative art and corresponding aesthetic culture of China's past dynasties as the teaching theme. The course content mainly selects painted pottery, bronze ware, lacquer ware, Han Dynasty stone sculptures, grotto murals, porcelain and wooden New Year pictures produced in Chinese creation and belief culture as research objects. They run through the main thread and process of Chinese culture and art. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Fine Arts
Introduction: The "Introduction to Art" course introduces the main types, works, masters, achievements and artistic concepts of ancient and modern Chinese and foreign art from the shallower to the deeper, and outlines a concise, clear and complete outline of the long and rich visual art. In the process of describing the characteristics of art and the methods of appreciating art works, it guides students to enter the door of art, appreciate its mystery, style and charm, and gain a deeper understanding of Chinese and foreign cultures through visual art materials.

Name: Traditional Chinese Architecture
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Traditional Chinese Architecture is open to undergraduate students of all majors at Peking University, with the purpose of allowing students to understand the Chinese architectural tradition and the architectural expression of Chinese traditional culture. Therefore, we do not focus on the discussion of traditional Chinese architectural theory, but hope to do specific analysis and interpretation through cases. _x000D_
The course breaks through the usual chronological system of traditional history teaching, starting directly from case analysis, starting from the campus, and directly analyzing the charm of traditional Chinese architecture from near to far. The main cases involved will include: the architecture and gardens of Peking University, the Forbidden City, the Temple of Heaven, the Summer Palace, and some important ancient buildings in Shanxi. The main selection of cases in Beijing and areas around Beijing is used as case analysis. It is also designed to allow students to easily conduct on-the-spot investigations through class study, experience the charm of traditional architecture in an immersive on-site experience, and understand what traditional Chinese architecture is? Its beauty, its value and essence. _x000D_
In the second half of the course, the history of traditional Chinese architecture will be systematically introduced in chronological order, and relevant research results at home and abroad will be introduced to help students have a comprehensive understanding of traditional Chinese architecture, better structure and improve the knowledge system. _x000D_

Name: Ancient Eastern Civilizations
Introduction: This course is a compulsory professional course in the world ' s ancient history and focuses on the development of ancient civilizations in Egypt, Western Asia and India and their cultural achievements. The selection of some of the classic works is guided by the theme, which builds students ' ability to master and apply history, discover and solve problems. The main topics are: the origin of the language and the country, the relationship between the ancient Near East, the ancient monarchy and the divine power, the ancient law and society, mythology, etc.

Name: Asian History
Introduction: The re-emergence of Asia was a major event that affected the development trend of world history in the 20th century. Learning Asian history is of special significance to Chinese students. This course covers the history from ancient times to the present day, focusing on describing and analyzing Asian history as a whole from the perspectives of national evolution, maritime history, environmental history, and cultural exchanges. At the same time, it breaks through the Eurocentric construction of Asia by comparing the similarities and differences between Eurasian and European history, and inspires students to think about Asian history from Asia.

Name: Social History of Modern China
Prerequisite: Arts students have requested courses in China ' s recent modern history, and science and technology students have requested courses in public theory.
Introduction: The development of modern Chinese society is the most rapid and complex period in Chinese history. The study and research of modern Chinese social history is extremely important for deepening our understanding of the causes and directions of social changes and cultivating the quality and methods of comprehensively observing and analyzing social problems. In the past writing and teaching of modern Chinese history, the content of social history was relatively weak, which was not conducive to a comprehensive understanding of modern Chinese history and did not meet the needs of social development. The course teaches topics on major social development elements such as population structure, political system change, social organization and mobilization, technological progress, behavior and lifestyle, social spiritual culture, etc., and finally summarizes the methods and characteristics of the integration of modern Chinese society. The course covers the two major periods of the Republic of China and the People's Republic of China. In order to deepen the understanding and grasp of basic historical facts, historical materials and analytical methods, the course focuses on the period of the Republic of China. The purpose is to master the basic content of various elements of China's modern development through the course, and apply it to understand or study the development and changes of Chinese society.

Name: Theory and Practice of Choral Fundamentals
Introduction:
The basic course of chorus is a course that combines music theory and practice, professionalism and popularization. The content of this course mainly includes three aspects:_x000D_
1. Study and practice of basic music theory. Including: learning to read and sing staff proficiently; learning and practicing basic intervals, harmony and basic polyphony. _x000D_
2. Learning and practicing basic vocal skills. Such as the use of breath in singing; the pronunciation of chorus; the expansion of the vocal range, etc. _x000D_
3. Appreciation and practice of famous Chinese and foreign choral works. Through appreciating and singing the works of different writers from different periods at home and abroad, we will gain a basic understanding of the history of Chinese and foreign choral music and some classic choral works, thereby generating an interest in further learning and experiencing music creation, and laying a solid foundation for improving students' musical literacy. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Historical Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Chinese historical geography is a general elective course for all students in the school. This course involves various departments of Chinese historical geography, such as changes in political regions and local administrative systems, transportation roads and military geography, changes in rivers and lakes and the environment, climate fluctuations and human activities, agricultural production and regional development, urban development and spatial structure, etc. Through this course, we hope that students can understand the spatial basis of major political and military activities in Chinese historical periods and the interactive relationship between human activities and the environment, and help students understand Chinese history and China's national conditions.

Name: Introduction to Chinese History and Culture
Introduction: The purpose of teaching this course is to enable history undergraduate students to have a preliminary understanding of some important basic knowledge of Chinese history, broaden their horizons, and provide the necessary foundation for further in-depth study of other specialized knowledge. This course describes the introductory knowledge necessary for learning Chinese history, including (1) how to read - how to use reference books to read ancient classics, the external form and classification of ancient classics, the origin of stone inscriptions, and how to understand ancient documents more quickly and deeply by relying on the research results of the Qing Dynasty. (2) Understand the time unit for recording history - era, and understand the astronomical calendar basis for measuring era. (3) Understand the geographical environment, the spatial stage of historical activities, and understand the evolution of geographical construction in the past dynasties, as well as the important changes in rivers, canals and waterways. (4) Understand the important core factors of ancient Chinese society - the bureaucracy and the evolution of the closely related imperial examination system. (5) Understand the basic conditions of clothing, food, housing (including funerals), and transportation in ancient social life, and enrich the specific understanding of ancient society.

Name: Topics in Pre-Qin History
Introduction:
An elective course for senior undergraduate students in the Department of History, 2 hours per week, 32 hours in total. _x000D_
This course takes the history of the Pre-Qin Dynasty as the subject, roughly in order of the times, selects several important issues in the history of the Pre-Qin Dynasty, and teaches them in special topics. The teaching method is mainly classroom lectures, and the performance evaluation mainly consists of two parts: thesis assignment and the final open-book examination. _x000D_
The content of the course mainly involves historical materials and methods for the study of Pre-Qin history, the origin of Chinese civilization, the characteristics of early Chinese states and the Shang and Zhou polities, religious beliefs and shamanic rituals, agriculture and land systems, the evolution of the political system in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, the development of commodity economy and currency in the Spring and Autumn and Warring States periods, pre-Qin punishment and ethnic issues, etc. Through such a special research and narration method, I try to grasp the main clues and characteristics of the historical development of Pre-Qin Dynasty, and gain an understanding of the research issues and results in this field. The curriculum is generally arranged to cover one topic every 2-3 class hours. _x000D_

Name: Ancient Chinese History Exercises
Introduction: In order to cooperate with the teaching of "Ancient Chinese History", the main basic course for undergraduates in the Department of History, the small class "Ancient Chinese History Exercise" strengthens students' reading of basic historical materials and basic treatises. Through discussions, it enhances students' understanding of ancient Chinese history and increases their interest in learning. This course is based on the "four keys" of ancient Chinese history research such as "catalog, official positions, geography, and chronology" as the core. Through teacher lectures and classmates' practice, it cultivates students' basic abilities in ancient Chinese history research.

Name: Tang Poetry and Tang History
Introduction:
To interpret the historical value of literary works through various subjects of the history disciplines, for example, by taking Downo poetry;
(c) The development of literary training for students in non-literacy.

Name: Introduction to Art History
Introduction to Film
Introduction:
This course is a professional core course for the drama, film, television and literature major of the School of Art and a broad platform course for the whole school. This course takes movies as the object and is based on the forefront of film research. On the basis of systematically explaining the basic principles of film art, aesthetics, culture, industry, etc., it places films in a broad cultural background for in-depth analysis, covering the history of film art, film art and other arts, the language of film art, the creation, production, dissemination and acceptance of films, film criticism, film culture, film media and other important theoretical dimensions and knowledge points. The course also conducts in-depth analysis of a number of carefully selected representative and important films, and strives to explore the mysteries of the film art world through the analysis of classic cases and grasp the development context of film. _x000D_
The teaching of this course focuses on the use of visual teaching methods, focusing on the cultivation of students' open, comprehensive, cross-media, and interdisciplinary modern thinking methods and learning abilities. It strives to enable students not only to learn the knowledge and principles of film theory and film history, but also to improve their artistic accomplishment, strengthen their humanistic qualities, cultivate healthy, good, diverse and open aesthetic tastes, broaden their minds, and cultivate comprehensive and creative modern thinking abilities. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Ancient Chinese History
Introduction: This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduate students majoring in Chinese history in the Department of History. The difficulty level is between basic courses and postgraduate courses. It mainly introduces research methods and research experiences, and guides students to do their own research. The purpose is to train students' independent research abilities.

Name: History of Modern Sino-Korean Relations
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to cultivate and improve undergraduate students’ understanding of China-South Korea relations in modern times. Through the study of textbooks, historical materials and new archival materials, we will gain an in-depth understanding of the development of China-North Korea and China-South Korea relations from the end of the Joseon Dynasty to the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and South Korea in 1992. Specifically, the disintegration of tributary relations between Qing and South Korea in the late Qing Dynasty and the establishment of modern diplomatic relations, the reasons for the exile of Koreans to China before and after the demise of the Korean Empire in 1910, Koreans’ understanding and relationship with the Revolution of 1911 and the government of the Republic of China, the establishment and activities of the Provisional Government of the Republic of Korea, China during World War II The National Government and the Provisional Government of South Korea, the civil war between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party and the confrontation between the North and the South, the China-Korean War, the Sino-Soviet differences and North Korea's equidistant diplomacy, the China-North Korea and China-South Korea relations after reform and opening up, the North Korean nuclear issue and the Six Defense Talks, etc., to better grasp the relationship between the Korean Peninsula and China in modern times.

Name: Selected Readings in Chinese History B (Part 2)
Introduction: This course is "Ancient Chinese" in the Department of History. It is a compulsory language tools course for undergraduate students in the Department of History. The purpose of teaching is mainly to cultivate and improve students' ability to read ancient historical documents. The teaching content is divided into two parts: literary anthology and ancient Chinese knowledge, with the anthology as the main part. The anthology is prefaced by five documents: Jing, Shi, Zi, Ji, and Archaeology, and knowledge of ancient Chinese is interspersed between the anthologies. In teaching, we implement the principle of integrating theory with practice and teach selected works, with equal emphasis on literature and history. Teaching ancient Chinese knowledge is to systematize and deepen the vocabulary and grammatical knowledge that students have learned in the selected works. The entire teaching activity focuses on three links: classroom lectures, homework assignments, and paragraph summaries: through classroom lectures, ancient Chinese knowledge and historical and cultural knowledge are taught to students; through homework assignments and paragraph summaries, classroom teaching effects are consolidated, and students’ practical language abilities are cultivated and improved.

Name: General Survey of Archaeology
Introduction:
Archeology from prehistory to the fortnightly period mainly talks about the genealogy of Chinese prehistoric culture, the structural system of Chinese bronze culture, and related major archaeological discoveries and research, focusing on the significance of prehistoric archeology and three-generation archeology in reconstructing ancient Chinese history. _x000D_
The archeology section from the Qin and Han Dynasties to the Song and Yuan Dynasties follows four themes: cities, tombs, unearthed cultural relics, religion, and foreign civilizations. It briefly and systematically introduces important archaeological discoveries and research results. It mainly emphasizes four aspects: the transformation of urban form from closed to open, the hierarchy of tombs, the cultural heritage of unearthed cultural relics, and the exchange and integration process between other ethnic groups and foreign civilizations and Chinese civilization. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Foreign History (Part 2)
Introduction: Studying a society’s past requires reasons. In my opinion, there are two important reasons here. First of all, throughout the ages, Western civilization has spread from its birthplace - Europe and the Mediterranean to other parts of the world, and has had varying degrees of impact on these regions. Therefore, in order to understand the history of much of the world, it is necessary that we have some knowledge of Western society's past. At the same time, most of you will approach Western history from an outsider's perspective, and you may well end up bringing unique insights to the issue.

Name: European History
Introduction:
_x000D_
_x000D_
This course is an on-campus elective course that mainly teaches modern European history. The content includes the emergence of nation-states in early modern Europe, the content and influence of modern scientific concepts and democratic ideas, the national democratic revolutions and industrial revolutions in European countries, European nationalism and imperialism at the end of the 19th century, the two world wars and the decline of Europe, European diplomacy during the Cold War, changes in European politics, economy, society and culture in the 20th century, as well as the exploration of socialist revolution and reform in Soviet Eastern Europe, and Europe after the Cold War. While focusing on the introduction of historical events, the class also highlights the combing of historical context, analysis of historical issues and introduction of historical analysis methods.

Name: Research on Suicide as a Social Problem
Introduction: Suicide has become a growing global social problem and, together with cancer, one of the leading causes of death in today's society. The World Health Organization and many countries have attached great importance to this issue, and suicide science, which specializes in suicide, has developed. At present, the problem of suicide in our country has attracted the attention of society as a whole, yet awareness and knowledge about suicide prevention are very lacking for various reasons. According to the latest studies from abroad, the course will focus on the theory of suicide, methods of studying suicide, characteristics and causes of suicide among specific groups in the country and abroad, and methods and strategies for suicide prevention, based on a brief introduction to suicide science. Through this course, students are able to have a more systematic understanding of suicide, acquire knowledge about identifying and responding to common risk factors of suicide, develop a certain awareness of suicide prevention and provide an initial basis for future work.

Name: Sociological Reflections on Death
Introduction: The course " Thinking in the Sociology of Death " is one of the selected courses for undergraduate students across the board. At present, there are not many courses in higher education in the country related to the sociology of death, and there are relatively few teaching materials on the sociology of death. To this end, the course focuses on topics of priority in the context of China ' s socio-economic transition from a sociological perspective, especially in the context of the accelerated ageing of the population at the macro level, relating to dying, death and bereavement. The main subjects covered in the course include the actual background of the sociology of death, the subject of study, the theoretical basis of the subject, the methods of study, etc., with a focus on the interdisciplinary (especially sociological) and intercultural interpretation of death education, the process of death, the type of death, terminal care and the response to death.

Name: Film Analysis
Introduction: The course will systematically develop students ' ability to read films from a unique perspective, including film narrative models, lead design, pioneer films, underground film theory, etc.

Name: General Survey of Criminology
Introduction:
This course covers the basics of four courses in criminal law, criminology, financial crime, and legal empirical analysis offered by the Faculty of Law. Why did you open this class? Why should students learn about a phenomenon as far away from us as possible? In fact, crime is not necessarily far from us. First, as potential victims, we need to know the patterns of crime in order to prevent victimization. As potential violators, we also need the protection of criminal law. Because criminal law is a double-edged sword to fight crime and to limit the abuse of power by the judiciary. Secondly, how crime is understood and treated is also an important basis for distinguishing between civilizations and cultures. It was therefore important to learn to treat crime with a scientific calm. Third, crime research is also a science that requires a multidisciplinary knowledge background. In view of the fact that this course is offered by students of various specialties throughout the school, the knowledge of crime goes beyond the confines of the discipline and leads to a higher level of teaching.
This course will accompany students in moving from a vivid case analysis to a variety of criminal areas, inspire students to observe and understand crime from a variety of perspectives, to understand crime phenomena and responses to crime in a scientific manner, and to develop a basic approach to the overall management of crime.

Name: Data Analysis and Statistical Software
Introduction: Using data analysis as an entry point, the course presents the most common statistical analysis software (R+SAS) based on common regression analysis theory. In the end, it is hoped that the students will achieve a goal. That is to say, skilled in using statistical software to analyse common data problems.

Name: Shadow Central Banking
Introduction: The China Shadow Bank is an advanced seminar course focusing on monetary policy and macroeconomics. The purpose of this course is to increase students ' understanding of central banks, macroeconomics, interest rate liberalization, foreign exchange issues, trade issues, Chinese financial markets, etc. The panel discussion will be a class organization plan. The participants were divided into groups and gave weekly lectures in the fields of open market operations, foreign exchange markets, macroeconomic news and steel and real estate. Thematic discussions will also be held on a weekly basis. The Professor will regularly invite outsiders such as academics, central bankers and financiers to the seminar.

Name: Money and Finance
Introduction: This course will systematically elaborate on some major issues in the fields of currency, banking and financial markets. The purpose is to let everyone understand the important role of currency in social and economic development; understand the role of the financial system in providing risk sharing (risk sharing). Sharing, liquidity, information and other financial service functions; examine the operating mechanisms of financial markets, commercial banking systems, and central bank systems, as well as the roles they play in the process of currency operation and monetary policy transmission, so that everyone can see clearly how currency in financial financing "flows" through all aspects of economic activities, reflecting its function as the "blood" of economic operations. Currency, interest rates, money demand, money supply, monetary policy, inflation, etc. are important categories and contents of macroeconomics, which overlap and overlap with the content of this course, but this course will focus more on analyzing the issues involved in their operation and transmission processes. The business, functions, organization and management of commercial banks and central banks in this course are also included in the "Commercial Bank Management" and "Central Bank" courses, but the latter pays more attention to specific operational and practical businesses; the content about financial markets and their actors is discussed in detail in courses such as "Investment" and "Financial Markets and Financial Institutions", and specific investment analysis methods and knowledge of practical operations of financial markets are explained. The content of "Money and Finance" is mainly conceptual, theoretical, and framework knowledge. It provides some preparation and establishes a knowledge framework for various "professional" courses in finance. Each "professional" course further expands and deepens its related content. Therefore, monetary finance is not only the foundation of each "professional" course, but also provides a comprehensive framework for "integrating" professional knowledge.

Name: Securities Investment
Introduction: This course explores the basic principles of investing in financial securities. We will begin by examining portfolio selection theory and its impact on the risk-return trade-off. Techniques for valuing risk-free investments (such as government bonds) and risky investments (such as common stocks) will be reviewed. Finally, we will examine derivatives pricing theory and apply it to the valuation of futures and options contracts.

Name: Financial Econometrics
Introduction: This course is a required course for undergraduate students majoring in finance. The main purpose of this course is to introduce how to use financial data to build econometric models and conduct empirical research on relevant financial theories and the relationship between financial variables. In order to facilitate the use and understanding of the method, basic modeling and inference methods are introduced according to the cross-sectional, time series and panel data types. Mainly introduces the application methods of basic multiple regression models in the financial field. Then, based on the feature of a large amount of time series data in the financial market, the basic model of stationary time series - the ARMA model is discussed; the last chapter introduces the panel data analysis method.

Name: Investment Banking
Introduction:
Domestic and global financial systems are comprised of a variety of interlinked institutions whose interactions create the form and structure of the financial system. These institutions range from central banks, commercial and investment banks, institutional investors, and financial markets for stock, bond and other assets to currency regimes, the global balance of payments, and fiscal and regulatory policies that affect monetary conditions. The main objective of this class is to help construct a conceptual framework of the financial markets for finance students and to ensure that they are able to develop for themselves a context in which to place their more specialized finance classes.

In this class we will attempt to outline and develop a “geography” of China’s financial system and its links to the global system in order to develop a framework within which to understand the Chinese financial system, its future development, and its role within the current global crisis. We will consider the purpose of a well-functioning financial market, the necessary components of such a market, the role of financial balance sheets in the way the system responds to shocks, and the implementation of monetary policy. We will examine the different kinds of financial markets and their inter-relationships.

Name: Supply Chain Management
Introduction:
With the emergence of a globalized economy and the rapid development of information technology and e-commerce, the environment for business survival and competition has changed. In the past, firms faced competition with their counterparts. In the age of global markets and the digital economy, firms rely on alliances and collaboration between upstream and downstream firms to gain advantage in market competition. In other words, it is now a competition between the supply chain (which includes the business chain of suppliers, suppliers, customers, customers, etc.) and the supply chain.
This was followed by research on supply chain management theory. Today, supply chain management has become a popular subject in business and engineering colleges and is widely featured in corporate strategy reports, business and academic journals and teaching materials.
Supply chain management is also of interest to scholars and industry in China. The exploration of supply chain theory and practice in the context of China ' s economic environment is a common subject for Chinese scholars and industry. The delivery of undergraduate courses, on the other hand, will help to advance the groundbreaking theoretical and practical development of our supply chain management in the future.
The course will present basic concepts, theories, research status and practical experience of enterprises in supply chain management. A combination of theory and case studies and examples will be used in teaching, not only to equip students with the basic knowledge of supply chain management, but also to apply it in their work practices. There is also a desire to develop students' interest in research in this field.

Name: Fixed Income Securities
Introduction: This course includes tools for fixed-income securities, pricing and risk management.

Name: Financial Markets and Institutions
Introduction: This course mainly includes two parts: financial markets and financial institutions. The financial markets section will discuss the organization and microstructure of primary and secondary markets, as well as the submarkets of various financial instruments such as stock markets, currency markets, treasury bond markets, corporate bond markets, and municipal securities markets. The financial institutions section will discuss depository financial institutions such as commercial banks, and non-depository financial institutions such as investment funds, investment banks, and financial companies. The characteristic of this course is that it not only grasps the latest developments in the theory and practice of modern Western financial institutions and financial markets, but also closely combines it with China's reality to describe and analyze the historical changes and current problems in the corresponding fields in China. It not only provides a framework introduction to basic theories and market operations, but also provides in-depth discussions on hot issues in financial markets and institutions at home and abroad.

Name: Tax Law and Tax Accounting
Introduction: This course is for students in the third year of accounting. The main elements of the tax law (including the VAT law, the turnover tax law, the corporate income tax law, the personal income tax law, etc.) and its collection; the accounting treatment of enterprises after tax obligations arise; and simple tax planning methods.

Name: Hot Topics in Chinese Finance
Introduction:
This course is a new course for undergraduate, master's and doctoral students that discusses hot and cutting-edge issues in China's finance. _x000D_
When it was first offered, it was initially considered to adopt a method of half lectures by professors and half students speaking in groups, so as to enhance students' understanding of a series of important issues affecting China's finance. _x000D_

Name: Equity Securities Investment
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to describe several basic methods of stock value assessment, including methods of discounting cash flows, relative valuation methods, and real options pricing. The advantages and disadvantages of several methods are compared. In addition, the course describes strategies and the main ways in which business values can be enhanced.

Name: Topics in Chinese Social and Economic Research
Introduction: Try to put the geographical and natural environment, human exploration and understanding of nature, ways of survival, challenges and responses to nature and humanity, social structure, beliefs, values, civilization interaction, social development stages and other factors into an analytical framework to understand the evolution and direction of China's society and economy.

Name: International Finance
Prerequisite: Prerequisite courses or experiences in corporate finance and financial investment would be ideal
Introduction: This course aims to provide a conceptual framework within which corporate and individual decision-making in an international context can be analyzed. We will apply the principles of investment and corporate finance to study multinational corporations in the global economy.

Name: History of Western Art
Introduction:
As one of the important components of Western civilization, Western art's existence and development have witnessed the value orientation and changes of Western civilization. It is a creative fusion of materialized form and spiritual expression, and contains the value of allowing future generations to feel and understand the rich and vivid spiritual power within it. The history of Western art is very fascinating, especially its classic works, which are often fascinating and unforgettable. The word "classical" comes from the Latin "classicus", which means "first-class". I think that college students, whether they are studying literature or science, should know a little about art history. This is an important way to experience and understand the first-class cultural achievements of mankind. _x000D_
This course is specially designed for university quality education, with a special focus on introducing the humanistic connotations of classic works of Western art history, and cultivating students' ability to read and interpret Western art masterpieces, so as to deepen their understanding of European culture and enhance their own aesthetic taste. _x000D_
The teaching process is accompanied by a large number of exquisite slide materials, some of which were taken by the teaching teachers on site in Europe. In addition, there is a special online course area: http://wah.bdwm.net, where you can browse images of major works and exchange learning experiences. _x000D_
About 440 students enter this course each semester, and they are still left with a lot to learn by the end of the course. I believe they will continue their journey into Western art history in their future careers. _x000D_

Name: Financial Engineering
Introduction: The course will systematically teach concepts, principles and applications of the direction of financial engineering. The course covered the basics and practices of financial products and technology development, the theory and application of risk management, and the trading of financial derivatives. The financial derivatives covered in the course included basic derivatives such as forwards, futures, swaps and options, as well as innovative products from bond and stock markets.

Name: Business Ethics
Introduction:
The influence and role of corporate ethics issues in the current market economy process have attracted more and more people's attention. Judging from the development of domestic enterprises and markets, the significance of corporate ethics and business ethics should be said to have become an important factor affecting social development and market development. _x000D_
Business and corporate behavior need to pay attention to the relationship between different stakeholder groups. Even our personal behavior and career development planning must also handle the relationship between individuals and the relationship between individuals and organizations. In these behaviors, in addition to professional requirements and the constraints of social laws and regulations, there is also a very important factor, which is the consideration of ethical norms. _x000D_
The study of corporate ethics involves the rationality of corporate decision-making, ethical thinking about management behavior within the enterprise, coordination between the enterprise and relevant interest groups in competition, and the harmonious handling of corporate management activities, social development, and even the natural environment. These issues not only determine the competitiveness of an enterprise, but also determine its sustainable development. They are the basic requirements of modern society for enterprises, and they are also a challenge that reality poses to human management behavior. _x000D_
    In our business school teaching, we focus on arranging such a course related to enterprises and business ethics issues, which is also a manifestation of social responsibility in order to adapt to the development needs of modern society and business. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Business
Introduction:
China's remarkable economic growth over the past 30 years has transformed the global business landscape. The Chinese market and its extraordinary growth are important not only to China but increasingly to the rest of the world. _x000D_
_x000D_
In this course, we will take a closer look at China's business landscape, as well as the opportunities and challenges faced by multinational and domestic enterprises. We will better understand China's fundamental factors and institutional changes in the context of globalization. This course will start from the perspective of corporate decision-makers and will also cover some important functional level issues.

Name: Aerobics
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Aerobics is a highly artistic sports event that integrates gymnastics, dance, and music, is based on aerobic exercises, and features fitness, strength, and beauty as its main features. _x000D_
    This course mainly teaches basic aerobics movements (including basic posture movements, basic difficult movements and basic step combinations), and the national aerobics mass exercise standard three-level routines. Through practice, you can cultivate correct posture, create a beautiful posture, improve body coordination and flexibility, and create routines suitable for your own exercise, so as to improve health, stimulate vitality, and delight the body and mind. _x000D_
2． Safety precautions:_x000D_
(1) Wear appropriate sportswear and shoes that are conducive to exercise_x000D_
(2) Pay attention to the safety of yourself and your classmates during class. If you have chest tightness, palpitation, dizziness or other physical fatigue, please report it to the teacher, who will arrange it according to the situation. _x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Master the basic techniques and related theories of aerobics, and cultivate students' lifelong sports concepts. _x000D_
2． Master a lifelong physical training skill and develop students' comprehensive qualities in practice. _x000D_

Name: Art History
Introduction: The history of art is taught ten times in succession, at 14-15 times, and a comprehensive combo and presentation of world art reveals the differences in the history of art and art in different times and cultures. This course, which is offered once a year during the autumn semester, is offered without pre-elementary courses, with an introductory presentation on the basic concepts of the history of the arts and the structural relationship of the content throughout the course, and a concluding comment on the question of summarizing the content.

Name: Financial Modeling
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the design and methods of empirical research in the fields of asset pricing and corporate finance, as well as the application and computational analysis of financial data. The course is divided into two parts: the first part is empirical research topics, including the predictability of stock returns, testing of asset pricing models, event research, corporate finance and governance, etc.; the second part is financial data and empirical methods, including financial database extraction methods and processing methods, and the application of SAS software for empirical analysis.

Name: Integrated Business Plan Competition
Introduction: This course is a course jointly offered by the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Center of the Guanghua School of Management and the Dingman Entrepreneurship Center of the University of Maryland Smith School of Business. It mainly allows students to form groups to write business plans and participate in business plan competitions organized by the Innovation and Entrepreneurship Center. It recommends outstanding candidates to participate in the 7th "China Business Plan Competition" organized in cooperation with the Dingman Entrepreneurship Center and other international entrepreneurship competitions.

Name: Mathematical Methods in Finance
Introduction: The course will introduce important quantitative tools in finance (especially in the field of financial derivatives pricing and its risk management): for example, stochastic processes, stochastic calculus and partial differential equations, as well as numerical implementation methods of models such as Monte Carlo simulation. At the same time, this course avoids boring and simple mathematical derivation. While paying attention to methods, it will use vivid examples to support the application of quantitative methods in financial modeling. This course will lay the foundation for students to understand some issues in finance from a quantitative perspective or engage in quantitative research.

Name: English Public Speaking
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Prerequisite: University course on modularization in English
Introduction:
This course systematically introduces and discusses all aspects involved in English public speaking, and assists students in completing self-introduction, explanatory, and persuasive speech tasks. It aims to firstly improve students' expression and communication skills in oral speeches, and secondly improve students' speech writing skills. In addition, this course will, to a certain extent, cultivate students' critical thinking skills in oral presentations and speech manuscripts, as well as their ability to use the Internet and libraries to search, collect, and organize information. _x000D_
This course organically links English oral expression training with written writing exercises, strengthens students' comprehensive training in English active production ability, and lays the foundation for students' English application in future practical work. _x000D_

Name: Baseball and Softball
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
Baseball and softball are very interesting and competitive sports. They are comprehensive sports that integrate running, jumping, throwing, hitting, and passing, as well as wisdom, bravery, art, and reaction. It is a collective confrontation event between two teams through alternating offense and defense, playing full games, and the team with the most points accumulated as the winner. Baseball and softball sports can effectively train physical qualities such as speed, strength, and agility, and improve judgment, adaptability, and independent combat capabilities. Softball is influenced by baseball and is known as the "twin sister". This course mainly teaches the basic knowledge, techniques, tactics, competition rules and refereeing methods of baseball and softball, and learns how to appreciate high-level baseball and softball games. _x000D_
2. Safety education matters_x000D_
Strengthen safety education during the study of this course. Students with congenital diseases need to apply for explanation from the teacher and obtain the teacher's consent before taking classes; do not wear objects unrelated to sports such as keys, glasses, etc., abide by classroom disciplines and follow the teacher's instructions, attend classes strictly according to the regular requirements of physical education classes, strictly observe classroom disciplines, and ensure that no injury accidents occur. _x000D_
1. Prepare and organize activities carefully and comprehensively, and develop the habit of warming up each part of the body before practicing and relaxing after exercise. Activities should be gradual, with speeds ranging from slow to fast, and ranges of movement ranging from small to large. _x000D_
2. It is strictly prohibited to play on slippery lawns, muddy grounds or venues with obstacles to avoid injury. _x000D_
3. When passing the ball, do not position too closely; the passer should pass the ball in the same direction; do not pass the ball in crowded places; pass the ball with different strength and techniques at different distances. _x000D_
4. When catching the ball, you should pay attention to the hand shape of the ball. The technique should be correct, the judgment should be accurate, the reaction should be quick, and the ball should be accurately positioned to avoid hitting the ball. _x000D_
5. When two or more people are catching low-rolling balls and high-flying balls, they should shout "mine" to avoid collisions; when facing the sun to catch high-flying balls, they should block the light with their hands or gloves and see the ball clearly before catching the ball. _x000D_
6. When practicing catching the ball, you should concentrate, zoom in, and pay attention to the ball coming from different directions at any time. _x000D_
7. When picking the ball, you must enter the practice area from behind, and inform the practitioner that you need to pick the ball. You can only pick the ball after stopping practice. _x000D_
8. When hitting the ball, try to avoid hitting the body with pitches and self-balls, and "throwing the bat" is strictly prohibited. _x000D_
9. When practicing batting, you must hit the ball in the same direction. When swinging, you should pay attention to the fact that there are no people or obstacles three meters away from the front, back, left, and right, or hit the ball in a place where there are no obstacles in the field. _x000D_
10. When running the bases, the batter runner must enter the restricted lane and step on the outside base pad when running to first base. The runner should see the incoming ball clearly to avoid being hit. _x000D_
11. Runners and defensive catchers should try to avoid collisions. Defensive players are not allowed to stand on the base mat when the ball is not coming to avoid injuries due to collisions due to blocking fouls. _x000D_
12. When a base is entered and a score is scored, the defensive player should give up the base pad and is strictly prohibited from blocking the base to avoid collision with the runner. When sliding the base, you should act according to your ability. _x000D_
13. Students who are resting on the sidelines should face the court and watch the situation on the court to avoid being hit by the ball. _x000D_
3. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students’ physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, as well as the ideology of “health first”. _x000D_
2. Improve health, enhance physical fitness, and comprehensively improve students' physical and psychological qualities. _x000D_
3. Students are required to master the basic techniques and tactics of softball and learn basic rules and refereeing methods. _x000D_
4. Improve students' technical and tactical abilities and physical fitness through practice, and cultivate their interest in softball. _x000D_

Name: Conservation Biology
Introduction:
Conservation biology is a comprehensive discipline that emerged in the United States in the 1980s. Its purpose is to solve the crisis of rapid decline in biodiversity caused by excessive population growth and excessive destruction of natural resources. Conservation biology in my country only began to rise in the 1990s, and it has received increasing attention and has gradually become a popular subject. Peking University took the lead in offering this course in 1995. _x000D_
Conservation biology is a science with value trends. The development of its theory and practice is of great significance to the protection of the environment and natural resources, as well as the sustainable development of our society. As an emerging discipline, conservation biology has the following characteristics, many of which are different from other disciplines: 1. Crisis handling, urgency, and integration with practice; 2. Comprehensive, interdisciplinary; 3. Value trends; 4. Science on an evolutionary scale; 5. Long-term; 6. "Fuzzy" science. _x000D_
Conservation biology is even more important today to realize the Chinese dream of sustainability and better nature.

Name: History of Western Philosophy
Introduction: The course is structured to teach the historical development and core issues of Western philosophy in a way that combines time order and problem planning.

Name: General History of the World (Part 1)
Prerequisite: For all arts and engineering students
Introduction:
The core goal and content of the course: to guide students to clearly grasp the overall process of world historical development since the beginning of civilization, and to clearly understand the rise and decline of various civilizational regions in the process of historical development, as well as the exchanges and communications, collisions and conflicts, absorption and rejection between different civilizations. To this end, this course will take historical time as the main axis and tell it from two levels. First, how does communication occur between different civilizational regions? Geographical exploration and discovery, expansion of oceans and land, transoceanic trade and commerce, international investment of capital, diplomatic activities between nation-state political bodies, and people-to-people cultural exchanges are all means and methods for contact between civilizations. In this process, there were both "civilian attack" and "military plunder". At this level, the concept of space is important. Second, how did various civilizational regions change after contact? What are the underlying reasons for the changes? And what further consequences occurred? Specifically, which civilization has been developed and which civilization has been curbed? What changes have occurred in the internal mechanisms of each civilization, including its ideological system, economy, social and political systems, and what kind of worldwide impact and results have they produced? Cultural hegemony of discourse? Dominate the world economic system? and others. This level directly enters the core of each civilization and touches the essence of historical evolution. _x000D_
So, within this narrative structure, are there any ideological concepts and value systems that are commonly accepted by different civilizations? Yes, what is it? Is it modern civilization? If so, what does modern civilization refer to? Enlightenment and rational way of thinking, free and democratic political system, production and lifestyle based on modern science? Of course, if we determine that these are the common values ​​of mankind, we should also admit that while they have become universal concepts, each civilization has its own unique path of development and means of achievement. The formation and application of these paths and means are based on their respective historical traditions, cultural customs, and geographical features. _x000D_

Name: Electronic Commerce
Introduction: This course is designed to familiarize students with current and emerging Internet-based e-commerce business models and technologies. We will discuss management topics such as e-commerce competitive strategies, various e-commerce models, and how to manage B2C or B2B e-commerce projects. Technical topics such as technical infrastructure for e-commerce, website interface design, network security, etc. In addition, we will investigate China's leading e-commerce companies and analyze their competitive strategies.

Name: Practice of Chinese Enterprise Management
Introduction: Through high-quality, multi-field and multi-dimensional industry lectures, students can have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the cutting-edge information of today's Chinese enterprise management practices, broaden their horizons, and cultivate their ability to apply theory to practice. Combined with the diversified industry backgrounds of alumni, it focuses on sharing actual cases in the business management process.

Name: Introduction to American Poetry
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This is a poetry course for non-English majors. In chronological order, it introduces the eight most representative poets in the history of American literature, namely Poe, Whitman, Dickinson, Frost, Eliot, Stevens, Plath and Bishop. It focuses on a close reading of the works, combined with the poet's life and historical and cultural background, trying to clarify each poet's unique artistic achievements and show the development trajectory of American poetry. The purpose is to stimulate students' interest in poetry, cultivate their ability to analyze English poetry, and improve students' English proficiency and literary literacy. _x000D_

Name: Human Resource Management
Introduction:
Throughout your career after graduation from a professional to a supervisor to a business leader or even a business leader, whether you are engaged in marketing or finance, ICT or management consulting, you will gradually find that your knowledge and ability to work with others, influence others, lead teams and then manage organizations are key constraints in your career development. _x000D_
This course will lay a solid foundation for you to understand the organization, understand management and establish personal professional leadership from the perspective of a business general manager. This course will reflect the basic concepts, main theories, practical experience, management methods and skills, research findings and development trends of the discipline of human resource management from both practical and theoretical aspects. The course content includes the relationship between human resource management and organizational strategy, work and organizational design strategies, employee recruitment and selection techniques, employee performance management methods, compensation system design and management methods, employee incentive system design methods, employment relationship management, and human resource management research foundations. At the same time, this course will also explore the ability requirements of managers, methods to improve influence, and the concepts, theories and abilities of personal career development and management from a personal perspective. _x000D_

Name: China's Economic Reform and Development
Introduction: This course is the subject of the course, with Ning as its moderator, Wang Chiu, Zhu Sun Li, Zhang State-owned, Cao Fengxiu, Chen Liangyu and Chen Yuyu as its lecturer.

Name: Accounting Information and Data Analysis
Introduction: Accounting information plays an important role in corporate strategic planning and business management. This course focuses on how to use statistical methods to perform data analysis on various accounting information. This course will introduce the use of accounting information databases, the use of statistical methods in accounting research, the use of various statistical software, basic tools for data analysis and common problems.

Name: Behavioral Finance
Introduction:
This course presents behavioural finance research distinct from classic finance.
The course begins with a brief recapitulation of the key tenets of the classic financial theory: the desired utility function, the effective market hypothesis, the price-value equivalent hypothesis, the principle of arbitrage and the fragmentation of assets, and the testable meaning that these theories imply. This is followed by empirical evidence that these hypotheses cannot be established in the real market.
The second describes the two pillars of behavioural finance: limited arbitrage and individual psychological bias (conscience, preference).
It then presents a wide range of market variations and interprets them with the theories learned.
Finally, we present the latest developments in behavioural finance, particularly the findings of the recent financial crisis.
The behavioural finance discipline is characterized by a strong combination of theory and empirical evidence, mutual validation and development, as well as by a broad and non-single approach, and is a typical example of a joint interdisciplinary approach, which will also be the style that this course will be taught, allowing students to move from theory to empirical evidence to a deeper understanding of financial markets and humanity.

Name: Evolution and Innovation of Financial Services Information Systems
Introduction:
The generation and exchange of information is at the heart of the financial services industry. The emergence and development of digital information technology in the twentieth century has had a profound impact on the financial services industry. This impact is not only reflected in the improvement of the efficiency of traditional financial services and the reduction of service costs. More importantly, driven by the evolution of information technology, new financial service categories and service models have emerged, significantly improving the overall efficiency of the economic and financial systems. At the same time, special needs in financial services and changes in the behavior of service objects also provide directions for the development of information technology. In the past half century, various economies around the world have shown coordinated development and evolution of technology and financial services. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course introduces applicable theoretical frameworks for the evolution of financial services information systems. Through a combination of lectures and case analysis, students are helped to understand, master and apply methods of analyzing financial information technology; they also learn and discuss the collaborative evolution relationship between technology and services. We will also introduce important information technology concepts and application scenarios in financial services. Finally, under the leadership of teachers, students will conduct empirical analysis of actual cases at the forefront of the development of financial services technology. _x000D_

Name: Venture Capital and Innovation Finance
Introduction: This course examines how venture capital can finance technological innovation. The course is designed mainly for students in financial science, especially those interested in venture capital, entrepreneurial entrepreneurship, technological innovation or R & D-intensive enterprises.

Name: Advanced Mathematics (Type D)
