Introduction: Liberal Arts Advanced Mathematics is a course that combines basic mathematical theory and applied mathematical methods to adapt to the trend of liberal arts penetration in modern science. Its teaching content and methods have obvious liberal arts characteristics. Currently, the Department of Mathematics teaches liberal arts advanced mathematics courses to undergraduates and some graduate students in various majors such as journalism, society, government, information management, Chinese, archeology, national affairs, and language, as well as economics and management departments, including calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics. Teaching all the above content requires approximately 120 hours.

Name: Functional Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemistry is the basis for creating various materials of the physical world. Through chemical means, substances with various functions can be created. This course targets various functional substances used in daily life and industrial production; starting from the atomic and molecular levels, it systematically explains their molecular structure characteristics, mechanism of action, preparation methods, representative substances, typical application examples, etc. We also conduct experimental observations on some phenomena that are contrary to our "basic common sense", such as plastics that make sounds, plastics that emit light, plastics that conduct electricity, "thermal shrinkage", etc., and conduct class discussions on their mechanisms of action. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students can master the molecular structural characteristics of various functional substances, the chemical mechanism of their formation and function, and have the ability to select and flexibly apply certain chemical functional materials.

Name: Folklore Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Introduce various types of folklore, such as myths, legends, stories, jokes, proverbs, riddles, ballads, folk games, folk costumes, folk festivals, dietary customs, folk architecture, folk art, etc., promote folklore knowledge, and introduce traditional Chinese culture.

Name: General Biology Laboratory
Introduction:
This course is aimed at students in life sciences and related majors. The teaching orientation focuses on cultivating students' biological experimental abilities, qualities, and habits. Contents include_x000D_
Basic experimental content in plant biology, animal biology, microbiology, cell biology, biochemistry and molecular biology, such as microscope use_x000D_
Use, animal and plant morphological anatomy observation, aseptic operation, basic biochemistry and molecular biology experiments, etc. After studying this course, students will be able to master _x000D_
Master the basic experimental principles and techniques of biology, reach professional basic levels in terms of knowledge, operating techniques and application abilities, and prepare for subsequent professional courses_x000D_
Lay the foundation.

Name: General Biology (C)
Introduction: The lectures are intended for students majoring in arts and sciences who are interested in life sciences. Biology is the science that studies life. Today's biology is at the most exciting time in history. Biologists are unraveling the mysteries of life that plague mankind. This course not only teaches the basic knowledge and research ideas of biology, but also focuses on introducing some cutting-edge fields and achievements in the development of biology. The theme of biological research: the multi-layered nature of life, the unity of structure and function, and the idea of ​​evolution are throughout. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students can broaden their knowledge, stimulate creative thinking, and lay the foundation for fully utilizing life science background knowledge in various fields in the future. _x000D_

Name: Classical Chinese
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for all majors in the Chinese Department (including Chinese students and international students); it is an elective course for students in other departments. This course is a basic course and a tool course in language. The basic purpose of teaching is to cultivate and improve students' ability to read ancient documents through the study of ancient languages, lay the necessary foundation for further study and research of ancient Chinese language, literature, history, philosophy and other aspects of knowledge, and to better inherit the excellent culture of the motherland.

Name: Modern and Contemporary Chinese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course aims to outline the relationship between modern literature and modernity by explaining literary activities in the history of modern and contemporary Chinese literature since the 20th century, combined with the analysis of important writers and iconic literary phenomena, and how this literary modernity practice participates in changing the cultural life of modern China.

Name: Chinese Reference Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is divided into two parts: lecture and internship. The teaching part mainly introduces the characteristics and types of Chinese reference books, main sorting methods, how to find Chinese words, ancient and modern books, chapters and sentences, newspapers and periodicals articles, biographies, geographical documents, encyclopedia knowledge, historical events, etc. It also appropriately introduces the use of various Chinese reference books using modern information technology resources, and pays attention to the supplement and introduction of new reference books. The internship is to allow students to consult and use commonly used Chinese reference books in the form of homework after completing the content of each unit, so as to become familiar with and master the correct use of Chinese reference books and better serve learning and scientific research. Internships account for six credit hours, and the rest are lecture hours.

Name: Ancient Chinese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Systematically teach the history of literary development from the pre-Qin Dynasty to modern times, sort out the evolution of different literary genres, explain the causes of the formation of certain important literary phenomena, and explain important writers and works, so that students can have a preliminary understanding of the appearance of ancient Chinese literature.

Name: Ancient Chinese Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: It is proposed that the course be divided into a number of topics, providing a more systematic presentation of the main aspects of ancient Chinese culture and providing students with a basic understanding of the general framework, basic features and contemporary significance of ancient Chinese culture. This course focuses on the knowledge related to Chinese culture, while emphasizing awareness of the problems, comparative perspectives, contemporary perspectives, i.e. drawing from the historical phenomena of Chinese culture, focusing on comparisons of cultures, especially in Central Europe, and exploring the impact of Chinese culture on China ' s historical development and its contemporary values.

Name: Authentication and Conservation of Ancient Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Outline the history of the compilation, formation, printing, and circulation of ancient Chinese books, and deepen the understanding of Chinese book culture; through lectures and internships, students will have a preliminary understanding of the methods of ancient book identification, a preliminary understanding of the styles of ancient books in different periods, and cultivate students' interest in working on ancient books in the future.

Name: Studies in Dream of the Red Chamber
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Basic course in ancient Chinese literature history
Introduction: The course will introduce the relationship between Cao Xueqin's family background and the creation of "A Dream of Red Mansions" and the main versions of "A Dream of Red Mansions". It will focus on exploring the reasons for the creation of "A Dream of Red Mansions" from the perspective of literary history. It will elaborate on the social significance of the description of the love and marriage of the aristocratic family and Bao Daichai in "A Dream of Red Mansions" and discuss the image creation of the main characters in the book. It will also analyze the artistic characteristics of "A Dream of Red Mansions" from the aspects of the combination of narrative and lyricism, details and psychological description. At the same time, some important debates in the study of "A Dream of Red Mansions" are reviewed.

Name: Foundations of Classical Philology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: It is a discipline that collates and researchs Chinese traditional ancients, so that undergraduates learn the most basic knowledge of classical literature.

Name: Studies in Qu (Chinese Verse for Song)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course combines traditional music theory and takes the music styles that were widely created by literati in the Yuan, Ming and Qing dynasties as the object of study and analysis. On the basis of the text, it introduces the emergence of music styles, their popularity, different styles and characteristics, the maturity of drama and the classification of themes.

Name: Peking University and a Century of China
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Peking University is the earliest comprehensive national university in China. Since its founding, the fate of Peking University has been closely linked to the fate of the entire China. For more than a hundred years, Peking University has witnessed the ups and downs of China's history, and has always been at the center of China's ideological, cultural and political struggles. Peking University was once the cradle of China's New Culture Movement and the birthplace of the "May Fourth Movement". It was also the earliest major site for the spread of socialism and the promotion of "Mr. De" and "Mr. Sai" in China. Almost every important ideological, cultural and political movement over the past century will have a corresponding response at Peking University. Yan Fu, Cai Yuanpei, Chen Duxiu, Hu Shi, Lu Xun, Li Dazhao, Liu Bannong, Deng Zhongxia, Shao Piaoping, Mao Zedong, Fan Wenlan, Feng Youlan, Jin Yuelin, Wei Jiangong, Jin Kemu and many other outstanding figures have taught, studied or worked at Peking University. Thanks to the sincere efforts of teachers and students of all generations, Peking University has passed on the torch and continued to sing, and has become an institution of higher learning with the most complete education, the most active thinking, and the most developed culture in China over the past century. _x000D_
_x000D_
The purpose of this course is to help our students become familiar with the history and culture of Peking University and understand the historical context and trajectory of the formation of the "Peking University Spirit". This course does not seek to be comprehensive. It will focus on thematic discussions on important historical figures and major events that have emerged at Peking University over the past hundred years from the perspectives of education, literature, culture, and political thought. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Contemporary Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a close reading course on contemporary poetry, dedicated to a detailed and multi-layered discussion and analysis of contemporary poetry in the 1980s. Combined with specific poems, it shows the development and main characteristics of contemporary poetry. And through the interpretation of specific works, we make corresponding evaluations on the relationship between contemporary poetry and the new poetry tradition, the main aesthetic goals of contemporary poetry, and the basic issues of contemporary poetry.

Name: Readings in the Classics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The subject is a selection of literature, history, intellectuals, linguistics, etc., in ancient writings, leading reading.

Name: Studies in Wartime Chinese Literature of the 1940s
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: In the 1940s, the war against Japan and the ensuing civil war of the Republic of China strongly shaped the shape and direction of China ' s new literature, and its inherent possibilities were fully released. The course is an attempt to return to the scene of “China during the war” and to examine the aesthetic dynamism and political potential of literature in the 1940s in dealing with the war and responding to historical challenges, using as a case study the writings of writers such as Shen, Ding Ling, Sardin, Xiao Hong, Zhiling, Feng Zhilong, Feng Zheng and Mudan.

Name: Studies in Ming and Qing Vernacular Novels
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will select and introduce several novels with relatively high artistic achievements in the Ming and Qing Dynasties. The main titles include: "The Three Treasures Eunuch", "Vinegar Gourd", "Journey to the West", "Continuing the Plum in the Golden Ping", " "The Story of a Marriage that Awakens the World", "The Words of a Wild Old Man", "Gu Wanyan", "The Wizard of Oz", "The Legend of Jin Yunqiao", "The Complete Story of Second Plum", "Yu Jiao Li", "Pingshan Leng Yan", "Flower Moon Traces", "He Dian", etc. This course will mainly introduce the current research status, publication and dissemination status, theme ideas and artistic characteristics of these novels, so that students can have a better understanding of the development of full-length novels in the Ming and Qing dynasties.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (I)
Introduction: This course is one of the most important basic courses for mathematics majors. The first volume mainly includes limit theory and univariate differential calculus. This course is the basis for mathematical analysis (II) (III), and is also the basis for many subsequent courses such as differential equations, differential geometry, complex variable functions, real variable functions, probability theory, basic physics, theoretical mechanics, etc. Mathematical Analysis (I) will provide an important course in training the basic abilities and thinking methods of college mathematics. Having a good foundation in mathematical analysis (I) plays a key role in future study and research.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (I) Problem Session
Introduction: This course is mainly a supporting course for Mathematical Analysis (I), providing problem-solving methods and techniques for basic exercises in limit theory and differential calculus of functions of one variable. This enables students to have a deep understanding and mastery of the content of Mathematical Analysis (I).

Name: Advanced Algebra (I)
Introduction: We will study specific objects in higher algebra: systems of linear equations, n-element column (row) vector spaces over the field of numbers (rational, real and complex numbers), determinants, operations on matrices, cancellation and similarity of matrices, diagonalization of matrices, contracts between quadratic forms and matrices, Witt's theorem, classification of real quadratic forms, positive definite quadratic forms. (Hermitian) inner product of n-ary column vector spaces over the field of real (complex) numbers.

Name: Geometry
Introduction: Geometry and its Exercises is the first geometry course offered by the School of Mathematical Sciences of Peking University (for all undergraduates in the school and some undergraduates in Yuanpei’s experimental class). It is one of the most important basic courses in our college. This course is responsible for the important task of cultivating students' geometric thinking and strengthening students' geometric quality. This course mainly introduces the theory of spatial analytic geometry. It also appropriately introduces the basic ideas of geometry, such as geometric invariants, and the relationship between groups and geometry. Use algebraic methods to discuss the geometric properties and invariants of space curves and surfaces. Connect graphics and equations organically. Specific contents include: vector algebra, planes and straight lines in space, common curved surfaces, coordinate transformations, simplification and properties of quadratic curve equations, orthogonal transformations and affine transformations, projective planes and projective transformations. Therefore, this course is not only an extension and expansion of the students' knowledge of plane analytic geometry, but also lays a solid foundation for students to take multivariable calculus, physics and other courses at the undergraduate level.

Name: Geometry Problem Session
Introduction: In the exercise class, the teacher reviews the essence of the course and explains the exercises and examples that match the course to strengthen the cultivation of students' geometric qualities; in terms of thinking methods, the main emphasis is on key points and ideas, inspiring and guiding students to observe, explore, guess and demonstrate on their own, so that students can actively and vividly learn the course content; in order to allow students to better master basic knowledge and understand students' learning situations in the course, we sometimes use the method of asking students to discuss and explain to cultivate students' innovative ability.

Name: Introduction to Computation
Introduction:
Basic Purpose: First course in computer science technology. The purpose of the first part of the course is to help students understand the basic principles of computers and master basic computer usage techniques. The course mainly discusses programming (using a mathematical software, such as Maple, Mathematica or Matlab). Through examples of various mathematical problems, it helps students deeply understand the process of solving mathematical problems using computers and calculations, and the characteristics of this problem-solving method; understand the basic concepts and basic methods of programming language and programming, and become initially familiar with a programming language and the basic process of programming. This course is a course that combines theory with practice. Students need to complete a small number of paper assignments and have 2 hours of computer programming practice every week. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Mathematical Analysis (II)
Introduction: This course is one of the most important basic courses for mathematics majors. Basic content includes integral calculus and series theory. This course is the basis for the study of Mathematical Analysis (III) and many subsequent courses such as differential equations, differential geometry, functions of complex variables, functions of real variables, probability theory, basic physics, theoretical mechanics, etc. Mathematical analysis is also an important course for training the basic abilities and thinking methods of college mathematics. Having a good foundation in mathematical analysis plays a key role in future study and research.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (II) Problem Session
Introduction: This course is mainly a supporting course for Mathematical Analysis (II), providing problem-solving methods and techniques for basic exercises in definite integrals and series theory. This enables students to have a deep understanding and mastery of the content of Mathematical Analysis (II).

Name: Advanced Algebra (II)
Introduction:
On the basis of advanced algebra (1), we talk about (1) one-variable polynomial rings, matrices on one-variable polynomial rings and their applications---Hamilton-Caylay theorem, minimal polynomials of matrices, discrimination of matrix similarity, and proof of the existence and uniqueness of the Jordan canonical form of matrices in the complex number field. (2) General linear spaces, linear transformations, matrix representations of linear transformations, linear transformation characteristic polynomials, the relationship between the factorization of minimal polynomials and the direct sum decomposition of invariant subspaces of linear transformations, the minimal polynomial discriminant method for diagonalizability of matrices, the second proof of the existence and uniqueness of the Jordan canonical form of matrices in the complex field; _x000D_
(3) Dual space. Dual space and dual basis, the transpose of linear mapping and the transposition of matrix, the natural isomorphism of linear space and its quadratic duality. _x000D_
(4) Bilinear mapping and metric space. Specifically, we will discuss bilinear types and their metric matrices, the equivalence of bilinear types and the contract of matrices, symmetric bilinear types, quadratic types and symmetric matrices, skew symmetric bilinear types and skew symmetric matrices, Euclidean spaces, symmetric transformations and orthogonal transformations, the Witt decomposition theorem of real orthogonal spaces, the general Witt decomposition theorem of orthogonal spaces, and the proof of Witt elimination theorem. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Japanese Culture and Art
Introduction:
As an integral part of world civilization, Japanese civilization was greatly influenced by Chinese civilization in ancient times, but Japan's original civilization was still formed spontaneously. Moreover, through historical refinement and improvement, it has formed the characteristics of its own national culture. When we explore the phenomena that are most characteristic of Japanese national culture, Japanese culture and art become particularly eye-catching. And understanding Japanese culture and art is a shortcut for us to understand Japan. _x000D_
This course will describe the essence of Japanese culture and art from the perspectives of history, folklore, and art to clarify the characteristics of Japanese aesthetic consciousness. Course content includes:_x000D_
1 Japanese fine arts (painting, gardens, architecture, crafts)_x000D_
2 Japanese opera (gagaku, noh, kyogen, kabuki)_x000D_
3 Japanese arts (tea ceremony, flower arrangement, incense ceremony)_x000D_
In order to help students understand the above content, the first two lectures of this course will briefly teach basic Japanese courses such as Japanese geography and nature, Japanese history, Japanese folk beliefs, and Japanese seasonal customs. Under appropriate circumstances, Japanese tea ceremony, flower arrangement, incense ceremony, and Noh art (only one of them will be shown each semester) will be demonstrated on-site to help students better understand the characteristics of Japanese culture, art, and aesthetic consciousness. _x000D_
This course will also organize some students to go to Japan every summer to investigate Japanese history and culture to help students deepen their understanding of the course content. _x000D_

Name: Mathematical Analysis (III)
Introduction: This course is one of the most important basic courses for mathematics majors. Basic content includes multivariable differential calculus and integral calculus. This course is the basis for many subsequent courses such as differential equations, differential geometry, complex variable functions, real variable functions, probability theory, basic physics, theoretical mechanics, etc. Mathematical analysis is also an important course for training the basic abilities and thinking methods of college mathematics. Having a good foundation in mathematical analysis (III) plays a key role in future study and research.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (III) Problem Session
Introduction: This course is mainly a supporting course for Mathematical Analysis (III), providing problem-solving methods and techniques for basic exercises in differential calculus and integral calculus of multivariate functions. This enables students to have a deep understanding and mastery of the content of Mathematical Analysis (III).

Name: Abstract Algebra
Introduction: Basic knowledge of abstracted generation mathematics. Group, ring, domain basic knowledge.

Name: General Biology (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Prerequisite:
None.
It's recommended that we choose General Biology Experiment.
Introduction: Life is the greatest creation of the universe, the most complex combination of chemical elements, and the most glorious way of existence of matter. Ordinary atoms, after being combined into a structure like a cell, can carry out independent material metabolism, energy conversion and information exchange. They can produce offspring that are similar but not identical to themselves. They live and evolve endlessly, forming a colorful biosphere on the earth. It is no exaggeration to say that life is the greatest miracle! How do these ordinary elements maintain the existence of life, how do they ensure the continuation of life, and how do they promote the evolution of life? This course will answer these questions one by one. This is a relatively comprehensive, professional, yet easy-to-understand answer. Each of us is a member of the big family of life, and we all contain the deepest mysteries of nature. Let us understand ourselves through "General Biology".

Name: History of Sino-Japanese Cultural Exchange
Introduction: The history of cultural exchanges between China and Japan is the most splendid part of the history of cultural exchanges between China and foreign countries. Its long history, extensive content, rich achievements, and far-reaching influence are among the best. The two-thousand-year history of Sino-Japanese cultural exchanges gave birth to the initiation of Japanese civilization and the formation of Japanese culture, and also enabled ancient Chinese civilization to be best promoted and protected outside the region. Today, the essence of ancient Chinese culture preserved in Japanese culture has become a database and copy of China's current process of revitalizing traditional culture. Therefore, researching and studying the history of Sino-Japanese cultural exchanges has great historical and practical significance. This course takes the history of Sino-Japanese cultural exchanges from ancient times to 1840 as the teaching content.

Name: English Literary Classics and Film
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
"English Classics and Movies" is a B-level college English course. This course is a comprehensive course that integrates knowledge of British and American literature, selected readings of British and American classics, appreciation of movies adapted from classics, and audio-visual training. Designed for non-English majors who are interested in British and American literature and want to further expand their existing literary knowledge and improve their existing language skills. _x000D_
    The purpose of this course is to effectively combine literature and film, two different art forms, so that non-English major students can have a general understanding of the development of British and American literature in a short period of time, stimulate students' interest in reading original English works, and improve their language proficiency and appreciation ability. _x000D_
    This course will systematically introduce to students the main stages and characteristics of the development of British and American literature, as well as the literary career, creative ideas, artistic characteristics of writers, as well as the themes, plot structures, characterizations, language styles, historical significance, etc. of representative works. The teaching content is mainly based on textbooks, and relevant knowledge will be supplemented and explained in class. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Probability Theory
Introduction: Probability is a measure that describes the likelihood of a random event occurring. Probability theory gradually enters the study of complex random phenomena through the study of simple random events. It is an effective method and tool for studying complex random phenomena. Probability theory is also the basis for learning statistics.

Name: Complex Analysis
Introduction: The underlying theory and methodology of a variable's multiple function.

Name: Ordinary Differential Equations
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, high algebra, geometric resolution
Introduction: Ordinary differential equations is an important basic course for all majors in the mathematics department of comprehensive universities, and it is also a mathematics course with strong application. The purpose of this course is to learn and master the basic knowledge of ordinary differential equations and prepare for subsequent courses (mathematical equations, differential geometry, functional analysis, etc.); through interspersed examples (especially famous examples that successfully used differential equations to explain practical phenomena in history), students will develop their awareness and preliminary ability to use mathematical theories to solve practical problems.

Name: Research-Based Learning
Introduction: The purpose of the course "Research Study" is to hope that students can understand the entire process of research work through this course, thereby increasing their enthusiasm for learning and preparing themselves for undergraduate scientific research and future research work. The course content includes topic selection, that is, raising and condensing questions, conducting research or solving problems, using latex software to write a standardized mathematics and applied mathematics article, simulating the review process of international mainstream academic journals to mutually evaluate and revise the paper, and finally presenting the results of one semester's research and learning in the form of an academic report.

Name: Reflections on the Sociology of Education
Introduction: This course is open to undergraduates from all majors in the school. It specializes in introducing the general knowledge, methods and theories of educational sociology by learning the basic principles of sociology. Conduct special analysis and discussion on educational phenomena as social issues and contemporary education focus issues, and try to use sociological theories to think and explain.

Name: Introduction to Financial Mathematics
Introduction: This course will focus on basic mathematical models and methods in financial calculation analysis. Specifically, it includes: basic concepts and methods of interest calculation, calculation of annuity cash flow model, basic methods of calculation of general investment return rate, principal and interest decomposition process of cash flow, fixed income securities, interest risk analysis, calculation of financial income in random situations and other basic issues in financial mathematics.

Name: Mathematical Statistics
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, high algebra, probability theory
Introduction: Mathematical statistics is a widely used basic discipline. It mainly studies methods for scientific analysis and processing of random samples, including how to effectively collect data, how to estimate parameters, how to perform tests, how to study the relationship between variables, and how to make statistical decisions, etc. As the most basic professional course in statistics, its main purpose is to enable students to master the basic concepts and basic statistical ideas of this subject through teaching, and to have the ability to use commonly used statistical methods in conjunction with the knowledge of mathematics and probability theory in prerequisite courses to solve some practical problems, to initially understand the new developments in mathematical statistics research and to initially establish a statistical way of thinking.

Name: Real Analysis and Functional Analysis
Prerequisite: Advanced Math B, linear algebra, constant differential equation
Introduction: Learn and master the basic knowledge of Lebesgue measure space, Lebesgue integral, Hilbert space and Banach space, cultivate students' ability to understand abstract function spaces from geometry and topology, cultivate students' in-depth analysis ability, and cultivate students' ability to use abstract space as a tool to research and solve problems.

Name: Computer-Assisted Translation and Writing
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The characteristic of this course is that it teaches the process of translation and writing, recognizes the intrinsic connection between translation and writing as a second language, and introduces computer assistance to greatly improve the speed and level of students' translation and writing. By introducing computer software tools commonly used in translation and writing, such as Trados, Yaxin, etc., and by introducing translation memory, students can train translation memory tools in practice, and in the process build their own translation terminology database and sentence pair database, and use these tools to improve their translation ability and level. In terms of writing, it focuses on practical stylistic writing and briefly introduces how to encourage students to try creative writing on the basis of proficiency in practical writing skills. The style of teaching practical writing will be divided into letters, chart descriptions, reports, resumes, etc. according to the genre; according to the writing purpose, it will be divided into students' applied writing (including CET level 4/6, TOEFL, IELTS, GRE, etc.), study abroad application documents, etc. Creative writing includes simple narratives, prose, and simple poetry. In this process, tools such as English writing assistants and parallel corpora are introduced to help students improve the accuracy and level of writing, striving to enable students to write English practical essays with correct grammar, clear meaning, and fluent language before graduating from college, and on this basis, cultivate the feeling and interest in writing other literary styles in English.

Name: Mathematical Models
Introduction: Against the background of some typical examples in the fields of physics, ecology, environment, medicine, management, economy and information technology, the course describes how practical problems can be studied and resolved through the development of mathematical models. It highlights the background and mathematical substance of common algorithms. At the same time, the self-study and innovation skills of students are being developed and enhanced, and students are being encouraged to look for problems in their lives, to develop appropriate mathematical models and to solve them, and to learn from modelling practices.

Name: Securities Investment
Introduction: The securities investment course focuses on introducing how to use mathematical models to analyze related portfolio selection issues and investment performance evaluation issues encountered in securities investment. It mainly includes quantitative models such as the Markowitz asset portfolio model, capital asset pricing model, and arbitrage pricing model. This allows you to initially master the quantitative analysis methods of securities investment analysis in financial mathematics.

Name: Fundamentals of Derivative Securities
Prerequisite: Primary probability theory, mathematical statistics, calculus, linear algebra
Introduction:
_x000D_
This course is mainly taught to senior undergraduate students majoring in financial mathematics, and is designed to allow students to understand the basic knowledge of basic financial derivatives. The content of the course includes the concepts, principles, pricing methods and practical applications of derivatives such as forwards, futures, swaps and options contracts. Specifically, it includes the definition of the above products, market mechanism and hedging strategy, arbitrage pricing method, Black-Scholes-Merton model of option pricing, binary tree model, and basic numerical methods. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Investment Funds
Introduction: Investment funds are a wide range of investment vehicles accessible to households and institutional investors. The industry has grown rapidly over the past three decades. Investment funds are one of the largest investment vehicles in the global capital and money markets, with a scale of trillions. This course introduces undergraduate students to the three basic categories of investment funds: mutual funds, hedge funds, and private equity funds. It is expected that students will have a good understanding of the management of investment funds and fund investment techniques through the study of this course.

Name: Career Planning for University Students
College: Student Affairs Department, People's Armed Forces Department
Introduction: The course content runs through the entire process of university education. It is mainly used to guide students to understand themselves and the external work world objectively and accurately, to help students scientifically position their career development direction and formulate career planning plans that suit their actual situation; to guide students in school to engage in internships and quality development activities related to their own career development direction, so that students can gain perceptual knowledge of professional positions and certain practical work abilities, thereby laying a good foundation for future job selection and career development.

Name: Survey of Spanish Culture
Introduction: This course aims to enable students to master the main characteristics of Spanish culture and have a basic understanding of Spanish history, social culture and other conditions. The study of the course will help students engage in China-Spain economic, trade, cultural, educational and other exchanges in the future. By studying this course, students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding of the specific manifestations of Spanish architecture, art, customs and other cultures. Although this course is taught in Chinese, it will also teach Spanish vocabulary and sentences that are frequently used in cross-cultural communication to help students avoid friction and conflicts caused by cultural differences when interacting with Spanish people.

Name: Applied Multivariate Statistical Analysis
Introduction:
Introduction and Introduction (2 lessons)_x000D_
   Application of multivariate statistical analysis, .Graphic representation of multivariate statistical data_x000D_
Multivariate normal distribution and parameter estimation (6 lessons)_x000D_
   Random vectors, the definition and basic properties of multivariate normal distribution, conditional distribution and independence_x000D_
   Normal distribution of random arrays, parameter estimation of multivariate normal distribution_x000D_
Hypothesis testing of multivariate normal population parameters (6 lessons)_x000D_
   Distribution of several important statistics, test and confidence region of single population mean vector_x000D_
   Test of multiple population mean vectors, test of covariance matrix, independence test, normality test_x000D_
Discriminant Analysis (6 lessons)_x000D_
    Distance discrimination, Bayesian discrimination method and generalized square distance discrimination method, Fisher criterion_x000D_

Name: Applied Stochastic Processes
Introduction:
This is a required professional course for undergraduates in the School of Mathematics. It is a follow-up course to "Probability Theory" and introduces the most basic types of random process models and their properties, such as random walks, Markov chains, jump processes, Poisson processes, Brownian motion, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
A random process is a family of random variables defined in the same probability space, where the indicator set is usually one-dimensional and interpreted as time. The sequence of independent and identically distributed random variables discussed in probability theory is a random process. There are a large number of examples of random processes in natural sciences, economic activities and daily life. For example, the time and magnitude of an earthquake in a certain place, the daily trading volume of the stock market, the number of customers waiting at a certain service point, etc. If you pay attention, random processes are everywhere. Many random processes have different names due to their special properties, such as Markov process, stationary process, Gaussian process, second-order moment process, etc._x000D_
_x000D_
In order to show that a certain proof method has a wider scope of application, in 1906 the Russian mathematician Markov proposed a class of random processes with special properties, which later generations called Markov properties or Markov properties. Random processes with Markov properties are called Markov processes, or Markov processes for short. Random walks, Poisson processes, Brownian motions, etc. are all Markov processes, which are mathematical abstractions of some specific examples. It has wide applicability and is also the main content of the course "Applied Stochastic Processes"._x000D_
_x000D_
Like other disciplines, stochastic process theory has both intuitive background guidance and rigorous logical derivation. Our original intention is to show more of the intuitive background of stochastic processes, and leave the rigorous derivation based on the basis of measure theory in the subsequent graduate course "Stochastic Process Theory". In many cases, we only use simple and intuitive random events such as throwing dice to describe, but accurate and rigorous expressions are still inseparable from the probability space hidden behind it. By the way, the "application" in the course title is just used by the Department of Probability and Statistics of Peking University to indicate that this is an undergraduate course to distinguish it from graduate courses in the same direction. We firmly believe that stochastic process theory can be used to describe, understand, and solve practical problems. We hope that through studying, students can initially understand and master the basic knowledge of stochastic process theory, and think that stochastic process theory is both interesting and useful like us.

Name: Game Theory and Society
Introduction: The cross-cutting theme of the course is: How can humankind work better together? Society is made up of people, and society exists by and for people. As rational individuals, we each have our own interests and are pursuing our own happiness. It is by nature, and nothing can change. But progress in society can come only from mutual cooperation among people, and only through cooperation can it bring win-wins and happiness to everyone. That is our collective reason. However, decision-making based on individual rationality often conflicts with collective rationality, leading to the emergence of so-called “prisoner dilemmas” that are detrimental to the well-being of all. In addition to individual interests, another important reason preventing people from working together is our limited knowledge. Even today, despite the fact that human knowledge of the laws of nature has increased significantly and has truly been achieved “in nine days, but in five years”, our knowledge of the human race itself is still insufficient for us to understand the best way to pursue happiness. It is relatively easy for ordinary people to accept knowledge of the natural sciences, but it is difficult to accept knowledge of social sciences. We are short-sighted, arrogant, narrow, self-righteous and know only that we do not know it, and often do not understand what our real interests are. It is our ignorance that has led to many conflicts in human society. Many seemingly beneficial conflicts are actually conflicts of ideas. In fact, most of the shameless behaviour that harms people is also essentially the result of ignorance. The harmdoers think they are maximizing their well-being, but often the result is “smart” and “smart” to their own detriment. Some people are good in their hearts and care for the well-being of others, but ignorance is also a disaster for humanity. The planned economy is a typical example. Fortunately, as the only rational animal on Earth, human beings have not only natural creativity, but also the ability to “take a long head”. In a long history, human progress has been achieved through the invention of a variety of technologies, institutions and cultures, overcoming obstacles to prisoners ' plight and moving towards cooperation. Innovations such as words, words, words, property rights, money, prices, companies, profits, laws, social norms, values, ethical standards, even clocks, computers, networks, etc., are important means for humanity to emerge from the plight of prisoners and to achieve cooperation. Of course, each of the advances brought about by cooperation has been accompanied by the emergence of new prisoners ' plight. The Internet, for example, provides a space for greater human cooperation, but it also offers new opportunities for kidnapping. A history of human civilization is a history of the constant creation of prisoners' plight and their emergence from it. Human cooperation and progress cannot be made without the contributions of some great thinkers. Two thousand years ago, the Axis era saw the emergence of such great thinkers as Confucius, Mirgasoni, Aristotle and Jesus. They have set the foundations of human civilization by making the world a place for themselves. Their thoughts reduce human ignorance, become the core and pillar of future generations ' ideas and continue to affect our ways of behaviour and way of life. Economics is only 238 years old, starting with Adam Smith's State Richness. But the contribution of economics to the spirit of human cooperation and the rise in moral standards is enormous. Adam Smith proved, on the basis of rational human assumptions, that markets were the most effective means of working with people. Today, we see that the spirit of cooperation and the moral standards of countries that truly follow Adam Smith's philosophy and operate a market economy are much higher than those of non-market economies. Perhaps the most outstanding achievement in the scientific field of society as a whole since the middle of the twentieth century has been the development of game theory. The game theory examines how rational people make decisions in an interactive environment. The game theory is called “non-cooperative game theory”. Such a name can easily be misinterpreted among non-professionals as teaching people how not to cooperate. This is a pity. Indeed, the game theory is really concerned with how to promote human cooperation. The prisoner dilemma model provides us with ideas on how to overcome the prisoner dilemma. Only by understanding why people do not cooperate can we find effective ways to promote cooperation. Society is the interaction between people: when one makes decisions, one must consider not only what choices one has, but also what choices others have, because no one's behaviour is given and what everyone gets is the result of what everyone chooses. This is true not only of individuals, but of all organizations such as business, government, state, etc. The interaction between people creates a variety of social systems (including laws, cultures, etc.) that are known as social rules of the game. Game theory is a discipline that studies and predicts the behaviour of individuals and organizations in situations of interaction and the formation and evolution of these rules of the game. Initially developed by mathematicians, after decades of efforts by economists, it has become the main research methodology in economics and is becoming the methodological basis for the whole of society ' s science, widely applied in areas such as economics, law, politics, anthropology, sociology and history. The game theory is a way of thinking, and although its research is applied to some deep mathematics, the basic idea of the game theory is very intuitive. In this course, I will start with some examples of life by gradually introducing the basic concepts of game theory, so that students learn to analyse real economic and social problems using game methods. I will pay particular attention to the evolution of rules of interpretation (social system) from the formation of customs, social norms and laws. The course is intended for undergraduate students in the second and third grades of the entire humanities and social sciences, including sociology, law, history, politics, economics and management. This course is also suitable for scientific and technical students. Of course, students taking this course must be curious about social issues. The option does not require prior training in the economics base. In order to be theoretically rigorous and save space, some mathematical formulas and graphs will be used in the course, but I will try to keep the use of mathematical tools to the minimum necessary, and it should not be difficult for any student who has studied primary mathematics to take the course.

Fourth, pay attention to the comparison of Chinese and Western music cultures, especially conduct special research on the impact of romantic music on modern Chinese music; fifth, make full use of the convenience of the Internet in retrieving music cultural information, encourage and organize students to search for cutting-edge information, and open special forums. Name: Chinese Rhetoric
Introduction:
The ancients once said: "People don't have words, so they can use them... The reason why people use words is to respect the emperor and protect the country. Therefore, words must be cultivated, and speech must not be bad." "The most important thing is to establish virtue, then there is meritorious service, and then there is speech. Although it will not be abolished for a long time, these are called three immortals." It can be seen that "building speech" was regarded by the ancients as one of the three major pursuits in life, and the core of "building speech" is rhetoric. _x000D_
     Rhetoric is an ancient yet young subject, born in ancient Greece in the fifth century BC. It was once one of the three major school education courses in the Middle Ages (grammar, rhetoric, logic). In the 20th century, rhetoric became a prominent discipline in the United States. Our country's rhetorical thought originated in the sixth century BC. The history of human development shows that rhetoric is not only a language use phenomenon that selects pronunciation, words, sentence patterns, figures of speech, etc., but also is not only a use of language, music, pictures, images, architecture, environment and other media symbols involving hearing, vision, touch, etc. to construct effective texts and spread information to influence and change other people's emotions, attitudes, thoughts, concepts and even Social behavior and social phenomena of social behavior are also a human communication phenomenon, a human communication order and social order, a way and method of constructing public power and public order, handling social affairs, and formulating public policies. It is a system of social fairness and justice, a human lifestyle, and a cultural tradition and cultural form. Rhetoric is a landscape, an artistic conception, and a pursuit of life. Life is inseparable from rhetoric, and rhetoric is a required course in life. _x000D_
      "Chinese Rhetoric" teaches the basic knowledge and theory of Chinese rhetoric, including the basic concepts of rhetoric, the structure and function of various rhetorical devices and rhetorical methods, style, rhetorical rules, rhetorical principles, as well as the skills and methods of discourse organization, discourse understanding, and discourse coordination. It summarizes the history, current situation and development trend of Chinese rhetoric research. Through the teaching of theoretical knowledge of Chinese rhetoric, this course strives to enable students to grasp the rules of Chinese rhetoric, enhance rhetorical communication skills, improve language expression, discourse understanding and rhetorical appreciation, enhance the ability to use language for social and interpersonal regulation, improve social adaptability and overall quality, while enriching students' knowledge structure, cultivating their basic qualities, expanding their theoretical horizons, and improving their academic literacy. _x000D_

Guoxue is the collective name for my country’s traditional academic culture, and classics such as The Book of Songs, The Book of Rites, The Book of Changes, The Historical Records, Zizhi Tongjian, The Analects of Confucius, and Laozi are the most important parts of Chinese culture. Name: The Earth's Environment and Human Society
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Secondary mathematics, English, language, physics, chemistry
Introduction:
"Earth Environment and Human Society" is a school-wide elective course that can be taken by students regardless of arts or science. The course summarizes the development process and achievements of human society, specifically analyzes the use and impact of human society development on water, atmosphere, and land in nature, and introduces in detail the changes and impacts on the global environment caused by various processes required for social development such as energy and raw material production, infrastructure construction, production and processing of food and daily necessities, and the manufacturing and use of transportation tools. The course discusses the current environmental governance measures and their effectiveness, explores the problems that can be improved or yet to be solved, and constructs some feasible green recycling governance measures. _x000D_
      At this stage, people's understanding of the concept of environmental protection is very important, and there are many people who are willing to practice it. In order to comprehensively improve the global environment and achieve sustainable development of human society, the course provides an objective description of the living environment conditions in cities and rural areas, discusses the recycling and reuse methods of waste in daily life and the efforts that individuals can make for environmental protection, and proposes practical methods for public participation in environmental protection and governance. What aggravates environmental pollution is our improper handling of daily waste. Therefore, the course proposes specific implementation plans for waste classification and recycling, explains the feasibility of avoiding pollution from the source, gives various current methods of waste treatment and ways of recycling waste, and focuses on the use of enzyme decomposition to transform waste. This is a low-cost, practical and feasible treatment method that everyone can participate in, so as to mobilize everyone's enthusiasm. _x000D_
      The teaching format of this course is a combination of classroom lectures and student discussions. The course content is basically related to real life or can be found online. Students who enter Peking University through the college entrance examination will not have any difficulty in understanding. The classroom lectures introduce the key points of the course content, present arguments based on the content, encourage students to interact, stimulate students' interest in active discussion and enthusiastic participation, and guide students to deepen their understanding of environmental pollution and management through discussion and practice. After each class, open-ended assignments related to the content of the class are arranged. The environmental issues involved in the class content are deepened by reviewing relevant information, and the consequences of these problems, treatment plans and efficiency are analyzed and summarized, and feasible and low-cost treatment plans are conceived. The homework for each class will be discussed in the next class on the better management plan proposed, and then the new content will be taught. _x000D_
      In addition to classroom content lectures and homework discussions, there are also visits and internships. The visit lasts for 4 hours and takes students to visit ecological parks or environmental protection research institutes, allowing students to feel the physical and mental effects of a good environment and showing them the importance and feasibility of pollution control. The experiment lasts for 2 hours, and involves actual hands-on production of the enzyme decomposition method mentioned in the course content. Such an experiment, on the one hand, cultivates students' hands-on ability, and on the other hand, arouses students' interest in conducting in-depth research, hoping to inspire more people to contribute to environmental protection. The final assessment takes 4 semester hours and is mainly conducted in the form of a course paper. The topic is self-written and does not limit each student's space for performance, but it must be related to the theme of the global environment and human society. _x000D_

Name: Meaning and Usage of English Vocabulary
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
"English words, sense and use" is a module B course, which is a highly practical English vocabulary learning course. It mainly introduces the meaning of words, the relationship between words and meanings, and the role of word meanings in context. This part of knowledge focuses on exploring the role of lexical meaning in discourse, the relationship between lexical cohesion and discourse coherence, and includes three parts. _x000D_
_x000D_
First, the relationship between vocabulary and meaning. This part involves the five major relationships in vocabulary meaning: polysemy, homonym or homonym, synonymity, antonym, and so on. The polysemy relationship of a word means that when a word first appears, it is only used as the name of a certain thing, phenomenon, property or behavior, so it has a single meaning. In the process of language development, it gradually acquires new meanings, forming a polysemy relationship of words. Polysemy is the result of changes in word meaning. It can be divided into original meaning and derived meaning, central meaning and secondary meaning, and the way words change. Homograph or homonym relationship means that words have the same shape or pronunciation but different meanings. Synonymous relationship refers to the relationship between words that express the same logical concept. Synonyms have the same meaning but different usage. The phenomenon of synonyms in English is very common, but synonyms are complicated. This part includes the origin of synonyms and the differences between synonyms. Antonym refers to the opposite or antagonistic relationship between the meanings of words. Including relative antonyms, complementary antonyms, and transposition antonyms. The five major relationships of vocabulary meanings give students a complete overview, definition, change and development of English vocabulary meanings. When students have a comprehensive understanding of word meanings, their use and choice of words will be justified. This part of knowledge can improve students' ability to use English vocabulary. _x000D_
_x000D_
Second, the matching relationship. The second purpose of course teaching is to help students enhance their awareness of collocations, use vocabulary accurately and improve their writing skills. There is no way to learn English collocation by yourself, because it is relatively difficult and is the basis for writing words and sentences. This is one of the reasons why English writing has become one of the most difficult learning tasks for students among the four major skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing. In English, syntactic rules are obvious and can be summarized, while collocation rules are implicit and cannot be logically analyzed or deduced from the combination of words. There is freedom and arbitrariness in collocation, which is difficult to predict, and collocation is everywhere. Wrong matching of word meanings is the direct cause of writing failure. Effectively solving students' difficulties requires teaching through curriculum. _x000D_
_x000D_
Third, the relationship between word meanings in context. The third teaching goal of the course mainly explores the relationship between the cohesion of vocabulary meanings and discourse coherence, as well as the role of vocabulary meanings in discourse and context. This part of the content includes the relationship between context (linguistic context, situational context, cultural context, pragmatic context), coherence, lexical cohesion and discourse coherence. The relationship between word meanings in context can not only improve students' ability to find logical relationships during reading, but also improve students' ability to plan text layout during writing_x000D_
