Introduction: By introducing the inseparable but often unknown relationship between music and mathematics, this course aims to explore the connection between music, an abstract art, and mathematics, as well as physics, psychology and other subjects, compare the similarities and differences between the two thinking methods, open up the boundaries between arts and science, improve students' artistic accomplishment and analytical ability, and ultimately achieve the purpose of improving students' comprehensive quality. It is precisely because of this consideration that the course design does not require students to have prerequisite courses in music or mathematics. Instead, as the teaching progresses, some music theory knowledge and mathematics knowledge that are directly related to the course content are gradually introduced. In terms of music, students will start from scratch, first introducing the most basic music theory knowledge such as musical sound system, note names and roll call, and staff notation, and then gradually teach intervals, scales, modes, chords, and harmony progressions, until modern musicology's pitch-class set theory, neo-Riemannian theory, etc. In terms of mathematics, only a high school mathematics level of knowledge is assumed. We try our best to introduce the geometry, algebra (group theory), combinatorial counting and other aspects that need to be used in a more detailed and intuitive way. If you have studied advanced mathematics, it will definitely be helpful to understand the course content. But even listeners who have not studied advanced mathematics can still understand the close connection between music and mathematics and some related mathematical ideas and methods through this course. In fact, the mathematical knowledge corresponding to the more difficult parts of music theory, such as temperament, harmony, etc., is not complicated, mainly proportions (fractions), logarithms, etc. As for mathematics (including some acoustics) content such as solutions to wave equations and Fourier series, the corresponding musical phenomena are relatively easy to understand, such as the relationship between pitch and string length, overtone series, timbre, etc.

Name: Optics Seminar
Introduction: The main teaching content is the expansion of the basic knowledge taught in the optics course, the latest frontiers of optical research, and new applications in other disciplines, deepening students' understanding of basic knowledge, improving their ability to independently solve problems, mastering cutting-edge trends in scientific research, and inspiring innovative thinking. The teaching method is mainly based on student discussion, and the teacher inspires and guides the discussion.

Name: Quantum Mechanics Problem Session
Introduction: Quantum mechanics.

Name: Chinese Character Tai Chi and Health Cultivation
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. The Chinese character Tai Chi refers to the concept of Tai Chi, which is based on the rise, fall, opening and closing of human body hardware, the rise and fall of software Qi and the expansion and contraction of consciousness, with the transformation of yin and yang as the general outline. Achieve the dynamic balance of body, mind, spirit and wisdom of the human body, and the harmonious state of the six roots of eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body and mind. Tai Chi with Chinese characters integrates culture, self-cultivation, music, and innovation. It is a traditional sports event that combines culture, philosophy, and artistry. _x000D_
This course is taught by words and deeds; 25 minutes before each class, read classic works and textbooks; classics such as the University, the Tao Te Ching, the Diamond Sutra, and the Heart Sutra. After reading, students are required to discuss each chapter for 5 minutes; students should combine their own study and life during the discussion. The teacher asks questions for 5 minutes. The teacher raises questions and the whole class discusses them together. Teach by example; the teacher teaches the structure of the inter-body frame and the same teacher builds the frame for each student. Teach the basic movements of Tai Chi in Chinese characters (hands, eyes, body, methods, steps, basic strokes, simple Chinese characters, basic strokes of Chinese characters and the coordination of hands, eyes, body, methods, and steps). _x000D_
Through the study of Chinese character Tai Chi and health care classes, students can understand the relationship between words and deeds, learn about traditional national sports, and organically combine students' morality, intelligence, body and beauty to achieve the purpose of self-cultivation. _x000D_
Through the study of Chinese Tai Chi and health care classes, students can establish a correct outlook on life and values, grasp the status of their own lives, and make students aware of the constant lack of desire to see its wonders; the constant presence of desire to see its application in life. _x000D_
Through the study of Chinese character Tai Chi and health preservation, students can improve their physical flexibility, coordination, and flexibility to achieve the purpose of improving health, stimulating vitality, and pleasing the body and mind. _x000D_
Through the study of Chinese character Tai Chi and health preservation, students can write different Chinese characters and practice different routines every day according to their emotional changes. This allows everyone to find their own form of exercise based on their own physiological conditions and characteristics. _x000D_
2. Safety precautions_x000D_
(1) Wear loose clothing (such as; traditional health clothing or sportswear)_x000D_
(2) Students are required to pay attention to their own physical safety. If they have chest tightness, palpitation, headache and other physical conditions, they should report it to the teacher. The teacher arranges according to the situation. _x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students' lifelong sports awareness and master the concepts of traditional national sports and the Chinese character culture system. _x000D_
2. Practicing practice to master and achieve accuracy, effectiveness and effort. _x000D_
3. Improve self-cultivation and improve one’s personality. _x000D_

Name: Modern Physics Laboratory (II)
Prerequisite:
General physics experiments, atomic physics.
It can be read at the same time as quantum mechanics, solid physics, nuclear physics and particle physics introductory.
Introduction: Modern Physics Experiment is a comprehensive experimental course for senior students majoring in physics. It is divided into two parts: Modern Physics Experiment I and Modern Physics Experiment II, which are started in the spring semester and autumn semester respectively. The content covers independent experimental projects and open research frontier physics experimental projects in the fields of atomic and molecular physics, nuclear detection technology and applications, lasers and modern optics, vacuum and thin film preparation, X-ray electron diffraction and structural analysis, magnetic resonance, microwave, low temperature and superconductivity, semiconductor physics, nonlinear physics, etc. Many of the experiments were Nobel Prize-winning experiments that played a milestone role in the development of modern physics. They are representative in terms of experimental methods and technologies. They also absorb the scientific research results of our school teachers. In recent years, large-scale scientific research-level instruments and equipment have been introduced, and experiments that reflect the cutting-edge of physical science have been added. In terms of experimental arrangements, students are exposed to technologies commonly used in modern physical experiments such as spectroscopy, vacuum, nuclear detection, low temperature, scanning probes, and weak signal detection. Each experiment also has certain physical content to improve students' ability to integrate theory with practice and solve practical problems. Students do seven independent experimental projects in different fields each semester. In the second semester, students with excellent grades in the first semester are allowed to choose open research-based cutting-edge physics experimental projects. _x000D_

Name: General Relativity
Prerequisite: Mathematic physics, advanced mathematics, theoretical mechanics, electrodynamics
Introduction: With the development of modern cosmology and space physics, general relativity has become increasingly important both scientifically and technologically. It is a course that theoretical physicists should be proficient in and is no longer independent of other physics courses. In this course, the basic principles, theoretical foundations and applications of general relativity will be introduced.

Name: Human Survival, Development and Nuclear Science
Introduction: Through this course of study, students not only acquire basic knowledge of contemporary nuclear science applications, unmask the “mysterious veil” of the atomic nuclei, have a correct understanding of radioactivity, can analyse the “pros and cons” of the use of nuclear technology, overcome blind “nuclear fears” and have the capacity to participate in general discussions on nuclear technology issues; but also have a deeper understanding of the research methods of the natural sciences, improve their scientific qualities and enhance their capabilities for scientific research and exploration.

Name: Solid State Physics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge and basic theories of solid-state physics, enabling students to understand and master the basic concepts and problem-solving methods of solid-state physics, laying a good foundation for further study, research and practical work. Course content includes: structural types of solids, crystal structures, lattice vibrations, thermal properties of crystals, defects in solids, phase changes, free electron theory of metals, energy band theory, movement of electrons in solids in electric and magnetic fields, transport properties of solids, etc. This course also partially covers some more specialized, currently important and active fields: such as semiconductor physics, superconductivity physics, surface physics, disordered systems, low-dimensional systems and mesoscopic system physics, etc.

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 1)
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the history of Western philosophy from Thales to Hegel, analyzes the origin and significance of various philosophical ideas and concepts, and lays a preliminary foundation for students to engage in further philosophical research in the future.

Name: Chemical Laboratory Safety Techniques
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
The laboratory is an important base for scientific research and talent training. It is also a place full of risks and frequent accidents. In particular, chemical laboratories use a variety of hazardous chemicals and electrical equipment, and often involve dangerous factors such as high temperature, high pressure, vacuum, radiation, magnetic fields, and strong light, which can easily cause safety accidents. Therefore, chemical experimenters should master solid laboratory safety knowledge and skills and have excellent safety qualities. _x000D_
    The School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering of Peking University has always attached great importance to laboratory safety work. In order to ensure that students can conduct chemical experiments safely and smoothly, in 1993, we were the first to offer chemical laboratory safety technology, a required course for chemistry majors, in domestic universities. In 2016, this course was included in the core courses of chemistry majors. _x000D_
    The teaching content of chemical laboratory safety technology includes laboratory safety facilities, fire safety, pressure vessel safety, electricity safety, hazardous chemicals, basic safe operations of chemical experiments, personal protection during experiments, emergency response to experimental accidents, laboratory hazardous waste disposal, etc. It not only covers general knowledge of science and engineering laboratory safety, but also has the characteristics of chemical laboratories. The course combines theoretical explanations with practical training, adopts flexible teaching methods, and focuses on the analysis of real hidden dangers in the laboratory. It aims to strengthen the safety awareness and responsibility of experimenters, teach safety knowledge, train safety skills, cultivate safety habits, and protect experimenters from enjoying the fun of chemistry in safety. _x000D_
_x000D_
    _x000D_

Name: Chemistry Today
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Chemistry Today is a compulsory course for first-year undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. The course covers eight secondary disciplines of chemistry, including inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry, chemical biology, applied chemistry, polymer chemistry, and theoretical and computational chemistry. Through typical literature reading, teacher lectures and student discussions, students can understand the research fields, research methods, and cutting-edge developments of each secondary discipline of chemistry, and have a preliminary understanding of the overall picture of today's chemistry discipline. At the same time, it guides students to develop the habit of active learning, improves students' ability to read literature, and to a certain extent cultivates students' habit of understanding the frontiers of the subject through independent literature review. In class, students are encouraged to think independently, dare to ask questions, and actively participate in discussions. _x000D_
    Today's chemistry courses are currently organized in the form of small class lectures and discussions. That is, eight teachers provide typical literature on related majors (including required readings and optional readings) in advance, and raise several questions about the fields covered by the literature that need students to discuss in class. At the beginning of the semester, the literature and discussion questions are compiled into handouts and distributed to students. Students are divided into eight groups, each group has 20 to 23 people, and each group is equipped with a teaching assistant. The content of each teacher's lectures is relatively fixed, and students listen to eight different lectures in a certain order. In classroom teaching, 50% of the time is used for teacher lectures and 50% for student discussions. _x000D_
    There is no exam in this course. The final grade of the semester is determined by a comprehensive evaluation of three aspects: attendance and class performance (30%), midterm paper (30%), and final paper (40%). _x000D_

Name: Sino-Soviet Relations and Their Impact on China's Social Development
Introduction: This course does not focus on general relations between countries, but takes the relationship between China and the Soviet Union as the vertical axis to show the ideological dispute between the two parties that transcends national interests, and analyzes and evaluates major theoretical issues related to this, revealing how the contradictions in the national interests of China and the Soviet Union and the ideological debates between the two parties influence and promote each other. In addition, this book pays more attention to the impact of such a complex Sino-Soviet relationship on the development of Chinese society. It attempts to explain the important reasons for the tortuous development of China in the first 30 years after the founding of the People's Republic of China from the perspective of Sino-Soviet relations, and then explains the premise and significance of building socialism with Chinese characteristics today.

Name: Organic Chemistry (I)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to organic chemistry, focusing on the reactions and properties of hydrocarbon compounds, various functional group compounds, and general heterocyclic compounds. This course introduces the Chinese and English nomenclature, structural characteristics, physical properties, spectral properties, main reaction properties and applications of organic compounds, laboratory and industrial preparation methods of various compounds, and systematically teaches various basic concepts and theories in organic chemistry, main organic reactions and reaction mechanisms, organic synthesis ideas, analytical methods of organic compounds and other knowledge content and scientific methods. Through the study of this course, students will systematically master the core knowledge content of organic chemistry, understand the development history of organic chemistry, and the development trends and application prospects in cutting-edge fields.

Name: Intermediate Analytical Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, general chemical experiments, quantitative analytical chemistry, quantitative analytical experiments
Introduction: This course is a follow-up course to the Quantitative Chemical Analysis Experiment, with a separate course of 30 hours and a credit. In the first few weeks of the course, students choose their own subjects of interest based on the subjects offered by the instructors. It can be a test object, experimenting with multiple analytical methods and comparing the advantages and disadvantages of different methods; it can also select multiple topics. Require independent access to information, independent design of programmes and independent testing. Schoolmates are encouraged to communicate with each other, especially those who do the same subject, and can discuss it in the course of their classes, and then design and implement their own programmes. The design laboratory report must be prepared independently and in a format that follows the form published in papers in specialized journals such as Analytical Chemistry.

Name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory (I)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Organic Chemistry Experiment (I+II) is a compulsory basic course for undergraduates in the School of Chemistry and Yuanpei College. The arrangement of the organic chemistry experiment course focuses on cultivating students with a rigorous scientific attitude and good laboratory work style, who can master the basic operations, skills and methods of organic experiments, and become professionals who can adapt to the needs of future development. Cultivate students to develop the habit of questioning and thinking, the habit of persevering despite difficulties, the habit of timely summary and diligent communication, so that students have good abilities of observation, analysis, judgment, expression and evaluation. _x000D_
The teaching content of the organic chemistry experimental course includes: learning basic operations; learning basic reaction devices, feeding methods, condition control, reaction post-treatment and product purification; proficiency in basic experimental techniques such as basic operations and reactions; flexible and rational use of various experimental techniques.

Name: Quantitative Analytical Chemistry Laboratory
Introduction: Quantitative analytical chemistry experiments are taught to undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. Through the study of this course, they can master the basic knowledge, basic operations and basic skills of quantitative analytical chemical experiments, as well as typical analysis methods and experimental data processing methods.

Name: Probability and Statistics (A)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Introduction to Information Science and Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is a lecture course. It is mainly taught by well-known professors from the main research directions of the School of Information Science and Technology on the development history, development status, basic knowledge and development trends of various disciplines of information science and technology. Through course study, students can have an overall and comprehensive understanding of various disciplines and fields included in the field of information science and technology; students will have a clear concept of computer software, computer architecture, computer theory, nanoelectronics, quantum electronics, communication technology, microelectronics, intelligent science and other disciplines.

Name: Introduction to Computation A
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: As one of the science courses with the widest coverage at Peking University, the "Introduction to Computing" course is based on Peking University's online teaching platform, relying on Peking University's National Computer Experiment Teaching Demonstration Center, and supplemented by multiple course websites with different professional characteristics to build a multi-level and open online teaching and experimental environment. Peking University's online teaching platform provides all teachers with a fully functional and stable online teaching and interactive platform, and provides students with a rich variety of teaching resources. Students can obtain the resources of the entire course online teaching environment and complete the course content steadily and solidly.

Name: Introduction to Computation A Computer Lab
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: New Year ' s course, which does not require a first course.
Introduction: This experimental class is a computer-based internship class in "Introduction to Computing A". It is a necessary part of the programming course and helps to understand algorithms and master programming methods. The main teaching goal is to complete the content taught in the "Introduction to Computing A" class through the online programming grid platform, practical programming training, and under the guidance of teaching assistants.

Name: Thermal Physics
Introduction: Thermal science is a course that enables physics students to systematically study and deal with the thermophysical properties of systems (gas, liquid, solid) composed of a large number of microscopic particles. Through the introduction and analysis of some basic physical phenomena, this course explains that following statistical laws is a basic characteristic of a system composed of a large number of particles. The course systematically and comprehensively introduces the basic concepts and the microscopic methods of applying statistical methods to deal with multi-particle systems. The course also introduces the macroscopic methods of summarizing the basic laws and basic concepts of thermodynamics through experimental observations. The main contents of the thermal science course include: equilibrium state and equation of state, the zero law of thermodynamics and temperature, the first law of thermodynamics, the second law of thermodynamics and its relationship with the development of modern science (such as cosmology), transport processes and main laws in gases, microscopic models of ideal gases, wheat Maxwell's speed and rate distribution law, particle distribution according to height and Boltzmann distribution, energy equipartition theorem according to degrees of freedom, statistical interpretation of the second law of thermodynamics and entropy, microscopic explanation of gas transport properties, vapor-liquid phase change, first and second type phase changes, molecular forces and non-ideal gases, etc.

Name: Electromagnetism
Introduction: Electromagnetism is part of classical physics. This course explains the basic experimental laws of electromagnetic interaction, and based on this, gradually reveals the objective characteristics, properties, internal connections and motion change rules of the electromagnetic field, a special form. Due to the ubiquity of electromagnetic phenomena and its wide range of technical applications, electromagnetism has become an important foundation for physics, other natural sciences, and technical sciences. The main contents of electromagnetism are: experimental laws of charge interaction, properties of electrostatic fields, conductors and dielectrics in electrostatic fields, basic laws of DC circuits and their applications, experimental laws of current interaction, properties of constant magnetic fields, movement of charged particles in magnetic fields, transformation of electromagnetic fields between different reference systems, electromagnetic induction and transient processes, magnetic media, basic laws of AC circuits and their applications, Maxwell's electromagnetic field theory and electromagnetic waves, and the electromagnetic unit system.

Name: American Culture and Society
Introduction: On the road to China's modernization, American factors have an all-round influence. An in-depth understanding of the United States has become an unavoidable issue for generations of people who have fought for the rise of China. In the modern history of the world, the founding and development of the United States are unique. How do you view the development trajectory of the United States? What is unique about America? What are America’s problems? What do Chinese people think of the United States? What do Americans think of China? Observing others is positioning yourself. The basic purpose of this course is to enable students to observe and analyze the United States from multiple perspectives such as politics, law, economy, society, history, and culture. This course is jointly taught by teachers from Peking University’s Department of History, Department of Philosophy, Department of Sociology, Law School, School of Art, Economic Center, School of Education, School of Foreign Languages, School of International Relations, and some departments from the School of Natural Sciences.

Name: Information Theory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Information theory is the basic theory about data representation, compression and transmission. This course focuses on the basic concepts and core theorems of information theory - entropy, mutual information, source coding theorem, channel coding theorem, as well as some applications of information theory in the field of artificial intelligence - Kolmogorov complexity, minimum representation length, and maximum entropy principle. These concepts and principles lay an essential foundation for students’ further study in machine learning, pattern recognition, signal processing and other fields.

Name: Programming Practicum
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The programming internship course is based on the basic programming course to cultivate students' practical abilities and good programming habits. Enable students to master a high-level language and be able to write standardized program codes, laying a good foundation for further study of other professional courses.

Name: Fundamentals of Microelectronics and Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: As a basic hardware platform course for information science and technology, this course mainly teaches general knowledge of microelectronics technology and circuit basics, including the working principles of semiconductor components, the design and manufacturing process of integrated circuits, the development of the microelectronics industry, the working mechanisms of common electronic systems, and the construction and analysis methods of simpler analog and digital circuits.

Name: Basic Circuits Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
"Basic Circuit Experiments" is a basic experimental course established by the School of Information Technology to improve undergraduate students' hands-on ability in circuits, familiarize themselves with commonly used instruments and equipment, and lay a solid foundation for electronic circuit learning and experimental research. It is a basic experimental course for various future courses and experiments related to electronic circuits. It is the first experimental course to gain a perceptual understanding of theoretical courses. This course will take the experimental skills of electronic circuits as the main line, based on 7 specific experiments, and introduce relevant knowledge and skills from shallow to deep. This course is for second-year undergraduates and takes place in the fall. It is the most basic course required for students in the School of Information Science and Technology. _x000D_
   It is required that students and readers who have not been exposed to electronic experiments can master the basic knowledge and basic skills of circuit experiments through experiments. Lay the foundation for future work, study and research in this field. For students and readers majoring in electronics, these experiments can be a basic knowledge and skill preparation before entering professional experiments. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course Features_x000D_
1) Focus on the basics: 7 experiments are carefully designed from the shallower to the deeper, starting from basic circuit welding training, understanding electronic components and circuit board diagrams, learning to use basic test instruments, to circuit construction, testing and experimental data processing. _x000D_
2) Focus on abilities: By designing some expanded experimental content, students can gradually learn to learn and think in experiments, and cultivate students' interest, quality and ability in circuit experiments. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Modern Electronics and Communications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Electronic Circuits (A)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: "Electronic Circuits" is a main basic course for undergraduates majoring in electronics and is listed as a required course. Content includes: commonly used semiconductor devices, basic amplifier circuits, feedback amplifier circuits, integrated operational amplifiers and applications, waveform generation and conversion, power amplifier circuits and DC power supplies, introduction to current mode circuits, etc.

Name: Introduction to Atomic Physics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Atomic physics, as a branch of physics, mainly studies one level of material structure. This level is between the levels of molecules and atomic nuclei. Like other levels, it must answer: What is this level composed of, how do these components move, and how do they interact. _x000D_
Introduction to Atomic Physics, as a preliminary introduction to the experiments and theories of atomic physics, mainly introduces the classic experiments and physicists in the field of atomic physics in the 20th century, as well as basic quantum theory, understands the development principle of "experiment-theory-experiment" in atomic physics, and learns to deal with simple atomic energy levels and configurations. _x000D_

Name: Optics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course covers wave motion, wave electromagnetic theory, light transmission, geometric optical, wave supercharge, oscillation, interference, distillation, Fourier optical, laser, etc.

Name: Methods of Mathematical Physics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics (mathematic analysis), linear algebra (high algebra), electromagnetics.
Introduction:
This course is offered by the School of Information. Students from the School of Physics and Yuanpei can also take it as an elective. This course includes analytic functions, series solutions to ordinary differential equations and integral transformation methods, Green's functions and delta functions, basic solutions to second-order linear partial differential equations, as well as the main properties and applications of basic special functions. In response to the needs of students in the School of Information, it appropriately strengthens the introduction of integral transformations and the specific applications of basic solutions to commonly used second-order linear partial differential equations. Therefore, it involves the content of advanced mathematics and general physics in the preparatory course, and is closely related to subsequent courses. _x000D_
    Through the study of this course, students are required to master the basic knowledge of complex variable function theory, understand several integral transformation methods (mainly Fourier transform and Laplace transform) and their applications in physics. Focus on mastering the establishment of mathematical physics equations and the establishment of definite solution conditions, especially learning to apply basic methods such as separation of variables to solve hyperbolic equations, parabolic equations and elliptical equations. At the same time, you will be familiar with some common special functions, such as Legendre polynomials, Bessel functions and spherical Bessel functions, etc., and understand their properties. _x000D_
    After studying, students can physically simplify and model basic transmission phenomena, and solve mathematical problems of general electricity, heat, magnetism, force, etc. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Circuit Analysis
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The "Principles of Circuit Analysis" course is an important basic circuit theory course for science and engineering students in colleges and universities. It is a high-quality course in Beijing. It is listed as a main basic course for undergraduates and a major platform course in schools at Peking University. It is a "seminar-based small class teaching" course for undergraduates piloted by the school. It is offered to second-year undergraduate students in the electronics direction of the School of Information Science and Technology. It has 5 hours per week, including 3 hours of large class teaching and 2 hours of small class discussion, with 4 credits. _x000D_
The main contents of the course include: basics of linear circuit analysis, time domain analysis, frequency domain analysis, basics of network analysis, network theorem, dual-port network analysis, chain network and transmission line, and nonlinear circuit analysis. _x000D_
"Principles of Circuit Analysis" is the first professional basic course for all majors in the electronics discipline. The basic concepts and basic methods described and studied in it are commonly used in all professional fields of the electronics discipline. It can be said that the basic laws followed by many major inventions are also described in this course. Therefore, the curriculum is basic and important. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Circuit Analysis Seminar
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Introduction to Environmental Materials
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Materials are the basis of human clothing, food, housing and transportation, and the development of materials is a symbol of human civilization. While people enjoy the various conveniences brought by materials, the development and production of materials also bring potential threats to human survival. This course starts from a new perspective, describing and evaluating the environmental impact of the entire life process of material production, processing, use and disposal, and how to evaluate, design and select materials to reduce the environmental load of materials. Specific contents include the basic concept of sustainable development, the requirements of sustainable development for environmental protection and material development; the relationship between material application and development and contemporary global environmental issues, the causes of contemporary environmental hot issues, control strategies and my country's actions to implement international environmental conventions; the environmental load analysis of materials; the general tool for environmental management "life cycle assessment method" and its application examples in material evaluation; the basic ideas of material recycling design and its important role in reducing environmental load; the evaluation and application of materials with the lowest environmental load, etc.

Name: Volleyball
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Volleyball is a collective confrontation event across the net that mainly uses hands to control the ball. Volleyball is called "flying ball in the air". Different groups of people can practice on different venues. In a volleyball game, one person cannot hit the ball continuously, so each participant needs to be integrated into the collective from emotion to behavior. Participating in volleyball can help cultivate an individual's psychological ability to grasp and control, and improve an individual's thinking agility, willpower, attention, imagery, prediction, athletic ability, interpersonal skills, and one's own coordination and flexibility. _x000D_
2． Safety Precautions_x000D_
(1) In volleyball class, you must wear sportswear and rubber soft-soled sports shoes that are convenient for movement. _x000D_
 (2) Students with short-sightedness should try to wear glasses with lighter resin in class. Girls with low blood sugar should bring some candy to class. _x000D_
 (3) It is prohibited to wear ornaments with angular stones in volleyball classes. _x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
_x000D_
  1. Teach the basic theoretical knowledge of volleyball and understand the emergence, development process and current situation, characteristics, development trends and trends of modern volleyball. _x000D_
  2. Learn and initially master the basic techniques, tactics and practical skills of volleyball. Understand the general organization and competition arrangements and on-the-spot refereeing methods of volleyball. _x000D_

Name: Electronic Circuits Laboratory (A)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The teaching purpose of Electronic Circuit Experiment (A) is to cultivate students' basic experimental skills and interests, develop scientific and orderly work habits, and at the same time understand some practical applications of electronic circuits and the progress of modern electronic technology, cultivate experimental skills that combine software and hardware, and lay a solid foundation for future scientific research work. _x000D_
The experimental content of this course is divided into two parts: circuit experiment and computer simulation experiment. Circuit experiments include transistor amplifiers, operational amplifiers, peak detectors, two-phase oscillators, LC voltage-controlled oscillators, complementary symmetrical power amplifiers, waveform generators, regulated power supplies, and analog phase-locked loops. Computer simulation experiments include feedback amplifiers, filters, Wien bridge frequency selective amplifiers, etc.

Name: Signals and Systems
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, multiple function, linear algebra
Introduction:
"Signals and Systems" is a core basic course for communications and signal processing majors. Many of its concepts and methods are widely used in many fields such as communications, automatic control, signal and information processing, circuits and systems. In recent years, with the continuous development of the theory and application of information technology, the concepts of signals and systems have gradually expanded. In addition to traditional majors, this course is affecting more and more other majors and fields. _x000D_
_x000D_
    In order to facilitate explanation and learning, this course can be roughly divided into two parts: signal analysis and system analysis. For each part, a variety of corresponding analysis methods can be derived, including time domain analysis, frequency domain analysis, complex frequency domain analysis and other types of effective analysis methods. The teaching purpose of this course is to enable students to understand various classic signal and system analysis methods and master some of the commonly used analysis methods and means; at the same time, it is also hoped that through the study of this course, students can further understand some related new theories and methods, and lay a solid foundation for their further study and development in the field of information technology in the future.	_x000D_

Name: Modern Physics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Digital Logic Circuits (Small Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
This course is a supporting small class class for "Digital Logic Circuits". _x000D_
It is divided into ordinary classes and experimental classes for separate teaching. Classroom discussions are conducted in small classes, and methods such as project research, student reports, and group discussions are introduced in the interactive process to enhance students' active learning ability. At the same time, in accordance with the teaching concept of "Learn By Doing", the number of hands-on design hours for students will be increased. The experimental class arranges 4 hours of HDL learning experiments and 12 hours of Project experiments. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Digital Logic Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Digitization is the current development trend of information technology and information industry that is changing with each passing day. It plays an important role in various electronic design systems such as communication equipment, digital entertainment, digital wearable devices, digital medical care, smartphones, smart TVs and Internet of Things systems. The course "Digital Logic Circuits" is an important basic circuit theory course for science and engineering students in colleges and universities. It is currently a national quality course and is listed as a backbone basic course for undergraduates at Peking University. It is a "seminar-based small class teaching" course for undergraduates piloted by the school. It is offered to second-year undergraduate students in the electronics major of the School of Information Science and Technology. It has 5 hours per week, including 3 hours of large class lectures and 2 hours of small class discussion, with 4 credits. _x000D_
In this course, on the basis of in-depth study of digital logic circuits and digital system design theory, students are proficient in the analysis and design methods of digital logic circuits. They are familiar with the functions and usage of various devices that make up digital systems, including SSI, MSI, MEMORY, ADC/DAC, CPLD and FPGA devices. They also learn the hardware description language VHDL and initially master the design methods of digital systems. _x000D_
This course focuses on the basic principles and methods of digital logic circuit analysis and design, as well as digital system design methods. Allow students to apply the principles and methods they have learned to understand and recognize common circuits, and cultivate students' independent thinking ability, scientific thinking methods and knowledge-seeking and innovative spirit. _x000D_

Name: History and Culture of Chinese Immigrants in America
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
Explore the history and cultural issues of Chinese immigrants in the United States by reading contemporary literature and other works and watching films. The main topics discussed include the history of Chinese immigrants to the United States, the culture and traditions of Chinese immigrants, and the integration of Chinese culture in the United States with other cultures. _x000D_
Students will discover some of the major issues in the history and culture of Chinese immigrants in the United States, and gain a certain understanding of some of the current issues in education and culture. _x000D_
This course aims to improve English proficiency through reading contemporary works. Through reading and discussion, students improve their language skills and broaden their horizons on Chinese American history and cultural issues. _x000D_

Prerequisite: General physics, electromagnetics, theoretical mechanics, mathematical physics

_x000D_

2. Class hours: 45 class hours of teaching, 16 class hours of exercise classes; _x000D_

_x000D_

_x000D_
1. "Electrodynamics" is an important theoretical basic course that systematically explains the basic theory of electromagnetic fields on the basis of electromagnetism. It is also an essential foundation for entering subsequent professional courses (such as "Quantum Mechanics" and "Quantum Electrodynamics").  _x000D_

Name: Digital Logic Circuits Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
1. Electronic lines
2. Electronic circuit experiments
3. Digital logical circuits
Introduction:
"Digital Logic Circuit Experiment" is a basic circuit experiment course that complements the "Digital Logic Circuit" theoretical course. It is listed as the main basic course for electronics majors at Peking University. The students are mainly undergraduates from the Department of Electronics and Microelectronics of the School of Information Science and Technology. There are also some students from Yuanpei class and undergraduates from other science departments. On average, 80-100 undergraduates are taught every year. _x000D_
The main purpose of this course is to enable students to master the basic principles and basic methods of digital logic circuit analysis and design; to enable students to flexibly apply the principles and methods they have learned to analyze and design digital logic systems from top to bottom and/or bottom to up; through scientific and systematic experimental training, to cultivate students' logical thinking ability, analysis and problem-solving ability, and to cultivate students' ability to self-renewal of knowledge and continuous innovation. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Communications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Signals and systems, electronic lines of communication, probability theory and random processes.
Introduction:
Through this course, students can correctly understand the basic theory and working principles of communication systems, and then understand modern communication technology and its applications.       The main features of this course are:_x000D_

      2. Pay attention to the physical meaning of theoretical issues and the understanding and mastery of physical images. _x000D_
      3. Pay attention to the cultivation of application ability combining theory with practice. _x000D_
      4. Pay attention to the cultivation of independent thinking ability, scientific thinking methods and knowledge-seeking and innovative spirit. _x000D_
      5. Strengthen the theoretical foundation and professional background, and expand the depth and breadth of knowledge. _x000D_

Name: Solid State Physics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

The solid physics course focuses on the interaction of microparticles in solid materials, motion patterns and their relationship with solid structures and material properties.

Name: Shaolin Staff

 This course mainly focuses on learning basic martial arts skills, basic movements, grappling and fighting techniques, and basic Shaolin stick skills. Through the study of this course, students can master a sports skill and achieve the purpose of strengthening physical fitness, cultivating will, increasing strength, stimulating fighting spirit, resisting beatings, defeating enemies and enriching extracurricular cultural life through routines, fighting and other forms of sports. _x000D_

Name: English News Reading
Prerequisite:
There is no pre-course requirement. Undergraduate students who love English, like news, want to read English newspapers, and listen to English programmes are allowed to attend. Yours keeps reading English newspapers. The English version of China Daily is a reference. Prior to the selection, students can read the Chinese daily online, which is almost understandable, and then come to the classroom with confidence in the Chinese daily and other mainstream newspapers in the United States, as well as in mainstream English newspapers around the world. Learning through this course:
1. The aim is to help students become familiar with and to improve their reading of mainstream newspapers in the United States and to provide them with a more comprehensive picture of Western media coverage and our English-language news coverage.
2. Systematically describe the terminology and expressions frequently used in the English-language media, in particular those that have a specific meaning in the media.
