Name: Quantitative Analytical Chemistry
Introduction:
Quantitative analytical chemistry is one of the main basic courses for students majoring in chemistry. Together with the instrumental analysis course and the intermediate analytical chemistry course, it forms a complete series of analytical chemistry courses. Its theories and methods are not only the foundation of the analytical chemistry major, but also the foundation of all other chemistry-related courses and majors. While teaching students the basic principles and methods of analytical chemistry, we also enable students to establish a strict concept of "quantity", cultivate their ability to engage in theoretical research and practical work, and develop a rigorous scientific style. _x000D_
The course is mainly targeted at first-year university students majoring in chemistry. It provides both Chinese and English teaching. Students can choose the teaching language class according to their needs and interests. The content of the course includes introduction, data statistics and analysis methods, volumetric titration methods, gravimetric analysis methods, molecular spectroscopic analysis methods (including UV-visible spectrophotometry, molecular fluorescence spectrophotometry, infrared spectroscopy, and an introduction to Raman spectroscopy), separation methods in analytical chemistry, as well as ideas for solving practical analytical chemistry problems and evaluation of analytical methods. _x000D_

Name: Organic Chemistry (II)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: This course provides a comprehensive introduction to organic chemistry, focusing on the reactions and properties of hydrocarbon compounds, various functional group compounds, and general heterocyclic compounds. This course introduces the Chinese and English nomenclature, structural characteristics, physical properties, spectral properties, main reaction properties and applications of organic compounds, laboratory and industrial preparation methods of various compounds, and systematically teaches various basic concepts and theories in organic chemistry, main organic reactions and reaction mechanisms, organic synthesis ideas, analytical methods of organic compounds and other knowledge content and scientific methods. Through the study of this course, students will systematically master the core knowledge content of organic chemistry, understand the development history of organic chemistry, and the development trends and application prospects in cutting-edge fields.

Name: Organic Chemistry Problem Session
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: This course is a basic course for undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. This course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories and basic knowledge of organic chemistry. And understand the basic methods of studying organic chemistry, and cultivate students' scientific thinking methods and ability to analyze problems. The combination of theoretical teaching content and experimental courses enables students to fully master the basic content of organic chemistry, stimulates students' potential and innovative spirit, and lays a solid foundation for further study.

Name: Intermediate Organic Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Important research objects of organic chemistry include organic reaction mechanisms, organic synthesis methodology and total synthesis of natural products. Organic reaction mechanism is an important part of organic chemistry theory. It studies the intrinsic nature of organic reactions through the specific changes of organic molecules during the reaction process, thereby effectively controlling organic reactions and improving the efficiency of reactions. In-depth study and flexible mastery of reaction mechanisms can enable students to deepen and further improve the theoretical knowledge level of organic subjects. Organic synthesis is the essence of organic chemistry. In particular, the total synthesis of natural products not only requires students to have a certain breadth and depth of basic organic knowledge, but also requires students to have the ability to rigorously scientific reasoning methods and the skills to flexibly apply knowledge. Therefore, it is very important to teach this knowledge and provide relevant training to students. With the rapid development of modern organic chemistry, this course will continuously update the knowledge content taught to further improve students' overall knowledge level in organic reaction mechanisms and organic synthesis. _x000D_
    The prerequisite course for this course is organic chemistry. The intermediate organic chemistry course is offered to increase the teaching time on organic reaction mechanisms and organic synthesis, improve students' knowledge level in these two aspects, and further cultivate students' independent thinking ability in analyzing and solving problems. _x000D_

Name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory (I+II)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Organic Chemistry Experiment (I+II) is a compulsory basic course for undergraduates in the School of Chemistry and Yuanpei College. The arrangement of the organic chemistry experiment course focuses on cultivating students with a rigorous scientific attitude and good laboratory work style, who can master the basic operations, skills and methods of organic experiments, and become professionals who can adapt to the needs of future development. Cultivate students to develop the habit of questioning and thinking, the habit of persevering despite difficulties, the habit of timely summary and diligent communication, so that students have good abilities of observation, analysis, judgment, expression and evaluation. _x000D_
    The teaching content of organic chemistry experimental courses includes: learning basic operating techniques; learning basic reaction devices, feeding methods, condition control, reaction post-processing, product purification and other synthesis methods. _x000D_

Name: Intermediate Organic Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Intermediate Organic Chemistry Experiment is the follow-up course of Organic Chemistry Experiment (I+II) and is an elective course for students of the School of Chemistry and Yuanpei College. _x000D_
    In the intermediate organic chemistry experiment, students are required to use the theoretical knowledge and experimental techniques they have learned to discover and solve problems encountered in specific topics; strengthen their understanding of newer research fields in organic chemistry, learn relevant basic knowledge, cultivate the ability to reproduce literature methods, and focus on examining the research potential reflected in experiments. Further cultivate good experimental and research habits, including reviewing and sorting literature, recording and collecting data, analyzing and evaluating results, and completing complete specifications of reports. The selected experimental projects are mainly multi-step synthesis. The experiments have certain significance in theme, certain difficulty in operation, certain characteristics in method, and certain comprehensiveness in training. _x000D_

Name: Inorganic Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Inorganic chemistry is an ancient but brand-new subject with very rich content, involving all elements and compounds in the periodic table. It not only includes basic theories, but also has wide applications in the fields of energy, materials, environment, life and other fields. _x000D_
    This course is the main basic course for chemistry majors. It is offered in the first semester of the second grade and is based on the general chemistry and general chemistry experiments taken by the first grade. In the general chemistry and experimental courses, students have learned the basic concepts and principles of chemistry, including chemical equilibrium and chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, chemical bonds and molecular and crystal structures. They have a certain understanding of the basic principles and laws of chemistry, and have mastered basic knowledge of the properties of some elements. Therefore, this course will take the periodic table of elements as the object, focus on the main line of "structure-bonding-reaction-application", and adopt the method of "selecting typical elements, emphasizing basic knowledge, focusing on material applications, and integrating cutting-edge developments". The course will introduce the properties, structures, reactions, etc. of elements and their basic compounds. On the basis of summarizing the classic properties of elements and their compounds, it will explore important scientific issues combined with the latest academic research and application fields of inorganic chemistry. Through the study of this course, students are required to systematically master the basic properties, bonding and important structural types of elements and their compounds, understand the generation and transformation rules of inorganic compounds, and develop students' ability to consider problems by combining basic knowledge with issues of concern in cutting-edge fields. This course is also the basis for the Intermediate Inorganic Chemistry course. _x000D_

Name: Structural Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Common chemistry, organic chemistry, general physics
Introduction:
Structural chemistry is a main basic course for undergraduate students in the School of Chemistry. It takes electronic configuration and geometric configuration as the two main lines, and systematically teaches three theories and three types of structures: quantum mechanical theory and atomic structure, chemical bond theory and molecular structure, lattice theory and crystal structure. It lays three foundations for undergraduate students: foundations of quantum chemistry, foundations of symmetry and foundations of crystallization chemistry. These foundations play an irreplaceable role in helping students establish microstructure concepts and principles and master modern representation methods. _x000D_
This course is taught to second-year undergraduate students. In addition to undergraduates from the School of Chemistry, students from Yuanpei College, School of Physics, and School of Engineering also take this course, about 150 people each year. Teaching is organized according to large class lectures, small class discussions and model practice (making molecular and crystal structure models). _x000D_

Name: Inorganic Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, analytical chemistry, structural chemistry, physical chemistry, instrumentation analytical chemistry, organic chemistry and corresponding experimental courses
Introduction:
1. Reasons for setting up the course_x000D_
    The predecessor of this course is an inorganic chemistry experimental course that has been offered to first-year undergraduates for many years. The course is positioned as basic inorganic chemistry, so the main content of the course is the properties of elements and the synthesis of simple inorganic substances. In the curriculum system before 1997, there were no follow-up inorganic chemistry experimental courses for the whole college, only specialized experimental courses for inorganic chemistry majors. This has caused two major problems: First, most students mistakenly believe that "inorganic chemistry is elemental chemistry, that is, test tubes, beakers; precipitation, dissolution; color development, discoloration, etc." and have little understanding of modern inorganic chemistry, resulting in students not liking to learn inorganic chemistry. Secondly, in the teaching of basic experimental courses, the experimental techniques and methods used in inorganic chemistry research are basically not covered, which reduces students' knowledge and related skill training, forming a large gap between basic experimental course skill training and front-line scientific research needs - students who have learned (basic) inorganic chemistry experimental courses basically do not have the basic skills to conduct research in related fields of inorganic chemistry (this is in huge contrast with basic organic chemistry experiments). _x000D_
    During the education reform in 1997, in accordance with the education reform policy of “downplaying the majors and strengthening the foundation”, the School of Chemistry decided to merge the original inorganic chemistry experimental courses with the general chemistry experimental courses, and then open a new (intermediate) inorganic chemistry experimental course for junior undergraduates in the college, supporting the intermediate inorganic chemistry theory course, to solve the aforementioned problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course design ideas: _x000D_
    In view of the development trend of the intersection and integration of inorganic chemistry and other disciplines to form new sub-disciplines, new research fields, new technical means and methods, this course selects a number of suitable experimental projects from various branches of modern inorganic chemistry (such as metallo-organic, bioinorganic, inorganic materials, complex chemistry, nanochemistry, solid chemistry, atomic cluster chemistry, etc.) and organically integrates the technologies and methods used in modern inorganic chemistry research into each experimental project. In the experiment, inorganic synthesis is used as a carrier. Through synthesis and characterization, students who choose the course can not only gain a perceptual understanding of inorganic chemistry through experiments, but also gain training in relevant inorganic chemistry experimental methods and skills. _x000D_
    The course process is carefully designed to combine multiple related contents as much as possible, and strive to enable students to obtain high-intensity and large-information training within a limited time. In order to maintain the novelty of the experiments, we will try to open different experimental projects every year if conditions permit. _x000D_
Part of the content of the experimental course is adapted from foreign teaching materials, and some experiments are compiled based on the scientific research results of our teachers. We hope to narrow the distance between basic experimental courses and scientific research and arouse students' interest in learning. Currently, 11 experimental projects have been developed (7 are offered per academic year) Experimental projects: _x000D_
Experiment 1 Synthesis and characterization of green long afterglow fluorescent materials SrAl2O4:Eu2+,Dy3+ (8 hours, transformation of scientific research results of our institute)_x000D_
Experiment 2 Synthesis and characterization of heterometallic trinuclear oxygen center carboxylic acid complexes (8 credit hours, transformation of scientific research results of our school)_x000D_
Experiment 3 Crystal Growth (8 hours, independent research and development)_x000D_
Experiment 4 Preparation and characterization of 1,3,5-trimethylbenzenetricarbonylmolybdenum (8 hours, converted according to literature)_x000D_
Experiment 5: Separation of C60 from p-tert-butylcalixarene (8 hours, transformation of scientific research results of our institute)_x000D_
Experiment 6 [Co(II)(Salen)] Preparation of oxygen carrier and determination of oxygen absorption properties (8 hours, compiled based on foreign textbooks)_x000D_
Experiment 7 Synthesis and identification of chromium acetate dihydrate (8 hours, compiled based on foreign textbooks)_x000D_
Experiment 8 Determination of octahedral crystal field splitting energy (Δ.) of Cr(III) complex (compiled based on foreign textbooks)_x000D_
Experiment 9 Photochemical synthesis and characterization of C60 derivatives (8 credit hours, transformation of scientific research results of our institute). _x000D_
Experiment 10: Preparation of nickel ammonia complex, and determination of composition and properties (designed experiment 1, independent research and development). _x000D_
Experiment 11: Experiment to determine the optimal composition and dosage of cosolvent for the synthesis of lanthanum terbium sulfide oxide (designed experiment 2, 8 hours, transformation of scientific research results of our institute)

Name: Instrumental Analysis
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, quantitative analysis, general physics,
Introduction: The course of instrumental analysis covers the theory of various instrument methodologies and the application of instrument technology. This course allows students to learn the principles and theoretical foundations of electroanalytical chemistry, spectroscopic analysis and separation methods, including learning related instruments and applications. Electrochemical methods include potentiometric analysis, coulomb analysis, electrolytic analysis and voltammetry; spectroscopic methods include atomic absorption spectrometry, atomic emission spectrometry, mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy; chromatographic analysis methods include gas chromatography and high performance liquid chromatography. After completing this course, students should have a certain understanding of modern instrumental analysis methods, as well as a certain understanding of the composition of instruments and the application of various methods.

Name: Instrumental Analysis Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry theory and experiments, general physics theory and experiments, quantitative analysis theory and experiments
Introduction: Instrumental analysis experiment is a compulsory course for students majoring in chemistry. It is an experimental course offered in conjunction with the instrumental analysis theory course, with the purpose of enabling students to master the basic principles, basic instrument composition and basic applications of various analytical instruments. This laboratory course will help students integrate a basic understanding of the physical principles of a variety of instruments, including atomic, molecular spectroscopy and mass spectrometry, nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, chromatography and other separation methods, and electroanalytical methods. This course is also designed to help students learn how to operate various analytical instruments.

Name: Fundamentals of Applied Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Applied chemistry is an important part of the chemical discipline and an inexhaustible driving force for the continuous development of chemistry in applied fields. The research object of applied chemistry is not mainly the basic principles and laws of the chemical discipline itself, but the basis of the practical application of chemistry, which belongs to the category of applied basic research. This course mainly introduces basic knowledge of surfactants, food additives, dyes and pigments, cosmetics, labeled compounds, radiopharmaceuticals, etc., so that students can have a clear understanding of the relationship between the composition and properties of fine chemicals in terms of chemical mechanisms, while cultivating students' ability to apply radioisotope technology in scientific research such as chemistry, biology, and medicine. This course focuses on application and the cultivation of students' abilities; the course content is closely related to the reality of production, life and environment, and is inspiring and interesting; it lays a foundation for students to further learn and apply chemical knowledge.

Name: Structural Chemistry Seminar
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering

Name: Retrieval and Use of Electronic Resources
Introduction: Overview of electronic resources; reference database ⑴—world-famous comprehensive search tool (English); reference database ⑵—professional search tool (English); reference database ⑶—Chinese search tool; utilization of full-text databases and full-text services; electronic journals; electronic books and newspapers; factual databases.

Name: Polymer Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for undergraduate students in the School of Chemistry. Polymer materials are indispensable materials for modern society and people's daily lives. "Polymer Chemistry" is the basis for the synthesis of these materials. Together with the elective courses "Polymer Physics" and "Polymer Materials", it constitutes the basic teaching content of polymer science. Organic chemistry is the basis for synthesizing polymers. Students must first complete the "Organic Chemistry" course. _x000D_
This course will mainly teach the basic concepts of polymers and the development history of polymer science and industry. On this basis, we focus on teaching two basic methods of synthesizing polymers: stepwise polymerization and chain polymerization. Stepwise polymerization includes traditional polycondensation reactions and polyaddition reactions. It mainly teaches the basic principles of synthesizing polymers from small molecules through the stepwise polymerization reaction mechanism, the main methods of controlling the molecular weight and structure of polymers, and the synthesis methods of polymers with important industrial applications (polyester, polyamide, polycarbonate, polysulfone, polyimide, phenolic resin, epoxy resin, unsaturated resin, silicone resin, etc.). Chain polymerization mainly includes the polymerization of olefinic monomers and cyclic monomers, including free radical polymerization, free radical copolymerization, ionic polymerization, coordination polymerization, ring-opening polymerization, etc. The teaching content includes polymerization kinetics, methods to control polymer composition, three-dimensional structure, terminal structure, molecular weight and molecular weight distribution; on this basis, the concept of living polymerization and developed polymerization methods are introduced, as well as the application of this method to synthesize polymers with special structures. Finally, a brief introduction to polymer modification methods, types and applications of functional polymers, and the latest advances in polymer synthetic chemistry will be given. _x000D_
The course teaching will not strictly follow the sequence and content of the textbooks. We hope that students can learn to use the Internet and literature to learn more about polymer chemistry. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Life Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
This course mainly introduces the basic content of biochemistry, focusing on the four important biological macromolecules of sugar, lipid, protein and nucleic acid. It also introduces some of the latest developments in life sciences, striving to enable students to understand the basic concepts, basic knowledge and basic theories of biochemistry. In order to enable students in the Department of Chemistry to have a certain knowledge storage when they enter the field of life sciences to engage in research, the teaching of this course pays attention to the students' chemistry background, focusing on explaining the relationship between the structure and function of biological macromolecules, making it easy for students to learn and understand. At the same time, through learning, they can understand and understand the chemical movements in life from the level of molecules and molecular aggregates, and have a basic understanding of the chemical nature of life phenomena. _x000D_
    This course will focus on the molecular structure, physical and chemical properties, biological functions and metabolic processes of four biological macromolecules, focusing on a relatively comprehensive teaching of proteins and nucleic acids. The molecular structure and properties of sugars and lipids have been studied in the organic chemistry course. This course will not go into details, but will focus on their functions and metabolism. In view of the fact that students have a strong chemistry background, this course pays attention to the introduction of inhibitors and drug action mechanisms involved in proteins or nucleic acids. In this way, on the one hand, it can improve students' interest in learning, and on the other hand, it has practical significance for students to engage in chemical biology research or drug research in the future. _x000D_

Name: Intermediate Analytical Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Quantitative analysis of chemistry and basic instruments
Introduction:
Intermediate Analytical Chemistry is one of the basic courses of the School of Chemistry. Its main purpose is to teach analytical chemistry skills, techniques and methods that are not covered in quantitative analytical chemistry and basic instrumental analytical chemistry, but are often used in scientific research and practical work, so that graduates of this school can adapt to future work needs as soon as possible. _x000D_
It mainly introduces the quality assurance of the analytical testing process; the sampling, processing and preparation of analytical samples; commonly used separation and enrichment methods; the application of various hyphenated technologies, various new technologies and new methods in industrial and agricultural production; and some case studies. Allow students to keep abreast of the latest international new technologies, new methods and new applications of analytical chemistry. As new technologies and methods in analytical chemistry continue to emerge, the teaching content of this course should be constantly updated and improved. _x000D_

Name: Computer Applications in Chemistry and Chemical Engineering
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
This course is one of the elective courses for undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. This course is suitable for all undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. This course will teach students how to use advanced computer technology to solve practical problems in the fields of chemistry and chemical engineering, thereby improving their efficiency in future scientific research and work. It will also cultivate students' ability to engage in scientific research and practical work, as well as their rigorous scientific research style. _x000D_
    The characteristics of this course are that it is concise and practical; theoretical courses and computer-based practical courses are closely coordinated and complementary; while clarifying the basic knowledge and usage methods of commonly used chemistry and chemical engineering software, attention is paid to introducing students to new developments and new results in the application of computers in chemistry and chemical engineering, so as to broaden students' horizons, inspire students' ideas, and improve students' interest in learning. At the same time, students are encouraged to use computer technology to help solve practical problems in undergraduate scientific research or experiments. _x000D_

Name: Physical Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Basic theoretical and experimental courses in general chemistry, analytical chemistry (incorporation analysis), organic chemistry, and physicochemistry (incorporative chemistry)
Introduction:
Physical chemistry experiment is one of the compulsory basic courses for cultivating chemistry professionals. This course can provide students with the most basic experimental methods, skills training and preliminary research ability development. The teaching objectives are: to deepen students' understanding of physical and chemical principles through typical experiments, improve their ability to flexibly apply physical and chemical principles and master the basic methods and skills of physical and chemical experiments; to cultivate the ability to correctly record experimental data and phenomena, correctly process experimental data and analyze experimental results; to strengthen the concepts of "experimental error" and "significant figures", to develop good habits and lay a solid foundation for graduation thesis and subsequent scientific research work. Based on the characteristics of physical chemistry experiments that mostly rely on physical measuring instruments and often rely on indirect measurement methods, in the arrangement of experimental content, we insist on retaining classic experimental methods and measurement techniques, and guide students to understand the development of modern measurement technology. In the data processing link, based on the training of manual drawing methods to process experimental data, students are guided to gradually master computer drawing and data processing methods. In the process of experimental teaching, students are taught the general principles of physical chemistry research methods by analyzing the design ideas, variable conversion and data processing skills of classic experiments, drawing inferences from one example and applying point to point. At the same time, the quality of experimental reports is strictly controlled, the processing and expression of experimental data and the analysis and discussion of results are standardized with reference to the standards of scientific research papers, and a scientific experimental assessment and performance evaluation system is gradually established and improved. _x000D_
    At present, the total planned hours of the physical chemistry experiment course are 105 hours. The basic physical chemistry experiments include 12 basic experiments, which are conducted in a group cycle, and are all single-person group operations. The content covers the main branches of physical chemistry, including: (1) Thermodynamic experiments: calorimetric techniques, phase equilibrium experiments, chemical equilibrium experiments and determination of other thermodynamic parameters; (2) Kinetic experiments: simple series inversions Application, determination of complex reactions and modern rapid reactions; (3) Electrochemical experiments: determination of reversible electrode potential, research on thermodynamics and irreversible electrode potential of primary cells and cyclic voltammetry; (4) Surface chemistry and colloid chemistry experiments: preparation and properties of colloids, research and determination of characteristics of highly dispersed systems and surface properties; (5) Structural chemistry experiments: analysis and determination of electrical and magnetic properties of molecules, etc. _x000D_

Name: Inorganic Chemistry Seminar
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering

Name: Physical Chemistry (II)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, general physics, general chemistry, structure chemistry.
Introduction: The task of this course is to introduce the basic principles, methods and applications of chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, electrochemistry and surface and colloid chemistry. The purpose of this course is achieved through classroom lectures, self-study, discussion classes, calculation exercises, examinations and other teaching links.

Name: Mass Spectrometry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Organic chemistry, quantitative analysis, instrument analysis
Introduction: As one of the most important classical analytical chemistry methods, mass spectrometry has been widely used in drug metabolism, clinical, toxicology, pesticide determination, environmental protection, petrochemistry and other fields. In the field of basic research, the development of high-resolution and high-sensitivity mass spectrometry technology in recent years and its combination with various efficient separation methods have brought traditional mass spectrometry analysis methods into the study of small molecules to large molecules (such as proteins). Therefore, offering courses related to mass spectrometry analysis for senior undergraduate students in the School of Chemistry and teaching the latest cutting-edge results in the development and application of mass spectrometry technology will help broaden students' horizons, inspire students' ideas, and stimulate students' interest in scientific research.

Name: NMR Analysis
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, organic chemistry, instrument analysis
Introduction:
Nuclear magnetic resonance technology is an important experimental method in the fields of physics, chemistry, life sciences, and materials science, and has a wide range of applications. Nuclear magnetic resonance is an indispensable and important analytical method in research in various disciplines of chemistry. This course mainly caters to the needs of senior undergraduate students majoring in chemistry to participate in laboratory research. It is based on the NMR analysis method in the instrumental analysis course and teaches the basic theoretical knowledge, construction methods, and application of one-dimensional to multi-dimensional NMR in the structural analysis of organic molecules and biological macromolecules. _x000D_
    This course will be based on the explanation of basic theories and combined with specific examples, focusing on the representation content, analysis skills and limitations of multi-dimensional NMR spectroscopy. It strives to enable students to initially master the design concept, data analysis methods and application scope of multi-dimensional NMR experimental methods. When using NMR research in the future, they will not only know what is happening, but also know why it is so that they can better use NMR technology to solve practical problems encountered in scientific research. While teaching students theoretical knowledge and analytical methods, this course will also introduce the cutting-edge and latest achievements in the field of nuclear magnetic resonance, focusing on broadening students' horizons, inspiring students' ideas, and improving students' interest in learning. The course will organically combine theory with practice, strengthen quality education, and cultivate students' independent and logical thinking abilities. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Business Operations and Management
Introduction: Through high-quality, multi-field and multi-dimensional industry lectures, students can have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the cutting-edge information of today's Chinese enterprise management practices, broaden their horizons, and cultivate their ability to apply theory to practice. Combined with the diversified industry backgrounds of alumni, it focuses on sharing actual cases in the business management process.

Name: Group Theory and Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
The content of the "Group Theory and Chemistry" course is based on the symmetry point group to which molecules belong. It discusses some properties that molecules must have due to their symmetry and how to use symmetry to solve some problems encountered in the analysis of molecular electronic structures and molecular spectra. We are now applying to open this course to undergraduates as an elective, mainly for the following three reasons. _x000D_
(1) Adapt to the needs of the construction of inorganic chemistry elective courses_x000D_
"Group Theory and Chemistry" was started by Professor Li Lemin in 1981 for the first graduate students of the School of Chemistry, Peking University, with the purpose of enhancing the theoretical foundation of graduate students. In 1994, Professor Takamatsu began teaching this course. From 2007 to 2008, Associate Professor Wang Bingwu served as a teaching assistant for this course. In 2009, he began to teach the course "Group Theory and Chemistry" independently. In the early days of the course, "Group Theory and Chemistry" was taught as a required course for undergraduates (the specific year was not found). Later, due to the large content of undergraduate courses, it was again taught only for graduate students. In terms of course development, "Group Theory and Chemistry" is one of the basic theoretical courses in inorganic chemistry and has been in operation for 33 years. As a student at the School of Chemistry at Peking University, I have always been praised for my solid theoretical knowledge and practical abilities. Opening this course to undergraduate students as an elective course can provide undergraduate students with an opportunity to improve their basic theoretical knowledge and also meet the needs of the construction of inorganic chemistry elective courses. _x000D_
(2) The course content is suitable for undergraduate electives_x000D_
Symmetry is a basic property of molecules and is highly relevant to courses such as "General Chemistry Principles", "Inorganic Chemistry", "Intermediate Inorganic", "Organic Chemistry", "Physical Chemistry", and "Quantum Chemistry". Group theory is a basic tool for studying issues related to symmetry. It can connect the symmetry of molecules with the properties of molecules. It is very important in understanding molecular symmetry issues and can deepen the understanding of molecular properties from a theoretical level. Due to the length of the course, there is no explanation or even introduction to group theory in the above basic courses. Therefore, it is very necessary to add an elective course to provide students with the opportunity to deeply understand the problem of molecular symmetry. _x000D_
(3) Comparison of similar international courses_x000D_
Internationally, many university chemistry departments or inorganic chemistry majors offer "Group Theory and Chemistry" courses or related content, mainly in the following three forms:_x000D_
(i) Open as a course to both postgraduate and undergraduate students. For example, UC Berkeley offers the course "Molecular Symmetry and Chemical Applications of Group Theory". This course belongs to the "Introduction to Bonding Theory" section of the "Advanced Inorganic Chemistry Series" and is taught by Professor Jeff Long. The course is mainly for first-year graduate students, but also for other interested students, including undergraduates. The main textbook of the course is "Chemical Application of Group Theory" (F. Albert Cotton), which is also the main reference book for the "Group Theory and Chemistry" course. Wayne University, Case Western Reserve University, etc. also use this method to teach the application of group theory in chemistry. _x000D_
(ii) Open as a separate course to undergraduate students. For example, Princeton University offers "Group theory in Chemistry". This course is open to undergraduate students and uses "Symmetry through the Eyes of a Chemist" as the teaching material. At the same time, "Chemical Application of Group Theory" is an important reference book. Universities such as Michigan Technological University also use this approach. _x000D_
(iii) Taught to undergraduate students as part of a course. For example, at Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), the required course "Principles of Inorganic Chemistry II" for all students will have a section on "Systematic presentation of the chemical application of group theory"; Stanford University will have a section on "Group Theory" in "Inorganic Chemistry II"; Arizona State University will have a section on "Group Theory for Chemistry" in "Quantum Chemistry I"; UC Berkeley will have a section on "Inorganic Chemistry". Chemistry" also has sections on "Symmetry and Group Theory." UC Berkeley teaches the application of group theory in chemistry in both undergraduate and graduate courses, which shows that it attaches great importance to it. _x000D_
Therefore, please grant your application to open this course as an optional course to undergraduate students. _x000D_

Name: Spectral Analysis
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Modern spectroscopic analysis is an important means of determining molecular structure, which has greatly promoted the overall development of the chemical discipline (mass spectrometry and nuclear magnetic resonance technology won the 2002 Nobel Prize in Chemistry). This course teaches the basic principles of modern spectral analysis and advanced analytical methods and technologies; the characteristics of mass spectrometry, infrared spectrum, ultraviolet spectrum, hydrogen nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum, carbon spectrum and two-dimensional nuclear magnetic resonance spectrum of common organic compounds; teaches the method of using the four major spectra to comprehensively analyze the structure of moderately complex organic compounds, and teaches the new developments and new technologies of mass spectrometry analysis and nuclear magnetic resonance and their application in the structural identification of organic compounds. Enable students to systematically master the basic theories, new methods and new technologies of the four major wave spectra.

Name: Interface Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: The task of this course is to systematically introduce the characteristics of various phase interfaces and surfactants, as well as various physical and chemical effects on the interface, so that students can master the principles and theories, understand experimental and theoretical research methods, and introduce some important applications in scientific research, production and life, and gain preliminary practical experience in the use of surfactants. _x000D_

Name: Intermediate Physical Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Intermediate physical chemistry experiment is an elective course and must be taken by students who want to be exempted from the examination recommended by our graduate students. This course is an improvement course for physical and chemical experiments. Together with the physical and chemical experiments, it constitutes a complete course system for physical and chemical experiments. The purpose is to train students to comprehensively apply the knowledge they have learned, fully understand and analyze a specific problem, formulate their own experimental solutions and verify them experimentally. This will help students adapt to the transition from verification-based experiments to research-based experiments and cultivate innovation capabilities. Develop good habits and lay a solid foundation for future scientific research activities. _x000D_
    At present, the total planned hours of the intermediate physical chemistry experiment course are 45 hours and 1.5 credits. It is conducted in the form of designed experiments. Students can complete it independently or in groups of 2 or 3. The designed experiment topics are given by the instructor or students choose the topics independently based on the existing conditions in the laboratory. On the basis of fully understanding the instructor's intention in setting the question, students write and design experimental plans, and collectively discuss revisions and improvements. Then use about five weeks to conduct experiments to verify your ideas. Finally, submit an experimental report, which is required to be written according to the research paper format, and also arrange an oral report to present your research results. _x000D_

Name: General Survey of American History
Introduction: This course is a general history course of the United States. It outlines the development of American history from the 18th to the 20th century, describes the formation and evolution of the American economy, politics, law, and social order, analyzes the causes, dynamics, and mechanisms of the evolution of American history, and discusses the relationship between the United States and the world. Topics discussed in the course: The origins of the North American colonies; the political culture of the colonial era; the War of Independence and the founding of the United States; the early market revolution, democratization and reform movements; slavery and the abolitionist movement; the Civil War and Reconstruction; the process of industrialization and its costs; the evolution of U.S. foreign policy; the Great Depression and the American welfare state; the civil rights movement and the 1960s; the Cold War and the globalization of U.S. interests. The purpose of this course is to help students understand the growth process of the United States and the American nation, understand the complexity of American history and the historical meaning of American thought, and learn to use historical methods to observe and analyze the United States and its history. This course is mainly lecture-based and students are encouraged to participate in class discussions. Course assessment content includes: reading reports, final exams, attendance and other assignments.

Name: Catalytic Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Common chemical, physical and structural chemistry
Introduction: Based on the basic knowledge of undergraduate general chemistry, physical chemistry and structural chemistry, this course covers solid surface adsorption and catalytic reaction kinetics. The main catalyst systems include homogeneous complex catalysts, solid acid catalysts, metal catalysts, metal oxide catalysts and their catalytic effects, the main preparation and characterization methods of catalysts, new developments and frontiers in catalytic chemistry, etc., aiming to cultivate students' ability to solve practical catalytic chemistry problems.

Physical organic chemistry involves the relationship between the structure and properties of organic compounds, as well as related theories and research methods of organic chemical reaction mechanisms. It is _x000D_
