Name: Fundamentals of Chemical Engineering
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
As an indispensable part of the knowledge structure that undergraduate students majoring in science and chemistry majors and applied chemistry majors should have, "Basics of Chemical Engineering" is listed as a compulsory basic course or main basic course for undergraduate students in almost all colleges and universities majoring in science chemistry and applied chemistry majors. _x000D_
Basic purpose: _x000D_
1. Improve students’ awareness of industrialization in scientific research and establish a technical and economic perspective; learn the main methods in engineering technology to avoid a single thinking model; 2. Understand the problems and solutions that may be encountered in the industrialization of scientific research results; introduce advanced technical means in scientific research or development work; _x000D_
Content summary:_x000D_
1. Quantitatively analyze the performance of various reactors (including various laboratory reactors) and optimize the selection of reactors; _x000D_
2. Quantitatively analyze various separation methods (including laboratory separation methods), and introduce advanced separation technologies and equipment; _x000D_
3. Heat transfer control, full utilization of energy, and control, transportation and measurement of fluid systems. _x000D_
This course uses chemical process development as a guide to introduce various unit operations such as fluid power processes, heat transfer processes, mass transfer separation processes, and the basic principles of chemical reaction engineering (the so-called "three transmissions and one reverse"), process analysis, and knowledge of related chemical equipment. _x000D_

Name: Accounting
Introduction: Accounting is a basic course and one of the core courses in business administration courses. When investors make investments, they often use various analytical tools and techniques to assist in reducing decision-making uncertainty, and financial statements are an important source of information. The purpose of designing this course is to provide a teaching and discussion environment for effective learning of financial statement knowledge. The main content of the course includes: basic accounting principles and applications of modern corporate financial accounting, accounting treatment methods for basic economic businesses and events, and the preparation principles of the three main accounting statements (i.e., balance sheet, income statement and cash flow statement), etc. After studying this course, students will be familiar with all conventional accounting procedures and methods, master the preparation of accounting statements and the disclosure of accounting information, develop certain professional judgment skills and the ability to solve accounting practical problems, and lay the foundation for learning relevant subsequent courses (such as corporate finance, intermediate financial accounting, financial statement analysis, etc.).

Name: Corporate Financial Management Seminar
Introduction:
This course is a small-class teaching course that is in conjunction with the compulsory course "Corporate Financial Management". The positioning of small class teaching is to deepen understanding, locate interests and improve abilities. Courses are taught every other week, with two lessons each time. _x000D_
In each course, the instructor will have a more in-depth discussion with the students on some of the content taught in the "Corporate Financial Management" large class lectures. Small class discussions will be based on students' problems and areas of interest. The professor will design after collecting students after listening to the large lectures to ensure that small class discussions promote students' understanding and improvement. _x000D_

Name: Academic English Writing
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Class B courses offered by the English Studies Section of the University
Introduction:
As an international language, English has always been valued at all levels of education. This course is an academic English writing course for non-English major undergraduates at Peking University. According to the writing requirements of the "College English Teaching Guide" for non-English major undergraduates, the teaching goal of this course is to hope that college undergraduates can master the English academic vocabulary and grammar system proficiently, and through teachers to guide students to read different types of English academic articles, understand the basic knowledge and requirements of academic writing, and gradually cultivate students' ability to use English for comprehensive analysis and logical thinking. By systematically learning the methods and techniques of English writing, achieving flexible application and functional output, students can write English practical essays with correct grammar, clear meaning and fluent language before graduating from college. On this basis, students can develop the feeling and interest in writing other genres of articles in English. In addition, from the perspective of academic writing standards, this course also requires students to learn to correctly cite academic documents and other people's opinions, put forward and organize appropriate and powerful arguments, and avoid behavior that violates academic norms and violates academic ethics. _x000D_
This course can help students improve their English use and expression level, exercise their logical thinking ability, activate the input and output efficiency of their foreign language knowledge, develop good academic writing habits, and cultivate good academic ethics. It can lay a solid foundation for English academic writing for students at high-level, research-oriented universities starting from the undergraduate level. _x000D_

Name: Chaos and Fractals in the Natural Sciences
Introduction:
Chaos dynamics, fractal theory and catastrophe theory, founded in the 1970s, have a common purpose of revealing the regularities in complex phenomena in nature. These theories are commonly known as non-linear science. Since its inception, the research on nonlinear theory has made remarkable progress and has become the scientific frontier of the 21st century. Nonlinear dynamics is of great significance to solve various complex phenomena and problems in physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy and earth sciences. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course strives to start with familiar problems for students, focusing on physical concepts and geometric images, and introduces important concepts and applications such as chaos, fractals, bifurcations and mutations in non-linear theory from the shallower to the deeper, in order to broaden students' horizons, master basic concepts and methods, and achieve the purpose of applying what they have learned. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course theoretically answers the following interesting scientific questions: 1. Will a butterfly flapping its wings in Brazil, South America, cause a storm in Texas, USA? 2. Is it correct to say that China’s coastline is 18,000 kilometers long? 3. Do messy sequences, such as DNA sequences, protein sequences, etc., have structures? _x000D_
_x000D_
Through the study of this course, you can enrich your understanding and new perspectives on natural phenomena:_x000D_
1. A certain system can not only have certain results, but also have uncertain results; _x000D_
2. For multi-scale systems, physical quantities change with scale, but there may be invariants in the system; _x000D_
3. Understand the nature and structure of the system from the chaotic signals (chaotic time series). _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Polymer Physics
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Organic chemistry, physicochemistry, high molecular chemistry
Introduction: “High Molecular Physics” is designed mainly for undergraduate students in grades 3 and 4. The course focused on basic concepts and physical images of high molecular physics. The curriculum reads as follows: (1) single chain image of high molecules, solubility properties of high molecules; (2) high molecular condensation, including microphase separation of high molecular glass, crystallization, liquid crystallization, high molecular mixtures, sedentary homogenes; (3) viscous elasticity and molecular movements of high molecules; (4) the mechanical and electrodynamic properties of high molecules. In the course, we will also present some important experimental techniques used in high molecular physics research.

Name: Materials Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, structural chemistry, general physics, physical chemistry, intermediate inorganic chemistry
Introduction:
This course is a professional basic course for undergraduate students majoring in materials chemistry, and is also an elective course for graduate students in various majors in the School of Chemistry. Through the study of this course, students are expected to master the basic knowledge and basic principles of materials chemistry, understand the development status of materials chemistry, and lay the foundation for students to engage in scientific research in materials chemistry. Features of the course: combination of knowledge transfer and cultivation of scientific research ideas; combination of basic knowledge transfer and introduction to research frontiers. _x000D_
   The course content is divided into three parts:_x000D_
1.	Experimental part: Teach the preparation methods of inorganic materials and basic characterization methods of materials; _x000D_
2．	Basic principles: including the crystal structure and electronic structure of inorganic materials, defects in materials, defect balance and their impact on material properties, phase changes and phase balance of materials, the relationship between the physical properties of materials and the symmetry of the material structure, etc. _x000D_
3.	Introduction to main functional materials: Introducing the basic knowledge and development status of dielectric materials, conductive materials, magnetic materials, fluorescent materials, channel materials, glass materials and nanomaterials. _x000D_

Name: Polycrystalline X-Ray Diffraction
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Briefly introduce the basic principles of crystallography, the properties of X-rays and the basic principles of diffraction experimental methods; focus on the characteristics and methods of polycrystalline X-ray diffraction and its application in scientific research. Focus on phase analysis and identification, indexation of powder diffraction patterns, correction of unit cell parameters, determination of grain size, quantitative phase analysis and other issues, and discuss from the principles, experimental methods, and data analysis. This article further introduces the principle of the Rietveld method, which currently uses powder diffraction data to analyze crystal structures, and discusses its application in structural analysis through examples. Briefly introduce the characteristics and usage of some commonly used software, such as Fullprof, PowderX, Powdercell, etc.

Name: Physical Chemistry (I)
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, general physics, general chemistry, structure chemistry.
Introduction: The task of this course is to introduce the basic principles, methods and applications of chemical thermodynamics, chemical kinetics, electrochemistry and surface and colloid chemistry. The purpose of this course is achieved through classroom lectures, self-study, discussion classes, calculation exercises, examinations and other teaching links.

Name: Appreciation of British and American Short Stories
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: Undergraduate students who have completed College English Level 4 have read many English articles of various genres through basic courses, including expository essays, argumentative essays, novels, etc. Since the text selection for basic courses is limited by the length, it is impossible for students to read a large number of English novels. Even if they can read a few articles, they often only have a superficial understanding. This course is designed to meet the reading needs of literature-loving students in novel works, to systematically understand the components and writing techniques of short stories, and to improve their reading comprehension and literary appreciation abilities. This course selects 14 famous short stories from the United Kingdom and the United States. Each story is about 1,500-3,000 words. It is divided into 7 parts according to the basic elements of the novel, which are: plot, character, background, viewpoint, theme, symbol, and style. When explaining each element, the teacher selects two novels as examples. The first one is lectured by the teacher to guide students to deeply understand the theme and writing characteristics of the novel; the second one is explained by the students themselves and presented in a group format. This course requires students to preview selected novels before class and actively participate in class discussions.

Name: Solid State Physics Seminar
Introduction: A small discussion session with solid physics. The number is limited to 15. Focus on specific topics. Students have more opportunities to discuss and discuss with their teachers.

Name: Quantum Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite:
Structural Chemistry
Secondary Physicochemistry or quantum mechanics
Introduction: This course is intended for senior undergraduate students and graduate students majoring in physical chemistry and inorganic chemistry. It provides a systematic introduction to ab initio electronic structure theory for molecular systems. The course assumes that students have some basic knowledge of quantum mechanics. The content covers the basic contents of modern electronic structure theory, including Hartree-Fock method, various post-HF electron related methods and density functional theory. The course includes about 12 hours of computer-based internship. The purpose is to familiarize students with commonly used quantum chemistry calculation software, understand its main functions, master basic usage skills, and deepen their understanding of the classroom content by combining it with actual calculations of simple systems.

Name: General Polymer Materials: Structure, Properties and Applications
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: General-purpose polymers are indispensable materials for modern social life. This course starts with an introduction to the applications of general-purpose polymers and guides students to understand the relationship between the chemical structure, aggregate structure of general-purpose polymers and material properties, especially mechanical properties. Finally, combined with recent progress in new material research and development, we will introduce the high performance of general-purpose polymers.

Name: The Japanese Economy
Introduction:
In the real world, Japan's economy is the second largest economy in the world and has important connections with our country's economy. The Japanese economy and Japan-China economic relations have an important impact on changes in the Asia-Pacific and world economic patterns. In theoretical research, Japanese economic research is closely related to the theoretical frontiers of economics, international political economy, management, sociology, history and other disciplines. However, it is undeniable that the Japanese economy remains one of the most misunderstood among the major economies. _x000D_
    The teaching of this course will use the basic ideas and analysis methods of economics, but there are no requirements for students' professional background. Each lesson starts with a representative case or event, and then introduces a theoretical analysis of an important issue in the Japanese economy. This course is mainly about lectures, supplemented by discussions. This course plans to invite external experts to give special lectures on the growth of Japanese companies, the evolution of the Japanese financial system, ODA and other issues. Documentaries will be used as supporting material for some parts of this lesson. _x000D_

Name: Concepts and Approaches in Biology
Introduction: Starting from the basic concepts of biology, some classic experiments and articles are introduced, as well as the development of related fields. Let the freshmen who have just entered the school experience the breadth, depth, depth and beauty of biology; arouse their strong interest in learning and researching life sciences. Through some famous research examples, students are taught how to raise questions and hypotheses based on the observation of some phenomena, verify these hypotheses through experiments, and finally develop them into widely accepted theories; the specific content includes the understanding of the intrinsic connections of various organisms in the biological world; the study of communities, groups, individuals, organs, tissues, genomes, genes, non-coding RNA and other different levels and their interaction with the environment is of great connotation for life sciences The application of methods from computer science, mathematics, physics and other disciplines in life sciences has greatly promoted the development of life sciences.

Name: Analytical Chemistry Laboratory (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Analytical Chemistry Experiment (B) is taught to non-chemistry major undergraduate students. Through the study of this course, they can master the basic knowledge, basic operations and basic skills of quantitative chemical analysis experiments, as well as typical analytical methods and experimental data processing methods.

Name: Physiology
Introduction: The main content is the physiology of human and mammalian organs, and the differences in physiological functions of certain animals in different living environments are introduced. Specific contents include: the structure and transport function of cell membrane; nerve excitation and conduction; muscle excitation and contraction; digestion and absorption; blood function; blood circulation; respiration; energy metabolism and temperature regulation; osmotic regulation and excretion; endocrine-hormone regulation; sensory function of the nervous system; motor function of the nervous system; advanced functions of the nervous system.

Name: Physiology Laboratory
Introduction: Cooperate with the experimental content related to the "Physiology" course design, observe and record physiological phenomena, verify classic and basic physiological laws, and consolidate theoretical knowledge of physiology. At the same time, students' physiological surgical operation skills and basic ability to design experiments are cultivated, and students' ability to analyze and solve problems is trained.

Name: Organic Chemistry (B)
Introduction: This course is a compulsory basic course for undergraduate students in the School of Life Sciences, with 3 hours per week. Through the study of this course, students will receive systematic training in the following aspects. (1) Comprehensively systematically master the naming rules of organic compounds, structural characteristics and description methods of organic compounds, properties of organic compounds, and the relationship between structure and properties, deeply study and understand the important reactions and partial reaction mechanisms of various organic compounds, and master the basic concepts of stereochemistry; (2) Understand and master the mutual transformation between functional groups, and be able to complete simple organic synthesis designs and related synthesis reactions; (3) By learning various organic compounds The basic properties of compounds, understand the chemical methods for identifying various organic compounds, and initially master the general methods of separating and purifying organic mixtures; (4) Through the study of hydrogen nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy and infrared spectroscopy, initially understand the application of spectroscopy in structural analysis of organic compounds, reaction mechanism research, and organic synthetic chemistry; (5) Understand and partially master the structure and properties of various biological (macro) molecules involved in the field of life sciences, and some related organic chemical reactions. During the teaching process, the application characteristics of organic chemistry in the fields of life, medicine and other fields will be highlighted, and some organic chemical reactions related to biological (macro)molecules, cells, and surface modifications will be appropriately introduced. In addition, the teaching objectives of this course are not to engage in basic research in organic chemistry. Therefore, content related to molecular orbital theory, complex reaction mechanisms, and complex but less useful reactions in the fields of life and medicine are not within the scope of this course. In general, this course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories and basic knowledge of organic chemistry; understand the basic methods of researching organic chemistry; and learn how to apply the knowledge of organic chemistry to the fields of life sciences and medical sciences.

Name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
Organic chemistry experimental course B for undergraduates in the Department of Medicine is compulsory for about 390 students every year. The three-stage progressive teaching mode of "Basic Operations - Comprehensive Basic Operations - Organic Synthesis" is adopted to enable students to obtain more comprehensive training in organic chemistry experimental skills. The experiment covers basic operations such as distillation, reflux, extraction, recrystallization, column chromatography, and thin layer chromatography; uses multi-component mixture separation to strengthen basic operations; uses n-bromobutane to train the preparation of liquid compounds; designs a multi-step drug synthesis starting from benzaldehyde to hydantoin, and trains the preparation of solid compounds. _x000D_
    Due to the large number of students enrolling in the course and limited laboratory resources, we completed the teaching in two rounds of 8 hours per class, 2 days per week. _x000D_

Name: Biochemistry Laboratory
Introduction: Biochemistry experiment is a main basic course and is a basic experimental course that is matched with the biochemistry theory course. This course is open to all undergraduates in the School of Life Sciences, some undergraduates in Yuanpei College, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering and other colleges, double majors or minor undergraduates. There are about 100 students per academic year. The course content includes the separation and purification, quantitative determination and property identification of biological macromolecules. The experimental techniques involved include the preparation technology of biological macromolecules, spectral analysis technology, chromatographic separation and analysis technology, electrophoresis technology and ultracentrifugation technology. The biochemical instruments students learn to use include centrifuges, adjustable pipettes, protein electrophoresis devices, protein semi-dry transfer instruments, protein-nucleic acid detectors and recorders, spectrophotometers, microplate readers, etc. With the continuous development of biochemistry theory and experimental technology, the teaching content is constantly updated, new technologies are added, and new experiments are added. The teaching content is based on the syllabus of each semester.

Name: World History of Film
Introduction: This course strives to provide an overview of world film history or a new understanding of film history. The course mainly explores three main aspects: how the film medium is used, that is, how film language is gradually produced, developed, matured and standardized. 2. The environment of the film industry - how the production, distribution and screening conditions of films affect the development of film media. 3. How did the global trend of film art and the nationalization trend of the film market emerge?

Name: Physical Chemistry (B)
Introduction: Physico-chemistry is a discipline that explores the basic patterns of material change from the interlinkage between chemical and physical phenomena, as well as the principles, patterns and methods of behaviour of all chemical systems, which is the theoretical basis of chemistry. Research in life sciences requires the application of physico-chemical fundamentals, and experimental methods of physico-chemicals play an important role in the development of life sciences. The course is a one-year course in basic physics and chemistry for undergraduate students in the life sciences. Emphasis is placed on the underlying principles and methods of physico-chemistry, which includes, inter alia, chemical thermal sciences, electrochemistry, chemical dynamics and adhesive chemistry. Learning through this course will provide the basis for future application of physico-chemical principles and methods to analyse and solve problems in life sciences and related fields.

Name: Basic Molecular Biology
Introduction:
Molecular biology is the science that studies the morphology and structural characteristics of all biological macromolecules such as nucleic acids and proteins, as well as their importance, regularity and interrelationships. It is the basic science that allows humans to truly uncover the mysteries of the biological world at the molecular level and shift from passively adapting to nature to actively transforming and reorganizing nature. _x000D_
Molecular biology is one of the themes of contemporary biological research. It is the fastest growing, most dynamic and energetic field. Especially in recent years, with the development of molecular biology research technology, the research of molecular biology has developed rapidly. Moreover, it interpenetrates and promotes each other with other disciplines such as genetics and biochemistry. Mastering the basic principles and techniques of molecular biology is very important for studying other subjects such as genetics, biochemistry, cell biology, neurobiology, and developmental biology. Therefore, molecular biology is an important professional basic course for third-year undergraduates majoring in biological sciences and biotechnology. _x000D_
This course mainly explains the molecular transmission and expression of genetic information. It provides a comprehensive and systematic introduction to basic issues of modern molecular biology such as chromosome structure, DNA replication forms and characteristics, DNA transposition, deciphering of genetic codes, protein synthesis and operation, principles of gene expression regulation, cancer and oncogene activation, and the molecular mechanism of immunodeficiency virus (HIV). Through 50 hours of classroom teaching, the course not only introduces students to the basic knowledge of molecular biology, but also provides students with a certain understanding of the development history, basic concepts, basic techniques and methods of molecular biology, and some new developments. To enable students to master the basic knowledge of molecular biology and have a basic overall understanding of this science. Its goal is to enable students to master the basic biochemical properties of nucleic acids; to be familiar with the storage and expression process of biological information; to master the basic metabolic processes of DNA, RNA and proteins, especially the general structure and biological function of genes, modification and regulation of gene activity, and basic knowledge related to genes and development; to master the basic technologies and principles of molecular cloning and DNA recombination, to understand the basic research methods of modern molecular biology, to understand the basic pathogenic principles of cancer and other diseases, as well as new achievements and developments in gene therapy.

Name: Plant Biology
Introduction:
Plant biology is a comprehensive botany course, which includes some basic knowledge of traditional plant morphology, physiology, developmental biology, taxonomy, ecology, biogeography and evolutionary biology. It introduces the growth and development, structure and function of plants from a dynamic perspective, as well as the processes and results of plant ontogeny and phylogeny. From cells, tissues, organs, individuals, groups to species, this article systematically introduces the variation patterns and laws of different plant groups in terms of morphological structure, growth and development, reproduction, diversity, classification and distribution, system and evolution, in order to better understand and explain the relationship between the morphological structure, function, evolutionary adaptation and diversity of plants. _x000D_
      The course adopts a variety of teaching methods such as classroom lectures, group discussions, and small topic discussions. It aims to enable students to acquire basic theories, basic knowledge and basic professional skills of plant biology, and to master the history and development trends of some important theories and major discoveries in plant biology. The course focuses on the cultivation of students' innovative thinking ability, independent observation, analysis and problem-solving abilities, and also serves to "cultivate high-quality botany professionals who can adapt to the requirements of modern society".

Name: Basic Molecular Biology Laboratory
Prerequisite:
Molecular Biology Theory Course, study of the principles of experimental studies.
Theoretical course in microbiology, studying the principles and methods of microbiological operations.
Introduction:
This course is designed to train students in basic experimental methods and techniques in molecular biology. During the experiment, students will master the basic principles and result analysis methods of basic molecular biology experiments, and gain corresponding experimental skills and operational training. The course includes the following parts:_x000D_
1. Isolation and purification of plasmid DNA. Understand the basic structural characteristics of plasmid vectors, master the technology of extracting and purifying plasmid DNA, learn to use centrifugation equipment, and learn to culture bacteria. (6 hours)_x000D_
2. Restriction endonuclease digestion of plasmid DNA. Understand restriction endonucleases and enzyme cutting conditions, and learn to analyze the enzyme cutting patterns of plasmid DNA. (6 hours)_x000D_
3. DNA agarose gel electrophoresis. Systematically master the basic techniques of agarose gel electrophoresis and learn to analyze electrophoresis patterns. (6 hours)_x000D_
4. Preparation of E. coli competent cells and introduction of plasmid DNA molecules into prokaryotic cells. Understand the concept of cell transformation and its significance in molecular biology research, and learn the method of preparing E.coli DH5α competent cells by calcium chloride method and the method of transferring exogenous plasmid DNA into recipient bacterial cells and screening transformants. (8 hours)_x000D_
5. Use PCR technology to amplify the GFP gene. To enable students to understand the principles, influencing factors and precautions of using PCR for gene amplification. (8 hours)_x000D_

Name: Film and Television Music
Introduction:
Basic purpose: _x000D_
Films, which were born in the late 19th century, and television, which was born in the 1920s, have become the audio-visual arts with the greatest influence, the largest number of viewers, the most popular and popular audio-visual arts in the world today. The music that influences them is the most active and artistically appealing and indispensable part of the film and television arts. This course takes history as the basis and famous Chinese and foreign film and television music masterpieces as the latitude, and introduces a number of famous films in simple and easy-to-understand terms. Business cards of famous Chinese and foreign film and television music, masterpieces, music fragments of masterpieces, and successful musical works in various forms and genres, combined with the works, introduce the development, expression techniques, functions, functions, meanings, etc. of film and television music. They can experience film and television music works from an aesthetic perspective, make full use of multimedia, and combine theory with sight and hearing, so that students can fully appreciate and appreciate the artistic beauty of film and television music. _x000D_
Content summary:_x000D_
  Introduction to film music, the combination of film images and music, music of different film types, feature film music, overview of film music, TV drama music, TV cultural program music, TV film music, TV advertising music, etc. _x000D_
Teaching method: mainly classroom lectures, using multimedia, audio, etc._x000D_
Student performance evaluation method: final examination of each semester (percentage system). _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Emergency Treatment of Cardiovascular Disease
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
Data show that nearly 550,000 people die from sudden cardiac death in my country every year. Effective cardiac treatment is crucial: within 4 minutes of cardiac arrest, immediate high-quality cardiac compressions and timely electric defibrillation are likely to save a fresh life; immediate treatment for acute myocardial infarction can avoid myocardial necrosis to the greatest extent and reduce the mortality rate; correct handling of sudden palpitations, amaurosis, and brief loss of consciousness can lay the foundation for subsequent treatment. Unfortunately, time and life are often missed due to the patient not being diagnosed and treated in time, the witnesses not being able to provide timely and effective rescue, or various other factors. Doctors lament that if more time is given, the clinical results will be different, but the regret of medicine is that there are not so many ifs. _x000D_
Every second counts in the treatment of cardiovascular emergencies. For this reason, Professor Chen Hong, director of the Heart Center of Peking University People's Hospital, has specially opened a summer course on "Cardiovascular Emergency Treatment". The teaching content includes four units: sudden death first aid, acute chest pain diagnosis and treatment, arrhythmia identification and treatment, and treatment of transient loss of consciousness. The teaching format is: theoretical teaching + internship or apprenticeship. _x000D_
It is hoped that through the study of the "Cardiovascular Emergency Treatment" summer course, students will be able to learn the basic principles and procedures of manual first aid for sudden cardiac death and the treatment of cardiovascular emergencies. _x000D_

Name: Cell Biology
Prerequisite: Initial courses: physics, inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, biochemistry
Introduction:
Basically, the lectures are taught in the order of the textbook content and chapters. It is divided into seventeen chapters and fifty-four sections. Main content_x000D_
_x000D_
Taking the cell's membrane system, skeleton system, gene expression system and gene expression as the framework, it introduces the structure of cells from the perspective of cell biology_x000D_
_x000D_
structure and its functions. At the same time, he also teaches about cell proliferation, differentiation, aging, and the origin and evolution of cells and other related cell biology_x000D_
_x000D_
Basic knowledge of physics.

Name: Cell Biology Laboratory
Prerequisite: First, the "cytology" course helps to understand the cytological phenomena involved in the experiment.
Introduction: "Cell Biology Experiment" is a basic experimental course for undergraduate students. The purpose of the course is to help students master the basic principles and operating methods of cell biology experiments through several representative experiments, intuitively observe various cells and cell life activities, and learn to record and analyze experimental results. Among them, the core experimental technology is microscopic imaging technology, and the core biological concepts are "diversity of cell structure and function" and "compatibility of cell structure and function".

Name: Genetics
Introduction: Genetics is a highly logical subject. The idea of ​​genetic analysis runs through the entire development history of genetics, and has always guided research in the cutting-edge fields of life sciences, playing an irreplaceable role. Starting from Mendel's laws, this course takes the structure and function of genetic material as well as the laws of inheritance and variation as the main line. It systematically introduces the basic principles of classical genetics and modern genetics, taking into account the development frontiers and hot spots of genetics, and always runs through the idea of ​​genetic analysis. During the teaching process, the core ideas and methods of genetics are emphasized, and students are focused on cultivating students' ability to analyze and solve problems, so that students can not only understand the development history of genetics, master the basic concepts and theoretical systems of genetics, correctly understand the relationship between genetics and other subjects, but more importantly, be able to master the methods and ways of thinking of genetic analysis. The teaching content of this course closely focuses on the two core missions of stable transmission of genetic material and determining traits. From genes to genomes, it introduces the inheritance and mutation laws of viruses, bacteria, fungi, plants, animals, humans and other biological models at multiple levels such as molecules, cells, individuals, and groups. It strives to build an all-round and multi-level ideological system and knowledge structure of genetics. The specific contents of this course include: Mendelian genetic analysis; chromosomal theory of inheritance and linkage analysis; gene concepts and mutations; chromosomal aberrations; genome analysis; genetic analysis and genetic transformation of fungi; genetic analysis of bacteria and viruses; human disease and inheritance; extranuclear genetic analysis; gene expression and regulation; epigenetic analysis; genes and development; genes and tumors/developmental abnormalities; population inheritance and evolution. In addition, this course will help students deeply master and flexibly apply the knowledge they have learned by arranging exercises and exercises.

Name: Biostatistics
Introduction:
Biostatistics uses probability theory and mathematical statistics methods to investigate, collect, organize, and analyze experimental data related to biological sciences, so as to judge and analyze biological science issues and reveal their regularity. Biostatistics can also provide a basis for experimental design, production, and practice in biological sciences. _x000D_
_x000D_
The biostatistics course mainly introduces basic knowledge of probability theory, statistical inference, variance analysis, regression analysis, non-parametric statistics, etc. Through learning, students can initially master the methods of biological science experimental design, data collection, analysis, and inference, and develop students' ability to actually apply statistical methods. _x000D_

Name: Genetics Discussion Section
Prerequisite: The subject is chosen at the same time as the theoretical course on Genetics.
Introduction: This course is an accompanying discussion session for the compulsory subject of genetics.

Name: Advanced Neurobiology
Introduction: The Molecular and Cellular Neurobiology course is an elective course for undergraduate students who are interested in neuroscience or who need further study in neuroscience-related fields. The main content of this course is that through study, electives can not only understand and master the basic knowledge of neurobiology, but also understand the scientific research methods and thinking methods of neurobiology. The course content mainly covers the basic structure of the nervous system, the generation and conduction of intracellular nerve signals, the transmission of nerve information between cells, the development of the nervous system, the neural mechanisms of auditory and visual information processing, the advanced and complex functions of the brain, the development and plasticity of the brain, etc. Mainly introduces the basic concepts of neurobiology, basic research methods and the latest research progress in neurobiology. The course has discussion classes to promote active learning and communication between students and teachers.

Name: Fundamentals of Pharmacology
Introduction:
Pharmacology is a life science that studies the interaction between drugs and the body. It is a required course for students in all majors of medical science. Pharmacological science provides important research and analysis methods to clarify the nature of life activities, reveal the treatment principles of diseases, and promote the development of biological sciences. The main content of pharmacology is to describe the processes and effects of drugs in the body, clarify their mechanisms of action, and describe adverse reactions of drugs, so as to provide theoretical basis for basic research and rational clinical drug use. _x000D_
Since undergraduates majoring in life sciences and related majors in comprehensive universities do not systematically study pharmacology, problems often arise in basic research work due to a lack of theoretical knowledge in this area. Through the study of the basics of pharmacology in this course, undergraduates majoring in life sciences in comprehensive universities and undergraduates in related majors can understand the internal processes, effects, mechanisms of action, adverse reactions of drugs, basic research and rational drug use of drugs, so that students can be competent in future basic research work. _x000D_

Name: Go (Beginner)
Introduction:

Chess is a traditional chess project that originated in our country and has a history of more than 2,000 years, and it is the chess that the ancients used to refer to in their “books and paintings”. The black-white, two-colored round and square boards with grid lines are the pieces of chess, each of which holds the same kind of game against the other, falls on the board in turn and ultimately wins with the same number of pieces on the board, which are simple but complex. Through matchmaking, intellectual, pottery and accommodative skills can be developed to improve resilience and overall quality. It's an excellent intellectual sports project.
The main subjects of this course are the rules of chess, the basic technical tactics and the theoretical system of chess.
