Name: Appreciation of Modern and Contemporary Architecture
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course will focus on sorting out the occurrence and development of Western modern architecture, combined with the development clues of other Western arts in the same period, to separately discuss the architectural thoughts of the four major modern masters of the first generation, and examine the main influence and different manifestations of their thoughts in Western contemporary architecture. Ultimately, it will reflect on the gaps and differences between the current situation of Chinese modern and contemporary architecture and Western architecture of the same period, thereby raising regional issues and international issues of Chinese contemporary architecture. _x000D_
    By placing the issues of modern and contemporary Chinese architecture in a broader international perspective, we hope to not only expand non-architecture students' general vision of architecture, but also hope that they can re-evaluate and examine Chinese modern and contemporary architecture and urban issues in conjunction with their own majors. _x000D_

Name: Nietzsche's Thus Spoke Zarathustra
Introduction: This class is a reading class for the famous Western philosophy-literary work "Thus Spoke Zarathustra". You should read through the 90 chapters of the book, and focus on some main chapters. Nietzsche's works have a great influence in China, especially this masterpiece, which has been translated into more than ten versions since Lu Xun. This lesson uses the latest translation for interpretation.

Name: Disease Detective Work
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Epidemiology has become an indispensable methodological discipline in the study of diseases and health that targets populations. This course uses storytelling to interpret and analyze classic examples of disease epidemiological research at home and abroad in ancient and modern times. It aims to introduce epidemiological research ideas and methods, especially its role in discovering and exploring the causes of disease, preventing, controlling and treating diseases. Epidemiological methods are an important methodological discipline, not only applicable to the medical field, but also to other natural science fields. Through storytelling, this course will lead students to "detect" diseases and help students cultivate and improve their scientific research thinking skills in simple and in-depth ways.

Name: Fascinating Science in the Solar System
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Humanity's modern scientific enlightenment began with the observation of the solar system: the formulation of Newton's laws largely came from human beings' summary of the laws of planetary motion. The emergence of modern science and technology has promoted further human exploration of the solar system. On the other hand, these explorations themselves have also made huge contributions to the development of various disciplines. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is open to students from various disciplines (including liberal arts students and science students). It selects some interesting observational phenomena in the study of the solar system. While introducing these interesting phenomena, it also explores the scientific principles behind them. Therefore, the purpose of this course is not only to show the colorful solar system, but also to use the solar system as a platform to demonstrate the power of logic and critical thinking in modern scientific research: When encountering an unsolved mystery, how should we solve it? _x000D_
_x000D_
To this end, our class assignment questions will be more open-ended and will not have standard answers, but will encourage more original ideas and critical thinking on existing knowledge. We strongly encourage students to ask questions and actively participate in class discussions and group discussions. At the end of the semester, each student will complete a thesis on a topic of their own choice (or choose one of the given topics). The final grade will be composed of homework (30%), discussion participation (20%) and thesis (50%).

Name: Classics of Chinese Folk Instrumental Music
Prerequisite: There are no prior course limits for this course
Introduction: The first is the international summer school curriculum, Chinese National Music, in 2009; the second is the school-wide elective course, Chinese Traditional Music Studies, in 2010; and the third is the school-wide popular selection course, Chinese Music Theory and Practice (1-7). The changes were based on exploration, reality and adaptation of teaching content and methods. In 2018, the Chinese National Instrument Book was renamed after the three rounds of teaching, with three original purposes: first, based on famous work, emphasizing listening and appreciation, and refining Chinese music; second, streamlining the system, sharpening its focus, and seeking to achieve excellence and depth; and third, inviting Chinese music students to the classroom, explaining their names, inviting prominent Chinese musicians to conduct classroom concerts, performing live performances, sharing hearts, and giving students a deeper and more comprehensive understanding of Chinese culture, based on a combination of rationality and sense, performances and mutual appreciation.

Name: Basic Skills in Scientific Research
Introduction:
This course is intended to challenge highly motivated, gifted undergraduate life sciences majors to acquire the fundamental skills necessary to communicate research progress both orally and in written form.

The students will have direct experience with poster presentations, oral presentations, scientific ethics, abstract writing, literature review and the writing of a standard scientific manuscript for publication.

Upon completion of the course, students will have a high awareness of the typical responsibilities of international research scientists, with enhanced motivation and competence, after having participated in simulations of real world scientific communication.

Name: Advanced Cell Biology
Introduction: In order to improve the quality of teaching and better help students understand the basic knowledge of cell biology and the research trends in cutting-edge fields, we plan to offer a cell biology (small class, 15-30 students) course (48 hours of teaching + 24 hours of special discussion) in the spring for second-year undergraduate students in the School of Life Sciences who have a solid foundation and excellent grades, and who may continue to work in life sciences in the future. While focusing on the teaching of basic knowledge, this course keeps up with the development of cutting-edge fields and appropriately involves current new technologies and new ideas; it cultivates students' rigorous and realistic scientific attitudes and innovative scientific research abilities. It is also equipped with experimental courses (64 hours) corresponding to the basics and progress of modern cell biology to deepen the understanding of the course content.

Name: Chess (Beginner)
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
Chess is the most popular intellectual competition in the world. It is not restricted by region, gender, age, venue, or equipment. It has the functions of quality education, cultural exchange, scientific research, and entertainment. It is known as the "gymnastics of wisdom." Learning chess can promote the all-round development of observation, attention, memory, thinking, imagination, independent operation ability and creativity. It also plays a positive role in moral education and the cultivation of good psychological qualities such as firmness and courage, aggressiveness, fair competition, and alertness and adaptability. _x000D_
This course mainly teaches the basic rules of chess, basic techniques and tactics, as well as basic knowledge of chess competition, history and culture. Through teaching exercises and explanations, students can initially master the actual game ability and basic knowledge of chess. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students' interest in chess, which is conducive to the overall development of physical and mental health. _x000D_
2. Enable students to master the basic knowledge and skills of chess and be able to play the game skillfully. _x000D_
3. Let students have a preliminary understanding of chess culture and gain some inspiration for their study, life and future development. _x000D_

Name: Advanced Genetics Laboratory
Prerequisite: It's best to start with genetics theory, life science basics.
Introduction:
Genetics experiments have always been a required course for undergraduates in the School of Life. It is offered in the spring semester of each year. The teaching targets are second-year undergraduate students, with an average number of about 120 students per year. Starting from the fall of 2015, genetics experimental courses were added in the fall semester. _x000D_
    Genetics experiments have always focused on continuous improvement. In the past three consecutive semesters, we have adopted a new teaching model in four classes and introduced many new course contents and teaching methods. The feedback from students has been very good. Students in the lower grades (grade 1) were exposed to knowledge and experiments that they had never learned or practiced before, and reported that they benefited a lot. Students in senior grades (grades 2-3) have better feedback. Many knowledge and experimental designs that they did not understand before were suddenly understood through the training of our experimental courses. However, since the original experimental class only had one credit, the content and class hours of the course were far beyond the limit, and students asked for additional credits. _x000D_
    Therefore, this course is improved on the basis of basic genetics experimental courses and designed to coordinate with basic experiments in modern life sciences. Experiments are designed for the purpose of studying gene functions, and new teaching models such as open research results and open laboratories are adopted to allow students to complete this course in the form of completing small projects. _x000D_
    In addition to the classic basic technical training in genetics, the experimental content allows students to directly participate in genetic hybridization and molecular testing of related links in the scientific research laboratory, and confocal observation of brain imaging phenotypes after gene knockout and labeling, so that the experimental class can be directly integrated with the cutting-edge of scientific research. Let students establish the following knowledge framework: using genetics ideas and using knowledge and experimental techniques from different disciplines to achieve the purpose of studying gene functions. _x000D_

Name: Australian Studies
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is co-taught by David Walker, BHP Billiton Chair Professor of Australian Studies at Peking University, an academician of the Australian Academy of Humanities, and an academician of the Academy of Social Sciences, and Dr. Chen Changwei of the School of International Relations of Peking University. It intends to provide a systematic explanation and analysis of Australia from the aspects of history, politics, economy and culture, covering Australia's indigenous culture, construction of political system, economic development, immigration movement, ecology, resources, environment, lifestyle, values, film and literature, etc. This course will also examine the historical process of how Australia went from "maintaining white racial purity" to developing "multiculturalism", and how a country closely related to its British heritage adapted to and faced the reality of the rise of Asia. _x000D_
This course is designed to help students gain a comprehensive and profound understanding of Australia, including its historical traditions and its status and role in today's international society. With the development of bilateral relations between China and Australia in recent years, the two countries have become increasingly interdependent in politics, economy, culture and other aspects. At present, China is not only Australia's most important trading partner, but also has replaced the United Kingdom as the main source of new immigrants to Australia. Therefore, it is of obvious value and significance for Chinese students to understand Australia, an important country in the South Pacific.

Name: Squash
Introduction:
Squash is an indoor sport invented by the British in the 19th century. Squash in the true sense was invented by students of the famous aristocratic school - Harrow School. It was named after the ball made a sound similar to the English "SQUASH" when it violently touched the wall, which is now recognized as squash. In 1864, the first dedicated squash court was built in Harrow, marking the official founding of the sport. _x000D_
Squash is a new sport suitable for people of all walks of life and of all ages. It is also known as a lifelong sport. As an activity to exercise and improve health, squash is a long-term health investment that can benefit people physically and psychologically, and enhance their self-confidence and willpower. Squash is a highly interesting sport and plays a great role in training basic physical qualities, especially in improving agility, speed, endurance and coordination. _x000D_
Squash is an elegant and entertaining sport that is suitable for all ages and is not restricted by seasons or climatic conditions. It has the characteristics of sufficient exercise in a short period of time. Each round is about 20-30 minutes. The amount of exercise is equivalent to 2-3 hours of tennis. For modern people with busy work, it has excellent effects in eliminating physical and mental fatigue and tension. _x000D_
Currently, more than 80 million people in more than 80 countries and regions around the world engage in this sport, with the largest number of people in Europe and the United States, and more than 10 million people in the United States alone. In Asia, Pakistan has the largest number of participants in the sport and has won the world championship many times. There are also four famous tournaments in the professional squash world, namely the British Open, the Hong Kong Open, the Championship held in New York, USA, and the World Open. Every June, another super tournament is held for the top 8 players in the world in the previous year. A match can be a best-of-three or best-of-five match, depending on the choice of the match organizer. Each game should be played to 11 points. The first player to reach 11 points wins, but when the scores are tied at 10, the game should continue until one player leads by two points. Both players can score. The server wins a point and retains the right to serve. The receiving side counts one point when winning a rally and gains the right to serve. _x000D_
Through squash exercise, you can cultivate comprehensive abilities such as speed, endurance, strength, agility, coordination, etc., and comprehensively improve physical fitness; it can improve aerobic metabolism, improve cardiopulmonary function, and promote the overall development of physical and mental quality. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to the History of Western Civilization
Introduction: Introduction to the History of Western Civilization is a general elective course in world history and is a national quality course selected by the Ministry of Education (2006). It aims to analyze and see through the characteristics and development process of Western civilization from a Chinese perspective. The characteristics of Western civilization, national character, national character, way of thinking, cultural traditions, advantages and disadvantages are taught in different topics, and the integration of civilizations is discussed from the perspective of globalization. It is believed that the mutual influence and integration of Eastern and Western civilizations will lead to the development of world civilization.

Name: Game Theory
Prerequisite:
"Calculus": It is required to be able to find derivatives and integrals. _x000D_
"Probability Theory": It is required to understand the probability distribution function and master the concepts and calculation methods of Bayes' rule and mathematical expectation.
Introduction:
The theory of gaming is the theory of multi-person interactive decision-making, which is the cornerstone of the rationality of social sciences, even referred to as the mathematical foundation of social sciences.
The course is closely focused on non-cooperative game theory and systematically teaches the basic concepts, ideas and methods of game theory, including complete information static game, full information dynamic game, incomplete information static game and incomplete information dynamic game.
This course combines political, economic and social examples to solve the game, with cases, experiments, discussions throughout the classroom.

Name: Immunology
Introduction:
Introduction: including a brief history and prospects of the development of immunology (empirical immunology period, scientific immunology period, modern immunology period); basic content of immunology; immunopathology and immune diseases; immunology applications, etc.	_x000D_
Immune organs: central immune organs, peripheral immune organs_x000D_
Immune cells (1): monocytes and macrophages, neutrophils, NK cells, eosinophils, basophils and mast cells_x000D_
Immune cells (2): T, B lymphocytes and antigen-presenting cells_x000D_
Immune molecules (1): basic structure of antibody molecules, characteristics of antibody molecule classes and subclasses, Fc receptors of antibody molecules, molecular mechanism of antibody class switching, antibody gene rearrangement and B cell development, etc. _x000D_
Immune molecules (2): components of the complement system, alternative pathways of complement activation, MBP pathway of complement activation, classical pathways of complement activation, complement receptors and other functions of the complement system, etc._x000D_
Immune molecules (3): major histocompatibility complex; structure and polymorphism of human MHC genes, antigen peptide binding units of MHC molecules, processing and presentation of protein antigens, etc. _x000D_
Immune Molecules (4): Cytokines, main characteristics and types of cytokines, cytokine receptors; Cytokines and clinical, etc._x000D_
Antigens and adhesion molecules: physical and chemical properties of antigens, T and B cell epitopes in antigen molecules, immunogenicity of antigens, classification of antigens, adhesion molecules including integrin family, selectin family, functions of adhesion molecules, etc._x000D_
Cellular immune response: activation of T cells, specific recognition of antigens, dual signal model of T cell activation, effects of cellular immune response, MHC restriction of ɑβ-T cells, functions of helper T cells and killer T cells_x000D_
Humoral immune response: humoral immune response induced by TI antigen and primary and secondary humoral immune response induced by TD antigen, etc._x000D_
Hypersensitivity reactions: IgE-mediated hypersensitivity reactions, type II and type III hypersensitivity reactions, cell-mediated type IV hypersensitivity reactions, etc._x000D_
Anti-tumor immunity_x000D_
Application technology: Immunological detection methods and applications

Name: Neurobiology
Prerequisite:
Undergraduate students with a foundation in biology can take this elective. _x000D_
This course introduces basic knowledge of neurobiology to undergraduate students. The content includes basic knowledge of the nervous system, basic knowledge of cellular and molecular neurobiology, and the main functions of the central nervous system. The lecture content mainly focuses on the basic knowledge of cellular and molecular neurobiology, explaining in detail all aspects of the information transmission process between nerve cells, laying a foundation for students to further study neuroscience.
Introduction:
This course is an introduction to the basic knowledge of neurobiology for undergraduates. The content includes basic knowledge of the nervous system, basic knowledge of cellular and molecular neurobiology, and the main functions of the central nervous system. The lecture content mainly focuses on the basic knowledge of cellular and molecular neurobiology, explaining in detail all aspects of the information transmission process between nerve cells, laying a foundation for students to further study neuroscience. _x000D_
The purpose of the course is to provide undergraduate students with a preliminary understanding of the basic knowledge of neurobiology and lay a foundation for their further study of neuroscience. Due to the rich content of neuroscience, it is impossible for this course to explain all the knowledge of neuroscience. More than 30 class hours introduce some basic knowledge of neurobiology.

Name: Modern Greek Film and History
Introduction:
This course aims to provide a perspective on the historical process of modern Greece through nearly fifty years of contemporary Greek cinema. _x000D_
Greek films have attracted much attention in recent years. Greek directors have conducted in-depth investigations and reflections on important events in modern Greek history, such as the defeat of Asia Minor in 1922, the great political schism between the two wars, the civil war, and the military dictatorship of the 1960s and 1970s. Other topics, including rural out-migration, urbanization and immigration in the mid-20th century, gender relations, the living conditions of women, especially women in small towns, identity confusion in modern Greece and its relationship with the historical inheritance of ancient Greece, etc., are also discussed in this course. _x000D_
Greek film directors are particularly outstanding in their clear understanding of social problems and the condition of human existence in an alienated environment, sometimes blurring reality, homesickness and dreams, and expressing them in a poetic and touching way. In addition, this course will also mention the relationship between film and history, literature and art. _x000D_
Greek film directors this course will examine include Theo Angelopoulos, Michael Cacoyannis, Pantelis Voulgaris, Tassos Boulmetis and Yannis Smaragdis. _x000D_

Name: Concise Quantum Mechanics
Prerequisite: None. It's just high school math and physics.
Introduction:
Quantum mechanics was born in the early twentieth century and is one of the most profound revolutions in the history of science. It subverts many basic concepts in classical physics and describes for us the magical behavior of atoms, molecules and smaller elementary particles. Moreover, the technological revolution it brings has profoundly changed and is profoundly changing all aspects of human society. Despite its importance, for a long time quantum mechanics was concerned only by physicists and a few chemists and philosophers. Recently, with the development of quantum information technology, quantum mechanics has attracted more and more public attention. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course attempts to provide a serious yet popular introduction to quantum mechanics to all students at Peking University (including liberal arts students). Popularity means telling and showing the beauty and magic of quantum mechanics to as many people as possible. Being serious means using mathematics to describe the most profound results in quantum mechanics, rather than just describing them in words. It is impossible to understand any science accurately without mathematics. Peking University students are familiar with high school mathematics knowledge. For any mathematics beyond the high school level, such as matrices, linear spaces, etc., I will introduce as much as needed, without going too deep. Therefore, these mathematics beyond the high school level are not difficult. As long as students have the patience to do some simple after-school exercises, they will quickly become familiar with and master them. Without practice there is no understanding. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will first briefly describe the development history of quantum mechanics, introduce the fathers of quantum and their legendary deeds, and then try to give a brief overview of classical physics at the high school physics level. After these preparations, we start to talk about the magical quantum mechanics: quantum state, quantum probability, linear superposition, quantum entanglement, Bell's inequality, Heisenberg uncertainty relation, Schrödinger's cat, quantum isomorphism, quantum measurement, quantum communication, quantum calculation, multi-world explanation, etc. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Modern Biotechnology
Introduction: Research in modern biotechnology has moved rapidly to molecular levels, and the whole research methodology and detection methods are very different from traditional biotechnology, and these differences determine that the focus of the course is on the revolutionary changes that have taken place in various areas of biotechnology, so that students can fully understand the similarities between tradition and modern biotechnology. In addition, modern biotechnology is a highly technical discipline developed on the basis of disciplines such as molecular biology, biochemistry, microbiology and genetics, so the course will focus on examples of applications that present some of the patterns common to modern biotechnology applications and development, as well as the principles and methods common to some of the special circumstances, so that students can learn some of the solutions to problems, not just new technologies and new advances; and to learn from scientific thinking, thereby enhancing the capacity for independent thinking, independent judgement, which is the basic qualities of modern biotechnology research.

Name: Introduction to the Development of Medicine
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
"Introduction to Medical Development" brings together the advantages of academicians and well-known professors from Peking University School of Medicine, and the essence of cutting-edge fields in medical-related disciplines. It focuses on hot topics in the medical field and adopts a simple and easy-to-understand approach. In just dozens of hours, students will have an overview of the trends and hot spots in today's medical development, gain a preliminary understanding of medical development, increase their interest in medicine, and enrich their medical knowledge. _x000D_
    "Introduction to Medical Development" adopts the method of medical science education and is taught by well-known experts and professors in relevant majors, so that students can understand the current research and development trends of basic medicine, clinical medicine, stomatology, pharmacy and preventive medicine. The course content covers: genetic composition and research of human diseases, clinical application of stem cell bioengineering, research on blood diseases and bone marrow transplantation, organ transplantation, assisted reproductive technology, current status and future of cardiovascular disease treatment, mental illness and mental health, as well as the development trends of surgery, orthopedics, oral science, modern drug research, and the current status and future of my country's public health development. _x000D_

Name: Animal Biology Laboratory
Introduction: Animal biology is one of the basic courses in biology. Animal biology experiments deepen students' understanding of animal biology theory through morphological observation and internal structure anatomy of real animals, gain a more comprehensive understanding of the morphology and physiological functions of various categories of animals, and gain an in-depth understanding of the basic laws of life that correspond to structure and function, as well as the evolution of animals from simple to complex. At the same time, students' basic experimental skills will be improved through hands-on anatomy training, and students' ability to discover and observe wild animals will be improved through field observation tasks, laying the foundation for subsequent biological science experimental research. Teacher lectures and students' practical operations are the main teaching methods, supplemented by multimedia interaction, individual tutoring and field practice.

Name: Animal Biology
Introduction:
Animal biology is one of the basic courses in biology. Use classroom lectures, group discussions and other forms to help students master the basic characteristics of the main categories involved in the evolution of animals, the interrelationships between morphological structures and functions, the basic laws of animal life activities, the theory and important stages of biological evolution, the geographical distribution of animals and their relationship with the environment, etc., laying a solid foundation for the study of subsequent courses. _x000D_
Main teaching content: basic characteristics of animals; concepts of animal tissues, organs and systems; distribution, morphological structure and function of basic animal tissues in the animal body; the position of animals in biological boundaries and basic knowledge of animal classification; early embryonic development of animals, including germ layer differentiation. concepts such as morphology, body cavity type, animal body, and segmentation; the progressive characteristics, adaptability characteristics, specialization characteristics, systematic evolutionary processes of key animal categories with great evolutionary significance, and their significance in animal evolution; the classification status of important groups and representative species of animals in each major category. Using the method of comparative anatomy, students will learn about the evolution and adaptive significance of the structure and function of animal organ systems from aspects such as animal protection, support and movement, excretion and water-salt balance, respiration, digestion, circulation, lymphatics and immunity, nerves, endocrine and regulation, and reproduction, and understand the basic laws of animal life activities and the unity of the animal body. In addition, this course is also required to understand the life history of the earth and the important stages of animal evolution, the development of Darwinian evolution and post-Darwinian evolution, as well as the neutral theory, small evolution, and large evolution of molecular evolution. And from the perspective of biodiversity conservation, understand the geographical distribution, fauna, animal diversity and relationship with the living environment of animals. _x000D_

Name: Plant Biology Laboratory
Introduction: The Plant Biology Experimental Course is an experimental course offered in conjunction with the Plant Biology Theory Course. It is a compulsory backbone basic course for undergraduates in the School of Life Sciences. The experimental course content includes basic experiments in various branches of plant biology, such as plant cytology, plant morphological anatomy, plant taxonomy, plant physiology, etc. The purpose is to deepen students' understanding of the basic theories and experimental principles of plant biology, master the basic skills of plant biology experiments, stimulate students' interest in learning plant biology, and further cultivate students' scientific thinking ability to find, think about, and solve problems in practice.

Name: Exercise, Nutrition and Weight Loss
Prerequisite: There is no need for a first course, which is open to students of the North who are healthy.
Introduction:
The improvement of social productivity promotes the process of social civilization, but also brings about overnutrition and insufficient exercise. Exercise, Nutrition and Weight Loss is an applied course that teaches students to use sports human science as the theoretical guidance, scientific exercise methods as the main means, and reasonable nutrition as the auxiliary method to consume fat beyond normal weight, so as to obtain or maintain the ideal weight and body composition ratio. _x000D_
The teaching content of the course mainly consists of three parts, which are summarized in one word as "NEW". "N" refers to "Nutrition: Nutrition", which teaches the basic knowledge of nutrition; "E" refers to "Exercise: Exercise", which tells the scientific core of exercise; "W" refers to "Weigh Losing: Weight Loss", which teaches the practical operation of fat loss. The first two parts are the basis and premise of the third part. The third part is the synthesis and application of the first two parts. _x000D_
The teaching format of the classroom can be represented by another letter "PEPPER", which also reflects the requirements of the course. "P" refers to Presentation, including teacher's theoretical lectures and student discussion statements; it also refers to Practice:, balanced dietary practice in nutrition classes; "E" exercise: exercise practice, also refers to Evaluation, exercise ability assessment and dietary assessment. “R”: Report, kThe experimental or practical report required for the course. Therefore, the requirements of this course are that students have topic discussions after the teacher’s theoretical explanation; they will also carry out relevant physical activities in accordance with the teaching progress, and sports shoes and loose sportswear are required; they must write a practice report after the classroom activity practice class; they must write an experimental report after the measurement and evaluation course. _x000D_

Name: What a Plant Knows
Introduction:
Enter the plant world you don’t know and think about the real existence of life! _x000D_
      How does the Venus flytrap know when to close its leaves? Can it really feel the insect's tiny, spindly legs? How do cherry blossom trees know when to bloom? Can they really remember the weather? _x000D_
      For centuries, we have been amazed by the diversity and form of plants. Renowned biologist Daniel Chamowitz now gives a rigorous and engaging explanation of how plants experience the world, whether it's the colors they see or the schedules they follow, in Plants Know the Answers to Life. _x000D_
Highlighting the latest research in areas such as genetics, Daniel Chamowitz takes us into the inner world of plants, contrasting their feelings with our own, revealing that we have more in common with sunflowers and oak trees than you know. Daniel Chamowitz will show you how plants tell up from down, how they know when a neighboring species has been attacked by a swarm of hungry beetles, whether they appreciate the Led Zeppelin music you've been playing to them, or whether they prefer the melodious riffs of Bach. Through the investigation of plant touch, hearing, smell, vision and even memory, we have to think: Are plants aware of their surrounding environment? _x000D_
     The course "Plants Know the Answers to Life" is a rare in-depth attention to the grass we walk on, the flowers we smell, and the trees we climb, allowing us to better understand science and our place in nature.

Name: Plant Morphogenesis
Introduction: Plants are one of three types of multicellular eukaryotes on Earth. We can understand the differences between plants, animals and fungi from the senses, but why these differences occur, this course will analyze this issue. First, we will introduce the characteristics of plant cells and their origins, and then we will introduce the basic framework through which multicellular organisms are formed - the sexual reproductive cycle. It is on this framework that plants, animals and fungi have developed different morphogenesis strategies due to their different ways of acquiring energy. On this basis, we will analyze how cells assemble into more complex structures. Different from other perspectives that introduce plants, we will analyze the morphology of plants from three aspects: morphological boundaries, genetic consistency and life cycle completion to help everyone understand that a plant is not an "individual" as we usually think of it, but a coral-like aggregate composed of many "developmental units" that can complete the life cycle relatively independently. We will also introduce how plants, like animals, start from a single-cell zygote. Driven by photosynthetic autotrophy, they continue to increase the photosynthetic area, thus forming the appearance you see. Because of the increase in photosynthetic area, they face increased internal and external stress, and are forced back to the sexual reproduction cycle that occurs at the single-cell level. What is even more interesting is that such a process from single cells to multicellularity and back to single cells occurs not only in the diploid state, but also in the haploid state. In short, we will help everyone understand how such unique forms of plants are built from a new perspective.

Name: Animal Histology and Embryology with Laboratory
Introduction:
Histology and Embryology is a professional life science course that studies the microstructure and morphogenesis of animal bodies. It is a continuation and in-depth study of animal biology. It is a necessary preparation for branches such as physiology, cell biology, and developmental biology. It is also an important basic course in the field of medical research. _x000D_
    This course uses paraffin section observation of tissues of various vertebrates (fish, frogs, chickens, mice, rabbits, horses, cats, dogs, etc.) as the basic experimental method to learn in detail the four basic tissues of animals: epithelial tissue, connective tissue, muscle tissue, and nervous tissue. After learning the basic organization, we took the human body structure as an example to learn the ten major organ systems of animals: nervous, endocrine, circulatory, immune, respiratory, digestive, urinary, reproductive, skin, and sensory. The focus is on the cellular composition and specialization of each organ, the morphology and regularity of tissue composition, and how to achieve unity with physiological functions. Then, under the theoretical framework of histology, we gain an in-depth understanding of the early development process of animals from fertilization, cleavage, germ layer formation to organogenesis. _x000D_
     This course also offers experiments that complement the theoretical courses, focusing on the unity of theory and practice. Observe sections under a light microscope to further enhance your intuitive understanding of the structure of cells, tissues, and organs. You can also learn the research methods and common techniques of paraffin sectioning and H&E staining of animal tissues, and make sections by yourself. _x000D_
    For students majoring in non-biology, systematic study and understanding of the structure and functions of the human body will help lead a scientific and healthy life.

Name: Plant Diversity and Evolution
Prerequisite: Plant biology, general biology or related courses
Introduction:
The world of plants is rich and colorful. Human life is inseparable from plants, and the survival and development of other life forms on the earth also directly or indirectly depend on plants. There are more than 300,000 species of plants existing on the earth. They respond to different environments in very different ways, and their reproduction strategies and methods are also different, resulting in a plant world with diverse morphological structures and different biological characteristics. So how did such rich diversity of plants come about? What is the evolutionary relationship between them? How were crops, the main economic plants on which humans depend for survival, domesticated? All these questions can be explained through studying this course. At the same time, by understanding the morphological structure characteristics, life history characteristics and species distribution characteristics of various major types of plants, we hope to have an overall understanding of the plant kingdom (in a broad sense) and lay the foundation for students to further understand the biological mechanisms of plant growth, development and inheritance. _x000D_
    This course will take the phylogeny of plants as the main line, use evolutionary biology theory, and follow the evolutionary sequence from ancient to modern, simple to complex, aquatic to terrestrial to introduce the diversity and evolution of plants. It will also combine the latest research results, especially molecular biology, developmental biology, and plant biology. Based on the research results at the genome level, we explore the origin and evolution of various major plant groups and some important innovative traits, such as algae, liverworts, mosses, lycophytes, true ferns, gymnosperms, and angiosperms; and focus on introducing some key taxa that are connected in the phylogeny of various groups. At the same time, the course will also systematically introduce the concept and composition of plant species diversity and the identification of common ornamental plants and cultivated crops. This course focuses on cultivating students' innovation and practical abilities. It combines theoretical teaching, special discussions and field identification of plant diversity, cultivates students' innovative thinking ability through a variety of teaching methods, and promotes the mastery and understanding of plant diversity and its evolution through theoretical teaching and the cultivation of practical abilities. _x000D_

Name: Career and Life
Introduction: This course is for undergraduates in the School of Life Sciences. It focuses on the problems faced by students in the School of Life Sciences and provides in-depth study of the theories and techniques of self-awareness and decision-making. It guides students to enhance their awareness of planning, form a correct outlook on career and life, accurately position themselves, cultivate a confident and self-improvement mentality, and provide useful assistance to students in their academic planning, emotional planning and career planning during their time in school.

Name: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Geo-related knowledge, algorithms and data structure (B), computational overview (B)
Introduction: This course is mainly designed for undergraduates who are not majoring in GIS, so it focuses on GIS applications so that students can understand what problems GIS can solve and master the basic skills of using GIS software for data analysis in work and research.

Name: Folklore Research
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: By understanding and studying the main theories, schools and research methods of folklore research, we can increase our knowledge, activate our thinking and develop new ideas. Focusing on the combination of theory and practice, we hope to enhance students' theoretical application and analytical abilities.

Name: Animals and Human Society: An Archaeological Perspective
Introduction: This course will use rich archaeological discoveries and research in major regions of the world, combined with knowledge from ethnology, anthropology, zoogeography and other fields, to teach the relationship between animals and humans in the long historical process from the origin of mankind to the emergence of civilized society. It will enable students to understand the role and significance of animals in the development of human society in different periods, and to understand humankind's own history and culture through this perspective. This course also aims to encourage everyone to think about the relationship between humans, animals, and nature through the past and the present and future.

Name: Public Economics
Prerequisite:
A foundation in microeconomic principles will be helpful in studying this course. _x000D_
This course will also introduce relevant basic concepts and analysis methods of economics as the course progresses. _x000D_
Introduction:
Public economics often starts with market failure and concludes that the public sector needs to intervene. This course does not stop at simply listing the main manifestations of market failure, but intends to further explore whether there are private solutions to market failures and the limitations of private solutions. Then, by revealing the dilemma of public decision-making rules and the possible distortions in the public decision-making process, it explains the various possibilities of "government failure". Through comparative analysis from market failure to government failure, this course hopes to help students better grasp the boundaries between market and government, and deepen students' understanding and insight into important and common public economic issues. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is divided into three parts: first, we discuss the necessity of the public sector from the perspective of market failure, and then explore the possibilities and limitations of private solutions to major aspects of market failure, such as public goods, externalities, and the tragedy of the commons. Secondly, we discuss public economic goals, not only elaborating on various understandings of efficiency goals and fairness goals, but also discussing the rationality and policy implications of freedom as a public economic goal. Third, analyze the rules and processes of public decision-making: in terms of rules, discuss the meaning, characteristics and dilemmas of the principle of unanimous consent and majority voting; in terms of process, elaborate on the behavioral characteristics of the main participants on the demand side and supply side of public decision-making, and implement their impact on the operational efficiency of the public sector; and conclude with an in-depth analysis of government failure. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is not intended to be taught according to a certain textbook, but based on the course syllabus. As the topics related to the course develop, relevant literature is recommended to be read, and discussions and writing of reading reports are encouraged. _x000D_

Name: Rock Climbing
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Rock climbing is a fashionable sport derived from mountaineering. Rock climbing is a sport that relies on hands and feet to grasp the protruding fulcrums and cracks on the rock wall to compete on climbing skills on cliffs or artificial rock walls. Rock climbing requires students to have the courage to move forward on rock walls of various heights and angles, and continuously complete turning, pull-ups, leaps, leaps and even jumps and other exquisite climbing skills. It integrates strength, endurance, coordination, flexibility and balance abilities, and integrates fitness, entertainment and competition. It is an exciting and beautiful extreme sport. It is called "artistic gymnastics on the rock wall" and "ballet on the cliff" by rock climbing fans around the world. _x000D_
2． Safety precautions:_x000D_
Rock climbing is an outdoor sport with certain challenges. It has the nature of adventure or simulated adventure. Therefore, during the implementation of the project, professional protection technology and professional protection equipment are required, which require a high degree of attention from students and teachers. You must keep in mind during the course that it doesn’t matter if you have poor rock climbing skills, but it will be serious if you have poor protection awareness and skills. _x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students' physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, as well as the ideology of "health first". _x000D_
2． Improve health, enhance physical fitness, and comprehensively improve students' physical and psychological qualities. _x000D_
3. Through rock climbing, students can improve their courage to move forward without fear of difficulties and their superb climbing skills. _x000D_
4. Through rock climbing, students' strength, endurance, coordination, flexibility and balance abilities are improved, allowing people to perform in thrilling situations_x000D_
Enjoy the beauty in the performance. _x000D_

Name: Life in Geological History
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: There are no special pre-course requirements for this course.
Introduction: “Life in Earth History” is a popular course for students in the arts and literature across the school, designed to inspire students to think rationally and to inspire students to explore the unknown world. A total of 12 lectures were given by 5-6 teachers of the Prehistoric Institute of Life and Environmental Sciences of the Institute of Earth and Space Science. The first two addresses basic concepts, principles and methods of paleontology, geology, bioclassification and evolution. The latter 10 points of entry for the discovery and significant evolution of some of the key biochemical groups, with the evolution of terrestrial higher plants and vertebrates as the main thread, starting with taxonomy, taking into account the latest discoveries and advances in the field of palaeontology, as well as the results of the teacher ' s own research, as examples, and describing the mystery of biological evolution from the point of view of researchers. In addition, the course provided for one visit to the school geological museum and one internship in the field of fossil gathering in Kyoto.

Name: Social Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Social psychology studies the social psychology and social behavior of individuals and groups and their development rules. This course will cover important concepts and theories in mainstream social psychology. The main contents include: how individuals view themselves and others, how to view and think about social phenomena, human aggression and helping behavior, the formation and change of attitudes, social influence and its manifestations, the basis and intimacy of interpersonal relationships, group psychology and behavior, how culture affects people, social psychological factors that affect human health, and the latest positive psychology and cyberpsychology. This course focuses on the application of social psychology knowledge in social life, the formation and maintenance of interpersonal relationships, the principles of interpersonal communication and conflict resolution, and smooth teamwork. It also focuses on contemporary scholars’ research on human psychology and behavior under different cultural backgrounds. Through the study of this course, students should master the basic concepts, basic theories and commonly used research methods of social psychology, and be able to use this knowledge to explain the social psychological phenomena that occur in our society.

Name: Behavioral Ecology and Conservation Practicum for Wild Primates
Introduction:
Primates, the leader of all things, are a special category of mammals with diverse behaviors, live in groups, and are highly social. Studying the behavior of primates helps us understand the origin and evolution of animals, human society, and behavior. The "Behavioral Ecology and Conservation Practice of Wild Primates" course will lead students to visit the places where wild primates (such as langurs, macaques, golden monkeys, gibbons, etc.) live. By learning animal behavioral ecology research methods, they can directly observe and study the social structure of wild primates, the relationships between individuals and social units, population status, living environment and their social behaviors, including breeding behaviors, feeding behaviors, friendly behaviors, infanticide behaviors, parenting behaviors, aggressive behaviors, etc. It is hoped that through these observations and learning, we can glimpse the shadow of our human ancestors and think about the evolutionary mechanism of animal and human society and behavior. If you love nature and wildlife, come and join our courses! _x000D_
    Through the study of this course, students can master and practice the field investigation and research methods of animal behavioral ecology. On the basis of field observation, students can understand basic knowledge such as the distribution, species, social structure and behavioral characteristics of primates in the world and China, understand the relationship between other animals in primate habitats, such as birds, mammals, insects, plants and primates, think about the evolution of animal and human society and behavior, and cultivate their interest in field research. At the same time, we explore the conservation biology issues of wild animals by participating in community conservation. _x000D_

Name: Conservation Biogeography
Introduction: Life on earth is facing severe challenges from humans. One of the main reasons is the change in surface space utilization pattern caused by development. To formulate environmentally friendly land use plans, or to make the most reasonable investment of limited protection resources in biological groups and geography, we need to have a necessary understanding of the principles, concepts and skills of biogeography. Conservation biogeography is a new discipline. In 2011, several professors from the University of Oxford in the UK wrote the first textbook in six years. It uses the principles, theory and analysis of biogeography to solve problems related to the distribution and dynamics of organisms in biodiversity conservation, including the delineation of important biodiversity areas, protected area design, dynamic conservation planning, biological corridors, invasive species and biological community homogenization. These are the knowledge urgently needed in China and even the global biodiversity conservation actions. This course is suitable for graduate and undergraduate students in conservation biology, ecology, environmental biology, biogeography, or related fields.

Name: Archery
Prerequisite: None. Students who can't shoot can also choose classes.
Introduction:
Archery, also known as Archery, is a sport that uses the elastic force of a bow to shoot out arrows and compete for accuracy within a certain distance. As far back as 10,000 years ago in the Mesolithic Age, humans invented bows and arrows for hunting and fishing. Later, bows and arrows became one of the weapons used in war. Today, bows and arrows exist as a favorite sport for people. _x000D_
Archery class is a physical education course open to all undergraduate students at Peking University. Specific contents include: introduction to the development history of archery; basic knowledge and skills of archery; archery aiming skills, etc. _x000D_
This course adopts a combination of theory and practice. In the process of introducing the origin and development of the project, the basic theory, basic techniques and basic tactics of the semester, students will be familiar with and understand this sport that has a long history but is not yet popular. Then, they will conduct training from shallow to deep, so as to achieve a more proficient mastery of the basic skills of archery, understand the competition rules, and then participate in the competition. This course aims to allow students to learn more sports skills, knowledge and methods, cultivate students' healthy bodies and sound personalities, understand traditional Chinese culture, and make it a means of lifelong physical education choice.

Name: Mathematical Thought, Ancient and Modern
Prerequisite: A semester's course on advanced mathematics.
Introduction: Interpret mathematical classic knowledge, understand the mathematical ideas, thinking methods and values ​​behind mathematical knowledge, and improve high-level mathematical literacy. The plan covers: Some important values ​​in mathematics. Four basic ways of thinking in mathematics. The essence of mathematical existence. Ancient Egyptian and Mesopotamian Mathematics. Ancient Greek Mathematics. Ancient Chinese Mathematics. Ancient Indian Mathematics and Medieval Arabic Mathematics. European Mathematics before Newton-Leibniz. The radical solution of a cubic equation of one variable and the symmetry principle behind the equation. (Most of the mathematical knowledge points involved in the previous ones are middle school mathematics, and a very few are advanced mathematics.) If there is still class time, choose to introduce some mathematical ideas from Newton-Leibniz and later. (The mathematical knowledge points involved in this part are mainly advanced mathematics, and a few of the most important modern mathematical concepts.) The teaching pace and selected content can be adjusted according to the specific circumstances of the class.

Name: Film and Television Appreciation
Introduction:
Basic purpose: _x000D_
This course is open to all students in the school. Based on the intensive reading and appreciation of Chinese and foreign film classics and the explanation of the basic knowledge and principles of modern film and television art, film art will be placed in a broad artistic dimension and a grand cultural background for in-depth analysis in many aspects. The teaching of this course focuses on the use of visual teaching methods and the cultivation of students' open and comprehensive modern thinking methods. This course strives to enable students to not only learn knowledge about film art and film history, but also improve their artistic accomplishments, strengthen their humanistic qualities, cultivate healthy, diverse and open aesthetic tastes, broaden their minds, and develop comprehensive and creative modern thinking abilities. 2 hours and 2 credits per week. _x000D_

Teaching methods: classroom lectures, using multimedia, video and other technologies. _x000D_

Name: Practical Networking Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
This course consists of two parts: theoretical and experimental. _x000D_
      The first part is mainly theoretical explanation. Introduces the most basic knowledge in computer networks. The main contents include: overview of computer networks, basics of network communication, computer LANs and wide area networks, network interconnection and Internet basics, network security, fault diagnosis and maintenance, etc. _x000D_
      The second part is mainly based on computer experiments. In the virtual machine environment, experiments such as the establishment, configuration and maintenance of the local area network are completed based on the Windows network operating system. The main contents include: basic use of virtual machine software, management and configuration of network operating systems, establishment of peer-to-peer networks, establishment and configuration of client/server networks, practical operation management and application of networking, etc. _x000D_

Name: Video Editing
Introduction: Understand the basic concepts, basic processes, editing methods, special effects synthesis and output of video and audio editing, and be familiar with the basic operating procedures of Avid Media Composer non-linear editing software, as well as the use of pre-production shooting equipment. Cultivate students to master practical skills such as video material collection and management, video editing, sound editing, sports special effects and special effects, subtitle special effects, color correction, and video output.

Name: Peer Psychological Counseling
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
In life, people usually tell their friends, peers or family their troubles before seeking help from a professional psychologist. As such, peer counselling is a special form of counselling, which is a process in which trained or supervised non-professionals provide counselling services. In this process, peer guidance assistants provide psychological and emotional support to peers through the use of active listening, problem-solving skills and the integration of knowledge about human development and mental health.
This course will describe the basic concepts, techniques, ethics and specific problems faced in peer counselling, such as cultural race, the influence of sexual orientation, and the handling of relationships.

Name: Animation Appreciation and Practice
Introduction:
Fully digital teaching method teaches today's popular art and development trends. While teaching the principles and applications of animation art, we will also analyze the current popular film and television special effects technology and teach digital art technology and its application and development prospects. Through comprehensive practical art training, we teach two-dimensional painting, three-dimensional painting, concept art design, character design, game design, interaction design, etc. _x000D_
Principle knowledge teaching + painting creation practice + special lectures by famous experts_x000D_
It enables students with zero foundation in animation art and digital art to master animation art knowledge and digital art technology through 1-2 semesters of study and practice, and can create animation and digital art works independently or in teams. _x000D_
Keywords: animation, digital art technology, concept design, character design, interaction design, game design. _x000D_

Name: Art and Aesthetic Appreciation
Introduction: The teaching of Art and Aesthetics includes the Astrologers ' Habitat world and the strengthening of aesthetic education, chapter I, art, chapter II, painting, chapter III, sculpture, chapter IV, architecture, chapter V, design, chapter VI, calligraphy, chapter VII, music, chapter VIII, dance, chapter IX, theatre, chapter X, film, chapter XI, photography, chapter XII, arts and religion, chapter XIII, beauty and life, chapter XIV, Chinese aesthetic spirit. The concept of the Central and Western arts, explaining the definition of the art, understanding the identity of art and works of art, and understanding its place and role in culture. In the case of different works of art, there are differences of perception, and even in the case of the same works of art, different views emerge. In China's traditional view of art and art, which is “art and culture”, art and works of art are seen in terms of their dimension, structure and the place and role of art in culture. The complexity of the art of human painting makes it seem difficult to establish a comparison between East and West, but we are more likely to see the results of the peaks of the art of East and West painting. Because the characteristics of the geographical civilization associated with the drawings at this time are brought to light, they enable viewers to feel deeply about the “modernity” of the East-West civilization through painting. Sculptures are presented in form, and in our traditional way, we usually divide sculptures into two large categories: a cylindrical and a floating. We Chinese ancients also have a special contribution to make to the space shape of the sculptures, by way of example: "Standing," "Stamp", "Stamping Mountain Water Wall", "Strength." China ' s traditional architecture and art are manifested in four ways: the beauty of its image, the beauty of its humanities, the beauty of its territory and the beauty of its landscape. The architectural function of beauty is twofold: the physical function and the artistic function, and the architectural function is one of plastic arts. China's traditional buildings are compared with Western traditional buildings in the form of buildings. From an artistic point of view, design is discussed separately on the meaning of design, its philosophical nature, contemporary issues, complex relationships, etc. The chapter provides a critical interpretation of the current design-induced social problems, leading students to become consumers with reasonable aesthetic abilities and aesthetic standards for design work. This chapter deals with the broad and wide-ranging nature of the aesthetic features of many works in the history of calligraphy in China. It deals with what constitutes a calligraphy, the visual form of a calligraphy work, the feelings of a calligraphy work, and the interpretation of the four parts of it. “Music” presents the uniqueness of music from the perspective of science, aesthetics, historians, morphology, etc., with a concise narrative and anecdotal examples of music different from other arts; the language of music and its structure; and the morphological characteristics of traditional Chinese music. Inducing viewers to become true “sympathetics” through emotional, rational organic combinations. What kind of art is music?

Name: English Reading
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is aimed at students who are weak in English reading when they enter school. The textbooks used in the course are a collection of selected linguistics, philosophy, economics, archaeology, psychology and other fields. Through students' self-study of vocabulary before class, preview of texts, teachers' analysis of classic chapters and students' group discussions in class, students' interdisciplinary awareness and thinking ability are enhanced, and students' ability to summarize and paraphrase literature, as well as their ability to translate English into Chinese, lays a solid foundation for improving academic English ability. After the influence of the course, students will be able to cope with the reading part of the CET-4 and CET-6 exams more easily. _x000D_
The course also uses a global personalized reading network platform as a course auxiliary tool to facilitate students' independent learning. This online platform provides students with newspaper and periodical consultation articles that meet their reading abilities every week. Students are required to spend 1 to 2 hours per week after class to complete online reading content, expand their vocabulary through scientific training, and use reading strategies such as summarization and prediction to improve their reading ability. _x000D_
During the semester, teachers will provide a series of text-related book lists and require each student to choose a favorite book to complete independent reading and make a reading report. _x000D_
    The course adopts a closed-book examination format, with no midterm test. The final paper accounts for 50% of the total grade, and daily grades account for 50% of the total grade. Regular grades include reading summaries, book reports, online reading and classroom word tests. _x000D_

Name: Data Structures and Algorithms (A)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: (c) Design and analysis techniques to equip students with data structure and algorithms, improve the quality of programme design, select a reasonable data structure based on the nature of the problem sought and exercise the necessary control over the complexity of time space. The ability of students to design and achieve efficient data structures and algorithms for future learning, research and work. The basic design principles of this course programme can be summarized as follows: (1) Emphasis on training in basic data structure and algorithms to develop the capacity of students to use data structure and algorithm fundamental theory to analyse and solve problems from a problem-solving perspective. (2) Focus on the development of practical and engineering competencies, which enable students to adhere to the norms of software development and establish knowledge systems for data structure and algorithm design and problem resolution. The main focus is on data knowledge and algorithmic knowledge systems and the computational thinking capacity to solve problems. Focus of the course: Knowledge systems that capture data structure and algorithms in both breadth and depth, basic data structure and classical algorithms, theoretical, abstract and design methods. The difficulty of the course is: the development of mathematical abstraction capabilities, such as abstract questions, algorithms and abstract data structures; search and retrospective thinking in tree and chart structures; time- and space-efficiency analysis and trade-offs in sequencing algorithms; efficiency in retrieval and indexing; balance issues in data structures, such as AVL, stretching trees, mangroves, and B/B+ trees; selection of suitable data models based on practical problems, design of suitable algorithms and use of theoretical knowledge acquired to solve them; application and development of data structures and algorithms at the forefront of disciplines. In response to the above-mentioned priorities and difficulties, the course offers teaching of data structures and algorithms at the theoretical, abstract and design levels, focusing on the basic concepts of data structures and the presentation of abstract data types, allowing students to use different abstract data types as a basis for design at different stages of design and to consider the structure and algorithms of processes at appropriate abstract levels. Each data structure begins with its mathematical characteristics, introducing its abstract type of data; then discussing its different storage methods, discussing with students the study of possible algorithms achieved by different storages; and then discussing the advantages and disadvantages of various storage methods and algorithms in conjunction with algorithm analysis and discarding inappropriate methods. In this way, students are fully motivated to actively study, enabling them to learn about the data structure and the computational thinking involved in algorithms.

Name: Set Theory and Graph Theory

In terms of teaching, the Peking University version of "College English Audio-visual and Listening Tutorial 1-2" is used as the main teaching material, and the classroom is used as the guide, and students are conducted in a model that combines a large amount of independent learning after class to gradually improve students' English listening and speaking abilities.

Name: Sanda (Chinese Kickboxing)
Introduction: The spread of martial arts is a technical-strike project in China. It can work out and defend itself, while being fun and entertaining; it can develop fresh, courageous and upward qualities. It is a traditional sports project for the Chinese nation, and IAF has nearly 90 countries as members. Major competitions such as the World Cup, the Asian Games and the World Games all have disassembly projects and are included in the 2008 Olympic Shows.

Name: Renaissance Artworks and Biblical Stories
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course uses the biblical-themed art works of the Renaissance as an opportunity to teach commonly used biblical allusions and examples of their use in literary works, news, speeches, etc. to improve students' cultural background, reading and writing skills. The allusions and proverbs in the Bible are often quoted in conversations and writings, and have become a habit. Without understanding the original meaning and extended meaning of some commonly used allusions, one cannot fully understand and appreciate literary works. The Renaissance was a peak in the history of European painting. The works advocated humanity against theocracy, but the content of the works was mostly taken from biblical stories, such as Giotto's "Flight to Egypt", Leonardo da Vinci's "The Last Supper", Masaccio's "David Carrying the Head of Goliath", etc. This course uses these works of art as a window to introduce biblical stories with intuitive and vivid pictures, allowing students to understand biblical allusions while appreciating the works of art and use them in after-class writing.

College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Through the study of this course, you can lay a solid foundation for subsequent professional basic courses and professional courses. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Computer Systems
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The Introduction to Computer Systems course is a basic professional course built in 2012 by the Institute of Information in cooperation with Carnegie Mellon University in the United States. The course provides a good professional basis for follow-up courses for undergraduate students in computer science and technology, from hardware to software, from compilation language to C language program design, from bottom operating system to network interface with I/O interfaces. The course consists of both theoretical knowledge presentation and hands-on training; it is a comprehensive and professional basic course with the design and in-depth study of the details of the major courses. The curriculum, which is the first course of follow-up specializations, is designed to enable students to move more quickly in the follow-up basic courses, such as computer system structure, compilation techniques, operating systems, computer networks, etc., and to promote further change and innovation in the follow-up courses.

Name: Introduction to Mao Zedong Thought and the Theoretical System of Socialism with Chinese Characteristics
Introduction: This course takes the Sinicization of Marxism as its theme, takes the historical process of the Sinicization of Marxism as its main line, and focuses on socialism with Chinese characteristics. It reveals the historical process of the Communist Party of China integrating the basic principles of Marxism with China's reality from the unity of theory and practice, history and logic, and accurately explains the theoretical results of the Sinicization of Marxism, namely Mao Zedong Thought and the theoretical system of socialism with Chinese characteristics, etc., so that students can correctly understand the theoretical results of the Sinicization of Marxism in guiding China's revolution, construction, and The important historical position and role in the reform, grasp the basic theory and spiritual essence of Marxism in China, establish correct beliefs and common ideals of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and enhance the consciousness and firmness of implementing the party's basic line and basic program, so that contemporary college students can deeply understand the importance of adhering to the guiding position of Marxism, strengthen college students' ideals and beliefs in taking the path of socialism with Chinese characteristics under the leadership of the party, and make their due contributions to building a moderately prosperous society in an all-round way and realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation.

Name: Floorball
Introduction: FLOORBALL originated in Sweden in the 1970s. It first started in schools and has been widely loved by students. Currently, this emerging sport has been carried out in more than 30 countries around the world, with more than 1 million people participating and more than 300,000 registered athletes. In 1994, the first FLOORBALL World Championship was held in Switzerland and has been held for five times so far. Formal floorball competition is a team sport played indoors. The competition venue can be made of wooden boards, hard plastic rubber and other materials. The standard venue is 40 meters long and 20 meters wide, with barriers around it. Floorball is similar to ice hockey and hockey. The game is played with feet, similar to basketball; each team has 6 players and can be a mixed team of men and women, including a goalkeeper. Floorball equipment is simple and easy to operate. Through floor ball (FLOORBALL) exercise, you can cultivate comprehensive abilities such as speed, endurance, strength, agility, and coordination, and comprehensively improve physical fitness; it can improve aerobic metabolism and improve cardiopulmonary function; cultivate the excellent quality of challenging yourself, defeating yourself, and moving forward courageously; cultivate team spirit and promote the overall development of physical and mental quality. The floorball (FLOORBALL) class mainly teaches basic techniques and basic knowledge, so that students can master the basic skills of floorball (FLOORBALL) and learn to pass, catch, hit, defend, lead and other techniques. Floorball does not involve much physical collision and confrontation, and emphasizes flexibility and coordination.

 In terms of course content, there are three main parts: _x000D_

Name: Computer Organization
