Name: Biometric Recognition
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: A major feature of the information age is the digitization and invisibility of personal identity. How to accurately identify a person and ensure security is a key social issue that must be solved in today's information age. At present, most of the various identity management in our country and even the world use certificates, magnetic cards, IC cards and passwords. These means cannot avoid forgery or loss, and passwords can also be easily stolen or forgotten. These bring great inconvenience to managers and users. Biometric-based authentication avoids these hassles. Therefore, more and more researchers are engaged in this field, and the industry has more and more products. In May 2003, the Hong Kong SAR government issued the first smart ID card that stored fingerprint characteristics. In November 2003, the British Home Office also began to implement a six-month pilot of electronic biometric identification technology to prepare for the future nationwide launch of a new ID card system. The U.S. government has also begun collecting index finger fingerprints of all foreign citizens entering and exiting the country in early 2004 to prevent terrorist attacks and enhance homeland security. It is obvious that biometric identification technology will make great achievements in law, security, finance, commerce, military and various situations involving identity authentication. As Bill Gates once asserted, biometric identification technology will become an important innovation in the IT industry in the next few years. This course will systematically introduce the origin, development and current situation of biometric identification technology, teach students knowledge in related fields, expand students' horizons, and cultivate research interests. Through classroom lectures, demonstrations and organizing students to read books and papers in the field, students will be led to learn and master the basic knowledge and technology in the field of biometric identification, laying a solid foundation for students to independently carry out research work.

Name: Theories of Japan and the Japanese
Introduction: Japan is my country's close neighbor. At present, the economic and trade relations between China and Japan are getting closer and closer. In 2003, the bilateral trade volume reached 130 billion US dollars. Japan is my country's largest trading partner, and my country is Japan's second largest trading partner. In addition, Japanese companies are investing more and more in China. The number of personnel exchanges between the two countries every year reaches more than 3 million. Despite this, the political relations between the two countries and the feelings between the two peoples show signs of cooling down. In addition to the frictions caused by economic and trade exchanges themselves and historical issues and territorial issues, the reason is also a lack of understanding and even misunderstanding between the two countries. This has led to frequent emotional words and deeds between the two countries. As the world economy becomes increasingly integrated, China and Japan, as major countries in East Asia, maintain cooperation with each other as a prerequisite for promoting regional integration. Therefore, it is necessary for both sides to analyze each other objectively and rationally. It is from this awareness of the issue that this course prepares to conduct a systematic analysis of Japan from the aspects of geographical environment, historical development, political system, economic growth, cultural characteristics, national character, social structure, foreign relations, security policy, etc., in order to deepen the mutual understanding between China and Japan.

Name: Web Programming with JavaScript
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
When it was first released in 1995, no one could have imagined that the JavaScript language would develop to what it is today: from a lame language that was hosted in browsers and was not taken seriously, it has gradually become a full-stack programming language that crosses browsers and servers, providing a conceptually simple language solution for the design of web programs. JavaScript contains many widely criticized language features. However, the flaws are not concealed. The powerful vitality of JavaScript is closely related to its own elegant features/mechanisms. The two most important features/mechanisms are: "prototype chain" and "asynchronous I/O mechanism". The prototype chain provides a new program reuse mechanism that is different from the class-based inheritance mechanism in traditional object-oriented languages; the asynchronous I/O mechanism is contrary to the traditional view of improving the operating efficiency of software systems through multi-threading. These two features/mechanisms embody the innovative nature of the JavaScript language and its running support environment. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course mainly introduces web programming methods based on JavaScript language. Specifically, this course contains three main parts: basic syntax of JavaScript language; JavaScript browser-side programming; JavaScript server-side programming. In terms of basic syntax, it mainly introduces the development history and core features of the JavaScript language, basic data types and basic syntax of JavaScript, objects, functions, closures, prototype chains, regular expressions, and other related high-level language features. In terms of browser-side programming, it mainly introduces HTML language, CSS language, JavaScript DOM programming, and JQuery toolkit. In terms of server-side programming, it mainly introduces the Node.js module management mechanism, Node.js asynchronous I/O framework, Node.js asynchronous I/O framework, Node.js HTTP server programming, and Web programming based on the Express framework.

Islam and the close interaction between Islam and world politics have become a topic of endless debate among political circles, academic circles, and the general public. _x000D_
A series of major theoretical and practical questions that urgently need to be answered are before the world: How to understand Islam? How do you evaluate contemporary Islamic revival trends and revival movements? How to understand the interaction between Islam and the process of social modernization? How to understand the relationship between Islam and the Western world in today's world situation? Is the rise of Islamic power threatening the security of the Western world, and therefore Western countries want to actively intervene, or is Western hegemony and power politics trying to dominate political and social changes in the Islamic world, thus triggering the resurgence of anti-American and anti-Western Islamic forces? Major issues such as this have made the study of the relationship between Islam and world politics a cutting-edge topic in the current discipline of international politics. _x000D_
This course is an attempt to comprehensively and systematically sort out these issues. Through the development and spread of Islam and Islam, representative cases from typical countries and regions are selected for analysis and discussion. Pictures and audio-visual materials are interspersed. From the perspectives of theory, history and reality, it focuses on the study of three aspects of issues in world politics: Islam and secular politics, Islam and nation-states, and Islamic tradition and modernization process. _x000D_
Through classroom lectures and discussions inside and outside class, students can gain a more comprehensive and systematic understanding of Islamic factors in world politics, further understand the complexity of world politics, have a clear and correct stance on the main issues involved in the course, and have a macro grasp of the interaction between Islamic factors and world politics today.

At the same time, because it is an English class (learning English as a foreign language), this course also has explanations and exercises for language difficulties. Name: Science in the Solar System
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The modern scientific enlightenment of humans began largely with observations of the solar system. There is no doubt that the law of the planetary movement in Kepler was the most important inspiration in the process of presenting the Newton sports equation and the law of gravity. The emergence of modern science and technology has greatly facilitated further human exploration of the solar system and has solved one puzzle after another. On the other hand, these explorations themselves have contributed significantly to the development of disciplines.

The course is intended for students from various academic backgrounds (including arts and science students) and is tailored to select some of the promising observations in solar system research. While introducing these interesting phenomena, the course will lead students from a logical point of view to explore the scientific principles behind them through a series of inquiries. Thus, the purpose of this course is not just to demonstrate a plethora of solar systems, but more to demonstrate the logic of modern scientific research and the power of critical thinking by using the solar system as a platform: how should we solve this puzzle when it comes to unresolved questions?

In order to achieve this objective, the course will avoid traditional teaching methods (i.e. “sight-seeing” detailed presentation of the planets of the solar system) and more classification and organization of the nature of science. Interactive questions, reflections and answers will also be a major part of the curriculum. Students are strongly encouraged to ask questions and actively participate in classroom and group discussions. The final rating of achievement will consist of attendance/classroom discussion participation (15 per cent), homework (25 per cent, open reflection on the main) and final examination (60 per cent, selection and abbreviation on the subject, avoiding over-examination of intellectual content and encouraging the use of logical thinking to obtain answers).

Name: Geomorphology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Geomorphology is the science that studies the characteristics, causes, development, structure and distribution of land surface morphology. Classroom teaching is based on the geomorphological force system. Landforms mainly formed by exogenous forces include slope landforms, river landforms, karst landforms, glaciers, permafrost landforms, desert landforms, loess landforms and coastal landforms; landforms mainly formed by endogenous forces include geotectonic landforms, fold landforms, fault landforms and volcanic landforms. The summer course "Field Internship in Geomorphology" is an important supplementary content of this course. It is a two-week field teaching internship in the Datong Basin and the coast of Qinhuangdao.

Name: Geomorphology Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The internship areas mainly include the Datong Basin in Shanxi and the Qinhuangdao area in Hebei. The Datong Basin is my country's richest landform type (including mountains, plains, rivers, volcanoes, alluvial fans, various loess landforms and neotectonic activity traces and landforms, rich Cenozoic sedimentary types and good outcrop profiles) and rich historical and cultural landscapes. It is also an important energy and chemical industry base in my country and is located in an ecologically fragile zone in my country. It has a long history of geomorphological research and a good research foundation, so it is the most ideal geomorphology teaching practice area in my country. The Qinhuangdao area has a very complete and typical combination of coastal landforms, as well as typical coastal plains and distinctive bedrock mountain landforms. It is also a very important port city and the most important seaside tourist city in my country. The two regions include most of the landform types and geomorphic processes that are objects of geomorphological research. Through the study of this internship course, students will systematically learn and master the basic methods of geomorphological field research under the guidance of teachers. Including how to collect and relevant documents around the research purpose, and formulate field investigation and research plans; how to observe, measure, analyze, research, describe and record various macro and micro landform phenomena; data collation, analysis and research, chart drawing, research report writing, etc. Through internships, you can also gain more perceptual understanding of issues such as physical geography, economic geography, historical and human geography, scenic tourism, resource development and environmental protection.

Name: Organic Chemistry (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory basic course for undergraduates majoring in City and Environment, School of Environmental Science and Engineering, and Department of Medicine. It is divided into 13 chapters, 4 hours per week, 4 credits. Currently, "Organic Chemistry" (Third Edition) written by Professors Jiang Shuojian, Ding Youjun, Li Mingqian and others, and "Organic Chemistry Questions Analysis" written by Jia Xinru and others are used as the main reference textbooks. With the rapid development of organic chemistry and biology in recent years, there has been more and more interpenetration between disciplines, and environmental scientists have increasingly required in-depth knowledge of organic chemistry. Therefore, this course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories, and basic knowledge of organic chemistry; and to master the basic methods of researching organic chemistry. However, due to limited study time, the content must be focused. _x000D_
    The main purposes and requirements of this course: (1) By studying organic chemistry courses, students can systematically master the nomenclature, structure, properties and the relationship between structure and properties of organic compounds, have a deeper understanding and master the important reactions and reaction mechanisms of various organic compounds, learn stereochemistry well, and establish stereoscopic concepts. (2) Understand and master the mutual transformation between functional groups and be able to complete simple organic synthesis. (3) By learning the basic properties of various organic compounds, learn the chemical methods for identifying various organic compounds. Learn the general methods of separating and purifying organic mixtures. (4) In order to highlight the key points and compress the teaching hours, some adjustments have been made to this course. Students are not taught or required to master the contents of chapters such as sugars, terpenes, steroids, and nucleic acids. In addition, because the students in this course are not trained to engage in basic research in organic chemistry, molecular orbital theory and complex reaction mechanisms are not taught. Only interested students can enrich it through self-study. _x000D_
The teaching content of this course mainly highlights the relationship between structure and properties, and explains the physical properties and chemical reactions of various compounds from the perspective of structure. Elucidate the influence of intramolecular and intermolecular interactions on their properties from the perspective of molecular structure. Through common explanations, students can draw parallels, and through individual descriptions, they can distinguish each other. Pay attention to regularities, so that students can establish scientific thinking methods. In view of the characteristics of students, this course leaves the clear descriptions of physical and chemical properties in textbooks to students' self-study, and only explains the rules in class. Appropriate content on biological properties and applications has been added to guide students to understand the significance of studying organic chemistry to the development of their majors, improve learning interest and consciousness, and expand their knowledge. _x000D_

Introduction: "World Cultural Geography" is a general elective course for liberal arts and science undergraduates in the school. It aims to introduce the pattern of world cultural geography and its formation and development process. To train students to observe and analyze the occurrence, development and spatial distribution characteristics of cultural phenomena in the world from a geographical perspective. Specific contents include: basic research methods of world cultural geography, division of world cultural regions, world population distribution and population migration, the origin, spread and regional differences of agriculture, the origin and spread of cities, regional differences and characteristics of urban forms, the spatial distribution and interrelationships of the world's major languages, religions and races, the geographical discovery and the formation of the world colonial system, world geopolitics and the spatial structure characteristics of the world geographical system, global economic integration, urbanization phenomena and their accompanying political, economic and social issues, etc.

Name: Hydrology and Water Resources
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: First, a brief introduction is made to the research objects, development process, branches of hydrology, and the basic status of water on the earth; then the principles and significance of water cycle and water balance, and the processes or mechanisms of the main basic links of the water cycle (precipitation, evaporation, infiltration, runoff) are discussed; the main water bodies on the land surface or their special parts (rivers, lakes, swamps, estuaries) and the main hydrological characteristics of groundwater are discussed again; and finally the basic situation of water resources is discussed.

Name: Soil Science and Soil Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Focusing on the main contents of soil science and soil geography research, this course is divided into four parts: The first part systematically explains the physical and chemical properties of soil and its nutrients_x000D_
The cycle process; the second part focuses on the formation and development of soil and soil classification system; the third part focuses on the main soil types in China_x000D_
and its spatial distribution characteristics, as well as the main principles and methods of soil survey and zoning; the fourth part discusses soil quality degradation from the perspective of soil resources_x000D_
ization, its influencing factors and management strategies.

Name: Television Program Production and Planning
Prerequisite: It is recommended that the selection of courses be preceded by a better understanding of the basic use of single and home-based cameras and a better appreciation of, and reading of, video and content analysis.
Introduction: This course is open to all majors in the school and teaches basic content about TV program planning and production to undergraduates in film and television planning and production (especially students who are not majoring in film and television communication). This course enables students to become familiar with the process, way of thinking, production methods, etc. of TV program planning and production; master basic shooting and post-editing techniques; have certain TV program production skills; at the same time, have a deeper understanding of film and television works; and achieve the ability to complete a TV program independently or in collaboration with others.

Name: Basic Italian (1)
Introduction:
Italian civilization is one of the important sources of Western civilization. It has made immortal contributions to the progress of human civilization and has become a basic academic accomplishment for scholars who study Western civilization. _x000D_
"Basic Italian" is a component of the "Italian Plan" and is a public elective course for undergraduates at Peking University. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic knowledge and skills of Italian, understand the civilizational achievements and social life of Italians, and provide basic language support for students who hope to engage in in-depth research related to Italian civilization; at the same time, they broaden their language horizons and provide conditions for in-depth study of European studies and understanding of Western civilization. This course is taught by Professor Hanmei from the University of Rome, Italy, and uses Italian textbooks. Italian cultural activities will be organized during the teaching period. Students can participate in relevant activities of the Cultural Section of the Italian Embassy and make use of various resources in the library of the Cultural Section of the Italian Embassy. This course lasts for 1 year, with 6 hours of study per week. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to the Atmospheric Environment
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course focuses on the basic concepts, system components and interrelationships of atmospheric environmental science, mainly including air pollution processes, climate change, ecological health effects and environmental policies. The content covers urban haze weather, Antarctic ozone hole, photochemical smog, acid rain, epidemiological surveys, and policy measures to solve air pollution problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course is positioned as an introductory course for undergraduate students to understand the scientific research of atmospheric environment. Students should have a basic advanced mathematics learning background and hope to initially understand and master a series of basic research techniques and scientific knowledge related to the field of atmospheric environment. The course will focus on cultivating students' research interest in atmospheric environmental science and their ability to use mathematical and physical methods to comprehensively analyze and solve practical problems. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings of Classic Journalism
Introduction: This course is a required professional course for undergraduates majoring in journalism. It is a business and knowledge-based development course closely related to professional courses in news interviewing and writing. This course hopes to guide students through the study and analysis of 50-60 Chinese and foreign classic news works to have a more comprehensive understanding and deeper understanding of successful experiences in topic selection, structure, content organization, language use, ideas or value expressions of excellent news works, so as to improve their news gathering and writing abilities.

Name: Chinese Language Proficiency
Introduction: The teaching content of this course is mainly divided into three major sections: Chinese character cultivation, Chinese word cultivation and Chinese expression cultivation. We hope that based on the study of the development profile, characteristics and other basic knowledge of the ancient and modern Chinese language, as well as comparative analysis with other languages ​​in the world (especially alphabetical scripts), students are expected to gain a deep understanding of the uniqueness and particularity of the Chinese language in the world's language and script systems, and enhance their sense of identity and pride in national languages ​​and related cultures. On this basis, further master the basic characteristics of Chinese words and the basic rules of Chinese expression, and have a more comprehensive knowledge and understanding of examples of Chinese language use and various problems that may arise, so that in future study and news communication work practice, Chinese can be used more standardized and effectively, and good language expression and communication effects can be achieved.

Name: Media Operations and Management
Introduction:
The media industry has become an important force in social development, showing a continuously rising influence in economic development and cultural communication. With the flow of capital, frequent media cross-cultural communication activities, and intensified competition in the international market, the development of the media industry plays an important role in many countries. With the reform of media policies, technological development and acceleration of globalization, China's media industry is undergoing tremendous changes. _x000D_
The course mainly explores the following three aspects: (1) basic theoretical knowledge of the media market, products, customers, and business models; (2) analysis of factors such as strategy, human resources, market, technology, and financial management in media organizations and enterprises; (3) discussion of new developments and issues in the media market and media enterprises. _x000D_
The teaching method of this course is a combination of teacher lectures and student participation, including extended reading, course discussions, group reports, case analysis, etc. _x000D_

Name: Media Ethics and Law
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for undergraduates in the School of Journalism and Communication. It aims to systematically introduce the basic norms of communication ethics and communication laws and regulations in my country, so that after completing this course, students can acquire overall knowledge in this field and cultivate healthy and good professional qualities and concepts in communication ethics and laws. The teaching of this course places special emphasis on:_x000D_
1. The historical, social and institutional conditions for the formation of communication ethics, laws and regulations in China;_x000D_
2． Basic norms of communication ethics, laws and regulations in China;_x000D_
3. Current status of communication ethics and implementation of laws and regulations in China;_x000D_
4. Some thoughts on improving communication ethics, laws and regulations in my country. _x000D_

Name: Research Methods in Communication
Introduction: The course is designed to train students in methods of discovering, observing and analyzing human communication activities. The course consists of three parts, namely the methodological foundation and method system of communication research; methods of data observation and collection; and data analysis and processing techniques.

Name: Chinese Philosophy (Part 1)
Introduction: This course will select the most representative philosophers in ancient China, teach their philosophical thoughts, and construct a dialogue between different thoughts. This will introduce students to the basic issues, basic ideas and their general evolution of ancient Chinese philosophy, and present the diverse theoretical systems within the tradition and their different ideas for solving problems.

Name: Ethnic Issues in World Politics
Introduction: This course starts from the concept of ethnicity and theoretical debates, focusing on ethnicity, ethnic relations and ethnic issues in major countries and regions in the world. Through representative case selection, we conduct comparative research on ethnic policies in different countries and regions. The course will also cover topics such as ethnocultural diversity and globalization related to ethnic issues. On this basis, we can further understand and understand China’s ethnic groups, ethnic relations and ethnic policies.

Name: Selected Readings in Western Culture
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This is a course on Western thought and culture offered in English. This course will guide students to read some classics of Western culture in order to gain a basic understanding of and think about some important aspects of Western culture. The reading content involves the Bible, Greek and Roman mythology, literary works by Shakespeare and other writers, classics of Western thought, science and religion, etc. _x000D_
Students will read relevant articles and books and make class reports in groups. Reading selected classics is the fundamental guarantee for achieving the teaching objectives of this course. Students will read approximately 3,000 words per week. _x000D_
How the course is conducted: There are two classes per week. The first class will provide classroom lectures, questions and discussions on the reading articles and books assigned last week; the second class will provide historical and cultural background knowledge for next week’s reading topic. In addition to class discussions, students will also participate in the course in the form of group class presentations. There will be an open-book exam at the end of the semester, including a basic knowledge section on Western culture and an essay question section. Class discussion, class report and final examination account for 30%, 30% and 40% respectively in the final assessment. _x000D_

Name: Journalism Theory
Introduction: Through basic analysis of various issues and various theories related to the operation of journalism, it helps students establish a basic understanding of news media and analyze the operation of modern journalism from multiple perspectives such as institutions, ethics, audiences, and history. At the same time, it builds a basic knowledge framework for students to understand news media, such as necessary political, economic, cultural knowledge, etc.

Name: A Brief History of Documentary Film
Brand Research
Prerequisite: Advertising generals, social surveys, advertising psychology
Introduction: The main contents of this course include the following aspects: brand-related concepts, generation and development processes, basic concepts and theories related to brand identity systems, basic content of brand strategy, brand expansion strategies and their advantages and disadvantages, methods of building brand equity and strategies for brand communication.

Name: History of Western Social Thought
Introduction:
This course attempts to provide students with a basic understanding of the emergence and development of various Western social thoughts before the birth of modern sociology through the study and discussion of the social thoughts of major thinkers in Western history; to broaden students' theoretical horizons and enable students to initially possess the ability to think sociologically in a broader theoretical and historical context. In terms of content, it mainly teaches the social thoughts of major thinkers from ancient Greece to the emergence of modern sociology, including various social thoughts in ancient Greece and Rome, various social thoughts in the medieval period, and various social thoughts in the modern period. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Theory and Technique of Chinese Calligraphy
Introduction: This course focuses on teaching the theory and practice of Chinese calligraphy creation. It explains the aesthetic ideas in the theory of Chinese calligraphy art, as well as the aesthetic requirements and expression techniques of calligraphy creation. Based on the students' actual calligraphy level, it focuses on selecting textbooks and reference books related to the art of Chinese calligraphy as teaching models. Through extensive study and practice, students are trained to gradually master the expression techniques of Chinese calligraphy art.

Name: The Great Dream of the Red Chamber
Introduction: This course invites well-known Red Studies scholars from both sides of the Taiwan Strait and three places to teach the art and aesthetics of "Dream of Red Mansions". Introduce the cultural and artistic value of "Dream of Red Mansions" as a whole and its position in the history of Chinese literature. Through exemplary analysis of characters, plots, and texts, students are guided to improve their artistic appreciation of the Chinese literary classic "A Dream of Red Mansions" and enhance their perceptual understanding of traditional Chinese culture. Through the reading and analysis of "Dream of Red Mansions", college students can enhance their understanding of life and pursue a more meaningful, valuable and interesting life.

Name: Online Communication
Introduction: This course is designed to help students understand and master the basic knowledge of new media and network communication and its impact on traditional media and communication theory; understand the impact of the development of new media and network on individuals, businesses and society; and learn to use network and new media means to conduct research and innovation in public relations, advertising, and marketing.

Name: Radio and Television Journalism
Prerequisite:
Journalism principles
Western News History
Chinese News History
News and contemporary Chinese reforms
Introduction: It enables students to grasp the origin, evolution, and internal laws of television news at home and abroad, grasp the special relationship between television broadcasting and news, and provide training for in-depth theoretical research and front-line practice in the future.

Name: Visual Communication
Introduction: The content of this course includes design basics, graphic composition, color composition, visual graphic design, font design, logo art design, layout design, comprehensive packaging design, etc., which are both independent of each other and integrated into one. Students are required to endow some complex and unique spiritual content with visual language, embody it in material form, and form colorful and distinctive design works.

Name: Advertising Planning and Creative Strategy
Prerequisite: History of Chinese and Foreign Advertising
Introduction:
Advertising Planning and Creative is the basic course for undergraduate students in advertising. Teachers will be structured in the light of the professional characteristics of the subjects to be taught during the school year and the length of the course, with theoretical content taught in approximately 7-8 major courses, after-school training topics, and the rest of the course sessions will be organized in sub-group exercises and guided by teachers. The course is delivered in a multimedia format, which leads students to reflect on specific issues such as the place and significance of creative ideas in advertising design, the relationship between advertising and the creative industry, creative thinking and their expression, in the context of the unique context of contemporary advertising ideas in China.
The specifics are: 1. Is “creative” teaching, training? 2. Advertising and creativity in contemporary advertising strategies (what is the status of Chinese graphic design and the development of Chinese advertising)? How can the application and research of “creative” differ in graphic design and advertising? 3. Selection and application of indigenous creative resources (in combination with contemporary advertising practices in China and abroad, thinking about the creative expression of the Chinese element, and presenting practical attempts on the indigenous application of creative ideas using several indigenous resources as examples)

Name: Body Conditioning (Women)
Introduction:
1. Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Physique is a sport that uses freehand body exercises to create a well-proportioned body shape and graceful posture. It is a form of exercise based on aerobic exercises with the main purpose of strengthening physical fitness, correcting posture, and cultivating self-confidence. This course focuses on learning the basic movement combinations and correct practice methods included in the body shape, including barre exercises and physical fitness exercises. Under the accompaniment of music, express yourself through body movements and cultivate elegant manners and manners. _x000D_
2.Safety precautions:_x000D_
(1) This course requires practitioners to have good musical literacy and a sense of music rhythm. For safety and special characteristics during training, they must wear elastic tight clothing or fitness pants and sports T-shirts, gymnastics shoes or dance shoes. At the same time, they must also pay attention to supplementing appropriate water and paying attention to a reasonable combination of diet and nutrition during and after training. _x000D_
(2) Pay attention to the safety of yourself and your classmates during class. If you have chest tightness, palpitation, dizziness or other physical fatigue, please report it to the teacher, who will arrange it according to the situation. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course tasks_x000D_
1. Cultivate students’ physical exercise habits, strong willpower and “health first” ideology. _x000D_
2.. Improve health, enhance physical fitness, and comprehensively improve students' physical and psychological qualities. _x000D_
3. Improve and shape the body shape, cultivate elegant temperament and demeanor, and cultivate students' self-confidence and aesthetic sense. _x000D_
4. Enable students to fully master the basic knowledge and methods of physical exercise and improve their body control capabilities. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Psychology in Everyday Life
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
The content is closely related to the student ' s life and forms are closely related to the student ' s needs
It's a theme: "Recognize yourself, perfect yourself."
Ten topics: adaptation, learning issues, interpersonal relations, communication, self-confidence, love, crisis response, career planning, sex and homosexuality, suicide and life-related meaning.
The first four, “Know Yourself”, will be taught by teachers, and the next ten themes will divide students into groups.
Classroom RPG: Students choose their own theme groups according to their preferences, live RPG. Active participation, self-expression.
Share and discuss: Relax, share awareness.

Name: Audiovisual Language
Introduction: On the basis of summarizing and summarizing the previous theoretical research on audio-visual language, the characteristics of audio-visual language with Chinese characteristics are outlined, and the special expressive power of film and television works is studied from three aspects: single shot, shot combination and the overall form of film and television works. Cultivating the visual thinking ability of undergraduate students majoring in radio and television journalism also allows postgraduate students majoring in communication to start from the study of audio-visual language and gain a more thorough understanding of the characteristics of film and television culture, providing a more professional knowledge background for the research and dissemination of film and television culture.

Name: World History of Journalism
Prerequisite: The first course is not required, but the chosen students need to read and become familiar with the world's near modern history.
Introduction: This course is a required course for journalism majors and the main basic course of the School of Journalism and Communication. It will use a broad perspective to help students grasp the historical process and basic laws of the development and evolution of foreign journalism and communication, and understand the famous events, figures, and trends of thought in the history of foreign journalism and communication, as well as the main issues currently existing in the field of international journalism and communication.

Name: History of Chinese and Foreign Advertising
Introduction: The Chinese and Foreign Advertising History course is a required course for advertising majors. Among them, some Chinese courses are divided into three sections: ancient, modern and contemporary, systematically teaching the history of the development and evolution of advertising in China from ancient times to the present. The key contents of the course include the ancient and modern changes in advertising activities and advertising ideas in China, the introduction of Western advertising concepts and the establishment of the modern advertising agency system since the late Qing Dynasty, the image changes of early Chinese advertising, advertising and the evolution of Chinese society and culture after the reform and opening up, etc. This course only gives a brief introduction to ancient Chinese advertising, and focuses on the two important time periods of advertising in the Republic of China and advertising since the reform and opening up, thereby strengthening the practical connection between historical research and the development of the current advertising industry. The foreign courses are divided into three sections: ancient world advertising, American modern advertising, European modern advertising, and Japanese modern advertising. They systematically teach the history of the development and evolution of advertising around the world from ancient times to the present. The key contents of the course include the ancient and modern changes in advertising activities and advertising ideas, the birth of modern advertising concepts and the establishment of the advertising agency system, the image changes of advertising in the early world, advertising and social changes and cultural evolution, etc. This course only gives a brief introduction to ancient advertising, but focuses on the development of modern advertising in various countries around the world since the Enlightenment and the comparison of advertising industries in various countries, which are two important time periods, thereby strengthening the practical connection between historical research and the development of the current advertising industry.

Name: Communication Theory
Introduction: The main teaching and reading content of this course adopts a combination of Chinese and English, combined with reading materials, film and television materials, and other audio-visual materials, in order to integrate complex theoretical propositions into communication and media phenomena in daily life, and inspire students to think about the mutually constitutive relationship between human communication behavior, media information technology, and social politics, economy, and culture.

Name: International Political Economy
Prerequisite: Political science, economics, theory of international relations, history of international relations
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the main content of international political economics, including the five major theories of international political economics, the politics of international trade, the politics of transnational investment, the politics of international finance, the political economy of development and transformation, and the political economy of regionalism.

Name: Theory and Technique of Chinese Painting
Introduction: This course focuses on teaching the artistic techniques of Chinese painting landscapes, explaining the various expression forms of Chinese painting art, as well as its artistic aesthetic requirements and expression techniques. Based on the actual painting level of students, Chinese painting-related teaching materials and reference books are selected as teaching models. Through a large number of practical exercises, we will guide students in the art practice of Chinese painting and train students to gradually master the artistic expression techniques of Chinese painting.

Name: The Art of Dunhuang
Introduction: It is an open-ended subject for undergraduate students and aims to help students understand and understand the important world art treasure. The course will be conducted in 11 directions, namely, the shining Buddha Palace — Silk Road and Tung Mok Gak, Tung Sing Flying Arts, Dong Sung Man Painting Art, Tung Sung Shun Sung Shaun Art, Tung Shun Sung Shaun Art, Tung Sung Shung Art, Tung Sung Sung Shung Dynasty and Dance, Tung Sung Shung Art, Tung Shun and Music Art, Tung Sung Shung Sung, Tung Sung Sung and the Tung Sung Yung Yung, and the conservation and transmission of Tung Sung Sung Sung and Art, in an effort to present the full and complete face of the glorious arts. While giving students an account of the evolution and evolution of their history, using representative works of art as an example, they bring together, in-depth and shallow talk about the richness of the fine arts and encourage and stimulate further interest in and reflection on it.

Name: Advertising Media Research
Introduction: Systematically introduces the basic knowledge and strategic planning methods of advertising media. At the same time, it is linked to the actual industry and introduces the development status and operation model of the advertising media industry. This enables students to independently observe and analyze the development of advertising media and simulate strategic planning of advertising media.

Name: Graduation Internship
Introduction:
1.	Graduation internship is a compulsory part of the undergraduate teaching plan. _x000D_
2．	The internship unit is arranged by the student's own contact and the college. Students who are unable to contact the internship unit themselves must obey the college's arrangements and practice in the designated unit and within the designated time. In principle, after students start their internship, the internship unit will not change. If the internship unit is changed without authorization, no internship grade will be given. Students who are rejected by the internship unit due to personal reasons will have their internship results cancelled. _x000D_
3.	The college arranges internships for students in the seventh semester, and the internship period must be 4 consecutive months. Students can start their internship during the summer vacation of the sixth semester, and the internship time shall not be later than the second teaching week after the start of the seventh semester. _x000D_
4.	Interns must leave the contact information of the person in charge of the unit (or department) where they go so that the internship guidance team can understand the student's internship situation. _x000D_
5.	During the internship, strictly abide by the disciplines of the unit where you work. _x000D_
6.	Strictly abide by school disciplines during the internship. be safe. _x000D_
7.	After the internship, you must submit an internship summary (no less than 5,000 words) and an internship appraisal (the appraisal must have the official seal of the internship unit). Submission deadline is the last day of finals week. The college will hold an exhibition of internship results. _x000D_
8.	Internship grades are finally determined by the college’s internship guidance group. _x000D_

Name: Media and Social Change
Introduction: To further enable students to understand the relationship between media and social changes and better apply relevant knowledge of communication and journalism. We have always paid attention to the relationship between the media and social transformation and social change, and this has been reflected in relevant courses and related research. This course is currently also offered to graduate students, with a large amount of practical and theoretical preparation. Students are required to have relevant basic knowledge in sociology, communication, political science, and journalism.

Name: Program Concept and Planning
Introduction: This course provides students with basic program creativity and planning abilities through theoretical review, case studies, practical exchanges and simulated actual combat. Different from traditional theoretical research on TV programs, this course focuses on enabling students to understand the industry ecology of program production and acquire basic knowledge and methods in program creativity and production. Compared with purely practical courses on radio and television program creativity and planning, this course sublimates and summarizes the knowledge from the industry, and elevates specific methods to the level of methodology through generalization and summary. This course can not only serve as an enlightenment for undergraduates who are exposed to program production for the first time, but also prevent students from being overly obsessed with specific technologies and getting a glimpse of what is going on. The assessment methods of this course include case analysis and planning plan. The former focuses on examining students' research and analytical abilities, while the latter focuses on examining students' practical ability, understanding ability and execution ability. For excellent case analysis papers, course teachers will contact core journals for publication; for excellent planning plans, course teachers will contact program production units to promote specific practices.

Name: Daoyin and Health Cultivation
Introduction:
Daoyin is an excellent traditional sport of the Chinese nation and an ancient method of cultivating the body and mind. It is an organic combination of body movements, breathing coordination and consciousness adjustment to achieve the purpose of dredging qi and blood, regulating emotions and promoting physical and mental health. Ancient Chinese Baduanjin, Wu Qin Xi, Yi Jin Jing, Nei Yang Gong, etc. all belong to the category of ancient guidance.      _x000D_
    Through the study and experience of Wu Qin Xi, Baduan Jin, Yi Jin Jing, Wu Shi Zhuang, Tai Chi, Zhan Zhuang and other related contents, this course can enhance students' ability to self-regulate their body and mind, improve students' nervous, circulatory, respiratory, digestive, muscular and other system functions, and contribute to the inheritance of the excellent traditional culture of the Chinese nation, as well as the formation of enhanced cultural identity and cultural confidence.

Name: Feature and Documentary Production
Introduction:
As a core professional course in radio and television journalism, the content and tasks of this course are mainly to allow students to understand the historical development and main genres of documentaries, understand the relationship between feature films and documentaries, learn the creative concepts and implementation techniques of documentaries from the perspective of the creator, and understand the basic strategies of documentary creativity, shooting and editing through work appreciation and discussion. _x000D_
At the same time, this course attaches great importance to practicality and requires a group of three students to complete a documentary at the end of the semester, with a length of no less than 30 minutes. Due to the limited training hours of the class plan, the documentary was mainly created by students in their spare time after class. The experiment mainly trains students' cognition of feature film and documentary creative thinking, topic selection and planning skills, shooting and production skills, etc. _x000D_

Name: Creative Communication Management
Introduction: This course is a new course. The main content is to introduce and discuss new theoretical methods and applications of Internet marketing communication. Through case discussions and other methods, students can stay on the cutting edge, become familiar with applications, and strengthen the training of operational abilities.

Name: Frontiers in Contemporary Journalism
Prerequisite: Basic journalism courses, such as news dissemination history, news writing, news editors, etc.
Introduction: In today's era of informationization and globalization, global news information reporting and dissemination are undergoing rapid and tremendous changes in terms of media, technology, methods, content, purpose, etc. Although traditional news reporting methods are still the basis for all news dissemination, it is necessary to understand and master these new changes in contemporary news development in a timely manner in order to better adapt to and meet the actual needs of contemporary news dissemination and achieve better dissemination effects. This course is designed for this purpose. The main content covers newspaper journalism, television news, online news, visual journalism, data journalism, convergence journalism, citizen journalism and other new issues in contemporary practice, and explores responses and solutions. The course is organized by the Department of Journalism, with on-campus teachers and senior industry workers sharing teaching tasks.

Name: Public Communication
Introduction: The game between private interests and public interests in public space empowered by new media affects the development of advertising and public relations industries. This requires an understanding of the meaning and mechanism of communication from the aspects of public expression, public narrative, and public opinion. It also requires an in-depth discussion of power relations and the power of emotional expression in our daily lives.

Name: Introduction to Classics of Marketing Communication
Prerequisite:
It is recommended that they be chosen after the publication of the Advertising General.
It would have been better if there had been too many mathematics and statistics courses to choose.
Introduction: This course mainly introduces and organizes students to read and discuss classic Chinese and foreign literature on business and business communication (including research papers, monographs, biographies, etc.), as well as recently published relevant works that have a wide impact or inspiration in academia or industry (including theoretical research and industrial analysis, reports, etc.). The main purpose of the course is to strengthen students' professional literature foundation through reading and discussion, and in the process cultivate students' spirit of seeking truth and correct opinions, habits of independent thinking, and ability to express ideas in writing.

Name: Understanding the Internet
Prerequisite: Students are only required to experience the use of computers, the Internet and mobile devices.
Introduction:
The world is facing unprecedented challenges. How can we find solutions to global problems? What role will technology play in these solutions? The key is innovation. _x000D_
_x000D_
The key to innovation lies in the Internet. Around the world, people can use the Internet to improve their quality of life as standards, technology, business practices and government policies interact and inspire each other to maintain an open and universal platform that promotes innovation, creativity and economic opportunity. _x000D_
_x000D_
The Internet itself is an innovation. It’s hard to imagine a more complex man-made system than the Internet. The unprecedented horizontalization and disintermediation created by the Internet has had a huge impact on almost all levels of human society. _x000D_
_x000D_
Only a single dimension, such as technology or economy, is not enough to explain the Internet as an innovative phenomenon. It requires the help of multiple disciplines - such as philosophy, sociology, political science, psychology, management, anthropology, communication, history and even law - to gain a better understanding of how the Internet works and how people behave on the Internet. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching Internet cognition requires clarifying the relationship between the development of the Internet and changes in technology, wealth, and civilization, so as to look back on the past, grasp the present, and look to the future. Ultimately, we will find that it is ideas that change the world, not just technology, capital or systems. _x000D_

Name: General Geology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: A basic earth science course for undergraduates majoring in geography, environment, city, ecology, etc. The main contents include the material composition of the earth's crust - the basics of minerals and petrology, mastering mineral concepts, characteristics and identification of common minerals, rock classification and main rock type characteristics; 2. Crustal movement and geological structure, introducing basic knowledge about geological structures and geotectonic structures, focusing on fold structure, fault structure, and plate tectonics theory; 3. A brief history of crustal evolution, including the formation and evolution of the earth's crust, tectonic movements, sea and land changes, climate changes, biological evolution, and mineral resource characteristics in major geological historical periods.

Name: Economic Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Why are economic activities concentrated in a few areas? Where should companies choose to invest? What industries should a city or region develop? Why do some cities grow fast and others grow slowly? What cities are likely to develop into world cities? Why does commodity trade occur between the two regions? Why do migrant workers flow from the central and western regions to the eastern coastal areas? Why can China become the world's factory? Why are multinational companies flooding into the Chinese market? These economic issues have one thing in common, that is, they all involve space. Economic geography can answer these questions. Economic geography focuses on economic activities from a spatial perspective, emphasizing the impact of space or location on economic activities and the reconstruction of space by economic spatial layout. _x000D_
   This course is an introductory course to economic geography, aiming to introduce students to the research objects, research contents, research methods and theoretical systems of economic geography. The course content is arranged according to the research objects of economic geography, including factors, enterprises, industries, cities and regions from micro to macro. Taking the location selection, spatial distribution, spatial structure and spatial interaction rules of these research objects as the main line, relevant theoretical models, analysis methods and research results are introduced. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic principles of economic geography, learn preliminary economic geography analysis, and lay the foundation for further study of economic geography. _x000D_

Name: Meteorology and Climatology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: It is one of the basic courses for various majors in Geography and Ecology and the School of City and Environment. It provides a comprehensive and systematic introduction to the basic knowledge of meteorology, including related developments in atmospheric science. This course covers the core issues of macroeconomics - the main theories of growth and volatility. All content revolves around the above two questions. The overall framework of our course is divided into four parts: _x000D_
The first part includes chapters one and two. The first chapter is an introduction to macroeconomics, which introduces the research objects and research methods of macroeconomics, as well as the basic context of the development of macroeconomics. Chapter 2 is an introduction to national income accounting, introducing the national income flow cycle model, the meaning of gross national product and its accounting methods, and important equations in national income accounting. _x000D_
The second part includes chapters three, four and five, which is the analysis of aggregate demand. The theory of national income determination is one of the core contents of macroeconomics, but it does not refer to the accounting results of national income, but to the determination and changes of equilibrium national income. Equilibrium national income is the result of the interaction of demand and supply. Aggregate demand analysis assumes an excess of aggregate supply, which is the basic approach of traditional Keynesianism. This is because traditional Keynesianism was produced in the context of the Great Depression. Unemployment and idle resources meant that aggregate supply was in excess and did not constitute a restriction on the determination of national income. At the same time, it believes that aggregate demand is insufficient, so there is an aggregate demand analysis that "aggregate demand determines equilibrium national income." In aggregate demand analysis, the price level is exogenously given. Chapter 3 is the product market equilibrium model, which assumes that there is only a product market and no money market in the economy. Therefore, not only is the price level given, but there is no need to consider the role of interest rates. On this basis, the decision to balance national income and the role of government departments are analyzed. Chapter 4 is the simultaneous equilibrium model of product and money markets, which assumes that not only product markets but also money markets exist in the economy. As a result, interest rates began to become an important endogenous variable. This chapter discusses in detail the IS-LM model, the core of aggregate demand analysis, and derives the aggregate demand curve. Chapter 5 studies the role of the government in the simultaneous equilibrium model of the product market and money market, including the constraints of the demand management policy multiplier, the structural effect of output, the certainty of policy effects, the comparison of the effectiveness of fiscal policy and monetary policy, and policy mix issues. _x000D_
The third part includes Chapters 6, 7, and 83, which are analysis of aggregate demand and aggregate supply. Under normal circumstances, the assumption that the price level is fixed is unrealistic, which seriously restricts the explanatory power of aggregate demand analysis. Therefore, it is necessary to study the model in which aggregate demand and aggregate supply jointly determine equilibrium national income. Chapter 6 is the general equilibrium macroeconomic theoretical model. On the basis of analyzing the equilibrium conditions of the labor market, the aggregate supply curve is derived based on the production function, and then the aggregate demand analysis and aggregate supply analysis are combined to study the determination of national income in the simultaneous equilibrium model of the product market, money market and labor market. Chapters 7 and 8 discuss the role of the government in the simultaneous equilibrium model of the three markets, including policy effects in the general equilibrium model, constraints on the policy multiplier, and differences in economic policy opinions among the main schools of contemporary macroeconomics. The theory of inflation and unemployment was discussed, the impact and causes of inflation, the relationship between unemployment and inflation, and government policy issues in controlling inflation and unemployment. _x000D_
The fourth part, Economic Growth Theory, includes Chapters 9 and 10, which is the dynamization of the basic theories of macroeconomics. We mainly discussed two basic questions: Why are some countries so much richer than others? How to explain the large increases in real income over time? Chapter 9 discusses the Solow growth model, which is the basic reference point for almost all growth analysis. The Solow model takes technological progress as a given and explores the impact of the split of output between consumption and investment on capital accumulation and growth. Chapter 9 introduces and analyzes the Solow model and evaluates its ability to answer core questions about economic growth. Chapter 10 introduces the new growth theory. The new growth theory is a very cutting-edge theory in macroeconomics that has seen many new developments since the 1990s. The first part of this chapter discussed the sources of knowledge accumulation, the allocation of resources to knowledge accumulation, and the role of knowledge accumulation in growth. The next article discusses the accumulation of human capital and physical capital. _x000D_

The prerequisite course is "Principles of Accounting".

Name: Property and Liability Insurance
Introduction: This course teaches the principles, types of insurance, operation and supervision of property and liability insurance, and trains students to analyze and solve theoretical and practical problems in the field of property and liability insurance. This course also includes relevant content on reinsurance products and operations management. The course is suitable for students who hope to join the insurance industry in the future, or engage in insurance-related work in securities, consulting, investment, supervision, social insurance management, academic research, etc. The course is taught in Chinese, there is no final exam, and some course materials are in English.

Name: Insurance Asset Management
Prerequisite:
Economics
Microeconomics
Macroeconomics
Insurance principles
Financial accounting
Introduction: The "Insurance Asset Management" course is a course that integrates general economic theory, finance theory, insurance theory and common laws and regulations to explore the theory and practical operation of insurance asset management. This course mainly hopes to help students understand the particularity of insurance asset management by introducing the basic theory of insurance asset management, regulatory and legal environment, domestic and foreign practices, etc., gain a deeper understanding of China's insurance asset management practices, stimulate students' research interests, and open a window for practice for students.

Name: Outdoor Team-Building Training
Introduction:
Course Introduction_x000D_
1. Expansion training is a team education activity that incorporates outdoor game activities into targeted project concepts and is conducted in accordance with the experiential learning model. Under specific survival environments and adventure conditions, physical activities are used as the carrier, team learning is used as the model, and interactive games are used as the content to comprehensively improve students' physical, psychological and social adaptability. It uses a series of activities such as high-altitude projects, medium-altitude projects, low-altitude projects, ground projects, mental projects, theoretical projects, outdoor projects, etc. to cultivate students' active self-challenge ability and good teamwork ability. Expansion training courses can cultivate students' hands-on ability, physical and mental control, frustration resistance, communication skills, self-recognition, self-motivation and self-transcendence, leadership, responsibility, integrity, teamwork, etc. _x000D_

(1) Expansion training focuses on all-round safety, including physical, psychological, behavioral, environmental, equipment, etc. safety. _x000D_
(2) Students who are in good health and strictly follow medical advice and are not suitable for taking risks or strong stimulation can participate in activities in accordance with the principle of "challenge based on choice". _x000D_
(3) Dress appropriately for sports. _x000D_
(4) Have accident insurance or medical assistance system. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Public Finance
Introduction: Finance is a branch of economics that studies government revenue and expenditure activities and their impact on resource allocation and income distribution. It mainly includes: the welfare economics foundation of finance; market defects and fiscal functions; public choice of budget plans; basic tax theory and tax system; fiscal expenditure theory; public debt theory; coordination of central and local fiscal relations, etc.

Name: Human Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Human geography is an important basic course for the majors of resources, environment, urban and rural planning management and urban planning. _x000D_
      This course strives to reform the traditional teaching ideas of human geography, focusing on arousing students' interest points, emphasizing both theory and practice. By analyzing a large number of scientific research cases, especially urban and rural planning and local development strategy research cases, combined with the background and characteristics of Peking University's scientific thinking in urban planning, it emphasizes the use of human geography in national economic construction, especially in urban and rural planning practice. As a professional basic course, the above teaching ideas are suitable for the characteristics of first- and second-year undergraduates majoring in resources, environment, urban and rural planning management, and urban planning. They will arouse their interest in further learning the major and understand the specific uses and important thinking characteristics of human geography. It plays an important role in cultivating students majoring in urban planning under the background of science. _x000D_
      The supporting textbook "Human Geography: Theory and Application" for this course complements the teaching process, with special emphasis on the following three aspects: first, the shift from focusing solely on "knowledge" to emphasizing "interestingness"; second, the shift from focusing solely on "theory" to "equal emphasis on theory and practical application"; third, the shift from focusing on "subject introduction" to "establishing the characteristics of subject thinking". _x000D_

Name: Fine Arts Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Art internship is a compulsory course for undergraduates majoring in urban planning. It is a continuation and deepening of the "Art and Cartography" course. It aims to cultivate the ability of urban planning students to understand and express urban space, improve their plastic arts accomplishments, and exercise their hand-drawing skills. The content of the internship is mainly urban architecture and landscape architecture sketching, and also takes into account the study of design colors. _x000D_
The course is mainly divided into three parts: First, architectural sketching, which lasts for five days. The sketch objects select historical buildings, modern buildings, landscape gardens and architectural sketches on the university campus; the second is city and landscape sketches, the sketch objects are more diverse, and historical sites, modern square buildings, urban historical districts, etc. are selected, which lasts four days; the third is design color exercises, using computer-assisted learning, which lasts one day. All internship locations are in urban areas and suburbs of Beijing. _x000D_

Name: Cultural Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Cultural geography is an important subject in geography, and the curriculum mainly introduces the way in which culture is produced and the main types of culture to students, while also extending their horizons, leading them to understand and discuss cultural phenomena from a spatial perspective.

Name: Population Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Introduce the basic theories and methods of population geography, and elaborate on the main characteristics and major issues in the population development of the world and China from a spatial perspective. The content mainly includes population quantity and population growth, population distribution, population movement and migration, population composition, population development planning and forecasting, etc. During the teaching process, the basic knowledge of world and Chinese population is combined with the theoretical methods of population geography, and the introduction is interspersed with the introduction of the spatial characteristics of China's population and its development and evolution processes and trends in the form of cases. _x000D_
Through teaching, students can master the basic theories of population geography, understand the main spatial characteristics and major issues of population growth in China and the world, understand the structural characteristics and development and evolution trends of China's population, understand the dynamic process and mechanism of China's population distribution and redistribution, and master the basic theories and methods for analyzing regional and urban population development issues. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese and Foreign Urban Development
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Systematically teach Chinese and foreign urban planning and urban construction, compare China and the West based on historical processes, and sort out the context of urban planning ideas and construction practices. In addition to introducing historical facts, it focuses on analyzing the interactive relationship between social background, planning trends and urban construction in each historical period, in order to enrich students' urban historical knowledge, improve their theoretical understanding of the history of urban construction, and lay a solid foundation for the study of urban planning majors.

Name: Urban Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Urban geography studies the relevant issues and development laws of urban development from the perspective of geographical space. The core content is to examine urban spatial organization from the two geographical systems of region and city, that is, regional urban spatial organization and intra-city spatial organization. The teaching purpose of the urban geography course is to enable students to master the basic theories and methodologies of urban geography through course teaching, including urban formation and development conditions, regional urbanization, regional urban systems and urban internal spatial organization; to understand the basic knowledge of urban distribution and development in China and the urbanization path with Chinese characteristics; to improve the ability to independently analyze urban problems; to master the basic principles and methods of regional urban system planning. _x000D_
Students are required to read extracurricular materials, connect with regional and urban development practices, think actively, and ask more questions. It is against rote memorization of provisions in books. Students should have a certain basic knowledge of geography and bring a provincial atlas of China to class. Teaching interaction is encouraged, and students are especially welcome to ask questions at any time in class. 1-2 class discussions will be arranged. _x000D_

Name: Architectural Design (I)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
"Architectural Design" is a compulsory course for urban planning majors. It aims to enable students to master the basic knowledge of architecture, equip them with architectural design concepts and skills, and lay a solid foundation for architectural cognition and design for urban planning majors. _x000D_
Architecture designs and constructs various artificial environments and structures in cities, towns, and landscape gardens. Architecture is a combination of art and science. It is also a product of technology, art, and society. It requires strong technical knowledge, a perceptual artistic aesthetic, and attention to humanities and society. _x000D_
This course covers the basic theories, principles and methods of architecture, introduces the historical and modern built environment, and covers the basic principles of architectural analysis, evaluation and aesthetics. The architectural drawing part includes tool application, labeling, dimensions, drawing techniques, etc. for freehand and instrumental drawing to improve the expressive skills of architectural drawing. _x000D_
    The project assignments in the course train the composition techniques of form and space, take root in the social and cultural environment, and promote the harmony between architecture and human scale. To enable students to seriously devote themselves to the study of basic design principles, design composition and expression techniques, and then seek broader and more critical design strategies. _x000D_

Name: Urban Economics
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Microeconomics and economics principles (the teacher explains the relevant background in detail in the course of the course without having had a modest impact)
Introduction:
Cities are highly concentrated social and economic entities in modern society and are important producers of social wealth. The spatial arrangement and organization of its internal residence and various economic and social activities is a highly complex dynamic system. There are two main forces that play a major role in this system, one is the power of the market and the other is the power of the government. Urban economics studies the spatial arrangement and formation of spatial structure of various urban economic activities under the influence of the market. Urban planning represents the power of the government to spatially arrange and guide various social and economic activities in the city through the allocation of urban land uses. Therefore, planners should understand the market and know how to guide and regulate the market through planning. Urban economics is a discipline that can help planners understand the mechanisms and laws of market forces in cities. _x000D_
The specific research content of urban economics can be divided into two parts: basic theory and urban problem analysis. Basic theories include macro urbanization and urban economic growth theory, micro urban internal spatial structure theory and urban public economic theory. Among them, the theory of urban internal spatial structure is the core theory of urban economics. It uses the resource allocation mechanism in the land market to derive the spatial distribution rules of urban economic activities, and provides a theoretical explanation for the well-known urban spatial phenomena. Urban problem analysis mainly focuses on "urban diseases", such as urban unemployment, urban traffic congestion, urban poverty, and urban crime. Through economic analysis, we find out the causes of the problems and explore policy approaches to solve them. _x000D_

Name: Urban Sociology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Introduce the origin, development and genre of urban sociology, systematically teach urban sociology research methodology and methods, scientifically explain the basic theories, methods, and changing trends of urban sociology from the aspects of urban life time, urban living space, urban living space, urban consumption space, etc., analyze Chinese urban sociology research and Chinese urban issues from the perspective of China's urban transformation and Chinese urban units, and provide services for the formulation of harmonious social policies and urban social planning.

Name: Social Psychology
Introduction: Through learning, students can understand the basic theories and basic knowledge of social psychology and the past and latest research progress in the field of social psychology. At the same time, combined with the psychology and behavior of Chinese people, students can use scientific methods to conduct research on social and interpersonal issues. Through the study of this course, students can also have a deep understanding of themselves, society and psychological issues related to daily life, thereby cultivating them to deal with the problems they face in a scientific attitude. and can engage in basic social psychology research

Name: Planning Cartography and Computer-Aided Techniques
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
