Introduction: "Planning Drawing and Computer-Assisted Technology" is an important practical required course for undergraduate students majoring in urban and rural planning in my country. The course is based on teaching planning drawing specifications and computer-aided design software application methods and exercises, and allows students to complete a series of drawing assignments based on topics provided by the teacher.

Name: Urban and Rural Community Spatial Planning and Design
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: "Urban and Rural Community Space Planning and Design" is an important practical required course for undergraduates majoring in urban and rural planning in my country. The course is based on teaching the theory of urban and rural community planning, combined with case interpretation, current situation analysis and discussion, and allows students to complete course design and research reports based on topics provided by teachers.

Name: Principles of Urban Planning (1)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Initial courses: urban planning overview, urban development history, urban geography (or synchronization)
Introduction: "Principles of Urban Planning 1" is an important professional basic course required for urban planning and related majors. The content almost covers the basic principles of all-round professional knowledge involved in the urban planning process. This course is based on urban planning theory, principles and layout methods, and takes the planning and layout of various urban elements as its core content. On the basis of elaborating the composition of the modern urban planning system and the evolution of domestic and foreign urban planning ideas, theoretical methods and practices, this course focuses on teaching the preparation methods and basic content of my country's urban planning, expounds the relationship between urban planning and regional planning, and analyzes the natural conditions and environmental factors that affect urban construction; according to the editor The requirements for urban master planning respectively introduce the nature and development scale of the city, and the planning and layout of each urban component element: industry, warehousing and logistics, external transportation, urban road systems, residential communities, and public spaces; as well as related content on urban heritage protection and urban renewal, disaster prevention and reduction, urban agglomeration planning, and village and town planning. The final course develops students' comprehensive planning abilities based on urban planning principles through typical analysis of different types of urban planning examples and comparison of urban planning plans. _x000D_

Name: Urban-Rural Spatial Cognition Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The spatial awareness internship in urban and rural areas is an essential component of the undergraduate teaching of five-year urban planning and is the subject of a professional assessment mission. The internship was based in the city of Kyouta. In the start-up phase, systematic hands-on instruction began with the main bases in Tianjin City and New Coastal Zone, Beijing and Tangshan. When conditions are ripe, they are gradually extended to the cities of Ishijia, Chengde and Zhang Jiaguchi, which form the basis of the Kyyo Jin-Tang, with Kyoto as its centre. (a) The Beijing Metropolitan Area as the basis for teaching internships, which fully reflect the special features of the urban planning profession, which “maintenance the geology-based system of planning and teaching science and research in the field of science and technology”, and which is the result of a long-term study of urban planning in China in the areas of urbanization, regional research and planning, innovation space and innovation groups, economic geography, etc., which can be achieved through continuous teaching internships. (2) The new Tianjin Sea Zone, one of China ' s three major urban centres, serves as a pilot zone for comprehensive national reform, exploring new models of regional development and providing experience and models for national development reform. This region serves as a training ground for students to understand the most critical issues in our urbanization process. (3) The cities within the metropolitan area are characterized by characteristics such as nature, size, industry, history, culture, etc., which facilitate the organization of internships in accordance with the teaching tasks. (4) Beijing is the centre of the capital city circle, which is well suited and well-developed in terms of transport, and which facilitates internships. In recent years, the Department of Urban and Regional Planning and the Department of Urban and Economic Geography of our house have been responsible for such tasks as the master plans for the cities of Tianjin and the master plans for land use, as well as for a number of planning and research projects in other cities in the metropolitan area (e.g. the master plans for land use in Beijing city, the plan for urban-rural integration in Hebei). At the same time, Beijing University and Tianjin signed a memorandum for active participation in the construction of the new district of Tianjin Coast, which provides scientific and intellectual support for the development of the new zone, opening up and sustainable development of the coastal zone, and provides a good basis and prospect for the city ring to serve as a training ground for our institution. I have entered into a cooperative agreement with Tianjin City Planning Institute and Tianjin Economic Technology Development Zone (Teda) for the establishment of a teaching internship.

Name: Introduction to Mineral Resource Economics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Mineral resources are a basic production resource and labor object. Today, in the era of information society and knowledge economy, 70% of agricultural production materials are still related to mineral resources, and more than 80% of industrial raw materials come from mineral resources. After the 1960s, human development and utilization of mineral resources increased rapidly. Mineral resources play an increasingly important role in modern industrial production and national economic development. Not only that, the importance of the development and utilization of mineral resources to national security has gradually been recognized by governments of various countries, thus giving a certain political color to the pure commodity of mineral resources. With the development of economic globalization, the survival and development of a country's economy are increasingly affected by international political economy. The ability of sovereign states to effectively control and protect the operation and development of their own economies is actually weakening. Decisions that used to be within the national scope are increasingly made by some international raw materials associations and international institutions. _x000D_
The development and utilization of mineral resources is closely related to the development and prosperity of a country and nation. Mineral resources are not only the foundation of national economic development, but also have always been a tool in international political struggles and the driving force of major wars. Therefore, the research objects faced by mineral resource economics not only involve mineral resources and their own economic value, but also involve many fields such as international politics, international trade, law, geography and human environment. The development and utilization of mineral resources is a conscious social and economic activity of mankind. It is not only restricted by the status of mineral resources, but also by many factors such as the economic and technological level at that time, the laws of various countries and regions, and environmental protection regulations. Mineral resource economists should not only tell people how to best utilize and distribute mineral raw materials, how to avoid waste, and how to keep the burden on the environment within certain limits based on the discovery and exploitation of mineral resources. More importantly, they should provide clear and practical policy information for a country or region's resource development and utilization in the context of global economic integration, and protect the country's economic and political interests related to mineral resources in the ever-changing international political and economic arena. _x000D_
First, the national economic significance of mineral resources and the geological basis for the formation of mineral resources are taught. Gold is used as an example to discuss the gold market and its economic status. Describe the market structure and form, mineral resource management policy planning and social issues, and conduct analysis of the mining situation. Teach the economics and resource issues of metal mineral resources including ferrous metals, non-ferrous metals, rare metals, and precious metals. Regarding global energy and energy demand issues, lectures focus on coal, oil, natural gas, and nuclear energy resources and their issues. On the basis of discussing resource economic issues, the issue between mineral resources and national security is analyzed and studied, because mineral resources are an important guarantee for national security and economic development. In the process of development and utilization of mineral resources, environmental problems will inevitably arise. How to efficiently recover and utilize mineral resources is the key to maintaining stable development of society. This not only involves the sustainable development of society, but will also affect the rise of the Chinese nation and changes in the international political landscape. Environmental issues are related to everyone's survival and the prosperity of various countries. How to balance resource development and utilization with environmental protection is a complex political and economic issue. When the development of mineral resources on land reaches its limit, mining mineral resources in the ocean has become an inevitable trend, and it has also caused huge international disputes. Entering the blue ocean and competing for living space and resources are currently the key issues that leaders of various countries are considering. We all must seriously think about the fact that humans obtain the resources and environment for survival and development from the earth, and the relationship between humans and the earth continues to evolve.

Name: Fundamentals of Remote Sensing and Principles of Image Interpretation
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Remote sensing is the basic knowledge and basic means that undergraduates majoring in geography, resources, environment, and planning should master. The course "Basics of Remote Sensing and Principles of Image Interpretation" aims to introduce students to the basic principles of remote sensing and the basic methods of modern remote sensing technology. The main contents include the introduction and development status of remote sensing, the physical foundation and technical system of remote sensing, the foundation of aerial remote sensing, the interpretation of aerial photographs, the foundation of satellite remote sensing, the interpretation of satellite photographs, remote sensing digital image processing, remote sensing image analysis, microwave remote sensing topics, vegetation remote sensing topics, and atmospheric remote sensing topics. _x000D_
    The course has no prerequisites for students who choose the course, but requires students to have basic computer operation skills and the ability to accept new technologies and methods. _x000D_
    While this course focuses on the basic theoretical knowledge of remote sensing, it also attaches great importance to the cultivation of students' practical abilities, so a total of 7-8 classroom internships are arranged. The internship closely follows the classroom content and uses advanced remote sensing software and new data materials to train students in technical methods of remote sensing image interpretation and digital processing. _x000D_
    The electronic reference books, classroom PPT handouts, application software, and internship data for this course will be uploaded to the FTP server of the School of Urban and Environment 1-2 days before class for students to download before and after class. The course has a dedicated QQ group for communication and consultation between course-selecting students and course teachers. _x000D_
    I hope to have happy cooperation, smooth communication, mutual learning and common progress with my classmates. We strive to make this course a basic course that students enjoy learning, can learn easily, and can use what they learn.

Name: Urban Design
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Fine arts mapping, architectural overviews, landscape green land systems
Introduction: This course is a required course for fifth-year urban planning (engineering) undergraduate students. The purpose of the course is to enable students to master the basic concepts, theories, and methods of urban design, and to master the means and techniques of investigation, conception, design, and expression in urban design projects. Students need to have a comprehensive understanding and comprehensive grasp of the design of urban space, landscape, architecture, sketches, and facilities, so as to adapt to the needs of future urban planning and management and other practical work. In the first half of the course, students will be assigned to do several spatial cognition and design exercises, including inspection records, spatial analysis, small-scale hypothetical designs, etc., to train their abilities and skills in cognition of urban spatial elements, coordination of structural relationships, and organization of behavioral streamlines. In the second half of the semester, a comprehensive design assignment will be assigned to train the practical ability to comprehensively examine urban spatial phenomena, identify problems, and solve problems. In this process, basic knowledge of urban design theory, history, methods, future trends, etc. will be introduced throughout the course. Students are required to read a certain amount of urban design literature at the same time to acquire a certain degree of theoretical literacy.

Name: Urban Road and Traffic Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course mainly consists of four parts: comprehensive road traffic, departmental road traffic, regional road traffic and urban road traffic. _x000D_
Comprehensive road traffic focuses on analyzing the macro-influencing factors of road traffic, including three major factors and six factors: natural factors (natural environment, natural resources), socioeconomic factors (population and cities, industry and economy), and technical policy factors (technology, policy), as well as the overall principles of road transportation layout, and elaborates on the composition and economic and geographical significance of China's eight vertical and eight horizontal main transportation corridors_x000D_
Departmental road transportation will introduce the five main modes of transportation such as railways, highways, aviation, shipping, and pipelines one by one. While understanding the technical characteristics of each, it will focus on teaching the relationship between stations and ports of different transportation modes such as train stations, bus stations, airports, and corresponding transportation lines and the city, as well as the layout requirements in the city; this is also an important content of external transportation in urban road transportation planning; _x000D_
Regional road transportation focuses on exploring the relationship between regional transportation and urban development, such as the impact on the nature, scale, layout, industry, rise and fall of cities, especially the important impact of railways (such as Qinghai-Tibet Railway, Beijing-Kowloon Railway), rivers (Yangtze River) and other linear economic belts on regional socio-economic development. At the same time, the content division and method of regional road traffic planning are introduced with examples; _x000D_
Urban road transport is the focus of this course. Based on a comprehensive review of the development history and conceptual changes of urban roads in ancient and modern times, both at home and abroad, the content and methods of urban road system planning and design are taught, including urban road functions, classification, spatial layout, planning principles, route design, intersection reconstruction, etc., and theoretical knowledge is applied to specific urban practice through more than two actual case planning. _x000D_

Name: Real Estate Appraisal
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Real estate price evaluation is an important intermediary activity in establishing the order of real estate transactions. The evaluation price is an important reference for land output transfer, real estate transactions, real estate taxation and other management and activities involving real estate prices. Our country implements a qualification certification system for real estate appraisers. The core subject for obtaining professional qualification certificates for real estate appraisers and land appraisers is real estate appraisal. Real estate valuation is a required course for those engaged in real estate research, real estate appraisal, real estate agency, and urban land use. _x000D_
      This course starts from the concept, characteristics and factors affecting prices of real estate, and systematically teaches the theory of real estate valuation and various valuation methods, as well as the writing and requirements of valuation reports. It focuses on teaching the principles, applicable objects and conditions, valuation procedures, data collection, formulas and calculations, key parameter calculations, valuation difficulties and keys of the three real estate valuation methods of market method, income method and cost method, and appropriately supplements the knowledge of laws and regulations related to real estate valuation. _x000D_

Name: Urban Planning Systems Engineering
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Urban planning theory and practice, system thinking, advanced mathematics
Introduction: Urban planning systems engineering is a discipline that applies holism-based ideas and methods such as systems thinking, systems thinking, operations research methods, and complex network theory to the study of urban planning and design as complex systems. This course mainly consists of four components: systems theory of urban planning, systems methods, principles of operations research, and complexity science. System theory includes system thinking, system methods, information entropy measurement, etc. System analysis methods are mainly black box methods, including regression analysis and neural network modeling. Operations research methods include linear programming, analytic hierarchy process and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation. Complexity science focuses on self-organizing network theory, especially scale-free network analysis. If time permits, we will also teach predictive analysis based on nonlinear modeling and predictive analysis based on gray systems such as the GM(1,1) model.

Name: Principles of Urban Planning (2)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course is an important professional basic course required for urban and rural planning and related majors. On the basis of the urban and rural planning theory and planning system, the content and preparation of urban and rural spatial planning at all levels and types introduced in the prerequisite course "Urban Planning Principles (1)", "Urban Planning Principles (2)" will further teach urban and rural land use as the core of urban and rural planning discipline research, introduce the goals and content of other spatial planning such as land use planning, territorial planning, etc., and introduce the principles and practical knowledge of urban land development. During the course teaching, students are guided to form an interest in in-depth professional learning and expanded research, and master the basic methods of in-depth learning and research. The purpose of this course is to cultivate students to establish a comprehensive and correct concept of urban development, and to lay a scientific theoretical foundation for students' future practical operations of urban and rural spatial planning and urban land development.

Name: Introduction to Historical Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
"Introduction to Historical Geography" is a course offered to undergraduate students in the School of Urban and Environment. It aims to introduce the formation and development process of China's geographical pattern. It mainly includes the basic theories and research methods of historical geography, the growth and decline of China's territory, the division and management of political regions, the formation and development of water and land transportation roads, the rise and fall of cities, the transfer of political, economic and cultural centers, the increase and loss of population and migration, the exchange and integration of ethnic groups, as well as the natural environment change issues in Chinese history, such as the diversion of rivers, the demise of lakes, the disappearance of forests, etc. The teaching content covers both Chinese historical human geography and historical physical geography. It is an introductory course for students majoring in geography to understand the development and change process of Chinese geography. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is mainly taught by teachers, using multimedia and other teaching tools to vividly and intuitively display the changing process of China's geographical pattern in the form of pictures, slides, etc. While teaching knowledge, pay attention to guiding students to do a small amount of topical research that they are interested in, and organize class discussions based on students' independent research work, encourage students to actively participate in class discussions, discover problems, and solve problems, cultivate students' ability to think independently, make independent judgments, and write independently, initially cultivate students' basic ability to read and use historical documents, and cultivate students' preliminary ability to analyze problems from the perspective of historical geography. While imparting basic professional knowledge and cultivating students' research abilities, this course is especially beneficial to science and engineering students in broadening their horizons and developing ideas, strengthening their cultivation and quality in Chinese history, and broadening the horizons and developing ideas of students in various majors. _x000D_
_x000D_
In addition to classroom lectures and discussions, teachers will organize one or two field internships to inspect some important historical and cultural sites and relics. Classroom knowledge is compared with extracurricular reality to deepen students' understanding of Chinese history and geography. _x000D_

Name: Comprehensive Urban Planning (Course Design)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite:
Principles of urban planning
Transport geography and urban road traffic planning
Settlement planning
Building General
Park green land planning
Urban geography
Technology for urban planning
Introduction: Urban planning is a highly applied subject, and this course is a design practice course for urban master planning. On the basis of systematically summarizing the course knowledge related to urban master planning, through the analysis and research of specific city basic data, understand the characteristics and problems of the city; determine the urban development goals and scale according to the regional planning goals and city nature positioning, and clarify the development and construction requirements in the planning area; carry out construction land assessment price, select and determine the scope of urban construction land; adjust the urban layout structure, build a transportation system inside and outside the city, and propose the layout of main urban functions, public service facilities and infrastructure; determine the development goals and overall layout of the green space system; determine the content and requirements for historical and cultural protection and local traditional characteristics protection. Finally, planning results are formed that meet the requirements of the city's master plan.

Name: Research Methods in Human Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course aims to help students understand the changes in ideological trends in the development of contemporary economic geography methodology, understand the representative methods of different ideological trends, and their theoretical premises, advantages and limitations. On this basis, starting from discussing how to plan a research project, quantitative data collection methods and preliminary analysis techniques, qualitative data collection methods and analysis strategies are systematically introduced, and combined with spatial analysis techniques and spatial critical thinking, students are organized to further discuss the methodological issues of economic geography based on specific socio-economic issues. And combined with extracurricular research practice, students are guided to carry out creative practice facing specific problems.

Name: Tourism Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Up to 2nd grade of the institution, with some basic knowledge (or understanding) of geography
Introduction:
This course is an elective course for senior undergraduate students in the School of Environment. Recommended for sophomores and above. _x000D_
Purpose: Through the study of this course, students will not only understand the basic concepts and academic progress of tourism geography, but also emphasize a certain amount of research training so that students can master some basic research methods. _x000D_
Lectures: Mainly conducted in class (if possible, industry leaders and travel agencies may be invited to give lectures). _x000D_
Internship: including literature review, review, presentation, etc., tourist survey, special research, etc. It is generally recommended to do this in groups. _x000D_
Discussion: in class, after class in the same group, between groups_x000D_
Assignment: Review, literature review, tourist survey and special research are all included in the assignment scope_x000D_
Exam: Open book (exam paper and answers on tourism geography, purpose is to urge students to review)_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
Introduction:
"Introduction to Xi Jinping's Important Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era" is offered by the School of Marxism at Peking University. It is an important part of the 2017-2018 series of innovative courses on ideological and political theory supported by the Beijing Municipal Education Commission. _x000D_
The course consists of 8 lectures, focusing on Xi Jinping’s important thoughts and comprehensively describing the concepts and developments in China’s internal affairs, diplomacy, military, culture and other aspects in recent years. _x000D_
The course invites famous theoretical experts to teach in the form of lectures, which is of great significance in guiding college students to study classic works and think about major theoretical and practical issues. _x000D_

Name: Regional Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: It is recommended that the master plans for cities and towns be completed first.
Introduction:
This course first starts with the concept, regionality, hierarchy and other characteristics of region, and gives an overall introduction to the development and tasks of regional science, the characteristics and requirements of regional research, the characteristics and trends of regional development, and the content and tasks of regional planning. _x000D_
Regional planning has strong contemporary and practical characteristics. The course will analyze the impact and requirements on regional planning of the international background of knowledgeization, informatization, globalization, climate change, etc., as well as my country's policies on building a well-off society, a new socialist countryside, the scientific outlook on development, overall urban and rural planning, building a harmonious society, and building a low-carbon city, especially functional areas. The important influence of planning is discussed in the new situation: regional space view, location view, market view, resource view and development view, as well as the resulting changes in regional planning characteristics such as planning goals, planning concepts, planning priorities, planning effects, public participation, planning implementation, and new concepts such as sustainability and regional coordination. _x000D_
The basic theoretical system of regional planning includes three major frameworks. First, regional spatial structure theory, which studies the distribution of regional land use types, the structure of regional urban systems, and the characteristics of social and economic development in spatial layout. It is an analysis of the objective regional development landscape, based on location theory, such as classical location theory, modern location theory, modern location theory, and new location theory; second, regional development (development) theory, including economic development Theory, spatial development theory, development stage theory, etc., studies the strategic model of regional development, the dynamic mechanism of regional development, the strategies and tactics of regional development, etc., which is a combination of objective regional development laws and subjective man-made strategies, such as the theory of regional division of labor, the theory of regional industrial structure correlation, the theory of regional production complex, the theory of competitiveness and industrial agglomeration, innovation and diffusion theory, growth theory, point-axis theory, etc. Third, the theory of regional planning and regulation, the ways in which regional planning, market and government play a regulatory role are its main contents. _x000D_
The course will also focus on the content system of regional planning, including regional analysis, regional industrial development, regional residents and urban-rural coordination, regional land use and space control, regional infrastructure and ecological environment, regional coordination and policy and other planning requirements, as well as regional planning research methods such as regional analysis and SWOT analysis. At the end of the course, the practical process of regional planning preparation will be introduced. _x000D_

Name: Traffic Analysis, Simulation and Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
"Traffic Analysis, Simulation and Planning" is one of the basic professional courses in the urban and rural planning major, resource management and urban and rural planning major. Transportation is one of the most important economic sectors in cities and regions. It is the external manifestation of human social and economic activities and one of the key infrastructures supporting urban and regional development. At the same time, traffic problems, such as traffic congestion, energy consumption, environmental pollution, traffic accidents, traffic social equity, etc., also put pressure on the sustainable development of cities and regions. Traffic analysis simulation and planning courses have become one of the main courses offered by international and domestic universities in urban planning majors. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course teaches the phenomena and mechanisms of urban and regional traffic problems, the basic principles of urban and regional traffic flow, traffic analysis theories and methods, traffic simulation macro and micro models and their applications, traffic planning model construction and planning preparation, and policy evaluation of traffic planning and management. Specifically, it covers traffic survey methods, traffic occurrence and attraction, traffic distribution, traffic mode sharing, non-aggregated models, traffic allocation and its extended models, combination models, dynamic traffic analysis, microscopic traffic flow simulation, traffic planning plans and their evaluation, traffic policies and their evaluation, etc. By taking this elective course, students will understand the basic theories of urban and regional transportation, become familiar with the basic methods and models of urban and regional transportation analysis, master the key models and technologies of traffic simulation, master the transportation planning model and planning preparation, master the key models and technologies of transportation planning evaluation, and become familiar with the key technologies of transportation demand management policy evaluation. _x000D_
_x000D_
The courses are mainly taught to undergraduate students in their second year or above in two majors: Urban and Rural Planning, Resource Management and Urban and Rural Planning. _x000D_

Name: Integrated Social Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Students in urban planning after third year of undergraduate studies
Introduction:
Urban planning is a discipline that closely combines theory and practice. The comprehensive social practice internship course requires students to directly participate in teachers' specific research or practical project work, so that students can apply the theoretical knowledge they have learned in relevant practices of this major, deepen their understanding of classroom knowledge, and initially master basic methods such as research, data review, data analysis, and map drawing for related research and practice. _x000D_
This course is jointly undertaken by all teachers from the Department of Urban and Regional Planning and the Department of Urban and Economic Geography. Each teacher arranges the internship content for the intern students based on their own scientific research projects. The research directions of teachers in the two departments cover various related fields of human geography and urban planning. _x000D_

Name: Urban Infrastructure Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Urban infrastructure planning is one of the main contents of urban planning and one of the results that must be submitted for urban planning review and approval. This course is combined with urban planning principles to teach the basic principles and methods of urban infrastructure planning. The main contents include: introduction to urban infrastructure, urban water supply and drainage engineering planning, urban power supply planning, urban land vertical planning, etc.

Name: Urban Heritage Conservation and Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Urban heritage is a heritage of cultural economic (potential) value within urban and rural spaces, reflecting the historical and cultural dimensions of urban and rural areas, which is an important component of cultural heritage through conservation, maintenance and sustainable use in different forms. In China, urban heritage, involving the world ' s cultural heritage, historic and cultural centres (towns, villages), historical neighbourhoods, preservation units at all levels, and modern-day buildings of excellence, is an important aspect of ensuring the sustainable development of urban and rural societies.
The course consists mainly of an overview of the literature on urban heritage, historical analysis, category comparisons, value assessments, social research and conservation planning, six main chapters, with references, cases and indexes.

Name: Planning and Design Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: For students in the fourth year of urban planning, they are required to spend 4 summers at the Planning and Design Institute

Name: Urban Regulatory Detailed Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Urban planning principles, planning mapping and mechanical aids
Introduction: "Detailed Planning" is a required professional course for undergraduates majoring in urban and rural planning in my country. It is a course that pays equal attention to theory and practice. The curriculum is based on teaching the theory of controlled detailed planning, combined with case interpretation and group discussions, allowing students to complete course design and research reports based on specific topics.

Name: Urban Planning Management and Regulations
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Urban planning management is an important part of the urban planning discipline. _x000D_
      Our country implements a qualification certification system for urban planners. One of the important contents of obtaining an urban planner is urban planning management and regulations. This course is a required course for those engaged in urban planning management, urban planning and design and other technical work, real estate development, operation and management, etc. _x000D_
      This course is divided into three parts: the first is the theoretical part, involving relevant knowledge of administrative management, administrative law and basic knowledge of urban planning and management. The second is management operation. According to the composition of the urban planning management system, it covers urban planning preparation and approval management, construction project site selection management, construction land planning management, construction project planning management, supervision and inspection of urban planning implementation, etc. Its concepts, management tasks, management objects and characteristics, management content and basis, management procedures and operational requirements are introduced respectively. Requirements for planning and management of historical and cultural heritage protection. _x000D_
      On this basis, according to the characteristics of our department, relevant contents of real estate management law, land management law and their relationship with urban planning management are added. _x000D_

Name: Integrated Social Practice Survey
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
_x000D_
    Comprehensive social practice investigation ability is a basic professional skill that students majoring in urban planning must master. It is also one of the basic requirements for teaching urban planning majors proposed by the Urban Planning Professional Steering Committee of National Colleges and Universities. "Social Comprehensive Practical Investigation" is a course that pays equal attention to theory and practice. The course requires students to select topics on urban issues, conduct on-site surveys, questionnaires and related interviews, and finally complete a social survey report, from which outstanding works will be selected to participate in the national urban planning professional competition that year. _x000D_
_x000D_
    Through the establishment of the course, students majoring in urban planning will have the following abilities: the ability to collect data and information through observation, interviews, questionnaires, etc.; the ability to use qualitative and quantitative methods to comprehensively analyze, predict and evaluate various data and information; and the basic ability to research planning and related issues and propose countermeasures. _x000D_

Name: Money and Banking
Introduction: What is the relationship between currency issuance, interest rates, and prices? Why are long-term bond yields generally higher than short-term bond yields? What are the main differences between bank deposits, stock markets and bonds? What factors determine investment decisions? How does the central bank formulate and implement monetary policy? The main purpose of this course is to help students understand the basic operations and practices of currency, banking and finance by learning basic theories, and thereby learn to analyze actual economic phenomena.

Name: Urban Public Space Planning and Design
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The narrow concept of urban public space refers to those outdoor spaces for public use in daily life and social life of urban residents. It includes streets, squares, outdoor venues in residential areas, parks, sports venues, etc. In the field of Western urban built environment research, the concept of public space was introduced into related works from the fields of sociology and political philosophy in the 1960s. Because it reveals the inner connection between material space and abstract social and political space, it has aroused extensive discussion among scholars in the field of built environment research. Urban public space provides a place for a variety of urban activities and provides opportunities for communication and integration of different groups of people. Its openness and tolerance ensure the generation of urban vitality, which is of great significance on many levels. _x000D_
This course aims to explain the existence and formation process of existing public spaces by understanding the socio-economic and institutional factors behind specific physical spaces, and explore solutions to existing problems. During the design and transformation process, the focus was on understanding the social institutional reasons that affect the generation of public space in the context of rapid urbanization in contemporary China. Then, by comparing the similarities and differences between Eastern and Western public spaces affected by social and political factors, we can understand the spatial attributes of the design plots and design and transform the selected plots based on specific value standards. _x000D_

Name: Urban Ecology and Environmental Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Ecological foundations, integration of natural geography, geologic overviews, etc.
Introduction:
This course is one of the required courses for the backbone major of urban planning as determined by the Urban Planning Professional Teaching Steering Committee. The teaching content revolves around the basic knowledge and application of ecology, requiring students to: master the basic knowledge of ecology, an introduction to urban environment, environmental effects under the influence of urbanization, characteristics of urban ecosystems, etc.; be familiar with the relationship between people and the environment in cities, as well as important ecological application fields closely related to urban research and urban planning; understand biodiversity protection, ecosystem management, ecological restoration, ecological engineering, ecological planning, ecological city construction, industrial ecology and circular economy, etc., and be able to apply them to urban environmental planning practice. _x000D_
    The teaching plan is mainly aimed at guiding and cultivating students who are interested in urban and rural planning and landscape architecture, taking into account the needs of students who are interested in ecology and ecological applications. The goal of the course is to enable students to fully understand the basic concepts and laws of ecology after the teaching of this course, and to be able to flexibly apply this knowledge to the research and practical applications of land use, urban and rural planning, and resource utilization and protection encountered in combination with specific cases, and to be able to take the initiative and be far-sighted in the process of coordinating various complex relationships encountered in urbanization practice. _x000D_

Name: Urban-Rural Recreation and Tourism Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course is divided into 11 classroom teaching sessions, explaining the relationship between tourism, recreation and urban and rural development, the characteristics and classification of tourism products, and also explaining in detail the theoretical knowledge and precautions that should be mastered in the planning and design of different types of tourist destinations and recreational spaces. _x000D_
At the same time, students individually undergo research training in three units: literature review, research design, and paper writing. The research training needs to be combined with the content learned in the course, at least content that is closely related to urban and rural tourism and recreation. _x000D_

Name: Industrial Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Industrial geography is a subdiscipline of economic geography. Its main task is to understand the impact of the human industrialization process on the geographical landscape in which we live by describing and explaining changes in industrial space, as well as the impact of the uneven development of industrialization on local areas. The research focuses on the location selection and influencing factors of enterprises, as well as the macro-industrial spatial layout and the evolution of regional development policies, especially the impact of technological innovation on regional industrialization development, how the local environment affects industrial technology innovation, and thus affects the lasting advantages of regional industrial development. By teaching the general theory of industrial geography and the specific topics of industrial sectors, the course helps students understand the main factors affecting industrial location changes, landscape changes and environmental impacts that are closely related to human industrialization. It also combines practical content such as regional development and urban planning management to cultivate students' ability to conduct industrial technical and economic analysis of specific regions.

Name: Advanced Lecture Series on Urban Planning Topics
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Urban planning principles, urban planning management and legislation
Introduction: This course is a series of special lectures for senior undergraduate students in urban and rural planning and related majors. Topics will cover: urban and rural development factors such as population and land, urban and rural development strategies such as multi-plan integration, rural revitalization, and national-level new district construction, new urban research directions such as big data, informal space, and urban governance, and urban construction investment and financing issues such as land finance and PPP.

Name: Chinese History and Culture in English
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The course "Chinese History and Culture in an English Context" examines several Chinese cultural phenomena in a historical context, including ancient mythology, classic philosophy, strategic thought, ancient inventions, traditional education, women and marriage, and contemporary Chinese youth. This course is not a general introduction to Chinese history and culture, but an in-depth study and discussion of hot or confusing topics in cultural exchanges between China and foreign countries. This course will enhance students' in-depth understanding of the origin and evolution of Chinese civilization through various teaching methods such as classroom lectures, audio-visuals, discussions, and keynote speeches. Help students view Chinese historical traditions, Chinese cultural characteristics, Chinese national psychology, and the relationship between China and the world from multiple perspectives. Improve students' ability to read English works and use English to express ideas, and promote students' academic interest and sense of mission in cultural exchanges between China and foreign countries. Turn English learning into a way for Chinese people to go global and promote Chinese culture, so as to promote mutual understanding and dialogue between different cultures.

Name: Linear Algebra
Introduction: Linear algebra is a branch of mathematics. The first problem to be solved in linear algebra is to solve a large number of linear equations that appear in practice. The tools used are matrices, vectors and determinants. Vectors and matrices are not only used to solve linear equations, but are widely used in many fields of natural science, humanities, economics, management, and engineering technology. Therefore, it is necessary to conduct further in-depth research on them. Therefore, research on linear transformations, vector inner products, orthogonal matrices, eigenvalues ​​and eigenvectors of matrices, quadratic forms, etc. are introduced. In recent years, with the widespread application of computers and the rapid development of science and technology, linear algebra has been increasingly widely used, making linear algebra an important basic course. This course teaches the basic theories and methods of linear algebra and provides corresponding basic training.

Name: Probability and Statistics
Introduction: Probability theory and mathematical statistics are a branch of mathematics that studies the regularity of a large number of random phenomena in nature, human society and technological processes. Probability theory abstracts random phenomena into random variables to study its general regularity. Mathematical statistics starts from collecting, sorting and analyzing random data in practical problems to make inferences, predictions and decisions about problems. To a large extent, probability theory is the basis of mathematical statistics. Mathematical statistics is the application of probability theory and has greatly promoted the research of probability theory. With the rapid development of modern science and technology, this subject has developed vigorously and has more and more applications in many fields such as natural sciences, economics, humanities, management, and engineering technology. Probability theory and mathematical statistics is an important basic course. This course focuses on introducing its basic concepts, theories and methods and providing necessary basic training.

Name: Global Environmental Issues
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The course will focus on current global environmental issues related to climate change, stratospheric ozone depletion, biodiversity and persistent organic pollutants and international compliance.

Name: Civil Procedure Law
Prerequisite:
Constitutional science
Jurisprudence
General provisions of civil law
Introduction:
Civil Procedure Law is a required professional course for law school undergraduates. It mainly introduces how parties and courts use litigation, the most formal dispute resolution method, to apply the law to resolve civil disputes. Through the study of this course, students will think about legal and philosophical issues in civil litigation from a professional perspective and prepare for their future legal career. _x000D_
_x000D_
The structure of civil litigation determines the resolution of substantive issues. In terms of theory, this course will guide students to explore the relationship between some basic theoretical categories in law from the perspective of civil procedure law, such as entities and procedures, courts and parties, public rights and private rights, etc. At the same time, students will also be introduced to the basic theories of civil litigation, such as right of action, subject matter of litigation, res judicata, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
In terms of practice, the course will provide students with the key points of various systems of civil litigation in my country, such as jurisdiction system, evidence system, preservation system, etc. At the same time, the contents of various litigation procedures and non-litigation procedures will also be explained so that students can use these procedures to resolve civil disputes. In short, it helps students learn various operations of civil litigation and lays the foundation for future legal practice.

Name: Constitutional Law
Prerequisite: The first year of the university curriculum does not require prior courses.
Introduction:
Constitutional law is a compulsory course for undergraduates in the law department and a basic course in law. Main lectures: Constitution_x000D_
basic theory, our country’s constitution and historical experience, our country’s national nature and economic system, our country’s state_x000D_
Structure and organizational form of political power, our country’s national administrative agencies, judicial agencies, prosecutorial agencies, our country’s citizens_x000D_
Basic rights and obligations, my country’s electoral system, national flag, national anthem, national emblem, etc.

Name: Tort Law
Prerequisite: Legal fundamentals, constitutional law, general principles of civil law, law of claims
Introduction:
This course is based on current laws such as the Tort Liability Law and the General Principles of Civil Law, and is closely integrated with the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, especially based on a large number of court judgments. It absorbs the latest research results at home and abroad, integrates theory with practice, and systematically expounds the basic principles and rules of tort law. _x000D_
On the basis of introducing the basic knowledge of tort law, this course focuses on the basic scope and thinking mode of tort law, the determination of the right to infringement and the normative approach of tort law, etc. The basic principles of tort law are not discussed or not specifically discussed in traditional textbooks. It specifically discusses the system effect of result liability and the attribution principle of tort law. In the case of typed tort liability, it focuses on the discussion in combination with court judgments. It strives to enable students to master the rules of tort law and at the same time grasp the basic principles of tort law; to improve their ability to analyze and solve problems while acquiring knowledge. _x000D_

Name: General Principles of Civil Law
Introduction: The General Introduction to Civil Law course is one of the most important professional courses for law school undergraduates. It is one of the basic courses for cultivating law students’ legal knowledge and legal thinking. It is one of the backbone professional courses for law school undergraduates and is also a prerequisite course for many related courses, including property law, debt law, family law, intellectual property law, civil procedure law, company law, maritime law, instrument law, international economic law, private international law, etc. The general course on civil law takes the main concepts of legal relations, legal acts, and civil rights as basic clues, and tells the history and evolution of civil law, the basic principles of civil law, the functions and concepts of civil law, the origin of civil law, the relationship between civil law and related legal departments such as commercial law, economic law, and civil procedure law, the natural person system, the personality rights and identity rights of natural persons, the legal person system, the unincorporated organization system, the theory and system of legal acts, the agency system, the statute of limitations system, etc.

Name: Specific Crimes in Criminal Law
Introduction: The course presents fundamental theoretical issues of the criminal law segmentation. In accordance with the logical system of the sub-rules of our criminal law, the various types of crime are presented, analysed and studied on a case-by-case basis.

Name: History of Chinese Legal Systems
Introduction: The history of Chinese legal system is a basic course for law majors. It introduces the historical period of the origin and development of Chinese law, describes the form, content, basic principles, characteristics and historical status of the legal system in different periods, explores the relationship between legal thought and social changes and the evolution of the legal system, and enables students to understand the historical experience and national characteristics of China's legal system construction.

Name: Administrative Law and Administrative Litigation Law
Introduction: This course is one of the 14 core courses for law majors in colleges and universities determined by the Ministry of Education’s Higher Education Institutions Teaching Steering Committee for Law. This course comprehensively, systematically and in-depth explains the basic theories and basic knowledge of administrative law and administrative litigation law. The scope of research mainly includes the general principles and principles of administrative law; the general theory of administrative law subjects and the responsibilities, powers, management methods of administrative subjects and the rights and obligations of administrative counterparts; the general theory of administrative behavior and the nature, characteristics and structure of administrative behavior. Requirements, legal requirements and operating procedures for various types of administrative actions; the general theory of administrative relief and administrative reconsideration, the nature and function of administrative litigation, the scope of cases, jurisdiction, procedures and adjudication standards of administrative reconsideration and administrative litigation; the general theory of administrative compensation and the components of administrative compensation liability, liability principles, scope of compensation, methods, standards and procedures, etc. This course mainly takes my country's administrative legal practice and administrative law theory as the basic research objects, and at the same time absorbs and draws on the results of foreign administrative law research. This course strives to form and establish a theoretical system of administrative law with Chinese characteristics on the basis of inheriting, criticizing and abandoning various academic schools such as control theory, management theory, administrative power standard theory and counterpart rights standard theory in foreign administrative law.

Name: General Principles of Criminal Law
Introduction: This course focuses on explaining the general knowledge of criminal law and describing and clarifying the norms of criminal law. Provide comprehensive and systematic lectures on some basic theoretical issues in my country's criminal law, especially the latest results of theoretical research on criminal law, and appropriately introduce theoretical knowledge and the latest development trends of foreign criminal law. Pay attention to interspersing some cases in the lectures to explore some problems existing in practice and strengthen the connection between theory and practice.

Name: Criminal Procedure Law
Prerequisite: Constitution, jurisprudence, criminal law, civil procedure law
Introduction: Criminal procedure law is a legal discipline whose main research objects are criminal procedure legislation, criminal procedure practice and criminal procedure theory. It is one of the fourteen basic courses offered by the law school and is also a key subject in the national judicial examination.

Name: Law of Obligations
Introduction: Obligation law is one of the components of civil law, which is the basic course of the law school. Obligation law includes contract law, tort law, unjust enrichment, management without cause, etc. and their common rules and theories. Among the fields of civil law, the rules and theories are the most complex, most practical, and most widely applicable.

Name: Civil Law Case Studies
Prerequisite: General principles of civil law, creditor law, property law
Introduction: Combined with key civil and commercial law knowledge, a typical case of civil and commercial law is provided every week for students to analyze and discuss. The content of the cases mainly involves the general principles of civil law, property law, contract law, tort liability law and other fields. If necessary, a small amount of commercial law cases including company law and bankruptcy law can be analyzed and discussed.

Name: Labor Law and Social Security Law
Prerequisite: Basic courses in jurisprudence, civil law, civil procedure, etc.
Introduction: "Labor Law and Social Security Law" is a highly practical legal course that comprehensively and systematically studies the legal adjustment of labor relations and the basic theory and main legal guarantees of social security under the socialist market economy. The main content of this course includes: (1) Basic theory of labor law: the adjustment object of labor law, historical evolution, basic principles, legal status and system, labor legal relations, etc.; (2) The main content of labor law: labor employment, labor contract, collective contract, labor wages, working hours and vacations, Occupational safety and health, employee rewards and punishments, trade unions, etc.; (3) Legal mechanism for labor dispute resolution; (4) Supervision and inspection of labor laws; (5) Basic theory of social security law and social insurance such as pension, unemployment, work-related injury, disease, maternity, and social assistance, social welfare, and social preferential care systems.

Name: Public International Law
Prerequisite: Compulsory courses (including constitutional, administrative, civil, criminal, procedural, etc.) for the first two academic years prescribed by the Faculty of Law
Introduction: Public international law mainly refers to the sum of legal norms among the subjects of international law, including legal norms in peacetime, as well as legal norms between belligerents and between belligerents and neutral states during armed conflicts (or wars). Its characteristics mainly manifest in the following aspects: First, the subjects of international law are mainly sovereign states. Intergovernmental international organizations can become subjects of international law under certain conditions and within a certain scope. Second, international law norms mainly come from international treaties, international customs and general legal principles. Third, the enforcement of international law mainly relies on the individual or collective actions of sovereign states. Under certain circumstances, intergovernmental international organizations may also take collective enforcement measures. Fourth, the overall development of international law is restricted by factors such as international politics and international economy. Therefore, before studying this course, you need to have a good foundation in domestic law, as well as basic knowledge and training in international politics and international economics.

Name: Forensic Psychiatry
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the basic theories and methods of psychology, psychiatry, forensic science and other related disciplines through classroom lectures, and conducts analysis and discussion based on the combination of case theory and practice in judicial practice. Through the study of this course, students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding of the basic knowledge of forensic psychiatry, and initially master the theories and methods of forensic psychiatry as well as the basic principles of forensic identification.

Name: Negotiable Instruments Law
Prerequisite: General principles of civil law, property law, creditor law, contract law
Introduction: The main content of this course involves general issues of bills and bill law: legal relationship of bills; bill behavior; bill rights; bill forgery, alteration and cancellation; bill defense; bill loss and remedy; main contents of bill of exchange, promissory note, check system, etc. _x000D_

Name: Criminal Enforcement Law
Introduction: "Criminal Enforcement Law" is a limited elective course for law school undergraduates, with 2 hours per week. The course mainly teaches an overview of criminal execution law, the historical development of criminal execution, criminal execution legislation, criminal execution agencies, execution of penalties (life penalty, freedom penalty, property penalty, qualification penalty), criminal management and correction, criminal labor, social protection of prisoners, etc. This course emphasizes the integration of theory with practice. Through classroom lectures, special discussions and visits, students can master the basic theories of criminal execution law, understand the basic practice of criminal execution legislation and execution, and improve the knowledge structure of criminal law.

Name: Economic Law
Introduction: Economic law is the newest legal sector that has developed most rapidly since the twentieth century. It is the legal sector that has emerged from a new stage of capitalism and industrial development. Initially based on institutional economics and macroeconomics, it has been influenced by social law, legal economics and many economic theories since the 1980s, and in practice has been reflected in public policies and changes in the relevant legal system, represented by privatization, marketization and privatization of public functions in the United States and the United States. The course focuses on the core theories of the various sectors governing economic law and will also analyse and explore legal issues and practices relevant to China. Specific elements include the sources of economic law, the theoretical framework, public-private relations, substantive justice and social theory, regulation theory, property theory, contract theory, organizational theory and public liability theory, which relate to relations between Governments and the market, State enterprises and State property systems, fair competition, relationship contracts, inter-firm relations, etc. The curriculum is guided by the basic framework of economic law, the history of economic law and its trends, the core issues facing it, and the framework system, through teaching and guidance of reading, discussion, etc., leading the students of the selected course. Requirements: To understand and understand the framework of existing economic law regimes, to read the relevant major research literature, including some in foreign languages, and to be able to use the knowledge gained for institutional and case analysis.

Name: Property Law
Introduction:
Property law is one of the components of civil law, which is the core course of the law school. It involves one of the most basic parts of civil law. It has complex theories and norms, strong practicability, and wide application. This course will cover an overview of property rights, changes in property rights, protection of property rights, ownership, usufruct rights, security rights, possession, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
    _x000D_

Name: Private International Law
Introduction: The course will focus on a number of important areas of private international law, such as the basic doctrine, the basic principles, the basic norms and the basic regime of the application of the law, as well as on conflict of laws and the application of law in the field of subjects involved in foreign affairs and commerce, foreign property rights, foreign intellectual property rights, foreign debt rights, foreign marriage families, and foreign inheritance rights, beginning with relevant theory and practice at home and abroad. Since the country is now a multi-jurisdictional country (the Mainland, Hong Kong and Macao), the subject of inter-district conflict of laws will also be addressed separately in this course. In order to ensure that the substantive interests of foreign commercial parties are adequately and effectively safeguarded, the course will also provide a detailed analysis of international civil proceedings and international commercial arbitration.

Name: Chinese Shuttlecock (Jianzi)
Introduction: Shuttlecock kicking was invented by the ancient Chinese. According to historical documents, it originated in the Han Dynasty and has a history of more than 2,000 years. It is the pride of the Chinese nation's sports culture. "Chinese shuttlecock" is a special representative of national sports. After long-term practice and exploration, it was discovered that this exercise has a fitness effect that cannot be compared with other sports. From the perspective of sports medicine, the technical movements of shuttlecock kicking require the full cooperation of all four limbs. It is a whole-body exercise. It is mainly completed by the lower limbs such as crossing, knocking, stretching, turning, and falling. Through movements such as leg lifting, jumping, bending, and turning, the feet, legs, waist, neck, eyes and other parts can be exercised. Long-term participation in shuttlecock kicking exercise can not only promote blood circulation and metabolism, enhance cardiopulmonary function, improve body flexibility, but also have a significant weight loss effect. Shuttlecock kicking requires accurate technical movements, so that the shuttlecock flies in the air without landing, and each action must be completed in an instant. It makes the person's brain highly concentrated and single-minded, thus eliminating distracting thoughts, making shuttlecock players feel physically and mentally comfortable and infinitely energetic.

Name: Development Economics
Introduction:
This course is offered to dual-major undergraduate students at the National Institute of Development, teaching the basic principles and analytical tools of development economics. The course focuses on the integration with Chinese reality. The prerequisite courses for this course are Intermediate Microeconomics and Intermediate Macroeconomics. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Intellectual Property Law
Introduction:
This course is a basic law course for undergraduates at Peking University Law School, aiming to enable students to:_x000D_
1. Master the basic structure and principles of China’s intellectual property legal system: mainly including the Patent Law, Trademark Law, and Copyright Law; _x000D_

Name: Criminology
Introduction: Criminology is a comprehensive science that uses theoretical and empirical research methods from multiple disciplines to study crime problems. For law students, criminology and criminal law are two disciplines that reflect and complement each other. Criminal law considers how to punish criminals in the face of existing crimes, which is a kind of "clinical medicine." In the face of possible victimization and danger, criminology considers how people can prevent future crimes, which is a kind of "preventive medicine." As a normative legal science, criminal law involves more the use of deductive logic, while as a factual science, criminology involves more the use of inductive logic. Criminal law norms focus on the limitations of judges' power and the protection of defendants' rights, which is a kind of value evaluation; while criminology focuses on the decision-making basis of criminal policy, which is a kind of description and explanation. From the perspective of research methods, criminal law focuses on qualitative analysis, while criminology emphasizes comprehensive analysis that combines qualitative and quantitative analysis. The category system of criminal law is self-contained and self-sufficient, and is a closed discipline, while criminology is a comprehensive science composed of theoretical methods from multiple disciplines and is an open discipline. Criminology is one of the basic subjects for law students to improve their knowledge structure.

This course will help students master the bankruptcy legal system from the corporate system level and the extended level of the civil law system. _x000D_

Name: International Economic Law
Prerequisite: Private international law, public international law, general public law, contract law, corporate law, intellectual property law, paper law, maritime law, insurance law, international commercial arbitration and international civil action
Introduction:
1. Concept_x000D_
  International economic law is the sum of legal norms that regulate international economic activities and international economic relations. That is, the sum of legal norms and legal systems that adjust the legal relationships formed in the transnational transaction circulation of goods, technology, capital, and services in international economic exchanges. International economic law is a marginal complex involving various legal norms including international law and domestic law, "public law" and "private law", international commercial law and foreign-related economic laws of various countries. The marginality and comprehensiveness of this emerging discipline are a faithful reflection of the objective reality that international economic and legal relations are extremely complex, and are also the practical need to scientifically adjust this complex relationship. It is a legal norm that regulates economic exchanges that transcend a country's national borders. The objects of adjustment are not limited to the economic relations between national governments, international organizations, and national governments and international organizations, but also include a large number of various economic relations between individuals belonging to different countries, between legal persons, between individuals and legal persons, and between them and foreign governments or international organizations. _x000D_
2. Scope of international economic law_x000D_
1. Legal norms and systems related to international trade_x000D_
It is a general term for the legal norms that regulate trade relations between countries and other trade-related relations. International trade law regulates international trade relations, which is an important part of international economic relations. It mainly includes four aspects of law: (1) Domestic laws that regulate international trade, such as contract law, maritime law, bill law, and insurance law; (2) National regulations on international trade management, such as customs law, tariff law, foreign exchange management law, and import and export licensing laws; (3) International legal norms and international trade practices related to international trade, such as bilateral or multilateral trade agreements; (4) Norms for handling trade disputes, such as arbitration laws and laws on international civil procedure. _x000D_
As far as international trade in goods is concerned, it includes legal norms and systems related to international goods sales contracts, international goods transportation, international goods transportation and insurance, international payment and settlement, and import and export legal controls. International trade in goods is a transnational trade that can occur between countries, international organizations, natural persons and legal persons. The legal norms involved include both international law and domestic law, public law and private law, such as bilateral and multilateral treaties related to international trade, domestic foreign trade laws, import and export control laws, foreign exchange management laws, contract laws, civil laws, legal provisions related to anti-dumping, customs laws, etc. _x000D_
The legal systems and legal norms related to international trade in services include legal norms and systems related to commercial services such as legal services and computer and related services, communication services, construction services, sales services, educational services, environmental services, financial services, health and social services, cultural and sports services, transportation services, etc. _x000D_
Legal norms and systems related to international intellectual property protection include those related to the international protection of industrial property rights, international protection of copyrights, and international license trade. The protection of intellectual property rights has been adopted at the international level through many international conventions, such as the Paris Convention for the Protection of Industrial Property, the Berne Convention for the Protection of Literary and Artistic Works, and the Universal Copyright Convention. At the intersection of trade and intellectual property rights, there are the Agreement on Trade-Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights, etc. _x000D_
 2． Legal norms and systems regarding international investment_x000D_
Including legal norms and systems related to capital export, capital import, investment protection, etc. International investment law is the general term for the legal norms that regulate international private direct investment relationships. Its legal norms involve foreign investment law, overseas investment insurance law, etc. in terms of domestic laws, and involve multilateral investment guarantee conventions, bilateral investment protection agreements, etc. in terms of conventions. _x000D_
3. Legal norms and systems related to international currency and finance_x000D_
Including legal norms and systems related to the control of international currencies, multinational banks, international loans, international securities, international financing guarantees, and multinational banks. To sum up, there are mainly three aspects:_x000D_
(1) Contents related to the international monetary legal system, that is, each country’s confirmation of whether its currency is freely convertible, its own exchange rate system, foreign exchange controls, etc. _x000D_
(2) Content related to international financial accommodation mainly refers to international loans, international securities investment, international financial leasing, etc. _x000D_
(3) Legal control of multinational banks, that is, the legal control of the establishment and operating activities of overseas branches of multinational banks by the host country and the home country of the multinational bank. _x000D_
4. Legal norms and systems regarding international taxation_x000D_
Including legal norms and systems related to international tax jurisdiction, international double taxation and international overlapping taxation, international tax evasion and tax avoidance, etc. With the emergence and development of international tax relations, international tax law has formed a new legal department and is a branch of international economic law. _x000D_
5. World Trade Organization Law_x000D_
The main content includes an in-depth understanding of the meaning, nature, purpose, and organizational structure of the WTO, the process of its creation, the main results of the Uruguay Round negotiations, an understanding of the organizational and institutional relationship between the WTO and GATT, familiarity with the WTO rules for trade in goods, the basic principles of GATT and its exceptions, and the main agreements to adjust non-tariff barriers. _x000D_
