Name: Internet Finance and Big Data
Introduction: "If banks don't change, we change banks." - Maroon. Do you want to go into this wonderful world when the giants of the Internet go into military finance, when the battle for mobile payments is on the rise, when the P2P loans grow wildly, when the battle for small loans is on the rise, when the price of bitcoin is a hundred times higher, when the Internet and the financial industry are colliding so hard that new Internet finance is emerging? What is Internet finance? What are the core and development trends in Internet finance? Will Internet finance change China’s financial business system? There is a perception that Internet finance is Internet-based finance, not just science, technology and data finance. From the perspective of a change in the structure of financial rights, Internet finance can broadly be divided into three levels: “trading technology”, “trading structure”, and “compact of power”. Transaction technology refers to technologies that reduce the cost of financial transactions and increase the efficiency, ease and security of transactions, i.e. new technologies that include the channels of transactions (e.g. online payments), as well as those that optimize services and control risks (e.g. remote mail assessments, data review). It covers a wide range of elements, such as mobile payments, supply chain finance, financial vertical searches, web-based community-based finance services, etc. At its core are new information technology, data technology and Internet technology applications in the financial sector, including data finance. Traditional trading structures are generally centralized, with borrowing funds going to banks and insurance going to insurance companies. As a result of historical and regulatory factors, the number of financial institutions is limited and often monopolistic, with information spreads and policy spreads taking advantage of excess profits, while the choice of users is extremely limited. Mr. Xie Ping predicted: “In the financial age of the Internet, intermediaries such as banks, issuers and exchanges are ineffective, loans, stocks, bonds, etc. are issued and traded directly online, and full-payment payments are made, and direct transactions between demand and supply of funds can achieve the same resource allocation efficiency as direct and indirect financing. Markets are fully effective and close to the non-financial intermediaries described in the general equilibrium theorem. Internet finance takes the form of both indirect financing by commercial banks and direct financing by capital markets.” According to the prevailing Western doctrine, modern government is the product of a public contract and a contract of power. The financial sector, as a central component of the functioning of the national economy, is of a mandatory nature. At the same time, high entry thresholds and complex policy barriers tend to result in oligopolistic patterns of functioning financial enterprises enjoying policy dividends and gaining unfair competitive positions. The large size of the financial oligopoly has a substantial impact on the economic performance of the country, resulting in corresponding financial power. This is not exclusively a result of fully competitive financial powers, which limit the free choice of the market and are mandatory in practice. An analysis of the current ills of the financial system, which stem mainly from the excessive concentration of financial power, runs counter to the flat and decentralized character of the Internet economy and to the spirit of the Internet of sharing, collaboration, inclusion, choice and democracy. The essence is that economies of scale in the industrial age are over-scrambled in the financial sphere, the evolution of which is the result of a race, but the free will and choice of the general public have never played a leading role in this process, making it difficult to call it a democratic, equitable and voluntary contract. This compact of coercive powers is now being challenged by new technologies, and the experiments have brought us to try and explore new financial contracts. The discussion of Internet finance is dependent on big data, which are becoming a huge economic asset and a new century of minerals and oil, which will bring new entrepreneurial directions, business models and investment opportunities. A shift in thinking can be cleverly used to stimulate new products and services. The large population and the market for applications are highly complex and dynamic, making China the largest data country in the world. Addressing such large-scale data-induced problems and exploring large-data-based solutions are important tools for industrial upgrading and efficiency improvement in China. Data mining would not only become a source of competitiveness for companies, but would also be part of national competitiveness. In the context of the problems facing modernization in the country and the challenges of education, transport, health care and so on, it is even more important to address the problem through the innovative approach of big data. The first part of the course will be devoted to the basic industrial structure of the Internet and related information economy analysis, followed by an in-depth discussion of Internet finance, as well as related large data economies and their applications.

Name: History of Chinese Sociology
Introduction:
Modern sociology in China originated in the late Qing Dynasty when Western learning spread eastward and the Reform Movement took place. This was also when China began to actively integrate into the modernization process in the political, economic, social and cultural fields. At first, Kang Youwei and Liang Qichao held the idea of ​​"organizing a group to form a meeting", and later Yan Fu's idea of ​​"group learning as the key link" all laid the foundation for the establishment of Chinese sociology. During the Republic of China, the development of Chinese sociology not only had a sound disciplinary configuration and diverse schools, but also expanded to various social science disciplines and even the field of humanities and history, becoming a leading theoretical and methodological force in the academic world. Scholars from various schools have put forward various overall concepts and strategies ranging from people's sentiments to institutions, from culture to politics. This is an important tradition that today's social scholars must inherit when conducting research. _x000D_
This course systematically explains the teaching method combined with text reading, and systematically sorts out the ideological context and academic tradition of Chinese sociological research since the late Qing Dynasty and the Republic of China, especially the basic problem pattern of sociology and social history established by Kang Youwei, Liang Qichao, Yan Fu, Wang Guowei, Liu Yizheng, Xia Zengyou, etc. in the late Qing Dynasty and the early Republic of China, as well as the rich development of Chinese sociological research in various regions, departments, and fields after the 1920s, especially the efforts of the Yanjing School to sinicize sociology.

Name: General Psychology

Introduction:
“Psychology is the science that studies human behavior and mental processes.” Like most other introductory psychology textbooks, the main teaching reference book "Psychology and Life" for this course also puts this line at the beginning of the first chapter. This is perhaps an accepted definition of psychology: people, behavior, mind, science. We can use various ways to understand the research carried out by psychologists on this road for more than a century and the various interesting but serious conclusions drawn. In this lesson, I will serve as your tour guide, trying to use my own understanding to lead you into this magical journey. The general tour itinerary is as follows: First, we will construct a brain, and then study how this brain feels and interprets information, how to react, how to gain consciousness, how to remember and forget, how to think, how to love and grieve, and understand how it develops over time and how it has its own characteristics... Until the end of this lesson, we will see how terrible and tragic mistakes the brain can make if it is sick. During this period, we will also learn how this brain forms a group with other brains, how they communicate with each other, and so on. In short, throughout our journey, we will always have such a wonderful brain accompanying us. In addition, please remember these relationships: genes and evolution, nature and nurture, individual and environment, individual and group. We will emphasize these relationships throughout the course, and they are—at least from my point of view—the most important thread in understanding psychology. _x000D_
The purpose of this course is not only to let everyone understand the knowledge of psychology, but more importantly, to learn how to use the acquired knowledge to study psychological issues. Throughout the learning process, I basically will not explain concepts in detail in class (introductory courses in any subject will emphasize a clear understanding of concepts, and general psychology is no exception. I hope that the textbook can work well with your smart brains to complete this job, which is very important - whether it is for the exam or for other courses in which you can better learn this subject in the future!). What I hope is to guide everyone to use the knowledge they have learned as much as possible, to deliberately observe every problem around them from a psychological perspective, and then ask questions. No matter how much information you get, no matter how many concepts you remember, only when you truly establish a psychological thinking framework and go beyond the limitations of the thinking patterns you are accustomed to to observe and think about all the problems you face about human beings can you truly begin to understand psychology and be able to better learn the following courses. _x000D_

Introduction: Publishing Enterprise Management is a relatively professional management course. It was formed to adapt to the complex and changeable environment of my country's publishing industry, the increasingly fierce market competition, and the increasing difficulty of operating publishing enterprises. As a branch of management science, it focuses on studying how publishing companies formulate and implement scientific management and strengthen their own operating capabilities to ensure their own survival and sustainable development.

Name: Chinese Culture and Society in Contemporary British and American Documentaries
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a special listening and speaking course for undergraduate students. The teaching content is 12 documentaries on Chinese culture, art, economic development and other themes shot by the United Kingdom and the United States since the 21st century. The specific content includes the current situation of marriage and love in contemporary China, the craze for young people to learn classical music, Chinese food culture, modern urban life, Chinese gardens, ancient Chinese art, Made in China, etc. The purpose of this course is to further improve students' listening and speaking skills through the understanding and appreciation of these documentaries: they can basically understand English documentaries at a normal speaking speed, and make in-depth oral expressions on some social, cultural, and artistic topics. Through the analysis and investigation of the Western perspective presented in the documentary, students' cross-cultural sensitivity can be improved to a certain extent, and at the same time, they can deepen their understanding of Chinese society and culture.

Name: Arts Training (III)
Introduction:
Courses are only available to high-level art troupes. _x000D_
Cultivating new talents with parallel development of theoretical and practical abilities, and exploring an interdisciplinary education model with two-way interaction between research and techniques are the foundation of this course. Chinese music, in the current era of globalization, has made a leap from quantity to quality in both its conceptual connotation and extension than before. Different from the situation before 1840, all musical life that takes place in China and is related to Chinese culture can be accepted and understood as the category of Chinese music. Through different forms of combinations and designs such as concert performances, voice arranging, band arrangement, chamber music training, original classic reading, comparison of Chinese and Western music history and culture, and in-person guidance and performances by global music masters, the course uses a hierarchical teaching method to eliminate the deficiencies and limitations of previous music training in combining theory and practice, and on the basis of fully developing students' musical interests. On the basis of this, combined with the cutting-edge experience of similar courses around the world, it emphasizes cross-disciplinary interaction, integration inside and outside the classroom, step-by-step, elementary, intermediate, advanced, 1-6 stages, under the premise of collective teaching and group training, with high-level concerts and relatively solid theoretical study and research, in order to achieve the goal of Peking University in China's leading position in relevant courses within the specified time. Those who pass will be divided into groups according to the voice part and level to participate in the Chinese Music Society Orchestra and Transmission Class to participate in class training. In addition to attendance, course evaluation includes concert performance and reading and learning of theoretical classics.

Name: Topics on Eminent Journalists
Prerequisite:
Students who are interested in international journalismStudents who are good at speaking, reading, and writing English in an academic environment and are interested in doing bilingual programsOpen to undergraduate and graduate students
*This course is designed for in-classroom students because the course may engage more discussion and Q-A with our guest speakers from media.
Introduction:
The course "Special Topic for Famous Journalists in English Media" is mainly designed, hosted, lectured and summarized by teacher He Shu. In one semester, we plan to invite a number of famous journalists from authoritative English media to teach English to students, leading students to become familiar with mainstream English media in the world and English media in China, and learn how to spread Chinese stories to English-speaking audiences. Students will gain valuable experience from famous journalists in English media, quickly improve their professional skills, and lay a solid foundation for serving English media or engaging in international communication in the future. _x000D_
During Teacher He's introduction and organized discussion of the guests and their business, combined with the guests' lectures, students will work in groups to complete a mid-term short video assignment of an English or Chinese-English bilingual report. The format is determined according to the topic. The works will be displayed in classes, WeChat official accounts and larger platforms. The end of the period is an independently completed English report. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Sociology of New Media
Introduction: This course mainly teaches students relevant sociological research findings since the proliferation of new media such as the Internet and mobile phones. That is to say, this course will focus on the role of new media such as the Internet and mobile phones in society, and systematically show students the social changes they have brought to their users. This involves "new media and globalization", "new media and culture", "new media and community", "new media and politics", "new media and crime and deviant behavior", "new media and health", "new media and family", "new media and ethnicity" "Group and Race", "New Media and Education", "New Media and Stratification", "New Media and Gender", "New Media and Religion", "New Media and Creative Industries", "New Media and Time and Space", "New Media and Mass Media and Communication" and so on.

Name: Film and Television Culture and Criticism
Introduction:
This course comprehensively and systematically teaches the theories and methods of film and television culture and criticism. It combines cases from Chinese and foreign film history and television history to show the context and practice of different critical theories. It helps students study film and television cultural phenomena from the perspective of film and television theory, master the basic methods of film and television criticism, and learn to write film and television criticism articles. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Primary Texts in Chinese Art Theory
Introduction: Based on the order of chronological development, this course selects some representative Chinese art classics, gives appropriate theoretical explanations based on text interpretation, and introduces the academic research results on the interpretation and analysis of the original texts. The purpose is to enable learners to grasp the basic issues and development of Chinese art and establish a preliminary theoretical framework for the study of Chinese art.

Name: Public Relations Planning and Crisis Management
Prerequisite: Dissemination of general remarks, public relations
Introduction: This is a professional optional course that mainly introduces the theories and strategies of public relations planning and crisis management. Specifically, the course mainly covers: the history and basic theories of public relations; general principles and strategies of public relations planning; basic concepts and principles of crisis management; public relations planning and management of different types of crises; the particularity and management model of crisis public relations planning and management in the new media environment, etc.

Name: Choir (Intermediate)
Prerequisite: The philosophy and practice of the chorus. Students in the art choir are required to take courses, and those who are not in the choir are required to pass.
Introduction:
Chorus (Middle) Course Outline_x000D_
1. Course Outline:_x000D_
    The "Chorus" course is divided into three levels: elementary, intermediate and advanced. The main contents include the following aspects: (1) Introducing the overview, main achievements and major events of the development of choral art in China and abroad in various periods; (2) Analyzing the main performance characteristics of choral works of different periods and genres in China and foreign countries; (3) Studying singing composers and their representatives who have made outstanding contributions in the field of choral art. (4) Understand the development of Chinese and foreign music theory and the evolution of music styles by practicing choral classic works; (5) Keep an eye on and learn new Chinese and foreign choral works today to improve a deeper understanding of choral art; (6) Hold regular performances of choral works to increase the role of the second art classroom. _x000D_
2. Course Commitment: _x000D_
    Choral art is one of the important branches of music art. Its emergence, development and transformation have an important impact on the development of music art. The significance of the "Chorus" course in comprehensive universities is: firstly, to enable students to have a deeper understanding of the emergence and development of musical art, and to have a clearer understanding of the formation and evolution of musical styles. Secondly, this course combines theory and practice. Students can enter into the practice and creation of music during the course, and practice and recreate Chinese and foreign choral works from simple to advanced. _x000D_
    Theory and practice of choral fundamentals. Students in the art troupe and choir must take courses, while students who are not in the choir must take exams to select courses.

Name: Introduction to Journalism and Communication
Introduction: This course introduces the basic subfields of news communication from the three aspects of people, information, and media, such as inward communication, interpersonal communication, small group communication, verbal and non-verbal communication, and basic concepts and theories in mass communication. It focuses on the media technology characteristics, organizational production characteristics, media standard management and effect research of news communication, and also provides a preliminary introduction to related research methods.

Name: Information Policy and Regulation
Introduction: The course mainly involves basic issues of information law and basic principles of information law, and introduces and teaches information rights and obligations and other related issues involved in the collection, organization, processing, dissemination, service and utilization of information from the perspectives of government, public welfare, commerce, citizens and network information subjects. The focus includes issues such as information disclosure, information confidentiality, information property rights and information security.

Name: Introduction to Information Literacy
Introduction: Information literacy includes library literacy, media literacy, computer literacy, Internet literacy, research literacy and critical thinking skills. Information literacy education has attracted the attention of people from all walks of life in various countries. Education departments and libraries in the United States, Britain, Australia and other countries have carried out information literacy education to varying degrees. At present, in addition to information retrieval courses in our country's college courses, the construction of information literacy courses is still very imperfect. Information literacy cultivation should become an important guideline for guiding curriculum construction. This course will focus on four basic points: information needs, information acquisition, information evaluation and information use. Among them, information demand refers to clarifying what type of information is needed and the quantity required; information acquisition refers to clarifying the way through which the required information can be found. The relevant skills and methods in the acquisition process require a full understanding of the type and content of the information carrier; information evaluation refers to the evaluation of the obtained information. Evaluation, not all relevant information is available, the quality of information varies, and you need to have the ability to identify and analyze information; information use refers to the reasonable use of high-quality information obtained, including understanding the relevant norms and standards of citation, establishing an awareness of academic integrity, and introducing relevant skills in information use. The course lecturer has been offering the "Spanish Reference Book" course for undergraduates and the "Information Retrieval and Utilization" course for college-to-undergraduate students since 2002. He has a full understanding of information retrieval and information literacy. This course plans to expand and deepen on the basis of the original course.

Name: Chinese Philosophy (Part 2)
Introduction: It aims to enable students to master the most important and basic knowledge of Chinese philosophy and understand the historical development and theoretical characteristics of Chinese philosophy. The characteristic of this course is to teach philosophy through the history of philosophy, specifically through the theoretical form shown in the historical development of Neo-Confucianism in the Song and Ming Dynasties (from Han Yu to Dai Zhen), sort out, analyze and study the content and form of Chinese philosophy, and then explore its theoretical paradigm and lasting value.

Name: New Materials Today
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Materials are the backbone of modern society. The materials used by humans vary with time, so materials are also called the scale of human civilization. New materials are an area of ​​high technology developed vigorously by various countries and receive great attention. This course will be taught in two phases. The first stage introduces some of the most basic issues in materials, such as: introducing the types and basic characteristics of materials, the research trends and development directions of new materials, the crystal structure and microstructure of materials, the synthesis methods of new materials, the structure and performance characterization methods of materials, etc. The second stage will focus on introducing important new structural materials and functional materials, such as special alloy steel, precision ceramics, amorphous materials, superconducting materials, magnetic materials, optical materials, semiconductor materials, energy materials, nanomaterials, biological materials, etc.

Name: Communication Theory
Introduction: In the age of modernity, globalization and digitization, mediating communication is at the centre of human life. Research in this area is important for our understanding of contemporary societies. The main objective of this course is to introduce students in journalism and communications to relevant theories on media technology, media production and use, and to help them understand how the media and society interact and shape each other. The contemporary social media environment consists of four important elements: media technology, media organization, media content (text) and media users. These four dimensions are interconnected and together form the complete cycle of mediating transmission. The course consists of four parts. The first component of media technology will introduce philosophy and social theory on technology and social relations. We will briefly trace the historical development of modern media and communication technologies and select key media for focused discussion, such as printing, television and the Internet. Understanding the importance of media technology from the perspective of civilization and social development would be an interesting intellectual experience. Part II, Texts, presents a range of tools for analysing texts, such as semantics, on-site scheduling analysis, narratives and type films. They can be used by students to interpret the large number of media texts encountered daily. Part III, “Media institutions”, focuses on institutions that specialize in the production of media texts. Here, students will understand the critical framework used to analyse the dominant position of the media industry, using them to analyse the social, cultural and political impact of the media. It also discusses contemporary topics in media organization and management in order to participate in public discussions on media social organizations. Finally, the “audience” section explores the pattern of diverse research audiences, ranging from traditional effects to the national aspirations of cultural research. Teachers will encourage students to use their own experience of media consumption to discuss and debate issues related to media culture and media consumption. The course will lead students to explore theoretical maps of media and cultural research. This will help them to be skilled in using theoretical terms and discussing theoretical issues. The aim is to encourage students to reflect critically on the various media phenomena and to participate actively in public discussions on understanding and building media and social relations.

Name: Photojournalism
Introduction:
Photojournalism is a compulsory course offered by journalism majors. During the learning process of journalism majors, students’ mastery of news photography knowledge is an indispensable part of their knowledge structure. News photography mainly uses momentary images to reveal news facts and disseminate news information. It is a form of news reporting that uses cameras to record news facts on the spot. The course is a highly practical course that cultivates students' practical abilities on the basis of firmly establishing the concepts of authenticity, imageness and timeliness of photojournalism. _x000D_
_x000D_
The photojournalism course is divided into a theoretical part and an experimental part. The principles and methods of photojournalism, as well as photography-related techniques and ethics are taught in the classroom, and students’ works are analyzed based on outdoor shooting. The purpose of this course is to cultivate students' professional qualities in photojournalism, photojournalism interviewing and news photo editing skills, so that students can master photography skills, independently shoot news photos with suitable composition and certain impact, and cultivate professional talents in photojournalism.

Name: Data Journalism
Introduction:
Welcome to take "Data Journalism" as an elective. We live in a digital world. Almost everything in this world can be described by numbers. All our stories, histories, and relationships can be presented in digital form. In the digital age, digital journalism refers to the knowledge and skills that intensify the use of digital information in the process of producing and publishing news. It reflects the increasing interaction between content production and other fields such as design, computer science and statistics. _x000D_
This course starts with an introduction to data journalism, including classic cases and well-known newsrooms. It then explains how to obtain data, how to identify data, and how to clean data. From the two perspectives of data description and data analysis, it will be practiced with students and learn to make charts, geographical information maps, and social network diagrams based on data. Finally, based on understanding and analyzing data, discover the function of interacting with readers, and learn to tell stories and write news based on data. _x000D_
This course helps students use data to produce in-depth content products through the analysis of case studies and hands-on practice in student groups. Arrange an interactive session with teachers and students from the Sun Yat-sen University Data Lab during your course. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Information Resource Management
Introduction: This course is a general platform course, aimed at middle and lower grade students from various departments, and introduces the basic concepts, work contents and methods of information resource management. It strives to enable students to establish intelligence information awareness, understand the attributes and characteristics of various information resources, master necessary information collection and analysis tools, and prepare to fully utilize the effectiveness of information resources in their respective fields of study, research and work in the future.

Name: Pronunciation and Listening-Speaking Vocabulary
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The course provides a comprehensive explanation of the pronunciation methods and techniques of the voice of American English-language speech, acoustics, accents, monotonouss, slides, etc., and helps university students improve their English speech appearances by learning from two perspectives about the pronunciation of the words recommended in the University English Curriculum (the words generally required in the English language glossary, a total of 4794 words, and some higher and more demanding words) and by learning to use international sound signs to learn the pronunciation of strange words, thereby laying a solid foundation for the learning of English in terms of the sustainability of university students ' ability to hear and speak.

Name: Introduction to Cultural Industries
Introduction: The cultural industry is a sunrise industry in the 21st century and a growth point for China's economic development. Developing the cultural industry requires cultivating comprehensive talents who are familiar with the basic connotation of the cultural industry, are proficient in the operating rules of various categories of the cultural industry, and understand both culture and management. Through introductory lectures and analysis of practical cases, students can understand the basic theories of the cultural industry and the basic content of the cultural industry, help students understand the cultural industry from a combination of theory and practice, and master the theoretical knowledge and practical work abilities necessary to engage in the cultural industry.

Name: A Brief History of World Art
Introduction: This course "A Brief History of World Art" is a core compulsory course for sophomore students in the School of Art. It is designed to help students gain an overview of the development history of world art before choosing to enter more professional studies. Since the topic covers a wide range of topics and the course time is quite limited, the instructor carefully arranged the teaching content. On the one hand, try to choose the most representative and far-reaching regions and time periods. On the other hand, with the intention of getting rid of the influence of Eurocentrism in the current discussion of general art history writing, the course attempts to cover the art of regions including Africa, America and Southeast Asia. While explaining important sculptures, architecture, paintings and arts and crafts to students, it also enables them to have an understanding of general aesthetic terms and general research methods in the art history discipline, and stimulates their further interest and thinking in art.

Name: Advertising Planning
Prerequisite: Advertising generals, social research methods, advanced mathematics, market surveys

Name: Creative Copywriting
Introduction:
"Creative Copywriting" is a professional basic course for undergraduate students in advertising. Teachers will arrange and design the courses based on the professional characteristics and class hours of the lecturers at the beginning of each school year. About 7-8 large lectures will teach theoretical content and assign exercises after class. The remaining class hours will be divided into group exercises and guided by the teacher. The course is taught in a multimedia format and guides students to conduct research-based thinking on specific issues such as the status and significance of creativity and copywriting in advertising, the relationship between the advertising industry and the creative industry, and creative thinking and expression based on the unique context faced by contemporary Chinese advertising creativity. _x000D_
Specific contents include: 1. Can “creativity” be taught and trained? (Students will be led to understand how “creativity” courses are taught in design schools at home and abroad, allowing students to think about this issue themselves) 2. The position of creativity and copywriting in contemporary advertising strategies (What is the development status of Chinese graphic design and Chinese advertising? The application and research of “creativity” have their own differences in graphic design and advertising) What's the difference? Introduce relevant theories and think about and discuss) 3. Selection and application of local creative resources (combine the creative practice of Chinese and foreign contemporary advertising, think about the creative expression of "Chinese elements", and use several local resources as examples to introduce practical attempts to localize the application of creativity)_x000D_

Name: Creative Writing
Introduction: Through a series of writing training and practice, this course helps students understand the functions and modes of writing, and express their thoughts and emotions through various imaginative and creative forms. Creative writing includes fictional writing and non-fiction writing, covering novels, poetry, essays, drama scripts, film and television scripts, documentary literature, oral history writing, literary criticism, art criticism, etc.

Name: Analysis of Dramatic Masterpieces
Introduction: This course selects masterpieces by famous Chinese and foreign drama masters. Through close reading of the texts, it explains the background and production methods of these texts, elucidates the subtleties of these works, and helps students understand the basic knowledge and reading methods of drama, so as to understand drama and enrich their humanistic qualities.

Name: Film and Television Theory and Criticism
Introduction: The Film and Television Theory and Criticism course strives to provide students with a comprehensive introduction to Chinese and foreign film and television criticism theories and criticism history, and to provide important experiences and lessons for China's current film and television criticism practice. This course is based on the professional research of the teaching faculty and requires students to have certain theoretical and practical qualifications.

Name: Art Collecting and Authentication
Prerequisite: This course is the first of its kind.
Introduction: This course "Art Collection and Appraisal" is a required course for art history majors. The purpose is to further strengthen students' understanding of the spread of specific artworks after their creation, based on their knowledge of art history. These artworks mainly include calligraphy and painting, ceramics, jade, bronze, etc. The course will combine individual cases with general rules, and will be developed from two aspects: collection and appraisal. As far as collection is concerned, the course mainly involves the ways, means and purposes of artworks being acquired and preserved by private individuals, research institutions or museums. As for appraisal, it mainly involves the analysis and judgment of the creator, age, material and finishing techniques of artworks.

Name: Images and Society
Prerequisite: Some knowledge and understanding of the underlying theory of social science, first studying sociological theory and understanding global social issues
Introduction:
Image is a mode of communication, and together with text and sound, it constitutes the ideographic system of our society. With the development of media technology, one of the important features of modern society is that images fill every corner of people's lives. On the one hand, they expand people's perception range and life experience, and on the other hand, they supplement or replace many traditional expression methods, such as text and conversation. Compared with other forms of expression, the temptation of images is obvious, because it brings us an intuitive, emotional, relaxed and spectacular experience of expression, and has become a favored medium for many social communications. The preference for visual symbols in advertising, news, publicity, entertainment and other activities has further pushed the entire society towards an image explosion. Images have transcended phenomena and become a unique social and cultural landscape. _x000D_
        _x000D_
This course is designed for students who love and care about image culture and the social role of images. The course focuses on introducing and discussing the important media that make up the visual culture of contemporary society—photography, film, television, and new media—as well as the social and cultural nature of these media. This course mainly covers three aspects: first, a brief introduction to the cultural and social history of the emergence, development and becoming of important communication media of the above-mentioned media, with an emphasis on the process and reasons for the formation of social usage patterns of these media; second, a discussion of the techniques and methods of visual representation, the process of people interpreting and experiencing visual symbols, and the social relationships caused by viewing; third, a discussion of the interaction between images and social consciousness, and an examination of how images maintain, question or change some important concepts in modern society, such as gender concepts, concepts about nature and science, national consciousness, class consciousness, etc. The three aspects are intertwined with each other to form a critical examination of the relationship between images and society. _x000D_

Name: News Reporting and Writing
Introduction: Course Chinese Introduction: In the discipline content structure of journalism, journalism practices (including gathering, writing, editing, and evaluation) directly related to the dissemination of news information have always been regarded as the most basic and important professional fields. In this field, news interviewing and writing not only cover the entire process of news information from collection to writing, but are also the material basis for news editing and news commentary to function. As a required course for journalism majors, this course aims to combine classroom lectures with various extracurricular trainings to enable students to systematically master the guiding ideology, basic principles, business skills, writing methods, etc. of news interviewing and writing, effectively improve the professional ability of news information interviewing and writing, and lay a solid professional foundation for the realization of high-quality news information dissemination.

Name: General History of Chinese Art (Part 2)
Introduction: "General History of Chinese Art" starts from the origin of Chinese art to the Ming and Qing Dynasties, according to the sequence of historical development, and uses a large number of exquisite pictures to provide a relatively complete and comprehensive teaching, including various art categories, art schools, representative figures, classic works and other important knowledge points. Attention is also paid to absorbing the research results of the Chinese art history community in the past thirty years, such as new perspectives, new materials, etc., so that students can have a basic understanding of the results and trends at the forefront of academic research. Strive to enable students to systematically grasp the development context of Chinese art history through study. This course also focuses on expanding students' aesthetic abilities, improving their artistic accomplishments, and enhancing their humanistic qualities.

Name: Art Law
Introduction:
This course introduces the theory and practice of legal principles, intellectual property rights, commercial contracts, value assessment, etc. related to art law, and analyzes it based on classic cases in the fields of performing arts, visual arts, and audio-visual arts. This course aims to cultivate the legal thinking and legal application abilities in the art field among students from the art department. Students are required to understand the basic legal issues of art law, understand the legal rules involved in the field of art activities through a general study of relevant departmental laws, and focus on learning the relevant content of intellectual property law, so that students can have a clear understanding and general application ability of patent rights, trademark rights, copyrights, etc. involved in the art and cultural industry. _x000D_
This course also requires students to understand international conventions and practices and foreign legal systems related to art law. _x000D_
This course is a new course, and teachers will continue to explore and improve the course plan during teaching.

Name: Art Masterpieces of the World's Great Museums
Introduction:
This course is open to all students in the school and provides a brief introduction to 11 world-famous museums. _x000D_
Museums are the memory organ of society and the gene bank of nature, humanity, and history. Leading college students to visit famous museums around the world is leading them to learn a condensed and vivid history of the development of human civilization. Famous museums around the world gather art classics in human history, leading college students to appreciate the fine collections of world-famous museums. It is an excellent way for college students to gain rich artistic experience and understand the history of world art. _x000D_
The objectives of this course are:_x000D_
1. Stimulate college students’ interest in visiting museums, enable them to systematically understand the collection scope, characteristics and representative collections of world-famous museums, and discover traces of historical civilization. _x000D_
2. Guide college students to love art classics, become familiar with art classics, learn art classics, and improve college students’ artistic literacy. _x000D_
3. Enrich the spiritual world of college students and enhance their aesthetic taste and pursuit. _x000D_

Name: Topics in the History of Women in Ancient China
Introduction:
Women are an important force in the creation of Chinese civilization. However, in ancient traditional history books with men as the main creative force and men as the writing objects, women were aphasic and submerged outside the historical perspective. In this regard, modern scholars have unearthed many details about the lives of ancient Chinese women through careful exploration and gaps in history. Today, these details have been compiled into historical works on ancient Chinese women in different aspects, including political, economic, literary, military, and medical... This course will use gender theory and difference theory, important theories in the study of women's history in the world today, to display and interpret different aspects of ancient Chinese women's lives from a novel perspective, striving to enable students to see vivid images of ancient Chinese women. _x000D_
This course will explore the life of women of different classes and periods in ancient China from multiple aspects such as politics, military, law, concepts, economy, body, text, and women’s historical materials, as well as the materials for studying Chinese women’s history and their interpretation methods. _x000D_
In addition to using written materials, this lesson will be supplemented by pictures, video materials, etc., so that students can have a more intuitive understanding of the history of women in ancient China. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Culture
Introduction: This course is an elective course for all undergraduate students in the college. Basic cultural knowledge of ancient China will be introduced according to categories such as writing and books, religion, philosophy, literature, history, regulations and systems, social customs, and cultural exchanges between China and foreign countries.

Name: Program Concept and Planning
Introduction: This course provides students with basic program creativity and planning abilities through theoretical review, case studies, practical exchanges and simulated actual combat. Different from traditional theoretical research on TV programs, this course focuses on enabling students to understand the industry ecology of program production and acquire basic knowledge and methods in program creativity and production. Compared with purely practical courses on radio and television program creativity and planning, this course sublimates and summarizes the knowledge from the industry, and elevates specific methods to the level of methodology through generalization and summary. This course can not only serve as an enlightenment for undergraduates who are exposed to program production for the first time, but also prevent students from being overly obsessed with specific technologies and getting a glimpse of what is going on. The assessment methods of this course include case analysis and planning plan. The former focuses on examining students' research and analytical abilities, while the latter focuses on examining students' practical ability, understanding ability and execution ability. For excellent case analysis papers, course teachers will contact core journals for publication; for excellent planning plans, course teachers will contact program production units to promote specific practices.

Name: General Urdu (I)
Introduction: Urdu is the national language and official language of Pakistan. It is one of the modern languages ​​widely used in the South Asian subcontinent. It is an essential language for understanding the history and culture of the region and carrying out all-round cooperation. This course uses "Basic Urdu Course" as the teaching material. It is an introductory language course for students with no basic knowledge. It requires students to master the reading and writing of letters, as well as the spelling rules of words, so that they can recognize, read and write, use reference books, master basic verb tenses, and be able to communicate simply.

Name: Radio and Television Program Hosting
Introduction: The program host is an important person responsible for the presentation of radio and television media programs and is directly related to the communication effect of the program. It is not only closely related to all aspects of program production, but also has very special and comprehensive requirements for individual professional qualities. This course is based on oral communication, focusing on sorting out the historical evolution and current situation of the development of electronic media program hosting, introducing the communication characteristics and communication art of program hosting, and conducting in-depth analysis using excellent Chinese and foreign programs as cases. It closely integrates theoretical teaching, case observation and hosting training, so that students in this major will have a comprehensive rational understanding and basic practical ability of the program hosting industry, thereby improving their ability to create, control and comment on various types of TV programs, broaden their theoretical horizons, and enhance their overall quality.

Name: Radio and Television Program Production
Prerequisite: Before taking this course, students should be familiar with the process of radio and television program production, master basic radio and television program production techniques and skills, and be proficient in using related shooting and post-production equipment and software.
Introduction: This course is open to students majoring in radio and television in the School of Journalism and Communication. Conduct in-depth appreciation and analysis of radio and television programs such as news, in-depth reports, news commentary and analysis, documentaries, promotional films, dramas (micro-movies), etc., and complete the production of different types of television programs through groups to further improve the level of radio and television program planning and production.

Name: News Editing
Introduction: This course is mainly divided into chapters such as the role of news editors, the positioning and product design of news media, the planning and organization of news reports, newspaper layout design, and the selection and processing of news manuscripts. It introduces the main content and internal logic of contemporary news editing work, and studies various new phenomena and issues related to it, hoping to enable students to understand On the basis of the relationship between changes in contemporary media forms and news editing work, students will understand the basic characteristics and development trends of contemporary news editing work, master the main content and work processes involved in news editing work, and through the study of theoretical knowledge and practical operation training, they will have the theoretical foundation and preliminary work skills to engage in news editing work.

Name: Comparative Studies of Chinese and Western Journalism
Prerequisite: College English Band IV or English level
Introduction: This course intends to examine the commonalities and differences between Chinese and foreign media themes and media through movies, blogs, online newspapers, television and other media. The course will select representative annual or major cases for comparative study, such as Chinese and foreign media’s coverage of China’s Two Sessions, coverage of the American film Oscars, sports Olympics, the U.S. presidential election, and major cultural festivals in various countries, etc. The course will combine theories such as cross-cultural communication and rhetorical studies to explore major issues such as politics, race, class, religion, and the environment. This course can better help Chinese and foreign students understand how different media report on people's daily lives and the political life of various countries. Through online media, students can not only grasp current affairs information in a timely manner, especially current affairs and hot news happening in China, but also be able to critically analyze media reports from various countries around the world.

Name: History of Chinese Social Thought
Introduction: This course introduces the basic content of traditional Chinese social thought, focusing on the reading and understanding of original texts. Through the study of this course, students should master the basic methods of reading ancient Chinese classics and some main concepts of traditional social thought.

Name: Low-Carbon Economy and Carbon Finance
Introduction:
This course is designed to:_x000D_
(1) Have a certain in-depth understanding of low-carbon economy, carbon finance, carbon trading, and comparison with traditional economics. _x000D_
(2) Learn about the low-carbon economic environment and understand its relationship with economic issues and economic decision-making. _x000D_
(3) Learn decision-making and writing communication methods in an economic context. _x000D_
(4) Form a team with classmates to complete the research report together and experience team spirit. _x000D_

Name: Psychological Development Training for University Students
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: The "Road to Success" credit course is a general elective credit course within the university, and the course cycle is one semester (half a year). The course content is compiled by international education experts based on the characteristics and social needs of Chinese college students, combined with multiple leadership and professional ability training courses. The content includes values ​​and attitudes, leadership principles, relationships and skills, as well as career planning and development. The materials include content from leadership training series such as Dr. John Maxwell and Dr. Tim Elmore from the United States, as well as professional training tutorials from the world-renowned corporate training company Achieve Global Inc. The course is taught by a team of experts, including education and training experts, executives from multinational companies and outstanding individuals, who introduce the latest corporate cases and practical skills.

Name: Introduction to Political Science
Introduction: This course is designed to help college freshmen gain a more comprehensive understanding of the current landscape of political science research, and hopes to provide interested students with a simple path map for further study. After introducing the basic concepts of politics and political science, this course will introduce several major areas of political science in sequence: international politics, comparative politics, and political philosophy. The subject introduction section will also introduce the research methods and theoretical perspectives of political science.

Name: Administrative Leadership
Introduction:
1. Understand the position of leadership science in the discipline of organizational behavior, as well as its related theoretical basis and academic development frontiers (macro, meso, micro)_x000D_
2. Understand the added value of leadership science and its knowledge system to management science (such as its close connection with sociology, contribution to management organization theory, etc.)_x000D_
3. Understand the position of a leader as an outstanding individual in the life of the organization and society as a whole, and understand the possibilities and limitations of "man can conquer nature" from the perspective of organizational theory_x000D_
4. Understand the philosophical dimension of leadership science. Epistemology determines how we understand the world, while ontology tells us what the world is like. What you see may not be real. This course will allow students to think deeply about the world you see, as well as the original and more real appearance of individuals, leaders, organizations, and societies in this era_x000D_
5. Understand the practical value of leadership science to administrative management, and look at the impact of different leadership types and practice methods on organizational output efficiency and effectiveness from the perspective of organizational behavior_x000D_
6. Understand the practical significance of leadership science to Peking University students, the future social leaders, to help each student achieve their potential and better serve the country and society.

Name: Public Organizational Behavior
Introduction: Public organizational behavior is an important course for students majoring in public administration and public policy internationally. This course will be based on the international frontier and systematically teach important contents such as how public organizations and non-profit organizations motivate employees, leadership development and training, decision-making, organizational structure design, organizational development and change, etc. The course adopts case teaching method and focuses on combining theory with public sector practice.

Name: Public Economics
Introduction:
Public economics research has a profound tradition, which originated from the political economic analysis of Adam Smith, John Mill and David Ricardo_x000D_
, after experiencing the public finance tradition focusing on tax analysis, gradually developed into public economics, and returned to_x000D_ with the development of new political economics
its roots. As an important branch of economics, it provides the basis for practical policy analysis. Although the research field and analysis of public economics_x000D_
Methods vary greatly over time, and providing a theoretical basis for practical decision-making is always their basic purpose. The content of this course is an attempt to apply this theory_x000D_
, providing a clear and logically consistent analytical framework for economic policy research. _x000D_
By its most general definition, public economics is the study of economic efficiency, distribution, and government economic policy. The subjects covered by this subject are quite scattered_x000D_
, such as dealing with market failures caused by the existence of externalities, analysis of motivations for tax evasion, and explanations of bureaucratic decision-making. Because all these aspects are involved_x000D_
, public economics has evolved from its original focus on government tax collection and expenditure to now focusing on every aspect of the interaction between the government and the economy. So this course_x000D_
Trying to understand both how and what decisions governments should make. _x000D_
To understand how governments make decisions, it is necessary to study the motivations of decision-makers in government, how decision-makers are selected, and how decision-makers are influenced by outside groups_x000D_
body influence. To determine what policies should be enacted, the effects of other feasible policies need to be studied and their consequences estimated. Introduction to these two aspects will be_x000D_
It will be carried out specifically in the teaching of this course, and we hope that students can gain a clear and concise grasp and understanding.

Name: Principles of Political Science (Part 1)
Introduction: This course includes eighteen aspects including politics and political science, interests and politics, political power, political rights, political rule, political management, state, political parties, political associations, political psychology, political thought, political socialization, political revolution, political reform, and political democracy. It elaborates theories and views on the nature of human social politics and basic aspects of political life. This course is the main theoretical basic course for political science and administrative management majors. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic theories and analytical methods of political science, understand the nature and basic laws of politics, form the basic ability of political analysis, and make theoretical preparations for the study of other courses in political science and administrative management.

Name: Principles of Public Administration
Introduction: This course is not only a general professional basic course for the School of Government, but also an elective course for schools and departments such as the School of Law and the Department of Sociology. This course comprehensively and systematically teaches the knowledge of the government (national administrative agencies) in managing national affairs, social affairs and its own affairs. Through the study and research of the nature and phenomenon, subject and object, concept and technology, content and form, system and process, history and future of these activities, students will be able to understand the regularity of public administration, as well as the administrative theories and methods that promote the scientificization, legalization, standardization, rationalization, efficiency and modernization of these activities. On the basis of a comprehensive and systematic mastery of administrative management knowledge, this course combines theory with practice to enhance students' ability to understand and grasp current administrative management practice issues, especially the ability to understand and analyze contemporary Chinese public administration issues. It enables students to gradually develop the ability to observe, think, analyze and solve problems in the administrative management field. It also creates good conditions and lays a solid professional theoretical foundation for studying other public administration courses.

Name: Frontiers in Political Science
Prerequisite: For undergraduate students in grades 3 to 4, they should normally complete one of the following basic courses in philosophy and social sciences: Political science generals, legal generals, sociological generals, economics generals or philosophical generals.
Introduction: This course will introduce the latest developments in political science, and teach cutting-edge issues, academic trends, representative schools and important scholars in political science research at home and abroad. It focuses on basic political issues such as politics, state, government, rule, governance, citizenship, power, authority, rights, and legality, as well as the latest research results on basic human political values ​​such as freedom, democracy, equality, justice, rule of law, dignity, and peace. In addition, this course will also briefly introduce important controversial issues in domestic and foreign political science, such as debates on national sovereignty, universal values, common values, the Chinese model, civil society, civil rights, and political legitimacy, as well as popular trends in domestic and foreign political science, such as neoliberalism, neoconservatism, neo-Marxism, new authoritarianism, social democracy, communitarianism, nationalism, and populism.

Name: Modern and Contemporary Chinese Society and Culture in English Non-Fiction
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is an English cross-cultural special course for undergraduate students. Communication between China and the West is inseparable from both parties' understanding of each other. Understanding oneself in the eyes of the other party is an important way to understand the other party, and because it is related to oneself, it can further help adjust communication strategies and promote better communication effects. Under this concept, this course improves students' English reading and writing skills, logical analysis skills, and cross-cultural literacy by interpreting non-fiction works by English authors on China since modern times, such as memoirs, realistic works, news reports, etc.

Name: Human Resource Development and Management
Introduction: The course teaches the basic concepts, important theories and related technical methods of human resource development and management that help organizations achieve success through both theoretical and practical aspects. The course content includes basic theories of human resource development and management, job analysis and job design, human resource planning and recruitment, personnel selection, training management, performance management, salary management, labor relations, etc. This course is highly applicable. The lectures are centered around cases, paying attention to practical development trends, and inviting practical experts to share management experience.

Name: Applied Statistics
Introduction:
The course starts with application examples and subject overview of statistics, guides students to understand the basic concepts of statistics, introduces the logic and methods of statistical inference, and then gradually explains commonly used statistical analysis techniques in depth. On this basis, students will deepen their understanding of basic theories and methods through practical operations and case analysis, laying the foundation for further mastering statistical knowledge and technology and developing empirical research thinking. _x000D_
The course is divided into two parts. The first part is basic theory, including the subject overview of statistics, basic concepts of statistical inference, and the logic and methods of statistical inference; the second part is applied practice, including descriptive statistics, contingency table analysis, variance analysis and correlation analysis, general linear regression analysis and robust regression analysis, logistic regression analysis, factor analysis, data quality assessment, design of quantitative research, writing of quantitative research reports, etc. _x000D_
The course is mainly lecture-based, supplemented by three after-class assignments. The assignment content involves application training of all basic statistical analysis methods taught, and SPSS software and STATA software will be used. _x000D_
The credit hours are allocated as follows:_x000D_
Lecture 1 Overview of Applied Statistics (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 2: Steps and methods of data analysis (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 3 Data Collation (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 4 Methods of Descriptive Statistics (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 5 Logic and Methods of Inferential Statistics (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 6 Correlation Analysis, Contingency Table Analysis (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 7 Variance Analysis (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 8 General Linear Regression Analysis (6 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 9 Logistic Regression Analysis (6 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 10 Introduction to other statistical analysis methods (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 11 Factor Analysis (3 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 12 Data Quality Assessment (6 hours)_x000D_
Lecture 13 Quantitative Analysis Paper Writing (2 hours)_x000D_
Total review (1 credit hour)

Name: Real Estate Economics and Management
Introduction:
Real Estate Economics and Management is an elective course for students majoring in urban management in the School of Government. _x000D_
The purpose of this course is to enable students to initially master relevant theories in the field of real estate economics and management, master the operating rules of the real estate market, and master core issues in the field of real estate economics and management such as land rent, cycles, and bubbles. Understand the relationship between real estate market economic behavior and real estate macro-management, and promote students to establish a multi-dimensional thinking system on real estate economic and management issues. _x000D_
The course adopts a teaching method that combines teacher lectures, classroom discussions, and students' self-study, and strives to form a symmetrical and balanced teaching model with two-way interaction between teachers and students. The teaching content includes the introduction of theories related to real estate economics and knowledge related to real estate macro-management, focusing on the internal connections and external influences of relevant knowledge. _x000D_
The course requires students to conduct independent and group research. Students should carefully study relevant literature and form a reading report on a certain issue. _x000D_
In view of the practical problems of real estate economics and management, students should collaborate with teachers, focus on integrating theory with practice, and highlight the timeliness and pertinence of the course. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Political Science (Part 2)
Prerequisite: The first course is " Political Science Principles " (upped), and the first course is 03232570.
Introduction: This course includes eighteen aspects including politics and political science, interests and politics, political power, political rights, political rule, political management, state, political parties, political associations, political psychology, political thought, political socialization, political revolution, political reform, and political democracy. It elaborates theories and views on the nature of human social politics and basic aspects of political life. This course is the main theoretical basic course for political science and administrative management majors. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic theories and analytical methods of political science, understand the nature and basic laws of politics, form the basic ability of political analysis, and make theoretical preparations for the study of other courses in political science and administrative management.

Name: Constitutional and Administrative Law
Introduction: This course is based in China and is world oriented. The first to introduce and compare the constitutional and administrative law traditions of Christian Western civilization, Islamic civilization and Chinese civilization, to summarize the basic human consensus and the special problems of China, and to demonstrate the problems and prospects of China. The curriculum will consist of five components: concepts and methods, historical traditions, rationales, basic systems and institutional changes. It focuses on the rule of law, the relationship between the world ' s geopolitical economy and constitutional law, constitutionalism and revolution, fundamental human rights, separation of powers and checks and balances, rule of law government and judicial review. The course focuses on raising China's issues in comparative studies and will combine the knowledge resources of humanities and social sciences in an attempt to showcase a range of new areas of constitutional and administrative law in empirical and normative research.

Name: Organization and Management
Prerequisite: Management science generals, administrative sciences, management thinking history
Introduction:
This course is one of the required courses for students majoring in administration, political science and other majors. It aims to study the general management laws in organizations, explore the basic theoretical knowledge of the emergence, development, operation and change of organizations, and understand the main analytical tools of organizational management. _x000D_
    The main contents include: the concept and foundation of organization, the development of organizational theory, organizational goals and functions, organizational structure and system, organizational psychology and organizational behavior, organizational relationships, organizational processes, organizational change and development, organizational culture, etc. _x000D_
    The course strives to highlight practicality and combine case analysis.

Name: Management Operations Research
Prerequisite: University economic management, higher mathematics, computer application base
Introduction: Management operations research uses advanced mathematics, linear algebra, statistics, matrix theory, stochastic processes, discrete mathematics and other mathematical knowledge to study the reasonable arrangement of human, material, financial and other resources in the national public management system through analysis, modeling, calculation and computer simulation, and provides decision-makers with well-founded optimization plans to make the country's public management, government policies and social governance more accurate, scientific and rational. The main contents include: mathematical programming (also including linear programming; nonlinear programming; dual programming; integer programming; dynamic programming, etc.), graph theory, network flow, decision analysis, queuing theory, inventory theory, game theory, prediction theory, decision simulation, multi-objective evaluation, etc.

Name: Public Policy Analysis
Introduction: The importance of public policy research for the modernization of national governance systems and capacities is self-evident. In the face of the multitude of social problems and conflicts associated with industrialization and the post-industrialization transition, the urgent need for policy in the country's governance poses a very realistic demand for the development of public policy disciplines. The complex mechanisms behind the review of public policy gains and losses and interpretations have become the historical responsibility of policy scientists, thus helping Governments to promote the interests of society as a whole through the formulation and implementation of high-quality public policies. This course is an introductory course in the direction of public policy, focusing on the broad interpretation of the basic concepts of public policy, the scope of research, the methods of research, etc., and is controlled in depth, with more in-depth content to be discussed in subsequent courses. The main theoretical and analytical methods of public policy research will be taught in the context of realistic cases. In terms of content, the course will build on the traditional policy process framework and policy networking model, expand the discussion to include disciplines such as science philosophy, politics, economics, sociology and communication, as well as new research methods such as big data analysis, policy simulation, etc., and train students to examine and research public policy issues with a broader analytical perspective.

Name: Government and the Rule of Law
Introduction: Cultivate the legal thinking of undergraduates from various majors in the School of Government and clarify the relationship between government and the rule of law. (1) Enable students to master the basic concepts, basic characteristics, basic rules, basic classifications, basic systems and basic methods of law, and master the basic concepts and basic characteristics of the rule of law. (2) Enable students to fully understand the origin and development of law, understand the value and principles of law, understand the significance of freedom and fairness in the rule of law, and the status and role of procedural justice in the rule of law. To enable students to fully understand the formation of government and the relationship between government and the rule of law. Enable students to fully understand the important position and role of the government in the rule of law, and at the same time enable students to deeply understand the mechanism of government administration in accordance with the law and its operation and development within the framework of the rule of law. Name: American Government and Politics
Introduction: As the only superpower and the most developed economy in the world today, the United States has made remarkable achievements in less than 300 years. As the background and foundation of all social development, politics is an important aspect of the development and strength of the United States. It has also become an object of imitation, learning and catching up for many post-developing countries (including China). On the other hand, the special characteristics of the United States make it difficult for any mechanical and rigid copying efforts to succeed. Through this course, students should be able to have a basic understanding of the development process of American politics, the basic system and the major issues facing today. Through passionate explanations by teachers, students are led into the palace of Chinese and foreign classic books, savor the ideological connotations of classics, appreciate the cultural connotations of classics, and construct a thought-oriented reading path to stimulate reading interest, enrich the spiritual world, and cultivate humanistic sentiments.
