Introduction: This course is a section of the history of ancient Chinese literature, a main course in the Chinese Department. The course lasts for two academic years. This section is a section of the history of literature in the pre-Qin and Han Dynasties, which lasts for one semester. The content includes two parts: the history of pre-Qin literature and the history of literature of the Han Dynasty. The pre-Qin period was the period when Chinese literature and ideological scholarship originated and matured. Hundreds of flowers blossomed and hundreds of schools of thought contended. Poems include the Book of Songs and Songs of Chu, which stand side by side. They are models of realistic and romantic poetry in my country respectively. Articles include Zuozhuan, National Policy, and the writings of hundreds of schools of thought, which have been regarded for generations. Classical classics such as the Book of Changes and the Book of Changes are not only great texts through the ages, but also Confucian classics, which have modeled society and human ethics for thousands of years. The key points of this lecture are: 1. The achievements and influence of "Three Hundred Poems". 2. The achievements and influence of Chu Ci. 3. The achievements and influence of historical biographies. 4. The achievements and influence of Zhuziwen. During the Han Dynasty, Yuefu poetry and ancient poetry inherited the legacy of poetry and poetry, and reached new peaks and opened up new paradigms. Fu's works rose to prominence and were hailed as "the literature of a generation". The history of Mabaan has its own unique characteristics, and they are both ancient and modern. The rest, like the scholars, have no lack of elegance and are also pure Chinese learning. The key points of this section are: Nineteen Yuefu folk songs and ancient poems; Fu; "Historical Records", etc.

Name: Close Reading of Tang and Song Poetry Masterworks (I)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The Tang and Song Dynasties were the golden period of ancient Chinese poetry creation. A large number of poems are not only exquisite works of language art, but also the crystallization of the personality strength, aesthetic spirit, imagination and creativity of the Tang and Song poets. This course selects representative works of important poets and lyricists from the poetry range of the Tang and Song dynasties, classics that have been recognized throughout the ages, and general masterpieces with certain characteristics. It explains the words and allusions, analyzes the images and artistic conceptions, and conducts detailed interpretation and artistic appreciation of the works by using methods of understanding people, discussing the world, and restoring scenes. Interpret the outlook on life, nature, history, society, relatives and friends, love, etc. reflected in the work; discuss the spiritual personality power and moral sentiments of the work; analyze language arts and writing characteristics; focus on exploring the expression and significance of the work's creativity and imagination. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students will understand the general path of interpreting ancient poetry works, master the general professional interpretation methods, and understand how ancient poets and poets faced life, society, nature, relatives and friends, and art; they will further understand the characteristics of creativity and imagination embodied in poetry works of the Tang and Song Dynasties, and understand the importance that ancient people attached to creativity and imagination. _x000D_
The course is roughly divided into two sections: Tang and Song Poetry and Tang and Song Ci. Each section is taught for one semester, and one of the sections is taught according to the situation in each semester. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Han Dynasty Literati and Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
In ancient Chinese society, following the Qin Dynasty, the Han Dynasty underwent major changes in social and political systems and ideological and cultural aspects and gradually consolidated them. The literary achievements of this period may not be as dazzling as those of the Tang and Song Dynasties, but in terms of the development and manifestation of the "literati", a special character type in ancient China, the shaping of the form and concept of literary writing, the enrichment and maturity of literary expression means and styles, the Han Dynasty can be said to be a very important stage, and played a key role in the establishment of the Chinese literary tradition. _x000D_
This course is roughly divided into two parts. First of all, teachers teach the evolution and characteristics of Han Dynasty literati, the expressions and concepts of Han Dynasty poetry, etc., and combine the changes in social and political structures and ideological ideologies to examine the relationship between literati and social politics through literature. Combined with the changes in the daily life of scholars, they observe the establishment of literati's unique aesthetic taste and its expression in literature. At the same time, through the specific analysis of several cases, it presents the literati's attitude and conceptual value towards literature, as well as the contradictions therein. On this basis, it comprehensively describes the features and changes that occurred in different aspects of literary writing by Han Dynasty literati, and reveals the unique nature and scope of ancient Chinese "literature". _x000D_
Afterwards, students will conduct research on special topics in literature, or on specific writers and their works. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports and participate in discussions of other students' course reports. _x000D_

It shows students the charm of English poetry and its Chinese translations from both theoretical and practical perspectives, stimulates students' enthusiasm for learning English, cultivates students' ability to appreciate English poetry, and masters certain translation skills.

Name: Lu Xun Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Lu Xun's thoughts and literature embody China's "modern" principles - a kind of third world modernity. This course focuses on the interactive relationship between Lu Xun's thoughts and literature, exploring the formation of his thoughts, the occurrence and development of literature, and the spiritual history process of transition. With the question of how "modernity" can be "appropriated" and "surmounted", we will look at the possibility of reinterpreting Lu Xun's thoughts and literature, and explore its significance for our world today.

Introduction: This semester's "Introduction to Religious Studies" will be divided into three parts, examining the three forms of treatment of religion in Chinese and Western civilizations. The first part focuses on ancient Western religions, that is, political religions in city-states; the second part focuses on Christianity and modern Western religions, that is, spiritual religions in society; the third part focuses on traditional Chinese religions, that is, ethical religions; the core idea running through the three parts is Shinto teachings. 4. Enable students to master the theoretical knowledge and basic skills of orienteering and hiking, and understand and master the methods and means of self-rescue in the wild. Improve survivability. Name: Chinese Archaeology (Part 1-2)
Prerequisite:
Introduction to Archaeology
China Archaeology (Previous Stone Age Archaeology)
Introduction:
The lower limit of China's Neolithic Age reaches the emergence of the first dynasty, Xia, and the upper limit exceeds 10,000 years ago. Some archaeological data show that it can even reach about 16,000 years ago. _x000D_
Human culture in the Neolithic Age did not have the restrictions of today's administrative divisions. Therefore, although the focus of this course is China, it will also cover several surrounding areas, such as Eastern Siberia, the Far East, the Korean Peninsula, Japan, and Southeast Asia. _x000D_
The Neolithic Age, which lasted for more than 10,000 years, can be further divided into four major stages according to current understanding, namely the early Neolithic Age, the middle Neolithic Age, the late Neolithic Age and the end of the Neolithic Age. The last stage is also called the Longshan Age. _x000D_
In the early Neolithic Age, humans successively made several epoch-making inventions, namely agriculture, pottery making and grinding stone tool technology. From then on, they transitioned from a hunting and gathering economy that relied passively on natural resources to a production economy, which was the starting point of all civilizations. _x000D_
In the middle of the Neolithic Age from 9000 to 7000 AD, agricultural technology had initially developed in the middle and lower reaches of the Yellow River and Yangtze River, forming the southern rice agricultural economic and cultural zone and the northern dry farming economic and cultural zone, where people generally adopted a stable and settled lifestyle. _x000D_
After that, in the late Neolithic about 2,000 years ago, various production technologies, including agriculture, further developed. The population increased, the size of communities expanded, and settlements differentiated. By around 5,000 years ago at the latest, societies in some developed areas had shown an obvious trend of complexity. This complication trend is manifested at the settlement level. Large central settlements have generally appeared in various places, occupying more resources and people. The surrounding small ordinary settlements have formed a dependent relationship with them, forming a settlement group together, thus forming the prototype of a local political system. Within settlements, especially within large central settlements, there are obvious differences in wealth and status among social members, as well as professional differentiation between craftsmen and farmers, thus leading to demands for some kind of social management mechanism. _x000D_
From the Longshan period, which spanned more than a thousand years from 5,000 years ago, marked by the first metal production, social productivity continued to advance. Conflicts between settlement groups became increasingly fierce, and violence and war began to become common phenomena in social life. Some local societies evolved and developed early state forms while continuing the process of complexity that had begun previously, laying the foundation for the subsequent dynastic era. _x000D_
China is located in the eastern part of the Eurasian continent. It is blocked by the alpine zone in the north, the Gobi Desert in the west, the Tibetan Plateau in the southwest, and the tropical rainforests in Southeast Asia. Cultural exchanges with the outside world are greatly restricted. As a result, the human culture here has developed many characteristics in the process of development and evolution, which are different from the culture on the west side of the Eurasian continent and the South Asian subcontinent. On the other hand, China has a vast internal territory, with different natural conditions, climate environment, and natural resources. Its culture and the society behind it also have their own characteristics, forming a pattern of diversified development. However, these local cultures are adjacent to each other without serious geographical barriers, and exchanges are frequent. Over time, the cultural landscape gradually converges. In the middle and lower reaches of the Yellow River and Yangtze River, as well as in western Liaoning, where the agricultural economy is the most developed, there is a region with the highest degree of cultural development as seen from archaeological material data. This region is the source of power that has driven the historical process of East Asia for thousands of years. At the latest around 5,000 years ago, the result of this long-term exchange and convergent evolution further showed the so-called "evolutionary trend centered on the Central Plains" in this cultural group with the highest degree of development. This phenomenon of multicultural convergence and development is highly summarized as “diversity and unity”.

Name: Chinese Archaeology (Part 1-1)

The content and work flow of the collation of excavation data; the classification of archaeological data and the basic principles of archaeological typology; the chronology of archaeological data; the extraction and correlation of historical information contained in archaeological data; and the construction of a data information database. _x000D_

The main content and preparation of archaeological reports; other forms of data publication.

Name: Zooarchaeology
Prerequisite: Introduction to Archaeology or Chinese Archaeology
Introduction: Most of the animal remains found in archaeological sites are the result of human behavior. Studying the cultural characteristics of these animal remains and the technology of how humans used these resources, and examining changes in human society are the main areas of zooarchaeology research. Therefore, zooarchaeology studies archaeological issues such as human behavior, production activities and social economy at that time, as well as the ancient environment of human life at that time, and is an important branch of archeology. The course focuses on the collection techniques of animal remains unearthed from archaeological sites, identification methods of animal bones, data collection and analysis, and systematically introduces the research results of zooarchaeology in my country and the prospects of this subject. Students are required to master the basic skills of identifying animal bones, make correct identifications of animal remains unearthed from archaeological sites, conduct sorting and preliminary research, and lay a solid foundation for further learning.

Name: Topics in Field Archaeology Techniques
Introduction: This course includes four parts: "Archaeological Surveying", "Archaeological Drawing", "Archaeological Photography" and "Computerized Archaeological Mapping". "Archaeological Surveying" mainly teaches the basic principles and methods of field archaeological surveying and mapping, the basic methods of total station and RTK surveying, and the basic steps and methods of archaeological site surveying and mapping. "Archaeological Drawing" mainly teaches the basic principles of field archaeological drawing, the basic methods of manual drawing and its operational practice, including two major parts: relic drawing and relic drawing. "Archaeological Photography" mainly teaches photography principles, camera construction, and field archaeological drawing practices, including photography of ruins, ruins, and relics. "Computer Archaeological Mapping" mainly teaches the principles of computer graphics and imaging, the mapping of ruins and relics based on vector graphics, and the archaeological mapping technology based on raster images. _x000D_

Name: Museum Exhibition Design
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the theory and methods of museum display design. The course is divided into two parts. The first is the basic exercises of display design. The content includes the spatial concept of display design, hand-drawing techniques and computer graphics. The second part is the application of display design. It will be combined with physical exhibitions to learn and practice various components involved in the display design process such as architecture, display space analysis and creation, comprehensive graphic design, application of 3D design software, and construction organization.

The archaeological cultures that are focused on include: Xinzhai Period remains, Erlitou Culture, Xiaqiyuan Culture, Yueshi Culture, Erligang Culture, Yinxu Culture, Early Zhou Culture, Western Zhou Culture, and the cultures of various feudal states in the Zhou Dynasty. The bronze culture of the surrounding areas during the Xia, Shang and Zhou Dynasties will be briefly taught. _x000D_

Focus on teaching the research process of major academic issues in the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, such as the exploration of Xia culture, the exploration of pre-Shang culture, the exploration of pre-Zhou culture, etc. In the process of teaching the brief history of these studies, emphasis will be placed on various academic perspectives and their evolution, as well as the changes in archaeological theoretical methods involved. Name: Chinese Archaeology (Part 2-2)
Introduction: The Qin and Han Dynasties lasted from the second half of the third century BC to the end of the second century AD, and passed through several dynasties: the Qin Dynasty, the Western Han Dynasty, the Xinmang Dynasty, and the Eastern Han Dynasty. During the Qin and Han Dynasties, China formed a unified, multi-ethnic, and vast country, and its institutional civilization, material civilization, and spiritual civilization all reached a new height. This course systematically introduces archaeological discoveries and the latest research results of the Qin and Han Dynasties, and discusses important academic issues based on documentary records. The teaching of this course is supplemented by field visits, physical inspections and a large number of slides, etc., in an effort to make the teaching visual and vivid.

Introduction: This course introduces the significance of museum collections and teaches the processes and methods of collection, appraisal, registration, classification, preservation, borrowing, cancellation, and statistics. It also discusses issues such as digital museums, museum digitization, functional zoning of museum buildings, warehouse management, collection management regulations, illegal trade of cultural relics, prevention of illegal trafficking of cultural relics, and recourse to cultural relics. The purpose is to enable students to pay attention to museum collection management not only from the practical work level, but also from the theoretical and institutional levels. _x000D_

Name: Plants and the Environment
Introduction: After a long evolutionary history, the earth, our home, has a rich and diverse variety of plants. They perceive the world in their own way, adapt to and even change the world. The sunlight captured by plants through photosynthesis provides energy for the earth's ecosystem and a source of food and clothing for our lives. However, changes in the earth's environment caused by human activities over the last century have triggered a global ecological crisis, which requires us to pay more attention to the harmonious development of plants and the environment. "Plants and Environment" will present you with a world of plants that can be seen, heard, touched, and full of vitality. It will introduce the close relationship between plants and the living environment in simple and easy-to-understand terms, connect the research results of ancient and modern natural history, plant physiology, and modern molecular biology, unlock the unique life code of plants, feel the history of the development of plant scientific research, and grasp the frontiers and future development directions of modern science and technology.

Name: Traditional Chinese Opera and Culture
Introduction: Opera is one of the essences of traditional Chinese culture. The many existing opera texts and stage performances not only contain all aspects of ancient and modern Chinese life, but also represent a complete presentation of the emotions, tastes and ideological world of the Chinese people. This course reveals the close relationship between opera and traditional Chinese culture through the interpretation of opera texts and the analysis and display of opera stage images.

Name: Topics in Rural Child Nutrition, Health and Development
Introduction: It is estimated that the number of anemic people worldwide is about 2 billion, with maternal and child anemia being the most serious among them. According to conservative estimates, about 200 million children aged 0-5 years old are unable to realize their cognitive development potential due to poverty, poor nutrition and health, and lack of care. Anemia among infants aged 6 to 12 years old in rural areas of my country is as high as over 50%, and about 40% suffer from lagging intelligence or motor abilities. The anemia rate among school-age children in poor rural areas is also as high as about 30%, and anemic children have poor academic performance. Health problems such as maternal malnutrition, childhood parasitic infections and myopia are still quite common in rural areas. How to understand the problems existing in the nutrition, health and development of rural children and their impact on achieving poverty alleviation, reducing the quality of human resources and income gaps between urban and rural areas, and surmounting the middle-income trap? This course will sort out the current status and problems of nutrition, health and development of rural children in the world and in my country, relevant scientific research results and some possible solutions. The purpose is to help students better understand the impact and policy implications of existing problems in nutrition, health and development of rural children, and to cultivate students' ability to use scientific impact assessment methods to explore, analyze and solve nutrition, health and development problems of rural children.

Name: Healthy Lifestyles and Health Communication
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
With the rapid development of my country's economy and society and the continuous improvement of people's living standards, people's lifestyles have undergone great changes. The incidence of various chronic non-communicable diseases and certain infectious diseases related to lifestyles has increased significantly, and the harm to the health of the general public has become increasingly serious. At the same time, due to the improvement of living standards, more and more people are beginning to pay attention to and pursue health, hoping to enjoy a healthy life. However, due to various reasons such as culture and history, the health literacy level of Chinese residents is very low, and the proportion of people who meet the requirements is only 6.48%. The proportion of chronic diseases is less than 5%. Many people do not know how to pursue health, and some people's good wishes for health are misguided and even exploited by cults and superstitions. The profound lessons have made us realize that it is very important and necessary to carry out extensive health education, provide scientific guidance to the masses and college students, and comprehensively improve the health literacy of the people. In the people's efforts to pursue health, the most important, cost-effective, and simplest thing to pay attention to is to change unhealthy behaviors and adopt a healthy lifestyle. As long as we pay attention to learning, cultivating and establishing a healthy lifestyle in our daily lives, we can effectively reduce the chance of suffering from many diseases and improve the health level of the people. _x000D_
      In the course "Healthy Lifestyle and Communication", the following will be introduced in a more systematic way: 1. The concept and connotation of health; 2. The "four cornerstones of health", that is, health knowledge and skills in reasonable diet, moderate exercise, smoking cessation and alcohol restriction, mental health, etc.; 3. Reproductive health, that is, sexual education, STD/AIDS prevention and safe sex, etc.; 4. Common first aid and treatment; 5. Introduction to health communication methods and techniques. This course will try its best to use easier-to-understand language and more lively and interesting participation and practice, so that students can learn and master health knowledge and skills while having fun and practicing while learning. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Japanese Vocabulary

Composition refers to word formation, and the teaching content includes word formation components and structural types as well as word formation including conversion and omission. This course also uses the method of comparative linguistics to compare Chinese and Japanese homographs from multiple perspectives such as word meaning and word class. The difference in sense of speech refers to the subtle differences in sense of speech between many synonyms belonging to different categories in Japanese. Introduction: It mainly explains articles on various themes and genres, and strives to combine the learning of language knowledge with the content of the articles, so as to not only improve students' Japanese understanding and expression skills, but also improve their reading and appreciation abilities.

Students have mastered the pronunciation, intonation, basic grammar and sentence patterns of Japanese, as well as about 4,000 commonly used vocabulary words, and have certain comprehensive abilities in listening, speaking, reading, writing and translation_x000D_

Teaching theoretical knowledge of translation, and through translation exercises in different genres such as words, sentence patterns, essays, news reports, scientific articles and literary works, students can master the general rules and basic methods and techniques of Chinese-Japanese translation, and improve the level and ability of Chinese-Japanese translation. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Classical Japanese Literature
Introduction:
This course studies Japanese classical literary works and is taught to third- and fourth-year undergraduate students who have taken "Japanese Literary Grammar" or have certain reading abilities in ancient Japanese literature. Through learning, students are initially exposed to Japanese classical literary works, cultivating students' sensibility and interest. At the same time, it cooperates with the "History of Japanese Literature" course to enable students to have a basic understanding of outstanding works and famous chapters in the history of ancient Japanese literature, as well as some background knowledge such as social history of ancient Japan, and improve their ability to understand, analyze and appreciate classical literary works. _x000D_
    Specifically, the reading scope is wide, covering representative Japanese classical literary works from the previous generation to modern times, including "The Kojiki", "Kojin Wakashu", "The Tale of Bamboo", "Pillow Grass", "The Tale of Genji", "The Tale of the Past", "Uranso", "Oshu Trail", "Ugetsu Monogatari", etc.; the reading method is more detailed, selecting classic paragraphs and chapters from classic works for intensive reading, and starting from the works in ancient literature. Students are required to master the status and significance in the history of study, the content of the selected chapters, relevant background knowledge, and the explanation of classical grammar phenomena. Of course, in view of the actual situation of the students, this course also pays attention to the combination of learning and appreciation. The difficulty and length of the selected passages are paid attention to the actual level of the students, so that students can understand and appreciate the works on the basis of improving their language ability, and feel the charm of Japanese classical literary works. _x000D_
    The teaching method combines teachers' intensive lectures with student reports and group discussions, emphasizing teacher-student interaction and students' active participation, encouraging and guiding students to express their opinions on the selected works, and improving students' independent learning ability. The teaching features focus on the introduction of various literary forms and styles, and improve students' humanistic qualities through the practice of reading various works. _x000D_

Introduction: Mainly teach articles on various themes and genres from the perspective of chapter structure, cultural background, etc., and answer questions raised by students. Students are required to do sufficient preview before class, and discuss the key points and difficulties of the article in class, in order to deeply understand the ideological connotation of the work and truly understand and master the expression characteristics of Japanese. Name: Contrastive Studies of Japanese and Chinese
Introduction:
Basic requirements: Through reading relevant literature and teaching by teachers, students are required to have a comprehensive understanding of the differences between Chinese and Japanese in pronunciation, phonology, characters, vocabulary, grammar, and language use, as well as the relationship between the two. _x000D_
Key points and difficulties: The focus is on the differences in vocabulary, grammar, and language use between Chinese and Japanese, as well as the history of contact between Chinese and Japanese. The difficulty lies in the unique grammatical categories of Japanese and the ambiguity of Japanese expressions. _x000D_

Name: Thesis Writing Guidance
Introduction: This course mainly teaches 1) the basic composition of a paper, precautions for chapter design, the use of punctuation marks, and writing standards for references and annotations; 2) an overview of the three paper writing directions of language, literature, and culture and an introduction to feasible topic selection.

Name: Rural Sociology
Introduction: This course selects several important areas in rural China and provides a more in-depth analysis of the basic institutional framework and actual operation methods of rural China in a thematic manner. Focus on exploring the structural characteristics, change process, and problems faced by China's rural society in modern times.

Name: Japanese Poetry
Introduction: The course "Japanese Poetry" mainly teaches the characteristics and nature of Japanese poetry. According to the chronological division of Japanese literary history, the study of related poetic works will be carried out according to the time of poetry creation. "Man'yoshu" is the oldest extant poetry collection in Japan. It is generally believed to have been written around 760. This work is one of the major works of Japanese literature of the previous generation. The verse work "Kokin Wakashu" (905) among medieval literary works is another poetry collection after "Man'yoshu". They and the verse work of medieval literature "New Kokin Japanese Songs" (1210) are the result of collective creation. These three works are the first objects of study in our course. In subsequent modern literature, Matsuo Basho (1644-1694), a representative figure in verse creation, and his works are the focus of our study. Matsuo Basho created the art form of haiku. The rhetorical characteristics of waka of this period, the rhetorical characteristics of "Okura Hundred People" and haiku are all important contents that we need to understand and master. After entering the Meiji period, modern poetry ushered in a prosperous period, and well-known poetry schools and authors continued to emerge. We will study several representative poets and their works. Such as: Hakushu Kitahara, Kotaro Takamura, Sakutaro Hagiwara, Kenji Miyazawa, etc. Modern tanka, modern tanka, haiku and their representative creative figures and works are also the main content of this course.

Name: Business English (I)
Introduction: This is a two-semester English course taught to freshmen. The purpose is to improve students' English reading and listening skills, which can help students develop their communication skills, expand students' international business knowledge, and use the language more fluently and confidently in an international business environment.

Name: Business English (II)
Introduction: This is a two-semester English course taught to freshmen. The purpose is to improve students' English reading and listening skills, which can help students develop their communication skills, expand students' international business knowledge, and use the language more fluently and confidently in an international business environment.

Name: Mathematical Analysis
Introduction: This course is one of the most important basic courses for mathematics majors. The basic contents include limit theory, integrability theory of definite integrals, and convergence and uniform convergence of function sequences. This course is the basis for many subsequent courses such as differential equations, differential geometry, complex variable functions, real variable functions, probability theory, basic physics, theoretical mechanics, etc. Mathematical analysis is also an important course for training the basic abilities and thinking methods of college mathematics. Having a good foundation of mathematical analysis plays a key role in future study and research.

Name: Advanced Algebra
Introduction: This course is an important foundation for learning and researching modern mathematics, and has important applications in the fields of natural science, social science, and economics. This course enables students to learn and understand basic knowledge such as polynomials, linear spaces, and linear transformations. Through learning, students can develop mathematical thinking, innovative spirit, and preliminary ability to solve practical problems.

Name: The Rise of Great Powers
Introduction:
Nine countries have been (or are now) "world powers" in modern times. This course tells the history of the rise and fall of these nine countries, looking for the regular characteristics of the rise and fall of great powers, thereby providing meaningful thinking for China's modernization and China's international status. _x000D_
The earliest "world powers" were Portugal and Spain, which embodied the early mercantilist stage of capitalism. In Europe, Portugal and Spain were the first to step out of the feudal state and establish early nation-states centered on the rule of autocratic monarchs. They then used the power of the state to promote mercantilism and enter the development stage of early capitalism. Portugal and Spain carried out large-scale colonial expansion during the "Geographical Discovery" and "carved up" the world for the first time. However, Portugal and Spain retained too many feudal remnants in their social structures, and the two countries began to decline in the 17th century. _x000D_
The 17th century was the century of the Netherlands. At that time, it monopolized sea lines of communication, controlled global trade, and was the most powerful maritime power. The Netherlands embodies the heyday of commercial capitalism. It developed early mercantilism to the extreme, and its creations in business and finance still have a profound impact today. The independence of the Netherlands was the prerequisite for its strength, and the formation of the nation-state laid the foundation for its sudden rise. The problem of the Netherlands was that it failed to move from "merchant" to "heavy industry", which led to its decline in the 18th century. _x000D_
In the 18th century, capitalism shifted from "merchant" to "heavy industry", with Britain and France becoming the leaders in this period. The rise of Britain and France also started with the emergence of nation-states and was also based on mercantilism. However, the mercantilism of Britain and France has developed to the late mercantilism stage, which is characterized by focusing on production rather than simply "doing business", which built a bridge for the subsequent transition to industrial society. The rise of Britain and France marked the transformation from commercial capitalism to industrial capitalism. Britain took the lead in moving towards industrial society because it was the first to possess the political and social prerequisites for launching the industrial revolution, that is, to overcome autocracy and establish a constitutional system. The Industrial Revolution changed Britain and the world. France was the second country to start the Industrial Revolution, and it was also the country to overthrow the absolute monarchy after Britain. The Industrial Revolution, led by Britain and France, became the trend of the times. Industrial capitalism also swept the world under the leadership of Britain and France. Britain and France were the world powers of that era. _x000D_
On the one hand, the liberal capitalist development model of Britain and France was very successful, but on the other hand, it also had major flaws and caused many social problems. It is difficult for post-development countries to copy this model. As a result, some countries began to look for new ways to catch up with Britain and France while avoiding their mistakes. Germany and Japan are two typical countries. _x000D_
Germany had always lagged behind and was not reunified until the 1870s. However, after reunification, Germany's economy developed rapidly. By the beginning of the 20th century, it had caught up with and surpassed Britain and France, creating a miracle of industrialization. Germany's achievements are due to a new development model, in which the state no longer acts as a "night watchman" but plays an important role as the driving force of industrialization. However, while achieving rapid development, Germany embarked on the wrong path. Prussian militarism tradition and highly expanded German nationalism pushed Germany to the path of waging war again and again. The German way was a variant of capitalism. Japan in Asia also embodies this variant. Japan followed the path of capitalist development after the Meiji Restoration and quickly completed industrialization according to the German model. But Japan, like Germany, quickly embarked on the path of military expansion, and eventually failed in the war, bringing huge disasters to other countries and itself. _x000D_
The Soviet Union is the only "world power" that has taken the socialist path so far. The Soviet Union created a development model that was completely different from capitalism and achieved great success. After the October Revolution, the Communist Party of the Soviet Union assumed the mission of leading Russia's industrialization. When Lenin was still alive, he proposed the development goal of "Soviet power plus electrification." Stalin identified socialist industrialization as the party's main task and basically completed this task through two and a half "five-year plans", making the Soviet Union the second largest industrial country in the world and laying a strong industrial foundation for defeating Nazi Germany. The success of the Soviet Union was attributed to the "planned economy". In this development model, the power of the country was fully exerted, and all resources in the country were uniformly dispatched, achieving astonishing achievements in the early stages of economic take-off. But the problem with the Soviet Union was that when the shortcomings of the "planned economy" were fully exposed, the Soviet leaders did not realize the necessity of reform and missed the opportunity for reform, which resulted in the disintegration of the Soviet Union from a difficult situation, leaving behind major historical lessons. _x000D_
In the 20th century, the United States advanced capitalism to a new stage. The United States had the advantages of Britain when it became independent. After the westward expansion and the Civil War, it became a vast country. The industrial revolution developed rapidly in the second half of the 19th century, and by the beginning of the 20th century it became the world's largest economic power. The United States adopted the liberal capitalist model at the beginning of its industrialization, but during the development process the original model was constantly modified, eventually forming a new "hybrid" capitalist economic model and becoming the culmination of modern capitalism. After World War II, it became the leader of the Western bloc and one of the two superpowers. After the collapse of the Soviet Union, it became the world's only superpower and is currently trying to dominate the world. But the attempt of a dominant United States to dominate the world is also impossible, and facts have proven this. _x000D_
The "big country" of an era embodies the historical trend of that era. The country that leads this trend is the "big country" of this era. If it loses this leadership ability, it will lose its status as a "big country".

Name: Organization and Management Seminar
Introduction:
This course is a small-class teaching course in conjunction with the required course "Organization and Management". The positioning of small class teaching is to deepen understanding, locate interests and improve abilities. There are seven courses in total, each lasting two hours. _x000D_
In each course, the instructor will have a more in-depth discussion with the students on some of the contents taught in the "Organization and Management" large class lectures, and try to answer the students' relevant questions. In addition, teachers will propose relevant discussion topics, supplemented by role-playing, case analysis and other forms to help students further understand the application of the concepts, theories, and frameworks taught in "Organization and Management" in real life. _x000D_

Name: Organization and Management
Introduction: The course is a basic course on organization and management. Through this course, students will be able to acquire theoretical knowledge about the individual (personality, attitude, motivation, consciousness, etc.) in the organization, the group and team, as well as the organizational level and the relationship between the organization and the environment, to provide them with a knowledge base for future courses, and to provide the necessary preparation for the students to move to work.

Name: Fertile Soil Program
Introduction: The basic content of this course is to systematically explain the basic knowledge of social research to students, and organize them to use the summer to go to various social practice bases for temporary training. The "Fertile Soil Project" aims to allow students to combine practical research knowledge with on-the-ground practical experience, help them master the basic methods of academic research, and accumulate practical experience in social research; at the same time, it also aims to provide students of Guanghua School of Management with an opportunity to understand the national conditions, social conditions, and people's sentiments at the grassroots level, truly participate in the management and operation of grassroots self-governing organizations and local enterprises, and combine the economic management knowledge learned in the classroom with local reality. While students gain knowledge from the teachings of the Fertile Soil Project, they can also gain a variety of experiences in different situations, which has strong guiding significance for their future development.

Name: Information Technology and Corporate Strategy
Introduction:
If you ask: In the capital market, which sector is growing the fastest? That must be an information technology related industry. If you ask: What are the elements that can rejuvenate traditional industries? It must also be a new business model led by information technology. Therefore, "Internet +" has become my country's national strategy, and all walks of life are trying to use information technology to increase efficiency, expand markets, strengthen services, and interconnection. It can be said that information technology has never attracted the attention of the whole society as it does today, and will profoundly change the way the economy operates, macro and microeconomic management methods, production and lifestyle, investment and financing decision-making methods, and even national security strategies, etc. _x000D_
As a student of the School of Management, it has become very necessary to engage in the fields of capital markets, business management, and academic research on economic management in the future. It has become very necessary to understand the latest trends in information technology and master the basic thinking and methods of information technology. However, information technology is a relatively unique field of engineering technology. It is not only complex in content, but also has unique ideas. It is difficult to gain knowledge through simple browsing and diligent self-study. _x000D_
The "Information Technology and Enterprise Strategy" we offer, from the perspective of enterprise development strategy, comprehensively explains the basic ideas of information technology in a simple and easy-to-understand style, introduces the latest development of information technology in depth, and attempts to answer the following questions: How to enable enterprises to gain development opportunities and how to make enterprises more competitive. Therefore, for students who are interested in joining the fields of capital markets, macroeconomic management, corporate strategic management, corporate operations and management, new economic research, etc. in the future, this course will be the right choice for you. _x000D_
The teaching content is divided into four modules, the general situation is as follows:_x000D_
Part One: Principles and Ideas of Basic Information Technology_x000D_
On the basis of the prerequisite course "Management Science" and combined with the experience of financial electronics, the basic principles and ideas of information technology such as computers in information systems, computer operating systems, local area network technology, international Internet technology, digital signatures and information security are explained. _x000D_
Part 2: Introduction to typical information systems_x000D_
Introduce the concepts, architecture and basic principles of common transaction processing systems and decision support systems in enterprise operations. _x000D_
Part Three: Development Organization and Operation Ideas of Information Systems_x000D_
Combined with the informatization experience of large financial enterprises, the development organizational structure and operation ideas of information systems are introduced. _x000D_
Part 4: The latest development of information technology and enterprise choice_x000D_
Through topics such as: How Wall Street views emerging information technology, cloud computing and applications, the Internet of Things and applications, big data and its application in commercial banks, the application prospects of blockchain technology, etc., it introduces the latest progress in information technology and related corporate development strategic decision-making issues. _x000D_

Name: Risk Management and Insurance
Introduction: China's economy has entered a new normal, and various risks are increasingly emerging. How to effectively manage risks is crucial. The basic purpose of this course is to cultivate students' awareness of "risks are everywhere and at all times" through the teaching of this course, and to master the basic ideas and common methods of how to correctly assess the level of risks they face and how to choose appropriate methods to manage risks. On this basis, master the basic principles, main fields and scope of application of insurance.

Name: Financial Case Analysis
Introduction: This course is a case analysis course on corporate finance. It takes modern companies as the main research object and analyzes and discusses corporate financial management activities. The content mainly includes case analysis on company value and capital budget, capital cost and capital structure, listed financing, mergers and acquisitions, basic derivative financial instruments and risk management. This course focuses on application and requires students to master the application of basic theories in corporate finance in corporate finance and investment practice.

Name: Appreciation of Greek and Roman Mythology
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
Greek and Roman mythology is the source and treasure of ancient Greek literature and art. It has had a very profound impact on the entire Western civilization, culture, literature, art, philosophy, and ideology. It has deeply penetrated and enriched the English language: some vocabulary phrases in English are derived from characters or allusions in Greek and Roman mythology. _x000D_
This course focuses on the famous characters and stories in ancient Greek and Roman mythology, and also introduces their influence on the language, literature, and art of Western countries, especially English-speaking countries, and attempts to explore and understand the factors of Greek and Roman mythology in some Hollywood films in recent years. _x000D_
Classroom teaching is mainly in English, combining regular teaching with multimedia presentations, and organizing students to perform small-scale drama performances in small groups. Students' classroom performance, attendance and performances will account for 40% of the semester's overall evaluation, and the final exam will be in a closed-book format. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Society (Part 2)
Prerequisite: There are no prior course requirements for this course. However, it is hoped that students will have a certain English base because of the use of English for teaching and for homework and discussion.
Introduction: The main content of this course is to help students understand contemporary Chinese society, including the historical evolution, social structure and system of Chinese society, as well as today's major social issues. The course mainly includes three major modules: the cultural and historical background of contemporary Chinese society, social structure and social stratification, and population development and diversity. In each module, we will set up different course topics that are intrinsically linked to guide students to understand the economic, cultural and political aspects of contemporary Chinese society from different educations. In the module on the cultural and historical background of contemporary Chinese society, we will mainly introduce China’s ideological system, political system and modern Chinese history, so that students can have a certain understanding of the historical and cultural background of Chinese society. In the social structure and social stratification module, we will introduce topics such as occupation and social mobility, household registration and immigration, education, income and consumption in detail to help students understand the uniqueness of Chinese society. In the population development and diversity module, we will teach the diversity of social groups from a demographic perspective. Through introductions to topics such as population and health, family, and gender, students will have a holistic and macroscopic understanding of Chinese society.

Name: Financial Statement Analysis
Introduction: This course is an advanced course in accounting information analysis and securities investment. It is suitable for students who are preparing to engage in securities investment, investment banking, venture capital, industrial investment, or corporate finance. Students taking this elective should have taken, or are equivalent to taking, an introductory financial accounting course.

Name: Intermediate Financial Accounting
Introduction: This course uses the concepts, principles and methods revealed in elementary financial accounting to comprehensively explain the accounting treatment of the main transactions, events and situations that cause changes in the elements of the financial statements of an enterprise under the condition of going concern (involving all procedures of recognition, measurement, recording and reporting, with a focus on recognition and measurement); the preparation of the entire set of financial statements and financial reports of the enterprise; in addition, it also discusses some special issues in the field of financial accounting, thereby laying a solid foundation for further learning of advanced accounting.

Name: Internal Control and Internal Auditing
Introduction:

As can be seen from the framework diagram, in terms of control focus and control implementation subjects, the enterprise's internal control system consists of three subsystems: (1) Internal control subsystem at the corporate governance mechanism level; (2) Internal control subsystem at the enterprise operation level; (3) Internal control subsystem at the enterprise management level. _x000D_
From a dynamic perspective, during the implementation of the internal control system, each internal control subsystem and the overall system need to be continuously tested and optimized. _x000D_

Name: Advanced Management Accounting
Introduction: This course is designed to deepen students' understanding of the design and implementation of enterprise internal management control and cost accounting systems. Students should understand how various control and cost systems operate, their strengths and weaknesses, and the principles of system design. This course will also give you the opportunity to gain an in-depth understanding of some current topics in cost analysis and management, and develop a knowledge base for applied cost analysis that goes beyond basic concepts and tools. Important topics covered include activity-based costing, costing for pricing decisions, budgeting, performance measurement systems, and transfer pricing. We will examine the current practice of these elements of management control in decentralized business organizations, as well as the conceptual issues associated with designing effective management decision and control systems.

Name: Advanced Financial Accounting
Introduction: This course builds on basic and intermediate financial accounting and is designed to provide students with a deeper understanding of advanced topics in financial accounting. This course will cover accounting issues not discussed in basic or intermediate accounting courses. Major topics include accounting for passive investments, equity method accounting for investments, consolidated financial information, intercompany transactions, and other financial accounting topics.

Name: Auditing
Introduction: Auditing is a social discipline that specializes in studying auditing theories and methods, exploring the laws of auditing development, and effectively supervising economic activities. Auditing science is produced on the basis of auditing practice. What has been tested and proved by practice is a correct reflection of the nature of objective things and their laws. Audit theory must be used to guide audit practice, otherwise it will become a theory that is divorced from reality. Since early financial auditing was aimed at reviewing accounting accounts and statements, it was called "accounting by its side", "accounting by its side" or "account checking". Therefore, some people include auditing as a branch of accounting in a broad sense, namely accounting, accounting analysis and accounting inspection. Therefore, it is believed that the object of auditing is accounting. Without accounting, there would be no auditing. Auditing and accounting are twin brothers. Auditing has developed into a comprehensive applied science. It is not only highly theoretical, but also practical and technical. Its theoretical nature is mainly reflected in the discussion and study of auditing activity rules and their applications in auditing, and a high-level summary and scientific summary of auditing practice. Its practical nature is mainly reflected in the fact that auditing science can be applied in audit practice, guiding audit work, and has obvious economic and social effects; its technical nature is mainly manifested in the fact that auditing science absorbs various scientific achievements and provides various scientific and technical methods and means for audit activities.

Name: American Environmental Thought
Introduction:
_x000D_
The United States is the main birthplace of the contemporary environmental movement. Americans' ideas about the nature of nature and the relationship between humans and nature are influenced by European ideas, but also show their own uniqueness. This course will focus on the works of several major American environmental thinkers (Thoreau, Muir, Leopold, Carson, etc.), introduce Americans' understanding of environmental issues, outline the historical development of American environmental thought, and its contribution to the world environmental movement. _x000D_
Specifically, this course will cover early Americans’ attitudes towards nature, transcendentalist views on nature, the establishment of the national park system, the resource protection movement and its debates, the ecological movement and the new view of nature, the environmental crisis and the birth of the modern environmental movement, the development of environmental ethics, etc. _x000D_
Features of this course: (1) Multimedia teaching will be used to show the natural scenery and geographical features of the United States; (2) Focus on reading the original works of American environmental thinkers to cultivate students' appreciation of nature and life while understanding the development of American environmental thought; (3) American philosophy, history and culture will be used to increase the knowledge and interest of the course. _x000D_
Environmental education is one of the important contents of general education for college students. This course welcomes students who are interested in environmental protection and American culture to take this course. _x000D_

Name: Cost and Management Accounting
Introduction: Management accounting plays an important role in corporate strategic planning and operation management. This course focuses on how to use management accounting information to help managers plan, control and make decisions. This course will introduce the concept of cost and basic accounting methods, activity-based costing, JIT (Just-in-Time), cost-volume-profit analysis and budget control and other modern management tools.

Name: Topics in Accounting, Auditing and Financial Management
Introduction: Accounting is a discipline with outstanding practical characteristics. Years of practice have proven that only by stepping out of the bookstore, breaking the old theoretical framework, and integrating it extensively with practice can accounting students truly master effective knowledge. In response to this goal, the Department of Accounting has launched the course "Special Topics in Accounting, Auditing and Financial Management". The course arrangement focuses on the effective combination of academic and practical aspects. It widely invites industry veterans to jointly teach, closely links business management education practice with advanced financial accounting education concepts, and integrates accounting, auditing and auditing. It organically integrates multiple knowledges of accounting, finance, internal control, and management. It is committed to cultivating students with a global perspective, while at the same time having an in-depth understanding of China's national conditions, broadening their horizons, sharing resources, and improving accounting and financial concepts in all aspects, helping students grow into managerial financial accounting experts with sustainable competitiveness.

Name: Chinese Finance
Introduction: Over the past 40 years of reform and opening up, China's financial industry has made considerable progress. Its development path, organizational form, operation methods, risk accumulation and release characteristics, formal and informal rules, and interaction with the real economy are all different from other economies and have obvious Chinese characteristics. Existing finance textbooks are mostly based on Western markets and have obvious deficiencies in interpreting China's magnificent financial landscape and its tortuous and subtle historical evolution. This course will describe the institutional background of China's financial industry and sort out the historical context of China's financial development. On this basis, based on academic research and problem-oriented, it will reflect on the historical choices of key nodes in the reform and opening up of the financial industry, summarize the experience and lessons of the development of China's financial industry, concretize China's financial development model, contribute to the in-depth integration of financial theory and Chinese practice, and predict the future development direction of China's financial industry. It is hoped that after studying this course, students will be able to grasp the historical process of changes in China's financial system, understand what a "good financial system" is, and actively think about the key nodes of China's financial development in the future, as well as the correct choices we should make.

Name: Studies in Masterworks and Their English-Chinese Translations
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The course "Study on the Translation of English-Chinese Masterpieces" selects about fifteen works translated by famous modern and contemporary Chinese and foreign translators. Introduction:
"Business War Simulation" is a program in which, under the guidance of teachers, students form a senior management team of a virtual enterprise and conduct practical exercises on business operations in the ever-changing market competition environment simulated by computer software. Evaluate enterprise performance through multi-period business decisions. The purpose is to allow students to experience management decision-making without risk, learn knowledge, apply knowledge, and develop talents in simulated business management practices. _x000D_
This course has the following features:_x000D_
(1) Comprehensive application of management knowledge; general management courses basically involve knowledge in a certain management field, while "Business War Simulation" requires the application of knowledge from courses such as "Production Operations", "Marketing", "Financial Management", "Strategic Management", "Human Resources Management", "Statistics", "Operations Research" and other courses. This kind of "application" also requires students to choose to apply the knowledge they have learned based on analysis and judgment of competitive scenarios, which can improve students' ability to integrate and comprehensively apply knowledge from multiple management courses. _x000D_
(2) Close to actual business operation exercises. For students in physics, chemistry and other faculties, doing experiments in the laboratory is a necessary part of learning. It is impossible for students from the School of Management to directly go to actual high-level management positions in enterprises to "practice". The "Enterprise Competition Simulation System" independently developed by Wang Qiwen, Zhang Guoyou and others of Guanghua School of Management has built a simulation platform for students that is close to the real market environment. The problems encountered in decision-making are living cases with no ready answers. It is a management exercise with low risks and realistic effects. This course uses the second generation of business competition simulation, namely BizWar. It offers greater ease of use and flexibility. _x000D_
(3) Cultivate students’ teamwork spirit. The teaching method of this course is that 3-4 students form a company's management team, serving as the company's general manager, production manager, marketing manager, financial manager, and human resources manager. Decisions are made for each period through consultation and discussion, which is conducive to cultivating students' ability to cooperate and communicate with others. _x000D_
(4) Cultivate emotional intelligence in success and setbacks. Business war simulation is a multi-period dynamic process, the situation is ever-changing, and it is difficult to encounter the good "luck" of smooth sailing. When students encounter difficulties such as product backlog and financial constraints, how to diagnose problems, find solutions, and turn danger into safety requires not only knowledge and ability, but also the will to not be arrogant in victory and not discouraged in defeat, which is conducive to cultivating and improving students' emotional intelligence. _x000D_
(5) Cultivate students’ entrepreneurial spirit and innovation ability. In the business war simulation, students will understand the major issues that senior managers of enterprises need to pay attention to, as well as the ups and downs of enterprise management, which will be of great benefit to students in the future when they work in enterprises or even start their own businesses. During the course, teachers will inspire students to use their creativity and develop suitable decision-making support tools, which will help improve students' innovative abilities. _x000D_
(6) Cultivation and enhancement of Excel skills. This course exercises students' ability to develop and use Excel. Help students make scientific management decisions through Excel-assisted decision-making tools. _x000D_
(7) Interesting nature of the course. The initiative of students to participate, the competitiveness of business competitions, the complexity of simulation scenarios, and the variability of the game process make this course uniquely interesting. _x000D_

Name: Financial Analysis and Quantitative Investment
Introduction:
The latest research in behavioral finance and economics shows that investors are always likely to make irrational decisions. Whether in a calm or turbulent market environment, mispricing will exist due to human weaknesses. To overcome these weaknesses, we must find an investment strategy. This investment strategy is a completely rational and systematic investment strategy that eliminates subjective factors from the decision-making process. _x000D_
	Quantitative investing is exactly the ideal investment strategy. Quantitative investment is based on rigorous rules, and investment decisions do not rely on investors' subjective judgments. In the field of quantitative equity investment, strict rules are also called alpha factors. These alpha factors are refined based on solid financial and accounting theories. Market anomalies in academic research have been transformed into alpha factors by quantitative investors, and the multi-factor model formed by the weighted combination of these alpha factors is the core of quantitative equity investment. _x000D_
	After the 2008 financial crisis, multi-factor models have become a mainstream strategy in the field of quantitative investment. In 2011, the scale of quantitative investment and hedge funds in the United States reached more than 2 trillion US dollars. In many large stock exchanges around the world, nearly 50% of trading volume comes from various quantitative investment methods. It can be said that after more than 40 years of development, quantitative investment has become one of the most important investment methods in the Western financial market. However, real quantitative funds are still relatively rare in the country. The reasons for this phenomenon are that on the one hand, my country's capital market is not yet mature, and on the other hand, there is a shortage of talents who are proficient in quantitative investment theory and practice. In the long run, fundamental quantification has broad development prospects in China's capital market, especially China's A-share market. China's A-share market is generally considered to have low market efficiency, and the weaker the market efficiency, the more opportunities there are to discover alpha factors. _x000D_
	This course focuses on quantitative equity investment from the perspective of financial analysis and company fundamentals. It aims to provide students with the theoretical framework and practical guidance of quantitative equity investment and to cultivate future quantitative investment talents for China's capital market. Specifically, this course will be divided into three parts. The first part introduces the basic methods and logic of financial analysis. Multi-factor models based on fundamentals are different from quantitative investment models based on statistical arbitrage or high-frequency trading. Understanding fundamentals is the key to multi-factor models. The second part introduces the main alpha factors: value factor, quality factor and momentum factor. The value factor exploits investors' cognitive biases to find stocks that are undervalued, the quality factor evaluates company performance to find stocks that are expected to generate value appreciation, and the momentum factor exploits investors' underreaction to information to find stocks that continue to rise in price. Among them, both the value factor and the quality factor need to be based on rigorous fundamental analysis and reflect the concept of modern value investing (value + quality); while the momentum factor is an effective means of measuring investor sentiment. The third part introduces the basic methods of multi-factor model modeling, including factor evaluation, backtesting, weight allocation, risk control and dynamic adjustment of multi-factor models - these are all at the forefront of theory and practice. At the same time, this section will introduce how to implement and detect these alpha strategies using professional software. Bringing these industry-focused contents into Peking University classrooms will greatly arouse students' enthusiasm for learning, provide students with opportunities to understand the industry, and master basic hedge fund trading strategies and methods. _x000D_
    This course will focus on the discussion of value factors and quality factors, integrate the accounting and financial knowledge learned by students, and lay the foundation for further learning and practical operations. Through the study of this course, students will be able to: (1) Proficient in valuing individual companies and discovering mispricings; (2) Proficient in using financial analysis methods to evaluate company performance; (3) In-depth understanding of the ideas of quantitative investment and establishing theoretical intuition for quantitative investment; (4) Proficient and flexible in mastering methods of constructing investment portfolios, and efficiently constructing quantitative investment strategies. _x000D_
    This course is an advanced course in accounting information analysis and securities investment, suitable for students preparing to engage in fund management, investment banking, securities analysis and financial consulting. Students who choose this course must have taken basic courses in accounting and finance. _x000D_
    The coursework for this course consists of two parts: the first part is to build an Excel value evaluation system according to the tasks assigned by the textbook, and the second part is to write an analysis report according to the tasks assigned by the textbook. The analysis report is divided into chapter report and general report, and specific requirements will be given gradually. Course assignments are all group assignments to cultivate students' team spirit and sense of cooperation. Final assessment of your grade in this course includes group assignments, class tests, and a final exam. _x000D_
