Name: Ethnicity and Society
Introduction:
The course "Ethnicity and Society" is a general elective course offered by the Department of Sociology at Peking University to all undergraduates. It is a basic knowledge course with a general education nature. _x000D_
At present, most countries in the world are multi-ethnic countries. Race and ethnic relations and nationalist movements have always been major global issues since modern times. In recent years, wars, civil wars, and social conflicts in various countries are more or less closely related to ethnic issues. There are 55 ethnic minorities in China, with a total population of more than 100 million. Ethnic autonomous areas account for 64% of the country's land area. With the support of foreign political forces and extremist religious forces, ethnic separatist activities also exist in some ethnic minority areas in China. Consolidating ethnic unity and national unity has become one of the core issues in China's social development. Under such international and domestic situations, Chinese college students need to know more about basic knowledge and research methods on national and ethnic issues and have certain analytical and discerning abilities. _x000D_
This course is guided by Marxist-Leninist ethnic theory, while systematically introducing the theories and research methods of Western ethnic sociology, and discussing the evolution of ethnic relations in today's world in conjunction with the modernization process. As for the source of basic theory, we pay attention to integrating the theoretical essence and knowledge accumulation from several aspects. First, the theories and methods of dealing with ethnic relations in Chinese history; second, absorbing the theories of ethnic groups and ethnic relations from European and American countries; third, the practice of ethnic theories and ethnic policies of the former Soviet Union; fourth, the experience of other countries such as India in establishing "national identity" in the process of "nation creation." _x000D_
The subject background of the course is sociological race and ethnic studies, and it also extensively absorbs basic theories, research methods and perspectives from other disciplines (history, political science, anthropology, ethnology, demography, international relations, etc.). The course embodies the 10 main characteristics of sociological ethnic studies: (1) Emphasis on the study of real society rather than the verification of ethnic history; (2) Pay attention to the mutual relationships between ethnic groups rather than the ethnic groups themselves; (3) Pay attention to combining the two levels of individuals and groups; (4) Pay more attention to comprehensive research on various factors; (5) Try to explain the formation and development trajectory of various phenomena in ethnic relations; (6) Pay attention to absorbing and borrowing from modern social science research methods and means, combining qualitative analysis with quantitative analysis; (7) Focusing on empirical research; (8) Combining research with relevant national policies; (9) Combined with regional development research; (10) Pay attention to the development trend of domestic ethnic relations in the process of modernization. Therefore, it is a comprehensive course that takes into account both basic theory and practical application. _x000D_
The course systematically introduces the ethnic policies of various countries and the goals of dealing with ethnic relations. It also introduces sociological research topics related to ethnic issues and the quantitative index system for measuring ethnic relations in a specific region. The design of the indicator system is based on the actual situation of these topics. The course introduces the practical application of these research methods and quantitative indicators through a large amount of statistical data and various survey data from the United States, the Soviet Union, and China. It enables students to systematically master sociological ethnic relations research from theories, methods to specific research topics. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Music
Introduction: As an important carrier of culture, music has brought together quite a wealth of historical information on primitive art, life customs, and religious culture. Its historical development has its own characteristics and laws, but is also interconnected and influenced by each other. This course focuses on the five major categories of Chinese and foreign music, namely: court music, folk music, traditional music, modern music, and popular music. It teaches the content and knowledge of their genre classification forms, music style characteristics, representative figures, representative works, styles and schools, etc. Through the study of this course, students can be helped to understand the main forms in music, become familiar with the musical language in music, and understand the excellent repertoire inherited in our music, so as to comprehensively understand the status and value of music in human culture. This course takes the study of the mutual relationship between music and culture as the overall teaching premise. It designs courses based on different topics and different perspectives. It uses teachers’ classroom lectures on topics and learners read relevant academic works around the topics after class. It introduces many cutting-edge topics into learners’ horizons, in order to expand students’ professional knowledge and further improve them.

Name: Logistics and Supply Chain Management
Introduction: With the formation of the globalized economy and the rapid development of information technology and e-commerce, the survival and competitive environment of enterprises have also changed. In the past, companies faced competition with similar competitors. In the era of global markets and digital economy, companies must rely on alliances and collaboration with upstream and downstream companies to gain advantages in market competition. This means that the competition now becomes a competition between supply chains and supply chains. In this context, the concept of supply chain management has attracted great attention from the business community and academia in the past two decades, and has been further developed in theory and practice. In today's enterprises, important positions such as supply chain manager, supply chain director or supply chain VP have also appeared. Therefore, supply chain management is an important course for business school students, whether they are developing in the corporate world or academia.

Name: Introduction to Primary Texts in Western Art Theory
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to guide senior undergraduates how to read some original works on Western art and to cultivate students' good thinking and critical skills. At the same time, it is hoped that through the study of this course, students can combine their own interests and use established Western art theories and methods to advance their own research.

Name: Journey to the West and Chinese Culture
Introduction: "Journey to the West" can be said to be a genealogy of texts that has profoundly influenced Chinese culture. From the Tang and Song Dynasties to the present day, it has been presented in various forms such as opera, folklore, novels, paintings, movies, and television, reflecting the material culture and spiritual temperament of each era. This course takes "Journey to the West" as its theme, explores the connections between these different texts, and uses it to present different aspects of Chinese culture.

Name: Introduction to Dance
Introduction: Through the teaching of the theoretical knowledge of dance in general, the course provides students with basic theoretical knowledge of dance and understanding of the historical origins of different species, the language of action and aesthetic features.

Name: Principles of Aesthetics
Introduction: An overview of the quality of aesthetics, a brief description of the history of aesthetics and basic aesthetics, leading students to an initial knowledge of aesthetics and entry into aesthetics.

Name: Applications of Regression Analysis in Management Research
Introduction: This course presents the various statistical analysis methods commonly used in management studies (e.g. regression analysis).

Name: Business Activity in China: A Management Perspective
Office Automation
Introduction:
Management and office work not only refer to sitting and working in an office, but also include a wide range of fields including transaction processing, information management and decision-making process. It is inevitable that computers will enter the management and office fields. Therefore, understanding and mastering related basic concepts, basic methods and skills is not only conducive to understanding the new concepts of management and office in modern society, but also has certain significance for studying in school, improving learning and work efficiency, and assisting the study of other professional courses. _x000D_
      This course is based on an overview of office systems and office automation systems, and discusses the basic elements, functions and characteristics of OA systems. The course focuses on two important areas in office automation systems: computer applications and network construction, and teaches their basic concepts, working principles and applications in office activities. According to different teaching objects, the courses focus on teaching functional units such as word processing, spreadsheets, databases, electronic documents, electronic schedule management, electronic postal services, electronic typesetting, speech processing, graphics and image processing, management information systems, and decision support systems. Through the application of specific general-purpose software, students can deepen their understanding of important concepts and specific methods, establish the concept of integrated processing of office activities, master the basic methods of using computers to complete paper organization and writing, data management, model operation, problem discussion, information release, time management, etc., as well as the ability to apply specific systems to solve specific problems in management, office and learning. _x000D_
      The course also involves the analysis and design of modern office equipment and office automation systems and the discussion of some typical issues in the implementation of office automation systems. _x000D_

Name: Office Automation Computer Lab
Introduction:
This course is an internship for the Department ' s office automation programme.
The internships are based on the delivery of the office automation course, providing students with the general functionality and usage of the office software, with a certain level of thinking and capacity to apply the automated system to address specific issues in office activities, and increasing awareness and understanding of the development context, basic functions and system functions of the office automation system in the application.

Name: Media and Society
Introduction: This course is taught based on the book COMMUNICATION IN HISTORY: Technology, Culture, Society, as the main content. Today, as information technology represented by the Internet has increasingly become an important tool for our work, study and entertainment, and has brought great changes to our society and life, new communication media have received great attention. In order to better understand the important role of new communication media as well as its limitations and development prospects, it is necessary to conduct a historical review of the emergence, development and impact of media on our society. This course uses communication, sociology, history, information science and other related disciplines to provide a relatively comprehensive and systematic introduction to the emergence and development of media, the relationship between media and information, and the impact of media on all aspects of our society. The main chapters of this course: Chapter 1/Study of Media and Media Theory. Chapter 2/The original communication medium-language. Chapter 3/Rock paintings and new archaeological discoveries. Chapter 4/Media in the Early Civilization Period. Chapter 5/Civilization without writing - the Incas and knots. Chapter 6/The Invention of Writing. Chapter 7/Printing Revolution (1). Chapter 8/Printing Revolution (2). Chapter 9/Media in the Age of Electrical Communication. Chapter 10/A medium for disseminating information in a wide range - newspapers. Chapter 11/Advertising and movies, consumer culture and mass entertainment media. Chapter 12/The Age of Television. Chapter 13/Computer and Internet Age.

Name: Arts Training (I)
Introduction:
Courses are only available to high-level art troupes. _x000D_
This course is a symphony orchestra rehearsal class, mainly for third-year undergraduate students who have just entered orchestra studies. The course content is based on orchestra training repertoire, with rehearsals and performances organized by band conductors and instructors.

Name: Modern Astronomy
Prerequisite: There is no pre-course requirement for this course
Introduction:
Astronomy is one of the oldest disciplines in the natural sciences, and its origins can even be traced back to ancient times. With the development of people's understanding of the natural world and the application of arithmetic and geometry knowledge, astronomy eventually broke away from primitive religion and belief. As Aristotle, Copernicus, Newton, Einstein, and Hubble, generations of philosophical and scientific giants put forward epoch-making theories one after another, today's astronomy has developed into a mature subject system. _x000D_
_x000D_
Today, with the development of technology, astronomical research methods have changed rapidly, including advanced observation technologies such as adaptive optics and comprehensive aperture, as well as efficient computing capabilities such as supercomputers. In fact, the core issues that astronomers are concerned about are still propositions such as the origin of the universe, the ultimate fate of our planet, and the existence of extraterrestrial civilization. Although the final answers have not yet been found, with the update of detection technology, we are constantly gaining new understanding of these propositions. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course hopes to explain the basic concepts of astronomy, introduce the main research fields and research frontiers of astronomy, including the development history of astronomy, the solar system and planets, stars, galaxies, and the evolution of the universe, etc., so that students with different professional backgrounds, especially students who are not majoring in physics, can understand some common concepts of astronomy and the latest research progress.

Name: Arts Training (II)
Introduction:
Courses are only available to high-level art troupes. _x000D_
This course is a symphony orchestra rehearsal class, mainly for third-year undergraduate students who have just entered orchestra studies. The course content is based on orchestra training repertoire, with rehearsals and performances organized by band conductors and instructors.

Name: Engineering Drawing
Prerequisite: It is best to have received basic training in engineering design and design aesthetics, and have a certain understanding and experience of the needs of mechanical engineering design and the transformation of design ideas. After possessing these basic skills, students can fully understand the drawing expression methods, labeling specifications, and process requirements of engineering drawings, and basically master the ability to independently draw mechanical drawings that are relatively simple, comply with design specifications, and express clearly.
Introduction: "Engineering Drawing" teaches the theory and methods of drawing and reading engineering drawings. It is a core course on professional basic theory with strong practicality for non-mechanical engineering majors. Based on the theory of parallel projection, the course teaches the basic principles of engineering drawing formation, introduces relevant national standards, and introduces the drawing and reading methods of professional drawings.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (I)
Introduction: Calculus is an important basic course for this major. It provides the necessary foundation for the teaching of many subsequent courses, and also provides the necessary training for cultivating students' ability to work independently. Students mastering the basic content and methods of this course play a key role in meeting professional business training requirements.

Name: Linear Algebra and Geometry
Introduction: Linear algebra and geometry is one of the two introductory courses in college mathematics. Its research objects are determinants, linear equations, vector algebra, analytic geometry, quadratic forms, linear spaces, linear transformations, etc. The concepts and methods of linear algebra are widely used in subsequent courses. It is not only a very good mathematics course, but also a very good tool subject. It is widely used in many fields. For example, the solution of linear equations is the most basic algorithm of modern computer technology. Most models in physics and humanities need to be expressed through linear space.

Name: General Survey of Modern Engineering
Introduction:
Through special lectures, the history, current situation and development trends of various fields of modern engineering are introduced. To enable students to initially understand the basic concepts and fundamentals of modern engineering
Basic knowledge, understand the history, current situation and development trends of various fields of modern engineering.

Name: Mathematical Analysis (II)
Introduction: Calculus is an important basic course in engineering colleges. It provides the necessary foundation for the teaching of many subsequent courses, and also provides the necessary training for cultivating students' ability to work independently. Students mastering the basic content and methods of this course play a key role in meeting professional business training requirements.

Name: Ordinary Differential Equations
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), linear algebra and geometry
Introduction: Ordinary differential equations is an important basic course for all majors in the School of Engineering. The basic content includes elementary solutions, theory of linear differential equations and systems of equations, methods of solving linear differential equations and systems of equations with constant coefficients, basic theories of ordinary differential equations, and introduction to basic concepts and methods of qualitative theory and stability theory of ordinary differential equations. The learning requirements of this course are to master the basic concepts, basic solutions and basic theories of ordinary differential equations, and to develop the ability to analyze and solve problems using analytical methods.

Name: Theoretical Mechanics
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, general physics
Introduction: The basic knowledge of theoretical mechanics is widely used in engineering practice, such as static analysis, motion analysis and dynamic analysis. Theoretical mechanics is the main prerequisite course in mechanics major courses. Its basic concepts, basic theories and basic methods are the necessary foundation for a series of subsequent professional courses.

Name: Numerical Methods
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation
Introduction: Teach the theories and algorithms for using numerical methods to solve common mathematical problems, including interpolation and fitting, numerical differentiation and numerical integration, direct and iterative solutions to linear equations (sets), nonlinear equation (set) solution, matrix eigenvalue and eigenvector solution, and numerical solution to initial value problems of ordinary differential equations, etc., to cultivate the ability and skills in programming scientific calculation programs.

Name: Mechanics of Materials
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, theoretical mechanics
Introduction: As a basic mechanics course, the mechanics of materials course has the characteristics of an introduction to solid mechanics. Through the basic concepts of material mechanics, tension and compression, torsion and bending, complex stress states, pressure rod stability, elastic rod system energy method, etc., it mainly introduces the concepts and calculation methods of elastic rods and rod system structures in terms of strength, stiffness and stability, laying the foundation for subsequent courses.

Name: Advanced Algebra
Introduction: As a follow-up course to "Linear Algebra and Geometry", this course aims to deepen students' understanding of the abstract description of linear algebra. The main contents include: polynomial theory, linear transformation, Euclidean space and Euclidean transformation, Jordan standard form, λ-matrix, etc.

Name: Methods of Mathematical Physics (Part 1)
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), linear algebra and geometric, constant differential equation
Introduction: This course is a main basic course for undergraduate students majoring in Theoretical and Applied Mechanics of the Department of Mechanics and Engineering Science, School of Engineering, Peking University. It teaches various mathematical theories and methods used in mechanics, physics and various engineering scientific research, including the theory of functions of complex variables, variational methods and integral transformations, partial differential equations, etc. This course focuses on teaching students to master the above mathematical theories and methods to solve various mathematical physics problems that arise in mechanics, physics and engineering science.

Name: Mechanics of Materials Laboratory
Prerequisite: Students who choose a course must take the material mechanics course at the same time or have already taken the course.
Introduction: As an auxiliary course of the "Material Mechanics" course, the "Material Mechanics Experiment" includes mechanical properties testing of metal materials in tension, compression, bending, torsion and pressure rod stability experiments. Through course experimental teaching, students can deepen their understanding and mastery of basic knowledge of materials mechanics and train basic skills in mechanics experiments.

Name: Arts Training (VI)
Introduction:
Courses are only available to high-level art troupes. _x000D_
Cultivating new talents with parallel development of theoretical and practical abilities, and exploring an interdisciplinary education model with two-way interaction between research and techniques are the foundation of this course. Chinese music, in the current era of globalization, has made a leap from quantity to quality in both its conceptual connotation and extension than before. Different from the situation before 1840, all musical life that takes place in China and is related to Chinese culture can be accepted and understood as the category of Chinese music. Through different forms of combinations and designs such as concert performances, voice arranging, band arrangement, chamber music training, original classic reading, comparison of Chinese and Western music history and culture, and in-person guidance and performances by global music masters, the course uses a hierarchical teaching method to eliminate the deficiencies and limitations of previous music training in combining theory and practice, and on the basis of fully developing students' musical interests. On the basis of this, combined with the cutting-edge experience of similar courses around the world, it emphasizes cross-disciplinary interaction, integration inside and outside the classroom, step-by-step, elementary, intermediate, advanced, 1-6 stages, under the premise of collective teaching and group training, with high-level concerts and relatively solid theoretical study and research, in order to achieve the goal of Peking University in China's leading position in relevant courses within the specified time. Chinese Music Theory and Practice (1) is the first stage of the series of courses (Part 1). Learners need to have a certain foundation of Chinese and Western musical instruments and take the pre-class exam. Those who pass will be divided into groups according to the voice part and level to participate in the Chinese Music Society Orchestra and Transmission Class to participate in class training. In addition to attendance, course evaluation includes concert performance and reading and learning of theoretical classics.

Name: Introduction to Robotics: Programming and Practice
Introduction: This is an introductory course for students to understand the theory and practice of robotics. In the course project, students will build a simple robot and program it to interact with the environment and complete basic tasks involving movement, sensory data, and decision-making. The course content is divided into the following three aspects: The first part is a brief introduction to robotics, covering its history and current developments. Students will conduct relevant experiments using fish-shaped robots and body-sensory controlled humanoid robots developed by the in-house team. The second part involves the programming practice of various robot hardware, such as switches, LED lights, buzzers, sensors and transmission devices. The final part covers the design and construction of the robot, as well as the demonstration of innovative applications. Students will be asked to build simple robots to solve some real-world problems.

Name: Engineering CAD (1)
Introduction: Teaching AutoCAD basic operations and CAD graphic development techniques. These include CAD Basics, AutoCAD Graphics Operations, Document-based Secondary Development Technologies, Windows Graphic Interactive Technologies, and ObjectARX Programming Technologies. The course focused on CAD graphic development techniques based on C/C++.

Name: Probability and Mathematical Statistics
Introduction: Probability and mathematical statistics are one of the important branches of mathematics that pay equal attention to theory and practice. This course is aimed at senior undergraduates and graduate students. It teaches the basic knowledge of probability theory, random variables and their probability distributions, numerical characteristics of random variables, parameter estimation of random variables, hypothesis testing, linear regression analysis and the basics of stochastic processes.

Name: Methods of Mathematical Physics (Part 2)
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, mathematical physics (top)
Introduction: This course mainly explains the basic theory of partial differential equations, including the basic concepts of partial differential equations and three common basic analytical solution methods (separation of variables method, integral transformation method and Green's function method).

Name: Fluid Mechanics (Part 1)
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), constant differential equation, mathematical physics equation, theoretical mechanics
Introduction:
The substance consists essentially of two main categories, liquids and solids, in which flow can occur, which can result in continuous macro-formation, and liquids, gases, plasma, etc., which are widely present and involved in natural and industrial technologies. For example, air and water are the most common fluids. Unlike the truncation, fluid movements usually have numerous degrees of freedom and mobility patterns are much more complex and require a quantitative characterization of the concept of the field, with the control equation being a differential equation of time and space coordinates as a variable. Hydrodynamics focuses on the effects of various forces, the static and motional state of the fluid itself and the dynamics and flow patterns of the fluid and solid walls when they are relatively mobile. As an important branch of mechanics, as in mechanics itself, hydrodynamics is both a basic science and a technical science with wide application. Its applications cover the fields of aviation, space, astrophysics, geophysical, atmospheric, ocean, hydro, mechanical, energy, power, chemical, light, mining, metallurgical, civil, transport, automation, information, agriculture, biology, medicine, environment and sports.
This course is compulsory in the third year of the undergraduate degree in theoretical and applied mechanics at Beijing University. The primary teaching of basic concepts and basic content of hydrodynamics gives students an initial qualitative and quantitative understanding of the subject and provides a more solid basis for subsequent learning and work.
The course is taught in the next two semesters. Three hours a week. The main features of the fall semester are the preliminary theory and condensation, basic concepts of hydrodynamics, basic equations of hydrodynamics, vortex movements in fluids, hydrostatics, Bernoulian points and kinetics.

Name: Solid Mechanics Laboratory
Introduction: This course seeks to provide students with basic experimental methods in solid mechanics, with basic experimental skills and some experimental theory. To this end, the course consists of two main components: the basic principles of the methods in solid mechanics experiments; and specific experimental methods and techniques. The main elements are: 1. The theoretical basis for modelling experiments; 2. Test machines and devices for measuring deformation

Name: Introduction to Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
Introduction: This course is intended for senior (3rd-4th grade) undergraduate students in the School of Engineering. In view of the thermodynamics and statistical mechanics problems that will be encountered in modern mechanical research, this article systematically introduces systematic thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, especially the basic methods and applications of modern thermodynamics and statistical mechanics. Through the course, students can understand the basic principles of thermodynamics and statistical mechanics and related common methods.

Name: Environmental Mechanics
Introduction: This course is an elective course offered to undergraduate students in the School of Engineering. The purpose of the course is to enable students to understand mechanical issues related to the environment. The main content includes the transport and diffusion laws of pollutants in the atmosphere and waters, seepage theory in porous media (soil, rock strata), basic mechanical characteristics of common environmental disasters (floods, tsunamis, dam breaks, landslides), and numerical simulation methods of environmental (disaster) mechanics. Through the study of this course, students are required to understand the basic equations of environment, seepage and hydrodynamics, analysis methods of typical environmental mechanics problems, and numerical simulation methods of complex environmental disasters, laying a foundation for the study of subsequent professional courses and research in related majors.

Name: Arts Training (VII)
Introduction: Through the teaching of the history of the lesbian spectrum, the method of analysing the actions of the lesbian spectrum and the experience of the reading practice of the lesbian spectrum, the course gives students an initial insight into the way in which the lesbian spectrum analyses the ways in which the human action language is described and lays the foundation for the analysis of different types of dance using the action-based language. The course is carried out from the perspective of the Raban “Structural Dance Spectronomy” and provides students with an understanding of the basic elements of human action in the Raban “Structural Spectronomy” perspective, through the recognition of the “Structural Building” symbol of human action. It also provides students with an analytical syntax of human action by means of tiered instruction in the “structured dance spectrum”, which gives them the initial ability to analyse the language of dance action. Following the development of the analytical capabilities of the “action cornerstone” and “action structure”, the course will provide students with an understanding of the rich elements of human action and an initial understanding of the different styles of the dance arts analysed by the “power dance spectrum”. The final course will enable students to learn about the motivations, messages or intentions of human actions and to analyse their salient features through the experience of the "thematic dance spectrum". High-level arts groups are selected.

Name: Theory of Vibrations
Prerequisite: Material mechanics, elasticity, mathematical physics equations, calculus, algebra
Introduction: The main content of this course is the linear vibration theory of the limited freedom system and continuum, which includes the inherent vibration and dynamic response of the limited freedom system, the inherent vibration and dynamic response of structures such as poles, beams, plates, etc., and approximate calculation. Briefly describe the characteristics and nature of non-linear vibration systems.

Name: Fluid Mechanics Laboratory
Introduction: Fluid mechanics experiments are indispensable for students majoring in mechanics, especially those majoring in fluid mechanics. This course can improve students' ability to analyze and solve problems, and enable students to have a deep understanding of typical fluid physics phenomena. The course teaches classic fluid experimental methods and techniques and guides students to conduct independent experiments.

Name: Fundamentals of Continuum Mechanics
Prerequisite: Calculus, linear algebra, theoretical mechanics, thermal or thermodynamics
Introduction: This course is the common foundation for a series of related courses such as fluid mechanics, elastic mechanics, and plastic mechanics. The plan is to teach tensor operations, continuum kinematics, strain stress states, basic conservation laws, establish models of ideal fluids, viscous fluids and elastic bodies, and analyze some simple examples of continuum motion.

Name: Aircraft Design and Propulsion
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the main principles of jet propulsion technology, the basic structure and main design methods of aeroengines. The course will help students understand the main criteria for current aircraft engine selection, and understand the basic composition, main functions and basic technical parameters of each component of an aeroengine. Students will also learn how to apply a variety of fundamental knowledge to complex engineering problems. Through the study of this course, students will be able to select power systems for different aircraft and design the main technical parameters of power devices for new flight systems.

Name: General History of China (Ancient Period)
Introduction: General History of China (Ancient Part) is a general elective course for the whole school and is taught to non-history undergraduate students. This course takes the general trend of the evolution of ancient Chinese political history as the main clue, allowing students to have a relatively clear framework for the development of ancient Chinese history. At the same time, we pay attention to the historical process of major issues such as the formation of the Chinese nation and the formation of China's territory, and strive to grasp the characteristics of each historical stage in the development and evolution of ancient politics, institutions, economy, and society. During the teaching process, the knowledge and academic aspects of history are combined, and the latest research results in the academic field are absorbed, hoping to enhance students' interest in ancient Chinese history and stimulate students' thinking.

Name: Theory of Elasticity
Prerequisite: Mathematic physics equation, theoretical mechanics, material mechanics

Name: Advanced Dynamics
Prerequisite: Calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, general physics, theoretical mechanics
Introduction: Advanced dynamics mainly introduces preliminary analytical dynamics, micro-vibration theory and dynamics of three-dimensional motion of rigid bodies. The theory and methods of analytical dynamics have important applications in modern physics and engineering practice, and are also the basis for later courses in mechanics majors. Microvibration theory has important applications in modern engineering practice. The three-dimensional kinematics and dynamics of rigid bodies are the theoretical basis of aerospace vehicles.

Name: Fluid Mechanics (Part 2)
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), constant differential equation, mathematical physics equation, theoretical mechanics
Introduction:
Materials basically include two categories: fluids and solids according to their motion forms. Fluids are forms in which flow can occur, that is, continuous macroscopic deformation. They also include liquids, gases, plasmas, etc., which are widely present and involved in nature and industrial technology. For example, air and water are the most common fluids. Different from rigid bodies, fluid motion usually has countless degrees of freedom, and the flow pattern is much more complex, which needs to be quantitatively described using the concept of field. The governing equation is a partial differential equation with time and space coordinates as independent variables. Fluid mechanics mainly studies the static state and motion state of the fluid itself under the action of various forces, as well as the mechanical interaction and flow laws when there is relative motion between the fluid and the solid boundary wall. As an important branch of mechanics, like mechanics itself, fluid mechanics is both a basic science and a technical science with wide applications. Its applications cover aviation, aerospace, astrophysics, geophysics, atmosphere, ocean, water conservancy, machinery, energy, power, chemical industry, light industry, mining, metallurgy, civil engineering, transportation, automation, information, agriculture, biology, medicine, environment, sports and other fields. _x000D_
    This course is a required course for third-year undergraduate students majoring in Theoretical and Applied Mechanics at Peking University. It mainly teaches the basic concepts and content of fluid mechanics, so that students can have a preliminary qualitative and quantitative understanding of this subject and lay a solid foundation for future study and work. _x000D_
    This course is taught in two semesters, the upper and lower semesters. 3 hours per week. The main content of the spring semester is the irrotational motion of ideal incompressible fluids (including plane potential flow, axisymmetric potential flow, introduction to finite span wing theory, unsteady potential flow and additional mass, etc.), the motion of viscous incompressible fluids (including similarity laws, accurate solutions to laminar flow, low Reynolds number flow, boundary layers, preliminary turbulence, etc.), basic gas dynamics, etc.

Name: History of Modern Chinese Political Development
Introduction: The history of modern China is the process of the Chinese people striving for national independence and achieving national prosperity. It is the overall process of the transformation of Chinese society from a semi-colonial and semi-feudal society to a new democratic society and even a socialist society. It is also the process of China's transformation from a backward traditional agricultural country to a modern country. Therefore, the essence of political development in modern China is to create an independent nation-state and to develop the country in the direction of democracy and rule of law. This course takes the changes in the political field in the process of China's modernization as the main line, uses the Marxist political development theory as the guide, draws on the reasonable factors of Western political development theory, and conducts theoretical analysis of major events and important representatives of China's modern political development, such as China's party politics and political development in the early Republic of China, May Fourth political culture and Chinese political development, the maturity of Mao Zedong Thought and Chinese political development, the Cultural Revolution and the development of contemporary Chinese politics, Deng Xiaoping Theory and contemporary Chinese political development, comparative research on the political development of contemporary China and Russia, etc. In the process of discussing the development of modern and contemporary politics, the focus of teaching is democratization and legalization under the effective control of the state, especially the legalization process and the restrictive role of political culture on political development.

Name: Introduction to Public Administration
Introduction: This course is not only a general professional basic course for the School of Government, but also an elective course for schools and departments such as the School of Law and the Department of Sociology. This course comprehensively and systematically teaches the knowledge of the government (national administrative agencies) in managing national affairs, social affairs and its own affairs. Through the study and research of the nature and phenomenon, subject and object, concept and technology, content and form, system and process, history and future of these activities, students can understand the regularity of public administration and management, as well as the administrative theories and methods that promote the scientificization, legalization, standardization, rationalization, efficiency and modernization of these activities. On the basis of a comprehensive and systematic mastery of administrative management knowledge, this course combines theory with practice to enhance students' ability to understand and grasp current administrative management practice issues, especially the ability to understand and analyze contemporary Chinese public administration issues. It enables students to gradually develop the ability to observe, think, analyze and solve problems in the administrative management field. It also creates good conditions and lays a solid professional theoretical foundation for studying other public administration courses.

Name: College English ABC (I) (2)
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
The College English ABC (1)-(4) series of courses are aimed at undergraduate students of Peking University. The textbook used for College English ABC (1) is "New Concept English 1". This course aims to consolidate students’ English grammar and vocabulary learned in high school and further improve their comprehensive English abilities, especially their English listening, speaking, reading and writing abilities. Students are required to master a cumulative vocabulary of about 4,000 words, be able to read quickly at a speed of 200 words per minute, and be able to write a short essay of about 120 words in half an hour with relatively coherent content and basically correct grammar. In addition, by studying this course, students can enhance their cross-cultural awareness and thinking skills, develop independent learning habits, and lay a solid foundation for future English learning. _x000D_
Students are required to prepare before class and review after class according to the teaching arrangement, log in to the teaching platform for more than two hours of independent study every week, and complete prescribed online exercises, online tests and other tasks on time; teachers deepen students' understanding and mastery of the content they have learned through intensive lectures, testing, and organizing student discussions or reports in class.

Name: Modern Chinese Political Thought
Introduction: The content of this course is based on two main points, one of which is modernism and ideas that have prevailed in the form of the Qinghuang-Congan regime (1898-1949), such as socialist genres — anarchism, neo-villageism, Kirt, Tows, etc. — orthodox, Confucianization, restructuring, etc.; liberalism and conservative sects that advocate the “third path” between the two parties of the Communist Party; and intellectual and cultural rivalries among the factions. The second is post-CCP ideological debate, particularly after the reform and opening up of non-officials active in civil society, such as the New Confucianists, the New Authority, the New Left, the New Right, the New Nationalism, neo-populistism, the New Stateism, and so on, as well as reflections on revolutions and reforms and discussions about public intellectuals.

Name: Principles of Economics
Prerequisite: The curriculum requires students to have a high school mathematics base and no prior course requirements
Introduction: Principles of Economics is a compulsory course for undergraduates in the School of Government of Peking University. It is a basic course that helps students learn and master the basic knowledge of economics. This course will be taught in the form of special topics, focusing on relevant knowledge such as market supply and demand, elasticity and its application, resource allocation efficiency, taxation, production costs, market competition, production and growth, financial system, unemployment, monetary growth and inflation, etc., so that students can more completely grasp the basic theoretical framework of economics, have a more comprehensive understanding and deeper understanding of relevant economic knowledge, and have a certain understanding of cutting-edge economic theories. This course requires students to have a high school mathematics foundation.

Name: College English ABC (II) (2)
College: Department of English Language and Literature

Name: Islam and the Modern World
Introduction: This course is an optional course in general education for undergraduate students, which is based on materialism and uses history, sociology and politics. A disciplinary perspective looks at history and civilizational processes related to Islam. Islamism is an important element of contemporary international politics, and an understanding of the history and status of the Middle East region is an important condition for our understanding of the state of development of the world in the twenty-first century. The course will describe the religion and history of the Islamic region from a historical perspective. Name: New Public Management
Introduction:
In the late 1970s and early 1980s, a massive wave of administrative reform took place worldwide. This movement for change in public sector management, which engulfs both developed and developing countries, is called “new public administration”, “managerialism”, “market-based public administration”, “post-bureaucratic model” or “business-based government”. By the late 1990s, there was a growing tendency to use the concept of “new public administration”.
The understanding of new public management differs from the usual view of “marketization and socialization of public governance”. This course interprets the new public administration with a new perspective, considering that the core and essence of this reform is the transition from traditional bureaucratic layers of science to competitive bureaucracy, a new structure of balanced relations shaped by specific historical conditions in the 1980s between freedom and equality, government and markets, democracy and authority, social elites and ordinary people.
In response, the course will validate this entirely new interpretation through the following thematic analyses: democratic political analysis; bureaucratic administrative analysis of the subject; economic assumptions analysis; democratic political criticism; bureaucratic administrative criticism; contracting outsourcing, franchising and government contracting; transformation of government regulation patterns; entrepreneurial theory of government; innovation in resource-sharing governance models; competitive bureaucracy; democratic bureaucracy; the mystery of bureaucratic discipline; public administration; and limits to new public administration. The course will show students what a “change balance” and “competition bureaucracy” is and work with them to comprehensively analyze and validate the achievement of this “balance”.

Name: Educational Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: General psychology, development psychology, study of psychology (recommended first), university English (through level 4)
Introduction: Educational psychology courses (taught in English) can not only promote students to master the foreign language of educational psychology, but also improve students' ability to read original English works. It can also broaden students' horizons, so that their understanding of educational psychology is not limited to domestic research, and gradually approaches the international level of students of the same age and major. Through the study of this course, students must understand students' cognitive development and students' individual differences, master the views of behaviorism, cognitivism and social constructivism on learning, master the definition and stimulation of motivation and its relationship with teaching and learning, and master the impact of the creation of teaching environment on teaching. The purpose of this course is to enable students to master systematic theoretical knowledge of educational psychology, improve students' understanding and analytical and critical abilities of educational psychological phenomena, and enable students to initially apply the principles of educational psychology to discover, analyze and solve various practical problems in education and teaching during the course learning process.

Name: Research Methods in Psychology: MATLAB
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: It's suggested to start with Experimental Psychology.
Introduction: This course introduces basic methods of psychological research. Let students master the use of Matlab for psychological experiment programming and data statistical analysis; become familiar with commonly used psychophysical methods and use psychtoolbox to program psychological experiments; let students master the use of Matlab for common data statistical analysis and create charts that comply with journal specifications;

Name: Psychological Statistics (2)
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Psychological Statistics (2) is the second statistics course for undergraduates in the School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences. It extends the content of Psychological Statistics (1) to cover the basic use of statistics in psychological research. The goal of this course is to teach students how to correctly handle data in a variety of psychological research and applications. As a required course for undergraduate students in psychology, this course also provides preparation for the graduate course "Advanced Psychological Statistics."

Name: Research Methods in Psychology: MATLAB Computer Lab
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: "Psychological Research Methods - MATLAB Computer Practice" starts from the research ideas and methods of psychology, allowing students to systematically master the application and programming implementation of MATLAB software and PSYCHTOOLBOX toolkit in psychological research. The content includes mastering the basic knowledge of MATLAB and PSYCHTOOLBOX, using MATLAB and PSYCHTOOLBOX to design and generate visual and auditory stimuli commonly used in psychological experiments, response input, and interfaces with commonly used external devices (including virtual reality devices). And through practice, use MATLAB to conduct convenient data statistical analysis and create paper charts that conform to the APA paradigm, and use MATLAB programming to implement a variety of common psychophysical experimental designs.

Name: Psychological Measurement
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: First courses: experimental psychology; psychological statistics;
Introduction: This course is compulsory undergraduate instruction in the basic theory of psychological measurements and common measurement types.

Name: Experimental Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Psychology is an experimental science, and all branches of psychology require experimental methods to be studied. Experimental psychology is a branch of psychology regarding experimental methods, so it can be said that experimental psychology is the foundation of all psychology disciplines. _x000D_
The teaching purpose of experimental psychology can be summarized as follows: to learn the theories and experiments of experimental psychology and basically have the ability to independently design psychological experiments and analyze research results. _x000D_
The course first introduces general research methods such as experimental methods, psychophysical methods, and reaction time, and then selects major processes such as attention, perception, vision and hearing, memory, thinking, consciousness, psycholinguistics, emotion, and attribution to illustrate the application of the above methods. _x000D_

Name: Physiological Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: On the one hand, this course teaches the basic knowledge of physiological psychology and lays a solid foundation for students to study in related fields. On the other hand, students are introduced to cutting-edge scientific research work based on the lecturer's own scientific research work and the progress of international scientific research work in related fields. They not only learn the thinking and methods of scientific research work, grasp the research trends in related fields, broaden their horizons, but also learn the latest research technologies in related fields. The teaching content will also be considered to be combined with experimental courses to coordinate theoretical and practical teaching content. This course mainly introduces the history and research methods of physiological psychology, especially the brain imaging research methods that have emerged in recent years. Teach the research findings using these methods on perception, attention, memory, emotion, social cognition and other fields, as well as the psychological theories proposed based on these findings.

Name: Cognitive Neuroscience
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: General psychology, experimental psychology (or cognitive psychology)
Introduction: Cognitive neuroscience is an emerging edge subject that is rapidly developing in the international academic field in recent years. It is the intersection between cognitive science and neuroscience. It is necessary to combine the basic theoretical concepts of cognitive science, including physical symbolism, semiotic theory, ecological phenomenology, and modular theory, with the technical achievements and theoretical progress of contemporary brain research, and conduct highly interdisciplinary research on the laws of intelligent activity and brain mechanisms of the human brain. After an overview of the two major discipline systems of cognitive science and neuroscience, this course focuses on the use of different methods to study the neural mechanisms of different cognitive processes, including the main results and existing problems. This course can enable students to have a new understanding of new research progress on the basis of biological brain and intelligence in contemporary high-tech theoretical and technical issues.

Name: Psychology of Aging
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
According to predictions, by 2050, my country's elderly population over 65 years old will reach more than 320 million, accounting for approximately 1/5 of my country's total population and 1/4 of the world's elderly population. The issue of population aging and the resulting series of psychological issues such as improving the quality of life and life satisfaction of the elderly have become a hot topic for gerontology experts in my country and even around the world. How should we deal with the challenges posed by aging? Through the study of geriatric psychology, we can have a new understanding of the above series of problems and come up with corresponding solutions. _x000D_
Geriatric psychology is a science that studies the changes, characteristics, and laws of psychological activities of individuals and groups during the aging process after adulthood. It is a branch of developmental psychology that studies the psychological characteristics and changes of individuals in old age, also known as aging psychology. It is also an integral part of the emerging gerontology. Since human psychological activities are based on the functions of the nervous system and other organs and are restricted by society, geriatric psychology involves both biological and social aspects. The scope of research includes human psychological processes such as perception, learning, memory, and thinking, as well as changes caused by aging such as intelligence, personality, social adaptation, and geriatric diseases. Through the study of this course, students can have a more systematic understanding of the aging process and corresponding psychological changes, and make their own contributions to improving the quality of life of the elderly and promoting social harmony.

Name: Abnormal Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: There is no restriction on the need for pre-course courses for dual-degree students because they come from the faculties. If it's possible to finish general psychology, develop psychology, then do psychopsychiatry. Learn.
Introduction:
This course systematically introduces the definition, objects, and history of abnormal psychology; the biological basis of psychological abnormalities_x000D_
_x000D_

_x000D_
Memory, thinking and emotion, consciousness disorders, etc.; emotional psychosis: schizophrenia, affective psychosis; neurosis: obsessive-compulsive disorder, _x000D_
_x000D_
Phobia, anxiety disorder, hysteria, etc.; personality disorders, psychosexual disorders, psychophysiological disorders, intellectual retardation, etc.

Name: Physiological Psychology Laboratory
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
The purpose of the physio-psychological experiment course is to give students, through experiments, an initial mastery of the basic operating methods and techniques of physio-psychological experiments, as well as the validation and consolidation of the basic theories of physio-psychology. The main experimental technical methods include animal behaviour measurement techniques, neurosectionology, tissueology and animal brain surgery. The main experiment was sexual.
Hormonal base, hunger and thirst for brain mechanisms, learning, memory behavioral observations, emotional physiological indicators. A total of 12 experiments were conducted. Experimental animals are dominated by rats and mice.

Name: Topics in Neuroeconomics
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
This course will introduce some cutting-edge issues in neuroeconomics, which is an emerging frontier field. The content will include the cognitive and brain basis of value, risk, learning, choice, trust, morality, games and other issues in human decision-making, as well as its applications in finance, law, marketing, developmental psychology, computational psychiatry and other fields. The course is mainly aimed at graduate and undergraduate students with relevant background knowledge in psychology, economics, computer science, or neurobiology. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Techniques and Practice in Psychological Research
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Psychology research technology has developed rapidly driven by cutting-edge research methods such as brain imaging. This course is aimed at the actual needs of senior psychology undergraduate students in cultivating their scientific research capabilities. It combines the existing experimental equipment and conditions of Peking University to provide a comprehensive introduction to technologies including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), electroencephalography (EEG), electroencephalography (MEG), functional near-infrared imaging (fNIRS), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), and eye tracking. The teaching content includes the working principles, practical applications, data collection, analysis and processing of various technologies. At the same time, if conditions permit, practical operations or data processing will be carried out on the technologies involved in the course to achieve the best combination of theory and practice. Finally, this course will briefly introduce computational models commonly used in brain and cognitive science research. The study of brain mechanisms of cognitive and psychological processes is an important development trend in all fields of psychology in the future. The design of this course takes into account the different needs of research in various directions of psychology in examining brain mechanisms. Therefore, it is suitable for senior undergraduate students in various directions of basic psychology and applied psychology.

Name: Advanced Techniques in User Experience Research
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
User experience research integrates methods from psychology, design and computer science, and is committed to improving products, increasing user satisfaction, reducing user errors, and improving ergonomics. User experience research is an important direction in the application of engineering psychology and human-computer interaction to social practice. User experience research is an important factor in product success. Therefore, many high-tech companies and other product companies have user experience researcher and designer positions, such as Baidu, Alibaba, Tencent, etc. Many students who graduate from departments of psychology, sociology, design, and computer science work in user experience, product design, and product managers. _x000D_
_x000D_
"Advanced User Experience Research Technology" will explain to you 1. Commonly used user experience research methods, such as focus interviews, eye tracking, prototype design, card sorting, etc.; 2. Prototype design and tools (Axure, JustInMind); 3. A/B testing; 4. Introduction to Python language programming; 5. Introduction to eye tracker operation and the application of eye tracking technology in user experience; 6. Using Python to control and analyze eye tracker data 7. Work and successful experience in Fortune 500 companies. _x000D_
_x000D_
The lecturer professor, Dr. He Jibo, will invite Mr. Zhou Qi, the founder of the Python programmer community (technical director of Youshi Eye Tracking Technology Company), and Dr. Tan Zhiping, a senior eye tracker expert (President of Digital Synopsys), to share their experience in Python and eye trackers. _x000D_
_x000D_
We will provide 20 eye trackers so that every student can operate and use eye trackers. Master the key core technologies for user experience research in enterprises, such as prototyping, data analysis, and eye tracking technology. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is suitable for students from the Department of Psychology, Sociology, Design and Computer Science, as well as those working in user experience research, product design, product managers and entrepreneurship. This course is also suitable for undergraduate and postgraduate students. The Python data analysis methods and eye trackers described in the course will be of great help to you in basic research work and paper writing in psychology. _x000D_

Name: Social and Personality Development
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course aims to introduce the main theories and research methods in the field of children's social development. The general rules of children's social development, influencing factors and the current research status in this field are introduced in a topic-by-topic manner.

Name: Time and Cognition
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Time plays an important role in cognitive processing and daily life that cannot be ignored. This course uses an all-English teaching method. Through the introduction and discussion of a series of topics such as temporal perception, time distance estimation, sensorimotor synchronization, subjective present, daily rhythm, etc., it aims to provide students with a broad perspective in the fields related to time and cognition, understand the cutting-edge issues and research methods in this field, stimulate students' curiosity and enthusiasm for scientific research, and lay a solid foundation for them to engage in related research in the future.

Name: Contemporary Chinese Law and Society
Introduction: Law is a basic phenomenon of modern society. Since the end of the 19th century, from the reform and reform to the construction of the rule of law, China has gradually moved towards the rule of law. We are in an era of rule of law. Against this background, the historical origins, development process, difficulties, challenges and future trends of China's rule of law have become topics that every Chinese citizen should be concerned about and understand. This course is taught to all undergraduates in the university. The content revolves around a series of key issues in contemporary Chinese law and society. It not only teaches the basic knowledge of Chinese law (especially public law), but also pays attention to the interaction and interweaving of Chinese legal thought, discourse and practice with multiple factors such as politics, economy and culture in the historical process. The goal of this course is to help students establish their interest and basic understanding of legal issues, gain an understanding of the perspectives and approaches from which lawyers view the world and think about problems, encourage students to explore the connection between law and the profession, and understand the legalization process we are currently experiencing.

Name: Consumer Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: One of the main elements of the curriculum, which applies the basics of psychological studies, is the basic concepts of consumer behaviour, consumer psychology and marketing, the needs and motivations of individual consumers, personality and consumer behaviour, the psychological image of consumers, the role of perception, the participation of learning and consumption, attitudes and consumption, communication and consumption behaviour, group dynamics and consumption, the role of families, social class and consumption, the influence of culture, consumer decision-making and marketing. The course is based on the operation of international market marketing, lessons learned, systematic analysis of consumer behaviour, exploration of appropriate marketing responses, development of expertise in consumer psychology through theoretical and practical integration, and two to three weeks of internship.

Name: Human-Computer Interaction and User Experience
Introduction: This course is a professional course that systematically introduces the principles, methods and user experience of human-computer interaction. Content includes: basic concepts, models and processes of human-computer interaction, human-computer interface, user experience and user research, interaction design and evaluation, etc. This course is targeted at undergraduate students in the Department of Information Management. The teaching methods include classroom lectures and discussions, after-class assignments and team projects.

Name: Cognitive Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Cognitive psychology emerged in the mid-20th century to study the inner processes of psychological and behavioral events. This course will combine specific research to teach the basic contents of cognitive psychology: perception, attention and consciousness, memory and knowledge representation, representation, language, reasoning and decision-making, etc. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Psychological Counseling and Therapy
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences

In addition, the curriculum is based on the knowledge and skills of certain psychological measurements. The basic objectives of this course are: (1) knowledge: initial knowledge of the ethics and underlying theory of psychological counselling and treatment; (2) skills acquisition: initial knowledge of the basic skills of psychological counselling and treatment. This course focuses on the following issues: (1) What is psychological counselling and treatment? (2) What are the theories of psychological counselling and treatment? (3) What is the process of counselling and treatment? What technologies are used? The main elements of this course are: (1) Basic knowledge: definition of psychological counselling and treatment, ethics, therapeutic relationships, basic theory of dynamic psychotherapy, basic theory of cognitive therapy, basic theory of behavioural therapy, basic theory of family therapy, basic theory of diagnostics, etc. (2) Basic skills: effective listening, technical clarification, inter se, clinical norms and strategies, assessment techniques, identification, definition and evaluation of treatment objectives, etc. As we have encountered clinically, counselling and treatment is a complex process, and learning the theory and technology of counselling and treatment requires a long time to accumulate, and this course is the first step you take into clinical counselling and treatment practice. I am pleased to be able to start studying and exploring the mystery of psychological counselling and treatment with the students who have taken this course, and I hope that the students who have taken this course will be able to participate actively in the teaching process and acquire the required knowledge and basic skills by means of discussions, exercises, etc., so that our teaching and learning can become an effective interaction that will provide a good basis for further in-depth learning of psychological counselling and treatment in the future. In this course, there are various forms of teaching, including teaching, training, experience and discussion. By doing so, I hope that the students who have chosen this course will not only have a relatively systematic understanding of the theory and techniques of psychological counselling and treatment, but will also have an unexpected gain: find themselves more open to themselves and better able to explore themselves. Now, let's get into this class and learn and experience the process of inner growth!

Name: Learning and Behavior
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Learning and its behavioural shaping is a very important field of study in psychology and neuroscience. Research in this area focuses on how people and animals learn to obtain rewards and avoid risks, as well as on the principles and nervous mechanisms behind these phenomena. This course will provide a systematic introduction to classic studies and theories, such as the reflection of classical conditions and the reflection of operational conditions, and on this basis describe the basic principles of learning and its application in different areas of psychology. The course will also describe the nervous mechanisms behind learning and how learning to influence behaviour by regulating basic cognitive processes in the brain. The course will conclude with an introduction to the application of learning theory in the area of contemporary artificial intelligence.

In parallel with teaching and analysing classic works, teachers conduct an in-depth analysis of the author ' s life, the general style of creation and the historical background of the work, the aesthetic soundings and the content of ideas.
