Name: Life Education: Foundations of a Successful Life
Introduction:
Life education courses provide college students with basic and necessary life knowledge and skills, helping them understand personal management, self-awareness, interpersonal relationships, love and sex, and start making wise choices. Our goal is to give students the confidence to begin a holistic, healthy and meaningful life journey. _x000D_
After completing this course, students should be able to develop plans to manage their time, money, and stress based on their personal values. Understand and articulate what special and unique qualities they have in their relationships with others. Build multiple healthy relationships, set boundaries for each relationship, and be able to resolve conflicts in relationships step-by-step. Clearly explain healthy relationships and sexual responsibility, and the steps they take to prepare for a successful relationship and marriage. _x000D_
This course consists of 4 modules and 15 lessons. It includes four major modules: 1) wise decision-making, 2) my relationship with myself, 3) my relationship with others, 4) love, sex, and marriage. The first module, Wise Decisions, includes 5 lectures: 1) The foundation of a successful life; 2) Wisdom and responsibility; 3) Personal time management; 4) How to manage stress, 5) Personal money management; The second module, My Relationship with Myself, includes 4 lectures: 1) Understanding myself, 2) Am I who others see me? 3) Develop character and 4) my values. The third module, "My Relationship with Others," includes 3 lectures: 1) Lifelong Friends, 2) Conflict Resolution, and 3) Interpersonal Relationship Workshop. The fourth module "Love, Sex, and Marriage" includes 3 lectures: 1) Is it love? Or something else? 2) Why does true love have to wait? 3) Prepare for marriage. _x000D_
This course uses flexible and diverse educational methods such as teacher lectures and students' active participation in group discussions. Emphasis is placed on students applying the knowledge and principles they have learned to their own lives. _x000D_
This course is completed in conjunction with a team of professional teachers sent by the Red Cross Society of China College Student Soul Sunshine Project Office to work with our teachers. Bilingual teaching in English and Chinese.

Name: Selected Readings from Classic British and American Essays
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The course draws on the historical developments in British and American scripts, and provides a basic understanding and understanding of the cultural evolution and linguistic characteristics of English and American scripts by reading and giving lectures on some of the classic excerpts of English and American scripts at the beginning of the 17th and 20th centuries. It significantly enhances English reading skills and understanding and awareness of the negative British and American cultural consciousness contained in English. It also provides a basic understanding of major British and American historical events and of the state of critical thinking in various historical periods, and lays the foundation for future higher levels of English writing and literary translation for students. It is a basic course for the development of English for the purpose of understanding Western culture and thus for the exercise of English. In order to enhance the skills of English (language) in the course, the language of instruction in the course is mainly English and is explained in a limited number of Chinese languages. There may be classroom discussions in the course where students choose to ask questions and discuss them in English or Chinese, depending on their needs.

Name: Population Sociology
Introduction: The course provides students with the most basic demographic knowledge and presents basic theories and research methods for understanding and analysing demographic phenomena and demographic changes from a sociological perspective.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course selects a series of representative modern Chinese poets as objects of discussion, such as Hu Shi, Guo Moruo, Wen Yiduo, Xu Zhimo, Dai Wangshu, Bian Zhilin, Ai Qing, and Mu Dan. Based on the analysis of specific works, it shows the efforts of modern Chinese poets in language, form, and concepts, thereby outlining the trajectory of the pursuit of modernity in new poetry. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Social Survey and Research Methods
Introduction:
Social survey research is a process of collecting data, analyzing data and making scientific explanations in an objective and systematic manner, following strict procedures and using effective methods in order to discover and answer various problems in the social field. The purpose of this course is to systematically introduce the basic principles, procedures, methods and applications of social survey research. _x000D_
There are four basic methods of social science research: statistical survey method, field research method, experimental method, and literature method. This course focuses on explaining and discussing the four research methods widely used in sociological research. It introduces in detail the methodological background, basic principles, essential characteristics, related concepts, logical methods, operating procedures, limitations and application scope of each research method, and lists a large number of examples to illustrate. The purpose is to enable students to master the basic survey research methods of sociology and the main sociological methodological viewpoints, lay a foundation for learning and mastering the theories and methods of various fields, sub-disciplines, and topics of social research, and be able to engage in and organize general and professional social survey research. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Tang Dynasty Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The novels of the Tang Dynasty are an extremely important part of ancient Chinese novels. They have achieved a high degree of achievement and have a great influence on the literature of future generations. This course will be taught in the following three parts: 1. The current research status of novels in the Tang Dynasty; 2. The overview and influence of novels in the Tang Dynasty; 3. An in-depth introduction to famous novelists and their works in the Tang Dynasty, leading students to read classic novel texts in detail. This allows students to gain a comprehensive and intuitive understanding of Tang Dynasty novels.

Name: General Survey of World History
Introduction: This course is a basic course for world history majors for undergraduates in the Department of History at Peking University. It aims to help students understand as much basic information about the subject of "world history" as widely as possible, learn basic theories and methods for macroscopic examination of human history, cultivate the ability to independently construct an understanding framework of overall human history, and lay the foundation for future professional studies. The basic contents include: 1) Explanation of the concept of "world history" (origin and evolution; the significance of learning world history; the construction process of the Chinese world history discipline; the main traditions of the Western world history discipline); 2) the basic situation of modern Western macro-world history (from the perspective of cultural unity) On the transformation to cultural pluralism, the major schools of contemporary global history or history of civilization); 3. The basic viewpoint of the Peking University version of "History of World Civilizations" ("World History" should be understood as the history of world civilizations evolving in interactions - explained in conjunction with the basic processes of world history).

Name: Social Statistics
Introduction: The course provides a systematic presentation of the underlying principles, basic concepts and main elements of social statistics, detailing the operational procedures and specific methods of statistical descriptions and inferences by the measurement level of variables. Through this course, basic knowledge of statistics and commonly used statistical techniques will enable the processing of most statistics in an independent and complete manner. Since the course is intended for undergraduate students, the course is limited to primary social statistics and is limited to single and double variables.

Name: Social Psychology
Prerequisite: " Social science generals " , " Foreign sociology doctrine (up and down) "
Introduction:
Course objectives

1. Basic knowledge of the conceptual framework of social psychology, classical research, frontier debates, research hot spots and basic methods.
2. Starting to develop a literature literacy capacity in English and a search for documentation in Chinese and English.
3. Initial knowledge of the problem of social psychology and research perspectives, and the ability to use theories and methods to analyse and explain the psychological difficulties of social transformation in China.
4. To lay the foundations for the study of social psychology.

Name: Chinese Society
Prerequisite: Sociological overview, development sociology, organization sociology
Introduction: Undergraduate courses in sociology. Using a sociological perspective, the course selects materials such as documentaries of historical archives, as well as case videos of contemporary society, to discuss recent changes in society, with a view to helping students understand the characteristics of group roles/social relations/social structures/social organization/social behaviour/social conflict and order/social mindsets in Chinese society.

Name: Sociology of Development
Prerequisite: Social science generalists, foreign sociological literature
Introduction: Use sociological analysis methods to study the changes and consequences of economic and social systems. Different from general development sociology, the two characteristics of this course are (1) emphasizing empirical research and empirical research methods; (2) focusing on China studies. Taking China's development process in the past century as the main line, we will discuss various methods and issues in empirical research on institutional changes and social transformation. Through the study of this course, students can become familiar with some basic issues and viewpoints in the field of China studies, and learn to use sociological methods to understand and analyze real-life problems.

Name: Data Analysis Techniques
Prerequisite:
Sociology General
Social surveys and research methods Learn.
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the basic principles, operations and applications of SPSS (statistical package for the social science) data analysis. The main contents include: basic knowledge of SPSS and data entry, writing SPSS command files, using Frequencies for data summary, descriptive statistics (application of Descriptives and Explore), data transformation, cross-summarization and correlation analysis (Crosstabs Application), difference in descriptor population mean (application of Means process), mean comparison analysis (T-Test process), analysis of variance ANOVA, correlation analysis (Correlate process analysis), simple linear correlation (univariate linear regression analysis), SPSS statistical graphics, etc.

Name: Social Stratification and Social Mobility

Name: Behavioral Economics
Introduction:
Behavioral economics is currently a frontier and hot research field in economics. Behavioral economics starts from exploring whether the assumption of rational people is fully consistent with reality, combines psychology and economic analysis methods, studies how human psychological factors affect economic behavior, and then provides unique policy suggestions. This is of great significance to our understanding of financial crises and real economic behavior. _x000D_
This course systematically introduces the main content and methodology of behavioral economics, discusses its development process, and its mutually reinforcing relationship with neoclassical economics. This course will draw on a large number of laboratory experiments, field experiments and empirical evidence to describe how people systematically deviate from the rational person assumption in actual decision-making. The main topics include: social preferences, reference point preferences, time preference inconsistency and self-control issues, deviations in probability judgments, overconfidence, limited game thinking ability, etc. On the basis of this evidence, we will discuss how to modify existing economic models to more accurately describe people's decision-making psychology and behavior. We will also focus on the application of these behavioral models in various economic fields, such as labor supply, savings and consumption, risk decision-making and finance, and also introduce the results of the development of behavioral finance to a certain extent. Finally, we discuss policy recommendations from behavioral economics. This kind of advice is usually low-cost, highly effective and implicit, and often even contains maternal and humanistic care. _x000D_

Name: Greek and Roman Mythology
Introduction:
It is generally believed that ancient Greek civilization is one of the two main sources in the history of the development of Western civilization. It has the same important status and influence as the Hebrew civilization, which is the other main source. Mythology is an essential part of ancient Greek civilization. It was later integrated with ancient Roman mythology and is usually collectively referred to as Greco-Roman mythology. It has been passed down from generation to generation and has lasted for about three thousand years. Greek and Roman mythology had a very important impact on the formation and development of Western language, culture, thought, literature and many other aspects, and its influence still exists today and has spread to other regions and nationalities in the world, such as China, Japan and other Asian countries. _x000D_
For students majoring in English language and literature, a more systematic understanding of Greek and Roman mythology will help to gain a broader and deeper understanding of English language, literature and culture, as well as a broader and deeper understanding of the history of the development of Western civilization and its typical characteristics. This course is intended to be based on "Greek and Roman Mythology" and self-compiled English materials. It will teach the historical background of the formation and evolution of Greek and Roman mythology, read and analyze classic stories and legends about Greek and Roman gods and heroes, and explain their multi-faceted value and significance. _x000D_

_x000D_

This course is divided into two parts. The first is to learn the theory, methods and techniques of socioeconomic survey in the classroom, master the CHARLS questionnaire, and practice interview skills. The content of the CHARLS questionnaire covers many aspects, including basic demographic information of the respondent and his/her family, family composition, transfer payments between family members, respondent's health status, use of medical services, use of medical insurance, employment, retirement, income, expenses and assets, etc. The survey of each household takes about 3 hours, and the questions are very professional, so learning the content of the questionnaire is an important part of this course.	_x000D_

Name: Stylistic Appreciation of English Literature
Prerequisite: Course on fine reading, general reading, introduction to literature, analysis of works
Introduction:
This course is designed to help students improve their ability to appreciate and analyze literary styles. When reading literary works, students tend to focus on the plot, characters, and story background, ignoring the artistry of the author's choice of words and sentences, and the important role the author's word choice plays in expressing the theme. This situation is especially common when reading and analyzing novels. The artistic value or subtle expression of thematic meaning of many literary works depends to a large extent on the author's choice of words and sentences. This course requires students to break away from the interpretation routines that focus on the storyline, characters, background, etc., pay full attention to the artistry of the author's word choice, and better grasp the connection between the author's word choice and sentence meaning and the meaning of the theme. Strive to achieve a better understanding of the artistry and thematic significance of the work through stylistic analysis. _x000D_
This course introduces some practical stylistic analysis models and methods and compares these different methods. The focus is on helping students improve their ability to appreciate and analyze stylistic styles. _x000D_
The main object of analysis is novels, especially short stories. _x000D_
Key Points and Difficulties: Unlike content components such as plot, characters, and background, the artistry of the author's choice of words and sentences is difficult to grasp. Students lack sensitivity in this area at the beginning. It is necessary to help students gradually master the method of stylistic analysis through class analysis and student practice, and better examine the relationship between the author's choice of words and sentences, the theme, and the artistic effect. _x000D_

Name: Macroeconomics and Health
Introduction: Over the past 30 years of reform and opening up, China has transformed from a highly centralized planned economy to a dynamic socialist market economy, experienced rapid economic growth rarely seen in human history, and has become the world's second largest economy. Economic growth promotes national wealth, while constantly changing the stage conditions of social and economic development, making it inevitable to transform the economic development model. The "Twelfth Five-Year Plan" proposes that transforming the economic development model is the main line of China's future development, and "people's livelihood first" is the central principle of national resource allocation. As the connotation of people's livelihood and well-being, the relationship between national health and economic development is fundamental: health is not only the eternal goal of human development, but also the human capital necessary for human development. Since the outbreak of SARS in 2003, China has begun an unprecedented social discussion on the issue of "difficulty and expense of medical treatment". Macroeconomics and health investment are the core issues. The reform of the national medical system was subsequently launched, and the State Council's medical reform plan was introduced in 2009. In the past four years since the implementation of the national medical reform, through the relevant institutional arrangements and impacts of the medical reform, have there been any changes in national health, service efficiency, and the macroeconomy? Recently, the Third Plenary Session of the 18th CPC Central Committee clearly stated that the market should play a decisive role in allocating resources. How should the national medical reform carry out corresponding transformation and upgrading? This course will guide students to systematically discuss the "ten major relationships" between macroeconomics and national health, the medical market, and the medical reform system from the perspective of human development.

Name: Intensive English Reading (IV)
Introduction: Basic objectives of the curriculum: This course is compulsory for the second grade of English undergraduate students and selects 8-10 classic articles on Western thought and literature for students to read carefully. Students need to understand the main ideas and arguments of the articles and to know the complex language of the articles, and the hard words of focus should be interpreted in English (paraphrase).

Introduction:

Name: Consumer Culture and the Aesthetics of Existence
Introduction:
The following content will be taught in class and designated works will be read to improve students' ability to understand contemporary consumer culture. Teaching content: The aesthetic dimension of consumer culture, the oppression of capital covered by aesthetics, the disenchantment of the concept of destiny, consumer culture and the objectification of people, consumer culture and self-shaping, consumer culture, aestheticism and the Bubo tribe, the historical evolution of the image of Salome, the symbolic value and aesthetic generalization of commodities, the illusion of the middle class and the expansion of capital, resistance to consumer culture: guerrilla warfare and pleasure, beauty, capital and agency aesthetics. _x000D_

Name: British and American Drama
Introduction: Selected readings of six modern plays will give students a preliminary understanding of the language and form of drama. The scripts read are all representative works of important writers, and are representative in terms of ideological content and dramatic form. Combined with reading the script, a systematic introduction to the theory and practice of drama will be given.

Name: Literature and Society
Prerequisite: This course is optional for the third year of the English major, and students should have a better English base before opting for the course and complete the compulsory English literature history and choice.
Introduction:
Through complete reading of six famous satirical works (Johnson's play "The Fox", Dryden's poem "The Sons of Flecknoe", Pope's poem "The Robbery", Swift's satirical novel "Gulliver's Travels" (Volume 4), Byron's poem "The Phantom of the Trial" and Orwell's allegorical novel "Animal Farm"), students will improve their ability to analyze and appreciate literary works and their critical writing skills, and deepen their understanding of British literature and social development. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Practicum in Financial Markets and Institutions
Prerequisite: Basic courses in financial market science, finance or similar finance.
Introduction: The course brings leading figures from the financial practice community to the classroom, where professionals teach them practical knowledge of the financial field and communicate with them in close proximity with a view to building bridges between theory and practice. The course mainly invites heads of departments or senior practitioners of large financial institutions to act as lecturers and to present and discuss issues of focus and interest in China ' s financial markets, covering the priority operations of financial institutions such as investment banks, commercial banks, funds, trusts, leases, venture capital, Internet finance, etc. For each type of institution, the course will provide detailed information on the pattern and development prospects of the sector, its internal organizational structure, business model, products and services, corresponding career opportunities, etc.

Name: History of English Literature (II)
Prerequisite: The course is compulsory for English literature students who have completed a two-year course in English literature called Quest, British History I and other first and second grade English literature and English writing.
Introduction: The course teaches English literature during the period of romanticism, Victoria and the twentieth century, mainly before World War II.

Name: Contemporary Chinese and American Fiction in Comparative Perspective
Introduction: This course is designed for senior undergraduate students to understand and study the historical background, narrative methodology and subject expression of contemporary novels in the United States by reading the works of seven contemporary American novelists. The course covered seven contemporary writers in the United States: Von Niguigutt, Kosinski, Bath, Reed, Doktoro, Deliro, and Kufuor. We will discuss contemporary Chinese writers who have similar creative methods (morning, Yuhua, Suboy, Yip, Wang Xiaobo, Yang Jinghui) and use comparative methods to analyze the use of Chinese and American writers' writing techniques such as Yuan novels, mimics, historical facts and fictional combinations, as well as literature, and discussions on topics such as war, trauma, ideological intervention, historical narratives, etc.

Name: Chinese-English Translation
Introduction:
The main content of the course is Chinese-English translation at the sentence level and discourse level. The course includes literary translation and practical translation in economics, trade and law. Through classroom explanations, discussions and translation exercises, students will be familiar with the characteristics of Chinese-English translation and improve their practical translation abilities. This course focuses on cultivating students' ability to reorganize sentences in translation according to the characteristics of English text and deal with inter-sentence cohesion, style, tone, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Contemporary American Literary Thought
Introduction: By reading some of the key statements that discuss contemporary American theorists and writers, senior students are presented with their rethinking of the history, nature and direction of American literature.

Name: Self, Crisis and Redemption in the Modern European Novel
Prerequisite: At least two of the four subjects, British History (I-II), American History (I-II), or equivalents.
Introduction: In this course, we will read the novels of five to six European writers from the late nineteenth century to the late twentieth century. These writers include Dostoyevsky, Proust, Wolf, Kafka, Kamu, etc. We will explore the following questions: what is the search for the existence of “self”, for the richness and depth of inner life, for self-perception and self-deception, and for the salvation of love, memory and artistic creation? How did their work reflect — or even foresee — on the social and political life of the twentieth century, in which the crisis took place? How do these writers think about personal responsibility, conscience and guilt? Have they raised other possibilities of spiritual transcendence in the era of their own Christianity? How does the narrative art of each of these writers expand or change our sense of time and space, so that we can rediscover the history of the individual and the community? (Each time the subject is taught, the selected author and the subject may be slightly adjusted.)

Name: Zen and the Art of Gardens
Introduction: Chinese classical gardens are an extremely vivid carrier of cultural information. It not only has a visible and touchable perceptual form, but also is rich in spiritual significance because it materializes the cultural concepts of its creators and appreciators. Historically, Chinese classical gardens have naturally integrated the religious pursuit and aesthetic interest of Zen Buddhism. They used the affinity relationship between man and nature as a guide to arrange various spatial combinations of different architectural groups, and seamlessly integrated some of the basic characteristics of religion and architecture into one place. The purpose of this lesson is to help everyone gain a deeper understanding of the characteristics of Chinese Zen culture and the unique artistic charm of classical gardens by discussing the impact of Zen culture on Chinese classical gardens.

Name: Information Security
Introduction:
Information security studies the science of confidentiality, integrity, identification, access control, non-repudiation protection, detection and response of information in information systems. The course includes relevant theories, attack methods and protection techniques. _x000D_
The textbook used is the 21st Century Information Security Planning Textbook for Colleges and Universities published by People’s Posts and Telecommunications Publishing House, which is one of the best-selling textbooks in the series. The textbook has a reasonable structure, is easy to learn and use, has substantial content, contains a large number of exercises for students to practice, and is equipped with PPT electronic materials. It is used as a teaching material in many 985 and 211 universities.

Name: Foundations of Theoretical Computer Science
Introduction:
"Fundamentals of Theoretical Computer Science" is a professional elective course for senior undergraduates in the college. Let students have a comprehensive understanding of the basic contents of computability and computational complexity theory; master some basic methods and techniques of this subject; and lay a good foundation for the study of subsequent courses (such as computational complexity). _x000D_
_x000D_
Content includes: several computing models (Turing machines, recursive functions, type-0 grammars, S language) and their equivalence; Church-Turing thesis; undecidable problems; recursive sets, recursive enumeration sets; formal languages and automata (including regular languages and finite automata, context-free languages and pushdown automata, context-sensitive languages and linear bounded automata); time and space complexity, NP completeness, etc. _x000D_

Name: Foundations of Information Science
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, high algebra, probability theory
Introduction: The course will describe basic concepts, models, theories and methods of information science. Based on a communication model, the course examines the nature of information, its underlying principles and methods of acquisition, transmission, detection, storage, processing and control. Chapter 1 describes the history, current status and trends in information science. Chapters 2 and 3 introduce measures of information: entropy and information exchange and discuss their nature. Chapter 4 discusses the coding of the source, giving the origin code theorem and several common coding methods. Chapters 5 and 6 deal with error coding of the channel, introducing the capacity of the channel and giving the code, code and nature of the channel code theorem and linear code. Chapter 7 introduces the theory and algorithm of the distortion rate and applies it to, inter alia, image compression.

Name: Set Theory and Graph Theory
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, linear algebra, data structure
Introduction: Learning and mastering basic knowledge of aggregate theory and graphics, with a focus on building the combined capacity of students to deal with the fragmentation of the binary relationship.

Name: Computer Image Processing
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, linear algebra (high mathematics), numerical analysis (calculation method), digital signal processing
Introduction: This course is a professional elective course that teaches digital image processing technology to undergraduate and graduate students in the School of Mathematical Sciences. The content includes the basic concepts of digital images, acquisition of digital images, processing technologies such as transformation, smoothing, sharpening, and restoration of digital images, analysis technologies such as segmentation, matching, and moving target estimation of digital images, and compression and coding technologies of digital images and videos. The course is mainly taught one by one in the form of special topics. Each topic will eventually analyze and discuss a typical image processing problem, and you will need to write programs to further learn and master related theories and methods.

Name: Survey of British and American Drama
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: Selected readings of six modern plays will give students a preliminary understanding of the language and form of drama. The scripts read are all representative works of important writers, and are representative in terms of ideological content and dramatic form. Combined with reading the script, a systematic introduction to the theory and practice of drama will be given.

Name: Machine Learning
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, computing methods, probability statistics
Introduction: Machine learning is a discipline about computers building probability and statistical models based on data and using the constructed models to predict and machine analyze data. This course mainly teaches some important methods commonly used in machine learning.

Name: Digital Signal Processing
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, linear algebra, resolution geometry (higher mathematics)
Introduction: This course is a professional elective course for undergraduates and graduate students in the School of Mathematical Sciences to teach the theory and application of digital signal processing. The content includes the sampling, filtering, convolution and correlation of digital signals, Hilbert transform, Fourier transform and its spectrum analysis, filter design, as well as in-class discussion and analysis of some typical signal processing application issues, etc. It is also necessary to write programs to further learn and master related theories and methods.

Name: Artificial Neural Networks
Introduction: This course describes the basic concepts, models, properties and learning algorithms of artificial neural networks, providing an intelligent theory and method for information processing. Chapter 1 introduces the characteristics of artificial neural networks, the basic problems and goals to be solved, and the brief history, current situation and trends of development. The structure and classification of artificial neural networks are also given. Chapter 2 introduces feedforward artificial neural networks, including perceptrons and their learning algorithms, adaptive linear units and BP networks and algorithms. Chapter 3 introduces feedback artificial neural networks, mainly including the stability of discrete and continuous Hopfield networks and their applications in associative memory and combinatorial optimization, cellular neural networks and their applications. Chapter 4 introduces self-organizing competitive artificial neural networks, including competitive learning networks, self-organizing mapping models SOM and automatic model selection theories and methods. Chapter 5 introduces the radial basis function (RBF) neural network. Finally, Chapter 6 introduces deep learning theory and algorithms.

Name: Artificial Intelligence
Introduction: Artificial Intelligence is a compulsory professional basic course for graduate students (optional for senior undergraduates), aiming to teach the basic theories and methods of artificial intelligence. The main contents of this course include: intelligent agents, search technology, constraint satisfaction problems, first-order logic, automatic reasoning, knowledge representation, planning methods, uncertain reasoning, decision-making, machine learning, language, robots, etc. Please refer to the handouts for this course content. _x000D_

Name: Deep Learning: Algorithms and Applications
Prerequisite: The curriculum requires students to be familiar with at least one programming language and basic knowledge of machine learning.
Introduction: Deep learning is the core technology that has made breakthroughs in artificial intelligence in recent years. This course will introduce a range of topics in deep learning, including mathematical foundations, theories, algorithms, and issues that need attention in practical applications. The course requires students to be familiar with at least one programming language and have a basic understanding of machine learning. Coursework includes the application of deep learning models in computer vision and natural language processing.

Name: Symbolic Computation
Introduction: Mathematics and many related disciplines deal with objects that are abstract symbols that have meaning. These symbols include numbers, polynomials, rational functions, trigonometric functions, geometric figures, logical formulas, and computer programs. Introducing appropriate symbols, establishing the operation rules and reasoning mechanisms between them, and studying the properties, uses and interrelationships of these symbols will build the corresponding discipline. Unlike numerical calculations, operations and reasoning between symbols are usually formal and precise, and therefore error-free. Symbolic computing studies how to represent and process meaningful abstract symbols on computers, designs effective algorithms for symbolic operations and reasoning, and programming languages ​​and software systems suitable for implementing these algorithms, and effectively implements the designed systems and algorithms and applies them to a variety of theoretical and practical problems. Its main branches include computer algebra and analysis, geometric calculations, automatic reasoning and programming, etc.

Name: Frontiers of Optics
Introduction:
The course, which was co-sponsored by several teachers of the Institute of Optical Sciences, covered all aspects of the frontier of modern optical, teaching history, current status and hot spots in their respective fields of study in accessible languages, giving students an overview of the frontier of modern optical research. The course was conducted in the form of a literature review of a topic of interest chosen by the students themselves.
Specific presentations included: photoclinic principles and new photocrystalm micro-incorporation photons; mono-molecule imaging, spectral measurements and mono-molecule manipulation methods and their application in the interaction of single molecules with nanostructures; soft display techniques and organic solar cells; optical micro-murals and their applications; quantum optical and quantum information based on surface ionogenesis; applications of Fs-SNOM systems based on ultra-high-time and spatial resolution in optical and nanodynamics; ultra-speed kinetic detection and control of molecules driven by flight-second lasers; detection and manipulation of flight-seconds and asecond pulses of internal dynamics processes in atomic molecules; flight-second laser 3-dimensional processing; self-rotonics and self-rotors; flight-speed and non-linear optical images and their application in chemistry and biodynamics; non-linear transmission and applications of flying-second lasers.

Name: Computational Physics (B)
Introduction: Computational physics is a discipline that uses computers to solve physical problems, and its core foundation is numerical analysis. This course focuses on teaching basic processing methods for various common numerical problems in computational physics, covering basic contents such as numerical solutions to linear and nonlinear equations, numerical differentiation and integration, interpolation and polynomial approximation, boundary value problems, initial value problems, numerical solutions to partial differential equations, signal processing methods such as Fourier transform, and processing and fitting of random numbers and data. Although the class focuses on teaching algorithms for basic problems, students will be required to use the knowledge they have learned through several major assignments to design appropriate algorithms based on specific problems and program to solve actual physical problems.

Name: Social Psychology (B)
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course will cover important concepts and theories in mainstream social psychology, including: how individuals view themselves and others, how to view and think about social phenomena, human aggression and helping behavior, the formation and change of attitudes, social influence and its manifestations, the basis and intimacy of interpersonal relationships, group psychology and behavior, how culture affects people, social psychological factors that affect human health, and the latest positive psychology and cyberpsychology. Through the study of this course, students should master the basic concepts, important theories and commonly used research methods of social psychology, and be able to use this knowledge to solve social and psychological problems they encounter.

Name: General Physics (I) Seminar
Prerequisite: This course is organized in parallel with the general physics course, which is designed to help air travel students digest the content of the course and to provide targeted counselling to students, with a view to laying the groundwork without promoting discussion.

The purpose of the seminar is to help digest the teaching content of the lectures and provide targeted tutoring to students, aiming to lay the foundation without engaging in discussions of an improved nature. We believe that although the enrollment level of students is slightly lower than that of Peking University students, as long as educators provide appropriate guidance and help, they can also become outstanding students. This is also the contribution we should make to the national defense industry. _x000D_
        The teaching content of general physics is general physical mechanics and electromagnetism, each accounting for 30 credit hours. The 30 credit hours of the seminar are divided into 15 credit hours for mechanics and 15 credit hours for electromagnetics. Specifically, 2 hours per week are used to digest the content of the major class, and conduct specific discussions, analysis, and exercises on the content and problems that students do not understand in the major class, so as to lay a solid foundation and improve their learning ability.

Name: Fundamentals of Computer Applications
Introduction: Knowledge of key concepts and typical applications of computers and computer networks, including word processing, data processing and management, web information retrieval, graphics, images and audio processing.

Name: Introduction to Aeronautics and Astronautics
Introduction: This course inspires every student's yearning and strong interest in aerospace by introducing the development history, current technology level and future development trends of the aerospace field. The course introduces the composition, classification and working principles of aircraft structures, power systems, weapon equipment, electronic equipment and ground equipment, allowing students to understand the advanced aerospace technology in a timely manner, expand their knowledge, and form preliminary engineering awareness, laying a certain foundation for future professional courses.

Name: History of Indian Buddhism
Introduction:
Through learning, students are more fully aware of the history of Buddhism in India, its growth and even its demise.
Some of the major historical events, classic teachings, personality ideas, sectarianism and their related theoretical problems are preliminary.
Understood. This course includes, first, teaching an overview of the history of Buddhism in India, taking into account the milestones of Buddhist development. Two.
In conjunction with the reading of the source material, the key figures and classical ideas and their implications are explained. III. Phased presentation

Presentation on the formation and development of the Buddhist Church.

Name: Aviation Sports 1
Introduction: 1. Course Introduction 1. Physical fitness is a person's ability to engage in physical activities that require speed, endurance, strength and flexibility. The physical fitness course mainly teaches knowledge and methods related to healthy physical fitness and the role of physical activities in improving aerobic fitness, muscle strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition. The teaching content mainly includes healthy physical fitness exercise methods, light equipment fitness methods and strength training methods. 2． Course requirements: (1) Wear suitable and lightweight sportswear. During the study period, you must master the safety knowledge of classroom equipment. While taking elective courses, you should continuously enhance your physical movement ability. (2) Students who suffer from chronic metabolic diseases, asthma, hypertension, heart disease and other diseases that are not suitable for high-intensity physical activity should take this course with caution. 2. Course tasks 1. Teach physical health and fitness exercise methods, light equipment fitness methods and strength training methods. 2. Cultivate students’ physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, and the ideology of “health first”. Understand the knowledge, skills, attitudes and behaviors that contribute to a physically active and healthy lifestyle, and achieve the goal of lifelong physical activity.

Name: Crowds and Networks
Prerequisite: Computer and mathematical knowledge required in first grade
Introduction: The course is based on two main theories - graph theory and game theory - to deduce behavior and interactions in the context of networks. Graph theory is a theory that studies network structures. Game theory provides a model of individual behavior. The key point is that the results of individual behavior depend on the behavior of other individuals. These problems have traditionally been scattered across many different disciplines. As public interest in networking grew, different scientific fields began to come together around the study of networking issues. The central goal of this course is to understand the basic forces behind networks and strategic behaviors by combining practices in each field, and to study the mechanisms that can channelize these forces to produce some overall effect. For example, the impact of specific auction mechanisms on bidding behavior and final prices; the impact of the Internet search engine industry on Web content creation, etc.

Name: Introduction to Sun Tzu's Art of War
College: Student Affairs Department, People's Armed Forces Department
Introduction:
This course systematically introduces the military thought of "Sun Tzu's Art of War" and its application in modern warfare. Teaching not only focuses on imparting the essence of traditional military science, but also focuses on improving students' strategic thinking ability. _x000D_
The main content of this course is:_x000D_
In the "Introduction", we explain the origin, spread, author, version and other related background issues of "The Art of War", the book's ideological system and its modern value; _x000D_
Interpret the original text of "Sun Tzu's Art of War" chapter by chapter, introduce the different views of the academic community on annotating these original texts, answer questions and resolve doubts, and strive to interpret the original text in line with Sun Tzu's original meaning; _x000D_
_x000D_
The total course hours are 32 hours. _x000D_
This course will highlight the two basic features of "correct interpretation" and "flexible application" of "The Art of War". _x000D_
Use the "Sun Tzu" method to teach "Sun Tzu" lessons. Teaching strives to be lively and lively. Adopt a teaching method that combines classroom lectures and discussions. Teachers are happy to answer all questions raised by students related to the lecture content, and encourage everyone to emancipate their minds and actively participate in class discussions. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Principles of Automatic Control
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation
Introduction: Feedback control is one of the key technologies in modern engineering and an important link in the design of aerospace vehicles. The main content of this course is to introduce the characteristics and design methods of feedback control systems, including: the necessity and advantages of feedback control, the response characteristics and performance indicators of the system in the time domain and frequency domain, PID control design, stability and stability criteria, root locus design method of single-input single-output linear system, Nyquist criterion, frequency domain design method and state space design method. The main software for system response and controller design is MATLAB.

Name: Engineering Mathematics
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation
Introduction: (b) The plural plane dot set, the compound variable function, the solver function, the fraction of the compound function, the grade of the resolution function, the odd point, the number of leftovers and their applications, the angle theory, the preservation transformation, the Laplace transformation; the differential equation in mathematical physics, the detached variable solution, the Bessel function, the Legendre multiform and its properties, the method of fractional transformation, the form of the fraction of the basic resolution.

Name: Mechanics of Materials
Prerequisite: calculus (i), calculus (ii), linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, theoretical mechanics
Introduction: As a basic mechanics course, the mechanics of materials course has the characteristics of an introduction to solid mechanics. Through the basic concepts of material mechanics, tension and compression, torsion and bending, complex stress states, pressure rod stability, elastic rod system energy method, etc., it mainly introduces the concepts and calculation methods of elastic rods and rod system structures in terms of strength, stiffness and stability, laying the foundation for subsequent courses.

Name: Electronics Laboratory
Introduction:
This course focuses on cultivating students' electronic technology experimental skills and is based on 14 specific experiments. Starting from understanding basic electronic components, the use of instruments and equipment and basic circuit welding operations, it gradually trains students to master the design, assembly, measurement, debugging and simulation of analog circuits and digital logic circuits. The course also introduces new technologies and processes such as patch mounting technology and integrated circuit technology. _x000D_
This course includes a total of 1 major lecture (4 credit hours) and 16 experiments (4 credit hours each).

Name: Aircraft Structural Mechanics
Prerequisite: Linear algebra, advanced mathematics, material mechanics
Introduction: The evolution of the structure of the aircraft and the evolution of design thinking were described. On the basis of the energy method, the receptivity and deformation characteristics of the basic thin-wall elements that make up the structure of the vehicle (including, in particular, closed doors, open-mouth wall rods and composite cross-section poles), plates and shells, and the corresponding mechanical analysis methods are presented. On that basis, the theory and methodology for the analysis of the static and stationary poles combined with the plate structure were presented.

Name: Fundamentals and Practice of Aerodynamics
Introduction:
Flying freely in the sky like a bird has been the desire of mankind throughout the ages. Today, 110 years after the realization of powered flight, the pursuit of safe, comfortable, energy-saving civilian aircraft and high-speed, maneuverable, stealthy military aircraft is still the dream of aerospace people. As one of the most complex machines made by mankind, aircraft integrate cutting-edge technologies such as materials, structures, electronics, control, and propulsion. The realization of flight relies more on the understanding, understanding and utilization of aerodynamics and flight mechanics. _x000D_
As an introduction to aeronautics, this course briefly introduces thermodynamic properties, viscosity, compressibility, vortices, laminar flow, turbulence, wind tunnels, atmosphere, especially the aerodynamic characteristics of wings. It aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the principles of lift and drag generated by aircraft, the basic theory of interaction between airflow and aircraft, research methods, and testing methods. Furthermore, through the production and test flight of aviation models, students will gain practical experience with the components and overall structural layout of the aircraft, learn the skills to fly the model, analyze the impact of aerodynamics on aircraft flight, solve problems encountered during flight, deepen the understanding of aerodynamics and flight mechanics, and lay a solid theoretical foundation for actual flying aircraft in the future. _x000D_

Name: Communications and Computer Networks
Introduction:
It is an undergraduate course covering basic concepts of networking and communication. The course covered the main computer network communications technologies, ranging from basic signal and data transmission, LAN-wide media access control and exchange techniques, to wider networked route and end-end transmission controls. At the same time, new industry concepts such as wireless networks, mobile computing and mobile Internet have been introduced, as appropriate, to enable students to understand developments in research in industry and academia.

The course will be conducted on a bottom-up basis. They are taught mainly in the classroom and are supplemented by post-school thinking. The curriculum will be based on a web-based pilot series, as appropriate. The main content of the course is based on teaching materials, and the Internet dominates protocol cases.

Students must have basic computer basic knowledge of computer programming logic.

Name: Cryptography and Cyberspace Security
Prerequisite: The course is offered to students of the Academy of Physicians in the Air Flight class and requires students to have a certain base in higher mathematics and in the subject of the General Computation.
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to provide undergraduate students with scientific background to learn about the rationale, techniques and applications of cryptography and to acquire the theoretical foundation, expertise and basic practical skills of network and information security.

Name: Engineering Thermodynamics
Introduction: Energy and its utilization are the material basis for human survival. The main form of energy that humans obtain from nature is thermal energy. The rational and effective utilization of thermal energy is the core and main body of the entire energy utilization. Engineering thermodynamics is a science that studies the mutual conversion laws of heat energy and other forms of energy. It is a summary of experience in continuously developing and improving energy utilization. On the basis of striving for students to have a deep understanding of the nature of energy phenomena, this course allows students to understand the latest developments and trends in energy conversion technology and engineering thermodynamics.

Name: Engineering Fluid Mechanics
Introduction: Hydrodynamics is an important basic subject in the fields of engineering, energy, aviation and mechanics. This course will systematically introduce basic concepts of hydrodynamics, basic theory, commonly used analytical methods, and relevant engineering applications; it will develop the analytical and solvency skills of students on basic hydrodynamics issues and lay the foundation for future studies and research.

Name: Flight Dynamics and Control
Prerequisite: Autocontrol theory, multiple function and linear algebra, theoretical mechanics, mathematical analysis, constant differential equation, aerodynamics
Introduction: Force analysis of aviation aircraft, methods of establishing flight motion equations, planned flight and aircraft performance, guidance flight and guidance laws, flight motion linearization approximation methods, flight dynamic characteristics analysis, aircraft stability and maneuverability, basic composition and basic principles of flight control systems, and flight control methods.

Name: Aviation Sports 6
Introduction: "Aviation Sports" is a compulsory examination course in the common basic module of the "joint training" of aviation flight and military command officer academic education for trainees. It uses physical exercises as the main means, aviation sports skills and methods as the main learning content, and the main purpose of building a strong physique for flight students. It is the main course in the flight talent training curriculum system, and it is also a necessary skill for the dual-student training of Peking University and Air Force Aviation University. Dual student pilots study scientific and cultural knowledge at Peking University, and they must pay more attention to the cultivation of physical fitness. Among the necessary military, political, cultural, sports, management and other qualities for military flying talents, physical fitness is an important material foundation and one of the core qualities. The quality of aviation sports training directly determines whether students are competent to fly, and even affects the length of flight life of pilots and the strength of the air force's combat effectiveness. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Political Science
Introduction:
Political science
Political science is an ancient subject, and it is a knowledge of how human collective life is organized. The “political science doctrine” is an introductory course in political science, which deals mainly with fundamental issues of political science, core concepts, research methods, major theories and academic streams, explaining the relationship between ideas, theory, institutions, policies and behaviour, and illustrating the relevance of the various academic outcomes developed under political philosophy and political scientific thinking to real politics. Through the study of “political science”, the capacity for political analysis can be systematically trained and enhanced.

Name: Jewelry Appreciation and Jewelry Culture
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Jewelry and jade are the precious essence that nature has nurtured and dedicated to mankind for millions of years. It is one of the important objects for mankind to understand nature. This course uses multimedia and other modern teaching methods to teach and discuss the basic characteristics, evaluation and identification, aesthetic appreciation of the main varieties of jewelry and jade, as well as the development of jade in my country and jade carving art. This course enables students to master and understand the basic concepts, main types, processing techniques, evaluation and identification methods, and aesthetic appreciation of jewelry and jade. They will also be familiar with the status of ancient jade in Chinese history and culture, the style and craft characteristics of jade production in various historical periods and their relationship with the historical background and productivity development level, and understand the characteristics of my country's jade carving art and modern jewelry culture. _x000D_
This course is taught by three teachers: Dr. Wang Changqiu, Professor Cui Wenyuan, and Professor Wang Shiqi. _x000D_

Name: The Old Summer Palace: History and Present Condition
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: As it is an optional school-wide course, it is open to students from all faculties, both within and outside the school, and there is no pre-course.
Introduction:
The Old Summer Palace is the collective name for the three gardens of the Old Ming Dynasty, Wanchun Garden and Changchun Garden. It was built in the 46th year of Kangxi's reign (AD 1707). It is one of the last representatives of royal gardens in China's feudal society. It is the culmination of the centralized gardening culture in the 18th century and a material carrier for the exchange and integration of Chinese and Western architectural culture and artistic values. In October 1860, the Old Summer Palace was robbed and burned by invading officers and soldiers of the British and French allied forces, which shocked the government and the public and horrified the world. It is the site of physical evidence of the crimes of modern imperialist powers in destroying human civilization in the world. Currently, there is considerable controversy over how to protect and utilize the ruins of the Old Summer Palace. _x000D_
This course is a cutting-edge academic course based on the "Preliminary Survey on the World Heritage Application of the Old Summer Palace in China". It involves topics such as the historical documents and materials of the Old Summer Palace, historical geographical environment, garden landscape construction, cultural heritage value, existing issues of the ruins, and disputes over the protection of the ruins. The course adopts a teaching method that combines classroom teaching with field trips.

Name: The Psychology of Love
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Main content of the course:_x000D_
A systematic analysis of human love from a psychological perspective. Mainly based on attachment theory, it provides a comprehensive introduction to the origin of love, individual differences in love, and the manifestations of love. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching method: _x000D_
This course will be conducted through a combination of classroom lectures and reading extracurricular materials. In the classroom, explanations are mainly provided in the form of projection, and the Peking University teaching website provides downloadable reading materials. At the same time, in class, we will also provide some corresponding attachment-related questionnaires as auxiliary tools to help students understand themselves and establish good interpersonal relationships. _x000D_

Name: Film Music
Introduction: It is formed through the accumulation and development of "Music Research in Master's Film Creation" (2009-2012, public elective course) and "Film and Television Music and Sound" (2017, professional course). The course is developed around the seven fulcrums of film music’s concept, attributes, history, function, creation, aesthetics, and evaluation. It emphasizes the cutting-edge nature of knowledge and pioneering methods, focuses on cultivating students’ problem awareness and critical thinking ability, and highlights the integration of theory and practice. The course covers a wide range of works, with a particular focus on milestone masterpieces in the development of film music. If film is the director's art, visual communication is like the main body of narrative, and music is like two wings, indispensable. It is particularly worth noting that the systematic analysis of film music, regarding the types of film music, is an important and original feature of the course that makes it different from previous courses.

Name: Fundamentals of Astronautical Technology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Learning basic space technology, including space systems, spacecraft orbits, space transport systems, spacecraft design and working principles, space environment and environmental experiments.

Name: Exploring the Mysteries of Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Psychology is the science that helps people to achieve this. But the psychology we encounter in our daily lives is replete with non-scientific content; we need a more scientific and effective knowledge of our abilities.
The purpose of this course is to help people understand what science psychology is, to master the psychological thinking of science, and to look at the familiar life in and around the world from an objective point of view, so that they can understand themselves more clearly and take control of themselves. The curriculum is self-contained, with a core thread running through the entire curriculum, and draws theoretical evidence from the conclusions of classical psychological experiments, focusing on the development of psychological thinking patterns rather than mere knowledge point presentations.

Name: Academic Chinese Writing for International Students
College: School of Chinese as a Second Language
Prerequisite: No, Chinese level is above level 6
Introduction:
This course aims to cultivate foreign students’ ability to use Chinese for academic writing. _x000D_
The course content mainly includes three parts:_x000D_
1.	Learn the writing characteristics, writing paradigms, and writing styles of Chinese academic papers, as well as the language expression characteristics of Chinese academic papers, including vocabulary, sentence patterns, paragraphs, etc. _x000D_
2.	From the perspective of language expression function, learn commonly used writing methods in academic papers, including narrative, explanation and description, definition and example, contrast and comparison, discussion and defence. _x000D_
Three.	Academic paper writing training, including paper title and titles at all levels, abstract and keywords, introduction, literature review, argumentation (such as citations, etc.), conclusion, references, appendix and acknowledgments, etc. _x000D_
This course integrates writing skills and language proficiency training. Through sample reading and analysis and discussion of common errors in essay writing by international students, foreign students will have a general understanding of the characteristics of academic essay writing, understand the difference between academic Chinese and non-academic Chinese, and learn various common Chinese academic essay writing standards; understand the writing methods of various necessary components of Chinese academic essays, and ultimately enable students to have the ability to independently write academic essays in Chinese. _x000D_

Name: Outdoor Exploration
Introduction: The basics of outdoor sports are based on the basic knowledge, techniques and skills common to outdoor sports as the main teaching content, with the purpose of cultivating students' physical fitness, psychological quality, interpersonal skills, teamwork awareness, environmental awareness, environmental behavioral adaptability and certain social skills for participating in outdoor sports and related competitions. Through the teaching of the course, students can master the basic knowledge, skills and techniques of participating in outdoor sports, strengthen their bodies, form good behavioral habits and health and psychological quality, and comprehensively improve their overall quality.

Name: General Survey of Video Games
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Electronic games and interactive media will be an important part of the cultural entertainment and leisure field in the future (the current market has exceeded the theater box office). In the future, its revenue, number of employees, and people served will become one of the most mainstream components in society. Regardless of people's likes and dislikes, there is no doubt that video games will become a huge industry in the next few decades. This can also be seen from the fact that the Ministry of Culture organized the China E-Sports Entertainment Competition (CEST) and the General Administration of Sports established the National Mobile E-Sports Competition (CMEG). _x000D_
_x000D_
Education related to video games is not just a simple course. A relatively comprehensive education requires many years of professional degree education. The corresponding majors abroad have been developing for many years - in the United States alone, there are hundreds of schools offering undergraduate degree education in game design, and about half of them offer master's degree education. Taking the Southern California (USC) major and curriculum design education, which ranks first in the game design major rankings of The Princeton Review, as a reference, you can get a glimpse of the content scope of this major. At USC, majors related to game and interactive media design include: _x000D_
○ Master's Degree School of Engineering Computer Science (Game Development) _x000D_
○ Master's degree School of Cinematic Arts Interactive Media (Games and Health)_x000D_
○ Master's Degree School of Cinematic Arts Interactive Media_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Major School of Engineering Computer Science (Games)_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Major School of Cinematic Arts Interactive Entertainment_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor College of Engineering Video Game Programming_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Video Game Design and Management_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game Design_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game Animation_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game Audio_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game Entrepreneurism_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game Studies_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Cinematic Arts Game User Research_x000D_
