○ Undergraduate Minor School of Fine Arts 3-D Art for Games_x000D_
○ Undergraduate Minor School of Education Learning Design and Technology_x000D_
○ MBA Cinematic Arts (Media Arts, Games and Health)_x000D_
_x000D_
From the above table, we can see the importance and weight of games and interactive media - it can be seen that the related knowledge, technology, and fields of this type of education have a very rich content range. Just the research and development of games involves design, programming, art, animation, management, psychology and other fields; as for an industry and industry, there is still a lot worth learning and observing from the perspectives of economics, marketing, management, social psychology and other aspects. _x000D_
_x000D_
At present, there are some related courses at Peking University, but the number is very small, and they mainly focus on some specialized topics, such as "Programming Methods for General Chess Games" by Teacher Li Wenxin, and "Game-Based Innovative Thinking" by Teacher Shang Junjie. Some teachers have introduced game design into their programming classes, but they mainly focus on algorithms (such as path-finding, etc.). _x000D_
For such an important technical and social field, and there are already many graduates working in the video game industry, it is imperative to educate Peking University students in this area. Considering the comprehensive subject system of Peking University, it is very reasonable and necessary to offer an introduction or general course in this field to all students in the school so that students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding. _x000D_

Name: Child and Adolescent Psychiatry
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Psychiatry is an important and integral part of modern medical science and focuses on the causes of mental disorders, pathology, pathology and clinical patterns, as well as related issues of prevention, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation. Child and adolescent psychiatry is a new profession, nearly 50 years behind normal psychiatry. In the United States, the most famous child psychiatry textbook, Child Psychiatry Kanner, L. Child Psychiatry. Charles Thomas: Springfield, IL, 1935 (Kanner), was published in 1935. Child psychiatry was not accepted as a medical profession until 1957. My country has evolved since the 1970s. Children and adolescents are vulnerable to mental disorders. At present, the prevalence of mental illness among our children and adolescents is above the international average of 15-20 per cent. There is an increase in behavioural disorders, juvenile delinquency, and many childhood illnesses are characterized by difficulties in prognosis and treatment. The introduction of mental health for children has become a requirement of the times, and awareness and mental health for children is urgently needed. This lecture will be structured as a framework for the classification, naming and diagnosis of mental disorders of children, published by the World Health Organization (WHO) Standard 10 (ICD-10). The purpose of the lectures was to familiarize the audience with and understand the basic theory, basic knowledge, basic skills and recent developments in mental medicine for children and adolescents at home and abroad. Videos, audio recordings, simulations, and a variety of media formats and modes of interaction can also be used to stimulate positive thinking among listeners. The clinical presentation of a mental disorder is followed by a typical clinical case, which better helps listeners understand and acquire knowledge. This lecture is suitable for students of higher educational institutions specializing in clinical medicine and psychology and can also benefit from it as a good choice for counsellors, therapists and caregivers working with mental health workers, especially children, even if they are merely listeners interested in psychology and psychiatry or have an interest in spiritual phenomena.

Name: Intensive French (Beginner)
Introduction: The aim of this course is to teach students at the zero starting point, at 32 school hours, the sound rules of French, to acquire a good knowledge of important grammar, to gain a full understanding of basic grammar, to be able to apply common terminology and practical sentences, to read medium and advanced French with the help of dictionaries and to hear, speak, write and translate, and to engage in general international cultural exchanges and scientific research.

Name: Theoretical Mechanics (B)
Prerequisite: General physics, advanced mathematics, linear algebra
Introduction: The Theoretical Mechanics (B) course is part of a theoretical course for physics students at the College of Physics after general physics and is the basis for the follow-up of several theoretical physics courses. The main focus of the course is on the teaching of analytical mechanics (specifically LaGrand Zhig and Hamidon). The course applies the analytical mechanics approach to a wide range of kinetic systems, ranging from simple mass movements to binding multi-liberal systems and rigidities. The main specifics of the course are provided in the syllabus.

Name: Physics of the Solar Atmosphere and Heliosphere
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
This course systematically explains the main detection results in the solar atmosphere and heliosphere, as well as the physical models established to explain the observation results. Explain basic characteristics and physical processes by comparing observations with theory. _x000D_
The course covers: quiet characteristics of the various layers of the solar atmosphere (photosphere, chromosphere, transition zone and corona) as well as explosive activities (such as chromosphere spicules, transition zone explosive events, flares and coronal mass ejections), the origin of the solar wind (matter and coronal mass ejections) Energy supply mechanism), interplanetary structures (interplanetary magnetic clouds and corotating interaction zones), waves (such as shock waves, Alfvén waves) and turbulence (Alfvén turbulence), outer heliosphere, heliosphere boundaries (terminating shock waves and heliopause). _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Space Exploration and Experimentation
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the basic principles and technologies of space exploration as well as the history, current situation and future development of space exploration. It mainly includes magnetic field measurement, mass spectrometry measurement, spectrum measurement, particle radiation measurement and space remote sensing technology. In addition, this course also includes teaching visits and experiments.

Name: Introduction to Space Weather and Forecasting
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Space weather is an emerging discipline in space science. Space weather refers to the state and change of the solar surface, the solar wind, the magnetosphere, the ionosphere and thermosphere at short or short notice. Their state and changes can affect the performance and reliability of space and terrestrial technology systems and endanger human life and health. Bad space weather can cause the collapse of satellite operations, communications, navigation and power station transmission networks, causing socio-economic damage in all its aspects. The course will focus on the impact of solar-induced changes in space weather on the Earth and its surface technology systems. The objective of this course is to enable students to apply science thinking more deeply to understand space weather and how we can use knowledge learned to reduce the impact of bad space weather on our technological systems.

Name: Ionospheric Physics and Radio Wave Propagation
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The ionosphere is a part of the Earth's upper atmosphere. This part is ionized by the ultraviolet radiation of the sun. This ionized part is enough to affect the propagation of radio waves. This course takes the history of ionospheric research as the main line, focusing on the formation of the ionosphere, the morphology of the ionosphere, the current in the ionosphere, and the propagation of electromagnetic waves in the ionosphere.

Name: Introduction to Planetary Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The course consists of 10 chapters, the first of which is an introduction, which provides an overview of the fundamental features of the solar system, the objects, content and methods of scientific research on planets, and, in particular, some of the basic concepts frequently encountered in subsequent chapters. Chapters II to VI deal with the Moon and Earth-like planets, including Earth, Mercury, Venus and Mars. Chapters VII to IX present the woody planets and their satellites, analysing the strange atmosphere, the various rings and the thousands of strange satellites of such planets, with a focus on strengthening the description of several satellites that may have life. Chapter X deals with small objects in the solar system, mainly dwarfs, asteroids and comets. The methods and significance of detecting and studying asteroids and comets were emphasized. Chapter XI is a front-line issue in planetary science, including methods of detection and research of the berth belt, the Alt cloud and extra-solar planets.

Name: Physics of the Middle and Upper Atmosphere
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Teaching purpose: introduce the basic state of the middle and upper atmosphere, raise the physical problems contained therein, and describe the basic methods to solve these physical problems. Main contents: Basic knowledge of relevant space physics, structure of middle and upper atmosphere, thermodynamics and dynamics, coupling of neutral atmosphere and ionosphere, applications. Features: This course not only introduces basic knowledge, but also focuses on the refining of physical problems and the introduction of basic research methods. It strives to enable students to acquire basic skills in research methods of this discipline through the study of the course. _x000D_

Name: Health Education for University Students
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: A course on health education for university students, a systematic presentation of health information closely related to university students, an introduction to the prevention, diagnosis, treatment, etc. of common physical and mental diseases, and a detailed presentation of the basic commons of first aid. A brief overview was also provided on nutrition and health, rational use of medicines, etc.

Name: Media and International Relations
Prerequisite: The first course is not required, but the chosen students need to read and be familiar with the current history of contemporary international relations and have better English reading skills.
Introduction: The course will help select students to familiarize themselves with the main theoretical perspectives on “Media and international relations”, the main ways in which the media play a role in different forms of international relations and its influence in our external relations, taking into account specific cases.

Name: Chinese Culture and Society
Introduction: This course is a cross-cutting course between national conditions research and cultural studies that is closely related to the practical work of journalism and communication. There are approximately 10 special research topics per semester. The main purpose is to guide students, based on the standpoint of dialectical materialism and historical materialism, to comprehensively understand the many phenomena and problems of China's contemporary development based on the inheritance and development characteristics of national culture, and to gain an in-depth understanding of China's national conditions and historical and cultural causes, in order to draw constructive opinions, so that they can better use mass media means when engaging in news communication activities in the future, guide the broad audience correctly and effectively, and play their due role in the comprehensive and sustainable development of China's society and economy.

Name: Fitness and Bodybuilding
Introduction: Fitness and bodybuilding is a sport that uses bare hands or various equipment exercises to develop muscles, increase strength, enhance physical strength, improve the body shape and pleasure the body and mind. One class per week, two hours.

Name: Video Interviewing and Writing
Prerequisite: Media and social change, journalism theory, communications theory, new media introduction, audio-visual language, video editing
Introduction: Video interviewing and video writing are the two most important basic skills for video producers. This course aims to enable students to master the inherent laws of video communication and systematically recognize the particularities of video interviewing and writing, so as to avoid shortcomings and maximize strengths, achieve the ultimate goal of video communication, and provide theoretical training and practical experience for their future front-line practice or academic research.

Name: Space Exploration
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Space refers to a vast area from more than 60 kilometers to 200 AU (the average distance between the sun and the earth) from the earth's surface. This area is the space range that spacecraft can directly reach, and it is also the area that has a direct impact on the earth's ecological environment. With the development of space technology, human space activities are increasingly moving into deep space. What is the purpose and significance of this development? This is one of the questions to be answered in this course. The main contents of this course also include the characteristics of various regions in space and their impact on human beings; the significance and methods of space exploration; the history and future of space exploration; space resources and utilization; and the fourth dimension of modern warfare-space warfare.

Name: General English (II)
Introduction: This course aims to cultivate students' comprehensive ability to use English. Through basic language training and chapter explanation and analysis, students can gradually improve their text reading comprehension ability, understand the expression methods and characteristics of various English questions, expand their vocabulary and become familiar with common English sentence patterns, and acquire basic oral and written expression skills. At the same time, teachers encourage students to actively participate in various language communication activities in the classroom, acquire basic communicative skills, and meet the requirements for listening, speaking, reading, writing, translating and other skills.

Name: General English (I)
Introduction:
This course aims to cultivate students' comprehensive ability to use English. Through basic language training and chapter explanation and analysis, students can gradually improve their text reading comprehension ability, understand the expression methods and characteristics of various English questions, expand their vocabulary and become familiar with common English sentence patterns, and acquire basic oral and written expression skills. At the same time, teachers encourage students to actively participate in various language communication activities in the classroom, acquire basic communicative skills, and meet the requirements for listening, speaking, reading, writing, translating and other skills. _x000D_
This course is for international students with zero starting point in English. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Modern Chinese History
Introduction: This course is a professional elective course for undergraduates in the Department of History. It mainly focuses on special training on the imperial examination system and basic official system of the late Qing Dynasty. Through a combination of teacher lectures, reading materials and classroom discussions, it is hoped that it will help students gain a deeper understanding of the system and culture of the late Qing Dynasty, enhance their sense of history, and lay the foundation for further independent research.

Name: Practical Chinese Rhetoric
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Modern Chinese, ancient Chinese, Chinese ancient literature, Chinese contemporary literature
Introduction: This course is intended for foreign students (undergraduate) in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature to teach various rhetorical issues in the practical application of Chinese. It strives to combine the teaching with students' actual cases in speaking, sentence making, and composition. It is hoped that it will help international students improve their practical ability in language use and their ability to appreciate the art of language use in literary works.

Name: The Economy of the European Union
Introduction:
The advent of the euro in 1999 attracted the world's attention. While people are paying attention to its impact on the European economy, the world economy and the international monetary system, they are also bound to explore the background of the euro's creation. In fact, the birth of the euro is not accidental, it is the inevitable result of the development of European economic integration. _x000D_
_x000D_
As the largest regional trading bloc in the world today, the EU is a pioneer in regional economic integration. In today's world of economic globalization and regional economic integration, especially with the full launch of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area on January 1, 2010, it is not only necessary for us to study and examine the policies and measures adopted by the EU in the process of economic integration, but it is also of great practical significance. _x000D_

Name: China's Foreign Trade and Economic Strategy
Prerequisite: International trade theory, China's foreign trade overview
Introduction: The content of the course is to combine the principles and theories of international trade that students have learned with the practice of China's foreign trade and economic development. From the perspective of China's economic development, it explains the main trade strategies that China should adopt at different stages of development, the main means and methods of different trade strategies, and how to deal with possible counterattacks from other countries in the implementation of trade strategies. At the same time, it introduces the decision-making process and methods of the trade strategies of major international trading countries to maximize students' application theory, so that students have the ability to understand and solve international trade strategic issues, initially master the process and methods of formulating national foreign economic and trade strategies, and form preliminary awareness and experience of strategy formulation.

Name: History of Chinese Buddhism
Introduction:
This course includes: (i) Teaching Chinese Buddhist history in the light of the periodic characteristics of Buddhist dissemination and development in early China
Overview; (ii) Introduction to translation, interpretation and dissemination of Buddhist classics; (iii) Integration of raw materials
In this context, the main mission of Chinese Buddhism is to explain its philosophy, religious genre and its theoretical characteristics. (iv) Contact
The country ' s socio-cultural background describes the exchange and integration between Buddhism and traditional Chinese culture. At the same time, in class.
The actual situation is taught, information is selected and discussed on an open basis.

Name: International Investment
Introduction: This course explains global capital allocation and the resulting investment opportunities, as well as the classic investment theoretical schools formed from the perspective of capital flows and the formation mechanism of the international monetary system. Finally, the interactive relationship between China and foreign investment is explained based on China's reality. The course will use the software of a certain futures company for practical simulation.

Name: Topics in the World Economy
Introduction: The content of this course covers current major practical issues in the fields of international trade, international finance, international investment and international economic cooperation. It will also compare the mechanisms and evolution of mature market economies, developmental market economies and transitional market economies. It focuses on the impact of the development of major countries on the world economic pattern and its implications for post-development countries. The characteristic is that it uses a large amount of data and facts to explain, inspiring students to discover problems and patterns on their own, rather than boring lists and simple summaries; it also strives to allow students to apply the "experience" gained in practice through group discussions and final exams in the form of papers, cultivate research interests, and get involved in academic standards.

Name: Marketing
Introduction:
Content summary:_x000D_
Marketing behavior is one of the most important components of human social life, so it needs to be studied from a scientific perspective to form a systematic thought and tool system to guide corporate marketing behavior under competitive conditions. Due to changes in supply and demand and competition, marketing ideas continue to progress and develop, forming a five-generation marketing ideological system that is replaced and inherited in five stages. Marketing ideas of different generations have their main ideological systems and key action standards. Under the guidance of system theory, humans can clearly analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the marketing ideas of enterprises and competitors, and which one comes first, thus providing an effective tool for corporate marketing decision-makers to ensure that their own marketing ideas are ahead of their opponents. Value strategic marketing (five generations of marketing tools) is currently the only ideological tool in China that can judge whether a company's marketing ideas are ahead of its main competitors. Under this skeptical system, the main logic and structure of this course are also very clear, namely market theory, value theory, competitive advantage theory, and integrated marketing theory, including integrated marketing ideas and mechanisms such as products, prices, channels, agreements, services, and personnel management. This provides students with an effective tool to systematically master marketing and achieve leadership in marketing thinking. _x000D_
Classroom teaching is adopted. Under the guidance of the teacher, students conduct case studies from the perspective of the vice president of marketing of a virtual real company, striving to analyze the marketing behavior of the company under study and the marketing ideas behind it, and improve their understanding of the course through program design and innovative plans. _x000D_
The exam is conducted in the form of a final case report.

Name: Economic History of the World
Introduction: Teaching the history of the world economy since 1,000 years

Name: International Marketing
Prerequisite: Need for a knowledge base in microeconomics and macroeconomics
Introduction: Do you want to know the reasons why international education exhibitions have become so popular in China in recent years and the reasons behind the enthusiasm of Chinese students to study abroad? While the “One Belt, One Road” initiative injects vitality into the economic development of China and the world, how many international marketing opportunities will it bring to Chinese and foreign companies? In the era of mass entrepreneurship and innovation, how many marketing opportunities are waiting for us to explore? If you are interested in these questions, then this course will not only help you find the answers, but also provide you with a key to opening the door to international marketing! International marketing knowledge and concepts not only contribute to the planning and implementation of Chinese enterprises' "going global" strategies, but also contribute to the "going global" of Chinese culture.

Name: International Finance
Introduction: This course studies all aspects of international financial accommodation, including international currency movements, capital movements and credit movements, as well as international and national political, economic and social factors that govern the changes and development of international financial relations. The specific content includes international balance of payments, foreign exchange and foreign exchange rates, international reserves, foreign exchange management, international monetary system, international financial market, etc. The content involves the basic theory, practice and policy of international finance.

Name: Development Economics
Introduction:
Development economics takes the economies of developing countries as the research object, studies the laws of how developing countries can get rid of poverty and develop into a modern economy with generally improved people's living standards, studies the specific processes and conditions of development, and the policies and strategies that should be formulated to achieve economic, social and institutional changes as soon as possible. _x000D_
    _x000D_
    This course includes four articles with a total of ten chapters: _x000D_
    The first "Introduction" consists of two chapters. It mainly discusses the research objects and learning purposes of development economics, introduces the characteristics of developing countries, and discusses the differences and connections between economic development and economic growth. _x000D_
    The second part, "Dual Economy Development Model", consists of three chapters, mainly discussing the transfer and employment of wealthy rural labor force under the conditions of dual economy, the relationship between industrialization and the development of the agricultural sector, the transformation process of China's dual economic structure and the main problems it faces. _x000D_
    The third part, "Modern Economic Growth Theory", consists of three chapters, mainly discussing the intrinsic relationship between material capital accumulation, population and human capital accumulation, technological progress and economic growth, and analyzing the characteristics and trends of China's economic growth. _x000D_
    The fourth part, "Structuralist Theory of Economic Development," consists of two chapters. It mainly discusses the structuralist theory of the Latin American school, the balanced growth and unbalanced growth strategies of economic development, the intrinsic relationship between industrial structure changes and economic development, and analyzes the characteristics of industrial structure in the process of China's industrialization and its contribution to economic development. _x000D_

Name: Electronic Commerce
Introduction:
The development of e-commerce and information technology has made the characteristics of the "new economy" increasingly prominent. This economic model takes informatization and globalization as its two pillars. Informatization has promoted the expansion of the production possibility frontier, the prominence of new economic characteristics, and the expansion of the economic growth multiplier effect; globalization has enabled network trade and network finance to go hand in hand, overcoming some of the shortcomings of traditional foreign economic and trade relations, but it has also brought about some new risks and even crises, which have attracted great attention from international organizations such as the WTO. _x000D_
This course will systematically introduce all aspects of knowledge in the field of e-commerce, as well as basic economic issues, economic ethics, system construction and other aspects involved in e-commerce. Specifically, it includes seven chapters: e-commerce and economics, e-commerce and new market structures and pricing mechanisms, e-commerce and market externalities and network utility, e-commerce and government economic functions and non-governmental mechanisms, e-commerce and economic growth and business cycles, e-commerce and economic ethics and system construction, e-commerce and business practices and technological innovation. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: A Brief History of Modern Financial Theory
Introduction: The Brief History of Modern Financial Theory discusses the main concepts of finance from the 1950s to the present, as well as financial theories and schools of finance, in a coherent historical perspective. Emphasis is placed on understanding the monetary and financial essence, on the inherent logic of financial theory and on the important implications for the economy itself.

Name: The Japanese Economy
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the history of Japan's economic development, analyzes the formation, role and transformation of Japan's economic operating mechanism, discusses Japan's economic growth strategy, Japan's economic development model and its changes, Japan's position in the world economy and China-Japan economic relations.

Name: Multinational Corporation Management
Introduction: This course is an elective course for senior undergraduates majoring in International Economics and Trade in the School of Economics. It mainly introduces the basic principles and methods of multinational company management. Through this course, students can understand and master the main issues in the operation and management of multinational companies, and prepare themselves for further in-depth research on multinational business issues and related practical work.

Name: Economic Geography
Introduction:
"Economic geography" is a major component of geography and the most developed branch of the geographical science system in most countries. The development and research characteristics of economic geography are, on the one hand, closely related to the development of economic activities, and on the other hand, they are significantly influenced by geography, economics and other related disciplines. _x000D_
As an independent discipline, economic geography only has a history of more than a hundred years. However, its development goes back much further.

Introduction: 4-hour course in public Italian

Name: Monetary Economics
Introduction:
This course is offered every spring and autumn semester. The content is arranged according to the specific arrangements of the instructor. It systematically introduces the origin and evolution of market economy, exchange economy, liquidity, and currency. _x000D_
_x000D_
The content includes: The role of currency in transactions is to study the impact of currency as a transaction medium on transactions. _x000D_
_x000D_
The research methods of this course have a wide range of applications, and the research objects include the role of currency as a medium of exchange, the cost of currency, the relationship between currency and banks, credit and monetary policy, etc.

Name: General English (III)
Introduction: Through practical tasks such as reading, writing, listening, speaking, and translating, this course cultivates students with a solid language foundation and strong comprehensive application ability, develops the habit of independent learning, and integrates language learning into the process of understanding, thinking, and discussing various issues in real life.

Name: English for Specific Purposes
Introduction: The focus of the course is on learning basic statistical concepts and methods, while gaining experience in collaborating with the Practical Data Science project. In the classroom, students will use R-Statistical Software to learn data visualization and analysis techniques, use multiple data sets and engage in applied economic analysis topics. Upon completion of the course, students will be able to: (i) read critical economic studies; (ii) use statistical methods in their work; (iii) write professional reports and repeatable studies; and (iv) further develop a course on statistics/measurements economics

Name: General English (IV)
Introduction: This course aims to cultivate students' comprehensive ability to use English. Through basic language training and chapter explanation and analysis, students can gradually improve their text reading comprehension ability, understand the expression methods and characteristics of various English questions, expand their vocabulary and become familiar with common English sentence patterns, and acquire basic oral and written expression skills. At the same time, teachers encourage students to actively participate in various language communication activities in the classroom, acquire basic communicative skills, and meet the requirements for listening, speaking, reading, writing, translating and other skills.

Name: Labor Economics
Introduction: Why is it that the average annual working hours per worker in the United States is 1,800, while in Europe it is only over 1,300? Why has the wage gap between high-skilled and low-skilled labor around the world been increasing in the past 30 years? How much is expected to increase your income by studying for one more year? What are the driving forces of urbanization? This course is designed to answer relevant questions. This is a basic course on labor economics and policy analysis, which is introductory and introductory. This course emphasizes the application of microeconomic theory and empirical research using simple econometric tools. This course focuses more on enhancing students’ research and policy analysis abilities. The content will mainly include labor supply and demand, taxation and welfare policies, human capital, health, education, income distribution inequality, labor mobility, unemployment, labor incentives within enterprises, demographic changes, etc.

Name: Selected Readings in European Literature
Introduction: This course is designed to help students carefully read two epic poems that have had a profound impact on the history of European literature - Virgil's "Aeneid" and Dante's "Divine Comedy". It is hoped that students will have a deeper understanding of the European classical tradition and Christian tradition. The textbooks use English translations of the two epic poems, all classroom instruction is in English, and all written assignments and examinations are in English.

Name: Appreciation of Shakespeare's Masterpieces
Prerequisite: English courses at the university, passing the 6th grade English examination. British history.
Introduction:
This course is taught in English and is a general humanities elective course for senior undergraduates across the school. Shakespeare's plays are the essence of Western literature and are also a required humanities course in many universities in the United Kingdom and the United States. It is very necessary to offer this course for senior undergraduates at Peking University to directly study and appreciate some famous passages from Shakespeare's plays in the original text. _x000D_
Purpose of course teaching: This course aims to improve undergraduates’ Western humanities literacy and appreciation of English literature. The course selects the original works of Shakespeare's plays, supplemented by the introduction of historical background and other materials. Through classroom lectures and discussions, students can: 1) enhance their understanding of the Western humanistic spirit and cultivate comprehensive humanistic qualities; 2) have a basic understanding of Shakespeare's dramatic art and expand their knowledge and understanding of Western classic art; 3) read and appreciate some of Shakespeare's plays in English, and consciously improve their English language reception and expression abilities at a higher level. _x000D_
Course content: The original text of Shakespeare's famous plays (mainly dramatic monologues or dialogue sections of a certain length) has about 50 paragraphs and about 1200-1500 lines of poetry, covering tragedies, dramas, historical dramas and sonnets. The lectures are appropriately interspersed with the summary of the drama, the historical background of the English Renaissance, and Shakespeare's comments. _x000D_
Course teaching format: mainly lectures, supplemented by an appropriate proportion of classroom discussions and reading exercises. _x000D_
Course grade evaluation: A combination of daily grades (answering questions, reading aloud plays, etc.) and final exams (closed book exams or small papers): daily grades account for 30% and final exams account for 70%. _x000D_
Requirements for students who choose the course: 1) Have great interest in Western culture (literature); 2) Excellent college English scores (a score of 80 or above in Peking University Band 4 or National Band 4 examination; 3) Strong English listening and speaking skills. _x000D_

Name: Economic History of the People's Republic of China
Prerequisite: Economics principles, middle microeconomics, middle macroeconomics, econometrics
Introduction: Economic history is an important branch of theoretical economics. Its content is to use economic methods to analyze historical changes, explain the economic reasons behind major historical events, and then explain the laws of historical evolution from an economic perspective. Many major modern economic events and economic policies can be traced back to history, so economic history can provide some reference for today's economic development. Today, as economics becomes increasingly mathematical and physical, economic history courses play an important role in cultivating students' economic intuition. This course uses economic methods to explain the major historical events that occurred in China after 1949, especially the institutional changes after the reform and opening up in 1978. The teaching will combine staged teaching with special topic teaching. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Economic Thought
Introduction: This course mainly explores from the perspective of economics the records and reflections of Chinese sages on the contradiction between "limited resources and endless human desires" since the origin of human civilization. It mainly includes the economic thoughts of hundreds of pre-Qin scholars, economic policies in various historical periods from the Qin and Han Dynasties to the late Qing Dynasty, and the economic thoughts of relevant figures.

Name: Chinese Financial Markets and Institutions
Prerequisite: No, students are encouraged to study basic financial knowledge.
Introduction: The course aims to help students understand the overall functioning of different financial markets and institutions in the context of the United States and China. We will focus on financial products traded in different financial markets, financial services, and financial instruments, and then on the mechanisms and characteristics inherent in these products, particularly on the risks and benefits of products. All parts of the course have been analysed by the United States market as an example of a general financial phenomenon, followed by a discussion of the similarities and differences between financial markets and financial institutions in China.

Name: Corporate Financial Management
Introduction: This course is the first course on corporate finance management, introduces basic concepts and techniques and establishes an analytical framework for financial decision-making.

Name: Value Proposition and Business Model Design in Technology Entrepreneurship
Introduction:
Any successful business must create value for its customers through an effective business model. This principle may seem straightforward, but the discovery of user value propositions and the design of business models are the most challenging issues faced by entrepreneurs, especially technology entrepreneurs. In the past half century, the vigorous development of technological innovation has promoted research on the theoretical framework of innovation and entrepreneurship. Through nearly two decades of empirical research, the theoretical community has a more advanced grasp of the value creation process, especially the value proposition and business model design models in technological innovation. In recent years, theoretical circles have proposed a series of tools to help technology entrepreneurs design effective organizational value propositions and business models. _x000D_
_x000D_
    Two design tools, the value proposition canvas and the business model canvas, have become widely popular and used among technology entrepreneurs in recent years. However, it is not easy to use these two tools correctly and effectively to help technological innovation enterprises discover promising entrepreneurial opportunities and formulate reasonable entrepreneurial plans. This course will explain, demonstrate, and train the use of these two tools in technology entrepreneurial projects through theoretical discussion, case explanations, and hands-on experiments. The theoretical discussion part of the course will explain the particularity of technology entrepreneurship, deeply analyze the internal logical structure of the two tools, and explain the basic principles of the first stage of lean entrepreneurship. The case explanation part will analyze practical cases in the form of a reverse classroom to help students deepen their understanding of the use of tools. During the course of the course, student groups will combine their own technical backgrounds and try to design a new user value proposition under the guidance of teachers, and design business model support for this value proposition. _x000D_

Name: Quantitative Marketing Models
Introduction: With the rapid accumulation of large amounts of data, more and more business decisions will be driven by data. Therefore, the ability to quantitatively analyze data to obtain valuable information is very important. This course will introduce a series of quantitative models widely used in corporate marketing decisions. Through practical data analysis exercises, the course emphasizes a deep understanding of these models and the ability to apply them to solve real-world problems.

Name: Chinese Business Management Thought
Prerequisite: The first courses are: "The economics of science" or "Microeconomics", "Macroeconomics".
Introduction: This course is aimed at undergraduate students and aims to teach the evolution, change and development of business management ideas in China over thousands of years. The content covers ancient outstanding business economic ideas such as the merchant school, the theory of importance and importance, and the theory of good causes, modern Shanxi merchants' management ideas, and modernization ideas in the fields of finance and finance during the Republic of China. Through learning, it can help students deepen their understanding of various economic issues that have emerged in the current process of China's economic reform, and inspire attention and thinking about real economic issues.

Name: Behavioral Science in Marketing
Introduction: From animals to humans, from ancient times to modern times, from childhood to old age, from the sensory world to responses to prices, what kind of behavioral laws do they contain? How can these laws be applied to marketing? This course will introduce in detail how behavioral science helps us describe and understand market behavior from the perspective of psychology, as well as the behavioral laws revealed in the marketing process. We will start with the history and research paradigms of behavioral science, focusing on the application of various branches of psychology (cognitive, developmental, neuroscience, etc.) and different theories in marketing strategies and market research. In addition, we will explore current issues of concern in marketing and whether we can use existing theories to explain new behaviors. The course content will combine a large number of empirical studies and real-life cases to enable students to understand the importance of behavioral science to marketing.

Name: Sports Marketing
Introduction: Based on the basic theories of marketing, the formulation and implementation of corporate sports marketing strategies, the operating mechanism of sports intermediaries, consumer behavior characteristics and their influencing factors are elaborated and interpreted, and combined with the analysis of relevant cases and student completion of homework, so that students can understand and master certain sports marketing strategies and their implementation skills.

Name: Securities Investment
Introduction: This course takes a strict approach to the core concepts and skills of safe investment and portfolio management. The main concern is the trade-off between risk and benefit, which will be analysed in the framework of average differences. Along this line, the two main theories of asset pricing will be interpreted as capital asset pricing models and arbitrage pricing theories. The empirical examination of both theories will also be discussed. The initial courses of this course are in basic economics, statistics and finance.

Name: Economic History and Economic Growth
Introduction:
We examine the strategies that different countries adopt to promote economic growth and development to maximize their advantages - and minimize their disadvantages. We use economic tools (theoretical and empirical) to structure our analysis. _x000D_
_x000D_
Much of the first part of the course focuses on strategies to maximize the value of a country's stock of human capital, using the Philippines, Iceland, and Singapore as examples. _x000D_
_x000D_
The second part of the course examines the economic growth of China, India, and Japan, specifically examining the timing and nature of their economic acceleration and the challenges they face in maintaining high performance. _x000D_
_x000D_
The third part of the course focuses on institutions as a result of economic growth and as a source of growth performance. It considers the role of inherited institutions - as is the case in South Africa and Saudi Arabia - and the failure of formal institutions in the form of corruption. _x000D_
_x000D_
The fourth part of the course considers how we can, and perhaps should, measure economic growth, taking into account the environment, health and welfare, and GDP.

Name: Western Dramatic Literature
Introduction: This course will expose students to a wide range of Western dramatic literature: the ancient Greek dramas of Aristophanes and Sophocles; medieval Passion plays; plays from Shakespeare's time and the Restoration of Charles II; up to the naturalistic plays of Ibsen, Chekhov and O'Neill; the Expressionist plays of Strindberg; the absurdist plays of Ionesco and Albee; to modern and contemporary Western playwrights, including Sam Shepard, Harold Pinter and David Mamet. The purpose of this course is to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the history of Western theater through in-depth study of repertoire and playwrights. While understanding the long history of Western drama and the representative development and evolution in the history of English, students will also gain an in-depth understanding of contemporary Western culture and thought through the study of contemporary playwrights, as well as an in-depth understanding of idioms and idioms in contemporary British and American English through the language used by contemporary playwrights.

Name: Landscape Aesthetics
College: College of Architecture and Landscape Architecture
Introduction:
This course uses a large number of documents and pictures from the history of art and landscape design to systematically teach and analyze the history of people's aesthetic perception of landscape/landscape and the history of artistic expression. It aims to help students better understand people's perception, imagination and reflection of the surrounding environment in history, and cultivate students' basic abilities in landscape art and landscape aesthetics. It can also provide certain professional help to students in art history and landscape history, architectural design and urban planning, and related majors. _x000D_
_x000D_
The main content of this course involves three parts:_x000D_
1. The development and thought of gardens. _x000D_
From the day it was born, the issue of landscape has been inseparable from the philosophical thoughts of various eras. This course will introduce classical period landscapes, medieval gardens, Renaissance gardens, Baroque gardens, British landscape gardens and American national parks in chronological order. _x000D_
2. The expression of landscape in the art of painting. _x000D_
The history of landscape design and landscape painting has a high degree of consistency, both in terms of aesthetic experience and philosophical thinking. Especially after the landscape painting period in the 17th century, humankind's understanding of landscape and environment developed rapidly. This course will teach the development history of landscape painting according to the clues of time during the development of the above-mentioned gardens, focusing on the expressions of landscape by Claude Lorraine in the Classical Period, Constable and Turner in the Romantic Period, and Monet and Cézanne in the Impressionist Period. _x000D_
3. Modern landscape expression form. _x000D_
Since the concept of landscape design was established in the 19th century, the expression of landscape has begun to develop in many aspects. This part mainly introduces the modern urban landscape represented by Paris in the 19th century, the land art of the mid-20th century, monument landscape, and landscape expression in photography. _x000D_
4. A comparative perspective: Chinese landscape_x000D_
Chinese garden thought has been studied by many scholars. This course will be based on Western teaching clues and explore how to view the particularity and contemporary contributions of Chinese gardens from this perspective. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Early Modern Western Philosophy
Introduction: "Modern Western Philosophy" will trace the development of Western philosophy from Descartes to Hegel. Starting from the 17th century, Western philosophy entered the modern period and lasted until the 19th century. A basic thread running through modern philosophy can be said to be the principle of subjectivity. Around this main line, modern philosophy can be divided into two major stages: the 17th and 18th centuries were the first stage, which was mainly characterized by the dispute between British empiricism and continental rationalism surrounding issues such as the source of knowledge, methods of cognition, and standards of truth. The representatives of continental rationalism are Descartes, Leibniz and Spinoza; the main representatives of British empiricism are Bacon, Hobbes, Locke, Berkeley and Hume. The second stage was from the end of the 18th century to the middle of the 19th century. German philosophers summarized the previous thoughts to varying degrees and in different ways, especially the dispute between empiricism and rationalism, and created German classical philosophy represented by Kant, Fichte, Schelling and Hegel. German classical philosophers saw that since the Renaissance, humans have certainly been liberated from the shackles of God, but the mechanistic cosmology of the 17th and 18th centuries once again made human spirit and subjectivity subject to the causal inevitability of nature. As a result, they once again fought to maintain human agency, autonomy and subjectivity. Without exception, they all start from the spirit and strive to realize the unity of the world on the basis of spirit.

Name: Introduction to Emotionally Intelligent Robots
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Strong artificial intelligence is an ideal that people have been striving for for a long time. Intelligent robots are the physical sustenance of this ideal and appear in various forms in many science fiction literature, film and television works. Intelligent robots can understand human language and understand people's voices; they can look into people's eyes and recognize the surrounding environment; they can feel, react and think better, and they can also gain experience and grow through learning. And emotional capabilities are crucial for intelligent robots. Without the ability to understand and express emotions, it will be difficult for intelligent robots to interact naturally with people, let alone proactively identify people's negative emotions and respond positively. _x000D_
    This course introduces emotionally intelligent robots, demonstrates the robot's movement, perception, control, intelligence and architecture, explains the role, expression, recognition, regulation and psychological basis of emotion, discusses the robot's emotion recognition model for humans through various perception methods, and finally explores the robot's emotion regulation method. This course also includes practical sessions on building robots using LEGO EV3. _x000D_
    This course is an introductory course for undergraduates across the school. It does not involve complex mathematics or physical reasoning and operations, nor does it require excessive computer programming skills. It mainly discusses the concepts, principles, models, and implementation of emotionally intelligent robots. It is hoped that students who choose this course can have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of emotionally intelligent robots and lay a solid foundation for further learning or related applications. _x000D_
    This course is assessed through a combination of regular classroom results and final papers. _x000D_

Name: Investment and Personal Finance
Prerequisite: The first courses, such as Accounting Principles or Investment Banking, Corporate Finance, require students to have some prior financial knowledge.
Introduction: Investment is a “money-making” process. Modern human beings must face the problems of investment and wealth management regardless of their occupation. Because of the time value of the currency, inflation is more likely to erode individual wealth under the currency-based system. If the focus is not on investment management, individual assets may be automatically redistributed “market”. The vast majority of financial management activities are related to capital markets. Investment banks and wealth management are two sides of the same capital market, and investment banks are sellers and buyers of wealth. The saying that “selling is always smarter than buying” means that financial market sellers are better informed by the use of financial engineering analysis tools to design products, and it is necessary to start research from the seller to make wealth management more effective. The course began with a presentation on the re-marketing of investment banks, the sponsorship system, the enterprise rating system, the project evaluation methodology, asset securitization, overall listing, de-marketing, shell listing, shell listing, mergers and acquisitions, and an attempt to provide a comprehensive picture of investment banking operations, taking into account the cases. On this basis, the time value of the currency, the construction of the portfolio, the analysis of the investment environment, the application of investment instruments, the analysis of investment returns and risks, the development of wealth management strategies, the development of financial management strategies, the formation of quantitative expectations, the development of asset allocation plans, the adoption of fundamental selection shares, the selection of times through technical analysis, and how to manage financial risk, and, finally, the assessment of financial management performance. To equip students with basic skills in financial management and prepare them intellectually for their future personal financial planning.

Name: Python Language Fundamentals and Applications
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course is intended for zero basic students at the university level in arts and sciences without prior courses.
Introduction:
This course is based on the lecturer’s many years of practical teaching experience in teaching data structure and algorithm courses (Python version) at Peking University. It is aimed at college students and the general public with zero programming knowledge. It comprehensively teaches the basics of Python language, cultivates students’ computational thinking abilities, and explains the classic extension modules in Python language, so that students can use Python language to solve various common problems. _x000D_
The content of this course includes programming and computational thinking, Python language history, development environment, programming style and overall overview of the language, basic data types and container types, basic calculation statements and control flow structures, function definitions and parameters, introduction and application of several basic extension modules, object-oriented programming, advanced language features such as exception handling and generators, and the introduction and application of several advanced extension modules. _x000D_
This course focuses on the practice and application of the Python language. Vivid cases and programming exercises are interspersed in the course to guide students to actively establish a computational thinking model and deepen their learning experience of the programming language through program algorithms to solve problems. And have the ability to further study courses such as data structures and algorithms, artificial intelligence, and big data processing.

Name: Virtual Reality Content Creation
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course is open to students in the arts and literature at the school level, without prior courses.
Introduction:
Virtual simulation technology, which consists of virtual reality, augmented reality and simulation, has become a hot topic of innovative technology in recent years. 2016 is known as the first year of VR (virtual reality). Various VR hardware and systems have been explosively unveiled. Virtual reality will subvert many industries in the next 5 to 10 years. Virtual simulation can be applied to many fields involving the national economy and people's livelihood, such as academic research, education and training, leisure tourism, urban planning, and security emergency response. _x000D_
This course is a parallel extension of the public elective course "Virtual Simulation Innovation Application and Practice". It introduces various types of virtual reality content, and focuses on strengthening practical teaching links to teach the characteristics of virtual reality content creation, tool platforms and development practices to improve students' innovation ability, practical ability and employability.

Name: Introduction to Web Technologies
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
This is an overview course through which students can gain a comprehensive understanding of the software architecture of the World Wide Web and the evolution of various related technologies. _x000D_
This is also an online course, which basically cancels classroom lectures and mainly teaches through courseware and forum communication. _x000D_
The content covers an overview of Web protocols, Web architecture, HTML, Perl, PHP, Javascript, Java, XML, Web2.0, etc., with corresponding programming exercises every week. _x000D_
Through this course, students will have first-hand practical programming experience in the software technologies involved, and improve students' independent learning abilities based on the Internet.

Name: Fundamentals of Digital Media Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Probability statistics, algorithm design and analysis
Introduction: This course enables students to master the basic concepts and principles related to digital media technology, and master the representative algorithms and applications of image and video analysis, including primitive detection, image segmentation, foreground description, background modeling, and object recognition. Through course practice, you will initially acquire the ability to carry out scientific research in the field of digital media technology, such as local invariant descriptors, converting flat video to stereoscopic video, and moving target detection and tracking. Understand how these hot spots break through and innovate compared with traditional aspects, and choose one of the topics to carry out scientific research practice. _x000D_

Name: Automatic Control Theory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Linear algebra

As a result, there is no requirement to start with courses in circuit mechanics, signals and systems.

At the same time, the basic methods of perception modules closely related to robot control are introduced. The practical part arranges practical exercises on affective computing and robot perception, requiring students to combine theory with the implementation and evaluation of affective computing under the physical vision platform.

Digital signal processing

Name: Technological Innovation and Entrepreneurship
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: The curriculum is open to students at all levels and in all professions, without prior requirements.
Introduction:
In the 21st century, where science and technology are changing rapidly and society is changing rapidly, it is no longer enough to master only one professional skill to adapt to the ever-changing workplace, and it is not enough to achieve a fulfilling and complete self. In view of this, with the support of the "Computer Science Department Alumni Lecture Fund" initiated by classmates of the Department of Computer Science in 1984, the "Career Planning and Leadership Development" summer course was offered for six consecutive years from 2008 to 2013, which was well received by students who chose the course. In recent years, courses have become more and more focused on innovation and entrepreneurship. Therefore, starting in the spring of 2016, a new public elective course on “Technological Innovation and Entrepreneurship” was established at Peking University. _x000D_
     The course aims to cultivate students' innovative thinking, enable students to understand basic entrepreneurial processes such as industry analysis, demand understanding, product design, and business planning, and master entrepreneurial skills such as team building and leadership development. The course focuses on students listening to lectures, inviting many outstanding entrepreneurs and successful entrepreneurs to give lectures, interspersed with a large number of classroom discussions, and supplemented by practical case analysis of the Internet of Things, corporate big data, artificial intelligence, high-tech industries, etc. _x000D_

This course introduces fifteen great poets in chronological order: Chaucer, Spenser, Shakespeare, Donne, Herbert, Milton, Blake, Wordsworth, Coleridge, Byron, Shelley, Keats, Tennyson, Browning, and Christina Rossetti, starting from the end of the fourteenth century to the end of the nineteenth century, trying to show the development trajectory of English poetry in the past five hundred years. The purpose is to stimulate students' interest in poetry, cultivate their appreciation of English poetry, and improve their English proficiency and cultural literacy. _x000D_

In addition to their own great achievements, low-dimensional manifolds have also promoted the vigorous development of geometric group theory and opened a new chapter for dynamical systems.

Name: Critical Thinking and Academic Writing
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course will introduce students to the requirements and rules of critical thinking and academic writing, focusing on text analysis, the construction of effective arguments and the use of evidence and secondary data, and explaining the basic process of writing. _x000D_
Students strengthen their critical thinking abilities and refine their rhetorical skills by reading challenging material in a variety of genres and writing with an emphasis on revision and style. _x000D_

Introduction: Regression analysis is a course closely integrated with practical applications. Through the study of this course, you will master the theory and methods of regression analysis, and be able to correctly interpret regression results; at the same time, you will master some basic theories and techniques of applied statistics, and be able to use statistical software to solve practical problems.

We are also preparing to gradually cultivate students’ interest and research abilities in modern German history through student reports, discussions and other teaching methods.

Introduction: In addition to teaching error analysis, polynomial interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration, numerical methods of nonlinear equations, and numerical solutions to initial value problems of ordinary differential equations, this course also teaches fast Fourier transformation and Monte Carlo method, which are the contents of traditional numerical analysis courses. This course emphasizes not only the mathematical analysis and principles of various numerical algorithms, but also the implementation of the algorithms.

Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, upper algebra, differential equation
Introduction: This course is an elective course for senior undergraduate students majoring in computational mathematics, and is a prerequisite course for the "Computational Fluid Dynamics" course for graduate students majoring in computational mathematics. The content of this course is a systematic introduction to the basic concepts of fluid mechanics, basic theories and the derivation process of the involved partial differential equations.

Name: Convex Optimization
Prerequisite: Mathematic analysis (high math), upper algebra (linear algebra)
Introduction: Convex optimization is a broad discipline increasingly used in scientific and engineering computing, economics, management, industry and other fields. It involves establishing an appropriate mathematical model to describe the problem, designing appropriate calculation methods to find the optimal solution to the problem, studying the theoretical properties of the model and algorithm, and examining the computational performance of the algorithm. This introductory course is suitable for senior undergraduate and graduate students in mathematics, statistics, computer science, electrical engineering, operations research and other disciplines. Teaching content includes an introduction to convex sets, convex functions and convex optimization problems; basic knowledge of convex analysis; dual theory; gradient algorithm, approximate gradient algorithm, Nesterov acceleration method, alternating direction multiplier method; interior point algorithm, applications in statistics, signal processing and machine learning.

Name: Algorithms in Big Data Analysis
Introduction: Big data brings unprecedented opportunities and challenges to data analysis and processing. This course introduces some algorithms in big data analysis: sparse and low-rank representation of data, sparse and low-rank matrix optimization, graph and network flow problems in social network computing, optimization algorithms for machine learning and data mining, stochastic optimization algorithms, parallel computing, etc.

Name: Textual Analysis and Appreciation of British and American Short Stories
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: Through the study of basic courses, non-English major undergraduates have read many English articles of various genres, including expository essays, argumentative essays, novels, etc. However, students are limited by the length of text selections and cannot read a large number of English novels. Even if they can read a few, they often only have a superficial understanding. This course is designed to meet the reading needs of literature-loving students in English short stories, and to systematically understand the components and writing techniques of short stories, so as to improve reading comprehension, text analysis and literary appreciation, and enhance their understanding of Western culture. This course selects 15 famous short stories from the United Kingdom and the United States. They are divided into seven parts according to the basic elements of the novel, which are: background, characters, plot, point of view, theme, symbol, and style. When explaining each part, the teacher selects two novels as examples to guide students to deeply understand the themes and writing characteristics of the novels. Students are required to preview selected novels before class, participate in class discussions, and complete essay writing.

Name: Algebra Seminar
Introduction: As a special course to cultivate high-quality basic talents, this course will enable students to master the basic concepts, basic theories and basic methods of algebra, receive basic training in algebra, and lay a solid foundation for the study of further algebra courses. Cultivate students' mathematical thinking methods and self-study abilities. The main content of this course includes preliminary knowledge of groups, rings, and modules.

Name: Homological Algebra
Prerequisite: High algebra, abstract algebra, ring and model.
Introduction: The main content of this course is the theory and application of homology and cohomology in category theory. It is one of the important foundations of algebra, algebraic geometry, algebraic number theory, complex manifolds and other disciplines. From an international perspective, most of today's world-class universities offer this course for students to take. According to reports from students studying abroad in our college, they found it difficult after going abroad due to lack of foundation in this area. The establishment of this course is meaningful for building a world-class university and cultivating high-level basic mathematics talents.

Name: Qualitative Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations
Prerequisite:
Functional Analysis II is a basic course for graduate students and an elective course for senior undergraduate students. Prerequisite courses include: _x000D_
1. Real variable function_x000D_
2. Functional Analysis I. This part mainly includes banach space and bounded operator theory.
Introduction: This course is a systematic introduction to the basic knowledge of linear operator theory based on undergraduate functional analysis. If functional analysis I corresponds to the Fredholm theory of integral equations, that is, the theory of bounded operators, then II corresponds to the study of (unbounded) differential operators, especially the study of the Schrödinger operator. Its physical background is quantum mechanics. The main purpose of the course is to understand the following key points: self-adjoint expansion of unbounded (symmetric) operators; perturbation of self-adjoint operators; convergence of self-adjoint operators; spectral decomposition theory of self-adjoint operators; semigroup theory; and concepts related to Feynman road integrals, such as Feynman-Kac formula, Werner measure, etc. The course is basic in the theoretical aspects of differential equations and analysis.

Name: Real Analysis

Name: Qualitative Theory of Ordinary Differential Equations
Prerequisite: Regular differential equation, differential equation, general correspondence analysis
Introduction: In this course, we will teach the basic contents of qualitative theory, including: phase plane analysis, preliminary branch theory, existence of periodic solutions, Poincare-Bendixson theorem, Denjoy's theorem of homeomorphisms on circles, and normative theory of mapping and vector fields.

Name: Fundamentals of Nonlinear Analysis
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge of modern mathematical analysis research, mainly about differential calculus in infinite dimensional space, nonlinear operator theory and functional critical points. It is a basic course in geometry, dynamical systems, differential equations, computational mathematics, operations research, probability, etc. Teach analysis in infinite-dimensional space; compressed image principle; implicit function theorem; transversality and Sard-Smale theorem; topological degree theory and variational method, etc.

Name: Theory of Biological Evolution
Prerequisite:
1. There is a biological basis
2. Suggested attendance by students who are interested in this subject but believe in the creationism of theology
3. Recommended that students be carefully selected (Chinese and biological fundamentals)
4. English-based (some animations and terms in English)
Introduction: The theory of evolution is fundamental to the foundations of biology and its basic principles apply to all areas of the life sciences. The purpose of this course is mainly to enable students to have a comprehensive understanding of the emergence, revision, development and continuous improvement of the main arguments of Darwin's theory of evolution; at the same time, they will have an understanding of Lamarckian evolution theory, Kimura's neutral theory, and Gould's punctuated equilibrium theory. This course will start with Darwin's theory of evolution, trying to use the principles and laws of evolution to explain phenomena and issues from ancient fossils to today's colorful biological world, from changes in biological morphology to changes in genetic material, from the origin of biomolecules to the origin of human beings. In the 1950s, several famous population geneticists He made important contributions to the improvement of Darwin's theory of evolution. Although Mr. Kimura of Japan is not as famous as Darwin, his "neutral theory of evolution" was once thought to overthrow Darwin's theory of evolution and caused a sensation in the world. Now people realize that both the neutral theory and the balance theory are important supplements to Darwin's plan theory. With the rapid progress of the human genome and the determination of the genomes of various model organisms such as Escherichia coli, yeast, nematodes, fruit flies, Arabidopsis, rice, corn, mice, chimpanzees, and even extinct Neanderthals, people have gained a deeper understanding of life and discovered many new problems. This course will try to answer these questions from an evolutionary perspective: Evolution occurs at all levels of organisms at any time and at any time. Is there a connection between them? How to conduct research? This course will provide you with some of the latest scientific research progress to illustrate these issues. In short, this course will introduce to you the latest methods, research results and trends in the field of evolution on the basis of teaching the basic concepts, principles and laws of evolution, so that everyone can truly understand the words of a genetics master: "Without evolution, biology will be meaningless."

Name: Mathematical Methods in Image Processing
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, linear algebra, numerical methods
Introduction:
We live in the digital age, and the generation, dissemination, integration, analysis and processing of data have become an indispensable part of our lives. Images are undoubtedly one of the most important types of data, not only because we frequently use images in daily communication, but also because images can present the physical world very concisely and are widely used in many fields. The rapid development of computer technology allows us to use very profound and exquisite mathematical tools to design effective solutions to problems in image processing. Therefore, many mathematical methods in image processing have been accepted and widely used in many different fields, including the field of natural science, high-tech field, social media field, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is suitable for graduate students and senior undergraduate students majoring in applied and computational mathematics, engineering, and computer science. The course content includes (but is not limited to) variational methods, partial differential equations, wavelet analysis, and their applications in image processing, including image denoising, deblurring, segmentation, registration, medical imaging, computer graphics, computer vision, etc.

Name: Bayesian Theory and Algorithms
Introduction: Bayesian analysis is an important branch of statistics and has important applications in data analysis. The purpose of this course is to learn and master the basic theory, reasoning and calculation methods of Bayesian analysis; and to cultivate students' awareness and ability to use Bayesian theory to solve practical problems by interspersing recent examples of Bayesian models.

Name: Sample Surveys

Introduction: This course is an important branch of mathematical statistics. It is a discipline about how to effectively extract samples to collect data and make statistical inferences and analyzes of various indicators of the population. This course will systematically teach various sampling methods such as simple random sampling, unequal sampling, stratified sampling, multi-stage sampling, cluster sampling, systematic sampling, two-phase sampling and their corresponding statistical inference methods. It will also discuss some common issues in sampling practice. It has wide applications in natural sciences and social sciences.

Name: The American Political System
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will take the form of student reading, teacher explanation, group discussion, etc. to introduce students to a series of related topics in the field of the American political system. Upon completion of this course, students will have a more comprehensive understanding of the American political system and how it operates, as well as a deeper and more sensitive appreciation of the role of political analysis in understanding the workings of society. This course focuses on explaining the political system and operational processes of the U.S. government (such as the Constitution, Congress, presidential system, legal system, etc.), and also provides common analytical methods that need to be used in political research. What is politics? What is power? Who gets what? When and how was it obtained? The way these issues are interpreted not only helps understand the American political system, but can also be used to analyze other topics.

Introduction: Develop students' ability to use mathematics to study random events in non-life insurance. Through teaching, students are required to master relevant loss models, use statistical theory to estimate loss distribution, and master methods for determining rates and withdrawing reserves.

The main purpose of this undergraduate course in financial time series analysis is to cultivate students' solid foundation in the basic theories of linear time series, including the theories and methods of models, forecasts, and parameter estimation.
