Name: Introduction to Engineering Design
Introduction: This course is a compulsory professional course for the engineering analysis major of the Department of Mechanics and Engineering Science, School of Engineering, Peking University. It teaches selected teaching and practice covering loads, steel structures, design methods, stability and reinforced concrete, as well as general engineering software, so that students can master important engineering knowledge, calculation and design capabilities within a certain range.

Name: Engineering Economics
Introduction: Engineering economics is an interdisciplinary subject of engineering and economics. It is a subject that studies and analyzes engineering technology practical activities and the economic accounting and benefits involved. This course takes common projects or practices in various engineering fields as the main research subject, and uses technical and economic system analysis as the main research tool. It teaches how to use various mathematical tools and computer knowledge to conduct project evaluation and design, how to effectively utilize resources and improve economic benefits; how to realize the necessary functions of products, operations, and services at low cost in a shorter life cycle. In terms of research methods, this course involves the basic contents of general engineering theory, statistics, economics, industrial engineering and accounting. The teaching method pays equal attention to methodology teaching and case teaching, and guides students to use the content they have learned to carry out simple engineering practice training.

Name: Engineering Theory of Elasticity
Prerequisite: Engineering mathematics, theoretical mechanics, material mechanics
Introduction: The engineering elasticity mechanics course uses tensors as tools to systematically expound the basic concepts, basic principles and basic methods of classical elasticity mechanics. It not only focuses on the systematicness, completeness and rigor of the theory, but also focuses on integrating theory with practice. The main contents include: strain theory, stress theory, constitutive relations, basic equations of elastic mechanics, solutions to plane problems and cylinder torsion problems, etc.

Name: Innovation Practicum in Engineering
Introduction: The Engineering Innovation Practice Course is a course that focuses on students’ hands-on practice. Students will work in small groups to complete the entire process from original creativity to innovative design to hands-on production of prototypes of innovative works to comprehensively enhance students' innovative awareness, innovative spirit and innovative practical abilities.

Name: Advanced Seminar in Economics
Prerequisite: Secondary microeconomics, intermediate econometrics, at least one essay course
Introduction: This course is offered to third- and fourth-year undergraduate students in economics and double majors at the National School of Development. The purpose is to provide thesis guidance for students who have completed most of the courses, have excellent grades, and are ready to take the path of economic research. The content includes guidance on topic selection, intensive reading of literature, and guidance on thesis. This course uses small class teaching and uses a combination of teacher lectures and student reports to guide students to learn scientific research paradigms and paper writing methods.

Name: Aerospace Information Engineering
Prerequisite: Modern generals of engineering, aerospace generals
Introduction: Aerospace information engineering is the core research direction in the field of aerospace engineering. This course will combine domestic and foreign aerospace engineering practices to extract core theories and technologies such as aerospace information acquisition, aerospace information organization, aerospace information storage, aerospace information processing, aerospace information transmission, aerospace information distribution, aerospace information application, etc., as the main teaching content of the course to make up for the deficiencies in the knowledge system of our school students in this professional field. Course teaching is organized in the form of classroom lectures, literature reading, discussions, and reports. Through the study of this course, students will master the basic theory and technical system of aerospace information engineering, understand the research hot spots and development trends in aerospace information engineering, and lay the foundation for students' future scientific research and engineering practice.

Name: China's Macroeconomy
Introduction: This course is designed to help senior undergraduates gain a deeper understanding of several important macroeconomic phenomena that have occurred in China since the reform and opening up, especially in the past 20 years, as well as the economic laws behind these phenomena. It also trains students to use standardized and rigorous macroeconomic research methods to conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis of real-life macroeconomic phenomena and related economic policies, fully understand the gap between China's real macroeconomics and mainstream macroeconomic textbook models, and improve their ability to conduct economic analysis of real problems.

Name: Economic and Political Philosophy
Introduction: This course is a small class class with equal emphasis on teacher teaching and student discussion. It aims to develop students' interest in thinking about the philosophical issues behind economics and cultivate their critical thinking skills. The course will consist of both empirical facts and theoretical discussions. The former will present the distributional consequences of the market, especially its performance in China and India, and discuss the general laws of income and wealth distribution under market economy conditions; the latter will discuss the philosophical meaning of general equilibrium, people in the market, social justice theory, public choice, political systems, etc. The course will require students to read a large number of original works and participate in class discussions. The course will also arrange debates among students on designated topics. Class participation and debate count towards course grade, and students are required to submit a term paper.

Name: Appreciation of Classical Chinese Gardens
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course will focus on sorting out the occurrence and evaluation mechanisms of Chinese classical gardens. By placing the management practice of mountain building and water management in Chinese classical gardens within the broader landscape management of Chinese art, it is possible to combine the management of artistic conception of Chinese classical gardens with the management of landscape artistic conception of traditional Chinese landscape poetry and landscape painting, expand students' theoretical vision of the knowledge system of Chinese art, and promote students' cross-field and interdisciplinary thinking. _x000D_
This course will also use French classical gardens as a reference and explore the environmental concepts of Chinese and Western cultural differences from a cultural comparison perspective, rather than just seeing this difference as a gap. This will be conducive to targeted and effective reflection on China's modern and contemporary cultural environmental concepts from a cultural history perspective. _x000D_
By placing China's modern and contemporary environmental issues in a broader international perspective, we hope to not only expand non-garden major students' general vision of Chinese classical gardens, but also hope that they can re-evaluate and examine China's modern and contemporary environmental issues based on their majors.

Name: Ancient Eastern Civilizations
Introduction: "Ancient Eastern Civilization" will systematically introduce ancient civilizations in West Asia, including Sumerian civilization, Akkadian civilization, Babylonian civilization, Assyrian civilization and ancient Persian civilization, as well as ancient Egyptian civilization, ancient Indus Valley civilization, Hittite civilization, Ebla civilization and Elamite civilization, from 3300 BC to 331 BC. Specific content includes history, culture, literature, writing, archeology, history of interpretation, and the research history and current situation of each civilization.

Name: Fundamentals of Combustion
Introduction: "Fundamentals of Combustion" is the main technical basic course for the first-level disciplines of power engineering and engineering thermophysics, aerospace power, energy and environment, etc. It is a specialized subject that studies the conversion of fossil fuel chemical energy into thermal energy.

Name: Global Innovative Product Design and Team Practice
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
"Global Innovative Product Design and Team Practice" is a major course of the World Classroom iPodia Alliance initiated by the University of Southern California in the United States and jointly offered by universities in five other countries. Students register and choose iPodia courses at their own schools, take courses at the same time in iPodia remote interactive classes distributed in various partner schools, and form teams to complete innovative project collaborations that break the barriers of space, school and culture. Students who choose courses scattered around the world enjoy unified course content and are evaluated using unified academic standards, just like "one classroom". _x000D_
"Global Innovative Product Design and Team Practice" mainly includes three teaching contents: 1) lectures and discussions; 2) cross-cultural experience; 3) team innovation projects. There are also some alternative course projects, such as students from different schools participating in the course gathered in a certain school after the semester to carry out cross-cultural innovative practices. All details of the course are described in the course schedule.

Name: Numerical Simulation of Turbulence
Introduction: This course teaches the basic theory, modeling, and numerical simulation methods of turbulence. The content includes the statistical properties and phenomenological model of turbulence, Reynolds mean equation, eddy viscosity model and Reynolds stress model, shear turbulence, uniform isotropic turbulence, wall turbulence, direct numerical simulation and large eddy simulation, and scalar turbulence.

Name: Topics in Methods of Mathematical Physics
Prerequisite: Introduction to mathematical physical methods, or basis for mathematical physical methods, or mathematical physical methods, or mathematical physical methods (up and down), as well as linear algebra, advanced mathematics
Introduction:
This course introduces generalized functions, Hilbert spaces, integral transformations, integral equations, integral solutions to differential equations, nonlinear equations, solitons, wavelet transforms, mathematical methods in field theory, preliminary group theory and other mathematical physics knowledge as well as new developments in recent years to meet the higher requirements of teachers and students in some majors. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Solid State Physics Problem Session
Introduction: The course addresses the application of solid physics curriculum knowledge to address specific issues and to give students flexibility in basic concepts of solid physics and ways to address them

Name: Quantum Mechanics (II)
Introduction: On the basis of quantum mechanics I, introduce the basic theory of He atoms and multi-electron atoms, mainly discussing the perturbation theory and variational method in quantum mechanics; Hartree theory, Hartree-Fock theory and Thomas-Fermi theory. Rotation spectrum and vibration spectrum of diatomic molecules and polyatomic molecules. Basic concepts of valence bond theory. Introducing the Feynman path integral method in quantum mechanics (taking free particles and oscillators as an example). Introducing WKB approximation, Bohr Quantization conditions, tunneling of potential barriers. Coherent state description of states in quantum mechanics; introduction to phase in quantum mechanics, including experimental observation of the Aharonov-Bohm effect; quantum mechanical phase effects caused by gravity; introduction to Berry phase and Aharonov-Anandan. Discuss the concepts of density matrix theory and Wigner function in quantum mechanics.

Name: Advanced Quantum Mechanics
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic skills of how to use the principles of quantum mechanics to calculate the physical quantities of few-body and many-body boson and fermion systems, and prepares for further study of quantum many-body theory and quantum field theory. The content includes: the second quantization (particle number representation) method, the permutation symmetry of the identical multi-body particle system, single particle creation and annihilation operators, as well as the expressions of boson and fermion single and two-body operators in the particle number representation and the calculation of the corresponding matrix elements; formal perturbation theory and scattering theory. The contents include representation theory, general properties of time evolution operators in interaction representations and their formal solutions; angular momentum theory. The content includes three-dimensional space rotation group and its linear representation, quantization of rotational rigid body system, definition of irreducible tensor operator group and application of Wigner-Eckart theorem; application of group theory method in quantum mechanics. Mainly introduces the symmetry operation group of quantum mechanical system, the classification of eigenstates of quantum system according to the irreducible representation of its symmetry operation group, the application of eigensign theory and the selection rules of transition matrix elements; the time reversal symmetry of quantum mechanical system. The content includes the time reversal symmetry of the Hamiltonian, the properties of the inverse unitary positive operator, the change of internal degrees of freedom under time reversal transformation and Kramer's theorem; relativistic quantum mechanics. Mainly introduces the Klein-Gordon equation, the Dirac equation and its relativistic covariance, the spin of Dirac particles, the plane wave solution of free electrons, and the introduction of the concept of antielectrons. At the same time, the non-relativistic approximation of the Dirac equation in the electromagnetic field and the derivation of the spin-orbit coupling interaction term are introduced.

Name: Quantum Statistical Physics
Introduction: This course is a necessary theoretical basis for studying quantum many-body systems for graduate students who are preparing to engage in research in theoretical physics and condensed matter physics. The teaching of the course focuses on the explanation of physical concepts and the ability to apply basic theories to solve problems.

Name: Particle Physics
Introduction: Enable students to understand and master the basic knowledge, basic concepts and basic methods of particle physics. It is suitable for students majoring in physics who are purely physics-oriented. This course is a theoretical physics course for undergraduates majoring in physics, and can also lay a solid foundation for future graduate courses in theoretical physics. This course provides an intuitive and accurate explanation of new physical mechanisms, physical concepts, and physical laws in particle physics, focusing on new important developments and development trends in particle physics. Focus on inspiring people to think about problems physically. See http://www.phy.pku.edu.cn/~shzhu/par_2011.htm

Name: Group Theory
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of advanced mathematics, linear algebra, solid physics
Introduction: This course is one of the main basic courses for graduate students and is also suitable for senior undergraduate students to take as an elective. Through the study of this course, you can master the mathematical theory of more systematic groups and their representations and the practical application of group theory in physics, and use it as a powerful mathematical tool to solve related problems encountered in research.

Name: Quantum Field Theory
Introduction: Quantum field theory is the basic quantum theory for the treatment of micro-basic particles and their interactions, and the theoretical foundation necessary for research in particle physics, field theory, etc.

Name: Plasma Physics
Introduction:
This course is an introductory course in plasma physics for undergraduate and graduate students. Teach the basic knowledge of plasma physics and fusion, and introduce relevant progress in laboratory plasma, space and astrophysics research. It is conducted through classroom lectures and self-study on special topics. Strive to highlight the key points of the class content, explain with scientific research cases, and introduce the latest cutting-edge research. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Topics in Nonlinear Physics
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the principles and methods of nonlinear dynamics and pattern dynamics in nonlinear science and their applications in physics, chemistry and biology. Through the study of this course, you can master the basic theories and methods in nonlinear science and lay the foundation for applying them to the research of complex problems in various disciplines. This course covers a wide range of knowledge and requires candidates to have taken advanced mathematics and general physics. It is suitable for graduate students interested in physics, chemistry, biology and other majors.

Name: Lie Groups and Lie Algebras
Introduction: This enables students to have an understanding of the basic structures of Lie groups and Lie algebras as well as the representations of Lie groups and Lie algebras commonly used in physics. It is suitable for undergraduate students majoring in pure physics and graduate students majoring in theoretical physics in the School of Physics.

Name: Physical Properties of Quantum Materials
Prerequisite: Quantum mechanics, solid physics, generals, etc.
Introduction: The so-called quantum materials are material systems that exhibit macroscopic quantum effects. In recent years, the physical properties of quantum materials have become one of the most important research fields in current physical sciences (physics, materials science, nanoscience, etc.). This course starts from the perspective of experimental science and introduces the current scientific research progress and achievements related to the physical properties of quantum materials, as well as experimental methods and means. Provide students with relevant knowledge reserves, while cultivating students' scientific research abilities in reading relevant literature and designing relevant experiments.

Name: Quantum Theory of Many-Body Systems
Prerequisite: Advanced quantum mechanics, quantum statistics, solid physics
Introduction: Green's function is an important theoretical method for dealing with quantum many-body system problems and is one of the core contents of quantum statistical physics. This course focuses on the basic concepts of Green's function: zero temperature and finite temperature Green's function, S matrix, Wick theorem, Feynman-Dyson expansion, spectral representation theory, Hartree-Fork approximation, RPA approximation. Two-particle Green's function, vertex angle function, etc. Use the Feynman graph expansion of the Green's function and the equation of motion method to solve physical problems raised by the electron transport process and phase transitions caused by multi-body interactions: such as the conductance of metals, ferromagnetic phase transitions in the tunneling conductance S=1/2 Heisenberg model, superconducting Green's function, Josephson junction; as well as the Hubbard model, Anderson model, Kondo effect of strongly correlated systems, etc. Through teaching, students can master the basic concepts of Green's function and the ability to deal with many-body theoretical problems.

Name: Theory of Solids
Prerequisite: General physics, quantum mechanics, thermodynamics and statistical mechanics, electrodynamics, solid physics, advanced quantum mechanics, quantum statistics
Introduction:
Solid State Theory is a specialized course for graduate students majoring in condensed matter to learn the basic concepts, analytical methods and research overview in this field. This course focuses on key concepts and theoretical methods that are widely used and fundamental, such as many-body problems and energy band methods for analyzing solid electronic structures. At the same time, some important research fields and current scientific research trends are introduced to lay a solid foundation for students to engage in scientific research. This course will specifically cover the following content:_x000D_
1.	Some methods for dealing with multi-body problems include Thomas-Fermi approximation, Hartree-Fock approximation, RPA and Green's function method, etc. _x000D_
2．	Solid electronic calculation methods, including Bloch function, density functional and pseudopotential method, etc. _x000D_
3.	Phonon theory. _x000D_
4.	The principle of symmetry breaking and macroscopic quantum phenomena, including superconductivity, superfluidity, ferromagnetism and antiferromagnetism, etc.

Name: Fluid Mechanics
Prerequisite:
Higher mathematics, mechanics and thermal studies are the first courses.

Chapter I. Mathematics Basics - Theory (8 hours)
Chapter II Basic concepts of hydrodynamics (10 school hours)
Chapter III Basic equation group (10 hours)
Chapter V. Fluid vortex movement (10 academic hours)
Chapter IV. Fluid electrostatics (3 academic hours)
Chapter VI Benuly points and their application (2 academic hours)
Chapter VII Fluid fluctuations base (6 hours)
Chapter VIII. Introduction (2 hours of schooling)
Introduction: The atmosphere and ocean are the most common fluids, and their movement and changes affect our human life and production. Fluid mechanics is the basic discipline that studies the macroscopic motion laws of such fluids. It is widely integrated with other disciplines to form a number of vibrant disciplines, such as biological fluids, computational fluids, environmental fluids, magnetic fluids, geofluid mechanics, etc. This course mainly introduces the basic concepts of fluid mechanics, basic equations of motion, vortex motion, hydrostatics, fluid fluctuations, etc. The course focuses on understanding the nature of physics, emphasizing the basic ideas of establishing mathematical models, and then mastering the general laws and solution methods of fluid motion. Students must complete their homework carefully and master the necessary basic knowledge and academic ideas.

Name: Introduction to Plasmonics
Prerequisite: There's a need for some kind of electrodynamic, solid physics, optical knowledge.
Introduction:
As a research hotspot at the intersection of nano-optics and materials science, surface plasmon polaritons (SPP) can achieve mutual coupling and resonance with incident photons, thus proposing new ideas for the development of nanoscale optoelectronic devices. This course mainly introduces the preparation of SPP nanostructures using micro-nano processing technology, uses near-field optical microscopy (SNOM) to study SPP focusing, waveguide and resonance enhancement effects, and uses finite difference time domain (FDTD) method to verify simulation calculations of experimental results. The main course content is as follows:_x000D_
In terms of SPP focusing, the single-point subwavelength focusing phenomenon of SPP by metal nanostructures and the separation of focused SPP and excitation light background were studied. Micro-nano processing technologies such as focused ion beam etching and electron beam exposure are used to prepare SPP excitation, propagation, and focusing nanostructures. In terms of SPP waveguides, the enhancement of silver nanowire SPP coupling and emission efficiency, and the control of light emission color of silver film surface dielectric SPP waveguides were studied. On the other hand, by studying the CdS dielectric waveguide on the surface of the silver film, the excitation of the dielectric-bearing SPP (DLSPP) waveguide mode is achieved. In terms of SPP focusing enhancement applications, in-plane focused SPP waves are used to capture and screen polystyrene colloidal beads; to enhance the luminescence of LED devices; and to integrate with graphene to prepare enhanced photodetectors, field effect tubes and other applications. _x000D_

Name: Nonlinear Optics
Prerequisite: Optical, electromagnetic, electrodynamic and quantum mechanics
Introduction:
This course is most of the content of the original "Nonlinear Optics and Spectroscopy" course for the optics major. According to the development of the discipline in recent years, it has been listed as a required course for the major in the revision of this professional course. The main content of this course is divided into 15 chapters. _x000D_
Main content of this course: We will teach about the nonlinear process of interaction between light and matter. That is, nonlinear optical phenomena and theories caused by nonlinear interactions are considered. Semi-classical theory is mainly used to study the nonlinear interaction between light and matter. Matter - quantized, corresponding to microscopic state changes - coherent state - concept of dipole moment. Use the Schrödinger equation in quantum mechanics to solve it. The light field still uses the classic Maxwell equation and is processed by introducing a nonlinear polarization intensity vector. _x000D_

Name: Physics of Semiconductor Devices
Prerequisite: Quantum mechanics, optical, electrodynamics, thermodynamics and statistical physics (or balanced-state statistical physics)
Introduction: This course will teach the physical foundation and cutting-edge areas of semiconductor devices, including basic properties of semiconductors, diodes, transistors, lasers, modulators, and biochemical sensors. From the most basic energy band theory and Maxwell's equations to current research hotspots, ultrafast lasers, surface plasmon lasers, electro-optical modulators, etc., while mastering the basic physical foundations and basic principles, you will also understand the latest cutting-edge research and developments in semiconductor device physics.

Name: Experimental Methods in Nuclear and Particle Physics (I)
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic principles and experimental methods of nuclear physics and particle physics experiments. The content includes the interaction mechanism between particles and matter, basic knowledge of errors and data processing, various radiation detection methods and various measurement techniques. This course is suitable for undergraduates, graduate students and researchers engaged in the fields of experimental nuclear physics, particle physics and nuclear technology applications.

Name: Topical Laboratory in Nuclear and Particle Physics
Prerequisite:
(1) Modern physics experiments (1)
(2) Atomic nuclear physics
Introduction: The curriculum is divided into theoretical and experimental teaching. The classroom theory requires three sessions, focusing on the interaction of rays and materials, the working principles of various types of detectors, the functionality of basic electronic instruments and the method of their use. Ten experiments (selected seven) have been introduced in the laboratory component to enable students to learn experimentally about particle and ray detection techniques and measurement methods, to acquire some common and basic experimental skills and to understand their application in environmental protection, the field of nuclear power and the frontier of science.

Name: Introduction to Nuclear and Particle Physics
Prerequisite:
Studies in general physics, advanced mathematics, some theoretical physics, some mathematical methods.
Studying quantum mechanics or at the same time
Introduction:
Course Purpose: This course is offered to senior undergraduate students to provide a professional foundation for students who may engage in nuclear technology-related work in the future, and to provide scientific knowledge for students who are interested in the microscopic world. The course introduces the basic knowledge and basic laws of nuclear physics and particle physics accumulated over the past hundred years. It also systematically guides students to understand the current development status and main frontiers of the discipline, as well as the progress and prospects of related work at home and abroad. The characteristics of the course are that it is close to reality, guided by experimental phenomena, and has a strong research and conceptual nature. The course pays attention to basic training and the cultivation of scientific research quality. By studying this course, students can have a deeper understanding and grasp of the phenomena and laws of the microscopic world. _x000D_
_x000D_
Summary: The atomic nucleus is a quantum multi-body complex system based on a variety of basic interactions. It is a microscopic level of material structure, contains rich intrinsic degrees of freedom and symmetry, and stores most of the visible mass and energy in the universe. In the past century, nuclear science has been at the forefront of material science and has had a significant impact on human survival and development as well as the status and security of the country. It has become an important symbol of measuring comprehensive national strength. The development of today's unstable nuclear map is closely related to major interdisciplinary scientific issues such as the generation process of heavy elements in the universe and climbing the island of super-heavy elements, and will bring wide applications in new nuclear samples, nuclear data, nuclear energy devices and nuclear detection technology. _x000D_
_x000D_
Historical evolution: Heaven moves vigorously, the terrain moves smoothly, and it is human nature to study things and gain knowledge. Ancient Greece had the theory of atoms, and by the end of the 19th century it had become deeply rooted in the hearts of the people, believing that atoms were the basic elements of all things. In 1896, Becquerel accidentally discovered natural rays coming from inside atoms, showing that atoms were variable. Later, Marie Curie, Rutherford and others classified cognitive radioactivity. In 1911, Rutherford discovered that atoms have extremely small cores, revealing a new level of material structure. After 1930, the use of accelerators greatly improved scientists' ability to explore the microscopic world. By the 1950s, a general understanding of more than 200 stable atomic nuclei was established using protons and neutrons as components. Later, he went deep into the microscopic level inside protons and neutrons, developed the standard model of particle physics and verified it experimentally. At the same time, the territory of the atomic nucleus is gradually expanding to tens of thousands of unstable nuclei and highly excited new states of matter, and new quantum many-body phenomena are emerging one after another. Entering the 21st century, microscopic and cosmic cross-basic research is booming in various complementary directions. Nuclear energy and nuclear safety have become increasingly prominent in the country's core interests. The cross-application of nuclear technology is in the ascendant. The development of nuclear science and technology has entered a new active period.

Name: English for Frontier Science and Technology
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course uses English articles on cutting-edge science and technology as its subject matter to cultivate students' reading ability. The selection of materials includes scientific and technological articles, scientific reports and Internet articles in scientific and technological journals (Scientific American, New Scientist, Discover, Science and nature, etc.), comprehensive and financial newspapers and periodicals (such as National Geographic, The Economist, Fortune, Businessweek, etc.). The content covers artificial intelligence (AI) (including deep learning, self-driving cars, natural language processing (NLP), etc.), big data, cloud computing and Internet security, virtual reality (VR) and augmented reality (AR), intelligent manufacturing (3D printing), medical technology (including gene therapy, stem cell therapy, etc.), neuroscience (brain and behavioral science), environment and new energy, climate, rocket launches, and human settlement on Mars. _x000D_
After taking this course, students should be able to read scientific and technological articles of certain difficulty relatively smoothly and understand the latest developments in the field of science and technology. By analyzing and comparing articles and discussions from different sources, we explore the impact of technology on human life, form our own understanding and knowledge, and enhance critical thinking skills. _x000D_

Name: Computer Graphics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Computation general, advanced mathematics, linear algebra
Introduction:
Computer Graphics (CG) is a computer discipline that studies how to use mathematical algorithms to convert two-dimensional or three-dimensional geometric primitives into image information suitable for display on computer display devices. The main research content of computer graphics is to study how to represent two-dimensional and three-dimensional geometric shape information in computers, as well as the related principles and algorithms of using computers to calculate, transform, process and display graphics. _x000D_
One of the main purposes of computer graphics is to use computers to synthesize realistic images. To this end, it is necessary to establish a geometric representation of the scene described by the graphics, and then use some kind of lighting model to calculate the lighting effect under the hypothetical light source, texture, and material properties. Computer graphics is closely related to another discipline, computer-aided geometric design. Graphics also regards curved surface modeling technology and solid modeling technology that can represent geometric scenes as its main research content. At the same time, the results of realistic graphics calculations are provided in the form of digital images, and computer graphics is closely related to image processing. _x000D_
The research content of computer graphics is very extensive, such as graphics hardware, graphics standards, graphics interaction technology, raster graphics generation algorithms, curve and surface modeling, solid modeling, realistic graphics calculation and display algorithms, non-realistic rendering, as well as scientific computing visualization, computer animation, natural scene simulation, virtual reality, etc.

Name: Introduction to Raman Spectroscopy
Introduction: On the basis of emphasizing both the theoretical foundation and experimental work, a focused introduction and discussion will be given on light scattering theory, Raman experimental principles and techniques, and new developments and applications of Raman spectroscopy.

Name: Surface Physics
Introduction: This course can be used as a professional course for graduate students in physics (mainly condensed matter physics), chemistry, materials science, interdisciplinary science and other related departments. The purpose is to enable graduate students in various related majors to understand the current status and trends of the development of surface physics, and to master some experimental techniques and theoretical methods of modern surface physics. This course not only teaches the basic knowledge of surface physics, but also focuses on the close connection with cutting-edge topics, in order to cultivate and improve students' ability to transition from book learning to practical research.

Name: Introduction to Econophysics
Introduction:
Economics is a theory that studies the laws of human economic activities, that is, the laws of the creation, transformation, and realization of value—the laws of economic development. Mainstream economics has formed a highly quantitative axiom system, which plays an important role in various economic and financial practical activities. However, deviations often occur when describing real economic and financial phenomena. The recurring economic and financial crises are a striking example. Unlike economists, physicists view axioms with suspicion. If empirical observations do not fit a model, no matter how conceptually sophisticated or mathematically simple the model is, it must be discarded or revised. Over the course of the development of physics, many accepted ideas have been proven wrong, and physicists have gradually learned to view their own models critically and cautiously. _x000D_
_x000D_
The strictly empirical scientific thinking of physics may be a useful inspiration and supplement to economics. In recent years, as an emerging discipline, scientific papers on economic physics have appeared in large numbers in a variety of high-level physics journals, gradually gaining a certain influence. This course provides a systematic introduction to the basic knowledge in the field of economic physics. The main contents include: efficient market theory, basic mathematical statistics, price time series analysis, stochastic models of price dynamics, scaling properties, financial markets and turbulence, positive and negative correlations between stocks, stock portfolios and options, etc. In addition, some basic concepts and applications related to small world networks, institutional trading models, financial market sentiment and financial big data are introduced. _x000D_

Name: Cultivating Social Entrepreneurship
Introduction: This course is guided by the national innovation and entrepreneurship development strategy and policy goals, based on the rich achievements of innovation and entrepreneurship teaching in the past seven years and the excellent teaching team, and integrates the national "mass entrepreneurship and innovation" concept and policy into classroom teaching, focusing on cultivating and improving the analytical and practical abilities of young students. This course was jointly developed by the School of Economics of Peking University and the Youcheng Entrepreneur Poverty Alleviation Foundation. It is hoped that through course study, students will establish a basic understanding of innovation and entrepreneurship, enhance their understanding and awareness of the future development direction of social economy, and help students find a future career development direction that combines their ideals with reality. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Cryptography
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Primary digital theory, theoretical computer base, probability theory and mathematical statistics
Introduction:
The content of the basic cryptography course mainly includes three parts: private key cryptography, public key cryptography, and cryptography protocols. The specific content starts from the theoretical basis of modern cryptography such as one-way functions and pseudo-random number generators. It not only covers the classic applications of modern cryptography such as symmetric/asymmetric encryption algorithms, digital signatures, and homomorphic encryption, but also includes the progress of emerging research directions such as blockchain and quantum cryptography. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students will understand the basic principles and ways of thinking of modern cryptography, become familiar with the description and logical expression of cryptographic objects, understand common cryptographic constructions and applications, and learn and master mathematical tools and techniques for cryptographic research and analysis. This knowledge will not only help students establish a macro concept of modern cryptography from the basics to the cutting-edge, but will also lay a solid foundation for students who are interested in engaging in theoretical computer or cryptography research in the future. _x000D_
This course is a highly theoretical course that requires the completion of basic knowledge teaching tasks and at the same time, the cultivation of students' practical application abilities through the introduction of appropriate practical applications. _x000D_

Name: Vocal Performance (Advanced)
Prerequisite:
Chapter Teaching content Course Lesson hours_x000D_
The first stage of vocal music basic knowledge and vocal skills training theory and practice 8_x000D_
The second stage of vocal skills training and singing of vocal music works theory and practice 12_x000D_
The third stage Vocal skills training, vocal music singing and performance theory and practice 12_x000D_
Stage 4 Exam 4_x000D_
	Total Theory and Practice 34 hours_x000D_
Introduction: The course "Vocal Singing and Performance (Advanced)" is designed for undergraduates who are interested in vocal singing and have a certain musical foundation. This class provides students with further training in vocalization, breathing, singing and analysis of vocal music works in the form of small lessons, and teaches singing skills and music theory according to students' different levels. Through the singing practice of a large number of vocal music works, students are guided to master the correct and scientific vocal singing methods.

Name: Superconductivity Physics
Introduction:
This course first introduces the history of the discovery of superconductivity and related phenomena, then discusses the electrodynamic and thermodynamic properties of superconductors, and then introduces the teaching of London theory, Pippard theory, Ginzburg Landau theory and Bardeen-Cooper Schriever theory. Other contents include: the properties of the second type of superconductor, the Josephson effect, the fluctuation effect in superconductors, the discovery and properties of high-temperature cuprate superconductors, and also includes some special topics, such as carbon 60 superconductors, magnesium diboride superconductors, iron-based superconductors, superconducting quantum interferometers, etc. _x000D_
      This course relies as little as possible on complex formulas during the teaching process, with special emphasis on the discussion of physical images and their mechanisms. _x000D_
      This course is suitable for undergraduates, graduate students, and those conducting research in superconductivity-related fields. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Practical Low-Temperature Physics and Technology
Introduction: Low-temperature physics is an important part of the field of physics. Low-temperature technology has also become a conventional detection method in the field of scientific research, and is not limited to the field of physics. Although there are many excellent books in the field of cryogenics, some of them are more suitable for reference than for learning, so this course will provide beginners with an introduction to the field. Beginners mainly include graduate students and undergraduate students who are about to join the laboratory or are newly involved in laboratory work. The course will cover vacuum technology, low temperature knowledge, refrigeration methods, common measurement methods and design examples. This course plans to provide safety knowledge and scientific research knowledge related to cryogenic laboratories, and cultivate students' ability to operate and design cryogenic systems.

Name: Materials Physics
Introduction: The content of this course mainly consists of four parts. The first part is the basics of material physics, introducing atomic structure and chemical bonds, crystal structure, defects and dislocations. The second part is material preparation, which mainly introduces the currently widely used methods: thin film growth and crystal growth. The third part is some analysis methods in materials research. The fourth part introduces the optical, electromagnetic and other physical properties of materials. The course will be interspersed with some of the current cutting-edge research on semiconductor materials and solid materials to familiarize students with some of the frontiers of materials research and build a bridge between learning and research.

Name: Introduction to Marine Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The ocean occupies approximately 71% of the global surface area and plays a pivotal role in Earth system science. Marine science is a comprehensive discipline that studies the properties of the ocean and its changing laws, as well as the development and utilization of the ocean. It is an interdisciplinary science that is independent and highly related to multiple disciplines such as marine environment, marine biology, marine chemistry, ocean physics, marine geology, and atmospheric science. _x000D_
This course introduces students to the basic knowledge of marine science, the basic methods of studying marine science, and the current cutting-edge hot spots in international marine scientific research from different research directions and research fields such as marine geology, ocean circulation, ocean-atmosphere interaction, marine chemistry, marine biology, marine environment, marine observation, ancient oceans, and marine technology and national security. Through the study of this course, students can enhance their interest in the ocean and lay the foundation for engaging in marine science and related research in the future. _x000D_

Name: Ideological and Moral Cultivation and Fundamentals of Law
Introduction: This course is one of the required courses for the whole school. It is an ideological and political theory course set in accordance with the national "05" education plan. The Ideological and Moral Cultivation Course of Peking University won the title of Beijing Excellent Course in 2006 and the National Excellent Course in 2007. It is currently one of the core courses of quality education at Peking University. This course educates college students on the correct outlook on life, values, and moral values ​​through the analysis and discussion of life theory and practical issues such as life, ideals, and morality. Through course study, college students can further understand the general characteristics of university study, understand the basic requirements for college students' ideological and moral cultivation, grasp the general rules for healthy growth of college students, clarify the responsibilities and missions that college students must bear in the great cause of building socialism with Chinese characteristics, and consciously cultivate good moral qualities.

Name: Astrophysics
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, general physics (lower grades with a better mathematical base can also be chosen directly).
Introduction:
As one of the oldest natural sciences, astronomy plays an irreplaceable role in the development of human civilization, and astrophysics is the mainstream of its development to this day and the most dynamic part of the field. Many terms popular in academia, such as dark matter and dark energy, gravitational waves, black holes, neutron stars, etc., are inseparable from "astrophysics". The extreme environments manifested by several celestial processes that cannot be matched by ground-based laboratories provide an excellent opportunity for humans to understand basic physical laws. The implementation of more and more advanced space detectors and observation methods other than electromagnetism (cosmic rays, neutrinos and even gravitational waves, etc.) is bound to usher in the golden age of astrophysics in the 21st century. In order to adapt to this historical trend, world-class universities have always regarded "Astrophysics" as a core required course for astronomy undergraduates, and have attached great importance to popularizing astrophysics knowledge among physics students. This course has been offered as a backbone basic course at Peking University. It aims to systematically introduce the subject of astrophysics to astronomy and physics undergraduates and cultivate their basic astrophysics qualities. It is the basis for further learning other related courses. _x000D_
_x000D_
The teaching purpose of the course is to use the basic principles of classical (including general relativity) and quantum physics to understand several astronomical phenomena at a qualitative and semi-quantitative level, and to understand and understand the cosmic environment in which humans live. It is worth mentioning that basic physical laws are vividly demonstrated behind some celestial processes; therefore, the study of this course helps students deepen the physical concepts they have learned and cultivate their ability to learn and apply them.

Name: Experimental Methods in Nuclear and Particle Physics (I)
Prerequisite:
Optical, electrodynamic.
(Optics, Electromagnetic field and Electrodynamics)
Introduction: Through the study of this course, graduate students can master theoretical and experimental knowledge in scientific fields such as ultrafast lasers, ultrafast laser spectroscopy and applications, and lay the foundation for future work in the frontier fields of optics. Students are required to have studied optics, electromagnetism or electrodynamics.

Name: Frontier Physics Laboratory
Prerequisite: General physics experiments (1), general physics experiments (2), modern physics experiments (1).
Introduction:
_x000D_
    "Frontier Physics Experiment" is a research-based experimental course that follows "Modern Physics Experiment I" and is offered in parallel with "Modern Physics Experiment II". It is only available to students with excellent results in "Modern Physics Experiment I". It lasts for one semester and is worth 3 credits. Students who elect this course must devote no less than 12 hours per week to the course, including no less than 6 hours of laboratory work. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course adopts a teaching model in which front-line scientific research teachers guide students to conduct research projects. Students are required to focus on hot scientific issues, use international high-level research documents as teaching materials, find ways to repeat the experimental content of selected documents, complete verification experimental work, and make a comprehensive review of the verified work. On this basis, students are encouraged to work closely with their instructors to produce innovative scientific research results. _x000D_
_x000D_
  The final grade of the course is comprehensively evaluated by four parts: teacher evaluation, experimental notes, oral report and research report. _x000D_

Name: Nuclear Astrophysics
Introduction:
1. Introduction to Nuclear Astrophysics_x000D_
2. Nuclear physics knowledge, nuclear element abundance_x000D_
3. Nuclear Reaction Network, Universe and Element Synthesis_x000D_
4. Basic properties of galaxies, H and He burning stars_x000D_
