Name: Introduction to Anthropology
Introduction:
Society is the goal, which is the so-called "different culture" research. After the 1930s, anthropologists' research also began to involve the society and culture in which they were born and raised, as well as highly civilized societies (such as China, etc.). _x000D_
Generally speaking, society is made up of people. Human activities are naturally inseparable from basic survival needs such as food, clothing, housing and transportation. This leads to corresponding forms of economic production and political governance. At the same time, these activities are also controlled by symbols created by people themselves, such as language and writing. In this way, there is symbolic control and unifying religion, and symbols are "culture". These physical and spiritual cultural and social formations vary among every human group (the boundaries of which themselves vary). Anthropologist Geertz said: "Anthropology is such a mirror, which shows how diverse human beings are." The study of these social and cultural differences constitutes the focus of anthropologists. The task of the anthropologist is not only to describe these differences but also to try to provide an understanding and explanation of the interrelationships between these differences. Anthropologists even have to study the theory of knowledge of whether a foreign culture can be understood and whether the description of a foreign culture can have truth value. _x000D_
One of the focuses of this course is to introduce the basic concepts, issues, research methods and classic works of socio-cultural anthropology from the perspective of social science, so that students can have a more systematic understanding of the basic concepts and problem awareness of socio-cultural anthropology. This course will reflect on and criticize these basic concepts when introducing anthropological issues from a social science perspective. _x000D_
This course takes as another focus the research cases and reflections of Chinese anthropologists on Chinese society and culture. This course will introduce the research cases of Chinese anthropologists, the development context and problem directions of Chinese anthropology, as well as the dialogue between contemporary Chinese anthropology and international anthropology, etc. _x000D_
This course will invite some domestic and foreign anthropologists to give special lectures on specialized branches or fields of anthropology according to the course situation. _x000D_
This course invites experts and scholars in some branches of contemporary anthropology (such as kinship studies, medical anthropology and cultural studies) to teach the basic and cutting-edge issues of this branch. _x000D_
Anthropological film is an important part of anthropology. During the course, the film and television practice of anthropologists and the characteristics of ethnographic films will be introduced. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Practical Software for Scientific Research
Prerequisite: All English teaching materials (Chinese speaking) require students to have a certain basis in English; preferably in C language
Introduction:
ROOT is widely used in data analysis work (including drawing) in international high-energy physics, nuclear physics, nuclear medicine, economics, astronomy and other fields involving data processing. This software is a completely free software developed based on C/C++ and can run on Linux and Window platforms. It can quickly improve your scientific research capabilities and ensure that your research work can continue uninterrupted wherever there is a network. For detailed instructions, please see its website:_x000D_
http://root.cern.ch/drupal/content/about_x000D_
For ease of understanding, the English introduction is attached._x000D_
_x000D_
Note: This course does not teach commonly used software (such as Excel, Matlab, etc.); ROOT itself is very popular in foreign scientific circles and is almost a necessary tool for scientific research. Students who elect this course must be prepared to learn the basic operations of Linux.

Name: Beijing and Shanghai: A Tale of Two Cities in Chinese History
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course studies and discusses the modern historical development, mutual exchanges and mutual influence of two important cities in China - Beijing and Shanghai. By examining the residential life, ethnic exchanges, and urban changes in two different cities, this course will give students an in-depth understanding of the cultural forms of Chinese cities in different historical periods, such as imperial culture, commercial culture, regional culture, and modern culture, as well as their role in reform and opening up, and the rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Through comparative research, this course will discuss how Beijing and Shanghai have used local and external resources in similar or different ways to respond to various historical challenges. This course will organize discussions according to chronological order and different topics to facilitate better comparative research across time and regions. This course can help students better understand the profoundness and richness of Chinese culture, especially the development of diverse societies and urban cultures in the two metropolises of Beijing and Shanghai.

Name: Introduction to Taiwanese Politics
Introduction: This course aims to enhance students' understanding of the Taiwan issue, enhance their understanding of the importance and complexity of the Taiwan issue, and deepen their understanding of the Chinese government's Taiwan policy through the introduction and analysis of Taiwan's political development and related economic and social conditions.

Name: Academic English Reading
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: "Academic English Reading" is a specialized reading training class that requires students to read extensively and carefully. The course is difficult. The textbooks use 4 volumes of the "New Edition of College English Reading Course" (Advanced Edition) from Shanghai Foreign Language Teaching Press, as well as the unpublished fifth volume. A certain amount of reading materials after class are recommended. In addition to providing students with basic reading training and improving students' reading ability and interest, this course also trains students' academic reading ability, teaches students the ability to look up a dictionary, rewrite and summarize in English, focuses on the conceptual teaching of English language, cultivates students' English thinking ability, and lays a solid foundation for learners' future academic reading and writing.

Name: International Law
Introduction: Public international law is the law that regulates international relations. It is rooted in and regulates international relations. The continuation and improvement of human civilization cannot be separated from public international law. As China moves toward the world, public international law becomes more and more important in safeguarding China's rights and interests; as the world moves into China, public international law has an increasing impact on China's interests. In today's world, strengthening the study and research of public international law and improving the understanding and mastery of public international law are of particularly important legal value and practical significance for distinguishing the rights and wrongs of international disputes, regulating state behavior, defending national sovereignty and territorial integrity, adhering to the basic norms of international relations, and maintaining world peace and security. This course strives to fully and accurately expound the basic principles, basic systems and basic norms of public international law, reflecting the new content of the development and changes of public international law. At the same time, it will provide in-depth analysis and interpretation of some prominent issues in current international relations in conjunction with public international law, focusing on cultivating students' practical ability to analyze and solve problems using the knowledge they have learned about public international law.

Name: Stochastic Processes
Introduction: The porcelain process, the updated theory, the Brown movement, the Levy process, the quartz process, the Ito process and the Ito random points.

Name: Operations Management and Optimization
Prerequisite: It's recommended to start with advanced mathematics.
Introduction: This course presents basic theoretical approaches to business management and optimization, such as simpleness, queuing, inventory management strategy, non-linear planning, dynamic planning, etc.

Name: Ancient Chinese History (Part 1)
Introduction: This course takes the general trend of the evolution of ancient Chinese political history and institutional history as the main clue, allowing students to have a relatively clear framework for the development of ancient Chinese history. This course also pays attention to the historical process of major issues such as the formation of the Chinese nation and the formation of China's territory, and strives to grasp the characteristics of each historical stage in the development and evolution of ancient China's politics, institutions, economy, and society. During the teaching process, the knowledge and academic aspects of history are combined, and the latest research results in the academic field are absorbed as much as possible, hoping to enhance students' interest in ancient Chinese history and stimulate students' thinking.

Name: Fundamentals of Accelerator Physics
Prerequisite:
Higher mathematics
Linear algebra
Electric dynamics
Introduction:
This course mainly introduces the basic concepts and physical principles of particle accelerators. _x000D_
From the birth of the particle accelerator to the present: the fundamental driving force for its development is to explore the four basic problems faced by mankind: the basic composition and movement laws of matter, the universe, and life, as well as the operating laws of human thinking. The largest ion accelerator in the world today is the LHC, which has just been built in Geneva. It can accelerate protons to TeV. They can be used to search for Higgs particles, test the Standard Model, etc. However, in order to study major issues related to the basic composition of matter such as dark matter and supersymmetry breaking, accelerators with PeV and quadrillion electron volts that can accelerate energy a thousand times higher than existing ones are needed. Due to the limitations of the accelerating electric field, such accelerators can only be built in outer space. This course will introduce in detail the development history of accelerators, the physical principles and limitations of various accelerators. After studying this course, students can understand the working principle of the LHC, the largest ion accelerator in the world today. At the same time, this course focuses on the close integration of basic knowledge and cutting-edge experimental research to expand students' academic horizons and help students become familiar with the cutting-edge of accelerator physics research, such as laser plasma accelerators, as soon as possible. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Environmental Science
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
Environmental science is a comprehensive discipline that integrates natural sciences, humanities and social sciences, and technical sciences. Its core connotation lies in the understanding and adjustment of the relationship between human activities and the ecological environment, so as to achieve harmony between man and nature. As a multi-disciplinary applied basic discipline, environmental science does not have many esoteric principles. It is mainly a systematic integration of multi-disciplinary applications to reveal and solve environmental pollution phenomena and environmental problems. Environmental protection and sustainable development have become the themes of the 21st century. Basic knowledge of environmental science and basic understanding of environmental issues should become the basic knowledge and cultural qualities that any college student possesses. More importantly, in the Internet age of information diversity and knowledge explosion, comprehensive perspectives and systematic thinking are of more real value. The knowledge and concepts of environmental science are just suitable for students to gain such gains and training. _x000D_
This course strives to guide students to gradually enter environmental science in the context of globalization and China's economic boom, with the depth of the times and an international perspective. The course is designed into five parts: "Environmental Issues, Environmental Science and China's Environmental Issues"; "Natural Ecosystems and Human Society"; "Environment and Health"; "Environmental Pollution Mechanisms and Control Methods"; "Global Environmental Issues and International Conventions"; "Environmental Policy and Management". The course content strives to summarize the basic principles of each main branch of environmental science (environmental ecology, environmental chemistry, environmental toxicology, environmental engineering and environmental management), and also includes basic knowledge of related disciplines such as demography, urban science and resource science. As an introductory and introductory course, this course has no prerequisites and is suitable for students from all majors to take courses. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Biophysics
Introduction: This course is designed for students in physics interested in studying the theory of biological quantification and in life sciences who wish to learn about biological quantification methods. The presentation of the chosen biophysical field is based on the basic concept of physics and quantitative methods as the basis for thinking and research, focusing on the energy, information processes in the biological system, on the spatial structure, diffusion, dispersion and drive of the biomolecule, as well as the thermodynamic statistical effects within the cell, biochemical reaction dynamics, regulation of network dynamics, etc. The purpose of the curriculum is to provide students with the necessary knowledge to study biomolecules and life phenomena by physical means, to give them an initial understanding of and, to some extent, an understanding of the basic methods of studying biological systems by quantitative means.

Name: Quantum Optics
Prerequisite: Quantum mechanics, optical, atomic physics and electrodynamics
Introduction: Supplement basic knowledge related to particle number representation, angular momentum, etc. and optics in advanced quantum mechanics. Learn and master basic knowledge such as quantization of electromagnetic fields, quantum state representation of light, distribution functions and quantum statistical properties of light. Establish the J-C model of the interaction between light and matter, and understand the "collapse-recovery" phenomenon in two-level atoms, resonance fluorescence, and electromagnetic induction transparency in three-level atoms. Learn about the latest developments in quantum optics, quantum information and atomic optics. Cultivate students' optical qualities and lay the foundation for future scientific research work.

Name: Outline of Earth History
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of secondary school geography.
Introduction: Taking the earth system as the outline and the formation and evolution of the earth as the main line, it introduces the formation and development process of the earth and the laws of evolution and change; through 34 hours of study, students can initially understand the history and laws of the earth's evolution and movement, as well as the basic characteristics of the new earth outlook.

Name: Optics Demonstration Laboratory
Introduction: The Optical Demonstration Experiment Course is a supporting experimental course offered by the Physics Demonstration Laboratory of the Department of Physics of Peking University for all science students studying optics courses in the school. It demonstrates more than 30 experiments on light interference, diffraction, polarization, and three-dimensional display applications to stimulate students' interest in learning, deepen their theoretical understanding, and understand the experimental culture. This course is conducted in a dark room environment for two hours. In order to ensure the teaching effect, there are no more than 50 students in each class. Students can also observe some experiments independently after class.

Name: Renewable Energy and a Low-Carbon Society
Prerequisite: Common knowledge of natural and human sciences
Introduction: Fossil energy has achieved the progress of modern society, but it has also brought great pressure to human society. On the one hand, the increasing shortage of fossil energy has put pressure on sustainable social and economic development; on the other hand, the continuous consumption of fossil energy has produced more greenhouse gases. In order to seek a model of sustainable social development, the development of renewable energy has increasingly become the preferred goal of the international community. Starting from the actual situation of my country's current energy production and energy consumption, vigorously developing new energy and renewable energy is our country's future energy development strategic requirement. The white paper "China's Energy Situation and Policies" points out that renewable energy is a priority area for China's energy development. In order to adapt to the new situation of energy conservation and emission reduction and the development of low-carbon economy in my country, this course plans to teach students to understand my country's renewable energy development plan and what opportunities and challenges it faces, why it should take the road of low-carbon society, the international development situation and experience of low-carbon economy, how China should face the current contradiction between development and emission reduction, and the special situation of energy structure and population, so as to formulate strategic decisions suitable for the sustainable development of China's economy. The content of this course mainly includes an introduction to my country's energy structure, global climate change trends, impacts and countermeasures, international experience in low-carbon economic development, China's development strategy and technology roadmap for implementing a low-carbon society, its mid-term goals in 2020 and long-term goals in 2050, as well as China's renewable energy development plan and the role of modern optics in the development of renewable energy.

Name: Mathematical Beading and Molecular Geometry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemistry is a discipline that studies the composition, structure, properties and changes of matter; geometry is a branch of mathematics related to size, shape and spatial distribution; and art is human exploration and creation of the world through true and emotional reactions. This course will combine the three and is a course that combines the science and art of nanospace order. The course will focus on geometry and symmetry. On the basis of introducing relevant background knowledge in science, history and humanities, the course will allow students to analyze structural models of various chemical molecules and crystals, and use traditional Chinese three-dimensional beading techniques to construct various ball accumulation models and skeleton structures related to the nano-world. Deepen students' understanding of the rich material structure, improve students' interest in mathematics and science, and cultivate their scientific and humanistic qualities.

Name: New Concepts in Chemical Engineering
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
The teacher of this course uses modern multinational companies as examples to introduce the innovation and sustainable development of modern chemical companies based on his many years of career experience in modern multinational companies. And through examples, the relationship between the modern chemical industry and other industrial industries and the future development trend of chemical industry are explained. Finally, we introduce in detail the basic qualities needed for talents in the new era, as well as job search and career planning._x000D_
    This course is conducted in various forms such as lectures, student group discussions and student speeches. In order to improve students' abilities and insights in all aspects while learning knowledge! _x000D_
   Let students have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the development concepts, basic structure and operations of the modern international chemical industry and chemical companies_x000D_
   Introducing the basic quality requirements of talents in the new era, as well as the design and planning of future career development, thereby helping students enter modern enterprises more easily, adapt to the work requirements and rhythm of modern enterprises more quickly, and become qualified modern industrial talents as soon as possible! _x000D_

Name: Contemporary International Politics
Introduction:
This course is based on the international environment faced by China, and strives to reflect the new theories, new issues, and new characteristics of contemporary international politics, and to deeply understand the nature of contemporary international politics. It is a general course for undergraduates majoring in non-international politics throughout the school. _x000D_
_x000D_
On the basis of teaching the basic concepts, analytical frameworks and research methods of international politics, we focus on studying the evolution of the contemporary international political landscape, countries and national interests, international strategies and foreign policies, new developments in international organizations and global issues, etc., and further explore conflict and cooperation, war and peace in international politics, as well as the role and influence of economic, ethnic, religious and cultural factors in international politics. _x000D_
_x000D_
Since the modern West began to study international politics, it has generally gone through three stages of development: the first stage, mainly focused on issues such as war and peace, relations between major powers; the second stage expanded to the economic field, such as interdependence and economic security; and now it has entered the third stage. A series of non-traditional security threats, such as environmental protection, public health, transnational crime and other issues have become important areas of international political research, emphasizing that the study of international politics must have a new perspective. Since problems and challenges are comprehensive, observations and responses must also be comprehensive and systematic, which requires this course to include the above-mentioned different development stages in a timely manner for comprehensive research and teaching. _x000D_
_x000D_
Therefore, this lesson strives to:_x000D_
1. It is not a purely theoretical professional course, but it will insist on implementing the classic Marxist theory on international politics, the international political theory of Western countries, and China’s theoretical discussion on international politics and foreign relations in teaching, so that students can consciously apply Marxist theory when studying international politics, consciously safeguard China’s national interests, and consciously combine theory with practical issues; _x000D_
2. It is not a simple description of the current situation, but an analysis of the major issues and phenomena of contemporary international politics; _x000D_
3. It is not a repetition of the history of international relations, but it will summarize the major events and experiences in history; _x000D_
4. Comprehensive research, using theory to guide the analysis and research of practical problems, and summarizing historical experience from practical problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
In terms of specific content, this course will focus on the new development of contemporary international politics since the end of the Cold War. Some major international events can be traced back to the end of the Second World War. Through the organic combination of the history, theory and current situation of international politics, as well as the specific analysis of politics in different regions, a comprehensive, detailed and focused discussion and research on contemporary international politics will be carried out, so that students:_x000D_
1. Master basic international political theories and methods;_x000D_
2. Deepen our understanding of the nature of contemporary international politics;_x000D_
3. Establish a comprehensive and correct worldview;_x000D_
4. Improve the level of independent scientific research;_x000D_
5. Lay a solid foundation for further observing and analyzing international issues, learning and researching international political theory. _x000D_

Name: Biophysical Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Physicochemical methods play an important role in studying the structure and function relationships, dynamics and biomolecule recognition processes of biological macromolecules, and are one of the cutting-edge directions in cross-research between chemistry and biology. In this course, students will learn the basic principles and applications of the main physical and chemical methods used in the study of biological macromolecule structure, dynamics and biomolecule identification, and understand important developments in related fields.

Name: Fundamentals of Chemical Development
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite:
Inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry,
Chemical base
Introduction:
The teaching content of courses such as "Fundamentals of Chemical Development" and "Principles of Chemical Engineering" and "Fundamentals of Chemical Engineering" are quite different. The teaching contents of courses such as "Chemical Engineering Principles" and "Chemical Engineering Fundamentals" mainly focus on the purely intellectual fields of science and technology; while the teaching content of "Chemical Development Fundamentals" mainly focuses on cultivating students' ability to apply the various chemistry and chemical engineering knowledge they have learned to analyze and solve problems in connection with actual production, so that students can master the basic abilities and thinking methods of amplifying laboratory results into large-scale industrial production devices in accordance with the laws of optimal economic operation, with special emphasis on cultivating students' practical abilities. _x000D_
The teaching is divided into ten chapters as follows:_x000D_
1. Overview; _x000D_
2. Develop amplification methods; _x000D_
3. Test; _x000D_
4. Technical and economic data;_x000D_
5. Type and design of reactor; _x000D_
6. Synthesis and optimization of process flow; _x000D_
7. Investment, cost, depreciation and profit; _x000D_
8. Market forecast and production scale; _x000D_
9. Technical and economic evaluation; _x000D_
10. Conceptual design and basic design. _x000D_

Name: Advanced Electrochemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Electrochemistry is one of the important third-level subjects of physical chemistry. The development of modern science and technology has brought vitality to this traditional discipline. The principles and techniques of electrochemistry have been widely and deeply applied in the fields of energy, materials, life sciences, etc. The development of these disciplines has promoted and promoted the in-depth development of the electrochemistry discipline, forming a series of new subject directions, such as semiconductor photoelectrochemistry, bioelectrochemistry, spectral electrochemistry and nanoelectrochemistry developed in recent years. This course strives to lay a solid theoretical foundation of electrochemistry for chemistry majors, while introducing the cutting-edge areas of electrochemistry development and guiding students to search for literature and learn consciously.

Name: Soft Matter and Hard Science: The Mesoscale World from Micro to Macro
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Soft matter, also known as complex fluid, has the typical characteristics of weak stimulus and strong response, covering material systems such as polymers, colloids, liquid crystals and biological macromolecules, and is a hot and cutting-edge field of modern scientific research. The scale of the soft matter system is between micro and macro (nano to micron). Due to the complex interactions involving multiple space and time scales, especially the significant effect of entropy, it presents unique structures and properties. Soft matter science is a highly interdisciplinary subject with a very wide range of applications. _x000D_
This course aims to systematically teach the basic physical properties, basic theories and key research methods of soft matter systems, use physical principles to understand the rich and colorful phenomena involving physics, chemistry, materials, life and other soft matter fields, and try to find the common laws and mechanisms behind many phenomena to establish connections between these disciplines. This course contains five parts. 1. Force, energy and interaction modes in soft matter; 2. Phase transition and mean field theory in soft matter; 3. Molecular motion forms of soft matter; 4. Self-assembly; 5. Physics in special soft matter systems. By studying this course, undergraduate students will have a systematic understanding of the basic concepts and theoretical foundations of soft matter science, and master the interaction forms, modes of motion, and theoretical foundations of physical phenomena of soft matter. The course also enables students to master the cutting-edge and cross-cutting issues in today's soft matter scientific research, improve their ability and awareness to proactively apply theoretical knowledge and multidisciplinary knowledge, and increase students' scientific research literacy. The course will take the form of classroom lectures and case studies to achieve the teaching purpose. _x000D_

Name: Radiochemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: "Radiochemistry" is an optional course offered to senior undergraduates in the School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering of Peking University and other science departments under the new situation of my country's nuclear energy development. The purpose is to enable students who elect this course to learn and master the basic theories and methods of radiochemistry, establish serious radioactivity and protection principles and methods, and cultivate students' ability to engage in applied research and practical work in radiochemistry and nuclear technology as well as their rigorous scientific style. This course is designed for students who have a solid foundation in chemistry and are interested in radioactivity and its applications. The course covers the nuclear properties of radionuclides, decay characteristics, measurement methods and techniques, protection principles, and applications of radioactivity in industry, agriculture, defense and other fields. In order to expand students' horizons and improve their ability to review relevant literature and summarize, this course arranges certain class hours for students to report on topics related to radiochemistry in groups.

Name: High-Performance Polymer Materials
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: High-performance polymer materials occupy a particularly important position in various application fields such as civil, national defense, and aerospace. This course starts from introducing the types and applications of high-performance polymer materials, and guides students to understand the structure-activity relationship, molecular design, modification and molding processing of high-performance polymer materials, especially the reasons and mechanisms for high performance. Finally, through classroom discussions on some high-performance polymer materials, students can understand how to comprehensively consider material form, specific technology, etc. during application.

Name: Molecular Biology
Introduction: Molecular biology is the science that studies genes and their activities at the molecular level. This course will explain the core knowledge of molecular biology from the overall perspective of the genome, comprehensively and emphatically elaborate on the basic theories and main technologies of molecular biology, and highlight the frontiers and trends of molecular biology, especially the latest advances in genome and white matter research. This course attaches great importance to the source of knowledge and grasps the research frontier. While explaining systematic knowledge, it also provides students with research ideas on how to analyze the mysteries of life at the molecular level. Its main contents include: 1) Main techniques for studying genes and their activities, 2) Important events precipitated in the development of molecular biology, 3) Prokaryotic transcription and its regulation, 4) Eukaryotic transcription and its regulation, 5) Interaction between DNA and protein during transcription, 6) Post-transcriptional processing of RNA, 7) DNA recombination and transposition, 8) Genome, transcriptome and proteome and their interrelationships. Through the study of this course, students can have a relatively systematic and comprehensive understanding of the basic laws of gene activity at the molecular level. At the same time, students can cultivate their ability to analyze and solve problems and their sense of innovation, and lay a theoretical and technical foundation for the future use of molecular biotechnology to analyze important biological issues of interest in life sciences.

Name: Chemical Engineering Drawing
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemical Engineering Drawing is a basic course that teaches drawing and reading engineering drawings and illustrating spatial geometric problems. According to the "Basic Contents of Chemistry Teaching for Scientific Chemistry Majors and Applied Chemistry Majors" formulated by the Science Chemistry Teaching Steering Committee of the Ministry of Education in 1998, "Chemical Engineering Drawing" is a compulsory basic course for undergraduate students majoring in applied chemistry. According to the national "Technical Drawing" and "Mechanical Drawing" standards, the content of this course includes drawing geometry, mechanical drawing, how to use AutoCAD, etc. It mainly cultivates students' ability to read and draw engineering drawings. They can read general engineering drawings and draw simple engineering drawings.

Name: Chemical Information Retrieval
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Chemical information retrieval is an elective course for chemistry majors and is open to undergraduate students majoring in chemistry. Course content includes: the use and search methods of SciFinder, Web of Science, Reaxys, EB on Web, Derwent patent database, and various chemical series and manuals. _x000D_
    In addition to introducing important databases in the field of chemistry and teaching specific search methods, the course also explains the working principles of databases and the application of new technologies in the literature field. Through this course, students can learn necessary literature knowledge, understanding of databases, and the ability to fully utilize existing data and information in the big data era. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: This course provides students with a systematic introduction to the basic chemical composition and chemical transformation laws of the earth's environment, and conducts an in-depth analysis of the changes in the earth's environment under the influence of human activities, especially the key chemical issues involved in some global environmental issues. In terms of knowledge structure, it not only highlights the complexity and variability of the environmental system, but also reflects the changing chemical laws and the powerful role played by chemistry in researching and solving environmental problems. It is an environmental chemistry course suitable for students with a strong background in chemistry.

Name: Outline of Modern Chinese History
Introduction:
The course "Outline of Modern and Modern History of China" is a compulsory ideological and political theory course for undergraduate students in my country's ordinary colleges and universities stipulated by the Propaganda Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the Ministry of Education. This course mainly teaches the history of China's resistance to foreign aggression, struggle for national independence, overthrow of reactionary rule, and realization of people's liberation in modern times. It helps students understand the history and national conditions of the country, and enables students to understand the historical process and inherent laws of social development and revolutionary development in modern China, so as to deeply understand why the people chose Marxism, the Communist Party of China, and the path of socialism. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course implements special lectures, and teachers implement teaching group combinations, divided into 4 teaching groups; implement the "four-in-one" teaching management method of course host, classroom teacher in charge, topic lecturer and teaching assistant. It is mainly based on classroom lectures, supplemented by other practical links, including playing documentary documentaries or movies, writing experience, organizing classroom discussions, visiting exhibitions or museums, etc. Adopt flexible and relaxed assessment methods. The usual score is 40%, including a short paper discussed in class, and the final exam is 60% (open book). _x000D_
"_x000D_

Name: Radiation Chemistry and Technology
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Common chemistry, inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry.
Introduction:
Radiation chemistry is a branch of chemistry that studies the chemical effects produced by the interaction between ionizing radiation and matter. Radiation processing technology is a science that studies the process and technical issues of product processing using ionizing radiation technology. At present, with the rapid development of radiation processing, more and more radiation processing products are widely used in daily life, such as wires and cables, heat shrinkable tubes, etc. At the same time, radiochemical treatment of tumors and diagnosis of diseases in hospitals are also inseparable from irradiation devices, which require students to understand the relevant biological effects of radiation and necessary radiation protection knowledge. Therefore, studying radiation chemistry and technology courses can help students develop scientific research ideas, use ionizing radiation knowledge to prepare new materials that cannot be obtained by traditional chemical methods, and at the same time improve their own radiation protection level. _x000D_
    The course content mainly includes the basic principles of radiation chemistry, basic methods of radiation chemistry research, radiation dosimetry and radiation protection, and applications of radiation chemistry. Among them, the basic principles of radiation chemistry involve the interaction between ionizing radiation and matter, the generation and reaction of transient products in the radiation chemistry process, radiation chemistry of liquid water and dilute aqueous solutions, polymer radiation chemistry, etc. The basic method of radiation chemistry research is mainly to use pulse radiolysis technology to study the kinetics of radiolysis reactions. Radiation dosimetry involves many dose unit concepts and dose measurement. This part of the content is the basis of radiation chemistry research, as well as the basis of radiation biology and radiation therapy. Radiation protection is also based on radiation dosimetry. The application of radiation chemistry focuses on the basic principles of radiation processing, as well as important application areas of radiation processing such as polymer material modification, food preservation and radiation sterilization. _x000D_

Name: Deep Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic principles, methods and practices of deep learning in different fields. The first part of the course introduces the development status, theory and basic methods of deep learning. The second part of the course introduces the deep learning framework TensorFlow. The third part of the course introduces the application of deep learning in different fields including computer vision, natural language understanding, network analysis, and recommendation.

Name: Nature Conservation
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Natural geography, plant geography, general ecology and conservation of biology, etc.
Introduction: At present, the country has raised the construction of "ecological civilization" to a level that is related to the success or failure of building a moderately prosperous society in an all-round way, and there is an urgent need to build a harmonious relationship between man and nature and nature. This course discusses the role of social and cultural factors such as environmental ethics, national culture, ancient ecological wisdom, and religious culture on nature protection from a multi-dimensional perspective, and provides an economic explanation of nature protection behavior through specific cases. Taking the type, function, structure and planning and design of nature reserves as the starting point, it systematically discusses the application of geography, ecology and biology theories as well as remote sensing and geographic information system technology in the planning, design and management of nature reserves. Finally, the current hot issues in nature protection are introduced and the development trends are prospected.

Name: Convex Analysis and Optimization Methods
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course will teach the basic concepts of convex analysis, such as convex sets, convex functions, convex hulls, subgradients, conjugate functions, convex envelopes, nearest neighbor operators, etc., and on top of that, basic optimization methods, such as KKT conditions, coordinate descent, (sub)gradient descent, (accelerated) nearest neighbor Gradient descent, Frank-Wolfe algorithm, Lagrange multiplier series algorithms (staggered direction method, linearized staggered direction method, etc.), dual problems, penalty function method, quasi-Newton method, stochastic (sub) gradient method, etc., and finally introduces several problem transformation techniques. In addition, depending on time availability, you may choose to teach optimization on manifolds. This course will be oriented to the needs of machine learning. It will explain the derivation and proof of most theories and methods and try to use examples in the field of machine learning. It requires high mathematical ability.

Name: Machine Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course teaches the basic theory of machine learning, focusing on generalization of theory and core algorithms. Details are provided in the syllabus.

Name: Algorithms in Game AI
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course teaches the artificial intelligence algorithms involved in game AI design and applies the algorithms to the practice of Botzone game against platform publishing. The course first introduces the definition and classification of game problems, and then introduces the algorithms for solving game strategies one by one, including classic algorithms such as Alpha-Beta search, Monte Carlo tree search, and reinforcement learning. It also assigns homework accordingly, and finally helps students implement the core algorithm of AlphaGO and participate in the Botzone game competition.

Name: Mathematics in Information Science
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course covers important mathematical foundations in information science and computer science. It is an advancement based on previous content such as discrete mathematics and introduction to computing theory. The main content of the course includes high-dimensional space, singular value matrix decomposition, random walk theory and Markov chain, learning theory, massive data-related algorithms, topic models, etc. _x000D_

Name: Big Data Management Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
None
Python or Java programming language
Introduction: The introductory course on big data technology builds a bridge and link for students to the "big data knowledge space". Based on the principle of "building a knowledge system, clarifying basic principles, guiding primary practice, and understanding related applications", it lays the foundation and points out the direction for students to "deeply cultivate" in the field of big data. The course will systematically teach the basic concepts of big data, big data processing architecture Hadoop, distributed file system HDFS, distributed database HBase, NoSQL database, cloud database, distributed parallel programming model MapReduce, memory-based big data processing architecture Spark, stream processing and other big data related technologies, as well as the application of big data in various fields such as the Internet, biomedicine and logistics. In important chapters such as Hadoop, HDFS, HBase, MapReduce, and Spark, entry-level practical operations are arranged to allow students to better learn and master key big data technologies.

Name: Genomic Data Analysis
Prerequisite: Molecular biology, advanced mathematics, computer programming base
Introduction: Contemporary life sciences and medicine are moving towards the era of big data represented by high-throughput sequencing. How to model, analyze and interpret genomics big data will determine whether we can quickly and accurately discover new biological phenomena and patterns and provide precision medicine to patients. This course will introduce common data types in genomics, such as WGS, RNA-seq, Hi-C, and single-cell sequencing, as well as statistical analysis and graphing methods commonly used in data analysis, including exploratory data analysis, linear regression, analysis of variance, Bayesian models, data dimensionality reduction, and clustering. Genomics literature and data will be discussed in the course, and programming environments such as R language will be used for data analysis and graphing exercises.

Name: Close Reading of the Four Books
Introduction:
The "Four Books" is the most core and essential part of ancient Chinese classics, and has a foundational role and influence on Chinese culture. This course uses Zhu Xi's "Collected Annotations on Chapters and Sentences of the Four Books" as the reading material, combined with other ancient annotations, selects the most important chapters in the "Four Books" for detailed explanation and elucidation. Through the study of this course, students can have a closer and direct understanding of ancient Chinese classics, especially the core classics of Confucianism. It plays a positive role in promoting the inherent Chinese culture. _x000D_
