Name: Introduction to Sociology
Introduction: This course will focus on the society we live in and its constituent elements, human socialization, gender and sexuality, primary social groups, social organizations, communities, classes and strata, social systems, deviance and social control, social problems and social changes, etc.

Name: C++ Programming
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: It is suggested that there be a basis for the design of the programme, including but not limited to: C, Basic, Pascal, JavaScript, Java, etc.
Introduction:
C++ is an important computer language with modern programming ideas (OOP), which is helpful for in-depth understanding of computing machines and writing fast and efficient computer software. _x000D_
The main purpose of this lesson:_x000D_
Mainly introduces the basic concepts of C++ language and object-oriented programming methods. It is a language programming course that can be gradually mastered through a large number of program examples and related exercises during the learning process. It mainly trains students to master the basic elements of programming languages, _x000D_
During the learning process, learners gradually master the object-oriented functions of C++, thereby mastering the basic knowledge and basic skills of object-oriented programming. Lay a solid foundation for programming in subsequent courses. _x000D_

Name: Learning and Modeling in Molecular and Materials Science
Prerequisite: Micro-centres, linear algebras, and one of the following courses: Quantum mechanics/calculating physics/calculating chemistry/statistical mechanics/molecular dynamics/computing materials science/mechanical learning
Introduction: Recent advances in physical modeling and machine learning offer many new opportunities for advancement in the fields of molecular and materials science. We will introduce and discuss some of these examples. Examples come from quantum chemistry, density functional theory, molecular dynamics, coarse-grained models, computational materials science, and more. In addition to relevant basic theory, we will pay particular attention to the guiding principles for using machine learning in physical modeling processes, and how learning and modeling can complement each other in related problems. In addition, we will provide hands-on internships in machine learning and molecular dynamics.

Name: Parallel Computing II
Introduction: The main purpose of this course is to teach the use of distributed parallel computers, MPI-based parallel programming methods and their applications in scientific and engineering calculations, especially in numerical solutions to partial differential equations. The focus of the course is on technical research rather than on the theory and algorithms of parallel computing itself. We hope that students who have completed this course will be able to successfully design programs for different practical problems on supercomputers.

Name: Ethnic Issues in World Politics
Introduction: This course starts from the concept of ethnicity and theoretical debates, focusing on ethnicity, ethnic relations and ethnic issues in major countries and regions in the world. Through representative case selection, we conduct comparative research on the ethnic policies of different countries. The course will also cover topics such as ethnocultural diversity and globalization related to ethnic issues. On this basis, we can further understand and understand China’s ethnic groups, ethnic relations and ethnic policies.

Name: Chemical Biology
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemical biology is an emerging discipline that is developing very rapidly. The content of this course is based on the current status of subject development, summarizing and improving the knowledge system of chemical biology. It is mainly composed of three parts: "Molecular basis of chemical biology, core technologies of chemical biology, and cutting-edge applications of chemical biology".

Name: Politics, Economy and Diplomacy of the Middle East
Introduction:
This course is a restricted elective course for undergraduates in the School of International Relations. It systematically focuses on the politics, economy and diplomacy of the Middle East since the end of World War II. The course content is divided into four units:_x000D_
The first unit teaches Middle Eastern concepts, Middle Eastern history and civilization, Middle Eastern nations and languages, Middle Eastern religion and culture, Middle Eastern geography and resources, and Middle Eastern politics and economy. _x000D_
The second unit teaches the political upheaval in the Middle East, political transformation in the Middle East, monarchy in the Middle East, and the relationship between politics and religion in the Middle East. _x000D_
The third unit teaches oil and the Middle East economy, natural gas and the Middle East economy, water resources and the Middle East economy. _x000D_

Name: Practical Basic English Writing
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is for non-English majors in college English. In view of the prominent problems in students' writing such as poor content, loose structure, single sentences, and insufficient vocabulary, it discusses and introduces the four main types of English writing in detail, explains the characteristics and methods of paragraph writing, and practices writing short articles of about 400 words. _x000D_
This course abandons the method of "student writing - teacher marking", in which students practice more, teachers comment less, and students throw away the essay after marking it. It organizes teaching according to the "process method" and helps organize students to revise their essays multiple times through classroom discussions, student mutual correction, group activities, etc., and gradually improves students' writing ability during the teaching process. _x000D_
This course will also introduce several commonly used practical texts such as letters, recommendation letters, cover letters and thesis abstracts to improve students' practical ability in English writing. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Geography
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
This course starts from the perspective of man-land relationship and focuses on teaching the basic principles, basic issues, basic knowledge and basic research methods of physical geography and human geography. It is a geographical knowledge content that undergraduate students in geographic information systems, remote sensing and other related majors must master. The course plays a very important role in helping students master the basic research and thinking methods of geography, correctly understand and solve the basic geographical problems faced in subsequent studies, and establish the concepts of coordinated development of man and nature and sustainable development of social economy. _x000D_
    The course mainly includes two knowledge units: basic physical geography and basic human geography. The basic unit of physical geography first introduces the research objects, tasks and basic methods of physical geography. Then, starting from the integrity of the geographical environment, it systematically introduces the formation process, basic characteristics, functions and status, distribution and change rules of various physical geographical elements of the earth's surface system, mainly including the crust, atmosphere, hydrology, biology, soil and landforms and other physical geographical elements. On this basis, we will conduct in-depth study of the mutual relationships and interactions between various physical geographical elements, the basic integrity and difference laws of the natural geographical environment, and the relationship between humans and the natural geographical environment. The basic unit of human geography first introduces the basic concepts and subject system of human geography, and then introduces the basic principles of human geography such as the theory of man-land relationship, the laws of population growth and migration, classical location theory, and regional-urban development strategies. On this basis, a brief introduction is given to the hot research topics of geographical information science in the fields of disasters, environment, health, social networks, smart cities, etc. _x000D_
    The main goal of this course is to enable students to comprehensively master the basic knowledge of geography, understand the generation and development mechanisms of various common physical and human geography phenomena, cultivate students' thinking methods and abilities to analyze and solve problems from a geographical perspective, and lay a solid foundation for later professional courses in geographic information science. Course study can enable students to better combine geographical information science knowledge with basic geographical knowledge, improve students' interest and ability to use geographical information science professional knowledge to analyze and solve specific geographical problems, thereby enhancing their subsequent scientific research potential. _x000D_
    The main teaching methods of the course include classroom lectures, exercises and special discussions. Class lectures are taught using multimedia courseware; exercises refer to exercises given based on the lecture content, which are completed by students after class; class discussions refer to specific questions, usually divergent questions, given based on the teaching content, and extended reading outside class, followed by discussions in class and submission of reports. _x000D_

Name: Europe in the 18th and 19th Centuries
Introduction: The 18th and 19th centuries were the modernization period of major European countries and the creation period of global modern society. The modern civilization we see, pursue or criticize now was born in Europe during this period. Therefore, understanding the history of Europe during this period will help us gain a deeper understanding of the era in which we ourselves live.

Name: Arms Control and Disarmament
Introduction:
This course is an elective course for the Department of International Politics, open to senior undergraduates. System Introduction Seminar_x000D_
_x000D_
history, theory and methods of arms control and disarmament. Particular emphasis will be placed on analyzing U.S.-Soviet relations, regional relations, and China since the end of World War II_x000D_
_x000D_
The general process and characteristics of arms race, arms control and disarmament in peripheral relations. This lesson explores China's views on arms control and disarmament_x000D_
_x000D_
policies and military force distribution strategies.

Name: Advanced English Writing
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is taught by foreign teachers. It aims to improve students' English writing level and ability through writing narratives, argumentative essays and other topics, train students to use English vocabulary systematically, and guide students to use correct and reasonable grammatical structures and language to accurately express their thoughts in English. By paying attention to the writing process, students' creative thinking abilities are further inspired, thereby improving academic research and writing literacy.

Name: Water Environmental Chemistry
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Water environmental chemistry is an important branch of environmental chemistry. It mainly studies the formation, distribution and circulation process of various elements and compounds (natural and synthetic) in natural water, as well as the connection with other environmental media, which clearly reflects the intersection of geoscience and chemistry. The earth's water environment mainly includes terrestrial water bodies and ocean water bodies. The two are closely related but also significantly different. Since global industrialization, the impact of human activities on the water environment has far exceeded that of most natural processes. Various types of pollutants are discharged in large quantities. Water bodies are extremely important receptors in nature. They play a decisive role in the migration, transformation, and fate of pollutants at different spatial scales and time ranges, as well as closely related biological and ecological effects (such as teratogenesis, carcinogenesis, mutagenesis, and changes in aquatic ecotoxicology). _x000D_
The main content of the course includes: land water bodies (fresh water) and ocean water bodies (salt water). It involves the formation and distribution of chemical components of natural water and their connection with environmental conditions, so as to comprehensively understand the overall chemical status of the natural water environment; on this basis, it discusses the migration and transformation rules of various major pollutants (such as heavy metals, persistent organic pollutants, endocrine disruptors, etc.) in the water environment, as well as the corresponding biological and ecological effects, and provides an overview of the latest methods and technologies in international water environment chemistry research. The course content is arranged from simple to complex, with pictures and texts, and the complex is omitted and simplified. Through the dynamic introduction and introduction of literature and materials, special attention will be paid to the frontiers of current international water environmental chemistry research, as well as the hot spots and difficulties in research. Although there are certain requirements for students' prerequisite courses, as a professional elective course, we will try to explain the more complex principles of action and basic reactions in a concise and concise way during the teaching process, and try to avoid cumbersome formula derivation and calculations. _x000D_
Through course study, students can initially understand and master the basic principles, important reaction processes, and advanced research methods and means of water environmental chemistry. This will lay a good theoretical and practical foundation for future research on the biogeochemical behavior of pollutants in water environments and even multi-media environments.

Name: History of China's Foreign Relations
Introduction:
This course aims to reconstruct the history of China's foreign relations, break through the narrative paradigms of "Orientalism" and "Eurocentrism", and highlight the subjectivity of Chinese history. _x000D_
    1840---1949 was the most tragic century in Chinese history. China's modern foreign relations during this period unfolded against the following two backgrounds: On the one hand, in the mid-19th century, the development of China's external world had created a political culture that was completely different from the traditional international relations in East Asia. The differences in eras and regions between China and foreign countries, as well as the aggressive policies of great powers, made it inevitable that China-foreign relations would be characterized by conflict. On the other hand, while Sino-foreign relations are experiencing fierce conflicts, the humiliated Chinese people's basic style of viewing the outside world and reflecting on their own traditions is also undergoing drastic changes. China has since been involved in a major change that is still ongoing today. Politically speaking, the theories about governing a country and bringing peace to the world, theories about power and even various political vocabulary left by the ancients have been challenged like never before. From a cultural perspective, this change has reversed the so-called Confucian logic of cultivating knowledge through studying things and cultivating knowledge: we have to start by coping with the current situation, move to political revolution, move to cultural revolution, and finally move to the revolution of man himself. To a certain extent, the diplomacy of the Republic of China was a continuation of the diplomacy of the late Qing Dynasty, because the basic issues of China's modern diplomacy - sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity - had not been completely resolved, and this historical mission was not completed until the founding of New China. _x000D_
    To grasp a century of diplomacy, we not only need to clarify the ins and outs of typical events involving China and foreign countries, but also try to reflect on history. This period of history of Sino-foreign relations is not only of great significance in the historical development of China, but also in the history of the development of world civilization. Because China, with such a profound and long-standing cultural tradition, has been able to basically achieve integration with the world's heterogeneous civilizations in just over a century, its significance is also inspiring. In this amazing change, we have seen the tenacious adaptability of the Chinese people and the huge potential inherent in Chinese culture. A century of diplomacy has left behind a history of humiliation and heroic stories, but few people know the details of the weak country diplomacy carried out by China's first generation of diplomats wearing Confucian robes. Diplomacy has experienced many ups and downs over the past century. This course not only requires students to master diplomatic history, but also hopes to cultivate students' patriotism. If it is beneficial to students' academic thinking and even their life concepts, it will be a big gain. _x000D_

Name: Religious Relations in the Age of Globalization
Introduction:
After the end of the Cold War, especially after the 9/11 incident, religious issues have become increasingly prominent and severe. Many international hot issues and major conflicts are mostly deeply affected by religious factors or religious backgrounds. "Interdisciplinary and multi-religious research" has become a frontier field in the international academic community. This course will focus on major issues of concern to the international academic community, such as the diversity of world religions, religious traditions and Eastern and Western cultures, religious conflicts and dialogue among civilizations, etc. It is committed to using interdisciplinary theories and methods to examine the current religious status of major regions or countries in the world, and actively explores the methodological concepts of "resolving religious conflicts, promoting dialogue among civilizations, and building a harmonious world." _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is a cooperative project between Peking University and the Blair Faith Foundation. The Institute of Religious Culture of Peking University is responsible for organizing teaching activities. Professors from the Department of Philosophy, the Department of Religious Studies, the Department of Sociology, the School of Foreign Languages, and the School of International Relations are jointly taught. Well-known foreign experts are invited to teach relevant topics to build a teaching platform for international cooperation. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Micromorphological Analysis of Cultural Relics
Introduction:
Microscopic observation and description of archaeological and cultural relic samples are the basis for cultural relic protection and scientific and technological archaeological research. Due to the large variety of samples involved, researchers are required to have a basic and extensive understanding of various microscopic observation methods, sample preparation methods, typical structures of common sample materials, and corresponding scientific expressions. _x000D_
This course selects the most common types of wood, fiber, rock, ceramics, pigments, diatoms, pollen, phytoliths, etc. in archaeological and cultural relic samples. It combines basic knowledge of biology, wood science, petrology, ceramic technology, environmental archeology and other disciplines to teach the typical microscopic morphology and observation description of the samples. Key points; and combine theoretical courses with laboratory operations to teach the principles and usage of stereomicroscope, biological microscope, polarizing microscope, mineralogy microscope, electron microscope, as well as basic microscopic sample preparation methods such as freehand sectioning method, resin sectioning method, smear method, and grinding method. _x000D_
This course has no other prerequisites and is suitable for first-year undergraduates majoring in cultural relics protection in the School of Archeology and Museology, as well as undergraduates of any grade in other majors. _x000D_

Name: Archaeometry
Introduction: Teach the application of modern science and technology in archaeology, including various chronological methods, physical and chemical analysis methods applied to the study of cultural relic materials, production techniques and the origin of cultural relics, and new developments in biotechnology in the field of archaeological research. Pay attention to the cutting-edge trends of the subject, constantly add the latest research results into the teaching content, broaden students' horizons, and improve students' scientific literacy.

Name: Conservation of Organic Cultural Relics and Laboratory
Introduction: Organic cultural relics are an important part of cultural heritage, including paper, textiles, lacquered woodware, leather, bone and horn tools, etc. Because their constituent materials are natural polymer materials that are prone to deterioration and decay, it is difficult to protect organic cultural relics and there are many problems that need to be solved. Conservation and experimentation of organic cultural relics is a compulsory course for students majoring in cultural relics conservation. It adopts a teaching method that combines theoretical courses with practical courses. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic properties, deterioration characteristics, and protection of organic cultural relics of various materials, as well as basic knowledge and practical skills. This will enable students to know how to choose protection materials and protection techniques, so that they can engage in actual protection and treatment work in the future, and lay the necessary theoretical and practical foundation for students who are interested in doing research in this area in the future.

Name: Introduction to World Heritage
Introduction:
World Heritage is one of the important research topics at home and abroad, and has received widespread concern and attention from the public. This is not only because world heritage carries human civilization and embodies important information about natural changes, but also because the research and protection of world heritage increasingly help people look to the future of their own development, rationally plan current behaviors, and adjust their attitudes toward life in a timely manner. In a sense, the protection and research of world heritage is a microcosm of mankind's pursuit of sustainable development and sustainable coexistence with the earth. _x000D_
The "Introduction to World Heritage" course will guide students to understand the value of heritage from an academic perspective, learn heritage protection and research methods, understand and spread the concept of sustainable development, and promote the inheritance and sustainable use of heritage from generation to generation. This course has outstanding interdisciplinary research characteristics and is a platform for effective combination of academic research and sustainable development practice. _x000D_
World heritage protection is one of the important ways to embody the concept of sustainable development. The word "heritage" itself means "intergenerational sharing and inheritance", especially the "world heritage" as the common wealth of all mankind. Inheritance determines that heritage undertakings are always closely linked to protection - this protection is not only reflected in the cultural field (cultural heritage), but also in the natural field (natural heritage). World heritage sites around the world, with their limited area, bear the responsibility of protecting and inheriting the most typical material culture and natural wealth. The reasonable protection and sustainable use of a wider range of heritage sites with it as the core can provide a comprehensive and appropriate interpretation of concepts such as environmental protection, intensive resource utilization and cultural diversity protection in real society. The protection, utilization and development status of world heritage reflects the degree of sustainable social development in a region and is an indispensable part of embodying the concept of regional sustainable development. _x000D_
Sustainable development is both the goal and the means of World Heritage protection. The World Heritage cause originated in the context of the rapid development of industrialization and urbanization in developed countries, which determines that the cause has been closely related to social development from the very beginning - it originates from development and thrives from development. The main challenges at present and in the future also originate from development. Therefore, the World Heritage cause has always had the substantive connotation of sustainable development. More importantly, breakthroughs in a large number of real heritage protection problems must be effectively solved based on the comprehensive judgment of sustainable social development. _x000D_
Many of the problems contemporary China faces in its economic development can be traced back to the development history of developed countries in Europe and the United States. In the comprehensive development of economy and society, it is of clear practical significance for China today to properly handle the original proposition of cultural protection and environmental protection in developed countries and achieve balanced and sustainable social development. In short, China's world heritage research must be combined with the concept of sustainable development, integrated into the general trend of sustainable social development, and make due contributions to the overall development of society. _x000D_

Name: General History of Chinese Art (Part 1)
Introduction: "General History of Chinese Art" starts from the origin of Chinese art to the Ming and Qing Dynasties, according to the sequence of historical development, and uses a large number of exquisite pictures to provide a relatively complete and comprehensive teaching, including various art categories, art schools, representative figures, classic works and other important knowledge points. Attention is also paid to absorbing the research results of the Chinese art history community in the past thirty years, such as new perspectives, new materials, etc., so that students can have a basic understanding of the results and trends at the forefront of academic research. Strive to enable students to systematically grasp the development context of Chinese art history through study. This course also focuses on expanding students' aesthetic abilities, improving their artistic accomplishments, and enhancing their humanistic qualities.

Name: Developmental Biology
Prerequisite: It is recommended to begin with genetics, cell biology.
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to introduce students to one of the most important sub-disciplines of life sciences today - developmental biology. The course starts with an introduction to developmental biology, taking the embryonic development of model organisms such as nematodes, Drosophila, zebrafish, mice and Arabidopsis as the basic content, and systematically introduces students to the ideological methods, experimental techniques and cutting-edge advances in developmental biology research. The expected teaching effects are: 1) have a basic understanding of the principles of development; 2) have a basic understanding of the basic processes of animal and plant development; 3) have a basic understanding of model organisms, including Drosophila, nematodes, zebrafish, mice, and Arabidopsis; 4) have a basic understanding of developmental biology research routes and methods; 5) have a basic understanding of current research progress in developmental biology; 6) have a new thinking about the phenomena of development and biological evolution.

Name: Paleontology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The basic purpose of teaching paleontology is to enable students to understand the basic principles of paleontology, master the basic research methods of paleontology, understand the research frontiers and hot spots of the subject, and establish the concepts of historical biodiversity and earth-life co-evolution. _x000D_
By introducing the concept of the fourth dimension - "time" into the current category of life based on the current time section and three-dimensional geographical distribution, students can understand the history and evolution of life, understand the entire process of the origin, evolution, succession, extinction and recovery of life on earth over the past 3.8 billion years and explore its reasons. Appropriately introduce the latest research progress in the field of paleontology at home and abroad as well as some theoretical issues of biological evolution, such as: "Darwinism", "Punctuated Equilibrium Theory" and the "Coordinated Stasis" hypothesis recently proposed abroad, encourage students to participate in teaching and discussion, and cultivate students' creative thinking ability. This course introduces the basic morphology, classification, ecology, evolution, geological history and phylogeny of the main paleontological groups, and enables students to master the main biological groups and main representatives of each era, and initially learn how to identify fossils of each major category. _x000D_

Name: Paleontology Seminar
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Classes for classical biology courses.

Name: General Petrology (II)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The sedimentary rock part mainly introduces the basic concepts, principles and research methods related to sedimentary diagenesis, so that students can master the formation rules of sedimentary rocks and the characteristics of common sedimentary rocks through the study of this course. The metamorphic rock section mainly introduces the basic concepts, principles and research methods of metamorphism, masters common metamorphic rock types, mineral composition and structural characteristics, and understands the origin of various metamorphic rocks and their relationship with the geotectonic environment, laying the foundation for further discussion of metamorphism and crustal evolution.

Name: History of Marxist Philosophy
Prerequisite:
Introduction to Marxist Philosophy
Western philosophy.
Introduction: This course follows the clues of historical development, and based on the most authoritative literature, by sorting out the background of the times and interpreting classic texts, it outlines the germination, emergence and evolution of Marxist philosophy. It also combines cutting-edge issues in contemporary society and philosophical research to explore the practical value and transcendent nature behind the historical original image of Marxist philosophy, thereby deepening students' overall understanding and grasp of the characteristics and spirit of Marxist philosophy.

Name: Intermediate Physical Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, linear algebra, general physics, structural chemistry, physical chemistry
Introduction:
Peking University has made major reforms to the undergraduate chemistry major teaching system since the 2003 class, dividing the professional basic courses into two levels: basic and intermediate, in order to achieve the goal of teaching students in accordance with their aptitude and diversifying training. "Intermediate Physical Chemistry" is an elective course that students majoring in undergraduate chemistry, materials chemistry and other related majors who will become graduate students should take. It is hoped that through the study of the course, students will have a relatively comprehensive and systematic grasp of the basic principles and basic methods of quantum mechanics and statistical thermodynamics, and understand the transition state theory of chemical reactions; so that they will receive rigorous scientific training and have the ability to apply these basic principles and methods to analyze and solve problems, laying a solid theoretical foundation for the training and improvement of graduate students. _x000D_
    Based on the above considerations, the basic idea of this course is to train high-level talents in chemistry majors to accurately master the basic theories of modern physics. It emphasizes the introduction and application of modern scientific language, focuses on the systematic introduction of basic theories, and uses modern language symbology to concisely and systematically introduce the basic principles of quantum mechanics and statistical mechanics. The language is concise and comprehensive, and at the same time explains the profound things in simple terms, laying a solid foundation for students to gain a deeper and broader understanding of chemical systems. Therefore, students can apply the basic principles learned to the reading of contemporary scientific literature and scientific research work as soon as possible, building a bridge between theoretical learning and scientific research practice. The course content is not extensive, but the amount of information is sufficient, making it worthwhile for students to take it as an elective. _x000D_

Name: Intermediate Inorganic Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Common chemistry, inorganic chemistry, structural chemistry
Introduction: This course is an improvement course in inorganic chemistry, which deepens and broadens the knowledge of inorganic chemistry based on general chemistry and inorganic chemistry. The course content is mainly based on modern inorganic chemistry, combined with the development of cutting-edge fields of inorganic chemistry, and teaches relevant theories and methods. The main contents include molecular symmetry and group theory foundations, coordination chemistry, metal-organic chemistry, atomic clusters and metal-metal bonds, inorganic solid chemistry, and bioinorganic chemistry. Through the study of this course, candidates are required to master the basic concepts and basic theories of modern inorganic chemistry, comprehensively understand the basic laws of inorganic chemical reactions, be familiar with the characterization of inorganic compounds and research methods, and have an understanding of the current cutting-edge research fields of inorganic chemistry, improve their ability to analyze and solve problems, and read inorganic chemistry literature, thereby broadening and deepening their knowledge and understanding of the subject of inorganic chemistry.

Name: Colloid Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Colloidal chemistry is a chemical discipline that studies colloidal systems. The so-called colloidal system refers to a dispersion system formed by fine particles with a particle size of approximately 1-1000 nm evenly dispersed in a continuous medium. Colloidal chemistry has a wide range of applications in the fields of advanced materials, nanotechnology, cosmetics, food, medicine, biotechnology and environmental protection. This course focuses on the basic principles of colloidal chemistry and gives a brief introduction to the current cutting-edge research fields of colloidal chemistry (such as nanomaterials, colloidal crystals, etc.). The main content includes various basic properties of colloids (such as dynamics, optics, rheology, electrical properties and colloid stability) and the formation rules, characteristics and practical applications of various dispersion systems with colloid systems as the core.

Name: Biochemistry Discussion Section
Prerequisite: Biochemistry needs to be selected at the same time as biochemistry.
Introduction: This course is an accompanying discussion session of the compulsory subject " Biochemistry " .

Name: Mathematics in Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemistry absorbs the concepts and theories of statistical mechanics and quantum mechanics and has become the cornerstone of molecular science. The teaching content of the "Mathematics in Chemistry" course focuses on mathematical methods in chemical statistical mechanics and quantum mechanics, and provides a systematic introduction to mathematical analysis and algorithm tools commonly used in chemical research. It is committed to allowing undergraduate students/low-level graduate students to have a relatively complete and comprehensive basic understanding of relevant mathematical knowledge in chemical research in a short period of time, laying the necessary foundation for their study and research in senior undergraduate and postgraduate stages.

Name: Machine Learning and Its Applications in Chemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, linear algebra, general chemistry.
Introduction: Machine learning is a multi-field interdisciplinary subject that studies how to use computers to learn from data to acquire new knowledge and skills and improve their own performance. The application of machine learning in the field of chemistry has a long history. For example, the DENDRAL expert system developed in the 1960s is a successful example, which can infer the composition of chemical molecules in a sample from mass spectrometry data. On the other hand, deep learning has achieved tremendous development in the past 10 years, which has led to revolutionary breakthroughs in subjects such as machine learning and artificial intelligence, and has brought huge shock to human society with typical examples such as AlphaGo. Now, this breakthrough has penetrated into various fields, including chemistry: deep learning has been successfully applied to organic synthesis analysis (M. H. S. Segler et al., Planning chemical syntheses with deep neural networks and symbolic AI, Nature 555, 604 (2018)), protein structure prediction (in 2018, AlphaFold won the protein structure prediction competition CASP). This course will introduce the basic knowledge of machine learning and analyze typical application examples of machine learning in the frontier fields of chemistry, so as to better face the challenges and opportunities that machine learning brings to the chemical discipline.

Name: Comprehensive Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite:
Upon completion of the compulsory course of professional chemistry experiments at the Academy of Chemistry, the integrated chemistry experiment course was taught in the fourth grade. “Scientific” experiments are introduced in the integrated chemical laboratory curriculum. The “scientific type” experiment was completed in the fourth grade.
The “scientific” experiment is an exploratory research experiment that guides teachers in their interaction with students and is directed by the teachers to access relevant information, design experimental programmes, develop specific experimental steps and implement them. Students can choose the most suitable method to be used in scientific experiments using many advanced modern instruments and new experimental techniques. When the experiment is freely arranged between the student and the academic group in which it is carried out, the duration of the experiment is one term, which cannot be extended, and the actual duration of the experiment must be greater than 200 hours.
Introduction:
The School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering of Peking University (hereinafter referred to as the School of Chemistry) has begun to explore the organization and teaching model of experimental courses since 2000, and has gradually formed basic experiments, professional experiments, research experiments and comprehensive chemical experiments based on the internal connections of disciplines and the systematic nature of technology. _x000D_
The teaching goal of the comprehensive chemistry experiment course is to cultivate the innovative ability and independent scientific research ability of senior undergraduate students. _x000D_
The School of Chemistry at Peking University has very good scientific research advantages, attracting a large number of students to join the academic group in advance to participate in scientific research activities. The academic group of the School of Chemistry has cutting-edge research topics and advanced scientific instruments, which can expand students' horizons and better cultivate students' comprehensive qualities. Based on this feature of the School of Chemistry at Peking University and the management model of classified teaching and training for undergraduates implemented by the School of Adaptation, while the name of the comprehensive chemistry experiment course remains unchanged, "unit-type" experiments will no longer be set up in the course, and "research-type" experiments will be further extended to academic groups to expand the connotation of experiments and set up as "scientific research-type" experiments. The "scientific research" experiment is completed in the senior year and is a required course for graduate students in our college. It is an integral part of the graduation project (thesis) and cannot be separated. In principle, the "scientific research" experiment and the graduation project (thesis) are completed within the same academic group. _x000D_
In the "scientific research" experiments, through the careful guidance of teachers in the academic group and the interaction among graduate students in the academic group, students' experimental skills and scientific research abilities are further improved, students' innovative consciousness and ability are further cultivated, and students' exploratory spirit and problem-solving ability are further enhanced, making comprehensive chemistry experimental teaching one of the important platforms for cultivating outstanding undergraduates and laying a solid foundation for future work in the field of chemical science. _x000D_
The "scientific research-based" experiments in the comprehensive chemistry experiment course place higher requirements on the breadth and depth of knowledge mastered by students. Through the platform of the academic group of the School of Chemistry, students learn new design ideas for chemical experiments and comprehensively apply various experimental techniques, and become familiar with, understand and master the development trends, research methods and related experimental means of the chemical discipline. After the "scientific research-oriented" experimental training in the comprehensive chemistry experiment course, students have a deeper understanding of the knowledge belonging to various disciplines, which is conducive to grasping the internal connections among them. _x000D_
The "scientific research-based" experiments in the comprehensive chemistry experiment course are interdisciplinary and multi-skill comprehensive training, and the content of the "scientific research-based" experimental course is completed within the academic group. Students independently conduct comprehensive and innovative research under the guidance of teachers, truly feel the true meaning of engaging in chemical research, cultivate their enthusiasm and initiative to love science, learn science, and use science, further cultivate their scientific literacy, and improve their ability to conduct scientific research. _x000D_
A "scientific research" experiment is an exploratory research experiment in which teachers interact with students. Under the guidance of teachers, students review relevant information, design experimental plans, formulate specific experimental steps, and implement them. Students can choose the method they think is most appropriate and apply many advanced modern instruments and equipment and new experimental techniques in the scientific research experiment process. The time for the experiment is determined by the student and his/her academic group and can be arranged freely. The experiment time is one semester and cannot span semesters. The actual experiment time must be greater than 200 credit hours. _x000D_
In order to ensure the normal progress of the "scientific research-oriented" experimental courses, students must attend the course introduction class, and a sign-in system is implemented in the course introduction class. _x000D_
Teaching method_x000D_
For "scientific research-type" experiments, the application for "scientific research-type" experiments begins in the semester before the start of the course. Students are free to choose the academic team and instructors of the School of Chemistry, determine the scientific research content, design the experimental plan, and carefully fill out the "Comprehensive Chemistry Experiment "Scientific Research-type" Experiment Application Form". When filling out the form, you must seek truth from facts, be serious and detailed, and do not commit fraud. The application form must be signed and approved by the instructor (the explanation part of the application form contains the responsibilities of the instructor). Submit the application to the comprehensive chemistry experiment host/lecturer within the specified time, and the host/lecturer will review and approve the application. After obtaining the qualification to do "scientific research" experiments, students must choose the comprehensive chemistry experiment course in the school's course selection system, otherwise the application will be invalid. The academic team prepares experimental instruments and materials based on the number of students and scientific research content, guides teachers to assist students in completing "scientific research" experiments, and is responsible for the student's schedule management. The host/lecturer is responsible for the mid-semester inspection. After completing the "scientific research" experiment, students must submit a "scientific research" experiment report in the required template (with the instructor's signature and score) and an experiment record book within the specified time before they can obtain the corresponding grades and continue to complete their graduation project (thesis). _x000D_
Host/lecture teachers and instructors must evaluate student performance fairly, objectively, and strictly. _x000D_
Any behavior such as forging, altering data, plagiarizing other people's literature, etc. found in the "scientific research type" experimental report is considered cheating and will be dealt with in accordance with the relevant regulations of the School of Chemistry. Special reminder: You cannot use other scientific research projects and other materials as the final report of the "scientific research" experiment of this course. This is a serious violation of academic regulations. Once discovered, it will be dealt with according to the relevant regulations of the School of Chemistry. _x000D_
Evaluation method for "scientific research" experiment results: Within the specified time, the final "scientific research" experiment report and experimental record book signed by the instructor, with scores and comments must be submitted to the host/lecturer within the specified time, accounting for 45% of the "scientific research" experiment score; the host/lecturer of the comprehensive chemistry experiment will review the final report and experiment record book, and meet the course requirements, and the assessment score will account for 55% of the "scientific research" experiment score. The final "scientific research" experimental report must be submitted in paper form, electronic version and the original experimental record book. _x000D_
The host/lecture teacher is responsible for determining each student's final "scientific research" experimental score, which will be reported to the academic administration of the college as the score of this comprehensive chemistry experiment course.

Name: Risk Management and Insurance
Introduction: This course is open to all undergraduates and international students on campus and is taught in English. It aims to teach the basic knowledge and principles of risk management and insurance, and introduce the basic principles of life insurance, health insurance, property insurance, liability insurance and reinsurance. Provide tools and guidance for students to improve their own risk awareness and risk management level, and improve students' English communication skills.

Name: Southeast Asian Culture
Introduction:
After World War II, Southeast Asian studies became an independent research field, and its main research results focused on historical research. With the deepening of research, the content of Southeast Asian studies has gradually become more detailed, resulting in many branches, including the focus on and research on Southeast Asian culture. _x000D_
This course mainly teaches the religion, folk customs, clothing, food, architecture and other aspects of Southeast Asia, as well as the spread and influence of various Chinese, Indian, Arab and Western cultural types in the region. It enables students to understand the common characteristics of Southeast Asian culture and the special cultural phenomena of each country, the cultural development process of Southeast Asian countries, and the cultural exchanges between Southeast Asia and other regions, and expands students' international horizons. _x000D_

Name: Biochemistry
Prerequisite: " General Chemistry " and " Organic Chemistry " (may go to school with the class). It would be preferable if the students had the basis of Physicochemistry.
Introduction: This course focuses on the chemical characterization of major families of biomolecules, including proteins, nucleic acids, sugars, and lipids, as well as biological metabolism—the chemical reactions that provide the energy and raw materials needed by cells. The main contents include the structure and function of proteins (including enzymes), sugars, nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), and lipids; bioenergetics; glycolysis, pentose phosphate pathway, and gluconeogenesis; metabolic regulation; citric acid cycle and oxidative phosphorylation; metabolism of glycogen, fatty acids, amino acids, and nucleotides; hormone regulation and integration of mammalian metabolism, etc.

Name: Research Skills in the Molecular Biology Laboratory
Introduction: Life science is an experimental science, and most research work must be conducted in the laboratory. For newcomers entering the laboratory, the problem they face is how to get familiar with the laboratory correctly and quickly, prepare for scientific research, and understand the operating rules and key details of the experiment. This knowledge is generally obtained only through oral communication, but this method takes a lot of time, and it is not easy to distinguish what is trivial and what is critical. This course will systematically introduce the basic knowledge of biological laboratories from many aspects such as the composition of laboratory hardware and software, the formulation of experimental plans, the recording, analysis and display of experimental data, and the key experimental details and precautions in conventional molecular biology experiments. This will help undergraduate students who are about to enter the laboratory or have just started their scientific research career to be able to independently familiarize themselves with the environment from the beginning and develop good scientific literacy.

Name: Genomic Biology Techniques
Introduction:
Genome biology is a hot subject in the field of life sciences and has made rapid progress in recent years. Under this trend, in the past 20 years, especially after the emergence of high-throughput sequencing technology in 2007, genome biology-related technologies have promoted research in a large number of related biological fields and achieved a large number of breakthroughs. With the emergence of a large number of new technologies and methods, these genomic biology studies have greatly promoted the development of life sciences, and the demand for talents in related disciplines is also increasing. _x000D_
Traditional biological research focuses on proposing hypotheses and collecting evidence. Over the years, a large amount of data and conclusions have been accumulated, which seems complicated. However, the broader background behind these biological phenomena and biological processes is the global regulatory patterns and evolutionary principles at the genome level. _x000D_
This course examines various related biological processes from the different perspective of genomic biology, and teaches the research ideas of genomic biology and the application of related technologies in biological research. Help students learn and use the latest genomic biology technology and learn and apply various omics research tools at the whole genome level. The tools of genomic biology acquired in the course will enable the study of many global biological questions. _x000D_
Students are expected to achieve the following results through course study:_x000D_
1. Gradually establish the thinking habits of quantitative and global research in biological research. _x000D_
2. By understanding the key technical principles of genome biology, you can gain insights into practical biological research. _x000D_
3. Master the latest cutting-edge developments in the field of genome biology. _x000D_
This course is an introductory course in genomic biology for postgraduate students, requiring previous study of genetics and cell biology. _x000D_

Name: Molecular Ecology
Prerequisite: General biology, general ecology, or equivalent biology
Introduction: Species adapt to changing environments through phenotypic diversity determined by genetic diversity. Understanding the natural laws and genetic principles of biological adaptability under different environmental conditions is crucial to the research and protection of biological diversity. This course will systematically introduce the application of population genetics, phylogeography, phylogeny, landscape genetics, high-throughput sequencing genomics and other methods in the molecular ecology of animals and plants in the form of special literature reading, classroom lectures and group discussions. It will focus on how to reconstruct the evolutionary model of species at the population level, infer the evolutionary process, and study basic scientific issues related to phenotypic polymorphism, genetic polymorphism, adaptability, invasive species, habitat fragmentation, behavior, population history and taxonomic status of species and populations. This course is suitable for graduate students, senior undergraduate students in the fields of life sciences and ecology, and all students interested in using genetic methods to study biological diversity.

Name: Mathematical Modeling in Biology
Introduction: Starting from basic mathematical concepts, the mathematical modeling process is introduced. Let undergraduates realize the usefulness of mathematics in biology, cultivate their ability to think about quantifiable biology, and then mobilize their strong interest in learning and scientific research.

Name: Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis
Prerequisite: Genetics, cytology, developmental biology, molecular biology
Introduction: The summer course "Molecular and Cellular Mechanisms of Carcinogenesis" is an advanced course designed for graduate students at Peking University by Professor Lai Zhichun of Pennsylvania State University. The course takes the molecular and cellular mechanisms of carcinogenesis as an example. While clarifying the process of cancer formation and discussing the use of molecular genetics methods to reveal the molecular and cellular mechanisms of carcinogenesis, it also opens up ideas and methods for students to study biological issues. The topics taught are carefully selected and focus on the molecular mechanisms of developmental abnormalities and carcinogenesis, involving some basic principles and latest advances in cell biology, developmental biology and tumor biology. For example, it involves fields such as stem cells, animal cloning, cell division and apoptosis signaling pathways, and the molecular basis of normal cells developing into tumor cells. The focus of course study will be on the genetics and related signaling pathways that induce carcinogenesis. It strives to provide students with a basic understanding of the progress of cancer biology and how to conduct research in this field. The learning requirements for this course should have certain knowledge of molecular biology and genetics. This course is taught entirely in English, with necessary explanations and explanations in Chinese.

Name: Frontier Literature Reading and Discussion in Life Sciences (1)
Introduction:
The cutting-edge literature discussion course in life sciences is a literature discussion course offered by the School of Life Sciences. The main teaching targets are students in the intensive challenge class of life sciences. This course will continue the characteristics of the intensive challenge class literature discussion class. A literature discussion class will be organized by student groups. With the help of the instructor, they will independently select several cutting-edge issues in biology, such as neural circuit, circadian rhythm, etc., and systematically explain the origin of the field, the emergence of important concepts, discuss the core original literature in the field, and explore what are the current main issues and challenges. Each literature discussion invites experts in the field to guide the discussion process and guide students' academic speeches. _x000D_
The course reference book is the classic textbook The Craft of Scientific Presentations: Critical Steps to Succeed and Critical Errors to Avoid, Springer. Through this course, students need to master basic academic presentation skills and lay a solid foundation for future academic communication. _x000D_
This course is a required course for students in the life science intensive challenge class. _x000D_

Name: Methods in Bioinformatics
Prerequisite: Molecular biology, advanced mathematics, computer base
Introduction: This course introduces the main computational methods in bioinformatics research to train students' ability to apply computational biology methods to solve practical biological problems. The course content starts with basic sequence comparison and proceeds step by step to introduce and discuss cutting-edge/hot topics in current research such as deep sequencing data analysis and systems biology.

Name: Population Genetics
Introduction:
Population genetics studies the frequency and distribution of alleles, genotypes, and haplotypes in natural, artificial, and simulated populations, with the goal of understanding the causes, maintenance, and elimination of genetic differences over time and space scales. Population genetics is a core discipline of evolutionary biology and conservation biology, and its theory is an important basis for understanding the evolutionary process and formulating strategies to protect global biological genetic diversity. _x000D_
This course will focus on the basic principles and theories of population genetics, and focus on practical research and application cases in the fields of evolutionary ecology and conservation biology. _x000D_

Name: Nucleic Acid Biology
Introduction: Nucleic acid biology describes the role of various ribonucleic acids (such as mRNA, Riboswitch, Ribozyme, miRNAs, long noncoding RNAs) in life processes, disease occurrence, and therapeutic applications. The content covers the basic methods and mechanisms of gene regulation centered on ribonucleic acid, technical methods of nucleic acid biological research, as well as the role of ribonucleic acid in the occurrence of diseases and its application in disease treatment. At the same time, the teaching content will be adjusted according to the latest developments in the field.

Name: Advanced Course in Molecular Medicine
Introduction:
Molecular medicine covers the research of molecular biology theory and the development of technical systems as well as its application in the development of medicine. In terms of specific content, molecular medicine research involves elaborating from the molecular level the basis of molecular medicine such as genomes, genes, gene transcription and their regulation, cell cycle and signal transcription, and the molecular mechanisms of pathological changes in major diseases. It also involves the development of key research technologies required to carry out the above research and apply the above research results in the medical field, including diagnosis, treatment and new drug research. _x000D_
The Institute of Molecular Medicine of Peking University is a landmark, internationally open, multidisciplinary research institution built in Phase 985II. At the beginning of its establishment, the institute focused on cardiovascular disease and metabolic disease research, integrating basic research, technology transformation, and preclinical research, embodying a one-stop research strategy of "from molecules to people." Cardiovascular disease has become the number one killer of adults in my country, with 4 out of 10 people dying from cardiovascular disease; metabolic diseases are also doubling every 12 years. Hypertension and cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases alone have annual medical expenses of nearly 300 billion yuan. Due to differences in genes, diet, and environment between Chinese and Western populations, the epidemic characteristics and risk factors of cardiovascular disease in my country are not exactly the same as those in Western countries. It is a major challenge facing our country to deeply reveal the mechanisms of major cardiovascular diseases and pathological processes, and to explore new effective prevention and treatment measures on this basis. The Institute of Molecular Medicine takes the country's needs as its own responsibility and carries out relevant basic and translational medical research. _x000D_
This undergraduate course on advanced molecular medicine, which is mainly offered by scientists from the Institute of Molecular Medicine, also features related fields of cardiovascular and metabolic syndrome. It covers the isolation of cardiovascular disease-related genes in the Chinese population and disease genomics, nucleic acid technology research, cell signal transduction, myocardial regeneration and stem cell repair of myocardial damage, vascular biology, nerve and cardiovascular interactions, metabolic syndrome, primate disease models and preclinical research, genetically engineered animal research, new drugs, preclinical research on cell and gene therapy, signal regulatory networks and systems biology strategies for cardiovascular disease, etc. The goal of the course is to enable students to understand how to elucidate the physiological and pathological mechanisms of diseases at the molecular, cellular and overall levels based on the major social needs related to the national economy and people's livelihood, starting from the own laws of biomedical research, and transform the results into strategies for prevention, diagnosis, classification and treatment. _x000D_
