Name: Summer Research Practicum
Introduction: The summer internship activity for undergraduate students started in 2008 and has been successfully held for three times in the School of Life. The purpose of establishing a "practice system" in the undergraduate teaching system is to provide undergraduates with an opportunity to understand the different roles that life sciences play in social life, to help students understand and master the knowledge, ways of thinking and working methods contained in life sciences, and to better understand society, understand society, and experience society. This will not only lay the foundation for everyone to enter the field of basic research, but also lay the foundation for everyone to seek development opportunities in various fields such as enterprises, social management, and personal entrepreneurship. The units where students conduct summer practical activities come from different channels and belong to different social fields at home and abroad. During the trial implementation phase of this outline, members of the undergraduate education guidance group of the college will contact relevant units to establish cooperative relationships. This activity will be directly responsible for the leadership of the hospital, and the working group designated by the education steering group of the hospital will be responsible for the specific organizational work.

Name: Microbiology
Prerequisite: This course is a basic course for junior undergraduate students and does not require other courses.
Introduction: This course enables students to understand and master the basic life activity laws of microorganisms, strengthen their ability to integrate theory with practice, and comprehensively apply knowledge, and understand the application scope, problems and prospects of microorganisms, so as to obtain a more complete basic theory and practical ability of microbiology, and gain inspiration. The main contents taught in this course include pure culture and microscopy techniques of microorganisms, cell morphology and reproduction methods of microorganisms, structure and function of microorganisms, nutrition of microorganisms, viruses, growth and control of microorganisms, genetics of microorganisms, etc.

Name: Introduction to Western Literary Classics
Introduction:
The content introduced in this course includes Western literary masterpieces from ancient Greece to the 20th century. On the basis of summarizing the main characteristics of the times and cultural features in the history of Western literature, we select famous Western literary figures and masterpieces from different countries to carry out detailed introduction and analysis. Strive to teach the background knowledge of Western literature and clarify the basic context of the development of Western literature. At the same time, we try to explain as much as possible the characteristics of Western literary masterpieces that "infuse people's hearts with an unconquerable passion for all things that are great and more sacred than themselves." Vivid and spiritual, it guides readers to understand the essence of those Western literary works that "do not just show individuals and their affairs, but show knowledge about the entire species, the world and life, show people and the various shapes, contradictions, and disasters of their existence, and show the most impenetrable mystery of human beings." I hope it will be helpful to students who take this course in deepening people's understanding of Western culture and literature, enhancing people's understanding of the differences between Chinese and Western culture and literature, and developing people's ideas for comparative research. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Genetics Laboratory
Introduction:
This course is designed to closely match the genetics course. Through the teaching of experimental design and concepts, to the actual genetic experimental operation, you can deepen your understanding of the classroom teaching content and expand your thinking space. _x000D_
    Our genetics experiments organically integrate experiments at the cell chromosome level, genome level, and functional genome level. It not only includes classic confirmatory experiments, but also introduces experiments for modern gene function research that are closely related to scientific research. First, by showing and teaching different model animals (such as Drosophila melanogaster, nematodes and zebrafish), students will be able to realize the importance of model animals in genetic research. Through chromosome preparation, observation and the introduction of the use of Drosophila balanced chromosomes, students can truly understand chromosomes as carriers of genes from a practical level and understand how genes transmit genetic information through chromosomes. In the classic forward genetics confirmatory experiment, we will use a hybridization experiment to simultaneously analyze and verify the three laws of genetics (free combination of genes, the law of segregation, and the law of linkage), sex-linked inheritance, and analyze the genetic distance between genes; the interaction of genes is realized through genetic experiments in corn. Reverse genetics experiments in the modern post-genomic era emphasize the importance of gene mutation in studying gene function. The purpose of studying the phenotype of the target gene after gene mutation is achieved through the basic strategy of loss of function or gain of function. "The Gal4/UAS system (known as the Swiss Army Knife of Drosophila genetics research) induces oncogenes to be ectopically expressed in Drosophila" can achieve the purpose of gain of function, and "Using the Flp/FRT system to construct Drosophila Mosiac clones" (obtaining homozygous mutant clones)" can achieve the purpose of loss of function. At the same time, the different purposes that can be achieved through the flexible and combined use of these systems are taught, allowing students to design their own experiments, thereby achieving the purpose of using genetic concepts and tools to study gene functions in scientific research. _x000D_
    _x000D_

Name: Creative Practice II
Introduction:
With the continuous development of our country's society and economy, innovative talents are the most important embodiment of core competitiveness in the process of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Colleges and universities play an important role in cultivating innovative talents. The abilities of independent thinking, independent judgment and independent learning are indispensable basic qualities for innovative talents, and the cultivation of these abilities requires the integration of new teaching concepts and teaching methods for reform and practice. _x000D_
An ancient saying goes: "Those who know something are not as good as those who are good at it, and those who are good at it are not as good as those who are happy." That is to say, interest is the greatest motivation for learning, and taking pleasure in it is the best state of learning. If you are interested in the content you are studying and researching, you will enjoy it, and then change from passive to active, fully mobilizing students' subjective initiative and creativity, and at the same time improving learning efficiency. If this kind of "good" and "enjoyable" learning content can combine theoretical learning with practical activities, it will maximize students' ability to understand knowledge and use it flexibly. _x000D_
This course takes the above-mentioned innovative talent training as the main goal, takes students' curiosity and interest as a "good" and "enjoyable" as a starting point, uses personalized practical projects as a carrier, is based on open multi-field resources, and is guaranteed by a multi-disciplinary instructor team. It fully mobilizes students' subjective initiative and encourages them to discover problems and set up projects in areas of interest. And in the process of practice, they can think independently and learn spontaneously, discover and cultivate their innovative thinking and innovative practical abilities through self-discovery, self-organization and independent operation, and improve their communication, collaboration, management and scientific expression, and truly become "patriotic, inspirational, truth-seeking and practical" innovative talents with harmonious personality, solid foundation and comprehensive ability. _x000D_
The course applied for this time is an upgraded version of the previously offered "Creative Practice". In the teaching practice in the spring and autumn semesters of 2019, we gradually summarized the experience and shortcomings of this type of project-oriented courses, and initially established a feasible teaching system and a multi-disciplinary teacher team. During repeated discussions, plans for further upgrading and reforming the curriculum were determined. The content of this new course upgrade mainly includes: the refinement of the large subject areas involved in the practical project, and the deepening of the project content. This course will be mainly dedicated to cross-directional projects between life sciences and other science disciplines (such as information science, etc.). We will add more guidance in related fields during the project design, implementation, and evaluation processes. _x000D_

Name: Biostatistics
Prerequisite: Math courses at undergraduate level for non-math majors
Introduction:
This course provides some of the most important topics in analyzing data often seen in biological research. Specific topics are
- Random events and probability distributions
- Confidence interval estimations
- Hypothesis testing and its application to group comparisons
- Issues of power and sample size
- Study design and analysis of variance
- Regression methods and correlation analysis
- Categorical data analysis
- Nonparametric statistical methods
- Survival analysis
This course introduces a statistical software (R), with plenty of examples and lab sessions for analyzing data and implementing the topics of this course. This course also encourages active participations from the students with sessions of problem solving, research paper discussion, and group projects.

Name: Cognitive Science and Economics
Introduction: Cognitive science studies the mental world of humans. Economic activity is the largest experiment in human society, and every market participant is an active observer of the experiment. This course introduces integrated theory, fundamentals, and modeling approaches in economics and cognitive science. Economics and psychology in the 20th century were developed within the framework of Newtonian mechanics. Integrating economics and cognitive science in interdisciplinary research in the 21st century requires moving beyond the tradition of Newtonian mechanics. This course will introduce a series of new modeling methods to characterize subeconomic analysis, currency, economic policy, Pareto efficiency, markets, the "invisible hand", etc. The course is designed to be self-contained and does not require any prerequisite courses. It starts from basic concepts and brings them into cutting-edge topics, from the shallower to the deeper, so that the audience can keep up with the progress of the lecture, learn systematic knowledge, and understand and master the characteristics and methods of interdisciplinary subjects. This course has been developed and taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in the United States for many years. In recent years, it has been taught many times at Tsinghua University, Renmin University, and Sun Yat-sen University. It has aroused widespread interest among students and teachers in various liberal arts disciplines in China and the United States and received high course evaluations.

Name: Reasoning and Decision Making
Introduction: This course covers a wide range of higher-order cognition and theory of mind, including logic and reasoning psychology, decision theory and decision-making psychology, rationalism and behaviorist game theory, language tasks and experimental methods, and their applications in management science, political science, international relations, and educational testing and assessment. Traditionally these fields have been developed independently and taught separately. This course adopts an interdisciplinary model and focuses on building an integrated model of composite fields. Along this line, discussions are carried out at the theoretical, empirical and practical levels. The course is designed to be self-contained and does not require any prerequisite courses. It starts from basic concepts and brings them into cutting-edge topics, from the shallower to the deeper, so that the audience can keep up with the progress of the lecture, learn systematic knowledge, and understand and master the characteristics and methods of interdisciplinary subjects. This course has been developed and taught at Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute in the United States for many years. In recent years, it has been taught many times at Tsinghua University, Renmin University, and Sun Yat-sen University. It has aroused widespread interest among students and teachers in various liberal arts disciplines in China and the United States and received high course evaluations.

Name: Basic Laboratory in Modern Life Sciences
Introduction: The basic experimental course of modern life science is a basic experimental course for undergraduates in the School of Life Sciences. The content includes basic experiments in different branches such as molecular biology, biochemistry, cell biology, genetics, microbiology, botany, zoology and bioinformatics. The purpose is to cultivate students' comprehensive experimental abilities in experimental design, operation, data analysis and summary, master the basic principles and skills of biological experiments, and lay a good foundation for undergraduates to enter the research laboratory to carry out scientific research projects.

Name: International Relations and East Asian Security
Introduction: Issues of war and peace, conflict and cooperation have long been central issues in the study of international relations. Although the end of the Cold War and the accelerated development of globalization have brought new topics to traditional international relations research, they have not changed the reality that international security is the core research field of international relations. Whether from a historical perspective or from the current international political reality, East Asia is a rare region in the world where the interests of major powers are criss-crossed, and it is also a region that has a decisive impact on China's national security. This course aims to enable students to master the historical context of the development and evolution of international relations in East Asia since modern times, and strive to combine existing international relations theory with East Asian security issues, treat East Asia as an integral part of the international system, and conduct in-depth discussions on important issues such as the region's historical heritage, power distribution, balance of power, military alliances, multilateral security cooperation, regional hot spots, economic interdependence, and the relationship between political development and regional peace. In the discussion, we not only pay attention to the universal significance of the theory, but also pay attention to the uniqueness of the East Asian region, and understand the conflicts and cooperation among countries in the East Asian region from the dual dimensions of theory and reality.

Name: Social Anthropology
Introduction:
After social anthropology appeared in Europe in the mid-19th century, especially in the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Russia, and Japan, it initially developed under different names (such as anthropology, sociology, ethnology, and ethnography). At the beginning of the 20th century, functional anthropology, the Annales School of Sociology, and historical concretism emerged in Britain, France, and the United States, and modern ethnographic methods and anthropological theoretical explanations matured. By the 1950s, with the emergence of structural anthropology in France and the emergence of new evolutionary theories in the former Soviet Union, the United States and China, the discipline experienced an important stage. Since the 1970s, based on the previous foreshadowing, it has entered the period of post-structuralism, political economy, and post-modernism. _x000D_
Social anthropology explains human existence from a social and cultural perspective. Its basic branches are classification, kinship, religious anthropology, political anthropology, and economic anthropology. On the basis of basic branches, social anthropology also focuses on the study of ethnic groups, material culture, cities, medical care, and history. _x000D_
Since the end of the 19th century, China has begun to introduce social anthropological knowledge from Europe or indirectly from Japan. From the 1920s, national scientific research institutions and comprehensive colleges and universities established specialized research institutions (among which Academia Sinica and Yenching University were particularly important). By the 1940s, domestic disciplines had approached the level of advanced countries in anthropology (such as France). In the 1950s, the subject name was banned, but research was still carried out and was used in large-scale national and social historical surveys. In the 1980s, social anthropology was rebuilt in comprehensive colleges and ethnic colleges under the names of "anthropology" and "ethnology" respectively, and developed with their own characteristics. _x000D_
In the 1980s, the Department of Archeology and the Department of Sociology (including the Institute of Sociological Anthropology) of Peking University established anthropological research directions and courses, such as cultural anthropology, community studies, and comparative sociology. The course "Social Anthropology" was officially established among undergraduate students in 1996 as an auxiliary theoretical methods course for sociology majors. In 1998, Peking University established a master's degree program and a doctoral program in anthropology. Since then, the undergraduate course "Social Anthropology" has also become an integral part of the preliminary teaching work of this degree program, and was later defined as a "main basic course." This course is an introductory course to the subject. The teaching content includes: (1) history of the subject; (2) research content; (3) research methods; (4) history of theoretical evolution; (5) introduction to subfields; (6) Chinese anthropology; (7) interpretation of academic and practical significance, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Special Lectures in Sociology
Introduction: It teaches the basic scope of sociological research in a vivid, easy-to-understand, and relevant way to students' lives, and cultivates students' understanding and love for sociology. It is an introductory course for newly admitted undergraduate students to learn about sociology professional knowledge, so that newly admitted students can understand the basic scope and preliminary knowledge of sociological research, and achieve the purpose of loving the sociology major.

Name: Urban Sociology
Prerequisite: Social science generals, foreign sociological doctrine, social research and research methods
Introduction: Course Chinese Introduction: Cities occupy an extremely important position in human life and social development. With the acceleration of urbanization around the world, urban research has also received increasing attention. Basic questions such as how cities grow and decline, how they are constructed and run, how they give meaning to social life, and urban development trends constitute the central issues discussed in urban sociology. This course will give a general introduction to urban sociology from the basic perspectives, important themes, main theoretical perspectives, and basic methods of urban research.

Name: Studies in Modern and Contemporary Chinese Literature and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Current Chinese literature, literature theory, comparative literature and comparative culture
Introduction: This course is a follow-up course to "Modern Chinese Literature" and "Contemporary Chinese Literature", which are compulsory courses for undergraduate majors in the Chinese Department. It is dedicated to improving students' scientific research capabilities and completing the transition from learners to researchers as soon as possible. The establishment of a research course focusing on "Chinese Modern and Contemporary Literature and Culture" is a summary and improvement of relevant professional courses, helping students to form a conscious awareness of methodology, from selecting thesis topics, collecting materials to writing, refining students' problem awareness, cultivating their good study style, and laying a solid foundation for students' academic thesis, dissertation writing and further study.

Name: Chinese Literature of the Last Three Decades of the Twentieth Century
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is basically a macroscopic study. However, this macroscopic research is based on microscopic interpretation, and presents the context of historical development through the analysis of specific texts and some important historical details. This course has the intention of not only helping students understand the literature of the last 30 years of the 20th century, but also making students aware of a research idea and a research method. _x000D_
While this course rationally explains a series of literary phenomena, it will also attach great importance to cultivating students' perceptual abilities. Because in the view of the lecturer, to grasp literature, rationality alone is not enough - overemphasis on rationality may even prevent you from ever getting close to literature. Today, when scientism is the mainstream of academic research, there are very serious problems in literary research. When living literature is studied in a surgical anatomy style, we have lost the proper artistic feeling towards literature. This course will promote an attitude towards studying literature: be a reader first, then an interpreter. _x000D_

Name: Politics and Diplomacy of Modern China
Introduction: This course mainly teaches several issues in the fields of modern Chinese politics and diplomacy. The main teaching content includes the political activities and major political events of the upper class of modern society, with special attention to the internal contradictions of the ruling group that determines the political destiny of the country and serves as the political representative of the country. At the same time, the changes in the modern power structure, the evolution of the political system, and the relationships between the central and local governments, gentry and imperial power, monarchy and republic, reform and revolution, domestic affairs and foreign affairs are discussed. It also includes the understanding of issues such as diplomacy and wars between China and foreign countries in modern times, etiquette conflicts in Sino-Western exchanges, unequal treaty privileges and modern foreign churches in China. The basic purpose of the course: to enable students to have a deeper understanding of the main clues and development trends of China’s political and diplomatic history during this period; to understand the latest academic trends and research results related to this topic; to understand the basic historical materials and historical facts related to this topic. At the same time, starting from this topic, students’ reading and analysis abilities of Chinese and foreign original documents will be trained.

Name: Selected Topics in Systems Biology
Introduction: This course, which focuses on in-depth literature, focuses on concepts, principles, methods, current trends and challenges arising from the combination of theory and experiments in biology. Each session addressed one aspect and discussed in depth two articles. Students should carefully read the articles to be discussed before classes and actively participate in the discussions in the classroom. The mentors are responsible for inspiring, guiding the discussion, giving appropriate instruction and concluding the discussion. The course covered randomness and noise in biological systems, hypersensitivity and synergy, loosing, evolving image generation, quantitative issues in evolution, genomics and biological network analysis, synthetic biology, understanding disease and drug interactions from the perspective of biological networks. The subject is compulsory for postgraduate students at the Centre for Theoretical Biology. Post-graduate and undergraduate students from other faculties are welcome.

Name: Ecology Field Practicum
Introduction: Ecology is the study of the relationships between organisms and between organisms and their environment. Ecological research is mostly carried out in the wild environment and has its own special research methods and implementation processes, which cannot be learned and experienced through general classroom teaching. This course will bring undergraduates with certain basic knowledge of biology to wild environments such as nature reserves, mainly in the northern part of Minshan Mountain in Sichuan Province, with Wanglang National Nature Reserve in Pingwu County as the core base, and covering several surrounding field sites in Tangjiahe National Nature Reserve, Jiuzhaigou National Nature Reserve, and Laohegou Nature Reserve. By allowing students to participate in field ecological research projects, students learn the basic processes and research methods of field ecological research. Through the study of this course, students will deepen their understanding of the basic concepts of ecology, understand the basic processes and operating methods of ecological field research, master basic methods such as experimental design, data acquisition, and data analysis, cultivate students' basic field investigation and scientific research abilities, and lay the foundation for future field research in zoology, botany, conservation biology, and ecology.

Name: Numerical Methods: Principles, Algorithms and Applications
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, linear algebra, computer program design, probability statistics
Introduction: The content mainly includes direct solutions to linear equations, iterative methods, calculation methods of matrix eigenvalues, singular value decomposition and applications, calculation methods of linear programming and nonlinear programming problems, solution of nonlinear equations (sets), polynomial interpolation/approximation, fast Fourier transform (FFT), numerical integration, Monte Carlo method, numerical solution of differential equations, etc. Focuses on introducing numerical methods, their principles and applications.

Name: Fundamentals of Biopharmaceutical Technology
Prerequisite: There is no requirement for the first course.
Introduction: This course teaches the basic knowledge and latest developments related to biotechnology pharmaceuticals from the beginning to the end. This course explores the applications and basic strategies for producing recombinant proteins, recombinant vaccines and other biologically active proteins from the perspective of biomedicine. The content of this course includes: the basic concepts of biopharmaceuticals; the characteristics of biotechnological drugs; the principles and development process of successful biotechnological drugs, as well as the mechanisms and precautions for the treatment of related diseases. The content of this course also includes basic research methods of biotechnology drugs and basic knowledge and progress in some major related fields, such as the basics of animal cell pharmaceuticals, genetic engineering vaccines, gene therapy, and molecular agriculture using plants as bioreactors. This course is an introductory course for students who are interested in biotechnology pharmaceuticals or want to engage in biotechnology drug-related industries in the future. It can serve as the basis for a deeper understanding of biotechnology drug-related fields.

Name: Computational Systems Biology
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, calculus, constant differential equation
Introduction:
With the generation of massive biological data and the significant improvement of computing power, mathematical modeling and computational simulation of complex biological systems have become another important scientific research method in the field of life sciences in addition to experimental and theoretical methods. In recent years, the intersection between mathematics and biology has become closer and closer. The use of systems biology methods to explore the intrinsic characteristics and quantitative laws of life mechanisms is being widely used in various fields of life sciences. At the same time, the intersection with various branches of biology also raises new questions for applied mathematics, with both opportunities and challenges. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will systematically teach mathematical models and computational methods in computational systems biology. It uses cell and developmental biology as the background and combines specific biological systems to understand systems biology from the perspective of mathematics and calculation, and master the modeling, analysis and calculation methods in biomathematical problems. _x000D_

Name: Frontier Literature Reading and Discussion in Life Sciences (3)
Introduction:
The cutting-edge literature discussion course in life sciences is a literature discussion course offered by the School of Life Sciences. The main teaching targets are students in the intensive challenge class of life sciences. This course will continue the characteristics of the intensive challenge class literature discussion class. A literature discussion class will be organized by student groups. With the help of the instructor, they will independently select several cutting-edge issues in biology, such as neural circuit, circadian rhythm, etc., and systematically explain the origin of the field, the emergence of important concepts, discuss the core original literature in the field, and explore what are the current main issues and challenges. Each literature discussion invites experts in the field to guide the discussion process and guide students' academic speeches. _x000D_
The course reference book is the classic textbook The Craft of Scientific Presentations: Critical Steps to Succeed and Critical Errors to Avoid, Springer. Through this course, students need to master basic academic presentation skills and lay a solid foundation for future academic communication. _x000D_
This course is a required course for students in the life science intensive challenge class. _x000D_

Name: History of Banned Books in China
Prerequisite: It's better to have students studying Chinese history, book history, Western culture, history, etc.
Introduction: This course introduces a brief history of banned books in ancient my country, starting from the pre-Qin Dynasty and ending in the late Qing Dynasty. The content involves the background, form and characteristics of banned books in ancient society. It focuses on some important book-banning events in the history of our country, such as burning books and entrapping Confucian scholars, and literary inquisition. The history of banned books is an important topic in the study of book history. Teaching the history of banned books in ancient my country will help students increase their knowledge of literature and history, better understand the social, political and cultural significance of books in various historical periods, and enable them to critically inherit the national cultural tradition. At present, how to ensure citizens' freedom of speech and freedom of the press while effectively curbing bad publications that affect social security is a problem that modern society must solve. Through the teaching of this course, we summarize the ancient experience of banning books and compare the pros and cons. It is of immeasurable historical significance and practical value for contemporary college students to explore, study and promote the cultural heritage of ancient China, promote the construction of socialist civilization and establish a harmonious society.

Name: Philosophy and Life
Introduction: Within the framework of Western philosophy, this course discusses major life themes such as truth, goodness, beauty, love, justice, self, freedom and death. The course combines history and theory to focus on demonstrating the life wisdom of Western philosophers. Does life have meaning? Why and how do we pursue truth, goodness and beauty? What is the source of pain? Do you know the secrets and techniques of love? How do we face death? Are we free or predestined? This course draws on the resources of ancient, medieval, modern and contemporary Western philosophy to explore various answers to the above questions.

Name: Industry Internship Practicum
Introduction: The main elements of this course are the organization of more than four weeks of practical training for students at industry-related establishments, training in relevant skills prior to the practice and the presentation of a report after the practice. The aim is to guide students to develop an in-depth understanding of industry ' s operating patterns and directions through their hands-on experience, and to set individual career development goals, leading to a rational planning of their studies and careers.

Name: Social Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Social psychology studies the social psychology and social behavior of individuals and groups and their development rules. This course will cover important concepts and theories in mainstream social psychology. The main contents include: how individuals view themselves and others, how to view and think about social phenomena, human aggression and helping behavior, the formation and change of attitudes, social influence and its manifestations, the basis and intimacy of interpersonal relationships, group psychology and behavior, how culture affects people, social psychological factors affecting human health, and the latest positive psychology. This course focuses on the application of social psychology knowledge in social life, the formation and maintenance of interpersonal relationships, the principles of interpersonal communication and conflict resolution, and smooth teamwork. This course will also focus on contemporary scholars' research on human psychology and behavior in different cultural backgrounds. Through the study of this course, students should master the research content, research methods and main research results of social psychology, and use them to understand related social life and events.

Name: Archaeology and the Reconstruction of Ancient History
Introduction: The reconstruction of ancient history is the disciplinary mission of Chinese archeology. Over the past century, Chinese archeology has made remarkable contributions to the reconstruction of ancient history. This course aims to guide students in reading classic documents, firstly establishing a correct view and framework of ancient history; and then by systematically describing relevant archaeological discoveries, using the dual evidence of archaeology and literature, to tell the ancient history of China reconstructed by archaeology.

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 1)
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the history of Western philosophy from Thales to Hegel, analyzes the origin and significance of various philosophical ideas and concepts, and lays a preliminary foundation for students to engage in further philosophical research in the future.

Name: Chinese Philosophy (Part 2)
Prerequisite: Chinese Philosophy (up), Introduction to Philosophy, etc.
Introduction: It aims to enable students to master the most important and basic knowledge of Chinese philosophy and understand the historical development and theoretical characteristics of Chinese philosophy. The characteristic of this course is to teach philosophy through the history of philosophy, specifically through the theoretical form shown in the historical development of Neo-Confucianism in the Song and Ming Dynasties (from Han Yu to Dai Zhen), sort out, analyze and study the content and form of Chinese philosophy, and then explore its theoretical paradigm and lasting value.

Name: Fundamentals of Epigenetics: From Chromatin to Human Disease
Introduction:
Although the extension of some concepts of epigenetics is still controversial, epigenetics is undoubtedly a rapidly developing field in modern life sciences. In recent years, with the breakthrough of new technologies and the establishment of new methods, rising research interest has promoted the rapid development of the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, and the regulatory mechanisms of important life processes using chromatin as carriers in eukaryotic cells have also been deeply explored. In particular, research on human health and disease has found that epigenetic regulation plays an increasingly prominent role in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. This course starts with the research history of chromatin and epigenetics, and systematically introduces the basic concepts of chromatin and epigenetics. The course not only introduces landmark research in the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, but also introduces classic and modern research methods on chromatin. Focusing on the mechanism of epigenetic regulation in core issues such as cell fate determination and maintenance of genome stability, this course mainly introduces the dynamic changes of chromatin, focusing on the molecular mechanisms of epigenetic regulation (including nucleic acid modifications, histone modifications, and dynamic regulation of nucleosomes, etc., and in-depth discussion of the establishment and maintenance mechanisms of gene transcription silencing); finally, this course focuses on the relationship between chromatin and epigenetic regulation disorders and human diseases, including cancer, diabetes, and many neurological diseases. _x000D_
_x000D_
     This course is intended for upper-division undergraduate and graduate students interested in epigenetics and chromatin biology. In this course, 3/4 of the class time is generally spent on lectures, and 1/4 of the class time is devoted to student-led discussions of 2-3 research papers. At the end of the semester, each student writes a short research proposal based on one of the topics discussed in class. Through classroom training, students not only learn key concepts and current advances in the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, but also strengthen critical thinking and presentation skills, as well as research proposal writing. _x000D_

Name: Intensive Literature Reading and Academic Presentation (2)
Introduction: Life science is currently one of the most active fields in the entire natural sciences. Literature reading is the most effective way to obtain accurate research information, and listening to academic reports is the most direct opportunity to understand the cutting-edge of this field. This course is designed to improve the ability of our students to effectively obtain accurate and accurate research cutting-edge trends. _x000D_

Name: Psychological Statistics II Computer Lab
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course is a supporting course for "Psychological Statistics II" and explains the use of SPSS software involved in Psychological Statistics II. The course introduces the interface and functions of SPSS. The main content includes: non-parametric test, advanced variance analysis, reliability analysis, factor analysis, preliminary experimental design, multiple regression, logistic regression, covariance analysis, partial correlation, survival analysis, cluster analysis, etc. This course is conducted simultaneously with "Psychological Statistics II" and cannot be conducted separately. _x000D_

Name: Frontiers of Earth Science (First-Year Seminar)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
This course is offered to first-year freshmen of the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It aims to introduce freshmen to earth sciences and inspire their interest and love in earth science learning and research. _x000D_
      Earth science is a basic discipline that studies the processes and changes of the earth system (including the atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, biosphere and solar-terrestrial space) and their interactions, including geology, geochemistry, geophysics, geographic information systems, space physics, etc., as well as other derivative disciplines. _x000D_
      In the 21st century, mankind is facing increasingly serious problems of resources, environment and natural disasters. The 21st century is also an era of vigorous development of space technology. Earth science and space science are both a basic science and a science widely used in modern national defense and national economic construction. Taking the earth and its far and near space as the research object, the basic research results obtained are the common wealth of all mankind. Modern earth science and space science research still play a very important role not only in traditional fields such as aerospace, resource exploration, and prediction and defense of natural disasters. It also plays an increasingly important role in new fields such as nuclear explosion monitoring, site selection and seismic design of major and lifeline projects, earth environment monitoring and prediction, and digital earth. It plays a very important role in the national economy and modern national defense construction. The construction of the national economy and modern national defense urgently require us to cultivate more and better professionals in earth and space sciences. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Earth Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
"Introduction to Earth Science" covers the basic knowledge of each secondary discipline in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It is a basic course to guide students into the door of earth science. It is also a required course for all majors in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. The main purpose of the course teaching can be summarized as the following three points:_x000D_
Through lectures and in-class internships (including field internships), students can master basic earth science concepts such as space and the planet Earth, the earth's structure, the earth's material composition, the earth's internal and external dynamic processes, the earth's basic physical characteristics, and earth observation technology. _x000D_
Earth science is characterized by its vast research objects and long history, but students lack an overall understanding of earth science in middle school. Therefore, it is necessary to teach students "Introduction to Earth Science" to initially establish the concepts of time and space in earth science, understand the thinking characteristics of earth science, learn to use standardized earth science language, and lay a good foundation for the study of subsequent courses in earth science. _x000D_
It enables students to have an understanding of the overall picture of earth science and adjacent disciplines and the cutting-edge research trends of the disciplines, to have a preliminary understanding of the basic content of the subsequent courses of each major, to understand the connections between the majors and subsequent courses, to grasp the connotation of earth science from a macro perspective, and to lay the foundation for cross-research among various branches of disciplines.

Name: General Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Mainly to meet the needs of current economic construction and talent cultivation for the 21st century, and with reference to various relevant latest teaching materials from the United Kingdom, the United States, Russia and other countries, major changes have been made to the teaching content of the small class course. This course is taught by combining classroom teaching, discussion, in-class practice and field practice, with the purpose of expanding students' knowledge and stimulating students' thirst for knowledge. The content of the course mainly includes the following aspects:_x000D_
	① Facing the 21st century In view of the major issues faced by mankind in the 21st century such as population, resources, environment, disaster reduction, etc., the teaching content of "Introduction to Earth Science (2)" includes "resources and environment", "geological disasters and protection" and other knowledge closely related to economic construction, laying a foundation for the teaching subjects to conduct research in related fields in the future. _x000D_
② Broaden the knowledge of the teaching objects. Starting from the origin of the universe and the solar system, the earth's position in the universe and the evolution of the earth are described, including the geological processes of the earth's atmosphere, hydrosphere and internal layers, so that students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding of the earth and its related knowledge, and comprehensively broaden the knowledge of the teaching objects. _x000D_
③ Discuss the relationship between man and earth. This article introduces the relationship between humans and the earth system in a relatively systematic manner from several aspects, including the impact of the movement of the earth system on human activities, the connection between humans and the earth system, human geological effects, and the role of humans in the earth system. Let the teaching subjects fully understand the environmental awareness that human beings only have one earth, and take on the task of protecting the earth and the environment. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: General Geology Seminar
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: Fundamentals of Space Science and Technology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The "Fundamentals of Space Science and Technology" course is a basic course offered to all students in the Department of Science and the Department of Information and Engineering Science. Its purpose is to enable students to master the basic knowledge of space technology, broaden their horizons, and understand the role that space science and technology plays in promoting human progress.

Name: Fundamentals of Spatial Information Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General Earth Sciences, Front Lines in Earth Sciences
Introduction: The course mainly teaches the basic theories and methods of spatial information science, so that students can basically understand and master the theoretical foundation, mathematical foundation, method foundation and technical foundation of spatial information science and technology. The course content is divided into three parts: remote sensing information science, geographic information science, and satellite navigation and positioning science. While teaching the basics of science, it also deepens students' understanding of knowledge through rich application examples, and initially cultivates students' ability to analyze and solve problems using spatial information science and technology methods.

Name: Theory and Practice of Chinese-English Translation
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
The "Chinese-English Translation: Theory and Practice" course uses detailed and solid explanations of English-Chinese translation techniques and a large number of translation exercises to enable students to master the basic skills and abilities of bilingual translation. They can use the translation skills they have learned to bilingually translate articles of certain difficulty, and the translation will be smooth, accurate in wording, and free of obvious grammatical errors, mistranslations and missing translations. _x000D_
      The course is divided into fourteen units. Each unit is based on the theoretical basis of differences in Chinese and English word meanings, sentence patterns, thinking patterns, etc., and introduces one or two translation techniques and strategies, such as "conversion between complex English sentences and Chinese parallel sentences", "translation of English clauses", "part-of-speech conversion in English-Chinese translation", "sequential translation and reverse translation", "word addition and subtraction", "passive voice translation", etc. In conjunction with each technique, a large number of typical and difficult example sentences and passages are provided for students to practice and practice. Example sentences and translated chapters cover knowledge in various fields, such as politics, economy, science and technology, diplomacy, tourism, education, environmental protection, literature, history, sports, art, etc. Although non-English majors at Peking University will not work as professional interpreters or translators in the future, they will enter various fields such as my country's politics, economy, science and technology, culture, education, sports, and art, and conduct academic research and academic exchanges in their respective fields. Therefore, the ability to translate excellent results from two cultures into Chinese or English is very important. _x000D_

Name: GIS Design and Applications
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
From the two aspects of design, development and application methods, students can master the development ideas and development methods of GIS, clarify the logical and physical structure of GIS, and learn from _x000D_
The technical route and main technical methods of underlying GIS development. Lay a good theoretical foundation and mastery for students to implement geographic information system engineering in the future_x000D_
Application method. Cultivate their thinking and practical abilities on how to apply geographic information systems. _x000D_

Name: Mathematical Models in Earth Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Probability theory and mathematical statistics, linear algebra, computer algorithmic languages.
Introduction:
With the development of computer technology and mathematical methods, quantitative analysis has become an integral part of geoscience research and engineering applications. Since geological variables are more or less random or fuzzy, this course mainly introduces students to classic multi-source statistical methods and commonly used fuzzy mathematical methods. _x000D_
    According to the course plan, the main contents are as follows:_x000D_
    (1) Through an introduction to the development achievements in the fields of the old three theories "cybernetics, systems theory, and information theory", the new three theories "dissipative structure theory, catastrophe theory, synergy theory" and econometrics, clarify the necessity and feasibility of quantitative research on complex geoscience problems; combined with the development process of quantitative geoscience research, clarify the research objects, content, and methods. _x000D_
    (2) Introduces the mathematical methods for preprocessing raw geoscience data and distinguishing concentration and dispersion to initially analyze the basic rules of the data; introduces mathematical methods for spatial analysis and research on point-like and linear objects, such as the E.W. Dijkstra method. _x000D_
    (3) A series of mathematical methods based on the least squares method are introduced, such as single regression, multiple regression, stepwise regression analysis methods for analyzing and forecasting geographical data, and trend surface methods for analyzing the overall trend and local variability of spatial variables, and application cases are analyzed. In order to meet the needs of the trend surface analysis method, the algorithm for automatically generating trend surfaces and residual contours is introduced in detail. _x000D_
    (4) In order to avoid the subjectivity and arbitrariness of traditional qualitative classification methods, the numerical clustering classification method and its application are introduced; in order to identify the attribution of geographical types and determine regional boundaries, the discriminant analysis method and its application are introduced. In addition, the basic knowledge of fuzzy mathematics is introduced, and based on this, the principles and applications of fuzzy cluster analysis and fuzzy comprehensive evaluation methods are clarified. _x000D_
    (5) In order to reduce geographical research elements and simplify the system, the mathematical principles, calculation methods and application examples of the principal component analysis method for dealing with corresponding problems are introduced. _x000D_
    (6) In order to realize quantitative research on the development strategy and feasibility of geoscience issues, several basic data processing models are introduced, such as geographical system simulation model, geographical environment identification model, input-output model, optimal location model, and optimal planning model. _x000D_

Name: Geographic Information Systems Engineering
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The course starts from the development and needs of geographic information system engineering, combines geographic information system engineering project development experience and related research results, and systematically introduces the basic principles, technical methods, implementation processes, application examples and development trends of geographic information system engineering. The lecture will be carried out based on the key issues currently considered in the development and management of geographic information system projects. The main contents include: introduction, demand survey and feasibility analysis, system design, system implementation, system testing, system maintenance and evaluation, geographic information system engineering management, geographic information system engineering application, and discussion of geographic information system engineering trends and issues.

Name: Applications of Remote Sensing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Remote sensing overview, remote sensing digital image processing, GIS overview, geology base
Introduction:
Purpose: On the basis of mastering the basic theory of remote sensing and image processing methods, familiarize yourself with and master the processes, methods and typical application examples of remote sensing applications. _x000D_
	Including: understanding remote sensing data sources, mastering data selection principles and methods; mastering the principles, methods, ideas and strategies of data processing and analysis; understanding typical application examples: including classic examples and new application examples. _x000D_
	Content: Main methods, techniques and strategies in the entire process of remote sensing data acquisition, processing, analysis and application, as well as analysis of typical examples. _x000D_
	Features: Theoretical analysis, method introduction and application examples are closely combined, and classroom explanations are combined with experiments (including after-class exercises)

Name: Fundamentals of Satellite Navigation and Positioning
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
Advanced Data, Survey of Mapping
It's best to have a programming base that will help the experimental course progress.
Introduction:
Satellite navigation and positioning technology is a very important development direction in the field of earth observation. Its applications cover a wide range of applications. Satellite navigation equipment has become an indispensable tool for the military, public security, surveying and mapping, ocean, geology, mining, agriculture, environment, aerospace and other fields, as well as transportation, environment, meteorology, earthquakes and other fields that are inseparable from people's daily life. There are many global satellite navigation systems in the world, and my country is also developing the Beidou global navigation system. The development and application of these satellite navigation systems have had a profound impact on the development of related fields in my country and even internationally in recent decades. How to efficiently use the data obtained by satellite navigation equipment to further analyze various dynamic information in related fields has become an important part of frontier exploration in these fields. Therefore, knowledge about satellite navigation and positioning technology and its applications is an indispensable course for majors in the field of earth observation. _x000D_
This course aims to give students a comprehensive understanding of the basic knowledge of satellite navigation and positioning, including its basic principles, methods and simple applications. It focuses on the composition of the American GPS system and my country's Beidou system, signal processing, calculation principles of single-point positioning and navigation, real-time dynamic positioning and navigation methods, etc. It also combines experimental classes to allow students to master relevant algorithms and the use of user modules (receivers), laying the foundation for further in-depth study and application of relevant theories and technologies of satellite navigation and positioning. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Computer Science and Programming
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is introduced from Harvard University's most popular course - CS50, which is an introductory course to computer science and programming. The purpose of the course teaching is to cultivate students' computational thinking and use computers to solve problems more efficiently. The course content includes basic concepts of computer science, algorithms, data structures, packaging, resource management, information security, software engineering, website development, etc. Programming languages ​​covered in the course include C, Python, SQL, JavaScript, as well as CSS and HTML. The exercises are drawn from various fields and disciplines in real life. To study this course, students do not need to have any computer-related prerequisite courses.

Name: Selected Readings in Foreign History (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is one of the required courses for undergraduate majors in the Department of History. It includes (1) and (2) and lasts for two semesters. The first semester mainly includes ancient and early modern parts. The course uses the English version of "A Brief History of Western Civilization" by Pawlek as the basic textbook. In addition to sorting out the basic development clues of world history, the main content of the course focuses on cultivating students' ability to read English historical documents, using the first and second volumes of the English version of the historical collection "Heritage of Western Civilization" as the main reference and reading documents. The teacher's classroom teaching content is mainly limited to introducing the historical background and the ins and outs of the literature related to the reading, and the rest of the class time will be used for students' questions and discussions. Teachers will focus on cultivating students’ understanding of English literature accurately and, to a certain extent, on improving their ability to listen, listen and write in English.

Name: First-Year Orientation in History
Introduction:
_x000D_
This tutorial course is offered to freshmen in the Department of History in the first semester after they enroll. It provides a comprehensive introduction to the subject and major, academic consultation, guidance, and planning, and guides the freshmen to integrate into a good living and learning environment as soon as possible, familiarize them with the characteristics of various professional fields in the history discipline as early as possible, master exploratory learning methods, clarify their aspirations, and lay a solid foundation for subsequent university study and major selection.

Name: Selected Readings in Foreign-Language Historical Sources (Part 1)
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to help students further master the ability to read and understand historical materials and historical research works in English or other foreign languages, including the ability to translate foreign languages ​​into accurate Chinese. The teacher will give a detailed introduction to the historical background and doctrinal history of the selected specific documents, and guide students to conduct in-depth discussions on the historical issues touched upon by the relevant documents. This course is divided into two semesters, the upper and lower semesters. Generally, documents and works on ancient world history and modern world history will be read respectively.

Name: General Burmese (I)
Introduction: This course mainly teaches language knowledge about the pronunciation, basic vocabulary and grammar of Burmese. Teaching is mainly in the form of classroom explanations and exercises. After completing a cycle of study, students are required to master the pronunciation essentials of Vietnamese, master certain vocabulary and basic grammatical rules, conduct simple daily conversations in Burmese, and access relevant historical, political and other information in Burmese, laying the foundation for further learning.

Name: Social and Historical Survey
Introduction:
This course is a supporting course for "Social Survey and Historical Research". Students who choose the course form a group in the "Social Survey and Historical Research" class to formulate a research plan, and then conduct fieldwork according to the research plan. _x000D_
The investigation content includes: collection of local archives and documents, visits to relevant government departments, social groups, government agencies, enterprises and villages, oral interviews and questionnaires, on-site observation and experience, etc., and generally lasts 2-3 weeks. _x000D_
After the field survey is completed, a social survey report needs to be written in groups based on the survey data, modified based on the teacher's opinions, and then submitted to a formal survey report. _x000D_
