Name: Selected Readings in Foreign-Language Historical Sources (Part 2)
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to help students further master the ability to read and understand historical materials and historical research works in English or other foreign languages, including the ability to translate foreign languages ​​into accurate Chinese. The teacher will give a detailed introduction to the historical background and doctrinal history of the selected specific documents, and guide students to conduct in-depth discussions on the historical issues touched upon by the relevant documents. This course is divided into two semesters, the upper and lower semesters. Generally, documents and works on ancient world history and modern world history will be read respectively.

Name: Introduction to Philosophy
Introduction: The Greek meaning of "philosophy" is "love of wisdom". For more than a thousand years in ancient times, the Middle Ages and modern times in the West, philosophy has been regarded as the source and foundation of all scientific knowledge. To this day, philosophy still plays a central role in university humanities education. This course mainly explains Western classic philosophical texts such as Plato's dialogues ("Phaedo" and "The Apology of Socrates") and Descartes' "Meditations on First Philosophy" to enable students to understand the way philosophers explore world order and the inherent tension of philosophical life.

Name: Modern World History Exercises
Introduction: This course is a deepening and practice course for the basic course of modern and contemporary world history. It is neither a study course that teaches basic knowledge nor a research course that explores and solves new problems. Rather, it is a research preparation course that introduces important research results, demonstrates innovative research methods, and strengthens students' awareness of original innovation. The basic purpose of setting up the course is to prepare students to start independent research and write academic papers. The course covers important historical topics such as the rise of modern Europe, the British Revolution, the Enlightenment, American Independence, the French Revolution, the Industrial Revolution, scientific socialism, World War I, the October Revolution, fascism, the Cold War, European integration, national liberation movements and the development of developing countries. The course teaching adopts a lively and lively practice class method. First, the teacher designates reading materials such as monographs and papers, and then the students read, understand, and take reading notes, and then report them in the form of a class report. Finally, there is an interactive discussion between the teacher, the speaker, and other students participating in the class.

Name: Selected Readings in Foreign-Language Historical Classics (Part 1)
Introduction: A compulsory course for undergraduate majors in the Department of History, bilingual teaching in Chinese and English. This course aims to deepen students' understanding of European history. Focusing on Greek democracy, the rise of the Roman Republic, the rise and fall of empires, the impact of the Germanic peoples' invasion of Europe, the nature of feudalism, Pope Gregory's church reforms (the dispute between church and state), the Renaissance in the twelfth century, the nature of the Reformation, Luther and the rise of the early modern state, the popular literature of historian Robert Scribney The course includes cutting-edge topics such as cultural studies, the German Peasant War and the origin of modern European politics, and the Republic of the People. The course selects reading materials from three aspects: historical overview, original historical materials, and academic debates. While introducing the views and methods of foreign historians (including famous modern historians), it introduces learners to the sacred hall of historical research.

Name: Topics in German History
Introduction: This course covers the formation of the German nation, the religious reform, the Prussian bureaucracy, the problems of the German Confederation, the German Enlightenment, German liberalism, the model of the road to German national unification, Bismarck and the Bismarck Empire, the structural crisis of the Wilhelm Empire and the rise of German nationalism, etc.

Name: History of Modern International Politics
Introduction: The "Modern International Political History" course is about the basic content of the development of world political history in the modern historical period. First, we define "modern history" and believe that it is a series of political and social changes that occurred in the world with the rise of the second industrial revolution. We then discuss the rise of "new freedom", the "Russification" of Marxism (the Russian October Revolution), the rise of the fascist movement, the impact of World War II, the construction of the "welfare state", the nature of the Cold War, the end of the welfare state and the rise of neoliberalism, the end of the Cold War and "globalization", the "clash of civilizations" and the rise of new right populism, etc.; we believe that, The "modern history" mainly in the 20th century is a political history full of the mutual game between "freedom" and "rationality", and a society that has undergone tremendous changes through the development of modern economy. It has experienced the ups and downs from freedom to rationalism, and then from rationalism to "neoliberalism" (reliberalism or second liberalism). It is a history of "modern" people striving towards their ideals and reality.

Name: The European Enlightenment
Introduction: The European Enlightenment Movement in the 18th century was one of the important roots of modern civilization and a central issue in Western philosophy and social science thinking for two hundred years. This lesson briefly introduces its process, analyzes its gains and losses, explores its significance, and discusses its problems.

Name: Topics in Japanese History
Introduction: The basic purpose of the optional course "Special Topics in Japanese History", which is mainly for undergraduates in the Department of History, is to enable students to comprehensively and systematically grasp the development and evolution of Japanese history, while exploring its particularities and clarifying its universality. On the basis of familiarity with the basic knowledge of Japanese history, students will enhance their ability to study the basic skills, theories and methods required for historical research.

Name: History of Western Political Thought
Introduction:
_x000D_
History of Western Political Thought_x000D_
Political thought is the product of human thinking about the dilemmas and problems of collective life. "History of Western Political Thought" mainly explains the changes in Western political thought from ancient Greece to ancient Rome to the Middle Ages and the post-modern period (20th century). It discusses the different political concepts and theories formed in different political life forms and historical backgrounds in different periods. It focuses on introducing representative figures, works, opinions and theoretical contributions in each period, and strives to show the development of Western political concepts and the historical panorama of political civilization. Studying the "History of Western Political Thought" is an important way to understand the development of Western politics. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Foreign-Language Historical Classics (Part 2)
Prerequisite: Selected Readings in Foreign-Language Historical Classics (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is designed to help undergraduate history majors read and accurately understand English historical works. The selected textbooks are excerpts from historical masterpieces written by world-famous historians. The content covers topics related to modern and contemporary world history, historical philosophy, historical methods, etc. Students should make in-depth reading preparations for the textbooks before class. The basic task in class is to explain the text sentence by sentence, requiring accurate understanding, and to learn relevant historical knowledge in the textbooks. The basic feature of this course is the organic combination of professional foreign language improvement and historical knowledge accumulation. Students have the most active space to express themselves in the classroom and have ample opportunities to interact directly with teachers. Through learning, they will realize what a real English history professional course should be like, master the basic methods of reading English historical works, and learn a large amount of professional historical knowledge that is not accessible in general history courses.

Name: Earth Hazards
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Earth Disasters focuses on introducing various natural disasters that occur on the earth. The purpose of this course is to introduce the physical processes that cause natural phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanoes, storms, floods, landslides, ozone holes, and global warming. To lay the foundation for students to understand earth science and cultivate their interest in earth science. The main contents include the origin of the universe, the internal processes and disasters of the earth, and the external processes and disasters of the earth.

Name: Geophysical Signal Processing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course systematically introduces geophysical signal processing theories and methods, focusing on the basic concepts and principles of digital signal processing theory, laying a solid mathematical theoretical foundation for the analysis and processing of geophysical signals. Based on the characteristics of geophysical signals, relevant specialized geophysical signal processing theories and methods are further taught.

Name: Terrestrial Gravimetry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General physics, advanced mathematics, mathematical physics
Introduction: Gravity is a branch of geophysics. The main task of this course is to study the science of the earth's shape, external gravity field, internal structure of the earth, plate movement and deformation. Through the study of this course, students are required to master the basic knowledge of the earth's gravity field, the measurement and compilation of gravity data, the analysis and interpretation of gravity data, the research methods of gravity and the shape of the earth, the research methods of gravity and the earth's structure, the earth's gravity model and calculation methods, and lay a solid foundation for further research on the earth's gravity field and related earth science issues.

Name: Fundamentals of Earth Medium Mechanics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, mathematical physics, theoretical mechanics
Introduction: This course is a compulsory professional basic course for undergraduates majoring in solid geophysics. Its content is the basis for other courses in this major (such as seismology, geodynamics, etc.). It is also the basis for further study of plastic mechanics, fracture mechanics, viscoelastic mechanics, nonlinear mechanics and other mechanical courses. Through teaching this course, students can master the basic concepts, basic equations and basic principles of earth medium mechanics, laying a foundation for subsequent courses; students can master the basic problem-solving ideas and methods of earth medium mechanics, and understand their application in earth science.

Name: Geomagnetism and Geoelectricity
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, general physics, mathematical physics, electromagnetics
Introduction: This course will focus on teaching the basic principles, research methods and classic research results of geomagnetism and geoelectricity. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students will have an overall and clear image of geomagnetism and geoelectricity, which will lay a good foundation for further in-depth study and engagement in geophysics or other earth science research.

Name: Numerical Computation Methods in Geophysics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course requires pre-learning: mathematical physics equations, algorithmic language base
Introduction: The use of numerical methods to solve partial differential equations in geophysics is an important part of various geophysical forward and inversion problems. With the rapid development of computer hardware and software, its applications are becoming more and more widespread. The purpose of this course is to introduce numerical methods for solving partial differential equations in geophysics, laying the foundation for further study or scientific research in geophysics and related fields. The main contents include: introduction to partial differential equations in geophysics, finite difference method, spectral method, Fourier quasi-spectral method, Chebyshev quasi-spectral method, and numerical calculation of seismic wave fields in complex earth media. The characteristic is that the introduction of theories and methods is closely combined with program calculations, and the theory and methods are understood through calculation examples and result analysis. Enable students to learn several of the most common methods and initially master the calculation process through numerical experiments.

Name: Seismology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics (1,2, 3); general physics; mathematical equations
Introduction: Seismology is an important part of geophysics. The purpose of this course is to introduce the theoretical basis of modern seismology and lay the foundation for further study or scientific research in geophysics and related fields. The main contents include: basic elastic mechanics and seismic waves, body waves and ray theory, surface waves and free oscillations, determination of the earth's internal structure, and earthquake sources. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Geophysics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Solid geophysics is an important discipline in Earth science, and its purpose is to observe and study the Earth and its physics fields using physics methods. This course is aimed at students in the lower grades of the university and presents the principles and features of the basic geophysical field on a case-by-case basis. Since solid geophysics is an observation-based science, the course included exercises to study the Earth ' s internal structure and seismic parameters using observation data. Teaching provides students with a comprehensive understanding of the physical fields of geophysics and fosters interest in the geophysical profession.

Name: Rock Mechanics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, mathematical methods, general physics, elasticity
Introduction: Rock mechanics is a professional basic course for many engineering disciplines such as mining engineering, geological engineering, petroleum engineering, hydraulic engineering, railway engineering, highway engineering, geotechnical engineering, underground engineering, etc. This course emphasizes the combination of theory and practice, highlighting the teaching and guidance of basic rock mechanics theory, basic knowledge and basic skills, including the composition and mechanical properties of rocks and rock masses, rock constitutive relations and strength theory, in-situ stress and its measurement technology, and rock mechanics test technology. It also provides examples of the application of rock mechanics theories and methods in rock engineering design, construction and maintenance, and earthquake prediction, cultivating students' ability to analyze and solve rock mechanics and engineering problems.

Name: General Petrology (I)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Before choosing crystallography and optical minerals, students should choose crystallography and minerals.
Introduction: "Crystal Optics" mainly studies the basic principles and methods of identifying minerals under polarizing microscopes. "Photomineralogy" is the study of the characteristics of the crystal structure and chemical composition of rock-forming minerals based on various optical phenomena produced when visible light passes through transparent crystals. Crystal optics and optical mineralogy are not only important foundations of petrology, but are also widely used in ceramics, castings, building materials, etc. Magmatic petrology is about the classification and classification principles of magmatic rocks, the basic characteristics of various rock types (including ultrabasic rocks, basic rocks, neutral rocks, and acidic rocks), rock types, mineral combinations, structural structures, and chemical composition characteristics, as well as the petrogenesis theory of each rock type and the geotectonic environment in which it was formed. The course also introduces basic experimental petrology theory and its explanation of the origin of rocks; the relationship between magmatism and plate tectonics and mantle plume structure, the process of crust-mantle interaction, and the significance of magmatism in the formation of continental crust.

Name: Historical Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Courses in general geology, mineralology, sedimentary rockology, paleontology and tectonic geology
Introduction: Geohistory is a comprehensive historical subject that requires students to learn and master the basic principles and methods of applied petrology, paleobiostratigraphy, sedimentology, and historical tectonics for comprehensive analysis through study, and to be able to use this knowledge to solve practical problems and comprehensively understand the history of the development of the earth.

Name: Structural Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General geology, rockology, solid mechanics base
Introduction: Structural geology is one of the important basic courses for earth science majors. It mainly introduces the deformation mechanism, behavior and process of rocks in the lithosphere under the action of geological stress, as well as the various geological structural phenomena formed. Based on the theory of rock deformation mechanics and deformation mechanisms, the course focuses on important structural types such as foliation, lineation, folds, fissures, joints, faults, extensional structures, thrust-nappe structures, strike-slip faults, and ductile shear zones. Based on the ideas of geometry-kinematics-formation mechanism-evolution process, the course will introduce the geometric forms and combination methods of the above-mentioned structural types, discuss their kinematic methods and kinematic discrimination, explain the physical conditions and deformation mechanism of their formation, and explore the mechanical action mode, geological environment and dynamic process of their formation. At the same time, the course will also introduce some basic methods and basic skills in structural geology research, such as geological cartography, geometric projection, quantitative and qualitative analysis of stress and strain, case geological analysis, etc. The characteristic of this course lies in the organic combination of geometry-kinematics-genetic mechanism, and focuses on the combination of foundation and frontier.

Name: Regional Geology Field Practicum
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Basic courses in mineralology, rockology, tectonic geology, palaeontology, geohistorics, geomorphology and fourth-class geology; first general geological internship.
Introduction: Geology is not only a self-contained theoretical discipline, but also a highly practical discipline. Regional geological survey practice is a core link in undergraduate teaching. Through teaching activities that combine theory and practice, students can initially master the basic knowledge, basic methods and basic skills necessary for systematic field geological surveys. At the same time, they can also understand and train new ideas, new theories, new methods and new technologies in the development of modern earth science and technology to a certain extent. Mainly include: (1) Professional skills: The focus of field practical teaching is to cultivate students' observation and reading ability, practical ability, theory-to-practice ability, geological thinking ability, ability to use geological survey equipment, and strengthen training of their language-text-graphic expression ability; (2) Professional thinking: to cultivate students' pioneering, innovative and scientific abilities. Research awareness, deepen the understanding of basic geological theories learned, and lay a solid foundation for subsequent course teaching, senior professional internships and graduation thesis internships; (3) Professional quality: Field teaching internships should reflect the tradition and characteristics of the school, cultivate students' diligent and rigorous, realistic and innovative spirit, unity and cooperation, and improve students' overall quality.

Name: Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: This course requires basic knowledge of geosciences, inorganic chemistry, mineralology and rock science.
Introduction: Geochemistry is a science that uses chemical science as a theoretical basis to study the chemical composition, chemical reactions and chemical evolution of the earth. It takes elements, isotopes, their chemical reactions and chemical evolution as the research objects. It is one of the basic courses in geoscience majors. The purpose of the course is based on the geochemical properties of elements and isotopes, organically combining the geochemical behavior of elements with geological processes, focusing on exploring the distribution, migration, evolution and other laws of elements and isotopes in celestial bodies, the earth and geological bodies, as well as the physical and chemical environment when they were formed, and applying modern science and technology and basic theories to analyze the importance of geochemical processes in earth evolution, mineral resources, human living environment and other aspects. Through teaching, students can master the basic concepts, basic principles and experimental techniques of geochemistry, and understand the research status and development trends of geochemistry. Through chemical analysis experiments, students learn the basic principles and methods of analyzing the content of trace elements in geological samples, and master the basic skills for engaging in geochemical experiments.

Name: Geochemistry Small-Group Discussion
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Discussion course for the geochemistry course, with initial courses: Earth science generals, mineral science, rock science
Introduction: "Geochemistry Small Class Class" uses a combination of classroom teaching, discussion and practice to teach, with the purpose of expanding students' knowledge, stimulating students' thirst for knowledge, and cultivating innovative geochemistry talents. Geochemistry is a science that uses chemical science as a theoretical basis to study the chemical composition, chemical reactions and chemical evolution of the earth. It takes elements, isotopes, their chemical reactions and chemical evolution as the research objects. It is one of the basic courses in geoscience majors. The purpose of the course is based on the geochemical properties of elements and isotopes, organically combining the geochemical behavior of elements with geological processes, focusing on exploring the distribution, migration, evolution and other laws of elements and isotopes in celestial bodies, the earth and geological bodies, as well as the physical and chemical environment when they were formed, and applying modern science and technology and basic theories to analyze the importance of geochemical processes in earth evolution, mineral resources, human living environment and other aspects. Through teaching, students can master the basic concepts, basic principles and experimental techniques of geochemistry, and understand the research status and development trends of geochemistry. Through chemical analysis experiments, students learn the basic principles and methods of analyzing the content of trace elements in geological samples, and master the basic skills for engaging in geochemical experiments.

Name: Ore Deposit Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Learners are required to have the base of General Geology, preferably in geology, tectonic geology, mineralology, rock science, geochemistry, etc.
Introduction: The most important purpose of studying solid earth science is to master the scientific theories and technical methods to solve the increasingly severe mineral resource problems, and this ultimate purpose is concentrated in "Mineral Deposit Science". "Mineral Deposit Science" is an important branch of solid earth science. It is an applied basic science and is equivalent to the "user terminal" of earth science. It comprehensively and systematically introduces the types and characteristics of mineral resources, mineral formation methods, formation conditions, time and space distribution rules, and provides strategic guidance and technical methods for the scientific search, development and utilization of mineral resources. Therefore, "Mineral Deposit Science" has both a certain degree of professionalism and a strong comprehensiveness; it has both extensive practicality and theoretical relevance. Course teaching is required to closely combine modern scientific theories with actual materials, mineralization, mineral deposit types, and typical examples, so that learners can understand and verify mineralization theories, master basic knowledge of mineral deposits, and improve their ability to analyze and solve practical problems. In the course system, the types of mineralization geological processes are used as the main line, and the mineral resources formed by the internal processes of the earth and the mineral resources formed by the external processes of the earth are introduced sequentially. Finally, the distribution of important mineral resources at home and abroad and their causes are introduced. The goal of the course is to cultivate relevant professional research and decision-making talents for scientific research institutes, national functional departments or mining companies.

Name: Integrated Geological Field Practicum in the Three Gorges Region
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General Geology, Crystal Minerals, Rocks, Palaeontology, Earth History, etc.
Introduction: This course is based on the previous comprehensive geological internship (Three Gorges Internship) and is a field practical course for geology majors to learn sedimentology, stratigraphy and paleontology. The purpose of offering this course includes: 1) Through field observation of geological sections, students can better master the basic knowledge of geology by integrating theory with practice; 2) Through field inspections of several sections, students can understand the main types of sedimentary rocks, sedimentary structures and structures, as well as the main types of biological fossils, analyze and Determine the types of sedimentary facies and the stratigraphic development sequence and changes shown in stratigraphic sections, and understand and understand the geological development and evolution history of the Yangtze Massif in South China; 3) Through the practice of this course, students can learn and understand the basic field work methods of sedimentology, stratigraphy and paleontology research, and exercise and cultivate students' skills in field geological work.

Name: Integrated Geological Field Practicum in the Wutai Mountains
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Earth science general, ordinary rock science, geochemistry, tectonic geology Learn.
Introduction: Wutaishan Comprehensive Field Geology Internship is based on field geological cognitive practice and related professional classroom learning, and is set up to train students' comprehensive ability in field geological investigation and ability to conduct rock and structural research in metamorphic rock areas. Work in the Wutai Mountain-Hengshan area for 1.5 weeks from the end of June to the beginning of July every year. The internship inspected 8 routes and 30 observation points.

Name: Compact Data Structures and Big Data
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course teaches compact data structures and corresponding algorithms, probabilistic methods, and statistical tools for processing big data, especially web big data. Perhaps the largest big data at present is the data flow on the Internet. The analysis of this big data can provide a theoretical basis for improving network performance, user experience of network applications and network security. However, network big data cannot be retained. Against this background, this course teaches a series of compact data structures that have been gradually developed over the past 30 years and their theoretical analysis. These data structures can be used to reduce big data into smaller sizes for easier storage and application. The data structures and algorithms in this course can be divided into two categories: (1) Counting and modeling, including probabilistic counting, bitmap algorithms, FM sketch, hyperloglog sketch, virtual bitmap, virutal FM sketch, virtual hyperloglog, countMin, counter braids, randomized counter sharing, and virtual counters; (2) Member search and classification, including Bloom filters, counting Bloom filters, Bloomier filters, blocked Bloom filters, multi-set filters, and multi-hashing tables. Students will not only master these data structures and algorithms, but also learn their applications in network data measurement, security, and other fields. Not only will you master relevant theoretical knowledge, but you will also have to implement some algorithms and apply them on actual network data.

Name: Evolutionary History of Vertebrates
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course is a bilingual course taught in Chinese and English. The purpose is to enable students to understand the origin of vertebrate animals directly related to humans and the evolutionary history of each major category. The course teaching content will take into account the needs of ordinary students and professional students, focusing on ordinary undergraduates. Therefore, this course does not include the description and classification of the main categories of vertebrates, but rather traces the evolutionary process and important turning events in its 500 million-year history, as well as the relationship of these events in the evolution of the overall vertebrate system.

Name: Paleoceanography and Global Change
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course is an introductory course for paleoceanography and paleoclimatology. It briefly introduces the basic principles of the earth's climate system, the basic principles, methods and latest progress of paleoceanographic research, as well as related environmental and oceanic climate changes in earth history, and prediction of future climate changes. By studying this course, students can understand the basic concepts of paleoceanography and paleoclimatology and the application of proxy indicators, as well as the status and hot spots of research in this field at home and abroad.

Name: Fundamentals of Isotope Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: International Distinguished Scholars Forum in Earth Science (I)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Earth science overview; Earth system evolution; general geology
Introduction: The course consists of a series of short courses with internationally renowned scholars and the content of the course is based on the international experts invited during the semester

Name: Marine Environment and Dynamics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Marine environmental evolution and dynamics are important components of Earth system science research. This course is designed for third-year undergraduate students who are interested in geodynamics and system evolution. This course will provide an in-depth demonstration of geodynamics and how magnetic records of oceanic materials can be used to study the structure and dynamics of the surface Earth. Then we will introduce ocean magnetic anomalies and their origins, forward and inverse simulations of magnetic anomalies, and issues such as the structure and dynamics of mid-ocean ridges and ocean hot zones. The second part of the course focuses on marine sediments and marine environmental change processes. This part will first introduce the physical and chemical properties of marine sediments, and then explore various complex physical, chemical, and biological processes in the marine sedimentary environment. This is followed by an introduction to marine sediment magnetostratigraphy and environmental magnetism, and how these properties can be used to reconstruct environmental and climate change issues. The teaching method combines classroom lectures, discussions, laboratory practice and analysis. Through course study, students can gain an in-depth understanding of scientific frontiers such as ocean dynamics and environmental evolution, and broaden their horizons.

Name: Frontiers of Artificial Intelligence and Industry Trends
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Humanity has rapidly entered the era of artificial intelligence. McKinsey reported that in the next 20 years, 50% of human jobs will be replaced by artificial intelligence. The White House also recently released a report stating that artificial intelligence is a transformative force in this era. Recently, Professor Stephen Hawking said in a speech on October 16, 2016 at the establishment of the Institute of Artificial Intelligence at the University of Cambridge in the United Kingdom: The emergence of artificial intelligence will be the most important event in human history. _x000D_
_x000D_
Currently, all top high-tech companies, such as Google, Facebook, Baidu, Alibaba, etc., are investing a lot of human physics in artificial intelligence research and development. Take Google as an example. After several years of research and development on Google Brain, starting this year, the company has required all project teams to use artificial intelligence technology. Moreover, Google has begun to claim that it is not an Internet company, but an artificial intelligence company. _x000D_
_x000D_
In this huge torrent of artificial intelligence, the most scarce thing is compound talents who understand both artificial intelligence and industrial development. The introduction of this course hopes to strengthen the industrial knowledge shortcomings of outstanding science and engineering students in our school by inviting outstanding experts in the artificial intelligence industry from around the world to systematically describe the current cutting-edge technology of artificial intelligence, as well as the latest developments, challenges and future trends in the industrial field. It allows students to understand how the knowledge they have learned can be combined with the needs and development of the industry, thereby promoting students' interest in in-depth study and research of artificial intelligence, and cultivating students' ideas for using top technologies to solve practical problems. _x000D_

This course will cover the core technology development of artificial intelligence and its real development and application in various industries, including deep learning platform industry, deep learning hardware industry, image recognition industry, speech recognition industry, intelligent dialogue, driverless driving, intelligent medical care, intelligent finance, home robots, industrial robots, intelligent recommendations, intelligent security and other fields, and then outline the profound impact of artificial intelligence on future industries. Give students an industry overview of the development of artificial intelligence and understand the current status, challenges and future of artificial intelligence in various industries. _x000D_

These teams will be assigned industry mentors to provide guidance and deepen their understanding of the relationship between artificial intelligence and industry through projects. _x000D_

Name: Compiler Practicum (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Principles for compilation. Target audience: undergraduate students

Name: ACM/ICPC Competition Training

Peking University's ACM International Collegiate Programming Competition (ACM/ICPC) is in a leading position in the country. Peking University's Online Judge --- POJ is the most influential ACM/ICPC competition training platform in China, and it also has a high reputation and a large number of users internationally. _x000D_
The Peking University ACM/ICPC competition team is an elite gathering, and most of the team members have achieved excellent results in the National Informatics Olympiad for Middle School Students or won gold medals in the ACM/ICPC Asian Qualifiers. Through years of accumulation, the Peking University ACM/ICPC competition team has formed an effective systematic training method. _x000D_
This course is designed for students preparing to participate in ACM/ICPC, and it will definitely be of great help in improving the competition results of participating schools.

Name: Introduction to Frontier Computing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: This course is an introductory one and is intended for students who are able to study, with no special pre-course requirements.
Introduction:
Computers are the inventions that have had the greatest impact on mankind so far. The basic ideas of classical computers were determined more than 70 years ago. They mainly include: Turing's general computer conceptual model to prove "uncomputable numbers" in 1936, Shannon's switching circuit theory in 1938, and the von Neumann architecture in 1945 that separated software and hardware. Computers entered the stage of history as a general-purpose machine. After that, the development of computers mainly benefited from the technological progress of transistors and integrated circuits (Moore's Law), as well as the development of software engineering, the Internet and various computer applications, but the basic ideas and basic principles behind it have not changed. _x000D_
_x000D_
The future of computer science requires fundamental and disruptive innovations in ideas, theories and methods. Since the new century, neurocomputing (neuromorphic computing/computational neuroscience) based on neuroscience has shown strong vitality, and neural computers constructed with neural devices are expected to become real "computers"; artificial intelligence is reviving, deep learning, reinforcement learning, machine perception, etc. are developing rapidly, and the new generation of artificial intelligence will profoundly change human social life and change the world; theoretical computer science is expected to break through, and quantum computing, biological computing, etc. will move from concept to practice, and it is possible to redefine the concept and limits of computing. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course focuses on the cutting edge of computer science and lays the foundation for students to achieve disruptive theoretical and technological innovations.

Introduction:
Discrete Mathematics I is a required degree course. The main contents of this course include: set theory, basic logic, automata, graph theory combination, counting, and discrete probability. _x000D_
Discrete mathematics is a basic core course for computer science and technology majors. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students can master the basic principles of discrete mathematics, cultivate their ability of abstract thinking and careful generalization, and master the necessary description tools, mathematical methods and logical expressions for dealing with discrete structures. To enable students to develop good professional theoretical qualities and the ability to use learned knowledge to analyze and solve practical problems. This will lay a good foundation for students to study basic computer theory and professional courses in the future. _x000D_

Name: Algorithm Design and Analysis (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: First courses: computational overview, program design exercises, data structure and algorithms, mathematical analysis (or advanced mathematics), advanced algebra (or linear algebra)
Introduction: Starting from algorithm design, this course systematically introduces the general methods and common patterns of algorithm design. Focusing on issues such as the correctness of the algorithm, the complexity of the algorithm, and the complexity of the problem, it also introduces the basic methods of algorithm proof, the mathematical foundation and common techniques of algorithm analysis, and the basic theory of problem complexity analysis. The main contents include: algorithm analysis basics such as algorithm proof, asymptotic analysis and recursive solution; common algorithm design methods such as recursion, divide and conquer, greedy, dynamic programming and backtracking; computational complexity theories such as NP-completeness and polynomial reduction; advanced algorithm design methods and related analysis methods such as approximate algorithms, random algorithms, local search, parallel algorithms and online algorithms.

Introduction: This course is compulsory in the second year of the second year of the undergraduate studies in computer science. Name: Visual Computing and Deep Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Mathematics courses such as advanced mathematics, linear algebras, numerical optimization, and one of the common programming languages of C++ and Python.
Introduction:
The main teaching content of this course is basic knowledge in the field of computer vision, such as image classification, target detection, image segmentation, moving object tracking, etc. In many computer vision tasks, the current best algorithms are often based on deep neural network technology. This course will also introduce the basic knowledge of deep learning, its combination with computer vision, and the practice of deep learning. _x000D_

Students should have taken prerequisite courses such as advanced mathematics and linear algebra before taking this course. The goal of the course is to enable students to have the preliminary ability to solve application problems such as image classification and target detection on the basic theories and important issues of computer vision and deep learning after studying this course. _x000D_

Name: Mathematics in Information Science

Name: Computational Game Theory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Data Structures and Algorithms, Discrete Mathematics, Python language fluency
Introduction: This course explores the richness of computational game theory, which harnesses the power of computers to solve abstract strategic games. The course integrates the ideas of artificial intelligence, theoretical knowledge in combinatorics, human-computer interface design, parallel and distributed computing, software engineering, etc. Students will learn the mathematical foundations of abstract strategy games and the basic theory of combinatorial games, combined with special cases of combinatorial mathematical games including hyperreal numbers. They will learn how to calculate the upper limit of the size of a game tree, write programs to implement a simple recursive solver for loop-free games, and solve the game retrogradely, and then extend their inverse solver for use in a distributed environment through the "Apache Spark" API. As the final project of the course, students will work in teams to select and program an abstract strategy game, solve the game, program a graphical interface to ensure flawless operation of the system and perform performance analysis work.

Name: Operating Systems A (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: General calculations, data structure and algorithms, micromechanical principles
Introduction:
Any computer must be loaded with the corresponding operating system before it can form a functioning computer system. The performance of the operating system determines the performance of the overall system; the safety and reliability of the operating system itself determines the security and reliability of the entire system. The operating system is the core and basic operating platform of software technology. Therefore, students in related majors must learn and master the basic principles and professional knowledge of operating systems. The purpose of this course is as follows:_x000D_
1. Introduce the basic concepts, basic structure and operating environment of operating systems. _x000D_
2． Introduce operating system principles, design methods and implementation technologies. _x000D_
3. Introduce the evolution process, development research trends, new technologies and new ideas of operating systems. _x000D_
4. Introduce various representative and typical operating system examples (for example: Windows, Solaris, Linux). _x000D_
5. Cultivate students' basic abilities to analyze and solve problems, and cultivate creative talents. _x000D_
_x000D_
The operating system course is a professional basic course for computer science and technology majors. This course not only has a rigorous classical theoretical system and is closely integrated with practice, but also has the characteristics of rapid development of relevant design principles and technologies, and strong depth and breadth of course knowledge points. In the arrangement of the course content, emphasis is placed on the combination of classic operating system theory and contemporary advanced technology, aiming at students' professional foundation characteristics. While teaching the basic principles of operating systems, it focuses on guiding students to explore the currently widely used example operating systems Windows and Linux; by completing Windows kernel programming and Linux kernel programming projects, students can deepen their understanding of operating system principles and basic concepts in practice, and at the same time exercise students' system programming abilities and skills. _x000D_

Name: The Conscious Turing Machine: Cognitive and Computational Science
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Thanks to major advances in cognitive neuroscience, science is beginning to move toward understanding how the brain achieves consciousness. In 1988, cognitive neuroscientist Bernard Baars proposed the global workspace model (GWM) of the brain and outlined its implications for understanding consciousness. In 1990, Seiji Ogawa and others at Bell Labs invented fMRI, allowing neuroscientists to witness the brain working in real time. Thus, the pursuit of consciousness, once only of interest to philosophers and theologians, now began to be pursued and explored by scientists of all disciplines. _x000D_
_x000D_
This short course will consider the question of consciousness from a theoretical computer science perspective. We will give a precise formal definition of a Conscious Turing Machine (CTM), also known as Artificial Intelligent (AI), and explore the properties of this form.

Name: Machine Learning in Computer Vision
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Machine learning methods have been used in computer vision for a long time, but since the introduction of deep networks in 2012, the nature of machine learning and its impact on the field have changed dramatically. This course takes image recognition, human detection, human body modeling, and optical flow estimation as examples to compare machine learning technology before 2012 and after 2012. First, the course introduces basic methods of image processing, including optical flow analysis; secondly, regarding methods before 2012, the course introduces decision trees, random forests, and deformable part models, and reviews how these techniques are used for human detection and tracking; then, the course discusses some details of deep convolutional neural networks, including convolutional pose machines and openpose human tracking systems; finally, the course reviews deep learning methods for supervised and unsupervised optical flow estimation.

Name: Computer Networks
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
(1) "Computer Organization and Architecture" and "Operating Systems" or "Introduction to Computer Systems": Computer network is a comprehensive subject that includes computer system software and hardware, involving knowledge in the field of data communications. The core level includes the design and implementation of various distributed algorithms, and the application of various types of computer networks. To learn and master the basic principles of computer networks, you must understand the basic components of a computer system and the core software functions of the operating system. Lay the necessary professional foundation for learning computer network architecture and working principles. _x000D_
(2) "Introduction to Computing" or "Programming": This course includes a 2-credit internship. The internship requires students to apply the theoretical knowledge of computer networks they have learned to solve a practical problem. Therefore, you must master at least a high-level language and basic programming skills to be able to extend a program running on a single machine into a distributed system running on a computer network.
Introduction:
Computer network and communication technology is one of the fastest growing subject areas in recent years, with new technologies emerging and new products changing with each passing day. In order to enable students to have certain judgment and control capabilities in the complicated world of network technology, this course will focus on the essence of network science and technology (such as connection establishment and management, error control, flow control, congestion control, routing and quality of service mechanisms, etc.), teach network concepts and technical principles, and select typical network protocols and network products as cases for analysis, so that learners not only acquire necessary network knowledge, but also have strong analysis and solution capabilities for problems encountered in the network. _x000D_
    Based on the description of the computer network architecture and the popular Internet protocol set, this course focuses on the error control, flow control and media access technology of the data link layer, the routing technology and congestion control of the network layer, the connection management and network programming interface of the transport layer, as well as the transmission technology and service quality mechanism for real-time streaming media applications. Finally, it introduces the basic methods of computer network security assurance from the perspectives of information security and network security. Through the study of this course, students will not only understand the overall picture of computer networks, but also master basic network principles and network application development technologies, laying a good foundation for further in-depth study of related network courses and the development of network-based distributed applications.

Name: Principles of Compilers
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Introduction to computer systems, data structure
Introduction: This course describes the design and implementation methods of compilers. Its core is a series of ideas and technologies used to translate high-level language programs into various machine languages, including lexical analysis, syntax analysis, syntax-guided translation, intermediate code generation, code optimization, etc. In addition to being used to construct compilers, these ideas and techniques are widely used in many other computer fields. This course consists of two parts: theoretical lectures and hands-on practice. The purpose is to help students understand and master the theories taught in class through hands-on construction of compilers.

College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Course Introduction:_x000D_

The focus is on the data management architecture, which is usually built on a distributed parallel computing platform (such as MapReduce and SPARK), runs a parallel distributed data management platform, uses a main memory system (including OLTP-oriented row storage and analysis-oriented column storage), including multi-modal systems that process multi-source heterogeneous data. This course will cover the basics of these big data systems. _x000D_

College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: linear algebra, program design, mathematical logic, probability statistics

At the same time, presentations on topical topics such as translation of statistical machines, extraction of big information, etc., are expected to provide students with more cutting-edge research progress. The empirical approach involved in this course is mainly data-driven, text-oriented, model recognition and machine learning; it is hoped that, through the learning and exercise of the course, students will be able to choose appropriate algorithms and optimize methods, stand-alone programming, and easily respond to larger text data when they encounter practical problems. We hope that students who continue their studies and are about to enter the workforce will benefit from this exercise.

Name: General Russian (I)

Its teaching feature is the use of "invisible grammar", that is, big vocabulary and small grammar. It focuses more on the application of language rather than teaching grammatical rules. Name: The Making of Modern China: Institutions, Currents of Thought and Figures
Introduction:
Course purpose:_x000D_
The establishment of modern China's nation-state is not only due to its own development factors, but also due to the expansion of Western modernization and colonial movements. In this process, institutional changes and cultural transformation influence and promote each other. _x000D_
The establishment process of modern China discussed in this course includes the three stages of the late Qing Dynasty, the Republic of China and the People's Republic of China. It involves the discussion of the country's basic political system, important social trends of thought and key figures, and attempts to give students a new perspective on understanding modern China.

Name: Classics of Ancient Greek and Roman History
Introduction: This course, which mainly leads students to the original books of ancient Greek and Roman historians, analyses the characteristics and internal mechanisms of Western ancient civilization through specific text reading, enabling students to understand and grasp the origins of Western civilization more comprehensively from the political, historical, philosophical, religious and other points of view through the important myths of history.

Name: Software Engineering

"Software Engineering" is an important professional basic course for undergraduates in the School of Information Science and Technology of Peking University.
