Name: Introduction to Intelligent Robotics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Basic programming practices and a mathematical basis. There is no special advance course requirement.
Introduction:
Intelligent robotics technology integrates high and new technologies from multiple disciplines such as computers, cybernetics, information and sensing technology, artificial intelligence, and bionics, and is a core course in the field of intelligent science. Intelligent robot technology is a hot topic in current scientific and technological research, and has received widespread attention in important application fields of intelligent science such as industrial automation, aerospace, military, robotics, monitoring and detection, etc. _x000D_
The main purpose of this course is to teach comprehensive theoretical basic knowledge in the field of intelligent robots, including the basis of intelligent dynamics, robot positioning, environmental perception, planning and navigation, automatic control and other theoretical and technical knowledge. At the same time, experiments and practical teaching activities are carried out based on the Peking University Smart Vehicle Mobile Robot Experiment Platform, so that students can gain a rational and perceptual understanding of mobile robots from multiple levels, and cultivate students' hands-on and ability to combine theory and practice. _x000D_

Name: Computational Foundations of Neural Networks
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Mathematical statistics, Python programming, digital media technology base
Introduction:
Neural network is an interdisciplinary field of computational neuroscience and artificial intelligence. Its ultimate goal is to simulate the mechanism of biological visual perception, calculation and reasoning to achieve or surpass human intelligence. This course takes biological visual information processing systems as the starting point, focusing on teaching the basic theories, methods and technologies of neural network computing, and closely integrating the application of brain-like visual engineering systems to lay a solid foundation for subsequent related research and application development. In terms of content setting, this course starts from two aspects: theory and algorithm, course design and reporting, and is closely connected with related cutting-edge research and application fields. It is a professional basic course with both theoretical and research backgrounds. This course requires a solid foundation in mathematical statistics and programming technology, and it is a course that pays equal attention to theory and practice. _x000D_
This course emphasizes the learning of basic theoretical knowledge, as well as the cultivation of hands-on ability and independent thinking ability. It encourages students to use neural network theory, methods and technologies independently or collaboratively to conduct relevant research. At the same time, it is combined with the current scientific research projects, and strives to make the course consistent with the latest international research and development trends. _x000D_

Name: Physics in Information Science (Part 2)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Physics in Information Sciences (up) or Mechanical Science
Mathematics or Math Analysis.
Introduction: This course is mainly aimed at junior undergraduate students majoring in information science and engineering. It mainly covers the main content of general physics such as electromagnetism, optics, and quantum theory, and is closely combined with examples and applications from information science and technology. Through the study of this course, on the one hand, you will master the content of general physics and understand the importance of physical laws in information science and technology, and at the same time, you will lay a solid foundation for applying the ideas and methods of physics in the research of modern information science in the future.

Name: Physics in Information Science (Part 1)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is mainly aimed at junior undergraduate students majoring in information science and engineering. It covers the main contents of general physics such as mechanics and thermal science, especially closely integrating examples and applications from information science and technology. Through the study of this course, on the one hand, you will master the content of general physics and understand the importance of physical laws in information science and technology, and at the same time, you will lay a solid foundation for applying the ideas and methods of physics in the research of modern information science in the future. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Parallel Programming
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Introduction to computer systems or other system structure courses
Introduction: Limited elective courses for majors. Parallel programming is one of the core technologies of computer science. The tremendous development of new architectures in recent years makes it important for students to acquire skills in this area. This course covers the basic theories, principles, parallel language principles, and programming tools of parallel programming. This course is oriented towards multi-core, many-core including GPU, and cluster parallel architectures.

Name: Python Programming and Introduction to Data Mining
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Computation overview; advanced mathematics (mathematic analysis); higher algebra (linear algebra)
Introduction: Python and related data analysis software platforms are one of the fastest growing directions in the field of computer technology. Based on the introduction of Python language and programming knowledge, the course uses Python software packages such as NumPy and SciPy to conduct special practical learning on basic data analysis tasks in fields such as matrix decomposition, graph analysis, text mining, image processing, signal processing and spectral analysis. It strives to provide students with a deep understanding of the use of Python and related software packages through the practice of specific tasks. The course will also focus on explaining the basic data models and essence behind data analysis in various fields.

Name: Practical Methods in Frontier Scientific Research
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course will be taught by a senior editor of Nature Publishing Group. Through learning, it will help students master high-level scientific paper writing skills and understand the scientific issues concerned by top academic journals such as Nature, thereby laying a solid foundation for cultivating scientific research capabilities.

Name: Cognitive Science
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Cognitive science is an interdisciplinary subject related to the study of mind and intelligence. Its subject content involves philosophy, psychology, neuroscience, linguistics, anthropology, artificial intelligence and other fields. In the mid-1950s, many researchers began to study theories of mind based on complex representations and computational processes, and cognitive science, a new discipline, emerged. _x000D_
The purpose of cognitive science is to use scientific methods to study the information processing process in the structure, function and generation mechanism of intelligent systems. This field has become the foundation and core of information science and technology, machine intelligence, control systems and other fields. For students majoring in information science, technology and artificial intelligence, it can provide basic perspectives and methods for exploring the working mechanism of the human brain and mind, and provide new ideas for comprehensively understanding the principles of biology and machine intelligence, learning various machine learning and intelligence theories, and designing new machine intelligence systems. At the same time, it will also provide the necessary knowledge base to discover future research problems in areas such as artificial intelligence. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Environmental Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course consists of five parts. The first part introduces the basic concepts, basic research methods and related disciplines of environmental science; the second part introduces the main characteristics of the earth's environmental system from the natural and social and humanistic perspectives; the third part is environmental pollution issues, mainly introducing environmental pollution of various environmental media (air, water, soil); the fourth part is ecological issues; the fifth part is global environmental issues; the sixth part introduces environmental disasters and their risks. Through the study of this course, students can have a preliminary and comprehensive understanding of the basic characteristics of environmental science, provide help for future related scientific research, teaching and practical activities, and also lay a solid foundation for further study of other subsequent courses in the field of environmental science.

Name: Environmental Economics
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Environmental issues are a cross-cutting scientific issue involving many disciplines. Different from environmental science and environmental engineering, environmental economics is a discipline that applies economic principles to solve environmental problems. It can provide important basis for management, planning, policy formulation, etc. _x000D_
    The research contents of environmental economics mainly include: (1) Basic theories and methods of environmental economics. Including the relationship between environmental issues, externalities, public goods, etc.; (2) Economic analysis of environmental costs and benefits. Including economic loss assessment of environmental pollution and damage, methods of environmental governance benefit assessment, etc.; (3) Use economic means to manage the environment and formulate environmental economic policies. Study how to use economic levers such as taxation, finance, and credit to regulate the relationship between economic activities and environmental protection, and the relationship between polluters and polluters. _x000D_
    Environmental economics is an interdisciplinary subject that involves many fields such as environmental science, environmental management, environmental engineering, economics, resource science, ecology, geography, etc. It is also an applied subject that not only emphasizes teaching students relevant theories, but also emphasizes specific working methods. _x000D_

Name: Applied Mathematical Statistics Methods
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The research objects of environmental science are mostly random phenomena affected by many complex factors. Mathematical statistics method is one of the effective means to study these random phenomena. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course systematically explains classical mathematical statistics methods from an application perspective and combines research examples. The teaching focuses on the basic characteristics of random variables and explains the description and testing of variable size, discreteness and distribution characteristics. Specific contents include: data preprocessing, overall feature characterization, hypothesis testing for size comparison, hypothesis testing for discrete degree comparison, distribution testing, variance analysis and regression analysis. _x000D_
_x000D_
    The biggest difference between this course and other statistics courses is that this course does not focus on the derivation process of statistical methods, but particularly emphasizes the application prerequisites and basic requirements of specific methods, and emphasizes how to correctly use corresponding statistical methods. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Chemistry
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Introduction to general chemistry and environmental science (non-essential)
Introduction: Study the existence, behavior, and effects of potentially harmful chemicals in environmental media, and how to reduce or eliminate the environmental hazards they cause. Reveal the important physical-chemical processes and molecular mechanisms of pollutants in soil, water and other major environmental media, including phase transfer, migration, chemical degradation and transformation.

Name: Environmental Geoscience
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Environmental geoscience is an interdisciplinary subject of environmental science and earth science. It takes the human-environment system as its research object, mainly studies the composition, structure, formation, evolution of the earth's natural environment, as well as the interaction and impact of human activities and the environment, and applies the theories and methods of a series of sub-disciplines of earth science to study environmental issues and protect the environment. As an emerging discipline, environmental geosciences has not yet been finalized in its content and discipline system. At present, the relatively clear sub-disciplines include: environmental geology, environmental geochemistry, environmental geography, pollution meteorology, environmental hydrology, environmental marine limnology, environmental soil science, etc.

Name: Frontiers of Environmental Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The course content covers various research fields of environmental science, including the sources and emissions of environmental pollutants, the environmental behavior and fate of pollutants, the migration and transformation of pollutants at micro-interfaces, the ecotoxicity and risks of pollutants, environmental pollution and human health, the restoration of polluted environments, environmental pollution and global climate change, environmental benchmarks and standards of pollutants, environmental quality monitoring, environmental economics and management, etc.

Name: Integrated Environmental Science Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This summer course highlights the combination of basic classroom teaching and simulation effect demonstrations with field practice and hands-on activities. Under the specific guidance of teachers from relevant majors, on the basis of early classroom theory, principle learning and basic operational skills training, students who choose the course will personally participate in comprehensive internship activities at representative field sites in the later stages of the course, including: collection of multi-media environmental samples such as atmosphere, water, soil, sediments and organisms (including preparation and use of instruments and equipment; target area selection, sample point layout and positioning), various sample pre-processing (separation, extraction, purification, concentration, etc.) and detection work, and finally complete a detailed and scientific internship report. This course is interconnected and complementary to related courses such as environmental monitoring and experiment, water environmental chemistry, soil environmental chemistry, environmental toxicology, and environmental risk assessment. Through comprehensive experimental design in multi-media environments, students will develop ideas and methods for comprehensive analysis and research of environmental science issues, and understand And master the techniques and means to explore the sources and generation of environmental pollution, migration/transformation and other fate behaviors, as well as the qualitative and quantitative research on its ecotoxicological effects, as well as the acquisition and processing methods of experimental analysis data, deepen the understanding of environmental science, and improve students' ability to comprehensively analyze and solve problems.

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (Geophysics and Space Physics)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Presentation of basic knowledge, research methods and front-line hotspots of geophysical and space physics research.

Name: Frontiers of Environmental Science Fall Lecture Series
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The course content covers various cutting-edge research fields in environmental science, including the sources and emissions of environmental pollutants, the environmental behavior and fate of pollutants, the migration and transformation of pollutants at micro-interfaces, the ecotoxicity and risks of pollutants, environmental pollution and human health, the restoration of polluted environments, environmental pollution and global climate change, environmental benchmarks and standards for pollutants, environmental quality monitoring, environmental economics and management, etc.

Name: Environmental Engineering
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Environmental engineering solves environmental problems through sound engineering theory and practice, including control of water, soil and air pollution, drinking water safety, disposal and recycling of wastewater and solid waste, etc. The course content includes four modules: water treatment, wastewater treatment, air pollution control, and solid waste disposal. This course is mainly open to undergraduates majoring in non-environmental engineering and focuses on introducing the relevant scientific principles of the main engineering technology methods to prevent and control environmental pollution and improve environmental quality. Through the study of this course, you will understand and understand the basic principles of major pollution control methods, and develop your ability to analyze and solve actual environmental pollution problems.

Name: Environmental Health Risk Assessment
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Modern life is highly dependent on a variety of synthetic chemicals, which also create an environment full of chemicals. As a result, people are exposed to chemical substances at all times through exposure to air, water, food, cosmetics, building materials and various items of life. Especially in recent years, with the rapid growth of the economy, environmental pollution incidents have occurred in the country, such as the problem of melamine in milk and the increase in the blood lead of children as a result of heavy metal contamination, and the health effects of chemical substances have been of increasing public concern. It is therefore an issue for Governments and the scientific community to reflect on how to effectively manage chemicals while fully enjoying the benefits of chemicals and prevent them from threatening human health and ecological safety. In 1992, the United Nations first introduced the basic concept of chemical risk management, emphasizing the need for enterprises to undertake autonomous risk management based on risk evaluation. Currently, risk evaluation has become an indispensable tool for managing chemicals in countries such as the EU and the United States. In recent years, our scientific community has begun to focus on the issue of risk management of chemical substances, and research has flourished. Unfortunately, however, there is some ambiguity in the concept of risk evaluation and the lack of the necessary methodological support, which makes it difficult to deepen research on risk evaluation and hinders the application of risk evaluation methods to chemicals management in the country. As a result, the course focuses on the teaching of chemical risk assessment methodologies, enabling selected students to master the basic concepts and basic methods of risk evaluation and to quantitatively evaluate the health and ecological risks of various chemical substances through case studies. Human exposure to chemicals varies widely, and differences in occupational, lifestyle, living space, age, sex, economic status, etc., lead to significant differences in the amount and type of chemical substances exposed. At the same time, different chemicals have different physico-chemical properties and uses, which also determine their different environmental behaviour. These exposure pathways and the complexity of environmental behaviour pose difficulties for the evaluation of chemical exposures. It is therefore particularly important to identify exposure factors for chemical substances and to project exposures. On the other hand, there are very wide variations in the toxicity levels and toxicity mechanisms of different chemicals, and the sources of toxicity data are extensive, with some from animal exposure data provided by specialized agencies, others from epidemiological surveys, and those at different positions often citing different toxicity data. However, regardless of the type of toxicity data used, many assumptions are implicit in each data and need to be understood before treatment of toxicological and epidemiological models or dose-effect analysis. Finally, as any chemical substance is toxic, only at different doses presenting toxicity, the organic integration of hazard and exposure evaluation is at the core of the risk evaluation. The course systematically addresses the rationale and methodology for chemical risk evaluation from the perspective of both human health risks and ecological risks and presents a number of application cases, focusing on the results of the author ' s research, including: 1. Presentation of the development history of international risk evaluation and risk management to help readers reflect on the nature of risk evaluation; 2. Presentation of human exposure assessments of chemical substances, methods of hazard assessment of carcinogenic and non-carcinogenic chemicals and their risk calculation, using human health risk assessments as the subject of human health risk evaluations, as well as cases of mercury and lead risk evaluations, to enhance the understanding of health risk assessment methodologies; 3. Ecological risk assessment methodologies, focusing on hazard assessment methods at different levels, including physiological levels, individual levels, population levels, ecosystems, and their application in environmental benchmarking. In order to provide students with the capacity to actually carry out risk evaluations, the course will be based on the mathematical skills commonly used in risk evaluations in a case-by-case context.

Name: Remediation of Contaminated Environments
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Environmental pollution is currently a widespread problem both within and outside the country. In order to protect the environment and human health, it is necessary to rehabilitate the contaminated environment and remove pollutants from environmental media. The course focuses on basic principles, techniques and practices for the remediation of contaminated environments, including the rehabilitation of contaminated soil, the rehabilitation of contaminated groundwater, the rehabilitation of contaminated sediments and the restoration of contaminated surface water. In addition, methods of surveying the contaminated environment, risk evaluation, remediation criteria and regulatory systems were presented, and case studies of restorations were conducted for each environmental medium.

Name: Numerical Simulation of Environmental Pollution
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Students are required to have knowledge of undergraduate mathematics, physics and chemistry with a certain computer software and hardware base
Introduction: Numerical simulations and models of environmental pollution are the main tools and technologies for understanding the physical and chemical processes of environmental pollution, quantifying the causes of environmental pollution and pollution source-sink relationships, and predicting the occurrence and development of environmental pollution. They have developed rapidly in recent years and have been widely used in environmental pollution research and early warning and forecasting. They have become indispensable tools and are expected to gain faster development and application. Environmental pollution forecasting models cover many fields of knowledge such as computational mathematics, physics and chemistry, weather and climate, and data processing and integration. Through the study of this course, students will be initially familiar with and master the basic knowledge of numerical models of environmental pollution, modeling ideas and platforms, and big data processing. Through computer practice, you can initially master the operation and use of numerical models of air pollution. Through the study of models, we can further understand and consolidate the theory and knowledge of atmospheric chemistry, physics, atmospheric environment, and causes of air pollution, and integrate the theory and practice of numerical simulation of other environmental media.

Name: Integrated Belt and Road Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course is a comprehensive internship for regional integrated urban-rural development and urban-rural eco-environment awareness studies. The course is directed at senior undergraduate students at the Urban and Environmental Institute. The aim is to provide students, through internships, with an understanding of the characteristics and problems, mechanisms and patterns, responses and experiences of different geographical settings, stages of development and types of development, resource use in rural and urban development, spatial organization of economic and social activities, planning and management of urban and rural development.
In conjunction with the “one-way” initiative, internships are selected each year in the typical regions of the countries concerned, through integrated internships to promote students' awareness of the development situation in different regions, undertake comparative studies, deepen theoretical understanding, improve professional academic standards and develop the capacity to analyse problems in a comprehensive manner.
The course was held in the Tokyo Metropolitan Circle region of Japan. The main teaching features of the region include:
(1) Spatial development and industrial transformation in metropolitan circles
(2) Mega-City Space Organisation
(3) Protection and utilization of historical and cultural landscapes in metropolitan areas
(4) Suburbanization and spatial reconstruction of metropolitan areas
(5) The development path and effectiveness of the New City New Zone (building of the City of Science)
(6) Upgrading of urban transformation in ports (Yokohama)

Name: English for Environmental Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course uses multimedia-assisted teaching to provide students with some illustrations and animation demonstrations that are easy to understand the text as much as possible, guiding students to organically combine English learning and professional learning, so that students can master basic English terms, vocabulary, expressions, and writing methods in various major fields of environmental science. This will lay the foundation for students' future English literature reading and English paper writing. It will also enhance students' professional knowledge about environmental science and engineering, and improve students' listening and speaking skills in professional English.

Name: Scientific Software Applications and Literature Retrieval
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
"Scientific Software Application and Literature Retrieval" is a practical course that aims to help students master literature retrieval and management in scientific research and paper writing, as well as the use of common scientific software. The first half of the course will introduce the electronic resources available in libraries and the Internet, as well as common methods and techniques for conducting literature searches around the research subject. The second half focuses on the main functions of commonly used scientific software, mainly involving word processing, data processing, graphing, database management, mathematical modeling, statistical analysis, image processing, and professional chemistry software. _x000D_
The specific teaching content will be adjusted at any time with the update and development of the above types of software. Using the Peking University Teaching Network platform, students who have chosen courses in the past can upload and share materials, providing a richer perspective and material for the teaching content of this course. In addition, the exciting parts of student reports are constantly being absorbed into teaching content. The overall teaching fully reflects the characteristics of mutual teaching. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students will master the basic usage of common scientific software, understand literature retrieval methods, and lay a good foundation for scientific research at the middle and senior levels. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Microbiology
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: This course is an elective course in environmental science and engineering. Through this course, students are given the basics of classification, structure and physiological activity of micro-organisms, their status and effects in environmental ecology, and their application in environmental pollution management projects. To lay the groundwork for follow-up professional courses and practice in future work. The main course presentations were: (1) Classification and cell structure of micro-organisms, general morphological characteristics of various types of micro-organisms; knowledge of special morphological structures and viruses of micro-organisms; familiarity with the broad biological characteristics of bacteria, nematodes, blue green bacteria, genuine nuclear micro-organisms, etc. associated with environmental engineering; (2) The growth and reproduction, nutritional structure and nutritional type of micro-organisms, metabolic and respiratory effects, environmental temperature, dissolved oxygen, toxic and harmful substances, radiation, etc., on micro-organisms; mastering basic concepts of genetic and mutation and understanding of the application of genetic engineering in the environment. (3) The role of micro-organisms in the physical cycle of nature, understanding the mechanisms of the role of micro-organisms in the management of environmental pollution; familiarity with the distribution of micro-organisms in natural ecosystems and detection techniques; understanding the interrelationships of micro-organisms. (4) Microbiological mechanisms for major pollutants; mechanisms for micro-organisms to treat sewage and soil pollution; By studying these things, the students have to... (1) Basic knowledge of micro-organisms, including, inter alia, the biological metabolism, growth characteristics, genetic characteristics and ecological habits of micro-organisms; providing the basis for the application of follow-up studies on the toxic effects and biological functions of micro-organisms; (2) Knowledge of the ecological characteristics of micro-organisms and their effects in the evolution of biogeochemicals and their underlying role in the environmental purification of pollution; (3) Understanding the toxic effects of micro-organisms on the environment and the role of micro-organisms in polluting the environment provides a solid theoretical basis for understanding and understanding the mechanisms of micro-organisms in environmental engineering. (4) Knowledge of microbial methods and their theoretical basis for biotoxicity testing of contaminants, and provision of theoretical and methodological basis for learning and research in ecotoxicology and environmental health courses for subsequent environmental pollutants.

Name: Introduction to New Media
Introduction: This course is mainly for junior undergraduate students majoring in journalism and communication. It focuses on the development of new media technology, communication effects, main types, application characteristics, etc., and also involves the macro management, micro management, mobile media, etc. of new media. It provides introductory teaching on new media from the three levels of history, theory and practice of new media.

Name: The Marxist View of Journalism
Introduction: Journalism theory is a professional basic course for journalism majors, and Marxist journalism concepts are the basic theory guiding my country’s journalism practice. This course is of great significance for understanding the journalism theory and journalism practice of socialism with Chinese characteristics. Through the study of this course, students can master the subject nature and attributes of journalism, understand the historical development and practical connotation of Marxist views on news; and combine practical application of Marxist positions and viewpoints to analyze the truth, objectivity, fairness of news, as well as professional concepts such as press freedom and responsibility.

Name: English Public Speaking
Prerequisite: Have a good foundation in English, like spoken English and give speeches. No prerequisite courses required. This course is taught entirely in English. In each class, each student must actively interact and give a speech in English under the teacher's classroom content design.
Introduction: Basic purpose: To acquire and improve effective English speaking skills

Name: History of Chinese Journalism
Introduction: To enable students to master the basic history and patterns of the creation and development of Chinese journalism, to learn about the main stages of the development of Chinese journalism history, the evolution of the system and important events and personalities, and to prepare students to view and understand China ' s news and communications industries from a historical perspective.

Name: Co-Evolutionary Strategy: From Startup to Corporate Transformation
Introduction:
The course, using the framework of the newly developed co-execution strategy (see Episode Strategy: Redefining the Life Cycle of the Enterprise), discusses how an enterprise can develop and implement an enterprise strategy in the context of the UVCA environment (uncertain future directions and paths to development). The conceptual framework of the repertoire strategy consists mainly of four elements of the repertoire strategy, four phases of the repertoire strategy and four dimensions of the repertoire strategy.

The repertoire strategy consists of four components: users, organizations, markets, products, considering the two dimensions of management (people and affairs) and enterprise boundaries (internal and external). The user is outside the enterprise, the organization is inside the enterprise, the market is outside the enterprise and the product is inside the enterprise.

In accordance with business development patterns, the repertoire strategy consists of four phases: the lean entrepreneurship phase (from 0 to 1), the lean growth phase (from 1 to N), the lean expansion phase (from N to N+) and the lean transformation phase (from N+ to Z). Enterprises need to adopt a coherent and built-in development strategy appropriate to that stage of development at different stages of the strategy.

Name: Frontiers of Computer Networks
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: A first course would be sufficient if it referred to basic computer knowledge, such as the General Computation.
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to introduce key concepts and principles of the computer network. The course will combine a top-down and bottom-up approach to the Internet and its protocols. Examples of network structures, protocols and applications described included e-mail, Web and media flows. This course will cover communication services (e.g. TCP/IP) required to support such web applications. After describing the implementation and deployment of communications services in the physical network, including the cable and wireless area network environment, the course discusses network management. Throughout the course, Internet architecture and protocols will serve as key examples of the rationale of computer networks.

Name: Environmental Toxicology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Through this course, students are helped to master the absorption, migration, distribution, transformation and excretion process of environmental toxic and harmful substances in organisms; the toxic pathways and toxic action sites of environmental toxic and harmful substances; the "three-cause" effect and the toxic mechanisms of carcinogenesis, teratogenesis and mutagenesis; neurotoxicity, immunotoxicity, endocrine disrupting effects, hepatotoxicity, nephrotoxicity, bone toxicity and other target organ toxicity and their toxicological mechanisms; master the basic research methods and experimental skills of environmental toxicology; and understand the domestic and foreign research progress and development trends of environmental toxicology.

Name: Western Political Thought (Ancient)
Introduction: This course guides students to read Greek (including some Roman) literature, history and philosophy documents to understand the basic characteristics of ancient Western political thought, grasp the main political issues faced by the Western city-state world, and understand the rise, structure and decline of the city-state political world.

Name: Western Political Thought (Medieval)
Introduction: The course continues with Western Political Thoughts (Old Ages), teaching Western political thinking from the Roman Empire to the Middle Ages. Focus on Augustine and Dante.

Name: Political Philosophy
Introduction: This course attempts to lead students into the ideological world of political philosophy by explaining the classics of Western political philosophy, so that students can familiarize themselves with the basic issues and ideological context of ancient and modern political philosophers such as Plato, Aristotle, Augustine, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Locke, and Rousseau, understand the basic themes of political philosophy, such as justice, government, sovereignty, freedom, democracy, etc., and be able to think about a series of core issues such as individuals and countries, politics and morality, politics and religion, etc., and cultivate students' rational analysis and thinking abilities about political reality.

Name: Basic Latin (2)
Prerequisite: Elementary Latin (1), Elementary Latin 1 is the prerequisite course for this course. Or you can self-study the first 28 lessons of Wheelock's Latin, or similar content from other textbooks.
Introduction: This course is aimed at students who are interested in learning classical Latin. It systematically teaches classical Latin grammar, vocabulary and Roman cultural knowledge through grammar explanations, classroom exercises, written assignments, class tests, mid-term and final tests, etc., so that students can fully master the basic grammar and vocabulary of classical Latin within one year, and have the ability to read selected excerpts from the original Latin text. This course is a compulsory course for the Western Studies Group of the "Classical Philology" project.

Name: Gamified Innovative Thinking
Prerequisite: It would be useful, but not necessary, to learn relevant courses such as game design.
Introduction:
The so-called gamification (Gamification) refers to the application of games or game elements, game design and game concepts to some non-game situations. Such as applying games or game concepts in marketing. Gamification currently has broad applications in education and training, product design, human resource management, marketing and other fields, such as WeChat red envelopes and other cases. _x000D_
_x000D_
Gamification actually has a long history of research, but after it became popular in the business field in 2010, it attracted widespread attention from society. Kevin Werbach from the Wharton School also offers a "Gamification" course on Coursera, which is very popular. _x000D_
_x000D_
The person in charge of this course, Mr. Shang Junjie, has been studying gamification learning for a long time and has rich research experience in gamification. He has also covered relevant content in previous courses for graduate students and undergraduates. This time, we hope to guide students to have a more in-depth discussion. We will use project learning methods. Through lectures, case analysis, group discussions and project design, we hope to allow students to fully understand the concept, connotation, application fields, application methods and strategies of gamification. We also hope to promote the current innovation and entrepreneurship education. _x000D_

Name: Health Cultivation in Traditional Chinese Medicine
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: This course revolves around the idea that "nurturing health means nourishing one's nature". Preserving health means protecting or repairing people’s self-healing and self-repairing abilities. Using simple and simple methods to find a way to return to nature's fitness is exactly what modern people are increasingly lacking. Health preservation is not only a technical means, but also an attitude towards life. Traditional Chinese medicine health care is one of the essences of extensive and profound traditional Chinese medicine. Most of the famous traditional Chinese medicine doctors in the past dynasties are not only long-lived and healthy old people, but also happy and wise men with a happy mood. On the basis of introducing the basic knowledge of traditional Chinese medicine and related traditional Chinese medicine culture, this course systematically introduces the theoretical principles of traditional Chinese medicine health care and the inherent essence of traditional Chinese medicine's emphasis on health care in preventing and treating diseases. It also introduces specific methods and concepts from the topics of spiritual health care, diet health care, sexual health care, exercise health care, drug health care, meridian health care, physical health care, and daily life health care. The lecturer focuses on combining the mysterious and profound theories of traditional Chinese medicine with daily life examples and clinical phenomena in an easy-to-understand manner. This course has always been one of the most popular elective courses among students.

Name: Studies in the Modernization of Latin American Countries
Prerequisite: The first course for history students is World History, which is not required by other faculties.
Introduction: Among the Third World, Latin America was the first region to be colonized and involved in the capitalist world system. It was also the first region to gain national independence and explore the path to modernization. In the process of modernization, Latin American countries have tried various development models and proposed various development theories. Their historical experience of modernization has important reference value for my country's reform, opening up and modernization construction. In the international environment of globalization, Latin America has become increasingly important on the international stage, and economic, political and cultural exchanges between China and Latin America have continued to increase. To understand today's world, we cannot understand and study Latin America. This course provides students with a preliminary understanding of the modernization path in Latin America and major countries through various methods such as explanations, readings, and classroom discussions. On this basis, students can write an academic paper on a certain issue to improve their academic research capabilities.

Name: Solar Activity and Human Society
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The sun is the source of all things on earth, and solar activities have a great impact on modern human society. When the sun is highly active, it will emit strong electromagnetic radiation and high-energy particles, and may eject large clumps of material. This is a solar storm. When a solar storm propagates near the Earth's orbit, it will produce brilliant auroras, but it will also change the Earth's space environment to varying degrees, damage artificial satellites and spaceborne instruments, and affect the operation of communications, navigation, power and other systems. Long-term changes in solar activity are also closely linked to the earth's ozone hole and meteorological disasters such as droughts, floods, and ice ages on the ground. This course will systematically explain the evolution of the sun and stars and the main phenomena that occur on the sun. It will detail the impact of different types of solar storms on the high-tech systems of human society after they reach the earth space. It will also introduce the connection between solar activity and weather, climate, and human production and physiological activities. It will also describe the interaction of solar radiation and magnetic field with other celestial bodies in the solar system. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Economic Growth
Introduction: Since the onset of industrial civilization, the overall level of the human economy has experienced unprecedented general growth. Humanity's average income and living standards have increased significantly. The global population has increased by more than six times, and human life expectancy has doubled. At the same time, the pace of long-term economic growth that accompanies industrial civilization differs across countries, and the gap in income and living standards between countries has expanded unprecedentedly compared to the era of agricultural civilization. The question is, what key factors determine the vast differences between countries such as the wealth of the United States and the poverty of Africa? For another example, in the past thirty years, were the growth rate of China's economy and the deceleration of Japan's economy just short-term economic cycle fluctuations or long-term growth trends? How will the trend of mankind’s “Great Economic Divergence” evolve? Needless to say, this is a challenging, controversial, and fascinating subject. Economic growth is a special economic analysis centered on this theme. This is not only the focus of long-term research by economists, but also an issue of great concern to all sectors of society. This course will systematically teach the key points, basic principles, determinants, and empirical cases of economic growth. Specifically, this course will systematically analyze the main determinants of economic growth and their interrelationships based on economic growth theory. These main factors include three major categories: factor accumulation (physical capital, human capital), labor productivity (technological progress, production efficiency), and basic factors (government, distribution, culture, geographical conditions, etc.).

Name: Quantitative Geography and Planning Systems Engineering
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics (microcentres, linear algebra, probabilities and statistics)
Introduction: During the geometric revolution, while mathematical methods were introduced into geography, systematic analysis methods were also introduced into geographical research. The former developed into computational geography through quantitative geography; the latter developed into geographic information science through geographic information systems. Computational geography and geographic information science represent two frontier fields in geography today that have reached the same goal through different paths. This course will be based on the computing and informatization direction of geography, and teach basic quantitative analysis methods and systems engineering methods in geography according to the needs of geospatial analysis and urban planning. Quantitative analysis methods include three aspects: first, spatial measurement (commonly used spatial index), second, quantitative analysis (basis of multivariate statistical analysis), and third, geographical mathematical model (basic quantitative geography theory). Urban planning systems engineering includes two aspects: first, system thinking and system analysis methods (qualitative theory), and second, operations research methods (quantitative analysis methods). The quantitative analysis method integrates traditional quantitative geography, computational geography and today's geographical computing ideas; the systems engineering method integrates traditional systems thinking, system analysis and geographical information science ideas. The teaching objectives of this course are divided into two levels: the basic level is to master the basic knowledge of geometric methods and urban system analysis, and the advanced level is to guide students to understand the ins and outs of computational geography and geographic information science, so as to provide background technology training and lay a preliminary knowledge foundation for future frontier research in geography.

Prerequisite: The course is devoted to visual production concepts and methods and is oriented towards the actual exercise of video clippings without training in the use of editing software. Introduction:
Excellent film and television works are inseparable from three basic elements: sociological, poetic and technical. Sociology focuses on the artistic value of film and television works, while technology explores the means of realizing film and television content. There are many courses and books in these two fields, and everyone is familiar with them. Only in between - poetry, that is, about the art of editing, there are very few discussions and not many courses. I have been teaching "video editing" courses for more than ten years, and I know that even with the available editing tools, many people still don't know how to edit. This is just like being able to use Word and having a good dictionary does not mean that you can become a literary master. _x000D_
This is a basic course on film and television production. It introduces the basic ideas, methods and processes of editing, summarizes some production experiences and techniques, and provides learning and reference for beginners to help them improve the efficiency of editing and avoid detours. The course has four modules. The first module is to understand the basic unit of editing - lens, including the scene, angle, viewpoint and length of the lens. It is the basic unit of film and television production and provides knowledge preparation for video editing. The second module is shot assembly, including shot editing, direction matching, segment assembly and transition. This is the basic practice of film and television production. It introduces the general rules of shot assembly and how to use lenses for narrative and performance. The third module is interspersed in the middle of the second module, which is about the pre-filming practice of film and television, introducing the operating methods of the camera, shooting key points and precautions. The fourth module is paragraph editing, including motion editing, sound editing, genre editing and montage editing. Genre editing among them summarizes the production techniques of several typical scenes such as comedy, thriller, erotica and song and dance. This part of the content not only focuses on the hierarchical structure of film and television content, but also focuses on the artistic expression of film and television works. _x000D_
It should be emphasized that the "Film and Television Production" course does not teach the operation of non-linear editing software. Students are required to take elective courses such as "Video Editing" in advance and become proficient in mainstream non-linear editing software such as Avid Media Composer and Final Cut Pro before taking this elective course. "Film and Television Editing" is positioned as the intermediate link between film and television art and film and television technology. It is suitable for beginners with little film and television production experience.

Introduction:
This course is an experimental course that integrates multiple fields of biology such as microbiology, zoology and botany. It uses the newly built Peking University Biological Herbarium as the teaching base and is jointly taught by multiple teachers. The course content is rich and the design concept is to combine scientific experiments and artistic creation, integrating science, artistry and practice. The following introduces the teaching content of each subject:_x000D_
The Biological Herbarium of Peking University has a long history. The Department of Natural History began to cultivate talents in the production of animal and plant specimens during the Imperial Academy. In 1924, the Biological Herbarium was established based on specimens collected by the famous botanist Mr. Zhong Guanguang. Professor Hu Jingfu, the founder of insects in my country, collected a large number of insect and invertebrate specimens. In the early days of liberation, the departments adjusted the herbaria of Tsinghua University and Yenching University and merged them into Peking University. Over the past 100 years, many predecessors have devoted a lot of effort to the collection, identification and standardization of specimens. So far, Peking University undergraduate biology field internships have always insisted on teaching students how to make animal and plant specimens. The newly completed Peking University Biological Herbarium integrates animal and plant herbariums and has a rich collection of specimens. It is a unique teaching base where students can see a large number of precious animal and plant specimens and learn the classification and production of scientific specimens. _x000D_
Microorganisms are tiny and have the characteristics of wide distribution, wide variety, rapid reproduction, and different colors and shapes. After students learn the basic operations of the experiment, they can use the petri dish as a "canvas" and use various microorganisms as pigments to create unique works of art. For example, using colored fluorescent proteins expressed by genetically modified Escherichia coli (E. _x000D_
The zoology content takes the class Insecta as an example. The class Insecta is the most prosperous group of animals in the world, with a wide variety of species. Entomology has become a classic course in many universities. In the course, students learn about the status and classification characteristics of Insecta in the animal kingdom, appreciation of excellent specimen works, methods of collecting and preserving insects, methods of making insect specimens, and students can make insect specimens and insect specimen artworks by themselves. _x000D_
The botany content takes Specimen as an example, which is an important document for plant taxonomy and ecological research. The course will introduce the development history, functions and production principles of plant specimens. Plant specimens have always only highlighted the scientific aspect, but in recent years people have paid more and more attention to the production of aesthetic plant specimens, which requires students to combine scientific and artistic aspects when making them. Excellent works will be collected by the herbarium and displayed for a long time. _x000D_
Pressed Flower Art is an art form derived from plant specimens. In recent years, domestic pressed flower art has gradually entered university classrooms. The course content includes the development history of embossed art, appreciation of international award-winning outstanding works, pressed flower materials, production of embossed daily necessities and embossed decorative paintings, etc. Students use dry flat plant materials such as roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and bark to design and create ornamental and practical works of art. _x000D_
This course provides students with interdisciplinary learning opportunities. By learning scientific vocal methods and techniques, students can master the basic abilities of chamber chorus; at the same time, they can learn and sing relatively simple and highly artistic two-part and multi-part chamber chorus works.

Name: Large-Sample Statistical Theory
Introduction:
This is to increase the current two-credit "Theory of Large Samples" to three credits to provide additional content. Current classes are popular with graduate and undergraduate students. This extended course will provide the necessary statistical theoretical foundation and improve students' theoretical analysis skills and methods to meet the needs of big data and data science.  Main coverage: _x000D_
Weak Convergence, Central Limit Theorem, Delta Method, Moment Estimator; _x000D_
M-Estimator and its consistency and asymptotic normality, MLE and GMM estimation; Projections; U-Statistics. Markov; Markov Chain and MCM; _x000D_
Limit Theorem for dependent processes; The bootstrap method; Introduction to Empirical Processes and Its Applications._x000D_

Name: Vocal Performance
Introduction: As part of the basic aesthetic education, the course "Vocal Singing and Performance" is mainly aimed at students who are not majoring in vocal music. It teaches basic vocal music theory and singing methods, and also includes practical content such as vocalization, breathing, singing and analysis of vocal music works. It also teaches singing skills and methods according to the students' different vocal music foundations. By practicing classic vocal works, students are guided to scientifically and correctly master vocal singing methods. While mastering the basic theoretical knowledge of vocal music majors, students can analyze and process general vocal music works, have certain singing performance abilities, and improve students' appreciation of music works and other aesthetic accomplishments.

Name: Introduction to Advertising
Introduction: 1. Overview and review (The History of Advertising); 2. Market Research (Marketing Research); 3. Advertising Planning; 4. Advertising media (Media Communication); 5. Creative Idea; 6. Public advertising (Publicity);7. Corporate Identity; 8. Advertising Agency; 9. Advertising Culture; 10. Advertising Laws.

Name: Film and Television Editing
Prerequisite: The course is devoted to the concept and methodology of video clips and is oriented towards the actual exercise of video clips without training in the use of editing software. Students who choose to take “video editing” courses are required to master at least one of the mainstream non-linear editing software such as Final Cut Pro, Adobe Premiere pro.
Introduction:
Excellent film and television works are inseparable from three basic elements: sociological, poetic and technical. Sociology focuses on the artistic value of film and television works, while technology explores the means of realizing film and television content. There are many courses and books in these two fields, and everyone is familiar with them. Only in between - poetry, that is, about the art of editing, there are very few discussions and not many courses. I have been teaching "video editing" courses for more than ten years, and I know that even with the available editing tools, many people still don't know how to edit. This is just like being able to use Word and having a good dictionary does not mean that you can become a literary master. _x000D_
This is a basic course on film and television editing. It introduces the basic ideas, methods and processes of editing, summarizes some editing experience and techniques, and provides learning and reference for beginners to help them improve the efficiency of editing and avoid detours. The course has four modules. The first module is to understand the basic unit of editing - lens, including the scene, angle, viewpoint and length of the lens. It is the basic unit of film and television editing and provides knowledge preparation for video editing. The second module is shot assembly, including shot editing, direction matching, segment assembly and transition. This is the basic practice of film and television editing. It introduces the general rules of shot assembly and how to use lenses for narrative and performance. The third module is interspersed in the middle of the second module, which is about the pre-filming practice of film and television, introducing the operating methods of the camera, shooting key points and precautions. The fourth module is paragraph editing, including motion editing, sound editing, genre editing and montage editing. Genre editing among them summarizes the editing techniques of several typical scenes such as comedy, thriller, erotica and song and dance. This part of the content not only focuses on the hierarchical structure of film and television content, but also focuses on the artistic expression of editing works. _x000D_
It should be emphasized that the "Film and Television Editing" class does not teach the operation of non-linear editing software. Students are required to take elective courses such as "Video Editing" in advance and become proficient in mainstream non-linear editing software such as Final Cut Pro before taking this elective course. "Film and Television Editing" is positioned as the intermediate link between film and television art and film and television technology. It systematically, comprehensively and hierarchically introduces the universal logic and general rules of film and television editing, and summarizes the editor's editing concepts, operating ideas and industry experience. It is suitable for beginners with little editing experience.

Name: Fundamentals of Managerial Economics
Introduction:
The purpose of this course is to help non-economics undergraduates, graduate students, masters in business administration (MBA) and financial specializations to understand the underlying theories and methods behind economics and management science, to analyse critically the micro- and macroeconomic environment in which business management operates, and to take stock of quantitative analysis in economics to assess the market environment and business management under open economic conditions.
The course consists of two main segments: the first part focuses on consumer behaviour, market demand and consumer surplus, production and cost theory, market structure and balance, enterprise pricing strategy, game theory and information economics, and general equilibrium theory. The second part focuses on the theory of economic growth, the System of National Income Accounting, the monetary and banking base, inflation and unemployment, fiscal and monetary policy and an open international economy.

Name: Advertising Psychology
Introduction: This course enables students to master the process of the emergence and development of advertising psychology, understand the basic concepts and theories of advertising psychology, and master the application of the basic principles of advertising psychology in market research, advertising planning, creativity, media placement, etc.

Name: Social Conflict and Its Management
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite:
First general psychology.
It would be better if social psychology could be repaired first or at the same time, and organizational management psychology could be studied.
Introduction:
This course is practical; emphasizes starting from the basic concepts, theories, and major findings of psychology; and examines how to improve your professional and personal life by developing interpersonal skills. This course particularly emphasizes understanding and effectively managing self-cultivation that is closely related to interpersonal relationships through classroom interactions, case discussions and role-playing; effectively handling interpersonal problems and ultimately gaining help in career development. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Meteorology
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite:
No prerequisite courses required. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course content summary: Meteorology takes the atmosphere as the research object and explores its characteristics and status. This course is divided into 4 main parts. The first part is an overall understanding of meteorology and meteorology, including the basic components of the atmosphere, weather phenomena and processes, the atmosphere, the status of the atmosphere in the earth system; the relationship between meteorology, climate and weather; the research objects, tasks and brief history of meteorology. The second part is a meteorological description of the static properties of the atmosphere, including meteorological elements, earth-atmosphere energy balance and distribution, atmospheric circulation and role of water; isoline analysis and statistical analysis methods of meteorological elements; identification of atmospheric stability, cloud shapes and symbols; changes and roles of water vapor in meteorological processes. The third part is the meteorological description of atmospheric dynamics and movement patterns, including air pressure distribution, atmospheric forces, simple equilibrium motion; atmospheric circulation at various scales, mean wind belts; the relationship between air pressure and wind, and the statistical description of wind; and the relationship between mean movement and weather systems. The fourth part is weather situations and processes, including mid-latitude weather systems, low-latitude weather systems, and severe weather processes; weather chart analysis of weather situations; meteorological analysis and forecasting methods. _x000D_
_x000D_
Class hour allocation: 2 class hours for the first knowledge point; 6 class hours for the second knowledge point; 6 class hours for the third knowledge point; 2 class hours for the midterm exam; 6 class hours for the fourth knowledge point, 6 class hours for the fifth knowledge point; 4 class hours for the sixth knowledge point; 2 class hours for the final exam and 2 class hours for the exam. A total of 36 credit hours. _x000D_
Introduction: This course is one of the introductory courses in atmospheric environmental science. It uses rich and colorful weather processes and atmospheric phenomena as learning and teaching content. It is the basis for further understanding of atmospheric environmental issues such as air pollution and climate change. This course provides a preliminary introduction to basic meteorological phenomena, processes, observations, and applications from the perspective of environmental science, so that students can understand the intersecting characteristics of meteorology with chemistry, physics, biology, earth, environment and other disciplines, and provide a more comprehensive perspective and knowledge base for students majoring in environmental science to learn and understand atmospheric environmental issues.

Name: Fundamentals of Air Pollution
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, university physics, university chemistry.
Introduction: Air pollutants are first emitted into the atmosphere through man-made or natural sources. As the atmosphere moves and spreads, most of them will undergo atmospheric chemical reactions to form new pollutants. Eventually, it leaves the atmosphere and collects on the earth's surface due to sedimentation and cloud and rain clearance. This course is an introduction to the basic knowledge of air pollution. The first chapter tells what air pollution is, and the second chapter explains the behavior of pollutants in the atmosphere through mathematical and physical equations. Chapter 3 describes the estimation method of air pollution primary source emissions. Chapters 4 and 5 describe the atmospheric chemistry and atmospheric physical processes of pollutants. Chapter 6 focuses on the removal process of air pollution in the atmosphere. Chapter 7 briefly introduces how to solve the mathematical and physical equations of air pollution. This course is taught to undergraduate students in their second year or above.

Name: Fundamentals of Atmospheric Chemistry
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Description of the generation of typical air pollution issues (O3, aerosols, persistent organic matter, etc.), important pollutants in the atmosphere, and their presence and transformation.

Name: Environmental Radical Chemistry
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
This course aims to become a theoretical foundation core course in the field of environmental science. Through the free radical chemical reaction process, a universal chemical reaction type, it communicates the media and objects of concern for environmental pollution problems such as atmosphere, water, soil and cells, so that third-year undergraduates can better integrate the knowledge they have learned in inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry and physical chemistry into the understanding and solution of specific environmental problems. _x000D_
This course will be taught by a teaching and research team composed of four young teachers from the Department of Environmental Science and Department of Environmental Engineering of the college. The course content takes into account the four major fields of atmospheric free radical chemistry, water and soil free radical chemistry, free radical processes in cells, and free radical cutting-edge measurement technology. It will be perfectly connected with the undergraduate prerequisite courses "Environmental Issues" and "Environmental Science", allowing students to gradually think about the causes and control solutions of secondary pollution problems that are of concern in the field of environmental science and engineering through the important perspective of free radical chemistry. _x000D_

Name: Analysis and Visualization of Environmental Measurement Data
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
This course is offered to undergraduate students in the School of Environmental Science and Engineering. This course is based on Igor and Matlab software to manage and comprehensively analyze environmental measurement data. The main contents include: _x000D_
(1) Basic application of various processing software for environmental measurement data; _x000D_
Understand the different current data processing software and have the ability to select the correct data processing software according to needs; be able to use several softwares for simple data programming, data reading and preliminary processing; master the basic application of drawing software, and prepare graphic and text tables that can be published according to the needs of the article. _x000D_
(2) Method of comprehensively analyzing environmental measurement data and meteorological parameters; _x000D_
Master the ability of comprehensive data analysis. You can use statistical methods to analyze data on meteorological, gaseous pollutants, and physical properties of particulate matter. Master data smoothing, fitting, and bad pixel removal methods. Interpret the physical and chemical information and atmospheric process mechanisms reflected in the data based on comprehensive analysis of data. _x000D_
(3) Main network information, combined with observation data, has the ability to comprehensively analyze and interpret data. _x000D_
The main sources of network information and the main measurement principles; network data processing methods and the ability to combine actual observation data, with the ability to comprehensively manage, analyze, visualize, and interpret data. _x000D_

Name: Multidisciplinary Perspectives on Environmental Decision Making
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The solution of environmental problems requires the comprehensive application of interdisciplinary knowledge, especially environmental decision-making issues, which require the intersection of environmental science, environmental engineering, sociology and other perspectives. This course will be jointly taught by well-known professors from the School of Science of the University of Melbourne and Peking University, so that students can further understand the methods and approaches to solving different environmental problems in the context of fully understanding environmental issues and environmental decision-making needs. Summer courses are conducted in the form of professors’ lectures, field practice, group discussions, and presentations. The course uses different perspectives on environmental issues as an entry point, and also provides an in-depth analysis of the differences in environmental issues between Australia and China, including water pollution, air pollution, urban environmental management, environmental decision-making, biodiversity, environmental simulation, etc.

Name: Occupational Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course systematically introduces psychological issues in career selection and management. The main content includes: knowing oneself (an individual's career interest type, aptitude, career motivation, temperament and personality, etc.) and knowing others (occupation classification and standards, career competency requirements), striving to achieve person-job matching; career decision-making methods and career maturity assessment; psychological assessment and selection in career; career development and planning; career management at the individual and organizational levels; career guidance and consultation; career transition and career stress adjustment, etc. The teaching purpose of this course: on the basis of systematic classroom teaching, combined with case discussions and the introduction and use of professional psychological assessment tools, focusing on integrating theory with practice, cultivating students' awareness of career design and management, and possessing corresponding abilities. At the same time, cultivating students' interest in applying psychological knowledge to practice, and exercising relevant research abilities.

Name: China's Environmental Problems and Environmental Policy
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
Environmental problems are serious problems faced by human society at this stage of development. Environmental pollution brings huge risks to human health, and climate change threatens human survival. Environmental problems are mainly by-products of human production and life activities, and their occurrence is closely related to the behavior of each individual. Solving environmental problems requires everyone's participation, and it also requires public policy makers to create conditions to motivate people's participation. This course aims to systematically introduce environmental problems, their causes and solutions. _x000D_
_x000D_
China's environmental problems are very serious. China has made great achievements in economic and social development in the past few decades. However, the rapid economic development and the inefficient and intensive use of resources and energy have also made China's environmental problems increasingly prominent. The atmosphere, water, and soil are seriously polluted, the city is besieged by domestic waste, and environmental accidents such as chemical plant explosions and ocean oil spill pollution occur frequently. When introducing environmental issues, this course mainly uses China's environmental issues as a case study to explain. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course aims to enable students to understand the current status of environmental problems and their root causes, and to cultivate students' awareness of taking the environment into consideration in future work and their ability to propose solutions to environmental problems. The course covers universal environmental science and public policy theories, focuses on the practical problems faced by China, highlights the interdisciplinary characteristics of environmental issues, and explains the course content by answering a series of fundamental questions: _x000D_
_x000D_
First, what is environment? In other words, what are people talking about when they discuss environmental issues? The phrase "environment" appears in many contexts, and environmental pollution and environmental problems are also familiar phrases in daily life. However, the connotation and extension of the environment are often not well understood and explored insufficiently. This course intends to start from the most basic concepts and lead students to think and discuss about the essential concepts of the environment. _x000D_
_x000D_
Second, what are environmental issues? Frequent smog days in recent years have brought air pollution into most people's horizons. However, environmental problems are not only air pollution, but also water pollution, soil pollution, forest degradation, and climate change. This course aims to introduce environmental problems by classification and explain their occurrence mechanisms, so that students can understand the diversity of environmental problems and help them connect the basic scientific knowledge they have learned with real-life problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
Third, what environmental problems does China face? China is facing serious environmental problems. What environmental problems does China face? How severe are these environmental problems? This course intends to explain environmental issues by mainly taking China's environmental issues as an example, describing its history and current situation, and making predictions about possible future conditions. _x000D_
_x000D_
Fourth, what are the root causes of environmental problems? What is the relationship between environmental issues and human production and life activities? Will human production and life activities necessarily cause environmental problems? In other words, under what conditions will human production and living activities produce environmental problems? This course intends to explain the causes of each type of environmental problems, with special attention to the main sources and root causes of environmental problems in China. _x000D_
_x000D_
Fifth, why should we pay attention to environmental issues? What impact will the existence of environmental problems have on current people and their descendants? When only considering the impact of the environment on humans, what value judgments are made? This course will start from the impact of environmental issues on human health and survival to explain why we are concerned about environmental issues. It will also explore the impact of ecological environment degradation on other species and the issue of the environment as a trade barrier. _x000D_
_x000D_
Sixth, how to reduce or even eliminate the impact of human activities on the environment? To answer this question, two more fundamental questions need to be answered: What are the factors that affect people’s production and life activities?
