How can we get people to take environmental factors into account in their decision-making? This course intends to introduce the factors that influence people's behavior from the perspectives of psychology and economics, as well as the policy tools that can be used to influence people's behavior. _x000D_
_x000D_
Seventh, how to formulate effective environmental policies? What factors need to be considered in formulating environmental policies? People have diverse production and life activities. What considerations need to be taken when designing policies to encourage changes in these activities? This course intends to explain the characteristics, theory behind and applicable scope of each type of policy tool, and use China's environmental policy as an example to connect theory and reality. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Law
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: This course is for undergraduate students majoring in environmental science. The main purpose is to enable students to understand the basic knowledge of environmental law and master the basic content of Chinese environmental law through teaching, so as to lay the necessary foundation for future work in environmental protection or related fields.

Name: Environment and Development
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Taking sustainable development as the basic research object, specifically the system composed of people and people and people and the environment, its realistic research object is the system composed of economy, society and environment. The course includes the following parts: first, an introduction to the general issues of environment and development (the origin and connotation of sustainable development); then, an analysis of the goals, development paths, implementation approaches of sustainable development of human society, and solutions to issues of intergenerational equity and intergenerational equity, etc., and an introduction to the applied theory of sustainable development; finally, an introduction to the management system of sustainable development, as well as foreign and domestic sustainable development strategies and their implementation status.

Name: Environmental Planning
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: Environmental valuation; environmental economics; mathematical statistics; geographic information systems
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the basic theories and methods of environmental planning, elemental environmental planning, comprehensive environmental planning and typical cases of environmental planning. The specific content is divided into 11 chapters, including: conclusion, theoretical basis, planning content, technical methods, water environment planning, atmospheric environment planning, land use planning, solid waste management planning, ecological city planning and environmental planning decision support system

Name: Corporate Environmental Management
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Environmental management is the shared governance of the three principals: government, business and the public. The main thrust of the first course in environmental management is an integrated and systematic approach to the theory, methodology and practice of environmental management, focusing on the government level. From an enterprise perspective, this course teaches the passive and active responsiveness of enterprises to environmental issues, as well as changes and adjustments in production and business practices.

Name: Pollution Ecological Engineering
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
"Pollution Ecology Engineering" is an important basic course for environmental engineering, environmental science and ecology majors. Teach the basic principles of pollution ecology, the ecological process of migration and transformation of pollutants in environmental media, biological enrichment, and health diagnosis and evaluation of polluted ecosystems; focus on teaching pollution ecological control and restoration technology systems, design methods, and cases. _x000D_
The teaching purpose of this course is to enable students to master the basic theories, basic principles, technical systems and engineering design methods of pollution ecological engineering, to cultivate students' ability to apply modern ecological technology to solve environmental pollution problems, and to lay a solid professional foundation for students to engage in environmental engineering, environmental science, environmental management, and municipal engineering research and design in the future. _x000D_
Chapter 1 Introduction_x000D_
Basic concepts of pollution ecology, ecological engineering, restoration ecology, ecosystem ecology and pollution ecological engineering, and the scientific system of pollution ecological engineering. _x000D_
Chapter 2 Principles of Pollution Ecological Engineering_x000D_
Restoration ecology theory, basic ecological theory, environmental self-purification principle, action principle of microorganisms, plants and animals, and migration and transformation principle of typical pollutants. _x000D_
Chapter 3 Pollution Ecological Processes and Effects_x000D_
Ecological processes and effects of typical pollutants in receptors such as rivers, lakes, reservoirs, oceans and ecotone wetlands, biological toxicity, biological enrichment, biological amplification, and ecosystem health diagnosis and evaluation method systems. _x000D_
Chapter 4 Pollution Ecological Control Project_x000D_
Practical equipment for pollution ecological control technology, water pollution ecological control technology such as biological beds and artificial wetlands, solid waste biological fermentation and high-value utilization technology, gas pollutant plant and microbial control technology, and case analysis of typical pollution ecological control projects. _x000D_
Chapter 5 Pollution Ecological Restoration Project_x000D_
Planning and design of pollution ecological restoration projects, practical technologies for pollution ecological restoration, deep treatment and resource reuse technology of tail water from sewage treatment plants, hydrothermal extraction of petroleum waste resources and microbial harmless disposal technology, sewage pit and pond renovation, black and odorous water body treatment and river and lake ecological restoration technology, cyanobacteria and diatom bloom formation mechanisms and prevention and control technology, drinking water source protection and ecological restoration technology, landscape wetland and ecological river valley construction technology, typical cases of ecological restoration project design for sponge cities, rural environments and industrial sites. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Systems Analysis
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
This course briefly introduces the basic principles and common methods of environmental system analysis, including an overview of system analysis, models in environmental engineering, graphical methods of mathematical programming, simplicity programming of linear programming, network flow linear programming models, integer programming and its applications, decision theory, multi-objective water resources problems, dynamic programming and nonlinear programming, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
For representative excellent optimization methods, the course explains in detail from four levels: "oriented problems, main ideas, method techniques and application expansion". It also emphasizes the logic behind the generation of these excellent methods and possible sources of inspiration, and compares them with our own thinking methods, in order to overcome obstacles that hinder our innovative thinking, and ultimately improve students' logical thinking level and confidence and ability to create new methods.

Name: Industrial Microbiology
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Teach the basic knowledge of industrial microbiology, a brief history of the development of industrial microbiology, important microorganisms and their applications, growth and reproduction of microorganisms and their control, genetic variation and breeding of microorganisms, as well as the application status and research progress of industrial microorganisms in environmental engineering, fermentation industry, etc.

Name: History of Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: The origin of modern scientific psychology, its relationship with the development of philosophy, physiology, biology, and medicine, the origin, development, and characteristics of major schools such as structuralism, psychoanalysis, behaviorism, humanism, cognitive school, functionalism, and Gestalt school, and various countries including Germany, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The development of psychology in China and France, and the history of psychology in China, the course emphasizes theoretical reflection on the historical development of the discipline, and focuses on training students to evaluate and understand the history and current situation of the discipline from a broader macro perspective. Through vertical and horizontal comparisons and systematic analysis, it encourages long-term considerations and strategic predictions for the future. _x000D_

Name: Personality Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: The main content includes the theoretical assumptions of the six major personality theory schools including psychoanalysis, behaviorism, cognition, humanism, trait and biology schools, explanations of individual differences and individual behaviors, personality assessment methods, and their application in real life; influencing factors of personality development, relevant concepts of personality disorders, relevant research on personality psychology, culture and personality.

Name: Rhythms in the Brain
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: Senior undergraduate and graduate students interested in dynamic structures, neuroshocks and rhythmic activities in cognitive neurosciences are not restricted to specializations. There is no mandatory provision for pre-academic courses, and more than two years or more are recommended.
Introduction:
The brain is a dynamic system that is changing all the time. Our various cognitive activities arise from this dynamic system. Rhythmic activity is a ubiquitous and very interesting form of brain dynamics. In recent years, many cognitive neuroscience studies have discovered that rhythmic activity is a dynamic information organization method of the brain and is closely related to various cognitive processes (such as perception, information processing, attention, learning, memory, consciousness, etc.). _x000D_
This course attempts to introduce the basic findings of neural rhythmic activity and its relationship with cognitive processes from various perspectives. This course uses classroom teaching combined with classroom discussions and paper reports. This course is suitable for students who are interested in new concepts and methods of cognitive neuroscience. _x000D_

Name: Infant Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course introduces the characteristics, theories and research methods of individual development during prenatal and postnatal period from 0 to 3 years old. This course is an expansion and deepening of the "Developmental Psychology" course. Through this course, students can gain a more comprehensive and detailed understanding of infant psychological development and understand the latest progress in infant psychological research.

Name: Sensation and Perception
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course is mainly based on classroom lectures, combined with classroom discussions, to clarify the basic theories and basic concepts in the study of sensation and perception. This course focuses on the combination of theory and scientific research practice, and emphasizes exploring important issues in sensory perception research from the perspective of combining multiple research methods (including psychophysics, brain imaging, electrophysiology and computational models).

Name: Vision and the Visual Arts
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: The course describes visual psychology and nervous mechanisms for visual arts, which teach students to understand the process of external physical information input into the visual system. The course will be based on the path of visual information processing, combining the rich case of artistic works, and will present the effects of visual processes and phenomena such as brightness, colour perception, depth and stereoconsciousness, shape perception, vision illusions, attention and eye motion, ageing and eye disease on the creation and appreciation of visual arts, as well as neuroaesthetic studies that have emerged in recent years.

Name: Psychology of Emotion
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Emotional psychology is a discipline that is both old and young. Emotion is a common psychological phenomenon that affects people's lives all the time. Emotion is the focus of current psychological research, and it is also an international frontier and hot spot in multidisciplinary interdisciplinary research. This course will lead students to understand emotions from the history, methodology, and theory of emotion research, as well as the relationship between emotions and other psychological processes, such as emotions and cognitive processing, emotional decision-making and emotional intelligence, and clinical emotional disorders.

Name: Psychology of Art
Introduction: Art psychology is a course that combines art and psychology. It is a required professional course for art and design majors in colleges and universities. Art psychology is based on aesthetics, art, psychology and other disciplines. It mainly studies the laws of psychological activities in the process of artistic creation and the laws of psychological activities of appreciators in feeling and understanding works of art. Art psychology is an interdisciplinary subject of aesthetics and psychology. From the perspective of the aesthetic characteristics of psychological activities, it belongs to aesthetics. From the perspective of the psychological characteristics of artistic activities, it is an applied branch of psychology.

Name: Principles of Integrated Circuit Fabrication
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Semiconductor physics, MOS integrated circuit, bipolar integrated circuit

Name: HDL-Based Digital System Design
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
In the mid-1980s, when Verilog was first produced, the typical design size was 5,000 to 10,000 gates. The typical design method was to use schematic input tools for design, and simulation began to become a basic gate-level verification tool. The emergence of Verilog language not only solved the problems at the time, but also inspired a new generation of EDA technology revolution: from RTL to synthesis, Verilog language has become the mainstream language for IC design. _x000D_
    Throughout the 1990s, the Verilog language and related technologies developed rapidly. In 2001, IEEE approved a new standard: Verilog-2001, and in 2005, IEEE approved a new standard: Verilog-2005. Verilog language will become the dominant HDL language. From integrated circuit design to structural design or verification of digital systems, Verilog will provide you with great help to design smaller, better, and faster integrated circuits. _x000D_
    The course will introduce the basic functions of Verilog language, including digital hardware design and verification methods. Learn the basic concepts and syntax of the language, advanced design constructs, synthesizable design styles, and advanced verification constructs. In the course, you will also learn the comprehensive flow of digital circuits, including basic concepts, timing, area and power consumption optimization. _x000D_

Name: Principles and Frontiers of Life Science
Introduction:
Life science is one of the most important disciplines in the 21st century and has a significant impact on society. Life sciences are significantly related to human survival and life, health, economic construction and human development. It is one of the most popular basic disciplines in the world today. Its research progress and results will have a profound impact on mankind. Life science education is an essential quality for students to become modern talents. _x000D_
The development of life sciences is very rapid. New life phenomena and mechanisms are constantly being clarified. Research results that have a profound impact on human society are constantly emerging. New understandings and treatments for diseases that seriously threaten human health are constantly being developed. Therefore, general education in life sciences should not only explain the basic knowledge and principles of life sciences clearly, but also fully integrate the latest progress and research results in life sciences. Only in this way can we arouse students' enthusiasm for learning life sciences, understand the profound impact of modern life sciences on human society, and deeply understand that life sciences continue to produce revolutionary new technologies and methods when solving problems related to human health, population growth, resource crises, ecological environment degradation, biodiversity, and many other fields. _x000D_
Therefore, this course is based on teaching the basic principles of life sciences in a simple and in-depth manner, focusing on introducing biological knowledge closely related to human life and health, revealing scientific explanations of diseases and life phenomena that are of general concern to society, with special emphasis on introducing the major progress of today's life sciences and their far-reaching impact on current human society and the future. Through the study of this course, we hope that students can deeply understand the mystery of life, develop students' intellectual potential, comprehensively improve students' comprehensive quality, and lay a good foundation for cultivating interdisciplinary talents.  _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Auditory Cognitive Neuroscience
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course is mainly based on classroom teaching, combined with classroom discussions and paper reports, trying to comprehensively introduce the basic concepts, basic theories and neural basis of auditory cognition. By combining findings in the fields of cognitive psychology and neuroscience during the teaching process, and comparing it with visual research that students are more familiar with, various aspects of auditory research are introduced and discussed, including: neural processing mechanisms from general sounds to special sounds (such as speech, music, etc.), as well as advanced auditory cognitive processes in auditory such as attention, memory, and auditory scene analysis. This course is suitable for students who have a certain foundation in cognitive psychology, understand the basic concepts of neuroscience, and are interested in auditory research.

Name: Vision and Visual Neuroscience
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course will teach relevant knowledge about vision and visual neuroscience to junior graduate students in vision majors, graduate students in non-vision majors, and senior undergraduate students. The content is both broad, deep and difficult. The teaching format includes classroom lectures and paper discussions (students are required to have good English reading skills, pre-class reading, class discussions, no PPT), each accounting for 50% of the time.

Name: Neurobiology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Our cognitive functions are based on our brains, and neurons are the most basic units of the brain. In this course, we will first explain the cellular mechanism of these neurons, and then explore various cognitive functions such as sensation (perception), behavior, and memory from a neurobiological perspective.

Name: Probabilistic Models for Structured Data
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Pre-requisites: basic knowledge in statistics and probability, linear algebra, optimization, programming.

Target audience: Senior undergraduate students and graduate students in various disciplines (computer science, statistics, economics, finance, electronic engineering, biology, physics)
Introduction: This course is designed to introduce probabilistic models for structured data, where data points (such as sequential data and graph/network data) are no longer independent of each other. The course will cover the modeling, inference, and learning of cutting-edge probabilistic models, including hidden Markov models, Markov random fields, conditional random fields, and factor graphs, with applications across multiple fields such as text mining, medical fields, and social network analysis. By studying this course, students are expected to gain: (1) understand the mathematical expressions of multiple probabilistic models applicable to structured data, including their intuitive explanations, mathematical derivation, and proofs; (2) apply these models to practical applications; (3) propose the potential of new models for structured data.

Name: Machine Learning and Time Series Analysis
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Probability and statistics, linear algebra, optimization
Introduction: This course introduces machine learning models such as probabilistic models and deep learning. This course welcomes students who are interested in time series analysis and prediction based on machine learning/probabilistic models. Students with backgrounds in computer science, statistics, economics, finance, electronic engineering, biology, physics and other disciplines are welcome to participate. This course does not require programming skills, but programming is beneficial for hands-on experiments. This course covers several popular time series models, such as vector regression models, ARIMA models, hidden Markov models, Karman filtering and other models, as well as more advanced models such as neural networks (long short-term memory network, recurrent neural network, gated recurrent neural network), support vector regression model, Hawkes process, sparse VAR model, etc. At the end of this course, we hope that students can: (1) Understand the mathematical formulas of timing models. (2) Apply the time series model to real data. (3) Have the ability to develop novel machine learning models for time series applications and publish papers on them.

Name: Principles of Microcomputers B
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The "Microcomputer Principles B" course is a professional basic course for undergraduates majoring in electronic information at the School of Information Science and Technology. It is a backbone basic course at Peking University and an introductory course for college students to learn and master basic computer hardware knowledge, assembly language programming and common interface technologies. _x000D_
_x000D_
The main goal of this course is to enable students to master the basic composition, working principles and typical interface technologies of microcomputers in theory and practice, and to establish the overall concept of microcomputer systems, so that students have a solid foundation for using microcomputer technology to design and develop software and hardware, and have the ability and innovative consciousness to analyze and solve practical problems. Studying this course is of great significance for familiarizing yourself with and mastering the basic concepts and technologies of modern computers, as well as for studying subsequent related computer courses. _x000D_

Name: Physical Foundations of Microelectronics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is a basic course for the microelectronics major and is a preliminary course designed for learning semiconductor physics and semiconductor device physics. In the case of limited teaching hours, it helps students establish preliminary concepts and theoretical frameworks of quantum mechanics; master the basic concepts and analysis methods of quantum physics and the application of quantum physics in microelectronics, laying a good theoretical foundation for students' future study and research.

Name: Applications of Computational Modeling in Psychology and Neuroscience
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, introduction to statistics, introduction to computer language, psychology or neuroscience
Introduction: Can we predict human behavior quantitatively? How to simulate the human brain? What kind of model is a good model? In the past 30 years, computational modeling has been increasingly widely used in psychology and neuroscience, greatly advancing our understanding of the human brain and human behavior. This course will introduce the basic theories and techniques of computational modeling, as well as representative models from various fields of psychology and neuroscience.

Name: Medical Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
In this course, from the perspective of the application of psychology in medical practice, the introduction, research methods, psychological assessment and measurement, psychological stress, psychosomatic diseases, abnormal psychology, health psychology, patient psychology, nursing psychology, doctor-patient relationship, psychological intervention, neuropsychological rehabilitation, etc. will be taught, so that students can understand the important role of psychology in medicine and master basic knowledge of psychosomatic diseases and mental health. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Human Resource Development
Introduction:
Human resource development is an important area of ​​education discipline oriented towards learning in the workplace. Currently, many colleges of education in American universities offer undergraduate courses and high-level graduate courses in human resource development. Judging from the effectiveness of the advanced human resource development postgraduate course offered by the School of Education of Peking University, the course is very popular among students. Human resource development is a field that closely combines research and practice. With the deepening of learning theory and the continuous development of human capital theory, human resource development has become an increasingly important activity in modern organizations. This course mainly introduces the basic knowledge of human resource development, including introduction, human resource development process, and application of human resource development. The first part of the course focuses on the development process of human resource development, training and development, career development and organizational development, challenges faced by human resource developers and competency models. The second part of the course focuses on the learning process, including needs analysis, project design, project implementation, and project evaluation. The third part of the course introduces new trends in human resource development, including technological changes in human resource development, international frontiers, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: General Cyrillic Mongolian (I)
Introduction: This course is devoted to the official Mongolian language - Cyrillic Mongolian.

Name: General Cyrillic Mongolian (II)
Introduction: This course is devoted to the official Mongolian language - Cyrillic Mongolian.

Name: General Hebrew (I)
Introduction: The teaching content mainly includes: pronunciation, grammar, vocabulary, texts, oral practice, etc. During the teaching process, students are trained to correctly master pronunciation and intonation, master Hebrew grammar rules and the usage of important vocabulary, understand the content of the text, read the text accurately and fluently, and carry out conversations in prescribed situations.

Name: Principles of Political Science
Introduction: This course includes eighteen aspects including politics and political science, interests and politics, political power, political rights, political rule, political management, state, political parties, political associations, political psychology, political thought, political socialization, political revolution, political reform, and political democracy. It elaborates theories and views on the nature of human social politics and basic aspects of political life. This course is the main theoretical basic course for political science and administrative management majors. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic theories and analytical methods of political science, understand the nature and basic laws of politics, form the basic ability of political analysis, and make theoretical preparations for the study of other courses in political science and administrative management.

Name: Classical Chinese Poetic Meter and Composition
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: ancient Chinese, ancient Chinese literature, hymn, etc.
Introduction: Having a deep and systematic understanding of poetry rhythm and mastering the basic writing skills of rhymed poetry and lyrics is one of the basic abilities and qualities for students of the Chinese Department. This course will comprehensively explain the formal characteristics of classical poetry from both the language and literature levels, and requires students to pass practical writing training so that they can eventually create rhythmic poetry freely and skillfully use word cards for writing.

Name: Introduction to Studies in Tang Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course takes the history, poetics, and poetry art of the Tang Dynasty as the research and teaching objects. According to the natural stages of poetry development in this period, this article systematically describes the development of poetry in important periods such as the early Tang, the prosperous Tang, the middle Tang, and the late Tang, focusing on analyzing the creative achievements of important poets such as Wang Wei, Li Bai, Du Fu, Bai Juyi, Han Yu, and Li Shangyin. At the same time, we will explore the laws and links in the development of poetry history in the Tang Dynasty, and study the relationship between the poetry styles of each period and the culture, thought, art and other backgrounds at that time.

Name: Bibliography
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the basic content and knowledge of Chinese ancient book catalogs: the development and evolution of the meaning of "catalog", the classification evolution of ancient books catalogs, the preparation of ancient books catalogs, the types and characteristics of ancient books catalogs, the functions and functions of ancient books catalogs, etc.

Name: Textual Bibliography
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course teaches the history of the ancient Chinese version of Han, basic knowledge and methods of identification, and outlines the catalogue of the version.

Name: Exegesis of Classical Chinese Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is one of the basic courses for undergraduates majoring in classical literature. The main contents taught in this course include: the emergence and development of exegesis, the content of exegesis, the method of exegesis, how to read ancient annotations, and the content related to exegesis in the arrangement of ancient books, etc. Through the study of this course, we strive to enable students to initially master the basic theories and skills of reading ancient books and then organizing and researching ancient books.

Name: Introduction to the Records of the Grand Historian
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: As the most systematic and rich record of early Chinese historical documents, "Historical Records" is one of the most relied-upon basic documents for research on the literary history of Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties. Its own compilation style and narrative art also have very exemplary literary significance. This course will select and read some chronicles, families, biographies, tables, and books in "Historical Records", hoping to achieve three effects: (1) Cultivate students' conscious awareness of "historical sources", master the basic methods of sorting out historical sources, and lay a philological foundation for students to enter thesis writing and subsequent academic research. (2) Master the basic methods of literature comparison and text reading, and cultivate students' awareness of issues in reading. (3) Understand the historiographic characteristics of "Historical Records" and its artistic features in terms of style, narrative, character creation, historical theory, etc., understand the basic characteristics of early Chinese historical biographical literature, and explore its influence on later narrative literature.

Name: Textual Collation
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course teaches the history, basic knowledge, theory and methodology of the ancient Han National Academy in China, and the relationship between the Academy and the collections and supplements.

Name: European History
Introduction: This course is an on-campus elective course that mainly teaches modern European history. The content includes the emergence of nation-states in early modern Europe, the content and influence of modern scientific concepts and democratic ideas, the national democratic revolutions and industrial revolutions in European countries, European nationalism and imperialism at the end of the 19th century, the two world wars and the decline of Europe, European diplomacy during the Cold War, changes in European politics, economy, society and culture in the 20th century, as well as the exploration of socialist revolution and reform in Soviet Eastern Europe, and Europe after the Cold War. While focusing on the introduction of historical events, the class also highlights the combing of historical context, the analysis of historical issues and the introduction of historical analysis methods.

Name: Topics in Shakespearean Drama
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Lead students to carefully read the original texts of Shakespeare's plays. Through the explanation and analysis of the works, students will have a true understanding of the language, art and ideological connotation of Shakespeare's plays. At the same time, the students will explore the influence and role of Shakespeare's plays on modern Chinese literary writers and works based on Chinese translation.

Name: Research Methodology in Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The course presents both theoretical approaches and front-line issues in linguistic research and knowledge of linguistic field surveys.
The field survey component, based on the actual state of the Chinese language, systematically introduces the theory and methodology of the linguistic field survey and leads students to implement the language survey in a concrete manner so that they can effectively acquire the basic skills of the language survey. Specific elements include the basic concept of linguistic field surveys; various linguistic theoretical streams and field surveys; the necessary and optional steps of field survey practice; how to conduct surveys based on diverse needs; how to conduct surveys and sketches based on actual linguistic conditions; and modern instruments and methods of field surveys.

Name: Theoretical Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Musical, linguistic fundamentals, modern Chinese, ancient Chinese, Chinese dialects
Introduction: This course trains students' ability to extract theories from specific language materials and establishes the basic concepts of linguistics as a science. By systematically introducing the relationship between linguistic theory and materials and the corresponding scientific operating procedures, and taking linguistic problems in Chinese as the operating object, it is designed to stimulate students' interest in scientific research through various methods such as lectures, discussions, and exercises, and to promote students' transformation from learning to research.

Name: Introduction to Formal Grammar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course focuses on formal methods in natural language grammar research, covering part-of-speech types, phrase structure analysis and dependency structure analysis. The course focuses on how to accurately establish hypothesis theories describing natural language through formal means, and how to construct large-scale grammar sets and treebank annotation sets that serve automatic grammar analysis. This course will also briefly introduce the mathematical foundation of formal grammar.

Name: Chinese Dialectology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the knowledge of Chinese dialectology to help students integrate the basic knowledge of various branches of Chinese linguistics into the analysis and processing of dialect phenomena. It emphasizes the combination of theory and practice and focuses on cultivating the ability to observe, capture, analyze, and deal with dialect phenomena.

Name: Fundamentals of Experimental Phonetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course teaches experimental phonetics based on courses such as Modern Chinese and Dialects. The teaching contents include: the acoustic properties of speech, the acoustic phonetics basis of speech production and perception; the vocal forms and distinctive properties of vowels, consonants, syllables, stress and tones, etc.; experimental research methods of speech; and instruments for speech analysis and synthesis. This course also arranges experimental teaching of speech analysis.

Name: Human Language and Artificial Intelligence
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Introduction to courses:
The course presents cross-cutting areas between natural language research and artificial intelligence. From the perspective of the impact of the two disciplines on each other, the course describes the trajectory of the two disciplines and their forward-looking progress. While focusing on theoretical knowledge, the course also encourages active participation in content-related subjects and the development of hands-on practical skills. The curriculum includes, inter alia, the conceptual and historical development of natural language research, the historical development of artificial intelligence research, the relationship between natural language research and artificial intelligence research, the impact of natural language research on artificial intelligence research, and the impact of artificial intelligence on natural language research. In the course of the teaching, it involves meta-analysis, semantic role labels, photo profiling generation, natural language tasks such as visual questions and answers, knowledge mapping, and classic methods of artificial intelligence, such as long distance memory models, attention models, etc.

Name: Studies in Contemporary Chinese Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course examines the artistic experience created by Chinese novels in the 1980s and 1990s by exploring the artistic evolution and innovative experiments of contemporary novels, especially through the contemporary avant-garde movement in China in the late 1980s.

Name: Studies in the Production Mechanisms of Online Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course examines the development of Chinese online literature in the past 20 years. Through special research on the works of five important writers, it studies the literary connotation and artistic characteristics of their works, the significance and value of their creations in the history of genre development, and their interactive relationship with fans. In the study, the critical practice approaches of scholar-fans are explored. This is also a process of sorting out the history of Internet literature, and places the study of Chinese Internet literature in the perspective of the global media revolution. On the basis of understanding the history of the development of Internet literature, the ultimate goal is to establish a set of Internet literature evaluation systems that both inherently contain elite vision and are independent of traditional elite literature standards, in order to prepare for writing the history of Internet literature. The course will be conducted in the form of a seminar. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports, participate in writing practice, and participate in discussions with other students.

Name: Poetry Writing
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course inspires students' own creative potential and arouses students' creative desire by analyzing various constituent elements of modern poetry, such as the writing conditions of modern poetry, the aesthetic concept of modern poetry, the language concept of modern poetry, the communication method of modern poetry, the literariness of modern poetry, the literary ability of modern poetry, and the identity of modern poetry.

Name: Introduction to Terrestrial Water Bodies
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: An introduction is made to the formation and development of major land surface water bodies (rivers, lakes, swamps and estuaries) and groundwater, as well as the movement and changes of water, and their interconnections and effects with the environment and human activities. On this basis, the significance and importance of several types of water bodies (rivers, lakes and groundwater) as water resources are explained. Their distribution and changes are used as the main line to explain the current status of water resources and future water resources related to climate change, population growth, economic development, etc.

Name: Studies of Writers of the 1940s-1950s
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: The history of modern Chinese literature, the history of contemporary Chinese literature.
Introduction: This course selects five important writers to explore important literary and ideological history issues during the transition period from "modern literature" to "contemporary literature" in China in the 1940s and 1950s. It is divided into six topics. Topic 1, the methodology and core viewpoints of this course. The second topic, with Xiao Qian as the subject, discusses the contradiction between the writer's nationalistic emotions and political stance. The third topic, focusing on Shen Congwen, discusses the relationship between "literature and politics" through his experiences and literary creation in the 1940s and 1950s. Topic 4 discusses Feng Zhi, analyzing the contradiction and resolution between the writer's individual self-improvement and social responsibility. The fifth topic, with Ding Ling as the subject, discusses the relationship between "intellectuals and revolution". The sixth topic, taking Zhao Shuli as the subject, discusses the changes in the evaluation of Zhao Shuli in the contemporary left-wing literary circles in the 1940s and 1950s and the unique "modernity" connotation of Zhao Shuli's literature. The five writers basically cover the main relationship forms between writers and the new Chinese order. Through the analysis of specific writers' creations, thoughts, and personal experiences, we make a macro/micro dialectical discussion of important cultural/literary issues in the 1940s and 1950s from a broad social and cultural perspective.

Name: World Englishes and the English-Speaking World
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the current development status, theory and practice of the subject "World Englishes". The course content mainly includes British English, American English, Australian English, and the development and use of English in other countries and regions (including Southeast Asian countries and China). The purpose of this course is to enable students to understand the basic theories of World English and its localized development and use in the English world. The teaching requirements of this course are that students have a basic English foundation at undergraduate level or above and understand the differences and similarities between some varieties of English in various countries (such as British English, American English and Chinese English).

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 1) Discussion Section
Introduction: Read and discuss the original text of the designated Western philosophy.

Name: Directing Theory and Practice (I)
Introduction:
The study and research scope of this course focuses on film, taking into account narrative art works on television and online platforms (such as TV series and online movies). The course conducts a comprehensive theoretical and practical study of the director's work in narrative audio-visual art. _x000D_
This course combines the teaching concepts of specialized art schools and comprehensive university art schools, and refers to the teaching methods of many film schools in the United States, France, etc., forming a teaching mechanism that connects theory and practice. Through the study of this course, students will master a complete theoretical system of film directing and strong creative practice capabilities. _x000D_
_x000D_
Students should have basic knowledge of film and television art and a certain understanding of the basic aspects of film and television production. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching methods include: classroom narration, classroom discussion, classroom display, works and reports. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Ecology is the science that studies the relationship between organisms and the environment, and plays an important role in solving major issues such as resources, environment and sustainable development. Ecology follows four different levels of ecology: individual ecology, population ecology, community ecology and ecosystem. After studying this course, students will be able to understand the basic principles of organizational forms, structural functions, ecological effects, dynamic balance and other basic principles of the objective organic world from different levels, as well as the basic laws of biological development, to better protect the ecological environment and restore degraded ecosystems, and to lay the foundation for sustainable development. _x000D_
This course can: 1) train students to form the basic ecological concepts and principles needed to deal with environmental issues; 2) understand current global and domestic important environmental and ecological issues; 3) cultivate students' ability to analyze environmental and ecological issues. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Development History of Chinese Online Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course examines the development of China's Internet literature in the past 20 years. Through interviews with important website leaders, editors, writers, elite fans, etc., it discusses the development history of Internet literature, the creation process of various systems, the relationship between websites, authors, and readers, studies the unique production mechanism of Internet literature, and sorts out its development context and prospects. This is also a process of sorting out the history of Internet literature. On the basis of understanding the development history of Internet literature, the ultimate goal is to establish a set of Internet literature evaluation systems that both inherently contain elite vision and are independent of traditional elite literary standards, in order to prepare for writing the history of Internet literature. The course will be conducted in a seminar format and will be further developed in the spring semester. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports, participate in writing practice, and participate in discussions with other students.

Name: Film and Television Production (Fundamentals of Film Editing)
Introduction: This is a course that highly combines theory and practice. It is based on American academic editing theory and analyzes the editing theory, rules and techniques of Hollywood commercial films. The computer-based practice uses Avid MC, the most widely used film and TV series editing and synthesis software in the world's film industry, as the learning object. It teaches the production process, material management, editing, synthesis and color correction of movies and TV series. In addition, there are two classes to observe the post-production scenes of domestic mainstream movies on the Quantel IQ 3D film production platform.

Name: Close Reading of Modern Chinese Fiction Classics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
"Study of Modern Novel Classics" attempts to use the form of discussion courses to strengthen the reading of literary classics, and at the same time inspire students to focus on thinking about what irreplaceable historical mission literary classics bear for a country and nation while discussing modern novel classics. What power do classics have in shaping the nation? What is the unique value and significance of literary works for the future of mankind as a whole? Guide students to reinterpret classic literary books that have influenced modern Chinese history and Chinese people’s self-imagination and spiritual identity at all levels, and understand why literary classics shape the nation. How does each literary classic tell a so-called “modern Chinese story”? In this way, we can understand the role of novel classics in shaping the national character of modern Chinese people, inspire students to touch and inherit modern China's own traditions through classic general education and classic study, and especially inspire students to understand the significance of modern literary classics that are closely related to our current living conditions, and ultimately enable students to pass modern novel classics Through reading, we can understand the dilemmas of the 20th century conveyed by increasingly complex modern novels and the internal and external pictures of Chinese people’s experience in the 20th century, and then understand the classics of modern novels as an important way to understand the human survival situation in the 20th century and even today’s 21st century, and understand China’s own cultural traditions of the 20th century through these literary classics. _x000D_
        "Classic Study of Modern Chinese Novel" selects the classic works of modern Chinese novelists from the May 4th New Culture Movement in 1917 to the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949 for a semester. Trying to guide senior undergraduates in the Chinese Department to learn and comprehend modern classic novel texts during discussions. While teaching and analyzing classic works in each class, teachers will also conduct an in-depth analysis of the writer's life, overall style of creation, historical background, aesthetic sentiment and ideological connotation of the work. While enriching the literary horizons of the students who choose the course, it will also enhance their understanding, appreciation and recognition of classic Chinese novels, which will help them feel and understand modern Chinese culture and history, and then train students' ability to analyze literary works, which will ultimately help cultivate pure literary taste and literacy. _x000D_

Name: Reading and Interpreting the Bible
Introduction:
This course is designed to provide students with an in-depth understanding of important passages in the Bible. Class reading content includes: Genesis, Exodus, Judges, 1 Samuel, Job, Luther, Jonah, and the entire contents of the Gospels of Mark and John. Finally, the translation and characteristics of the English King James Bible are introduced. During the lecture, the main methods and research results of modern biblical studies will be introduced. The Bible annotation used in class is The New Oxford Annotated Bible, the language of instruction is English, and all written assignments and final exams are in English. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 2)
Introduction: The course focuses on mainstream thinking and concepts of contemporary Western philosophy. Given that contemporary Western philosophy is divided into two distinct types of style and sense, the curriculum is divided into two relatively separate sections, the continental European philosophy and analytical philosophy. Its main elements are, respectively, the main concerns of continental philosophy and the ideologue, and the analysis of philosophy and, in particular, the main concerns of linguistic philosophy, as well as strategies for solving them.

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 2) Discussion Section
Introduction: Read and discuss the original text of the designated Western philosophy.

Name: Animation Appreciation and Practice
Introduction:
Fully digital teaching method teaches today's popular art and development trends. While teaching the principles and applications of animation art, we will also analyze the current popular film and television special effects technology and teach digital art technology and its application and development prospects. Through comprehensive practical art training, we teach two-dimensional painting, three-dimensional painting, concept art design, character design, game design, interaction design, etc. _x000D_
Principle knowledge teaching + painting creation practice + special lectures by famous experts_x000D_
It enables students with zero foundation in animation art and digital art to master animation art knowledge and digital art technology through 1-2 semesters of study and practice, and can create animation and digital art works independently or in teams. _x000D_
Keywords: animation, digital art technology, concept design, character design, interaction design, game design. _x000D_

Name: Psychological Statistics I Computer Lab
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: This course is a supporting course for "Psychological Statistics I" and explains the use of SPSS software involved in Psychological Statistics I. The course introduces the interface and functions of SPSS. The main contents include: SPSS system overview, data management, chart production and editing, various t-test data, single-factor ANOVA, multi-factor ANOVA, correlation, and regression. This course is conducted simultaneously with "Psychological Statistics I" and cannot be conducted separately. _x000D_

Name: Quantitative Methods for Evaluating Literary Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The literary work covered in this course is a broad concept, encompassing both text-based and multimedia-based cinematography. Previous studies in this area have focused mainly on the application of qualitative research methods such as content analysis, which has led students to take a more scientific view of the content of literary works and their psychological impact on the human being, thus making a more objective quantitative assessment of literary works.
The course will teach how to evaluate literary works using statistics, questionnaires, etc., while changes in the biological parameters through which the different perceptions of literary works are presented by monitoring the pulses, eye moves, etc. of readers.

Name: The Image of China in Western Literary Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will study, in chronological order, important European and American works (mainly literary works) that depict China and present its image. The main purpose of this course is to introduce students to various Western images of China and how these images have changed over time. The course will also cover methods of image research.

Name: Studies in the Book of Changes
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Name: History of Islam
Introduction: This course introduces the historical process of the emergence and development of Islam, such as important historical events, classic teachings, sectarian origins and related theoretical issues of Islam. It cultivates students' ability to analyze and understand religious phenomena and arouses their interest in further research.

Name: English Translations of Du Fu's Poetry: Appreciation and Criticism
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Du Shiying's Translation: Appreciation and Criticism_x000D_
Du Fu's poems have been translated into many languages in the English-speaking world. As a unique and supreme expression of Chinese cultural spirit, Du's poetry is almost untranslatable; however, Du's poetry is also a world cultural heritage belonging to all times and mankind, and must not be untranslated. Poetry is what gets lost in translation, but it is also its reincarnation. Translation, as an interpretation and creation, has its pros and cons, and by observing its pros and cons, one can learn about people and the world, and thereby gain a broad understanding of humanities by examining oneself and others. This course selects the most representative English translations of Du's poems in the Western world in the past century. Through close reading, comparison and critical analysis of the texts, students can better understand and appreciate Du's poems, which are both Chinese classics and world literature, and have a close understanding of poetry translation and cross-cultural interlingual practice. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Paleography and Ancient History
Introduction: Since the beginning of the 20th century, a large number of ancient written materials buried underground have been unearthed, providing a wealth of information and new perspectives for the study of ancient history, and constantly writing new chapters in the history of ancient Chinese civilization. Among the unearthed ancient text materials from the Pre-Qin period, oracle bones, bronze inscriptions, and bamboo slips are the largest in number, and they play an important role in the study of the history of the Yin and Shang Dynasties, the history of the Western Zhou Dynasty, and the history of the Eastern Zhou Dynasty respectively. As a learner of ancient Chinese history, you should have an understanding of the role and value of ancient text materials in the study of ancient history. This course will introduce students to the major discoveries and research progress of ancient writing materials in the Pre-Qin Dynasty over the past 100 years through classroom lectures, so that they can understand the recording situation of ancient writing materials and the use of commonly used reference books; and through the study of original materials, students will initially master the interpretation and research methods of ancient writing materials, and cultivate the ability to use ancient writing materials in historical research.

College: Department of English Language and Literature

Name: Studies in European Integration
Prerequisite: General history of the world (part of the contemporary history of Europe and the United States); or European history (current part of the present)
Introduction:
This course is about the development of European integration and its ideological and theoretical research. European integration is a special phenomenon in the historical development of Europe since the second half of the 20th century. The conditions for its formation, the background of its emergence, the main historical process of its development, the main social and political characteristics formed during its development, and the general laws underlying its development are the main objects of our discussion. The formation of the history of European integration development is unique, that is, it is based on European culture, as well as the political, economic and other social environments in which it exists; on the other hand, it is closely related to the general development of world history, that is, world history after the late 20th century has increasingly closely connected different parts of the world. _x000D_
    European integration mainly revolves around the relationship between nation-states and European integration organizations. The development of European nation-states followed a historical process, during which their respective cultural and national spiritual characteristics were formed. The emergence of European integration organizations is the result of a specific development stage in modern European history. The relationship between the two interacts under modern historical conditions. The characteristics of European nation-states are the Anglo-Saxon culture, or liberal culture, of the United Kingdom, and the rationalist culture represented by France and other continental countries. The main reason for the emergence of European integration organizations is the demand for regional integration under modern historical conditions, including economic (the main body is the market), social (mainly reflected in social welfare) and political (mainly reflected in the governance of various governments) and other aspects. The interaction between the two is reflected in the different choices of different types of nation-states' attitudes towards integration, and also in the colorful integration process presented under the influence of different forces. This is how the development process of European integration was determined. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Russian History
Introduction: The special course on Russian history tells the history of Russia from the origin of the Russian state, through Kievan Rus, Tatar-Mongol rule, Muscovy, and finally ended with the Romanov dynasty. This course takes the form of a special topic and mainly explains this period of history from the perspective of interaction between political power and social culture. By sorting out the historical facts in politics, culture, social life and other aspects, combined with the introduction of the research trends of Russian history at home and abroad, the key issues in the process of Russian history are analyzed and sorted out.

Name: Writing History Papers

Name: Archaeological Discoveries and Historical Research
Prerequisite: Acronyms of archaeology (classes of great platforms, Academy of Archaeology)
Introduction: Since the twentieth century, China ' s archaeology has grown considerably, providing a wealth of information on underground soil extraction for research in China ' s ancient history, and has generated a number of major research topics. As a researcher in ancient Chinese history, it is important to have an understanding of the academic history, basic methods and theories of archaeology, to be able to make full use of archaeological information in research and to draw inspiration from archaeology theories and methods. At the same time, Chinese archaeology has been classified as a subject of history from the outset, and its research methods and orientations are marked by a strong historical stigma, so that Chinese archaeologists should also be aware of the basic historical material, research methods and major subjects of China ' s ancient history. The course is aimed at senior undergraduate students, mainly in the history and archaeology faculties, and aims to break the disciplinary barriers between history and archaeology, to sharpen their academic history and to integrate their information and research methods. The course is divided into three modules: the first consists of a study of the relationship between archaeology and history and a presentation of archaeological history; the second consists of a presentation of basic methods and theories of archaeology, including field archaeology protocols, archaeology and typologies, archaeological report writing and reading, and the theoretical streams of modern archaeology; and the third consists of a series of typical cases in which the typical doctrine and subjects of Chinese archaeology research are presented, focusing on the analysis of their methodological and theoretical successes and deficiencies. Through classroom lectures and discussions, under-class reading and final dissertations, the course provides students with an understanding of the academic history, basic theories and methods of archaeology, learns to read archaeological reports and extracts historical information from them, guides students in the integrated use of archaeological information and historical literature, integrates historical and archaeological methods, and tries to carry out research on a number of cutting-edge cross-cutting subjects.

Name: Russian Politics and Diplomacy
Prerequisite: History of international relations, Chinese diplomatic history
Introduction: This course is a comprehensive course that not only studies international politics, but also studies Russian history and reality. It takes the historical changes of Russia's national development as the main line, takes politics as the main content, and also covers economy, diplomacy, and culture. Studying this course requires taking the current practical problems in Russia as the starting point, using scientific methodology as the guide, combining theory with practice, history with the current situation, and linking the development of Russian society with the trends and laws of world development.

Name: History of International Political Thought
Introduction: The history of international political thought, in short, is the study of international politics from the perspective of intellectual history, or in other words, the comparison and examination of international political thought in the context of history. The research scope of this course is from ancient Greece to the post-Cold War period, which is a large span, but the focus is on the 500 years when the Western European international system began to take shape in the 16th century and gradually expanded to the world. Geographically speaking, this course mainly focuses on European international political thought. As far as the research object is concerned, this course focuses on examining and comparing the relevant discussions of some famous political thinkers and international political scientists on some important international political issues. The international political thoughts of Thucydides, Aquinas, Machiavelli, Hobbes, Grotius, Hume, Adam Smith, Rousseau, Burke, Kant, Marx, Karl, Niebuhr, Morgenthau, Wolfers, Waltz, Boole, Rawls, Wallerstein and many other classic writers, that is, their views on war and peace, balance of power, the relationship between international politics and morality, and international relations It peels off, sorts out, categorizes and compares views on a series of issues such as justice, pacifism, international intervention, international law, imperialism, international inequality, international community and diplomatic principles, systematically introduces and expounds the history of the occurrence and changes of various international political ideas, and uses it as a basis to understand the theory and reality of current international politics from the perspectives of intellectual history and intellectual history.

Name: The French Revolution and Napoleon
Introduction: The French Revolution and the Napoleonic era played an extremely important role in the history of the development of modern civilization. An in-depth understanding of them will help people better understand modern society, while further improving various academic qualities in the humanities and social sciences. This course will combine major historical facts and use the principles of historical materialism to explore the following questions: Why is the French Revolution different from the British and American revolutions and uniquely titled the "Great Revolution"? How did the “old system” lead to the “Great Revolution”? How did the "Reign of Terror" occur during the Great Revolution? Why did the Girondins and Jacobins fight against each other? Why did Robespierre have to get rid of Danton? Why did the Revolution oppose Christianity? Why did the "Thermidor Coup" happen? What changes occurred in French revolutionary political culture after Thermidor? What were the unconventional features of Napoleon's form of rule? What were the reasons for the rise and fall of Napoleon's empire? What historical impact did the French Revolution have?
