The course is conducted in two ways: classroom and indoor specimen observation. The study requires mastering the main anatomical characteristics of the human skeleton and commonly used human bone gender and age identification methods, understanding the basic research methods of the human skeleton and common abnormal pathological phenomena, and understanding how to use human bone remains to reconstruct the biocultural adaptation model of ancient people, so as to be able to adapt to the basic requirements for human bone processing in field archaeological work, and lay a solid foundation for in-depth study of other contents of physical anthropology.

Name: Zooarchaeology
Introduction:
Zooarchaeology is an important subdiscipline of archaeology. This course aims to introduce the theories, methods, and techniques for studying animal remains unearthed from archaeological sites, and to understand the relationship between human activities and animals in ancient societies, as well as the significance of animals to social development. The course will focus on the most common vertebrates at the site, especially mammals, while also taking into account birds and fish to ensure the integrity of the knowledge structure. In small class teaching, lecture notes, practical operations and exercises are the main focus. _x000D_
By studying this course, you should master the basic knowledge and research methods of zooarchaeology, master the structure and characteristics of animal bones and teeth, and be able to use modern comparison specimens to complete the identification of common types of animal remains unearthed from archaeological sites, including animal species, bone parts, age at death, gender, and traces of artificial processing. At the level of theoretical knowledge, by studying and studying cases, we should have an overall understanding of the development of animal resource utilization in the history of human development, and have a more systematic understanding of multiple topics such as hunting and gathering, animal domestication, animals and complex societies. _x000D_
The teaching method adopts a combination of large classes and small classes. Large class classes teach basic knowledge, theories and methods, applied research cases, etc.; small class classes are held in the zooarchaeology laboratory, making full use of various living animal specimens and specimens unearthed from archaeological sites, and combining practice and discussion.

Name: Field Archaeology Practicum
Introduction:
The Field Archaeology Internship is a basic field archaeology practical course for undergraduate and graduate students. The aim is to give students with some basic knowledge of archaeology a real understanding of field methods and techniques for obtaining archaeological information, as well as methods for initial collation and analysis of physical information. The course is based at the Archaeological Expedition Internship Centre of the Neo-Simborg Institute of Archaeology of the University of Beijing. There are currently three sites, one in 8 miles of Danzhou city, Henan province, one in the Qishan Zhou Temple, Xuanxi province, and one in the Shandong Tong Hills. In the following years, special emphasis was placed on the excavation of new stones, during the trade week and during the Qinhan period. The internships have good and complete living and learning conditions.
The course cycle consists of one semester and consists of two phases. The previous phase consisted of two parts, the first of a week-long field survey exercise, which required students to conduct field site surveys, study all field survey methods such as discovery of sites, site ground sweeps, collection of relics, GPS survey of site topography and relics, and documentation of survey contents. The second is a two-month field excavation exercise, in which field participants participate in the excavation of sites, each of which is responsible for the detection of an excavation unit (possibly a probe) and learning the whole process of the field excavation operation, including the clearing of layers, collection of relics, surveying, mapping, recording and familiarization with field databases. The second phase is a two-month-long internal sorting exercise for cleaning, numbering, categorizing, queuing, specialized research, cataloguing, and the preparation of exhumation reports.

Name: Archaeobotany
Introduction: The teaching contents of this course mainly include the research objects and characteristics of archaeological plants, sample collection analysis and data statistical methods, basics of botany, basics of identification of plant remains, current research status of the origin and spread of major crops, and the application of archaeological plants in the study of hunting and gathering societies and complex societies, etc. The teaching content pays equal attention to theory and practice, focusing on training students' practical, data analysis and preliminary research abilities. _x000D_

Name: World Prehistoric Archaeology
Introduction:
This course teaches the evolution and cultural development of prehistoric humans in the overall world pattern. It is divided into seven parts, including introduction, the emergence of the earliest humans, the evolution and cultural development of humans in the early, middle and late Paleolithic Age, as well as issues such as the Paleolithic-Neolithic transition and the origin of agriculture. _x000D_
    In the introduction, a brief history of the development of prehistoric archeology in the world, the geological and chronological background of prehistoric archeology, and the main research topics and methods will be introduced. Then, according to the chronological sequence of prehistoric archeology, the evolution and development of human physique, living style, technology, society and other aspects in different parts of the world from the Early Paleolithic Age to the Neolithic Age are introduced respectively. On this basis, major issues such as the origin and migration of early humans, the emergence and development of modern humans, and the origin of agriculture are taught from a world perspective. _x000D_

Name: Annual Term Paper
Introduction: Thesis is an undergraduate scientific training course, mandatory for third-year students, conducting subject studies under the guidance of mentors and writing academic papers.

Name: Archaeology of Southwest China
Introduction:
Chinese Archeology is a core basic course for undergraduate students in the School of Archeology and Museology of Peking University. After years of construction, the Chinese archaeological framework with the Central Plains region as the core and era as the main line has been basically established. Due to the vast territory of China, there are many differences in the cultural features of various regions. Just as ancient Chinese history has chronological history and local history, in addition to Chinese chronological archeology, there should also be Chinese regional archeology, such as Northeastern archeology, Northern archeology, Northwest archeology, South China archeology and Southwest region, in order to form a complete Chinese archeology. The archeology of southwest China is an important part of regional archeology in China. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Cultural Relics Law and Administration
Introduction: A well-developed legal system and law enforcement tools are powerful measures for the protection of cultural objects. Through studies, firm belief in the protection of cultural objects, knowledge of the legislative history, legislative principles and the legal system of the laws and regulations of China relating to the protection of cultural objects, initial knowledge and understanding of the basic provisions of the law relating to the protection of cultural objects, knowledge of the current situation and difficulties encountered in the protection of contemporary cultural objects in China, and knowledge of the methods used to protect cultural objects by law and other means of protecting cultural objects.

Name: Chinese Archaeology (Part 3-1)
Introduction: In the historical context of the three to five generations of the 10-country period, the course is structured in order of time to teach the city system, the transformation of the burial system and the basic knowledge of the relics and relics of handicrafts, religion and transportation, and to provide an update on the progress of the relevant research, analyse the interaction between archaeological materials and socio-political and cultural interactions, and provide students with basic general knowledge and dynamics of archaeology during the period, as well as with basic capabilities for further academic research in the future.

Name: Chinese Archaeology (Part 3-2)
Prerequisite: Chinese archaeology (next), Wei Jinh-Sun Dynasty and China's ancient history (next), namely, the history of Tang-Mingqing.
Introduction: China ' s archaeology (second part) is that of the Song Won-ming era. It is an archaeological method that explains the historical patterns of the Song Won-ming era through research into the relics and relics of that period. It is a stage in Chinese archaeology divided by generation, which is part of historical archaeology and is currently the latest. They include North Song, South Song, Liao, Kim, Won, and Ming Dynasty, as well as border dynastys such as Xixia, Yu Yi, Huixiang, Dairi, Sai Liao, Heik Khan Dynasty, and Tibet's local regime, represented by the Gug Dynasty. The sites belonging to this period are located in all provinces, municipalities and autonomous regions of the country. The national significance of this is beyond the scope of any of the previous inter-generational archaeology. Moreover, China's archaeology during this period is of greater global and international significance. As China ' s maritime foreign trade developed during this period, a large number of Chinese cultural artefacts of this period were found in many countries around the world to be extremely active in cultural exchanges. The Song Won-ming period was the last stage of China ' s feudal society, during which the political emperor ' s power was greatly expanded and the economy entered a period when the commodity economy was highly developed. This course is an introduction to and exploration of archaeological culture and research in this particular period of history. This includes prefaces, with particular emphasis on the changes and characteristics of archaeological working methods during this period. The archaeological cultural content of the dynasty of Song Liao Won-ming and the border dynasty is divided between the two generations. The elements of the dynasty include the basic archaeological profile and stages of the dynasty, the urban relics (including the capital city, the local city and the military relics), the mausoleums (including the mausoleum, the burial of the officials and the burial of the civilian population) and the artefacts, relics, the mining industry, transport, the cultural arts embodied in archaeological information, the exchange of culture and technology during the period. Taking stock of the historical background, characteristics and research methods of Song Won-ming in the corresponding chapter; The development of the capital city in the Song Wonming period, the type and layout of local cities, the general development and system of handicrafts, etc. A large number of photographs of archaeological discoveries during the period will be presented to the class, as well as appropriate visits to special exhibitions for the period. Through the curriculum, students are taught the basic theory of Song Won-ming archaeology, the framework system, research methods and the corresponding basic knowledge. It goes on to gain an initial understanding of the political system of the societies of the time, as reflected in archaeology, the development of the commodity and urban economies, the level of crafts, artistic achievements and organizational structure of handicrafts and transport. Through this course, students build a system of ambition and interest and acquire a degree of expertise for future specialized research.

Name: Physical Anthropology
Introduction: This course will focus on introducing the characteristics and evolution of human physique from an evolutionary perspective, focusing on the biocultural adaptation of human physique. The course introduces the basic concepts, theories and research methods of physical anthropology, including the evolution of human species, variations in modern human physique, etc. To this end, it first introduces the basis of evolutionary theory and genetic principles, then introduces the characteristics, classification, life and adaptation methods of primates that are closest to human biological relatives, then the evolutionary process of humans and related fossils, and finally the variation of modern human physique. It focuses on the biocultural adaptation of human physique in the context of different cultures and lifestyles, such as the impact of ancient human living environment, diet, nutrition, diseases, exercise patterns, etc. on the physique.

Name: Mediterranean Archaeology
Prerequisite: Students should have an archaeology approach, English base.
Introduction:
"Mediterranean Archeology" is a course for undergraduate students. "Mediterranean Archeology" covers the period from prehistory to the Romans' control of the Mediterranean in time, and geographically covers the areas surrounding the Mediterranean, including parts of Central Asia. _x000D_
The teaching content mainly uses the rich archaeological data in the area to give an introduction to the occurrence and development of ancient Mediterranean civilization with themes such as agriculture, commerce, metallurgy, social organization, early forms, writing, religion, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Archaeology and Social Memory
Introduction: Focusing on archaeological materials, through the comparison of archaeological materials and historical documents, the formation of historical memory is analyzed. It is intended to show how to analyze archaeological materials, understand the writing and application of documents, and initially understand the procedures for archaeological research in historical periods.

Name: Ancient Mongolian History
Introduction: This course focuses on the history of the Mongolian nation from the 13th to the 19th century. The main content is divided into four parts: the history of the Mongolian Empire, the history of Mongolia in the Yuan Dynasty, the history of Mongolia in the Ming Dynasty, and the history of Mongolia in the Qing Dynasty. It focuses on political history and social history, while taking into account cultural history and ethnic relations history. This course aims to enhance students' comprehensive understanding of ancient Mongolian history, further deepen the content of ancient Chinese history teaching on Mongolian history and northern ethnic history, and inspire students to use more systematic knowledge to analyze various historical and practical issues related to the Mongolian nation.

Name: Foreign Constitutional Law
Introduction: This course focuses on the United States Constitution. The course content is divided into two parts: the first part focuses on power and will take a longitudinal perspective and discuss the development of the United States' constitution in historical order from independence, founding, constitution-making, Civil War and Reconstruction, the New Deal, the civil rights movement, the revival of conservatism, to contemporary times. The second part focuses on rights and will discuss issues such as freedom, privacy, and equality based on jurisprudence in related fields.

Name: Ancient Chinese Bronzes
Introduction:
This course teaches the development and evolution of bronze ware shapes, patterns and inscriptions during the Xia, Shang and Zhou dynasties, and introduces the stages of bronze ware_x000D_
Dating methods and results, bronze ware zoning research status, and some methods and results of bronze ware special research.

Name: The College Experience and Student Development
Introduction: This course is designed for all undergraduate students in the school (especially junior students). This course is divided into 3 modules [1] The development and evolution of higher education, [2] Related theories and empirical research on the influence of higher education and student development, [3] Analysis of successful student experience cases and their own planning. The course first provides a basic theoretical thinking perspective and framework for scientific planning and design of one's own university study and life experience through the study of theoretical and empirical research on the development process and functions of higher education, the influence of higher education and student development. On this basis, the course will use group research to discover various effective teaching resources on campus, collect "successful cases" of student experiences around them, use relevant theories to analyze the influencing mechanisms behind the cases, and provide important reference and inspiration for students to plan their future campus experiences.

Name: Law and Artificial Intelligence
Introduction: On July 20, 2017, the State Council pointed out in the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan" that after more than 60 years of evolution, the development of artificial intelligence has entered a new stage, especially driven by new theories and technologies such as the mobile Internet, big data, supercomputing, sensor networks, brain science, and the strong demand for economic and social development. In the foreseeable future, the rapid development of artificial intelligence will profoundly change human social life and the world. It is worth noting that in this far-sighted national artificial intelligence strategic plan, the country has released many important signals for the development of law and artificial intelligence: first, the new plan supports the application of artificial intelligence in judicial work and legal services; second, the new plan emphasizes that while developing artificial intelligence, it attaches great importance to the research of relevant legal, ethical and social issues, and establishes artificial intelligence laws, regulations, ethical norms and policy systems; finally, the new plan proposes a new model of "artificial intelligence + This course is a preliminary response to the implementation of the "New Generation Artificial Intelligence Development Plan" in the legal field. It is mainly divided into three parts: The first part will briefly introduce the background of the rise of artificial intelligence and its application in various vertical fields; the second part will focus on the application of artificial intelligence in the legal industry, including applications in the judicial field and the legal service industry, as well as the impact of artificial intelligence on legal education and legal research; the third part will explore the relationship between artificial intelligence and law, ethics, society, employment, etc., focusing on the regulatory issues of artificial intelligence.

Name: History of Western Art (Part 2)
Prerequisite: The General History of Western Fine Arts.
Introduction: This course continues from "History of Western Art" and teaches the history of Western art from the Renaissance to the 20th century. Through the study and discussion of various art forms such as painting, sculpture, and architecture, students can understand the main periods, schools, and painters in Western art in the past 700 years, and then become familiar with the vocabulary and context of Western art.

Name: Archaeology of Ancient Peoples
Introduction:
China is a multi-ethnic country, which is the result of the long-term development and integration of ancient ethnic groups within China. Archeology is particularly advantageous in revealing the ancient material cultural relics of these peoples. It can conduct further research on the social organizational structure, human behavior, religious consciousness, cultural concepts, ethnic origin, etc. of ancient peoples based on detailed analysis of archaeological data and combined with research from other disciplines. _x000D_
This course first introduces the concept of ancient ethnic archeology, research objects and fields, as well as research status and methods, etc.; then it introduces the archaeological cultural remains of ancient ethnic groups in my country in multiple topics. _x000D_
The teaching purpose of this course is to enable undergraduates in archeology and related majors to understand the main content and latest research results of ancient ethnic archeology, to master the main content of the identified archaeological remains of ancient ethnic groups, as well as the main characteristics of the remains related to ethnic activities, to have a general understanding of the characteristics and research progress of ancient ethnic archaeological remains, and to provide the accumulation of basic knowledge for future research in this field and grassroots archaeological work.

Name: Introduction to Chinese Historic Architecture
Introduction: Chinese cultural relics buildings have a long history and rich cultural connotations, and are witnesses of Chinese history and culture. Through classroom lectures and course paper exercises, this course enables students to clarify the definition, connotation and related basic policies and regulations of Chinese cultural heritage buildings; understand the research purpose, significance and relationship between cultural heritage buildings and the development of Chinese society; understand the basic types, classic examples and overall development context of Chinese cultural heritage buildings; understand the research history, main research fields, research theories, methods, academic resources and major hot issues of cultural heritage buildings. Through case teaching and on-site investigation, students are cultivated to be interested in learning and protecting cultural relics and buildings, and to master the basic ability to engage in research, laying a good foundation for further study in the future.

Name: Introduction to Architecture
Introduction:
This course is the most basic course in architecture. The preliminary teaching and training content of architecture should help students initially establish a basic understanding of architecture; establish an understanding of architectural historical theories and types, building materials, building structures, architectural aesthetics and other factors. Through lectures and a large number of hands-on exercises, students can master the expression techniques and model making of architectural paintings, and master the basic methods of form composition. On this basis, students can have a comprehensive understanding of the architectural design process. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Drawing
Introduction: Sketching is the basis of painting modeling. Through the study and training of plaster and still life, architecture and landscape, students learn to use simple visual form language to describe, record and express objective objects, understand and master the modeling rules and rules of painting art, basic skills and techniques, improve students' aesthetic level and literacy, stimulate emotions, activate thinking, and improve creativity.

Name: Computer Fundamentals for the Humanities (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Computer Fundamentals (Part 1) consists of modules such as basic computer knowledge, computer operating systems and their use, multimedia knowledge and application basics, graphics and image production and processing basics, office software applications, computer network basics, Internet basic applications, information retrieval and utilization basics, and databases.

Name: Architectural Design (I)
Introduction: Architectural Design (1) is the introductory stage of architectural design. Through learning, students can initially master the basic principles, methods and steps of architectural design. Cultivate students' functional awareness, spatial awareness, construction awareness and environmental awareness. Learn how to combine architectural spaces. Master certain architectural expression techniques: process analysis, sketches at each stage, and models, which are the expression of results.

Name: Fundamentals of Color in Art
Introduction: The color class is a basic course in architectural art. It is expressed in two forms: watercolor and gouache. The painting form is mainly sketching. The teaching content focuses on outdoor architecture and scenery, so that students can more comprehensively grasp the relationship between color characteristics and expression techniques. The painting method adheres to a realistic style, guiding students to better understand the objective world, solidly training basic skills, opening students' thinking, stimulating emotions, and entering into the creation of architectural landscape color paintings.

Name: History of Chinese Architecture (Part 1)
Introduction:
This course systematically introduces the development process of ancient Chinese architecture by sorting out the existing architectural heritage on the ground in China and the architectural sites or architectural images found in archaeology, and discusses the status of ancient Chinese architecture in the history of world architecture, the relationship between ancient Chinese architecture and the natural environment, and the achievements of ancient Chinese architecture in various eras. _x000D_
This course is mainly based on classroom lectures, supplemented by physical models, field visits, classroom discussions, etc., to allow students to understand the technical and artistic characteristics of Chinese architecture, and to stimulate students' strong interest in further learning Chinese ancient architecture. _x000D_

Name: The Contemporary American Novel
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will focus on introducing contemporary American novels to students, leading students to read three novels, and study the characterization, plot development, themes, writing style, etc. in the specific cultural and historical background of the works. In addition to analyzing the work, students will have writing assignments to deepen their understanding of the novel's themes. The course content also includes literary writing skills, reading and comprehension skills, in-depth reading suggestions, etc.

Name: Architectural Design (II)
Introduction: Architectural Design (II) is the stage of continuous improvement of architectural design. Through learning, students can further cultivate their correct design ideas and working methods; focus on strengthening students’ understanding of the three major relationships between function and space, architecture and environment, and materials and components; giving appropriate consideration to different types and spaces. While combining time, it further trains students' ability to comprehensively solve complex problems; develop the habit of research and data collection; improve the expressive ability of architectural design, including the selection of appropriate drawing methods, diagrams, research models, design descriptions and content rearrangements, and the expressive ability of program introduction.

Name: Computer-Aided Architectural Drafting
Introduction:
"Computer Architectural Drawing" is a basic practical course for major majors and a course for basic education in architectural drawing and computers. It is divided into several main parts:_x000D_
(1) This course mainly covers the basic knowledge and operating skills of the AutoCAD system. The purpose of this course is to enable students to start from the basic concepts of computer-aided architectural design, master the drawing methods and techniques of computer architectural design drawings, and improve students' computer application level, comprehensive skills and practical ability. Lay the foundation for students to adapt to social needs. _x000D_
(2) Use 3DSMAX software to design courses for creating architectural decoration renderings and browsing animation works, cultivate students' ability to use computers to create indoor and outdoor architectural renderings and browse animation works, analyze and solve problems, and strengthen and consolidate the basic concepts and basic knowledge of the courses students have learned. Then, through analysis and research work, students will develop their ability to do scientific research, and achieve the creative ability to use computers to draw indoor and outdoor architectural renderings and browse animation works. _x000D_
(3) Use PHtoshop software for post-production of architectural decoration renderings, cultivate students' ability to use computers to create indoor and outdoor architectural renderings, and strengthen the contrast of light, shadow, distance, virtual and real, and relatively correct scale relationships based on architectural knowledge. _x000D_
(4) Use sketchup for architectural rough model analysis, real-time rendering and virtual tour of the building. _x000D_
(5) Understand the modeling of BIM software such as Revit and grasshopper Rhnion. _x000D_

Name: Modern Building Construction and Structural Selection
Introduction:
The course is divided into two parts: structural selection and building construction. _x000D_
The structure selection part introduces the basic concepts of building structure design, focusing on the overall structure design method. Starting from the structural system, aiming at the rationality and economy of the structure, it introduces the concepts and preliminary calculation methods of the geometric form of the building structure, vertical sub-systems, horizontal structural sub-systems, foundations and other structural parts. Through the study of this course, students can help students master the main factors affecting each part of the structure, establish an overall concept of the structure, and lay the foundation for the preliminary design of the building structure. _x000D_
The building construction section teaches the principles and methods of building construction. Through learning, students can understand and initially master the construction principles and construction methods of a large number of components of civil buildings (foundations, walls or columns, floors, stairs, doors, windows, roofs, etc.). Through the study of three aspects: building materials, structural systems, structural nodes and detail processing, students can have a deeper understanding of the design and construction of buildings.

Name: History of Chinese Architecture (Part 2)
Introduction: Through the study of architectural technology and architectural art, students can understand the basic characteristics and main types of Chinese architecture; through the study of archaeological materials and classical documents, students can also understand the "Tao of Chinese Architecture". Using ground construction data, unearthed archaeological data and various documents, we systematically introduce important issues, important research fields and related research methods in the development process of ancient Chinese architecture. It aims to guide students to comprehensively engage with important research issues, methods and theories in the field of Chinese architectural history, and initially establish an understanding of architectural archaeological theories and methods. Through a series of classroom teaching, after-class readings, classroom discussions and field trips on special topics, students can understand Chinese architecture, and further understand people and think about the wisdom and technological philosophy embodied in ancient Chinese architecture, as well as the social and historical significance it reflects. _x000D_

Name: Architectural Design (III)
Introduction: This semester's architectural design course is the stage of improvement and development of architectural design. Through two design topics (such as visitor center, heritage museum), starting from understanding the background of the design object and consulting literature, we will learn the design techniques of excellent Chinese and foreign heritage sites and heritage buildings, understand the principles of new architectural creation in heritage sites, and achieve an organic combination of heritage protection and utilization; further strengthen the study of design methods and basic design skills, and master the basic requirements for small-scale architectural design in complex environments (mountainous environments). _x000D_

Name: Traditional Chinese Architectural Construction
Prerequisite: China ' s history of architecture, computer mapping and performance
Introduction:
The course on traditional architecture in China is designed to provide students with the names and shapes of the components of the ancient Chinese buildings of Tang Song and Ming Qing, and of small wood, through a combination of literature and examples, as well as drawing and modelling practices. It identifies the basic patterns of the evolution of building formations and learns about the legacy of classic architecture and the basics of the specialized literature, such as Building French, Building French Notes and Qingueue Building Rules.
The course focuses on classroom teaching, conducting tests in the classroom, consolidating the foundation, setting up after-school work, arranging for students to read literature, making the contents of the teaching available to students in the form of hand-drawing and computer modelling, evaluating their work in the classroom and organizing discussions. Finally, in conjunction with short-term field trips, the capacity of students to conduct comprehensive research on literature and on what remains is being deepened, and students are required to submit study reports at the end of the school term.
In a variety of teaching methods, the curriculum mobilizes students ' initiative and motivation, equips them with the basic knowledge of the ancient architecture of China and gives them an initial sense of history and change, discovers the pleasures of exploration and the weight of history in the course of learning in time and space, and lays the foundation for the next phase of field practice teaching.

Name: General Survey of Ancient Roman Archaeology and Art
Prerequisite: Students should have an archaeology approach, English base.
Introduction: This course is designed for students beginning the study of Roman archeology. The course covers an introduction to the archeology, architecture, and art of ancient Rome. This era, named after the main historical figures, began with Italian culture under Rome (10th century BC) and covered the Roman Kingdom, the Roman Republic, the Roman Empire, and the fall of the Western Roman Empire in the 5th century AD. The areas of focus are the Mediterranean basin, Italy, and the provinces of the Roman Empire at that time.

Name: Cultural Heritage Field Survey and Mapping Practicum
Introduction:
The main elements of this course are to lead students in the field to observe, document, map and map the south and north of China during the main historical periods, not less than a hundred typical cases of cultural heritage in cities, temples, homes, gardens and parks and the civil service, to deepen through fieldwork the students ' awareness of the commons and characteristics of cultural heritage of different historical periods, different geographical regions and different types, to gain a good knowledge of the methods of observation and documentation of the field of cultural heritage, to develop a comprehensive, rigorous and standardized field data collection and subsequent compilation and compilation of reports, to accumulate first-hand research materials, to familiarize themselves with the use and operational skills of various mapping instruments, to acquire a good knowledge of the methods and processes of mapping cultural heritage, and to develop a capacity for teamwork.
The course is divided into three stages, i.e., the first stage of preparation of the information and skills for the field, with a focus on classroom teaching and practice, and the purpose, meaning, requirements and basic course of the course, as well as the principles and methods of use of the main tools. The second phase involves field mapping and mapping, in which the main elements of the training are methods of observing and documenting, as fully as possible within the unit time, the body of antiquities and its various environmental factors. The mapping component emphasizes the development of students ' capacities in the preparation, measurement and presentation of drawings of the architectural body of cultural objects. The third phase, which is a later stage, emphasizes the development of the capacity of students to prepare logical and informative hands-on reports and ultimately to produce maps. In each of the above stages of teaching, teaching, practice and summing up have been organized in a combination of teaching and learning.
The objective of this course is to enable students to meet professional requirements in terms of competence and interest, through an internship period, and to lay the capacity and psychological foundation for future work in the protection of national cultural objects.

Name: Cultural Heritage Conservation Practicum
Prerequisite: Cultural Heritage Field Survey and Mapping Practicum
Introduction:
This course focuses on practical and applied training based on theoretical learning. Under normal circumstances, this course will be carried out in conjunction with our school's cultural heritage teaching bases in Hangzhou, Shanxi and other places. Real cultural heritage building protection topics will be selected to train students to comprehensively apply the knowledge and skills learned in previous professional courses to achieve the results required for cultural relics work under real working environments and requirements, and apply them to cultural relics protection work. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students can not only improve their ability to comprehensively apply knowledge to solve practical problems, but also experience the work experience and mission of cultural relics workers, clarify their professional aspirations, understand the actual situation of cultural heritage protection, and lay a practical foundation for further theoretical learning. _x000D_

Name: Theory and Methods of Cultural Heritage Conservation Planning and Design
Prerequisite: Architectural design, traditional construction in China
Introduction:
China's long history has left behind hundreds of thousands of various immovable cultural relics that have witnessed the development and evolution of Chinese civilization. The protection of historical and cultural heritage faces various practical challenges. Since the 1990s, cultural relics protection has shown a vigorous development trend in both academic construction and practical work. Among them, large-scale site protection planning has become an indispensable practical link in cultural relics protection. _x000D_
The theory and practice course of cultural heritage protection planning and design starts from the actual needs and problems of China's cultural heritage protection, and uses theoretical teaching, case teaching and design practice to enable students to understand the problems and status quo, concepts and countermeasures of cultural heritage protection, and build a multi-disciplinary comprehensive knowledge system, so as to master the ability to discover, research and solve practical problems from the perspective of cultural heritage protection, and meet the needs of China's cultural heritage protection. _x000D_

Name: Cost Estimation for Traditional Architecture
Introduction: This course is based on teaching the principles, steps, methods and techniques of construction project quotation, project quantity calculation and preparation of project documents, combined with the characteristics of traditional architecture, preparing traditional construction project budgets, and cultivating students' ability to comprehensively apply the basic theories and technical knowledge they have learned to solve practical engineering problems.

Name: Western Philosophy (Part 2)
Introduction: The course focuses on mainstream thinking and concepts of contemporary Western philosophy. Given that contemporary Western philosophy is divided into two distinct types of style and sense, the curriculum is divided into two relatively separate sections, the continental European philosophy and analytical philosophy. Its main elements are, respectively, the main concerns of continental philosophy and the ideologue, and the analysis of philosophy and, in particular, the main concerns of linguistic philosophy, as well as strategies for solving them.

Name: History of Foreign Architecture
Introduction: The course on the history of foreign ancient architecture will take the history of ancient Japanese architecture as its theme. This course aims to provide students with an overall understanding of the relationship between Sino-Japanese architectural culture exchanges by narrating the history of ancient Japanese architecture, starting from the vertical and horizontal sections of architectural history, and thereby understanding the respective characteristics of each country's architecture in the East Asian wooden architecture cultural circle. This course also aims to cultivate students' historical awareness and perspective, and promote students' in-depth understanding of ancient Chinese architecture through their understanding of the ancient architectural history of neighboring countries.

Name: Marxist Philosophy (Part 1)
Introduction:
This course strives to demonstrate the broad scope of Marxist philosophical research and implement the following basic principles:_x000D_
(1) Adopt a comprehensive approach of "history", "theory" and "writing" (based on "history" and "writing" and focus on "theory") to comprehensively introduce the basic knowledge, basic documents and basic theories of Marxist philosophy;_x000D_
(2) Based on contemporary perspectives, guide students to understand cutting-edge issues in Marxist philosophical research;_x000D_
(3) In accordance with the principle of integrating academic and practicality, focus on researching and answering major theoretical questions raised by contemporary practice to Marxist philosophy;_x000D_
(4) Promote teacher-student interaction and two-way communication, and strive to improve students' enthusiasm for learning and enhance their philosophical thinking ability and theoretical acumen through classroom discussions and extracurricular reading guidance.

Name: Nutrition and Disease
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
If you have nutrition, you will be healthy. Good nutrition can prevent the occurrence of diseases. Chronic diseases such as diabetes, hypertension, obesity, etc., whose incidence rates have increased significantly in recent years, are mainly caused by unreasonable diet. One-third of cancers are related to diet. Surveys have found that good nutritional status can enhance the body's immunity and prevent the occurrence of infectious diseases. _x000D_
With the improvement of living standards, people pay more attention to nutrition. A survey last year found that medical-related professionals and clinicians lacked nutritional knowledge, and the general public even lacked scientific nutritional knowledge. This course has been offered as an on-campus and inter-campus elective at the Peking University School of Medicine for 10 years. Name: Qing Dynasty Scholarship and Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is different from previous literary history routines. It will re-examine the new changes in the classical poetry tradition in the Qing Dynasty from the perspective of the history of academic thought. It aims to guide students to return to the academic scene where the scribes of the Qing Dynasty lived and understand the special environment of humanities creation. _x000D_
The Qing Dynasty (1616/1644-1911) was the last dynasty of imperial China. It was not only the culmination of classical tradition, but also the beginning of modern times. The expansion of the multi-ethnic country in the Qing Dynasty established the territory of today's China and was the direct source of the consciousness of "China" in the national sense in modern times. The Qing Dynasty ideologically inherited the remnants of Neo-Confucianism from the Song and Ming dynasties, but was subject to the control of foreign imperial powers. It mainly played a role in educating the grassroots. On the other hand, it developed a new way of textual research in Sinology, using the exegesis of famous objects as a method, replacing "Neo-Confucianism" with "rituals", and creating a new academic paradigm, which formed the external context of poetic expression and literary criticism in this period. _x000D_
From the study of economics in the early Qing Dynasty, textual criticism during the Qian and Jiaqing periods, to the new study after Daoxian, the Qing Dynasty had a great academic boom, and poetry collections also showed a new look different from those of the previous generation. In the late Qing Dynasty, Zhang Zhidong once concluded that the Qing Dynasty anthology was "more practical than ancient collections"; after the Republic of China, bibliographer Wang Chongmin also pointed out that "the Qing Dynasty anthology is a collection of ancient and modern scholarship." The changes in Jibu studies in the Qing Dynasty are naturally related to academics, and the anthology itself is the carrier of textual research. In the Qing Dynasty, the literary standards of the Qing Dynasty were "pure, elegant, and upright." Ancient prose spread throughout the country under the promotion of scholars, teachers, and officials. The name "parallel prose" also came from the Qing people, and derived from the "classical Chinese" theory that was highly praised by sinologists during the Qian and Jiaqing Dynasties. These new changes in article studies are all driven by academic forces. They may be related to the secularization, grassroots, and practical trends of Neo-Confucianism since the late Ming Dynasty. They may originate from the reaction of the textual research trend, or they may benefit from the development of phonological exegesis. In terms of poetics, the Zong-Song poetry style disappeared and reappeared throughout the Qing Dynasty. The rise of "scholar's poetry" and "Tongguang style" in the late Qing Dynasty also reflected the new academic trend. Even novels such as "The Scholars" and "A Dream of Red Mansions" also reflect the paradigm evolution from "Neo-Confucianism" to "Etiquette". _x000D_
The entanglement between scholarship and literature in the Qing Dynasty was not only the synthesis of the literary and historical traditions of previous generations on the timeline, but also the product of the collision, dialogue, and integration of Chinese and foreign academic cultures. After the middle of the Qing Dynasty, the world situation changed drastically, and Western learning came with strong ships and guns, which had a huge impact on China's inherent social structure, academic thought, moral ethics, and literary expression. Especially with the introduction of modern Western literary concepts and literary history writing styles, literary education in the modern sense was gradually established, and new knowledge systems surrounding literature such as aesthetics, grammar, and rhetoric were successively introduced, which greatly changed the face of poetry creation and literary criticism. In this regard, the symbiotic relationship between scholarship and literature in the Qing Dynasty is a "direct and present tradition" that deserves a deeper understanding. _x000D_

In fact, as a research category in the history of philosophy in modern times, early intellectual historical materials cannot be regarded as “philosophical texts” by default, but are in urgent need of some kind of systematic argumentation that is inherent in traditional scholarship. Otherwise, we can neither determine the historical starting point of Chinese philosophy nor self-consistently explain whether early documents have philosophical significance. Being familiar with this method and its cutting-edge status in contemporary sociology is the third teaching goal of this course. _x000D_

Name: History of Western Political Thought (Part 2)
Introduction: This course introduces the main representatives, schools of thought and theoretical issues in contemporary Western political thought. It adopts a point-to-point approach to enable students to gain a basic understanding of the general development direction of contemporary Western political thought and at the same time form their own views on some core issues of contemporary political philosophy. At the same time, through the study of this course, students' theoretical thinking and logical abilities should be further strengthened.

Name: Social Science Literature Resources and Retrieval
Introduction:
The "documentary information resources" involved in this course are documentary information resources produced in China. In terms of time, it covers the past and present; in terms of carrier form, it includes paper documents and electronic resources; in terms of resource type, it includes the main sources of documentary information accumulated in the field of humanities and social sciences in China so far. _x000D_
    The literature information resource retrieval tools involved in this course are mainly the main types and main varieties in the existing Chinese retrieval tool system, including traditional printed retrieval tools, as well as electronic and online retrieval tools based on computers and network environments. _x000D_
    The main content of this course includes: an overview of Chinese humanities and social science literature information resources; the generation and evolution, content and characteristics, functions and distribution of main types of literature information resources; an overview of the Chinese search tool system; search of dictionary resources and Chinese words; ancient book resources and basics Full-text retrieval system for this ancient book; bibliographic retrieval tools and electronic book systems; digital newspaper and periodical resources and their retrieval systems; review of current affairs information resources and facts, data, and regulations; ideas and strategies, principles and methods, ethics and norms for retrieval and utilization of relevant literature information resources.

Name: Traditional Chinese Political Institutions
Introduction:
Traditional China is a community with a vast territory, a long history, and a national republic. Traditional China's political system is extremely rich, mature and developed. _x000D_
The scope covered by this course starts from the Zhou and Qin Dynasties to the Ming and Qing Dynasties. It mainly includes topics such as introduction, emperor system, prime minister system and civil service system, feudal system and county system, electoral system and imperial examination system, squire system, reform and restructuring, etc. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to National Security Studies
Introduction:
In April 2018, the Ministry of Education issued the "Implementation Opinions of the Ministry of Education on Strengthening National Security Education in Universities, Secondary Schools and Primary Schools" and decided to establish a first-level discipline of national security studies in colleges and universities in my country. This decision is the continuation of a series of important national security measures in my country in recent years. Particularly important nodes include the establishment of the Central National Security Commission, General Secretary Xi Jinping’s overall national security concept, the promulgation of the National Security Law, the review and approval of the National Security Strategy Outline by the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, and the holding of National Security Education Day activities. Under the overall security concept and guidance and the leadership of the Central National Security Commission, my country's national security ideological and theoretical system, supporting system design, legal infrastructure, overall coordination and planning, and education and publicity in the new era have made significant progress and achievements. _x000D_
      "Introduction to National Security" will introduce and discuss important issues at different levels under the overall national security concept: the ideological, theoretical and historical origins of overall national security; the cognition, construction and realization guarantee of national security; the political mechanism, management model, policy process and interaction of relevant actors of overall national security; the military, diplomatic, economic, industrial, psychological, public opinion, intelligence, geographical and other dimensions of overall national security; the contribution of major policy initiatives such as the "One Belt and One Road" to overall national security; future opportunities and challenges of overall national security research and policy, etc. After passing this course, students should initially have the ability to understand and analyze overall national security theory and practice. At the same time, this course will provide students who are interested in research and practice in the field of national security with the direction and space for further in-depth thinking and study. _x000D_
       This course will adopt a "platter" teaching model by multiple teachers, giving full play to the faculty advantages of the School of International Relations at Peking University in various fields related to national security, rationally allocating resources and expertise, and combining forces to explore national security opportunities and challenges in the "big changes unseen in a century" and provide students with a full spectrum of national security introduction and training. This course will be a combination of large lectures by teachers and small class discussions by teaching assistants, supplemented by group research reports, personal reading reports, multimedia resource sharing and other teaching methods. Some special chapters will invite extracurricular experts, scholars and senior officials in related fields to give special lectures. For group research projects with academic and policy innovation, the course will provide financial and other resource support on a case-by-case basis. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to World Socialism
Introduction: This course systematically describes the occurrence and development of the world socialist movement from the three levels of ideological trend, movement and system. It focuses on the emergence and development of Marxism and the emergence and development of the international communist movement under the banner of Marxism. It analyzes the reasons for the twists and turns of the world socialist movement and summarizes its important experiences and lessons. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Western Diplomatic Thought
Introduction: The course focuses on the origins of European and American (so-called “Western”) diplomatic thought. By sorting out the ideological context of Western politics and inter-state politics, we can clarify the origin and development of Western diplomatic thought. The development of Western diplomatic thought, which is rooted in Western political culture and history, has basically gone through ancient, modern and contemporary stages of development. In order to understand the ideological foundation of contemporary Western diplomacy, we must review the development process of Western political thought. Although it is generally believed that Western diplomacy began with the Thirty Years' War (1618-1648), the development of European civilization is an inseparable inheritance and evolution process with obvious stage characteristics. Therefore, this course strongly recommends and requires everyone to study the history and culture of the European Enlightenment period and before, especially the political culture. Otherwise, the understanding of Western diplomatic thoughts will become water without a source. Although it can stir people's hearts, it will ultimately be swaying without knowing why.

Name: Democracy in History and Practice
Prerequisite: Candidates need to have studied Political Science and China Political General.
Introduction: Democracy is the most important political phenomenon in the contemporary world and the central subject of contemporary political science discussions. The course will focus on the historical trajectories and realities of democratic development and will outline the basic concepts of democracy, the main theories and the relationship between democracy and economic development, social structures, political culture, national capacity, etc. On that basis, modern Western democracy is being reflected and the necessary intellectual reserves are being made available to recognize and discuss the political development of contemporary China.

Name: The Visual Bible: Christianity in Western Art
Introduction:
Course Introduction:_x000D_
The close relationship between religion and art goes all the way back to prehistoric cultures. For Western art in history, whether it is painting, sculpture, architecture and music, they are closely related to the development of religious culture. Looking at the history of art from a scientific perspective, in addition to partly reflecting the social, political, economic, religious, cultural and war history at that time, the important thing is that it reflects the history of human visual cognition and the description of the process of human visual cognition using self-created visual forms and symbols. Although Christianity is not a major religion in China, with China's reform and opening up, Christian cultural phenomena have become ubiquitous: people often quote idioms and concepts from the Bible in their daily lives; their lifestyles have also been affected, so much so that some Christian festivals have almost become national festivals. The achievements of Christian art in music, drama, film, painting, sculpture and architecture have attracted the attention of intellectuals. In modern civilized society, the relationship between scientific rationality and faith maintains a dynamic balance in people's spiritual world. Science tells us: Science cannot explain all problems. Name: Comparative Studies of Modern Bureaucratic Systems
Prerequisite: History of Western political thought, general political science, general Chinese politics.
Introduction: This course, which is aimed primarily at senior undergraduate students at the International Relations Institute, aims at providing students with a clearer understanding of modern bureaucracy by means of classroom teaching, classroom discussions and student self-study. In terms of content, comparisons are made, mainly through comparative methods, between the totalitarian bureaucracy of the Soviet Union, the civilian system of modern Western countries and the stratification of contemporary China, and the related bureaucratic theories are interpreted and evaluated. The bureaucracy used in this course is a neutral concept, referring to the system of executive authority established by the division of functions and posts, and the principle of hierarchical management. The bureaucracy was initially used to describe the form of government in Prussia. It was later understood as a derogatory bureaucratic administrative system. At the beginning of the twentieth century, German sociologist Weber used bureaucracy as a synonym for the “reasonable social system”. He argued that there were three types of authority to govern human society: traditional authority, super glamorous authority, legal and rational authority, both based on bureaucracy. There are three main forms of modern bureaucracy: the civilian system of modern Western countries. After the bourgeois democratic revolution, the rule of law in Western countries became more and more well organized, and a formal civil service was established, at a time when a well-developed bureaucracy had become an essential tool for sustaining real society. Modern bureaucracy is usually marked by an Order in Council, issued by the British Government on 4 June 1870, formally establishing an open competitive examination system. Its formation and creation partly met the desire of the emerging industrial bourgeois class to adapt the State apparatus to and protect productivity development, and were soon adopted by capitalist nations. Canada and the United States, under British influence, established their own civilian systems in 1882 and 1883, respectively. Germany, France, Japan have long maintained a feudal bureaucracy, and it was only after the Second World War that a modern civilian system was truly established. The examinations, appointments, administration, rights and duties of civil servants at all levels in the capitalist countries and retirements have formed a set of institutions and institutions aimed at the selection of good people, the improvement of administrative efficiency and the preservation of the capitalist system. The second is the totalitarian bureaucracy of the Soviet Union. Since the bureaucracy under the old system, as part of the State apparatus, was a tool for the domination of the class to exploit and oppress the people, Marx Engles made the abandonment of bureaucracy and the prevention of the bureaucracy of the socialist regime one of the important features of the socialist system. However, in real socialist practice, due to the premature conditions of the socialist revolution, the Soviet Union established a special bureaucracy, unlike the old one, which ran counter to the original socialist idea of Max Engles and was also described as a totalitarian bureaucracy. From the perspective of the modernization process of the Soviet Union and the effectiveness of socialist construction, the so-called so-called Russian bureaucracy has been mixed. On the one hand, these countries have rapidly accumulated the material conditions for industrialization through a strong bureaucratic State apparatus and, in the short term, have completed a centuries-old process of industrialization in Western countries, which has resulted in a faster improvement in the material standard of living and level of literacy of the population. On the other hand, with increasing bureaucracy among party officials, the socialist regimes in these countries are experiencing a serious crisis, mainly as a result of bureaucratic management that slows down and stagnates the growth of the economy; the population cannot reasonably share in the results of modernization because of the political, economic and cultural monopoly of officials and the gradual loss of confidence in socialism and the Communist Party. In the end, Sudong broke out. Following the dramatic transformation of the Soviet Union, the fight against bureaucracy became the most important and profound lesson learned by the existing socialist countries from the socialist practice of the former Soviet Union. Third is Chinese science. Since the establishment of the new China, China has followed the political model of the Soviet Union and stabilized its regime by establishing a system of science. The establishment of the system of sciences has contributed significantly to the stability of the country and its rapid transition to full-scale economic construction, but as its own development gradually begins to harm society, Maoist discontent with bureaucracy and its attempts to break the grip of the system on the State power are among the main reasons for its decision to launch a cultural revolution. The decade-long cultural revolution has caused considerable damage to the science system that was built after the establishment of the new China, but has also plunged China into turmoil. In order to repair the devastation caused by the Cultural Revolution and stabilize the country and develop its economy, Deng Xiaoping had to rely once again on the science-level system, which, after 1978, quickly re-established China ' s severely damaged science-level system, which quickly transferred the country to economic construction. At the same time as the rapid development of the country has been facilitated, the stratification has also brought about a number of negative problems. How best to prevent the formation of bureaucratic privilege groups within the hierarchy and the emergence of Chinese-style socialistism into authoritarian capitalism is key to the stability of Chinese society. In the process of the creation and development of modern bureaucracy, many theories have emerged that reflect bureaucracy. For example, there have been bureaucratic theories in Marx, Weber, Trotsky, Gilas and others.

Name: Christianity and Chinese Culture
Introduction:
This undergraduate course briefly introduces the history of the spread and development of Christianity in China since it was introduced to China in the Tang Dynasty, and uses the historical context_x000D_
Taking the interaction between Christianity and Chinese culture in Yuzhong as the starting point, we explore the following questions: Is there _x000D_ in Chinese culture?

Possible contribution? What is the ideological mechanism by which the interaction between the two produces creative cultural results?

Name: New Zealand History and Culture
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: New Zealand History and Culture is a cultural and language quality course taught entirely in English for Peking University undergraduates. This course is supported by the New Zealand Center of Peking University. Professors from Massey University in New Zealand and other universities are invited to give guest lectures. Teacher Liu Hongzhong provides comments and is responsible for the format of each teaching link of the course. This course aims to introduce and analyze the history and culture of New Zealand from a global perspective. The content is divided into topics, allowing students to have a more comprehensive understanding of New Zealand's history, culture and society, as well as the development profile of education, technology, environment, media, film industry, etc. The course content will be mainly composed of handouts, special lectures, movies, etc., and will use both classroom lectures and group discussions as the main methods. This course also encourages students to attend the New Zealand lecture series hosted by the New Zealand Center of Peking University and the New Zealand film screening series. This course has special Q&A time. Students are welcome to borrow books and magazines from the New Zealand Center. New Zealand scholars, experts, and New Zealand international students are invited from time to time to enter the classroom to interact with students and provide students with more learning opportunities. Through the study of this course, students can not only learn how to enter preliminary research on a certain subject, but also improve their practical abilities in English listening, speaking, reading, and writing in a relaxed and lively learning process, learn to adapt to the teaching methods of Western universities, and cultivate students' ability to study and research from the dual perspectives of globalization and diversification. It is especially suitable for students who are interested in comprehensively improving their English proficiency, entering English major courses, or studying abroad.

Name: History of Sino-Japanese Relations
Introduction: On the basis of briefly summarizing the important issues in Sino-Japanese relations in ancient and modern times and clarifying the basic context of the history of Sino-Japanese relations, this course focuses on elaborating on the development process and major events of Sino-Japanese relations after World War II, exploring and analyzing major issues in Sino-Japanese relations, the interaction between Sino-Japanese relations and regional and international relations, Japan's policy towards China and China's policies towards Japan, as well as the relevant research status of Sino-Japanese relations, so that students can systematically and comprehensively understand the basic historical facts, development changes and important issues of Sino-Japanese relations, cultivate analytical skills and lay a solid professional foundation.

Name: Political Economy Analysis of Global Governance
Introduction: The course content will conduct a political and economic analysis of global governance from three levels: the first is the historical level, which explores the historical process and theoretical evolution of global governance; the second level is the national level, which explores the interactive relationship between nation-states and global governance; and the third level is the global level, which explores the structure of global governance and its impact on the global political and economic order.

Name: Non-Governmental Diplomacy
Introduction: Modern diplomacy has broken through traditional and monopolistic government diplomacy, which has increasingly evolved into a general diplomacy that includes both governmental and non-governmental diplomacy. What does non-governmental diplomacy mean? What is its “independence” nature? What are the challenges that non-governmental diplomacy poses to government diplomacy and itself? Such issues have become an urgent new subject of modern diplomacy. The course seeks to provide a more comprehensive view and description of non-governmental diplomacy, to enable students to understand the causes and manifestations of the rise of non-governmental diplomacy and its place, role and development prospects in contemporary world and Chinese diplomacy theory and practice.

Name: Economics of Innovation
Introduction:
Innovation and R&D are key drivers of growth and prosperity in modern economies. Entrepreneurs and governments need to understand various forms of R&D and innovation economics, innovation systems and policies, and intellectual property protection issues. This forms the thematic direction of this course. _x000D_
This course will start from the history of R&D and innovation, involving the contributions of scholars such as Arrow and Nelson, including R&D management systems, the effects of intellectual property protection, innovative activities in agriculture, medicine, software and electronics industries, factors affecting the direction of innovation, accounting and analysis of the contribution of innovation to corporate performance and national economic growth, innovative activities in the public and private sectors, the relationship between innovation and market structure, antitrust issues, how developing countries obtain required technologies, and current progress and challenges in global intellectual property protection. _x000D_
This course also focuses on the issues of China's innovation economics, describing the reform process of China's science and technology system and education system, innovation fiscal and taxation policies and science and technology project support systems, science and technology park pilots, basic research, entrepreneurship, achievements in innovation and development, problems faced by innovation, and future transformation and reform directions. In addition, the course also involves cutting-edge literature on foreign innovation economics and research on Chinese innovation issues. _x000D_
Students in this course: _x000D_

2. Learn relevant issues in innovation economics, such as R&D, invention, creation, development, application and technology expansion_x000D_
3. Study the impact mechanism and contribution accounting of technological innovation on national economic growth_x000D_
4. Analysis of the impact of learning R&D investment on corporate performance_x000D_
5. Distinguish between different categories of intellectual property protection and how these systems encourage innovation_x000D_
6. Learn a simple optimal static model for patent system design_x000D_
7. Learning the dynamic model of patents on incremental innovation_x000D_
8. Learn and understand cutting-edge topics of innovation and intellectual property protection through discussions_x000D_
9. Understand the changes in China’s science and technology system and innovation policies, as well as its unique innovation governance system_x000D_
10. Research on China’s Innovation Issues_x000D_

Name: The Politics of International Trade
Introduction: This course is designed to help students understand the basic problem areas of international political economics research - the basic history, basic theories and related basic issues of international trade politics, and cultivate the basic ability to analyze international trade political issues. The teaching focus includes introducing the driving force, process, laws and operating rules of the formation and development of international trade policy and the global trade system. The main teaching contents include: the interactive relationship between the state, society, interest groups and international factors in formulating foreign trade policies; research on the trade policy process of the United States and China; research on the multilateral trading system (GATT and WTO); the role of interest groups in trade politics, etc.

Name: Strategic Management
Introduction:
"Strategic Management is a comprehensive course that introduces the functions and processes of strategic management. We will adopt a general management or overall management perspective and look at the core and essence of enterprise management from a strategic perspective and starting point. We will start from the overall internal relationship of the enterprise and the strategic positioning of the enterprise in the external environment, and explore the source of the enterprise's lasting competitive advantage and long-term excellent operating performance._x000D_
In the mainstream management school curriculum system, this course has a dual mission. Integrating the knowledge students have learned in various functional courses (such as marketing, accounting, etc.) and comprehensively applying it in strategic analysis is one of its missions, which is called the "capped course" function. The second mission is to examine in detail the basic framework, core content, research methods, and cutting-edge topics of contemporary strategic management, highlighting the essence of strategic management as an independent discipline and its special charm and application value. _x000D_
This course will introduce the main concepts, theories, and practices of strategic management, covering the basic areas of strategic management: the concept, essence, and characteristics of strategy, the perspective, quality, and skills of strategists; the analysis, decision-making, and implementation process of business strategy, the cultivation and application of the company's overall business strategy and core competitiveness, the creation and persistence of industrial competitive strategies and competitive advantages, the balance between competitive strategies and cooperative strategies, and the application of the concept of competition, as well as the analysis and application of competitive strategies in different industries, regions, and international environments. _x000D_
Strategic Management is a highly practical applied course. Its purpose is not only to introduce some basic knowledge, but also to encourage and cultivate students' habits, methods, and skills to analyze problems independently. This course requires students to treat modern Western strategic management theories and methods with an objective and critical attitude, and apply them appropriately to local conditions to understand, analyze, and respond to the specific issues and challenges of corporate management in contemporary China's political, economic, social, and cultural institutional environments. This course places more emphasis on the cultivation of students' global thinking and their familiarity and grasp of contemporary international management paradigms and standards. _x000D_
The teaching methods of this course include professor lectures, class discussions, case analysis, etc. Class discussion has the dual function of helping to understand the course content and training students' expression and communication skills. Case teaching enables students to have extensive and in-depth exposure to first-hand information and problems in specific management practices of various enterprises, which is beneficial to training their analysis and problem-solving abilities. To be honest, since undergraduate students rarely have work experience, our class lectures and discussions focus on inspiring ideas, broadening horizons, introducing knowledge, and cultivating interests. Moreover, due to the large class size, opportunities for discussion and case analysis will still be limited compared to lectures by professors. I hope everyone will be active and use class time efficiently. "_x000D_

Name: Politics, Economy and Diplomacy of Southeast Asia
Prerequisite:
