Introduction: This course aims to comprehensively examine and discuss the history, politics, economy, culture, foreign relations, ASEAN organizations, and other regional issues of Southeast Asian countries. The professor will guide undergraduate students majoring in international relations to learn and explore the "Small Country Avenue" of Southeast Asian countries in the era of globalization after the end of the Cold War, that is, how Southeast Asian countries formed two major development paths of national modernization and regional integration in order to strive for peace and development of their own countries and the region. This process is embodied in trends such as individual diversification, national modernization, integration into globalization, ASEAN integration, regional cooperation, and the balancing of major powers. This course particularly hopes that students can apply what they have learned, combine history with reality, combine theory with practice, learn and apply systematic dialectical thinking, and various theoretical and practical methods, including international relations theory, to observe, analyze and solve practical problems related to Southeast Asia. At the same time, this course also has a large multinational teaching assistant team.

Name: Cross-Strait Relations and "One Country, Two Systems"
Introduction:
After the rotation of political parties in Taiwan in 2000, the island's politics underwent tremendous changes. The current basic structure of Taiwan's politics has also undergone major changes: three political party rotations, "de-Sinicization" on the island, etc. This topic mainly observes the current situation and future of cross-strait relations from the perspective of political parties on the island and international relations. At the same time, the Chinese Communist Party’s policy toward Taiwan must be studied. This course aims to help students understand the current situation of Taiwanese politics and its impact on cross-strait relations through teaching. _x000D_
        There are no domestic teaching materials for research and analysis from the perspective of intra-island politics; this course will run through many methodologies of diplomatic decision-making and comparative politics. Through Taiwan-related film and television works, we will learn from Greek teaching to help students understand the historical status and future of the Taiwan Strait issue from the perspective of comparative politics, and learn from the reunification experience of other countries after the war to provide new thinking for China's peaceful reunification. At the same time, students are encouraged to actively think and speak, actively explore issues, write diligently, and exercise basic analysis and writing skills. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Party Politics
Prerequisite: Pre-requisites: political science doctrine, Chinese political parties and politics, Western political systems
Introduction: The main content of the Introduction to Political Party Studies is political parties and party theory. However, unlike general political party theory courses, Introduction to Political Party Science focuses on teaching the basic theoretical knowledge and technical knowledge of political parties, and on this basis, explores the general laws of political party operations. Specific teaching contents include the formation of political parties, the structure of political parties, the ecology of political parties, ethics of political parties, culture of political parties, funding of political parties, and the motivation for political party development.

Name: Introduction to Dance

Curators play the role of art distributors, connecting artworks, artists, art consumers and society. Art curators build a display platform and decide which art is passed on and to whom. Name: Australian Politics and Economy
Introduction: This lesson focuses on how Australia's leaders have responded to its integration into the global political economy. Courses cover multiculturalism, international education, climate change, trade and investment, and Australia's relationship with Asia. The main purpose of the course is to make students aware of the relationship between leadership and decision-making, especially the dilemmas faced by Australia's leaders in the face of Australia's alliance with the United States and the rise of China. Name: Topics in Globalization and Contemporary International Relations
Introduction: After the end of the Cold War, with the end of the bipolar pattern, international relations and the international pattern have entered a new period of development and change. Globalization continues to deepen, the European integration process accelerates, and the rise of China has become an important phenomenon in international relations. At the same time, the rise of nationalism after the Cold War, globalization has brought global political awakening, the clash of civilizations has replaced the struggle for hegemony as a major focus of international relations, and non-traditional security issues such as climate change, environmental protection, energy, water resources, public health, etc. have gradually become the core agenda of international politics. How to understand the complex and complex international relations phenomena in contemporary times, how has the international system evolved after the Cold War, and what is the underlying dynamic mechanism? What is the relationship between globalization and interdependence? Does Huntington’s Clash of Civilizations Theory Reveal the Limits of Globalization? Does European integration reveal a possible path for the evolution of the international system? Will the rise of non-traditional security issues subvert traditional international security concepts and practices? In the context of globalization, how should we understand the mechanism of traditional great power politics and its active role in the international system? What challenges do the rise of nationalism, the challenge of nuclear non-proliferation, and the rise of international terrorism after the Cold War pose to global governance? How to understand the relationship between China’s rise and the international system? etc. This course will focus on this series of major issues from the perspective of globalization, trying to lay a preliminary analytical framework for students to understand contemporary international relations.

Name: Introduction to Small States and International Relations
Prerequisite:
"History of International Relations"_x000D_
"Introduction to International Politics"_x000D_
"Introduction to China's Diplomacy"_x000D_
"Study on East Asian Issues"_x000D_
"European Studies"
Introduction:
This course is a research-based elective course for senior undergraduate students in the School of International Relations. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course intends to use the constructive impact of the combined effect of national size and the international system on national behavior as a theoretical clue to systematically explore the basic manifestations and causes of national characteristics and behavioral patterns of small countries, recognize and understand the role, role and unique influence of small countries in today's international relations, and explore their universal behavioral patterns in domestic politics and society, foreign strategy, international security, economic development, internal and external cognition, etc., as well as the basic patterns of asymmetric interactions between large and small countries. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course helps to expand professional horizons, enrich professional research perspectives, examine the evolution of international relations from multiple dimensions, understand the diversity and complexity of the world, gain insights into life, and promote open, inclusive, and dialectical academic thinking.

Name: Politics and Diplomacy of the South Asian States
Introduction: Undergraduate students were briefed on the political landscape, political parties and the development and characteristics of domestic politics in South Asian countries; and on South Asian countries ' foreign policy, foreign policy decisions, relations with outside Powers.

Name: Choir (Advanced)
Prerequisite: Theory and practice underlying the chorus; chorus (C). Students in the art choir are required to take courses, and those who are not in the choir are required to pass.
Introduction:
The requirement is that only the classmates of the choir may choose and that the other classmates must pass the examination before taking the course.
Content: It's difficult to talk about famous musicians and their works at different times in the history of music.
It's a piece of music, a piece of music, and a piece of music that gives students a good idea of the style of composers at all times.

I. General curriculum:
The chorus course is divided into three levels: first, middle and higher. The main elements include the following: (1) presentation of the general picture of the period of the development of the Chinese and foreign chorus, the main achievements and major events; (2) analysis of the main features of the different chorus works in different periods and in different streams; (3) study of the work of composers and their representatives who have made outstanding contributions in the field of the chorus arts; (4) learning about the development of the medium and foreign music theory and the evolution of the musical style through the practice of the classic chorus; (5) keeping abreast of and learning from the new chorus works of today, to raise a deeper understanding of the chorus art; and (6) periodic performances of the chorus work to enhance the role of the second art classroom.
II. Opening commitments:
Symphony art is one of the important branches of music art. Its creation, development and transformation have had an important impact on the development of music and art. The chorus course is of interest at universities: first, it gives students a more in-depth understanding of the creation and development of music art and a clearer understanding of the formation and evolution of music styles. The second course combines theory and practice, allowing students to enter music practice and creation in the course, and to practice and recreate medium- and out-of-the-clock chorus from a shallow perspective.
Theory and practice underlying the chorus; chorus (C). Students in the art choir are required to take courses, and those who are not in the choir are required to pass.

Name: Political Development in the Islamic World
Introduction:
The ups and downs of the Islamic revival movement in the 20th century pushed religions that seemed far away from reality to the forefront of the world political stage. The political development of countries in West Asia, South Asia and Central Asia, the core areas of the Islamic world, closely interacted with the changes in contemporary world politics. Especially since the 1970s, the fierce political changes and political transformations within the Islamic world have increasingly become one of the main topics of concern in political circles, academic circles and the general public. _x000D_
A series of major theoretical and practical questions that urgently need to be answered are before the world: How to understand Islam? How do you evaluate contemporary Islamic revival trends and revival movements? How to understand the interaction between Islam and the process of social modernization? How to understand the relationship between Islam and the Western world in today's world situation? Is the rise of Islamic power threatening the security of the Western world, and therefore Western countries want to actively intervene, or is Western hegemony and power politics trying to dominate political and social changes in the Islamic world, thus triggering the resurgence of anti-American and anti-Western Islamic forces? Major issues such as these have made the study of the political development of Islamic countries and the relationship between Islam and world politics a cutting-edge topic in the current discipline of international politics. _x000D_
This course is an attempt to comprehensively and systematically sort out these issues. By analyzing and discussing the development and spread of Islam and Islam, representative cases from typical countries and regions are selected for analysis and discussion. From the perspectives of theory, history and reality, it focuses on the study of three aspects: Islam and secular politics, Islam and nation-states, and Islamic tradition and modernization process in world politics. _x000D_
Through classroom lectures and discussions inside and outside class, students can gain a more comprehensive and systematic understanding of Islamic factors in world politics, further understand the complexity of world politics, have a clear and correct stance on the main issues involved in the course, and have a macro grasp of the interaction between Islamic factors and world politics today.

Name: Performance of Chinese and Foreign Art Songs
Introduction: This course mainly teaches students to basically master the correct vocal techniques and breathing methods. By learning different types and styles of Chinese and foreign art songs, it enhances the understanding of Chinese and foreign music culture and arouses students' interest in Chinese and foreign art songs. At the same time, it helps students to have basic stage performance abilities by learning relevant basic knowledge of performance and teaching practice activities. _x000D_

Name: Training in Economic Thinking
Introduction: This course is jointly designed and created by teachers from various subject areas in the School of Economics, and is specially offered to first-year students. The course aims to cultivate students' critical thinking and economic thinking. It starts from the perspective of interest and helps students initially understand the process and methods of economists' analysis of economic issues, stimulates interest in learning, and enhances students' understanding of various branches of economics.

Name: Financial Markets
Introduction: Financial Markets Science is a basic course in finance, which focuses on the general theory of the financial system and the financial system, on the general forms in which financial markets operate, and on the systematic presentation of financial markets, instruments and institutions.

Name: Commercial Bank Management
Introduction: The basic goal of this course is to elaborate and clarify the basic principles and applications of commercial bank management, hoping to help deepen the understanding and insight into important and common commercial bank management issues.

Name: Financial Derivatives
Prerequisite: Fixed-income base knowledge; derivative base knowledge
Introduction: The course focused on structured financial products. Structured products are a new type of financial product that combines fixed-income products such as deposits, zero-interest bonds with financial derivatives (e.g. forward, options, swaps, etc.) using financial engineering techniques. Modern structured financial products have not a long history, but they have become one of the fastest and most promising operations in the international financial markets today. The course focuses on equity linkages, interest rate linkages, foreign exchange linkages, commodity linkages, credit linkages, asset securitization products, analysis of the structure and concepts of innovation for each financial product, risk-benefit characteristics, hedge product risks and pricing through specific cases and data.

Name: Introduction to Financial Economics
Prerequisite: Macro and micro, calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, etc.
Introduction:
"Introduction to Financial Economics" teaches modern financial theory since the 1950s, and incorporates various principles and methods derived from modern theoretical financial economics that appear in courses such as "Investment" and "Corporate Finance" into a unified theoretical framework. The most important ones in modern financial economics are the no-arbitrage assumption and the general equilibrium framework. The central issue studied is the pricing of financial assets in an uncertain financial market environment. Portfolio analysis (MPT), capital asset pricing model (CAPM), arbitrage pricing theory (APT), option pricing theory, market efficiency theory (EMH), MM theorem, etc. are all components of the theoretical system of financial economics. _x000D_

Name: Financial Regulation
Prerequisite: First, courses in Financial Markets and Finance.
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the following contents: Introduction to supervision, banking supervision, securities supervision, insurance supervision, financial derivatives supervision, anti-money laundering supervision, supervision of other financial institutions, supervision of foreign-related financial institutions. Through lectures and discussions, students can master the theory and practice of financial supervision and prepare themselves for working in financial supervision departments.

Name: Introduction to Behavioral Finance
Introduction:
Behavioral finance is a cutting-edge subject in economics research, with high theoretical and practical value.
Traditional finance science, based on rational economic assumptions, focuses on developing and refining investment instruments to optimize expected returns and risks for investors. However, in real markets, investment decisions seem irrational and there are mistakes in future predictions, which pose enormous challenges to traditional financial theory. Behavioral finance analyses the behaviour and psychology of investors from a psychological and sociological point of view, and provides marketable forecasts and corresponding investment proposals.
Based on students' basic knowledge of financial economics, the course examines how “market psychology” is generated, how investors use these phenomena to raise awareness about financial markets and how these psychological and social factors influence changes in the prices of financial assets. At the same time, the rationales and concepts are being used to highlight their specific application in equity investment and financial markets.

Name: Investments
Prerequisite: International finance; monetary banking; probabilistic and mathematical statistics; financial markets.
Introduction: Building on contemporary investment science since 1963, the course focuses on the basic theoretical and practical operations of investment science and capital markets. Key elements include: (1) the investment base. (2) The securities market and its transactions. (3) Value assessment of non-fixed-income securities. (4) Fixed-income securities. (5) Derivative financial instruments. (6) Portfolio theory. (7) Investment management. (8) Acquisitions and mergers in capital markets. (9) Portfolio investment funds.

Name: Introduction to the Atmosphere
Introduction:
The atmosphere is most closely related to the lives of individuals and to the development of society. Every move we make, the economic development of the country and the improvement of the quality of life as a whole are closely related to the atmosphere. Atmospheric science is the science of studying atmospheric and atmospheric phenomena and predicting and retrofitting the atmosphere. It is widely applied in environmental science, oceanography, human activities and daily life. Climate anomalies and environmental degradation in many parts of the world are now associated with research in atmospheric and atmospheric science.

This course is a presentation of basic knowledge and theory of atmospheric and atmospheric sciences, aimed at understanding atmospheric and atmospheric phenomena, leading students to understand the dynamics of the atmosphere, atmospheric phenomena, the relationship between weather and life, the broadening of the natural knowledge horizon and the ability to learn to use and properly guide everyday life, and will therefore be taught in such multimedia forms as images and animation, which will inspire imagination and innovative thinking.

The curriculum will be taught in accordance with the traditional teaching content. First, the composition, evolution and structure of the atmosphere; then energy and temperature, water vapour, clouds, cloud formation, precipitation, air pressure and wind; then atmospheric circulation, front and cyclones, thunderstorms and tornados, typhoons; then human activity and climate change; and finally, atmospheric light.

Name: Introduction to China's Environment
Introduction: Global sustainable development is already facing environmental crises such as climate change, energy shortage, population growth, food emergency, water shortage, forest destruction, soil erosion, biodiversity loss, etc. These environmental crises are significant and complex in our country. This course will comprehensively teach the basic concepts of environmental protection and the basic content of environmental management. It will give a comprehensive introduction to the historical evolution and current characteristics of my country's environmental issues based on the development of my country's environmental protection undertakings. It mainly involves energy and climate issues, population and food issues, water resources protection and soil and water conservation issues, species invasion and biodiversity protection issues, big city disease issues, cultural assimilation issues, etc. At the same time, it will also conduct an in-depth analysis of the natural, social, and economic roots of the emergence and evolution of my country's environmental problems. The purpose of this course is to enable students in the Department of Development Economics to have an in-depth understanding of global environment and development issues, especially in my country, fully grasp the arteries of my country's environment and development evolution, and comprehensively master my country's environmental policies and environmental management approaches.

Name: Chinese Philosophy (Part 1) Discussion Section
Introduction: This course will select the most representative philosophers in ancient China, teach their philosophical thoughts, and construct a dialogue between different thoughts. This will introduce students to the basic issues, basic ideas and their general evolution of ancient Chinese philosophy, and present the diverse theoretical systems within the tradition and their different ideas for solving problems.

Name: Studies in Sanqu Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: History of ancient literature, history of ancient poetry.
Introduction: The song is the representative style of meta-literacy. The course will describe the origin and development of the metronology; in comparison with poems and words, in the interpretation of specific works, it will analyse the physique and style characteristics of the metronology; and in the reading of key writers and works, it will recognize the metronology, feel the charm of the metronology and feel the most personal content of the fragrance.

Name: Asian History
Introduction:
Asia is the continent with the largest area and the most populous population in the world; Asian civilization is one of the oldest civilizations in the world, and the world's ancient civilizations China, India, and Babylon were all born in Asia; Asia is also the birthplace of the world's three major religions, Buddhism, Islam, and Christianity; the 21st century will be Asia's century, and Asian history is an important part of world history. The scope of this course mainly covers East Asia, Southeast Asia, South Asia, Central Asia and other regions; the topic scope mainly includes geography, population, historical development, political economy, international relations and values, etc.; the teaching and research perspective mainly emphasizes the perspective of global history, regional interaction, the overall perspective of Asia and the interdisciplinary perspective. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: The Russian Economy
Introduction: Russia's transition economy is an important part of the world economy. This course not only studies Russia's current overall economic situation, comprehensive national strength and economic policy priorities, but also explores its current utilization of foreign investment and foreign trade, its participation in international investment practices, and its progress and development trends in energy cooperation within the framework of the SCO. Through a comprehensive and profound analysis of Russia's transitional economy, it provides our undergraduate students with detailed information on the latest economic development progress in Eastern European and Central Asian countries; it inspires students to use the economic theories and analytical tools they have learned to observe the current problems in the Russian economy and think about ways to solve real economic problems; it provides students with ideas and solutions that can be used for reference when they independently engage in national and regional economic research.

Name: Environmental and Resource Economics
Prerequisite: Basic courses or equivalent courses in the first and second grades of the School of Economics.
Introduction:
Environmental resource economics is a discipline that studies the process mechanism of the interaction between the economy and the environment, the optimal allocation of resources, and its equilibrium convergence process. _x000D_
The course is open to senior undergraduates and junior graduate students of Peking University. It is better to have first- and second-year college mathematical analysis and economics course knowledge. On the basis of inheriting the wide-caliber and thick-foundation teaching philosophy of the School of Economics, the emphasis is on a solid understanding of basic theories, essential insights into basic concepts, and proficiency in basic analysis methods. The teaching goal is to cultivate students' solid basic ability to use environmental economic analysis methods to solve economic and social development problems. _x000D_

Name: China's Foreign Economic Relations
Prerequisite: International economics or international trade + international finance
Introduction: This course aims to analyze and explain the development and characteristics of China as an open economy, especially the typical facts of foreign trade, foreign investment, utilization of foreign capital, participation in international division of labor and their impact on China's economic growth and economic development, and analyze China's economic and trade relations with major countries in the world. It is hoped that students will have a good grasp and understanding of the basic principles of international economics/open economy through the study of this course, and be able to use these basic principles to analyze the open Chinese economy.

Name: International Taxation
Introduction: International taxation is based on fiscal conflicts of interest and coordination between countries arising from income and property tax systems and falls within the cross-cutting disciplines of economics and law, including tax jurisdiction, international double taxation and its elimination, international tax avoidance, anti-tax avoidance and international tax agreements.

Name: Ecological Economics
Introduction: Ecological economics regards the economic system as a subsystem within the ecological system, focusing on the optimal scale of economic activities under ecological constraints, the optimal allocation of ecological resources and services, and the fair distribution of ecological wealth. This course comprehensively analyzes the system view, values ​​and development view embodied in ecological economics, and systematically introduces the development context, core viewpoints, basic theories and research methods of ecological economics. It not only covers the latest international scientific research and teaching frontiers, but also reflects the specific issues in the process of China's economic growth. It aims to provide Chinese college students with a new way of thinking for the future.

Name: Law and Economics
Introduction: "Economics of Law", also known as "Law and Economics" or "Economic Analysis of Law", is a marginal discipline at the intersection of economics and law developed in the past 40 years. It is also an important academic school in post-war contemporary Western economics. Legal economics takes "personal rationality" and corresponding methodological individualism as the basis of its research methods, takes "efficiency" of economics as the core measurement standard, and uses "cost-benefit" and maximization methods as basic analytical tools to conduct research on legal issues.

Name: Introduction to Environmental Law
Introduction:
Environmental law is an emerging and fringe subject in law, and one of the cutting-edge and popular topics in law and other disciplines of humanities, social sciences and natural sciences. _x000D_
This course will use a combination of case teaching and theoretical teaching to briefly and systematically teach the basic concepts and content of environmental law, the basic principles and basic systems of environmental law, and the main content of individual environmental and resource protection legal systems. It will also teach the main content of international environmental law. _x000D_

Name: Neural Mechanisms of Violent Behavior
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Various forms of human violence have received widespread attention. Understanding the brain mechanisms of violent behavior is one of the important prerequisites for more effective processing, response and prevention of this harmful behavior. This course focuses on the brain mechanisms that influence the early adverse experiences of people and individuals on the frequency of violent behavior in adulthood. The following three issues will be discussed in focus: 1) the brain mechanisms of early social isolation affecting violent behavior in experimental animals, 2) the role of resocialization in isolated animals and its brain mechanisms, 3) the violent behavior tendencies and brain mechanisms of adults who have experienced early isolation or other trauma. The evaluation of students taking this elective course is divided into three parts: (1) explanation of the assigned article and answers to questions; (2) participation in problem discussion activities in class; (3) final paper written according to one's own interests.

Name: Virtual Reality Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Virtual reality technology has become an important means of content presentation and technical validation in the industrial areas of defence and military, major engineering applications, engineering design and cultural entertainment, among others. Virtual reality technology is a multidisciplinary and integrated technology that involves theory and methodology in a wide range of disciplines, including computers, electronics and communications, mechanical and photovoltaic engineering, and mathematical physics, and is closely linked to relevant disciplines in such industries as engineering science. Virtual reality technology is one of the most rapidly developing information technology directions in the current high-technology field. Virtual realities and enhanced realities are collectively referred to as virtual realities, which differ in research methods and presentation, but have the same underlying theoretical and methodological tools. In the course of the current evolution of virtual reality, VR+ has become a development focus in all fields of development, as well as in the application of virtual reality in all disciplines and trades. It has enabled students to understand and master basic virtual reality methods and theories, made it easier for students to become familiar with and mastery of the relevant technological tools, contributed to students ' knowledge of virtual reality technologies themselves and increased their awareness of the development of other industries.

Name: Frontiers and Research Methods in Economics
Introduction:
The National Institute of Development is committed to promoting comprehensive research in Chinese social sciences, trying to organize interdisciplinary research, cultivating comprehensive senior talents for national development, serving my country's reform and development and the construction of a new global order with comprehensive knowledge collection, and serving the discovery and exploration of social sciences. _x000D_
This course aims to improve students' academic literacy and cultivate students' subject literacy and scientific spirit. It relies on the college's strong professors represented by Lin Yifu, Zhou Qiren, Zhang Weiying, Song Guoqing and other famous teachers, and combines their research fields and research experiences to teach cutting-edge economics theories and research methods. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Economic History
Introduction:
Economic history is an important branch of applied economics. Its content is to use economic methods to analyze historical changes, explain the economic reasons behind major historical events, and then explain the laws of historical evolution from an economic perspective. Many major modern economic events and economic policies can be epitomized in history, so economic history can provide some reference for today's economic development and economic policies;_x000D_
_x000D_
This course explains the development and changes of Chinese economic history in the context of world economic history, focusing on the late imperial period to modern times. The course will combine staged teaching with special topic teaching. This course will introduce some of the cutting-edge results of economics in historical development research in recent years. The objectives of the course are (1) to enable students to master and become familiar with some basic viewpoints in the field of Chinese economic history research in academia through the study of this course; to have an understanding of the general laws of economic development and evolution in China and the world in history, and to understand the economic factors behind major historical events in China; (2) to cultivate students' ability to combine economic theory with historical analysis, and to use economic methods to analyze historical issues; (3) to introduce several causal identification methods at the forefront of economic history research, so that students with spare capacity can carry out their own research. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Political Economy
Prerequisite: There is no requirement for an initial course, but it would be helpful to have attended a course on political science in general offered by the Institute of Government Administration.
Introduction: How did the contemporary international political and economic system form and evolve? What is the relationship between government and market under globalization? How involved should the government be in economic affairs? How do economic factors affect interstate relations and domestic politics? This course is dedicated to giving an introduction to the basic relationship between politics and economics in answering the above questions. Its main purpose is to help students understand and think about the interactions between politics, economic systems, forces, and actors at both the international and domestic levels.

Name: Data Analysis and Econometric Programming
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the basic methods and tools of data processing, statistical analysis and econometric programming. Through studying this course, students should be familiar with the basic commands of several common econometric programming languages ​​(Matlab, R, SAS, Eviews, Python, etc.), and be proficient in one of these languages ​​to program and implement commonly used econometric models.

Name: Economics Social Practicum
Introduction:
_x000D_
This course is carried out in various forms such as teacher guidance for students to conduct business visits and internships, field research and other forms. Guide students to go out of school, get in touch with society, understand national conditions and people's livelihood, combine theory with practice, let students understand social conditions during visits to enterprises and rural areas, guide students to use data and information from survey practices to conduct scientific research, write research papers, and deepen their understanding of scientific research results. In addition, it can also cultivate students to enhance their awareness of serving society. _x000D_

Name: Topics in the Chinese Economy Small-Group Discussion
Introduction: A mini-class discussion of the issues mentioned in the Chinese Economics Curriculum in conjunction with reading materials

Name: Training in Economic Research
Introduction: This course is offered to third-year undergraduate students. The purpose is to help students become familiar with economic research, train research methods, inspire research interests, and guide students in writing research plans. This course is taught in small classes and uses a combination of teacher lectures and student reports to guide students to discuss economic issues and then start systematic research.

Name: Agricultural Economics in Historical Perspective
Introduction: There are words in "Yi Zhuan" to "reveal the past and know the future", "take history as a mirror", "read history wisely"... History is to understand the connection between events, identify the causal relationship between events, and explore the laws of historical development. Agricultural economic thought can be traced back to ancient times. During the Spring and Autumn Period of my country, the works of Confucius and Mencius contained many discussions on agricultural management, land systems and stable people's livelihood. The "Columbian Exchange", population growth and migration laid the cornerstone of modern civilization. What impact did climate change, the Columbian Exchange, and steel have on the agricultural economy? How do the evolution of land systems and changes in political power at home and abroad promote the adjustment of agricultural structure step by step? How has rice farming culture affected the psychology of people in modern society? This course will teach students basic agricultural economic history knowledge against the long historical background of agriculture, and sort out the main events that promoted the changes in the global agricultural system. Under the framework of economics, analyze the inextricable and close connection between agricultural development and historical trajectories. "The use of history is of great benefit. It is an urgent task for mankind, and it is the main road of the country. It is indispensable for those who have a country and a family?" Taking this elective course is to look at human beings vertically and understand agricultural economy and rural development scientifically.

Name: China in Case Studies
Introduction: This course will conduct a number of case discussions about China, covering economics, management, strategy, investment, financing, and corporate governance, to deepen students' understanding of China's economic and management issues.

Name: Financial Accounting
Introduction: The course is a basic course that focuses on the basic accounting procedures of the enterprise, emphasizes the importance of accounting controls around the accounting system and the relationship of the enterprise organization, on the basis of the elaboration of accounting elements, accounting equations, accounting principles and accounting cycles, describes the business processing and reporting of assets, liabilities and equity interests, as well as the rationale for the preparation of the three major accounting statements (i.e. balance sheets, profit statements and cash flow statements) and the related financial ratio analysis, to help students gain a good understanding of the content and role of the financial statements and thus provide a solid basis for further learning follow-up courses.

Name: Applied Econometrics
Introduction: This course mainly studies basic econometric models and estimation methods. We focus primarily on linear regression models, but also perform analyzes on time series, panel data, instrumental variables, and discrete choice models.

Name: Value Investing
Prerequisite: Macroeconomics, Corporate Finance and Financial Accounting
Introduction:
This course consists of two parts. _x000D_
The first part focuses on the value investment theory of Graham and Dodd and will be developed through courses, cases and classroom discussions, including (1) assumptions and methods of value investment; (2) value assessment methods based on balance sheets and earnings; (3) construction of value-based risk control models; (4) design of search strategies for value investment opportunities; (5) supervision, investor protection, corporate governance and their impact on company value. _x000D_
The second part will allow students to immerse themselves in the specific practice of Graham and Dodd's investment principles. Through guest lectures and other forms, students will understand how to create an investment program that suits the investor's personality traits. The topics discussed by the guests include (1) search strategies; (2) valuation methods; (3) research methods; (4) investors’ risk management experience. _x000D_

Name: Strategy and Games
Introduction: Game theory is an effective tool for researching strategic sexuality. The course highlights some of the basic ideas, concepts and methods of gaming theory.

Name: The China Approach: Global Development Trends and National Diplomatic Strategy
Introduction: This course will organize lectures by experts in the field of international relations. The purpose is to broaden students' horizons and promote students' understanding of China's development ideas and positioning in the contemporary international relations pattern. It will encourage students to understand the national conditions and world conditions in a broader perspective, and help students develop a sound personality and a correct worldview and values.

Name: Economics in the Real World
Introduction: Pass on nearly 40 years of personal experience in observing economic phenomena and discovering economic laws, share with students the understanding and application of the academic tradition of economics, focus on the realistic constraints of economic behavior, and the logic of economic behavior under specific constraints, cultivate interest in real-world phenomena, and improve the ability to discover and analyze problems.

Name: Economics in the Real World Discussion Section
Introduction: Pass on nearly 40 years of personal experience in observing economic phenomena and discovering economic laws, share with students the understanding and application of the academic tradition of economics, focus on the realistic constraints of economic behavior, and the logic of economic behavior under specific constraints, cultivate interest in real-world phenomena, and improve the ability to discover and analyze problems.

Name: Introduction to Political Science
Prerequisite: calculus, probability theory, political economics, economics principles, middle microeconomics, middle macroeconomics
Introduction: This course introduces and discusses basic concepts and theoretical issues in political science from an interdisciplinary theoretical perspective. The innovation in teaching design lies in integrating the research perspectives of game theory, history, new institutional economics, neoclassical political economics and contemporary Western Marxist political economics into the discussion of basic concepts and issues in political science, and using the latest academic cutting-edge perspectives to reconstruct the understanding of political science. It also combines China's historical traditions and local political practices, and adopts a method of combining comparison and case discussion to stimulate students' thinking and academic imagination on basic political issues.

Name: Selected Readings from Das Kapital
Prerequisite:
Political economy (up and down)
Economics (up and down)
History of foreign economic thinking
Introduction:
"Das Kapital" is Marx's most representative and mature political economics research result, and is a must-read classic work for studying Marxist political economics. _x000D_
"Das Kapital" is an intermediate-level political economics course that selects the most important theoretical parts of "Das Kapital" and explains them in the form of special topics, so that students can deeply understand the methods and principles of Marx's economics and understand Marx's critical analysis of the capitalist mode of production by reading the original work. _x000D_

Name: Learning Management through Case Studies
Introduction: This course is offered to senior undergraduate students in business administration. It is an elective course that focuses on the integration and application of management knowledge. The course content covers the development process of typical enterprises in China, Europe and the United States and the role of management in them. The course uses interactive case teaching, focusing on basic management functions such as organization, leadership, control and innovation, to help students understand the decision-making process of managers and the main factors that influence decision-making. Focus on training students’ case analysis ideas, skills, professional presentation abilities and teamwork spirit. At the same time, through group case projects, students are helped to master case study methods, promote students' in-depth understanding and perspective of management practices, and exercise their abilities in academic observation, summary, and research.

Name: Insurance Law
Introduction: This course is an introductory course to insurance law. The main content is insurance contract law. It also provides a brief introduction to the civil and commercial law system, basic principles of contract law, and some insurance regulatory laws for economic management students. This course helps students majoring in insurance and other economic management-related majors understand the basic principles of insurance contracts and the legal relationships between insurance parties. The course is suitable for students who hope to join the insurance industry in the future, or engage in insurance-related work in securities, consulting, investment, supervision, social insurance management, academic research, etc.

Name: Entrepreneurship Simulation
Introduction:
According to the spiritual requirements of the "Basic Requirements for Entrepreneurship Education Teaching in General Undergraduate Schools (Trial)", in order to further enhance our school's ability to serve the national strategy, improve our school's education system, and expand our school's active role in the overall pattern of national economic structural adjustment and development mode transformation, the Institute of Industrial Technology, based on the development needs of students and the laws of talent training in our school, has offered "Entrepreneurship Basics" courses for three consecutive semesters and 2-credit courses for two consecutive semesters. The "Simulated Entrepreneurship" public elective course is planned to be offered to all students in the school starting from the first semester of 2015-2016. _x000D_
"Simulated Entrepreneurship", as an advanced course of innovation and entrepreneurship courses, will introduce the process and situation of virtual entrepreneurship based on the knowledge reserve of basic entrepreneurship courses, allowing students to actually experience and experience the complete entrepreneurship process under the guidance of teachers, thereby cultivating and exercising students' entrepreneurial skills and team spirit. This course will fully integrate high-quality teaching and teacher resources from universities, industry, investment circles, business circles and successful entrepreneurial alumni. Based on the basic concepts, basic principles, basic methods and related theories of entrepreneurship, starting from the identification and selection of entrepreneurial opportunities, a virtual entrepreneurial team will be formed around the entrepreneurial plan, and a passing mechanism will be set up to ensure the excellence of the virtual entrepreneurial team. Using business plan writing as a clue, they will jointly plan and design entrepreneurial plans, and integrate entrepreneurial resources. Under the guidance of teachers, each entrepreneurial team needs to complete a qualified negotiation plan and participate in a simulated entrepreneurial competition. _x000D_
 The "Simulated Entrepreneurship" course is a small class teaching model. It plans to enroll 30-50 students in groups of 5-8. In addition to the main lecturer, it is also equipped with entrepreneurship instructors, focusing on simulated practical teaching. By guiding the writing of business plans, combined with teaching methods such as case teaching, group discussions, practical exercises, and entrepreneurial guidance, it enhances the openness, interactivity, and effectiveness of entrepreneurship education and teaching, so that students can skillfully apply the basic knowledge and theories of entrepreneurship, and become familiar with the basic processes and methods of entrepreneurship. _x000D_
"Simulated Entrepreneurship" will integrate entrepreneurship education into Peking University's talent training system, focusing on guiding students to correctly understand the relationship between entrepreneurship and national economic and social development, focusing on guiding students to correctly understand the relationship between entrepreneurship and career development, systematically cultivating students' comprehensive qualities in integrating entrepreneurial resources, designing entrepreneurial plans, and founding and managing new ventures, focusing on cultivating students Entrepreneurial ability to identify entrepreneurial opportunities, prevent entrepreneurial risks, and take timely action; cultivate students' sense of innovation that is good at thinking, sensitive to discovery, and dare to be the first; challenge themselves, endure setbacks, and perseverance; professional ethics that abide by laws and regulations, be honest and trustworthy, and be good at cooperation; and cultivate students' sense of social responsibility to create value, serve the country, and serve the people. _x000D_

Name: Statistical Culture and Practice
Introduction: This course is a general course on statistics and data science for all students in the school. No advanced mathematical foundation is required. This course focuses on the background, thinking and practice of statistics and data science, important cases in the development process of statistics and data science, and their important role in interdisciplinary and even social development. The cases involved in this course are real observation records from nearly twenty different disciplines such as economics, society, public health, and natural sciences. In this course, students can not only experience philosophical speculation in statistical concepts, but also focus on using statistical methods to solve practical problems.

Name: History of Foreign Economic Thought
Introduction: This course takes the emergence, formation and development of Western economics as the main line, focusing on introducing and evaluating the historical background, main characteristics and basic content of the representative or dominant economic thoughts or theories in Western countries from the mercantile era to before Keynes, as well as their impact on social and economic development, and elucidating the laws and trends in the development and evolution of economic thoughts or economic theories. This course includes three parts: preclassical economics period, classical economics period and neoclassical economics period. _x000D_

Name: Artificial Intelligence, Robotics and Ethics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: There are no mandatory courses. It is better to have basic knowledge of artificial intelligence, intelligent robots, etc.
Introduction:
After years of development, artificial intelligence and robotics technology have made remarkable achievements. As the accumulation of multiple AI-related disciplines becomes more abundant and people's demand for AI technology in production and life continues to grow, artificial intelligence and robotics are entering a critical stage of development and application. _x000D_
      However, the rapid development of artificial intelligence and robotics brings both numerous opportunities and unprecedented risks and challenges. _x000D_
      Although governments in major international AI and robotics R&D countries have taken encouraging steps to address these challenges. But due to the disruptive nature of these technologies, more efforts are needed to strengthen and sustain this work. As artificial intelligence increasingly becomes an indispensable and difficult-to-separate component of our production, life, work, and learning, the public and policymakers have the responsibility to understand the capabilities and limitations of this technology. AI and robot ethics are no longer an afterthought. On the contrary, as a forward-looking ethics, it urgently requires artificial intelligence and robot design and development personnel to deeply understand the various value requirements of life and the environment, so that value concerns can be integrated into the early stages of artificial intelligence and robot technology research and development and product design. _x000D_
      This course is based on the comprehensive teaching staff of the four departments of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences (Department of Philosophy, School of Information Science and Technology, School of Engineering, and School of Journalism and Communication), and is in line with internationally renowned universities (such as Stanford, MIT, Harvard, etc.), and carries out undergraduate course teaching around the ethics and governance issues involved in artificial intelligence and robotics. _x000D_

Name: Financial Accounting Theory and Policy
Introduction: The value of theory lies in explaining and guiding practice. Financial accounting theory is the sublimation of financial accounting practice, and in turn guides financial accounting practice. The purpose of this course is to introduce students to the field of financial accounting theory and take how to conduct financial accounting theory research as the main content of the course. The course first introduces the basic knowledge of accounting research methodology, then discusses the basic theories of financial accounting, including the nature of financial accounting and the formulation, implementation and supervision of accounting rules. It then discusses the core topics in financial accounting research, including three topics: earnings management, corporate governance and accounting information, and accounting information and capital markets.

Name: Data Thinking: From Data Analysis to Business Value
Prerequisite: Students in the selected classes would like to have a basic introductory knowledge of statistics. The required a priori knowledge includes, but is not limited to: basic probabilistic theory, probability distribution, statistical volumes, parameter estimates, hypothetical tests.
Introduction: The core issue of the Data Thinking course is: How to make "data" generate "commercial value", and what is the methodology? What is the core concept? To this end, I would like to share with you a complete theoretical framework: data thinking. It includes three important aspects: (1) Data and value. Understand what data is? What is value? In what ways does value appear? How is it perceived by customers? (2) Regression analysis, including: concepts and techniques. At the conceptual level, understanding regression analysis is the basic methodology for defining business problems into data-analyzable problems. Learn the two most commonly used regression analysis models at a technical level: linear regression + logistic regression. (3) Productization of data models. How to turn a data-based model into a commercial product? What are the challenges and pitfalls? Is there a basic methodology that can be followed?

Name: The Chinese Economy
Introduction: The course will describe and analyse the history and reality of the Chinese economy from the two dimensions of economic development and institutional change, focusing mainly on the operational mechanisms, development performance and underlying logic of the Chinese economy during the planning period and the period of reform and opening up. The special features of this course are the analysis and presentation of the “China Story” based on the theory of economics and cutting-edge research, understanding the logic and evolution of China's economy from the perspective of its interaction with the Government, and defining and analysing the characteristics of China's economic development performance and its governance from the perspective of international comparisons.

Name: Dance Theory and Practice
Introduction: This course teaches the history and basic theory of dance movement analysis methods, coupled with corresponding dance practice experience, so that students can initially master the thinking method of analyzing and describing human body movement language, and lay the foundation for using movement ontology language to analyze different types of dance. The course starts from the theoretical perspective of dance movement analysis. By understanding the "structural cornerstone" of human movement - spatial symbols, students can understand the basic elements of human movement from the perspective of "spatial structure". Through the layered explanation of the elements of human movement, students can master the analytical grammar of human movement and initially develop the ability to analyze dance movement language. After the "movement cornerstone" and "movement structure" analytical abilities are formed, the course will teach students the "movement power" analysis theory to enable students to understand the rich elements that modify human body movements, initially understand the "movement texture", and find theoretical support for experiencing and analyzing different styles of dance art. The final course will allow students to learn to create new movement patterns by themselves through the experience of "movement spectrum" and "movement chorus", so as to continuously create new selves through human movement to adapt and transform the environment to generate new power in the dance experience.

Name: Cultural Policy
Prerequisite: Introduction to the cultural industry, art management.
Introduction:
This course mainly introduces, analyzes and interprets domestic and foreign cultural industry policies and laws, discusses cases, masters relevant norms, makes full use of favorable policies and norms, avoids legal policy risks, and has the level of macro-management of the cultural industry. The course will introduce and sort out the development paths of cultural industry policies and regulations, as well as the basic objectives and basic content of existing policies and regulations. At the same time, it will introduce the relevant policies and regulations in the main fields of the cultural industry. _x000D_
1. Understand the basic framework and key objectives of my country’s cultural and industrial policies, and analyze its existing problems and basic future trends. _x000D_
2. Understand the advantages and disadvantages of my country's cultural system and mechanisms in the development and prosperity of culture, and use cases to think, discuss and analyze the current cultural management system, the dilemmas, path choices and future development models in the restructuring and reform carried out in the fields of press and publishing, radio and television, theater troupes and performing arts. _x000D_
3. Understand the promotion policies and implementation priorities implemented from the perspectives of legislation, finance, market and corresponding active policy tools in order to make our country a cultural power, improve cultural soft power, and develop the cultural industry into a national pillar strategic industry, so as to better grasp the goals and directions of future cultural enterprise operations and planning, and make good use of, utilize and timely apply its support, encouragement and protection policies. _x000D_
4. Understand issues such as copyright ownership, copyright development and derivatives transactions in the products and services of cultural enterprises, as well as online copyright protection and dispute resolution mechanisms, as well as the division of related responsibilities and rights. Issues regarding the legal relationship between cultural enterprise employees and enterprises, such as disputes over personal works or professional works of cultural creation. Understand the subject, object and related rights and obligations of legal relationships based on relevant cases, so as to avoid infringement disputes while safeguarding one's own legitimate rights and interests. _x000D_
5. Understand the trademark types, scope, acquisition methods, authorization and brand operation strategies of cultural products and services, and understand the rights protection and risk avoidance issues in brand construction, maintenance and development and utilization through case analysis. _x000D_
6. Understand the subject qualifications required to engage in cultural industry business activities, business content management responsibilities, legal norms and policy constraints in business activities, including cultural market management policies and regulations (performing arts market, entertainment market, advertising industry market, art market, exhibition market, etc.) policies and regulations, and what is unfair competition, which situations are unfair competition, how to avoid monopoly operations and stop monopoly operations through legal weapons._x000D_
7. Understand the main risks brought about by the formulation, changes and adjustments of cultural policies in the strategic planning, positioning, development model, investment, tactical operations and specific operations of cultural enterprises, establish policy analysis, early warning and monitoring systems, and prepare plans and practices to avoid losses, penalties, legal disputes, etc. caused by related risks.

Name: China and Media Affairs
Introduction: The course will analyse the characteristics of the various media and the factors influencing their development from the perspective of a senior media practitioner. At the same time, the image of China in the world media will be analysed.

Name: Quantitative Reasoning Methods
Introduction: This course is an introductory course to statistics, especially social statistics. We'll cover how to collect data, describe it, and make statistical inferences based on statistics. We will also teach basic statistical concepts as well as statistical models, such as linear regression models. In this course, students will learn and use R software to perform statistical analysis and practice the statistical methods and models they have learned. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Finance
Introduction: Over the past 40 years of reform and opening up, China's financial industry has made considerable progress. Its development path, organizational form, operation methods, risk accumulation and release characteristics, formal and informal rules, and interaction with the real economy are all different from other economies and have obvious Chinese characteristics. Existing finance textbooks are mostly based on Western markets and have obvious deficiencies in interpreting China's magnificent financial landscape and its tortuous and subtle historical evolution. This course will describe the institutional background of China's financial industry and sort out the historical context of China's financial development. On this basis, based on academic research and problem-oriented, it will reflect on the historical choices of key nodes in the reform and opening up of the financial industry, summarize the experience and lessons of the development of China's financial industry, concretize China's financial development model, contribute to the in-depth integration of financial theory and Chinese practice, and predict the future development direction of China's financial industry. It is hoped that after studying this course, students will be able to grasp the historical process of changes in China's financial system, understand what a "good financial system" is, and actively think about the key nodes of China's financial development in the future, as well as the correct choices we should make.

Name: Global Business Strategy
Introduction:
The theme of the course is global business strategy. The professors analyzed and interpreted the Chilean economy, South American economic development, history, government environment, the impact of policies on economic development, as well as the development and future prospects of existing key industries: mining, agriculture, and the red wine industry. The course topics revolve around the following convenient developments: 1) Intercultural Business Challenges in Latin America; 2) Marketing in Latin America; 3) Economic Growth in Latin America: Challenges and Prospects; In conjunction with classroom learning, FEN arranged the following field trips: 1) Chinese Embassy in Chile, Ambassador to Chile Xu Bu explained the policy towards Chile and an overview of economic and trade cooperation with Chile; 2) Chilean Innovation and Entrepreneurship, inspected Start-Up Chile; 3) CODELCO, Chile's largest copper mining company; 4) Tarapaca Vinery, see how red wine is "grown" and learn to taste wine; 5) Banco de Chile, the largest bank in Chile, the development of Chile's financial industry; 6) Bank of Chile Innovation Center, innovation in banking services such as electronic payment; 7) Valparaiso Port, learn about port industry management and current trade conditions. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: The Chinese Economy: Technology, Growth and Global Connections
Introduction: This course introduces China's economic development in the context of globalization. Through lectures, case studies, and visits to institutions and businesses, this course will examine issues such as trade trends, foreign investment, public and private property rights, finance, labor, consumption, and key business sectors. The course will also discuss China's challenges and opportunities in the environment, energy, education and medical care. Taught by economic historians, this course will consider China's unique historical, cultural and business context, as well as global collaborations and influences. The course features readings and cases from academics, business leaders, economists, and journalists.

Name: Contemporary Korean Society
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to introduce students to various aspects of contemporary Korean society, including family, industrialization, gender, population, religion and political system. The course is focused on topics that are closely related to the life of Korean society, such as patriarchy, modernization, education heat, urbanization, authoritarianism, collectivism and anti-Americanism. Each of these topics is examined from a social, historical and comparative perspective. The selected reading materials are taken mainly from sociological textbooks to enhance students ' understanding of how society works and to develop their thinking to facilitate the use of the knowledge acquired in the analysis of other national societies.

Name: Dialogues with Global Innovation Masters
Introduction:
The "Dialogue with Global Innovation Masters" course mainly consists of a lecture group composed of different industry leaders from different countries to spread their practical experience and cutting-edge knowledge to students. This course aims to build an innovative education model that combines Chinese and Western, professional and industry, traditional university and private education resources, and teaching and immersion through close interaction between masters and students from various industries in various countries, inviting relevant Chinese scholars to dialogue with them, and in the form of lectures. _x000D_
_x000D_
The "Dialogue" lecture series has received widespread attention and praise from teachers and students since its inception in 2011. On the basis of summarizing the experience of more than a year, we further adjusted the professional fields and ratios of the speakers, forming a teaching knowledge system that is both highly professional and has a broad international perspective. We have built a teaching model that integrates master lectures, case analysis, achievement display, dialogue and comments from experts in related fields such as Peking University, and thematic interaction between students and masters. _x000D_
_x000D_
There are nine lecture courses in this semester, and ten internationally renowned and highly innovative leaders in the industry have been invited to Peking University to impart professional knowledge and review their entrepreneurial journeys, including new media pioneers, film and television art masters, animation production masters, academicians of the American Academy of Engineering, Japanese landscape design masters, nutrition experts, etc. They are among the few special talents in various industries who have rich innovative experience, master the most cutting-edge information, and have the most advanced skills. They represent the highest level and development direction of the industry. _x000D_
_x000D_
In this course, students can fully appreciate the masters from all walks of life in various countries, expand their international horizons, and accumulate life experience. They can understand the cutting-edge development trends in various fields, enrich their knowledge system, improve their academic abilities, and learn a variety of innovative concepts to inspire multi-directional thinking and broaden their academic thinking. _x000D_
_x000D_
Through this course platform, world-class masters gather in China to promote international knowledge exchanges, develop new models of educational inheritance, accelerate corporate innovation and development and economic transformation, introduce master-level wisdom resources to China's education and industrial development, and provide comprehensive solutions for sustainable and harmonious development. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course assessment plan: course participation (20%) + project report (75%) + volunteer service (5% + bonus)

Name: History of Foreign Legal Systems
Introduction: Teaching the essence of representative legal systems of different types in foreign history, their manifestations, their content characteristics and the processes and patterns of their evolution. There are two aspects: the history of legal developments and the history of legal systems. The former study the historical development of the law, i.e. the legislative history, mainly in relation to the formation of various laws, legislative documents, legislative guidelines, characteristics of national and regional laws over time and their origins and mutual influence; the latter study the historical development of legal principles and institutions, mainly in relation to the basic elements of the Constitution, civil law, criminal law and procedural law.

Name: History of Western Legal Thought
Introduction: This course is guided by historical materialism and provides a relatively systematic introduction to the emergence, development and changes of political and legal thought in major Western countries (Western Europe and North America) in different historical periods, different social classes and social strata. This subject is a basic course for the legal profession. The scope of its research includes the history of the development and changes of legal thoughts, theories and doctrines in Western countries over more than 2,000 years from the beginning of the ancient Greek and Roman slave states to the 1980s. The content is very rich. It uses the classic works of famous thinkers and jurists in Western history as basic clues, involving the legal thought of ancient Greece and Rome, medieval theological and legal thought, the natural law theory of various thinkers during the bourgeois revolution period, utilitarian law, analytical positivism law and the two major legal schools in the period of liberal capitalism. As well as various contemporary Western legal schools and trends of thought. Through the research and study of this course, the purpose of "making the past useful for the present and foreign knowledge useful for China" can be achieved.

Name: Criminal Law Case Studies
Prerequisite: General Principles of Criminal Law, Criminal Law Distinction
Introduction: This course adopts a discussion teaching method, focusing on 16 basic cases based on typical cases in criminal law theory and common difficult cases in judicial practice in recent years. It aims to enable students to understand and apply cutting-edge criminal law theories at home and abroad through case study, become familiar with the basic logical model of criminal law problem-solving, practice multi-angle argumentation methods for theoretical issues in cases, and finally master the ability to analyze and interpret real cases. The course cases involve general theoretical issues such as criminal law interpretation theory and basic principles, causality and objective attribution, intentionality and negligence, justified reasons, mistakes, joint crimes, unfinished crimes, number of crimes theory and concurrence theory, and penalty theory. It also involves personal crimes such as homicide, injury, and rape, property crimes such as robbery, theft, and fraud, as well as sub-theoretical issues such as corruption and bribery. Students should start studying this course after completing the general introduction and sub-sections of criminal law.

Name: Fundamentals of Moot Court
Introduction: This course will focus on virtual moot court cases, including an overview of moot courts (examples, skills training and competitions), how to discover dispute points, how to conduct international legal investigations, how to write pleadings, how to conduct oral arguments, etc.

Name: English for Specific Purposes II
Introduction: This course will study more than 60 U.S. contract law cases, which involve important contents of U.S. contract law such as offer and acceptance, contract consideration, contract interpretation, statutory defenses, anticipated refusal to perform and anticipated failure to perform, changes in circumstances, relief methods, etc.

Name: Family Law and Inheritance Law
Introduction: "Marriage, Family and Inheritance Law" is a professional course for law majors in colleges and universities. Based on the subject framework of marriage, family and inheritance law, it systematically and comprehensively provides basic theories and basic knowledge about marriage, family and inheritance law. The law of marriage and family inheritance is substantive law and domestic law. Marriage and family inheritance law is an applied law with strong practicality. As a branch of law, the research objects of this discipline are mainly various legal systems in the field of marriage and family inheritance and legal issues in real life. Marriage and family inheritance cases account for a large proportion of all civil cases. Many issues require in-depth study from both legal theory and practice. _x000D_

Name: Criminal Investigation
Introduction: Mainly teaches the objects, systems, research methods of criminal investigation and their relationship with similar disciplines, the tasks and basic principles of criminal investigation, the steps and methods of criminal investigation, on-site investigation, investigation interrogation, investigation experiments, search and seizure, identification, investigation, technical investigation methods, investigation methods of major types of criminal cases, etc. _x000D_

Name: Moot Court Training
Prerequisite: Note: The course is mainly concerned with coaching and training teams from the Northern College of Law to participate in the competitions, the distribution of which is based on the cycle and content of each competition and cannot be generalized. Before actually participating in competition training, students can start with a “Moot Court Basics”. The course will be organized around virtual mock court cases, including sessions of mock court overviews (practices, skills training and competitions), theories on cases and points of contention, international legal investigations, writing pleadings, oral arguments, etc.
Introduction: This moot court course cultivates outstanding legal talents with applied practical abilities and international legal literacy through training in legal retrieval, document writing, court trial skills and direct participation in domestic and foreign moot court competitions. The course is divided into two courses: "Moot Court Basics" and "Moot Court Practical Training". The content is related but the curriculum is independent. The “Moot Court Practical Training” course is offered in the autumn semester. The practical training course is mainly to coach and train each moot court team to participate in the competition. Students who choose the course are required to have the ability to represent the college in the moot court competition. Relevant level and ability are determined at the discretion of the course facilitator. The current competitions and number of members of the law school team are as follows: 1. Jessup International Law Moot Court Competition; 2. Lee-Li Cup Competition; 3. International Commercial Arbitration (VIS) Moot Court Competition; 4. International Humanitarian Law (IHL) Moot Court Competition; 5. International Criminal Court (ICC) Mock Trial Competition (English Competition); 6. International Criminal Court (ICC) Mock Trial Competition (Chinese Competition); 7. Asia Cup (Asia) Cup) International Law Moot Court Competition; 8. Price Media Law International Moot Court Competition.

Name: Insurance Law
Prerequisite: Civil law, creditor law, contract law
Introduction: The course is based on the current Insurance Law and, in conjunction with the judicial interpretation of the Supreme People ' s Court, is based on a large number of court decisions, draws on the latest results of the research conducted at home and abroad, is theoretically linked to practice and provides a systematic presentation of the basic principles and rules of insurance law.

Name: Law and Social Science
Introduction: The subject of Law and Social Sciences, called Social Sciences Law, emphasizes the use of knowledge and methods of social sciences to understand the legal issues of the real world, and focuses on empirical research on legal phenomena and the examination of causality.

Name: French for Specific Purposes
