Introduction: This course aims to enable students to understand the pronunciation rules of French, master important grammatical knowledge, comprehensively understand basic grammar, be able to apply common vocabulary and practical sentence patterns, have intermediate and advanced French reading skills and elementary listening, speaking, writing and translation abilities with the help of a dictionary, and be able to engage in general international cultural exchanges and scientific research.

Name: English for Specific Purposes I
Introduction: This course will study more than forty classic cases of American tort law. The teaching content will cover the most important parts of American tort law, especially negligence tort litigation, but it will also cover strict liability as an exception to negligence tort, as well as intentional tort. The instructor will also guide students in discussions related to tort theory in the classroom.

Name: Quantitative Methods in Law and Cost-Benefit Analysis
Introduction:
In recent years, quantitative analysis methods have begun to enter the field of legal research. Many researchers at home and abroad have begun to use statistics, simulation and other quantitative methods to analyze and evaluate the effects of legal implementation. These new studies have contributed a large number of empirical facts to legal research and have greatly promoted the development of legal science. In order to help law students better study these quantitative analysis literature and master basic quantitative analysis skills, we have specially designed this course. _x000D_
   In this course, we will focus on applying quantitative methods to identify causal relationships and conduct cost-benefit analysis. In the causal relationship identification section, we will introduce random experiments, regression analysis, instrumental variables method, difference-in-difference method and discontinuity regression method; in the cost-benefit analysis section, we will introduce various methods to evaluate the costs and benefits of laws and policies under the condition of market absence, as well as adjustments for uncertainty and income distribution. _x000D_
Throughout the course, we will avoid unnecessary mathematical reasoning, introduce various methods in intuitive language as much as possible, and use a large number of cases from law (especially economic law, intellectual property law) and other disciplines to help understand these methods. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students will have an understanding of the methods of identifying causal relationships and analyzing cost-benefit using quantitative means, will have the ability to read cutting-edge literature in the discipline, and will be able to conduct some simple quantitative legal research on their own.

Name: International Organizations and Global Governance
Introduction: International organizations have become managers and coordinators of global affairs, and are important tools and participants in global governance. On the basis of introducing the basic systems of international organizations, this course explores the status and role of international organizations in the process of global governance. Through case analysis of the functions and roles of international organizations such as the United Nations, World Bank, and International Labor Organization in global governance, we explore the types and models of global governance, and analyze the theories, issues, and controversies existing in global governance. Explore and explore the organizational mechanisms, principles and systems of global governance, and analyze the roles and functions of international organizations and international law in the process of global governance.

Name: Empirical Legal Analysis
Prerequisite: General principles of criminal law, hierarchy of criminal law, jurisprudence
Introduction: The "Legal Empirical Analysis" course is a course offered by Professor Bai Jianjun all year round for the LL.M. and senior LL.M. students at Peking University Law School, aiming to improve graduate students' academic research capabilities and teach legal empirical analysis research methods. Since its inception, this course has not only received high praise among graduate students in the Law School, but also has a certain influence among graduate students in departments such as Chenghuan College. Students taking undergraduate courses have conducted empirical research on legal issues through classroom study and after class, and have published several high-quality academic papers. After studying this course, graduate students can basically master various techniques of legal empirical research and form certain thinking habits of empirical research.

Name: International Law of the Sea
Introduction:
This course will systematically teach the relevant rules and systems of international maritime law, the formation, development and evolution of the "land and sea" spatial order concept, maritime dispute settlement methods, as well as the problems and countermeasures China faces when dealing with surrounding maritime affairs. In the teaching process, emphasis is placed on combining theory with practice, and theoretical analysis will be conducted in conjunction with current hot topics. _x000D_
    This course will invite some internationally renowned experts on the law of the sea to give special lectures or use mock courts to inspire students to think deeply.

Name: Law of Evidence
Prerequisite: Code of Criminal Procedure, Code of Civil Procedure
Introduction: Evidentiary law is a limited course in law on the subject of evidence. This course, which is based on the “Two Evidence Provisions” of the Supreme Court in 2010, the Rules of Evidence established by the Criminal Procedure Code of 2012, and the Civil Procedure Code, teaches the basic concepts, theories and systems of evidence in the law of evidence. The course, which is divided into five sections, “Introductory law of evidence and classification”, “Legal form of evidence”, “Judicial certificate” and “Special rules of evidence”, provides not only a comprehensive presentation of the concept of evidence, theoretical classification, legal form, object of proof, burden of proof, standard of proof, presumptions, etc., but also the basic principles of evidence law for the student system, rules on the exclusion of unlawful evidence, rules on correction of defective evidence, rules on authentication of physical evidence, rules on mutual corroboration of evidence, rules on evidence in procedural decisions, rules on evidence in sentencing proceedings, etc. The course will be guided by the purpose of “Conducting Chinese legal theory from the Chinese experience of the rule of law”, and will attempt to lead students to a more in-depth understanding of the Chinese system of evidence and to make some theoretical predictions and comments on its future development.

Name: Applicable Law in Foreign-Related Civil and Commercial Matters
Introduction: The course will focus on a number of important areas of private international law, such as the basic doctrine, the basic principles, the basic norms and the basic regime of the application of the law, as well as on conflict of laws and the application of law in the field of subjects involved in foreign affairs and commerce, foreign property rights, foreign intellectual property rights, foreign debt rights, foreign marriage families, and foreign inheritance rights, beginning with relevant theory and practice at home and abroad. Since the country is now a multi-jurisdictional country (the Mainland, Hong Kong and Macao), the subject of inter-district conflict of laws will also be addressed separately in this course. In order to ensure that the substantive interests of foreign commercial parties are adequately and effectively safeguarded, the course will also provide a detailed analysis of international civil proceedings and international commercial arbitration.

Name: Maritime Commercial Law
Introduction: This course attempts to combine my country's maritime legislation (mainly the Maritime Law promulgated in 1992) and judicial practice with international conventions and international practices, systematically introduce the basic theories and basic knowledge of maritime law, appropriately analyze some typical cases, and introduce new issues in the field of maritime law. This course is taught in 15 chapters, mainly including the following content: Overview of maritime law, general transportation management, ships, crews, maritime cargo transportation contracts (including voyage charters and multimodal transport contracts), maritime passenger transportation contracts, ship charters (time charters and bareboat charters), maritime towing contracts, ship collisions, shipwreck salvage, general average, limitation of maritime liability, marine insurance contracts, maritime pollution caused by ships, and settlement of maritime disputes.

Name: International Financial Law
Prerequisite: General principles of civil law, corporate law
Introduction: This course teaches the basic concepts, main theories and important systems of international financial law. It combines relevant academic research results and practical cases to systematically introduce the principles of international financial law and legal issues in practical operations. The content of this course mainly includes the legal system and cases of corporate cross-border stock issuance, the legal system and cases of corporate cross-border bond issuance, international syndicated loans and cases, project financing principles and cases, the establishment and investment of private equity funds, overseas investments of sovereign wealth funds and Chinese sovereign wealth funds, derivatives control and trading, foreign exchange control, foreign exchange reserves and foreign exchange transactions. This course not only introduces general issues of international financial law, policy, and regulation, but also discusses the special issues faced by Chinese enterprises in international financial transactions.

Name: Civil Procedure Case Studies
Prerequisite:
Law of Civil Procedure
Civil law
Introduction:
As a social science, law must strengthen students' ability to analyze and solve cases. With the strong support of the school and the college, Peking University Law School has opened three courses: criminal law case study, civil law case study and criminal litigation case study. They have had considerable influence in the legal education industry across the country. They are also among the best in the school's teaching evaluation, and the majority of students have benefited a lot. On this basis, it is imperative to establish supporting civil litigation case study courses. _x000D_
_x000D_
As part of the law school's case study course system, this course hopes to train students in the civil litigation thinking and skills they need as legal practitioners through a complete and systematic case teaching model, and improve students' ability to analyze practical cases. The course should help students learn the legal knowledge and application abilities contained in various basic legal departments, such as citing, interpreting and applying legal provisions, and train students to learn to use case precedents, doctrines and comparative law in the process. In addition, as an advanced course in civil procedure law, this course is also a supplementary course for senior students to make up for knowledge gaps and establish systematic thinking after studying the basic course in civil procedure law. _x000D_

Name: Accounting Law and Auditing Law
Introduction: This course is a transformation of "Financial Accounting", a traditional required course for economic law majors. It is based on the knowledge structure and way of thinking of law school students and selects concepts and knowledge related to legal applications in financial accounting. It is a course design from the perspective of "interdisciplinary research between law and accounting". By studying this course, law students can establish a basic knowledge structure for understanding business operations, and provide help for them to learn and deeply understand departmental laws related to economic activities, including civil and commercial law, economic law, etc.

Name: Classics and Frontiers of the Social Sciences
Introduction: This course is hosted by the Faculty of Social Sciences and is offered simultaneously by six departments: the School of Law, the School of International Relations, the School of Journalism and Communication, the Department of Sociology, the Department of Information Management, and the School of Government. An average of 3 hours per week. Each department teaches twice, 3 hours each time. Midterm and final exams are administered by the department

Name: Comparative Judicial Systems
Introduction: This course is committed to: 1) filling in some deficiencies in judicial knowledge in the entire undergraduate course system; 2) broadening horizons and increasing understanding of foreign judicial systems and related knowledge; 3) strengthening the understanding of the domestic judicial system, especially understanding some of the specific difficulties and obstacles faced in the process of establishing a modern judicial system today, and providing some thoughts on solutions. The main content involves an overview of the judicial system; the people's judicial organs (the nature, status, tasks, establishment, powers, judges, trial organization, etc. of the courts); the people's procuratorates (differences from the procuratorial organs of capitalist countries, the nature, status, tasks, establishment, leadership principles, prosecutorial personnel, etc.) of the people's public security organs (nature, tasks, organizational systems, national security organs, etc.); the people's judicial administrative organs; the lawyer system (the establishment and development of our country's lawyer system, the working institutions of lawyers, lawyer qualifications, etc.); Reform through labor and reeducation through labor; notarization system; arbitration system; mediation system.

Name: Introduction to Computation (C)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Introduction to Computing (C) is an important basic computer course. This course systematically explains computer principles and Python programming methods. The course focuses on the combination of theory and practice, and guides students to learn to use programming methods to solve simple application problems from the perspective of problem solving. _x000D_
Course content includes: computer principles, data types of Python language, control structures, functions and modules, text processing and numerical calculations, data processing and chart analysis, Internet technology, commonly used algorithms, etc. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Society: Structure and Change
Introduction: Based on the basic theories and research perspectives of sociology, students are led to read and understand sociological research results and classic documents about Chinese society, so that students can form a basic understanding of Chinese society. This basic understanding includes: (1) an overall understanding of China’s ideology and cultural spirit; (2) an overall grasp of China’s social structure and changing characteristics; (3) the ability to conduct empirical sociological analysis of the action logic of social actors in Chinese society.

Name: Information Technology and Applications
Introduction: Information technology generally refers to the sum of various technologies for collecting, transmitting, storing, processing, and expressing information. Information technology includes computer technology, software technology, communication technology, computer network technology, multimedia technology, virtual reality technology, information security technology, cloud computing technology, Internet of Things technology, etc. With the popularity of computers and the Internet, people increasingly use computers to produce, process, exchange and disseminate various forms of information. Through the study of this course, students can master the application methods of various information processing and processing tools, including computers and networks, thereby cultivating students' processing and innovation abilities and laying a good foundation for adapting to work, study and life in the information society.

Name: Introduction to Information Behavior
Introduction: The Introduction to Information Behavior course is mainly for undergraduates and introduces concepts, theories and methods related to information behavior such as information users, information needs, information query, information use and so on. Information behavior describes the interaction process between people and information in various situations, mainly including people's inquiry and use behavior of information, and using these information behaviors to solve various problems they encounter in personal, work and life. This course mainly teaches basic concepts, theories, classic models related to information behavior, basic methods for user behavior research, and cutting-edge research progress at home and abroad. Through the study of this course, students will be aware of the various information behaviors around us, understand the analysis methods of information behavior, and be able to conduct preliminary research on information behavior.

Name: Information Technology and Applications Computer Lab
Introduction: Information technology generally refers to the sum of various technologies for collecting, transmitting, storing, processing, and expressing information. The application of information technology includes computer technology, software technology, communication technology, computer network technology, multimedia technology, virtual reality technology, information security technology, cloud computing technology, Internet of Things technology, etc. With the popularity of computers and the Internet, people increasingly use computers to produce, process, exchange and disseminate various forms of information. Through the study of this course, students can master the application methods of various information processing and processing tools, including computers and networks, thereby cultivating students' processing and innovation abilities and laying a good foundation for adapting to work, study and life in the information society.

Name: Information Organization
Introduction: This course is a professional course that systematically introduces the theory and methods of information resource organization. Content includes: the meaning and types of information organization, the principles of information organization, the structural composition and compilation principles of information resource description, taxonomy, and subject method, introduction to typical classifications and subject thesaurus, natural language indexing and retrieval, information resource display and interaction, information organization of Web 2.0 and Web3.0, etc.

Name: Survey and Statistical Methods
Introduction: Surveys and statistics are important scientific research methods and are commonly used methods and techniques for collecting data, analysing data and predicting trends in theoretical research and practical applications. Through this course, students are informed about the whole process and process of social surveys, and learn about the common methods of social surveys and basic knowledge and basic methods of statistical processing of data. Through classroom lectures, case analyses, classroom discussions and course exercises, combined with data statistical analysis tools such as SPSS, learning about the design of survey studies, the implementation of questionnaires, statistical analysis of data, and the preparation of studies and analyses. Building the practical capacity of students in social surveys and in applying social survey methods and statistical analysis of data to various practical areas.

Name: Information Organization Small-Group Discussion
Introduction: The information organization small class discussion class is an attempt to carry out large class teaching and small class discussion in the core basic courses of the major in accordance with the requirements of the school's undergraduate curriculum reform. Large classes will follow the original teaching model, and the credit hours will remain unchanged. An additional 2 hours of small class discussion classes will be added every other week to introduce literature reading and discussion, practical sessions, and content extension into small classes. The large class focuses on teaching concepts, principles, and methods, while the small class focuses on operation, practice, and discussion based on the contents of the large class, and they cooperate with each other.

Name: Principles of Management
Introduction: Management is the process of effectively planning, organizing, leading and controlling the resources owned by an organization in order to achieve established organizational goals. Management is an applied and imprecise comprehensive discipline. It is both a science and an art. This course takes organizations as the research object, discusses how to use limited resources for alternative and competitive management activities in a specific environment, and focuses on analyzing and exploring the commonality of management processes related to a certain type of specific activities. It mainly includes five major chapters: introduction, planning, organization, leadership and control.

Name: Information Resource Development
Introduction: This course is based on the construction of information resources of information service institutions. Starting from the analysis of the concepts and functions of information, information media and information resources, this course systematically discusses the types, characteristics and functions of various information resources such as paper information media, non-paper information media, electronic and network; reveals the production, distribution process and management of information media. , control mechanism; and based on the actual situation of my country's information service institutions, comprehensively introduce the plans and principles of information media collection; conduct an in-depth analysis of information media selection and collection methods; introduce in detail the implementation of the information media collection automation system; and conduct in-depth discussions on the evaluation of information resources and the construction of the information resource guarantee system. _x000D_

Name: Copyright Law
Introduction: This course is taught based on my country's Copyright Law. It starts with the basic concept of copyright, the social significance of copyright law and legislative principles, and then introduces the evolution of the copyright system, the objects of copyright protection, the rights of copyright owners, the creation and protection period of copyright, publisher's rights and neighboring rights related to copyright, transfer and reasonable use of copyright, protection of copyright, management of copyright, and copyright trade.

Name: Database Systems Computer Lab
Prerequisite:
1. Computation overview
2. Programme design
Algorithms and data structure
Disconnected mathematics
Introduction:
Database is a warehouse that organizes, stores and manages data according to data structure. With the development of information technology and market, data management is no longer just about storing and managing data, but has transformed into various data management methods required by users. Database technology is the core part of various information systems such as management information systems, office automation systems, and decision support systems. It is an important technical means for scientific research and decision-making management, and has been widely used in various aspects.    _x000D_
_x000D_
The main contents include:_x000D_
Chapter 1 Overview of Database Basics_x000D_
Chapter 2 Relational Model_x000D_
Chapter 3 Structured Query Language_x000D_
Chapter 4 Data Modeling_x000D_
Chapter 5 Database Design_x000D_
Chapter 6 Database Management_x000D_
Chapter 7 Database Applications_x000D_
Chapter 8 Big Data, Data Warehousing and Business Intelligence Systems_x000D_
Database instance and application development_x000D_

Name: Database Systems
Prerequisite:
1. Computation overview
2. Programme design
3. Data structure
4. Disconnected mathematics
Introduction:
Database is a warehouse that organizes, stores and manages data according to data structure. With the development of information technology and market, data management is no longer just about storing and managing data, but has transformed into various data management methods required by users. Database technology is the core part of various information systems such as management information systems, office automation systems, and decision support systems. It is an important technical means for scientific research and decision-making management, and has been widely used in various aspects.    _x000D_
_x000D_
The main contents include: overview of database basics, relational database, structured query language, database design theory, database design, database management, database applications, big data, data warehouse and business intelligence system, database examples and application development_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Computer Networks
Introduction:
This course introduces the basic principles of computer networks. Content includes: _x000D_
_x000D_
1. A brief history of the development of network technology;_x000D_
2. Data communication technology foundation: including computer data communication model, analog communication and digital communication, data encoding, transmission media and data communication interface; _x000D_
3. Data link layer, stop and wait protocol, ARQ protocol and HDLC protocol; _x000D_
⒋LAN technology, including channel sharing technology, LAN architecture, IEEE802 family standards and LAN interconnection; _x000D_
⒌WAN technology, including routing mechanism, congestion control, frame relay, etc.; _x000D_
⒍Network interconnection, including the basic principles of network interconnection, Internet Internet Protocol IP, and Internet routing mechanism; _x000D_
⒎Transport layer, the Internet's transport layer protocol, including TCP and UDP; _x000D_
⒏Application layer, Internet application layer protocols, including DNS, SMTP, FTP, TELNET, HTTP, etc. _x000D_

Name: Information Architecture Design and Practice
Introduction: Today's Internet is composed of billions of websites, and every day users click and interact in such a complex information environment. This course introduces students to the basics of information architecture (IA), aiming to understand the information needs and activities of website visitors, and to create design elements to help users easily find the information they need in this complex information environment. This course will cover various theories, strategies, and techniques for building information, focusing on the information needs of large-scale websites, and explaining the structure, organization, tags, browsing, and search design required for the process of building a website. Through the study of this course, students can use the knowledge and skills of IA to understand real-world website construction, and combine the knowledge of project management and user experience to expose students to different practical activities.

Name: Information Storage and Retrieval Computer Lab
History of the Chinese Book
Introduction:
This course, which focuses on the development and evolution of the history of Chinese books, provides an in-depth study of the ancient Chinese book culture. Starting with the creation of scripts, the origin of books, the emergence of publishing activities in our history, in a time- and in-generational order, through the elaboration and analysis of historical times, codification institutions, organizational management, important results, etc., a coloured volume of the history of Chinese books stretching over the millennia, which is taught in an orderly manner to historically important publishing institutions, prominent publishers, major contemporary publishing events and landmark publications.
Also, in order to enhance interaction, the curriculum will be four-hour productions of ancient books, combining what has been learned with hands-on work, so that students can feel for themselves how a book is produced and written. Letting students experience knowledge is not only an accumulation of civilization, but also a bond of national emotion. Currently, there are mainly two forms of handwritten production: wired and folded.

Name: Information Services
Introduction: This course is now a professional core course of the Department of Information Management. It closely integrates the informationization process, the development of information economy and service economy, and the evolution of human information behavior. It deeply explores the basic theory and basic methods of "user-oriented" information services and their innovative application and development in various industries of the national economy and all aspects of social life, and strives to achieve the teaching purposes of basic cognition, professional identification, and pioneering practice of information services.

Name: Information Storage and Retrieval
Prerequisite: Algorithms and Data Structures; Database Systems; Information Organisations
Introduction:
Information storage and retrieval is one of the required courses for the "Information Management and Information Systems" major. The course content mainly includes the following knowledge units: _x000D_
①Basic knowledge of information retrieval: concepts, basic principles, development history, research objects and related disciplines of information storage and retrieval. _x000D_
②Mathematical models of information retrieval: including the three classic retrieval models of Boolean, vector, and probability and their respective improvement or optimization models. _x000D_
③Information retrieval system: including the type, basic structure, development and design of information retrieval system, etc. _x000D_
④Information retrieval technology methods: including text retrieval technology methods and non-text retrieval technology methods (mainly CBR retrieval technology for audio and video information), as well as Web search technology methods. _x000D_
⑤ Commonly used information retrieval systems and their use: including the basic processes of information retrieval operations, retrieval strategies, and the characteristics, functions, basic structures and query usage methods of various types of retrieval systems. _x000D_
⑥Information retrieval evaluation: including the history of information retrieval evaluation research, evaluation index system, evaluation case analysis, TREC project, etc. _x000D_
⑦Text information processing automation technology: automatic indexing, text clustering and classification, text filtering, text summarization, etc. _x000D_

Name: Innovation Engineering Practicum (Internship)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
This course is a summer practical course corresponding to the general elective course "Innovative Engineering Practice" in the spring semester. _x000D_
——The course content corresponds to the spring course; but it is completed using flipped classroom and blended teaching methods. _x000D_
_x000D_
Students need about two weeks to: _x000D_
● Watch designated course videos at a certain pace; _x000D_
● Listen to teachers’ lectures in the classroom and complete practical training under the guidance of teachers; _x000D_
● Conduct group discussions and prototype development after class; _x000D_
● Complete an on-site audition report at the end of the course. _x000D_

Name: Information Economics
Introduction:
Information economics is the branch of economics that studies information and how information systems influence organizational decision-making. Information economics has been widely used in the context of the rapid development of information technology, especially the Internet. _x000D_
      This course will first introduce the basic theories and methods of information economics. Secondly, this course will teach how to use basic economic methods to analyze strategic decisions related to information products and services, such as pricing, versions, channels and other decisions. _x000D_
      Through the study of this course, on the one hand, students can understand the theory and development status of information economics. On the other hand, they can combine the development frontiers of the Internet economy and initially master the research methods of using information economics methods to analyze organizational decision-making. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Data Mining
Introduction: Data mining is an emerging discipline that discovers knowledge from large amounts of data and has broad application prospects. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic concepts, principles and techniques of data mining, and be able to use data mining tools such as Clementine and SPSS to analyze real-world data and interpret the output results of data mining. Cultivate students' ability to conduct in-depth information analysis.

Name: Business Information
Introduction: This course is an elective course for all majors in the Department of Information Management. It mainly focuses on the study of literature, information resources and consulting activities in the business field. It allows students to have an understanding of the global business information environment, examine the impact of national economic development and the international trade of American enterprises and companies, and the diversified functions related to internal business of the company. It strives to enable students to understand what business information is needed by individuals within the organization and how to apply it, and to provide a general description of relevant external information resources.

Name: Interactive Information Retrieval
Prerequisite:
Information storage and retrieval

Students are advised to take their own courses after learning about the rationale and techniques of the information retrieval system.
Introduction: This course mainly introduces user interaction behavior in search systems, including all aspects of user search behavior, user search experience and user evaluation. It is a branch of Human Information Behavior (HIB) and an extension of the Information Storage and Retrieval course. This course has similarities with the human-computer interaction course, but the main difference is that it focuses on users' search behavior in search systems, search experience, and their evaluation of the system. The course content includes information retrieval system interface design, search task analysis, user query analysis, user search experience and other related theories, models, research and practice. It aims to encourage students to use the knowledge learned in the course to conduct user interaction behavior analysis and user experience analysis on various types of existing information retrieval systems, such as search engines, digital libraries, databases, mobile search and social network media, and then put forward suggestions for system optimization. This is a research-led course in which students have the opportunity to conduct evaluation research on search systems under the guidance of instructors.

Name: Informetrics
Introduction:
_x000D_
      The early names of informetrics, such as bibliometrics and information metrology, have always been classic research contents in the fields of library science and information science. With the deepening of the informatization process of human society, the importance of its research and teaching work has become more prominent and its name has become more current. _x000D_
    _x000D_
      Based on the review and analysis of the emergence, development and evolution of informetrics, the teaching of this course comprehensively describes its basic theory, main research methods and research results, helping students to correctly understand the basic concepts and meanings of measurement indicators in the field of informetrics, as well as the contents of classic laws, to skillfully use commonly used quantitative analysis tools and database systems, and to cultivate basic skills in solving practical problems, thus laying the foundation for subsequent in-depth thematic learning and research work. _x000D_
_x000D_
      This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduates and requires students to have a certain foundation in prerequisite courses. _x000D_

Name: Community Informatics
Prerequisite: Information management overview, qualitative data analysis, application of quantitative analysis
Introduction:
Community informatics emerged in the late 1990s, originating from the application of information and communication technology by special communities and various information practice activities. It is currently developing rapidly in North America, Europe, Australia and other regions. Social informatics was first developed from the practical field. Since the term was proposed by Professor Michael Gurstein, director of the Canadian Center for Community Informatics Research, Training and Development, it has had a strong practical flavor. Most CI researchers and teachers agree that CI is first and foremost an action-oriented field, emphasizing the key role of ICT in various community affairs and reducing digital inequality. _x000D_
      Professor Mike Goldstein defines social informatics as “the application of information and communication technologies (ICT) to various processes of the community, so that the community can gain ‘ability’ and ‘power’ (Enable & Empower)”; the research and practice goals of community informatics are to use ICT to help achieve various goals of the community, including narrowing the digital divide within and between communities; investigating how and under what conditions disadvantaged groups can access ICT And have an impact on itself, especially using the Internet to promote the economic development, social justice and political equality of this community. Community informatics focuses on exploring how the basic unit "community" of society generates, creates, processes and shares information and knowledge in the context of the information revolution. It uses investigation methods to explore the role and influence of ICT, cultural and social factors in this process. _x000D_
      This course aims to introduce the research results of Community Informatics from the international academic community and explore the impact of Community Informatics on China’s social development and the field of library and information science. It also enables students to initially master the basic concepts, theories, research methods, main research hot spots and cutting-edge issues of Community Informatics through classroom study, discussion and field investigation. _x000D_
      The course will be presented to students through a combination of literature study, classroom lectures, classroom discussions, on-site lectures by domestic experts, remote lectures by overseas experts, and field surveys.

Name: Techniques of Text Information Analysis
Introduction:
As a type of information, text information has a very wide range of applications. With the development of deep learning and natural language processing technology, the use of modern technology to solve problems related to text information has received increasing attention. Therefore, a course that systematically teaches text information analysis technology is needed. This course takes text information as the main object and systematically explains the technology, algorithms and implementation of text information processing and analysis. In terms of general technical algorithms, it includes Chinese word segmentation technology and intelligent models commonly used in text analysis. In terms of specific content, it includes network information crawling and parsing technology, multi-source information fusion and cleaning technology, information extraction technology, knowledge discovery and fusion technology, etc. _x000D_
       This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduate students. _x000D_

Name: Management Information Systems
Prerequisite:
Initial courses include:
1. General calculations
Students have basic knowledge of computer software and hardware, as well as the basis for programming languages.
2. Database systems
Basic knowledge of the conceptual rationale of the database and the basis for the use of a specific database management system.
3. Computer networks
Basic knowledge of computer network infrastructure and computer network applications development.
Management Learn.
Basic knowledge of organizational structure, planning and management decision-making methods in management science.
Introduction:
A management information system is a system composed of people, computers and other peripheral devices that can collect, transmit, store, process, maintain and use information. _x000D_
Its main task is to maximize the use of modern computer and network communication technology to strengthen the enterprise's information management. Through the investigation and understanding of the human, material, financial, equipment, technology and other resources owned by the enterprise, establish correct data, process and prepare various information materials and provide them to managers in a timely manner so as to make correct decisions and continuously improve the management level and economic benefits of the enterprise. _x000D_
Students majoring in information management and information systems will face the changes in globalized industries and business activities from the industrial age to the information age in the future. The content of this course covers five major areas of information system knowledge: basic concepts of information systems, information technology, business applications, development processes, and management challenges. It strives to enable students to understand how to use and manage information technology to optimize business processes, promote business decision-making, and gain competitive advantages. At the same time, it introduces the latest Internet technologies in today's networked enterprises and global markets, and the important role they play in enterprises' business activities. _x000D_

Name: Information Analysis and Decision Making
Introduction:
This course is divided into three parts: The first part introduces basic concepts such as decision-making types, decision-making procedures, and decision-making principles. The second part describes how to collect and analyze information on major decision-making issues to provide information guarantee for correct decisions. The third part introduces the quality of decision-makers, the effective cooperation of decision-making members, and how to make decision-making more scientific. The purpose is to enable students to understand and master the basic concepts and methods of information research, to know the common basic knowledge of scientific decision-making and information analysis, and to strive to apply what they have learned to management research propositions. _x000D_
   _x000D_

Name: Public Health Information Resources and Their Use
Introduction: Public health information is also referred to as user health information, which aims to study health information systems in terms of meeting the needs of general public health information. The course includes user health information, the conceptual and theoretical basis of user empowerment. User health information system application, construction, evaluation. Methods for analysing user information needs. Through this course of study, students are given a basic mastery of the methods used to design, construct and evaluate the application of health information. It can also analyse the information needs of specific user groups. The knowledge gained can be applied to libraries and information services.

Name: Library Automation
Prerequisite:
1. Library overview
2. General calculations
3. Database system
Introduction:
Library automation is a process with computer technology as the core, combined with network communication technology, to automatically control various library businesses. It uses computers to handle library business and provide corresponding services, such as: book acquisition, cataloging, periodical management, circulation management, bibliographic retrieval and administrative management, etc.   _x000D_
_x000D_
 The main contents of the course include: introduction, analysis of characteristics and elements of library automation systems, machine-readable catalogs, library automation system structure, library automation system manufacturers and products, protocols and standards in library automation systems, database technology in library automation, digital libraries and new knowledge service systems, and the development of future library automation systems.

Name: Information Systems Analysis and Design
Prerequisite: Course on information management and information systems
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory core course for the undergraduate major in Information Management and Information Systems in the Department of Information Management of Peking University. _x000D_
Information systems is a discipline that integrates management science, information science, systems science, behavioral science, computer science and communication technology. With the continuous development of information technology and the deepening of the informatization process, the theories and methods of information system analysis and design are also constantly developing. This course draws on advanced teaching ideas and teaching content from related courses at home and abroad, and strives to reflect new developments and trends in this field. It also incorporates many years of teaching and learning, as well as practical experience of teachers and students of the course. _x000D_
The teaching objectives include: on the basis of students possessing technical knowledge such as mathematics, computers, networks, databases, and related knowledge of management and operations research, they will comprehensively and comprehensively master the basic methods and technologies of information system analysis and design through classroom teaching and practical teaching links.

Name: Business Intelligence and Analytics
Introduction:
With the continuous advancement of information technology and the deepening of informatization, enterprises are also facing greater challenges. Business intelligence can assist enterprises in collecting, managing and analyzing structured and unstructured business data and information. It is very effective in improving business decision-making, taking effective business actions, and improving corporate performance. _x000D_
This course will first explain the basic concepts of business intelligence and how business intelligence can help enterprises cope with the challenges they face in the modern business environment. Secondly, it will explain a series of common business data analysis methods and their applications, including descriptive, predictive and prescriptive analysis. Finally, it will explain some high-level business analysis methods, such as heuristic search, Monte Carlo simulation and other methods, and their application in business decision analysis. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students will learn the basic concepts of business intelligence and analysis on the one hand; on the other hand, they will master the practical methods of modeling and analyzing data generated in business activities and supporting business decision-making. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Heart Health
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
The heart is the most important organ of the human body and the engine of life activities. The heart beats approximately 2.5 billion times in a person's life, supplying blood and oxygen to the human body. When there is a problem with the heart, it is unable to complete these tasks, leading to the most serious health problems and even death. At present, heart-related diseases have become the leading cause of death among adults in China and around the world. About 17 million people die from heart problems globally every year. Although the occurrence of some heart diseases is inevitable in the process of human aging, if you can start a healthy lifestyle as early as possible in adolescence, you can master enough knowledge to identify early signs of heart disease as early as possible, especially in adolescence, understand the basic knowledge of heart disease, so that early recognition, early identification, and early prevention are crucial to preventing the occurrence of heart disease and even death. In addition, popularizing heart disease knowledge and cardiac first aid methods among teenagers is a practical need for school education and is also a common practice in mainstream countries around the world. _x000D_
The purpose of this 2-week course is to enhance students' understanding of the working principle of the heart, the impact of heart disease, first aid knowledge of heart disease, and prevention of heart disease. _x000D_
In the course, we first provide an overview of the heart and related diseases, tracing back the understanding of heart structure, function and heart diseases from the 2nd century BC to the present, as well as the landmark progress in diagnosis and treatment. Then the risk factors related to heart disease, such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, diabetes, obesity, etc., are introduced. With the improvement of living standards, these risk factors are becoming more popular among adolescents. By strengthening the concept of risk factors, students can understand what heart-related indicators they should pay attention to during routine physical examinations and clearly understand the numbers related to their own health. It also introduces common heart diseases, especially the most common coronary heart disease. After having a preliminary concept of heart disease, we will further popularize the first aid knowledge of cardiovascular disease, focusing on explaining the life-saving first aid measures - cardiopulmonary resuscitation and the operation of automatic external defibrillator. In addition, in addition to explaining knowledge about heart and heart-related diseases and how to maintain individual heart health, we will also analyze and compare the global management models of such diseases within the framework of our country and the World Health Organization. The course will also cover the health and wellness knowledge of the motherland’s medicine for this disease. At the end of the course, we will introduce the latest developments in the heart field, including regenerative medicine in the field of basic research, telemedicine in the new technology field, and hot issues such as the impact of big data on human heart disease. These may play an important role in maintaining heart health and improving disease in the future. _x000D_

Name: Object-Oriented Programming with Java
Introduction: A comprehensive presentation of the basic knowledge of the subject-oriented programming language Java, the basic structure of the Java application and the necessary Java programming techniques, including the Java language profile and the operating and development environment, the Java language base, Java object-oriented programme design, common categories and interfaces, Java anomaly processing, multi-wire programming, database programming, web newsletters, graphical user interfaces, Web search techniques and information retrieval techniques.

Name: Object-Oriented Programming with Java Computer Lab
Introduction: Computer-based content includes basic Java language, Java object-oriented programming, common classes and interfaces, Java exception handling, multi-threading, database programming, network communications, graphical user interface, Web search technology and information retrieval technology.

Name: Multimedia Technology
Introduction: As multimedia technology becomes increasingly international and large-scale, it has changed human life and work patterns, and has become inseparable from people's lives. This course teaches the basic knowledge, principles and techniques of multimedia. It specializes in the data types, color science, compression algorithms, image compression standards, video coding standards, etc. of graphics and images. Together with the learning, editing, and design of multimedia tools, it improves and strengthens students' mastery and innovation ability in the field of multimedia knowledge (including text media, image media, audio media, and video media).

Name: Information Security
Introduction: 1 With the improvement of information technology, it has become an inevitable trend for people at all levels to use computers to transmit, access and process information. However, how to protect confidential information transmitted on the network and stored in computer systems from the threat of illegal activities such as theft, modification, forgery and destruction by unauthorized personnel is the key to information security. In order to meet the urgent needs of the times, this course takes the issues related to information security in information management systems and explains topics such as information security architecture, physical security, user identification, access control, cryptography, and management control from different levels of perspectives, such as environmental perspective, user perspective, system perspective, information perspective, and manager perspective.

Name: Digital Libraries and the Semantic Web
Prerequisite: Data structure; computer network; database system, information retrieval; information organization
Introduction: Digital libraries have two meanings. One is the research and development of Semantic Web, and the other is the extension and development of traditional libraries in the network environment. This course attempts to introduce the basic knowledge of these two aspects, and on this basis, uses the digital library as a generalized information system, discusses some basic issues of information collection, information representation, information organization, and information utilization, and studies the conditions and implementation methods required to realize automatic machine understanding and processing of each link of the information utilization cycle.

Name: Applications of Big Data Technology
Prerequisite: Computer overview, data structure and algorithm, database system
Introduction:
This course starts from a practical perspective and is based on the Python language. It teaches relevant analysis tools and software packages, introduces the big data technology platform architecture, and conducts practice based on specific fields such as public culture and intelligence analysis. Through the study of this course, you can develop the application capabilities of big data technology operation and analysis. _x000D_
This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduate students. _x000D_

Name: Electronic Commerce
Introduction:
With the advent of Internet technology, e-commerce has become an indispensable and mature business model in people ' s lives. E-commerce has entered a new stage of development marked by social and mobile commerce, driven by technologies such as Web 2.0 and mobile Internet since 2010.
This course will track recent developments and trends in e-commerce, teach basic concepts and principles of e-commerce and analytical methods of e-commerce strategies for enterprises. Through the course, students will be updated on the state of development of e-commerce, the technological basis of e-commerce, the classic model of e-commerce, and the strategies and implementation of e-commerce.

Name: Exploring the Blood Vessels
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction:
Vascular medicine is a comprehensive discipline that studies blood vessel-related diseases. With the development of medicine, the traditional subject classification method can no longer meet the current requirements for comprehensive prevention and treatment of vascular diseases. The blood vessel-centered health concept is conducive to the development of medical disciplines. _x000D_
Vascular diseases such as coronary heart disease, hypertension, diabetes, and stroke are currently the leading causes of death for people around the world. They can affect important organs throughout the body. They are related to many risk factors for metabolic abnormalities, such as hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and diabetes, and lead to progressive vascular damage and eventually vascular events, including acute myocardial infarction, stroke, uremia, peripheral vascular disease, etc., with high mortality and disability rates. The pathophysiological basis of the above-mentioned diseases is the lesions of the blood vessels supplying the above-mentioned organs, manifested as arteriosclerosis, atherosclerosis, etc. Therefore, to fundamentally reduce the fatal and disabling consequences of cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, we must not only pay attention to and treat serious vascular events, but more importantly, early detection of vascular lesions, early intervention, and early prevention to avoid the occurrence of end-stage vascular events. _x000D_
The vascular exploration course will start from the theoretical basis of the anatomical characteristics, physiological mechanisms, mechanical characteristics, genetic and environmental influencing factors of the vascular system, and elaborate on the pathogenesis of vascular lesions and clinical events, diagnostic methods, drug treatment, surgical procedures, interventional technology, prevention and rehabilitation treatment at home and abroad, and conduct an in-depth and simple discussion of the latest research results and clinical applications in this field. _x000D_
This course will invite experts with rich clinical and teaching experience as teachers, providing students with a good opportunity to broaden their horizons and enrich their medical knowledge. _x000D_

Name: General Japanese (IV)
Introduction: The curriculum expands the vocabulary of students to the appropriate size of the scenario to include specific scenarios for the purpose of learning to the point of use. At the cultural level, the aim is essentially to be polite and to be able to use the most natural and elegant Japanese language in the public sphere and in the open. The understanding of both grammar and words is based on the penetration of Japanese culture and language practices and is based on systematic presentation and re-learning. In the introductory phase, greater emphasis will be placed on repeated exercises and continuous familiarity with the most natural usage of Japanese to reach levels 3 and 4 of the International Japan and Capability Test.

Name: Argumentative Essay Writing
Introduction:
At the request of undergraduate sociology students, this course is prepared for fourth-year students (entering the thesis writing stage) who want to master the essentials of essay writing. The course is designed to help undergraduate students understand the logic of research thinking and argumentative writing. It is optional for students who want to join research work and improve their paper writing skills. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course content is taught according to the basic links required for argumentative papers: _x000D_
_x000D_
*Research Preparation_x000D_
* Build issue_x000D_
*Literature Assessment_x000D_
* Method selection_x000D_
*Organization information_x000D_
* Analysis framework_x000D_
* Theoretical explanation_x000D_
*Research Plan_x000D_

Name: Contemporary Western Social Thought
Introduction:
Observing life and understanding the world from the perspective of "society" has started from the beginning of modernity, and society has become the core category of modernity. Sociology or broad social theory attempts to establish a set of social logic and use "social" methods to reveal the secrets of the existence of modern society in a new way. In this way, social theory is different from the theoretical vision of natural science or humanities, and it also distances itself from classical thought. This is the basic question that we need to explore in the course, so as to understand the theoretical basis for modern social thought. This course achieves two teaching purposes by carefully tracing and analyzing social ideological traditions: _x000D_
1. Further clarify the concept and methods of "society" and outline the key clues of Western social thought;_x000D_
2. Sort out several important schools of social thought in the transformation of modern theoretical and empirical research, and present different analytical paths and their logical foundations. _x000D_

Name: Historical Sociology
Introduction: Through an introduction to the evolution of research trends and an introduction to classic research texts, it outlines some problem awareness, development context and application fields of historical social research (based on historical sociology in sociology, taking into account social history in history and historical anthropology in anthropology) that focus on culture, mentality and daily life. It demonstrates the importance and innovation of combining and implementing the historical dimension in social research, and cultivates students' ability to read original works and reflect on perspectives.

Name: Sociology of Labor
Prerequisite:
Social science generalists;
Data analysis techniques
Introduction:
_x000D_
1. Labor sociology is a branch of sociology that uses sociological theoretical systems and methods to study the structure, functions and operating rules of workers’ social labor activities. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Starting from the characteristics of workers’ labor activities, the main research contents of labor sociology include five major parts: workers, occupations, labor organizations, labor relations and labor social issues. The content of labor sociology can be studied at three levels: focusing on the individual level, mainly focusing on workers’ attitudes, behaviors, qualities, abilities, and socialization processes; career choice characteristics, career, career reputation, career mobility, etc. And study the relationship between these characteristics of workers and social development. Focusing on the group and organizational levels, it mainly focuses on labor organizations, labor relations, labor systems, and the cultural construction of labor organizations. Focusing on the social level, it mainly focuses on labor social issues and studies the relationship between individual survival and social maintenance. _x000D_

Name: Sociology of the Family
Introduction:
Starting from the origin, composition and social meaning of the so-called "nuclear families", this course will guide students to understand the meaning and issues of modern families from the perspectives of historical and comparative social studies, especially the position of the family in Chinese history and contemporary social changes. The core of this course is the triple relationship transformed from Fei Xiaotong's "Reproductive System": the relationship between husband and wife, the relationship between parents and offspring, and the relationship between offspring. On the basis of the three, this course will extend the understanding of family to social units beyond the home. The family cultivates the basic elements for the establishment and change of society, and also breeds the basic spiritual temperament for the establishment of a complex civilization. This course is no exception at home and abroad. This course hopes to prepare a preliminary knowledge base and problem awareness for students who are interested in exploring the family. _x000D_
The content of this course is divided into three parts: traditional, empirical and theoretical. Each section is taught approximately ten times. The traditional part mainly focuses on the morals and institutions of traditional Chinese families, including the ritual order and family property relations of traditional families, as well as the family in the traditional legal system. The core of the experience is the formation and consequences of what Fei Xiaotong calls the dual-lineage nuclear family in modern society. It has the greatest relationship with the second demographic transition. It is also the most important starting point for contemporary sociological research on the family. It is closely related to many empirical issues we encounter in today's Chinese society. The theoretical part will explain some of the most important theoretical clues for understanding the family, namely the transfer of patriarchy in the history of family development; the issue of "free will" union in modern marriage; the relationship between family power and state power, etc. _x000D_

Name: Social Game Theory
Introduction:
"Social interaction" is one of the core issues in sociological research. In interaction, individual actors are not separated and isolated, but respond to the actions of others and take into account the various possible reactions of others when planning actions. This interactivity is a basic feature of social behavior and is reflected in various social actions—whether it is friendships, cooperation with colleagues, market competition, or social movements, etc. _x000D_
     Game theory provides a perspective and a set of analytical tools for the rigorous study of interactive behavior. Since its emergence in the mid-20th century, the influence of game theory has gradually expanded, and it has now developed into one of the important basic tools in social sciences and has been widely used in various disciplines from economics to sociology. _x000D_
     This course strives to help students master the basic concepts and common analysis tools in game theory, as well as how to use game theory methods to research and analyze specific social phenomena. The course content includes basic game types, the concept of game "solution" or equilibrium, the role of information in strategic interactions, the analysis of repeated games and other topics. It also provides a brief introduction to the research on evolutionary game theory and behavioral games. In the course, you will learn how to observe and understand some important and basic sociological phenomena from the perspective of game theory, such as how cooperation is possible, the dilemma of collective action, social systems and their evolution, etc. _x000D_

Name: Social Survey Practicum
Introduction: Professional internships are arranged in the third year of college, and their purpose is to allow students to have a more specific and profound understanding of this major based on professional study and investigation. By following the tutor's field research in relevant units or projects, you can gain a deeper understanding of sociological applications and initially apply the professional knowledge you have learned into practice.

Name: Fundamentals and Applications of Geographic Information Systems
Introduction: This course is a methods course for undergraduates majoring in urban management in the School of Government. Geographic information system is an emerging technology for collecting, processing, analyzing and applying spatial information. It has been widely used in urban and rural planning, urban management, resource management and other fields, as well as in social and economic research. This course mainly introduces the basic concepts and principles of geographic information systems, focusing on the spatial analysis functions of geographic information systems. The course focuses on the introduction and application of spatial analysis methods based on geographic information systems.

Name: Anthropological Theory
Introduction:
What is anthropology? What are the basic questions, core concepts, and theoretical paradigms of anthropological research? This course introduces the development history of anthropological theory, different academic areas and their theoretical paradigms and representatives, and different theoretical aspects and themes. Through reading literature, classroom lectures, group reports, and critical writing, we help undergraduates majoring in anthropology and students from other majors interested in anthropology clarify the research boundaries of anthropology, define the research objects of anthropology, and master the intellectual tradition of anthropology. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Quantitative Methods in Urban Governance
Introduction: Cities and regions are complex systems containing multiple departments, multiple subjects, and multiple spatial and temporal dimensions. The analysis of urban governance and spatial planning issues requires the comprehensive use of multidisciplinary theories and analytical methods such as political science, regional economics, urban and rural planning, geography, statistics, and computer science. Among them, quantitative analysis based on various types of data is an important way to promote the scientific formulation of policies in multiple fields such as space, population, industry, housing, transportation, public facilities, and social governance. This course aims to enable students to master the basic principles and methods of quantitative analysis of issues related to urban governance and spatial planning, pays attention to the combination of method principles and real-life problems, and cultivates students' thinking ability to analyze real-life problems based on various types of data and their proficiency in the application of related software. The course will introduce students to basic quantitative analysis methods in the field of urban governance and spatial planning, including three sections. The first is the basic knowledge section, including course introduction, foundation of spatial analysis methods and the basis of urban political analysis; the second is the practical application section, including urban spatial measurement, population change analysis, industrial development analysis, housing supply and demand analysis, traffic management analysis, public facility layout analysis, and regional development and governance analysis; the third is the expansion section, including basic principles and methods of policy simulation, big data and urban governance, visualization and information communication, and summary of analysis strategies.

Name: Inequality, Social Institutions and Social Change
Introduction: Comprehensive presentation of basic sociological knowledge on social inequalities, social systems and social change

Name: Sociology of Deviance and Crime
Introduction: The purpose of this course is threefold: first, to introduce the definition of deviance and various theoretical perspectives to explain deviance; to clarify the relationship between deviance and social control (especially the judicial system and correctional institutions); secondly, to analyze specific classic cases of deviance research, especially examples of conceptual operations and material use, so that students can have an intuitive understanding of empirical research in the field of deviance; thirdly, to guide students to conduct research on local target phenomena on the basis of understanding the existing theoretical and empirical research results of deviance sociology.

Name: Casework
Introduction:
(1) Understand the nature of social case work and enable students to master the general theory and development of case work. _x000D_
(2) Introduce three basic theoretical models for the implementation of case work: psychoanalytic theory and psychoanalytic therapy, behaviorism theory and behavior therapy, and person-centered theory and person-centered therapy. Master the theoretical basis and value orientation of these three types of casework. _x000D_
(3) Learn the "psycho-social" therapy of social case work and its application in case practice. _x000D_
(4) Study and discuss the values and conflicts in casework practice. _x000D_
(5) Learn and discuss the core conditions of helping relationships. _x000D_
(6) Understand that social casework is a process of planned change. _x000D_
(7) Recognize, identify and discuss the different roles of social caseworkers. _x000D_
(8) Learn intervention skills in casework and their application in the process of helping others. _x000D_
(9) Increase awareness of the application of "self" in the process of helping others and understand its importance. _x000D_

Name: Community Work
Introduction:
This course teaches the basic theories, methods and practices of community work. _x000D_
Chapters 1 to 4 introduce the basic principles, theoretical foundations, practical models and methods of communities and community work; Chapters 5 to 9 introduce the practice of urban and rural community development in my country and discuss related issues. _x000D_
    The course strives to combine theory with practice. On the basis of learning from foreign community development experience, the course reflects on the local characteristics of community development in my country and cultivates students' good theoretical foundation and practical and reflective abilities. _x000D_
Teaching method:_x000D_
Classroom lectures are the main focus, combined with group discussions and community visits.               _x000D_
Student performance evaluation method:_x000D_
Regular homework accounts for 40%, and the final paper accounts for 60%. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Social Welfare
Introduction: This course is a required course for undergraduate students majoring in social work. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students can: 1) master the basic concepts, main theories and analytical frameworks of social welfare; 2) understand China’s social welfare ideas in different historical periods and the major contemporary social welfare systems; 3) use relevant theories and methods to conduct preliminary analysis and research on related welfare issues.

Name: Social History of China
Prerequisite:
This course is recommended for sophomore or junior students to take as an elective, and it can be studied in conjunction with the history of Chinese social thought_x000D_
Prerequisite course:_x000D_
Introduction to Sociology,_x000D_
History of Chinese Social Thought, _x000D_
Introduction: This course will introduce students to the specific evolution of Chinese society from pre-Qin to modern times. On the one hand, it focuses on introducing the main characteristics of Chinese society in each era, and attempts to establish horizontal structural connections between characteristics. On the other hand, it attempts to connect different eras and explore their diachronic vertical changes. Simply put, we hope that by studying simultaneity structures and diachronic changes, students can understand Chinese society from a historical perspective.

Name: Sociology of Religion
Introduction: This course will systematically introduce the research methods, conceptual framework, theoretical system, classic literature and latest developments in the sociology of religion. At the micro level, we will explore why people believe in religion and the social consequences of religious experiences; at the meso level, this course will introduce the organizational forms and changes of religion; at the macro level, we will strive to understand the impact of competition and regulation on the religious market. This course will also provide an introduction to classic studies to understand the social consequences of religion, including religion and conflict, religion and conformity, religion and civic engagement, religion and the economy, and more. Finally, we will introduce the debate between secularization theory and the market theory of religion. Through this course, students can understand the knowledge system and research frontiers of the sociology of religion.

Name: Linear Regression and Its Applications
Introduction: This course "Regression Analysis and Applications" will be a moderately difficult statistics course, open to senior undergraduate students who are interested in quantitative research (or are preparing to use quantitative methods for their graduation thesis). While teaching the basic ideas of quantitative research and focusing on regression analysis methods and applications, the course will also cover concepts and methods such as selection bias, processing of missing data, diachronic longitudinal data, hierarchical linear models, and causal inference in quantitative research. Through the combination of lectures, literature reading, classroom reports and discussions, and practical operations, students are able to ask questions on their own and use data (processing) and analysis methods to test and solve problems. .

Name: Topics in the World Economy
Prerequisite: Economics principles, international trade, international finance, macroeconomics, microeconomics
Introduction:
Explore the frontier topics of the world, the United States, Europe, the CIS, Japan, East Asia, developing countries, and the Chinese economy. Analyze current major practical issues in the fields of international trade, international finance, international investment, and international economic cooperation, as well as the mechanisms and evolution of relatively mature market economies, developmental market economies, and transitional market economies. _x000D_
The world economy is an important part that reflects international economic relations and global economic issues. This course not only studies the basic principles and development process of the world economy, but also involves the discussion of the current overall situation and hot issues of the world economy. In particular, it requires an in-depth and detailed analysis of the economic development trends of important countries and regions in the world economy, as well as the impact and development trends of globalization, regional economic integration, trade, finance and investment that play an important role in the current international economic system on the world economy. Through a comprehensive and profound analysis of the world economy, we provide our undergraduate students with detailed information on the latest developments in the current world economy; inspire students to use the economic theories and analytical tools they have learned to observe various problems and contradictions existing in the current world economy, and think about ways to solve real economic problems; and provide students with ideas and solutions that can be used for reference when independently engaging in research on the overall situation of the world economy, national and regional economies.

Name: Climate Change: The Scientific Basis of Global Warming
Introduction:
"Global warming" has become one of the global issues of common concern to human society today. Is "global warming" real in observation? Is "global warming" caused by human activities? Are the scientific theories surrounding this deceptive as argued? What is the likelihood and magnitude of continued warming in the future? What serious impacts will continued global warming have on human society and even natural ecology? What strategies should we adopt now to slow down global warming?
