A series of other questions are worthy of our in-depth discussion. This course is dedicated to introducing "climate change", the scientific basis of global warming, to students from various subject backgrounds, including liberal arts and sciences. It is hoped that it will play a certain basic scientific role in paving the way for future elite groups in Chinese society to understand the seriousness of the problem of "global warming". I hope that students in more fields can pay attention to and understand the urgency of addressing global warming through studying this course. This is the common responsibility of all mankind today, including China. _x000D_
_x000D_
We welcome all students to choose our course in the spring semester every year. We hope you will understand the challenges faced by global warming.

Name: Social Gerontology
Prerequisite: Social science generalists, foreign sociological literature
Introduction: In the 21st century, more countries will enter an aging society and experience a faster population aging process. This course introduces the development, characteristics and research issues in the subject field of social gerontology; especially the relevant theories and research methods on aging, the relationship between fertility, death and migration and population aging, the elderly care models, systems and related social policies in different societies, the role of culture in individual and social elderly care and assistance, and other issues related to aging.

Name: Social Policy
Introduction:
This course uses domestic and foreign social policies as empirical materials to guide students to understand the theories and methods of social policy analysis. By studying this course, students can master the following knowledge and abilities:_x000D_
1. Clearly express the basic theories and concepts of social policy analysis_x000D_
2. Ability to conceptualize policy issues and propose policy solutions_x000D_
3. Understand the impact of policy analysis in public policy _x000D_
4. Understand the role of the policy analyst_x000D_
5. Understand my country’s current social policies to solve social problems_x000D_

Name: Ethnographic Research Methods
Introduction: In response to the development trend that ethnographic research has increasingly become an important research method in the field of humanities and social sciences, this course will briefly introduce the development of concepts and methods of ethnographic research to undergraduates in the Department of Sociology, focus on teaching the practical application of ethnographic research in contemporary sociology and anthropology, and provide students with basic thinking and writing training in research design and planning.

Name: Social Security
Introduction: This course will introduce the development history, basic concepts, theoretical schools, and current major issues of social welfare and social security in my country and other countries. By studying this course, students should be able to master the basic theories and concepts related to social welfare and social security, and be able to summarize and summarize the characteristics of my country's social welfare. On this basis, the course requires students to select an area of ​​welfare issues that they are interested in, read discussions on core issues in this area, and compile their own analysis and understanding based on international research on relevant issues.

Name: Sociology of Organizations
Prerequisite: Sociological overview, sociological theory, social studies and research methods
Introduction: This course is designed to enable students to transition from the study of basic sociology courses to the application and development of sociological theory. This course uses organizational phenomena as a platform for ability cultivation, cultivating students' basic abilities to observe, discuss, and research organizational phenomena using sociological concepts, sociological theories, and social research methods they have mastered. Through classroom lectures and case analysis, students' ability to judge and analyze problems from a sociological perspective is cultivated.

Name: Group Work
Introduction: Group social work is an important method among the three major practice methods of social work. This course mainly introduces the basic principles of group social work, the theoretical basis of group work, group types, elements of group systems, group dynamics, group social work process and the evaluation of group social work. The purpose of setting up this course is to enable students to systematically understand the meaning, origin and development of group social work as well as the theoretical basis of group social work practice, to deeply understand the structure, process and development of group, and to comprehensively use various methods and techniques of group social work to organize the implementation of group social work on the basis of proficiency in mastering the principles and characteristics of different implementation stages. The course will explain practical theories while supplementing them with relevant cases. While paying attention to the analysis of practical theories, it will also focus on teaching group work skills and methods to prepare students for group social work.

Name: Freud and Psychoanalysis
Introduction: This course is offered to undergraduate and graduate students interested in the Department of Sociology and other departments in the humanities and social sciences. The topic is the study of Freud's psychoanalytic thought. This course adopts a lecture system. The purpose of this course is to introduce the main content of classical psychoanalytic thought, its origin and social background, and a brief history of development. The teaching structure of this course is based on the internal structure of Freud's thought, from the shallower to the more advanced, and gradually develops from the theory of classic psychoanalysis to social and political theory.

Name: Political Anthropology
Introduction: This course will systematically introduce "politics" from an anthropological perspective. This lesson will provide an introduction to political life through reading ethnography. This course will guide students to think about how to transcend the presuppositions of Western social and political theories and understand "political" phenomena and order-building issues. This course will start from the traditional political anthropological approaches such as "structure/agency", macro structure/micro process, and combine ethnography to introduce concepts such as power, nation-state, theater state and ritual state. This course will introduce new practices in contemporary political anthropology research, such as integration with film and television media, such as collaborative research and interventional practice research, etc.

Name: The Yellow Emperor's Inner Canon and Ancient Daoyin Exercises
Introduction:
"Huangdi Neijing" is a classic work that comprehensively discusses life phenomena. It is based on anatomy, guided by philosophical ideas, and formed through long-term observation and repeated verification of life phenomena. Gu Daoyin is the abbreviation of "Ancient Chinese Daoyin Health Technique". It is the crystallization of the practical wisdom of ancient people in understanding, exploring life and preventing diseases. Its unique exercise method contains profound philosophical and medical principles. _x000D_
     This course combines theory and practice and combines the Yellow Emperor's Internal Classic with ancient health-preserving principles. Through the study of this course, students can have a certain degree of understanding of the principles of the "Huangdi Neijing", and then improve students' depth of understanding of ancient Daoyin from an overall and principle perspective. It will also contribute to the inheritance of the excellent traditional culture of the Chinese nation, as well as enhance cultural identity and the formation of cultural confidence.

Name: Earth and Space
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Introduce the basic knowledge of earth and space science and its relationship with the development of human activities. Introduce the basic characteristics of the earth and space, and the historical process of human understanding and exploration of the earth and space. Through classroom introduction, students can understand and master the basic knowledge of the earth and space, laying a foundation for exploring the earth and space.

Name: Close Reading of English-Language Sociology Classics
Introduction:
Introduction to Chinese course content (in order to facilitate students' course selection, please be no less than 200 words, and you can attach an additional page)_x000D_
_x000D_
This course is an intensive reading course of classic English original works of sociology. In principle, students who choose this course do not need to be restricted to majors, but their English reading comprehension skills need to reach a certain level. The original texts for intensive reading in class are selected from several highly readable English sociology textbooks. In order to achieve the expected results, students need to carefully preview the original text before class, and then read, discuss and analyze it carefully in class under the leadership of the teacher, so as to integrate theory with practice as much as possible. _x000D_
The content of the course covers several classic discussions from the emergence of sociology in the West in the first half of the 19th century to the present. The teaching method is somewhere between intensive reading and extensive reading for English majors, and is combined with practical issues for in-depth discussion. In order to achieve an ideal teaching effect, the number of elective students should be controlled within 15, and a small multimedia classroom should be configured to use English audio-visual materials related to teaching. _x000D_
This course is mainly taught in Chinese. International students interested in taking this course must have Chinese communication skills. _x000D_

Name: Public Law and Intellectual History
Introduction: This course aims to think about a series of basic concepts and basic premises of the modern public legal order through the interpretation of a series of original classics of Chinese and Western ideological classics. It also aims to train students' ability to read texts intensively and raise new questions through research on the history of ideas. It also leads students to understand related issues such as national construction and constitutional changes, empires and international law, political parties and representation, political ethics and legal ethics, etc., to expand students' knowledge and prepare sufficient relevant literature knowledge for this course. The course content will be adjusted year by year based on the research progress of the lecturer.

Name: Reform of Contemporary China's Examination and Admissions System
Introduction:
This course is an interdisciplinary research course for graduate students and senior undergraduates. It integrates the basic principles of education, sociology, psychology and other disciplines to achieve a high degree of integration of theory and practice. Students who elect this course should have basic knowledge of educational history and a certain degree of understanding of educational policy and educational sociology. After completing this course, students should establish the basic framework for the reform of the examination and admissions system in China, be familiar with the policy content of the reform of the examination and admissions system, and have unique insights into the implementation of the reform of the examination and admissions system. _x000D_
The teaching methods of this course are "question-based heuristic" and "inquiry-based teaching". Taking the problem as the guide, reading literature and research and discussion as the main method, and arranging a certain number of research and practical activities to help students master the thinking and theoretical framework for analyzing practical educational issues. _x000D_
This course is 2 credits, 17 teaching weeks. The assessment method is a mid-term paper and a final examination. The mid-term paper accounts for 40%, daily discussions account for 10%, and the final examination accounts for 50%. _x000D_

Name: Studies in China's Ethnic and Frontier Issues
Introduction:
This course is offered to senior undergraduate students who are academically interested in ethnic and border issues in China. It aims to observe issues related to ethnicity, ethnic groups and border issues in Chinese history from a sociological perspective and method. The goal is to enable students to establish an awareness of the research on ethnic and border issues in China, grasp the main issues and academic context in related fields, and be able to conduct independent research in this field. _x000D_
This course will be conducted through a combination of teacher lectures and student discussions (the former accounts for 80% and the latter accounts for 20%). _x000D_
Specific topics include but are not limited to: (1) The way of connecting borders in the Chinese dynasty era; (2) Debates on the "Chinese" model; (3) "Ethnic" issues in historical discourse; (4) Border affairs ideas and ethnic systems during the Republic of China; (5) The evolution of ethnic theories and policies of the Communist Party of China; (6) "Ethnic identification" and related debates in the 1950s; (7) Ethnic history writing and nation-state construction. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Political Institutions
Introduction: The content of this course covers China's main political systems from the pre-Qin period to the Republic of China. It is taught by topic. The ancient part includes: imperial power system, central government organizational structure, financial system, judicial system, military system, local administrative system, etc. The modern part includes the political system of the Nanjing Provisional Government, the Beiyang Government and the National Government, the central and local administrative systems, and the military system, etc.

Name: Poverty and Development
Introduction:
This course teaches the basic concepts and theories of poverty and development issues, introduces poverty issues and anti-poverty efforts in developed and developing countries, and discusses topics such as rural poverty, regional development gaps, wealth differentiation, urban poverty, and microfinance poverty alleviation in my country. The course seeks to deepen students' understanding and insight into poverty issues. _x000D_
_x000D_

At the end of the semester, they will complete a term paper based on the outline of their speech (you can also choose another topic). _x000D_
_x000D_
Student performance evaluation method:_x000D_
Regular homework accounts for 40%, and the final paper accounts for 60%. _x000D_

Name: Theory and Research Methods in Political Science
Prerequisite: 1. Introduction to Political Science, course number: 03232660, Associate Professor Zhang Jian, Associate Professor Duan Demin, Assistant Professor Zhou Qiang, 51 class hours, the college only elects courses_x000D_
Introduction:
Basic purpose: _x000D_
1. Through the study of this course, students can systematically understand the basic development outline of theories and methods of modern Western political science research, the main contents and characteristics of important theories and methods, and understand the uses and research flaws of these theoretical methods. _x000D_
2. Based on the systematic explanation of political science theoretical methods, cultivate students' ability to appropriately choose theoretical research approaches and methodological tools in future related studies and research. _x000D_
Content summary:_x000D_
1. This course systematically explains some influential theories and methods in the field of modern Western political science research, as well as the application of these theories and methods in actual research. Its content not only involves an introduction to the content and characteristics of these theoretical methods, but also introduces relevant criticisms and comments. _x000D_
2. The content of this course has four parts. The first part describes the subject overview of political science, specifically explaining the history of political science's development, epistemological foundations, stratification of normative and empirical theories, topic setting, and methodological challenges. The second part describes the theoretical perspective of political science research, specifically explaining the theoretical connotation and evolution of pluralism, elitism, political system analysis and state construction. The third part describes the theoretical approaches of political science research, specifically explaining the research topics and theoretical methods of normative theory, behavioral analysis research approaches, rational choice theory, new institutionalism research approaches, national governance theory, etc. The fourth part explains specifically the content and evolution of theoretical methods of qualitative research, quantitative research, comparative political research, structure and actor research. _x000D_

Name: General Korean (I)
Introduction: This course mainly teaches Korean pronunciation, basic vocabulary, and basic grammar that must be understood in the basic stage of Korean. Through the explanation of texts and exercises on various specific topics, it improves students’ Korean listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation abilities, and stimulates the interest of non-Korean majors in learning Korean.

Name: Crowds and Networks
Introduction: The course is based on two main theories - graph theory and game theory, to deduce the behavior and interaction mechanism of crowds in the context of the Internet. Graph theory is a theory that studies network structure, and game theory is a model of individual behavior. Combining graph theory and game theory is intended to graphically explore the socioeconomic consequences of individual behavior and its relationship with other individual behaviors, integrating knowledge that was once scattered in many different traditional subject areas into a new knowledge field through the study of individual behavior. The central goal of the course is to enable students to understand the creative process of integrating knowledge and exploring unknown areas step by step through the discussion of individual behaviors, and to understand the basic forces and power balance mechanisms behind networks and strategic behaviors.

Name: Selected Writings on China by Eminent German Authors
Introduction: The Sino-German cultural relationship is a two-way interactive relationship between the two core sub-cultures within Eastern and Western cultures - the Teutonic civilization as the culture of northern Europe and the Chinese civilization as the culture of northern Asia - and has important paradigm significance. This course aims to reveal, clarify and substantiate this meaning from the specific perspective of the intellectual elite of German-speaking countries accepting Chinese traditional culture. This course first provides an overview of the historical development of Sino-German cultural interaction from ancient times to the present and the evolution of Chinese images in the German context. Based on this, it focuses on recommending, studying and commenting on the representative works of important philosophers and writers in the German-speaking area from the 18th to the 20th century, such as Leibniz, Kant, Jaspers, Goethe, Schiller, Kafka, etc., concerning China and its culture. This course requires students to have strong Chinese skills and good reading comprehension skills in English or German. By studying this course, students can expand their horizons on cultural exchanges between China and the West and lay a solid foundation for deepening related research.

Name: American Structural Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly uses the concluding work of American structuralism, linguist Hockett's "Course of Modern Linguistics" (Part 1) as the basic content, and also refers to the writings of other American structuralist linguists such as Bloomfield's "On Language" to systematically explain the background, basic language concepts and research methods of American structuralist linguistics. The purpose is to enable students to have a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding of linguistics, and to improve the level of linguistic theory and corpus analysis capabilities.

Name: Fundamentals of Chinese Phonetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course uses the phonetic system of Mandarin as an example to teach the basic knowledge of general phonetics. It mainly includes (1) basic knowledge of modern phonetics; (2) analysis of the sound, rhyme and tone system of Mandarin; (3) brief analysis of the prosodic characteristics of Mandarin; (4) "Chinese Pinyin Scheme" and the Beijing phonology system.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Function Words
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: On the basis of modern Chinese, some function words in modern Chinese are analyzed and explained with emphasis on both meaning and usage. Its purpose is to help students further understand and master modern Chinese function words, and to help students learn some methods of analyzing and researching function words as much as possible, so as to improve their ability to analyze and research. There are four chapters in total: Chapter 1 Introduction; Chapter 2 Adverbs; Chapter 3 Prepositions; Chapter 4 Research on Function Words.

Name: Biological Photography and Practice
Introduction:
Biological photography is a type of scientific photography that takes biology as the subject and serves life science research. The use of photography technology to describe the morphological characteristics of biological life activities serves the purpose of teaching, scientific research, and popular science. It also has the common requirements of authenticity, accuracy, simplicity, and beauty. This course has been changed to a public elective course in the school. The teaching and practical content focuses on ecological photography and general image processing, _x000D_
Students who are interested in microscopic photography technology should consult the academic affairs department to take the elective photomicrography and electron microscopy course in the School of Life Sciences.

Name: Economic Geography
Introduction:
Course name: Economic Geography_x000D_
Course Introduction_x000D_
The main part of the course is divided into two modules. The first module is based on the introduction of economic geography and mainly reviews the relevant theories of economic activity location, including the analysis of economic activity location and its influencing factors, agricultural location theory, industrial location theory, central place theory, multi-sector enterprise location theory, multinational company location theory, etc. The second module focuses on the regional analysis of economic activities and the globalization of economic activities, and will also review new developments in economic geography research at home and abroad. Specifically, it includes regional structure and organization, regional economic development, spatial organization between regions, globalization of economic activities and its regional response, industrial analysis of globalization of economic activities, research methods in economic geography, new developments in economic geography theory and practice, etc. _x000D_

Name: Urban Management
Introduction:
Through the teaching of this course, students can initially master the basic connotation, related content, relevant principles and research methods of urban management, and have the preliminary ability to use these theoretical methods to analyze economic, social, and political phenomena and problems in urban development. _x000D_
The course is divided into three parts. The first is the basic platform of urban management. Introduce the development context of urban management, reveal the new environment and several new trends of thought faced by contemporary urban development; introduce the main body composition of urban management and the relationship between the main bodies, and sort out the institutional framework of urban management; secondly, it is the important content of urban management. Including urban development strategic management, economic development management, environmental management, space management and social affairs management; the third is the most urgent problem that needs to be solved and the most worthy of discussion in contemporary Chinese urban management. This part includes urban residents, public housing, infrastructure, traffic management, city branding and emergency management.

Name: Urban Economics
Introduction: Urban economics is an emerging interdisciplinary subject and a typical branch of applied economics. The idea of ​​curriculum construction is to emphasize equal emphasis on basic theories, basic research methods and analytical tools, and empirical research and policy analysis. At the same time, the two major modules of urban socio-economic operation and urban public issues are highlighted. The course will mainly cover the following main contents: Chapter 1, Introduction to Research. Chapter 2, the emergence of cities. Chapter 3, urban spatial structure. Chapter 4, urban infrastructure. Chapter 5, urbanization theory and practice. Chapter 6, division of labor and intercity trade. Chapter 7, urban industrial agglomeration. Chapter 8, urban economic growth. Chapter 9, urban public goods. Chapter 10, urban government revenue. Chapter 11, Urban Public Expenditure. Chapter 12, Urban Public Policy. Chapter 13, urban regional governance. Chapter 14, research prospects.

Name: Urban Planning
Prerequisite: Students are required to have basic knowledge and skills in regional economics, economic geography and geographic information systems.
Introduction: This course is a required course for students majoring in urban management in the School of Government. Based on the introduction of basic contents such as cities, urbanization and urban development, the course covers the ideas and theories of urban planning, the nature, regulations and administrative operations of urban planning, urban planning support systems, urban master planning, urban land use planning, urban road traffic planning, urban detailed planning, etc. , comprehensively introduces the relevant knowledge and methods of urban planning to students; at the same time, the course uses practical research as an important auxiliary teaching method, organizes students to conduct field research, and conduct independent planning practices, aiming to enable urban management major students to master urban planning-related knowledge and urban planning practical experience.

Name: Monetary and Financial Policy
Prerequisite:
1. Mastery of high school mathematics
2. Mastering the basic concepts and rationale of microeconomics and macroeconomics
Introduction: Monetary and Financial Policy is an elective course for undergraduates at the School of Government of Peking University. It is a basic course that helps students learn and master the basic knowledge of macro-financial policies and the operation of financial institutions. This course will be taught in the form of special topics, focusing on monetary systems, credit, financial markets, financial institutions, financial innovation, financial risks, financial supervision, central banks, commercial banks, currency supply and demand theory and other professional knowledge related to monetary and financial policies, so that students can more completely grasp the basic theoretical framework of modern monetary and financial policies, have a more comprehensive and profound understanding of modern monetary and financial policies, and have a deeper understanding of monetary and financial theories. This course requires basic knowledge of high school mathematics, microeconomics and macroeconomics.

Name: Regional Economics
Introduction:
Regional economics, also known as spatial economics, is a branch of applied economics formed at the intersection of economics and geography. Regional economics focuses on using economic perspectives and methods to analyze the spatial characteristics of the economic system, including the location and spatial organization of regional economic activities, regional economic growth, division of labor and trade, coordination of regional economic development and regional relations, and related regional policy issues. _x000D_
This course is a required course for urban management majors. The main content includes: basic issues of regional economics, economic activity location and spatial organization (such as enterprise location selection, market areas and central places, urban systems, land use, etc.), regional economic development (such as regional income and employment, regional economic input-output, regional economic growth, regional professional division of labor and trade, etc.), regional policy (such as the goals and means of regional policy, regional policy evaluation, regional policy and decentralization, regional policy cost-effectiveness, etc.). _x000D_
Through this course, students can comprehensively understand and master the basic theories and knowledge of regional economics, become familiar with the basic principles, methods and skills of regional economics, and be able to use these principles, methods and skills to analyze actual regional economic and regional policy issues.

Name: Government Management Practicum and Field Research
Introduction: Urban renewal is an important means of urban revitalization. As the main form of urban renewal, neighborhood renewal is an important issue in urban development and plays an important role in the process of urban revitalization and urban development since the twentieth century. Exploring the neighborhood renewal model from the perspective of urban revitalization has important theoretical and practical significance. This course focuses on the practical issue of "Theory and Practice of Street Renewal from the Perspective of Urban Revitalization", is supported by the good hardware and software conditions of Peking University School of Government, and closely combines the needs of Peking University's discipline construction, teaching, scientific research and talent training. Research-based learning methods and practical teaching forms such as exercises, results reports and expert comments allow students to improve urban planning professionalism, systematic thinking, research capabilities and practical skills during the practical teaching process. They can also understand China's urban renewal and governance in the process of analyzing and solving practical problems, and cultivate awareness of the country and national conditions.

Name: China's Industrial and Economic Development in Global Perspective
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to help undergraduates understand the significance of the rise of China's industry to the world and China's economic development. In order to enable undergraduate students to understand the significance of industrial development from a global and historical perspective, this course will first introduce the role of the rise and fall of international industrial leadership in world economic development since the British Industrial Revolution started the modern economic growth process. The main content of this course, which is also the most distinctive content, is an introduction to a series of contemporary Chinese industrial development cases, including automobiles, civil aviation, nuclear power, high-speed railways, semiconductor displays, mechanical equipment and other industries. The introduction of these industrial cases is all based on the teachers’ empirical research on China’s industrial development in the past 20 years. These contents involve many lessons about technological innovation, corporate strategy, industrial competition and government policies that actually occurred in the process of contemporary China's industrial development. This course will help undergraduates find ways and conceptual tools to analyze and answer these questions theoretically.

Name: General French (II)
Introduction:
This course is a public language class open to all students in the school to meet their requirements for learning French language and culture. It mainly teaches French pronunciation, basic French vocabulary and grammar, and also teaches French national conditions, society, culture, current affairs and other knowledge in the text. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Topics in Chinese and Western Music
Introduction: "Special Topics in Chinese and Western Music" is a required professional course for undergraduate students at Peking University School of Arts. This course explains and discusses multiple cultural phenomena highlighted in the history of Chinese and Western music from a macro perspective. It aims to require students to understand and master the basic characteristics and cultural attributes of Chinese and Western music, thereby generating a strong interest in art and history and increasing academic knowledge about music culture. This course emphasizes the high correlation between music and social culture, and uses case explanations to guide students to pay attention to the details of music culture and initially understand the differences and connections between Chinese and Western music cultures.

Name: Calligraphy
Introduction: This course provides a detailed analysis and explanation of the relationship between Chinese philosophy and Chinese calligraphy art. The content mainly involves the interconnection between Chinese philosophical thought and the creative concepts and creative techniques of Chinese calligraphy art. It studies and analyzes the artistic concepts and artistic works of the most representative calligraphers in ancient and contemporary Chinese calligraphy art; through the study of Chinese calligraphy The analysis and explanation of the content of Chinese calligraphy art and the research and analysis of Chinese calligraphy art works clarify the ontology and connotation of Chinese calligraphy art, the aesthetic category and characteristics of calligraphy art and the aesthetic requirements of creation; enable students to comprehensively understand and understand the art of Chinese calligraphy, the creative charm of Chinese calligraphy art and the expression of the beauty of Chinese calligraphy art. Gradually cultivate college students' interest in the art of Chinese calligraphy, understand how to better appreciate the art of Chinese calligraphy, and improve college students' understanding and cultivation of the creative style and appreciation of Chinese calligraphy art.

Name: Painting Techniques
Introduction:
The teaching of Chinese painting in the art history major takes into account the fact that most students are starting from scratch and use limited study hours to strengthen and improve their modeling abilities. Facing different directions such as figures, landscapes, flowers and birds, we choose the most difficult ink figures as the basis for training. Through learning, students can understand the tradition and development status of ink and wash figure painting; improve students' ink and wash modeling ability and ability to quickly capture images; and their ability to integrate the language of plastic arts and use pen and ink to shape life forms. _x000D_
The teaching of this course is based on the teaching and analysis of Chinese and foreign art works, and arranges figure sketching. Choose ink and wash figure sketching based on the student's specific situation and basic conditions. Due to the limited number of class hours, ink character sketching focuses on the use of lines and ink colors for modeling, without coloring training. _x000D_
With the improvement of modeling ability, students' appreciation level and analysis ability of paintings will be improved_x000D_

Name: Thesis Writing in Art History and Theory
Introduction: Designed for undergraduate students majoring in art history, it emphasizes the combination of theory and practice. The content is divided into four parts: the first is the interpretation of the image, the second is the review of the exhibition, the third is the writing training of professional book reviews, and the fourth is the writing training of professional papers.

Name: History of Religious Art
Prerequisite: Chinese art history, Western art history, art overview.
Introduction: "Religious Art" is a professional basic course for undergraduates majoring in art history. It is usually offered in the second semester of the second year, with 34 class hours. Students take this course on the basis of the general history of Chinese and foreign art and the introduction to art. This course mainly teaches the history, classic works, main events, art schools, and representative artists of the world's major religious art. Through this topic, you can initially grasp the characteristics and scope of religious art, and understand the importance of religious art in art history. Understand the interaction and integration of different civilizations through the field of religious art. Then understand the relationship between religion and art, the two main forms of human civilization.

Name: Mesopotamian Art and Civilization
Introduction: Based on the general background of the development history of world civilization, this course guides students to understand the unique visual and material culture of ancient Mesopotamia, the "cradle of human civilization", through the explanation and investigation of the origin, development, style characteristics and historical changes of art and architecture in ancient Mesopotamia (Mesopotamia). The course strives to break through the vision of civilization under the framework of the traditional Western "Orientalism" and uses Chinese civilization as the ontology and potential comparison object. It guides students to think about the common problems faced by human civilization during the rise and fall of Mesopotamian civilization, and enhances the awareness and ability of civilized dialogue in the context of globalization. At the methodological level, the course is committed to introducing some basic research paths in the art history discipline into the teaching, that is, starting from visual materials, combining documentary records and archaeological materials, and exploring the unique civilizational forms and cultural traditions behind them through the viewing, interpretation and interpretation of "pictures" and "objects".

Name: History of Chinese Drama
Introduction: The emergence, development and changes of Chinese drama are one of the main contents of Chinese social culture and one of the symbols of Chinese culture. From the budding stage of opera to its emergence, development, and its heyday, traditional Chinese opera has experienced a unique path. After modern times, Western drama was introduced to China, resulting in the emergence of drama. This course examines and explains traditional Chinese drama, drama, and other dramatic forms together.

Graduation works as practical training are an indispensable part of the teaching process. This course combines the teaching experience of cinematography in the country and abroad, and breaks the whole script into several stages, each of which is directed and tested by teachers, creating a teaching mechanism for the theory and practice of play. Through the study of this course, students will be familiar with and master the complete film production process, confirm the film theory accumulated by students, and then improve their creative practice ability. Name: Economics of Art
Introduction:
Art and cultural behavior in contemporary society have diverse relationships with economic categories. At the same time, the creation and circulation of art and culture often must be integrated into the existing economic system to gain opportunities for survival and development. As a discipline, art and cultural economics aims to study and analyze the different levels of relationship between the art world and the economic world, as well as the impact of different art, cultural and economic fields on public and social life. _x000D_
This course is based on this. In order to achieve clear logic and facilitate the level and depth of teaching and learning, the course design is divided into two main categories, individual (micro) and overall (macro), or micro and macro categories, which are taught in sequence. At the individual level, we will explore the cultural-economic intersection behaviors performed by different art and cultural economic units (or actors), including producers, consumers, enterprises, institutions, governments, etc. In the overall category, it focuses on the overall structure of the entire cultural and economic market or field, the intersection of this structure with the social and cultural context, and the macro effects and social impacts it produces, as well as its different interaction models and effects with government policies and national governance. From empirical cases to theoretical analysis, through the teaching and practice of this course, we also hope that students can fully understand the important issues and overall picture of art and cultural economy, and lay the knowledge foundation for them to engage in related management work in the future.

Name: Theory and Practice of Investment and Financing in the Cultural Industries
Introduction: This course teaches knowledge of the theory of finance in the cultural industry, financing models and classic cases and acquires skills in financing the cultural industry through practical exercises.

Name: Creative Management
Prerequisite: Introduction to the Cultural Industry, a compulsory course for undergraduate students in the Ministry of Humanities, a compulsory course for undergraduate students in the management of the cultural industry at the Faculty of Arts, and a compulsory double degree in arts. The course is intended for students to master the basic concepts, characteristics, content and outreach of the cultural industry, to understand the composition of the cultural industry ' s values and industry patterns, to understand the development of the cultural industry in terms of its cultural resources, cultural technologies, cultural capital and cultural assets, as well as its academic life, to master the story-driven, creative strategies, management features of cultural finance and business innovation, and to become familiar with the landscape of cultural industries, cultural trade and policy governance.
Introduction:
_x000D_
This course requires students to have received introduction to cultural industry and cultural industry special research courses or related course training. After studying this course, students should master the essential characteristics, theoretical background, applicable advantages and limitations of creative management, and initially have the basic ability to analyze the development strategy, business model and organizational management of the cultural industry. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is an interdisciplinary applied special research course that combines cultural industry and management science. It mainly trains students to master the basic concepts, methods and tools of creative management, and conducts case analysis based on outstanding cases of domestic and foreign cultural industries. The basic content of the course includes the following: the essence and background of creative management; the theory, concepts and models of creative management; and the application of creative management principles in practical cases. _x000D_

Name: Innovation and Entrepreneurship in the Cultural Industries
Prerequisite: Introduction to the cultural industry, art management, creative management
Introduction: In recent years, as my country's economic development has entered a new normal, "mass entrepreneurship and innovation" have gradually become a source of motivation to stimulate the development of social innovation and promote economic quality and efficiency. The country has also identified innovation and entrepreneurship education reform as a breakthrough to promote comprehensive education reform in colleges and universities and comprehensively improve the quality of undergraduate education, and has issued a series of documents to promote the in-depth development of innovation and entrepreneurship education reform. Today, with the comprehensive implementation of quality education, domestic colleges and universities should update their educational concepts, set up relevant innovative courses in colleges and universities, and regard cultivating college students' innovative consciousness and innovative abilities as the core of college education reform. In 2017, Peking University was selected into the second batch of mass entrepreneurship and innovation universities and research institute demonstration bases, becoming an important highland for the country to promote transformation, upgrading and innovative development. Creativity and management are the core competencies of the cultural industry management major. Creativity is the wing of practical management, and practical management is the soil of creativity. Creative thinking ability is the basic quality that cultural industry management talents should possess. In today's training of high-quality cultural industry management talents, the penetration and penetration of innovative ideas is an important aspect of teaching reform. "Cultural Industry Innovation and Entrepreneurship" is a compulsory course for the cultural industry management major of Peking University School of Arts. After one semester of curriculum construction and teaching practice exploration, it is hoped that with the support of this project, the teaching content will be further reformed, the teaching methods will be updated, and through guidance, strengthening self-learning, independent thinking and diligent practice and other teaching methods, it can better stimulate students' creative vitality, build students' innovative and entrepreneurial thinking, and lay a foundation for students' knowledge accumulation and practical skills in the field of cultural industry management.

Name: English Lexicology
Prerequisite: English Language Structure (English Language Profession, Fall)
Introduction: "English Vocabulary" is a basic course for English major undergraduates. The course discusses the composition of English words, word collocations, word meanings, rhetoric, etc., and guides students to learn basic knowledge of vocabulary. Based on the "English Structure" course, it further improves students' English language abilities.

Name: Literature, Nature and Place
Prerequisite: Selected students should have completed their first and second year of studies in English and related literature and writing in English such as the Introduction to Literature.
Introduction: The relationship between human beings and nature is explored by studying a series of literature from the ancient West.

Name: Syntax and Semantics
Introduction:
English Grammar and Semantics explores several basic issues in the English grammar system. Topics include but are not limited to English nouns (line, number, case), English verbs (tense, aspect, modal verbs), English non-finite verbs (indefinite, participle, gerund), English adjectives, etc. The discussion focuses on the relationship between form, meaning and function. _x000D_
Students need to participate in class discussions based on reading literature.

Name: Western Thought and Modern China
Introduction: This course will explain, in the context of the exchange of ideas between China and the West, the responses and interpretations of Chinese thinkers to Western ideas in modern times on the levels of philosophy, literature, art, aesthetics, social and political thought, etc., and guide students to deepen their understanding and appreciation of modern Chinese culture in the context of the collision between middle school and Western learning. This course will be taught in Chinese, and students will be required to read relevant Chinese literature and write term papers in Chinese after class. This course will use a self-compiled collection of literature as the teaching material.

Name: Jane Austen's Novels in Their Historical Context
Introduction:
The uniqueness of Jane Austen's novels lies in its promotion and deepening of the development of the novel as a literary genre. Although British novels have gradually emerged since the first half of the eighteenth century, it was not until the emergence of Austen's novels that people truly perceived the close connection between novels and real life. Austen used exquisite and subtle writing methods to deviate from the "single" character structure in traditional novels and create complex and full character psychology, thus revealing the human nature of people from all walks of life in Britain. As an author, Austen intentionally leaves readers with ample space for thinking and establishes an effective interaction between the author and readers, which is also different from the didactic literature that was prevalent in the eighteenth century. Austen's trust and expectations for readers have led to people's increasingly rich pursuit and research on her works for more than two hundred years. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course mainly studies four novels by Jane Austen: "Sense and Sensibility", "Northanger Abbey", "Emma", and "Persuasion". The focus of the course is to explore the important position of Austen's works in the development of British novels since the 18th century by combining (1) the study of the original text, (2) the British social, cultural, and historical background of the author's life, and (3) the combing of representative documents about Austen's works, and analyze Austen's acceptance and departure from the novel tradition as a female author. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course will include an introduction and discussion of Austen's letters. Austen's letters show the author's side that is closer to life; Austen's emotional expressions, detailed observations of daily life, and sincere perceptions of literary creation in her letters complement and echo her novels, which can help students interpret Austen and her works from a more comprehensive perspective. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course will also cover Austen’s other works (including her childhood works), as well as the works of some contemporary British female writers (Mary Wollstonecraft, Maria Edgeworth, Jane West, etc.), aiming to guide students to analyze Jane Austen’s novels in the context of the times from a clear and rich perspective. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Language, Culture and Society in Translation
Prerequisite: English or Chinese translation, general linguistics, basic speech concepts, vocabulary, English literature, English country profiles, Western culture
Introduction: Translation has a long history of disputes over the standards of honesty, expressiveness and elegance. What kind of translation can be regarded as a "faithful" translation and a "good" translation? What theories and standards should the translation process follow? This course systematically considers the characteristics and differences of English-Chinese bilingualism in terms of language, culture, society, and ways of thinking, and uses the perspectives of lexicon, phonetics, comparative linguistics, cross-cultural communication, comparative culture and literary studies, translation theory, cultural anthropology, cultural theory, sociology, etc. to explore quality issues in English-Chinese and Chinese-English translation from the aspects of language form (vocabulary, syntax, etc.), content, media, pragmatics, etc. This course uses a comprehensive perspective to integrate theory with practice, emphasizing the three forms of translation: audio-visual, text and communication, so that students can understand the nature of translation in an all-round and multi-dimensional way, think deeply about the differences between English and Chinese in terms of language, culture, society, etc., systematically understand the transformation characteristics of second language culture and language in translation, deepen their understanding of English, Chinese and cultural connotations, and ultimately improve their theoretical reflection ability on translation. This course starts with a large number of cases of translation errors, uses a systematic comparative method, is based on linguistics, sociology, and cultural theory, and combines the three main forms of literary translation, audio-visual translation, and cultural communication to explore the polymorphism and multiple standards of translation, cultivate students' flexible and systematic understanding of translation, and thereby strengthen students' translation ability and theoretical level. _x000D_

Name: Christian Latin (2)
Introduction: Teaching the basic grammar of Christian Latin and reading the Latin Bible, focusing on classroom connections and extracurricular exercises, with quizzes, midterm and final exams every two weeks. The first semester focuses on reading short passages from the Bible, and the second semester focuses on reading Bible passages, with an appropriate introduction to the writings of ancient Christian writers on interpreting the Bible.

Name: General Italian (I)
Introduction: 6-hour public Italian for basics

Name: General Italian (II)
Introduction: 6-hour public basic Italian for Zero (ii)

Name: General Italian (III)
Prerequisite: Public basic Italian (i) and public basic Italian (ii)
Introduction: 6-hour public basic Italian for basic zero (iii)

Name: General Italian (IV)
Introduction: The second semester course is designed to fully complete the B1 level. Classroom communication is necessary with the aim of making students speak Italian more and more. This course is not only based on the study of grammar, vocabulary, morphology and syntax, but also hopes to provide a series of socio-cultural content that is essential in language learning. In addition, each week's teaching module includes a writing assignment to prepare students for the final Italian International Proficiency Certification Examination. In the second semester, according to the daily study and timetable, we will introduce some topics every month, such as newspapers, literature textbooks, etc.

Name: Mythology and Art of Ancient West Asia and North Africa
Introduction: This course aims to use "mythology" and "art" as the starting point, and through the investigation of relevant texts and images, to guide students to understand and explore the history and culture of ancient West Asia and North Africa. The course will launch a series of special topics around mythological motifs expressed in works of art and artistic phenomena arising from mythological concepts, discuss the intricate relationship between "myth" and "art", and consider how to use and interpret mythological texts and visual image materials within a broader methodological framework, making them a key to historical research.

Name: Aesthetics of Literature and Art
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course strives to analyze and grasp the logical starting point and value end point of literary aesthetics through sorting out the academic history of Chinese literary aesthetics research. It strives to stand at the forefront of the development of contemporary aesthetics, pay attention to absorbing new results of related disciplines and emerging science and technology research, and connect artistic aesthetics with people's aesthetic generation in terms of value theory. At the same time, the academic perspective of literary aesthetics is used to perspective and analyze the current situation of literature and art in contemporary China, focusing on theoretical and practical issues of practical significance, so as to form a positive interaction between the practice of literary and artistic creation and the construction of literary and artistic theory.

Name: Chinese Ancient Text Resources and Their Compilation
Studies in the General Catalogue of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: "Sikuquanshu General Catalog" is a classic work of Chinese classical bibliography and academic and cultural history. This course intends to teach the compilation, main content and academic influence of the "Sikuquanshu", focusing on reading the major and minor narrations of each department in the "Sikuquanshu" and the abstracts of basic classics. It aims to improve students' ability to read ancient Chinese classics, help students master the keys to traditional scholarship methods, understand the essence of Chinese classical academic traditions, and lay a solid foundation for future research in traditional culture and related fields.

Name: History of Western Philosophy (Ancient and Medieval)
Introduction: This course is the first part of the "History of Western Philosophy" series. It teaches the development of Western philosophy from Thales to the late Middle Ages, and analyzes the origins and significance of various philosophical ideas and important concepts during this period. The goal of this course is not only to allow students to acquire historical knowledge of Western philosophy, but also to improve students' cognitive abilities and critical thinking abilities.

Name: History of Chinese Ritual Studies
Introduction: This course will briefly review the history of rituals from the Western Zhou Dynasty to the late Qing Dynasty and the Republic of China to help students become familiar with the three "Lis" and their commentaries and interpretation traditions, as well as the relationship with the evolution of Chinese history, mainly focusing on the four stages of Pre-Qin, Han and Tang, Song and Ming, and Qing dynasties. It is hoped that it can help students gain a deeper understanding of the characteristics of Chinese civilization through rituals and lay a foundation for further study.

Name: Seminar in Classical Philology (I)
Introduction: This course is planned to focus on the topic of "History, Thought and Literature of the Wei and Jin Dynasties", and invites expert professors from the Chinese, History, Philosophy Departments, Archeology and Museum and other related fields to jointly teach. Through the combination of special lectures and seminars, while breaking down professional barriers, the characteristics and differences of each discipline in problem awareness and research methods are clarified.

Name: Comparative Studies of Religion in Chinese and Western Civilizational Traditions
Introduction: The course will place religion within the civilizational tradition of Central and Western China and will carry out intensive research. Each session will focus on different topics in Chinese or Western religious traditions. This course will place the religion of Central and Western China under their own cultural traditions for comparative study. Every time a class starts, a theme will be chosen. The theme for the fall of 2011 was: Chinese mourning system.

Name: Seminar on Plato's Republic
Introduction: This class will lead students to read Plato's "The Republic" carefully, allowing students to think deeply and discuss some related philosophical issues, thereby cultivating students' basic abilities in reading, thinking and writing.
