Introduction: Read and discuss relevant texts in conjunction with the “Marxist philosophy (up)” curriculum.

Name: Western Classical Thought (I)
Introduction: This course is dedicated to guiding students to understand the ancient Western intellectual tradition. It is planned to be offered for a long time and echoes the "Modern Western Thought" course, striving to demonstrate the depth and richness of the Western intellectual tradition. Different types of texts are selected each semester, either with questions as clues or with classic treatises as the center. Through careful reading of the texts, the contemporary vitality of ancient classics is highlighted in critical reflection. The course in the fall semester of 2016 will take Plato's "The Republic" as the main text, and re-examine the ideological challenges raised by this famous work from a contemporary perspective. It not only takes us back to Athens when reason was in its infancy, but also introduces us to philosophy itself. To this end, we will also consider relevant arguments in other dialogues such as the Phaedo, Protagoras, Gorgias, Phaedrus, and Timaeus. It aims both to clarify the inner construction of Plato's arguments in their specific context and to reveal the current relevance of Plato's thought by reviewing important contemporary research literature. This course will use a combination of lectures and small class discussions to not only showcase the charm of ancient philosophical thought, but also train students' general ability to reflect on philosophy.

Name: History of Chinese Classical Scholarship (I)
Introduction: For 2,000 years, the Confucian classic has been at the heart of Chinese culture, attracting intergenerational scholars to study its content, to write books, to shape the economics of different times, and to structure it into Chinese history. This course is mainly an objective recognition and introduction to the legacy and transformation of the erstwhile sciences from an economic point of view. Second, the history of history, which has been pending in history, has been rewritten and analysed. Second, the analysis and discussion of leading entrepreneurs and their work has enabled students to have a basic understanding of key transformational issues and events in history.

Name: Topics in the History of Religion
Introduction: This course is a special topic course focusing on religious theory. We will read Leibniz's "Theodicy" in detail in order to have a more comprehensive grasp of the idea of ​​theodicy and Leibniz's related assumptions about it. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Studies of Chinese Social Thought
Introduction: This course will lead students to systematically and intensively read classics in traditional Chinese social thought, so that on the basis of a general understanding of Chinese social thought, students can further deepen their in-depth study and understanding of certain classics, especially ancient ritual thought works, and improve students' ability to read classics. The construction of this course will lay a preliminary foundation for the development and improvement of China's local social theory and the Sinicization of sociology.

Name: History of Eastern Literature
Introduction:
Oriental literature is an important part of world literature. It has a long history and rich connotations. From the research perspective of world literature and comparative literature, its importance and status cannot be ignored. However, due to long-term historical reasons, Eastern literature is not valued by academics and students. Even some literary researchers cannot correctly grasp the status of Eastern literature in world literature. They do not know enough about Eastern literature and do not appreciate it much. As Mr. Ji Xianlin said: "Some influential scholars say they value Eastern literature on the surface, but in fact they despise it deep down. They are still the first in Europe." This has greatly affected scholars' knowledge and understanding of Eastern literature, and the status of Eastern literature and even Eastern culture in the history of world culture and civilization has not received due attention and recognition. As a big oriental country, China should have an in-depth understanding and research of oriental literature, and should strive to promote oriental literature, including Chinese literature, to the world so that it can receive its due status and evaluation. This requires every student who is a son of the East to have a certain understanding of Eastern literature, including Chinese literature. _x000D_
    Based on this spirit, in the context of the history of world literature development, this course defines the origins and value orientations of Eastern and Western civilization, culture and literature, examines the evolution and displacement, conflict and integration of the centers of Eastern and Western civilizations, macro-organizes the history of the relationship between Eastern and Western literature from a multi-dimensional perspective, and focuses on introducing a number of classic works in the history of Eastern literature. Combining the development history of literary trends around the world, case analysis is carried out from the perspectives of myths, epics, poems, novels, dramas, etc., in order to verify the facts of exchange, influence and communication in the development process of Eastern and Western literature. The focus is on analyzing the status, role and influence of Eastern literature, including Chinese literature, on the development of world literature. This course uses a teaching method that combines classroom teaching, extracurricular reading, film and television viewing, and classroom discussions. The purpose is to give students an overall impression of the history of world literature development, and then stimulate students' interest in thinking about how to construct a theoretical system that reflects the true process of the development of world literature, integrates the development of world literature from ancient times to the present, and sort out its development context. The main purpose of the course is to improve students' literary appreciation ability and cultivate students' love for Eastern literature, Eastern culture and Eastern civilization, so that they can be inspired and benefited from their studies, and have the confidence to contribute light and heat to the revival and development of Eastern civilization. _x000D_

Name: Social Media Theory and Applications
Introduction: As social media assumes more and more comprehensive functions in public life, how to use correct social media to obtain knowledge and accurate information, and how to identify and use a large amount of health information, scientific and technological information, and crisis information on social media have become important issues for every social media user. This course will introduce the latest research results on social media in Chinese and American literature; guide students to learn to critically select and use different social media channels; understand the criteria for judging online credibility; learn to scientifically analyze social media platforms and content; and understand the different roles of different social media users in social life.

Name: Economic Reporting: Theory, Issues and Commentary
Introduction: Economic reporting requires a certain amount of knowledge, at least familiarity with the technical vocabulary and basic thinking framework in the economic field. This course is dedicated to introducing the basic economic theories and concepts required for economic reporting, and accumulating necessary technical knowledge (which is a language in itself) so that students can understand and care about current events, and gradually form their own opinions. The course allows students to understand world trends by reading about 30 news reviews selected from major English media, and inspires students to think about economic policies and social phenomena. The course helps students analyze the opinions of well-known economists, policymakers and senior journalists on hot economic issues, learn their concise expression efficiency and rigorous reasoning, and accurate wording writing style, improve students' awareness of issues, and cultivate students' rational narrative and commentary qualities. The course requires students to practice expressing their opinions in English and become familiar with the writing process and basic patterns of economic news reports and comments while studying, discussing, and practicing. Interested students can further read recommended books, including longer academic papers, public speeches by policymakers, and research reports by industry professionals.

Name: Chinese Local Government and Politics
Prerequisite: China Government and politics, local government administration (recommendation)
Introduction:
This course is a professional elective course for senior undergraduate students. It aims to deepen the understanding and understanding of Chinese politics and initially cultivate independent research capabilities. As the main component of a national government organization (personnel, funding, administrative affairs, etc.), local government interacts directly with the people, and its operation is of great significance. In the United States, local government and politics are listed as important courses in the curriculum design of American politics. _x000D_
In terms of reading materials, this course will focus more on research-based books and papers rather than textbooks, thereby cultivating students' research skills and techniques. At the same time, the course will be based on Chinese local government and politics, but at the same time it will be combined with the theory of comparative politics to expand students' horizons. _x000D_
Basic requirements:_x000D_
Complete the required reading tasks before class, attend each lecture and participate in group discussions. Complete a book report and take the final exam. Thus achieving the following requirements: _x000D_
1) Be familiar with and master the basic theories and literature on Chinese local government and politics;_x000D_
2) Cultivate English reading ability;_x000D_
3) Master basic research methods and be able to conduct preliminary independent research; _x000D_
4) Cultivate the habit of independent thinking and critical thinking.

Name: Civil Society and Non-Governmental Organizations
Introduction: In the past thirty years, a large number of social organizations characterized by non-governmental and non-profit have emerged, resulting in the so-called global "association revolution" phenomenon. These organizations have shown great potential in public governance and political democracy. This course will comprehensively describe and analyze this phenomenon, and use rich data and examples to demonstrate the important role of various social organizations such as social groups, private non-enterprise units, foundations, and social enterprises in leading and promoting social progress. The course content is mainly divided into three parts: first, the government's regulatory system for non-profit organizations and its effectiveness; second, the partnership between non-profit organizations and the government; third, effective ways to build the capacity of non-profit organizations, including service and policy participation. This course will be approached from the perspective of the interactive relationship between the country and society, with equal emphasis on international experience and local practice, real experience and theoretical analysis. It will focus on exploring the concept and practical development paths and characteristics of social innovation, and focus on cultivating students' innovative consciousness and creativity.

Name: Calculus
Introduction: Calculus is an important foundation and starting point of modern mathematics. It has been widely used not only in the fields of physics, mechanics, chemistry, biology and other natural sciences. In recent decades, it has been used in social, economic, humanities and other fields, becoming an important research tool in these fields. Calculus originated from the capitalist industrial revolution. The development of industry required the precise description of the regularities of various movements - mechanical movement, celestial movement, fluid and gas movement, etc. For this reason, mathematics-calculus as a study of variables was born. Newton and Leibniz established calculus in the 17th century. It took more than a century and a half to form the system of calculus currently used. Economics is closely related to modern mathematics. According to statistics, more than half of the winners of the Nobel Prize in Economics since 1969 have benefited from the effective application of modern mathematics. Therefore, calculus, which is the basis of modern mathematics, is also an important basic course for economics majors. Calculus, which studies variables, is different from elementary mathematics, which mainly studies constants. Pay attention to its characteristics in learning methods.

Name: Agricultural Economic History and Its Quantitative Study
Introduction: There are words in "Yi Zhuan" to "reveal the past and know the future", "take history as a mirror", "read history wisely"... History is to understand the connection between events, identify the causal relationship between events, and explore the laws of historical development. Agricultural economic thought can be traced back to ancient times. During the Spring and Autumn Period of my country, the works of Confucius and Mencius contained many discussions on agricultural management, land systems and stable people's livelihood. The "Columbian Exchange", population growth and migration laid the cornerstone of modern civilization. What impact did climate change, the Columbian Exchange, and steel have on the agricultural economy? How do the evolution of land systems and changes in political power at home and abroad promote the adjustment of agricultural structure step by step? How has rice farming culture affected the psychology of people in modern society? This course will teach students basic agricultural economic history knowledge against the long historical background of agriculture, and sort out the main events that promoted the changes in the global agricultural system. Under the framework of economics, analyze the inextricable and close connection between agricultural development and historical trajectories. "The use of history is of great benefit. It is an urgent task for mankind, and it is the main road of the country. It is indispensable for those who have a country and a family?" Taking this elective course is to look at human beings vertically and understand agricultural economy and rural development scientifically.

Name: Buddhist Art and Archaeology: South Asia and China
Introduction:
As one of the three major world religions alongside Christianity and Islam, Buddhism has spread widely in many countries and regions in Asia. It has not only had a significant impact on their political, social, cultural and artistic traditions, but also enriched the spiritual lives of people of all ethnic groups in ancient times. For example, in China since the Northern Wei Dynasty, Buddhism has been a "prohibitory law that assists the royal government and a good deed that benefits benevolence and wisdom." ("Book of Wei: Shi Lao Zhi") In the Tang Dynasty, Chang'an City was divided into several "fangs", and almost each of them had a Buddhist temple, which was responsible for the spiritual restraint of the people in the fang. In addition, China traditionally calls Buddhism the Xiang (Image) religion; "'Xiang Jiao' refers to the use of images to teach people." (Liu Chen's Notes on "Selected Works") Therefore, Buddhist sculptures and paintings are important media or means for the dissemination of Buddhism. _x000D_
"Buddhist Art and Archeology: South Asia and China" is an elective course offered to undergraduates throughout the school. It intends to interpret the Buddhist cultural heritage of South Asia (including Central Asia) and China from the perspective of the intersection of archeology and art disciplines. The objects of Buddhist archeology mainly include ground-level Buddhist temple ruins, cave temple ruins and Buddhist relics; while the focus of Buddhist art history research focuses on the latter two items, namely grotto sculptures, murals and single statues. During the teaching process, teachers mainly teach from the perspective of Buddhist archeology, as well as art historical research methods.

Name: Population Health Economics
Introduction:
This course starts from the perspective of the population, focusing on the various factors that determine population health and people's health behaviors, as well as the role that the government can and should play. Although based on the theories and methods of economics, it will also fully integrate relevant theories, methods and research results in epidemiology, public health, medical sociology, especially the health promotion discipline. _x000D_
When teaching the above issues, this course will not only introduce relevant international theories to students, but also fully integrate it with China's actual situation. China is facing severe challenges in terms of the overall healthy development of the population and in terms of distribution; in terms of the overall construction and operation of the health and medical system, as well as in terms of its accessibility and fairness. The government's leading role, institutional design and resource allocation in dealing with these many challenges are indispensable. Individual and community involvement is also essential. _x000D_
The arrangement of this course is divided into two parts: basic theoretical introduction and topic analysis. Some topics will focus on some practical issues in China. Since its establishment, the Peking University Research Center for Economics and Human Development has completed a set of research projects on my country's health, covering major issues such as the construction of new rural cooperative medical care in rural areas, maternal and child health care, residents' medical-seeking behavior, rural medical and health human resources construction, and health promotion. This course will provide students with an introduction to these research projects and investigations, demonstrate relevant important research results, and explain relevant research methods. _x000D_
At the same time, relevant foreign literature will also be introduced to you in the form of special topics, especially literature related to health promotion and public participation. It is hoped that some of the concepts and methods can be critically applied by students to help promote my country's health promotion work. _x000D_
In addition to teacher lectures and expert lectures, this course especially encourages students to participate. Students will be arranged to read some important documents in depth in thematic groups, and students will give class introductions in groups. _x000D_
The main textbooks for the theoretical part are listed below. In addition to these teaching materials, there will also be courses based on the course progress_x000D_
Recommend other relevant teaching materials to students. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Environmental and Resource Economics Engineering
Introduction:
Environmental issues are related to the quality of residents' daily lives and economic growth; major environmental project decisions have taken the center stage of national decision-making in the past few years. Today in the 21st century, the formation, implementation and operation of environmental engineering are no longer a simple engineering technology plus "cost-benefit" analysis, but a comprehensive theoretical exploration based on cutting-edge engineering technology in a broader disciplinary background that integrates institutional economics, factor capital market theory, political economics, sociology and aesthetics. Introduction to Environmental Resource Economics Engineering is just such a cutting-edge interdisciplinary subject that is born in response to the needs of the times. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course is open to senior undergraduates and junior graduate students of Peking University. It is better to have first- and second-year college knowledge of mathematical analysis, environmental engineering, and economics. The course starts from the current major environmental issues, combines the basic concepts and methods of economics and engineering, and based on the discussion of growth mechanisms and development mechanisms, systematically teaches the empowerment, confirmation and important categories of environmental resources in the sense of the earth unit, discusses the process mechanism of the growth interaction between environmental engineering and the national economic system; introduces the decision-making frontier cases of major projects; and introduces the accounting and related software of major projects. The class emphasizes discussion features, such as interacting with classmates on the multiple mechanisms of smog formation and multi-disciplinary paths and entry points for solving it. Through the study of this course, students will acquire cutting-edge knowledge and innovative thinking skills in environmental resource engineering, laying a solid foundation for subsequent study and work.

Name: Environmental Accounting
Introduction:
Environmental issues are a new issue that accompanies economic growth. In recent years, as people have deepened their understanding of the externalities of economic development, environmental issues have become an important branch of development issues and have attracted attention from all walks of life and the government. Since environmental issues have both technical and value characteristics, especially the application of economic analysis methods as value analysis has been an important research direction on environmental issues since the new century. _x000D_
"Environmental Accounting and Environmental Accounting" re-understands a series of difficulties and contradictions arising from economic operations under the existing SNA theoretical framework, adopts the SEEA value analysis system at the macroeconomic level, and uses the FMA physical analysis system at the microscopic level. It strives to give students a more comprehensive understanding of the solutions to environmental problems and operating methods, and provides theoretical and practical tools for students to participate in environmental management and the formulation of environmental policies.

Name: Regional Economics
Introduction:
"Regional economics" is a comprehensive applied science that uses economic perspectives to study the development changes, spatial organization and interrelationships of economies in different regions. After World War II, with the deepening of international and domestic regional division of labor, especially the intensification of imbalances in economic development between countries and regions, governments of all countries have invariably strengthened their intervention in regional economic activities. As a result, regional economics gradually developed and matured as a relatively independent discipline in the 1950s. _x000D_
At present, regional economics has gradually evolved into a complete scientific system that mainly provides theoretical basis for regional economic decision-making of governments at all levels. It can be considered that regional economics is an ancient and young science that developed rapidly after World War II.

Name: Agricultural Economics
Prerequisite: Political economy, economics rationale, microeconomics, macroeconomics
Introduction:
This course is a required course for the "Department of Environmental Resources and Industrial Economics" of the School of Economics at Peking University and a restricted elective course for the School of Economics. Agricultural economics is an ancient and new discipline. Due to the special important position of agriculture in my country's national economy and the environmental attributes of agricultural production activities, as well as the basic characteristics of agricultural products as basic food resources, agricultural economic activities are an important research object for environmental resources and economic development. _x000D_
This course guides students to master the basic methods of agricultural industry analysis through the study of the basic principles, institutions and systems of agricultural economic activities; through the analysis of the main problems of my country's agricultural economic growth, it cultivates students' comprehensive understanding of economic laws, the ability to use sustainable development principles and methods to solve practical problems, and the comprehensive research ability. _x000D_

Name: Theory of Economic Growth
Introduction: This course aims to systematically introduce neoclassical growth theory and endogenous growth theory, and explore the endogenous relationship between a country's industrial structure, technology selection, institutional changes, population growth, income distribution, financial markets, economic globalization and other factors and the country's per capita gross domestic product (GDP) growth.

Name: Human Capital and Economic Development
Introduction: China has made outstanding achievements in the 40 years of reform and opening up, among which human capital plays a decisive role in economic development. This is not only true for China, but also for countries around the world. Through the study of this course, students can master: 1. The meaning and characteristics of human capital, human capital investment, human capital property rights and other related concepts; 2. The development process and theoretical system of human capital thought; 3. The role mechanism of human capital in economic development; 4. Labor market and macroeconomics, education investment and returns, unemployment and job search, personnel management, etc. in human capital and economic growth.

Name: Energy Economics
Introduction: Energy economics is a cross-cutting and cutting-edge new discipline that integrates management, resources, environment, economics and other superior disciplines to adapt to the times. It is also an emerging discipline that is urgently needed to be developed in response to China's energy situation at this stage. Energy is one of the most basic material foundations of the national economy. When energy is used as a necessity as an input into the production process, all aspects related to the energy commodity constitute the energy economy. Energy economy refers to the economic activities of the production, exchange, distribution and consumption of materials that generate energy. It is the sum of various energy industry economies and an important part of the national economy. Energy economics plays an important guiding role in contemporary economic development.

Name: Theoretical and Applied Linguistics
Introduction: "Theoretical and Applied Linguistics" aims to break the disciplinary barriers between language researchers, introduce students to different perspectives, core concerns, and cutting-edge issues in contemporary language research, and guide students to recognize and understand the complex multidimensionality of language and linguistic phenomena and the necessity of interdisciplinary research on language issues. The course not only involves the philosophy of language, generative linguistics, language typology and pragmatics, which are theoretical schools that explore the nature of language and the rules of language use, and take language as the object of scientific research, but also explore the interaction between language and identity, power, politics, conflict and ideology in a socio-political context. The course is taught in English and students will be guided to read English literature relevant to the course content.

Name: Politics and Diplomacy of the Central Asian States
Prerequisite: It would be better to have a basic understanding of Chinese diplomacy, Russian issues, etc.
Introduction:
This course falls within the scope of regional studies. Compared to theoretical courses, the main purpose of this course is to provide as comprehensive a picture as possible of the basic situation in the region, the main problems and trends. As an optional course, the course will focus on some of the more important and practical issues that have emerged in the Central Asian region since the 1990s, focusing on the relevant political, economic and diplomatic aspects.
Given the complexity of politics and diplomacy in Central Asia, the course will inevitably cover a wide range of historical cultural, economic, ethnic and religious issues and will therefore consider including them in order to gain a more comprehensive understanding of the underlying causes and context of political and diplomatic development in Central Asia.

Name: History of Japanese Culture
Prerequisite: Japanese must have at least a Japanese proficiency test level 2 or the equivalent, preferably with a world and Japanese general history.
Introduction:
The Japanese were influenced by Chinese, European and American culture and established their own cultural system. This lesson will explain the historical process of the formation of Japanese culture by displaying a large number of photos of cultural relics. _x000D_
      This course will focus on the decisive role that Buddhism played in Japanese culture, the Chinese cultural relics preserved by Shoso-in, the formation process from Tang style culture to national style culture, the formation process of Higashiyama culture and art (tea ceremony, flower arrangement, etc.), the relationship between Confucianism and Chinese studies in the Edo period, civilization and Westernization in the Meiji era, and the formation process of modern subculture. _x000D_
      Through the course, I hope everyone can understand the mainstream and characteristics of Japanese culture, especially the difference from Chinese culture. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Japanese Historiographical Classics
Prerequisite: World general history course, Japanese secondary or equivalent to Japanese secondary
Introduction:
This course mainly focuses on reading historical masterpieces in the field of Japanese language. Students who choose this course are required to have at least Level 2 of the International Japanese Language Proficiency Test or equivalent level of Japanese proficiency. _x000D_
      In addition to completing basic classroom lectures, this course will guide students to read a large number of Japanese works in terms of teaching content, providing professional academic training for students who are interested in further research on history. It is especially suitable for students majoring in world history who are interested in Japanese history research, students majoring in foreign studies, students majoring in Japanese in the School of Foreign Languages, and students majoring in Japanese history at the graduate level. It will also be helpful to students studying Chinese history.

Name: Close Reading of Contemporary Foreign Short Stories
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Current foreign short novels (2014), literary theory, contemporary Chinese literature, long novel studies since the 1990s.
Introduction:
This course selects the most representative contemporary short story classic examples from foreign countries for analysis and explanation, and guides students to discuss and study. Such as the masterpieces of novels by Munro, O'Connor, Borges, Dürrenmatt, Carver, etc., summarize the narrative methods of novels, study how novelists cut into the narrative of novels, and then carry out careful reading and analysis to understand how masters' novels refine ideas and develop text rhetoric and language style. This reveals the artistic differences between contemporary Chinese and foreign novels, and trains students to master unique literary masters and artistic expression methods of novels. Lay a solid foundation for literary research, literary criticism and novel writing. _x000D_
The course will be conducted in the form of a seminar. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports and participate in in-depth discussions of other students' course reports. _x000D_

Name: History of Northeast Asia
Introduction: The "History of Northeast Asia" course is to cultivate and improve undergraduate students' understanding of international relations in Northeast Asia. Through the study of textbooks, historical materials and new archival materials, we will gain an in-depth understanding of the development of international relations in Northeast Asia in modern times. Specifically, this article focuses on the background and results of the international relations between Europe, Asia, and Asian countries since the Opium War, including the international relations of Northeast Asia in the late Qing Dynasty (China-Russia, Japan-Russia, Japan-North Korea, China-North Korea, and China-Japan relations), the Sino-Japanese War, the Three Kingdoms Intervention, the Russo-Japanese War, the Revolution of 1911, Japan's annexation of Korea, the Kuomintang-Communist Civil War, the Sino-Japanese War, and the Soviet-Japanese-China-Japanese Treaty Jump Day. Korean relations include the attitude of the north and south governments of China towards the October Revolution, the Eastern Qing Railway Incident (1929), the Soviet Union’s attitude towards the September 18th Incident, the formation of the United Front between the Soviet Union and the Anti-Japanese War, the international relations in Northeast Asia after World War II, the origin and process of the Korean War, and the analysis of the reasons for China’s intervention in the Korean War, to better grasp the historical development of international relations in Northeast Asia since the Opium War. The books I read were mainly textbooks such as "History of International Relations in Northeast Asia", "Research on the History of International Relations in Modern Northeast Asia" and "History of Sino-Soviet Relations during the Republic of China I II III", supplemented by "Outline of the History of Sino-Soviet Relations", "History of Sino-US Relations (Part 1, 2)", "History of Soviet-Japanese Relations", "Collection of Sino-Soviet Relations (32 volumes in total)" and reference to first-hand materials or archives from the United States, Russia and China.

Name: Introduction to German Linguistics (I)
Prerequisite: Quest in German (I), Quest in German (II)
Introduction:
"Introduction to German Linguistics" is an elective course for undergraduates majoring in German in the School of Foreign Languages. It is taught to second-year undergraduates and above majoring in German and German history. This course takes the origin and development of language as the starting point, and the German learning sequence of German learners as the main clue. It uses the framework and way of thinking of linguistics to discuss and elaborate on difficult issues in German learning from the perspectives of basic concepts of linguistics, German history, German phonetics, German grammar and German semantics, while reviewing and consolidating the German language. The classroom discussions in this course mainly use German as the source of examples. At the same time, English, a compulsory second foreign language for undergraduates of Germanic languages, will be used as the second source of examples, mixed with a few examples from contemporary languages ​​such as Dutch and French, and ancient languages ​​such as Old High German and Old English (all including translation). It combines the academic and practical aspects of linguistics and absorbs the latest research results in the academic world. This course achieves the purpose of reviewing the German language, popularizing basic concepts of linguistics, and stimulating students' interest in and thinking about linguistics. _x000D_
This course will use classroom lectures as the main teaching method, supplemented by communication methods such as lectures, class discussions, and student reports. It strives to enable students to have a preliminary understanding of German linguistics while reviewing German grammar and improving their German proficiency. It will deepen students' understanding of German in terms of German history, dialects, semantics, etc., enrich students' knowledge structure, and while cultivating literary literacy, expand the theoretical horizons of linguistics, improve academic literacy, and promote students' all-round development in language.

Name: Intensive German Reading (III)
Introduction: This course is based on German Intensive Reading (I) and (II), and continues to guide students to get started in German, from the shallower to the more advanced, from cultivating students' preliminary German language communication skills and the five basic skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translating, as well as understanding the general social culture and national culture of German-speaking countries. To expand, deepen and further improve students' German knowledge and application level; pay attention to improving students' thinking, understanding, analytical and comprehensive abilities as well as independent learning style and ability, so as to lay a good foundation for further study of German language, culture and literature. _x000D_

Name: German Audiovisual and Speaking (III)
Introduction: Through listening exercises, students are exposed to various types of German conversations and articles, understand relevant content, and answer relevant questions, ultimately enabling students to have good German listening responses and oral expression skills.

Name: Area Studies of German-Speaking Countries
Introduction:
Basic requirements: Understand the latest basic political, economic and social developments in German-speaking countries, master the principle issues in their political, economic systems and social structures, and have an insight into the practical problems existing in the society of German-speaking countries. _x000D_
Key Points and Difficulties: Obtain relevant information by reading original German materials. _x000D_

Name: Intensive German Reading (IV)
Introduction: This course is based on German Intensive Reading (1), (2), and (3), and continues to guide students to get started with German. From the shallower to the deeper, it starts from cultivating students’ preliminary German language communication skills and the five basic skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translating, as well as understanding the general social culture of German-speaking countries. and national conditions, to expand, deepen and further improve students’ German knowledge and application level; pay attention to improving students’ thinking, understanding, analytical and comprehensive abilities as well as their independent learning style and ability, so as to lay a good foundation for further study of German language, culture and literature. _x000D_

Name: German Audiovisual and Speaking (IV)
Introduction: Through listening exercises, students are exposed to various types of German conversations and articles, understand relevant content, and answer relevant questions, ultimately enabling students to have good German listening responses and oral expression skills.

Name: History of Germany
Prerequisite: Excellent German reading (i), (ii) or learning German equivalent to 400 school hours
Introduction:
On the premise of focusing on the historical development of Germany before 1871, this course is divided into four parts: ancient times, the Middle Ages, modern times and modern times to briefly outline the basic trend and development of the German nation and country from ancient times to the present. It briefly presents the new situations and hot issues of the social and historical development of modern and contemporary Germany. It strives to reflect the new results and new perspectives of German historical research at home and abroad in the past one or two decades, introduces the opinions of many people, and conducts multi-angle analyzes of historical phenomena, events and figures with decisive influence. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: German Translation (I)
Introduction: Translation is a communicative act in which two cultures come into contact, and will be affected by factors such as language, culture, society, ideology, and the times. Starting from this perspective, this course combines theories such as stylistics and syntax to allow students to understand the basic steps of translation, and through two-way practice of German-Chinese and Chinese-German translation of the same type of text, students can master methods and techniques for solving common problems.

Name: Literary History of German-Speaking Countries with Selected Readings (II)
Introduction: It tells the literature of German-speaking countries from the classical literature of the 18th century to the end of realist literature at the end of the 19th century, including classical literature, romantic literature, Biedermeier period literature and realist literature. The focus of the course is to clarify the development context of German literature history, reveal the internal laws of literary development, and the relationship between literature and political, social, ideological and cultural history. The narrative content includes important literary concepts, stylistic knowledge, and works of classic writers in each period.

Name: Literary History of German-Speaking Countries with Selected Readings (I)
Introduction: It tells the literature of German-speaking countries from the early Middle Ages to the end of Enlightenment literature at the end of the 18th century (up to the Sturm und Drang period), including medieval court knight literature, the late Middle Ages, Baroque (17th century) and Enlightenment literature (18th century). The focus of the course is to clarify the development context of German literature history, reveal the internal laws of literary development, and the relationship between literature and political, social, ideological and cultural history. The narrative content includes important literary concepts, stylistic knowledge, and works of classic writers in each period.

Name: History of the Chinese Language (Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for third-year undergraduate students majoring in Chinese in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature. It teaches the history of Chinese vocabulary and grammar. We will introduce the basic aspects of Chinese vocabulary and grammar in various historical periods, and teach some important issues on the historical evolution of Chinese vocabulary by topic, and teach the historical evolution process and evolution rules of important grammatical phenomena. Through the study of this course, it is hoped that students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding of the basic facts of the evolution of Chinese vocabulary and grammar over more than 3,000 years from the Oracle period to modern Chinese, and learn to analyze and summarize the laws of the historical evolution of vocabulary and grammar.

Name: Advanced Mathematics (Type D) Problem Session
Introduction: Liberal Arts Advanced Mathematics is a course that combines basic mathematical theory and applied mathematical methods to adapt to the trend of liberal arts penetration in modern science. Its teaching content and methods have obvious liberal arts characteristics. Currently, the Department of Mathematics teaches liberal arts advanced mathematics courses to undergraduates and some graduate students in various majors such as journalism, society, government, information management, Chinese, archeology, national affairs, and languages, as well as various departments of economics and management. The content includes three parts: calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics. This course is an exercise course. This course consolidates the textbook content learned through exercises.

Name: History of the Chinese Language (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for third-year undergraduate students majoring in Chinese in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature. It is an improvement course in Chinese phonology. We will systematically teach the phonetic system of various historical periods in the history of the Chinese language, deeply analyze and explain its diachronic evolution process, explain various phonetic change phenomena, and summarize the rules of phonetic change. On the basis of teaching basic knowledge, we will contact practical problems that need to be solved in current phonetic history research, inspire students' ideas, and guide students to observe, analyze and solve problems.

Name: Financial Law / Banking Law
Prerequisite: Contract law, property law, company law
Introduction: Describe the basic legal framework and related regime of the Financial Code, which gives students a more comprehensive and preliminary understanding of the Code.

Name: Time Series Analysis
Introduction: Time series analysis is a general term for the method of studying and analyzing time series data, that is, one or more sets of data sequentially in time. A large amount of common data in economics, finance, environmental science and meteorology are time series data. Time series analysis aims to establish a time series model to describe the inherent dynamic laws of data, so as to explore and study the data generation mechanism and master the characteristics of data generated by various data generation mechanisms. On the other hand, based on data characteristics, we find appropriate and effective time series models to describe them. Through time series analysis, we can make rational predictions for the future based on past observations, study the relationship between multiple series, and so on. This method has wide applications in many fields such as economy, finance, environment, meteorology and so on.

Name: Introduction to Data Science
Introduction:
This is a basic course for data science majors. Main purposes: (1) To introduce the basic principles, models and algorithms of data analysis; (2) To obtain practical experience in data analysis. This course emphasizes the combination of theory and practical experience, using a model of large class classroom teaching and small class practical operation. Since this course is offered for the first time, students majoring in data science have priority in choosing the course. _x000D_
_x000D_
Main contents: data preprocessing, classification model, clustering model, regression model, feature extraction and model selection, dimensionality reduction, text analysis, graph algorithm and social network analysis, recommendation system, neural network and deep learning, distributed computing. _x000D_

Name: Integrated Mathematics and Physics I
Introduction: The main elements of this course include the calculus of single variables, constant differential equations and mechanics.

Name: Integrated Laboratory Course I
Introduction: This course lasts for one year and includes a total of 9 large-scale experimental trainings. It focuses on training students' hands-on experimental skills, basic experimental skills in physics, chemistry, electronics, and computer science, and focuses on the application of relevant knowledge in the study of classic problems in life sciences. Each large-scale experiment requires one day per week for 2-3 consecutive weeks to learn and operate. Students should carefully study relevant theoretical knowledge before class. Instructors are responsible for training students in basic experimental operation skills in experimental courses, inspiring and guiding experimental discussions, appropriately teaching background knowledge, and requiring students to write experimental reports. Contents covered in the course include: fluid mechanics and life phenomena at low Reynolds numbers, measuring yeast mutation rate, measuring simulated bacterial growth rate with a homemade photometer, measuring Avogadro's constant, Boltzmann's constant, biological motion and chemotaxis, radiation and random phenomena, cell mechanics, basic chemical synthesis, geometric optics and imaging basics. This course is a required course for the integrated science experiment class.

Name: Foundations of Chemistry
Introduction:
The course is divided into two parts: general chemistry and organic chemistry. In the general chemistry section, freshmen in integrated science classes will be introduced to the basic concepts of chemistry and _x000D_
Methods, mainly including basic laws of gases and liquids, chemical thermodynamics and chemical reaction directions, chemical equilibrium, molecular structure, crystal structure, coordination_x000D_
Chemistry of bit compounds and elements. In the organic chemistry section, organic chemistry is comprehensively introduced to enable students to master the core knowledge content of organic chemistry and understand organic_x000D_
The development history of chemistry and the development trends and application prospects in cutting-edge fields. Learn for subsequent biochemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry and other related courses_x000D_
Xi laid a solid foundation.

Name: Quantitative Molecular Biology
Introduction: The quantitative molecular biology course described in this course is for freshmen in the integrated disciplines of Yuanpei College and is offered in the first semester. This course includes the basics of molecular biology and four quantitative special topics: (1) Two-body systems; (2) Random motion of organisms; (3) Ratio equations; (4) Introduction to systems biology. This course is aimed at freshmen who have just entered the school. The knowledge involved in mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology will be appropriately supplemented, so no prerequisite courses are required. The biggest feature of this course is to provide a simple introduction to quantitative concepts for young people who have just entered university and begun to systematically study life sciences. Quantitative research involves the intersection and cooperation of different fields, which is a major trend in scientific research. For this reason, Peking University has established a cutting-edge interdisciplinary research institute, and the teachers work in the Quantitative Biology Center of the college. Through the study of this course, we hope that students can understand and accept the ideas of quantitative research and appreciate the charm of cutting-edge interdisciplinary subjects from the beginning of their university studies. This is the main purpose of this course. The content involved in this course is relatively easy to understand, laying a good foundation for students' future systematic learning. In the molecular biology part, you can take electives in the future: (1) Molecular Biology College of Life Sciences; (2) Nucleic acid biology RNA biology Wang Yangming College of Life Sciences (College of Life Sciences); (3) Biochemistry Lai Luhua (Integrated Science) Biochemistry (Integrated Science); (4) Biophysical Chemistry Lai Luhua College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering (College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering) Molecular Engineering) and other courses to continue to learn more. In the quantitative research part, you can continue to gain a deeper understanding in the future by taking elective courses such as: (1) Physical Biology of the Cell (Sun Yujie, College of Life Sciences); (2) Biomathematical Physics, Ge Hao, School of Mathematical Sciences. This course is the basis of the above courses, does not conflict with these courses, and can be well combined.

Name: Physical Chemistry (Integrated Science) I
Introduction: This course is a basic course offered in the second semester for undergraduates in the integrated science experimental class. The main content integrates the thermal content of physics and the physical chemistry content of chemistry, and also provides some preliminary introduction to the thinking methods of statistical physics. This course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories, basic knowledge and basic methods of studying thermodynamics and physical chemistry, and to cultivate students' scientific thinking methods and ability to analyze problems. The teaching content is combined with the regulatory mechanism of biological systems to enable students to understand the relationship between thermodynamics, physical chemistry and life sciences, and stimulate students' interest and innovative spirit.

Name: Contemporary Chinese Society
Introduction:
In this day and age, we are particularly interested in what is happening in China. Before the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949, China had experienced a century of humiliation from the Opium War in 1840 to the end of World War II. China had always been in the abyss of poverty and backwardness. It was not until the economic reforms in 1978 that China restored its ties with the rest of the world and ushered in a new era. Since 1978, China has experienced social changes that are unprecedented in terms of scale, speed, and impact in human history. All aspects of Chinese society are undergoing fundamental and permanent changes. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will introduce some of the most salient features of Chinese society, including work units, education systems, urban-rural divide, population migration, social inequality, marriage and family, ethnicity and religion. The focus of teaching is to understand China's social phenomena within China's historical, cultural, political and economic background. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will give students a sociological perspective for understanding China and enable them to learn to study other social changes in China. The long-term impact of these social changes is not only on the 1.3 billion Chinese people living in China, but also on other developed and developing countries in the world. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Chinese Society
Introduction: This course is a pilot general course of Yuanpei College, and priority is given to Yuanpei students. Through the study of this course, students will initially understand and master (1) the basic concepts and important research methods of sociology; (2) the basic impression of Chinese society from the perspective of sociological research, including historical traditions and contemporary reality; (3) the ability to use sociological methods to analyze some empirical phenomena in Chinese society. This course is conducted in the form of large class lectures + small class discussions. In addition to attending lectures, students are required to read bibliographies, participate in discussions in each small class, and complete 5 course assignments and a final open-book exam. Course grades are awarded based on small class discussions and research reports (40%), assignments (20%), and final exams (40%). _x000D_

Name: Physiology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Study the normal activity processes of various systems, organs and cells in the human body, especially the internal mechanisms of the functional performance of each organ and cell, and clarify how the functional activities of the human body as a whole coordinate and restrict each other, as well as the impact of changes in the internal and external environment of the body on these activities.

Name: Public Choice Theory
Introduction:
Public choice theory is the economic study of non-market decision-making, or simply defined as the application of economics to the analysis of political science research objects such as state theory, voting rules, voter behavior, political parties, and management systems. This course takes the origins of the state and the market as the starting point, explores the relationship between the government and the market, and uses economic analysis methods to explore the existence basis of the political market. This textbook focuses on the origin of the government and the market, the products of the political market, voter theory, party theory, and the operation and equilibrium of the political market. Finally, it discusses and expands the cutting-edge theory of public choice. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students can learn and understand the real situation of political markets other than economic markets, especially the topics that are the same as political science research objects based on economic analysis, and what new theories and conclusions will be analyzed using the methods of individualism, transaction existence, and rational choice in economics. This includes a rational understanding of voters, interest groups, government officials, politicians, and parliament. This provides a deeper understanding of the special phenomena manifested by changes in my country's economic system. Public choice implies a very important theoretical topic, that is, the economic analysis and rational understanding and grasp of the government and the market. Through the study of public choice theory, one can better sort out the understanding of traditional economic theory, and at the same time gain a deeper understanding of economic thinking about the political market. _x000D_

Name: Public Economics
Introduction:
Public economics is a basic course for undergraduate students majoring in finance. It teaches basic concepts, basic theories and basic facts in the main research fields involved in the finance major. It is an introductory course for this major. _x000D_
Public Economics and Public Finance are of the same origin, but since the 1950s, important financial scientists have preferred to refer to the discipline of finance as public economics. This is not just a matter of changing the name of a discipline, it reflects the expansion, development and update of the research scope, focus of investigation and analysis methods of this discipline. Finance mainly studies fiscal balance and expenditure, especially fiscal revenue issues. It cannot explain, analyze and solve related economic phenomena and problems. Public economics not only studies the fiscal balance and expenditure itself, but more importantly, studies the impact of fiscal revenue and expenditure and other government policies and activities on the economy, such as public goods, externalities, imperfect competition, The issues and theories of asymmetric information, etc., form the theoretical basis of how the government implements policies and the scope and methods of its activities, such as welfare economics, public choice theory, social redistribution, intergenerational analysis methods and techniques, etc., which not only greatly enrich the content of public economics, but also form a closer interconnected relationship with many surrounding disciplines. This course is based on this basic background to teach students a panoramic and theoretical study and mastery of the basic issues, basic concepts, and basic methods of this subject. Through the study of this course, it will lay a solid foundation for the study of other courses in this major.

Name: Incentive Theory and Economic Development
Introduction: Incentive theory is one of the most important achievements of economics since the 1960s. This course aims to provide undergraduates with a concise and complete tool for learning incentive theory and a brief introduction to the application of incentive theory in economic development. The literature on motivation theory is extremely vast. Students who are interested in learning motivation theory in depth can read the textbooks, reference books and relevant original texts listed in the course syllabus. It is worth pointing out that the instructor will provide a complete courseware for the classroom lectures. Therefore, the textbooks, reference books and original texts of the listed literature are all optional.

Name: Integrated Laboratory Course II
Introduction: The course lasts for one year, with a total of 9 large-scale experimental training, focusing on training students' experimental hands-on ability, basic experimental skills in physics, chemistry, electronics, and computer science, and focusing on the application of relevant knowledge in the study of classic problems in life sciences. Each large-scale experiment requires one day per week for 2-3 consecutive weeks to learn and operate. Students should carefully study relevant theoretical knowledge before class. Instructors are responsible for training students in basic experimental operation skills in experimental courses, inspiring and guiding experimental discussions, appropriately teaching background knowledge, and requiring students to write experimental reports. Contents covered in the course include: fluid mechanics and life phenomena at low Reynolds numbers, measuring yeast mutation rate, measuring simulated bacterial growth rate with a homemade photometer, measuring Avogadro's constant, Boltzmann's constant, biological motion and chemotaxis, radiation and random phenomena, cell mechanics, basic chemical synthesis, geometric optics and imaging basics. This course is a required course for the integrated science experiment class.

Name: Biochemistry (Integrated Science)
Introduction: This course is a basic course offered in the second semester for undergraduates in the integrated science experimental class. The course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories, basic knowledge and basic methods of biochemistry research, and cultivate students' scientific thinking methods and ability to analyze problems. The teaching content includes the core content of biochemistry and the latest developments in related fields, enabling students to realize the important role of biochemistry in the cutting-edge research fields of life sciences and related interdisciplinary subjects, and stimulating students' interest and innovative spirit.

Name: Plant Development and Molecular Biology
Introduction: The course focuses on cutting edges and hot spots in today ' s basic theory and application of plant science, detailing basic concepts of plant development biology and molecular biology, as well as research, recent developments, experiences and methods in various fields. The course included: signal transfer mechanisms for plant cell polarity and morphology; molecular mechanisms for plant stem cell separation and regulation; genetic mechanisms for the appearance of plant growth and growth signals; applications of plant genome analysis in plant development research; plant photoformation construction; and light signal molecular transfer pathways.

Name: Quantitative Cell Biology
Prerequisite: This course requires a certain calculus and programming base, and it is sufficient to complete the basic course of mathematics and physics in the first grade of the university.
Introduction: "Quantitative Cell Biology" is a basic course offered to second-year undergraduate students in the integrated science experimental class in the first semester. Students from other departments who have a certain mathematical foundation (calculus) and are interested in interdisciplinary life sciences are also welcome to take it. Today's life science research is moving in the direction of quantification and interdisciplinarity. Therefore, many world-renowned universities have established quantitative biology, a new and highly interdisciplinary discipline. This course is offered in the context of the increasingly important interdisciplinary field. On the one hand, the course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts and principles of cell biology, as well as the basic methods of studying cell biology. On the other hand, the course will also teach quantitative principles and models in various cellular processes, and train students to use mathematical physics tools to quantitatively analyze biological problems, so as to deeply understand the operating rules of biological systems. The teaching content includes the core content of cell biology and quantitative principles and models in related fields, and allows students to learn to use programming tools (such as Matlab) to simulate and analyze cellular processes, so that students can realize the importance of interdisciplinary subjects such as biophysics, mathematics, and chemistry, and stimulate students' interest and innovative spirit.

Name: Physical Chemistry (Integrated Science) II
Introduction: This course is a basic course offered in the second and third semesters for undergraduates in the integrated science experimental class. The main content integrates the thermal content of physics and the physical chemistry content of chemistry, and also provides some preliminary introduction to the thinking methods of statistical physics. This course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories, basic knowledge and basic methods of studying thermodynamics and physical chemistry, and to cultivate students' scientific thinking methods and ability to analyze problems. The teaching content is combined with the regulatory mechanism of biological systems to enable students to understand the relationship between thermodynamics, physical chemistry and life sciences, and stimulate students' interest and innovative spirit.

Introduction: This course will systematically explain the knowledge and methods of biophysical and biochemical system modeling related to cell biology, molecular biology, neurobiology, etc. The main mathematical tools will involve ordinary differential equations, probability theory, stochastic processes, etc. The physics, chemistry and even biological knowledge involved in this course will be supplemented in a timely manner; the characteristic of this course is that it uses mathematical language to describe and depict chemical processes and life activities, enriching students' horizons without losing rigor and allowing them to appreciate the charm of interdisciplinary subjects.

Prerequisite: This course is mainly aimed at students in the integrated science experimental class who have completed basic courses in their freshman and sophomore years, and will carry out basic training based on laboratory research during their junior year. Name: Selected Readings from the Zuo Zhuan
Introduction:
"Spring and Autumn" and "Zuo Zhuan" are important classics and historical masterpieces in ancient China. This course aims to introduce students to the basic content and cultural and academic value of "Spring and Autumn" and "Zuo Zhuan" in a systematic and general way through selected readings, and thereby improve students' ability to read and master original historical materials, train students' ability to use historical materials for textual research and analyze historical issues, and cultivate students' solid and realistic research methods and study style through careful and systematic reading. _x000D_
In terms of teaching content, Mr. Yang Bojun's "Zuo Zhuan Annotation on the Spring and Autumn Period" is used as the main teaching material for narration and reading, supplemented by other related works as references. The course consists of approximately 16 sessions and 32 class hours. First, the teacher will introduce the relevant knowledge of "Zuo Zhuan", the historical background involved and the value of historical materials, etc., and then use about 10 systematic demonstrations to read and explain the historical content, regulations and systems, ideological culture, etc. involved in Zuo Zhuan. In addition, one or two classroom inspections will be arranged. During the semester, we strive to conduct a themed class discussion and write assignments to test the results. At the end of the semester, the teacher will make a summary and provide guidance on the writing of the final paper. _x000D_
Grade evaluation method: The final grade is composed of parts. The first is the final exam (conducted by writing a paper), which accounts for 50%-60% of the total grade; the second is the daily homework and classroom examinations, which account for 20%-30% of the total grade; the third is the student's classroom performance, which accounts for about 10% of the total grade. _x000D_

Name: General Survey of Yin and Zhou Bronze Inscriptions
Introduction:
The inscriptions on Yin and Zhou bronzes are the most important unearthed documents. _x000D_
This course introduces the history of bronze inscription research, the discovery and publication of materials, and the compilation and use of related reference books. _x000D_
Selected lectures include the classification and format of bronze inscriptions, the era, content and font of the inscriptions, the evolution of glyphs, and textual interpretation methods. _x000D_
Furthermore, the inscriptions will be integrated to study the Yin and Zhou calendars, the chronology of bronzes, the name system (for example, the self-naming of bronze vessels and the naming of objects, the relationship between the names found in inscriptions and archaeological relics), social and political systems (for example, the sacrificial system, the appointment system, the family and marriage system), the economic system, the military system, etc., and further explore the social thoughts of the Yin and Zhou dynasties (such as the view of destiny, religion). _x000D_
The course combines Shang and Zhou archaeological materials and the staging and dating of Shang and Zhou bronzes. It is mainly aimed at undergraduates, masters and doctoral students majoring in archeology and cultural relics from the Shang and Zhou dynasties as well as those from the Qin and Han dynasties. After the study, you are required to learn to use various related reference books, have a general understanding of the content and research overview of bronze inscriptions, and gradually master the ability to interpret various common bronze inscriptions with the help of reference books. _x000D_

Prerequisite:

Introduction: The initial and ultimate goal of artificial intelligence is to build "intelligent machines" with intelligence comparable to humans. "General artificial intelligence" emphasizes the unity and integrity of intelligence, which is different from artificial intelligence research that focuses on specialized systems. This course uses a "non-axiomatic reasoning system" as an example to introduce the theoretical and technical issues of general artificial intelligence and compare various solutions. This system is able to adapt to the environment and solve problems despite relatively insufficient knowledge and resources, and uniformly realize various cognitive functions.

Name: Advanced Microeconomics (II)
Prerequisite: Students are assumed to be equipped with knowledge of some basic mathematics, e.g., multivariate calculus, analysis, and basic probability theory. No previous economics knowledge is assumed, but intuitions from some undergraduate courses will be helpful.
Introduction: This course is a first-year micro theory course for doctoral students in the School of Economics. It is now open to undergraduate students as part of the school’s honors course. The course mainly teaches game theory, covering basic theory and related applications.
