Name: History of the Byzantine Empire
Prerequisite: The ancient history of the world; the general theory of world history
Introduction:
The teaching purpose of this course is to improve the knowledge structure of the students who choose the course and strengthen their comprehensive ability to analyze problems, solve problems and express innovative academic insights. By the end of this course, students are required to have a relatively comprehensive grasp of the course content, understand the main clues and major issues of the historical development of Byzantium, as well as the main characteristics of Byzantine culture and its special status and role in the history of cultural development in the European Mediterranean world and even the world. The special role of Byzantine history and culture in the medieval history of the European Mediterranean world determines the importance of this course and its significance in improving students' knowledge system. _x000D_
The history of the Byzantine Empire (also known as the Eastern Roman Empire) lasted for more than a thousand years (330-1453). Its capital, Constantinople, was once the largest political, economic, cultural and religious center in medieval Europe and the Mediterranean world. The Byzantine Empire had a strong influence on the surrounding countries and nationalities at that time, especially in the cultural field. It became a bridge connecting the classical Greek and Roman era to the Italian Renaissance. It played an extremely important role in the formation of the Eastern European world, the development of Christian history, and the evolution of early modern European civilization. It occupies a very important position in world history. This course will first systematically introduce the main clues of Byzantine history, the stage characteristics of Byzantine history, the main content and characteristics of Byzantine culture and its historical status; secondly, based on the systematic introduction, it will reveal the development rules of Byzantine history and culture through all-round and multi-angle analysis. _x000D_

Name: Ancient Mesopotamian Civilization
Introduction:
"History begins in Sumer" has become a general consensus. If legible writing is used as the main symbol of civilization, ancient Mesopotamian civilization can be called the earliest civilization of mankind. As early as the late 4000 BC, the two great rivers here—the Euphrates River and the Tigris River— gave birth to the highly developed Sumerian civilization. At that time, not only did clay tablet documents appear that reflected a developed economy, trade, and management system, but also large public buildings such as temples and palaces of unprecedented scale appeared. At the same time, roller seals marking private ideas and institutions of power played an increasing role in economic life. There is no doubt that by the end of the 4th millennium BC, the Sumerian region in the southern part of the Mesopotamia had entered civilization. The Sumerians established a state there and established extensive trade links with the northern part of the Mesopotamia and the vast area of ​​what is now southwestern Iran. They spread their material civilization and cultural achievements to those areas, thereby establishing a so-called "Uruk world system." The exquisite gold and silverware, clay tablets and other non-daily items unearthed from the King of Ur's Mausoleum, the large number of clay tablets unearthed at Farah, the documents and archives unearthed at Abu Sarabih, etc. can all show that in the following centuries, the Sumerians lived together with people who spoke other languages in what was later called the United States by the Greeks. In the land of Sopotamia, they lived together, competed together, created together, and progressed together. Together, they turned the southern part of the Mesopotamia into the most developed civilized area at that time, which had a profound impact on the subsequent civilization process of the region and its surrounding areas, and even on the development of the entire human civilization. _x000D_
Around 3300 BC, the Sumerians invented cuneiform writing. Later, the Elamites, Eblas, Akkadians, Hittites, Babylonians, Assyrians, Ugarites and ancient Persians all adopted cuneiform writing in different forms to record their own languages. The use of cuneiform writing has a history of more than 3,000 years (from 3300 BC to the 1st century AD). The main writing material has always been clay tablets made of readily available soil. Since the clay tablets do not decay, the words written on them have been preserved for a long time. They carry precious information, take us into thousands of years of history, and reveal various secrets to us. _x000D_
The Sumerians not only invented writing and brought mankind from the barbaric era into the civilized era, they also made great achievements in the fields of architecture, art, politics, economy, religion, literature, medicine, law, calendar and other fields. Other peoples who used cuneiform writing also created new history in different fields, adding new glory to human civilization, making the cuneiform cultural circle the most glorious human civilization circle in the ancient world, and making great contributions to the progress of mankind. This course takes history as an outline and comprehensively displays the civilizational achievements of the Sumerians, Akkadians, Babylonians, and Assyrians in various aspects. It can be seen that many of today's civilizational achievements originated from Sumer. Only by understanding the past of human civilization can we better understand ourselves today. For thousands of years, although science and technology have continued to develop, human nature has never changed, and human nature has never changed. This lesson is about witnessing. _x000D_

Name: New Testament Greek (Part 1)
Introduction: As an important part of the Christian classic "Bible", the importance of the "New Testament" to Christian research is self-evident. Since the original text of the New Testament is written in Common Greek, serious reading and study of the Bible must be based on basic knowledge of ancient Greek. This course will teach the basic knowledge of the New Testament and systematically teach New Testament Greek grammar from scratch, so that students can initially acquire the ability to read the original text of the New Testament. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Classical Syriac
Introduction: As the liturgical language used by many Syrian churches in history and today, especially as the language used by the Syrian Eastern Church (the so-called Nestorians) that was introduced to China since the Tang Dynasty, Classical Syriac has special importance. On the one hand, Syriac is an important auxiliary tool for theology-related studies, such as biblical studies, patristic studies, liturgical studies, and Nestorian studies. On the other hand, it is a cultural bridge: during the Baghdad translation movement in the ninth century, many ancient Greek classics were first translated into classical Syriac, and then translated from classical Syriac into Arabic. Syriac was a bridge between Greek and Arab cultures at that time, and today it is a bridge for us to re-understand Greek and Arab cultures. This course will systematically teach Classical Syriac grammar from scratch.

Name: Introduction to Social History Research
Introduction: This course introduces the main trends in the development of history in China and abroad in the 20th century, introduces the origin of the research orientation of social history, and introduces the concepts, nature, methods, themes of social history, regional studies of social history, the anthropological orientation of social history, the relationship between social history and institutional history, etc.

Name: Ottoman-Turkish History
Introduction: Türkiye is a particularly important country both historically and realistically. The Ottoman Empire, which lasted for six hundred years and spanned three continents of Europe, Asia and Africa, was the predecessor of modern Turkey and the last Islamic empire, leaving a rich historical legacy for modern history. The modern Republic of Türkiye is the leading power in the Middle East. Its modern historical process and geostrategic status are worthy of our attention and study. This course focuses on the historical process from the Ottoman Empire to the Turkish Republic, especially the history of the modern republic, with special attention to political, social, cultural and diplomatic changes. In addition, this course will also introduce some preliminary Turkish knowledge to facilitate students to use reference books when reading and translating professional materials in English.

Including medieval economic systems, such as manors, guilds, and commercial organizations; medieval economic policies, such as monetary policy, tax policy, land policy, etc. I hope to understand the economic characteristics of the Middle Ages based on some understanding and analysis of the economic development trends of the region in different periods. Of course, we will also pay special attention to the social context of economic development.

Name: Ancient Chinese Literature (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is an elective course for non-Chinese majors in the Department of Humanities. The course will sort out the formation and development of ancient Chinese literature through the teaching of classic literary works of all dynasties, help students understand the generation and evolution of various literary styles, as well as the formation of writers' personal styles, literary schools, and literary trends, reveal the interactive relationship between literature and external factors such as society, ideology, and politics, and master the basic methods of reading, appreciating, and analyzing ancient literary works. Semi-thin sectioning technology. These experimental techniques play an extremely important position and role in plant scientific research. In view of the training direction of students, this course is mainly aimed at cultivating students to master advanced experimental skills in plant biotechnology and molecular biology research, so that students can be exposed to and master the necessary experimental methods to engage in biotechnology research through the study and practice of this course.

Name: Field Research in Economics
Introduction:
This course focuses on learning the theories, methods and techniques of enterprise surveys using the China Enterprise Innovation and Entrepreneurship Survey (ESIEC). This course is divided into two parts, one is classroom learning, and the other is participation in ESIEC field investigation. Through learning and practice, students will master the sampling principles and techniques of enterprise surveys, questionnaire design ideas and methods, organization and quality control methods of the survey process, and practice communication skills and interview skills. _x000D_
The China Enterprise Innovation and Entrepreneurship Survey (ESIEC) is implemented by the National Development Research Institute of Peking University and the China Social Science Survey Center. It aims to obtain micro-data reflecting the innovation and entrepreneurship status of Chinese enterprises through scientific sampling and field tracking surveys, and to promote higher-quality academic research and policy research. The sample covers 64,400 entrepreneurs or executives of companies in 161 counties in 25 provinces across the country. In April 2015, July to August 2015 and December 2016, the project team has carried out three pre-investigations in 4 county-level cities in 3 districts of Jiangmen City in Guangdong Province, Xiayi County in Henan Province and Baigou Luggage Industry Cluster Area in Hebei Province. The first formal investigation was carried out in 16 counties (cities and districts) in Henan Province from July to August 2017. The 2018 ESIEC survey will be conducted nationwide. _x000D_
ESIEC focuses on investigating entrepreneurs' entrepreneurial history, business creation process, relationships between enterprises, local business environment and the implementation effects of industrial policies, etc. _x000D_
Course study and field investigation work are equally important. Students who choose the course must not only participate in the entire course, but also complete about 15 days of field investigation work. _x000D_

Name: The Nineteenth-Century American Novel
Introduction: This course is aimed at senior undergraduate students majoring in English. Through reading and discussing classic American novels in the nineteenth century, they can grasp the tradition of American novels and the basic characteristics and spirit of American literature. Through literary works, they can understand the historical conditions of American society in the nineteenth century, the literary representation of major historical events, and the changes and development of American intellectual history in the nineteenth century. At the same time, students’ professional English reading, writing and expression skills can be further improved through careful reading of original literary classics.

Name: The Chinese Economy
Prerequisite: Economics principles (or primary microeconomics, primary macroeconomics)
Introduction: The main purpose of this course is to introduce students to China's economic reform and development process since 1978. The course will start with a discussion of China's economic history, especially the economic system before reform and the problems faced, and then discuss agriculture, industrialization, urbanization, international trade, labor market and income distribution, financial system and macroeconomic policies. Finally, we will discuss the achievements of China's economic reform, including growth and structural changes, as well as the new challenges it faces, and conclude this course by discussing whether China can overcome the middle-income trap.

Name: African Culture and Society
Introduction: This course uses vibrant cultural texts and art forms as a door to understanding African societies and Africans. Focus on Africa and China-Africa exchanges from a nuanced and more human perspective. The course will lead students to participate in African-related cultural practice activities, such as movies, modern art workshops, etc., and listen to African stories from diplomats and practitioners who have experienced Africa. The course aims to break the stereotypes of Africa created by mass media, expand students' international cultural horizons, and cultivate cultural criticism skills while enhancing knowledge of Asian and African cultures. _x000D_

Name: General Persian (I)
Introduction: The teaching content of this course includes Persian pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, dialogue, etc. By training students' listening, speaking, reading and writing skills, students will be able to read Persian materials with the help of dictionaries and have the ability to conduct simple daily conversations.

Name: General Filipino (I)
Introduction: Public Filipino is a public foreign language course in schools starting from scratch and is completed in two semesters. The purpose of this course is mainly to cultivate students' basic language skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing in elementary Filipino through the study of basic Filipino. The course is divided into intensive reading and extensive reading, learning original Filipino texts, and explaining basic Filipino grammar and syntax based on these texts related to Philippine folk culture, social life and other topics. It is also supplemented with special exercises in listening and conversation, and audio and video recordings are selected that suit students' abilities.

Name: Culture and Translation Criticism
Introduction:
The main content of the course consists of two parts. As the basis of this course, it first provides an overview and analysis of the translation history and traditions of China and the West, including representative translation achievements and characteristics in different historical periods as well as translators with outstanding achievements. It also introduces the development and evolution of the emerging discipline of translation studies in the past forty years, focusing on introducing and interpreting the role and significance of cultural studies in the development and practice of modern and contemporary translation theory research. _x000D_
On this basis, it introduces Chinese and Western translation criticism, including the history of its development and its critical characteristics in different historical periods. It focuses on explaining the connotation, basic techniques and application scope of modern and contemporary translation criticism, as well as the status and role of translation criticism in the overall disciplinary structure of translation studies. _x000D_
Discussing translation criticism from the perspective of cultural studies aims to clarify that translation criticism, like translation theory and practice, does not occur in a vacuum, but is related to specific historical and cultural contexts at various levels and forms. In the current context of increasing globalization at the economic and other social levels, the above connections have become more obvious and important. Therefore, the teaching and research of translation criticism related to it also have corresponding important value and significance. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in Canadian Fiction
Introduction: This course will focus on over a dozen Canadian novelists and their outstanding works, such as Margaret Laurence, Margaret Atwood, Roberts Davis, Michael Ondaatjie and others, as well as on important events in the life history of other Canadian writers, enabling students to familiarize themselves with the history of Canadian history, culture and literature and to gain an initial knowledge of the development and genre of Canadian literature.

Name: Western Classical Literature and Society
Introduction: This course is a literature course for lower-level undergraduate students in English language and literature. It will select important works from Homer to about the first century AD, including epics, tragedies, historical works, essays, and novels. Text reading and critical analysis are combined in the lectures.

Name: Group Counseling on Character Strengths for College Students
Introduction:
Positive psychology is a new trend of thought that emerged in Western psychology at the end of the 20th century. Its essential characteristic is that it is a science dedicated to studying the vitality and virtues of ordinary people. It advocates studying human character strengths, fully tapping the inherent potential constructive power of people, promoting the development of individuals and society, and moving humans towards happiness. Harvard University's famous happiness course is based on positive psychology. This course has the largest number of elective students at Harvard and became Harvard's most popular course in 2006. The core content of this course is to teach students how to treat life positively in order to achieve happiness. _x000D_
Positive psychologists have summarized 24 human character strengths and believe that these qualities are important factors that bring people happiness. These character strengths include creativity, gratitude, optimism, hope, curiosity, insight, courage, persistence, love, kindness, vitality, social IQ, teamwork, forgiveness, self-discipline, humor, etc. One of the ways to obtain happiness is to cultivate these positive personality qualities. This course is a general happiness course suitable for Peking University students designed based on the above viewpoints. _x000D_
Group counseling is one of the practical methods of social work. This course draws on relevant theories such as group counseling, positive psychology, and college student development. It will guide students to understand and cultivate positive personality qualities through group training and counseling, and focus on exploring and strengthening their own character strengths; allowing students to learn in a warm group atmosphere and In experiential activities, group members face and discuss common issues such as academic procrastination, self-worth, intimacy, career development, meaning of life, and stress response among college students. They learn to solve real-life problems by exploring and utilizing their own potential and resources, and achieve an improvement in happiness and personal growth. _x000D_
This course has a total of 16 classes, each class is 2 hours long. The course content includes classroom teaching and after-class practice. Since this course will be taught in the form of group tutoring, the course capacity is 30 people. _x000D_

With the research on "education and happiness" as the core, we explore the nature and source of happiness, how education can enhance happiness, and how to form the experience of happiness education. First, the cognitive aspect: (1) Let students think about what a happy life is; understand the diverse values ​​of a happy life. (2) Think about how to achieve a happy life; (3) Understand the role of education in a happy life and reflect on today’s education. Second, the practice of integrating knowledge and action. Strive to integrate knowledge and action, practice and experience the way of happiness on the basis of learning relevant ideas, enhance students' ability to experience happiness and obtain happiness, and master the methods to form a happy life. Third, understand and reflect on the research and policy effects on happiness in the field of education. _x000D_

Name: Education and Artificial Intelligence
Introduction: Recently, major breakthroughs in artificial intelligence, represented by major events such as AlphaGo's victory over the Go world champion, have three meanings for education. First of all, this is a victory for education. Secondly, it will have a positive promotion effect on education and teaching and improve the output and input ratio of teaching. Thirdly, it will challenge the existing education system and teachers’ work. This course will comprehensively introduce the complex relationship between education, educational technology and artificial intelligence from the perspectives of pedagogy, educational technology, educational economics, artificial intelligence, philosophy of technology, etc., analyze application cases of artificial intelligence in the field of education, and explore the possibility of applying cutting-edge technologies in the field of education.

Name: Chinese and Western Rhetorical Traditions
Introduction:
By studying the foundational works and major research works of the Chinese and Western rhetorical traditions, this course will understand and master the basic concepts of the Chinese and Western rhetorical traditions, analyze and compare some similarities and differences from the perspective of comparative rhetoric, understand the important research trends of Chinese and Western comparative rhetoric, and allow students to have a deeper understanding of the important influence of the rhetorical tradition in cross-cultural communication behaviors, such as second language writing, translation, and oral communication. _x000D_
The main materials for study include the Chinese-English bilingual version of "The Analects", Aristotle's "Rhetoric" (English translation), relevant chapters in the two books The Tao of Rhetoric and Comparative Rhetoric, and relevant academic articles by British scholar Andy Kirkpatrick. Teachers will guide students to explore the values, worldviews, and relevant philosophical concepts that are important in the art of applied language reflected in these materials. Through careful study and analysis of first-hand materials and related academic results, students will gain a deep understanding of the similarities and differences between Chinese and Western rhetorical traditions, and through case analysis, they will understand and master the practice of the art of applied language under these rhetorical traditions. _x000D_

Name: Design and Implementation of Online Education
Introduction:
The rapid development of information technology is affecting all aspects of today's society, and has also created a new form of education that combines Internet technology with the field of education - online education. At present, the widespread development of online education is causing changes in the education ecology. Online education is also one of the important ways to "build a lifelong learning system that serves the whole people" mentioned in the "China Education Modernization 2035" issued by the State Council. _x000D_
This course is designed to allow students to understand the concepts, theoretical foundations, and practical context of the field of online education. This course will first sort out the development context and main theoretical foundations of this field, which include industrialization theory, two-way interaction theory, and connectivism theory. Secondly, students will learn to use traditional Internet and mobile Internet platforms and tools to design online education course resources and teacher-student interactive activities.

Name: Selected Works of British and American Women Writers
Introduction: This course will introduce students to British and American women writers from the 19th to 20th centuries, including poetry and novels. The purpose of the course is to guide students in interpreting the works of female writers from the perspectives of history and literary criticism. Most of the female works involved are classic writers, such as Mary Shelley, George Eliot, Virginia Woolf, Kate Chopin, Toni Morrison, etc. Students are required to read all course plan chapters, learn to understand, analyze, and evaluate literary texts, submit reading reports, actively participate in class discussions, and write critical articles.

Name: Basic Russian (I)
Introduction: Basic Russian (1) is the most important professional compulsory course in the basic learning stage for Russian major students. It is taught to first-year Russian undergraduate students with a zero starting point. This course is divided into two parts: the first is an introductory course, the main task is to teach the pronunciation, intonation and writing of Russian, give a preliminary introduction to grammar, open a window for Russian learning, and lay a solid foundation for transition from entry to more in-depth oral and written training. There are 8 introductory lessons in total. Each lesson includes pronunciation, intonation, grammar, language training, and writing, as well as polite terms and cultural conditions, so that students can become interested in Russian communication and Russian culture from the beginning of their studies. The second is the basic course. The main task is to learn the changes in word forms, expand the vocabulary, and lay a solid foundation for the next step of learning dialogues and texts according to the theme and conducting oral and written training. There are 10 basic lessons in total, and each lesson consists of three parts: pronunciation, grammar, and language training.

Name: Russian National Conditions (Part 1)
Introduction: This course uses the integration of images, videos and texts to sort out the history of Russia in detail, introduce Russian geography and knowledge related to Russian cultural traditions, social status, customs and habits, etc., and strives to show a dynamic picture of the development and changes of the Russian nation over the millennium. Due to the historical and geographical connections between the Empire, the Soviet Union, and Russia (the CIS countries), part of the content also involves CIS countries other than Russia.

Name: Russian Phonetics
Introduction:
As an auxiliary course for Basic Russian (1), this course mainly focuses on training students’ Russian pronunciation and intonation, especially the typical mistakes that Chinese students tend to make when learning Russian, correcting and practicing repeatedly, laying a solid foundation for the transition from the introductory stage of pronunciation to more in-depth oral and written language training. _x000D_
The pronunciation part introduces Russian phonetic phenomena such as vowels, voiceless and voiceless consonants, weakened vowels, alternation of voiced and voiceless consonants, soft and hard consonants, continuous reading, and stress, and summarizes the key to correct pronunciation. _x000D_
The intonation part focuses on explaining the five tones of Russian, and combines certain exercises to help students understand the important role of tones in Russian language communication. _x000D_
On the basis of completing the teaching content of "College Russian (1)", some audio materials from the original Russian textbook "Traveling in Russia" are selected as supplements for classroom exercises, and the original Russian listening materials ? Русский язык для англоговорящих? are used as extracurricular supplementary homework. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to General Linguistics
Prerequisite: No specific requirements, but it would be preferable to have some knowledge of the structure of Chinese and a foreign language.
Introduction: This introductory course in linguistics provides a general exposition on the history of linguistics research, the functions of language, language and thinking, the symbolism of language, the structural system of language (speech, vocabulary, grammar), semantics, pragmatics, language development, language types, etc., so that students can have a systematic understanding of the nature of linguistics and language.

Name: Russian Reading: Cultural Background Knowledge (I)
Introduction: This course aims to use rich and colorful language and cultural materials to improve reading and comprehension skills on the premise of understanding Russian cultural background knowledge, consolidate and deepen the systematic knowledge of Russian vocabulary, grammar and rhetoric that have been mastered, and then improve students' language skills. While reading, students can better understand Russia, further expand their knowledge of traditional Russian culture and contemporary national conditions, understand all aspects of its social life, and achieve the purpose of improving the knowledge structure, expanding knowledge, and broadening their horizons. _x000D_

Name: Basic Russian (II)
Introduction:
Basic Russian (2) is the most important professional required course for Russian major students in the basic learning stage, _x000D_
The vocabulary, pronunciation, and language training part consists of dialogue and text parts. Using daily life and school life as themes, the most commonly used words and sentence patterns are taught to cultivate listening, speaking, reading and writing skills. _x000D_
The grammar items are based on the first volume, and the lexical and syntactic contents are intertwined and taught. The lexical part includes the basic meanings of the corresponding forms of verb bodies, the degrees of adjectives and adverbs, motion verbs, verb imperatives and presumptive forms, the declensions and usage of numerals and demonstrative pronouns, and the syntactic part includes the components of sentences, types of simple sentences, and basic knowledge of explanatory clauses, attributive clauses, time clauses and other items. _x000D_

Due to the historical and geographical connections between the Empire, the Soviet Union, and Russia (the CIS countries), part of the content also involves CIS countries other than Russia.

Introduction: Through literature reading and course study, students will systematically master the basic common sense of literary research, understand the development profile of Chinese and foreign literature as well as the main trends and schools, become familiar with major theoretical discussions and critical practices, and try to engage in research work under the guidance of teachers, laying the foundation for future language and literature study.

Classes are taught using original Russian teaching films and audio-visual materials, from simple to advanced, step by step, and entertaining. Improve students' Russian pronunciation, develop listening skills, and conduct basic oral training. _x000D_

Prerequisite:
1. Basic Russian: this is the first and second semesters of the first year of the undergraduate course, which focuses on speech learning and day-to-day thematic sessions with initial knowledge of some commonly used terminology and grammar.
Reading in Russian - knowledge of cultural background (I and II): This is a course offered in the second semester of the first year of undergraduate studies, which expands the vocabulary, the knowledge of the Russian cultural background and improves the skills of language use, based on the acquired vocabulary and basic grammar knowledge of the subject " Basic Russian " .
Introduction:
The "Russian Society and Culture Lecture Series" is mainly based on the existing teaching staff of the Russian Department. Each teacher will give full play to their respective research expertise and provide a series of lectures based on the theme of the course. The content covers Russian history, religion, art, folk customs, national character, Russian characteristics, idioms and ways of thinking, etc. This is an academic course designed to expand knowledge, develop research skills and independent thinking skills. _x000D_

On this basis, students can learn more in-depth Russian grammar in the second grade. Prerequisite courses include basic Russian, reading, listening and speaking classes, etc.
Introduction:
Grammar is the rules of language itself. Russian grammar is rigorous and logical and relatively complex compared to other languages. Therefore, it is necessary to recognize _x000D_ in the teaching process

After all, language is for speaking, and grammar is for practicing language. Therefore, after completing the explanations and exercises in the textbook, this course requires self-compiled exercises to consolidate classroom knowledge and achieve proficient application. In short, this course pays more attention to the practicality of grammar. The theoretical explanation is concise and comprehensive and has strong practicality. Through a large number of example sentences, students can have a more vivid understanding of the explanation content and it is easy to master. _x000D_

Name: History of Russian Literature (I)
Introduction:
Aims of teaching: To increase students ' knowledge of Russian literature and cultural horizons by providing them with a deeper understanding and understanding of the development of ancient and nineteenth-century Russian literature through presentations and lectures by teachers.
Teaching content: Russian ancient literature, 18th century literature, with emphasis on 19th century literature, including leading writers such as Pushkin, Lemontov, Gogori, Tugenev, Gonzalov, Ostrovsky, Nekrasov, Shedlin, Tolstoy, Dostoyevsky, Chekhov, and presentations of key works.

Reading in Russian - knowledge of the cultural background (I): This is a course offered in the second semester of the first year of undergraduate studies, which expands the vocabulary, knowledge of the Russian cultural background and improves linguistic skills on the basis of the terminology and basic grammatical knowledge acquired in the course " Basic Russian " .
Introduction:
"Russian Reading - Cultural Background Knowledge" (2) is mainly used in conjunction with the study of the "Basic Russian" course. "Basic Russian" is "intensive reading", which focuses on enabling students to have a solid grasp of the meanings and usages of common vocabulary as well as grammatical knowledge. However, the improvement and leap in language proficiency is inseparable from the amount of reading. Only with a large amount of reading can students' language sense and language application ability be more effectively cultivated. In addition, it is not enough to simply master language knowledge without understanding the language target country. The corpus used in this course involves Russian history, religion, national character, customs, Russian people's way of thinking, etc. This knowledge is of great significance for enriching students' knowledge reserves and improving their learning interest and quality level. _x000D_

Introduction: Basic Russian (IV) is the most important professional compulsory course for Russian language major students in the basic learning stage. It plays an important role in connecting the previous and the next in the entire teaching process. Its teaching focus shifts from completing situational communication tasks around daily life topics and teaching basic language knowledge to gradually transitioning to using social life topics as materials to develop coherent language and discourse communicative abilities. The teaching content covers many valuable social issues such as society, culture, history, humanities and environment. It not only covers topics that contemporary young people are concerned about, such as emotions, friendship, Internet and youth education issues, but also takes into account topics that young people should be concerned about, such as responsibility, environment, morality, culture, etc. In this course, more emphasis is placed on the close integration of language knowledge, skill training and the cultivation of students' creative thinking.

This course includes three components: watching videos, listening to recordings and speaking training.     In order to achieve this, attention needs to be paid to corrections at different levels: pronunciation (especially the Р, Ч, Щ, Л, Н sounds that are prone to errors), stress and weakening, intonation (too rigid or too loose and free), rhythm (the key points that must be highlighted and a relatively stable rhythm). _x000D_

Name: Russian Faith and Culture (Part 2)
Prerequisite: The Russian Faith and Culture is taught mainly in Chinese and mainly in the basics of several major Russian religious beliefs, with the aim of popularizing Russian culture, without the need for a first course.
Introduction:
Russia is a country with a strong religious heritage, especially the Orthodox Church, which plays a pivotal role in all aspects of Russian social life. In 988 AD, Russia accepted Orthodox Christianity from Byzantium. Since then, Orthodox Christianity has taken root in Russia and formed an indispensable part of Russian culture. It has left a deep imprint on the daily life, literature, art, and thought of Russians. For students studying Russian language and literature, if they want to have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of Russia, understand the character traits of Russian people, interpret Russian literature and art, analyze the historical changes of Russia, and see into the soul of Russia, it is difficult to avoid the important lesson of Orthodox Christian culture. The course "Russian Faith and Culture" mainly teaches Russian Orthodox culture, with a brief introduction to Russian polytheism, Buddhism, Islam, and shamanism culture. It aims to teach students the most basic content of Russian faith and culture, such as Russia's long-standing church architecture, saint legends, icon culture, religious festivals and music, etc., to help students understand the geographical, social, and historical aspects of Russia while also understanding a spiritual Russia. _x000D_
"Russian Faith and Culture" is taught in two semesters. The first semester is mainly about teaching basic knowledge of Russian faith and culture, so that students can have a preliminary understanding of this issue. The main contents include: Russian polytheistic culture, the 13 major festivals of the Orthodox Church, the four major Lent seasons, famous holy places and churches, icon art and Icon painters, etc.; the second semester focuses on theoretical and in-depth content to enable students to better understand Russian beliefs and culture. The main content includes Russian Orthodox saint culture, church music, prayer and confession, the influence of Orthodox Christianity on Russian literature, old rites, Buddhist culture, Islamic culture and emerging religions, etc.

Name: Functional Grammar of Russian
Introduction:
As a linguistic phenomenon, grammar has aspects of form and structure, as well as aspects of content, meaning, and function. Therefore, a comprehensive grammatical system can only be established through two descriptions: "from form to meaning" and "from meaning to form". _x000D_
If people's speech activities are divided into two processes: feeling and expression, then the process of feeling is to obtain the expressed meaning from the language form, and the process of expression is to express a certain meaning through appropriate language form. Therefore, formal grammar and functional grammar are interrelated and complementary. The task of functional grammar is to focus on deepening and expanding grammatical knowledge from meaning to expression form around the five centers of subject, object, indeterminacy, modality and relationship on the basis of students learning formal grammar, thereby improving students' verbal expression ability at a higher level. _x000D_

Introduction:
"Introduction to German Linguistics" is an elective course for undergraduates majoring in German in the School of Foreign Languages. It is taught to second-year undergraduates and above majoring in German and German history. This course takes the origin and development of language as the starting point, and the German learning sequence of German learners as the main clue. It uses the framework and way of thinking of linguistics to discuss and elaborate on difficult issues in German learning from the perspectives of basic concepts of linguistics, German history, German phonetics, German grammar and German semantics, while reviewing and consolidating the German language. The classroom discussions in this course mainly use German as the source of examples. At the same time, English, a compulsory second foreign language for undergraduates of Germanic languages, will be used as the second source of examples, mixed with a few examples from contemporary languages ​​such as Dutch and French, and ancient languages ​​such as Old High German and Old English (all including translation). It combines the academic and practical aspects of linguistics and absorbs the latest research results in the academic world. This course achieves the purpose of reviewing the German language, popularizing basic concepts of linguistics, and stimulating students' interest in and thinking about linguistics. _x000D_
This course will use classroom lectures as the main teaching method, supplemented by communication methods such as lectures, class discussions, and student reports. It strives to enable students to have a preliminary understanding of German linguistics while reviewing German grammar and improving their German proficiency. It will deepen students' understanding of German in terms of German history, dialects, semantics, etc., enrich students' knowledge structure, and while cultivating literary literacy, expand the theoretical horizons of linguistics, improve academic literacy, and promote students' all-round development in language.

Introduction: Translation (Chinese-French translation) is a language training practice course, which aims to improve students' ability to actually apply the French knowledge they have learned, master the basic rules and main features of translation between two languages, and cultivate students' ability to independently engage in translation work.

Name: History of French Literature with Selected Readings (Part 1)
Introduction: "French Literary History and Selected Readings" focuses on the history of French literature from the Middle Ages to the first half of the 19th century, and also guides students in reading classic texts. The course selects the most important writers and schools since the Middle Ages, introduces their leading ideas and artistic principles, and includes literary readings. This course is mainly taught in French and is accompanied by detailed courseware to facilitate students' understanding.

Name: Selected Readings from French Newspapers and Periodicals (II)
Introduction: This course aims to expose students to various news French materials and lively language styles through reading French newspapers and magazines, to understand French social politics, economy, culture and other aspects, and to pay attention to major news events in France, China and the world in a dynamic way. Through oral reports, written assignments, classroom discussions and questions and other forms, it will improve students' French expression ability and cultivate students' ability to obtain information and think independently through French.

Name: Intensive French Reading (VII)
Introduction: This course starts with a lot of reading, and implements the principles of combining student self-study with teacher guidance, and paying equal attention to understanding and expression, in order to broaden students' language horizons and knowledge, cultivate comprehensive French language skills, enhance their thinking ability and critical awareness, and improve their appreciation level.

Name: French Audiovisual and Speaking (VII)
Introduction: This course is a comprehensive French listening and speaking training course. It does not have fixed teaching materials. It mainly uses original French audio-visual materials, such as French Television 5 (TV5), Radio France Internationale (RFI), audio and video materials of various themes on the Internet, movies and TV programs, etc.

The translation materials are mainly excerpts of modern and contemporary Chinese literary works that have been translated into French, a small number of classic literary classics, a small number of news reports and other application-oriented articles. The translation materials focus on distinctive passages in terms of vocabulary, syntax, and style. Through explanations, teachers guide students to master basic translation principles and techniques on the basis of respecting language and cultural differences, so as to convey the cultural information and stylistic features of the original text in a clear translation.

Name: French Interpretation (Part 1)
Prerequisite: • Quest in French, general in French, history of France, general in France.
Introduction: This course is designed to provide practical teaching to students who already have a certain ability to use French vocabulary and grammar. It focuses on oral expression skills, familiarizes them with some scenarios encountered in oral translation, faces possible difficulties, and understands as much as possible the context of language use, so as to initially achieve the ability to cope with basic translation needs. After receiving basic vocabulary and grammar education, students need to have certain practical application abilities before they can start working or continue their studies. This class requires students to gradually get rid of their dependence on books, start to use language independently, and feel the texture of language and the use of language in different cultural contexts.

Introduction:
This course teaches the main genres, writers and important interpretations that emerged in the development of French literature from the mid-to-late 19th century to the 1950s, including realist novels, symbolist poetry, surrealism, stream of consciousness, existentialism, new novels, absurd dramas and other literary phenomena. _x000D_

Name: French Children's Literature
Introduction:
With the modernization of the view of children, children are no longer regarded by society as reserves or accessories of adults, but have become independent human individuals in the true sense. In this context, children's literature has gradually been regarded as an independent literary category. It not only has its own literary norms, but has also become an object of academic research. As one of the earliest countries where children's literature was born, French children's literature has shown a rich variety of creations in recent years, and has also made many remarkable achievements in research. _x000D_
In view of this, I hope to offer a "French Children's Literature" course for second-year undergraduate students majoring in French language and literature. The main teaching purposes are as follows: 1) To improve students' literary knowledge reserve, so that the listeners can accumulate theoretical and historical knowledge about children's literature and French children's literature, and to have basic children's literature text analysis skills; 2) By appreciating classic passages of children's literature works of various periods, further cultivate students' French language ability and enhance their literary literacy; 3) To allow the listeners to easily understand the reception of French children's literature in my country, and to explore the impact of French children's literature creation on the theory and practice of children's literature in my country. _x000D_
In order to achieve the above purpose, this course will adopt a combination of course explanation and text reading, so that students can have a comprehensive and three-dimensional understanding of French children's literature and its reception in China. The teaching content mainly includes the following modules:_x000D_
1. Common sense of children’s literature theory_x000D_
2. The historical evolution of French children’s literature_x000D_
3. Main styles and representative works of French children’s literature_x000D_
4. Overview of the translation and introduction of French children’s literature in China_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Modern European and American History Exercises
Introduction:
This course is a deepening and practice course for the basic course of modern and contemporary world history. It is neither a study course that teaches basic knowledge nor a research course that explores and solves new problems, but a research preparation course that strengthens students' original innovation awareness. The purpose of setting up the course is to prepare students for independent research and writing academic papers. The course covers important historical topics such as the rise of modern Europe, the British Revolution, the Enlightenment, American Independence, the French Revolution, the Industrial Revolution, World War I, the October Revolution, fascism, the Cold War, and European integration. We adopt a lively and lively practice class method, with teacher guidance as the supplement and student practice as the main focus. The course is as close to the actual requirements of scientific research as possible, and trains students' ability to master other people's research results, accurately ask questions, and analyze original materials. This course focuses on teaching historical research methods, and students from all majors, including European and American modern history, are welcome to choose the course. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Readings in Modern Chinese Documents
Introduction: This course is an elective course for undergraduates in the Department of History. It focuses on several important documents in modern China. Through a combination of teaching, reading and discussion, it aims to help students understand the catalog, types and properties of modern documents, train students in the preliminary ability to identify and use Qing palace archives, diary manuscripts and handwriting, guide students to discover problems from studying documents, and then write academic notes and essays to lay the foundation for further academic research.

Name: General Thai (I)
Introduction: This course mainly teaches language knowledge about Thai pronunciation, basic vocabulary and grammar. Teaching is mainly in the form of classroom explanations and exercises. After completing a cycle of study, students are required to be able to master the pronunciation essentials of Thai, master certain vocabulary and basic grammatical rules, conduct simple daily conversations in Thai, and access relevant historical, political and other information in Thai, laying the foundation for further learning.

Name: Intensive French Reading (V)
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to continue to expand students' French language knowledge after the basic stage teaching, enhance the comprehensive use of language skills, and improve the ability and accuracy of coherent expression in oral and written writing. Implement the principle of teaching more and practicing more. Appropriately teach basic knowledge of French style and rhetoric on the basis of reviewing and consolidating systematic grammar knowledge. While deepening basic vocabulary teaching, attention should be paid to expanding vocabulary and cultivating students' ability to analyze word meanings. Through detailed explanation of the text, the purpose of enriching language expression methods is achieved, and at the same time, students are guided to read the original works of French literary works, step by step, to expand students' language and literary horizons.

Name: French Audiovisual and Speaking (V)
Introduction: This course is a comprehensive listening and speaking training course, with special emphasis on listening training. It mainly uses original listening materials, such as radio concise news, report recordings, and movies, from easy to difficult, step by step. The training focuses on overall understanding and guides students to grasp the general idea.

Introduction: The course is divided into seven sections: narrative articles, official writings, narratives, essays, summaries, reports, and print. Help students to use French for writing with precision.

Name: Spanish Phonetics
Introduction: "Spanish Phonetics" starts from the theory of phonology and compares the phoneme system of Mandarin Chinese, local dialects and English. It explains the Spanish pronunciation system in detail for lower grade students, and helps students accurately and proficiently master standard Spanish pronunciation through a large number of pronunciation and reading practices.

Name: Introduction to Spanish History and Culture
Introduction: "Introduction to Spanish History and Culture" is a basic course for Spanish majors. It is also an intellectual course in the direction of world history for students majoring in "Foreign Languages ​​and Foreign History". Together with "Introduction to Latin American History and Culture" they form the basis of the overall knowledge system of Spanish world history and culture. According to the relevant provisions of the "Teaching Syllabus for the Basic Stage of Spanish Majors in Colleges and Universities" and the "Teaching Syllabus for the Senior Years of Spanish Majors in Colleges and Universities", this course takes history and culture as the entry point to enable students to have a relatively in-depth understanding of the overview and characteristics of Spanish history, culture, politics, society, military, and economy, establish a preliminary understanding of Spain and even the entire Spanish-speaking world, and reserve knowledge in the field of history and culture for the study of other courses. This course will sort out the clues of Spanish historical development, enable students to understand the ins and outs of major historical events, and guide students to think about their various impacts on today's Spanish society. At the same time, starting from representative works of Spanish literature, art, architecture, drama, and film, students will be guided to understand the development and characteristics of Spanish culture, and explore the cultural identity and attributes of Spain in the context of Western civilization. This course hopes that by learning Spanish history and cultural knowledge, it can not only stimulate students' interest and enthusiasm in learning Spanish, but also expand students' knowledge, enrich their knowledge structure, promote their formation of correct historical and cultural concepts, cultivate students' critical thinking spirit, develop independent thinking habits, develop research capabilities, and gradually grow into conscious and independent cross-cultural actors.

Name: Intensive Spanish Reading (I)
Introduction: This course aims to enable students to master Spanish pronunciation, pronunciation, writing rules, basic Spanish grammar and vocabulary, have preliminary Spanish listening, speaking, reading and writing abilities, understand the language characteristics of Spanish and apply them in practice, cultivate students' preliminary ability to communicate in Spanish, and have a deeper understanding of the culture and national conditions of Spanish-speaking countries. _x000D_

Name: Spanish Audiovisual (I)
Introduction: "Spanish Audio-Visual" (1) is a professional basic course for the first semester of the Spanish major. It complements the intensive reading class and the oral class. It first teaches students the basic pronunciation rules and methods of Spanish and cultivates their accurate sound discrimination ability, and then teaches students some basic listening skills to cultivate their listening comprehension ability. By listening to real-life conversations and teaching basic grammar and oral expression, we help students lay a solid foundation in language so that they can communicate with others in simple and practical ways on some daily life topics.

Name: Introduction to Latin American History and Culture
Prerequisite:
