Introduction: "Introduction to Latin American History and Culture" is a basic course for first-year undergraduate students majoring in Spanish and students minoring in Spanish. From a historical and cultural perspective, it introduces and analyzes major phenomena and issues in the history, politics, economy, culture, and society of Latin America. It provides a more comprehensive background knowledge for the study of other professional courses and future in-depth research, so that foreign language learning can be integrated into vivid historical and cultural situations.

Name: Intensive Spanish Reading (II)
Introduction: This course is designed to enable students to master Spanish pronunciation, basic grammar, and vocabulary, and to develop students' ability to communicate in Spanish and the basic skills of listening, speaking, reading, and writing in Spanish. Through the text, students learn common sentence patterns and grammar in Spanish, understand the language characteristics of Spanish, and apply them in practice, and have a deeper understanding of the culture and national conditions of Spanish-speaking countries. _x000D_

Name: Intensive Spanish Reading (III)
Introduction:
This course is a professional basic course for Spanish undergraduate students in their second year (first year). The purpose is to continue to train students’ comprehensive listening, speaking, reading and writing skills, consolidate their grammatical knowledge, and improve their practical language application abilities. At the same time, through text study, they can further understand the culture, history, literature, etc. of Spanish-speaking countries. _x000D_
This course uses the third volume of "Modern Spanish" as the teaching material, supplemented by foreign language teaching materials. It requires students to memorize and learn to use a large number of vocabulary; master the basic structure of various sentences; accurately understand language materials, master the main content, and conduct questions and answers, retell and make simple comments on related content. Able to conduct simple discussions around a certain topic. _x000D_
    Adopt a teaching method that combines classroom lectures with after-class homework and classroom discussions. _x000D_

Name: Spanish Audiovisual (II)
Introduction: "Spanish Audiovisual" (2) is a professional basic course in the second semester of the first-year Spanish major. It aims to improve students' listening level through audio and video materials and strengthen students' practical language communication skills. After one semester of study, students are expected to reach the A2 level stipulated in the EU Common Framework of Reference for Languages.

Name: Spanish Conversation (III)
Introduction:
Spanish spoken (iii) is a specialized course for the first semester. The course focuses primarily on the practical application of Spanish, and its content is set up in the daily life scene of the Spanish-speaking countries. From this semester onwards, the content of cultural backgrounds, such as economics, politics, religion, philosophy, literature and art, will gradually be expanded.

It should be noted that, in everyday life, the environment is often noisy and interlocutors do not usually take into account the fact that the other person is a foreigner, slowing down or choosing simple and understandable terms. So we need to teach students basic cultural backgrounds and commonly spoken languages. Knowledge of the cultural background can help students quickly understand the intentions of national interlocutors in their mother tongue, while knowledge of language, such as customary language, folklore, slanges, insulting language, cornering, word games, comparing phrases, songs, etc., can make students more motivated and interested.

The active participation of students in the classroom is very important. Teachers should encourage and direct students to participate in social work and practice in the classroom. There are numerous forms of communication and oral exercises (for more details, see “Teaching methods”) in which teachers can choose to practice according to the actual situation in the classroom.

Name: Practical Spanish Writing
Introduction: The "Spanish Practical Literature" course is a basic course for Spanish language and literature majors. It is taught based on the principles of practicality, prominence of abilities, and systematic design training. The course is based on theoretical introduction and strengthens practicality, using letters (the writing formats of personal letters, transactional letters, and business letters, common terms for various types of letters such as invitations, congratulations, condolences, thanks, requests, blames, apologies, etc.), notices, memorandums, and certificates. Based on the practical writings that students often use in their daily work and life, such as certified documents (certificates, applications, letters of attorney, certificates, notarial deeds), instructions, advertisements, invitations, contracts, meeting minutes, thesis writing, etc., the Spanish practical writing skills are explained in detail. The teaching tasks of this course are: to enable students to systematically master the practical uses of commonly used application articles and their writing essentials, to acquire the article writing skills and article analysis and processing abilities necessary for advanced application talents, to improve their actual writing skills to a certain extent to adapt to current and future writing needs in work, study, and scientific research, to provide necessary guarantees for the improvement of their overall work level, and to make sufficient knowledge preparations for the upcoming graduation thesis writing.

Name: Spanish Reading
Introduction: The Spanish reading class aims to help students broaden their learning horizons, enrich their reading content, improve their reading taste, and cultivate their basic ability and reading habits of critical thinking in Spanish through the reading and appreciation of a large number of Spanish texts. In view of the fact that a large number of selected texts come from Spanish classic literature and historical works, after studying this course, students will have an initial understanding of the charm of the Spanish humanistic world, thereby achieving the dual purpose of improving Spanish language application skills and enhancing cultural critical awareness.

Name: Intensive Spanish Reading (IV)
Introduction:
This course is a professional basic course for second-year Spanish undergraduates (Part 2). The purpose is to further train students in comprehensive and rigorous Spanish language skills, establish a systematic grammar system, and cultivate students' preliminary ability to study the national conditions, culture and literature of Spanish-speaking countries in Spanish. _x000D_
This course uses the fourth volume of "Modern Spanish" as the teaching material, supplemented by foreign language teaching materials. It requires students to further expand their vocabulary and master the structure and usage of various kinds of adverbs; to be able to talk to people from Spanish-speaking countries on general social life topics, to express their thoughts correctly, with basic language appropriateness, and no major grammatical errors; to read general news reports and simple reading materials with the help of reference books; to write short articles based on propositions, with coherent content, clear levels, smooth language, and no major grammatical errors. _x000D_
Adopt a teaching method that combines classroom lectures with after-class homework and classroom discussions. _x000D_

Name: Spanish Audiovisual (III)
Introduction: "Spanish Audiovisual (3)" is a language skills training course for second-year students majoring in Spanish. This course mainly uses "oral and written language" audio-visual materials, supplemented by real Spanish corpus with a speaking speed of about 120-140 words/minute, to provide students with systematic listening skills training, so that students can master the characteristics of normal Spanish speaking speed, be able to basically understand the main content of lectures and interviews on cultural and academic topics, be able to understand the overview of Spanish broadcast news programs for foreigners, initially master listening note-taking skills, reach the European Language Framework B2 level, and successfully pass the National Spanish Professional Level 4 Examination.

Name: Spanish Conversation (IV)
Introduction:
Spoken Spanish (IV) is a professional course in the second semester of sophomore year. This course focuses on the practical application of Spanish, and the course content is set in daily life scenarios in Spanish-speaking countries. Starting from this semester, the content of cultural background will be gradually increased, such as economics, politics, religion, philosophy, literature, art and other fields. _x000D_
    _x000D_
    It should be noted that in daily life, the environment is usually noisy, and the conversational person usually does not consider that the other party is a foreigner and slows down his speech or chooses simple and easy-to-understand words. Therefore, we need to teach students basic cultural background and commonly used spoken language. Cultural background knowledge can help students quickly understand the intentions of native-speaking interlocutors, while language knowledge, such as idioms, colloquialisms, slang, insulting language, tongue twisters, word games, comparative phrases, children's songs, etc., can make students more motivated and interested in learning. _x000D_
    _x000D_
    Active participation of students in class is very important. Teachers should encourage and guide students to participate in classroom communicative tasks and exercises. There are many ways to practice communicative tasks and oral exercises (see "Teaching Methods" for details), and teachers can choose and practice according to the actual situation in the classroom. _x000D_

Name: History of Spanish Literature with Selected Readings (Part 1)
Introduction: Introduce and explain the important literary schools and trends of Spanish literature, classic writers and their representative works from "Jarchas" to the 17th century. It will be explained in stages according to the Middle Ages and the Golden Century (Renaissance and Baroque). It will be combined with the introduction of the specific social and historical background and focus on the careful reading of the original text.

Name: Spanish Grammar
Introduction:
"Spanish Grammar" is a professional basic course for Spanish major students. It aims to consolidate and sort out the grammatical knowledge learned in the first and second grades, summarize common grammatical phenomena, and supplement the grammatical knowledge that has not been exposed before, so that students can establish a systematic and clear understanding of Spanish grammar and lay a solid grammatical foundation for the study of senior grades. _x000D_
      The main contents of this course include nouns, adjectives, articles, pronouns, demonstratives and possessive words, infinitives, numerals, verbs, prepositions, adverbs, active sentences, passive sentences and impersonal sentences, noun clauses, relative clauses, comparative sentences and adverb clauses, etc.

Name: Intensive Spanish Reading (VI)
Introduction:
This course is a professional basic course for Spanish undergraduate students in their third year (Part 2). The purpose is to gain a deeper understanding of Spanish grammar through extensive reading, and to generally appreciate and grasp the commonalities and differences in language and thinking between nations. After studying this course, students should systematically master and skillfully use Spanish grammar, understand preliminary knowledge of Spanish style and rhetoric; be proficient in using original dictionaries and master common vocabulary. On the basis of reading general original books, newspapers and literary works, students should be able to read some highly professional materials with the help of reference books. _x000D_
This course uses the fifth volume of "Modern Spanish" as the teaching material, supplemented by foreign language teaching materials. Compared with the prerequisite course, this course reduces the grammar and vocabulary exercises, expands the form of exercises to help understand, inspire thinking, and guide discussions, and supplements an appropriate amount of background knowledge materials based on the text content. It aims to enable students to transition from a simple understanding of the text to expressing independent opinions and insights on the text, and to express them accurately and fluently in Spanish, thereby training students' Spanish thinking and strengthening their ability to analyze and solve problems. _x000D_

Name: History of Latin American Literature with Selected Readings (Part 2)
Prerequisite: History of Latin American Literature with Selected Readings (Part 1)
Introduction:
_x000D_
(1) The development of modernist literature: earth novels and avant-garde poetry. _x000D_
(2) The "explosion" of literature after 1960 and the literature after the "explosion". Focusing on the origin, development, and characteristics of magical realism, it focuses on writers such as Asturias, Carpentier, Rulfo, García Márquez, and Cortázar, as well as classic works such as "One Hundred Years of Solitude"; important writers and poets such as Borges, Neruda, and Paz. _x000D_
(3) Contemporary Latin American literary world; the formation of a new era and a new “classic”_x000D_

Name: Spanish-Chinese Translation (Part 1)
Introduction: The Western Han Dynasty Translation (Part 1) course focuses on explaining how to correctly interpret the original text, accurately segment meaning units, understand the knowledge background of Western culture, and some techniques for translating from Western to Chinese (such as decomposing the structure of the original sentence, adding and subtracting words, translating contraction forms and proper nouns, free translation and literal translation, etc.).

Name: Spanish-Chinese Interpretation (Part 1)
Introduction:
This course is a required professional course for Spanish undergraduate students in their third year (Part 2). The purpose is to enable students to master the basic theoretical knowledge and skills of interpretation, understand the characteristics of interpretation and the necessary qualities of an excellent interpreter, understand the respective characteristics of Chinese and Western languages ​​in the interpretation process through a large number of interpretation exercises, master interpretation skills, and be able to perform general Western-Chinese, Chinese-Western consecutive interpretation, continuous translation and sight translation. _x000D_
    This course uses "Advanced Spanish Interpretation Course" (Chang Shiru) as the main teaching material, supplemented by some audio and video materials. The content covers a wide range of aspects, including politics, economy, diplomacy, culture, art, education, environment and other aspects. Through simulated scenario exercises and practices, students can understand the characteristics of spoken language and the similarities and differences between Western and Han cultures in terms of thinking, customs, and language characteristics, as well as the interpretation strategies and techniques that should be adopted, and cultivate students' basic on-site adaptability; enable students to master the translation methods of commonly used Spanish vocabulary and common sentence patterns; master digital translation skills; cultivate students' good interpreting habits; cultivate students' short-term memory ability and note-taking ability; cultivate students' awareness of cultural communication, etc. _x000D_

Name: Business Spanish
Introduction:
This course is a professional elective course for Spanish undergraduate students in their third year (Part 2). The purpose is to enable students to understand the commonly used vocabulary and sentence patterns of business Spanish and become familiar with oral and written expressions in typical trade situations; to cultivate students' basic skills in using Spanish to engage in foreign economic and trade activities; to master the characteristics and translation methods of business Spanish; to understand the social and business culture of Spanish-speaking countries and to initially cultivate students' business communication skills. _x000D_
This course uses "Spanish Economic and Trade Practical Texts" (Zhao Xuemei, Li Ziying) as the main teaching material, supplemented by foreign language teaching materials. To train students to master Spanish economic and trade terminology on the basis of understanding the basic characteristics of international economic and trade activities. After studying this course, students should be able to understand and translate general business conversation at a normal speed; be able to read business Spanish articles of medium difficulty and understand the author's views and attitudes; be able to use Spanish to introduce company status, conduct business consultation, communicate with customers, etc.; be able to use the language knowledge they have learned to write general business letters and emails in Spanish that comply with international business practices and format specifications, and achieve clear central ideas, reasonable structures, and appropriate language; and be able to translate general business materials. _x000D_

Name: Spanish Audiovisual (V)
Introduction: "Spanish Audiovisual (5)" is a follow-up language practice course for basic listening, and it is also a professional skills course for senior students majoring in Spanish. According to the relevant provisions of the "Teaching Syllabus for Senior Spanish Majors in Colleges and Universities" and the principles and difficulty grading standards of the "Common European Framework of Reference for Languages: Learning, Teaching and Assessment" (Marco común de referencia para las lenguas: aprendizaje, ense?anza y evaluación), the difficulty level of the audio-visual materials selected for this course is C1. It is mainly real audio-visual materials at normal Spanish speaking speed, supplemented by a small amount of transitional "readable written language" corpus. "Spanish Audio-Visual (5)" attaches great importance to the systematic training of listening strategies and skills. Through targeted exercises and extended tasks that combine full listening, selective listening and intensive listening, it helps students understand the characteristics of normal Spanish speaking speed, learn to record listening notes, develop coherent memory skills, overcome anxiety, and correctly understand the C1 difficulty level Able to understand the corpus content of Spanish for special purposes (such as tourism, foreign trade, etc.) at a normal speaking speed. Be able to understand real audio-visual materials on social issues in Spanish and original audio materials for academic humanities and social sciences. Basically understand the main content of film and television drama works, and be able to convey, interpret and comment on the corpus in standardized and correct Spanish. On this basis, strengthen the training of listening prediction and logic skills, and cultivate students' ability to understand long-form audio-visual materials on complex, abstract or unfamiliar themes. Even when the structure of the corpus is unclear, the meaning is unclear, or the meaning is obscure, students are required to be able to accurately follow, understand, and summarize the text content. At the same time, they will strengthen their language sensitivity, familiarize themselves with the rules of Spanish language use, acquire background knowledge strategies through learning, and use various knowledge tools such as grammar, syntax, morphology, phonetics, and semantics to accurately capture the contextual categories of corpus texts, explore and understand the implicit meaning of audio-visual materials, cultivate sociolinguistic abilities and pragmatic abilities, and help students grow into conscious and independent cross-cultural practitioners.

Name: History of Latin American Literature with Selected Readings (Part 1)
Introduction:
_x000D_
(1) An overview of the development of ancient Indian literature, focusing on "Popol?", "Oyante", "The Book of Chilambalan" and Aztec Lyrics. _x000D_
(2) Literature of the Conquest and Colonial Period (1492-1810): Introducing classic works such as "Columbus's Voyage Diary", "History of the Conquest of New Spain", "Review of the Inca Royal Family", "Legends of Peru", "Araucana", "First Dream". Among them, Sol Juana is the most difficult part. The original text should be read carefully in conjunction with the introduction of the specific social and historical background. _x000D_
(3) Literature of the Independence Movement and the Early Republic: Focus on the development overview of romantic literature and the rise of realism.

Name: Spanish-Chinese Translation (Part 2)
Introduction: Western Han Translation (Part 2) focuses on how to identify word meanings, pay attention to word selection and collocation, word translation, methods of translating various Spanish complex sentences from Chinese to Chinese, the use and transformation of verb tenses in Chinese to Spanish translation, and the translation of Chinese idioms in the process of translating from Chinese to Western.

Name: Spanish-Chinese Interpretation (Part 2)
Introduction:
The purpose of this course is to provide students with the basic theoretical knowledge and skills of interpretation, the characteristics of interpretation and the necessary qualities of an excellent interpreter, the respective characteristics of the Chinese and Western languages during the interpretation process in a large number of interpretation exercises, the mastering of interpretation skills, the ability to perform general West Hanhan, Hansi alternate interpretation, consecutive translation and visual translation tasks, and an initial understanding of the characteristics and techniques of simultaneous interpretation.
The course is based on the Advanced Spanish Interpretative Curriculum (API), which is supported by selected audio-visual materials. It has a wide range of political, economic, tourist, diplomatic, sports, educational and other aspects, as well as a number of topical topics that have emerged during the year. Introduction: This course is designed to help students sort out the history of film development in Spain and Hispanic America, and understand Spanish film criticism and theory. Name: The Contemporary Arab World
Introduction:
Through classroom lectures and after-class readings, this course guides students to analyze the century-old drastic changes in the Middle East from different dimensions and levels such as politics, economy, culture, society, military, and new media, and to sort out the causes, consequences, scale, scope, and impact of the profound evolution of Arab countries such as Tunisia, Egypt, Libya, Yemen, and Syria, which have successively fallen into turmoil, war, and regime change, as well as their impact on themselves, the regional power structure, and the world, so that students can have an understanding of the contemporary Arab world, especially the recent social upheavals. _x000D_

Introduction: This course follows the concept that language learning is most effective through meaningful communication. It organically combines grammar, vocabulary, and pronunciation learning through practical topics, taking into account language accuracy and fluency. Through extensive practice, students will develop a sense of Arabic language, become familiar with the standard Arabic pronunciation system, master simple Arabic listening skills, be able to conduct simple daily conversations, master common sentence patterns in spoken English, and master core high-frequency vocabulary.

The history of human civilization collides and interacts here. To this day, the Middle East is still one of the major regions that affects the development and change of the world pattern. Name: World Archaeology (Part 2)
Introduction: The primary task of archeology is to complete an empirically based narrative about human history. This narrative transcends the time and space limitations of collective memory and written records, helping us understand how humans as a species create culture; form different lifestyles; establish different social systems; and how the environment/landscape we live in changes and develops accordingly. In addition to early China and its neighbors (Northeast and Southeast Asia), this course provides an overview of the archaeological study of early periods in other regions of the world, providing a long-term historical framework from the origins of humanity, agriculture, and urban civilization, providing a comprehensive and broad introduction to the major patterns of social, cultural, economic, and political change from prehistory to the early state phase. In the first semester, the course begins with human evolution and dispersal; then considers the Holocene transition caused by climate change; the formation of settled societies; the origins of agriculture and Neolithic village society; and reviews various archaeological explanations. The second semester focuses on the rise of cities and the origins of early civilizations/states as a result of the later development of metallurgy, long-distance trade, and social complexity; this semester focuses on the prehistory and early historical politics of Eurasia, empires, and civilizations, as well as their expansion and periodic collapse.

Name: Chinese Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: History of Chinese literature (I), principles of literature, ancient Chinese (I)
Introduction:
Chinese literary theory refers to the theoretical understanding of literature by Chinese people from the pre-Qin Dynasty to modern times. This kind of theoretical cognition is often presented in the practical results of historical literary criticism. In the past, it was usually called "the history of Chinese literary criticism" or "the history of Chinese literary theory criticism." However, this name overemphasized its "historical" characteristics and relatively ignored its theoretical characteristics. This led to some people criticizing Chinese literary theory as "aphasic". In fact, Chinese literary theory should become an important ideological and theoretical resource for the construction of contemporary literary theory, just like Marxist literary theory and Western literary theory. This course intends to (1) connect ancient and modern times, focusing on ancient literary theory, supplemented by modern literary theory, treating modern literary theory as a modern leap of traditional literary theory, integrating ancient literary theory criticism and modern literary theory criticism into a system for cognition, paying attention to the connections and changes between ancient and modern Chinese literary theory, which is more conducive to understanding the characteristics of Chinese literary theory, and thinking about the theoretical significance and contemporary value of Chinese literary theory. (2) Paying attention to the theoretical nature of the course, in the past, the history of Chinese literary criticism was generally interpreted according to the historical dimension, which was similar to a branch of literary history, ignoring the own characteristics and theoretical value of traditional Chinese literary theory. This course aims to recognize and elucidate the theoretical uniqueness of Chinese literary theory as much as possible while respecting the historical nature of literary theory, conduct contemporary analysis and evaluation of traditional literary theory, and explore the contemporary theoretical value of traditional literary theory. (3) Pay attention to the intensive reading of classic texts. Literary theory teaching should not talk about some truths in a general way. It should select some important literary theory chapters in the history of literary theory and lead students to read the text intensively. It starts from clearing the text, connecting literary phenomena, understanding people and the world, interpreting the text, and then improving the theory, analyzing the meaning and judging the value, so as to cultivate students' ability to process text materials independently. _x000D_
This course is planned to focus on topics such as textual theory, literati theory, stylistic theory, literary mind theory, lexicon theory, grammatical theory, literary usage theory, and appreciation theory. Rong's "Poetry", Xiao Tong's "Preface to Selected Works", Tang Dynasty Poetry Style, Yan Yu's "Canglang Poetry Talk", Hu Yinglin's "Poetry Sou", Jin Shengtan's comments on "Water Margin", "The Romance of the West Chamber", Yuan Mei's "Suiyuan Poetry Talk", Wang Guowei's "Human Words", "Commentary on Dream of Red Mansions", "Song Dynasty" "A Study of Yuan Opera", Lu Xun's "On the Power of Moro Poetry", Hu Shi's "A Preliminary Discussion on Literary Reform", Chen Duxiu's "On Literary Revolution", Zhou Zuoren's "Literature of Humanity", "Common People's Literature", Mao Zedong's "Speech at the Yan'an Forum on Literature and Art", etc. This course guides students to have a more accurate and in-depth understanding of the basic characteristics, important theoretical concepts, propositions, and categories of Chinese literary theory, helps students construct a knowledge system of literary theory, and cultivates students' literary appreciation ability and literary theory thinking ability.

From the axis of time, Mongolia ' s problems in the twentieth century can be divided into the recent period of Mongolia, the cold war period of Mongolia (modern Mongolia), and the 10 years since the end of the cold war. It is necessary to strengthen the study and research of Mongolia after 1945 in order to develop students as high-end Mongolian researchers, as well as their work skills. This course will be conducted in five stages: 1945 - 1949, 1949 - 1962, 1962 - 1973 - 1973 - 1989, 1989 - 1994, with emphasis on building the capacity of students to rely on their linguistic advantages, analyse the history of the archives, raise questions and solve problems as the primary objective of the curriculum.

Name: Economic Growth and Fluctuations: Basic Principles and the Chinese Case
Introduction: This course introduces the basic principles behind economic growth and fluctuations from both long-term and short-term perspectives, allowing students to have a basic understanding of macroeconomics and then use these basic theories to explore China's economic development.

Name: Understanding the Chinese Economy from a Development Perspective
Introduction: Since the reform and opening up, China's economy has experienced rapid growth and has been hailed as the "Chinese Economic Miracle". Part of China's economic growth miracle can be explained by the classic theory of development economics, so there is a large amount of literature on this issue in academic circles. This course is based on the perspective of development economics. It first introduces the research objects and research significance of development economics, then combines representative events and phenomena in China's economic development process to introduce relevant development theories, and guides students to use these theories to understand China's economic development process.

Introduction: This course is an all-English course mainly for international students. Chinese students are also welcome to take it as an elective course. The purpose is to create an exchange environment and dialogue platform for Chinese and foreign students to learn by examining the development, characteristics and problems of China's education from a historical and comparative perspective, and its cultural foundation, and to promote the understanding and understanding of education in different countries and regions among students with different cultural backgrounds. The teaching content is divided into two parts: literary anthology and ancient Chinese knowledge, with the anthology as the main part. The anthology is prefaced by five documents: Jing, Shi, Zi, Ji, and Archaeology, and knowledge of ancient Chinese is interspersed between the anthologies. Introduction:
_x000D_
This course will introduce the interactive relationship between China's diplomacy and international affairs from a local perspective, analyze how China creates a favorable external environment for domestic economic and social development by fully participating in international and global affairs, and how this process affects China's own political and diplomatic behavior. This course is divided into three parts: introduction, main body and conclusion. The second half of the course focuses on macroeconomic issues, that is, the basic problems faced by society as a whole (such as unemployment, inflation, monetary policy, international trade, etc.).

Name: Studies in Japanese Society
Introduction: Japan is China's close neighbor and an important part of East Asian society. It is also a mirror and contrast to Chinese society. Understanding Japanese society will help us reflect on Chinese society itself. Moreover, in recent years, the translation of Japanese social studies in China has accumulated to a considerable extent, allowing for a more in-depth introduction and study of Japanese society based on Chinese literature. This course hopes to open a window for sociology students to understand the other in their immediate neighborhood.

Name: Global Environmental Outlook
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite: No pre-requisites required. Students who are interested in global and Chinese environment issues and policy implications are welcome.
Introduction:
The state of the environment at the global scale is the result of biophysical changes on the earth driven by the interaction between human activities and natural processes. Drastic changes (negative impacts) in the global environment may pose a huge threat to humans. Formulating and implementing sustainable economic and social development strategies and environmental protection policies to improve environmental conditions has received widespread attention from global policy makers. This course uses "Global Environment Outlook", the flagship assessment report of the United Nations Environment Program (UN Environment) every five years as the main reading book. It adopts the form of special lectures and is taught by Chinese scientists who participated in the scientific assessment work of "Global Environment Outlook" (GEO). This course focuses on the global environmental status, driving factors, change trends and future scenarios, policy responses and policy effects of global environmental protection, as well as the latest achievements and future development directions in international negotiations of environmental conventions and China's participation in international environmental governance. It enables students to understand the latest progress and hot issues of global and Chinese environmental status and policies, master environmental science knowledge, broaden their horizons, expand their ideas, and lay a solid foundation for future research or management work in the field of environmental science. _x000D_
This course is mainly taught in the form of 12 lectures, 2 seminars and 2 discussions. Special lectures are taught by experts involved in the writing and evaluation of the Global Environmental Outlook report, and two student discussions and reports are organized at the beginning of the course and at the end of the two main content modules. Students can choose topics related to the course content for discussion based on their majors, interests and instructor recommendations. The final examination is in the form of a term paper.

The content is divided into four parts: Pre-Qin part, Qin and Han part, Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties part, and institutional history part. The purpose of teaching is to enable students to understand the basic historical facts, main clues and major issues of this period of history through systematic study, and to understand the general situation of politics, economy, system, culture, nation, etc.; to learn the basic methods of historical research in this period, to understand important academic works, researchers and the latest academic trends, and to cultivate professional awareness. This lays the foundation for further study of the second half of ancient Chinese history, as well as various chronological and specialized history courses, and for writing historical papers.

It provides a detailed explanation and analysis of the interconnected content between the traditional Chinese philosophical aesthetic theory and the art of Chinese calligraphy. It also combines the calligraphy works and calligraphy art theories of the most representative calligraphers in the art of Chinese calligraphy in past dynasties to clarify the Chinese calligraphy art theory. The aesthetic scope and characteristics of Chinese calligraphy art and the ontological connotation of Chinese calligraphy art enable students to comprehensively understand and understand the aesthetic thoughts and theories of Chinese calligraphy art, gradually cultivate students' interest and hobbies in Chinese calligraphy art, and improve students' creation and appreciation of Chinese calligraphy art.

Name: American History
Introduction:
This course is a general history course of the United States designed for undergraduate students. Taught in Chinese. In 16 weeks, the course will outline the main development of American history from the 18th to the 21st century, describe the formation and evolution of the American economic, political, legal, social and cultural order, analyze the causes, dynamics and mechanisms of changes in American history, and discuss the relationship between the United States and the world. The main topics discussed in the course include: (1) The United States in the colonial era; (2) The American Revolution and the American Constitution; (3) The democratization and reform movement of the early federation; (4) Slavery, the American Civil War, and Reconstruction; (5) The process of American industrialization and its costs; (6) The evolution of American foreign policy in the 19th and 20th centuries; (7) Roosevelt's New Deal, Johnson's "Great Society" and the emergence of the American welfare state; (8) The United States during World War II and the Cold War; (9) The United States in the 1960s; (10) Challenges facing the United States in the post-Cold War era. _x000D_
_x000D_
As a general history course, this course will narrate the process of American history in chronological order, but focus on and echo the following themes: (1) The evolution of American core values - especially "freedom" - in history and its performance and changes as historical experience; (2) The origin and evolution of the American national system (including political and legal systems); (3) The historical experience of Americans of different races, ethnicities, classes and genders; (4) The connection between different reform movements in American history; (5) The relationship between American history and world history. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course hopes to achieve three basic purposes: first, to help students understand and become familiar with the main context of the development of American history, major historical turning points, major historical figures and schools of thought, and to lay the foundation for taking more professional American history courses; second, to help students understand the diversity and complexity of the development of American history, and its close connection with world history; third, to inspire and encourage students to explore and analyze the role of different forces such as economy, thought, system, social structure, culture, etc. in the development of the United States. _x000D_

Name: Art Archaeology
Introduction:
Art archeology studies the objects with artistic value excavated by archaeology, and the goal of the research is to restore ancient social culture. Various art objects as research objects are mostly discovered through field surveys and excavations. Archeology and art are naturally and closely integrated. _x000D_
The difference between art objects discovered through archaeology and those handed down from ancient times lies in the precise location, environment, distribution and coexistence with other relics. Therefore, the starting point of art archaeological understanding is different from traditional art history. It needs to be based on the collation and analysis of excavated objects using archaeological methods such as stratigraphy and typology, combined with ancient documents and handed down relics, to clarify the emergence and development process of art, as well as its connection with social and cultural development. And because these relics have artistic value and are related to art creation activities, it is also necessary to conduct visual, image, and spatial research on shapes, colors, compositions, genres, etc. based on aesthetic concepts. _x000D_
The objects of art archeology are complex and rich, including city sites, buildings, rock paintings, murals, sculptures, statues and various handicrafts, etc. These relics contain rich cultural connotations. Their design and shape reflect people's intelligence and wisdom, and are also a portrayal of daily life at that time. Decorative patterns are a reflection of people's ideology and are full of people's emotions. The production demonstrates superb scientific and technological achievements. Every minute detail of the ruins and relics will evoke people's nostalgia, as if they are wandering in a lively world, discovering strict hierarchy, happy life, wonderful inventions and aesthetic taste. _x000D_
Through fifteen special topics, this course introduces various archaeological relics in ancient China and explains the historical and cultural significance behind them.

Name: Computational Materials Science and Engineering
Introduction: The computational simulation of materials has become an important branch of material science, combining various relevant disciplines such as condensation physics, material physics, theoretical chemistry, material mechanics and engineering mechanics, and mechanical algorithms. By calculating simulations, we can understand not only the structure and function of the material from a micromechanical point of view, but also the design of new materials from a theoretical point of view. The course focuses on the rationale and methodology for material calculations and simulations and their application in engineering. To enable students to digitize the underlying physical and mathematical theory they have learned to design and develop new types of structural and functional materials through numerical simulations.

Name: Organic Materials and Devices
Prerequisite: Scientific basis of materials; semiconductor physics and devices
Introduction:
With the development of science and technology, the use of organic materials (including polymer materials) is becoming more and more widespread. For example, organic conductor materials, semiconductor materials, luminescent materials and nonlinear optical materials have all been developed rapidly in recent years. Among them, the development of organic photoelectric functional materials is the most prominent. Since the discovery in 1977 that polymers can conduct electricity like metals, rapid development in this field has completely changed people's original understanding of organic and polymer materials. With the commercialization of organic electroluminescent diode (OLED) materials in recent years, the research of organic materials has occupied an increasingly important position in the entire materials science. _x000D_
This course uses a teaching method that combines multimedia teaching and literature reading. It will focus on teaching the structural characteristics of organic materials, structural characterization methods of organic and polymer materials, electronic structures and energy level control methods of organic materials, doping and electrochemical behavior of organic materials, charge transport mechanisms and measurement methods of organic materials, luminescence principles of organic materials, and important application areas of organic optoelectronic materials (organic electroluminescent diodes, organic solar cells, and organic field-effect transistors). Through learning, students are required to flexibly master the research methods and characteristics in the field of organic materials, master basic basic knowledge of organic materials, and have the ability to read and understand related cutting-edge research fields. _x000D_

It will systematically explain the research characteristics, research methods and technical means of organic functional materials. Combined with the reading and discussion of cutting-edge literature, students will be comprehensively cultivated in their scientific research and engineering innovation and application capabilities in the field of organic and polymer functional materials.

Name: Studies in the Thought of Li Dazhao
Introduction:
Research on Li Dazhao’s Thoughts_x000D_

     This course mainly teaches Li Dazhao's life story and his main ideas. Focus on teaching Li Dazhao's major contributions in spreading Marxism, preparing for the founding of the Communist Party of China, promoting the sinicization of Marxism, and promoting the first cooperation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, etc., and comment on Li Dazhao's historical thoughts, youth thoughts, "Min Yi" thoughts, civilian thoughts, women's thoughts, etc. Watch documentary and historical films and television films related to Li Dazhao. Presented monographs at a symposium at the University of Sarimen, North Asia and Japan (the paper has been published in Japanese in a collection published by the University of Sichamirin). The social function of cartoons is promoted through comic books about China and foreign countries: humor, irony and compassion. Through cartoons from different historical periods in different countries, the social context and cultural characteristics of the time are analysed, thus explaining the characteristics and manner in which the cartoons are transmitted to society. Especially in today ' s information and Internet society, where the appearance of signage systems with cartoon features, such as expression kits, is becoming richer and more frequent, affecting our way of life and working.

Name: Analytical Chemistry (B)
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Analytical chemistry is a compulsory basic course for undergraduates majoring in chemistry, biology, medicine, environment, materials, etc. Its theories and methods are not only the foundation of the analytical chemistry major, but also the foundation of all other chemistry-related majors. Name: Comparison Theorems in Riemannian Geometry
Introduction: In this course we will learn the connection between the geometry and topology of complete Riemannian manifolds. The main tool is the comparison theorem, which compares general manifolds with long curvature space forms to derive the corresponding geometric and topological properties. Basic requirements for taking this elective course: Have a basic understanding of differential manifolds and algebraic topology.

Name: Introduction to Hyperbolic Geometry
Introduction:
This course teaches the basic theory of hyperbolic geometry and Klein groups, as well as related knowledge of hyperbolic manifolds. The course plan starts from the definition of hyperbolic space and provides a relatively complete introduction to the relevant results on finite volume three-dimensional hyperbolic manifolds, especially the hyperbolic Dehn's surgical theorem, Mostow's rigidity theorem and Margulis' lemma. The above roughly covers the first eight chapters of W. P. Thurston's preprinted lecture notes. Closely related to this part, the course also briefly introduces the content and motivation of the geometrization conjecture, especially stating the results of the geometric decomposition of manifolds, but does not discuss its proof. _x000D_
_x000D_
To take this course, students should have background knowledge of abstract algebra, topology and differential manifolds, and the level is equivalent to the corresponding undergraduate courses in the Department of Mathematics. _x000D_

Name: Geometric Group Theory
Prerequisite: The basic content of the abstract algebra on the mosaics is generally extended, and the notion of algebra on the fundamentals is better.
Introduction:
Geometric clustering is an emerging area of research using geometry and scaling-up methods to study infinite clusters. Its basic idea was first found in the three basic sets of judgement questions put by Dehn, a well-known German mathematician, around 1910: the word problem, the cross-cutting problem and the homogeneity problem. In particular, Dehn succeeded in resolving the word problem of the curve by using hyperbolic geometry. In the 1980s or so, important results, such as the geometric conjecture of the famous mathematician Thurston and the hyperbolic theory of Gromov, contributed significantly to the development of geometry as an independent field of research. Over the past two decades, geometry has achieved many important and influential work. For example, Israel's famous mathematician, Sela, has resolved the important assumption of the logic scientist Tarski's primary theory of the free community. Another important development is that in 2012, American mathematician Agol, based on the work of mathematicians, Wise, and others, completely resolved almost Haken's three-dimensional current, as well as a number of important contours of a hyperbolic flow. The Agol and Wise approaches are based mainly on geometrical fusions, which are unexpected to many of the purers. It is foreseen that geometry will continue to interact and make important progress with low-dimensional expansion and other important areas of research.

Thus, through the study of the curriculum, students should be familiar with the various ideological approaches that use the role of the constellation in geometric space to study the various characteristics of the constellation; in particular, the broad geometric characteristics of the constellation, such as growth rates, negative curvature characteristics, etc.; understanding the equivalence of the hyperbolic cluster; and the sub-groups of the hyperbolic cluster and their classification, as well as their role on their borders.

Name: Data Structures Problem Session
Introduction:
Basic purpose: to enable students to comprehensively understand the concepts of algorithms and data structures, master the implementation methods of various data structures and algorithms, and compare the characteristics of different data structures and algorithms. This enables students to not only learn the basic knowledge of data structures and algorithms, but also improve their ability to use computers to solve practical problems. _x000D_

Name: High-Dimensional Probability Theory
Prerequisite: Probability theory, linear algebra, mathematical analysis, introduction to machine learning.
Introduction: Data science and artificial intelligence have achieved great success in application fields, but they have also brought about new basic theoretical problems. Some advanced knowledge of probability and statistics is necessary to study these basic issues. The main purpose of this course is to provide knowledge in this area. Course content includes: concentration inequalities of sums of independent random variables, high-dimensional random vector inequalities, random matrix inequalities, empirical stochastic processes, Chaining, statistical learning theory, and deep learning theory topics.

Name: Number Theory I
Introduction: The roots of polynomials with integer coefficients are called algebraic numbers. Algebraic numbers appear naturally in the study of number theory, such as in solving Diophantine equations. Algebraic number theory is the theory of algebraic numbers. In this course, we learn the basic content of algebraic number theory, including related algebraic theory (through the method of commutative algebra), geometric theory (by exploring the analogy of algebraic integer rings and polynomial rings in finite fields), etc. _x000D_

Name: Software Analysis Techniques
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: This course has been changed from undergraduate to undergraduate from 2021 and no longer requires prior courses.
Introduction:
A large number of code artifacts will be produced during the software development process, including code, test data, configuration plans, etc. Analysis of these artifacts is one of the basic means of various software engineering tools. Typical software development tools such as compilers, code editors, testing and debugging tools, etc. are inseparable from the analysis of software products. In the industrial world, the basic platform departments of major companies have a large demand for talents who master software analysis technology; in academia, software analysis technology is one of the necessary basic knowledge for conducting research in the field of software engineering. This course will systematically introduce software analysis techniques. This course is offered to both senior undergraduate and graduate students. _x000D_
_x000D_
    Software analysis techniques are primarily used to answer questions about the nature of the program itself. Program analysis technology is the basic method for developing tools directly related to code, such as compilers, debuggers, and code editors. According to Gödel's incompleteness theorem, a large number of questions cannot be answered statically, so program analysis technology focuses on how to make correct approximations, or use dynamic data to make up for it when static analysis cannot be completed. However, the literature related to software analysis technology has the characteristics of wide content, many schools, and high mathematical foundation requirements, making it always difficult to learn software analysis technology. This course hopes to help students build a more complete knowledge system of software analysis technology through easy-to-understand explanations of this type of technology, understand the cutting-edge knowledge in this field, lay a foundation for further academic research in the field of software engineering, and cultivate the development ability of large-scale software engineering tools in practice. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course will be changed from an undergraduate course to an undergraduate course starting in 2021. Prerequisite courses will no longer be required, and some basic knowledge will be introduced. _x000D_
_x000D_
    The relationship between this course and the current courses of the School of Information Science and Technology: _x000D_
"Advanced Compilation Technology": The data flow analysis, inter-procedural analysis and other contents in this course partially overlap with the program analysis content in this course. However, "Advanced Compilation Technology" mainly teaches some applications of program analysis from the perspective of the compiler, while this course is not limited to one application, but focuses on program analysis itself. The overlapping content is different from "Advanced Compilation Technology" in depth and breadth. _x000D_
"Software Testing" and "Software Quality Assurance": This course mainly teaches the tools and techniques used in the actual software development process from a practical perspective. Because testing itself is also a process of program analysis, this course will cover a small amount of testing and other aspects, but it mainly discusses test data generation technologies such as symbolic execution from the perspective of program analysis, and has less overlap with the "Software Testing" course. _x000D_

Introduction: Time series econometrics is an important tool for analyzing economic dynamics. This course aims to introduce the theoretical foundation and analysis tools of time series. This course is divided into two parts. The first part introduces the mathematical foundation of time series analysis, including the basic theories of stationary and non-stationary sequences. Name: Creative Expression in English: TED Talks Listening and Speaking
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is based on cultivating students' English listening and speaking skills, especially their ability to express themselves creatively, through the appreciation of TED speeches. TED English speeches have become extremely influential around the world in the 30 years since their inception. The speech topics cover the latest achievements and innovations in the fields of science, technology and humanities. Its rich and fresh corpus and engaging speech methods are extremely beneficial to training Peking University students' English expression. This course is close to the thinking of college students and selects 24 classic TED speeches, and presents them according to six major themes - education and foreign language learning, stress and growth, creativity, work and success, environment, relationship and happiness. Through carefully designed course learning links, it is expected to help students make great progress in English creative expression. _x000D_
The concept of course design is based on problem-based learning (Problem-based Learning). From the beginning, students are encouraged to eventually make a TED-like speech. It provides sufficient solid language knowledge while activating students' personalized creativity, allowing each student to form a unique point of view according to their own interests or professional fields, and step by step through short statements to finally reach a longer speech. _x000D_
Another main content of the course is the study of the art and rhetoric of speech, combined with the text analysis of TED speeches, to help students understand and master the techniques and skills of English expression. The course is designed with many links, such as preview, background knowledge, vocabulary learning, appreciation of beautiful sentences, rhetoric and speech skills, outline of core ideas, critical and reflective discussion, etc., to enable students to deeply understand the highlights and shortcomings of each speech. At the same time, the course is combined with examples of TED speeches. After each topic, students share their opinions with the class for mutual review, practicing the skills of clear and powerful expression, especially the ability to share contagiously. The course focuses on sorting out and discussing the viewpoints of TED speeches, encouraging students to find ideas and information on their own, and helping students ultimately form a creative speech. _x000D_

The content covers the consistency and asymptotic normality of M-estimation and Z-estimation, semi-parametric estimation and effectiveness, regularization methods and theories of non-parametric and high-dimensional models, minimum and maximum lower bounds, etc. By studying this course, students will develop a comprehensive understanding of modern statistical theory and master the theoretical knowledge necessary for cutting-edge research in statistics and data science.

Name: Bioinformatics
Introduction: "Bioinformatics" is a main basic course for undergraduate students. With the rapid development of high-throughput biological measurement technology represented by deep sequencing, life science has become a data science. This course is based on the basics and systematically introduces the basic principles of the field of bioinformatics, especially the analysis and application of typical omics data such as genomics, transcriptomics, and proteomics. Topics include random wander, Poisson processes, discrete-time Markov chains, continuous-time Markov chains, Brownian motion, and diffusion processes.

Name: Environmental Economics
Introduction: This course is an applied economics course, and students are expected to have some basic knowledge of microeconomics. The goal of this course is to help students master the basic concepts of welfare economics and public economics, and to guide students to analyze and grasp policy tools for effectively solving environmental problems from an economic perspective. The following main contents will be covered: basic theories of environmental economics (such as relevant knowledge of welfare economics), social cost-benefit analysis, economic principles of natural resource utilization, and selection of policy tools for environmental protection. This course focuses on the practical application of economic principles and analytical tools, and hopes to inspire students in using economic theory to analyze and solve problems in real life. The programming of binding, binding and elucidation is an important research direction in the area of artificial intelligence for almost three decades, and the programming of binding is a declarative programming paradigm that presents the relationship between variables through binding conditions, giving some attributes of problem resolution. The course will describe the technologies and methods associated with the binding programming, the main elements of which will be taught, including the issue of binding compliance (CSP), the basic framework for binding programming, the means of binding solvency, the issue of consistency, binding dissemination and retrieval algorithms, and the appropriate presentation of current and emerging technologies.

College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: "Modern and contemporary architecture" is divided into two parts: "modern" and "contemporary". Considering that the general course is for non-architectural students at Peking University, this course starts with Victor Hugo's novel "Notre Dame de Paris" to lay out the historical background of modern architecture in Western Europe and understand the historical tasks and future directions of the pioneers of modern architecture. In the middle of the course, it starts with Tati in the movie "Play" "Time" is a turning point to discuss how modern architecture based on the logic of production has evolved into contemporary architecture aimed at consumption, in order to understand why a large number of contemporary wonder buildings are produced, and why it is so difficult to resist consumerism through architectural practice; in the last part of the course, the historical clues of the rise of Japanese architecture in modern times are sorted out to look forward to the possibilities of contemporary Chinese architecture.

Name: Principles of Biomedical Engineering
Introduction:
Biomedicine Engineering (Biomedical engineering, BME) is an emerging cross-cutting scientific, industrial and medical discipline developed on the basis of traditional natural disciplines such as physics, chemistry, biology, mathematics and modern natural disciplines such as modern medicine, engineering and so forth. It uses the principles and methods of natural science and modern engineering techniques to study human structures, functions and life phenomena at multiple levels, from molecular, cell, tissue, organ level to human system, and to provide engineering techniques for human disease prevention, diagnosis, guardianship, treatment, health care, rehabilitation and reproductive health services. In summary, the development of biomedical engineering is closely related to modern, high-tech technologies, which use electronics, nanotechnology, computer technology, material technology, optical electronics and ray technology, and the integration of many modern technologies, in close association with modern biology and medicine, to develop engineering methods and technologies relevant to human health.

The purpose of this course, which is compulsory for undergraduate students in biomedicine engineering, is to provide a systematic and comprehensive introduction to the relevant background, basic theory, applied technology and frontier dynamics of the development of disciplines in the field of biomedical engineering, to provide students with a better understanding and mastery of the various fields of biomedical engineering, and to guide and nurture students ' interest in biomedicine engineering, which is the basic course in which students in this field enter the specific orientations of the various professions at the advanced level.

Name: Molecular Biology Laboratory
Prerequisite:
Molecular Biology Theory Course, study of the principles of experimental studies.
Theoretical course in microbiology, studying the principles and methods of microbiological operations.
Introduction:
The purpose of this course is to train students in basic experimental methods and techniques of molecular biology. In the course of the experiment, students are given basic principles and analytical methods of the results of basic molecular biology experiments and are trained in the relevant experimental techniques and operations. The curriculum consists mainly of the following components:
1. Separating and purification of particle DNA.
2. Restrictive internal enzyme digestion of DNA.
3. DNA glucose gel electrocution.
4. Use of PCR technology to augment the GFP gene.
5. Import of macrointestinal coliform cell preparation and its external DNA molecules.
6. Screening of positive cloning and induced expression of external genes in the original nuclear cell.
7. RNA extraction and identification of plant organizations.

Name: Innovation Practicum in Energy and Environmental Systems Engineering
Introduction: This course allows students to carry out practical scientific research and engineering practice, with a special focus on energy and environment-related content. On the basis of meeting the laboratory safety requirements, students can choose scientific research topics set up by teachers from the Department of Energy and Resource Engineering, enter the laboratory, or carry out their own scientific research topics under the guidance of teachers. This course is currently a teaching experiment.

Name: Heat and Mass Transfer
Introduction: Heat and mass transfer is the science that studies the laws of heat and mass transfer. It is a basic course for energy and power engineering majors. This course is a basic theory course for undergraduate students. It aims to introduce the basic knowledge and theory of heat transfer. It conducts in-depth discussions on the three basic ways of heat transfer, namely heat conduction, convection, and radiation. It focuses on guiding students to understand the concepts and master the methods of analyzing and solving heat transfer problems through experimental methods, analytical methods, and numerical methods. At the same time, combined with reality, application examples in the engineering field, such as heat exchangers, are introduced to guide students to learn research thinking and methods, and master the ability to independently analyze application examples.

Name: Bioenergy and Biological Resources
Introduction:
Humanity is facing huge energy and environmental pressure. Current energy is mainly fossil energy, including coal, oil, natural gas, etc. Fossil energy has greatly promoted social development. However, fossil energy is non-renewable and has limited storage and will eventually be exhausted. On the other hand, the rapid use of fossil energy has led to increasingly serious environmental problems, including global temperature warming caused by greenhouse gas emissions, ozone layer destruction, ecosystem imbalance, etc. Over the past 30 years, the concentration of carbon dioxide in the air has increased by about 20%, approaching 400 ppm; the temperature has also increased by 0.6°C. At the end of 2015, the United Nations Climate Change Conference was held in Paris and the Paris Agreement was adopted. The agreement states that all parties will strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change, control the increase in global average temperature within 2°C compared with pre-industrial levels, and strive to control the temperature increase within 1.5°C; the world will reach the peak of greenhouse gas emissions as soon as possible and achieve a carbon-neutral development strategy of net-zero greenhouse gas emissions in the second half of this century. my country has proposed to achieve the peak of carbon dioxide emissions by 2030. At present, fossil energy accounts for more than 85% of my country's energy consumption structure, mainly coal, which is much higher than the proportion in developed countries. Therefore, improving the energy consumption structure, increasing the proportion of non-fossil energy, and developing new renewable alternative energy have become major issues that need to be solved urgently for human society. Among renewable energy sources, bioenergy is crucial and has received more and more research and attention. _x000D_
Bioenergy, as the name suggests, is renewable energy from biological sources. The carbon dioxide produced by its combustion can be reabsorbed and utilized by organisms, so it is beneficial to reduce carbon dioxide and maintain carbon balance. In terms of form, it can be divided into three types: solid (biomass such as wood), liquid (bioalcohols, biodiesel, biooil, etc.), and gaseous (biomethane, biohydrogen, etc.). The utilization of biomass can be traced back to humans drilling wood to make fire, while the utilization of liquid and gaseous bioenergy only began in modern times. According to different raw materials, bioenergy can be broadly divided into first generation, second generation, and third generation. The first generation of bioenergy comes from food crops such as corn, soybeans, sugar cane, etc., the second generation of bioenergy comes from non-food crops such as tung trees, etc., and the third generation of bioenergy comes from algae. Bioenergy currently on the market mainly comes from food crops, which have low yields and compete with food for arable land. In contrast, microalgae bioenergy is considered to be the most potential bioenergy due to its high yield and does not compete for cultivated land, and has received unprecedented attention. Biodiesel is a liquid bioenergy that has been mainly developed in recent years. It has low pollution, a wide range of sources, can be miscible with diesel in any proportion, and is suitable for any diesel engine. Biodiesel refers to fatty acid esters obtained through the esterification reaction of lipids such as animal, plant and microbial oils and short-chain alcohols (methanol, ethanol) under the action of a catalyst. The development of biodiesel is of great significance. This course will introduce the current situation, development trends, and cutting-edge progress in the field of bioenergy at home and abroad. It will focus on microalgae and describe the production technology, latest progress, and development prospects of bioenergy and biological resources, including algae separation, identification, and screening, cultivation technology and equipment, bioenergy preparation, and the production and development of various high-value products.

Name: Energy and Environmental Engineering Laboratory

Introduction: Energy shortage and environmental degradation have become obstacles to my country's continued development, and these three are interdependent and inseparable. However, the traditional professional setting only emphasizes one direction of energy and environment and lacks the necessary connections. It is against this background that the energy and environmental engineering experiment was established. This course combines various research directions of the Department of Energy and Environmental Engineering, focusing on environmental engineering, energy cycle principles and technologies, energy dynamics, new energy and other research directions, extracting common content and setting up 10 experiments. Name: Systems Thinking for a Complex Life I
Introduction:
An important feature of this course is the development of practical and systematic thinking towards complex challenges in university life. The salient ideas are, first, to move from a mechanized model of simple thinking to a deeper understanding of one's own; secondly, to use systematic thinking to actively adapt mindsets and behaviour patterns to address sub-health problems such as tangle, anxiety, depression and delay; thirdly, to foster a broad-based thinking under the concept of “one human being” and to promote the convergence of East and West cultures; and fourthly, to actively reflect on the value of life and climb its peaks in the challenges of future human development. The course will systematically present the “Health, Happiness, Wisdom” picture of the great health of life and encourage students to pursue true happiness.
In the light of the above, this course applies to all undergraduate students (graduate students) who can “open their minds, put their faces behind them and practice them actively” and to individual scholars who have some knowledge and pursuit. Introduction: Molecular Cell Biology is a basic course in biomedical engineering. This course introduces relevant knowledge of molecular cell biology, including basic knowledge of cells, structure and function of biological macromolecules, regulation, metabolism, and major new technologies.

Name: Anatomy and Physiology

Through the study of this course, students can acquire basic theoretical knowledge of human life activities and tissue anatomy and physiology, as well as the normal morphological structure and functional activity rules of the human body, in order to achieve a comprehensive understanding of human body structure; enable students to better apply knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, and lay a foundation for learning and solving related problems in the field of biomedical engineering.

Name: Anatomy and Physiology Laboratory
Prerequisite: None. The course on " Anatomy Physiology " is being taught in parallel.
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for undergraduates majoring in biomedical engineering and is conducted simultaneously with the teaching of "Anatomy and Physiology". It is divided into confirmatory experiments, design experiments, and comprehensive experiments. The main contents include: introduction to commonly used instruments, four basic tissues of the human body, movement system, nervous system, sciatic nerve-gastrocnemius muscle specimen preparation, measurement of visual field and blind spots, ABO blood type identification, measurement of clotting time, anatomy of the circulatory system, and measurement of human arterial blood pressure. Determination, cardiac auscultation, determination of the effective refractory period of the heart, premature ventricular contractions and compensatory intervals, experimental design of neurohumoral factors on the regulation of arterial blood pressure, pre-test on the regulation of arterial blood pressure by neurohumoral factors, formal experiments on the regulation of arterial blood pressure by neurohumoral factors, regulation of respiratory movements, spinal cord test - reflex arc analysis, etc. Through the study of this course, students can acquire basic theoretical knowledge of human life activities and tissue anatomy and physiology, as well as the normal morphological structure and functional activity rules of the human body, in order to achieve a comprehensive understanding of human body structure; enable students to better apply knowledge of human anatomy and physiology, and lay a foundation for learning and solving related problems in the field of biomedical engineering.

Name: Biomedical Engineering Design I
Introduction:
This course is a required course for undergraduates majoring in biomedical engineering. The prerequisite course is "Principles of Biomedical Engineering". This course is one of the problem-based learning (PBL) series of courses. It is also a basic course for students of this major to enter the specific direction of each major in their senior years. _x000D_

Finally, it introduces some examples of digital signal processing in the field of biomedical engineering, and looks forward to the cutting-edge technology in this field.

Introduction: Biomedical optics is a very important branch of biomedical engineering. This course focuses on the basic principles, engineering technologies, and clinical applications of biomedical optics. It mainly involves the basic properties of optics, the interaction between light and matter, basic principles of microscopy, super-resolution microscopy technology, photoacoustic imaging technology, optical coherence tomography, endoscopic systems, and the application of lasers in medical treatment.

Name: Biomedical Image Processing
Introduction: This course first introduces the application situation and characteristics of digital image processing in the field of biomedical engineering, and then comprehensively teaches traditional digital image processing technologies, including brightness transformation, linear and nonlinear spatial filtering, frequency domain filtering, image restoration and registration, color image processing, wavelet, image data compression, morphological image processing, image segmentation, region and boundary representation and description, and object recognition, etc. The course uses Matlab to enable students to master the application technology of digital image processing in the field of biomedical engineering.

The course also arranges visits to world-class laboratories or scientific research facilities, and direct face-to-face discussions and exchanges with famous scholars in the field.

Name: Introduction to Computational Biology
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, molecular cell biology or ordinary organisms Learn.
Introduction:
This course is an elective course for senior majors in biomedical engineering, and is also open to undergraduate students in biology, medicine and other related majors. Computational biology takes modern molecular biology data as its main research object, develops theoretical models and computational methods, and reveals the biological complexity of the genome, transcriptome, proteome, and metabolome, as well as the fundamental laws of life phenomena such as growth, development, heredity, evolution, and disease. This course focuses on the study of theoretical modeling and algorithms, including multivariate statistical analysis methods, stochastic process models, information theory methods, machine learning methods, etc., and discusses the application of the above methods in practical research (including gene sequence information analysis, gene prediction, gene chip data analysis and processing, protein classification and structure prediction, molecular evolution and phylogenetic trees, biological networks and other important issues). _x000D_
