Name: Cellular and Molecular Imaging
Introduction: As technology continues to advance, scientists are making fundamental breakthroughs in uncovering the fundamental mechanisms by which normal cellular physiological activities operate and have begun to decipher how these processes go awry in cancer and other diseases. Among all technologies, an emerging technology called cellular molecular imaging has become an indispensable means for our understanding of the molecular mechanisms of normal and pathological physiological activities. This technology can provide high-resolution spatiotemporal information of specific biological macromolecules in living cells without causing damage to them, which is not easy to achieve with traditional technology. This course is dedicated to familiarizing students with important techniques and principles of cellular and molecular imaging, including principles of cellular and molecular imaging, synthesis and characterization of molecular imaging probes and sensors, fluorescence microscopy imaging methods, ultra-high resolution imaging methods, quantitative imaging methods and multispectral imaging methods, etc.

Name: Solid State Physics (B)
Introduction: Solid state physics is a discipline that studies the microstructure of solids, atomic vibrations, electron motions and the motion patterns of various particles in external fields, the relationship between the macroscopic properties of solids (mechanics, thermal, acoustics, electricity, magnetism, optics, etc.) and the microscopic atomic electronic motions. It is an important branch of physics and the basis for advanced microelectronics, optoelectronics and other technologies and materials science. At the same time, the understanding and experimental methods obtained in solid state physics are also forming a very extensive and in-depth intersection with chemistry, life sciences, geosciences, energy sciences, etc. It is one of the very important cornerstones of the development of modern science.

This course, which emphasizes numerical rather than analytical interpretation of models, has largely liberated the thinking of researchers, allowing them to focus better on the intuition behind models than on specific solutions.

Name: Advanced Macroeconomics (II)
Prerequisite:
Advanced microeconomics (i)
Advanced macroeconomics (i)
Advanced econometrics (i)
Introduction: This course is a graduate-level macroeconomics theory course. Compared with undergraduate-level macroeconomics models, graduate-level macroeconomics models usually have the following characteristics: they have micro-foundations, are dynamic models, and contain stochasticity. Such models are often solved using recursive methods such as dynamic programming, which will be covered first in this course. In the main part of this course, we will study several representative models in the three major fields of contemporary mainstream macroeconomics. The first is a consumption-based asset pricing model. This type of model assumes that actors make consumption and savings decisions in a world of uncertainty. On this basis, it explores how asset prices are determined by macro fundamental factors. The second is real business cycle models, which reveal how the macroeconomy fluctuates cyclically due to changes in productivity and other real changes. The third is the New Keynesian model. The iconic feature of this type of model is the introduction of imperfect competition and nominal friction, which is particularly helpful for the analysis of the effects of monetary policy and policy formulation.

Name: Human Immunity and Health Cultivation
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: The purpose of the course is to prevent disease and maintain physical health by providing an immunological perspective on how to build a scientific lifestyle and move out of the various fault areas of life that affect the immunity of organisms. Immunization and immunity have been important topics for human health, and immunization factors play a very important role in the course of many diseases, such as malignant tumours, asthma, hepatitis and infectious diseases such as AIDS. But you know what? The immune system, like other systems in the human body, grows with the growth of the organism, with the ageing of the organism and with its ageing, with its characteristics at all stages of human development, and at all stages of development it is necessary to develop healthy immunization strategies to protect our immune system, to enable it to function fully and to achieve healthy survival. At the same time, the sensitivity of the immune system to the outside world, social development, increased environmental pollution and psychological stress, and even the use of various medical technologies, such as beauty surgery, can lead to injury to the immune system or even to collapse, leading to diseases. The teaching of the curriculum includes, inter alia, basic introductions to human immune systems and functions, immunisation against disease and the relationship between immunization and healthy survival. Through this course of study, students have an initial knowledge of the main mechanisms and general patterns of immunology and the functioning of the immune system and of the basic principles of immunization and healthy nutrition, as well as of the application of modern immunology techniques in the field of medical biology.

Name: Geometric Optics and Optical Instruments
Introduction: Geometric optics is based on basic experimental laws such as linear propagation, reflection and refraction of light, and uses geometric methods to discuss light propagation issues such as imaging. The terms, concepts, and laws of geometric optics are frequently used when analyzing and adjusting even the most modern optical instruments. In view of the lack of knowledge in this area among many students, this course allows students to master the basic principles of geometric optics and common optical instruments and the methods and skills of optical path construction through concentrated teaching and combined with basic physics experiments performed by undergraduates. They will be familiar with common optical components, geometric optical instruments and physical optical instruments, understand the modern optical instrument systems used in cutting-edge scientific research topics, learn the use of optical components and the safe operating rules of laser laboratories.

Name: Anglo-American Tort Law
Introduction: Tort law is a fundamental, traditional and independent body of law in British and American law, with a unique body of rules and principles of law, as well as diverse legal doctrines. For the purposes of tort law, tort law can provide the plaintiff with a remedy for the injury suffered; for the defendant, tort law can protect his freedom of action; and for the community, tort law can prevent damage in general. The Tort Law provides a private law remedy of law and, together with insurance law, social law, criminal injury compensation law and State welfare law of the nature of various health services, provides legal compensation to the injured party. This course covers specific forms of tort proceedings and corresponding respective legal rules, legal principles and public policies: unlawful infringement of land, unlawful infringement of movable property, unlawful assault of person, assault, damage to honour, fault law, liability for violation of statutory law, liability for violation of dangerous housing, liability for defective products, strict liability, liability for damage caused by animals, responsibility for violation of family law, financial liability for infringement, fraud and harmful lies, abuse of legal proceedings, etc. On this basis, the course will also explore legal theory, including moral theory of tort law, political theory of tort law, economic theory of tort law, and feminist theory of tort law.

Name: Introduction to the Physics of Quantum Information
Prerequisite: Quantum mechanics, quantum optical (recommended, not required)
Introduction:
Quantum informatics is an emerging interdisciplinary subject that uses the basic principles of quantum mechanics to encode, communicate, calculate and process information. Including quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum keys and other aspects. It has been the focus of intense attention in the fields of physics and information science for nearly two decades. Quantum entanglement and quantum nonlocality are the most peculiar properties of quantum mechanics that are different from classical physics. They are the core concepts and important resources of quantum information science. With the rapid development of quantum control experimental technology in recent years, how to control quantum states in physical systems has become a very active and important topic in the current international scientific research field. The 2012 Nobel Prize in Physics was awarded to physicists Serge Haroche and David Wineland for their groundbreaking experimental methods that "made possible the measurement and manipulation of individual quantum systems." An important application of quantum control is to study the quantum entanglement characteristics of quantum systems, such as the interesting "Schrödinger cat state": the cat is both dead and alive. The preparation and control of quantum entangled states play a very important role in quantum information communication, such as quantum storage and quantum teleportation. It also provides powerful tools and means for the security of quantum key distribution. Therefore, organizing the latest research progress in this area and introducing the current research status, research methods and future directions in this field to graduate students and senior undergraduates in the form of professional elective courses will help students expand their horizons, increase their interest, and enter research topics faster and better. _x000D_
    _x000D_
   The contribution of quantum information theory to physics is mainly to deepen people's understanding of quantum states and quantum entanglement. The concept of quantum entanglement was first proposed by Einstein, Podolsky and Rosen (EPR) and Schrödinger. They proposed "local reality" in the article, and based on this, they used ideal experiments to prove that quantum mechanics is incomplete. This problem is called the EPR paradox. Bell then proposed a plan to experimentally test the EPR paradox. Current research shows that one of the characteristics of quantum entanglement is quantum non-locality. Processes that are impossible to achieve in classical physical systems, such as ultra-dense coding and quantum teleportation, can all be accomplished using entanglement. Entanglement can improve the quality of information transmission in quantum channels with noise, and communication capacity also increases with the increase in entanglement capability. In addition, entanglement can also be used for quantum error correction. _x000D_
   _x000D_
    This course will introduce students to the basic knowledge, main research methods, practical plans and important progress in the field of quantum information science in a simple and easy-to-understand way. Through the study of this course, on the one hand, it provides the knowledge background of physics, mathematics, and computer science required to understand quantum informatics, so that everyone can understand and master the basic theories and research methods in this field, and on the other hand, it allows everyone to understand the domestic and foreign research trends in this field. This course can be taken either as part of a general education or as a prelude to continued independent study in the field. _x000D_
    _x000D_
    This course is intended for graduate students and senior undergraduate students majoring in optics, condensed matter physics and theoretical physics in the School of Physics, as well as information majors in other related departments. It will provide corresponding knowledge background introduction and scientific research training for students who are interested in engaging in quantum optics, quantum information and quantum computing, and cold atom physics research. This course will also help undergraduate students expand their knowledge and enhance their desire for scientific research and exploration. _x000D_
_x000D_
    The specific content of the course consists of seven chapters, which mainly introduce the distinction between classical and quantum information, the core resource of quantum information - quantum entanglement, and important applications of quantum information (such as quantum ultra-precision measurement, quantum teleportation, quantum keys, etc.). The focus is on explaining basic physical principles. The first chapter introduces the historical development of quantum information science, puts forward the basic concepts in quantum information and sorts out the quantum mechanical principles related to quantum information, which is conducive to the knowledge follow-up of senior undergraduates. Chapters 2 and 3 provide an in-depth introduction to the historical development, related concepts and entanglement analysis of quantum entanglement. As a core concept and important resource of quantum information, quantum entanglement plays a key role in the fields of quantum computing and communications. Chapter 4 introduces the non-local properties and manifestations of quantum mechanics, which makes the long-distance transmission of quantum states possible and is a valuable resource for the development of quantum information technology. This chapter will combine the latest research results at home and abroad to help graduate students understand the development trends of this topic and future scientific research topics. Chapter 5 explains the relationship between quantum entanglement and quantum information, focusing on important applications such as quantum teleportation, quantum keys, and quantum computing. Chapter 6 introduces the physical implementation methods of quantum information. Chapter 7 introduces the latest progress in quantum information physics. The content is mainly for teachers to guide students in literature reading and classroom discussions. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Atmospheric Physics
Introduction: The course teaches the principles and knowledge of static, thermodynamic and radiology in atmospheric physics and forms the basis for subsequent courses in cloud precipitation physics, satellite meteorology and remote sensing. Based on the introduction of atmospheric static science, the course provided more detailed presentations and discussions on atmospheric thermodynamics and atmospheric radiology. Atmospheric thermodynamics discuss in detail the phase of water in the atmosphere, the condensation process, the dry insulation process, the wet insulation process, the mixing process, thermal effort and applications and static stability. Atmospheric radiation discusses the interaction of radiation and matter, solar radiation, long-wave radiation and radiation transmission, including when dispersed, and concludes with discussions and observations of radiation balance.

Name: Introduction to Time Series Analysis in Atmospheric Science
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, linear algebra, computational overview, algorithms and data structure
Introduction: The overview of time-series analysis in atmospheric science has been applied in practice to some of these knowledge, especially observational, re-analysis and simulation data in atmospheric science, mainly after basic courses in mathematics, linear algebrae, computational overview, algorithms and data structure, which are over-skilled in undergraduate science. The course focuses on basic concepts of time series analysis of single variables, basic knowledge and achievement of algorithms, and deepens students ' understanding through the application of practical atmospheric information.

Name: Fundamentals of Atmospheric Dynamics
Prerequisite: Hydrodynamics, advanced mathematics, linear algebras, mathematical physics equations, atmospheric physics, atmospheric detection Learn.
Introduction: This undergraduate course is a core course for students majoring in atmospheric science. The main teaching content is: the basic laws of atmospheric motion and its equations; atmospheric vortex motion; quasi-geostrophic theory; atmospheric boundary layer flow; atmospheric fluctuations. Through the study of this course, students will have a basic understanding of why and how the atmosphere moves.

Name: Probability Theory and Data Processing
Introduction: This course is aimed at graduate and undergraduate students majoring in particle physics and nuclear physics, as well as those who use large statistics and random data processing in practical work. This course first introduces the basic knowledge of stochastic processes and probability theory (the content includes "Preliminary Probability Theory"); then it focuses on the commonly used principles and methods of parameter estimation, error processing, and hypothesis testing when processing experimental data (content includes: experimental error, parameter estimation and maximum likelihood method, curve fitting and least squares method, pulse measurement statistics, spectral data processing, etc.), as well as the Monte Carlo simulation method widely used in nuclear physics and particle physics experiments. Practical examples are given mainly using common problems in nuclear physics and particle physics experiments. Based on the development of international data processing technology in the fields of high-energy physics and nuclear physics, this course also introduces the currently popular artificial neural networks, large-capacity data technology and commonly used software in large-scale experiments. Through the study of this course, students should be familiar with and understand the general rules and common techniques of experimental data processing, understand the development trends in this field; master the methods of deriving standardized and credible physical results from raw data; and thus quickly enter the research of the subject independently.

Name: Research Methods in Engineering Science
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Scientific research is one of the key components of university education. The current university curriculum rarely involves systematic presentation of scientific research methods. As a rule, undergraduate and graduate students in the lower grades learn their own experimental techniques and research methods by following their senior classmates into project research. Such learning methods are often less efficient and take longer to truly master effective research methods.
The course will focus on scientific research processes and methods of study of interest to students, in the form of lectures and discussions on subjects, for students who have just started or are about to start their scientific research. Through the curriculum, students are able to gain a more systematic understanding of the research methods required by modern science institutes and provide a solid foundation for future research work.

Name: Semiconductor Physics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic physical knowledge of semiconductors, including electronic states in semiconductors, charge transport properties, carrier balance statistics, pn junctions, MIS structures, gold-half contacts and heterojunctions, etc. After studying, students should be able to master the basic knowledge of semiconductor physics, especially the I-V characteristics of various contacts such as semiconductor pn junction, MIS structure, gold-half contact and heterojunction, and be able to flexibly apply them to semiconductor devices. _x000D_

Name: Astronomical Techniques and Methods I (Optical and Infrared)
Introduction: The course presents basic observation equipment used for optical and infrared astrophysics observations, observation methods and treatment of observational data.

Name: Observational Astrophysics Laboratory
Prerequisite: Basic astronomical, general astrophysics, astronomical technology and methods I (optics and infrared)
Introduction: The course is aimed at students with a certain knowledge of the fundamentals of astronomy and offers a range of experiments in astrophysics, such as astronomical observations, image photometry and spectral data processing. Through practical telescope operations, the observation and processing of scientific data, students have the basic knowledge of actual astronomical observations and data processing, which can be applied to specific astronomical observations and obtain preliminary measurements. Provides the knowledge preparation and operational basis for future astronomical observation research projects for students specializing in astronomy.

Name: Astrophysics Seminar
Prerequisite: With a certain mathematical base, it would be preferable to start with an astronomical course.
Introduction:
Astrophysics, one of the oldest natural sciences, has an irreplaceable role in the process of the development of human civilization, and astrophysics has been the dominant and most dynamic part of its development to date. Many of the terminology popular in academia, such as dark matter and dark energy, gravity waves, black holes and neutron stars, are inseparable from “astrophysics”. The extremes demonstrated by the processes of several celestial bodies, which are not comparable to those of terrestrial laboratories, provide excellent opportunities for human understanding of basic physical laws. The golden age of astrophysics in the twenty-first century will be ushered in by an increasing number of advanced space detectors and by observations beyond electromagnetic (cosmic rays, neutrons and even gravity waves). To adapt to this historical trend, international leading universities have been making “astrophysics” courses a core compulsory subject for astrophysics undergraduates and have placed emphasis on promoting astrophysics among students of the physics class. The course, which has been offered at Beijing University as a core basic course, is designed to introduce astrophysics to students in the astronomical and physical sciences in a systematic manner and to develop their basic astrophysics quality as a basis for further study of other relevant courses.

The Astrophysics Discussion Course is conducted independently of Astrophysics, and students may choose either or both during the semester.

Name: Fundamentals of Physical Cosmology
Introduction: Cosmology is the most active discipline in the 21st century and the foundation of modern astrophysics. This course will introduce the basic knowledge of cosmology, understand the development trends of cutting-edge research, and enable students to have a scientific understanding of the evolution of the universe.

Name: Introduction to Topology in Condensed Matter
Prerequisite: It is proposed to begin with theoretical physics, quantum mechanics, some higher quantum mechanics, solid physics, higher mathematics.
Introduction: This course mainly introduces a cutting-edge topic in the field of condensed matter physics - topological order and topological phase transition, including its basic concepts, basic theories and applications, and current development status. The content covers the analysis of topological invariants, Berry phase, Berry connection, Berry curvature and its application examples, topology, edge states, topological stability, gauge invariance, topological superconductors and Majorana fermions in various quantum Hall effects (including integer quantum Hall effect, spin quantum Hall effect, quantum anomalous Hall effect, etc.). The course structure mainly starts from the classic model of the integer quantum Hall effect, and then gradually understands the physical phenomena from the theory of topology, and proposes important concepts such as topological invariants. It uses it as a starting point to describe some condensed matter systems that topological order can realize in physics. It introduces topological phases such as Chern insulators, Haldane Chern insulators, Kane-Mele insulators, topological insulators, and topological superconductors. Learn from the perspectives of mathematics and physics, and gain an overall understanding of the application of topology in condensed matter physics.

Name: General Relativity and Astrophysics
Introduction:
Albert Einstein developed the general theory of relativity more than 100 years ago. It is a theory that describes gravity among the four fundamental interactions in the physical world. The elegant mathematical form and profound physical connotation make general relativity one of the most important crystallizations of wisdom in human exploration of physics. In particular, for more than a century, general relativity has passed experimental tests from various fields and has become the generally accepted theory of gravity. _x000D_
_x000D_
        Nowadays, almost all well-known universities in the world with physics majors involve teaching general relativity or related disciplines. This knowledge is also very necessary for students majoring in astrophysics and theoretical physics at Peking University. Students from other majors are also interested in understanding the content of general relativity. This course will meet students' needs in this area, lay the foundation for students to engage in gravity-related scientific research in the future, and provide necessary theoretical support for related disciplines, which is suitable for the country's general direction of developing a scientific and technological power. _x000D_
_x000D_
       This course will start from the basics and pave the way for students to learn the general theory of relativity in depth. First, the course provides a concise introduction to the physical foundations of general relativity, thereby introducing its mathematical structure, namely Einstein's field equations. Next, the course will combine the latest developments in this field to discuss several simple and classic applications of field equations, including the weak-field low-speed approximation of Einstein's field equations, four classic experimental tests, vacuum sphere symmetry solutions, neutron stars and black holes, gravitational waves, etc. If there is time, some cosmology will be briefly touched upon. _x000D_

Name: Reading in Astronomical Literature
Prerequisite: "Basic Astronomy", "Astrophysics", "Astronomical Technology and Methods" I, II, "Stellar Atmosphere and Celestial Spectrum", "Theoretical Mechanics", "Electrodynamics", "Atomic Physics", "Advanced Mathematics"
Introduction:
Access to scientific and technical literature and specialized academic reports are basic skills that must be available to undergraduates and professionals at every senior level.
The course will provide an overview of important magazines in the astronomical field, as well as important astronomical literature and databases, and will present the structure, writing points and reading techniques of scientific and technical articles by analysing specific astronomical classic articles. Schoolmates exercise and practice a standard academic report and exchange skills based on their reading of astronomical professional literature. Through this course, students will learn not only the astronomical frontier, the classics, important literature, but also, and more importantly, the ability to interact with their astronomical counterparts.

Name: Theoretical Astrophysics
Prerequisite: “Basic astronomy”, “Electrodynamics”, “theoretical mechanics”, “atomic physics” or “quantitative mechanics”, “statistical physics”, “high-level mathematics”, “magnetic physics methods”.
Introduction: This is a compulsory course for undergraduate students in astronomy. The main elements of the course's study are: macro-writing of the physical volume of radiation fields, radiation-material interactions and absorption, the transfer equation of radiation in gaseous substances, local thermal balance assumptions and their possible deviations, radiation-absorption lines of the substance, composite fluorescent mechanisms for generating radiation lines, spectral stretching physics mechanisms, and learning how to model the star atmosphere.

Name: Astronomical Spectroscopy
Introduction:
? Review and expand knowledge of atomic physics and quantum physics _x000D_
? Discuss the structures, energy levels and transitions of atoms and molecules that are important in astrophysics_x000D_
? Discuss various important atomic and molecular physical processes in astrophysics_x000D_
? Analyze the formation and excitation mechanism of celestial emission lines and absorption lines in the entire electromagnetic band from X-rays to radio_x000D_
?The entire course will always emphasize various atomic and molecular physical processes, the observation of atomic and molecular spectral lines and their applications in astrophysics_x000D_

Name: Atomic and Molecular Spectroscopy
Introduction: This course is a required course for postgraduate students majoring in physical optics and an elective course for senior undergraduates. It mainly introduces the relationship between atomic and molecular spectra and atomic and molecular structures. It focuses on the basic knowledge of rotation, vibration and electronic spectra of diatomic molecules and polyatomic molecules. With the help of experimentally observed spectra, it explains the relationship between spectral phenomena and the internal structure of molecules. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic knowledge of atomic and molecular spectroscopy, understand the cutting-edge research of atomic and molecular physics, and lay the foundation for professional research in atomic and molecular physics.

Name: Topics in Astrophysics
Prerequisite:
At least two astronomy courses, such as Basic Astronomy and Astrophysics, were completed.
There is some knowledge of the general direction of the astronomical study.
Introduction: In this course, students who choose this course will participate in weekly symposiums held by research groups of the Department of Astronomy in the School of Physics or the Kavli Institute, and learn about the latest developments and hot issues in astrophysics through literature reading, academic discussions, academic reports, special research, etc., and initially master the basic methods, means and resources of astrophysics research, train and cultivate the basic ability to conduct scientific research, and lay a solid foundation for subsequent thesis research topics.

Name: Weather Analysis and Forecasting
Prerequisite: No requirements, but it would have been better if the Weather had been modified first.
Introduction:
This course is suitable for fourth-year undergraduate students and first-year graduate students whose undergraduate background is not majoring in atmospheric science. This course provides students with a unique opportunity to learn basic skills in weather analysis and forecasting. Students can learn basic and comprehensive knowledge of weather science, atmospheric dynamics, satellite meteorology, and radar meteorology from this course. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course content includes: basic principles of weather analysis and forecasting, basic concepts of weather-scale weather systems, such as blocking high pressure, fronts and cyclones, continuous rain in South China, plum rains, subtropical high pressure, typhoons, cold waves, seasonal changes with circulation, etc.

Name: Introduction to Conflict Studies
Prerequisite: History of international relations, political doctrine
Introduction: An optional course at the Institute of International Relations is characterized by a greater use of foreign research results, with more in-depth and theoretical aspects of conflict research.

Name: Computational Neuroscience
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Computational neuroscience is a new interdisciplinary subject that has developed rapidly in recent years regarding the study of nervous system functions. It absorbs basic theoretical fields such as mathematics and physics, as well as research theories and methods from related fields such as information science, to study the working principles of the brain that neuroscience is concerned about, and at the same time lays the foundation for the development of brain-like computing. It is a typical cutting-edge interdisciplinary subject that plays an important bridge role between brain science and artificial intelligence. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will systematically introduce the basic content and latest developments in the field of computational neuroscience, laying a complete foundation for students who are interested in engaging in computational or experimental neuroscience research. It will also expand the relevant knowledge of biological intelligence for students who are committed to brain-like computing or artificial intelligence research. The course content covers most basic knowledge in the field of computational neuroscience, including: neuron dynamics, synaptic dynamics, neural coding, neural network models, visual information processing mechanisms, multi-modal information integration, and the application of neuroscience knowledge in brain-like computing. The teaching method is mainly in Chinese, and the assessment method is to submit technical reports.

Name: Introduction to Visualization and Visual Computing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Reinforcement Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Artificial Intelligence Introduction

Students are required to master basic concepts and methods of artificial intelligence and have some practical experience in modelling and training programming.
Introduction: Reinforcement learning refers simultaneously to a class of problems, solutions to such problems, and an area of ​​research to these problems and solutions. Reinforcement learning solves the problem of how to choose appropriate actions in different environments in order to optimize a certain profit goal. It is usually assumed that the payoff of an action cannot be known until after it is executed, so the key issue is how to balance the exploration of unknown situations (which may have no payoff) with the problem of prioritizing actions with known better payoffs to maximize the overall payoff. This field has received widespread attention and continued research in recent years with the success of AlphaGo and AlphaZero. This course will introduce some problems in reinforcement learning research, existing solutions and latest progress through some problem examples. It is hoped that students will master the basic concepts and methods of reinforcement learning through reading and practical practice, and have the basic ability to apply reinforcement learning methods to solve practical problems, and lay the foundation for subsequent research in the field of reinforcement learning.

Name: Nanochemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: University physics, inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, analytical chemistry, structural chemistry, physical chemistry
Introduction:
Nanochemistry is a new branch of chemistry, a science that studies various chemical problems and their applications in the nanometer world (mesoscopic world) above atoms and below 100 nanometers. The research object of nanochemistry is a collection of atoms or molecules with at least one dimension below 100 nanometers. Its main tasks are to study chemical preparation methods of nanomaterials and structures, and to explore the properties and reaction laws of finite atomic or molecular systems. _x000D_
"Nanochemistry" is a professional elective course for chemistry majors. It studies the structure, properties and preparation methods of various important nanomaterials such as zero-dimensional materials, one-dimensional materials, two-dimensional materials, nano-mesoporous materials, various characterization methods, and typical device application characteristics. The main task of this course is to enable students majoring in chemistry to have a broad understanding of the chemical knowledge of new nanomaterials, and to provide the necessary knowledge and methods for future work, study and graduation thesis experiments.

Name: Stereochemistry
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: As one of the core fields in chemistry, stereochemistry has an important influence on and closely governs many aspects of the entire discipline. This course comprehensively teaches the knowledge system and development trends of stereochemistry in theory, experiment, application and other aspects. Specifically, it first describes the history, development, basic principles and concepts of stereochemistry, and the theoretical system that has been formed, so that students can have a comprehensive understanding of stereochemistry. This will prepare you for the next stage of specific content in various areas of stereochemistry. In further in-depth study of the two most important aspects of stereochemistry: asymmetric organic synthesis and asymmetric catalysis, it provides the necessary knowledge system for students majoring in organic chemistry. The second part of the tutorial further expands students' horizons and knowledge, covering stereochemistry in biological systems, drug stereochemistry, related inorganic stereochemistry, polymer stereochemistry and other branches.

Name: Chemical Biology Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: "Chemical Biology Experiment" aims to cultivate the interest and understanding of chemical biology as an emerging subject among undergraduate students majoring in chemistry, and train students to initially master the related technologies and methods commonly used in chemical biology research (especially those in biology). The course design is divided into four groups of experiments, including peptide synthesis, mass spectrometry analysis, molecular cloning, protein purification, nucleic acid modification, enzyme activity detection, site-directed insertion of unnatural amino acids, and bioorthogonal reactions and many other technical methods commonly used in chemical biology research.

Name: Studies in Paradox (Discussion Section)
Prerequisite:
Logical introduction
The course attempts to teach students a general idea of logic, the broad overall image of logical development to date, some of the most basic logical techniques and techniques, and the thoughts and spirit hidden behind logic technology. Specific elements include the following: first, logic is about the science of reasoning and reasoning, outlining the overall image of logic; second, subject logic, studying the logical nature of complex propositions determined by the synonyms and the reasoning between complex propositions; third, word logic, studying the logical nature of direct propositions (characters of nature) and the reasoning between them; and fourth, terminology logic, examining the logical nature of quantitative propositions and the reasoning between them. The subject logic, word logic and word logic are the focus of the course. In addition to this, the basic elements of the reasoning are taught.
Introduction:
Paradoxical studies

Some of the famous paradoxes that have been raised in history will be taught, including the Zino paradox and the infinity of the puzzle, ambiguity: the chain paradoxes, the logical-mathematic paradoxes, the semantic paradoxes, the taboos and the general paradoxes, the cognitive paradoxes, the paradox of rational action and decision-making, the moral paradox, the ancient Chinese paradox, further reflections on the paradoxes, etc. The main objectives of this course, which does not focus on the transfer of knowledge, are: to break the mindset of students through discussion and reflection of paradoxes, to expand their space of reason, to stimulate their intellectual curiosity, to foster their habit of independent thinking, to make them possible as creators and producers of knowledge; to develop a healthy, moderate skepticism attitude and a civilized attitude of tolerance and acceptance, and to make them independent, responsible citizens in democratic societies.
The course is part of a three-point series of general selections for undergraduate and postgraduate students from the North.

Name: Symphony (Introductory)
Introduction: This course is rehearsed for Symphony Orchestras and is aimed at first-year undergraduate students who have just joined the Orchestra. The content of the course is centred on the band ' s training tracks, and rehearsals and performances are organized by band leaders and mentors.

Name: Materials Physics
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
This course will understand the physical properties of materials from the perspective of condensed matter physics. You will learn the specific physical properties of materials such as mechanics, heat, electricity, magnetism, and light. You will learn to conduct qualitative or quantitative analysis of these properties, and understand these properties from the combination of atoms or molecules, crystal structure, electromagnetic structure, microstructure, interface, etc. Through these studies, it is possible to analyze the inherent governing factors from the observed properties and predict the physical properties of materials within a certain range. _x000D_
This course will introduce students to the electronic theory of materials, crystal structure, defects, microstructure, interface structure, low-dimensional materials (structure, size effect, quantum effect), mechanical properties (hardness, strength, plastic deformation, fracture), thermal properties (thermal expansion, specific heat, heat conduction), electrical conductivity properties (carriers, resistance, superconductivity), and magnetic properties (magnets, magnetization, magnetic regions, anisotropy). _x000D_

Name: Nature Conservation: Ideas and Practice
Introduction:
In 2011, the global population reached 7 billion, of which an increase of 5 billion occurred in just 85 years. Human needs have caused large-scale species extinction, the rapid decline of natural ecology, increasingly serious environmental pollution, and may even accelerate climate change... These crises have actually happened around everyone, affecting everyone's lives in various aspects such as health, quality of life, wealth, culture, etc. By 2050, the global population will reach 10 billion. If ecological and environmental issues cannot arouse the knowledge and participation of the majority of the world's people, the situation may be worse. In recent years, the Chinese government has raised ecological protection to a very high political level and implemented it in various industries at the grassroots level. Along with the positive changes, there are also some lack of scientific basis and inefficient practices. The broader concept and awareness of nature protection and the necessary scientific and practical knowledge are the shortcomings that China's ecological protection currently faces. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
This course is a general education version of Conservation Biology and is open to students from all departments. Conservation biology is a comprehensive discipline that emerged in the West in the 1980s. Its purpose is to solve the crisis of rapid decline in biodiversity caused by excessive population growth and excessive destruction of natural resources. Conservation biology in my country began to rise in the 1990s and has attracted increasing attention due to the growing environmental crisis. Conservation biology is a new discipline that responds to the current crisis and focuses on urgency. "Conservation" is its key word. This discipline aims to propose feasible solutions and is faced with the challenge of a large number of "uncertainty" problems. It needs to integrate interdisciplinary knowledge and pay close attention to the combination with practical actions; it not only needs to face the short-term crisis, but also needs to focus on the long-term effects on the evolutionary scale. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
The conservation biology course at Peking University was started by Professor Pan Wenshi in 1995. The current two teachers of this course have been involved in teaching this course from the beginning. They have more than 35 years (Lv Zhi) and 25 years (Wang Hao) of academic research and practical accumulation in the field of conservation biology respectively. They are active in domestic and international policy formulation, front-line actions of civil organizations, protected areas and enterprises, scientific research, citizen science and other fields. They can share the system of nature conservation, rich cases and the latest personal experiences with students in theory and practice. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is taught to students from all disciplines in the school. The content of the course starts from understanding and understanding the values and goals of natural ecology and biodiversity protection, as well as the philosophical ethics and scientific thinking behind it, and introduces cases in the field of international and domestic biodiversity protection; popularizing biodiversity knowledge from the levels of genes, species, ecosystems, etc.; from the perspective of protection It explains the practice of conservation from design to protected area actions; it demonstrates the integration of biology, economics, sociology, culture and other disciplines in nature conservation through examples such as giant pandas, snow leopards, and Sanjiangyuan; it also invites people on the front line of conservation from governments, non-governmental organizations, scientific research institutions, and ordinary citizens to introduce the most cutting-edge and hot topics in domestic and foreign conservation. _x000D_
_x000D_
The goals of this course are: to popularize the knowledge of conservation biology, guide students to recognize and understand the value of nature and biodiversity conservation, broaden and deepen students' perspectives on conservation issues, improve students' ability to use comprehensive knowledge to solve conservation problems, and implant the seeds of nature conservation in students' future career development. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Tagore
Introduction: The year 2011 marks the 150th anniversary of the birth of the greatest poet, literaryist and philosopher of India in recent times. As the first decade of the new century draws to a close, it is important to understand and re-evaluate the East-West culture and to increase understanding and friendship between China and India by re-reading the work and ideas of Tegor. The course seeks to conform to his original intent, namely, to reveal his main spirit, paying due attention to the diversity, complexity and inherently contradictory aspects of his manifestations, and to carry out multi-dimensional, multi-dimensional excavations to reveal the mythology, ethnology, philosophy, psychology, political science, history and literature of the great institutions and beliefs of the Tygor, especially the multiplicity of the key words. - Get as close as possible to the Tegor incarnate and reveal its true nature.

Name: Selected Topics in Chemical Kinetics
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Chemical kinetics is an important branch of physico-chemistry, which includes two aspects: macro-chemical reaction rates and mechanics (kinetics), micro-chemical fundamental processes dynamics (dynamics) and molecular reaction dynamics (molecular reaction dynamics). Building on the Physico-Chemicals course, the course provides students with further basic knowledge of chemical dynamics, research progress and frontier dynamics. This course has two main objectives, namely, to teach theoretical knowledge of chemical reactions, with knowledge of related areas, and to develop an understanding of chemical dynamics as a research method and tool that can be useful for future scientific research in other areas such as chemical biology and organic chemistry. The content of the course is divided into five parts, one on reaction speed and reaction mechanics, including a review of key chemical dynamics concepts, the relationship between reaction rates and response mechanisms and prediction of response mechanisms; the other on chemical reaction theory, which introduces the concepts of reaction cross-section and power surface, collision theory, transition-state theory (RRKM theory), etc., and further understanding of relevant theories based on the physical chemistry curriculum; the third on catalytic reaction dynamics and surface reaction dynamics, which mainly describe concepts and applications derived from chemical dynamics in the field of homogeneity and multi-comparability, as well as dynamic methods used in catalytic and surface chemistry studies; the other on hydrochemical reaction dynamics, which includes characteristics of the reverse of the fluid, treatment of kinetic control and proliferation control reactions, Marcus electronic transfer reaction theory, and important experimental research methods; and the other on the front lines of photochemical and atmospheric chemistry and molecular reaction dynamics. The course is focused on narratives and requires students to have relevant literature access, to write small literature reviews and to report and discuss with the classroom.

Introduction: In-depth learning and mastery of the basic theory of chromatography and cavity electronism, as well as of mass spectrometry, instrument structure and main operating parameters, based on the course on quantitative and instrument analysis, and the ability to apply chromatography and cavity analysis methods to solve practical problems. Name: Biochemical Analysis
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Analysis of chemistry is the discipline in which the composition and structure of the substance is measured and displayed, and is an important support for the development of all disciplines; biochemical analysis can be seen as the third transformation product of the analysis of chemistry, a biochemistry-related discipline, using analytical chemical manifestations to produce in situ, real-time, non-destructive research biomolecules, or single-cell, mono-molecules, etc. Biochemical analysis is a very broad discipline, and the course will focus on the most basic elements.
For example, the classification of mega-molecules, the composition and purity of proteins, chromatography separation, gel electro-simulation and hair tube electro-simulation applications, mass spectroscopy analysis and immunological analysis.

Name: General Geology (Earth Materials Systems)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Course on Earth science in general
Introduction: The teaching content of "General Geology - Earth Material System" is mainly adapted to the needs of current economic construction and talent training for the 21st century. It also refers to various relevant latest teaching materials from the United Kingdom, the United States, Russia and other countries, and has made major changes to the teaching content and teaching methods of the course.

Name: Integrated Physical Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Comprehensiveness is one of the basic characteristics of geography. Comprehensive physical geography is a discipline founded and named by Chinese scholars, and its emergence has direct origins with Peking University. Comprehensive physical geography has long been a required course for undergraduates at Peking University. The famous geographers Professor Lin Chao and Professor Chen Chuangkang have taught this course. This course explains the integrity of the physical geographical environment on the basis of introducing the research objects, content, purpose, characteristics and the relationship with the content of various disciplines of departmental physical geography. First, the spatial and temporal geographical laws of the natural geographical environment are discussed. The spatial geographical laws mainly discuss the regional differentiation and combination laws of the natural geographical environment; the temporal geographical laws mainly discuss the causes, occurrence, development, succession and change laws of the natural geographical environment. Secondly, the division of natural geographical hierarchical units at the regional scale - the theory and method of natural zoning - is discussed, focusing on the principles, methods and hierarchical systems of comprehensive natural zoning. Thirdly, the division of natural geographical hierarchical units at the local scale - land is discussed. Typology, focusing on the principles and research methods of land classification, classification and grading; fourth, a systematic introduction to the research frontiers of comprehensive physical geography, mainly involving land change science, comprehensive evaluation of ecosystems, and landscape ecology; fifth, the dialectical relationship between humans and the natural geographical environment is discussed from the perspective of the development of human-land relationship ideas and sustainable development. Finally, the application of comprehensive physical geography in agricultural development, landscape ecological design, tourism development, urban planning, regional development, and natural environment development prediction is analyzed. This course lays the foundation for training students to engage in comprehensive geography research, land science, regional scientific research, natural zoning, land resources survey, regional development and land remediation, urban planning, etc.

Name: Biochemistry
Introduction: This course will introduce the chemical nature of life, including the structural characteristics and functions of various major molecules that make up life (such as proteins, nucleic acids, sugars and lipids, etc.), the decomposition and anabolism of living substances, the energetics of life, etc.

Name: Advanced Macroeconomics (I)
Introduction: This course is designed for graduate students who do not intend to pursue a PhD in economics or to pursue a more comprehensive advanced macroeconomics course (one academic year). However, this course is still at an upper level of macroeconomics. Taking into account the study time limit of one semester, it is impossible for this course to accommodate exactly the same level of capacity as "Advanced Macroeconomics" for PhD students. Therefore, this course is appropriately streamlined from the "Advanced Macroeconomics" course, but the scope of knowledge is basically the same. Therefore, to study this course, you still need to have studied undergraduate "intermediate macroeconomics" and have some corresponding mathematical tools and related necessary knowledge.

Name: Fundamentals of NMR Spectroscopy
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Prerequisite: General chemistry, university physics, advanced mathematics, instrument analysis
Introduction: MRI spectrometry is one of the conventional means of chemical analysis and is widely applied in the material, biological and medical fields. The course is devoted to the fundamentals, status and future development of MRI and its application in small molecular analysis, high molecular and biomolecular research. This course is the basic part of MRI spectrum analysis, including the basic principles of MRI and onboard internships.

Name: Physics in the Life Sciences (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is mainly suitable for undergraduate students majoring in life sciences. It mainly covers the main contents of general physics such as mechanics and statistical physics, especially closely integrating examples and applications from biology and medicine. Through the study of this course, on the one hand, you will master the content of general physics and understand the importance of physical laws in the life process, and at the same time, you will lay a solid foundation for the application of physical ideas and methods in the study of modern biology in the future.

Name: Integrated Biology Field Practicum
Introduction: Biology field practice is an important learning content and basic teaching training for biology undergraduates. It is an important link for students to understand biodiversity and its relationship with the environment. It is not only a necessary supplement to the classroom knowledge and indoor experimental content of animal biology, plant biology and other biology courses, but also has unique form, content and effect. The content includes the identification of the main groups of plants in different habitats, the identification of terrestrial plants and marine intertidal zone algae, and the collection and preservation methods of specimens. The identification of the main groups of terrestrial animals (mainly insects) and marine intertidal zone animals, rodent population surveys, bird environmental records and animal behavior observations, and the collection and production methods of animal specimens. Through field practice, we cultivate students' ability to independently discover and solve problems, stimulate students' desire to explore the mysteries of nature, and then love nature and life sciences from the heart. In addition, field internships are also classrooms that cultivate the spirit of mutual help, unity and cooperation among classmates.

Name: Physics in the Life Sciences (Part 2)
Introduction: This course is geared primarily to undergraduate studies in the life sciences and covers the main elements of general physics, such as mechanics, statistical physics and electromagnetics, in particular the close integration of examples and applications from biology and medicine. Through the study of this course, knowledge of the general physical content and the importance of physical laws in the course of life is provided, while at the same time laying the foundation for the future application of physics in the study of modern biology.

Name: Bird Ecology and Conservation
Introduction: Bird Ecology and Conservation is a basic macrobiology course for undergraduate students from the Institute of Life Sciences of Beijing University and related disciplines, in the direction of zoological and ecological sciences. Courses are optional and are not subject to prior requirements. The course consists of three main components: 1) basic ecological content such as bird origin, classification, reproduction, migration, beeping, etc., 2) technical content such as field surveys, research methods, and 3) biodiversity conservation of birds. The course is planned to be held during the autumn semester for 17 weeks, with two hours per week. The course combines two forms of indoor teaching with outdoor internships, which are divided according to different modules of bird ecology and conservation, with a total of 26 hours per module of 2-6 hours. The out-of-door internships were based on six academic hours with the University of Beijing ' s Animal Sample Homes and Yan Gardens, including bird specimen tours and lectures, school-based bird ecology observations and bird survey methods. The final course of the term is the final examination, with two hours. In total, 34 school hours and 17 classes.

Name: Creative Practice
Introduction:
As our society and economy continue to develop, innovative talent is the most important expression of core competitiveness in the process of the great renaissance of the Chinese nation. Higher education institutions play an important role in the development of innovative talent. The ability to think, judge and learn independently is an essential foundation for innovative talent, and the development of these skills requires the integration of new teaching concepts and methods of learning into reforms and practices.
The ancient cloud: “The one who knows is less than the one who knows is the one who is better than the one who is happy.” That is to say, interest is the greatest motivation for learning, and pleasure is the best form of learning. Interest in the content of the studies and research will be entertained and, in turn, will lead to a proactive approach that fully mobilizes students ' initiative and creativity while improving learning efficiency. This “good” “joy” learning component, when combined with theoretical learning and practical activities, maximizes the ability of students to understand and apply knowledge flexibly.
The curriculum is based on the above-mentioned innovative talent development as its main objective, starting from the students' “good” and “joyful” curiosity and interest, with the individualized practice project as its vehicle, based on open multidisciplinary resources, guaranteed by a multidisciplinary team of mentors, fully mobilizing students' subjective mobility, encouraging them to identify problems in their fields of interest, setting up projects and learning independently, independently and spontaneously in practice, discovering and developing their innovative ways of thinking and practice through self-discovery, self-organization and self-organization, and developing their capacity for communication, collaboration, management and scientific expression, so as to truly be innovative in nature with harmonious personality, solid foundation and comprehensive competence.

Name: Laboratory Safety
Introduction:
The laboratory is the basic environment for colleges and universities to cultivate students' practical abilities and conduct scientific research. Biological laboratory safety is highly scientific and complex and requires systematic guidance and learning. Ensuring laboratory safety is the basic prerequisite for students to complete their studies and achieve results. At the same time, the construction of laboratory safety culture and the protection of environmental safety outside the laboratory are also basic qualities that personnel who conduct scientific research, study and training, especially graduates from world-class universities, should have. _x000D_
    This course systematically and comprehensively introduces all aspects of basic knowledge involved in laboratory safety, including general concepts, general principles, routine protection, technical specifications, animal safety, radiation safety, hazardous chemical safety, electrical safety, waste disposal and emergency treatment, etc. Through the study of this course, students will be equipped with the basic concepts and necessary knowledge for safe operations in the laboratory, so as to provide reliable guarantee for the safety of themselves, others and the environment. _x000D_

Name: Historical Vignettes of Modern Molecular Biology
Prerequisite: This course focuses on recent molecular biology and basic theory. It is hoped that students will have basic knowledge of biology and an interest in molecular biology.
Introduction: The course focuses on interesting people, discoveries and research-related stories in recent molecular biology, and critically reflects on the theoretical foundations of recent molecular biology.

Name: Fundamentals of Bioinformatics
Introduction:
This course mainly includes the following content_x000D_
1) Commonly used commands in Linux systems_x000D_
2) Basic operations of Linux system_x000D_
3) Linux system text editing_x000D_

Name: Fundamentals and Practice of Engineering Technology
Introduction: In response to the current state of the general engineering skills base and the need to improve hands-on hands-on skills of students specializing in biology, the course provides the necessary engineering skills training for undergraduate students specializing in biology, covering such areas as mechanical design, electronic circuit design, computer interface and control. With the strong support of the Institute of Life Sciences, a specialized engineering course laboratory was established for the course, and teaching and training facilities such as machine beds, 3D printers, electronic components and computer interface control were acquired. The course will not only provide basic theoretical lectures on engineering techniques, but also provide students with practical training in mechanics, electronics and computer control, improve their hands-on and problem-solving skills across the board and lay a solid foundation for subsequent scientific research.

Name: Spanish Language and Culture
Prerequisite: None. Students are not required to have a Spanish base.
Introduction: The Spanish language and Spanish culture (primary level) is an updated version of the Spanish cultural review, which was launched in 2013. The older version of the course, “Spanish and Spanish Culture (Preliminary)”, is part of the Spanish language study, which helps students at the zero starting point to acquire basic knowledge of Spanish and the usual expressions. The curriculum, which is based on the concept of “linguistic, cultural and spiritual”, is aimed, in terms of language, at providing students with an accurate command of Spanish pronunciation methods and spelling rules, a general understanding of the grammar of Spanish and the ability to use common language in areas such as catering, shopping, tourism and friendship. With regard to culture, the course is guided by specific cultural forms, such as food, festivals and human heritage, which lead the students into Spain and lead them to a detailed and in-depth understanding of the way in which the Spanish think, their ethnic identity, and to open a new door for those who may study, work, or travel, visit, or even work with Spanish.

Name: Neural Development and Plasticity
Introduction: This course is a post-graduate course and is taught entirely in English. The teaching content includes: neural development, neural circuit formation, synaptic plasticity, developmental neurological diseases, etc. The course will provide an in-depth understanding of the current status and challenges in these fields through the reading of classic and cutting-edge literature, as well as classroom narration and discussion. The course includes an introduction and background introduction by the instructor, as well as oral reports on the designated literature by students. Before each class, each student is required to submit a reading report (one page) of the literature read that day. In each class, two students jointly interpret a piece of literature, and then everyone asks questions and discusses it. At the end of each class, the teacher will comment on the students' reports, including the content and expression, and supplement the knowledge points that the students have insufficiently reported. The characteristic of this course is that it is mainly based on student reports, and all oral and written reports are completed in English. While learning neuroscience knowledge, students will have many opportunities to practice English written and oral expression, as well as gain an in-depth understanding of the progress and challenges of cutting-edge disciplines through discussions.

Name: Biological Fluorescence Imaging
Introduction: Biofluorescence imaging is the most commonly used technology in life sciences, and technologies such as ultra-high-resolution fluorescence imaging that have emerged since the 21st century have greatly promoted the development of basic research. This course will start from the principles of fluorescent dye/protein luminescence, and introduce imaging technologies such as wide-field fluorescence imaging, confocal, two-photon, ultra-high-resolution imaging, fluorescence resonance energy transfer, image analysis principles and applications.

Name: Frontier Literature Reading and Discussion in Life Sciences (4)
Introduction:
The cutting-edge literature discussion course in life sciences is a literature discussion course offered by the School of Life Sciences. The main teaching targets are students in the intensive challenge class of life sciences. This course will continue the characteristics of the intensive challenge class literature discussion class. A literature discussion class will be organized by student groups. With the help of the instructor, they will independently select several cutting-edge issues in biology, such as neural circuit, circadian rhythm, etc., and systematically explain the origin of the field, the emergence of important concepts, discuss the core original literature in the field, and explore what are the current main issues and challenges. Each literature discussion invites experts in the field to guide the discussion process and guide students' academic speeches. _x000D_
The course reference book is the classic textbook The Craft of Scientific Presentations: Critical Steps to Succeed and Critical Errors to Avoid, Springer. Through this course, students need to master basic academic presentation skills and lay a solid foundation for future academic communication. _x000D_
This course is a required course for students in the life science intensive challenge class. _x000D_

Name: Behavioral Neuroscience
Prerequisite: Physiology or neurobiology, advanced neurobiology Learn.
Introduction: The course will focus on the relationship between brain and behavior, and will cover subjects such as learning and memory, psychopharmacology, sensory neuroscience, sports, emotions, high cognitive functions, and diseases of the nervous system. The curriculum focuses on the integration of basic knowledge narratives and analysis of classical research articles.

Name: Introduction to Nuclear Law and Policy

"Introduction to Nuclear Law and Policy" is one of the publicly elected courses offered by Peking University Law School to all undergraduates. The main teaching content of this course includes nine major topics: an overview of nuclear law and policy, basic principles of nuclear law, the subject of nuclear law, nuclear energy utilization and licensing, safety control of nuclear facilities, safety control of nuclear activities, nuclear emergency, nuclear damage compensation, nuclear security and non-proliferation. It will comprehensively and systematically discuss the basic concepts and basic content of nuclear law, historical evolution and development, basic principles of nuclear law, nuclear and radiation supervision legal systems, and responsibilities in nuclear law. In addition, the course will also give a brief introduction to the nuclear law practices of major countries in the world and relevant international treaties. _x000D_
     The Introduction to Nuclear Law and Policy course is divided into nine aspects: an overview of nuclear law, basic principles of nuclear law, the main body of nuclear law, nuclear energy utilization and licensing, safety control of nuclear facilities, safety control of nuclear activities, nuclear emergency, nuclear damage compensation, nuclear security and non-proliferation. This course systematically teaches the basic concepts, basic theories and basic applications of nuclear law and policy. _x000D_
     This course is still blank in domestic universities. Considering that this course is a public elective course and is suitable for undergraduates from all majors in the school, the teaching of this course will be conducted using case-assisted teaching methods. _x000D_
     This course is suitable for third-year undergraduates majoring in nuclear physics and engineering, nuclear medicine and applied chemistry, and law, as well as undergraduates in natural sciences, humanities and social sciences, and other disciplines and interdisciplinary disciplines.

Name: Biology of Aging
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of cell biology and genetics.
Introduction: As the population of our country and many developed countries around the world enters an aging society, aging has become a subject that has a significant impact on society and development. Aging and healthy old age have also become current hot topics and research areas. This course teaches the basic principles and current main theories of aging, focuses on introducing aging knowledge that is closely related to human life and health, reveals the scientific relationship between aging and the occurrence of many aging-related diseases such as cancer, neurodegenerative diseases, and cardiovascular diseases that are generally concerned by society. It introduces the current major progress in aging science and its profound impact on current human society and the future. It also explains the current potential anti-aging approaches and practical significance, as well as the opportunities and challenges faced by anti-aging.

Name: Transactional Analysis in Interpersonal Communication
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Interpersonal communication analysis (Transactional Analysis, also translated into interactive analysis) was initiated by American scholar E. Burn, whose main thrust was to study the psychological patterns that people interact with each other in communication and communication, and to observe people by analysing their performance in communication, with a view to identifying the psychological factors that hinder communication and extract healthy communication patterns from them. Analysis of interpersonal communication not only helps us to better communicate with others, but also provides us with a psychological approach to growing up with others.
Analysis of interpersonal communication is currently one of the psychological theories that is very popular internationally. This theory is both an efficient psychotherapy theory and a very efficient psychological self-help tool that can effectively promote human mental health and enhance the quality of life and well-being of people.

College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The level of exploitation of mineral resources is a measure of the maturity of a country ' s industrialization, and mineral material science is the cornerstone of the second Stone Age of humankind. Western developed countries buy minerals from our country at very low prices, adding tens or hundreds of times more to the value of their products through deep processing, for which we need to pay a great deal of foreign exchange, to learn the science of mineral materials, to study new types of energy minerals and environmental mineral materials, to promote the high-value utilization of our mineral resources, to achieve the recycling of solid waste and to develop high-performance materials of good quality and affordable quality. The Scientific Overview of Mineral Materials will focus on the student system ' s understanding of the scientific systems and characteristics of materials; an overview of the system of material science disciplines, basic concepts, material types and classifications, principles and methods of material preparation, and the four main clusters of material composition, structure, performance, use, etc. and their interrelationships. Presentation of new results, trends, new information and foreground topics in mineral materials science. Description of major mineral material types and new high technology materials.

College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

This course systematically explains how to apply numerical simulation to space physics to describe the basic physical processes of natural phenomena in space, including single particle dynamics, magnetohydrodynamics, plasma dynamics and other processes. Introduce the applicable conditions and application directions of different numerical simulation methods. Describe in detail how to carry out numerical simulation, such as problem definition, numerical format, initial and boundary conditions, programming, multi-dimensional dynamic visualization, etc.

Name: Magnetospheric Physics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite:
Earth science overview (geophysics and space physics)
Space plasma physics base
Introduction: Understand the near-Earth space environment, understand the formation and dynamic processes of various regions of the magnetosphere, the main physical processes of the formation of auroral substorms, understand the mechanism of magnetic storms and their triggering mechanisms; understand the dynamic changes in the space environment where artificial satellites - low-orbit satellites (LEO), medium-orbit satellites (MEO), geosynchronous orbit satellites (GEO) and cross-orbit satellites (GTO) are located.

College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: Sustainable Campus Practice
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
University campuses have superior conditions for students' creativity, innovation and entrepreneurship. They shoulder the mission and responsibility of leading social development. They are also the first step for students to move from theory to practice and from the classroom to society. Sustainable development is the theme of ecological civilization construction. A sustainable campus, sometimes called a green campus, is to incorporate the theories and ideas of sustainable development into the daily teaching and management of the school.       Peking University is one of the first universities to carry out green campus construction and is a member of the Global Sustainable Campus Alliance.       This course takes sustainable campus practice as the theme, starting from the perspectives of campus management system, sustainable technology application, campus space planning, campus resource and energy utilization, etc., and using specific project design as a carrier to enable students to construct the overall conceptual framework of a sustainable campus, understand relevant theories and methods, master the implementation details of how to start from themselves and around them, understand the processes, factors involved, and existing difficulties, and finally form ideas and methods to solve problems. _x000D_
