      This course is open to all students in the school, making full use of the academic advantages of interdisciplinary and free exploration, fully mobilizing and cultivating the multi-disciplinary, multi-specialty and multi-personality cooperation abilities among students, and creating an atmosphere of innovation and creation. _x000D_

Name: Systems Theory and Systemic Psychotherapy
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
System Approach as a scientific discipline was founded by L. Von Bertalanffy, an Austrian-American and theoretical biologist. His monograph published in 1968: "General System Theory: Foundations, Development, Applications" is considered the foundation of systems theory. _x000D_
A system refers to an organic whole that is composed of several elements connected in a certain structural form and has a certain function. Everything from the universe to the microscopic atoms can be viewed as a system. The whole world is a collection of systems. _x000D_
Systems theory believes that openness, self-organization, complexity, integrity, relevance, and dynamic balance are the basic characteristics common to all systems. The core idea of ​​systems theory is the overall concept of the system. Any system is an organic whole, rather than a mechanical combination or simple addition of various parts. The overall function of the system is a property that each element does not have in isolation. At the same time, each element in the system does not exist in isolation. Each element has a certain position in the system and plays a specific role. The elements are interrelated and form an indivisible whole. An element is an element of a whole. _x000D_
The research objects of systems theory are various systems. Its basic thinking method is to always start from the overall point of view, analyze the structure and function of the system, and study the interrelationship and regularity of changes among the system, elements, and environment. _x000D_
Systems theory has been widely used in both natural and social sciences. In social life, people also form different systems. A family, a business, a school, a country... can all be studied from a systematic perspective and understand their laws. Therefore, psychological working methods guided by systemic thinking have emerged, such as systemic family therapy and systemic organizational management. These methods are fundamentally different from traditional psychological work. After introducing the systemic perspective, we often see different perspectives on individual mutual behaviors, information exchange, and the formation of epistemology. _x000D_
The emergence of systems theory has caused profound changes in human thinking. In the past, research problems usually involved decomposing things into several parts, isolating the simplest elements, and then using the properties of the parts to explain complex things. This method focuses on parts or elements and follows linear causal determinism. It is often more suitable for understanding simpler things, but is not competent for the study of complex problems. This course aims to introduce the basic ideas of systems theory, with a special focus on the application of systems theory in psychology, to help students understand the systematicity, openness, and complexity of human behavior. It also introduces the perspectives and methods provided by other emerging scientific ideas such as cybernetics and information theory to open up new ideas for understanding and organizing human behavior.

Introduction: The course will be based on an open, case-based, field-based approach to the design of energy systems that will deepen students ' knowledge of the system. Actively encouraging and guiding students to search for front-line literature on their own, promoting students ' access to frontier information on subjects, understanding recent developments in science and technology, and training students in their ability to innovate. These include, inter alia: (1) energy frontier technology overview, including basic concepts and general trends in energy technologies (2 hours of learning); (2) energy safety technologies frontier development and innovative thinking, including energy security technologies, distributed energy systems and portable energy supply equipment (4 hours of learning); (3) intellectual energy technologies frontier development and innovation, including energy routers, energy networks and smart control systems (4 hours of learning); and (4) green energy technologies frontier development, including heat pumps, residual heat recovery, and innovation (2 hours of learning). College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: Isotope Geology (Radiogenic and Non-Traditional Isotopes)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Isotope geology is an important branch of earth science. It mainly studies the changes in the abundance of different isotopes in various geological processes in nature to infer its evolutionary history, and then restore the past and present of the earth. This course will focus on teaching the basic theory and applications of radioactive and non-traditional stable isotopes. Radioactive isotopes are formed by radioactive decay of unstable radioactive parent bodies. The radioactive decay system records the formation age of rocks and the age of subsequent magma or metamorphic events. Non-traditional stable isotopes study the fractionation between minerals, between minerals and melts, and between minerals and fluids in different geological processes. Therefore, they can be used to trace the formation and evolution of the solar system, the differentiation of the earth, and the interaction of different spheres on the earth (atmosphere, hydrosphere and lithosphere).

Name: High-Temperature, High-Pressure Materials Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Rock science, mineral science, Earth science generals, university physics, university chemistry
Introduction: All substances under normal pressure will have extraordinary physical and chemical properties when placed under high temperature and high pressure conditions. For example, graphite will turn into diamond, single-atom inert gases will turn into complex chemically active molecules, non-conductive non-metallic sulfur will turn into superconductors, hydrogen will turn into metal... Pressure, as the most basic physical quantity, has an earth-shaking impact on human beings' existing knowledge and thinking patterns. The development of new technologies such as the realization of pressure beyond the center of the earth, the establishment of in-situ observation methods, and the improvement of micro-area integrated detection means have put high-pressure material science on the eve of a major breakthrough. It is the right time to understand and master certain scientific knowledge and experimental techniques of high-temperature and high-pressure materials, which will greatly broaden the horizons of young students.

Name: Compiler Practicum
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Through compilation internship training, students can further master the basic theories and techniques of compilation principles, learn to use tools for constructing compiled programs, and enhance their ability to develop large programs. The task of the compilation internship is to develop a compilation program. It inputs a program written in a high-level language, then performs lexical and syntactic analysis, type checking, and then translates it into intermediate code, and finally translates it into a program written in a computer language. Both the intermediate code and the final program need to be able to run on the simulator. Among them, MiniJava language is a subset of the standard Java language. _x000D_

Name: Micro/Nano Integrated Systems (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The main theme of the course is the presentation of the main system of expertise of the Weiner Integrated System and related experiments. Through this course, students acquire basic knowledge of integrated circuits, designs, MEMS devices and their application requirements, stimulate curiosity and innovation, learn to analyse problems, solve problems and develop initial scientific capabilities. Students participating in this course will be involved in some pilot projects and will have the opportunity to participate in the iCAN International University BioNetwork Innovation Entrepreneurship Competition.

Name: Digital Logic
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The "Digital Logic" course is a professional technical basic course for the microelectronics major. It is based on digital electronic technology and involves the basic principles, basic analysis and design methods in digital technology. Through the study of this course, students can acquire basic theories, basic knowledge and basic skills in digital technology, master the basic analysis and design methods of digital logic circuits, and enable students to have the preliminary ability to solve digital logic problems, laying the foundation for subsequent courses on digital systems. _x000D_

Combinational logic teaches the analysis and design of combinational circuits, combinatorial logic optimization, and standard modular combinational circuits; sequential logic teaches basic sequential devices, standard modular synchronous sequential circuits, analysis and design of synchronous sequential circuits, and their optimization. ADC and DAC basics will also be covered in this course. In addition, hardware description language and FPGA related knowledge will also be taught in the course. _x000D_

Introduction: This course tells the basic knowledge and basic theories of solid state physics, allowing students to understand and master the basic concepts, important methods and physical models of solid state physics, laying a good foundation for subsequent courses (such as "Semiconductor Physics" and "Semiconductor Device Physics", etc.) and future research.

Introduction:

Through the curriculum, students are able to master some of the physical and chemical phenomena that may be faced when the scale is reduced to micro-, nanoscales, and to design and develop the corresponding devices using the resulting measures.

Name: Introduction to Nanoelectronic Devices
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The modern microelectronics industry uses device scaling technology to integrate more and more devices into a single silicon chip to increase its device density and operating speed. However, in very large-scale integrated circuits, the "top-down" device size reduction technology will eventually reach its limits, including theoretical, technical and economic limits. Recently, scientists have proposed "bottom-up" technology that can solve this problem and continue to shrink CMOS devices. It is expected to realize nanoelectronics integrated systems in the future. _x000D_
     This course mainly introduces the latest progress in nanoelectronics, especially nanoelectronic devices and circuits realized by "bottom-up" technology, including materials and key technologies. This course is organized as follows: First, it introduces the history and current situation of "bottom-up" nanoelectronics, and discusses the basic theories involved in nanoelectronics, such as: electronic structure and properties of low-dimensional nanostructure materials, transport characteristics of nanoelectronic devices, etc., and then introduces the latest progress of nanoelectronic devices, including nanoelectronic devices, molecular devices and atomic scale devices based on carbon nanotubes and graphene. Then the key technologies and basic issues of nanoelectronic device circuits are discussed, and finally the various challenges faced by nanoelectronics are summarized. _x000D_

Name: Analog Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Higher mathematics, electromagnetics, microelectronics and circuit infrastructure
Introduction:
This course is a mandatory course in microelectronics and involves analysis, tectonic methods of low-frequency analogue electronic circuits. It focuses on components, fundamentals, features and applications for magnifying circuits, including computing, filtering, signal processing and steady voltage circuits. Through this course, students are equipped with the theoretical foundation and applied knowledge of more robust analogue electronic circuits, which lays the foundation for learning simulation integrated circuits.
As a compulsory subject in the Department of Microelectronics of the College, in the second semester, students should have completed courses on microelectronics and circuit infrastructure, circuit analysis, and will be studying analog integrated circuits in the third year, so that the course has a certain depth and breadth and is closer to integrated circuits. For example, when introducing semiconductor devices, more information is provided on the means of realization and the characteristics of the integrated circuit process; when teaching basic magnification circuits, more attention is given to equivalent circuits in the MOS tube.
This course is both theoretical and practical. On the theoretical side, including the rationale, frequency compensation, feedback, etc., for magnifying circuits, the practice is to calculate the various applications of amplifiers, including how to achieve additions and subtractions, calculators, logarithms, etc., and how to form instrument amplifiers, filters, signal generators, steady voltage power sources, etc. Students may choose e-routing experiments related to this course to further deepen their understanding.

Name: Principles of Analog Integrated Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Introduction:
This course is a basic course for undergraduate students on analog integrated circuit analysis and design. _x000D_
1. Undergraduate students should master the analysis and design technology of CMOS analog operational amplifiers through this course. Towards this goal, the basic components that constitute CMOS analog integrated circuits - MOSFETs, basic circuit modules (single-stage and differential amplification stages, current mirrors, operational amplifiers), and basic analysis methods (DC characteristics, AC characteristics, frequency characteristics, noise characteristics, feedback characteristics, stability) will be taught. Through the study of the above content, a solid foundation for analog integrated circuit design will be laid. _x000D_
2. The knowledge taught is highly practical. In view of the reality and technical prospect that CMOS analog integrated circuits are the most widely used in actual design, when arranging the teaching content, we will focus on the analysis and design knowledge of CMOS analog integrated circuits and not the design knowledge of bipolar integrated circuits. This is conducive to thoroughly explaining the common analysis and design methods of analog integrated circuits in limited class hours, so that students can master the knowledge that is most likely to be applied in the future. If students need to design bipolar or BiCMOS analog integrated circuits in the future, they can solve the problem by self-study based on the basic analog integrated circuit analysis and design methods learned in this course. _x000D_
3. Use more suitable teaching materials. The teaching team consulted various teaching materials in this field at home and abroad, and after discussion and comparison, decided to choose the Chinese translation of "Analog CMOS Integrated Circuit Design" (original work by Behzad Razavi). Therefore, it is commonly used by prestigious foreign schools such as UCLA and Berkeley. The use of the Chinese translation version prevents undergraduate students from spending too much energy on English reading and understanding, allowing them to shift the focus of their learning to analog integrated circuit analysis and design itself. _x000D_
4. Emphasize the close integration of theory and practice. Combined with the knowledge taught, a large number of examples are added for students to refer to when doing homework. Each chapter is arranged with required homework questions and selected design practice to urge students to further understand the taught content after class and apply the knowledge they have learned through homework questions and design practice, thereby deepening their mastery of knowledge and arousing their interest in learning.

Name: Fundamentals of Integrated Circuits for Wireless Communication
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Modern wireless communication systems are increasingly implemented through integrated circuits or even single system integrated chips. Therefore, the connection between wireless communications and the integrated circuits that implement them is getting closer and closer. Modern wireless communications must be implemented by integrated circuits, and a large category of integrated circuits needs to serve wireless communications and be designed to meet the special requirements of wireless communications. _x000D_
    This course first introduces the basic knowledge and basic theories of wireless communication, and focuses on the wireless communication knowledge that affects the design of integrated circuits and systems. Then it describes the integrated circuits that specifically implement wireless communication, and focuses on the basic knowledge and basic principles of integrated circuits for various modern wireless communication systems. _x000D_
    This course connects wireless communications and integrated circuits, which are two secondary subjects, so that students can integrate from principles, to systems, to circuits, and finally to sub-circuits and devices, combine basic principles with specific application technologies, understand and master the basic concepts, basic theories and important knowledge of integrated circuits used in wireless communications. It also lays a solid foundation for subsequent courses (such as "Advanced Analog Integrated Circuits", "Radio Frequency Integrated Circuits", etc.) and future related research. _x000D_

Name: Device Design and Applications in Modern Integrated Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Semiconductor package physics (or similar course, e.g. introduction to integrated circuit device)
Introduction: The course describes the design and analytical methods of mainstream semiconductor devices in modern integrated circuits from the perspective of integrated circuit applications, covering in-depth body physics, design of devices for different applications and associated test representation techniques. The use of design models for different applications (e.g., logic, storage, simulation/radio frequency, etc.) to build bridges between the physical and physical design of the device and its circuit applications is of greater practical utility. The content of this course is a good combination of physical knowledge of integrated circuit devices and practical applications in industry, which can build and improve the ability of students in microelectronics to solve practical problems in industry and innovate, and can provide a good basis for future research activities.

A major feature of this course is that it pays equal attention to course teaching and experimental teaching. It supplements the basic knowledge teaching in the classroom with a large number of experimental classes, allowing students to have hands-on contact with the most advanced material characterization equipment, so as to master theoretical knowledge and experimental skills more intuitively.

Name: Semiconductor Materials
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course covers materials physical infrastructure, materials preparation and presentation analysis technology base, new microelectronic material characteristics and applications, including, inter alia: the need for materials in microelectronic technology development; the basic nature and crystal characteristics of materials; the various membrane material preparation techniques and their principles; the technical principles and applications of material nature representation analysis; and new semiconductor materials, including new liner materials, new high K media and metal electrodes fence structure materials, new storage media materials, metallic silicates/nitrochemical materials, Cu/LK interface materials and technical features and applications. The course will be based on basic knowledge of the performance and application of micro-electronic materials and will seek to reflect the latest developments in the relevant fields and to inform students of the relevant basic knowledge and developments in this field.

The digital analog module of PSoC (Programmable System-on-Chip) can be composed of various commonly used peripheral devices, such as ADC, DAC, etc. Moreover, there are detailed datasheets for these devices. Students can gain a preliminary understanding of the principles and functions of these devices by studying PSoC. In addition, using the configurable functions of PSoC's configurable mixed-signal array system chip, various circuit functions can be easily implemented without adding additional peripheral devices, making it flexible and changeable. College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Soft electronics are the building of electrons and their connected circuits on a liner that can be extended, greatly expanding their application in complex shape scenarios, away from space shapes, sizes, shape variations and closer to actual application needs. This course is based on physics, chemistry, materials and biology. The cross-cutting perspective of disciplines describes emerging soft electronics, both in relation to semiconductor physics and materials chemistry of flexible devices and in relation to their application in areas such as information, energy, imitation, etc.

The content of the course, which covers, inter alia, organic/inorganic semiconductor physics, polymer chemistry and physics, device processes and displays, and typical soft electronics, is closely linked to recent research trends in related areas and leads to the development of multidisciplinary cross-learning and research capabilities of students.

Name: Advanced Integrated Circuit Processing and Manufacturing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Candidates must master basic knowledge such as college physics, advanced mathematics, electronic circuits, semiconductor physics, and semiconductor device physics. In particular, understanding basic theories such as electromagnetism, optics, and quantum mechanics will help to understand the advanced content of this course. In addition, electives are encouraged to have knowledge of scientific numerical calculations, programming languages, etc.
Introduction:
As the importance of integrated circuits in the life and production of the national economy becomes more and more prominent, the development of the integrated circuit industry has become the core content of Made in China. Among them, the level of integrated circuit manufacturing determines the level of a country's overall integrated circuit industry. It is also the link in the integrated circuit industry chain that is most likely to get stuck. Improving the level of integrated circuit manufacturing in our country needs to start from the cultivation of talent base. In addition, as Moore's Law faces many physical extreme challenges, integrated circuit manufacturing technology is on the eve of major changes. How to cultivate innovative and disruptive manufacturing technologies for the development of my country's integrated circuit technology from cutting-edge research will be a major responsibility for future students majoring in microelectronics. _x000D_
This course aims to expand the knowledge scope and cognitive horizons of undergraduate students majoring in microelectronics and integrated circuits and graduate students in microelectronics and solid-state electronics. As the teaching plan continues to advance, it will dynamically teach leading process technologies and principles in the field of integrated circuit manufacturing, conduct simulation training based on the latest technology examples in the industry, and cultivate professional research literacy and abilities related to advanced integrated circuit manufacturing.

Name: Food Security: Studies in Political Economy and Psychology
Introduction: Food has always been an old and young subject in China. The economic thinking of agriculture dates back to the ancient times, when Confucius and Meng had written many articles on the agricultural system and politics and the well-being of the people. The Columbus Exchange, population growth and migration have laid the foundations of modern civilization. The famines of the last century have left a deep memory of hunger to many. In the context of food trade and the supply of global food value chains, our dietary preferences and food consumption are also shifting, triggering modern thinking about obesity and health. Cross-cutting psychological research helps us to identify the mechanisms of food consumption decision-making and directs rational food consumption. Food security and consumption also require attention to food waste and environmental and energy sustainability. The course will begin with an understanding of food security at different scales, such as global, national and household scales, and will provide an overview of the evolution of global food security based on a recollection of the events of the Second Great Famine in history. Cross-cutting research in economics and psychology is used to understand differences in food consumption. The final course will also explore how the waste of food, environmental and energy issues in modern agriculture affect our future food security and consumption. Food Security: Political Economics and Psychology, with a focus on food security and consumption.

Name: Selected Lectures on Computational Problems in Society and Markets

It is of positive significance to embody this trend in university education and train students to form certain interdisciplinary thinking. Students will be asked to perform a number of experiments related to network data analysis, all of which can be completed on a personal computer. _x000D_

Name: Computational Photography: Imaging Model Theory and Deep Learning Practice
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Linear algebra, program design internship, mastering at least one of the languages of C++, Python or Matlab
Introduction:
Cameras play an important role in modern life, recording countless meaningful moments for people; for computer vision researchers, cameras capture visual information and provide input for almost all computer vision algorithms. If the input image quality is not high enough, no matter how advanced the computer vision algorithm is, it will encounter an insurmountable bottleneck. Computational camera science is an emerging interdisciplinary subject that integrates computer vision, computer graphics, and computational optics. By introducing calculations into the imaging process, it can capture visual information with higher performance and more dimensions than traditional cameras, and present content that traditional cameras cannot see clearly, accurately, or even see. In addition to the evolution of optical and sensor devices, the contribution of computational camera algorithms (super-resolution, high dynamic range, depth estimation, etc.) to the current richness and improvement of smartphone camera functions cannot be ignored. As one of the hottest technologies in the field of visual computing, deep learning has brought about performance breakthroughs that traditional methods cannot achieve in high-level computer vision problems such as target detection, recognition, and classification. Deep learning technology is also playing an extensive and active role in computational photography. By complementing traditional computational photography in terms of optical properties, physical constraints, and imaging models, it provides new solutions to many computational photography problems from a data-driven perspective. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course starts with the formation of digital images and the working principles and methods of digital cameras, introduces imaging models based on geometry and optics, and then provides an in-depth introduction to several types of important computational camera problems (high dynamic range imaging, photometric stereo vision, super-resolution, deblurring, depth cameras, etc.); each type of problem introduces classic methods based on physical imaging principles and signal processing and the latest methods based on data-driven and deep learning. Through the study of this course, students can comprehensively understand the process of digital image imaging and the working principles of cameras, and initially master the ability to use classic theories and cutting-edge technologies to enhance digital image quality and improve digital photography experience. _x000D_

_x000D_
They all say to cherish life. But what is life? Many scholars believe that they are interpreting life or even "prescribing" life. But if we understand that life is a natural phenomenon that appears on a time scale of 10 to the 9th power (one billion) years, and the recorded history of mankind is only a story that happened on a time scale of 10 to the power of 3 (thousands) years, wouldn’t you think there is something wrong with those who claim that they or the discipline they study “prescribes” life? _x000D_
_x000D_
In today's society, at least on our campuses, there are probably not many people who deny that we humans are living beings. But who can explain clearly what "life" is? People think or expect biologists to give standard answers, but the unfamiliar and awkward terminology used by biologists and the dazzling symbols in the slides of their lectures often keep most people who are not engaged in biological research at a distance. However, the tree wants to be still but the wind does not stop. Along with staying away from life sciences, there is often confusion about the various rumors brought about by new discoveries that are changing with each passing day and difficult to understand, and anxiety about facing the unpredictable living environment. The more rapidly life science develops, the farther away it seems from the public. Who should fill the growing gap in understanding of life between researchers and the public? _x000D_
_x000D_
Faced with the huge amount of information in the field of life science research that is increasing at a rate that exceeds "Moore's Law", it is obviously unrealistic to expect the public to understand life according to the model of professional biology education. However, both from the perspective of society and the sustainable and healthy development of life science itself, we have to find ways to let more members of society understand the nature and basic laws of life, so that they can follow the laws of life and build a harmonious life. Inspired by ancient cave paintings, Picasso painted a realistic cow with hair that must appear and transformed it into an abstract cow outlined with lines. This seemed to provide a worthwhile way to solve the above dilemma: to abstract the core elements from massive information in an abstract way. Looking at his few strokes, there are probably not many adults who would not immediately be able to tell that the master painted a "cow" and not some other animal. With the purpose of helping the audience think about the nature of life and understand the laws of life, Professor Bai Shunong of the School of Life Sciences designed the course "The Logic of Life" based on his understanding and perception of life formed during many years of research work. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is designed as a small class class (limited to 25 people) during the summer semester. 32 semester hours, 2 credits. Lectures, lectures, and discussions. It mainly introduces basic knowledge related to life and its inner connections around issues closely related to everyone's daily life. Scores are calculated based on three aspects: attendance and discussion participation (10%), two papers (each about 2,000 words), and the results of two lectures (papers and results account for 90% in total). Both papers use the theme of "Life as You Understand" to summarize one's own understanding of "life". Submit one at the beginning and one at the end of the course. The purpose of the paper is to help course candidates understand the changes in their understanding of "life" phenomena as the course progresses. The paper will be scored based on three aspects: whether the argument is clear, whether the argument is well-founded (whether there are references and the standardization of reference citations), and the rationality of the argument. _x000D_
_x000D_
What is particularly worth mentioning is that the lecture portion of this course will be undertaken by two professors from famous American universities. One is Long Manyuan, a professor of evolutionary biology at the University of Chicago. He is the founder and leader of international research on the origin of new genes. He will teach the basic principles of biological evolution for this course. The other is Qian Hong, a professor of applied mathematics at the University of Washington in Seattle, USA. With his accumulation of mathematics from his family, he went through astrophysics, biochemistry, protein structure calculation, and finally in the field of applied mathematics, he used mathematical methods to describe the complicated life processes and unearthed simple and beautiful basic laws. He will teach this course whether and how to use the logic of quantitative science to explain the inherent laws of living systems. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Nanoionics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Nanoionics is an emerging interdisciplinary subject with wide applications in new information storage devices, logic devices, neuromorphic devices, brain-inspired computing chips, lithium batteries, fuel cells and other energy storage devices and sensors. Nanoionics focuses on the ion transport properties in solid electrolytes at the microscopic scale, covering the ion transport phenomena in solids and the resulting electrical, optical and other properties in physics, chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, and microelectronics. Research on nanoionics has grown rapidly in the past two decades, occupying an important position in the development of information science and technology, new energy, brain-inspired computing and other fields. The main purpose of this course is to enable students to master the basic aspects of nano-ionics and nano-ion device physics related to current new information, energy storage, sensing and other technologies, understand the latest research and development trends in related fields, focus on introducing the physical images of related theories, and provide necessary professional theoretical knowledge and methods for students who are interested in related fields or engaged in related research. _x000D_
      The main contents of this course include the development history of nano-ionics, ion transport theory in solids, defect chemistry, typical nano-ion materials and properties, fuel cells, lithium-ion batteries, non-volatile resistive memories, sensors, etc. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Reconfigurable Systems
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
In recent years, the idea of ​​using reconfigurable logic represented by field programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) for computing has aroused people's interest. Reconfigurable logic has a unique property: after it is manufactured, it can be reconfigured to change the logic function it implements; and once configured, it can be regarded as a piece of hardware capable of implementing specific logic. _x000D_
    For many applications, reconfigurable logic can often achieve much better performance/power consumption indicators than general-purpose processors, with performance improvements ranging from several times to dozens of times in some calculations. Although the performance/power consumption specifications of reconfigurable logic are generally weaker than those of application-specific integrated circuits (ASICs) designed for specific tasks, its reconfigurable nature gives it an important advantage: it can be used to implement new applications whose performance/power consumption requirements cannot be met with general-purpose processors, and which cannot be implemented in time (or are too expensive to afford) with ASICs. _x000D_
    Currently, there is a hot spot in the world - researchers are using reconfigurable logic as an accelerator that can implement new functions in a timely manner, building reconfigurable systems to improve overall performance/power consumption indicators, and provide better features/market response time for innovative applications. Recently, Xilinx, one of the two largest FPGA manufacturers in the world, also released an extensible processing platform (Xilinx Extensible Processing Platform) composed of two ARM Cortex-A9 processor cores and FPGA. _x000D_
    This course intends to introduce the principles, composition, and structure of reconfigurable systems, teach the hardware programming language (Verilog) and programming methods on reconfigurable logic, discuss suitable applications and algorithms in reconfigurable systems, and introduce several cutting-edge research topics. In the course, there will also be certain practical exercises to design on the FPGA development platform. _x000D_
    Through the study of this course, students will master the basic knowledge about reconfigurable systems and be able to develop applications/algorithms for reconfigurable systems to make full use of high-performance/low-energy consumption reconfigurable systems.

Name: Neural Computation
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: In recent years, deep learning methods based on convolutional neural networks have achieved the best results in target detection and speech recognition. At the same time, neural networks are also regarded as reasonable approximations to the neural representation of the basic visual system. However, actual biological neural networks are much more complex than current neural networks. For example, only 5% of neuronal synapses in the network of the brain's visual cortex receive bottom-up input signals, and current neural networks basically only care about forward calculations. So, what is the function of the remaining 95% of a neuron's synapses? What is the computational function of recurrent connections in fetish neural circuits? What learning rules are knowable or achievable in real loops? Can we form new computational vision models and machine learning techniques from the knowledge we have gained about neural circuits? This course will discuss current relevant papers in machine learning, computer vision, and biology to explore answers to the above questions. This course is open to students at all levels, from undergraduates to doctoral students. The course content includes thesis study reports and discussions, course projects and teacher comments and explanations. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Climate Change Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The scientific overview of climate change is an optional course for undergraduate students at the University of Cities and Environment, which is taught in 16 different languages.

Climate change refers to changes in the functioning of the global scale Earth system caused by natural factors and human activities. Climate change, marked by global warming, has been an important expression of global change in recent decades. Climate change has profound implications for natural systems (e.g. freshwater resources, terrestrial and freshwater ecosystems, coastal zones and marine ecosystems) and human systems (e.g. population, economy, food security and human health). Currently, the facts, causes and projections of climate change are at the forefront of scientific issues of general concern to the scientific community, while adaptation and mitigation of climate change have become central to sustainable economic and social development. To this end, the course provides systematic teaching of the rationales and methods of global change science, based on the state of scientific understanding of climate change, the natural and socio-economic impacts of climate change, and three possible responses to climate change adaptation and mitigation.

The purpose of this course is to equip students with the basic knowledge and rationale of climate change science, to understand the effects of climate change, and to acquire the basic skills and methodology of climate change science research through the development of basic qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for climate change science research, with the ultimate aim of enlightening, clarifying concepts and preparing students to explore practicality.

Edge intelligent computing chips located outside the cloud have gradually become one of the important development directions of the next generation of artificial intelligence computing platforms. Therefore, machine vision technology based on edge intelligence is expected to have very broad application prospects and research value in the future intelligent society. _x000D_

Through theoretical lectures in the classroom and hands-on experiments on the edge intelligence development platform, students will learn the principles and development methods of key computer vision algorithms such as image acquisition, image preprocessing, image classification, and object detection. Name: Fundamentals of Parallel Algorithm Design
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Computation of general or C language-related courses
Course on Introduction to Computer Systems or Other System Structures
Introduction:
Parallel algorithms are methods and steps to solve problems using multiple combinations of computing resources. This method is based on the simultaneous characteristics of the mathematical/physical model, data-centred computational tasks are broken down, and mission time is planned according to the inter-mission dependency. Unlike the design of serial algorithms, which focuses on reducing the complexity of calculations, the design of parallel algorithms also addresses issues such as parallelity of calculations, simultaneous data access conflicts, computational division and load balance between processors, and data access locality of processors. The objective is to perform unrelated tasks simultaneously with different computing resources, and the speed of processing algorithms increases with the amount of computing resources available. Today ' s computing systems generally rely on increasing the number of processors to meet the growing data-processing demand. Whether it is the use of super-calculations to solve complex problems such as big data or the development of multi-nucleus/nuclear processors, the skills to design parallel algorithms are essential.

The course revolves around the development of parallel computing thinking and parallel algorithm design capabilities, presenting the underlying theory of parallel computing, the design methodology of parallel algorithms and the strategy of basic optimization, and case studies of typical parallel algorithms. At the same time, using the results of the construction of the National Platform for High Performance Computation of Educational Practice, a typical computing parallelization experiment was conducted to help students understand the basic features of parallel processes, master the design methods of parallel algorithms, familiarize themselves with basic parallel computing models and gain experience of parallel algorithm optimization. The course included: (1) the rationale for parallel computing, the architecture of parallel computers; (2) the data-centred task decomposition method, the parallel computing model for resolving conflicts between tasks and the distribution of data for access; (3) the operating mechanisms and features of parallel algorithms, evaluation methods, classical optimization strategies; and (4) the typical parallel algorithm design and optimization cases.

More enterprises have focused on the RISC-V architecture since the events of mid-climate, which many consider to be a breakthrough for Chinese cores, as the use of the architecture offers more autonomy. The system-level chip (SoC, System on a Chip) is inspired by the use of ASIC to achieve the chip set, and it should be created to integrate the different features of the complete computer directly into a silicon tablet. The SOC consists of a designable reusable IP nuclear, which is a self-soldable VLSI block with complex system functions, with multiple CPUs, GPUs, DSPs or their composite IP cores. The ASC design process is a very important one in chip design, and the ASC design process that we are introducing in the classroom allows students to understand the process of semiconductor manufacture by using, for example, 0.18m and 65nm of the plant and steps on the production line of the containment plant. The scientific power is the super-calculated power, and the two clusters are highly overlapping and reflect the importance of super-calculations. We will present the design priorities of the Supercalculator chip, including the design methods of the advanced 7 nm process.
This course begins with an introduction to the RISC-V processor, where the common SoC design concept is discussed, with a focus on the ASC design process, combined with the RISC-V MMU course experiment, which provides students with an intuitive and profound understanding of the design process for a single chip system based on the RISC-V processor, and provides a solid basis for future work on the design of the chip.

Name: Functional Programming
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Functional programming was born more than 50 years ago. In recent years, it has begun to receive more and more attention, and many new functional programming languages ​​have emerged, such as Clojure, Haskell, F#, etc. Even imperative programming languages ​​have added some functional programming features, such as C++ 11, Python, Javascript, etc. Some even have strong support for functional programming. "Functional programming" has the potential to become as mainstream a programming method as "object-oriented programming". Future-proof programmers should master functional programming methods. _x000D_
_x000D_
Functional programming is a programming paradigm that views computation as analogous to the evaluation of mathematical functions. The act of computing is to perform a series of transformations on data. The original data is used as the parameter of the function, and the function is evaluated. The result of the evaluation is the transformed data. The transformed data can be used as the parameter of other functions... until the desired result data is transformed. Functional programming has the characteristics of concise code, no side effects, and easy parallelization of programs. _x000D_
_x000D_
For students who are accustomed to imperative programming, learning functional programming can broaden their thinking, think about programming problems in a different way, and better understand the nature of computing. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course uses Scheme, a dialect of the functional programming language Lisp, as the programming language. In addition to learning to use scheme to write ordinary programs, one of the biggest highlights of this course is that you will learn to use scheme to write a complete scheme interpreter. _x000D_

It is better if you have preliminary knowledge of linear algebra, atomic physics, optics, quantum mechanics and other related courses.
Introduction: The course focuses on basic knowledge, state of development and future trends related to quantum information technology, with a view to expanding students ' knowledge in the area of quantum information technology and fostering interest in quantum information technology. The course is conducted in a thematic lecture-style format, with slides and some blackboard books. The course consists of 16 lectures covering: the concept and history of quantum information technology; basic concepts related to quantum information technology; quantum computing; quantum secure communications; quantum precision measurement; and the current status and future trends of cutting-edge quantum information technology, such as MRI.

Name: Probability Theory and Stochastic Processes
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Probability theory and random processes are a basic theoretical course for science and engineering students. It is a mathematical discipline that studies the objective regularity of random phenomena. With the development of science and technology, the thinking methods of probability theory and random process have been widely and deeply applied in many fields: digital communication systems, signal processing, control theory, adaptive filtering, etc. The teaching of this course enables students to master the basic concepts of probability theory and stochastic processes, understand its basic theories and methods, enable students to initially master the basic ideas and methods of dealing with random phenomena, and cultivate students' ability to use probability theory and stochastic processes to analyze and solve practical problems.

Name: Quantum Physics, Information and Life
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Einstein described the confusion of his student age in his self-statement (1946): “Mathematics is divided into many specialized fields, each of which can take a short life as we can. Physics is also divided into fields, each of which consumes a short life and does not satisfy the desire for deeper knowledge. Like Britane's donkeys, he can't decide which we should eat." – Are you, students? And the solution he offered was, "This will require us to separate what is really fundamental, the most important, from the remaining areas where there is much and no knowledge. To identify what could lead to deep knowledge, leaving behind many others and leaving aside what fills the head and diverts it from its main objective.” — This course is intended to help students grasp the dynamics of scientific development from the sea of diverse disciplines. Maxwell said in 1871: “In a few years, all important physical constants will be approximated, and the only work left to scientists will be to carry out these measurements and measure another decimal... But we do not have the right to embrace this idea of the untraceable rich diversity of everything in the heavens and the earth, nor the right to imagine the creativity of those fresh minds, and it will continue to embrace and reflect this rich diversity.” As Kelvin said in 1990, “Physics can already be considered complete, and the next generation of physicists seem to be doing little, but there are two small, disturbing clouds in the distance of the clear sky of physics.” — and it is these two little clouds that eventually gave rise to relativity and quantum mechanics. Since 1970s, theoretical physics and so on has been stagnating for decades, and until the twenty-first century, the edifice of science is cloudy, and economic and social development will enter a “new normal” with the breakdown of the law of Moore and the global epidemic, pending new developments. Einstein also said that “natural nature hides its secrets through its own nobleness rather than its guile”. — If we can no longer think with noble eyes, we should not wonder why the cornerstone of science, represented by physics, has been without real progress for a long time. The idea at the beginning of this course, which is often new, is to stimulate “new spiritual creativity” and to seek to be the pioneers of a new era, to make a paradigmal innovation of “up-to-the-ground” (in both words) and to show the way for today's scientific prisoners. - - - - - - - - Quantities, information and life are the three most important key words about us and the world: they dominate the evolution of micromatters in a very different way, behind the objective phenomena we know; life is the self-emergence, reproduction, perception, consciousness, will, evolution, interaction that naturally emerges in the world of the former substances, not only with regard to objective natural phenomena, but also with regard to our subjective spiritual world and social behaviour; information is the substance of the state and changes in the evolution of matter and life, and human beings not only have access to information, but also can use it to change social life in many ways. What is the role of information in the origin and evolution of the universe and life? Do quantum effects exist in complex structures and activities of life? What are the challenges and insights of life phenomena for the development of theoretical physics? What changes in computing science are possible as a result of developments in brain science? Can quantum computing be combined with neurocalculation in the future, so that strong artificial intelligence is possible? What kind of holistic change could quantum science bring to social science? Where is the dignity of life against the backdrop of the evolution of cosmic celestial bodies and the rise of artificial intelligence? As an Eastern scholar who has grown up on the soil of China's civilization, what kind of life and humanistic care should it be, and could it be possible to give direction for the future development of science? • “Large fisheries are often present at warm sea currents,” and the intersection of disciplines is most likely to revolutionize science. The course aims to help students build a global view of the frontier of science and to bridge the week of integrated education in cross-cutting disciplines. It will be aimed at zero-basic beginners, who will be presented with the above-mentioned themes. Teaching will be conducted in a manner that combines generality with research. The teaching will focus on the discovery of key points, drawings, ideas, and connections. It will also focus on the motivation of students to direct their attention and study at the forefront of academic literature, as well as on the conditions for students to participate in research and to continue their studies in the relevant fields at an early stage of their academic careers.

Name: Botany (Part 1)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Botany is an important basic subject in biological sciences and the main basic course for biology majors in colleges and universities. This discipline is a science that studies the morphological structure, physiological functions, growth and development laws of plants, the relationship between plants and the environment, the distribution laws of plants, and the evolution and classification of plants. This course includes two parts: morphological anatomy of seed plants and botany experiments. _x000D_
    The morphological anatomy of seed plants mainly includes the morphology, structure, development and function of seed plant tissues and major organs, while also understanding the connections between various organs. Through the study of this course, students can understand and master the shape, structure, function and development process of the major organs of seed plants (roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, seeds); and through the study of major organs, students can understand that all organs of the plant have a certain identity and a certain unity. And through the interconnection between various organs of the plant body, we can further understand and grasp the high degree of unity in the structure and function of the plant body. _x000D_
    Through the experiments in this course, students can master some basic operational skills in botany. Such as the operation of microscopes; freehand slicing, simple mounting, biological staining and permanent section production; biological drawing and other methods and techniques, so that students can master the basic knowledge and basic theories of plant morphology, anatomy and classification, understand the laws of plant growth and development, and master basic methods of experimental skills, laying a foundation for subsequent courses. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals and Applications of Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: "Fundamentals and Applications of Ecology" is an introductory course on ecology offered by the Department of Ecology for college freshmen. It is also a general education course on biological and environmental issues. Ecology explores the interrelationships between living things and their environment. An organism is its biological environment, so ecology also explores the relationship between organisms; humans are organisms, and ecology also explores the relationship between humans and the environment, and humans and other organisms. Ecology explores the existence forms, changing laws and internal mechanisms of all these relationships, and also explores how to use the wisdom contained in these relationships to benefit human civilization. This course is mainly taught by teachers from the Department of Ecology, and some are taught by teachers from other departments or external schools. _x000D_

Name: General Ecology 1
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge of individual ecology and population ecology to students majoring in the environment, enabling students to master the theoretical system and basic principles of ecology, laying a foundation for learning subsequent courses and engaging in ecological research and environmental protection work.

Name: General Ecology 2
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course is a specialized course for second-year university students. It contains two components: community ecology and ecosystem ecology. The basic theory and methodology of community ecology and ecosystem ecology are presented. Through detailed profiling of the structure, functions and dynamic features of communities and ecosystems, students are provided with initial theoretical knowledge of communities and ecosystem ecology and the necessary ecosystem analysis methodology to provide a solid basis for further scientific research and practical application.

Name: Field Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
A compulsory field internship course for the field ecology major. This course is based on the Peking University Ecosystem Observation Station in Bashang, Hebei Province. Multiple routes are designed along the gradient of several important geographical factors (climate, vegetation, soil). It aims to cultivate students' ability to observe wild ecological phenomena, master field investigation methods, and ask scientific questions through a combination of lectures and internships_x000D_
      During the internship, students observed different geography, vegetation, and soil patterns along the eight internship routes and obtained relevant data to gain an in-depth understanding of the characteristics and internal mechanisms of the patterns, raise scientific questions and hypotheses, and answer and verify these questions and hypotheses when conditions permit. On the basis of the obtained data, the geographical and ecological phenomena of the internship area are comprehensively analyzed. In this process, students need to comprehensively use knowledge and data to think and analyze issues with regional characteristics, and choose appropriate topics to write papers. _x000D_

Name: Experimental Techniques in Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences

Name: Animal Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Animal ecology is an important branch of ecology, which mainly studies the science of the relationship between animals and the environment, the response and adaptation of animals to the environment, the distribution of animals in space; the occurrence and regulation mechanism of animal populations; the relationship between animals, plants and microorganisms; the role of animals in the ecosystem; the application and important research methods and technologies of animal ecology in wildlife protection and management, sustainable utilization of biodiversity, animal disease prevention and pest control, alien species early warning, etc.

Name: Quantitative Methods in Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Ecology I, II; Probability theory and mathematical statistics
Introduction: This course is based on the knowledge of probability statistics/multivariate analysis and population/community ecology. Starting from the statistical distribution and sampling methods of ecological data, this course systematically introduces population analysis (including population estimation, age structure and dynamics, spatial pattern analysis), community structure analysis (including ecological niche, species diversity, community classification/ordering, and environmental interpretation), related quantitative methods for landscape pattern and spatial statistical analysis, and is supplemented by data analysis experiments based on the statistical software R. This course is intended to help students understand basic quantitative analysis issues in ecological research and master sampling design, management, common statistical analysis methods and practical operational skills for ecological data.

Name: Theoretical Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course teaches theoretical concepts and methods in ecology, covering commonly used ecological and evolutionary models, including individual level (metabolic theory), population level (logistic model, matrix model), community (competition, predation, food web), ecosystem (function, stability, metacommunity, island biogeography), etc. The course emphasizes theoretical concepts and thinking rather than mathematical derivation.

Name: General Ecology 3
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
General Ecology 3 is a compulsory undergraduate course in ecology at the Urban and Environmental Institute, which consists mainly of two components: landscape ecology and global ecology. The course consists of 15 lectures (Pasic Ecology 4 and Global Ecology 11) and two in-house internships on the principles and methods of landscape ecology and global ecology from three sides, namely, basic concepts and development processes, major research content and research methodology.
The objective of the course is to further learn the ecological fundamentals and basics of macro-levels such as landscape, regional and biosphere, based on the study of ecology at the life-forming level of individuals, populations, communities and ecosystems; and to develop basic skills and methodologies for macro-ecological research and master basic qualitative and quantitative analytical techniques for macro-ecological research.

Name: Frontiers of Ecology and Physical Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The course content covers various cutting-edge fields of ecology and physical geography, including theoretical frontiers such as earth systems, climate change, water resources, soil and underground ecological processes, biogeochemical cycles, biodiversity, and environmental evolution, as well as cutting-edge research in practical fields such as nature conservation, ecological restoration, watershed management, ecosystem services, and regional sustainable development.

Name: Biodiversity Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Biodiversity is the basis for human survival and social development, and the guarantee for the construction of ecological civilization and the sustainable development of the nation. The formation and maintenance mechanism of species diversity is one of the 25 major scientific issues that need to be solved urgently in this century, and its research is the cornerstone of biodiversity conservation and utilization. China has rich forest types and a large number of endemic and relict species, which have important conservation value. It is a key area for in-depth understanding of the formation and maintenance mechanisms of plant diversity and its response to global change. However, due to human influence, global species diversity is decreasing and this trend will accelerate in the future. The current species extinction rate is about 1,000 times higher than the natural background value. Some scholars even believe that the earth is facing the "sixth mass extinction of species." Therefore, protecting biological diversity has become a global consensus. This course will comprehensively introduce the concepts and theories related to biodiversity from several aspects such as the concept of biodiversity, the origin of biodiversity, the distribution of species diversity and its formation and maintenance mechanisms, the multi-dimensionality of biodiversity, biodiversity informatics, biodiversity and ecosystem functions, biodiversity threats and assessments, and biodiversity monitoring and protection.

Name: Academic Writing and Expression
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: “Academic Writing and Expression” is a school-wide elective course that is recommended for study in the first grade of the subject. The curriculum presents five modules through academic norm and dissertation, information literacy and the use of new literature resources, logical and analytical writing and critical thinking, vocabulary grammar, efficient and high-quality expression, which enhances the academic writing and expression skills of students.

Name: Educational Practice and Innovation
Introduction:
1. Basic purpose of the course_x000D_
Through case analysis, visits and surveys, special lectures, etc., we help students understand the new issues currently facing my country’s compulsory education and high school education, the ongoing characteristic practices and innovations, and the future development direction. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Introduction to Chinese Course_x000D_
Every student is a recipient of education, but do you understand how different types of educational institutions carry out innovative practices at different stages of education and in the context of the knowledge economy and data era? How effective is it? How are educational institutions managed? How do education and training service companies make money? How does an educational charity organization operate? On the basis of teaching the basic theories and methods of education, this course will invite researchers, practitioners from various educational institutions and innovation teams to give special lectures, and combine it with field surveys, debates and other forms to help students re-understand education from the perspectives of educational researchers and managers. _x000D_
For each educational stage, the course will be divided into two parts: educational seminars and special lectures. The former is mainly taught by classroom teachers, focusing on the introduction of basic theories, research themes and methods; the latter mainly invites educational managers and educational innovation teams to give special lectures, focusing on the discussion of hot issues, educational practice and innovative activities, and the future direction of education. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Atmospheric Physics
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Atmospheric physics is a discipline that studies the physical phenomena of the atmosphere and its evolution. It mainly studies sound, light, electricity, radiation processes, clouds and precipitation, near-surface atmospheric physics, stratosphere and middle atmospheric physics in the atmosphere. It is not only the basic theoretical part of atmospheric science, but also a major subject of environmental science, especially the atmospheric environment.

Name: Research Methods in Environmental Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite:
Basic course in mathematics,
Basic courses in environmental science,
Undergraduate studies course.
Introduction: It is a course on research methods for postgraduate students in environmental science. More than 20 years of teaching. Taking into account the increasing participation of undergraduate students in scientific research in recent years and the fact that many of the subjects, depths and results of undergraduate research are already comparable to postgraduate thesis, the postgraduate course is open to undergraduate students. Undergraduate students who wish to participate in undergraduate scientific research, particularly in the project for the advancement of the state of the art, learn through this course, gain a more systematic and in-depth understanding of the nature of environmental scientific research, become familiar with basic methods and tools, increase interest in environmental scientific research and gain an initial understanding of the substance of innovative research. Moreover, students in relevant disciplines, such as ecology and geography, can benefit from it. In fact, many students in these fields have been selected for this postgraduate programme in the past. The course will begin with a very brief presentation of the methodological basis for some very basic environmental scientific research. Such as the aims, objectives and significance of scientific research in the field of environmental science. Briefly describe how to identify and select appropriate research topics and content, how to build long-term research horizons and develop specific research plans, how to critically read literature, how to choose appropriate methods and design specific experiments, how to analyse and evaluate data, how to reason and draw conclusions, how to write research and degree papers, and how to make oral presentations on results. In addition, special information will be provided on plagiarization and self-piracy in scientific research, as well as on the differences between the two different references (citiation and quation). Following a brief system presentation, the course focused on laboratory modelling, field research and computer modelling methods through research examples in about 10 areas of environmental science research. The main purpose of presenting examples of these studies is to highlight critical thinking in scientific research, to develop the capacity to address problems that arise in scientific research, for example, how to deal with unintended results encountered in research, how to address problems such as the non-achievement of reservations, and how to derive potential new discoveries from failures. The following are specific examples of these studies. These examples are updated. One example of research is the morphology and biological efficacy of heavy metals in the micro-coastal environment. This is an example of how new discoveries are sought through unexpected experimental results. Example two: Bioavailability of POPs in human digestive tracts. This is an example of how critical understanding of previously officially published research results can be made, how practical research on fundamental theoretical applications can be learned and how innovative discoveries can be made through micro-observation of data. Case III: Development of several passive atmospheric samplers. The main purpose of presenting these examples was to highlight the value of new technological instruments in environmental scientific research and the potential for developing innovative research devices in this field. Several of the sampling devices described in the examples are organically simple, user-friendly and provide important information. Example 4 of the study: Multimedia fate simulation of POPs. This example is presented to illustrate the many potential improvements that can be made in some conventional approaches. This improvement often leads to new scientific discoveries. These are just a few examples. More examples of experimental studies, field observations and numerical simulations will also be covered.

Name: Principles of Limnology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Lake environment is called limnology at home and abroad. This concept is proposed to be different from oceanography. It takes inland water bodies (including lakes, rivers and wetlands) as the research object to study the formation and evolution patterns of lakes, swamps and watersheds, as well as their physical, chemical, biological processes and mechanisms. In terms of disciplines, P. S. Welch (1952) regarded this subject as a subdiscipline of ecology, which in the field of modern science belongs to freshwater ecology or aquatic ecology. _x000D_
    This course discusses the structure and function of lakes, reservoirs and wetlands from an ecosystem perspective, as well as the relationship between these water bodies and watersheds, overlying atmosphere and climate. It also discusses the application of basic limnology research in integrated watershed management and ecology. The purpose is to improve students' use of basic science to solve lake environmental problems. This course covers the background and development history of limnology, numerical models of limnology, watersheds, gases, pollutants, weather and climate and their role in aquatic ecosystem function. In addition, it also introduces acid deposition, nutrient patterns, surface processes and their occurrence mechanisms. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Monitoring and Laboratory
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Environmental monitoring technology is a basic technical means in environmental research. It mainly uses analytical technologies such as sample extraction, purification, and instrumental analysis to efficiently and sensitively separate target pollutants from complex sample media, and conduct an accurate qualitative and quantitative process to provide analytical support for research on the pollution characteristics, migration and transformation behavior of environmental pollutants, and ecological health risks. This course mainly introduces the monitoring technology of major pollutants in environmental media such as water, atmosphere, soil, and solid waste. The main content includes environmental analysis technologies such as extraction, pretreatment and purification, analysis, and biological monitoring of different pollutants in multiple types of samples.

Name: Environmental Processes of Pollutants in Soil and Water
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Environmental science, soil science, aquatic chemistry, etc. would be desirable.
Introduction:
The curriculum includes, inter alia, the following:
1. Introduction
2. Human relationship to the water and soil environment
3. Focus and hotspot issues of current soil and water environmental processes
Typical pollutants and sources in aquatic soils
5. Environmental processes of pollutants in water bodies
6. Environmental processes of pollutants in soil
7. Soil composition, nature and role in the contaminant environment
8. Soil adhesive properties and role in the contaminant water and soil interface
9. Interactions and impacts of pollutants and organisms in the water and soil environment
10. Nitrogen cycling and transformation processes in the soil and water environment
11. Phosphorus cycling and conversion processes in the soil and water environment
12. The formation, hazard and governance of black water bodies in cities
13. Common treatment techniques for pollutants in water
14. Rehabilitation and remediation techniques for contaminated soils
15. Sources, environmental processes, hazards and disposal of solid waste

Name: Research Methods in Physical Geography and Resource Environment
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Introduction part: On the basis of introducing the research objects, content and particularities of physical geography: 1) Analyze the methodology, scientific thinking and basic methods of physical geography research from the level of scientific philosophy, and introduce the basic procedures of physical geography research; 2) Introduce the development history of physical geography. The development and trends of geographical research methods include the investigation and description of physical geography, the explanation of the causes of physical geography phenomena, the comprehensive analysis of physical geography, the systematic research of physical geography, the positioning experimental research of physical geography, the quantitative research of physical geography, the model simulation research of physical geography, etc. In addition, it focuses on literature retrieval, acquisition of secondary data and socioeconomic surveys, positioning stations and semi-positioning monitoring, and presentation methods of research results. _x000D_
    Hydrology part: This part emphasizes the application of hydrological models and pays attention to practical operations. The content includes the compilation of hydrological data, the basic situation of representative distributed hydrological models, lumped hydrological models and black box models. The operation content includes: 1) processing of rainfall, runoff and evaporation data, generation of secondary flood processes, continuous series generation, and segmentation of groundwater processes; 2) parameters of the rainfall-runoff model and its calibration method. The main parameters include: evaporation parameters, surface runoff parameters, underground runoff parameters, slope flow confluence parameters, ground confluence parameters, river confluence parameters, etc.; 3) model simulation error analysis and accuracy assessment. _x000D_
    Phenology part: This part emphasizes the spatiotemporal coupling of natural landscape phenology dynamics, including the basic rules of plant phenology occurrence and the spatiotemporal simulation and prediction of plant phenology periods and growing seasons. The specific operation content is: 1) field observation of plant phenology; 2) preparation of phenology calendar; 3) division of phenological seasons; 4) optimal period plant phenology time model and spatial model based on daily meteorological elements; 5) construction method of plant phenology mechanism model; 6) scale conversion and spatiotemporal change unity analysis technology of plant phenology. _x000D_
    Land resources part: This part emphasizes the application of land resources evaluation and pays attention to practical operations.
