The content includes land resources investigation and data analysis, and the introduction of representative land resources evaluation models. Specific contents: 1) Land resources survey content and methods; 2) Land potential evaluation system, including evaluation methods and specific applications; 3) Land suitability evaluation system, including evaluation methods and specific applications. _x000D_
    Meteorology part: introduce the subject characteristics and main research materials and methods of meteorology, test learning results and deepen learning content through two internship studies, so that students can have a preliminary understanding of meteorology research methods and master basic research skills. _x000D_
The course content focuses on the five major research methods of atmospheric science: meteorological monitoring, meteorological diagnosis, meteorological reconstruction, meteorological simulation and meteorological prediction. It introduces the basic data and processing methods of meteorological analysis, the application of the output results of meteorological statistical analysis models and atmospheric circulation models, and conducts two internships on climate change law research and climate data reconstruction. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Integrated Practicum in Human Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Humanities, economic geography, urban geography, industrial geography, urban sociology
Introduction: This course is intended for students who have completed their studies in basic courses of specialization and partial courses of specialization in humanities, geography and urban and rural planning, and is part of a comprehensive professional internship programme. The course focuses on 7-10 days on resource utilization in urban and rural development, typical business patterns, and human geography in rural and urban cluster development. On the basis of an integrated understanding of spatial development in urban and rural areas, students choose either typical elements or typical geographical development as subjects for research and independently complete the internship report.

Name: Fine Arts: Drawing and Color
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Fine Arts: Painting and Coloring are compulsory courses in urban planning, focusing on basic quality development and basic skills training for students. The aim of the course is, on the one hand, to improve students ' ability to observe and analyse space patterns and to improve artistic literacy, and, on the other hand, to develop skills in space expression and to acquire a graphic language that accurately expresses space patterns.
The main content of the course is sketch practice, which is the foundation of all plastic arts. The exercise was conducted in three parts: the first was an indoor plaster geometry writer, which served as a basic sketching exercise, and was designed to explore basic painting techniques and styles, including contour lines, structures, subtleties and shadows, and to learn a little perspective of two points and three points. Five weeks; two for static sketches, real expression shapes, qualitative senses, quantum senses, light senses, etc., and three for architectural, landscape and urban space students, with an accurate description of the structure and perspective of the objects of the mass for three weeks. The last part is a two-week course on colour basics and design colours.

Name: Planning of Scenic Areas
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: On the basis of introducing the basic concepts, characteristics, functions and development history of landscapes and scenic spots, this course analyzes the main problems and causes of scenic spots in my country, proposes countermeasures for the protection and utilization of scenic resources, teaches the main content and key points of scenic spot planning, and the inspiration of international concepts such as national parks and world heritage on the development of scenic spots in my country.

Name: Feasibility Studies for Construction Projects
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Feasibility study of construction projects is an important part of project investment management and an important part of urban planning and construction. This course mainly covers construction project management procedures, time value of money and program economic comparison, project market analysis, project scale research, investment estimation, financing plan research, project economic evaluation and decision analysis, etc., so that students can master the basic knowledge of construction project investment decision-making.

Name: Big Data and Machine Intelligence
Prerequisite: There is a programming language base.
Introduction: With the popularization of computing equipment and the development of network technology, the amount of data in all walks of life is growing rapidly, and scientific issues in the management and application of big data have emerged. How to effectively process and analyze big data is a service that taps into the great value of big data: (1) It requires the support of data-friendly programming languages, such as Python, etc.; (2) It requires operating languages ​​for data management, such as SQL language; (3) It requires machine learning tools for data analysis and processing, such as TensorFlow, etc. The course is based on the Python language, helping students master the SQL language and TensorFlow machine learning library, and understand data management theory and the current status and progress of big data architecture from practice. Through course projects, students can practice intelligent applications such as speech recognition and machine perception of computer vision.

Name: Introduction to Environmental Nanotechnology
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: Nanotechnology is a strategic frontier field in the 21st century, and environmental pollution is a long-term and urgent problem that humans need to solve now and in the future. Environmental nanowater technology developed under this background is becoming an international interdisciplinary research hotspot and a systematic emerging discipline. This course aims to introduce the basic theories and principles of environmental nanotechnology applied to environmental remediation and pollution purification, as well as the environmental effects of nanomaterials. The course will start from the perspective of environmental application and environmental behavior of nanomaterials, and will be divided into three aspects: environmental nanorepair technology, environmental nanomonitoring technology, and environmental nanobehavior and toxicology. Comprehensive and systematic introduction to the principles and methods of nanomaterial synthesis and design suitable for environmental remediation and monitoring, the rules and principles of the interaction between pollutant molecules and materials at the nanoscale, and the manifestation of nanoeffects in the natural environment. The course content covers nano-adsorption technology, nano-photocatalysis technology, nano-heterogeneous catalysis technology and nano-filtration technology used in water, atmosphere and soil remediation; nano-sensors suitable for environmental monitoring and environmental indicator analysis; environmental risk assessment and full life cycle assessment of nano-materials. At the same time, important environmental nanotechnology topics will be carried out in conjunction with cutting-edge hot spots. This course enables students to master the basic principles of environmental nanotechnology at a macro level, and at the same time, have a thorough understanding of the research methods and development trends of environmental nanotechnology in a professional depth, and understand how to apply nanotechnology to solve environmental problems.

Name: Introduction to Literature Retrieval and Academic Writing
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge and elements of literature search and paper writing. The content includes: (1) retrieval of Chinese and English databases (such as China National Knowledge Infrastructure, China Science Citation Database, WOS, JCR, electronic journals published by various societies), special literature resources (such as domestic and foreign dissertation databases, domestic and foreign patent databases, environmental databases) and utilization of online academic resources; (2) oral academic reports and PPT production methods; (3) scientific paper writing methods, including the structure of project reports and scientific papers, the characteristics of each element, writing requirements and interrelationships, as well as the writing standards and academic ethics of scientific papers. This course has a clear structure, from easy to deep, step-by-step, simple and practical, and has strong pertinence, guidance and practicality.

Name: Principles of Chemical Engineering
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
Principles of Chemical Engineering is a main course in chemical engineering, environmental engineering and similar majors. It is a bridge between basic courses and professional courses. It is a required major technical basic course. It is an engineering discipline that comprehensively uses basic knowledge such as mathematics, physics, and chemistry to analyze and solve various physical processes in chemical production and environmental engineering. With the increasing complexity of environmental problems and the refined development of environmental engineering technology, the role of chemical engineering principles in environmental engineering science has become more and more prominent. _x000D_
The teaching content of chemical engineering principles is based on the physical processes in chemical engineering and environmental engineering as the background, studying the basic principles of several unit operations (fluid flow, heat transfer, absorption, distillation, drying, mechanical separation, evaporation, crystallization, adsorption, membrane separation, etc.), typical equipment structures of unit operations, equipment operating characteristics, design and calculation of processes and equipment, selection and modification of equipment, methods of research problems, etc. _x000D_
Principles of chemical engineering is an engineering science, and its teaching characteristics are to emphasize the perspective of engineering technology, strengthen the training of quantitative calculation, qualitative analysis and design capabilities of chemical and environmental engineering processes, pay attention to the combination of theory and practice, and cultivate and improve students' ability to understand, analyze and solve problems. _x000D_
Principles of chemical engineering should not only solve the basic laws of physical processes, but also complex and real production processes. It uses the principles of natural science to investigate, explain and deal with practical engineering problems. _x000D_
The course does not require prerequisites for students who choose the course, but requires students to have the ability to read books, search online, and operate basic computers. In particular, they must have a love for engineering subjects, the courage to challenge technical problems, and the quality of teamwork. _x000D_

Name: Environmental Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The course requires students to learn the thinking and methods of environmental chemistry research based on knowledge of general chemistry, analytical chemistry concepts and experimental methods, understanding and mastery of environmental pollution generation, detection of change processes, analytical techniques and data processing methods, and to deepen understanding of environmental protection. As an introductory course in the field of environmental chemistry research, students at all levels of specialization, such as environmental science and environmental engineering, and those working in related fields are involved. This course, in conjunction with the environmental chemistry theory course, provides practical examples of atmospheric pollution, indoor air pollution, water pollution and soil pollution. The experiments designed in this course are not simple analyses of chemicals, but reflect the full research philosophy. Either a complete set of processes for a certain type of contamination, including field sampling, sample processing, sample analysis, treatment of results and computation, or actual monitoring and modelling of a pollutant change process. The experimental design fully reflects the understanding of the process of environmental pollution change. The number of hours in this course is 6 per week, and given the time spent in the class, in practice class 1300-1800 is not limited to specific hours. The first period consisted mainly of studies on the operation and maintenance of basic equipment and basic experimental research skills, for approximately 4-8 weeks; the latter period was a combination of experiments designed for students on the basis of the condition of the swallow garden and the surrounding environment and completed approximately 6-12 weeks. The experiment is conducted in groups of 2-4 persons each; the previous experiment is conducted under the guidance of an instructor, who is primarily responsible for coordinating the integrated experiment. The previous experiment, each of which required the completion of an experimental report, was evaluated by the instructor on a percentage basis. The Integrated Experimental Cluster works together and each individual independently completes a pilot report. The report is available in electronic/paper format (specifically requested by the instructor) prior to the next experiment; the overall results of the course consist of the results of the previous pilot report (50 per cent total) and the results of the comprehensive pilot report (50 per cent).

Name: Environmental Risk Assessment and Management of Chemical Substances
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The issue of chemical environmental and health risks has become a significant global environmental problem facing contemporary human society, and the environmentally sound management of chemicals through scientific risk assessment and risk management has been placed on the United Nations environment and sustainable development agenda and as an important strategic objective. As a developing country with the largest production and consumption of chemicals in the world, the environmental and health risks of chemicals are becoming more and more acute and chemicals risk management needs to be strengthened. However, the country is still in a period of conventional “triple-waste” pollutant management, with the relative backwardness of research and management of chemical environmental risk assessment and risk management, the dearth of internationally mainstreamed basic knowledge and developments in chemical environmental risk assessment and risk management, and the lack of specialized courses in the national university education system for environmental science, which are not adapted to current developments in environmental scientific research and teaching. The course introduces the International Classic on Chemical Risk Assessment and Management, “Risk Assessment of Chemicals: An Investment” (2ed Evaluation, commonly known internationally as the “Red Book”), systematically teaching basic scientific knowledge on chemical risk assessment and risk management, closely integrating typical examples of practical scientific research and management practices in the field, and providing students with basic principles and methods of chemical environmental risk assessment and risk management, as well as regulatory and international action to develop future science and environmental management leaders with expertise in the field and an international perspective.

Name: Experimental Child Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Understand the research results of early development in child development psychology;_x000D_
Learn how early childhood development psychologists approach these issues;_x000D_
Focuses on habituation research methods and procedures used in infant research;_x000D_
Understand the relationship between these theories and empirical research;_x000D_
Read the corresponding literature to understand the dynamics of child development research. _x000D_

Name: Audiovisual Speech Processing Integration and Its Neural Mechanisms
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: Any course in psychology, neuroscience, information science
Introduction: There is a complex and close integration of human perception systems. There is also close functional integration of the hearing and visual systems during speech processing. The course will systematically discuss the functional linkages between these two cognitive systems during speech processing and the corresponding mechanisms. It is divided into three main sections: (i) the first part deals with the integration of hearing and visual speech processing; (ii) the second part focuses on the brain mechanism of hearing visual speech integration; (iii) the third part describes the role of hearing and visual integration in the process of speech creation; and (iv) the fourth part deals with machine processing of hearing and visual speech integration. The assessment of the classmates in the elective course consists of three sections: (1) lectures and answers to the articles assigned to them; (2) participation in the discussion of questions in the classroom; and (3) the final papers chosen in accordance with their interests.

Name: Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
Introduction: Abstract: Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Chinese Communists, with Xi Jinping as the main representative, have used great political courage and strong responsibility to put forward a series of new ideas, new thoughts and new strategies. They have systematically answered the major contemporary issue of what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics and how to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era from a combination of theory and practice. They have created Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era. Under the guidance of Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era, the Communist Party of China leads the people of all ethnic groups in the country to coordinate great struggles, great projects, great causes, and great dreams, promoting socialism with Chinese characteristics into a new era, and promoting the Chinese nation to usher in a great leap from standing up, getting rich, and becoming strong. Xi Jinping's thought on socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era is very rich in connotation, covering economics, politics, the rule of law, science and technology, culture, education, people's livelihood, ethnicity, religion, society, ecological civilization, national security, national defense and the military, "one country, two systems" and the reunification of the motherland, the united front, diplomacy, party building and other aspects, forming a system of ideological and theoretical systems that are complete, logically rigorous and interoperable. "Eight Clarifications" is an expression at the level of guiding ideology, focusing on how to see it, and answers the question of what kind of socialism with Chinese characteristics we should uphold and develop in the new era; "Fourteen Persistences" is an expression at the level of the action program, focusing on what to do, and answers the question of how to uphold and develop socialism with Chinese characteristics in the new era. The "Eight Clarifications" and the "Fourteen Perseverances" embody the unity of theory and practice of Xi Jinping's thought on socialism with Chinese characteristics for a new era.

Name: Overview of Politics, Economy and International Relations along the Belt and Road
Introduction: In September and October 2013, China's President, Xi Jinping, launched the joint “Silk Road Economic Belt” and “Marine Silk Road for the 21st Century” initiatives, which received high international attention and a positive response from the countries concerned. Building a “one-way path” is now a top priority for China's external relations development, based on the idea of building a community of human destiny. It is also an important step towards bringing China's economic transformation to the next level through a combination of national and international efforts. The course will focus on the special experiences and contexts faced by the relevant regions and countries along the “One Way” route in the process of building the “one Way” with China (including the region or country: 1. Economic and social environment; 2. Fundamental features of political development; 3. Significant political and economic risks; 4. Basic state of international relations in the region). In order to deepen the participants' awareness of the “One Way Forward” initiative and to enhance their understanding of the political, social and international relations situation in the regions and countries along the border.

Name: Negotiation Simulation and International Document Drafting
Prerequisite: History of international relations, theory of international relations
Introduction: Diplomatic negotiations are those conducted by States as subjects or as legitimate representatives authorized by them to achieve the objectives of the State ' s foreign policy, also known internationally as international negotiations. The purpose of the course is to present theoretical and practical approaches to diplomatic negotiations. The main elements include the theoretical framework for negotiating analysis, actors and stakeholders in contemporary diplomatic negotiations, specific factors influencing the negotiation process and outcome, and how negotiators prepare for negotiating strategies and apply negotiation techniques in a targeted manner. The special feature of this course is the integration of the theory of negotiation, practice and application, and students ' learning of the theory and strategy of diplomatic negotiation is not only useful for negotiating between countries, but also for negotiation and interpersonal communication in everyday life.

Name: Distinguished Lecture Series on Frontiers of International Organizations and Global Governance
Introduction: How do international organizations operate? How can international patterns be influenced? How can global governance be addressed? The course addresses the theoretical and practical aspects of how international organizations can address issues in the areas of security, development, energy, the environment and public health, through guest lectures. Through this course, students will (1) understand how different types of international organizations work, (2) understand and analyse in depth the role of international organizations in international relations and global governance, and (3) learn to write research plans to address important global issues of the moment.

Name: Comparison of Chinese and Foreign Cultures
Introduction: In the era of globalization, cultural identity and cultural differences are issues that have attracted widespread attention in international exchanges. Knowledge and understanding of different cultures are also the basic prerequisite for effective international exchanges. This course starts with the connotation of culture, the basic characteristics of culture, the main cultural types in the world, and the main theories and methods of cultural comparison. It introduces the basic characteristics of Chinese culture and foreign culture, the individuality and commonalities between them. The purpose is to allow students to have a basic experience of cultural issues, and to lay a certain foundation for improving their ability to understand the theory and practice of different cultures, as well as their ability to communicate internationally.

Name: Introduction to International Public Policy
Prerequisite: History of international relations, theory of international relations
Introduction:
The current global commons governance is facing many challenges and opportunities, which requires relevant practitioners and researchers to find answers from multi-disciplinary, multi-dimensional and multi-perspective perspectives. International public policy is not simply the study of relations between countries. It also covers domestic politics, domestic public policy processes, the influence of non-state actors, the role of transnational and supranational actions, etc. In addition to pure political and policy issues, international public policy also includes special issue areas such as health, education, refugees, environment, energy, counter-terrorism, economy and trade, arms control, etc. When thinking about the management and governance of the above-mentioned issues in the international commons, we need to take into account both national and global perspectives, consider the similarities and differences between different interests, systems, and cultures, and aim at the construction and operation of transnational and supranational governance mechanisms. _x000D_
_x000D_
"Introduction to International Public Policy" will introduce and explore the political mechanisms, policy processes and interaction patterns between relevant actors in the field of international public affairs. After passing this course, students should initially have the ability to understand and analyze major issues in global public policy based on a combination of theory and empirical evidence. At the same time, this course will provide students who are interested in research and practice in the field of international public policy with the direction and space for further in-depth thinking and study. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Politics and Public Policy
Introduction: This course is designed for undergraduate students, especially undergraduate students. The course will provide an overview of contemporary Chinese politics and public decision-making processes. The course highlighted China ' s political structure and relations between the State and society. Students will have an initial understanding of the contemporary Chinese Government, politics and society, as well as an understanding of the contemporary Chinese context of political and social decisions and social issues, and how to deal with them. Social movements, environmental protection, family planning, economic reform, political development, etc. Through this course, students have a comprehensive understanding of Chinese politics and society.

Name: Advanced Mathematics (Type D, Foundation)
Introduction:
1: Advanced Mathematics (Category D Basics) is a course that combines basic mathematical theory and applied mathematical methods to adapt to the trend of modern science and liberal arts penetration. The teaching content uses calculus as the basic structure. The course has the characteristics of liberal arts, art, and sports. It is more targeted for certain liberal arts groups, such as students with certain majors, international students, etc. The course positioning, difficulty, and requirements are slightly lower than Advanced Mathematics D. You can refer to the introduction of courses such as Advanced Mathematics A, B, C, and D to more accurately locate Advanced Mathematics (Fundamentals of Category D). It should be noted that Advanced Mathematics D is sometimes called Advanced Mathematics for Liberal Arts. However, if Advanced Mathematics for Liberal Arts lasts for two semesters, it usually includes three parts: calculus, linear algebra, and probability and statistics. The advanced mathematics (Basics of Category D) here refers to the calculus part, which requires one semester, about 64 class hours. _x000D_
2.	 The position of Advanced Mathematics D in the difficulty chain of similar courses (calculus courses) (from difficult to easy): _x000D_
         Advanced mathematics A > Advanced mathematics B > Advanced mathematics C > Advanced mathematics D > Advanced mathematics (Basics of Class D) _x000D_
Three.	 Characteristics of Advanced Mathematics (Basics of Category D), comparison with related courses, teaching purposes and requirements: Advanced Mathematics (Basics of Category D) aims to have a framework understanding of the development history and theoretical system of calculus. It enables students to understand why people often say that elementary mathematics is mathematics that studies constants, and advanced mathematics is mathematics that studies variables, why functions are one of the most basic concepts, why calculus is the starting point of modern mathematics, etc. The purpose of the course is to enable students to initially master the basic knowledge, basic theories and basic skills of calculus, establish the idea of variables, and cultivate the viewpoint of dialectical materialism. To enable students to receive preliminary training in using variable mathematical methods to solve simple practical problems. _x000D_
Four.	Credit hours: The credit hours of relevant courses are as follows: three semesters of Advanced Mathematics A, two semesters of Advanced Mathematics B and Advanced Mathematics C, and one semester of Advanced Mathematics D and Advanced Mathematics (Basics of Category D). _x000D_
Note: Advanced Mathematics (Fundamentals of Category D) has 2 hours of exercises every fortnight, which are not counted as credits. _x000D_
Five.	 Difficulty: Advanced Mathematics (Basics of Category D) is less difficult than Advanced Mathematics D, but it still has certain basic requirements, that is, it requires understanding concepts, basic methods, and being able to perform basic calculations and simple applications. _x000D_

Name: Sociology and Chinese Society
Prerequisite: None. This course is intended for students with cross-cutting projects on “Political, Law and Society”.
Introduction: The course guides students to read in depth the relevant studies and literature of Chinese sociology in the areas of family and family, ethnicity and the State, urban and rural development and social change. It is hoped that after completing this course, students will be able to obtain a sense of the main literature in these three areas and will be able to expand their reading. Through reading these empirical studies, there is also a degree of knowledge and mastery of some basic concepts and methods of sociology. The curriculum focuses on reading and teacher-led discussions, in which it is hoped that students will be able to acquire some of the basic methods of reading literature and, on that basis, to write some systems of learning.

Name: Chinese Politics
Introduction:
Basic purpose of teaching:_x000D_
Through classroom lectures, students can have a relatively comprehensive understanding of the organizational structure, basic characteristics of the operating process and historical development of contemporary Chinese politics, and initially grasp the cutting-edge issues in contemporary Chinese political research, laying a good foundation for students to further study basic issues in Chinese politics. _x000D_
Content summary:_x000D_
The plan is to teach in 13 topics, specifically including: the political system with the Communist Party of China as the leadership core; the Communist Party of China; the People's Congress system; the political consultation system; the Central People's Government; the political and legal system; the disciplinary inspection and supervision system; the propaganda system; the military system; the relationship between the central and local governments; local government; the ethnic regional autonomy system; grassroots governance; society and citizens. _x000D_
Teaching method:_x000D_
Lectures, class discussions, and students doing special research and reports are mainly lectures, and students are encouraged to participate in class discussions and conduct special research and make reports. (Class report requires students to prepare PPT). _x000D_
Student performance evaluation method:_x000D_
    Mainly through the submission of final papers, there are also mid-term assignments (special reports). Midterm assignments account for 30%, final papers account for 60%, and attendance and class performance account for 10%. _x000D_

Name: Legal Reasoning and Legal Method
Introduction: The Legal Thinking and Jurisprudence Approach is an ad hoc core course for the joint training project “Political, Law and Society”. The curriculum aims at developing students ' legal thinking skills and legal research methods. Through a combination of teaching, discussion, practice and practice, students are introduced to and trained in their initial thinking on the basic sectoral laws of criminal law, civil law, administrative law, procedural law, etc., so that they can understand the thinking patterns of legal professionals such as judges, prosecutors, lawyers and others, as well as the basic methods of conducting legal research.

Name: History of European Political Thought
Introduction:
For centuries, Europe has been one of the most intensive and active areas for the development of human politics and political thought. Compared with other regions, this region has a similar historical background, but has turned into opposition several times due to conflicting ideas. In history, Europe has been integrated and divided several times. _x000D_
The establishment of the Roman Empire spread the same values and ideas to all regions of Europe. However, with the division of the Roman Empire, the political, social, religious, and cultural differences between the Eastern and Western Roman Empire began to gradually increase. The Renaissance, Enlightenment, and Revolution swept through Europe, once again connecting its parts together. But with the establishment of the Soviet Union and the beginning of the Cold War, Europe was once again divided. After the 1990s, the Soviet Union collapsed and the political situation in Europe changed again. Europe today is at the end of an old era and the beginning of a new era. Its development will greatly affect the direction and model of human political development. Our understanding of history and judgment of the future affect our current choices. _x000D_
This course will introduce representative figures, schools, and concepts from various parts of Europe in various historical periods, including the historical background and issues of their birth, as well as their inheritance, negation, and development process, current situation, and trends. Treating European political thought as a whole can help students gain a deeper understanding of the history of human political development. _x000D_

Name: Readings in Classics of Politics, Law and Society
Introduction:
Lead students to read 16 works: "Shang Shu·Hong Fan", "Zhongyong Chapters", "Han Feizi·Youdu" _x000D_
                                       Qian Mu "Political Gains and Losses in Chinese History", Wang Yanan "Research on Chinese Bureaucratic Politics"_x000D_
                                       Maine's "Ancient Law", Aristotle's "Politics"_x000D_
                                      Montesquieu's "The Spirit of the Laws", Sartori's "New Treatise on Democracy"_x000D_
                                      Hannah Arendt "Resistance to the "Banary Evil"", Engels "The Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State"_x000D_
                                       Fei Xiaotong "Rural China Fertility System", Qu Tongzu "Chinese Law and Chinese Society"_x000D_
                                      Weber "Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism", Durkheim "The Division of Social Labor"_x000D_
                                      Huntington "The Clash of Civilizations and the Remaking of World Order"

Name: New Political Science
Prerequisite: Political science doctrine, sociological concepts, generalization of law
Introduction:
This course will introduce the basic knowledge, sub-disciplines and academic frontiers of political science, sort out and teach the basic principles, academic sources and disciplinary progress of political science, and strive to reveal the political logic behind real life. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will design 13 courses, which will teach the basics of political science, the history of political science disciplines, political power, political system, political culture, political value, political ethics, political psychology, political sociology and computational politics, and also design 3 discussion classes. The course includes the following content.

Name: Econometrics Problem Session
Introduction: This course introduces the basic theories and methods of econometrics and aims to cultivate the ability to use corresponding theories and methods in empirical research. Students are required to not only master the relevant theories of econometrics, but also be able to use econometric software to carry out empirical analysis of actual economic problems by the end of the course.

Name: News Narrative and Imagination in Global Communication
Introduction: This course aims to follow up students’ understanding of international news, analyze recent representative cases that have had a greater impact on regional or world situation development, and global journalism from the perspective of strategic narrative, and explore the remaining deficiencies in domestic media’s external communication. It is hoped that this course can inspire students' global news imagination and form their critical thinking on the evolution and development of international news in the new media environment, as well as their reflection on Chinese media narrative strategies.

Name: Topics in Egyptology
Introduction:
This course uses the major research topics of Egyptology as clues to introduce the development process and cultural achievements of ancient Egyptian civilization (3000 BC - 7th century AD). Analyze the characteristics of ancient Egyptian civilization from the aspects of language, mythology, royal concepts, artistic style, etc. And introduce the current status, latest research trends and future development trends of this subject. _x000D_
The ancient Egyptian civilization was characterized by its high degree of material development and the penetration of religion into various cultural fields. The former is reflected in long-term political unity and stability, a complete centralized system, the establishment and expansion of the empire, as well as the rich legacy of architecture and art, the high development of language and literature, etc. The latter is reflected in the close integration of political power and theocracy, the popularization and ritualization of religion, as well as unique architectural and artistic styles, lifestyles and customs, etc., which are also reflected in religious beliefs centered on the afterlife. _x000D_

Name: Genre Studies and Creative Practice in Online Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Systematic reading and research of classic works of online literature
Introduction: This course uses the criteria of "Internet Genre Novel Classics" determined by the lecturer's in-depth research, examines the creative practice of China's Internet literature over the past 15 years, and selects a group of outstanding classic works as representatives of the emerging Internet genres (especially those new genres with Chinese local characteristics). Through an in-depth interpretation of these works, we can unearth the literary origins, core pleasure mechanism, aesthetic characteristics of this online writing type, as well as the national psychological trends that promote the popularity of this type of writing. At the same time, refer to the commercial list of online articles and the grassroots criticism list, establish an academic online article recommendation list, and publish review text, so as to truly implement the academic online literature evaluation standards. Based on the understanding of online literature, establish an online literature evaluation system that both inherently contains elite vision and is independent of traditional elite literary standards, and establish a set of online literature critical discourse. The course will be conducted in the form of a seminar. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports, enter the website to participate in writing practice, and participate in discussions with other students.

Name: Politics, Economy and Diplomacy of the Eastern European States
Introduction: This course is a restricted elective course for undergraduates in the School of International Relations. It is also suitable for students from other departments who are interested in international politics. This course focuses on the political transition from socialism to capitalism after the drastic changes in Eastern Europe, the economic transition from the public planned economy to the private market economy, the military transition from the Warsaw Pact to NATO, and the diplomatic transition that corresponds to these. Track and study the development changes in Eastern European countries. _x000D_

Name: Japanese (I)
Introduction: Japanese is the basic Japanese language course of the Institute of International Relations for students studying in 19th grade early rice fields. Through oral exercises and practices, and the development and enhancement of oral skills, students are able to travel to Japan successfully for simple daily communication. To enable students to express their thoughts with a basic accuracy, the language is essentially decent and the voice and tone are more pure. In the end, it is possible to speak consistently on familiar topics.

Name: Japanese (II)
Introduction: The course is intended for students of the North-North-Obama two-degree programme.

Name: Advanced Mathematics D
Introduction: Note: The introduction to higher mathematics A, B, C etc. allows for a more precise positioning of higher mathematics D. i. Course orientation: Advanced Mathematics D (hereinafter referred to as " high D " ) is a course designed to adapt to trends in modern science and literature penetration, combining basic mathematical theory with the application of mathematical methods, which is currently being offered to certain subjects with mathematical needs in the faculties of journalism, society, government, trust, Chinese, archaeology, government and language. High-level D teaching content and methods are clearly literary. In particular: Advanced Mathematics D is sometimes referred to as advanced mathematics in the arts, but if advanced mathematics in the arts is two semesters, it usually includes three components of calculus, linear algebra and probability statistics. The higher mathematics D here refers to the calculus component, which requires a term of about 60 lessons. ii. The position of the high D in the difficult chain of the same class (microclassification course): High A > high B > high C  > high D > high (category D base) iii. Characteristics of high D, comparison with relevant curricula, teaching purposes and requirements: high D, which aims to provide a framework understanding of the history of calculus development and theoretical systems, allows students to understand why people often say that primary mathematics is the mathematics of constants, higher mathematics is the mathematics of variable studies, why functions are one of the most basic concepts, why calculus is the starting point of modern mathematics, etc., the purpose of the curriculum is to provide students with the basic knowledge, basic theory and basic skills of calculus, to build the ideology of variables, and to develop a dialecticisticism. The students are given initial training in using variable mathematics to solve simple practical problems. iv. Hours of study: The duration of the relevant course is as follows: High A three semesters, high B and high C two semesters, high D and high (base D). Two hours per week, an average of one hour per week, are scheduled for the high D subject. V. Difficulty: The difficulty of high D is lower than the difficulty of high C, but there are still some basic requirements, i.e. the need to understand concepts, to understand basic methods, to be able to make basic calculations and simple applications.

Name: Studies in Twentieth-Century Sino-French Literary Relations
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will focus on the major works related to China in the history of French literature and culture in the 20th century, as well as the important events involved in Sino-French literature and cultural exchanges. For example, the content includes the poetry of Xie Gelan and others, the novels of Malraux and others, the literary theory of Barthes and others, and the sinology of Ai Tianpu and others. The focus is to sort out the impact of Chinese thought and culture on France and the world, and then form a clearer understanding of the phenomenon of "Eastern learning spreading to the West" in the cultural exchanges between East and West in the 20th century, and gain a more comprehensive understanding of our own literature and culture.

Name: Artificial Intelligence Technology and Applications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: There are no mandatory courses. Better knowledge of basic computer classes.
Introduction:
After years of development, artificial intelligence has made remarkable achievements. It is profoundly changing our production and life and accelerating our entry into the "intelligent era". There are reasons to believe that no matter what profession or industry we are engaged in, artificial intelligence should be a necessary basic quality. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is intended for students majoring outside of Peking University’s intelligence disciplines. It strives to systematically present the basic overview of artificial intelligence to students, positioning the course as a necessary core quality course for modern college students. _x000D_

Name: C Programming
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences

Name: Introduction to the Humanities of Art
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly provides introductory lectures on art and humanities. Art humanities is an emerging research field of contemporary art. It is a combination of art science, value philosophy and aesthetics. It faces many difficulties in contemporary art, such as anti-art, anti-value, anti-ontology, zero-degree writing, flatness, etc. It is also concerned about the existing conditions of contemporary people, takes value as the core, and uses artistic clarification as a method to re-examine the relationship between art and human value. The close and unique connection highlights the humanistic significance of art, promotes the in-depth value dimension of art research, and at the same time enhances students' artistic accomplishment, humanistic awareness, and value judgment, so that students can more consciously express their own independent opinions and make their own judgments in the face of contemporary art, and also promote the spiritual ecological construction of contemporary art, culture, and society from the side.

Name: Analysis of Chinese Dialect Corpora
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Modern Chinese, Chinese hymn, Chinese dialect
Introduction: This article introduces the types of Chinese dialect data, how to obtain them, pre-analysis processing, some basic aspects of dialect data analysis, and how to implement computer-assisted analysis. It also introduces the basic functions and usage of the Access2000 interactive relational database management system.

Name: Introduction to Art History
Introduction: Art history is different from the history of a single category of art, such as art history, music history, dance history, drama history, film history, etc., but involves the development history of all art categories. Although there are various categories of art in different eras, there is always one art category that stands out in particular and becomes the representative art category of a certain era. This course will sort out the development of Chinese art based on this concept.

Name: Introduction to Art Theory
Introduction: The first part of this course introduces central issues in philosophical aesthetics and philosophy of art. It examines primarily contemporary English-language writers, but occasionally historical figures are also considered. The second part of the course explores philosophical issues related to art criticism in more detail. By the end of the course, students will have a general understanding of some of the key issues in the field of philosophy of art and a detailed understanding of a recent work on philosophical criticism of art.

Name: Introduction to Thoreau
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Solo is a writer and philosopher with far-reaching implications for the modern world. His political thinking has been widely echoed in East and West by the interpretation and transformation of Lev Tolstoy, Mahatma Gandhi, and American black leader Martin Luther King. His life-testing, wild thinking and natural writing, based on superstition, have joined the environmentalist movement of the United States, opening up the global “green” culture and becoming an important source of natural writing and ecological criticism. Since the 1980s, China ' s translation and research into Solo have grown more abundant, and as early as 1996 the United States-Kookbook, The Solo Collection, was translated and published, as well as the correspondence selection, the diary selection and several natural history collections, represented by more than 80 Chinese translations of Lake Walden, which constitute an amazing translation of history. But behind the heat of publication, there is a general trend towards romanticization and simplistic understanding of Solo, and the course attempts to put Solo back into the historical context of hyper-prospectism and the revival of the New England Renaissance, to learn from his life experiments and writing practices, and to bring Solo’s thinking into the current context by reading the text in detail.

Name: Introduction to Environmental Ethics
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The course aims to provide undergraduates with a comprehensive and systematic introduction to the theories, perspectives and methods of environmental ethics practitioners facing the challenges of environmental issues, to help students improve their understanding of environmental ethics issues, so that everyone can have more systematic analysis methods in the discussion and analysis of environmental issues, and at the same time, it can also improve students' environmental awareness.

Name: Close Reading of Leftist Literary Classics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
In recent years, the reading and research of left-wing literary classics has become both a hot topic and a difficult topic. Why read the left-wing literary classics carefully? How to read carefully? This course aims to guide undergraduate students in the Chinese Department to give their own thoughts and responses through the close reading and discussion of more than ten classic works. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Chinese Bibliography and Textual Criticism (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The "Fundamentals of Bibliography" course is based on the basic knowledge and discipline training of classical philology. It focuses on teaching the theoretical methods and practical experience of philology, guiding students to master the essence of philology training, thereby laying a solid foundation and providing lasting motivation for future engagement in Chinese classics and various research related to ancient China. This course is designed to be a four-credit course for a full academic year and is taught over two semesters. The "Fundamentals of Edition and Bibliography (Part 1)" was offered in the last semester, which mainly includes the formation and circulation of ancient books, edition records, edition analysis, edition types, edition identification, edition revision, history of editions, etc.; the "Basics of Edition and Bibliography (Part 2)" will be offered in the next semester and mainly covers the collection and arrangement of ancient books, catalog system, ancient book classification, catalog compilation, abstract writing, history of bibliography, etc.

Name: Foundations of Political Science: Systems and Issues
Introduction: This course is designed to help college freshmen gain a more comprehensive understanding of the overview, system classification and main research topics of today's political science research. It also hopes to provide interested students with a simple path map for further study, which is called a "ladder". It is intended to enable students to obtain intermediate-level, relatively extensive political science knowledge and gain a deeper understanding of certain issues.

Name: Introduction to Marxist Theory
Introduction:
Teach the research object and content of Marxist theory as a subject, the relationship between Marxist theory and other philosophical and social science disciplines, and the actual situation and development of Marxism in contemporary China and the world. _x000D_
   The main contents and questions involved in this course are: Marxism has profoundly changed China and the world. What has it brought to China and the world? What else can Marxism bring to us today? How does it affect the world today and the lifestyle of Chinese people? What has it brought to Chinese ideological theory and the development of Chinese philosophy and social sciences? How to use Marxist methods to study humanities and social sciences? How did a large number of famous masters such as Guo Moruo, Li Da, Ai Siqi, Jian Bozan, Fan Wenlan, Lu Zhenyu, Ma Yinchu, Fei Xiaotong, Qian Zhongshu, etc. use Marxism to carry out academic research and achieve pioneering achievements? What problems and challenges does the development of Marxism in contemporary China face? What opportunities and conditions are we facing? In the new era of becoming stronger, what kind of historical mission does Marxism face, and how do we innovate and develop Marxism? _x000D_

Name: Political Economy
Introduction:
Let students master the basic principles of political economics and understand its position in Marxism; let students master the main content of political economics of socialism with Chinese characteristics and understand its position in socialism with Chinese characteristics. _x000D_
1. The emergence, development, research starting point, objects, tasks and methods of Marxist political economics. _x000D_
2. Socialist Political Economics with Chinese Characteristics_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Classic Works of Marx and Engels (Part 1)
Introduction: This course aims to study and study the classic works of Marx and Engels. By directly reading the original classic works, it will guide students to understand the problem awareness, ideological methods and basic stance of Marxism, so as to master the spiritual gist of Marxism, improve their ability to analyze and solve problems using Marxism, and strengthen their belief in Marxism. Reading classics is the basic method of learning, and learning Marxism requires studying the works of classic writers as they are, so as to lay a solid theoretical foundation. This course is a required course for students majoring in Marxism.

Name: History of the Development of Marxism
Introduction: The history of the development of Marxism is a second-level discipline under the first-level discipline of Marxism. It aims to study the history of the formation and development of Marxism from the perspectives of ideological history and academic history. This subject is based on the basic theory of Marxism, follows the principle of the unity of logic and history, and explores the challenges and lessons learned at various stages of the emergence, dissemination, and development of Marxism, so as to deeply understand the essential spirit of Marxism and provide theoretical support for promoting the development and reality of Marxism.

Name: Marxism Outside China
Introduction: Various critical theories of Western Marxism reflect from one side the various contradictions and conflicts in human history and the evolution of human culture in the 20th century. The rise of Western Marxism not only has a profound theoretical basis, but also has practical cultural and historical reasons. In other words, the rise of Western Marxism is not purely the result of different theoretical interests, but the product of new responses to new cultural and historical backgrounds. We have found that different schools of Western Marxism, no matter how different their theoretical views are, no matter whether their theoretical conclusions are correct or not, have a common characteristic, that is, they all try to formulate new strategies for the proletarian revolutionary movement or human liberation movement based on new historical conditions. In other words, they are the new revolutionary situations and revolutionary conditions that have emerged in the 20th century. Or the changes in the cultural situation of human existence prompted some theorists or politicians to re-examine the theoretical perspectives and revolutionary strategies of Marxism, develop the alienation theory of young Marx under the new historical conditions, or accept the influence of modern Western humanism or scientism trends, which led to the emergence of various Western Marxist schools. Judging from the actual historical process, different schools of Western Marxism did not emerge at the same time, but went through a process of generation. It should be said that the formation process of the Western Marxist school is directly or indirectly related to the overall changes in human history in the 20th century, and can be grasped from the overall background of human culture and history in the 20th century. However, if we examine the differentiation of Marxism more specifically and stage by stage, we will find that there are certain differences in the cultural and historical backgrounds in which the Western Marxist schools emerged in the first half of the 20th century and the middle of the 20th century. Generally speaking, the focus of debate among Marxists in the early 20th century was the fate of the proletarian revolution and the revolutionary strategy. The first generation of Western Marxists represented by Lukács and Gramsci tried to formulate a new proletarian revolutionary strategy based on new historical conditions, thereby completing the historical mission of human liberation. The focus of Marxists in the mid-20th century was the universal survival situation of mankind. They tried to find new ways for modern people to get rid of the common cultural dilemma of alienation or reification and realize human freedom and liberation. Compared with early Western Marxists, the vision of Western Marxists in this period was no longer limited to the proletariat and its revolutionary movement, but broadened to the living conditions of modern people. We can start from the above two aspects and reveal in stages the cultural and historical background of the rise of the Western Marxist school in the 20th century. _x000D_

Name: History and Party Building of the Communist Party of China
Introduction: CCP S.S. research.

Name: Frontier Issues in Marxism
Introduction:
"Frontier Issues in Marxism" is a restricted elective course offered to undergraduates majoring in Marxist theory at the School of Marxism at Peking University and undergraduates from the "Dazhao Class". This course aims to help students gain an in-depth understanding of the status of Marxist research at home and abroad and the focus of academic debates, guide students to consciously read Marxist-related works, cultivate students' awareness of independent thinking and active exploration, and improve their Marxist theoretical literacy and scientific research capabilities. _x000D_
_x000D_
(Note: Classes start for the first time in the first semester of the 2019-2020 school year. Classes are only held in the autumn semester. Actual class duration: 30 hours)

Name: English for Marxist Theory Studies
Prerequisite: English for Junior and Senior High School Students
Introduction: This course is an English course for undergraduates majoring in Marxist theory, aiming to improve students' professional abilities. The course selects English examples of works by Marxist classic writers for explanation, analysis and research, and cultivates professional English literacy in terms of professional knowledge, vocabulary, cultural background and theoretical points.

Name: Sinicized Marxism
Introduction: The course provides a systematic account of the historical origins, cultural foundations and practical needs of Chinese Marxism and describes the theoretical system of Chinese Marxism. Special mention was made of some of the representative figures in the history of the development of Chinese Marxism and an analysis of the characteristics of Chinese Marxism from an international perspective. The course is based on the reading of classic literature and the exploration of academic issues. It is based on the classical text and focuses on theoretical frontier issues. It provides a comprehensive picture of the historical process of Marxist Chineseization and focuses on the major theoretical issues of Chinese Marxism. It focuses on both intellectual and intellectual aspects, and on teaching and research, and seeks to develop a curriculum that integrates political, academic and intellectual aspects.

Name: Twentieth-Century Chinese Aesthetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Chinese aesthetics in the 20th century is an important part of the history of Chinese aesthetics. It inherits the past and connects the future, summarizes Chinese classical aesthetics, absorbs Western aesthetics, and integrates Marxist aesthetics. Facing the current complex literary and artistic reality and social reality, it has produced important aesthetic ideas and produced many aestheticians. It is a very important academic resource for the study of contemporary Chinese aesthetics. Chinese aesthetics in the 20th century is closely related to Chinese literature, art, culture, politics, economy, and society in the 20th century. Aesthetics is a very important perspective to understand China in the 20th century. The purpose of this course is to enable students to understand the development process and achievements of Chinese aesthetics in the 20th century through the teaching of important aesthetic ideas in the 20th century, objectively evaluate its gains and losses, and lay a good academic history foundation for future study and research.

Name: Studies in Twenty-First-Century Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Twenty years have passed since the 21st century. During this period, many changes have taken place in contemporary Chinese literature, and many excellent works have emerged. However, general contemporary literary history courses rarely cover the latest writers' works and literary phenomena. This course will analyze some important literary works since the new century, thereby grasping the literary trend of the new century, and then pay attention to the relationship between literature and social reality, media technology and ideological culture, with a view to advancing the study of contemporary literature.

Name: Studies in Folk Narrative
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a work-selected course offered in conjunction with the "Introduction to Folk Literature" course. Based on a brief description of the basic theories of folk literature, it focuses on narrative and selects rich selections from important genres of folk literature such as myths, legends, stories, jokes, fairy tales, ballads, epics, raps and folk operas. Meaningful texts are introduced and analyzed from different angles. On the one hand, they show the aesthetic mechanism of folk literature that is different from writers' literature. On the other hand, they also reveal the diverse connections between folk literature and people's lives, highlight the essential phenomenon of folk literature as the living world, and stimulate students' direct interest in folk literature. Since most undergraduate students in the Chinese Department receive the influence of writers and literature and may be unfamiliar with folk literature, this course is temporarily planned to be mainly lectured by teachers. Students are required to submit a short course paper at the end of the semester for assessment.

Name: Introduction to Arts Management
Prerequisite: Completion of compulsory first year studies.
Introduction:
This course is a required course for undergraduate majors in cultural industry management. _x000D_
The main purpose of this course is to cultivate students' ability to understand and grasp the laws of arts management activities in today's global context. _x000D_
The main tasks of this course are: based on the current domestic art development, especially the current status of the operation of art institutions, and using the research results of art management in European and American countries as a reference, through systematic classroom teaching, students can independently understand and master the basic theories and practical principles of art management, and cultivate students' ability to understand and grasp the laws of art management activities in today's global context. _x000D_
This course requires students to complete classroom study, read designated references and complete book reports, actively participate in class discussions and presentations, complete practical inspections and submit inspection reports. Through the teaching of this course, students can independently understand and master the basic theories and practical principles of art management, understand the current status of domestic art development, especially the operation of art institutions, understand the research results of domestic and foreign art management, and cultivate students' ability to understand and grasp the laws of art management activities in today's global context, as well as the judgment and decision-making abilities that art management talents should possess. _x000D_

Name: Semantics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: Linguistic overview, modern Chinese, ancient Chinese
Introduction: The subject is an advanced subject in the undergraduate semantics theory. The aim is to provide students with a more comprehensive understanding and mastery of contemporary semantic theory and methods through semantic theory, analysis and practice, as well as initial Chinese-language analytical skills.

Name: Topics in the History of Social Life in Ancient China
Introduction: “Enhanced Historic Perspectives on the Life of the Nation” seeks out the material life of the ancient Chinese people, focusing on the lives and destinies of people of different ages and classes.

Name: Pedagogy of MOOCs
Prerequisite: The university computer base requires learners to have basic computer and Internet use skills.
Introduction: Overview of courses This course is designed for future teachers. Its teaching objective is to enable learners to rediscover and experience the uniqueness and advanced nature of the teaching profession with a new perspective and to update all aspects of traditional perceptions of teachers ' social roles, professional skills and future development. In short, in the era of advanced information technology, the teaching profession began to incorporate an entirely new component — Internet technology — thereby presenting a new teaching model and teaching method, the “teaching doctrine”. The core content of the course is the concept, design and implementation of the curriculum, which involves new concepts such as micro-curriculars, cross-curriculars, truncations, private broadcasts and fast courses. The objective is to provide learners with a new type of computer- and Internet-based teaching and methodological training. In the course of learning, learners who plan to pursue the teaching profession in the future will be provided with various forms of information-based pedagogical skills training that will enable them to acquire new teaching and scientific skills in a web-based environment, apply the new requirements of today ' s digital, networked era to teaching concepts, teaching methods and teaching skills, use the Internet to expand academic influence and expand career development space. The course consists of three core modules: 1. New educational ideas and teaching concepts in the Internet age 2. Career development plans for teachers under MOOC and SPOC 3. New teaching skills and methods required of teachers The curriculum has three main components: 1. To understand how information technologies can be used to design, organize and implement new models of teaching, including the currently popular mix of teaching, overturning of classrooms, eulogy and private broadcasting; 2. Studying a number of methods of micro-studies based on fast-track techniques, including mastery micro-studies, cartoons, video-screens, etc.; 3. Practical training on various web-based teaching skills, such as teaching audio recording, bookboard screens and greenback video filming techniques. Highlighted features of the course: emphasis on hands-on and hands-on skills, emphasis on the development of the learner ' s design skills, and a large number of operational exercises, including hardware and software exercises, will be arranged during the course. Course appraisal methodology: Pedagogical discussion participation (10 per cent) + hands-on training (60 per cent) + operational reporting (5 per cent) + cluster cases (25 per cent).

Name: Personal Finance
Introduction:
In today's society, the political, technological, social and economic environment we live in is changing rapidly every day, and various money-related choices have become more difficult: when and where to buy a house, what kind of car to buy, how to prepare for children's education and retirement, etc. Many financial goals that our parents seemed to have no need to worry about are beginning to trouble our minds. A gentleman loves money, and he must acquire it in a wise way. A gentleman loves money, and he must manage it wisely. A financial plan that comprehensively considers different needs at different stages of life can not only make it easier for us to maintain and increase the value of assets, but also tell us how to acquire, use, accumulate and control assets more easily and efficiently; it can help us allocate limited resources between future and current consumption in the most effective and reasonable manner, allowing people to enjoy life while ensuring future well-being. Systematic financial management training can last a lifetime. _x000D_
_x000D_
The "Personal Finance" course hopes to help students master the basic knowledge and important principles of personal finance by systematically introducing the basic concepts and elements of financial management and the steps of financial planning procedures, understand the main tools of personal and family financial management, and cultivate students' ability to analyze their own financial situation, determine short-term and long-term financial goals, formulate appropriate financial plans and implement them. This course uses multimedia teaching. While introducing basic concepts and ideas, it also uses real case analysis, different types of special discussions, etc. to learn how to conduct complete personal financial planning.

Name: Creative Digital Media Design
Introduction:
This course is a public elective course offered by the School of Education of Peking University to all undergraduates. It is a technology application course related to the educational technology major. The content involves technologies and skills related to digital learning/e-learning (E-learning) design and development, such as electronic courseware development, online course design, digital SLR photography and photo processing (portrait/landscape), video shooting and post-editing (micro video), and live video teaching, etc. _x000D_
The main teaching objectives of this course include three aspects: first, to cultivate and improve the "Digital Media Literacy" of undergraduates in various majors, that is, the ability to acquire, analyze, evaluate and produce various media information in an appropriate manner in the Internet digital environment; second, to explore and stimulate students' potential interest in the teaching profession, and to cultivate high-quality teachers with digital teaching capabilities (E-learning Skills) in the future Internet era; third, to let more outstanding undergraduates understand the educational technology discipline (Educational Technology). Technology), encourages aspiring candidates to apply for a recommended master's degree in this major upon graduation and become a new member of this dynamic academic field. _x000D_

Name: History of Educational Issues in the People's Republic of China
Introduction:
The history of educational issues in the People's Republic of China is based on the problems encountered in the 60-year educational development process from the founding of New China in 1949 to 2008. Looking at every stage of education in New China, we can see that "education", as one of the largest "public spheres", "public departments" and even "public markets", is often driven by various practical issues at that time. Since modern times, the problem demands of new education have been summarized as "education to save the country." In 1949, when the People's Republic of China was founded, the education field assumed the mission of "education to build the country" and participated in the order construction of a new political power in an unprecedented manner. At the end of the 20th century, the strategy of "rejuvenating the country through science and education" was proposed. New China's education has moved from "a poor country running a big education" to a "big country running a strong education", and from a country with a large population to a country with a strong human resources. "Popularization of higher education" and "the world's factory" coexist, causing each other. So far, the country has proposed a comprehensive reform strategy for education, and the clue of the "problem" of education is based on "cultivating people with moral integrity." It can be seen that Chinese education has traditionally cultivated virtues. Since modern times, it has carried various grand ideals of establishing and rejuvenating the country, and has become an important cornerstone of the new regime and New China. After more than 60 years of twists and turns, it has finally returned to the cultivation of individual virtues. _x000D_
The more intrinsic reason for organizing the historical materials and argumentation of the education history of the People's Republic of China from the perspective of "problems" lies in the "dilemma" attributes of education itself: private interests-public welfare, individual rights-state coercion, equality-freedom, inheritance-education, unity-diversity, nationality - Country, family - society, localization - internationalization, inner sage - outer king, self-cultivation - harmonizing the family - governing the country - peace in the world, group - self, a good life of individuals - a beautiful collective society... Among the choices of many dilemmas, the history of education in New China has shaped its own unique trajectory. _x000D_
Based on this historical view, the course content will be developed on the following three levels. First, lay out the historical process and stages according to time clues. The stage division focuses not only on the confirmation of the nature of educational issues by the grand historical framework, but also on the role of micro-events in the process of historical evolution. In order to understand the process and pattern of the educational history of New China, this course will sort out the context of ancient Chinese education from the perspective of the "big historical perspective", then introduce the history of China's "education to save the nation" since modern times, and finally enter into the consideration of the problem perspective of the educational history of New China that unfolded at the historical node of 1949. Secondly, the selection of historical materials at each stage includes four aspects: the education principles and policies of the state and government in various historical periods after the establishment of the new regime; major historical events, important historical figures, and important historical issues in education at all levels and types; the impact of factors involving New China's politics, economy, social changes, science and technology, etc. on education; and the role of education in promoting economic and social reform and development. But each stage has its own focus. Finally, the perspective and concepts of "history of educational issues" are adopted for the analysis of historical materials at each stage, guiding students to "make arguments based on history." _x000D_
It should be noted that the reason why this course focuses on "problem history" does not mean that education in the Republic is full of problems, but rather focuses on the clues of problems in history or the logical exploration of history. The course takes questions as the main content and is organized according to current educational issues: every lecture starts with a question and ends with a question. "History will repeat itself, but it will not be completely the same." The research and teaching of educational history in the past 60 years is different from traditional educational history in that it emphasizes the practical value and reference function of educational history research. Examining the educational history of the People's Republic of China from a problem history perspective can continuously go back and forth between history and reality to achieve the intersection of the two. _x000D_
In terms of standards for selecting and introducing educational history materials, this course is based on helping students understand current realistic educational issues. At the same time, it highlights the historical outline of educational issues. So far, the process and stages of educational development in New China have relatively clear focus points. From a long-term inspection of the educational issues focused on at each stage, we can also clearly see the historical overview of this educational issue and grasp the development context of this educational issue.
