To this end, this course uses the educational issues that have emerged continuously in the long history of China's educational development and the problems that have occurred repeatedly in the history of education as the basis for organizing the materials. _x000D_
This course will organize the arrangement and teaching process of course content based on a series of original archival documents and a basic educational history outline. These materials can also be provided to students for further in-depth exploration of related issues, and can also provide some guidance for the research of educational historians. _x000D_
In addition, reading and studying history requires future generations to find ways to immerse themselves in the situation at that time in order to understand the action logic and evolution logic of important historical figures and historical events. Therefore, in each historical stage, this course will also present some songs sung in schools at that time, movies watched by organizations, and novels popularly read to help students understand historical situations, historical events, and historical figures immersively. This is also a very important means in school education. The history of education cannot ignore life history. If you add a slight supplement of life history to the main line of institutional history, you will see the tension and mutual construction process between institutions and daily life. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Chinese Ancient Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The main subjects are ancient catalogues, versions, calibrations, identifications, etc., as well as ancient phrases, ancient usages, and the patterns and characteristics of ancient words.

Name: Introduction to Das Kapital
Introduction:
The first volume of "Das Kapital" systematically expounds the basic theories of commodity value, surplus value, capital accumulation, etc., profoundly reveals the nature of capitalist production relations and the development laws of the capitalist mode of production, and demonstrates the historical nature of the capitalist mode of production and its historical development trend that it will eventually be replaced by socialism. The theory elaborated in this volume is not only a guide to scientifically understand the essential characteristics of contemporary capitalist economy, but also the basic theoretical basis for upholding and developing socialism with Chinese characteristics. _x000D_
The first volume of "Das Kapital" consists of 7 parts and 25 chapters, which are roughly divided into three parts: The first part, the first part, studies commodities and currency, reveals the essence and general laws of commodity production, mainly expounds the labor theory of value, and lays a theoretical foundation for further analysis of the direct production process of capital. The second part, namely Chapters 2 to 6, studies the preconditions, process and essence of capitalist production, reveals the law of surplus value, and mainly elaborates on the labor commodity theory, surplus value theory and wage theory. The theory of surplus value production is the core theory of the first volume and the whole book. The third part, Chapter 7, studies the accumulation process of capital, reveals the nature and development laws of capital accumulation and capitalist reproduction, and mainly expounds the theory of historical trends of relative surplus population and capitalist accumulation. It is the foothold and concluding part of the first volume. _x000D_
The various theories developed around the "production process of capital" in the first volume not only form a relatively independent and complete theoretical system, but also provide a theoretical basis for further analysis in the second and third volumes. Therefore, Volume One occupies an extremely important position in the entire book of Capital. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Major Issues of Modern Chinese History
Introduction: This course is mainly for undergraduate students in this major. The modern history of China since 1840 is rich in content and covers a wide area. In the form of a special study, this course attempts to show students the development process of China's modern history from all aspects of historical development, in an all-round and multi-angle manner, through the introduction and research of major historical events and basic historical issues that have occurred in China since the Opium War. Its purpose is to enable students to understand and understand modern Chinese history from multiple levels and angles, and to have a deeper understanding of the social and historical development of modern China and its inherent regularities.

Name: Theory and Practice of the Great Rejuvenation of the Chinese Nation
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the theoretical and practical exploration of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, focusing on the impact of major historical events in China's modern history on the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation, and explaining the theories, goals, and strategic steps for realizing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation in contemporary China.

Name: Ancient Egyptian Hieroglyphs (I)
Prerequisite: Egyptian studies, or ancient Eastern civilization.
Introduction:
The compulsory professional course for Egyptian students in ancient history is an advanced course in ancient Egyptian hieroglyphics, with the aim of guiding students to begin reading and translating ancient Egyptian literature directly on the basis of basic Chinese-Egyptian grammar.
Requests:
1. A weekly translation of the ancient Egyptian literature;
2. Translation of relevant original historical material in conjunction with their paper requirements.

Name: Ancient Anatolian Civilization
Prerequisite: This course is a basic course and is usually offered in the first year of the program. There are no prerequisite courses. At the beginning of the semester, teachers introduce and distribute relevant course learning materials and information to students, introduce the basic situation of textbooks and reference books, and guide students to read and study based on their own situations. In addition, teachers appropriately distribute learning materials to students based on the actual situation to guide students' learning.
Introduction:
Ancient Anatolian civilizations are an important part of early human civilization. They not only have independent civilization origins and development paths, but also have relatively close connections and interactions with ancient civilizations in the surrounding world. For a long time, the research on ancient Anatolian civilizations has not received due attention in Chinese academic circles. Their civilization paths have been covered up by the research on civilizations of ancient powers or a major region. One of the results of such neglect is the incomplete understanding of the origin and early development of human civilization. It cannot reveal the universal and specific laws of the early development of human civilization, and it is impossible to establish a scientific and systematic research system on ancient civilizations. _x000D_
The content and framework taught in this course include the history and culture of the civilizations of the Asia Minor peninsula since prehistory, the third millennium, the second millennium and the first millennium BC, that is, the prehistoric history and culture, the history and culture of the Hattians, the history and culture of the Hittites, the history and culture of the Hurits, the history and culture of the Luvians and Paleks, the history and culture of the Phrygians, the history and culture of Lydia and Lycians, and the discussion of the historical and cultural development of Anatolia during the Hellenistic period and the Achaemenid period. In particular, we will focus on the history and culture of the Indo-Europeans and the relationship with the history and culture of other ethnic groups to analyze and understand the ancient civilization in this region as comprehensively as possible. On the basis of explaining the content of each part separately, connect and compare the similarities and differences of each culture in different historical stages, and the relationship with other cultures on the peninsula and outside the peninsula. Discuss issues such as the universality, particularity and diversity of the historical and cultural development of ancient Anatolia. _x000D_

Name: Akkadian Grammar
Introduction: This course is devoted to the grammar of the wedge language Acadian to enable students to read basic Acadian literature.

Name: Reading Sumerian Texts
Prerequisite: The course trains students to read the Sumerian language literature, starting with the Sumerian grammar course.
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to teach students how to read the Sumerian literature on the basis of mastery of Sumerian grammar.

Name: Reading Akkadian Texts
Prerequisite: This course trains students to read Aka German literature, with the initial course being Aka German.
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to teach students how to read the documents of the German language on the basis of their knowledge of the German language.

Name: Topics in Sui and Tang History
Introduction: This course intends to use the "cultural view of history" advocated by Mr. Chen Yinke to examine the historical background and development trends of the Sui and Tang Dynasties from a macro perspective (longer period and larger space), systematically study the humanistic environment and social structure of Sui and Tang Dynasties, and generally grasp and understand the status of Sui and Tang societies in ancient Chinese history, thereby enhancing people's understanding of Chinese society and traditions. Basic ideas: social history - overall history; history is formed under certain environmental conditions; the trend of cultural integration in multi-ethnic countries.

Name: Topics in Song History
Introduction: Presentation of Song Dynasty ' s history and its related research, helping beginners to establish the concept of Song Shi, inspire interest in exploration and lay the foundation for research.

Name: Theories of Social Development
Introduction: The course focuses on the theory of social development of Marxist classic writers, the historical process of modernization of the world and the evolution of the theory of development, the innovation of Chinese-style socialist development paths and theories and their contribution to the world. The aim is to equip students with the social development theory of Marxism and Chinese socialism, to acquire basic knowledge of modern and social development theory and to understand the patterns of social development.

Name: Introduction to Classic Works of Marx and Engels (Part 2)
Prerequisite: Introduction to Classic Works of Marx and Engels (Part 1)
Introduction: This course aims to study and study the classic works of Marx and Engels. By directly reading the original classic works, it will guide students to understand the problem awareness, ideological methods and basic stance of Marxism, so as to master the spiritual gist of Marxism, improve their ability to analyze and solve problems using Marxism, and strengthen their belief in Marxism. Reading classics is the basic method of learning, and learning Marxism requires studying the works of classic writers as they are, so as to lay a solid theoretical foundation. This course is a required course for students majoring in Marxism.

Name: Contemporary Capitalism
Introduction: The course focuses on analysing and exploring new changes in contemporary capitalism, revealing its development patterns and the crises it faces. This course will begin with a summary of the development patterns of capitalism as a whole, based on a brief history of capitalist development, in order to lay the foundation for our understanding today of the changes in contemporary capitalism. Secondly, the course will carry out a detailed analysis and discussion of contemporary capitalism ' s political system, economic system, cultural system, social structure and social policy on a case-by-case basis to reveal the patterns of development of contemporary capitalism and the problems it faces. Finally, there is a discussion of the impact of contemporary capitalism on the modern international political and economic order, the challenges to the contemporary socialist system and how we should actively address them.

Name: Topics in the Cultural History of Ancient Northern Chinese Peoples
Introduction: This course focuses on several topics in the cultural history of ancient northern China. The main content includes three parts: means of production and production methods, production and utilization of means of living, and material manifestations of spiritual culture. It focuses on the induction, comparison, and analysis of material data, and uses this as a basis to explain the cultural factors contained in them. This course aims to enhance students' comprehensive understanding of the culture of ancient northern Chinese peoples, further deepen the content of ancient Chinese history teaching on the history of northern ethnic groups, and inspire students to use more systematic knowledge of cultural history to analyze various historical and practical issues related to ancient national history. (This course requires your own computer classroom or multimedia classroom)

Name: Ming and Qing Palace Architecture and Interior Furnishings
Introduction: This course is divided into three parts. The first is the origin, layout and architectural history of the Forbidden City; the second is the development overview of interior eaves decoration, design and production, and decoration characteristics; the third is an overview of the original indoor furnishings, analysis of original restoration cases, and the thoughts, interests and hobbies reflected in the original furnishings.

Name: Topics in Italian History
Introduction: This course is an elective course for the history major of Peking University and is taught to undergraduate students in the history department. In view of the serious lack of Italian history in domestic history education at all levels, this course is designed as a general historical and chronological special course structure, covering the entire civilization process from the beginning of human settlement on the Apennine Peninsula to the present. Revealing the overall characteristics and stage characteristics of Italy's long historical process, summarizing the laws of conflict and integration of various civilizations on the Italian peninsula, and clarifying the main issues in the four major fields of politics, economy, society, culture and art have become the main tasks of this course. At the same time, since Italian civilization is a core component of Mediterranean civilization, and Mediterranean civilization occupies an important position in the entire human civilization family, this course also pays attention to the overall characteristics of Mediterranean civilization. In addition, this course pays great attention to the introduction of academic trends inside and outside Italy, especially in Italy. The course is equipped with a computer projector, which increases the amount of information. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic knowledge of Italian history and culture and understand the characteristics of Mediterranean civilization. Develop a unique perspective on Western civilization and improve historical research and appreciation. Students who are interested in Italy are welcome to audit this course.

Name: The Science and Culture behind Wine
Introduction:
"The Science and Culture Behind Wine" is a public elective course open to all students in the school. _x000D_
The purpose of the course teaching is to cultivate students' comprehensive understanding of wine, a biological product and modern business language, and to improve Peking University students' ability to appreciate wine, thereby improving students' self-cultivation. _x000D_
The main contents of the course include: wine grape varieties and cultivation management, wine brewing technology, the world's major wine producing areas, the impact of wine on human health, wine appreciation and wine culture, etc. _x000D_
The teaching goal of this course is to enable students to understand the science and culture behind wine, master the basic theories and methods of wine tasting, and become familiar with the world's major wine types and production areas. _x000D_

Name: The World of Education through Images
Introduction:
middle? Introduction _x000D_
This course is dedicated to helping students better understand the social, economic, legal, cultural and political background of education in China and other countries, with a particular focus on discussing education issues from both economic and legal perspectives. This course focuses on four important relationships: education and economic development; education and equal protection; education and the right to education; education and free choice. Topics in this course include education for minority and disadvantaged groups, gender and education, cross-cultural perspectives on teaching and learning, and more. We integrate film and documentaries into teaching to facilitate discussion, awareness and discussion of the subject matter. In terms of geographical selection, we focus on China and other East Asian countries. Course readings and discussions will have a strong comparative character (comparing China, Japan, the United States, and other countries). The fundamental purpose of curriculum design is to inspire students to think about education while receiving education; on the basis of thinking about education, they should further pay attention to and contribute to education. _x000D_

Name: Modern Chinese History Exercises
Prerequisite: First course: recent Chinese history, modern history
Introduction: This semester, “Counterday History Practice in China”, is a compulsory subject for undergraduate students at the Faculty of History. The basic objectives of this course are: to give students a basic overview of the history of China at this time, its main clues and its evolution; to acquire basic knowledge, basic theory and basic methods of recent history disciplines in China; to learn about the status of relevant research and important cutting-edge academic developments; and to learn about important historical facts, historical histories and knowledge points. At the same time, basic training is provided to students in their modern history cognitive skills, literature reading skills and initial scientific research skills, particularly in the writing of dissertations.

Name: Lecture Series on the Development History of New China
Introduction:
This course is a series of special lectures jointly offered by experts and professors. The full-time and part-time teachers of the "History Research Center of the People's Republic of China", a newly approved entity research institution established by the school, and invited external experts, each use their own unique research to jointly teach college students. _x000D_
      The People's Republic of China has passed 70 years. The rapid and huge social changes in these 70 years are far greater than any period of this length in Chinese history. Its distinctive development achievements and characteristics of the times are unprecedented. _x000D_
      Over the past 70 years, both revolution and construction have accumulated extremely rich historical resources, which are worthy of in-depth discussion, summary, study and reflection by today's people. _x000D_
      Only by conscientiously studying and in-depth studying the development process of our republic can we have a profound understanding of the historical path and current situation of revolution, construction, reform and opening up, and provide solid academic reference for China's future development. _x000D_
      The series of speeches and instructions by party and state leaders emphasizing that "the history of the Party and the country is a compulsory course" fully express the importance of education in the history of the Republic. Therefore, it is necessary to teach our college students the history of the Republic in which we live. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: General Survey of Paleography
Introduction:
Chinese paleography is a comprehensive subject. This discipline takes the written remains on pre-Qin relics as its main research object, uses the method of historical linguistics as its main research method, and interprets the historical facts and linguistic phenomena recorded in ancient written materials as its main research goal. Therefore, Chinese paleography can be regarded as an important branch of Chinese archeology, and it is also the most important growth point of historical linguistics and historical philology. _x000D_
Since the Han Dynasty, Chinese paleography has taken off and has a long history of development. By the first half of the 20th century, scientific Chinese paleography began to be established. In the second half of the 20th century, Chinese paleography made great progress and formed a set of strict norms and methods. At the same time, because the 20th century was an era of great discoveries of ancient writing materials, Chinese paleography has made extremely important contributions to the interpretation of archaeological data. _x000D_
   This course mainly includes: 1. An overview of the academic history of paleography; 2. Basic methods of paleography; 3. Discovery and introduction of ancient writing materials; 4. Selected lectures on ancient writing materials. It is hoped that through this course, lower-grade undergraduate students can have a good introduction to paleography and lay a foundation for future related courses. _x000D_

Name: Appreciation of Cultural Relics
Introduction: This course mainly tells the culture and history of China from the perspective of cultural relics. It selects a number of national treasure-level cultural relics from the Neolithic Age to the Yuan and Ming Dynasties, covering: pottery, bronze, jade, porcelain, calligraphy and painting, etc. Learn about the culture and history carried by cultural relics through each specific cultural relic.

Name: Modern British Poetry
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Prerequisite: None. University English-level examination level C
Introduction:
This is a poetry course for non-English majors. In chronological order, it introduces the nine most representative poets in the history of modern and contemporary British literature, namely Houseman, Hopkins (whose poems were not published until 1918), Hardy, Yeats (57 years old when the Irish Free State was established), Auden, Thomas, Larkin, Hughes and Heaney (who lived in Northern Ireland until 1972). It focuses on the close reading of the works, combined with the poet's life and historical and cultural background, trying to clarify the unique artistic achievements of each poet. Shows the development trajectory of modern British poetry. The purpose is to stimulate students' interest in poetry, cultivate their appreciation of English poetry, and improve their English proficiency and literary literacy. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: History of Daoism
Introduction: The historical development of Taoism, which originated from China's native beliefs, is not only a basic topic in Taoist research, but also a sample issue in the study of the history of Chinese beliefs and religious development models. As the basic work of Taoist research, the study of Taoist history has a large amount of research foundation. However, basic topics such as the research scope, research methods, material collection and narrative mode of Taoist history are worthy of further discussion. From a macro perspective, the history of Taoism is the epitome of the history of Chinese people’s beliefs and a typical representative of Chinese belief culture. From a specific perspective, the history of religion, which consists of Taoist sects and historical figures, is thin and unconvincing compared to the rich practice of Taoism and its close integration with the religious life of the Chinese people. This course uses the history of issues and special research methods, in addition to the clues of sects and historical figures, and on the basis of the existing general history of Taoism, trying to interpret the value of Taoism as a belief tradition in the lives of Chinese people and the world of belief based on the characteristics of Chinese belief traditions and the supernatural world. This provides a new aspect for the value of Taoism in Chinese culture.

Name: Enlightenment Philosophy
Introduction: This course will re-examine and evaluate modern Western philosophy from the perspective of enlightenment, thereby constructing a new interpretation paradigm and changing the long-term misunderstanding of modern Western philosophy in China. The reason why the Enlightenment is regarded as the main line of perspective on modern Western philosophy is because the Enlightenment is the overall process of modern Western history, including various factors of Western social transformation, various types of political systems, various forms of knowledge, and rational assumptions about cognition and practice. The ideas of modern Western philosophy originated, operated, and developed precisely in the context of the entire Western Enlightenment. More importantly, the issue of enlightenment is also an important issue facing Western philosophy today.

Name: German Classical Aesthetics and Philosophy of Art
Introduction: German classical aesthetics and art philosophy are the first peaks of modern aesthetics and are also important components of German classical philosophy. The aim of this course is to deepen the understanding of the ideas and to raise the level and depth of thinking in this field by choosing the classic aesthetic and artistic philosophy texts of the philosophers Kandeh, Schiller, Romanticism in Germany, Shelling and Hegel, on the basis of an initial understanding of the principles of aesthetics. The curriculum focuses on classroom teaching, while encouraging and directing students to study the classic texts and complete classroom reports, and preparing students to try to independently undertake preliminary studies on aesthetic history through reading and analysis of original texts and related research writings.

Name: Humanities Classics and Frontiers: Philosophy and History B
Introduction:
This semester's course focuses on moral and emotional issues in the ancient world, and will focus on relevant texts from Aristotle to demonstrate the richness of this topic and its relevance to contemporary life from different perspectives. The three leading teachers will demonstrate the basic methods of reading ancient classics and contemporary research trends from different academic backgrounds and disciplinary perspectives. _x000D_
Teacher Wu Tianyue will take "Nicomachean Ethics" as the core, focusing on the core topic of good life and rational ability, to explore Aristotle's concept of happiness, the basic nature of ethical research, functional argumentation, correct rationality and practical wisdom, lack of self-control and other basic ethical issues. Focus on the constructive role of reason in a good life and its operation. _x000D_
Teacher Cheng Wei will discuss the beginning of Aristotle's "The Eudemian Ethics=EE" and its discussion of voluntary behavior and responsibility. He will use this theme as a case to compare the similarities and differences in the methods and doctrines of EE and the Nicomachean Ethics. He will also examine the applicability of Aristotle's action/moral philosophy in the fictional world based on the discussion of the concept of Hamartia in the Poetics, especially the issue of the moral responsibility of the protagonist in ideal tragedy. _x000D_
Teacher Lin Lijuan will lead everyone to study some chapters of Aristotle's "Rhetoric", focusing on his discussion of emotion theory. She will combine relevant parts of "On the Soul", "Nicomachean Ethics", and "Poetics" to discuss issues such as how rhetoric stimulates emotions, Aristotle's definition of emotion, how to restrain emotions, etc., and will use individual emotions, such as shame, as examples to illustrate these aspects. In addition, in the discussion, she will try her best to take into account Aristotle's previous discussions on emotion and rhetoric, such as the Sophists and Plato, as well as relevant theories in contemporary philosophy of emotion. _x000D_

Name: History of Islam
Introduction: Introduce the history of the rise and spread of Islam, as well as Islamic sects and Arab Islamic culture. To enable students to understand the historical process of the emergence and development of Islam, to have a preliminary grasp of important historical events, classic teachings, sectarian origins and other issues, to cultivate students' ability to analyze and understand religious phenomena, and to arouse their interest in further research.

Name: History of Christianity in China
Introduction:
_x000D_
This course briefly introduces the history of the spread and development of Christianity in China since it was introduced to China in the Tang Dynasty. It uses the interaction between Christianity and Chinese culture in historical circumstances as an entry point to explore the following questions: Is there a religion in Chinese culture that is compatible with Christian spirit and thought? What are the essential similarities and differences between the two? Is it possible for the two ambitions to understand each other, interpret each other and coexist? Is it possible for the interaction between the two to contribute to the changes and evolution of Chinese and Western cultures? What is the ideological mechanism by which the interaction between the two produces creative cultural results? What factors have affected the fate of Christianity in China? Which factor is crucial? etc.

Name: Selected Readings in Indian Buddhist Classics
Introduction:
This course selects relatively important classics in the history of Indian Buddhism, with moderate length and difficulty level, and uses them as a discussion class_x000D_
for reading and discussion. Through the selection of original works, students can have initial contact with Buddhist classics and deepen their understanding of _x000D_
understanding of Buddhism and develop the ability to read and process original texts.

Name: Topics in Christianity
Introduction: This course is a course on the Crusades taught by Italian professor Nanetti hired by the Department of Philosophy and Religious Studies. There is little research on this topic in domestic universities, so we specially hired Professor Nanetti to teach this course. The course content covers the main events of the Crusades and will be of great significance to understanding medieval Christianity and the Christian view of war.

Name: Selected English Essays: From the Victorian Period to the Twentieth Century
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: "Selected Readings of English Prose: The Victorian Period from the 19th Century to the 20th Century" is a college English module C course for non-English major undergraduate students. This course is divided into four stages: 19th-century Victorian English prose, 19th-century American English prose, 20th-century English prose (Part 1), and 20th-century English prose (Part 2). It selects key writers from this period respectively, combines social and historical characteristics, takes into account the thoughts and academic tastes of the times, and covers the stylistic characteristics and changes as well as historical connections and influences of prose in this period. The teaching of this course focuses on classic writers and their works, intensifies literary criticism and literary appreciation, deepens the understanding of each writer and their prose style, and strives to achieve the unity of systematicity, ideological and academic aspects.

Name: Introduction to Chinese Aesthetics
Introduction: This course is a required course for graduate students majoring in aesthetics in the Department of Philosophy, and is also open to undergraduate students. It aims to enable students to understand the historical context and main fields of Chinese aesthetics, grasp the nature, scope and main research methods of Chinese aesthetics, the current status of research and the directions and focus of further research. This course requires students to have a preliminary knowledge base of Chinese traditional culture, Chinese philosophy and Chinese aesthetics, and to be able to read ancient documents independently.

Name: Studies in Contemporary Western Political Philosophy
Introduction: This course examines the core concepts, major issues and major schools in contemporary Western political philosophy. The class will discuss the debates surrounding how to define concepts such as "politics", "power", "justice", "freedom", "equality" and "democracy", as well as the theoretical and practical significance of these debates; it will also explore how political philosophy can actively explore, intervene in and reflect on various new and old issues facing contemporary society, such as institutional design, wealth redistribution, globalization, immigration, identity politics, populism, global warming, counter-terrorism, etc.

Name: Health Economics
Prerequisite: Ask your students to study economics principles (I, II) and learn the basics and language of microeconomics
Introduction: Health economics is an important sub-discipline of economics that emerged in the 1970s. It mainly studies various economic issues related to scarce health resources. The main contents of this course include health economics research methods, supply and demand for health services, health economic evaluation methods, asymmetric information problems in the medical and health service market, the collection, allocation and use of health expenses, international comparisons of medical financing systems, China's health system reform issues, etc. The purpose of this course is to help students master the basic principles of health economics, understand the main models of medical and health market operation, understand the operating mechanism of medical financing systems, including international typical medical insurance systems, and initially cultivate students' ability to combine economics and health service research methods to observe and analyze theoretical and policy issues in the medical and health field.

Name: Wang Yuanhua in Intellectual History
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course intends to examine Wang Yuanhua’s (1920-2008) lifelong academic and ideological experience from the perspective of the history of modern and contemporary Chinese thought, and explore the interaction between Wang Yuanhua’s academic exploration and work and the history of modern and contemporary Chinese thought. The course focuses on Wang Yuanhua's "three readings" (i.e. reading Hegel's "Little Logic" and "Aesthetics", reading Shakespeare, and reading "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons"), Wang Yuanhua's three reflections, etc. It is hoped that students will have a certain degree of understanding and grasp of the development process of Chinese modern and contemporary literary theory and ideological scholarship through the case of Wang Yuanhua. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Marx's Early Thought
Introduction: The focus of this course is on the ideas of the early Marx period, the Rhine period and before, and it is planned to develop the context of the early Marx thinking by reading and analysing the relevant texts.

Name: Modern Continental Philosophy
Introduction: This course explains the classic work "Totality and Infinity" by Levinas, a famous contemporary French phenomenological philosopher, to guide students to understand the basic issues and ideological context of contemporary phenomenology and French philosophy, and thereby understand the overall development trend of contemporary European philosophy.

Name: Hume's Philosophy
Introduction:
The course is based on the principles of humanity, human rationality, ethical principles, and natural religious dialogue, and systematically teaches the philosophy of peace. It covers the areas of intellectuals, physical education, moral philosophy, political philosophy and religious philosophy, and each course focuses on the complete structure of the philosophy.
By placing it in the context of modern Western enlightenment, the curriculum seeks to avoid and correct the one-sided emphasis on its empirical ideology, and attempts to present more comprehensively and honestly the basic idea of the philosophy of the disease and its academic significance in order to determine its importance in the history of Western philosophy.
It also had an important impact on modern philosophy of the twentieth century. His empiricalism, karma theory, psychology, naturalism, skepticism, moral philosophy, the theory of justice, etc., are topical issues of today ' s philosophical discourse. The curriculum seeks to develop an analytical approach from the point of view of modern philosophies in order to provide an in-depth interpretation of the peace texts, to guide students to a comprehensive understanding of the philosophy of peace and to enable them to reach out more quickly and better to the issues at the forefront of contemporary philosophies.

Name: Introduction to the Quran
Introduction: This course introduces the basic methods and related theoretical issues in Quran exegesis, provides a brief interpretation of the main chapters in the Mecca and Medina chapters of the Quran, guides students to read the original Quran, and arouses interest in further research.

Name: Topics in the History of Western Science and Technology
Introduction: This course will focus on the history of the development of Western science and technology after the Scientific Revolution by topic, so that students who are interested in studying the history of science and technology, philosophy of science and technology, science and technology policy and management will have a preliminary understanding of the development of modern science and technology.

Name: History of Contemporary Europe and the European Union
Introduction:
This course will introduce to Peking University undergraduate students the historical evolution of European history after 1945, especially the history of European integration. This course will examine the events that changed the course of the Cold War in Europe and led to the unification of Germany and the subsequent formation of the European Union. It will then focus on the post-Cold War process of consolidating and enlarging the European Union as a unified entity that emerged as an alternative pole in international relations. _x000D_
The confrontation of the first years of the Cold War led to the consolidation of the two blocs and the bipolar monopoly of nuclear arsenals. This in turn gradually inspired the emergence of détente in the 1960s as a bipolar monopoly of peace. The easing of bipolar confrontation and growing dissatisfaction with this new bipolar condominium ultimately strengthened the efforts of superpower allies Europe to seek independence in Primis and laid the foundation for new forms of mutual engagement. _x000D_
In the early 1960s, a number of fundamental trends in Western Europe converged to inspire a "new perspective" that ultimately led to the creation of the European Economic Community in the following decade. Washington's European allies are increasingly concerned about the transatlantic relationship, which is increasingly seen as an unfairly uneven hierarchy. Strategic parity between the superpowers and Europe's dependence on the US nuclear umbrella and economic design (especially the Marshall Plan) created an existential dilemma for European independence and sowed intellectual seeds in Europe for alternatives to the dictates of bipolar logic. If in the 1950s the European Economic Community had represented a promising new continental institution for indigenous innovation, it was almost natural that in the 1960s some Europeans looked behind the Iron Curtain for the possibility of what Egon Bahr called "change through reconciliation." _x000D_
The impact of détente and intra-European dialogue changed the course of the Cold War in the 1970s and eventually led to the institutionalization of dialogue, notwithstanding the establishment of the Conference on Security and Cooperation in 1975. _x000D_
The breakdown of Soviet hegemonic control in Eastern Europe in the 1990s, coupled with increased economic dynamism and integration on the Western Front through the European Economic Community, led to the first unification of Germany in the 1990s and the establishment of the European Union and the Maastricht Treaty. _x000D_
The 2000s marked the EU's eastward enlargement, the inclusion of the former Soviet satellites in Eastern Europe under a new common currency, the euro, and the new implementation of economic integration through the Lisbon Treaty. _x000D_
The course will conclude with an assessment of the EU's role in today's international system and its relationship with major powers such as the United States, Russia and China.

Name: International Security Studies
Introduction: This course aims to introduce the basic concepts and theoretical framework of international security as well as the main issues of international security since World War II, so that students can independently analyze international security issues and have a certain theoretical and historical depth. The course is mainly divided into three parts: the first part mainly introduces the basic concepts and theoretical framework, including the disciplinary positioning of international security studies in political science and international relations, its connotation and extension, direct use of force and coercive diplomacy, nuclear deterrence and conventional deterrence, offense and defense, crisis management, etc.; the second part focuses on the Cold War period, mainly introducing the international environment, national How domestic politics and technological progress have affected the strategic choices of major powers, and what are the experiences and lessons of these strategic choices in maintaining national security; the third part introduces some of the main challenges faced by international security after the end of the Cold War, including nuclear proliferation and nuclear disarmament, terrorism, the rise of great powers, military technological revolution, network security and network warfare, etc. Finally, it should be noted that this course mainly focuses on the so-called traditional security, and does not pay much attention to many non-traditional security issues-climate change, transnational crime, energy crisis, combating piracy, etc.

Name: Applied Econometrics
Prerequisite: This course is intended for the upper undergraduate students in Economics, Business or other social science majors. Graduate students are also welcome. Prior training in Introductory Econometrics or Statistics is required. The main focus of the course is to use econometric tools to solve real-world problems, and thus we will not spend much time on the mathematical derivation of basic models.
Introduction: This course aims to systematically introduce common research methods in econometrics and cultivate students' ability to independently use econometric models and computer software to analyze and solve empirical economic problems. The course mainly covers the following content: linear regression and selection of functional forms, heteroscedasticity and serial correlation, basic and advanced time series models, mixed cross-sectional and panel data models, discrete choice models, endogeneity and instrumental variable estimation, simultaneous equation models, etc. The computer programming techniques (SAS software) required to implement the above models will also be taught in class. At the same time, students will have the opportunity to independently use real-life economic data to conduct project research, thereby improving their scientific research capabilities.

Name: Political Game Theory
Introduction:
Over the past few decades, game theory has become one of the most powerful analytical tools and research approaches in political science-related fields. In this approach, individual decisions and behaviors depend on the expectations and behaviors of others, and the core of the analysis is the interaction between actors. Game theory models have been widely used to analyze war, diplomacy, negotiation and conflict resolution, inter-institutional relations, collective action, leadership, voting and elections, and other related political environments and scenarios. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will introduce basic game theory and its applications to political science. The goal of this course is to enable students who choose this course to master the necessary knowledge and abilities for introductory and advanced content of game theory, so as to understand the research related to game theory in different fields of political science, and have the ability to initially use game theory for academic exploration. _x000D_
_x000D_
To this end, this course covers basic concepts of game theory, including Nash equilibria and their major improvements, simultaneous and sequential games, repeated games, games with incomplete and private information, Bayesian equilibria, and more. In addition, this course will also introduce some core models used in political science research, such as the median voter theorem in public choice, bargaining in cooperation and competition in international relations, conflict models, etc. While highlighting the strengths of game theory, this course will also explore its shortcomings. Through teaching, discussion, practice and application, it will guide students to think about what are "good" and "appropriate" social science research paths, methods and tools. _x000D_

Name: Theory and Practice of Social Survey
Introduction: This course is a practical course for social surveys carried out by Yan Fu class students. It highly integrates the social science survey theories learned previously and further enhances students' research sentiment, research literacy and abilities in practice.

Name: Introduction to Academic Research in the Social Sciences
Introduction: Social research is the key to the development of an undergraduate understanding and analysis of a complex social world, the creation of an appropriate sense of experience and the internalization of theoretical education. The ability to train in social research, methodology (which includes scientific history and science philosophy) and methodology and research crafts are the three key levels, while research crafts and researchers ' materials and problems are the closest to awareness and the best to capture the researcher ' s personality, while teaching is the least easy. The course will begin with a research process to explore better social research techniques in interdisciplinary undergraduate training programmes.

Name: Introduction to Africa
Introduction: Being coerced into a modern world system with little control through exploitation and force is a major factor in most of Africa's modern problems and suffering. Therefore, this course uses time as the axis, starting from the pre-colonial period, colonial rule, post-colonial period and the era of globalization, to discuss African politics and the changes in Africa's position in the world system.	_x000D_

Name: Twentieth-Century Western Music
Introduction: Although "Western Music in the 20th Century" is a chronological history of the "General History of Western Music", it has become an independent discipline in the field of global Western music history research because it is close to the present and all-inclusive. Due to historical reasons, China’s teaching of Western music history has long had a “braised middle” phenomenon, that is, it only teaches the two stylistic periods of Classicism and Romanticism (1750-1900). The previous Baroque, Renaissance, Middle Ages, Ancient Greece and Ancient Rome periods, and the subsequent 20th century were rarely covered, hence the reputation. In recent years, this situation has greatly improved, and the level has also improved rapidly. Since the teacher studied for a doctorate in this subject at the Central Conservatory of Music from 2000 to 2004, he has taught this course many times for students in the musicology teacher training courses of his alma mater and Chinese universities. After teaching at Peking University in 2007, it was offered as a public elective course in the second semester of 2008, the first semester of 2009, and the second semester of 2010. It was established as a general elective course in 2011. "20th Century Western Music" is an independent course covering three major research topics, namely art music (classical music in a broad sense), folk music and commercial music (popular music). On the premise of following the three major topics, the course content has different emphasis in different semesters and is not the same. For example, in 2010, it was "Special Topic on Western Piano Music in the 20th Century", in 2011 it was "Special Topic on Art Music", in 2012 it was "Special Topic on Popular Music", etc.

Name: China and Africa: A Global Encounter
Introduction: The course is offered in English.

Name: Occupations and Modern Society
Introduction:
This course will teach students the important concepts and basic principles of occupational sociology and related social theories through a systematic introduction and criticism of the historical evolution and main academic achievements of Western occupational sociology. In the course, the social attributes of doctors, lawyers, engineers, accountants, university teachers, journalists, artists, firefighters, etc. will be discussed in depth. By comparing the similarities and differences between various professions, students will be provided with diversified theoretical perspectives and empirical research ideas for understanding the development of various traditional and emerging professions in contemporary Chinese society. _x000D_
_x000D_
The reading content of this course will start with the classic works of Durkheim, Parsons, the Chicago School, and the Neo-Marxist School, and introduce and sort out several major theoretical traditions of occupational sociology research, including social function theory, market control theory, jurisdictional conflict theory, etc., and take some major contemporary Western occupational sociology literature as examples to explore occupational division of labor, social structure, professional skills, careers, market competition, national regulation, globalization and other related empirical issues.

Name: Principles of Accounting
Prerequisite: Before learning Accounting Principles, it would be desirable for students to start with major courses in economics and finance.
Introduction: Principles of Accounting mainly talks about the introduction of accounting, accounting subjects and double-entry bookkeeping, accounting vouchers, accounting books, current assets, long-term assets, liabilities, owner's equity, expenses and costs, income and profits, financial statements, accounting management, etc. It is combined with cases of listed companies in China's capital market to make it as lively and interesting as possible.

Name: Frontier Issues in Japan's Economy and Society
Introduction:
As China's neighbor, the only Western country in the East, and the world's third largest economy, Japan's development experience has unique and important value to China. Before the mid-1990s, China paid attention to the reasons for Japan's rapid economic growth after World War II and explored experiences worth learning from. After the mid-1990s, China paid attention to the lessons learned from the bursting of Japan's bubble economy, aiming to seek advantages and avoid disadvantages. Entering the 21st century, the world's political and economic order has undergone profound adjustments. Japan's macroeconomic situation, monetary policy, industrial transformation and upgrading, long-term deflation, foreign economic strategy, and participation in regional economic integration have all attracted China's attention. _x000D_
This course is based on the lecturer's observation of the Japanese economy and society and in-depth contact with many policymakers. It reviews the history and policy origins of the current Japanese economic situation, the misunderstanding and misjudgment of Japan by the outside world, the way Japan handles relations with the United States, and an in-depth interpretation of corporate culture. It studies Japanese economic issues from a wide range of perspectives such as interdisciplinary politics, diplomacy, society, regionalization and globalization, and international comparison. It is hoped that this course will broaden and deepen students' knowledge and understanding of the Japanese economy, and it will also expand the research methods of Japanese economics. _x000D_

Name: Population Economics
Prerequisite: Economics, Microeconomics at Middle Level and Macroeconomics at Middle Level
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to discuss the socio-economic causes and consequences of demographic change in the context of China. With regard to the consequences of demographic change, the course will address the growing burden of pensions due to ageing, the role of population growth in economic development, the environmental consequences of population growth, and the economic impact of urbanization and migration. The course will also examine the economic incentives behind fertility, marriage and labour supply. For example, why do the functions of families change with economic development and are they still changing today? Why is the divorce rate rising so fast, fertility rates falling below replacement levels, and many young people delay marriage and even opt out? Is there a unique pattern of marriage and childbearing in China (or East Asia)? To what extent are the significant changes in these family life related to economic development and the changing role of women in the economy? Finally, the course will also address the differences in net benefits for individuals and society with regard to fertility, thus providing a theoretical framework for analysing government interventions on fertility.

Name: Social Practicum
Introduction: Social Practicum

Name: Welfare Economics
Introduction:
Welfare economics is an important branch of modern economics. Broadly and essentially, it is a "social lifestyle choice theory" that attempts to answer a highly imaginative question in a realistic spirit, that is, under given human, material and historical and cultural conditions, in what way should society as a whole organize its social life to maximize the happiness of each member of society. A more rigorous and clear definition is that welfare economics uses economic methods to study how to define social welfare on the basis of individual welfare, and how to rationally arrange social systems and use public policies to enhance social welfare. _x000D_
This course is a compulsory course for undergraduate students in the Department of Finance of the School of Economics. It aims to provide students with a preliminary theoretical basis for thinking about social systems and public policies through the introduction of the basic principles and perspectives of modern welfare economics and the discussion of a series of major issues facing the world today, and to cultivate students' ability to use modern economic methods to observe and theoretically abstract social and economic reality. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Local Public Finance
Introduction: "Local Finance" is one of the main courses in the finance major. Through the study of this course, students are generally required to understand the reasons for the emergence of local governments, master the model for determining the optimal scale of local governments, understand the theory of intergovernmental tax division and intergovernmental transfer payments, and understand the theory and current situation of local fiscal revenue and expenditure. Through the study of "Local Finance", students can master the theory, content, methods and China's current situation of local public expenditure, cultivate students' ability to think theoretically and consider practical issues in the field of finance, and also improve the necessary knowledge and skills for students to engage in finance and taxation work.

Name: Budget Economics
Prerequisite: Economics principles, fiscal science, public choice theory.
Introduction:
The budget is a series of plans and statements that take the annual revenue and expenditure plan as the core and reflect the government's expected future financial operations. It also covers the principles, methods, policies, etc. of budget preparation. It is a guiding document for national operations. Once adopted, all departments must strictly implement it. _x000D_
By nature, a budget is a legally binding document. _x000D_
Formally, the budget is the country's annual fiscal revenue and expenditure plan. _x000D_
From the content point of view, the budget reflects the process of centralized allocation of financial resources by the government. _x000D_
From a functional perspective, the budget is an important means of national macro-control and promotion of social development. _x000D_
From a procedural perspective, the budget is formed through political processes. _x000D_
From the perspective of its relationship with finance, budget is the mechanism for financial operation and its basic institutional framework. _x000D_
A good budget system is a necessary guarantee for the stable and healthy development of a country. It also contains a complete information disclosure mechanism, which allows the people to understand what the government has done and plans to do this year, and enhances their understanding and trust in the government. It also requires a complete budget process and a sound budget management system to supervise and control budget preparation and execution, auditing and evaluation. _x000D_
Budget economics is to look at the budget from the perspective of economics, use economic research methods to solve problems that arise in the process of budget preparation and execution, and use economic thinking to analyze and understand the role of the budget in the operation of the entire national economic system. Fiscal funds, how to bring extra-budgetary funds into unified management, how to ensure the efficient use of funds, how to improve external control, how to clearly divide the financial and administrative powers of the central and local governments, how to reasonably evaluate the implementation of the budget and provide guidance for subsequent work, these are all problems that need to be thought about and solved. Economics provides us with weapons that can be used. We should make full use of the knowledge we have learned to solve problems in the budget system. This is also a process of integrating theory with practice, using the knowledge of macroeconomics and microeconomics learned to solve specific economic problems. _x000D_

Name: Empirical Studies in Public Economics
Introduction: This course mainly teaches empirical methods in financial research. The focus is on how to set research questions in the study of government behavior, business and individual responses to policies, and how to choose appropriate measurement methods in empirical analysis. Especially in the study of fiscal policy, how to get the correct causal relationship. This course will help students master rigorous and standardized research methods through extensive literature reading and explanation, as well as data analysis of large databases, so that they can independently complete empirical research on fiscal policy.

Name: Cost-Benefit Analysis
Introduction:
Cost-benefit analysis is a method of evaluating the value of a project by comparing its full costs and benefits. This method was introduced into the field of government activities in the 1940s. "Cost-Benefit Analysis" has long been introduced into the classrooms of economics schools and business schools in developed countries. In the past, the focus of our country's government work management has been revenue management. With the development of the economy and the increase in government investment projects, people are increasingly paying attention to the economic and social benefits of project expenditures. This course mainly introduces the steps of cost-benefit analysis, the economic basis of cost-benefit analysis, the assessment of costs and benefits in the primary market and secondary market, the value of the social discount rate, the pricing methods of project impact, including the example method, indirect method and contingency pricing method, and will teach several cases of government cost-benefit analysis. By studying this course, students can accurately grasp the methods and theoretical basis of cost-benefit analysis, learn how to measure the costs and benefits of projects, how to determine the social discount rate and conduct cost-benefit analysis of projects. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Distinguished Speaker Lecture Series
Introduction: This course is open to all undergraduate students in the School of Economics (including students from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, international students, and students majoring in economics at Yuanpei College). The college will invite famous experts and scholars from academia, industry, and politics to provide a series of lectures for students and build a high-end platform to improve students' academic research capabilities, broaden their professional knowledge horizons, and enhance their comprehensive literacy.

Name: Financial Economics
Introduction:
This course is an optional course for undergraduate students in the Department of Financial Mathematics. _x000D_
Using a simple static model as the basic framework, we discuss the main conclusions involved in financial economics, including: equilibrium pricing of financial assets, non-arbitrage pricing, etc. Master the basic methods and concepts of analysis, general principles, and ideas for solving problems using relevant principles to lay the foundation for subsequent study of financial mathematics.

Name: Drug Quality and Global Health
Introduction:
The reform of the medical-sanitary system has to address the problems of access to health care, the high cost of medicines and the use of medications. The issue of assured medicines is essentially a matter of drug quality management systems, but it is a worldwide challenge that encompasses a wide range of aspects, including the development, production, registration, supply chain, safe use and regulation of medicines, as well as areas of commonality such as regulatory environments, industrial policies and the global economy. From an academic perspective, this is a typical cross-cutting and systemic science issue in life sciences, medical hygiene, engineering, management, law and economics.

This course, which is the first of its kind at home and abroad, will analyse, from a multidisciplinary perspective and the height of globalization, the history, state and trends of drug quality and global health, relevant national and international standards and implementation, provide students with an integrated and internationally integrated knowledge structure for future research, management, business and law-enforcement work in the field of medical health, and experience in field research.

The main elements of the course include:
1. Content and outreach of pharmaceutical quality (product and system quality, medicines, biological products, and medical devices)
2. Product-based quality of medicines (R & D, production, registration and regulation)
3. Drug quality from a commodity perspective (supply chain, use, alert)
4. Drug quality from a regulatory point of view (laws, regulations, policies)
5. Drug quality and industrialization policies
6. Global competitiveness and global health

Course characteristics:
• Classes (under 20), teaching in Chinese and English, extensive classroom discussions, applied scientific research
• Field research on first-class pharmaceutical enterprises (Kyono, extra-Kyoto), each student will receive an ad hoc scholarship covering part or all of the travel costs
:: Opportunities for learning and communicating with relevant heads of national and international leading enterprises and key government departments

Name: Judo
Introduction: Judo is an official event of the Olympic Games. It is a fighting skill that involves knocking down and subduing the opponent. Not only can you cultivate extraordinary mental and decisiveness in offensive and defensive games, but it can also improve students' physical strength, speed, endurance, flexibility and agility. Judo is a close combat skill that is not only a required skill for police officers, but also a required course for teenagers in developed countries in Asia and even Europe. Learning judo can protect yourself and others. Utilize students' most active brains and most plastic bodies to create a group of judo enthusiasts with quick decision-making and super strength and flexibility.

Name: Artificial Intelligence and Business Innovation
Introduction: With the enhancement of data acquisition capabilities and computing power, artificial intelligence technology has become a mainstream innovative technology. Artificial intelligence technology usually includes search algorithms, machine learning algorithms, natural language processing, image processing, and robotics. This course will first give a brief introduction to mainstream artificial intelligence methods and discuss the advantages and disadvantages of the methods. And focus on corporate innovation in the context of artificial intelligence. Help students understand the practical application of artificial intelligence in business innovation through course teaching and case analysis. In addition, this course will invite AI practitioners as guests to teach about the practical application of artificial intelligence methods in the industry, as well as related opportunities and challenges.

Name: Artificial Intelligence and the Socioeconomy
Introduction: Artificial intelligence is recognized as a technology that will have a profound impact on the future economy and all aspects of human society. This course focuses on exploring how artificial intelligence technology affects the social economy. We will explore the impact of artificial intelligence technology on the macroeconomy, labor market, and education; explore how artificial intelligence technology combined with big data changes business forms and business strategies, including personalized recommendation systems, market mechanism design, data transactions, and other issues. We will also discuss deeper ethical issues such as privacy protection, algorithmic discrimination, fairness and welfare. We finally explore how government policies affect the development of AI technology and social economy as a whole. _x000D_

Name: Econometrics
Introduction: This course mainly studies basic econometric models and estimation methods. We focus primarily on linear regression models, but also perform analyzes on time series, panel data, instrumental variables, and discrete choice models.

Name: Public Finance Theory and Policy
Introduction: This course is mainly for third-year undergraduate students. It mainly discusses the use of economic methods to analyze public finance and government policies. In China, the government plays a very important role in the economy. The main goal of this course is to provide basic economic tools to analyze how government policies affect a country's economy. In terms of content selection, we will cover some theoretical analysis to explain why the government intervenes in the market economy and how government expenditures and tax projects affect the economic behavior and welfare of economic individuals. At the same time, this course will also involve discussions on some real economic policies, such as medical insurance reform, social security reform, tax reform, etc.

Name: Selected English Essays: From the 16th Century to the Romantic Period of the 19th Century
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course guides students to read selected English prose passages from the Romantic period from the 16th century to the 19th century in chronological order, helping students understand the historical tradition of English prose and improve their understanding and appreciation of English prose. The history of English prose is also a brief history of English cultural thought. By reading English prose, browsing the historical and cultural background, and participating in class discussions, students can gain cross-cultural experience across the ages and expand their cultural horizons. _x000D_
The course has multiple assessment methods such as final closed-book written examinations, classroom tests, and writing. It strives to supervise students' learning while also evaluating students' learning results as fairly as possible. _x000D_

Name: Chinese Society (Part 1)
Introduction:
This course is taught entirely in English. It aims to introduce the basic characteristics and changes of Chinese society in terms of population, family, social mobility and wealth distribution since the 18th century (mainly before the reform and opening up) from a comparative perspective between the East and the West. The course content focuses on integrating quantitative historical international comparative research based on large-scale micro-databases of various administrative archives in recent years, focusing on comparing traditional understandings with new empirical findings, and discussing the similarities and differences between Eastern and Western societies, in order to help students understand Chinese society objectively, comprehensively, and systematically, and cultivate critical, analytical, and evidence-based thinking habits. _x000D_
_x000D_
At the same time, this course responds to the school’s teaching innovation concept and adopts the “flipped classroom” teaching model. Students are required to study teaching videos and reading materials before class, prepare weekly oral and written reports in groups, and then make full use of classroom time for teacher-student interactive in-depth discussions and heuristic teaching to cultivate students' soft skills in effective communication, teamwork, oral reports, professional writing, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
The teaching videos related to this course are based on the Coursera MOOC co-taught by the course instructor and Hong Kong University of Science Chair Professor James Lee since 2015. It is well-produced and has received good international response. The specific teaching plan of "Flipped Classroom" was also designed by the course teacher in collaboration with Professor Li Zhongqing. It has been practiced and improved many times as a regular course for the Master of Social Sciences at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, and the teaching evaluation is very positive.

Name: Theory and Policy of Industrial Analysis
Introduction:
This course studies the organization and behavior of firms, the structure and performance of markets, and how firms and markets interact. This course goes beyond the traditional microeconomic theories of perfect competition and monopoly, recognizing that a firm's decisions not only affect itself, but also have an impact on other firms. We will cover four groups of topics:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Monopoly; oligopoly; product differentiation and monopolistic competition. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Price discrimination; non-linear pricing; predatory pricing; vertical integration and restrictions. _x000D_
_x000D_
3. Information asymmetry; disclosure. _x000D_
_x000D_
4. Research and development

Name: Dream of the Red Chamber and Chinese Culture and Art
Prerequisite: None. But students who have studied Chinese ancient history and philosophy will help to understand the content of this course.
Introduction: The Red House Dream is the first of four classics in China, and the Qing generation writer, Cao Xing Seek, has written a long story. It is a literary work of world influence. It is the culmination of a universally recognized Chinese classical novel. It is the encyclopedia of China ' s feudal society and the conglomerate of traditional culture. The course “Red House Dreams” and Chinese Culture Arts, which is funded as a priority project of the Beijing University's Zoe Seren Cultural Development Fund, was initiated by and hosted by Yelang, Senior Professor of Philosophy and Social Sciences at Beijing University. The course was attended by experts from CHO and Red House Dreams, who invited students from the North to study the unique values of CHO and Red House Dreams from a variety of disciplines, including literature, art, history, aesthetics and philosophy. In this way, students are informed about the values and charisma of traditional Chinese culture and are motivated to learn and inherit it.

Name: English Contract Law
Introduction:
British contract law is widely used around the world, especially in the fields of international trade, arbitration, commerce and other fields. It usually exists as a principle rule. On the one hand, China has adopted the United Nations Convention on the Sale of Goods as a template and has accordingly absorbed it into the rules of contract law. On the other hand, extensive contract practice in international trade and other fields also involves the principles and applications of British contract law. At the same time, the contract law applicable in Hong Kong is also an extension of British contract law. Generally speaking, British contract law establishes a set of game rules that are complete, reasonable, logical, practical, practical, certain and predictable. _x000D_
Based on the current teaching configuration and curriculum plan of my country's law schools, this course adopts the cooperation method of Beijing Arbitration Commission/Beijing International Arbitration Center, from an international and practical perspective, combined with international arbitration practice, to provide elective students with schematic and applied knowledge of British contract law, and try to apply it in a Within the course time of the semester, it can quickly and quickly help students establish a preliminary understanding of the core principles and specific applications of British contract law, and help students establish a preliminary knowledge framework in the fields of international trade and arbitration. It can also help students better understand the history of contract development and the positioning and trends of Chinese contract law. _x000D_
This course is taught by two teachers in the same class. The on-campus teaching team is composed of professors Ge Yunsong, Zhang Zhiyong, Peng Bing and Deng Feng. The external experts are led by the famous international arbitration expert Professor Yang Liangyi. British and American contract law experts with both theory and practice are strictly selected to adopt a centralized teaching method. _x000D_
The course uses the works of Professor Yang Liangyi as the teaching books, supplemented by extended reading materials, is taught in Chinese, and is taught in a combination of classroom questions, discussions, after-class readings, homework and other methods. The final assessment is composed of daily attendance and homework, as well as a final paper or case study.

Name: Cross-Border Legal Services and Risk Management: Introduction to Cross-Border Lawyering
Prerequisite: Economic law, corporate law, contract law, etc.
Introduction: This course is a legal practice course jointly offered by Peking University Law School and the Hong Kong Law Society. It aims to systematically teach international lawyer practice and cross-border legal service skills to law school students, integrating theory and practice. The course includes seven lectures, covering cross-border investment, mergers and acquisitions, capital markets, antitrust, international commercial dispute resolution, legal risk management, trust and other fields. Lawyers will combine specific cases to improve students' legal analysis level and practical skills from multiple perspectives.

Name: Topics in Civil Procedure Law
Prerequisite:
Law of Civil Procedure
General provisions of civil law
Property law
Credit law
Introduction:
Civil Procedure Law is an advanced elective course for law school undergraduates. It mainly introduces how parties and courts use litigation, the most formal dispute resolution method, to apply the law to resolve civil disputes. Through the study of this course, students will think about legal and philosophical issues in civil litigation from a professional perspective and prepare for their future legal career. _x000D_
_x000D_
The structure of civil litigation determines the resolution of substantive issues. In terms of theory, this course will guide students to explore the relationship between some basic theoretical categories in law from the perspective of civil procedure law, such as entities and procedures, courts and parties, public rights and private rights, etc. At the same time, students will also be introduced to the basic theories of civil litigation, such as right of action, subject matter of litigation, res judicata, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
In terms of practice, the course will provide students with the key points of various systems of civil litigation in my country, such as jurisdiction system, evidence system, preservation system, etc. At the same time, the contents of various litigation procedures and non-litigation procedures will also be explained so that students can use these procedures to resolve civil disputes. In short, it helps students learn various operations of civil litigation and lays the foundation for future legal practice. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Informatization of Enterprises and Government
Introduction:
Informatization is one of the important means for enterprises to improve their competitiveness and for governments to improve management and service levels. It can not only improve resource allocation capabilities, but also greatly improve work efficiency. Therefore, the importance of informatization construction for enterprises and governments has gained widespread consensus. In practice, people gradually realize that the widespread application of information technology has triggered profound changes in strategic planning, operating models, organizational structures, and environments of enterprises and governments. Therefore, informatization is not only a technical issue, but also involves management, organization, culture, etc., but is a complex systematic project. _x000D_
