      This course systematically introduces the basic ideas and methods of enterprise and government informatization, and provides students with an information management roadmap through relevant case analysis, so that students can view problems in a new way, whether in traditional fields or emerging fields, and have the ability to explore and solve problems, so that they can calmly cope with the challenges of the knowledge economy in the information age and have a sustainable competitive advantage. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Public Cultural Services
Introduction:
As an introductory course in the study of public cultural services, the main elements of the basic concepts and theories relating to public cultural services are: the basic content of public cultural services; the subject of public cultural services (entity and responsibility); the equalization of public cultural services; the institutional guarantee of public cultural services; the provision of public cultural services (government supply and socialization); the evaluation of public cultural services; the international development of public cultural services and the system of public cultural services in the country; and the informationalization of public cultural services.

Through this course, students learn about the basic features of the theory of public cultural services, the main research content of the subject, the current state of practice and the problems that exist, develop awareness that the enjoyment of public culture is the basic cultural interest of the population, direct students to major social issues of public cultural services, build professional convictions and develop professional interests.

Name: Library Reference Services
Prerequisite:
Information resources development
Information resource retrieval and utilization
Introduction: Reference services play an important role in various library services. The library reference department is also an important department of the library. Studying the content and rules of reference services and new methods and new directions of reference services in the digital environment are important issues in the current field of library science research.

Name: Introduction to Health Informatics
Introduction:
Health informatics is an emerging multidisciplinary interdisciplinary field that focuses on the application of information technology in the medical and health field, thereby improving the level of services, education and scientific research related to public health care. Information science, medical informatics, health informatics, library and information majors in some European and American universities generally offer this course as an elective course for students. _x000D_
_x000D_
Health informatics can be defined as the evolving discipline of the collection, storage, retrieval, communication and optimal use of health-related data, information and knowledge. This course mainly introduces the basic concepts of health informatics, the main fields involved, the main research objects, research methods derived from computer technology and information technology, research methods derived from behavioral and social sciences, electronic health record systems, terminology and international standards, etc. Pay attention to the impact of the development of health informatics on the actual work of medical and health services in the digital environment, explore the health information needs of users, especially vulnerable groups, explore behaviors and countermeasures, and explore how to build health information resources that suit user needs. This enables students to have a clear understanding of the main concepts of health informatics, research methods, and information system knowledge, and to increase practical experience by completing projects and writing reports.

Name: Knowledge Taboos and the Development of Civilization
Introduction: The knowledge taboos taught in this course focus on the world's banned book phenomenon and banned book culture. The banned book phenomenon is a common accompanying culture in the development of human civilization. Through the investigation of the banned book culture in different regions of the world from ancient times to the present, the appearance and characteristics of knowledge represented by books in different eras are presented, and the intrinsic relationship between book order and social structure is understood. By explaining the phenomenon and culture of banned books in the world, the role of the right to intellectual freedom in the development of civilization is explained. The course content is conducted in the form of special topics, among which banned books in Christian culture, social culture and moral banned books, and ancient Chinese banned book culture are the focus of teaching.

Name: Fundamentals of Operations Research
Introduction:
Operations research studies the basic rules of human resource utilization and planning, so as to maximize the benefits of limited resources and achieve the goal of optimization. As a subject of optimization and decision-making, operations research can play a huge role in economics, science and technology, industry, management, military and other aspects. Therefore, it has received great attention from higher education institutions and personnel at home and abroad. This course teaches the basic knowledge of operations research through linear programming, transportation problems, integer programming, graph and network analysis, dynamic programming, decision analysis, game theory, prediction, optimization methods, etc., and cultivates students' interest in in-depth study and research in the field of operations research in the future. _x000D_
      This course introduces the basic ideas and methods of operations research. It is expected to enable students to use operations research thinking and methods to solve problems. When faced with widely varying actual situations, they can calmly determine goals, formulate plans, build models, and obtain answers, so as to remain invincible in the incentive competition in the information age. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to China's Frontier Issues
Prerequisite: Basic history and geography courses in humanities are sufficient.
Introduction: As an ancient Eastern Power, China has developed a unique concept of the State and borders in the course of its 5,000-year history, and its map and borders have changed many times. In recent times, China has suffered from a myriad of conflicts, and most of the aggression by Western colonizers against our country has begun on its borders. Since the establishment of the new China, the Chinese Government has developed a strategy of good-neighbourly diplomacy for peaceful coexistence. It has resolved most border issues with neighbouring countries and has created a favourable international environment for the modernization of the country. Through the introduction of the curriculum, it is hoped that students will have a general and thematic perspective on the evolution of the Chinese nation, the emergence of border issues, the New and Old China ' s border strategy, and the main border issues, and that independent thinking will be developed on the relevant issues. At the same time, by introducing the New China ' s border strategy, we will summarize China ' s achievements and problems in preserving sovereignty and unity.

Name: History of Anthropology
Introduction: This course is mainly offered to undergraduate students majoring in Anthropology in the Department of Sociology. It aims to give a basic and comprehensive introduction to the history of the development of Western anthropology. The content includes the prehistory of Western anthropology, the emergence and establishment of anthropology as a professional discipline in the United Kingdom, France, Germany and the United States in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, as well as the different anthropological traditions and changes that have been formed since then.

Name: Cultivating and Experimenting with the Entrepreneurial Spirit
Introduction: This course is guided by the national innovation and entrepreneurship development strategy and policy goals, based on the rich achievements of innovation and entrepreneurship teaching for more than six years and an excellent teaching team. It integrates the national "mass entrepreneurship and innovation" concept and policy into classroom teaching, focusing on cultivating and improving the analysis and practical ability of young students to carry out innovation and entrepreneurship activities. It is hoped that through course learning, students can enhance their understanding and recognition of the future development direction of social economy and help students find methodologies to combine their ideals with reality.

Name: Introduction to Government under the Rule of Law
Prerequisite: Constitutional and administrative law, which is a mandatory core course for teachers in the College, is fundamental to the study of the subject.
Introduction:
In the context of the era when governing the country according to law has become the basic way for the party to lead the people to govern the country, students in the School of Government, as the "reserve army" of leaders in the practice and theory of public administration, must be familiar with and master the subject knowledge related to law, so that they can deeply understand the essence of governing the country according to the law. However, it should also be noted that the School of Government focuses more on teaching the subject of public administration and cultivating students’ cognition and skills related to public management. If traditional law courses are taught in law schools, it will be divorced from the subject characteristics and teaching objectives of the School of Government. Therefore, the course "Introduction to Legal Government" will be based on the characteristics and purposes of this discipline, follow the teaching rules of this discipline, and achieve the integration of public administration and law. Specifically, this course has the following characteristics:_x000D_
(1) Rich and diverse teaching methods_x000D_
This is a course that not only emphasizes the study of academic theory, but also focuses on practical application and in-depth analysis and discussion of hot cases, forming a rich and diverse teaching method. Specifically, it mainly includes that in addition to teachers teaching basic theories and basic issues, teachers arrange or students collect materials, documents and data on various hot topics to form a "hot issue focused" teaching that summarizes relevant materials; students speak in class, and teachers make comments midway to introduce teaching content. _x000D_
(2) Pay attention to combining social hot spots and conduct case analysis_x000D_
The law itself often gives people a boring impression, and blindly combining legal principles and legal provisions often has a mediocre teaching effect. By appropriately selecting some hot cases and teaching them in conjunction with the course content, this course effectively increases the interest and timeliness of classroom knowledge. It also promotes students to have more in-depth thinking and debate on specific rule of law issues, guides students to pay attention to the government and rule of law phenomena happening around them, and provides knowledge foundation, thinking methods and logical training for future academic and professional careers. _x000D_
(3) Pay attention to the realization of mutual learning in teaching and respect the opinions of students_x000D_
To teach an undergraduate course well, the most important thing is to constantly listen to students’ opinions and suggestions, accept suggestions from classmates, improve teaching methods and adjust teaching content. This course attaches great importance to the collection and feedback of teaching opinions. It actively collects students’ opinions and suggestions on the teaching of this course through various methods such as individual student conversations, on-site collection in class, and after-class WeChat contacts, and makes timely adjustments and improvements during the teaching process of the course, so that the course can ultimately achieve the teaching purpose. _x000D_
(4) Organize practical exchange activities to achieve practical education_x000D_
This course is closely integrated with government management practice and law enforcement practice. Appropriate arrangements for practical exchanges and visits can enable students to have a more intuitive feeling and in-depth understanding of the law enforcement process and the relationship between government and the rule of law. This course integrates the opinions and needs of students, combines the key knowledge points taught in the course, and leads students out of the classroom through activities such as court hearing observations and exchanges with government officials, combining practical education with classroom education, and combining lecture teaching with on-site teaching to achieve better teaching results. _x000D_
(5) Pay attention to the construction of course websites and strengthen exchanges and discussions_x000D_
This course combines students' needs and suggestions to establish a course website to facilitate students' learning. It mainly includes multiple sections such as course introduction, student style, student forum, etc. The internal forum will also be regularly updated and uploaded with rich learning resources such as teaching courseware, recommended books, reading materials, current political hot topics, and related literature. Students can use the course website to post questions, organize discussions, share materials, communicate with teachers, etc. The independent and specialized course website provides more convenience for course teaching, notice release, exchange and discussion, etc., allowing students to download and share course resources at any time, increasing students' initiative to collect course-related resources, and guiding students to actively ask questions, answer each other, share experiences, and help peers. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Supervision and Oversight
Prerequisite: Political science, history of China's political system, Western political system, administrative science
Introduction: The teaching purpose of this course is to explore how to conduct effective supervision and inspection of public power to prevent abuse of power and rampant corruption. Abuse of power and rampant corruption can violate citizens' rights, undermine political legitimacy, and jeopardize the achievement of national goals. In China, supervision and clean government construction belong to a specialized research field. The basic content of this course includes: the concept of corruption; the types, characteristics and forms of corruption; the diffusion and spread of corruption; the measurement, diagnosis and early warning of corruption; the impact of corruption; the causes of corruption; anti-corruption target strategies and tactics; systematic anti-corruption; punishment of corruption; prevention of corruption; power supervision; administrative supervision; international anti-corruption cooperation and global governance; successful cases of national and regional anti-corruption, etc. While teaching in class, this course encourages students to participate in class discussions, pay attention to case analysis, and strive to cultivate students' problem awareness and research interests.

Name: Introduction to Comparative Politics
Introduction: Comparative politics is one of the most important components of political science. This course is an introductory course to guide students (undergraduate) into the field of comparative politics. Through the study of this course, students should be able to understand the overview of the field of comparative politics, including the conceptual system, research directions, main theories and methods, etc., and at the same time, to a certain extent, be exposed to the representative works of major scholars in this field.

Name: Scientific Literacy
Introduction:
The basic goal of this course is to improve students' scientific literacy. It is hoped that through the study of this course, students can acquire basic scientific literacy. Through the acceptance of major historical events in science and things related to science in daily life, students can understand the basic laws of scientific development, be able to know what is a statement of fact and what is a statement of opinion, be able to make clear judgments about science and pseudoscience, and know what errors in science are and the essential difference between them and pseudoscience. _x000D_
_x000D_
While teaching in the classroom, students are also encouraged to participate in interactions. At the same time, scholars inside and outside the school will also be invited to enter the classroom on specific topics to introduce students to the development and existing problems in various fields. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course does not require any prerequisite courses and the final grade is based on the report submitted by the student.

Name: Quantitative Historical Research
Introduction:
Chinese introduction: _x000D_
Most existing historical research is too qualitative and stays at the level of historical data collection and description. Even when drawing conclusions about the causal relationship behind historical facts, it is only speculative. It rarely conducts rigorous logical inferences in a statistical sense and makes exclusive empirical demonstrations. The shortcomings of this research method are obvious. In historical research, the compilation and descriptive work of primary historical materials is extremely important, but that is the first step in the entire research process, not the entire process. The ultimate goal of the research is to understand and learn general principles from historical experience, and to learn regular knowledge that is valuable to current and future human society. This course is based on using social science methods to analyze historical changes, thereby exploring the origin and context of the long-term development of human society, explaining the laws of historical evolution, and providing some reference for today's economy, social development and economic policies. _x000D_

Name: Political Institutions of Contemporary Western Countries
Introduction:
This course is a basic course for majors in political science and administrative management, especially the research direction of comparative politics. Students from other majors who are interested in this topic are also welcome to take it as an elective. _x000D_
This course will comprehensively and systematically introduce the contemporary (since World War II) political systems and their influence in major Western developed countries (the United States, Britain, France, Germany, Japan, Italy, etc.), including topics such as the constitution, national structure, legislation, administration, justice, political parties and interest groups, and electoral systems. It also includes the impact of these systems on the construction of political systems in major transition countries and regions (Russia, South Korea, Taiwan, etc.). This course will not be limited to a static description of relevant systems from a legal perspective, but will focus on exploring the causes, theoretical basis, operating characteristics, pros and cons of related reforms, and other issues behind each system. In order to adapt to the characteristics of the era of information explosion and network convenience, this course will focus on cultivating students' interest in learning and training independent research abilities. It will provide and guide students to read classic literature in various ways, adopt a combination of classroom lectures and discussions to strengthen teacher-student interaction, and strive to achieve the organic unity of theory and practice, static and dynamic teaching. I believe that this course will help deepen students' rational understanding of the models, characteristics and essence of political democratic systems in Western countries, and stimulate students' research interest in comparative political systems. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Chinese Society (Political Science)
Introduction: This course is a pilot general course of Yuanpei College, and priority is given to Yuanpei students. Through the study of this course, students will initially understand and master (1) the basic concepts and important research methods of political science; (2) the basic impression of Chinese politics and society from the perspective of political science research, including historical traditions and contemporary reality; (3) the ability to use political science methods to analyze some empirical phenomena of Chinese politics and society. This course is conducted in the form of large class lectures + small class discussions. In addition to attending lectures, students are required to read bibliographies, participate in discussions in each small class, and complete 5 course assignments and a final open-book exam. Course grades are awarded based on small class discussions and research reports (40%), assignments (20%), and final exams (40%). _x000D_

Name: Politics of Development
Introduction:
Development Political Science
As an emerging discipline in contemporary political science, political development (especially in less developed countries) has produced a wealth of research through academic discussions on the core issues of how developing countries can achieve democratic transformation, achieve social stability, overcome political corruption, resolve political crises and complete political and cultural transformation. These findings are collectively referred to as “political development theories”.

The Political Science of Development, based on the general logic of research themes and theoretical thinking, systematically synthesizes the important theories and perspectives developed by the Institute for Political Development, summarizing the theoretical results of development politics from both a macro and a micro perspective: At the macro level, the understanding and definition of the concept of political development by development political scientists is described. It provides an overview of the context, theoretical ideas and academic criticism of the two main theoretical factions of modernism, dependence, and, at the micro level, participation in political development, crisis theory, corruption theory, stabilization theory, cultural construction theory, institutionalization theory and democratization theory, respectively.

Name: Political Science
Prerequisite: Political science doctrine, sociological concepts, generalization of law
Introduction:
_x000D_
This course will sort out and teach the basic principles, academic sources and disciplinary progress of political science through an introduction to the basic knowledge, sub-disciplines and academic frontiers of political science. The main contents include the foundation of political science, history of political science disciplines, political philosophy, political culture, political ethics, political psychology, political anthropology, political sociology, comparative politics, international politics, geopolitics, political communication, political economy, political sociology, ecological politics and computational politics.

Name: Social Problems and Social Policy
Introduction:
This course uses domestic and foreign social policies as empirical materials to guide students to understand the theories and methods of social policy analysis. By studying this course, students can master the following knowledge and abilities:_x000D_
1. Clearly express the basic theories and concepts of social policy analysis_x000D_
2. Ability to conceptualize policy issues and propose policy solutions_x000D_
3. Understand the impact of policy analysis in public policy _x000D_
4. Understand the role of the policy analyst_x000D_
5. Understand my country’s current social policies to solve social problems_x000D_

Name: Topics in Russia's Political Transition
Introduction:
After the reform and opening up, political science researchers in our country gradually began to realize that there is no ready-made theory that can be copied, and they must explore their own development path and establish a political science theory suitable for China's national conditions. After the disintegration of the Soviet Union, the bipolar pattern was broken, and the binary opposition and debate in political theory about the European and American model and the Soviet model naturally disappeared. For Chinese political science researchers who once "took Russia as their teacher" and "took the Soviet Union as their teacher", they must make fundamental adjustments in terms of values, concepts, and even mentality. On the one hand, the disintegration of the Soviet Union means all-round changes in Russian politics, so it is necessary to comprehensively re-examine the Russian people's understanding, expectations and goals of their country, government, party, regime, constitution and other issues; on the other hand, the disintegration of the Soviet Union has proved that the Soviet experience has flaws, so a series of theoretical presuppositions about politics in Soviet academic circles must also be re-examined to eliminate potential problems in the process of our country's political development. In fact, Russia's current political situation and political development experience are becoming the two main issues that Chinese scholars pay attention to when conducting research on Russian politics. _x000D_
Therefore, this course attempts to teach Russian political transformation as a whole, providing students with a new perspective and way of thinking, guiding students to break away from the inherent logic of Western development politics, and use Russia's own historical background as the starting point to think about the basic characteristics, basic stages, and basic logic of the political system in the process of transformation. This course has a total of 48 class hours, taught in 16 weeks, with 3 class hours per week. The course is divided into two perspectives: static political system and dynamic structure, and political development and process. It is taught at three levels: political system, political interaction, and political elite. It is divided into 15 sections: general introduction, disintegration of the Soviet Union, constitution and law, president and prime minister, Duma and legislative body, political elite, political parties and multi-party system, civil society, interest groups, foreign policy, federal system, grassroots governance, political thought and culture, democratic transformation, and conclusion. _x000D_

Name: Commercial Film Narrative
Introduction: Commercial film narrative is the core of the current mainstream film creative mechanism, and has long been one of the basic courses for film majors in universities around the world. This course will start with "Character Creation" and gradually analyze basic film creation theories such as "Theme Statement Template", "Action Design", "Plot Clues Arrangement" and "Film Structure Planning", and introduce many professional training methods.

Name: Ancient Egyptian Art and Architecture
Introduction: This course is a required course for majors in ancient world history. It guides students to systematically understand the main content, historical evolution, symbolic significance and impact on later civilizations of ancient Egyptian art and architecture. It takes religious buildings such as pyramids and temples as well as tomb reliefs, murals and various worship statues as the main clues. Combining the basic knowledge of documentary materials and archaeological background, the religious connotation of ancient Egyptian art and architecture is analyzed and interpreted using the methods of history and iconography, so as to cultivate students' ability to comprehensively master and apply various types of historical materials, discover and solve problems.

Name: Modern Greek History
Introduction:
The world economic crisis of recent years and the further development and expansion of the European Union had again made Greece the focus of news. Domestic research into the ancient Greek and Byzantine era failed to address the political, social and institutional development of near-modern Greece, which is the key to understanding contemporary Greek economic and social problems. Therefore, the course seeks to provide students with an understanding of the historical context of the modern Greek economic crisis and the decisive impact of their social and institutional development on their political status by teaching the history of political, economic, social and institutional development in near-modern Greece.
The course will be divided into three main sections: one, the establishment of a modern State and the nineteenth-century Greek society; two, Greece and two world wars; and three, post-war Greece: democracy and the welfare system. The focus of the course is on the social and economic situation of Greece in the context of political conflict, while attention will be paid to modern Greece ' s efforts to achieve a balance between modernization and the preservation of cultural traditions.

Name: Religious Belief and Mysticism
Introduction: This course attempts to start from the mystical characteristics and ideas of different religions, understand the mystical beliefs and practices of different religious traditions around the world, and conduct comparative and integrated research among them. Understand the cultural value and universality of mysticism as an expression of faith during the teaching process. An introductory course to understand the connections and tensions between the mystical and communal aspects of religion.

Name: Postmodernist Philosophy

Reconciling the formation, development, fundamental features and philosophical underpinnings of post-modernism theory and exploring post-modernism

The response of Chinese academic thinkers to post-modernism is the course ' s path of academic care and thought throughout the course.

Name: Introduction to Musical Theater and Practice
Introduction: Musical, known as the 20th century cultural miracle, is good at using and integrating all artistic resources and is a highly integrated stage art. In the context of the various stages of the development of musical theatres, the course " General and Practical Musical Theatres " , through the study, analysis and rehearsing of selected works of Western musicals and Chinese musical plays, presents the European and American musical performances and their ecological environment, and, in accordance with their respective styles, introduces into the country an in-depth analysis of the country ' s more important original musical works for more than 30 years. To equip students with the relevant skills for the performance of the musical stage, to understand the patterns of the creation of the image of the dramatic person, to learn the analytical role, image design and methods and skills to represent it. This course will contribute to the development of an intuitive artistic instinct and a deep sense of reason, master the basic concepts of musical performances, raise awareness of musical performances, understand the history and realities of their development, and make more in-depth professional thinking and criticism of musical works. In practical rehearsals, the performance of students, hands-on skills, creative abilities, a sense of cooperation, and aesthetics in musical performances.

Name: Film and Television Technology (Non-Linear Editing)
Introduction:
Master general technical operations, such as cameras and computer non-linear editing, and be familiar with the basic technical points of each link in the film and television production process. _x000D_
Content summary:_x000D_
1. Optical and electrical principles_x000D_
2. Lens principle _x000D_
3. Film and film editing principles_x000D_
4. Principles of video technology and video editing technology_x000D_
5. Principles of audio and audio editing technology_x000D_
Teaching methods: classroom lectures and group or computer exercises _x000D_

Name: Historical and Cultural Analysis of American Political Speeches
Prerequisite: English courses at the university, passing the 6th grade English examination. British history.
Introduction:
In view of the fact that 40 years after the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and the United States, Sino-US relations have experienced a major setback, with the emergence of large-scale shutdowns other than "decoupling" and even the trend of all-out confrontation. It is necessary to reopen this political history and culture course about the United States. Under the teaching and guidance of teachers, students can have a preliminary and comprehensive understanding of the major events and ideological imagination of American political history, and then stand in the new era of reform and opening up. From the standpoint of China's path and cultural confidence in the new era of reform and opening up, we can improve political awareness, hone independent thinking ability, and improve ideological analysis capabilities. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is taught in English (supplemented by Chinese) about the historical and cultural ideas in important political speeches in American history, through the important political speeches in the United States_x000D_
The reading, understanding, analysis and evaluation of vocabulary can greatly improve students' English proficiency, cultivate the knowledge and skills of English speech, and accumulate knowledge of American social history and culture. This is a learning activity that improves cultural literacy, ideological discernment and political criticism abilities through the study of political English texts. It is a learning activity for some of our school's relatively high English proficiency_x000D_
High ideological preparation and English proficiency are very necessary, especially for undergraduates who are interested in studying in the United States. The purpose of this course is threefold: 1) To enable students to understand the language of English political speeches_x000D_
Have a basic understanding and experience of the characteristics of language and style; 2) Cultivate students' ability to effectively express their thoughts in public; 3) Have a basic understanding of the United States_x000D_
Have a general understanding of some major historical events and influential ideas in social history and culture and maintain the ability to think critically. Course content mainly includes: American Colonies, Constitution_x000D_
Political independence, territorial expansion and free economy, southern slavery and northern industrialization, Civil War and postwar reconstruction, industrialization and economic depression, World War I and World War II_x000D_
Reading and reading of the original English texts of important speeches in American political life in various historical development periods such as the war, the Cold War and the development of contemporary capitalism._x000D_
Commentary and analysis, understanding of the basic conditions of political economy and culture in various historical periods. The focus is on the understanding, stylistic analysis and criticism of the original text. _x000D_
Course teaching format: mainly lectures, supplemented by an appropriate proportion of classroom discussions and reading exercises. _x000D_
Requirements for students who choose the course: 1) Have great interest in American society, history and culture; 2) Excellent college English scores (Beijing University CET-4 or National CET-4_x000D_
80 points or above; 3) Strong English listening and speaking skills. _x000D_
