Name: Advanced Film Color Grading
Prerequisite: Prerequisite courses: 04331791 Audiovisual Language (Film Language), 04330088 Film Editing. Since film color correction requires certain basic knowledge of picture composition, light and shadow, and color matching, as well as proficiency in basic film editing techniques, only relevant operations and training can be completed.
Introduction:
Film school colours are the most technical work in the film and video production process, and there are few cinematographers at the hospital level, because of the need for higher colour talent, rigorous training and case studies, and the fact that no specialized courses are currently available in the global film education system, largely through the mouth and mouth of the teacher.
The course will begin with the basis of colour, the colour principle, the training of students in colour sensitivity, colour decomposition, colour matching skills, and the application of skills in school colour systems such as Da Vinci, Kwanta and Basselight.
The course will use raw materials from the institutional film industry to guide students in industry training in the production process of digital intermediate films in accordance with the industry standards.

Name: Information Economics
Introduction: Information economics uses game theory as a research tool to study the equilibrium and behavior of various game participants under information asymmetry. The main content of this course consists of two major parts. The first part is the content of game theory, including static and dynamic games as well as games of complete information and incomplete information. The second part is information economics, including the classic adverse selection model, signaling theory and mechanism design theory.

Name: Theory of Industrial Organization
Introduction: Industrial organization theory takes "industry" as the research object and mainly studies the organizational structure within the industry and between enterprises, as well as the business strategies, output decisions, pricing behaviors, non-price strategic behaviors of enterprises under certain organizational structure conditions, as well as the market performance brought about by their behaviors.

Name: International Development Policy
Introduction: Over the past few decades, China had not only made rapid economic progress but had also invested in infrastructure in developing countries, bringing new impetus and ideas to international development. These changes have led us to reflect on the question of how to rethink “development”. The course explored international development policy and the historical, political, economic and institutional factors behind it. Through learning, students will learn about discussions and debates around current international development issues and will have a theoretical framework for analysing such policy issues. In addition, the course will explore the role of emerging China in international development and its implications for regional and international relations. The subjects covered included the history of development, industrialization, poverty eradication, aid and development finance, energy and environment, international development mechanisms, South-South cooperation, China and the global development order.

Name: Fieldwork Practicum
Prerequisite: The first requirements of this course are " General Social Studies " , " Social Research and Research Methods " , both of which are specialized courses of the Department of Sociology.
Introduction:
In the training of research methods in the social sciences, research craftsmanship is closest to the researcher's awareness of materials and problems. This course will start from the research process and explore how to achieve the transformation from research interests to research questions in undergraduate training programs in sociology, how to put research questions into research practice and write research reports. This course is divided into two parts. In the first six courses, teachers will lead students to read and discuss, providing concentrated theoretical training on several core aspects of social science research techniques, and focusing on the study of some classic research examples of fieldwork. The second part is divided into unit exercises. Students will complete the training and writing of each unit one by one based on the issues they are interested in. In each training session, students will speak and comment on each other's results in this stage, and the teacher will comment on each research topic. The goal of this course is that students who choose this course can feel what the basic research qualities of social sciences are, especially the ability to cultivate their own hands-on search for materials, make full use of the library's literature resources, and develop their interests into research questions that can be explored. All writing training will also reflect students' thinking back and forth between reading and going to the field. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is a small class course. Two teachers are jointly responsible for the discussion, fieldwork and writing training of a class. Each class is limited to 8 students.

Name: General Georgian (I)
Introduction: This course is a series of Georgian language courses along the Belt and Road offered to students with zero basic knowledge. Based on the initial mastery of main grammar and basic vocabulary, students can further improve their comprehensive abilities in reading, comprehension and conversation through learning.

Name: Legal Practice
Introduction: The course is presented mainly by the partners of the large integrated law firm Zonta in Beijing, in accordance with their respective areas of specialization, to students in the form of thought training, statutory analysis, case presentation and market dynamics, with a view to enriching the students ' horizons, giving them a better sense of the theoretical knowledge they have learned and an initial understanding of the practice of lawyers and preparing them for future entry into the legal profession.

Name: The Society for Research in Chinese Architecture and Chinese Architecture
Introduction:
Focusing on the discovery and research of ancient Chinese architecture by the China Architecture Society, read all seven volumes of the "Transactions of the China Architecture Society". _x000D_
Mr. Zhu Qiqian founded the China Architecture Society in 1930 and initiated the study of Chinese architecture. There are two formal and document groups within the academy, chaired by Liang Sicheng and Liu Dunzhen respectively. They study the forms and historical materials of ancient buildings, and carry out large-scale field surveys of ancient Chinese buildings. _x000D_
In the short five years between 1932 and the outbreak of the Anti-Japanese War in 1937, members of the society conducted a large number of explorations and surveys on ancient buildings in China at that time with a scientific and rigorous attitude towards modern architecture, and collected a large amount of precious data, much of which still has extremely high academic value today. _x000D_
The research of the China Institute of Architecture is groundbreaking and has established a framework for the study of Chinese architectural history. The members of the society started with the ancient architecture of the Ming and Qing Dynasties, interpreted construction documents, and gradually went deeper, and then discovered and investigated the architecture of the Tang and Song Dynasties. The Architecture Society has continuously excavated historical materials and carried out field investigations in a sustained and planned manner. The understanding has become increasingly in-depth, and the framework of the history of Chinese architecture has been gradually built and the study of Chinese architecture has begun. _x000D_
"Transactions of the Architecture Society" reflects the academic progress of the society's members. By reading, beginners can follow the pace of the Architecture Society and gradually enter the research field of Chinese architecture. As a new discipline established in the early days of modern China, the study of Chinese architecture is also suitable to be connected with modern history and intellectual history, and becomes an integral part of core reading courses. _x000D_
Another feature of this course is that it guides students into the field by interpreting the research methods and sentiments of the institute, and focuses on the research orientation of combining literature and physical materials. _x000D_
"Transactions of the Construction Society" totals 7 volumes, 23 issues, and 22 volumes, with about 5,600 pages, including about 1,600 pages of illustrations. _x000D_

Name: Marxism and Literary Criticism
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will cover classic and contemporary Marxist literary and art criticism theories, as well as Marxist cultural and social theories. Topics that may be covered in this semester include: literature and art, history and cultural theory (base and superstructure analysis, reflection and mediation, typification and isomorphism, literature and ideological criticism, cultural sociology); the form and content of literature and art (Marx’s dialectics of form and content, Marxism and formalism, Lukács and literary form, Frederick Jameson’s Poetics of social forms); literature and art as production; aesthetics and politics (aesthetics and historical perspectives in literary criticism, writers and tendencies, the politics of literature and political literature); Marxism and Chinese literature and art (the debate on human nature and class issues in literature and art, the politicization, depoliticization and repoliticization of modern and contemporary Chinese literature, the Chinese form of Marxist literary criticism), etc. The purpose of this course is to expect students to have a clearer understanding of the theoretical characteristics, key propositions, development and critical methods of Marxist literary criticism based on careful reading and understanding of relevant classic texts. Teachers give lectures, students make a presentation on an issue of interest, and submit a paper at the end of the semester.

Name: Policy Analysis and Causal Inference
Prerequisite:
This course is intended for the graduate students (at Master or Doctoral level) or senior-level undergraduate students in Economics, Finance, and Management.

Prior training in elementary Econometrics or Statistics is required.
Introduction: This course provides an introduction to research design and econometrics, focusing on the study of public policy issues through the use of data analysis methods. This course will mainly cover three major topics: 1. Causality; 2. Main obstacles to determining causality, such as omitted variables, selection bias, economic selection (endogeneity problems and self-selection); 3. Statistical and economic tools to solve the above obstacles, including regression, randomization, instrumental variables, differences, regression discontinuity, etc.

Name: The Great Migration of Plants
Introduction:
Our food, clothing, housing and transportation are all inseparable from plants, but did you know that plants also migrate across the ocean to reach all parts of the world? Why did French economist Fabre say that "all the king's illegitimate children can leave their names in history, but no one knows the origin of wheat"? Do you know that along with the "migration" of plants, human economic and social activities have undergone tremendous changes? Conversely, what impact will human economic development have on plant growth and migration? For thousands of years, the roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds of plants have provided all seven nutrients needed by humans: water, protein, oil, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. But do you know what they actually look like? Do rice-eating southerners have different personalities from noodle-eating northerners? _x000D_
This course starts from the perspective of introducing the domestication and "migration" of plants. It not only allows students to understand the physiology and development of plants and pay attention to the hidden molecular regulatory mechanisms, but also combines the basic knowledge of agricultural economics to help people understand the interactive relationship between plant "migration" and human economic and social development. If you go back to the roots and love the collision between plants and agricultural economy, you are welcome to take "The Great Migration of Plants" as an elective! _x000D_

Name: Fiscal and Tax Law
Introduction: This course is guided by the Party's basic line, aims to establish the legal framework of the socialist market economic system, is based on China's current laws and regulations, is closely connected with the actual reform of the fiscal and taxation system, and systematically discusses important legal systems in the field of fiscal and taxation. The teaching content mainly includes: the concept, characteristics and fiscal system of fiscal law; budget law; tax law; national debt law and transfer payment system and other legal provisions.

Name: The Historical Development of Islamic Civilization
Introduction:
1. Help students understand the historical process and characteristics of Islamic civilization;_x000D_
2. Encourage students to learn history by reading relevant basic documents, especially original materials, establish an understanding of the basic methods of history, and form an interest and belief in history; _x000D_
3. Before each class, students are required to read the literature assigned by the teacher, and be able to answer questions related to the reading literature and participate in discussions in class; _x000D_
4. In the process of reading literature, students can further ask valuable questions based on the teacher's narration, thereby determining the theme of this course assignment; _x000D_
5. Understand the reality of Islamic civilization through course practice and observation. _x000D_

Name: Politics of Medieval Western Europe
Introduction: This course is one of the introductory courses in the study of medieval history. By introducing a large number of physical objects (especially various buildings) and documents that remain from the medieval period, students will be guided to have a preliminary perceptual understanding of medieval politics and culture, and will be able to gain a more systematic understanding of the basic historical facts, evolutionary context, and characteristics of medieval European political history.

Name: Modern Western Politics
Introduction: This course briefly but systematically outlines the development history of Western social and political thought in modern times, analyzes the origin and evolution of major Western social and political theories in modern times, and introduces the works and theories of thinkers who have had a significant influence on the development of modern Western history. Students taking this course should have some theoretical knowledge of Western history and social sciences.

Name: Basic Latin (1)
Introduction: This course is aimed at students who are interested in learning classical Latin. It systematically teaches classical Latin grammar, vocabulary and Roman cultural knowledge through grammar explanations, classroom exercises, written assignments, class tests, mid-term and final tests, etc., so that students can fully master the basic grammar and vocabulary of classical Latin within one year, and have the ability to read selected excerpts from the original Latin text. This course is a compulsory course for the Western Studies Group of the "Classical Philology" project.

Name: Introduction to Classical Studies
Introduction: This course is intended to provide a practical introduction to classical studies. The focus of the course is to understand and learn the basic methods and issues that classical scholars will face when conducting research. We will discuss how to use and examine various historical materials in different genres (such as epic poems, historical works, speeches) and different media (such as inscriptions, papyri, and coins) to help everyone master the most basic knowledge in the field of classics, including historical and cultural trends in the ancient world and the current status of research. This course will specifically focus on developing students' research skills and laying the foundation for future research work. _x000D_

Name: Latin Reading (1)
Introduction: This course is an intermediate Latin course. The main content is to read and translate selected passages from classical Latin literature (including prose and poetry), and conduct linguistic analysis of them. The focus of teaching is language training, as well as the literary and historical background of the texts read.

Name: History of Science and Technology
Introduction:
Looking at the creation and dissemination of science and technology from the globalization of knowledge in the pre-modern period. _x000D_
Understand the scientific revolution, the stages of the scientific revolution and the conditions for its emergence, understand the relationship between science and religion, the institutionalization of science, and the scientific revolution in China.

Name: Introduction to Medieval Studies
Prerequisite: A compulsory course in the direction of the classical language Bansi. The summer vacation in 2016 was organized by Dr. Clement Lenoble of Diplomacy.
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for students with a Western classical orientation in the classical language class. It matches the introduction to classics and introduces and guides students to understand the historical materials of European medieval studies, the status of research books and periodicals, the history of doctrine, and current research trends. Its basic teaching framework follows Professor Van Kanegang's "Introduction to Medieval Research Documents", but the content is expanded to more doctrinal history and takes into account the research status of Chinese academic circles. The course will be taught in English, and European and American scholars will be invited to participate in the teaching.

Name: Latin Reading (2)
Prerequisite: A one-year Latin language course is required to master Latin grammar.
Introduction: This course is an intermediate Latin course, followed by "Latin Reading (1)". The purpose is to improve the ability to read and understand Latin documents through intensive reading of selected passages of classical Latin documents and translation exercises, so that students can accurately read and understand Latin documents of intermediate difficulty.

Name: History of Ancient Greece
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the history of ancient Greece from the Minoan-Mycenaean civilization to the Hellenistic era. It introduces the research results and related debates on some important issues, so that students can understand the main historical facts of Greek history and have an understanding of the main research results and research directions in this field.

Name: Qualitative Research Methods in the Humanities and Social Sciences
Prerequisite: This course is suitable for senior undergraduate students who are interested in qualitative research and are about to begin writing academic and graduation thesis. It is required to have the ability to read English academic works, and to have the interest and courage to directly participate in field work.
Introduction:
This course aims to establish a systematic and in-depth understanding of qualitative research thinking and research methods for senior undergraduate students in the humanities and social sciences. Through mutual exchanges between undergraduates and graduate students, undergraduate students are trained to enter systematic research and paper writing. _x000D_
Course teaching content: Methodological theory teaching; method operation and analysis of research works using different methods; hands-on field ethnographic work training; direct communication with outstanding international and domestic qualitative research scholars through the academic platforms of the Institute of Humanities and Social Sciences of Peking University, School of Public Policy and Management at Tsinghua University, and Schwarzman College; detailed qualitative research data analysis and paper writing guidance. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course hopes to guide students to understand the five research consciousnesses of qualitative research, namely methodological consciousness, theoretical analysis consciousness, field work consciousness, historical consciousness and narrative consciousness. _x000D_
_x000D_
Throughout the core of the course: establishing methodological awareness. Such awareness is that any research method is a way for researchers to express their ontological and epistemological understanding of how the world operates. The course then guides students to understand the differences in methodological (epistemological and ontological) paradigms behind different methods of operation. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course focuses on improving students' four abilities. That is, 1) the ability to deeply analyze theoretical academic works (rather than just sort out research literature); 2) the ability to practice field work and analyze field data; 3) the ability to understand and evaluate good qualitative research; _x000D_

Name: Advanced Mathematics (D) Problem Session
Introduction: This course consolidates the content of the higher mathematics courses taught through lectures.

Name: Frontier Research and Criticism in Online Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course conducts a comprehensive frontier scan of Chinese online literature. On this basis, excellent works are selected for in-depth study and students are trained to write high-quality literary criticism. At the same time, some important trends were discovered and conducted in-depth research. This is also a process of sorting out the history of Internet literature. On the basis of understanding Internet literature, we will establish a set of Internet literature evaluation systems that both inherently contain elite vision and are independent of traditional elite literary standards, and establish a set of Internet literature critical discourse. The course will be conducted in the form of a seminar. Students who choose the course are required to make independent reports and participate in in-depth discussions of other students' course reports.

Name: Studies in Yuan and Ming Zaju Drama
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course hopes to enable students to have a more comprehensive and specific understanding and grasp of the opera literature of the Yuan and Ming dynasties in China through the description of the phenomenon of Chinese opera literature in the Yuan and Ming dynasties and the study of important original classics of opera literature.

Name: Topics in the History of Peking University
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the historical process of the founding and development of Peking University in modern times. Focus on teaching the special historical position of Peking University in the history of education and politics in modern China, and understand the important contributions made by teachers and students of Peking University to the progress of higher education, the country's modern transformation, and the revolution and construction of the Communist Party of China. This semester’s course focuses on the history of Peking University from before and after its founding to the War of Liberation. The main contents include special lectures, literature reading and classroom discussions, in addition to historical video material playback and social practice. _x000D_

Name: Intermediate Microeconomics Problem Session
Introduction: This course teaches at an intermediate level basic knowledge about economic decision-making by micro-agents and the role of markets in resource allocation. This course first discusses the decision-making issues of consumers and manufacturers under perfectly competitive market conditions. Then the general equilibrium theory and the welfare economics significance of competitive equilibrium are introduced. Finally, we turn to discuss several situations in which market mechanisms cannot lead to effective resource allocation, namely: imperfectly competitive market structures, the existence of externalities, the supply of public goods, and information asymmetry in economic transactions. This course is an important required course for economics majors. _x000D_

Name: Government-Market Relations in Historical Perspective
Introduction: Human economic activities have a long history, and their mysteries have not yet been completely cracked by economists. From classical economics to neoclassical economics, from institutional economics to new institutional economics, from Keynesianism to the Austrian school... Whether economists ignore or emphasize it, the relationship between "government" and "market" has always been an unavoidable issue in understanding the phenomenon of economic growth, and it is also a topic that is still being debated by economists to this day. Are "government" and "market" naturally opposed? Is "small government, big market" necessarily efficient? ...Observing from the perspective of a certain time, place, and time is one answer, and observing from the perspective of thousands of years of human civilization history spanning east and west may be another answer. This course systematically introduces theories and cases related to the "relationship between government and market", and establishes a complete framework for understanding "relationship between government and market" through comparison of Chinese and Western economic history and history of economic thought.

Name: Topics in Qing History
Introduction:
This course focuses on the major historical issues in the politics, economy, military, culture and other aspects of the Qing Dynasty, and focuses on special topics_x000D_
Lectures, reading basic historical materials and classroom discussions are combined to learn the history of the Qing Dynasty and its development patterns. _x000D_
The main contents include the rise of the Manchus and the founding of the Later Jin Dynasty, the entry of Qing troops into the customs and the anti-Qing struggles of people in various places, _x000D_
The strengthening of authoritarian centralization, the consolidation of the unified multi-ethnic country and ethnic policies in the early Qing Dynasty, the Qing Dynasty_x000D_
The restoration of the social economy of the dynasty and the feudal taxation system, the class structure of the Qing Dynasty and the social contradictions of the previous dynasty in the eighteenth century_x000D_
Dun, new changes in the ideological circles during the Ming and Qing Dynasties, cultural policies of the Qing Dynasty and the development of Sinology, etc. _x000D_

Name: Causal Inference in Statistics and Biostatistics
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, high algebra, probability theory, mathematical statistics
Introduction:
This course will introduce various scientific or statistical problems in causal inference. This is not the first time that the concept of causal reasoning has been proposed. In fact, we probably use the concept of causal inference every day without even realizing it. Without the development of causal inference, we wouldn't even be alive today. However, causal inference is not widely discussed in standard statistics textbooks. This may be due to the fact that the basis of statistics is based on probability theory, which focuses on the parameters of a joint distribution of samples drawn from a population. These parameters allow researchers to estimate the probabilities of past and future events and update these probabilities based on new information, assuming that experimental conditions remain unchanged. However, causal inference goes one step beyond these associated probabilities, inferring probabilities under changing experimental conditions. _x000D_
_x000D_
In this course, I will first introduce the basics of causal inference based on underlying fact models and give mathematical definitions of the causal parameters of interest. I will then introduce statistical issues in causal inference in randomized clinical trials, as well as statistical issues in causal inference in observational studies, showing how to make credible causal inferences without randomization. _x000D_

Name: Vocal Music
Prerequisite: None. Students who choose a course must have a certain musical theoretical basis.
Introduction:
The basic theories of vocal music are taught including: singing breath, singing resonance, singing vocal range, singing enunciation, musical expression, etc. According to the students' different voice conditions and problems, targeted training is carried out, including selecting vocal training songs and repertoire exercises suitable for each student, so as to teach students in accordance with their aptitude. Course features: Focusing on small classes, students will improve their individual singing and duet singing through a large number of Chinese and foreign folk songs, Chinese and foreign art songs, Chinese and foreign opera arias and duet selections. _x000D_
Students who choose this course must have a certain foundation in music theory. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Topics in Quantitative Finance
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, random process
Introduction: This course aims to introduce and explore mathematical, economic and physical models related to quantitative finance. Topics focus on portfolio construction, volatility estimation and modeling, interest rate-related products and modeling, and best execution strategies. Based on the needs of application, the first part of this course will focus on the introduction of stochastic control theory and statistical learning related knowledge. Students who complete the course should have basic knowledge of quantitative financial models and techniques related to their applications.

Name: Business Forecasting Analytics
Introduction: Forecasting is an important component of many management disciplines, such as economics, finance and marketing, and is a crucial part of business practices, government planning and strategic decision-making. Business Forecast Analysis aims to provide systematic interpretation of forecasting methods and hands-on training in business cases for students in disciplines such as economics and management. The course will begin with a presentation of key elements of the forecasting process, such as decision-making processes, forecasting philosophy, data acquisition, modelling and forecasting evaluation. The course will then introduce models and analytical methods commonly used in forecasting, the issues to which they should be used, and their specific application in business analysis. The prediction models that will be highlighted in the course include linear prediction models, non-linear prediction models, one-dimensional time series models, multi-course prediction models, model combinations and averages, high-dimensional factor models, state spatial models, Markov transfer models, hybrid data models, unstable models and volatility models. The cases covered include projected analyses of important variables such as GDP, price indices, consumer demand, inventories, retail volumes, consumption, interest rates, exchange rates, stock rates of return and volatility. Unlike related courses such as econometrics, the course emphasizes the background and scenario application of forecasting methods, rather than the theoretical nature and extrapolation behind forecasting methods.

Name: Integrated Chemical Kinetics
Introduction: This course is a basic course offered in the second and third semesters for undergraduates in the integrated science experimental class. The main content integrates the thermal content of physics and the physical chemistry content of chemistry, and also provides some preliminary introduction to the thinking methods of statistical physics. This course requires students to have a good grasp of the basic concepts, basic theories, basic knowledge and basic methods of studying thermodynamics and physical chemistry, and to cultivate students' scientific thinking methods and ability to analyze problems. The teaching content is combined with the regulatory mechanism of biological systems to enable students to understand the relationship between thermodynamics, physical chemistry and life sciences, and stimulate students' interest and innovative spirit.

Name: Fundamentals of CGE Economic Models and GAMS Optimization Programming
Introduction:
Empirical models and quantitative analysis have become important means of research in applied economics and public administration. "Slap on the head" and qualitative analysis can no longer meet the needs of economic policy analysis. For example, the government wants to reduce the export tax rebate rate in order to reduce the trade surplus. How much should the tax refund rate be reduced? What impact will it have on employment? What impact will it have on different related industries, such as clothing and agriculture? _x000D_
_x000D_
The Computable General Equilibrium Model (CGE) is a newly developed economic quantitative model that can be applied to many research fields (trade, finance, environment, etc.) and can give practical policy suggestions. Its characteristic is that it takes into account that all parts of the national economy are closely related and affects the whole body. It not only conducts quantitative analysis on the directly affected departments, but also considers the interdependence and correlation between various departments. This course starts from the basic input-output table of the data required by the model, and explains some basic functions of economics (production, consumption, investment, government and trade) and general equilibrium theory; it introduces relevant economic theories in a timely manner, and combines examples, exercises and programming to explain the basic principles and structure of the CGE standard model clearly and thoroughly; with the basic goal of mastering the standard CGE model, it explains the basic principles of the CGE model. All course examples are programmed in the operations research optimization software GAMS language, which is mainly used for optimizing and solving basic functions of economics and CGE model solving. It will also discuss how to use it for other optimization and solving problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course not only introduces the economic principles in CGE models, but also teaches hands-on GAMS programming with everyone, so that students can not only master the construction and design of CGE models based on theory and solve problems, but also write corresponding GAMS programs to simulate CGE models with computers. _x000D_

Name: Advanced Microeconomics II
Prerequisite:
Microeconomic Theory I and
Mathematical Economics

Name: Contract Economics
Introduction:
The topic of our discussion is the different types of basic dynamic contracts. These environments include information asymmetries, and we have two main goals: one is to describe the optimal allocation that is achievable (the so-called second-best), and the other is to find the right policy to implement the best allocation_x000D_
The main tools used in this article come from game theory and mechanism design. Previous knowledge of dynamic programming and repeated game theory will be helpful. We will begin with recursive methods for solving dynamic contracts and then examine various recursive methods that extend the classic contract problem, including finite commitments, hidden actions, and adverse selection. Finally, we focus on the application of the modeling techniques we have learned to contract theory to other macroeconomic problems. _x000D_

Name: Science and Its Applications
Introduction: As a discussion class in Yuanpei Freshman Seminar Class, this course provides a platform for students from different backgrounds to understand and understand science. Through study and discussion, students can learn about the development history and trends of science throughout the ages, understand the intrinsic connections between science, technology, and engineering, understand the characteristics and significance of interdisciplinary subjects, establish a scientific understanding of science, and lay a certain foundation for future study, work, and life.

Name: Fundamentals of Innovative Product Development
Introduction: For Peking University, which combines science and liberal arts, students lack knowledge and practical foundation in design, R&D, and manufacturing. For the students of Yuanpei, who have the broadest and most free intellectual horizons, this is also a big shortcoming. For contemporary scholars and researchers, it is also an important pillar of the knowledge structure to understand the research and development, production and other processes of modern products, equipment, tools, and invention prototypes, and to strengthen their understanding and gain personal experience through corresponding practices.

Name: Human Anatomy
Introduction: Systemic anatomy is to study the various organs of the normal human body according to the system in which they are located, and study their morphological structure, location and adjacency. Course content includes: motor system, digestive system, respiratory system, urinary system, reproductive system, vasculature (circulatory) system, nervous system, endocrine system and sensory organs. The teaching format is theoretical class (18 credit hours) and practical class (18 credit hours). The theoretical class is mainly taught by teachers, and the practical class is conducted in the anatomy laboratory. It adopts the form of small class teaching. The teacher's teaching is combined with students' observation of human specimens to achieve the interaction between teaching and learning. Multimedia imaging materials, human specimens, models, atlases, etc. are commonly used auxiliary teaching materials and teaching aids for learning anatomy.

Name: Physiology
Introduction: Through theoretical study, students can master the basic theories about the occurrence principles and regulatory mechanisms of various life activity processes of the normal human body, understand the development of modern physiology, and lay the foundation for further study of pathology and various clinical courses.

Name: Advanced Deep Learning
Prerequisite:
Data science guidance or machine learning;
In-depth learning
Introduction:
Deep learning is the core technology that has made breakthroughs in artificial intelligence in recent years and has gained important applications in many important fields. Based on the "Deep Learning: Algorithms and Applications" course, this course will provide a more in-depth introduction to advanced topics in deep learning, including mathematical foundations, theories, algorithms, and specific applications in several related artificial intelligence fields in advanced deep learning, allowing students to be able to complete the implementation of artificial intelligence tasks in practice and explore cutting-edge topics in deep learning. _x000D_
The course requires students to be familiar with at least one programming language and basic knowledge of machine learning and deep learning. _x000D_
The course requires students to engage in in-depth reading of articles and presentations on cutting-edge research topics. Major assignments include basic theoretical analysis of deep learning models, applications in computer vision, natural language processing, or game AI. _x000D_
Grade calculation: 40% for daily homework, 60% for major homework

Name: Conservation of Immovable Cultural Relics
Prerequisite: The immovable course is the last professional course in the cultural relics conservation major and requires a good foundation. These foundations include basic courses in science and basic courses in this major. Basic courses in natural sciences such as chemistry, materials science, geomorphology, and geology; professional basic courses in materials science for the protection of cultural relics, and some auxiliary courses such as cultural relics and architecture. Only with these foundations can students deeply understand the content of this course.
Introduction:
The Immovable Cultural Relics Protection Course is a professional basic course for the cultural relics protection major. _x000D_
The purpose of the course is to enable students to have a basic understanding of diseases of outdoor immovable cultural relics such as ancient tombs, grottoes, and ancient buildings, disease monitoring methods, and protection and treatment measures for various diseases through course study, operations, and new site investigations. And how to deal with the damage caused by various natural factors outdoors. In addition to technical protection, the protection of outdoor cultural relics also involves the planning of large sites. Students need to understand the history and planning methods of outdoor cultural relics protection planning. _x000D_
The course must first understand the natural geology and landforms, which are the environment in which outdoor cultural relics exist; in addition, we must understand the various weathering and geological processes in nature, as well as natural disasters, which are the causes of damage to outdoor immovable cultural relics. The study of these parts needs to be based on geomorphology and geology. _x000D_
After entering the content of cultural relics protection, you first need to understand the concepts and types of immovable cultural relics, the general methods of protecting these cultural relics, as well as protection-related regulations and concepts. The discussion of protection concepts is an important part of this section. The discussion and introduction of the International Charter also need attention in professional courses. _x000D_
Next comes the investigation, value assessment, and determination of protection plans for immovable cultural relics. This is the first and necessary step in the protection of immovable cultural relics. Investigations for the protection of immovable cultural relics include: historical investigation, current situation investigation, disease investigation, environmental investigation, geological investigation, and sampling analysis, etc. An evaluation is conducted on the basis of the investigation, and finally a protection plan is determined based on various principles. In conservation, attention should be paid to the principle of minimal intervention and the principle of not changing the original status. _x000D_
The following part is about the diseases and treatments of the constituent materials: immovable cultural relics are made of many materials. For example, the main constituent material of grottoes is rock, but there are also many types; ancient buildings are made of more materials, such as wood, bricks, stones, paintings, etc.; ruins are composed of earth, stone, etc. The compositional properties, causes of disease, and methods of protection are discussed individually for each type of material. Some composite materials such as murals are also included. _x000D_
In addition to material diseases, structural diseases of immovable cultural relics are also very common. The structural diseases and treatment section discusses the structural diseases of various cultural relics, such as cracking and collapse of grottoes; crookedness and cracking of ancient buildings; sinking of the tops of tombs, etc. After introducing the disease situation, the management of various diseases was discussed and many examples were given. _x000D_
Then there are geological diseases. The so-called geological diseases are the harm and destruction of cultural objects caused by problems in the earth and mountains that carry immovable cultural relics. These generally rely on engineering geological methods to solve. _x000D_
Water affects the safety of immovable cultural relics, including condensation, rain and snowfall, groundwater, river and lake water, and suppression. Diseases caused by these types of water and treatment methods are also introduced. _x000D_
Biological organisms are another type of natural factors that affect the safety of outdoor cultural relics, including lower plants, higher plants and animals. A preliminary introduction was made to the classification of organisms, and then methods of various biological destructions were introduced. The first is the diseases and treatment of lichen, moss, mold, etc.; then the treatment of grasses; the damage and treatment of termites; the impact of birds, bats, etc. on ancient buildings and the methods of driving them away to prevent their impact and damage. _x000D_
The prevention and control of natural disasters includes the principles and prevention of lightning, fire prevention and control, types and applications of fire-fighting facilities, etc. _x000D_
Environmental control refers to the need to understand and control the environment in order to protect outdoor immovable cultural relics. It is mainly the control of the small environment in the construction of the ruins museum: those factors are not conducive to the protection of the ruins, and how to control the small environment. _x000D_
Finally, there is the protection plan for the site. The purpose of protection planning is to coordinate construction and historical heritage protection in urban construction to achieve the purpose of protecting heritage. The content of conservation planning and the development process of conservation planning are introduced, as well as examples of successful and failed conservation planning. _x000D_

Name: Conservation of Inorganic Cultural Relics and Laboratory
Introduction: Through classroom teaching and corresponding protection and restoration experimental classes, students can have a preliminary understanding of the characteristics of several major categories of inorganic cultural relics, the main diseases and disease mechanisms, as well as the conventional protection measures that should be taken against various major diseases, and the basic requirements for cultural relic protection archives. Students are required to be able to deal with some practical problems in the protection of such cultural relics.

Name: Professional Internship in Cultural Relics Conservation
Prerequisite: Protection of organic cultural objects, protection of inorganic cultural objects, protection of immovable cultural objects, protection of cultural objects
Introduction: "Cultural Relics Protection Internship" is a core practical course for undergraduates majoring in cultural relics protection. Through the teaching and internship of this course, students participate in the actual work of cultural relics protection, confirm theoretical knowledge, and enrich the experience of cultural relics protection operations.

Name: Techniques for the Analysis of Cultural Relics
Prerequisite: General physics, inorganic chemistry, analytical chemistry, physical chemistry
Introduction:
The accurate extraction and scientific analysis of cultural relics information is an important link in correctly evaluating the value of cultural relics. The development of modern science and technology has provided many effective means for the extraction of cultural relics information. More and more cultural relic research institutions are equipped with various modern scientific instruments for the analysis and research of cultural relics. Through the study of this course, students will be helped to understand various technical methods used in cultural relic analysis. _x000D_
The main content of this course includes various analysis techniques commonly used in image observation of cultural relics, microstructure analysis, composition analysis, material structure analysis, etc. Among them, the image observation of cultural relics includes X-ray photography technology, neutron radiography technology, infrared imaging technology and other methods; the microscopic analysis techniques commonly used in cultural relic analysis include stereo microscope, metallographic microscope, polarizing microscope, scanning electron microscope, transmission electron microscope and other microscopic analysis techniques. Analytical methods include composition analysis of cultural relics including atomic absorption spectrometry, atomic emission spectrometry, X-ray fluorescence spectrometry and other composition analysis methods; composition and structure analysis of cultural relic materials include commonly used structural analysis techniques such as X-ray diffraction, infrared spectroscopy and Raman spectroscopy. It also introduces separation analysis methods such as gas chromatography and liquid chromatography, as well as commonly used detection methods for cultural relics such as color difference analysis and intensity analysis. _x000D_
The course will briefly introduce the development history of these analytical methods, focusing on the basic principles of various technical methods and the structure of instruments and equipment, and then illustrate the application of these methods in cultural relic analysis by analyzing practical application cases. Through the combination of classroom theoretical teaching, experimental demonstrations and visits to study, students can correctly apply modern analytical techniques to the analysis and detection of cultural relics, use scientific methods to analyze cultural relics, recognize cultural relics, and comprehensively obtain cultural relic information. The purpose and task of the course is to familiarize students with commonly used technical methods for cultural relic analysis, and to cultivate students' correct learning and research methods based on scientific research goals and scientific, reasonable and suitable analytical methods. It also improves students' ability to apply basic theoretical knowledge to practice. _x000D_
The nature of this course is an applied basic course. Through the study of this course, students will understand the principles and methods of various scientific and technological analysis techniques and their scope of application in the field of cultural relics protection. This will lay a certain foundation for future research on cultural relics protection. _x000D_

Name: Materials Science for Cultural Relics Conservation
Prerequisite: Inorganic, organic, analytical, high molecular, material science
Introduction:
Cultural relic protection materials are an important part of the restoration and protection of cultural relics. Restoration and protection cannot be carried out without protective materials. With good protective materials and improper operation methods, good results cannot be achieved. _x000D_
The course first discusses the concept of cultural relics protection, introduces the process of cultural relics restoration, puts forward the requirements for cultural relics protection materials, and the purpose of learning cultural relics protection materials. _x000D_
Since most of the cultural relic protection materials involve polymer materials, the course provides a basic introduction to polymer materials, including the synthesis, types, properties, aging, etc. of protective polymer materials. _x000D_
Then it introduces the commonly used acids, alkalis, salts and other materials needed in the cultural relics restoration and protection laboratory. These materials are commonly used reagents in the laboratory. _x000D_
Cleaning materials are the first materials encountered in the protection of cultural relics. The teaching content includes cleaning materials, how to use cleaning materials, and various cleaning methods used in the protection of cultural relics: acid cleaning, alkali cleaning, organic solvent cleaning, paste cleaning, dry cleaning and some special cleaning methods. _x000D_
Reinforcement is the second step in the protection process. The concept of reinforcement, the objects of reinforcement, and the requirements for reinforcement materials are introduced, and the standards for stone reinforcement and soil reinforcement materials are explained and discussed. _x000D_
The teaching content of bonding materials includes bonding principles, bonding procedures, influencing factors of bonding, and precautions for bonding in the protection of cultural relics. _x000D_
The content of repair materials is relatively complex, including mold replication materials, repair materials, temporary support materials, modification materials, decorative materials, etc. The requirements and types of these materials are also known. _x000D_
Sealing materials is the last step in the protection of cultural relics. It puts forward the requirements for protective materials and the key points for selecting protective materials, as well as the use of materials and problems that may easily arise in their use. _x000D_
Then there are three special materials for cultural relic protection, one is a corrosion inhibitor, one is an ultraviolet absorber, and the other is an insecticide and antifungal agent. _x000D_
The corrosion inhibitor section introduces the principles of metal corrosion, and then introduces the mechanism and types of corrosion inhibitors. _x000D_
UV Absorbers introduces the types, mechanisms of action and application examples of these materials in the protection of cultural relics. _x000D_
Insecticides and fungicides are materials used in the protection of cultural relics, mainly introducing types and application examples. _x000D_

Name: Applications of Chemical Analysis in Archaeology and Related Data Processing
Introduction:
This course teaches common chemistry and isotope chemistry techniques used in archaeology, including various techniques for component (element) analysis, carbon and nitrogen stable isotope ratio analysis techniques, lead and strontium isotope ratio analysis techniques, etc. It also combines relevant archaeological practices and student experiments with the hope that students can master preliminary chemical analysis techniques and understand the application of related techniques in archaeology. (This part is taught by Cui Jianfeng)_x000D_
At the same time, for the analysis data obtained from related analysis, especially the processing of multi-component chemical element data, this course also teaches the multivariate statistical methods, the application of basic software and the methods used in drawing when processing such data. (This part is taught by Bao Wenbo)

Name: Statistical Analysis and Business Intelligence
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The rapid development of network and computer technology has promoted the transformation of business models in itself and other industries, resulting in more and more data to be mined to extract commercially valuable information to optimize people's business models and decisions. _x000D_
    Statistical analysis technology is widely used in various fields in technologically developed countries, especially Europe and the United States. Talents who master statistical analysis technology can easily find a job even in the current economic downturn in Europe and the United States. Therefore, data analysis is a promising career and career. _x000D_
    The application of statistical analysis in China is not as extensive and in-depth as in European and American countries, but we are pleased to see that more and more companies realize the necessity and benefits of data analysis. Banks, telecommunications and Internet companies, as well as retail and manufacturing, where data is generated, are particularly urgent. Data analysis is a sunrise industry in China. _x000D_
This course covers SAS standard advanced data analysis methods and their corresponding theories, and is implemented through SAS Enterprise Guide on Demand. Through data preparation, data presentation, data analysis and modeling, and finally report generation, this process enables students to master the necessary theoretical foundation and practical skills. At the same time, the necessary SAS programming technology will be taught, so that students will have the skills required in both SAS programming and EG. _x000D_
    In addition to explaining general statistical analysis methods, this course will invite front-line managers and R&D engineers from SAS Beijing R&D to explain hot topics and development trends in the field of business intelligence, big data, high performance, mobile BI, etc., as well as SAS solutions. Through product display and data processing demonstration, everyone can have a close understanding of enterprise-level business intelligence. _x000D_
    Inviting companies into universities to offer courses on advanced and practical technologies in the industry is a useful attempt to break the isolation of traditional Chinese education and the disconnect between companies and schools. Schools, students and companies will all benefit from it. The company warmly welcomes this move by Peking University and hopes that more Peking University students will have the opportunity to intern and work at SAS Beijing R&D. _x000D_

Name: Cornerstones of English Literature
Introduction: Undergraduate studies help students learn about European classic literature, including Don Quijote, Faust, Mountain. Reading the bibliography is an English translation of European literature.

Name: Selected Readings in Medieval English Literature
Introduction:
This course guides students to read Middle English poetry and prose written in the 14th and 15th centuries. It has three main teaching objectives:_x000D_
_x000D_
First, students will master the pronunciation rules of Middle English within a few weeks, and will be able to recite Middle English poetry fluently by the end of the course. _x000D_
_x000D_
Second, in addition to the study of ancient languages, this course focuses on cultivating students' literary analysis skills. Based on the original texts of Middle English poems, it trains students' sensitivity to poetic rhythm and creative techniques. _x000D_
_x000D_
Third, the historical and cultural background of the 14th and 15th centuries is also one of the key points of study. Based on this, this course will help students gain an in-depth understanding of the interactive relationship between literature and history. The issues discussed in the medieval English literary works selected for this course not only comment on current events in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, but also provide profound reflections on the cultural phenomena at that time. The topics discussed are also closely related to today's modern society, which can be used as a mirror to view the past and the present. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course revolves around four main lines: chivalry, love legend, faith and statecraft. These four are the most common themes in Middle English literature, but this course pays special attention to the historical development of literary genres, thinking about the stylistic references and intersections between epics, legends, religious prose, and political essays. _x000D_
_x000D_
In the process of sorting out the history and historical context of literary development, this course will explore the origin, development, connotation and complexity of the early "classics" of English literature. _x000D_

Name: General Portuguese (II)
Introduction: This course is a public elective course open to all students in the school. The course is designed to provide students from other majors with an opportunity to learn and understand Portuguese and the cultures of the Portuguese-speaking world. Through one year of study, students will understand the characteristics of Portuguese and master basic vocabulary and common grammar in order to meet their daily needs.

Name: General Arabic (I)
Introduction: The courses include language knowledge of voice, vocabulary, grammar and basic language skills for listening, speaking, reading, writing and translation. Each course takes the form of sentences, conversations, texts, words, instructions, syntaxes, exercises and exercises, which are linked to each other ' s relevant sessions, with a variety of forms and content, a balanced distribution of words and a high repetition rate, in order to enable students to lay down a solid language base.

Name: General Georgian (II)
Introduction: By learning Georgian courses, you can initially master the basic grammar and common vocabulary of Georgia, be able to communicate simply in Georgian, and initially master the skills of reading simple articles with the help of a dictionary.

Name: The Chinese Practice of the Garden City
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: The courseconcerning “urban”----such as Urban History, Urban Planning, Conservation Planning of Urban Heritage and etc.----are suitable as the pre-studying ones of this course. .
Introduction:
Garden cities are planned settlements (towns, villages), usually far away from big city centers, that concentrate the best conditions of towns and villages for the purpose of sustainable economic, social and environmental development. _x000D_
    The garden city movement originated from the housing problems caused by the British Industrial Revolution in the 19th century. It gradually spread to the world in the 20th century and became the basic platform for the development of international modern urban planning. _x000D_
    China was influenced by the Garden City Movement in 1900. It started with the foreign concessions in the opening cities and continued in the urban planning practices of some cities. It is mainly reflected in urban parks, university campuses, large estates, etc., and is more reflected in some urban planning outline drafts. Since the 1990s, the garden city movement in China has been mostly combined with other concepts, such as environmentally friendly cities, green cities, low-carbon cities, livable cities, natural cities, etc. _x000D_
    Under the framework of the "Memorandum of Cooperation between Peking University and the University of Birmingham" signed in 2014, this course will cooperate with the International Iron Bridge Cultural Heritage Institute of the University of Birmingham, UK, especially to publicly hold the "Iron Bridge Valley - the Cradle of the Industrial Revolution" exhibition on the Peking University campus and conduct field surveys in garden villages and towns around Birmingham, UK. _x000D_
    This course welcomes all students who are interested in garden cities. Name: The Gothic Novel
Introduction: English Gothic novels began to rise in the 18th century. After several centuries of development, their charm has endured. Although Gothic novels gradually ceased to exist as an independent genre after the 19th century, some classic Gothic elements that were handed down before still appear frequently in contemporary literary works. In order to explore the enduring charm of Gothic novels, this course will provide you with a detailed overview of the historical development and changes of Gothic novels from the 18th century to modern times. It will also systematically introduce the commonly used expression techniques and narrative strategies in Gothic novels to improve students' ability to appreciate and analyze Gothic works. In addition, this course also traces the performance and application of Gothic elements in different national literatures to demonstrate the cross-regional evolution and trends of this genre.

Name: Russian National Conditions (Part 1)
Introduction: The course provides a detailed overview of the history of the Russian State in the form of images, screens and texts, as well as an introduction to Russian geography and knowledge of Russian cultural traditions, social realities, customs, etc., and seeks to present the dynamic picture of the evolution of the Russian nation ' s millennium development.

Name: Russian National Conditions (Part 2)
Introduction: This course is a follow-up to the Russian state of affairs. The main subject is history from the nineteenth century to the present. (c) To lay the foundation for students to learn about the national situation and continue their professional studies.

Name: Russian Faith and Culture (Part 1)
Prerequisite: The Russian Faith and Culture is taught mainly in Chinese and mainly in the basics of several major Russian religious beliefs, with the aim of popularizing Russian culture, without the need for a first course.
Introduction: Russia is a country with a strong religious base, especially the Orthodox Church, which plays an important role in all aspects of Russian society. In 988 A.D., Russia accepted the Orthodox Church from Byzantine, and since then it has taken root in the land of Russia and forms an integral part of Russian culture, placing a deep mark on the daily life, literature, art and thought of Russians. For students who study Russian languages and literature, it is difficult to avoid the important lesson of Orthodox culture if they want to have a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of Russia, an understanding of the character characteristics of Russians, a reading of Russian literature and art, an analysis of the historical changes in Russia and an insight into its spiritual identity. The course " Faiths and Cultures in Russia " , which is mainly devoted to teaching Russian Orthodox culture, is accompanied by a brief introduction to Russian multi-theistic, Buddhist, Islamic and Samanian cultures. The aim is to help students learn about a spiritual Russia while understanding the geographic, social, historical dimensions of Russia by teaching them the most basic elements of Russian beliefs and culture, such as the long-standing Russian church buildings, the legends of the saints, iconic culture, religious festivals and music. Faith and Culture in Russia is taught in two semesters, the first of which is based on teaching more basic knowledge of Russian faith and culture, in order to give students a preliminary understanding of the problem, including: the multi-religious culture of Russia, the 13 major Orthodox holidays, the 4 major Ramadan periods, the famous holy places and churches, the art of icons and icons, the high-profile saints, and the second of which focuses on theoretical and more in-depth content in order to give students a better understanding of Russian beliefs and culture, such as the sacrilegious culture of the Russian Orthodox Church, the sacrilegacy, the church music, the prayer culture, the culture of guilt and confession, the attitude to disease and death, the influence of the Orthodox Church on Russian literature and art, the traditional ceremonialism, the Buddhist religion, Islam and the shabinian culture.

Name: General Bengali (I)
Introduction: Bengali belongs to the Indian language family of the Indo-European language family. Bengali is mainly spoken in Bangladesh and parts of the Indian states of West Bengal, Tripura and Assam. The total user population is 270 million. The text uses the Bengali alphabet, which evolved from the ancient Indian Brahmi alphabet. There are 11 vowels and 40 consonants. Vowels generally have abbreviated forms. Bengali has obvious differences between voiced and voiceless consonants, aspirated and unaspirated consonants, and retroflex and non-retroflex consonants. Nouns and pronouns change in case and number, but nouns do not change in gender. Only some nouns referring to people and a very few adjectives from Sanskrit have gender differences. Verbs change in person and tense. There are many dialects, and the dialects in Kolkata, the capital of West Bengal, India, are recognized as the standard language of Bengal. Based on this, modern Bengali Mandarin and its written form - Bengali vernacular - have been widely used throughout the Bengali-speaking region. The dialects in Dhaka, the capital of Bangladesh, are obviously different from Bengali Mandarin, but Mandarin is commonly spoken in Dhaka. Rabindranath Tagore, the famous Indian poet and writer, wrote literature in his native language, Bengali. One of the earliest documents in Bengali is the 10th-century Buddhist poem Jurjabod. Bengali is the most oriental language in the Indo-European language family, close to Assamese. Bengali is influenced by Austrian and Sino-Tibetan languages. The 1972 Constitution of Bangladesh stipulates: "The official language of Bangladesh is Bengali." Bengali is spoken by 240 million people around the world. Making it the seventh most spoken language after Chinese, English, Hindi, Spanish, Arabic and Portuguese.

Name: History of the German Language
Introduction: This course is an elective course for undergraduates majoring in German in the School of Foreign Languages. It is taught to undergraduates majoring in German. This course will systematically teach the main characteristics and overall development context of the history of German development, systematically introduce the cultural and social conditions of each period of German development, and explore the internal laws of language development. This course will enable students to master certain basic knowledge of the history of the German language and have a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the evolution process, the latest research status and development trends of German. At the same time, they will improve their German language ability and gain preliminary training in linguistic research methods.

Name: German Translation (II)

Among them are “amphibious” critics such as Goethe, Heine, Thomas Mann, professional critics such as Alfred Kyle and Lacy Lanetsky, and “hotline” literary critics such as Floyd.

Basic requirements: To understand the development of poetry in the German-speaking country, as well as the characteristics and famous works of poetry in various literary periods, and to master the basic methods and steps for analysing and interpreting German poetry.

Name: History of India
Introduction:
India is an ancient civilization with a long history in the South Asian subcontinent. Before the partition of India and Pakistan in 1947, its territory included today's India, Pakistan and Bangladesh. Ancient India refers to the ancient period of the subcontinent before partition. For most of the time, the subcontinent was divided and did not have a unified country. However, during the Mauryan Empire, Gupta Empire, Delhi Sultanate and Mughal Empire, unification was basically achieved or achieved to a large extent. When the Mauryan Empire and the Mughal Empire were at their largest, they included all of the South Asian subcontinent except for the southern tip of the peninsula. The northwest boundary even exceeded the boundaries of the subcontinent and penetrated into today's Afghanistan. At its peak, it was about 2,500 miles wide from east to west and 2,000 miles long from north to south, with a total area of ​​more than 2 million square miles. _x000D_
The ancient historical development of India not only has the common characteristics of Eastern countries, but also has its own distinctive characteristics. For example, the period of division was longer than the period of reunification, land was owned by the state and multi-layered for a long time, private ownership was not developed enough, rural communes existed for a long time, the caste system became the basic social organization, religious conflicts existed for a long time, and cultural models were diverse and unified. _x000D_

Many newspaper and periodical articles can be brought to students in the fastest way to read, almost in sync with Pakistani readers. This enables students to follow Pakistan through timely Learn the language through major events at home and abroad, and enable them to have a more timely and accurate understanding of contemporary Pakistan's social, economic, cultural, political and other issues. This teaching method that closely combines language with real-life cultural background not only improves students' interest in learning, but also expands their international vision and knowledge, cultivates their reading ability and reading habits, thereby greatly improving the teaching quality of this course. _x000D_

This course also further expands students' knowledge of the Urdu language and Pakistani society and culture.

Name: Urdu Translation Course (II)

Political themes include the country’s annual Two Sessions, the country’s development, the country’s legal construction, etc.; economics is basically a translation exercise for the country’s economic development reports; while current affairs involve a lot of international situations, hot spots, relations between countries, and relations between my country and other countries. Materials come from newspapers, the Internet, news, etc. Students are required to obtain materials and translate them accurately and quickly. The focus of teachers' teaching is to guide students to master sentence patterns, how to choose the best sentence patterns, and translate the most accurate sentences.

Name: History of Urdu Literature with Selected Readings (Part 1)
Introduction: As the "first" part of the "History of Urdu Literature and Selected Readings of Literary Works", this course starts from the emergence and development of Urdu, combines the historical development and cultural characteristics of the northern part of the Indian subcontinent, the main area where Urdu originated and developed, and focuses on explaining the importance of Urdu classical literature. It is necessary to develop the context and main features, and conduct intensive reading and interpretation of the text in combination with specific works, so that undergraduates can understand the important works of famous Urdu poets and writers and their literary and artistic characteristics through the study of this course, in order to have a more concrete understanding of the history of Urdu literature. At the same time, students are encouraged to become more proficient in using the language, master more idioms and idioms, and enhance their practical ability to use Urdu and their understanding and recognition of South Asian culture.

Name: Survey of Islamic Culture in South Asia
Introduction: Medieval Islamic culture entered South Asia, and after centuries of coexistence and collision with traditional Indian culture, a new cultural phenomenon was formed, which is what we call South Asian Islamic culture. It has become the main representative of medieval culture in South Asia with its emphasis on real-life thoughts, Urdu with different styles, culture and art that combines religion and secularity, sculptures and paintings without idols at all, Islamic architecture with minaret domes, and unique folk customs. This course helps students further understand the history, society, religion and culture of medieval South Asia.

Name: Urdu Listening (Part 1)
Introduction: The Urdu Hearing (Audience) course focuses on hearing materials of about three to five minutes each, covering Southern Asian fables, folk stories, etc. The basic material is short and simple, the language is simple and the grammar base is simple. Students are required to understand the content in order to increase the level of hearing in Urdu, to improve their voice and tone, to meet the requirements of mastery of living words, grammar, special sentences and customary terms, and thus to repeat the meaning of the story in Urdu, with the aim of improving their ability to hear.

They not only represent the creation and development of Urdu works from a literary perspective, but also reflect the historical, cultural, and social psychological background. This course plans to select several representative works from different periods and explain some of their contents through detailed reading. Students are encouraged to use their spare time to select plays they are interested in and read them in full to gain a preliminary understanding of the development of Urdu drama.

List and analyze the best Italian version of "The Prince" (Giovanni Inglese) and the English translation (Harvey). Mansfield), Chinese translation (Pan Handian) fragments; G. This course is a basic course and a tool course in language. The basic purpose of teaching is to cultivate and improve students' ability to read ancient documents through the study of ancient languages, lay the necessary foundation for further study and research of ancient Chinese language, literature, history, philosophy and other aspects of knowledge, and to better inherit the excellent culture of the motherland.

Name: Chinese Folk Customs and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Folklore is concerned primarily with that part of a cultural tradition that is created, preserved, and transmitted in oral, customary, and material forms. This course will teach Chinese culture from the perspective of folklore, covering traditional Chinese myths, stories, legends, festivals, beliefs, art, clothing, architecture, etc. As an important carrier of traditional culture, these folklore matters are important materials for us to understand and understand Chinese culture.

Name: General Survey of Confucian Classical Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Chinese culture is dominated by Confucian ideas, the direct vehicle of which is the Confucian classic, known as the Book and known as the Studies. Without reading the book, there can be no understanding of Confucian ideas; without understanding of Confucian ideas, there can be no understanding of Chinese culture. Therefore, knowledge of Chinese culture begins with the Confucian classic. In the broad sense of learning, which is dominated by Confucianism, it is an orthodox of Confucian science. It manifests itself directly as a practical ethics, as well as as a political philosophy, one of self-interest, of physical integrity and of universal use. As a narrow academic category, the studies include research on the philosophy of Confucian texts, research on famous philosophies, discipline, literature studies on books, studies on economics and academic genres, studies on the evolution and evolution of history, studies on the relationship between studies and other academic groups, etc. In China's two thousand-year history before the “Four Fours”, the so-called academic profession was academically based, proudly known as the Literary Julein, well-known for its trophied classics, its diversity of denominations and its vastness, which constitute the core of China's ancient academic history and its main development, and represent the dominant ideology of Chinese society, with profound implications for academic, cultural and even political economic and social development, as well as for neighbouring countries such as Korea and Japan.
The subject of “Universal Studies” is intended to be introduced from the teaching of the content and exterior of the field of study, along with the evolutionary trajectory of the history of study and the backbone of the literature of study (restricted analysis of the history, history and literature), and is based on the flow of books, content, intellectual sense and historical compilation of the results of the studies, supported by the reading of texts.
