The curriculum is mainly taught in the classroom by schoolteachers and will have recommended literature, such as Uncle Lu's 1980 800 words in modern Chinese and Ma Jin (2004)'s Modern Mandarin Research Methodology.

Name: Ming and Qing Archaeology
Introduction: The archeology of the Ming and Qing dynasties is listed after the archeology of the Paleolithic to the Song and Yuan dynasties, but it is not a natural continuation of the series of courses on Chinese archeology. In addition to systematically introducing the archaeological remains of the Ming and Qing dynasties, the course also hopes to rethink the continuation and rupture of medieval and modern social history from the perspective of material culture; use richer documentary materials to explore the multiple possibilities for interpretation of archaeological materials, thereby stimulating reflection on the research model of historical archeology.

Name: Introduction to Ancient Chinese Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is designed to deepen international students’ understanding of ancient Chinese books and ancient Chinese culture. Classics are the most important carrier of ancient Chinese culture. This course provides students with an understanding of the form and structure of ancient Chinese books and various issues in the process of circulation through the introduction of ancient book catalogs, editions, collation, forgery identification, compilation, loss, compilation, publication, and dissemination. On this basis, master the basic methods of reading ancient Chinese books, develop the habit and ability to use and appreciate ancient Chinese books, improve personal cultural literacy and ancient writing skills, and lay the foundation for further learning of traditional Chinese culture.

Name: Research and Authentication of Cultural Relics
Introduction: Chinese culture is a culture of rituals and music, and the traditional Chinese lifestyle is a life of rituals and music (that is, the life of the heart). Ancient cultural relics are the material carrier of Chinese culture and the main tools for our ancestors' ritual and music life. Therefore, the basic characteristic of ancient Chinese cultural relics is that "vessels hide rituals", and ritual vessels have become the main component of ancient Chinese cultural relics. From the perspective of Chinese culture, this course briefly explains the characteristics, functions, categories and stages of the development and evolution of various forms, including the most representative jade wares (ceremony vessels used to honor heaven and nature gods), bronze wares (ancestral temple ritual vessels used to honor human ancestors and gods), as well as inscriptions and seals, as well as ancient calligraphy and painting from the perspective of Chinese culture, so as to enable students to have a basic understanding of ancient cultural relics in a point-by-point manner. The identification of cultural relics is an integral part of cultural relics research. In the study of cultural relics, we must first distinguish between the old and the familiar, distinguish the true from the false, and understand their value. Therefore, this course pays special attention to the general principles and basic methods of cultural relic identification.

Name: Conservation and Restoration of Museum Collections
Introduction: Through this course, students majoring in museology will have a systematic understanding of the basic methods and concepts of restoration and conservation of cultural relics in collections, and will be able to start thinking and looking forward to a certain extent.

Teaching mainly adopts practical operations, group discussions, reading reports and other methods.

Introduction: The course is based on the main thematic issues of museum research, with a more in-depth analysis and thematic exploration of different issues of museum science from different perspectives, such as collection, presentation, education and new museum science.

The cutting-edge literature on international trade and investment; third, how to use these theoretical and empirical analysis tools, how to use trade and investment data, to study various aspects of trade and investment policies, regulations, barriers, etc., on the behavioral performance of enterprises and industries, and on the impact on economic welfare. _x000D_

The problematic films of the "reform and opening up period" and the film industry's resurgence in recent years are equally eye-catching. _x000D_
    Selecting, watching, understanding, and comparing these films shot by different eras and directors will not only help understand the development of Russian and Soviet films, but also help enhance students' perceptual understanding of Russian and Soviet culture and historical development. Some film and television works adapted from famous literary works can help students understand the works vividly and deeply. _x000D_

Name: Medical Sociology
Introduction: Medical sociology is already a mature sub-discipline of sociology. In many countries in North America and Europe, medical sociologists are the largest professional group or one of the largest professional groups in the field of sociology. With the development of economy and society and the acceleration of global integration, the role of social factors in people's health and medical care has become increasingly prominent. With reference to the latest foreign textbooks and relevant teaching syllabus, this course will introduce the basic concepts, research fields, theoretical perspectives, and latest research results of medical sociology to students who choose the course. Combined with China's reality, it will explore various factors related to health and medical care and the interactions and mutual influences between these factors and health and medical care from a sociological perspective. Through the study of this course, students can have a relatively systematic understanding of medical sociology, form a preliminary "imagination" of medical sociology, and lay a good foundation for related work in the future.

The course is intended to help students understand the political, structural, institutional, workflow, membership models and projects of the United Nations. It will provide an in-depth analysis of the entities of the United Nations Secretariat in the area of peace and security, as well as United Nations consensus-building mechanisms, regional functions, etc. The course is designed to help students upgrade their career development skills within international organizations such as the United Nations. To this end, the course content focuses on the balance between basic knowledge and practical skills of international organizations.

Name: Smart Hardware Applications Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Digital Logic Circuit, Digital Logic Design
Introduction:
The main application scenario for computer technology, in addition to "calculation", is control. By using microprocessor computing capabilities, people can achieve very complex control logic. As electronic technology continues to develop, microprocessors are becoming more functional, while their chips are shrinking in size and their power consumption can be kept at a reasonable level. This has led to an increasing number of microprocessors applications, more industrial products being digitized and given “smart”.

The core microprocessor for achieving control systems can be an 8-bit MCS-51 single-piece machine or a universal x86 processor platform. Today, the ARM processor has acquired a wide range of applications, ranging from low-cost domestic electronics to high-end server computing platforms, where the shadow of the ARM processor can be seen everywhere. The course was taught using the currently popular Raspberry Pi development platform based on the ARM processor to complete the design of a smart hardware.

Raspberry Pi is a very expensive ARM platform that has been widely recognized by the market since its launch. It has an open interface, and many individuals and institutions have designed an off-site module based on Raspberry Pi for specific applications. The course's accompanying interface module enables multiple experiments such as digital input output, sensor data reading, etc., to facilitate quick student access to Raspberry Pi.

Through familiarization with the development platform through the completion of several basic experiments, students will complete the project design for a more complex smart system. The pilot project has its own proposition that students can turn their ideas into reality on the Raspberry Pi platform.

Introduction: This course is a compulsory course in the political theory of thought for graduate students in Chinese arts and sciences. It is designed to deepen their understanding of the development process of Chinese socialism theory and practice, to understand the achievements, challenges and strategies of Chinese road exploration in theory and practice, to understand the new expansion of Chinese roads since the eighteenth century and the new breakthroughs in Chinese Marxist theory, and to assert their confidence in Chinese socialism roads, theories and systems by comparing paths and thoughts. The teaching team for this course consists of teachers in the relevant subjects of the Marxist Institute, who are firmly committed to the political position, have in-depth research into the subjects taught and have extensive teaching experience. The basic teaching requirement is a combination of theory and history, guided by major issues, with academic logic and theoretical depth. The classroom instruction is combined with students ' interaction with reading the classics and classroom discussions.

Name: Introduction to the Dialectics of Nature
Introduction: The "Introduction to Dialectics of Nature" course is an ideological and political theory course that focuses on the education of Marxist theory of natural dialectics to help master's students master the Marxist view of nature, science and technology, science and technology methodology, science and technology society, understand the general laws of the development of nature and science and technology, understand the role of science and technology in social development, understand the significance of China's Marxist view of science and technology and the construction of an innovative country, and cultivate the innovative spirit and ability of master's students.

Name: Sociolinguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Sociolinguistics is currently the cutting-edge discipline of linguistics and applied linguistics. It studies the various aspects of the connection between language and society, involving the impact of various levels of society on language use, including cultural norms, social norms and situations. Issues mainly include: social variation and language evolution of language; social basis of bilingualism; society and language contact; identification of social groups from language; social attitude towards language; standard and non-standard forms of language; patterns and needs of common language use; language and power; language and social psychology, etc. The content of this course includes introduction, language communities and multilingual communities, language maintenance and language transfer, language variation and language contact, social variation of language, variation and language evolution, language variation and language use, language cognition and culture, and the application of sociolinguistics.

Name: History of Russian Culture (Part 1)
Introduction: This course is a required course in the direction of Russian culture and national conditions, focusing on the historical process of Russian cultural development and important cultural phenomena. This course will include units such as the origin of the Russian nation, the cultural development of Kievan Rus, feudal separatism and the Mongol invasion, the rise of Muscovy, Russian culture in the 17th and 18th centuries, and the reforms of Peter the Great. In addition to classroom lectures, literature reading, classroom discussions, and video viewing will also be arranged to enable students to have a deeper understanding of the development process of Russian culture.

Name: The Russian Language and Russian Cultural Studies
Introduction to Classic Works of Cultural Theory
Introduction: This course, which is compulsory for the country ' s cultural orientation, is designed to encourage students to further their cultural national studies by reading the original works of the cultural theoretical researchers, and by providing them with an understanding and mastery of the history, current situation, basic methods, and research paradigms.

Introduction: This course is a Russian elective course for postgraduate students in the fields of language, literature, cultural conditions and translation. It is mainly taught by foreign experts and is divided into two semesters. Through the study and text analysis of various types of corpus such as social politics, economy, literature and art, daily life, etc., this course enables students to deeply master the language and cultural knowledge they have learned, comprehensively cultivate students' listening, speaking, reading and writing skills, improve students' practical application abilities such as thinking, analyzing problems, and coherent narrative and expression in Russian, and lay a solid foundation for future scientific research, teaching and other practical work.

Name: History of Russian Culture (Part 2)
Introduction: The course, which is mandatory for the country ' s cultural orientation, focuses on the historical process of the development of Russian culture and on important cultural phenomena. This course focuses on the cultural development of Russia in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, including the first half of the nineteenth century, the Western European-Slavian debate, the second half of the nineteenth century, the revolutionary Democrats and populists, the “Silver Age”, the first half of the twentieth century, the second half of the twentieth century and the post-Soviet era. In addition to classroom instruction, reading of the literature, discussion in the classroom and visualization of the images will be developed to provide students with a deeper understanding of the development of Russian culture.

Name: History of Russian Literary Theory
Introduction: The History of Russian Literature is a comprehensive and systematic course on the development of Russian literature. It consists of four major components: Russian ancient literature, Russian eighteenth century literature, Russian nineteenth century literature and Russian twentieth century literature. The main theoretical schools involved are: realism, mythology, history culture, history comparison, history psychology, Marxism, religious culture, formism, Bakh, Tartu-Moscow. In accordance with the time series of historical developments, the course will teach important results of Russian ancient research into Russian literature and arts up to the twentieth century, particularly those that have had a significant impact on the development of world literature and arts since the twentieth century.

Name: History of Russian Social Thought
Introduction: The teaching content includes the history of the development of Russian social thought from the 10th century to the early 20th century, with the main ideological schools and representative thinkers as the axis. The purpose is to enable students to understand the social ideological disputes that played a key role in the history of Russian national development and their inherent logical relationships through the learning system of the course. Teaching is conducted in the form of teacher lectures and classroom discussions.

Name: Topics in Russian Literature
Introduction: Russian literature refers to literature created in Russian and mainly Russian literature, including Russian literature in Central Asia, Russian literature in Ukraine and Belarus, and Russian literature in the Caucasus. The course focused on the history and current state of Russian literature creation, studying the development of Russian literature and exploring the creative characteristics of non-Russian Russian literature in the context of Russian literature.

Name: Studies in World Poetry since Modernism
Introduction: From the perspective of stylistic evolution, influence transmission, style origin, and ideological evolution, we study modern postmodernist poetry that is placed in the process of literary modernity in the entire Western world since the 20th century across countries and languages.

Name: Marxism and the Methodology of the Social Sciences
Studies in the Commonwealth of Independent States
Introduction: This course is mandatory for postgraduate studies in the field of cultural nationalism. The curriculum is divided into two parts. The first is a comprehensive presentation of the cultural situation in the CIS countries, focusing on three areas: basic national circumstances, historical evolution and sociocultural development. Separate presentations were made on each of the independent States, including the 12 member States of Russia, Belarus, Ukraine, Moldova, Azerbaijan, Armenia, Georgia, Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan and the Baltic States - Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. Reaching a more inclusive, integrated and country-driven approach. On the other hand, in addition to general comments, discussions are given on a case-by-case basis on topics such as the combined power of the country, the history of the rise and collapse of the Soviet Union, political evolution, changes in the economic system, the current state of the industrial and agricultural economy, the rule of law and the legal system, religion, culture and the arts, external relations, and exchanges between China and Russia.

Name: Repertoire Practicum
Introduction:
The purpose of the course: to enable students to improve their comprehensive abilities (singing, performance) in a short period of time through the practice (rehearsal) of plays. _x000D_
Basis for starting the course: students with professional vocal training and certain stage performance training. _x000D_
Teaching requirements: First, students are required to be able to sing the entire opera completely; second, students are required to be able to shape characters through performances at the same time to adapt to the requirements of the modern opera stage. _x000D_

Name: Performing Arts
Introduction: The " Performing Arts " course is a compulsory course for stage directors, performances, film and visual performances and other professions associated with public performances. The main tasks of the course are to describe the general pattern of performance creation, to acquire the means of creative work and to liberate the nature of the student by practical exercise, including issues such as the development of the quality of the actor, the development of performances and lines, the relationship between performances and musical performances, the elements of artistic performances, the communication between the actor and the actor, the control of the first self, the methods of handling and the way of thinking about the performance. Through this course, students learn more systematically about the basic theory and basic knowledge of performing arts and raise awareness of performing arts; help them to feel and recognize people ' s interactions with people, music and body relationships, actor ' s relationships with viewers, etc., and improve their feelings and performance of music. Further study and in-depth study of the relationship between artistic performance and real life, and corresponding discussion of public behaviour from the point of view of performance.

Name: Aesthetics of Opera
Introduction:
This is the aesthetics basic course of "opera studies". From a cultural and aesthetic perspective, this course provides cultural and aesthetic coordinates for students to understand, appreciate, and create opera through a comparative study of the evolution of Chinese and Western poetry, drama, and music art. Tracing back to the "past life", focusing on the "present life", focusing on the current development and artistic composition of "Chinese Opera" possibilities. _x000D_
This class is aimed at potential appreciators and participants of opera who have a certain knowledge of art and love art. _x000D_
It is expected that the students will activate their artistic passion and interest in opera through this course, and then become active participants in Chinese opera and stage plays. _x000D_

Name: Artistic Direction
Introduction: It mainly solves the overall coordination of singing and accompaniment, music structure and emotional processing, language sense of various languages, music style processing, etc., to help students master the style issues of different countries, different eras, and different writers.

Name: Vocal Music
Introduction: Further standardize students' vocal methods, expand the scope of research, browsing and singing of vocal works and opera works, master the styles of various opera works through the rehearsal of multiple opera excerpts, and greatly improve singing ability and comprehensive expression to meet the needs of opera performances.

Name: Body Conditioning and Dance
Introduction: With the basic training in dance as the main component, students are systematically trained in physical coordination and physical expression; in the course of their teaching, they are expected to develop their ability to dance for the general role of opera and to be able to perform at a certain level of difficulty; and have a degree of knowledge of the basic styles of the various types of dance, such as ballet, jazz, contemporary dance, tap dance and Chinese folk dance.

Name: Cultural History of Opera
Introduction: It is an interdisciplinary course. The art of opera is placed in the historical connection of the social and humanities, in the cultural life of the time, in parallel with the development of sister art. It not only describes the opera's own history of development, but also pays special attention to the history of the acceptance of the work of the opera, the interaction between the social environment and the “acceptance of the opera” of a particular audience and the development of the opera: an opera history of observation and understanding in cultural contexts. At the same time, the basic issues of opera aesthetics are understood and discussed in practical cases.

Name: Basic Techniques of Artistic Language Expression
Introduction:
The course "Basic Skills in Artistic Language Expression" is a required professional course for stage directors, opera performance majors, film and television performance majors, and other majors related to public performance. Language is a symbolic system that uses speech as a material shell and consists of vocabulary and grammar. It is an important tool for communication between oneself and others. Language is also one of the most intuitive and effective means for actors to shape their characters. The accuracy of line processing directly determines the success or failure of an actor's second creation of a character. Artistic language mainly refers to the language used by actors when playing characters on stage. It is a refinement of life language, an exaggerated and modified language that originates from life and is higher than life. It often has the temporality and aurality of music and poetry, as characterization is often established through audible verbal language (lines) and visible actions (bodies) and felt emotions. For this reason, audio language plays a very important role in stage performances and public presentations. _x000D_
The main task of this course is to enable trainees to speak accurately, flexibly, and clearly through training methods such as looseness, purity, clarity, distance, beauty, patience, and depth in the process of expressing Mandarin Chinese. What is more important for professional actors is to train them to use lines to fully express the emotions of the characters during performance.   _x000D_

Name: Choral Rehearsal
Introduction:
The purpose of opening chorus rehearsal courses is to improve the comprehensive music ability, appreciation ability and musical cultivation of non-music major students through chorus training, enter into a deeper understanding and creation of music, and feel the significance of chorus training. _x000D_
   For students majoring in opera, the purpose is to browse more and learn more about choral works of different periods and styles. And apply what they have learned to cultivate students' ability as rehearsal organizers in the future. _x000D_
   This course requires students to have a certain musical foundation (notation reading ability, vocal skills)_x000D_

Name: Recitative
Introduction: Recitative occupies an extremely important position in the pattern. It is the narrative in the opera that is recited through language. It is also the most difficult part of the opera. The recitative plays a role in promoting the development of the plot, and is expressed in different languages, voices, moods, and intonations in different operas. There are three types of recitative: 1. Pure recitative 2. Recitative with orchestra accompaniment 3. Shangban recitatives, etc... In teaching, we should give students a comprehensive understanding and training through recitatives written by different periods, different styles, different languages, and different composers.

Name: Aria Performance Coaching
Introduction: This course is for first grade masters. Aria is a solo form of opera, with high demands on actors in their acting, voice, character formation, singing skills, language, etc. To develop the psychological qualities of students ' professional operars through the aria classes, to help students become familiar with the stage, to understand music, to master the rhythm, to mobilize their emotions, to enhance the performance consciousness of the opera stage and to understand the character of the characters in the play, thereby creating a vivid, visible and very attractive image of opera characters.

Name: Chamber Music Singing
Introduction: Indoor music is a delicate and implicit feature, with emphasis on the careful expression and overall balance of vocal music and bands, in order to enhance the professionalism, nuancedness and comprehensive artistic nurturing of vocal singers. As the essential basic qualities of opera performers, indoor music plays an important role in enhancing the depth and precision of band collaboration.

Name: Advanced Multivariate Statistical Analysis
Introduction: Multiple analysis refers to statistical analysis methods for multidimensional data. Our usual data are multidimensional. Large data starting several years have higher data dimensions. Multiple analysis is the basic method of statistics. With the extensive collection of multiple data in more scientific and social sciences, there is an urgent need for a more high-positioned multi-analysis course in North China. The course will cover statistical models and analytical algorithms for the analysis of multidimensional (multiple) statistics, including ultra-high-dimensional statistics. Multiple statistical methods can be applied directly to the practice of big data statistical analysis.

Name: Ideological and Political Practice
College: Peking University Committee of the Communist Youth League of China

Introduction:
This course, which is compulsory for students in the first year of undergraduate studies, is designed to guide and organize students to participate in practical activities such as social research, volunteering, music education, based on their growth and development needs, and to develop and promote the mindset, love, social awareness, and dedication of young students of the North.
The two-centre compulsory school curriculum is divided into three modules of music education, social practice, voluntary service. After the self-selection of the teaching system for first-year students, students are required to select two of these modules on the practical course platform and to complete the requirements. After the end of the third-year school year, the school board is given a single score in the teaching system.
The course requires students of selected subjects to participate in the corresponding theoretical courses, practical activities and presentations of results and to submit written work such as thought, reports, papers, etc.

Name: PKU Introductory Course in Mathematics
Prerequisite: Undergraduate students at the Faculty of Mathematics, or double-degree students at the university level, are not required to take courses.
Introduction: This course is a new course for undergraduate freshmen studying mathematical sciences across the school. Freshmen will face several major confusing questions when they transfer from middle school to university study: First, what to study in college mathematics or more advanced mathematics? What is the logical system of the course? Second, how to effectively study and research mathematics at Peking University? What resources are available at Peking University to help students learn mathematics? This course will introduce to undergraduate freshmen the organizational structure of Peking University mathematics, the logical system of Peking University mathematics courses, and the mathematics resources available at Peking University or at home and abroad. In addition, we will also introduce how to maintain a good attitude in a highly competitive environment.

Name: Statistical Thinking
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, program design, mathematical statistics
Introduction: This course provides a relatively systematic, basic and cutting-edge introduction to computer statistics. The course mainly includes: statistical principles, statistical reasoning, Bayesian inference, statistical models and methods, etc. Help students learn how to implement or apply statistical methods and models, and master the mathematical mechanisms contained in statistics, thereby cultivating students' statistical analysis and thinking abilities.

Name: Applied Survival Analysis
Introduction: Survival analysis is a statistical discipline that studies life span data and response time data. It is a core course in biostatistics, medical statistics and other disciplines. The Applied Survival Analysis course will focus on how to use modern survival analysis methods to process lifespan data. Through the study of this course, students will master the basic concepts of survival analysis and basic statistical methods, focusing on how to apply common biostatistical models to deal with practical problems. The main content includes description methods of survival data, regression models, interpretation of proportional hazard rate models, variable selection, model evaluation, promotion of proportional hazard rate models, parametric regression models and other models.

Name: Selected Topics in Mathematical Analysis II
Introduction: Mathematics Analysis II is an elective course on basic mathematics analysis (I, II) and advanced algebra and geometry at the Faculty of Mathematics, which aims to develop further learning and discussion by choosing some of the key topics of the mathematics analysis course. The course is located around some of the basic concepts involved in the mathematics analysis course, basic theory, basic methods and systematic learning of basic ideas, building the capacity of students to discover problems, evaluate problems and solve problems.

Name: Selected Topics in Mathematical Analysis III
Introduction: This course is an elective course that starts with Mathematical Analysis (I, II, III), an important basic course in the School of Mathematical Sciences. It aims to carry out further study and discussion by selecting some important topics in the Mathematical Analysis course. The course is positioned at the systematic study of certain basic concepts, basic theories, basic methods and basic ideas involved in mathematical analysis, so that students can better understand the ins and outs of a theory, a concept, and a method on the basis of improving their learning ability.

Name: Introduction to Plato's Republic
Introduction: Read the entire book of Plato ' Ideal Country, highlighting the difficulties, analysing the validity of the arguments of the dialogue, the issues and conclusions of the critical study. • A step-by-step approach to the question of “how human beings should live”, as well as solutions from the perspectives of political philosophy, spiritual philosophy, intellectuals, introspectives and political psychology.

Name: Geometric Representation Theory
Introduction:
Geometric representation theory lies at the intersection of algebraic geometry, group representation theory, modern number theory and mathematical physics. It has deep connections with the Langlands program, the geometric Langlands program, mirror symmetry (homological mirror conjecture and SYZ conjecture), Motives theory, and geometric quantization (quantization of Poisson manifolds). _x000D_
We emphasize that representation theory should be regarded as a mathematical view. _x000D_

Introduction: This course will introduce in detail the harmonic analysis method of a type of nonlinear dispersive wave equations such as nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation, nonlinear Klein-Gordon equation, KdV equation, nonlinear parabolic equations such as Navier-Stokes equation, Boltzmann equation and other important development equations. The overall well-posedness of the solutions of such equations will be introduced. For dispersive wave equations, the existence content of their scattering operators will also be introduced.

Introduction:
Dynamic systems study the change of state over time. It is a mathematical discipline with rich theories and applications. "Time" can be a real number or an integer. The former is called a flow, that is, a continuous time system, and the latter is called an iteration of mapping, that is, a discrete time system. Dynamic systems can be divided into several branches such as differential dynamic systems, topological dynamic systems, ergodic theory, qualitative theory of differential equations, Hamiltonian systems, complex dynamic systems, and stochastic dynamic systems. However, this distinction is not strict and often overlaps. Differential dynamic systems generally refers to a branch developed around structural stability, universality, topological conjugate invariants and other issues since the 1960s. This course is a course for graduate students and senior undergraduates. It focuses on discrete-time systems, that is, iterations of differential homeomorphisms. Introduction: Teach the basic concepts, basic principles, derivation and application of calculation formulas of the finite element method. Introduces various commonly used unit features. Systematic introduction to the finite element solution of plane trusses and rigid frames, the finite element solution of plane problems, the finite element solution of axial symmetry problems and three-dimensional problems, the finite element solution of elastic thin plate bending problems, and teaching of area coordinates, isoparametric elements, higher-order elements, coordinated elements and non-coordinated elements, etc. Teach convergence criteria and convergence analysis of linear interpolation triangle elements. And equipped with hands-on internship.

Name: Analog Electronics
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, linear algebra; or basic knowledge of calculus, delinear equations.
Introduction: This course is an important basic course in the basics of electronic technology. It is the first circuit course for undergraduates majoring in electronics and computer science and robotics engineering. The course introduces the lumped circuit hypothesis. The main contents include resistive components and networks, independent and dependent sources, amplifiers, energy storage components, first-order and second-order dynamic networks, time-frequency domain analysis and design, analog circuits and applications. Through the study of this course, students will understand the principles of electrical engineering and be able to apply engineering abstract models to analyze and design simple electronic circuits. Understand the use of simple models to represent nonlinear components in circuits, such as MOSFETs, etc., and understand the practical significance of the systems developed in the course. This course enables students to acquire basic knowledge, basic theories and basic skills in analog electronic technology through the analysis and design of commonly used electronic devices, analog circuits and their systems, laying a foundation for in-depth study and application of electronic technology.

Name: The Ancient Text of the Book of Changes and the Pre-Qin Philosophers
Introduction: The Ancient Book of Changes is the source of the pre-Qin scholars and the source of the entire Chinese culture. Ban Gu's "Han Shu?" "Yiwenzhi" lists the "Yi" at the top of the Five Classics and believes that "the five constant principles are necessary and necessary, and the "Yi" is the origin." Pre-Qin Confucians, Taoists, Mohists, military strategists, Legalists, Yin-Yang schools, etc. all originated from the ancient Zhouyi. The course systematically teaches the basic nature of the book "Book of Changes" and the basic content of the sixty-four hexagrams, explains the relationship between the ancient Zhouyi Classics and the pre-Qin scholars, presents the basic styles of the ancient Zhouyi classics and the pre-Qin scholars, and explores the status of the ancient Zhouyi classics in the history of pre-Qin and even the entire Chinese ideological development, in order to enhance the electives' ability and literacy in learning and researching pre-Qin and even Chinese traditional culture.

Name: Stochastic Mathematics
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics (or mathematical analysis, linear algebra), probability statistics (or probability theory)
Introduction: As an introduction to stochastic processes, this course emphasizes the intuition of probability based on a certain degree of rigor. The main content includes random variables, conditional probability and conditional expectation, discrete-time Markov chains, Poisson processes, continuous-time Markov chains, queuing theory, Brownian motion, etc. It also includes a large number of examples of the application of stochastic processes in physics, biology, computers and information, operations research, genetics, economics, actuarial science, finance and other disciplines. This course will try to explain it in a simple and profound way, focusing on arousing interest, comprehending ideas, and feeling the charm. This course is suitable for graduate students and advanced undergraduates who need to know how to apply probability theory and stochastic processes to study problems in the above fields.

Name: Financial Big Data and Quantitative Analysis
Prerequisite: There is a programming language base. There is a better basis for probabilistics, heights, statistics, linear algebras, etc.
Introduction: Financial big data is an intersecting field between the financial industry and the big data industry. It is currently a hot spot in the industry. It is related to computer architecture, data management and analysis, and financial applications and development. Quantitative investment has been around for decades abroad, but it has only been around for less than ten years in China. This is a very challenging area. Financial big data and quantitative analysis combine the essence of mathematical statistics, financial theory, sociology, psychology and other disciplines, while paying special attention to practice. Due to the diversity of individual participants in market games and the complexity of group effects, this discipline is characterized by great challenges and significant opportunities.  Through the study of this course, students will learn the methods and tools of big data and system analysis, help students understand the principles of market behavior, and master market data analysis methods and tools through data analysis and model construction. Finally, build models and algorithms through practice, use historical data to verify the effectiveness of the strategy, and conduct evaluation through real-time data.

Name: Aerospace Industry Internship
Introduction: Organize senior undergraduates to visit representative industrial units in aviation and aerospace, and engage in scientific research and practice activities appropriately when conditions (confidentiality, time) permit, thereby establishing a certain understanding of my country's aerospace research, development and production units, and pointing out the direction for students to continue in-depth study and research on aerospace sub-topics that they are personally interested in.

Name: Digital Electronics

At the knowledge level, we focus on the in-depth study of basic knowledge and the application of knowledge.

Introduction:
This course is a series of main courses in engineering machinery designed to cultivate students' mechanical design capabilities. The course teaching aims at cultivating general mechanical design abilities of moderate complexity. Through this teaching process, students learn the principles of mechanical devices and basic theories and methods in mechanism design, so that students can freely solve mechanical design problems of moderate complexity, and have the ability to expand mechanical design knowledge and solve corresponding practical mechanical design problems. _x000D_
This course mainly includes the composition and principle design of machinery, mechanical design theory and structural design methods of general parts. The main contents include: composition and analysis of mechanisms, calculation of degrees of freedom of mechanisms, motion analysis of mechanisms, planar link mechanisms, cam mechanisms, gear mechanisms, gear trains, intermittent motion mechanisms, basics of mechanical dynamics, connections, belt drives, shafts, bearings, etc.

Name: Introduction to Robotics
Introduction:
This course comprehensively and systematically introduces the basic knowledge related to robotics and preliminary robot engineering practices. The knowledge narrative is divided into three parts: (1) The basic knowledge part includes what robots are, the basic components of robots, a brief history of robot development, ancient robots, bionic robots, intelligent robots, robot competitions, etc. (2) Robot applications include military robots, industrial robots, agricultural robots, medical robots, commercial robots, household robots, etc. (3) Robot development includes soft robots, micro-nano robots, _x000D_
Cyborg system, new technologies for developing robots, human-computer interaction, machine ethics, etc. The practical part includes 5 practical units: wheeled robot, robotic arm, humanoid robot, aerial drone, and bionic robotic fish. By combining explanations with pictures, videos, physical demonstrations, and engineering practice sessions, students can gain a comprehensive and systematic knowledge and understanding of robotics, and stimulate students' interest in learning and researching robots. _x000D_

Name: Robotics Laboratory (II)
Prerequisite: A basic course of specialization in robotic engineering is required, including Model Electronics, Digital Electronics.
Introduction: As an experimental and practical course in robotics, emphasis is placed on building the capacity of students to integrate the design and realization of electromechanical power. Development of robotic system-driven technology and control practices. Through electric power, hydraulic pressure, air pressure drives, and the use and control practices of brakes, motors, students master all types of driving technology and understand the electric angle/velocity/closure loop control, hydraulic/pressure drive control, resistance control, etc. Experiments are being conducted on the design of electrical hardware and embedded software programs. Students have acquired the basic hardware design and software development capabilities required for analogue circuits, digital circuit basic knowledge, and embedded systems development through practical elements such as experimental testing, theoretical design, PCB design, embedded C program design.

Name: Robotics Laboratory (I)
Introduction: Based on the mechanical design courses and theoretical mechanics courses, dynamic modeling analysis and basic experiments are designed, focusing on cultivating students' ability to analyze the kinematics and dynamics of mobile robots, and the ability to analyze interactive forces during robot operation. Master the functions of typical mechanical structures through practical operations and mechanism design. Learn about cutting-edge technologies such as dual-arm collaboration, human-computer collaboration, and human-computer interaction. Encourage students to design new experimental content by themselves and practice the theoretical knowledge learned in class.

Name: Robotics Laboratory (III)
Prerequisite: First, Autocontrol Principles, Robotic Experiment (I) or Robotic Experiment (II)
Introduction: Based on students' mastery of basic theoretical knowledge of robotics, a specialized and complete robot innovation design and implementation course will be started. Strengthen students' understanding of the overall closed loop of robot perception-decision-making and movement, and carry out mechatronics experiments. Complete the full-process research and development of at least one type of robot, fully master all knowledge and integrate it.

Name: Scientific Computing
Prerequisite: Apply analysis or advanced mathematical equations or equivalent courses
Introduction: This course discusses several main scientific calculation methods for partial differential equations, namely finite difference, finite volume method, finite element method and quasi-spectral method, and introduces related mathematical theories. Courses are taught entirely in English.

Name: Applied Analysis in Engineering Science
Prerequisite: Calculus (Single variate, and multi-variate), Linear Algebra, Ordinary Differential Equations.
Introduction: The goals of this course include: (1) introducing modern (1900-1990) mathematical methods that are widely used in engineering science, nonlinear mechanics, and other physical sciences; (2) stimulating students' scientific research enthusiasm, including inspiring thinking, clarifying problems and modeling, and exploring corresponding mathematical methods; (3) bridging the gap between mathematical tools and their physical understanding.

Name: Planting Practicum for University Students
Introduction:
The course “Academy in Growing Practice” is a general labour practice course for undergraduate students. The purpose of the course is to help non-agricultural university students understand the important role of plants in the use of Earth ' s energy and human survival, the basic biology and agronomics of crop cultivation, the patterns of cultivation of several common crops (vegetables) and the exercise and enjoyment of physical and mental well-being through farming.

Apart from a small concentration of the course (approximately 16 hours), the remainder are indoor and outdoor practices at the planting base (the base is located in the school). Each student who takes this course is responsible for and completes an experiment to grow a certain area of crops (vegetables).

Based on the seasonal nature of crop and vegetable cultivation, the course begins in the second week of the spring semester each year, extending to the middle of the summer break and ends at the end of July of the year. The practice planting component is managed flexibly and allows for flexible use of time.

The summer climate may cause discomfort and students expected to work are advised to take this course.

Name: Bio-Inspired Robotics
Prerequisite: Mechanical design; general theory of robotics
Introduction: This course is intended for sophomore/junior students majoring in robotics, or juniors from the college or the entire school who are interested in this course. Through the study of this course, you can understand the research background, research status and development trends of bionic robots, master the kinematics and dynamics modeling technology of bionic robots, become familiar with the overview of bionic robot systems, information perception, motion control and optimization technology, understand the path tracking, positioning navigation and collaborative control technology of bionic robots, exercise bionic scientific thinking and expand the horizons of bionic science. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Cultural Anthropology
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: This course uses English as a medium to introduce the main theories and methods of cultural anthropology in an easy-to-understand manner, and reveals the commonalities and characteristics of all human cultures through systematic analysis, explanation and comparison of cultural phenomena and customs such as language exchanges, economic activities, kinship systems, and gender relations of different ethnic groups.

Name: Fluid Wave Dynamics
Prerequisite: Hydrodynamics (not necessarily engineering), calculus (not necessarily mathematical analysis of engineering)
Introduction:
This course focuses on linear waves and their nonlinear interactions. _x000D_
The linear waves introduced include: surface gravity waves, internal waves, Poincaré waves, Kelvin waves, Alfvén waves, sound waves, etc. _x000D_
Introduce the corresponding mathematical methods for processing linear waves including: variation principle, ray tracing, amplitude equation, etc. _x000D_
Nonlinear effects include: wave-mean flow interaction, Lagrangian mean theory, multi-modal interaction, wave-induced diffusion, etc. _x000D_

Name: Circuits and Electronics
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra and geometry, constant differential equation, general physics
Introduction:
Course Introduction: In order to further adapt to the needs of the development of aerospace disciplines and the comprehensive training of students in the School of Engineering, a basic course is specially opened for the electrical majors (control, navigation, guidance, ergonomics, etc.) in the aerospace disciplines. In view of the multi-disciplinary characteristics of Peking University School of Engineering and referring to the electronics curriculum of Harvard University School of Engineering, this course will cover as broad an electrical content as possible, mainly including lumped parameter circuit model analysis methods, basic analog and digital electronic circuit devices and related design methods, and strive to explain the overall framework of the basic theory of electricity to students in the School of Engineering within limited hours. _x000D_
Summary of content: DC circuits, circuit transition processes, AC circuits and time-frequency analysis methods of various electrical networks, etc. Basic analog and digital circuits such as diodes, transistors and field effect transistors, amplification, negative feedback, acquisition circuits, and combinational and sequential logic design ideas.

Name: Fundamentals of Aerodynamics
Introduction: The course focuses on the basic knowledge of aerodynamics, supplemented by the knowledge of aircraft aerodynamics, to help students deepen their understanding of basic knowledge and the application significance of aeronautical engineering. In the basic department, based on the classic content of ideal fluid mechanics, the basic concepts, basic principles and methods of aerodynamics are introduced to reflect the fundamentals of the course. In the application part, combined with the classic aerodynamic shape, the concept of lift, drag, and moment of the airfoil and its role in the aerodynamic design of the aircraft are introduced.

Name: Fundamentals of Control Theory
Introduction:
It introduces the basic knowledge of classical and modern control theory to engineering undergraduates and is also suitable for graduate students majoring in dynamics and control. Prerequisite courses are calculus and linear algebra. Knowledge of electronic circuits, signals and processing will also be helpful in this course. In addition, emerging machine learning-based control methods will be introduced, primarily through the completion of design software tasks, and students should have experience using Python or other similar programming languages. This course can be used as an elective course for undergraduate students in the Department of Aerospace Engineering of the School of Engineering. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Human Action (Economics Section)
Introduction: The method of praxeology is the method advocated by the contemporary Austrian School for studying economics and other social sciences, so this course is actually the economics of the Austrian School. Austrian economics is different from the neoclassical economics that currently dominates the world. Austrian economics has developed a complete economic theory, which is deeply critical of all aspects of mainstream economics. This course focuses on teaching and reading the economic theory works of Rothbard, a representative of the contemporary Austrian school. His works are not only the most suitable place for us to get started, but also the only way for us to get started. The clue of the course is to start from the most basic concepts of economics, build a theoretical system of an unobstructed market economy, then analyze the consequences of coercive intervention in the economy, and finally lead us to explore what we call fairness, justice and other ethical issues. The Austrian School is not an economics that only cares about technical tools and only considers utilitarian issues, but is always permeated with concern for basic human issues and discussion of scientific methods.

Name: Frontiers of Quantum Materials Lecture Series
Introduction: Let students learn about the latest developments in various directions of quantum materials. This course will be held every semester, once a week. Domestic and foreign experts and scholars invited by teachers from the Quantum Materials Science Center will give special reports. This course is graded based on student participation.

Name: Experimental Methods and Techniques in Cold Atom Physics
Introduction:
This course is aimed at graduate students and undergraduate students at Peking University who are interested in engaging in atomic-molecular-optical physics experiments, especially graduate students and undergraduate students who have a strong interest in cold atom physics experiments. The course has two purposes. First, it brings the students to the forefront of experimental research in cold atom physics and trains their ability to extract important unsolved physical problems from the literature. Second, it gives the students a key to learning and guides them to systematically understand the basic ideas and technical methods of precision circuits, precision optical paths, feedback control, vacuum and thermal control, so that they can continue to improve after the course, constantly hone their own methods of doing things, and start building their own instruments in the laboratory. _x000D_
_x000D_
There are no prerequisites for this course. Students taking the course are required to complete daily homework, class discussions and final papers. _x000D_
(The following are specific instructions)_x000D_
The field of cold atom experiments has brought together many major discoveries in basic science, among which outstanding representatives include laser cooling of atoms (Nobel Prize in Physics in 1997), Bose-Einstein condensation (Nobel Prize in Physics in 2001), optical comb and ultra-stable laser technology (Nobel Prize in Physics in 2005), measurement and manipulation of single quantum systems (Nobel Prize in Physics in 2012), etc. If the field of vision is expanded to the precise measurement and control of the atom-molecule-optical system, the modern version of the Michelson interferometer makes the direct detection of gravitational waves a reality (2017 Nobel Prize in Physics). This course will show students and analyze the ideas and technologies behind these exciting scientific discoveries, and combine these ideas and technologies with a series of research frontiers that are being developed, such as atomic clocks based on cold atoms (now reaching an accuracy of 10^(-18)), the realization and research of topologically correlated quantum systems, etc., so that students can not only continuously enrich their knowledge crystals in the massive literature, but also gradually refine the unsolved and non-trivial scientific problems that they are interested in, opening their minds for entering the laboratory to engage in scientific research. _x000D_
_x000D_
Cold atom experiments are very challenging because they often require us to build our own instruments for specific scientific problems. These instruments include precision circuits, precision optoelectronic instruments, frequency-stabilized laser optical circuits, vacuum systems, etc. There is a similar methodology behind the construction of these instruments, namely feedback and feedforward control of dynamic systems. This course will start from the above-mentioned specific types of instrument construction cases to systematically teach students the basic ideas of feedback control. At the same time, it will also introduce some essential skills in the construction and operation of precision optoelectronic instruments based on the instructor's own experience, laying a foundation for thinking methods and skills for laboratory work.

Name: Introduction to Astrophysics
Introduction: This course attempts to understand several astronomical phenomena at a qualitative and semi-quantitative level based on the basic principles of classical (including general relativity) physics and quantum physics, and to understand and understand the cosmic environment in which humans live. Astronomical science projects driven by major scientific issues are platforms for nurturing and developing high and new technologies, and promote social progress. Classroom teaching aims to introduce the subject of astrophysics to physics students in a popular way so that they can have basic astrophysics literacy.

Name: Creative Design and Fabrication with 3D Printing
Introduction: 3D printing is a revolutionary, digital additive manufacturing technology that manufactures three-dimensional objects by adding materials layer by layer. It integrates information, materials, biology, control and other technologies and will have an important impact on the future manufacturing production model and human lifestyle. 3D printing technology can extend from imagination to reality, bridge the gap between the virtual world and the physical world, and create a revolution in innovative product design and manufacturing.  The course takes 3D printing technology as the starting point. It first introduces students to the principles, process characteristics and application fields of 3D printing technology, and attempts to use this technology to design and manufacture creative products. At the same time, students carry out multi-dimensional thematic research and speculative exchanges through teamwork, guiding students to experience and think deeply about the basic connotation of new technologies and their far-reaching impact on future society, and then deeply examine the social shock and innovative effects brought about by new technological innovations, and try to comprehensively re-understand and think about technology, humanities and ecological environmental protection.

Name: Astronomical Spectroscopy
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the structures, energy levels and transitions of important atoms and molecules in astrophysics, the physical processes of important atoms and molecules, the formation and excitation mechanisms of celestial emission lines and absorption lines, and the observation of atomic and molecular spectral lines and their applications in astrophysics.

Name: Data Visualization Analysis in R and Applications in Atmospheric Science
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of advanced mathematics, atmospheric science, etc. can be studied at the same time as this course.
Introduction: R language is a complete data processing, calculation and graphics software system. Its functions include: data storage and processing system; array operation tools (especially powerful in vector and matrix operations); complete and coherent statistical analysis tools; excellent statistical charting functions; simple and powerful programming language: it can manipulate the input and output of data, realize branching, looping, and user-defined functions. As a rapidly developing scientific research tool, R language has extensive and powerful graphics capabilities, which are closely linked to its analytical capabilities. R is completely free, and the system is developing rapidly under the GNU license. New features and capabilities appear every few months. The R community is broadly drawn from application domain experts and statistics experts. In this course, we will first learn the basic usage of the R system, and then gradually gain a deeper understanding of R language data analysis and graphics processing. Finally, we will study how to use the R system to solve data analysis problems in atmospheric science, and we will enrich the R package with code implementations of atmospheric science data analysis cases as our contribution to the R community.

Name: Principles of Atmospheric Sounding
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, general physics, atmospheric physics
Introduction: Atmospheric Surveys teach the basic principles and instruments of cloud, weather phenomena, visibility, atmospheric temperature, humidity, pressure, wind, radiation and precipitation evaporation of atmospheric elements. Provides students with knowledge of methods of acquisition and processing of meteorological information for courses in atmospheric boundary physics, atmospheric currents, cloud physics, pollution meteorology, atmospheric radiology, kinetic meteorology, atmospheric circulation, weather science, weather forecasting, climate diagnostic analysis, etc.

Name: Atmospheric Physics and Sounding Seminar
Prerequisite: The course is a small discussion session and is offered in conjunction with two courses, Basics of Atmospheric Physics and Principles of Atmospheric Detection.
Introduction:
The existing "Basics of Atmospheric Physics" and "Principles of Atmospheric Detection" are the main basic courses for atmospheric undergraduates and the basis for learning other professional courses. They focus on the basic theories of atmospheric physics, principles of atmospheric detection and typical applications. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is based on the above two courses and offers small class discussions. The teaching method is mainly based on student discussion, and teachers provide appropriate guidance to enable students to deepen their understanding of theoretical knowledge and understand the application needs in practical scientific research, cultivate students' ability to think and solve problems, and guide students to contact the cutting-edge fields of atmospheric physics and atmospheric detection. The discussion content of this course includes a summary of atmospheric physics theory and detection methods, the latest progress, hot spots, difficulties, and prospects for the future. A total of 11 discussion topics are set. _x000D_
_x000D_
The number of students in atmospheric majors is generally less than 30. According to the current small class size of less than 15 students, students can be divided into 2 to 3 small classes. Small class classes are 2 hours per week, and each small class class is led by a teacher. Each student will have at least two topic reports, and each discussion will be moderated by the teacher. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Climatology
Introduction: Basic knowledge of climatology from the perspective of the global climate system.

Name: Synoptic Meteorology
Introduction:
Synoptics is one of the many branches of atmospheric science. Meteorology is an ancient subject with a history of thousands of years. Meteorological observation instruments were invented in the 18th century, and only a few countries had weather observation networks in the 19th century. In the 1930s, high-altitude observations and theoretical research pioneered the establishment of atmospheric dynamics and Rossby wave weather prediction principles. Computers drove the development of numerical weather prediction in the second half of the 20th century. _x000D_
_x000D_
    Synoptics, also known as synoptic synoptics or large-scale synoptics, is the science of describing or explaining weather phenomena or weather events (such as rain and snow). These weather phenomena or events occur in the atmosphere, and they can be described by atmospheric variables such as temperature, air pressure, water vapor and its gradients, and the winds that move the atmosphere. The distribution of these variables specifies the spatial structure and interactions over time. These spatial structures are called weather systems. Weather systems at different scales will have a decisive impact on weather and climate in various places. _x000D_

Name: Advanced Optoelectronic Technology Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Background of advanced optoelectronics experiments: In 1987, 1989, 1997, 2001, and 2005, five Nobel Prizes in Physics were awarded to five important technological inventions: laser spectroscopy, atomic clocks, laser cooling, Bose-Einstein condensation, and optical frequency precision measurement. These technologies are the core technologies of current high-precision laser technology, ultrafast laser technology, atomic clock technology, global positioning system, and high-precision measurement technology, and are also the embodiment of the highest level of laser technology. Advanced Optoelectronics Technology transforms the latest achievements of today's laser technology and quantum information technology into experimental courses for undergraduate and graduate students, allowing students to master the most cutting-edge technologies in the development of today's laser science. Through the following ten experiments, this experiment allows students to master the modern advanced optoelectronic technology using modern computers, electronics, modern lasers, precision machinery, and atomic physics. Mastery of these technologies will lay the foundation for the development of the next generation of optoelectronics and quantum information technologies in the future. _x000D_

Experiment 2 External cavity semiconductor laser characteristics experiment_x000D_
Experiment 3 Saturated absorption spectrum experiment_x000D_
Experiment 4 Semiconductor laser frequency stabilization experiment_x000D_
Experiment 5. Magneto-optical trap experiment (MOT)_x000D_
Experiment 6 Laser mode-locking experiment (1) - fiber femtosecond laser formation_x000D_
Experiment 7 Laser Mode Locking Experiment (2) - Femtosecond Laser Compression of Fiber_x000D_
Experiment 8 Blue light frequency doubling experiment_x000D_
Experiment 9 Electromagnetic Induction Transparency Experiment_x000D_
Experiment 10: Optical fiber femtosecond comb measurement of optical absolute frequency_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Quantum Computing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Quantum physics base, microelectronic and circuit base, general information technology
Introduction: The size of microelectronic devices predicted by Moore's Law will shrink to a series of physical limits in the near future. Scientific researchers are using nanotechnology to seek an information processing solution based entirely on quantum effects - quantum computing. Quantum characteristics may break through the limits of existing classical information systems in terms of improving computing speed, ensuring information security, increasing information capacity, and improving detection accuracy. A 250-qubit memory may store up to 2 to the power of 250, which is more than the total number of atoms in the known universe. Quantum algorithms such as the factorization of large numbers proposed by Shor in 1994 and the search of large databases by Grover in 1997 further revealed that this quantum parallel capability can be used to efficiently solve some problems that cannot be solved by classical computers, such as using quantum search algorithms to attack existing cryptography systems. Classical calculations require 1,000 years of calculations, while quantum computers only take less than 4 minutes. In this way, the picture of quantum computers becomes clearer and shows broad application prospects in the fields of national security and national life. Theoretically proposed quantum error correction algorithms and the foreseeable emergence of more efficient quantum algorithms indicate that quantum computers have matured in theory, so how to implement them physically has become one of the ongoing hot spots in basic experimental scientific research. Quantum computing and quantum information have also become a major challenge for basic and applied scientific research in the 21st century. Among the 100 major projects to be implemented in my country's "Thirteenth Five-Year Plan", quantum communications and quantum computing rank third, and relevant professionals are urgently needed to join them. In the research field of experimental solid-state quantum computing, there are still no complete practical technologies and methods. Researchers have explored possible physical implementation methods of quantum computing from many aspects. The most important link boils down to the scientific issue of finding the physical implementation of qubits with entangled states of dual quantum energy levels. This course uses the original English textbooks and their Chinese translations, and is closely integrated with cutting-edge research papers. It is targeted at senior undergraduate students majoring in various science and engineering fields such as physics and electronics. The main purpose of this course is to teach the main physical ideas and basic knowledge in the field of solid-state quantum computing, while discussing the latest research progress in this field, introducing new carriers of solid-state quantum information such as ion traps, quantum dots, superconducting electrons, topological states and correlation systems, as well as scientific and technical problems and experimental research related to quantum computing and quantum information. Having studied "Quantum Mechanics" will be helpful for this course, but is not a requirement.

Name: Gravitational Wave Astrophysics
Prerequisite: General physics, theoretical mechanics, electrodynamics, mathematical physics
Introduction: The detection of gravity waves opens a new window for humans to understand the universe. The course provides basic knowledge of astrophysics of gravitational waves and related relativism; it includes the theory of gravitational wave radiation in a broad relativism, the associated physics of the sources of objects producing gravitational wave radiation, numerical relativistic calculations, gravitational wave detection methods, and principles and data analysis of ground and space gravity wave detectors. Learning through this course will not only provide a more in-depth understanding of the advances in the scientific and technical frontier of the modern brand-new branch of astronomy and physics, but also lay the foundation for further scientific research.

Name: Atmospheric Physics Laboratory
Introduction: Atmospheric science is an experimental subject whose basic professional teaching requires the development and training of experimental skills, techniques and techniques related to atmospheric science. With an overview of the country's atmospheric sciences, only Beijing University's Atmospheric Physics Experiment course has been maintained and implemented, leading and leading. The curriculum not only deepens students ' understanding and understanding of the basic concepts of atmospheric detection and atmospheric physics, but also develops and improves students ' hands-on skills so that they can work smoothly in the future.

Name: Introduction to Academic Paper Writing at University
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: It is designed to help students understand the main components of the writing of academic papers and to develop practical exercises at each stage. Students understand the difference between writing academic papers and other writings, and then define the scope of the subject matter for their choice, narrowing the scope of the topic too ambitious to make it a study that can be done within the limits of competence and time. The course provides for critical reading to enable students to screen appropriate relevant literature when using electronic databases. In terms of writing norms, this course will teach field professors how to correctly quote and avoid plagiarization, and will lead students to the requirements of the rules for reading reference books, using as an example the Rules for the Documentation of Information and Documentation, a national standard of the People ' s Republic of China. The course will also provide information on practical approaches to dealing with the problem of childbirth in the first draft, as well as on the points of attention for the revision of the paper.

Name: Strong-Field Optical Physics
Prerequisite: Optical, non-linear optical, quantum mechanics, atomic molecular physics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic principles of femtosecond lasers and common diagnostic techniques for ultrashort pulse lasers, such as self-(mutual) correlation measurements, frequency-resolved optical switching (FROG) and direct electric field reconstruction spectral phase interferometry (SPIDER), as well as the application of femtosecond strong lasers in strong field physics, such as: nonlinear transmission, higher harmonic generation, multi-photon ionization and suprathreshold ionization, non-sequential double (multi) ionization, molecular dissociation, and research progress in attosecond physics, etc. This course focuses on the close integration of basic knowledge and cutting-edge experimental research to expand students' academic horizons and help students become familiar with the cutting-edge research in strong field physics as soon as possible.

Name: Optoelectronic Functional Materials
Introduction: It mainly introduces the basic knowledge and research progress of physical functional materials, especially the optoelectronic functional materials that have attracted widespread attention at home and abroad. Combining the perspectives of chemistry, condensed matter physics and materials science, it introduces materials with special optical, electrical, magnetic, thermal, acoustic and other properties that are widely used in the current high-tech fields. , including an overview of functional materials, electrical functional materials such as conductive materials, semiconductor materials, dielectric materials, ferroelectric materials, and superconducting materials, optical functional materials such as nonlinear optical materials, luminescent materials, photonic crystals, organic lasers, and supramolecular systems, photoelectric and other conversion materials, and photoelectric functional films and devices.

Name: Introduction to Analytic Philosophy
Introduction:
This course is primarily intended for undergraduate students who are not majoring in philosophy. The purpose is to enable non-philosophy majors to master the basic thinking methods of analytical philosophy and methods of researching problems. Understanding the methods of analytical philosophy will be beneficial for students in science, engineering or liberal arts, and will help learners master more rigorous ways of thinking. Through this course, students will have a preliminary understanding of a modern philosophical research style that is mainly in British and American countries and is now beginning to receive attention in continental Europe, and understand the fundamental issues it raises. _x000D_
This course is divided into three parts. The first part tells the history, origin and current situation of British and American analytic philosophy. The second part deals with basic problems in the philosophy of language and some popular solutions to the basic problems. Among them, there are mainly description theory of reference, causal theory of reference, behaviorism theory and usage theory of meaning, semantic analysis of context-sensitive expressions, the separation between semantic and pragmatic theory, etc. The third part gives a general introduction to several of the most concerning issues in analytic metaphysics in a summary way, including truth-maker theory, realism and anti-realism disputes between abstract objects and other objects, etc. For each topic, the core issues and the pros and cons of important solutions are pointed out to help interested students think further. _x000D_

Name: Observational Astrophysics I (Optical and Infrared)
Introduction: The course presents basic observation equipment used for optical and infrared astrophysics observations, observation methods and treatment of observational data.

Name: Observational Astrophysics II (High-Energy and Radio)
Prerequisite: Basic astronomical, astrophysics, astronomical technology and methods I
Introduction: With the advancement of technology, astrophysical observations have expanded from visible light to all electromagnetic bands. This course introduces the basic concepts, principles and methods of astrophysical observations in radio and high-energy bands based on "Astronomical Technology and Methods I".

Name: Applications of Networks and Big Data
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, university English, programming (MATLAB or Python)
Introduction: This course aims to learn network and signal processing technologies related to big data applications, that is, a series of computing and analysis techniques used to understand and interpret big data information. This course focuses on various big data theories and technologies (machine learning, networks, energy systems), and their practical applications in industry. The first goal of this course is to introduce the big data technology paradigm, the second goal is to comprehensively learn and master the key technologies of big data processing, and the third goal is to understand cutting-edge big data applications.

Name: Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design Seminar
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Signals and Systems (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics (or mathematical analysis), linear algebra
Introduction:
