"Signals and Systems" is a core basic course for communication and signal processing majors. The concepts of signals and systems involved in the course, as well as the analysis methods related to these concepts, are widely used in many fields such as communications, aerospace, circuit design, signal and information processing, etc. _x000D_
The content of the course covers basic concepts and analysis methods of signals, systems and control theory, including continuous-time and discrete-time signals and systems, time domain analysis, frequency domain analysis, s-domain analysis and Z-transform, sampling, communication systems, random signal analysis, linear feedback systems, and state space analysis. Through course study, students can lay a solid foundation in signals and systems, gain a broad understanding of their applications in filtering, sampling, communication, feedback systems, etc., and prepare themselves for studying related courses in the future. The course comprehensively uses a variety of teaching methods to train students' abilities in analyzing and solving problems, information search, independent learning, independent thinking, etc., and cultivate students' scientific thinking and innovative spirit. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Xi Jinping Thought on Socialism with Chinese Characteristics for a New Era
Introduction: Since the 18th Congress of the Party, the Communist Party of China, represented mainly by Xi Jinping, has taken on a great deal of political courage and strong responsibility, proposing a new set of new ideas and a new strategy of new ideas that, in combination of theory and practice, have systematically answered the major issues of the new era, namely, the maintenance and development of China-specific socialism, and the creation of China-specific socialism in the new era. The socialist ideology of Xi's new era of China is rich in economics, politics, the rule of law, science and technology, culture, education, people's lives, ethnicity, religion, society, ecological civilization, national security, national defence and military forces, “one country, two systems” and the reunification of the motherland, a united front, diplomacy and party-building, and constitutes a systematic, logical and coherent system of theory. The course seeks to provide a comprehensive and systematic account of Xi's Chinese-style socialist thinking in the new era, to help university students master the latest results of Marxist Chineseization, to learn to use Marxist positions, perspectives and methods to analyse domestic and foreign events, to upgrade their theoretical abilities and intellectual abilities and to become a good student at the height of the new era.

Name: Digital Logic Circuits (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Circuit analysis or simulation of electronic lines
Introduction:
Digitalization is the main development trend of the rapidly changing information technology and information industry, among which the key technology SOC (System On Chip) plays an important role in various electronic system applications such as communication equipment, smartphones, smart TVs and Internet of Things systems. The "Digital Logic Circuit" course is an important basic circuit theory course for science and engineering students in colleges and universities. It is currently a national quality course. Peking University is listed as a backbone basic course for undergraduates. It is a "seminar-based small class teaching" course for undergraduates piloted by the school. It is offered to second-year undergraduate students in the electronics major of the School of Information Science and Technology. It has 4 hours per week, including 3 hours of large class teaching and 1 hour of small class discussion, with 4 credits. _x000D_
In this course, on the basis of learning and mastering the theory of SOC digital systems, students will master the analysis methods and design methods of digital logic circuits, become familiar with the functions and usage of various devices that make up digital systems, including SSI, MSI, MEMORY, AD/DA, and FPGA devices, and finally master the design methods of digital systems. _x000D_
The final course project requires two people to team up to complete a digital system design on a self-selected topic. The course provides each group of students with a "MagicFPGA" or "BASYS2" digital system design and development board, which can demonstrate the functions of the digital products implemented by the group, such as multi-functional electronic clocks, game consoles, microprocessors, etc. After completing this course, students should have the ability to independently complete the design of medium-scale digital systems and can participate in the front-end design of SOC chips. _x000D_
This course focuses on the basic principles of digital logic circuits, analysis methods and design methods of digital systems. Allow students to apply the principles and methods they have learned to understand and recognize common circuits, and cultivate students' independent thinking ability, scientific thinking methods and knowledge-seeking and innovative spirit. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Basic Electronics Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Electronic circuit analysis and design (or circuit analysis + electronic circuit/simulation electronic technology), digital logic circuits, electromagnetics (or physics in information science)
Introduction:
This course is the first experimental course for electrical majors and is the basis for subsequent electrical experimental courses. This course is a core professional course for undergraduate students in the Department of Electronics. Among the electrical courses that students in the electronics department need to master, introduction to information science and technology, basics of microelectronics and circuits, and basic training of electronic systems are introductory in nature, and students can only understand the knowledge of electronics. Electronic circuit analysis and design, digital logic circuits, and basic electronics experiments are the basic courses for students’ electronics professional training. Among them, the content of basic electronics experimental design covers two theoretical courses. The course covers analog circuits, digital circuits and analog-digital hybrid circuits, and is an experiment in basic electronics knowledge. _x000D_
The experiment focuses on cultivating students' abilities, integrating the knowledge they have learned, and cultivating problem-solving and problem-finding abilities. At the knowledge level, we focus on the in-depth study of basic knowledge and the application of knowledge. _x000D_

Name: Microprocessors and Interface Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Calculating General A, Digital Logic Circuit
Introduction: Microprocessor and Interface Technology is a professional basic course for electronics and computer majors. The main content of the course includes: the programming structure, working mode, bus interface and I/O and memory organization of 80X86 series microprocessors and ARM series microprocessors; the composition, working principle and interface design of computer hierarchical storage systems; the functions, composition and transmission methods of I/O interfaces; buses and common bus standards. The main goal of the course is to cultivate students' application abilities, emphasizing the mastery of basic knowledge and basic technologies, as well as methods of analyzing and solving problems. On the basis of traditional content, it strives to reflect the new technologies of microcomputers and microprocessors, so that students can comprehensively and systematically understand the basic composition, working principles and operation methods of computer systems.

Name: Fundamentals of the Internet of Things
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Electronic circuits, digital logical circuits, signals and systems
Introduction:
The Internet of Things is the Internet between things. It is a communication network based on automated multiple information collection, efficient information transmission, and intelligent information processing and network management. The rise and development of the Internet of Things is another landmark development in the field of information technology after personal computers, the Internet and mobile communications. _x000D_
Internet of Things technology involves almost every field of information technology. The main content of the course includes Internet of Things concepts and system architecture, basic principles of computer networks and communication networks, wireless access technology, intelligent information processing technology, typical applications of Internet of Things, and the latest developments. _x000D_
This course takes the Internet as the main line, focuses on the basic knowledge and basic principles of the Internet of Things, and provides a comprehensive introduction to its key technologies, typical applications, evolution and development trends. Through this course, students can have a comprehensive understanding of the basic principles of computer networks, communication networks and the Internet of Things, understand the key technical principles of the Internet of Things, understand some new developments in the current field of information technology, and further broaden their horizons and inspire the spirit of innovation. _x000D_

Name: Principles of Communications (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of mathematical and signalling systems is sufficient, and it is best to fix signals and systems first, but not necessarily.
Introduction: Unlike the traditional course on the principles of communication, this course focuses on the fundamentals of communication from the perspective of the physical concept and further elaborates on the practical uses of specific technologies in the course, taking into account the practical applications that are common in our lives. Based on the above basic logic, the course focuses on the fundamentals of communication, including analogue and digital communications, and provides detailed lectures on such technologies as carrier-modulation techniques in analogue communications, modular conversion programmes in digital communications, basic concepts and models of communication channels, and information transmission programmes in digital communications. Through this course, students will learn about the basics and principles of communication and the image of basic and important knowledge points and technologies in communication, as well as the role of these technologies in the actual communication system, and, more importantly, the functionality and effectiveness of the core communication modules of the course will be felt through simple programming.

Name: Fundamentals of Information and Coding Theory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Probability statistics, linear algebras, digital logic circuits
Introduction: "Basics of Information Theory and Coding Theory" is a professional course for senior undergraduate students majoring in electronic engineering. This course is one of the basic communication courses. Studying this course will help students master the nature of communication and understand the principles and principles of communication system design and signal processing technology. Course content includes: information measurement methods, principles of information compression and distortion-free transmission, capacity under typical channels, source compression coding technology, channel coding technology, etc. The first half of the course mainly introduces the basic concepts and important theorems of information theory, and illustrates Shannon's basic ideas for solving communication problems through simple and intuitive examples. The course focuses on cultivating the way of thinking about problems, introducing problem-solving ideas and establishing physical images of communication systems. It does not have high requirements for strict mathematical derivation and proof. The second half of the course introduces basic channel coding techniques, including linear block codes, cyclic codes, and convolutional codes. The introduction of these coding techniques will help students further understand communication theory in information theory. In addition, the course will also analyze some typical communication systems from the perspectives of information theory and coding. Taking some of the more common technologies used in actual communication systems as examples, they are explained and illustrated from the perspective of information theory. This course requires students to have knowledge of probability statistics, linear algebra and digital logic circuits.

Name: Intelligent Electronic System Design and Practice
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Simulation of circuits, digital logic circuits, micromechanical principles and interfaces
Introduction:
As a required course at the research and innovation level in the electronic information science and engineering curriculum system, this course aims to cultivate students' comprehensive, research and experimental abilities and innovative awareness. It requires students to comprehensively use the theoretical knowledge and experimental skills they have learned to work in teams of three to realize a complete intelligent electronic system. The work usually includes a It consists of two parts: intelligent hardware prototype hardware with intelligent interconnection capabilities and intelligent perception capabilities, and a mobile phone or cloud application software with intelligent cognitive signal processing capabilities, thereby providing innovative solutions to various practical problems in reality, or providing new technology demonstration prototypes for leading future information industry applications. _x000D_
      This course uses a combination of classroom and experimental teaching, with open experimental teaching as the main teaching method. The course adopts a project-driven design experiment format, requiring three people to form a team and work together to complete an intelligent hardware project. Experimental questions are issued to students in the form of task sheets. During the implementation of the course, there are four checkpoints. Students take the initiative, and teachers only play the role of supervision, inspection, and answering questions. After students have gone through the overall scheme design, detailed system design, PCB design and production, unit circuit welding and debugging, system joint debugging, and system testing, the project will finally pass the defense acceptance. _x000D_
      The course provides certain financial support for each group's project, which is used by the students in the group themselves. In the smart hardware DIY section, each student must independently complete the DIY production of smart hardware examples of the "Smart Pomodoro Alarm Clock" and will receive this Pomodoro Alarm Clock as a souvenir of the course. At the same time, the Pomodoro Alarm Clock can also be used as an extracurricular smart hardware development platform for future students. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Introduction to Mobile Graphics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Graphics technology is an important part of computer science major. In real life, this technology is widely used in game design, computer graphics interface and data visualization. Since smartphones have become increasingly popular, graphics technology has also gained widespread support in mobile devices. Even mobile device user interfaces (UIs) are increasingly using the latest graphics technology to improve the user experience. As embedded application developers, they must not only master relevant graphics technology knowledge, but also must understand the specific limitations of mobile devices and their special programming methods. _x000D_
The main content of this course includes mobile device-based graphics technology, graphics processor (GPU) architecture and how to use OpenGL ES and OpenGL GLSL for graphics rendering. The software development kit (SDK) based on PowerVR is introduced in the course content, and the experimental platform is a microcomputer and Raspberry Pi. Students can either complete the design of graphics programs on a microcomputer or implement similar programs on embedded hardware platforms. _x000D_

Name: Radio Astronomy
Introduction:
Radio astronomy is a classic basic course in astronomy. The radio band is an important observation window in astronomy, and radio astronomy is used in almost all types of astrophysical phenomena. In recent years, with the stable operation of large millimeter/submillimeter wave interferometers such as ALMA, high-resolution radio astronomy observations have brought revolutionary progress to many fields. In today's era of multi-messenger astronomy, astronomy researchers, whether they focus on observation or theory, need to master the basic principles of radio astronomy in order to better understand the rapidly developing frontier progress, and then design and develop their own research topics. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is taught to graduate students and senior undergraduate students in astrophysics or related majors. This course fully considers the astronomical knowledge background of the students who choose the course. The teaching content is from the shallower to the deeper, starting from the basic concepts of radio astronomy. Through classroom lectures and extracurricular homework, you will gradually master the observation methods and related data analysis methods, and finally be able to design radio astronomy observations for research topics.

Name: Biomacromolecular Engineering
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: Biological macromolecules play a very important role in maintaining life systems. This involves the realization of multiple functions and the regulation of complex networks. Its molecular mechanism is extremely interesting and can be applied to the artificial design of nano-assembly systems and biological functional materials. This course is a basic elective course for senior undergraduates and graduate students. It is taught to students with a certain foundation in biochemistry. The content mainly focuses on understanding biological macromolecules from the perspective of traditional polymers, introducing in detail the influence of sequence, length, stereochemistry and topology on their assembly and function. For the four most common biological macromolecules, DNA, RNA, proteins and polysaccharides, the chemical modification and engineering strategies are discussed. By studying classic cases in the literature, we understand how to regulate and assemble biological macromolecules into functional materials. Finally, we give a brief introduction to complex assembly systems composed of a variety of biological macromolecules. The purpose of this course is to help students appreciate the beauty and mystery of biological macromolecular systems, have a clear understanding of various strategies and methods of biological macromolecular engineering, and be able to initially apply several of these strategies to design and construct functional assembly systems. The course materials strive to start from the basics of polymer chemistry and physics, and demonstrate the unique features of biological macromolecules through classic literature cases. This course is mainly based on classroom teaching, combined with invited lectures, design practice, laboratory visits and other activities, integrating theory with practice, leaving students with concrete knowledge. Grading for this course is based on homework, project design, and exams.

Name: Principles of Urban Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
"Urban planning", also known as "urban and rural planning" in my country recently, is a composite discipline that studies the coordinated development of urban and rural space, economic society, and ecological environment. It mainly studies urbanization and regional spatial structure, urban and rural spatial layout, urban and rural social services and public management, and the planning and design of the physical form of urban and rural construction. Urban and rural planning promotes the coordinated development of the country's economy, society, population, resources, and environment through the rational allocation and control of urban and rural spatial resources, and ensures social safety, health, fairness, and efficiency. _x000D_
This course is the core course of urban and rural planning major. The course content mainly includes the history and theory of urban and rural planning at home and abroad, urban land use planning, transportation planning, green space planning, community planning, and new era land and space planning. The course is mainly based on classroom lectures, combined with teaching methods such as literature reading, discussion, and classroom report. Through course study, students will have a comprehensive understanding of the history and theory of urban development and urban planning, as well as the core content and practice of urban and rural planning. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Cartography and GIS
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Maps express geoscience research results in the form of diagrams, so they are called the second language of geography. Geographic information systems are an extension of cartography. They use information technology to store, analyze, and display geographic information. They are also called the third language of geography. Therefore, cartography and geographical information systems are basic courses that must be mastered by all majors in geography. _x000D_
Fundamentals of Cartography and Geographic Information Systems is a new compulsory course for physical geography majors. The main teaching purposes are: (1) To train students to comprehensively master the basic knowledge of cartography and Geographic Information Systems, GIS data models and data structures, spatial data processing and editing, spatial analysis methods, and GIS cartography principles; (2) To train students Educate students to master the basic functions of commonly used GIS software, so that students can skillfully use GIS mapping, an important tool for geoscience research; (3) Cultivate students' ability to integrate theory with practice, and be able to comprehensively apply cartography and GIS principles and methods, and skillfully operate GIS software to carry out mapping, spatial analysis, etc., to solve actual geographical spatial problems. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (Earth System Science)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The Earth is the only planet known so far to sustain life. It has been a dynamic power system since its formation. Energy from the interior of the Earth and solar radiation maintain the continuous operation of this power system. The Earth is a system composed of the outer circle (atmosphere, hydrosphere, biosphere) and the inner circle (lithosphere, asthenosphere, mesosphere and core). The movement of matter in each sphere and the physical, chemical, and biological interactions between the spheres led to various geological processes, the birth of life, and the creation of the present earth. This course will be based on the idea of ​​systems theory and is divided into five modules, namely "Overview of the Earth System", "Subsystems of the Earth", "Vibrant Earth", "Historical Earth" and "Research Methods of Earth Systems". It will describe the basic concepts and main geological processes of the Earth system, especially from the perspective of the climate system and tectonic system and the interaction between the two systems, so that students can have a comprehensive scientific enlightenment on the relevant knowledge of the Earth system and lay the foundation for subsequent learning.

Name: Introduction to Earth Science (Foundations of Spatial Information Science)
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course is one of the core courses for first-year undergraduate students in the School of Earth and Space Sciences. It mainly teaches the basic theories and methods of space information science, so that students can basically understand and master the theoretical foundation, mathematical foundation, method foundation and technical foundation of space information science and technology. The course content is divided into two parts: remote sensing information science and geographic information science. While teaching the basics of science, it also deepens students' understanding of knowledge through rich application examples, and initially cultivates students' ability to analyze and solve problems using spatial information science and technology methods.

Name: Principles and Applications of Radar Remote Sensing
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Earth science overview, remote sensing overview, principles and methods for remote sensing applications
Introduction:
Microwave has the characteristics of all-weather and all-weather, can penetrate clouds, and can be used to detect underground structures. Microwave radar remote sensing and imaging have become one of the most important means of space remote sensing and earth observation technology. With the continuous improvement of spatial resolution, radar remote sensing has been widely used in resource exploration, disaster monitoring, weather forecasting, environmental monitoring, military fields, etc. This course systematically teaches the basic principles of radar remote sensing and its application in earth observation. The main contents include: the basic principles of radar remote sensing, hardware composition and calibration, radar data processing theory and methods, electromagnetic properties of typical ground objects, principles of interaction between electromagnetic waves and ground objects, radar image characteristics, radar interference principles, radar image interpretation and interpretation, and the application of radar remote sensing in earth observation. This course is aimed at senior undergraduates and requires students to have a foundation in earth science, electromagnetics, and remote sensing principles. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, students are required to master: understand the broad application prospects and latest development trends of radar remote sensing in space remote sensing and earth observation; master the basic principles and hardware composition of radar; understand the electromagnetic characteristics of typical ground objects, master the basic rules of the interaction between electromagnetic waves and ground objects; understand the radar Understand the basic theories and methods of data processing, understand the basic characteristics of radar images; understand the steps of using radar images to generate surface elevation and deformation variables; be familiar with the operating steps of radar image processing software; be able to perform basic interpretation of radar images, and master the basic methods of acquiring radar image information. _x000D_
After completing this course, students will have a solid foundation in mathematics and physics, good computer programming skills, and learn how to use radar remote sensing methods to analyze and solve specific scientific problems in earth observation. _x000D_

Name: Micromorphological Analysis of Cultural Relics Laboratory
Prerequisite: Micromorphological analysis of antiquities (selections or preliminary studies).
Introduction:
Microscopic observation and description of archaeological and cultural relic samples are the basis for cultural relic protection and scientific and technological archaeological research. Various microscopic observation methods, sample preparation methods, and typical structures of common sample materials are the basic skills that workers in this field should possess. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course teaches the principles, structure and usage of biological microscopes and polarizing microscopes through experimental operations, as well as basic microscopic sample preparation methods such as freehand sectioning, embedded sectioning, smearing, and grinding. Combined with the content of theoretical courses, the most common categories of diatoms, sporopollen, phytoliths, wood, fibers, pigments, rocks, ceramics, etc. in archaeological and cultural relic samples are selected to teach their typical microscopic morphology and key points of observation and description. The open research experiment part of the course focuses on cultivating students' ability to apply microscopic analysis methods to solve practical archaeological problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
    This course is suitable for first-year undergraduates majoring in cultural relics protection in the School of Archeology and Museology, as well as undergraduates of any grade in other majors. _x000D_

Name: Post-Translational Modification of Proteins and Its Regulatory Functions
Prerequisite: If you've studied biochemistry or molecular biology before, it will help to understand the course.
Introduction: Protein post-translational modifications play an important role in the regulatory functions of proteins. Modifications that occur on amino acid side chains include phosphorylation, glycosylation, methylation, acetylation, ubiquitination, ubiquitination, fatty acidation, etc. Understanding the types, principles of action and regulatory effects of these modifications can help us gain a deeper understanding of the biological functions of the proteins under study. In this course, we will systematically introduce the types of common protein modifications, such as phosphorylation, glycosylation, methylation, ubiquitination and other modifications, the principles of various modifications, and the roles they play in physiological processes such as important cell signaling pathways, DNA damage repair, and tumor development. Specific experiments on some modification methods will also be explained. It enables students to not only understand the principles of protein modification, but also helps them choose specific experiments to solve scientific problems in future experiments. This course will be helpful not only for students majoring in biochemistry, but also for students in other experimental disciplines.

Name: Archaeological Chemistry
Prerequisite: Science and technology archaeology, metallurgical archaeology
Introduction:
The course is divided into two stages. The first stage teaches the history of ancient chemistry, including an overview and general introduction to the history of chemistry, as well as the origins of alchemy and chemistry, a brief history of the development of metallurgy, a brief history of ceramic technology, a brief history of glass technology, etc. The purpose is to let students understand the development process of ancient chemistry, so as to have a basic understanding of the performance, history and age of appearance of relevant cultural relic production technologies in archaeological research. _x000D_
The second part teaches the application of chemical analysis techniques in archaeology and the processing methods and interpretation of related data. Through this part of the teaching, students will be able to understand the main chemical analysis techniques that can be applied in archaeological research, and provide a detailed interpretation of the data obtained by commonly used chemical analysis techniques in the form of cases. It is hoped that through the study of the course, in future archaeological research, they will be able to master what analytical techniques can be used to analyze different types of cultural relics, and what the archaeological significance of the obtained data is.

Name: Software Engineering (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Software engineering covers the entire process of software development. Students must first have good basic knowledge and skills in software development. Prerequisite courses include introduction to computing, programming internship, data structure and algorithm
Introduction:
This course covers the following:_x000D_
1) Taking the software life cycle as the main line, systematically teach the essence of software, basic ideas and mainstream methods of software engineering. _x000D_
2) Adopt a new generation of information technology, face emerging application models, and guide students to develop medium-sized new software systems in a team-based manner according to the typical software development organizational model, and apply software engineering principles, methods, technologies and tools for software development, management and maintenance. _x000D_
3) Help students to understand, initially master and apply problem-driven software engineering knowledge through project internships, improve creative thinking and innovation capabilities, and cultivate basic software engineering qualities and practical abilities.

Name: Intermediate Macroeconomics Problem Session
Introduction: Emphasis is placed on mastering contemporary macroeconomic analysis tools. Discuss issues related to China's macroeconomic policies and current situation. Including the determination of national income, output, employment and price levels, it also discusses economic models such as neoclassical, Keynesian, and monetarist, and requires a basic knowledge of calculus. The topics discussed will mainly include: economic growth, business fluctuations, inflation, and the interaction between the real and monetary aspects, etc. _x000D_

Name: Mathematical Economics
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra, probability theory, economics principles
Introduction: This course is mainly devoted to the development of the mathematical base of modern economics. The main tasks are: 1. Introductory factual basis and static optimization; 2. Dynamic optimization between continuous and discrete; 3. Numerical methods and calculation theory. The course will build the capacity of students to interpret and quantify and lay the methodological foundation for their future research.

Name: Advanced Microeconomics (I)
Prerequisite: Undergraduate calculus sequence and linear algebra
Introduction: This course teaches advanced microeconomics and broadens and deepens the content of intermediate microeconomics. Students are required to systematically and deeply master the theoretical system of microeconomics at a high level, understand the latest developments in the subject, and master corresponding mathematical analysis methods.

Name: Advanced Econometrics (I)
Prerequisite: Calculus, linear algebra and mathematical statistics
Introduction: Ecometeorology is an important branch in the field of economics; it is a compulsory basic course for doctoral students at the Faculty of Economics; it presents empirical methods and basic theories for studying the relationship between real economic variables and analysing real economic structures from the perspective of economic measurement. The purpose of this course is to guide the student system in empirical analysis and research of the underlying principles and methods of the real economy, in the scientific and artistic nature of research into the real economy, in the measurement processes and methods of empirical research into the real economy, and in the initial development of the capability to observe and analyse real economic phenomena.

Name: Applied Econometrics
Prerequisite: Pre-course requirements: introduction to econometric or similar level.
Introduction: Applied econometrics is an important branch of modern economics. It takes real economic problems as its research object, relies on mathematical statistics as its method, and pays attention to the summary of empirical data analysis rules. As a compulsory course for undergraduates majoring in economics, this course will systematically introduce the theoretical framework and basic methods of applied econometrics. It will also focus on the training of computer operation skills and the study and discussion of classic literature, with a view to cultivating students' practical application ability of relevant models and empirical analysis ability of real economic problems. Course content arrangement: linear and nonlinear least squares estimation methods, maximum likelihood estimation, time series and panel data models, limited dependent variable models (including discrete choice models, intercepted and tailed data models, count data models), endogeneity and instrumental variable estimation, simultaneous equation models, non-parametric and semi-parametric estimation methods, etc. _x000D_

Name: Archaeometry
Introduction: Teach the application of modern science and technology in archaeology, including various chronological methods, physical and chemical analysis methods applied to the study of cultural relic materials, production techniques and the origin of cultural relics, and new developments in biotechnology in the field of archaeological research. Pay attention to the cutting-edge trends of the subject, constantly add the latest research results into the teaching content, broaden students' horizons, and improve students' scientific literacy.

Name: Natural Product Chemistry
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Prerequisite: Common chemistry, analytical chemistry, organic chemistry, spectrum analysis
Introduction: Natural drug chemistry is a subject of theoretical and methodological research on natural drug active ingredients, such as applied modernity, biology, spectrometry, and is a compulsory subject of Pharmacology and related specialization at the Faculty of Medicine. Theoretical courses focus on the chemical structural characteristics of various natural products in natural resources, such as plants, micro-organisms and animals, biosynthesis pathways and the physico-chemical properties determined by their structural characteristics. On the basis of an analysis of the physico-chemical properties of the various components, the methods of extraction, purification and separation of the various components, as well as their main spectrum characteristics and biological activity, are presented. Through the study of this subject, students are equipped with the theoretical knowledge and skills necessary to study the chemical composition of natural drugs, laying the foundation for their future research in areas related to natural pharmaceutical chemistry.

Name: Pharmaceutical Affairs Law
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: "Pharmaceutical Law" uses the basic principles and methods of law, management, economics, and behavioral science to study various pharmaceutical practice activities, starting from ensuring the safety and effectiveness of drug quality, summarizing the laws of pharmaceutical supervision and management, and promoting the standardization, scientificity, and international development of pharmaceutical management. The main line of the course is legal supervision and quality assurance. The core content of the course is China's current pharmaceutical laws, regulations and administrative regulations. Through the study of this course, students should master the current Chinese pharmaceutical law system and the basic contents of important pharmaceutical laws, regulations and rules, become familiar with the relevant systems in pharmaceutical R&D, production, and operation, and truly establish the concept of administering drugs and operating operations in accordance with the law.

Name: Pharmacology
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Pharmacology: It is a discipline that studies the interaction between drugs and the body and provides basic theories for the rational use of drugs in clinical practice to prevent and treat diseases. It has extensive and close connections with basic medicine and clinical medicine, and is an important course in medical education. The main contents include general introduction to pharmacology, pharmacology of the efferent nervous system, pharmacology of the central nervous system, pharmacology of the cardiovascular system, pharmacology of the visceral system, pharmacology of the endocrine system, chemotherapeutic drugs and others. Through the study of pharmacology, students can understand the functions and principles of drugs and how to fully exert their clinical efficacy and reduce their adverse reactions.

Name: Modern Pharmaceutics
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Prerequisite: Analysis of chemistry, organic chemistry, physical chemistry
Introduction:
"Modern Pharmacy" is a required professional course for pharmacy majors. It is a comprehensive applied science that studies the formulation theory, production technology, quality control and rational application of pharmaceutical dosage forms. The basic task of this course is to enable students to master basic theoretical knowledge and basic skills such as dosage forms, preparation design, preparation and quality control, etc., so as to lay a foundation for engaging in the preparation and production of pharmaceutical preparations and the research and development of new dosage forms. The lecture uses the new edition of "Modern Pharmacy" by Peking University Medical Press as the basic textbook, and appropriately introduces some reference books. The teaching content is divided into two parts. The first part focuses on modern pharmaceutical dosage forms, including liquid preparations, sterilization and aseptic preparations, solid preparations, preparations for skin and mucous membranes, biological preparations, traditional Chinese medicine preparations, pharmaceutical preparation design, and drug stability; the second part talks about new dosage forms and new technologies, including solid dispersion technology, inclusion technology, emulsification technology, microencapsulation technology, nanotechnology, liposomes, sustained release and controlled release technology, targeted drug delivery technology, transdermal absorption technology, etc. During the teaching process, the teaching content can be updated in a timely manner based on the cutting edge of the subject. _x000D_
Classroom teaching adopts heuristic teaching, paying attention to introducing professional English vocabulary, assigning necessary thinking questions, and answering questions regularly. When giving lectures, we should not only focus on highlighting the key points, but also pay attention to expanding students' knowledge. Pay attention to cultivating students' self-learning ability and scientific thinking methods, and continuously improve their ability to analyze and solve problems. _x000D_
Pharmacy is a highly practical subject. While studying theory, we must focus on cultivating students' practical basic operational skills and improve students' ability to analyze problems, solve problems and work independently in practice. Theoretical courses are 54 hours and 3 credits. _x000D_

Name: Pharmaceutics Laboratory
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Pharmacy is an applied technical discipline with certain technological nature. Therefore, experimental classes are an important part of the entire teaching process. In the experiment, students are required to master the basic operations and experimental skills of various dosage forms through the preparation of typical dosage forms and commonly used preparations, laying a foundation for future hospital pharmacy work and the creation of new varieties, new processes, and new dosage forms. At the same time, because the quality of pharmaceutical preparation is directly related to the safety and effectiveness of medication, in experiments, students must be cultivated to pay attention to the quality of products.

Name: Theory and Applications of Modern Biotechnology
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Modern Biotechnology Theory and Application is a course that mainly introduces modern biotechnology. It teaches how to research and develop drugs through molecular biology and cell biology technologies such as genetic engineering, protein engineering, and cell engineering.

Name: Introduction to the Pharmaceutical Profession
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: This course aims to introduce students to the learning objectives, content, and methods of the pharmacy major; the current status, characteristics, development, research focus, and trends of various pharmaceutical disciplines at home and abroad, as well as the main literature, review methods, and academic standard requirements of each discipline, and to establish a full-discipline framework and scientific thinking methods for pharmacy.

Name: Medicinal Chemistry
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: "Medicinal Chemistry" is a compulsory professional course for pharmacy students and is included in my country's current practicing pharmacist qualification examination subjects. The teaching content of this course is formulated according to the teaching requirements of the pharmacy major (long-term study program). The teaching target is the undergraduate and master's students in the pharmacy major (long-term study program), that is, the starting point is the undergraduate level and the goal is the postgraduate level. The teaching goal of this course is to teach students the development overview of medicinal chemistry so that students can understand the subject background of medicinal chemistry and its importance in the field of pharmaceutical research and application; by learning the structural types and development of important drugs, learn the relationship between drug structure, properties, metabolism and action, and understand drug effects from a chemical perspective and molecular level; by learning the discovery methods and optimization principles of lead structures, master drug design The basic principles and methods of drug action; by learning the physical and chemical principles of drug action, receptor theory, and the action of chiral drugs, students can understand the principles of drug action and their structure-activity relationships from the molecular level; by learning computer-aided drug design, combinatorial chemistry, and high-throughput screening technology, they can understand the cutting-edge technologies and methods of modern drug design, so that students can initially acquire the basic ideas and innovative abilities to engage in new drug research and development. This course also involves the physical and chemical properties and synthesis methods of drugs, laying a foundation for students to engage in the production, storage, circulation, and use of drugs in the future.

Name: Pharmaceutical Analysis
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Prerequisite: General chemistry (B and above), general chemistry (B and above), analytical chemistry (B and above), analytical chemistry (B and above), organic chemistry (the Academy of Pharmacy offers courses or courses B and above).
Introduction: Drug analysis is an integrated subject in the field of pharmacological science and is the main subject of specialization in pharmacology in accordance with our own national circumstances. In order to ensure the safety, soundness and effectiveness of people ' s use of medicines, rigorous scientific management systems should be implemented in the development, production, supply and clinical use of drugs, and rigorous analytical testing of drugs should be carried out using effective analytical methods, so as to ensure, control and research on all aspects of improving the quality of medicines and achieving comprehensive quality control of medicines. It is a methodological discipline for research and development of drug quality control, using primarily chemical, physico-chemical or biochemical methods and techniques to study quality control methods for synthetic or natural drugs and their formulations that have been identified in chemical structures, as well as for some representative Chinese and biological and chemical formulations and their formulations. The task of the drug analysis discipline is not only static routine testing, but also deep into dynamic analytical studies of process processes, response history, bio-behavioural metabolic processes and integrated evaluation. The analytical methods used should be more sensitive, exclusive, accurate and rapid, moving towards automated, miniaturized, optimized and intelligent approaches.

Name: Pharmaceutical Analysis Laboratory
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Prerequisite: Common chemical experiments, instrument analysis experiments, organic chemistry (or pharmaceutical chemistry)
Introduction: “Drug analysis”, an application discipline that combines effective analytical methods and techniques to study and explore general patterns of quality control of synthetic or natural drugs and their formulations, is one of the important specialized courses in the field of pharmacology. “Drug Analysis Experiment” is an important component of drug analysis teaching, both as a strong complement to the theoretical curriculum and as a relatively independent one. The primary purpose of the drug analysis experiment is to enable the students involved in the experiment to consolidate basic knowledge, strengthen basic skills training and improve hands-on skills. Through the study of experimental subjects, the concept of the quality of medicines is further developed on the basis of theoretical courses, the mastery of basic principles, analytical methods and experimental skills for sample processing, identification, impurity examination and concentration determination, as well as the proper use of commonly used analytical instruments, the development of sound scientific attitudes and the ability to conduct independent analyses and obtain accurate analyses, and the initial ability to establish analytical methods based on the physico-chemical nature of the drug, providing a good basis for future work.

Name: Pharmacotherapy
College: Teaching Affairs Office, Health Science Center
Introduction: Pharmacotherapeutics is a course about the drug treatment of disease. Its main content includes clinical knowledge such as disease concepts, epidemiology, pathogenesis, diagnostic standards, clinical manifestations, and drug treatment knowledge of the disease. Knowledge of drug treatment of diseases is the key content. Drug treatment knowledge mainly includes the types of disease treatment drugs, mechanism of action, pharmacokinetics, adverse reactions, interactions, precautions, drug evaluation, rational drug selection, etc. Topics include drug treatment of respiratory diseases, cardiovascular diseases, endocrine system, gastrointestinal system, neuropsychiatric diseases, immune system and other diseases. Since pharmacotherapeutics is a course that is closely integrated with clinical practice and will develop with the development of clinical disciplines, this course will reflect the latest advances in clinical drug therapy.

Name: General Biology
Introduction: Teaching orientation: systematically and comprehensively introduce basic knowledge and principles of biology. The content covers viruses, microorganisms, algae, land plants, protozoa, metazoa, ecology, evolutionary biology and biological conservation, etc. This course is taught to students majoring in life sciences. It aims to cultivate students' understanding of the overall system and logic of the biological field, understanding of the evolutionary relationships and characteristics of various biological categories, and an in-depth understanding of the relationship between organisms and the environment. The purpose is to guide students to establish correct values ​​​​between humans and nature within the larger framework of the living world.

Name: General Ecology
Introduction:
Ecology was once coined by German scientist Ernst Haeckel (1834–1919). The word is derived from Greek, eco means house and residence, and logy means knowledge and research. Ecology is the science that studies the relationships between organisms and between organisms and their environment. _x000D_
_x000D_
Ecology has complex and detailed sub-disciplines. In the general ecology course, the main focus is on:_x000D_
-Individual ecology, that is, how animals adapt to their physical environment_x000D_
- Population ecology, i.e. the abundance, distribution and population dynamics of animals_x000D_
- Community ecology, intraspecific clock relationships, community composition and succession_x000D_
- Ecosystem ecology, the study of energy flows and material cycles in ecosystems. _x000D_
_x000D_
Ecology is now more than the multidisciplinary study of life. As the human population develops and expands, occupying most areas on the earth, encroaching on the habitats of wild animals, and consuming a considerable proportion of annual primary production, how organisms survive in the shadow of humans and the impact of humans on various ecosystems have become hot topics studied by ecologists. _x000D_

Name: Molecular Virology
Introduction: The course is divided into three parts. The first part mainly introduces the concept, classification, structure and transmission of virology; the second part mainly introduces the typical representatives of each type of virus, mainly introduces the content of molecular biology, covering genome structure, encoded protein function, and the interaction between viruses and hosts at the gene and protein levels; the third part mainly introduces the diseases caused by viruses, as well as the epidemic and control of viral diseases, especially the use of modern biological technology.

Name: Protein Chemistry
Prerequisite: Organic chemistry, biochemistry and molecular organisms Learn.
Introduction:
The focus is on the structure and functions of proteins. The structure levels that include proteins are: first-level structure, second-level structure, third-level structure, characteristics of the fourth-level structure, method of structural determination and relationship to physiological function. Research advances in protein chemistry and key techniques for separation purity and determination are also taught.
The main problems encountered in research such as life sciences and medicine are: first-degree sequence identification of proteins, post-translation modifications, dynamics, regulatory networks? And make up all the proteins and functions of the organism? Opportunities and challenges of proteomics research: from basic scientific research to disease prevention treatment, improvement of quality of life in combination with critical needs, from new methods to functional research.

Name: Fundamentals of Biopharmaceutical Technology
Prerequisite: There is no requirement for the first course.
Introduction: This course teaches the basic knowledge related to biotechnology pharmaceuticals from the shallower to the deeper level. This course explores the application and basic strategies of producing recombinant proteins, recombinant vaccines and other bioactive proteins from the perspective of biomedicine. The content of this course includes the basic concepts of biopharmaceuticals, the research progress of biotechnological drugs and the characteristics of biotechnological drugs. Introduce the principles, development processes, mechanisms and precautions of some successful biotechnology drugs for the treatment of related diseases. Introduces the basic research methods of biotechnology drugs as well as basic knowledge and progress in some major related fields, such as the basis of animal cell pharmaceuticals, genetic engineering vaccines, and gene therapy. This course is an introductory course for students who are interested in biotechnology pharmaceuticals or want to engage in biotechnology drug-related industries in the future. It can serve as the basis for a deeper understanding of biotechnology drug-related fields.

Name: The World of Education from an Economic Perspective
Introduction:
Educational policy is an important research topic in the field of education worldwide. In the past two decades, economists from all over the world have devoted themselves to the study of education policy and made important contributions. This course aims to help students understand how economists think about the formulation, implementation and evaluation of education policies on the basis of mastering the basic principles and main analysis methods of economics, and establish a system of economic thinking and methods for analyzing education policies. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is organized in the form of special seminars. Under each topic, one or two educational policies or reform projects with important influence at home and abroad are selected, the origin and development of the policies are reviewed, classic empirical studies are analyzed, and possible solutions, evaluation plans, and development directions are discussed. Through the study of this course, students will be able to systematically understand cutting-edge research in the field of educational economics, and skillfully use economic thinking and methods to analyze and study real-life education policies, laying a certain theoretical and methodological foundation for future social science research.

Name: Programming and Algorithms
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Programming is the key to opening the door to the computer world, and the C++ language is a powerful weapon to master this key. The "Programming and Algorithms" course will help you understand the basic principles and numerous practical skills of programming using the C++ language, and teach you to write "useful programs" that can truly be used by others. _x000D_
    The course does not mechanically introduce various C++ features, but continuously refines and improves solutions to specific problems. In the process, basic programming techniques and corresponding C++ program features are naturally introduced. In order to allow beginners to learn and master basic practical programming techniques, the course introduces a large number of programming techniques for solving practical problems, and also provides a detailed introduction to program debugging and testing techniques. _x000D_
    On the basis of the above, the course also introduces basic data structures and algorithms, commonly used C++ standard libraries, and basic computer system knowledge (such as memory management, I/O mechanisms, etc.) in order to lay a good foundation for learning advanced courses in programming or becoming an intermediate to advanced programmer in the future. _x000D_

Name: Literature Writing and Reporting
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
A public elective course for lower-level undergraduate students majoring in science and engineering. _x000D_
Cultivate students' academic abilities such as reading, summarizing, writing, and reporting scientific papers, and clarify academic ethics and academic standards.

Name: Communication Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
This course is for senior undergraduates and its teaching tasks are: _x000D_
1. Master the composition of the communication system, the functions of each part, and the main performance indicators, and deepen your understanding of the communication system. _x000D_
2. Master the basic principles and design methods of communication circuits, focusing on the impact of noise and nonlinearity on system performance, modulation/demodulation principles, transmitter and receiver scheme design, the principles, functions, technical indicators and analysis and design methods of each modular circuit, such as low-noise amplifiers, mixers, oscillators, phase-locked loops, modulation/demodulation circuits, power amplifiers and regulated power supplies. _x000D_
3. Cultivate students’ independent thinking ability, scientific thinking methods and knowledge-seeking and innovative spirit. _x000D_

Name: Computer-Aided Design of Electronic Circuits
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is one of the comprehensive design-level experimental courses in electronic information. The main training goal is to learn modern electronic circuit design and measurement methods and the use of design tools based on students' mastery of circuit analysis. The purpose of the comprehensive experiment is to improve students' ability to design and test technology for circuits and systems that combine software and hardware. Students are encouraged to organize themselves into groups to complete the tasks and cultivate teamwork capabilities.

Name: Optoelectronics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Optoelectronics mainly studies the mutual conversion of optical fields and electrical fields under different conditions. Relevant research and application areas involve the generation, detection, control, interaction of light and electric fields, and the devices used. Optoelectronic devices include emitters, modulators, electro-optical converters, photoelectric converters, and instruments and equipment that rely on these devices. Micro-nano optoelectronics, which has developed rapidly in recent years, will be the focus of this course.

Name: Nanotechnology and Nanoelectronics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Teaching purposes and basic requirements _x000D_
1. Understand the background and overall development trends of nanotechnology and nanoelectronics; _x000D_
2. Master the physical laws at the nanoscale, and have a preliminary understanding of the application of quantum mechanics and solid state physics at the nanoscale; have a preliminary understanding of the basic principles and processing technologies of nanoelectronics; _x000D_
3. Be familiar with the structure and performance characteristics of carbon nanotubes and one-dimensional semiconductor nanomaterials, and understand the basic preparation technology of nanomaterials; _x000D_
4. Understand the basic principles and methods of scanning probe microscopy and electron microscopy, which are important characterization and processing technologies for nanomaterials; _x000D_
5. Understand the electrical and optical properties and measurement methods and tools of nanomaterials; be familiar with the applications of nanomaterials in devices (electronics, optoelectronics, sensing, energy and biology); _x000D_

Name: Frontiers of Cell Genetics and Development
Introduction:
In recent years, it is common for undergraduates in the field of life sciences to not understand the relevant laboratories of our school, and do not understand the cutting-edge progress in many directions such as related cell development and genetics. As a result, when they graduate, they have a lot of confusion about whether to further engage in scientific research, the direction of future scientific research, and how to engage in scientific research. Specifically, some undergraduates have many problems and difficulties in designing their graduation thesis, contacting laboratories of interest, graduation and employment. At the same time, teachers generally responded that there was a lack of a good platform to fully communicate with undergraduates and graduate students, so that students could comprehensively understand the research direction and progress of the laboratory and showcase all aspects of the laboratory's research life. _x000D_
    In order to implement and implement the guidelines for strengthening undergraduate education proposed by the Ministry of Education, improve the scientific research and learning capabilities and levels of undergraduates and postgraduates from all aspects, and further strengthen the exchanges and communication between undergraduates and postgraduates with relevant professional tutors, the tutors in the cell biology direction of our school decided to jointly offer this cutting-edge course on cell genetic development. This course is co-taught by 17 doctoral tutors in the cell biology field of the School of Life Sciences. Each teacher will introduce to the students relevant cutting-edge developments in biological sciences such as cells, genetics, and development based on their own scientific research directions and backgrounds. _x000D_
    Through the development of this course, on the one hand, we can introduce the main cutting-edge advances in cell genetics and development to undergraduate and postgraduate students in detail, which will help students find the research directions of interest faster and better, and grasp the most cutting-edge scientific research progress. At the same time, we can use this course as a platform to strengthen in-depth exchanges between cell tutors and students in the School of Biological Sciences, help students answer questions, and further promote the healthy development of students in various aspects such as learning, life, ideological education, etc. The establishment of this course is also conducive to the development of the "college system" teaching format that is being promoted by schools and colleges. It is helpful for newly admitted students to understand various laboratories and ultimately choose their favorite research direction.

Name: Death in Chinese and Western Discourse
Prerequisite: None (provided that English is required to reach university level VI or equivalent)
Introduction:
Talking about life and death_x000D_
_x000D_
The purpose of this course is to educate college students on life and death from a discourse perspective based on genres, break the tradition of language taboos about death and dying, and explore and learn how to talk about life and death in a Chinese context. The course will first introduce and discuss the concepts and changes of death in China and the West, and then select Chinese and English samples of death discourse in different functional genres, conduct text presentation, summarize and compare genre characteristics, and invite students to make practical attempts in this genre. Students will learn how to talk about life and death, and cultivate the concepts of living toward death, cherishing and loving life.

Name: Selected Topics in Systems Biology
Introduction: This course focuses on in-depth literature reading, focusing on the concepts, principles, and methods arising from the combination of theory and experiment in biology, as well as its current development trends and challenges. Each class focuses on one aspect and discusses two articles in depth. Students should carefully read the articles to be discussed before class and actively participate in discussions during class. The instructor is responsible for inspiring, leading discussions, giving appropriate lectures, and finally summarizing. Topics covered in the course include: stochasticity and noise in biological systems, hypersensitivity and synergy, robustness, image generation in development, quantitative issues in evolution, genomics and biological network analysis, synthetic biology, and understanding disease and drug interactions from the perspective of biological networks. This course is a required course for graduate students in the Center for Theoretical Biology. Graduate students and undergraduate students from other departments are welcome to take the course.

Name: Topics in Indian Studies
Introduction: India is one of the world's ancient civilizations, an important neighbor of China, and a major developing country like China. As its comprehensive national strength steadily increases, India plays an increasingly important role in the international political, economic, and cultural stages. How to comprehensively and systematically understand India is of certain significance to students with different professional backgrounds. This course will start with hot issues, combine research results from different disciplines, and introduce the history and current situation of India from different thematic perspectives, so as to help students with different professional backgrounds better understand India.

Name: Introduction to Synthetic Biology
Introduction:
The Introduction to Synthetic Biology is a general selection course for undergraduate and graduate students. Synthetic biology is an emerging cross-cutting discipline that emerges from the shift in the research paradigm of life sciences from a “read/decomposition mode” to a “writing/formulation model”, involving biology, chemistry, engineering, physics, information and computing science. Its main research component is the use of engineering principles to design and re-engineer the genetic function components of living organisms to the entire genome and to create artificial life with unique design functions.
The content of this course includes principles of modularization and standardization of biological genetic components, assembly and representation of genetic components, classical artificial gene circuits of synthetic biology, artificial re-engineering of metabolic pathways such as artemisinin, gene combinations and editing techniques, non-natural orthodox genetic systems, applications of synthetic biology in the fields of industry, agriculture, energy and medical health, safety control and ethical norms of artificial life systems, and the International Genetic Engineering Machines Competition (IGEM) project excellence.
In addition, six laboratory operating courses are organized to enable students to actually experience the manufacture of specific functional life.

Name: Liberal Arts Lecture Hall of Science
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
The Neo-Confucianism Strengthening Lecture Series is positioned to "stimulate students' research interest in basic subjects, expand their horizons, cultivate students' ability to ask questions, analyze problems and solve problems, and guide them to think rationally and contribute to society"; combined with the current requirements of the Ministry of Education to promote ideological and political courses and ideological and political construction of courses, this series of courses will also serve as an important measure for the school to implement the ideological and political construction of courses. The teaching targets are mainly first-year undergraduate freshmen under the "Strong Foundation Program". _x000D_
The course is jointly taught by eight deans including the School of Mathematical Sciences, School of Physics, School of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering, School of Life Sciences, School of Urban and Environmental Sciences, School of Earth and Space Sciences, School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences, and School of Engineering. Students will be taught classic and cutting-edge scientific issues in mathematics, physics, chemistry, life, psychology, mechanics, geography, ecology, geology and other related disciplines in easy-to-understand language. On scientific issues, the course only provides a conceptual introduction and ideological guidance on the development history and current development frontiers of the subject, focusing on stimulating students' thinking and conducting in-depth discussions. This course also demonstrates the humanistic sentiments and social concerns of Beihang natural scientists.

Name: Cell Biology
Introduction: Cells are the basic units of organismal structure and life activities. Cell biology is the science that studies the basic life activity laws of cells and is one of the basic disciplines of modern life sciences. It mainly includes the study of cell structure and function, chromatin and gene expression, cytoskeletal system, cell proliferation, differentiation, aging and apoptosis, cell signal transduction, etc. It is an important basic subject in the current development of biology. This course explains the structure and function of cells, understands the operation and rules of intracellular life activities, analyzes the major life activities of cells (proliferation, differentiation, aging, apoptosis, etc.), and discusses the important roles and mechanisms of these major life activities in biological processes. It also introduces knowledge of cell biology that is closely related to human health, and tracks the current major scientific research progress related to cell biology. _x000D_

Name: Cardiovascular Biology
Introduction: This course will not only systematically introduce the basic knowledge and latest advances in cardiovascular biology, but also focus on the connection between molecular medicine and translational medicine. The content involves physiology, cell and molecular biology, cardiovascular development, etc. Suitable for senior undergraduate, master's and doctoral students.

Name: Modern Medicine and Health Culture
Introduction:
In response to current concerns about national health, global health, and overall health issues, reflections on the reform of the medical care system, and social debates caused by evidence-based medicine, translational medicine, precision medicine, and emerging high-tech medical technologies, it examines the development of modern medicine in the 20th century and the difficulties it faces from the perspective of social and cultural history. The "Modern Medicine and Health Culture" course will focus on three issues for study and discussion: (1) A review of the causes of the eugenics movement, the contraceptive and feminist movement, the craze for alternative medicine, the rise of bioethics, the reform of the medical care system, etc., and their profound impact on social culture; (2) Across different cultural traditions, examine the social and cultural factors involved in human health promotion and disease prevention and treatment within a global framework, as well as the social construction and evolution of concepts of health and disease; (3) The rise and application of high-tech medical technologies, such as gene editing, reproductive technology, brain science and mental reshaping, have had a profound cultural impact on human society. Provide students with a rich and vivid picture of human medical and health care activities, so that students can more comprehensively understand medicine and understand the significance of changes in medical models and disease concepts. They can not only face up to the social value of modern medical technology and health care, but also maintain a critical attitude towards the mainstream culture in health care activities. _x000D_
      This course implements multimedia teaching + classroom discussion (book report). Through rich historical documents, pictures and video materials, it expands students' understanding of human health and disease issues in a multicultural background, increases students' feelings about medical culture, and improves teaching effectiveness. It provides students with a certain amount of reading of classic literature, and evaluates students through classroom reports, classroom discussions, and course papers. _x000D_
      This course aims to improve the health cultural literacy of students with non-medical backgrounds and can be taken as an elective by arts and science students who want to learn about medicine and health care. _x000D_

Name: Protein Structure Analysis
Prerequisite: Inorganic chemistry, organic chemistry, biochemistry. Students who choose courses need to bring their own computers with pre-installed coot, pymol, and chimera that can connect to the Internet and log in to the online class. Auditing is prohibited.
Introduction: Structural biology has evolved over decades, its methods and theories have matured and mass protein structure data have been produced. The analysis, understanding and use of protein structural information are skills that need to be developed by those working in areas related to life sciences. This course is offered mainly to Masters, Ph.D. students and senior undergraduate students and is optional. This course, which starts mainly with amino acid, a basic component of protein, presents basic knowledge of protein structure analysis, acquisition and analysis, as well as the use of associated structural biology software and databases. The course is an optional course for undergraduate and postgraduate students in life sciences-related professions.

Name: Aesthetic Education Practice under the Scanning Electron Microscope
Introduction: This course takes biological materials as the main observation object, scanning electron microscopy as the main technical means, and students' practice as the main learning form. Gradually go deeper into the cool and incredible structures of living things, and understand life from the outside to the inside. At the same time, in the process of learning and observation, you can experience the artistic charm of scientific research and stimulate your interest in learning. Course content includes: scanning electron microscopy technology and biological sample preparation; observation of basic structures and life histories of common plants, animals, and algae; biological image beautification processes and application examples using Photoshop; implementation of group or individual optional projects. In this process, the course strives to guide students to gradually extend their focus from the external structural characteristics of biological materials to their physiological functions and evolutionary processes, helping them understand the structure and function of organisms, the relationship between individuals and the environment, and understand and appreciate the diversity and adaptability of biological species.

Name: Modern Techniques of Animal Specimen Preparation
Prerequisite: Experiments in animal biology or general biology or other animal anatomy
Introduction:
Peking University Biological Specimen has a long history. As early as 1907, when the Imperial Academy was in the capital, the Museum Internship Department was established, and Japanese teachers were invited to teach students how to make animal and plant specimens. The course content included three items: specimen making, model making, and teaching wall charts. The merganser specimens in the collection, which were collected in Tong County, Beijing in 1908, and whose coats are still vivid, were collected and made during this period. It has trained famous zoologists Liu Chengzhao and Hu Jingfu; botanist Hao Jingsheng, and academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences Wu Zhengyi. In 2014, Peking University’s new biological herbarium (which integrates animal and plant herbaria) was established. The newly completed herbarium has a rich collection of specimens and is a unique teaching base. All animal specimens are displayed in the first-floor exhibition hall. _x000D_
Animals are the most closely related and prosperous group of animals in the world, with many species. It would be a very meaningful job if the precious animals obtained could be made into valuable biological specimens or even works of art for teaching, scientific research or popularization of science by different people.
