Its value in zoology teaching is mainly reflected in its role as an intuitive teaching tool, teaching material to ensure practical teaching, and improving students' hands-on ability by making animal specimens; its value in scientific research is mainly to provide physical evidence for the publication of new species, and to provide genetic information for research on systematic evolution, biodiversity, and endangered species protection; its value in science popularization is mainly to popularize natural science knowledge and even enlighten people's minds through visits to the herbarium. _x000D_
This course is an experimental course that integrates zoology, morphological anatomy, taxonomy and other fields in biology. It uses the newly built Peking University Biological Specimen Hall as the teaching base. It is taught by experimental teachers who have studied under the descendants of domestic specimen-making families and German museum specimen-making masters for many years and have been engaged in experimental teaching and preparation of zoology and general biology. The course content is rich and well-designed The concept integrates scientific, artistic and practical aspects. The course content covers the most important parts of animal taxidermy production, including: the use of new materials and new methods to make internationally popular fish model specimens and artistic practice; the production method of amphibian skeleton specimens; the taxidermy method of the latest domestic bird display specimens; the basic anatomy of animals and the production methods of scientific specimens. In the course, students can learn about the status of animals in nature and their brief classification characteristics, appreciation of outstanding works, methods of making animal specimens, etc. It provides students with the opportunity to go into the museum and make their own animal specimens and dissect animals. _x000D_

Name: Opera Singing and Performance
Prerequisite: Students who have chosen “sing and perform” or “sing and perform” or have a certain sound base.
Introduction:
(1) To analyse the patterns and achievements of the development of the art of the opera and explore the space for its further development in the country through the process of the development of operas and musicals.
(2) Focus on the selection of high-quality operas and musical works from both the middle and the outside, analysing the factors of success from a variety of angles, including scripts, music, performances, etc., and identifying areas to be drawn upon.
(3) Designing works to guide students in their artistic practices according to their level, and enhancing their stage practical and artistic creativity through rehearsals of Chinese operas, western operas and classics of musical plays.

Name: Immunology in Everyday Life
Prerequisite: It is recommended that General Biology be revised to provide some insight into basic biological concepts and that more information be provided on molecular biology.
Introduction: This course mainly uses some basic immunology knowledge to analyze immunology-related events and scenarios in daily life, such as blood tests, inflammation, viruses and diseases, intestinal bacteria, and cancer. While analyzing the basic processes and principles of events or scenes, you can also learn immunological knowledge. Through the study of this course, it is hoped that students can master the basic principles of immunology and apply relevant knowledge to daily life, thereby improving scientific thinking and applying relevant immunology knowledge in daily life.

Name: Introduction to Stem Cells and Regenerative Medicine
Introduction: Stem cells and regenerative biology have developed rapidly in recent years and have become hot topics in life sciences, medicine and social research, and are expected to provide new strategies for the treatment of major diseases. This course will teach basic theoretical knowledge in the field of stem cells and regenerative biology, and combines research frontiers with social understanding. It aims to guide students' learning interests and enable students to understand the basic knowledge, research thinking and development status related to the field of stem cells and regenerative medicine. Classes will be taught in the form of a combination of background knowledge and topic discussions. Course work will be assessed through class discussions and term papers.

Name: Comprehensive Cell Biology Laboratory
Introduction: This course is a professional experimental technology course, open to senior undergraduates or junior graduate students who are about to participate in or have already participated in scientific research projects, and serves actual scientific research practice. It mainly includes cell biology technologies commonly used in the practice of life science research, as well as new technologies that have emerged in recent years to promote and innovate life science research, including: cell transfection technology, gene editing technology, flow cytometry technology (high-throughput single-cell flow cytometry technology), microscopy imaging (laser confocal microscopy technology, live cell workstation) technology, immunohistochemistry technology, immunofluorescence technology, 3D live cell technology, cell physiological function detection technology (such as cell viability detection, cell cycle/apoptosis detection, etc.). Through systematic study and practice of these professional experimental techniques with the most distinctive disciplinary characteristics of cell biology, students can acquire correct experimental skills and techniques, thereby cultivating students' ability to conduct scientific research independently.

Name: Frontiers of Life Science Technology and Industrial Innovation
Introduction:
Course Chinese Introduction (please be sure to fill in)_x000D_
The main content of this course is to invite outstanding representatives from the life sciences industry and industry research experts to provide classroom lectures and group case guidance for students who are interested in the life sciences industry. _x000D_
The purpose is to help students build an industrial knowledge framework, understand the cutting-edge dynamics of the industry, provide a platform for industrial research, peer exchanges, industry practice, and innovation and entrepreneurship, and guide students to have an in-depth understanding of the industrial operation model and development direction, carry out innovation and entrepreneurship practices, establish personal career development goals, and rationally plan their careers. _x000D_

Name: Education: Self, Society and Culture
Introduction:
This is a discussion class for freshmen from Yuanpei College in 2019. The course consists of two clues: First, based on the text study of Durkheim's "Moral Education", it starts from the common confusion when we grow up: Is discipline just an external police force? Where is the boundary between obedience and submission? Are self-interest and altruism contradictory? Behind these questions, we further discuss the relationship between individuals and society. What is sociality in individuals? What is the modern “infinity” disease? After the collapse of the religious edifice, how can education rebuild new sanctity and order with the help of reason. Second, closely following the course content, the teaching assistant seminar class selects important texts from the Republic of China period, providing local ideological resources and personal experience materials, making it easier for students to travel between China and the West, not only to deeply understand modern society, but also to find ways to live and coexist with themselves. _x000D_
Through course study, students can understand and master:_x000D_
(1) Basic concepts and core perspectives of education and sociology_x000D_
(2) Methods of studying classic texts_x000D_
(3) The ability to think critically and form problem awareness_x000D_

Name: First-Year Student Education Practicum
Introduction: In view of the unique training method of Yuanpei College, freshmen are faced with many choices of majors and courses after admission. The college offers this course after freshmen admission. It is committed to helping students adapt to university life, understand subject knowledge, broaden subject horizons, cultivate academic interests, and improve academic literacy training through freshman training camps, subject-specific lectures, personalized communication and guidance from tutors, and other activities.

Name: History of Ancient Greek and Roman Political Thought
Introduction: In the spring semester of 2017, the course will focus on the book Plato " Ideal Nations " , as well as on important research traditions and literature since the second half of the twentieth century. Through this course, students can learn the classic reading method, familiarize themselves with the fundamentals of ancient political thought and gain a deep understanding of the inner core of Plato political thought.

Name: Phenomenology and Ethics
Introduction: This course will teach students the classic original works of phenomenology such as Merle-Ponty's "Phenomenology of Perception" to guide students to become familiar with the basic principles, methods and research issues of phenomenology as a philosophical school, and cultivate students' philosophical thinking ability.

Name: Studies in the History of Western Ethics
Introduction: This course will explain to students the original ethical works such as Kant's "Foundation of the Metaphysics of Morals" and Nietzsche's "On the Genealogy of Morals". It will guide students to understand the basic issues and major schools in modern Western ethics. They will also be familiar with some of the major debates on ethical issues in contemporary academic circles, improve their philosophical thinking abilities, and broaden their horizons.

Name: Primary Texts of German Classical Philosophy
Introduction: The course is for senior undergraduate and graduate students. The lectures were given in Kant ' s " Jurisprudence " , an extremely important philosophical literature. The course will attempt to demonstrate a thorough and multifaceted interpretation of Kant's third criticism. In the era of enlightenment and early romance, Kant's breakthrough work consisted of two parts: aesthetic judgement and a purpose judgement. We need to focus first and foremost on the fact that the two parts are unified in a methodological sense by the exercise of judgement in the form of a unique reflection. Based on these textual conditions, the course will explore different but complementary interpretations. In addition, the course will cover “art and genius”, “American beauty as a moral symbol”, “Universal mechanistic principles of matter and co-purpose principles” and philosophical reflection on culture and physics-theology.

Name: Comparative Vertebrate Anatomy and Laboratory
Introduction: Comparative anatomy of vertebrates, as a traditional classical discipline, has been rejuvenated in recent years by the intersection of disciplines such as ecology, physiology, genetics, evolutionary biology, behavioural biology, biochemistry, molecular biology, material science and engineering mechanics. It is not only a discipline that describes the morphological structure, but also a discipline that analyses the biological structure and functions. It examines the structural principles of organisms under genetic and surrounding environmental impacts, finds the morphological foundations of different parts and understands the evolution of these structures in the development process. In the course of the course, emphasis is placed on the evolution of cartilage scavengers, skeletal scavengers, amphibians, birds and mammals, representing morphological anatomy of animals and horizontal comparisons between systems, and on the development of independent hands-on skills of students.

Name: Laboratory in Biomacromolecular Interactions
Introduction: In modern biological research, with the deepening of functional genome research, the study of biological functions of biological macromolecules plays a very important role. The interaction analysis of biological macromolecules has become an indispensable and important method in the current research on the functions of biological macromolecules. This course aims to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the main methods for studying the interactions of biological macromolecules, and to learn and master the current commonly used techniques for studying the interactions of biological macromolecules. In addition, this course encourages students to bring their own topics to class, that is, design experiments according to their own needs and interests (such as the topics of this research group), and implement the experimental plan after discussing with the instructor. It is hoped that students can apply what they have learned, master comprehensive experimental design and operation capabilities, experience the idea of ​​using biochemical methods to solve scientific research problems, and improve their comprehensive and standardized biochemical experimental skills.

Name: Mathematical Models and Methods in Bioinformatics
Introduction: This course is a professional elective course offered to senior undergraduates and graduate students in the Department of Probability and Statistics. Its purpose is to enable students to initially master the basic contents of bioinformatics and understand its application fields. This course focuses on several basic issues in bioinformatics, focusing on probabilistic and statistical modeling of these issues, and thus provides concentrated teaching on related probabilistic and statistical models. Requirements for students include: proficiency in basic probabilistic statistical models and algorithms in bioinformatics, mastering basic modeling methods of probabilistic statistics, and proficiency in applying relevant models for statistical analysis; at the same time, through seminars, graduate students can have an in-depth grasp of the mainstream scientific research trends in bioinformatics, the latest technology, and have a preliminary understanding of different application fields of bioinformatics. Cultivate students' research-based learning abilities, broaden their horizons, and lay a solid foundation for future research and application.

Name: The Art of Collaborative Piano
Introduction: “Cooperative piano”, also known as “piano accompaniment”, refers to the use of the piano as a melody-aided instrument, a term used to perform musical and artistic works in conjunction with human voice, instrumental music or theatre, which plays an important role in artistic works or industries such as classical music, modern popular music and opera drama. It not only deepens or enhances the performance and richness of musical and artistic works, it is also a central expression of the beauty of the synergy between human beings and musical instruments and music. The “Cooperative Piano Arts” course combines the piano's collaborative approach in the various musical works and as an entry point for practical performance guidance, classical and foreign musical arts appreciation and learning about the relevant theory. If you want to attract students who have some specialty in the piano, a musical base or a strong interest in this art class, you can also use the piano. Through systematic theoretical learning, musical appreciation, knowledge of this art and classical music work, and through practical piano performance skills, personal cooperation and accompaniment of the human voice or instrument, in-depth knowledge of the collaborative piano art, music art, and increased sense and appreciation of the beauty of music.

Name: Innovative Practice in Handicraft Making
Introduction: The practical content of the course is highly specialized in engineering, requiring learners to work creatively throughout the course. The content is easily accessible to beginners, not only in terms of basic scientific and engineering knowledge, expertise and practical training in engineering, but also in terms of the initial ability to use engineering skills to solve problems, but also in terms of training learners in the conscious pursuit of labour value achievement and spiritual satisfaction in practice, and the promotion of the subjective dynamics of innovative work. It covers a number of practical modules of labour creation, including the techniques of calving, carpentry, laser-added, 3D printing and electronics in design and prototype laboratories; intelligent car making techniques and processes in artificial intelligence laboratories; intelligent manufacturing of electronics production lines; welding and casting-forming processes in form manufacturing laboratories; car cutting processes in mechanical manufacturing laboratories, etc.; and the innovative labour practices of learners based on their own scientific base and preferences. In addition, there are a number of plant practices available to learners.

Name: Digital Circuits and System Design
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite:
Microelectronic and circuit base
Electronic circuit analysis and design
Introduction:
1. Basic design principles and methods for mastery of mathematical foundations, combination/limited status machines/time sequence circuits
2. Mastery of HDL modelling methods and digital system models
3. Learning from the design and trade-offs of digital systems, such as system models, performance and power optimization, cross-clock domain design, etc.; emphasizing the integrated ability to apply the knowledge acquired to address the somewhat challenging design of medium-sized digital systems

Name: Digital Circuits and System Design (Small Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Digital circuits and system design (theory course)
Introduction: Outreach workshops on classroom content to exercise innovative thinking through front-line research, group discussions, public speaking, etc.

Name: Introduction to Machine Learning for Earth Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Students must have experience in at least one programming language such as Python or Matlab or similar, and be able to use this for tasks such as loading and plotting a data file.
Introduction:
This course introduces basic machine learning (ML) concepts and demonstrates its applications in earth sciences. _x000D_
ML encompasses a range of different algorithms that are often used to make predictions based on complex and non-intuitive data. It has been very successful in many technical applications and can also be used in earth sciences. The purpose of this course is to provide an overview of the various ML algorithms, provide students with an intuitive understanding of how they work and their scope of applicability, and enable students to apply ML techniques to geophysical problems. _x000D_
This course will introduce the most important and commonly used ML algorithms. It will first introduce more basic algorithms, such as linear regression and logistic regression, multiple regression and principal component analysis, then introduce more advanced algorithms, such as artificial neural networks, support vector machines, and random forests. Finally, it will introduce unsupervised ML algorithms, such as K-means clustering algorithm. The course will theoretically introduce the basic working principles of each algorithm, allowing students to develop an intuitive understanding of the working principles. _x000D_
Each ML algorithm will be accompanied by a real-world case study from the earth sciences, from climate science, paleoceanography, volcanology, and remote sensing to seismology and petroleum geoscience. Each case study includes classroom exercises where students will use an ML programming language (such as Python or Matlab) to analyze real geophysical data and interpret their findings. _x000D_
This course not only exposes students to the most commonly used machine learning techniques, but also enables them to apply these algorithmic techniques to real-world cases in the earth sciences. The hours of this course will be equally divided into two parts: a machine learning theory course and a practical geophysical data course. _x000D_
This course is taught in English. _x000D_

Name: Mathematical Foundations of Quantitative Remote Sensing Inversion
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Inversion theory is a knowledge system composed of a series of mathematical methods based on linear algebra, probability and statistics. It is usually used to solve inverse problems, such as indirectly deriving information in the physical world that cannot or is not easily observed directly from observable data in experiments. Inversion theory is widely used in research in remote sensing science, geophysics, hydrology, atmospheric science, astronomy, biology and many other fields. With the advent of the big data era, the role of inversion theory in data analysis in various fields will become increasingly significant. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is mainly aimed at students from the School of Earth and Space Sciences of Peking University, especially students from the Institute of Remote Sensing. It teaches commonly used inversion methods in the field of quantitative remote sensing, such as linear regression, singular value decomposition, Tikhonov regularization method, iterative method, nonlinear inversion method, Bayesian method, etc. This course is based on linear algebra, supplemented by some basic probability and statistics knowledge. At the beginning of the teaching, some linear algebra knowledge will be reviewed based on the students' actual situation, and some required basic probability and statistical theories will be explained to facilitate students' understanding of the basic mathematical methods in inversion theory. Compared with the introduction of mathematical techniques in inversion methods, this course focuses more on explaining the applicable scope, application skills, and related MATLAB programs of various inversion methods. During the teaching process, there will be a large number of examples of the application of these inversion methods in solving different inverse problems, such as inverting the source position from seismic wave signals, inverting atmospheric composition from atmospheric light signals, solving inverse problems in tomography, etc. The assignment of homework emphasizes quality rather than quantity, especially the cultivation of students' ability to use these methods to solve practical problems.

Name: Academic Thesis Writing in Geophysics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
This course is designed to address issues such as drawing, wording, and structure that students encounter when writing English papers for geophysics majors. The purpose of this course is to improve students' drawing, speech, writing, and presentation abilities through the training of this course. This will lay a good foundation for students' future scientific research careers. _x000D_
_x000D_
The content covered in this course generally includes:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. How to draw and modify pictures in the paper. _x000D_
2. How to create clear and effective presentation slides_x000D_
3. How to write an English paper and what you need to pay attention to when submitting a paper.

Geophysics is a discipline that strongly relies on observational data. Through the analysis of large amounts of observational data, new phenomena are discovered and new theories are generated. From _x000D_

Master the ability to obtain data, process data, and interpret data, and cultivate the ability to discover and solve problems, in order to further develop in geophysics and related fields.
lay the foundation for scientific research in the field. The main contents include: investigation of surface geological phenomena; learning of cutting-edge geophysical processing technology; seismic observation_x000D_
Array design and seismic observation; seismic observation data processing and interpretation. _x000D_

Name: Modern Electronic Measurement and Laboratory
Prerequisite: Modern Electronic Circuit Foundations and Experiments
Introduction: This course introduces the principles and methods of measuring physical quantities using electronic technology. Through this course, students can learn data acquisition and processing methods, understand the impact of computer technology on measurement technology, and the application of virtual instruments in measurement.

Name: Evolution of the Earth System
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The earth is a system composed of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere; the evolution of the earth system involves the interaction between various layers. The earth was formed 4.6 billion years ago, and through a long period of evolution, it gradually formed a habitable planet suitable for human (biological) habitation. The evolution of habitable planets will provide historical habitability for humans to predict the future of the earth, and also provide theoretical constraints for the exploration of habitable extraterrestrial planets and extraterrestrial civilizations. This course will systematically introduce the basic concepts of the earth system and the evolutionary history of the earth system.

Name: Evolution of the Earth System Seminar
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The earth is a system composed of the atmosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere, and biosphere; the evolution of the earth system involves the interaction between various layers. The earth was formed 4.6 billion years ago, and through a long period of evolution, it gradually formed a habitable planet suitable for human (biological) habitation. The evolution of habitable planets will provide historical habitability for humans to predict the future of the earth, and also provide theoretical constraints for the exploration of habitable extraterrestrial planets and extraterrestrial civilizations. This course will systematically introduce the basic concepts of the earth system and the evolutionary history of the earth system.

Name: Paleoecology and Paleoenvironmental Analysis
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The main objective of the course on Palaeoecology and Palaeological Environmental Analysis is to master the basic methods of ancient environmental analysis by introducing basic theories of paleontological ecology and supporting basic knowledge of relevant sedimentology and sedimentary geochemicals. Pre-leaving courses include General Palaeontology and General Geology.
The main elements revolve around the basic concepts and theories of paleontology and highlight some methodological aspects of restoration of the ancient environment.

Name: Frontiers of Paleontology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: There are no special pre-course requirements for this course.
Introduction: "Evolution" is the eternal theme of life sciences. The diversity of life on earth today is the result of the long evolution of earth's history. The "Frontiers of Paleontology" course will be targeted at undergraduates in geology and biology. It will select the latest discussions from domestic and foreign textbooks and the latest research results in academia to provide in-depth and easy-to-understand lectures, so that students with different backgrounds can understand the basic concepts and research methods of "evolutionary biology" and enable students to have an in-depth understanding of paleontological research under the guidance of evolutionary theories and methods. _x000D_

Name: Seismogeology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: General geology, tectonic geology, geophysical base
Introduction:
Seismic geology is a borderline discipline between geology and solid geophysics. It mainly uses the theories and methods of geology and solid geophysics to study the causes of earthquakes, the laws of seismic activity, and the resulting earthquakes and geological disasters. Seismic geology has important theoretical and practical significance in seismic risk analysis, earthquake prediction, earthquake geological disaster mitigation and geodynamic analysis. _x000D_
This course mainly introduces the relationship between earthquakes and geological structures, analyzes the role of geological structures in the formation, occurrence and development of earthquakes, explains the research methods and techniques of earthquake geology, and studies the geological conditions for the formation of earthquake disasters. This course is suitable for science students with a certain foundation in geology and geophysics. _x000D_

Name: Physics and Chemistry of the Earth's Interior
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Prerequisite: Physical Geology, One year of college-level chemistry or physics (preferably both) and calculus.
Introduction:
Much of the Earth's interior cannot be observed directly, and much of what we know about the Earth's interior comes from seismology - our most informative probe of the deep Earth. Seismology reveals changes in seismic wave speed laterally and with depth. Translating this seismic information into knowledge about the structure, composition, and dynamical state of the Earth's interior requires other disciplines in the broadest sense, such as high-pressure mineral physics, geochemistry, and geodynamics. _x000D_
    The physics and chemistry of the Earth's interior determine not only deep Earth earthquakes, composition, and thermal structure, but also the dynamics of the entire Earth from the deep interior to the surface. Structure and dynamics are closely related to the formation and evolution of the Earth's interior. Students will be introduced to the physical and chemical structure of the Earth. The crust, mantle and core will be explored using a variety of geophysical and geochemical methods. The ultimate goal of this course is to develop a comprehensive conceptual model that draws on all contributing disciplines to understand the origin, evolution, and dynamics of the Earth. This course will be taught in English. _x000D_

Name: Trace Element Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Trace elements refer to all chemical elements that usually occur in nature in abundance below 1% or 0.1% and can be detected using modern analytical techniques. Trace element geochemistry is a branch of geochemistry that studies the distribution patterns, existence forms, activity characteristics, controlling factors and geochemical significance of trace elements in natural materials and natural systems. This course mainly introduces the classification of elements and the characteristics, fractionation and distribution rules of different types of trace elements and their controlling factors, including the thermodynamic basis of trace element geochemistry, distribution coefficients of trace elements and their controlling factors, trace element thermometers, chronometers, trace amounts in magmatism The behavior of elements and trace element traces enable students to initially master the basic theories and methods of trace element geochemistry, analyze the dissolution, precipitation and crystallization processes of trace elements during fluid and magma activities, and explain the origin and structural background of rocks and mineral deposits through the behavior of trace elements.

Name: Italian Language and Culture
Introduction: This course provides an introduction to Italian language and culture. During the first six days of the course, each day's lessons are divided into three main sections: Culture, Cities and Languages. The first two sections are linked together as aspects of each city's cultural, historical and artistic heritage will be presented. In addition, literature, music, important historical figures and other aspects of Italian culture will be introduced according to historical clues. Language classes focus on daily expressions, allowing students to master basic expressions based on grammatical explanations. Finally, a professor from the University of Turin will give a lecture on contemporary Italian society and Sino-Italian relations.

Name: International Negotiation and Diplomatic Document Writing
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to help students understand the basic concepts and theories of international negotiations and to master the basic strategies and techniques of international negotiations.

Name: Introduction to Big Data in Electromagnetics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: First course: Electrodynamics, signals and systems, probability theory
Introduction: This course introduces the basic knowledge and main application areas of electromagnetic data processing and mining, including electromagnetic spectrum, electromagnetic big data in the fields of wireless communication and remote sensing, WIFI data, basic methods of electromagnetic data mining, basic rules of Python language programming, and several applications of electromagnetic big data mining. This course is suitable as an elective course for senior undergraduate students.

Name: Introduction to Electromagnetic Wave Theory and Applications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The course presents basic knowledge of the theory of electromagnetic waves and the main areas of application, including the establishment and content of the Maxwell equation, methods of generation of electromagnetic waves and antenna principles, patterns of transmission and reflection and penetration of electromagnetic waves, as well as the use of electromagnetic waves as carriers of communication information, as tools for target detection and as means of energy use. This course is suitable as an optional course at the senior undergraduate level.

Through the teaching experiments of this course, students will learn to master basic optoelectronics experimental skills, learn to use commonly used instruments and equipment in optoelectronics experiments, understand commonly used optoelectronic components, and master basic skills and methods such as optical path adjustment, use of commonly used lasers, and parameter measurement, laying a foundation for subsequent courses and related professional experimental research.

Name: Biogeography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Biogeography is the science of studying the past and present distribution of organisms and the associated changes in the number and variety of organisms and their patterns worldwide. By teaching basic patterns of present-day biological distribution, the course leads students to analyse the formation process and the main control factors from an ecological, evolutionary and Earth-historic perspective, most notably by placing biogeography at a multidisciplinary intersection, thus providing students from different backgrounds with the basic knowledge needed to understand and study current global environmental changes. The course will cover biota of systems such as terrestrial, island and ocean, and will focus on changes in biogeographic patterns and their control factors at different time scales, which will help students to make scientific assessments of the possible consequences of future environmental changes.
Special features of biogeography:
1. Focus on teaching basic theories, basic knowledge and basic methods of biogeography
2. Focus on the impact of ecological, evolutionary and geological history on biological distribution
3. New results focused on interdisciplinary research, focusing on hot spots (e.g., development of island biogeography theory; controversy over the evolution of the fourth century)

Name: Introduction to Earth System Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Since the 1980s, developments in the fields of earth sciences such as global change have driven academic circles to treat the earth's major spheres as an overall object, directly promoting the birth of "Earth system science". In 1983, NASA established the Earth System Science Committee and published the "Earth System Science Report" in 1988, proposing the famous "Bretherton Figure", emphasizing the complex physical, chemical, and biological processes and interactions between the atmosphere, oceans, and biosphere. In 1996, "Earth System Science" was officially included in the teaching plan of American universities. MIT, UCI and other universities successively launched core courses related to earth system science in the 2010s and established departments of earth system science. _x000D_
_x000D_
Earth system science applies multidisciplinary theories and techniques such as physics, chemistry, biology, and mathematics to treat the earth as a whole object, emphasizing the interaction of physics, chemistry, biological processes, and human activities with the earth's past, present, and future. It is the basis for our in-depth understanding of the earth and the sustainable development of mankind. Driven by international projects such as the International Geosphere-Biosphere Program and Future Earth, Earth system science research has developed rapidly in the past two decades. Earth system science is considered to be the future development trend of geoscience. Therefore, earth system science is indispensable in the training of earth science undergraduates. This course mainly trains undergraduates to understand the interaction between different circles, the complex influence and feedback process, and the need to use a systematic perspective to study geographical, ecological and environmental issues. By using interesting issues on the historical evolution of the earth as an index, we cultivate students' interest in earth science, guide students to use holism to think about earth science issues, form scientific concepts of the earth system, learn to think about the process mechanisms behind phenomena, and develop reading literature, discussion and communication skills, and hands-on skills. _x000D_

Name: Experimental Methods in Modern Physical Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: Natural geography, Earth overview, geomorphology, meteorology and climate
Introduction: This course is divided into physical, chemical and biological sediment analysis and meteorological and climate observations.

Name: Physical Geography of the World
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: "World Physical Geography - The Physical Geographic Basis of Global Geographical Conflicts" focuses on the natural geographical basis of resource and environmental issues and even socio-economic conflicts in global hotspots. Facing the needs of major national development strategies such as the “One Belt, One Road” initiative, college students need to have a global perspective and learn to analyze the intricate factors behind global geopolitical conflicts, especially the underlying role of natural environmental factors. "The world is so big, why do geo-political conflicts of global concern occur here?" The teaching of this course is designed to inspire students. Through the teaching of core content, students can master the comprehensive physical geography analysis ability of hot resource and environmental issues and socio-economic conflicts from a global perspective. _x000D_

Name: Italian Renaissance Art
Prerequisite: Students who have taken courses in European history, Western literature, etc., are given priority.
Introduction: This course takes art history as its core and tells the history of the Renaissance in a multi-faceted and in-depth manner and its inspiration to modern civilization. What is "Renaissance"? To answer this question, this course explores the major artistic movements that spread across the Italian peninsula from the 14th to 16th centuries and the humanist ideas behind them. Topics include: the origin of general (liberal arts) education, the revival of ancient literature and art, "Renaissance Man" and Italian humanism, the relationship between art and science, politics, religion, mythology, philosophy, etc. Use a large number of visual materials to deeply appreciate the representative works of important Renaissance artists and architects, including early Renaissance painter Masaccio, sculptor Donatello, architect Brunelleschi, "Renaissance all-rounders" Alberti, Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo, as well as important representatives of the Venetian School, Titian and Giorgione. Through case analysis, we focus on the unity of painting, sculpture, architecture and other arts during the Italian Renaissance, as well as the important inspiration of the Italian Renaissance to modern and contemporary civilization.

Name: Frontier Research Methods in Computer Science
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Introduce some important elements of computer science research, cultivate the ability of creative thinking and critical thinking, cultivate the ability, methods and habits of discovering and solving problems, cultivate the ability of scientific writing and communication, time management ability, etc. At the same time, it also introduces the intellectual property rights and scientific research ethics involved in scientific research. Finally, this course will also introduce cutting-edge scientific research directions in related fields, and communicate with potential scientific research mentors and outstanding scientific research students.

Name: Introduction to Satellite Navigation and Positioning Systems

Introduction:
This course is a cutting-edge science and technology course developed to adapt to the current development of electronic science, technology and disciplines. This course is closely related to practical applications. By introducing satellite navigation systems such as GPS, GLONASS, GALILEO and my country's "Beidou", students can systematically understand the basic principles, technologies, applications, development trends and latest progress of satellite navigation and positioning. This course undoubtedly provides very useful knowledge for students in communications, navigation and other related fields. _x000D_
      In terms of teaching methods, this course adopts the form of "multimedia courseware teaching as the main part, supplemented by traditional blackboard writing", and uses heuristic, discussion-based and interactive teaching modes to give full play to students' learning initiative and enthusiasm. Through interactive teaching, students can broaden their academic horizons and master basic professional knowledge.

Name: Computer Networks (Honors Section)

Introduction: The course will introduce students to a range of basic knowledge and cutting-edge technologies of computer networks, including the Internet, top-down presentation of Internet protocols, wireless networks, mobile Internet, cybersecurity, sensor networks, 5G network frontier technologies, hot topics, etc. At the same time, the curriculum will be developed with practical applications, thus giving students the opportunity to experience computer networks at close range. Name: Energy and the Environment
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
