Many environmental problems are directly related to energy consumption and structural change. Through course delivery and learning, students will be informed about basic concepts, terminology and definitions of energy and the environment, the characteristics, formation, classification, resource characteristics, energy development, etc. of fossil energy, and the relationship between fossil energy and renewable energy use and development, the rationale and characteristics of key energy-efficient abatement technologies, the basic concepts of sustainable development, and the energy development strategies and environmental protection requirements in the context of sustainable development.

Name: Introduction to Software Testing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Software testing is one of the important ways to ensure software quality. This course will introduce the basic theory of software testing, so that undergraduate students in the Department of Computer Science will have the necessary testing knowledge base in the software development process, and will also lay a solid testing foundation for future scientific research work.

Name: Environmental Biology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Curriculum for environmental biology
i. Educational objectives of the curriculum: Environmental biology is one of the main branches of environmental science and is a discipline for studying patterns of interaction between organisms (including humans) and the environment subject to human intervention and their regulatory mechanisms. The teaching objectives of the environmental biology curriculum are to help undergraduate students in environmental science to lay the foundation for the biology required to learn about environmental science, to help students understand the biological effects of environmental pollutants and their behaviour in ecosystems, to understand the role of organisms in the purification of environmental pollution, to understand the interactions between environmental pollutants and organisms, to acquire basic knowledge, basic theories and related experimental skills in environmental biology, to help students broaden their academic horizons and knowledge structures, to improve overall integrity and to lay a solid professional foundation for future learning and work.
II. Teaching content: The curriculum focuses on the three core elements of biological effects of environmental pollution and ecological damage, biological interaction with the environment and bioremediation of the contaminated environment. It focuses on the basic knowledge of the core elements, related theories and research methods. It also covers some basic knowledge and methods of traditional biology, modern molecular biology, cytology, biochemistry, genetics, ecology, toxicology and bioinformatics.
The course combines theoretical, computer-based and experimental subjects, using theoretical subjects (2 credits) and computer-based practicals (1 credits) and experimental courses (1 credits).

Name: Environmental Evolution and Global Change
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course takes the history of the earth and humans over the past 2.6 million years as the main line, introducing the basic ideas and methods of long-scale environmental change research, as well as the important scientific data obtained in recent years and their significance.

Name: Botany (Part 2)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Plant classification and plant geography are essential basic knowledge and professional skills for majors such as ecology, geographical science, and urban and rural planning. This course includes classroom lectures on the evolution and classification of plant systems, plant ecological types, flora, and vegetation geography, as well as internships in campus plants and botanical gardens. Through the combination of theory and practice, students in related majors can establish a relatively complete knowledge system of "macrobotany" and have the ability to identify common plants and apply botanical knowledge, laying a foundation for studying courses such as general ecology, field ecology, and urban ecology, and for engaging in relevant professional scientific research and urban planning and other applied work after graduation.

Name: General Geology Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The Earth Introduction Field Practice Course is a field practice course for undergraduate and graduate students in the School of Environment. Students taking this course are required to have taken "Introduction to the Earth" or "General Geology" in the previous academic year (recently). The "Introduction to the Earth" course is a basic course on earth science, especially on the composition, structure and evolution of the earth's crust, for undergraduates majoring in geography, environment and other non-geology majors at Peking University. The course consists of three core parts: (1) The material composition of the earth's crust, describing Basic content of minerals and petrology, understanding important common minerals and rocks; (2) Geological structure of the earth's crust, introducing basic knowledge about geological structures and geotectonic structures, focusing on fold structure, fault structure, and plate tectonics theory; (3) A brief history of the evolution of the earth's crust.

Name: Integrated Physical Geography Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The Comprehensive Physical Geography Internship selects the Yellow River Delta in the lower reaches of the Yellow River and the Zhengzhou-Kaifeng section in the middle reaches to carry out internships on large-scale spatial differentiation patterns and local-scale natural complexes. From the perspective of the watershed, the pattern and process of the natural geographical environment are combined through water circulation to build a point-to-surface, comprehensive field internship base to provide a platform for students to carry out field physical geography practice. Through internships, students receive comprehensive physical geography field training. The content of the internship includes geology, geomorphology, climate, hydrology, soil, vegetation, landscape and land use. Based on the previous departmental geography (landform, soil, vegetation) internships, the relationship between the various elements of physical geography is analyzed, and the holistic thinking of the natural geographical environment is established. The understanding of the comprehensive physical geography classroom teaching content is deepened, the combination of theory and practice is strengthened, the students' geographical thinking and the ability to analyze and solve problems are cultivated, and good field work abilities are laid for students to engage in scientific research.

Name: Architectural Design (I)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite:
Fine arts: sketches and colors
Art internship
Introduction:
"Architectural Design I" is a compulsory course for the urban planning major. It aims to enable students to master the basic knowledge of architecture, equip them with architectural design concepts and skills, and lay a solid foundation for architectural cognition and design for the urban planning major. _x000D_
Architecture designs and constructs various artificial environments and structures in cities, towns, and landscape gardens. Architecture is a combination of art and science. It is also a product of technology, art, and society. It requires strong technical knowledge, a perceptual artistic aesthetic, and attention to humanities and society. _x000D_
This course covers the basic theories, principles and methods of architecture, introduces the historical and modern built environment, and covers the basic principles of architectural analysis, evaluation and aesthetics. The architectural drawing part includes tool application, labeling, dimensions, drawing techniques, etc. for freehand and instrumental drawing to improve the expressive skills of architectural drawing. _x000D_
    The project assignments in the course train the composition techniques of form and space, take root in the social and cultural environment, and promote the harmony between architecture and human scale. To enable students to seriously devote themselves to the study of basic design principles, design composition and expression techniques, and then seek broader and more critical design strategies. _x000D_

Name: Territorial Spatial Planning Management and Regulations
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: On the basis of introducing the characteristics and requirements of planning management activities, this course teaches the territorial spatial planning system and its current management characteristics, and explains it in accordance with relevant fields such as land use management, urban and rural planning management, historical and cultural heritage protection management, environmental protection management, forest, grassland, and ocean management. Relevant regulations involving the preparation and management, implementation management, supervision and management of major plans.

Name: Architectural Design (II)
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Architectural Design (2)" is a subject with a very broad concept and content. The reason for adopting such a teaching content is that in our era there is actually no shortage of ideas and so-called design concepts. When the current living environment is filled with those ugly houses labeled with new trends of thought, new concepts, new materials, new methods, new structures, new technologies, etc., which are full of so-called very design ideas and full of design theory labels, it just shows that we architects lack a "means" that can convert a series of "creative thinking" and design ideas into a spatial form language. _x000D_
As for the discovery, training and use of this "means", expressing "creative thinking" with an appropriate "means" is the main intention of this topic and the purpose of this architectural design class. _x000D_

Name: Urban Social Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Urban Social Geography is an important basic course for the Resource Environment and Urban and Rural Planning Management major and the Urban Planning major. _x000D_
    Urban social geography is an important sub-discipline of human geography. In recent years, Western human geography has emphasized the "cultural and institutional turn". Social geography has developed rapidly and is an important vehicle for human geographers to participate in the study of social issues. _x000D_
    The basic teaching idea of this course is to use the urban social geography course as a platform on which students can be taught step by step how to independently conduct an urban social geography research, which may be more useful than teaching them specific knowledge. One third of the course is arranged to teach basic theories, methods and research skills, including: research progress in Western urban social geography, various Western philosophical trends and their application in geographical research, urban social survey methods and paper writing skills. In the second third of the class period, three discussion sessions are arranged, including: topic selection discussion, mid-term report and final report. In the middle of the three discussion classes, the other third of the course is arranged to teach and discuss a series of research on Chinese urban social space carried out by the teacher. The purpose is to allow students to understand how to find innovative points based on existing literature, how to raise research questions, how to conduct empirical research, and how to write a document and highlight key points. After training in the above process and on the basis of "hand-in-hand" teaching, students can complete a research of their own and form a real thesis. Only by completing this painful "transformation" can students experience the ups and downs of scientific research and truly realize the transformation from knowledge learning to scientific research creation. Almost all students who persist in completing the above process and conscientiously complete investigations and paper writing have similar experiences. _x000D_
    The textbook "Spatial Perspective of Urban Society" accompanying this course is a "practical" record that teaches students how to conduct geographic research on urban society. In addition to introducing the theory, investigation and research methods of urban social geography, it also includes 20 papers from the two major aspects of macro and micro urban social space research, many of which are written by students in this class and can be used as a reference for students taking this course. _x000D_

Name: Landscape Planning and Design
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
What is the meaning of landscape? What is landscape architecture? What is the background of landscape architecture? What is the difference between landscape architecture and other related disciplines? What is the profession of a landscape architect? What does a landscape architect do? What is the relationship between landscape architecture and adjacent disciplines? What is the connotation of landscape and the development process of landscape architecture? What are the historical tasks of landscape architects in the context of contemporary Chinese characteristics? _x000D_
With these questions as the background, this course will combine theory, practical design projects and cases to explain and answer these questions. By analyzing the development process of urban landscape across scales and combining various skills of landscape planning and design, students can systematically master the development history, relevant theories and methods of landscape planning and design. _x000D_

Name: Jewish Civilization in Global Perspective
Prerequisite: No, students from all grades of the school (technical, scientific, literary, commercial, medical, artistic, etc.) are welcome to study and listen to the wonderful journey of global Jewish civilization!
Introduction:
Greek civilization and Hebrew civilization are two important sources in the origin of human civilization, and are known as the "Two Greek Civilizations" in history. As one of the important origins of Western civilization, Jewish civilization has had a huge and far-reaching impact on the development process of world civilization. Who are the Jews? What is the core of Jewish culture? Why has anti-Semitism continued to rage for two thousand years? How did the Jewish nation and the Chinese nation interact in history? What impact has the Jewish Renewal movement and the founding of the modern state of Israel had on the global Jewish community? Why are there such a high proportion of Jewish Nobel Prize winners, Hollywood celebrities, high-tech company founders, etc. in the world? What characteristics did the development of Jewish civilization present? This series of questions deserves our in-depth exploration. This course breaks through the limitations of disciplines and majors and is open to all Peking University undergraduates with backgrounds in liberal arts, science, engineering, medicine, business, art and other disciplines. It provides students with the opportunity to connect ancient and modern times, integrate China and the West, and examine Jewish civilization from a global perspective. It aims to play a certain basic scientific role in paving the way for future elite groups in Chinese society to understand the historical evolution of Jewish civilization and the interaction between the two major civilizations of China and Judea. It is hoped that students from different fields will learn about the major events and significance in the development of Jewish civilization by studying "Jewish Civilization from a Global Perspective", and understand the profound impact of these events on the development of the entire civilization. In the era of a community with a shared future for mankind, they will respect multicultural symbiosis, improve their innovation and critical thinking skills, and further understand world civilization. _x000D_
Students are welcome to choose the course "Jewish Civilization from a Global Perspective" and go on a wonderful journey of Jewish civilization! Course-selecting students with outstanding performance will have the opportunity to be recommended and receive full scholarships for short-term academic exchanges at academic institutions in Israel. _x000D_
 _x000D_

Name: French (1)
Introduction:
Students can use simple and commonly used phrases to introduce themselves, introduce a certain person, and ask questions about their personal situation, interests and hobbies, etc., and can handle very simple daily communications. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: French (2)
Introduction:
Students can use simple and commonly used phrases to introduce themselves, introduce a certain person, and ask questions about their personal situation, interests and hobbies, etc., and can handle very simple daily communications. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: French (3)
Introduction: In most cases, students can understand familiar topics related to hobbies, work, studies, etc. Ability to describe an event, an experience, or a plan and explain it.

Name: French (4)
Introduction: Students can understand specific or abstract views in a complex article. A professional discussion of the areas of their personal studies enables students to elaborate on many topics in a clear and detailed manner.

Name: Neuropsychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Neuropsychology is a field that studies the structural and functional characteristics of different areas of the human brain and the changes in psychological behavior and cognitive functions that occur after damage to various brain areas. At the same time, the psychological characteristics of the onset of diseases related to damage to different brain areas are studied.

Name: Key Issues in Consciousness Studies
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Human scientific development has entered a new milestone era, and the understanding of the brain mechanism of consciousness is also facing new breakthroughs. With this breakthrough, understanding of various brain dysfunctions and mental disorders will reach new heights. This course will discuss several core issues in the study of the brain mechanism of consciousness through literature reading, classroom explanations and discussions, and paper writing, in order to promote thinking about consciousness. The evaluation of students taking this elective course is divided into three parts: (1) explanation of the assigned article and answers to questions; (2) participation in problem discussion activities in class; (3) final paper written according to one's own interests.

Name: Scientific Writing and Communication
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: If you want to pursue a career in science in the future, you will have to write (most likely in English). Do you know your audience? How to refine words and sentences? How to organize a good story? In this class, you will improve your scientific writing and communication skills through concrete examples, extensive in-class exercises, and learning how to make constructive proposals.

Name: Frontier Literature Discussion in Psychology (1)
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
The Frontier Literature Discussion Course in Psychological Science is a literature discussion course offered by the School of Psychology and Cognitive Sciences. The main teaching targets are students in Zhang Xiangtong’s class in the School of Psychology. As a special course of Zhang Xiangtong’s class, this course is a literature discussion organized by student groups. With the help of instructors, they independently select several cutting-edge issues in psychology (including cognitive, clinical, developmental, social, and economic and organizational management psychology), and systematically explain the origin of the field, the emergence of important concepts, discuss the core original literature in the field, and explore what are the current main issues and challenges. Each literature discussion meeting invites students’ supervisors and experts in the field to guide the discussion process and guide students’ academic speeches. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course reference book is the classic textbook The Craft of Scientific Presentations: Critical Steps to Succeed and Critical Errors to Avoid, Springer. Through this course, students need to master basic academic presentation skills and lay a solid foundation for future academic communication. _x000D_
This course is a compulsory course for students in Zhang Xiangtong’s class in the School of Psychology. It can be taken as an elective course by undergraduate students majoring in psychology in the School of Psychology and Yuanpei College. _x000D_

Name: Health Psychology
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction: Health psychology is the science that studies the impact of psychological, behavioral and sociocultural factors on people's maintenance of health, illness and reactions after illness, and carries out psychological and behavioral intervention to help people maintain and promote health, and prevent and treat diseases.

Name: Adolescent Psychological Interviewing: Theory, Technique and Case Discussion
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
In the practice of clinical psychological consultation and psychotherapy, we often encounter problems of how to conduct in-depth interviews, how to properly understand the client and provide him with effective help. Mastering basic negotiation skills plays an important role in management psychology, interpersonal communication, and psychological counseling. _x000D_
This course will use modern imaging materials to help undergraduate students learn the basic concepts of psychological counseling, interviewing techniques, helping theories, communication skills, semi-structured interview skills, etc. through in-depth observation, analysis, understanding and discussion of psychological counseling-related imaging materials. _x000D_
The teacher teaching this course, Dr. Xu Kaiwen, associate professor, is an attending physician in psychiatry and has been engaged in front-line clinical work in psychiatry for a long time. Currently a part-time psychiatrist at United Family Hospital. Chinese Mental Health Association Psychotherapy and Psychological Counseling Professional Committee, Crisis Intervention Director. He is a member of the Psychiatry Branch of the Chinese Medical Association and a member of the Social Psychiatry Group. He has long been engaged in the research and treatment of mental illness, crisis intervention, and psychological trauma. His doctoral research thesis was on the study and intervention of offenders with antisocial personality disorder. _x000D_
Undergraduate students and dual-major undergraduates taking this course are required to take a prerequisite course in abnormal psychology. _x000D_

Name: The Ethics of Homeric Epic
Introduction: This course aims to teach the ethical thoughts of Homer's epic poems. It takes Homer's "Iliad" and "Odyssey" as the key texts, combined with modern research literature, and based on intensive reading of the texts, understands and discusses the ethical thoughts contained in these works, and uses this as an entry point to understand the general characteristics of ancient Greek history, culture, and philosophy.

Name: Wuji Ball (Qigong Ball Exercise)
Introduction:
Wuji ball is a new national fitness sport officially listed by the Social and Sports Center of the State Sports General Administration.     Wuji ball is an innovation based on inheritance and is a new type of health sport developed in line with the fast-paced lifestyle of modern people. It is a fitness sport with unique Chinese characteristics that integrates fitness, self-cultivation and nourishing the mind. It provides the public with an easy-to-learn and interesting healthy exercise method, allowing people to effectively and comprehensively improve their sub-health status. _x000D_
The essence of Wuji ball exercise is clear and the movements are simple; it does not deliberately emphasize basic skills training, is safe to operate, has distinctive characteristics, and has significant effects; it has a wide audience and can truly help practitioners stimulate their physical potential. It is an extremely pragmatic health exercise.     Infinity ball is also a sport that is not restricted by conditions and can be exercised in fragmented time. It is a good way to do micro-exercises in the office or at home. _x000D_
The curriculum system of this sport mainly includes a gradually upgraded technical system of three levels and nine sections and several sets of prescribed practice routines. It perfectly integrates sports technology and artistic performance, and can meet the practice needs of people of all levels.

Name: Modern Popular Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course teaches the existence significance and evolution of modern Chinese popular literature in the context of China's social and cultural development since modern times. Since the modern Chinese literature education of most citizens is limited to the scope of new literature, while the literary and artistic works they come into contact with and appreciate in daily life are mainly popular literature, this course not only has the significance of expanding the history of literature, but also has a clear function of guiding the practice of cultural life. Comparative study of new literature and popular literature can more systematically understand and grasp the dynamics and cultural value of the entire literary field.

Name: Form and History: Studies in Lu Xun's Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course attempts to explore Lu Xun's creation of modern novel forms within the historical context of modern China in which he lived and his interaction with world literature. Lu Xun can be called the creator of the modern Chinese short story form, but his short stories are not just short "stories" from the beginning, but contain profound "comments" on modern Chinese history, culture and society. This course will carefully read the texts of Lu Xun's novels in the dual context of modern Chinese historical situations and world literature. It hopes to use Lu Xun's novels as an example to launch theoretical thinking and discussion on the relationship between literary form and history.

Name: Close Reading of Reflections on Things at Hand
Introduction: This course is an intensive reading course for classical Chinese literature. "Jinsi Lu" is the outline of Neo-Confucianism in the Northern Song Dynasty, and it is also the outline of Zhu Xi's philosophy. Zhu Zichang said: "The ladder of the Four Masters (Four Books) and the Six Classics is the ladder of the Four Masters in "Jin Si Lu"." This course intends to adopt a group study method to deeply explore the rich ideological content in "Jin Si Lu", thereby demonstrating its historical status and role as an introductory book to Neo-Confucianism.

Name: Phonetics of World Languages and Methods of Investigation
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course systematically teaches field investigation methods of the International Phonetic Alphabet and phonology. First, the design principles of the International Phonetic Alphabet symbol system and the meaning of each symbol are introduced, and recordings of multiple languages ​​and dialects are used to train students' listening and pronunciation abilities. On the basis of students mastering the International Phonetic Symbols, a minority student is invited to serve as a native language teacher in the classroom to train students to use the International Phonetic Symbols to accurately record sounds, summarize phonemes, make and check homophone morpheme tables, and write phonological investigation reports.

Name: Biographical Literature: Studies of Classic Figures
Introduction:
Biographical literature, glamorous. Its literary values, historical significance, psychological utility and educational functions are unique. That is why its importance is increasingly recognized. According to Carlisle, “History is the fruit of countless biographys”. Emerson thought, "No history, no biography," and the great poet Yip used to admire the biography. He gave an extraordinary conclusion to the biography with an immortal poem: "All knowledge is biography."
In China, the Schumaer ' s Historic leaves us with countless cases of impact. Liang Kai is deeply involved in mythology, and his writing of a large number of myths has a tremendous impact. Hu loved biography throughout his life, because he was deeply aware of its value — “to make materials for the historians and to open the way to literature.” Here, Hu also ignored the most important function of biography: it was the first reading of quality education.
Empiricalism, self-inflictedness, identity crises and the limits of growth are eternal problems of humankind, to which the immortal biography provides excellent answers. We will focus on classics such as Caesar, Liu Bang, Yae Yu, Elizabeth, Rousseau, Franklin, Solo, Gandhi, Hu Chi, etc., in order to foster an original foundation and a sense of leadership.
In addition, the course will address theoretical issues of biographical literature: family spectra, theory of facts, fictional phenomena, structural principles, interpretation strategies, narrative characteristics, etc.

Name: Western Literature
Introduction: Western literature has a long history from ancient Greece to contemporary times. From a spatial perspective, it includes European and American countries, with a large number of countries. It only takes one semester to use the traditional way of telling literary history to conduct an overview and systematic combing. Even if it is only satisfied with teaching basic knowledge, this task cannot be completed. In view of this, this course is based on the historical changes of European literature, mainly taking literary classics as the main line, based on literary texts, and connecting the context of Western literature through a series of selected texts. In each class, experts in relevant fields select representative classics in Western literature. Starting from the teaching classics, through the methods of "looking forward and backward" and "looking left and right", they sort out the ins and outs of the classics in the process of literary changes, examine the status of contemporary national literature and transnational literature, and expand from classic reading to literary narratives of related eras. The entire course focuses on reading classics, talking about eras, and looking at history. A unique transformation process of Western literature is constructed from classics and eras.

Name: Studies in The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Prerequisite: The history of ancient Chinese literature, paragraphs I and II, ancient Chinese, literary principles
Introduction: "Wen Xin Diao Long" is a work on writing style written by Liu Xie during the Qi and Liang Dynasties in the Southern Dynasties. Qing Dynasty scholar Zhang Xuecheng called it "big in style but considers Zhou". Modern scholars generally regard it as a classic of Chinese literary theory, comparable to Aristotle's "Poetics" in the West. This course is based on the academic background of the history of Chinese literary theory and criticism, and is connected with the actual literary creation in ancient and medieval times. It selects some important chapters of the book to guide students to accurately understand Liu Xie's literary theory thoughts and viewpoints, and make appropriate interpretations and evaluations. It guides students to deeply understand the development of ancient and medieval literature in connection with "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons", cultivates students' thinking in Chinese literary theory, and guides students to think about the modern value of traditional literary theory. This course is a joint course for undergraduates and postgraduates, and the grades for undergraduates and postgraduates will be calculated separately.

Name: Exploring the Teaching Profession: Basic Literacy and Skills for Teachers
Introduction:
Course Objectives and Principles_x000D_
Course objectives: Every year, some undergraduates, masters and doctoral students from Peking University choose the teaching profession, and every year there are also many students on campus who teach or serve as tutors. This course hopes to help students who intend to engage in the teaching profession have a preliminary understanding of issues related to the teaching profession, prepare themselves mentally for becoming teachers, and teach some basic teaching skills. _x000D_
Through classroom discussions, group assignments, independent research, and observation of teaching videos, students will explore the various problems they will encounter as teachers, as well as the basic qualities and skills they should possess. The specific objectives of this course are as follows:_x000D_
1. Understand the requirements and pathways for the teaching profession;_x000D_
2. Understand our country’s school system and student situation;_x000D_
3. Form a teacher’s educational philosophy and feasible curriculum types; _x000D_
4. Master basic instructional design and classroom management skills;_x000D_
5. Clarify basic scientific research methods;_x000D_
6. Pay attention to hot issues in education and have an international teaching perspective. _x000D_
Curriculum Principle: One of the roles of teacher education is to help students learn to change from a student perspective to a teacher perspective to examine teaching and school education. Through this process, students refine and summarize their own educational experiences and concepts, and finally form scientific and feasible teaching concepts. Teaching is a complex activity, and teachers need to constantly learn from their own educational experiences and other teaching theories. This course can provide guidance and orientation for prospective teachers who are about to enter the teaching field. Therefore, the overall positioning of this course revolves around the following issues:_x000D_
1. Do I want to be a teacher? _x000D_
2. What do teachers usually do and what problems do they encounter? _x000D_
3. Am I interested in overcoming these problems and benefiting my students through my efforts? _x000D_

Name: Analysis of Contemporary Literary Classics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects the most classic and important works from the many literary works of contemporary Chinese literature and conducts a close reading of the texts. In order to improve the text reading ability of Chinese students and enhance their understanding of contemporary Chinese literature.

Name: Virgil's Aeneid
Prerequisite: Read Homer best, if not. In the course of the course, some chapters of Homer's poem are required. Section
Introduction: Virgil is one of the core courses of the modules of the course “Western Civilizations” at the University of Central Mount University's Boya College, and, together with courses such as “Homma Spoken” and “Dindin”, forms the course series of Western epic traditions. The “Virgir” course, which read the text of the Eneñas, looked at important omissions of past generations, especially modern times, and echoed the acceptance of this epic in the history of Western literature. The course aims to achieve three objectives: one to understand Virgil's writing purpose and to understand some of the basic facts and characteristics of ancient Roman civilization; the other to gain a general knowledge of Virgil's history of interpretation and criticism, to understand the development of Western classical academic research in the near modern era; and the other to understand Virgil's fundamental influence on Western literature from the point of view of his literary history.

Name: Dante and the Divine Comedy
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of European literature or Western philosophy
Introduction: This course aims to provide a close reading of Dante's great epic poem and the landmark work of medieval literature, The Divine Comedy. The course will cover many related issues, such as Dante's experience as a poet and an exile, the poet's use of "allegorical writing", and his thoughts on issues such as love, luck, poetics, and politics. By reading the key chapters of "Inferno", "Purgatory" and "Celestia", students will not only grasp the historical and cultural background of "The Divine Comedy", but also grasp the profound connection between this work and the history of classical poetry and thought.

Name: Language and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is an optional course for senior Chinese students in Chinese specialties and deals primarily with the relationship between language and culture from a methodological perspective. It is divided into three dimensions: the universality of languages and the commonality of cultures; the relativity of languages and cultures; and the role of languages as the main vehicle of culture in its interpretation. Language analysis explains complex cultural phenomena. The basic approach to the discussion of linguistic and cultural theory is analysed, mainly in the context of typical examples, through which students are able to interpret and address some of the linguistic and linguistic-related issues in their own relevant areas. These include: Language and culture are the same - the meaning of the origin of languages in the course of human origin; the differences between human and animal languages; the universality of human languages and common features of human behaviour; and the African hypothesis of human origin in terms of its origin, linguistic polarization and linguistic contact. Linguistic and cultural relativism - mechanisms for the formation of linguistic differences; a repertoire of Saarcher Wolf's hypotheses; the process of interaction of languages and thinking; the relationship between different languages and different modes of thinking, different cultures and spiritualities; and language as an important window of interpretation of thinking. Linguistic philosophy - linguistic analysis of British-American analytical philosophy; linguistic analysis of European interpretations of philosophy; position of language analysis in philosophical research. The expansion of language and culture is linked to the spread of language and culture; the expansion of language and culture; the contraction of language and culture; and the extinction of language and culture. Studies on endangered languages. The relationship between language and literature - the relationship between differences in language structure and forms of literature; differences in linguistic rhythm and differences in literary and musical characteristics. Thesis of linguistic and cultural bonds - the relationship between language and ethnicity; language is the most important evidence of national identity; linguistic homogeneity and national identity; the contribution of language to the maintenance of culture; the social variation of languages and the classification of social groups; the contribution of linguistic fossilization; and the re-establishment of prehistoric culture in combination with linguistic, archaeological and ethnographic evidence. Languages and science - languages and computers; languages and mathematics; languages and logic. Text and Culture - The Role of Words in Human Culture; Two Text Systems; The Relationship between Chinese and Chinese Language Culture.

Name: History of the Chinese Imperial Examination System
Introduction:
Basic purpose: To enable undergraduate students with a basic knowledge of Chinese general history to gain a deeper understanding of China’s modern history by understanding the imperial examinations that spanned 1,300 years. _x000D_
_x000D_
Six parts: _x000D_
1. An overall introduction to the imperial examination in ancient China. Focus: Long-term plausibility. _x000D_
2. The provisions of the imperial examination system and its evolution. Focus: The context of evolution. _x000D_
3. The role of imperial examinations in political life. Focus: Bureaucratic career. _x000D_
Fourth, the role of the imperial examination in social life. Focus: Regional differences. _x000D_
5. The role of imperial examinations in cultural life. Focus: Literary appearance. _x000D_
Sixth, two aspects of the research on the history of imperial examinations are introduced. Focus: Interpretation of traditional historical materials.

Name: Interpreting Ming and Qing Historical Sources
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to gain an in-depth knowledge and understanding of Ming and Qing society through interpreting historical materials; at the same time, it trains students' ability to read historical materials and understand the exact significance of historical materials from two aspects: philology and historical materials. Historical materials are selected from records, regulations, edicts, memorials, official documents, local chronicles, anthologies, notes, contracts, etc. from the Ming and Qing dynasties to understand and master the status of historical materials in the Ming and Qing dynasties. The course uses philological methods to interpret historical materials, and strives to raise research topics in the specific interpretation of historical materials. The teaching method is mainly course lectures, supplemented by online course forum discussions.

Name: International Legal Practice
Introduction: Jones Day is an international law firm operating in most commercial and financial centers around the world. This course is a lawyer practice course jointly offered by Jones Day and Peking University Law School. It aims to introduce the cutting-edge business of Jones Day to law students so that students can have a comprehensive understanding of international lawyer practice and make up for the lack of theoretical education in law schools. The course is divided into eight lectures, covering mergers and acquisitions, capital markets, antitrust, intellectual property, overseas financing, network security, legal compliance and other fields. The course consists of two parts: lectures in class and Q&A after class. Barristers will take students to analyze practical cases to effectively improve students' legal research and analysis levels.

Name: Interpreting Key Texts of Classical Scholarship
Prerequisite: Basic ability to read and write.
Introduction:
1. Starting from a certain basic classic of Confucianism (this time it is "The Book of Songs"), gain a more specific understanding of the characteristics of Confucianism in the Han Dynasty and even Chinese Confucianism. _x000D_

      Since the 18th National Congress of the Communist Party of China, the Communist Party of China has used great political courage and wisdom to propose the overall goal of improving and developing the socialist system with Chinese characteristics and promoting the modernization of the national governance system and governance capabilities. Name: Modern Chinese History Exercises

Introduction: This course is taught to undergraduate students majoring in Chinese history. Students are required to have basic historical knowledge such as modern Chinese history and modern world history. This course carries out small class teaching in the form of data research, reading discussion, and paper discussion.

Name: Mathematical Economics
Prerequisite: calculus, linear algebra, probability theory and mathematical statistics
Introduction: This course provides a mathematical foundation for macroeconomics and microeconomics at the undergraduate level. The course consists of three parts: (1) We first introduce basic mathematical analysis theory and static optimization theory. This course aims to lead students to read classic texts of Western literature since the 19th century, grasp the development trend of Western literature during this period, and become familiar with and use a variety of literary research methods. The selected genres include novels, poetry, and dramas, and the English works encourage students to read the original texts.

Introduction:

The basic objectives of the course are: (i) to teach the Italian Renaissance Age from the historical and Historic point of view in order to change the pattern of teaching of the existing monocultural history; (ii) to teach the major issues of Italian Renaissance in order to gain a comprehensive understanding of the glorious achievements of the Italian Renaissance Age; (iii) to continue to focus on the subject of artistic history, but not limited to the teaching of individual artists and their works, but also to describe the whole process and the overall landscape of Italian Renaissance Art development; (iv) to explain that artistic creation and production are the fundamental points of view of the Italian culture, so as to appreciate the achievements of Italian culture from the artistic perspective; (v) to explore the ideas, style and patterns of artistic creation, especially in connection with academic research, and to foster original thinking; (vi) to explain the glamour of Italian culture in the context of his own personal experience in Italy; and (vii) to focus on the place of Italian Renais Renais in the exchange of Central and Western cultures and promote the reflection of Western cultures.

The curriculum features: 1, which comprehensively covers the key issues of Italian Renaissance; 2, which highlights the overall contribution of Italian Renaissance; 3, which teaches the history of Renaissance with the first-hand experience in Florence and Rome; 4, which enriches the classroom by using visual materials such as graphic art pictures to the greatest extent possible; and 5, which provides information on Italian study abroad.

Name: Topics in the History of Western Political Thought
Introduction: This course aims to explore important works, figures, issues, concepts, trends of thought, schools, etc. in the history of Western political thought, guide students to deeply study classic works of Western political thought, understand Western civilization through the development of political thought, and use relevant political theories to think about political and historical issues. Name: Entrepreneurial Thinking
Introduction:
The ups and downs of the entrepreneurial wave provide opportunities to test and reflect on popular entrepreneurial methodologies and the entrepreneurial thinking on which they are based. The continued in-depth study of relevant research also provides insights for learning and understanding the general laws of new enterprise creation and growth. This course aims to use theoretical propositions, analytical frameworks, cognitive models and empirical research findings accumulated from domestic and foreign entrepreneurship-related research as well as entrepreneurial success and failure practices to help students learn and understand the essential characteristics of entrepreneurs’ thinking patterns and corresponding thinking abilities, master the transition from the growth path of managers to the growth path of entrepreneurs, and then grow into high-potential entrepreneurs. Action strategies improve the probability of a successful encounter between the inevitability of entrepreneurial opportunities and the contingency of entrepreneurial actions, thereby being able to get rid of the fate of serial entrepreneurial success and the possibility of continuous growth, and ultimately lay the academic foundation for students' thinking styles, thinking abilities and action strategies to enhance the well-being of others, achieve career ideals, and realize personal value through innovation and entrepreneurship. _x000D_
This course believes that entrepreneurial activities are a personalized journey of exploration with commercial motivations, an innovative journey to build a new way of connecting valuable actions and results, and a journey of learning and growth in which one reflects on oneself while understanding the world around him. Therefore, the course content will include the basic theoretical perspectives, thinking model framework and action strategies involved in a complete entrepreneurial enterprise and its growth process. Based on the understanding framework and analytical logic of entrepreneurial enterprises, the course will help students evaluate their entrepreneurial potential from the trinity of trait theory, action theory and cognitive theory, discover and develop their own entrepreneurial opportunities from a strategic perspective based on market positioning and a cognitive perspective based on pattern recognition, understand the challenges and opportunities of successful business models from the two levels of system construction and model innovation, and build the management philosophy of entrepreneurial organizations and innovative leadership to cope with growth challenges from the balance of causal logic and effect logic. At the same time, this course is aimed at the characteristics of the undergraduate group. The teaching content will take into account a reasonable balance between the practical experience of entrepreneurial enterprises and the findings of entrepreneurial academic research, aiming to improve students' independent learning abilities in related fields, so that they can continue to improve their entrepreneurial thinking level and entrepreneurial action capabilities with the times in the future, and lay a solid foundation for coping with unknown challenges in the future. _x000D_

Name: History of Thailand
Introduction:
Thai History is a compulsory course for Thai language and culture students, aimed at providing them with an overview of Thai history and a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding of Thai society.

The course system teaches the history of Thai migration from the Thai people before the rise of the south-central peninsula to the historical development of the Sukotai dynasty, the Ayotoye dynasty, the Twauri dynasty and the Bangkok dynasty. It describes important figures and events in Thailand ' s history, as well as the political, economic, cultural and country-to-country exchanges in Thailand at all times.

Name: Studies in Early Chinese Jade Artifacts
Introduction:
The development of jade in China has a long history since the Neolithic Age. It is the essence of Eastern culture and an important basis for understanding the emergence of Chinese civilization. There have long been records of "using jade as weapons" in "Yue Jueshu"; the archaeological community has also been hotly discussing China's "Jade Age"; exquisite jade is undoubtedly an outstanding representative of material culture in the prehistory of China and the world, especially in different regional civilizations from the Neolithic Age to the Bronze Age in China. The role of jade in society can be seen It plays an important role in the process of complexity; even "rituals", which gradually became the core content of traditional Chinese society in historical periods, originally had the original meaning of "a vessel for holding jade to worship gods and humans" (according to Wang Guowei's "Explanation of Ritual"), so "the ancients used jade in rituals" - this shows the special significance of jade in Chinese etiquette and ethical culture. _x000D_
      To understand the origin and characteristics of early Chinese civilization and even Chinese culture, jade is an unavoidable and most important research object. In the Neolithic to Bronze cultural stages, jade was not only one of the most outstanding material achievements, it was also an indicator of the scale and level of a settlement, a carrier of cultural dissemination and exchange, and a major reflection of social beliefs and spiritual fields. _x000D_
      This course will systematically introduce and sort out the regional and epochal characteristics of jade articles from the Neolithic Age to the Early Bronze Age in China, the use and circulation of jade articles in early social culture, and its role in the origin and development of early Chinese civilization. _x000D_
      Through the study of this course, students can become familiar with the basic characteristics of early Chinese jade and the development context of the jade handicraft industry, understand the importance of jade in building social order and early belief practices, and understand China's unique jade cultural tradition from the perspective of the formation and development of civilization. _x000D_

Name: Topics in German Classical Legal Philosophy
Introduction:
German classical philosophy is another unsurpassable ideological peak in the history of Western philosophy after ancient Greek philosophy. German classical philosophers represented by Kant, Fichte, Schelling and Hegel have successively pushed the approach of critical and speculative philosophy to the peak, and intensively created a series of systematic ideas of speculative idealism, which are unique in the entire history of philosophy. German classical philosophy is characterized by its comprehensiveness and systematicity. The representative philosophers of that period gave their own profound insights in almost all philosophical fields, including of course the fields of law and state philosophy. The first part of Kant's "Metaphysics of Morals" "Metaphysical Principles of the Doctrine of Rights", Fichte's "Foundations of Natural Right" and Hegel's "Principles of the Philosophy of Right" have all become classic works in the history of legal and political philosophy, and constitute increasingly important ideological resources in contemporary political philosophy debates. This course plan takes the legal philosophy of Kant, Fichte and Hegel as the theme, and guides students to systematically read relevant works to understand the profound insights of these philosophers on rights, politics and the state. _x000D_
The first semester of the course focuses on Kant’s legal and political philosophy.

Name: Studies in Marx's Theory of the State
Introduction:
The purpose of this course is to focus on the relationship between state and society, and on the basis of exploring the relationship between Marx and the theory of natural rights, which was the mainstream political philosophy trend in the past two centuries, to clarify Marx's unique position on major issues such as civil society and the political state, state and class, state and revolution. _x000D_
      In modern natural rights doctrines, especially the liberal state arguments represented by Locke and Kant, considerations of ownership occupy a central position. The purpose of people establishing a country is to protect ownership and freedom as a condition. This has almost become a unanimous consensus among modern liberal state theories. From the perspective of the state argument of the doctrine of natural rights, private ownership can only be obtained by individuals through submission to the political community. However, judging from the historical evolution of ownership forms, private ownership is not the first form of ownership under the state. On the contrary, it is the individual's possession of things that is established by getting rid of the control of the community. In modern countries, through the recognition and protection of private ownership at the constitutional level, state power is actually isolated from the field of material production and communication. This field thus obtains a status of independent existence parallel to the state on the surface. This is the separation of civil society and the political state. For the first time in the history of thought, Hegel conceptually clearly defined and named such a modern historical phenomenon and criticized it. Marx's thinking on national issues began precisely with the criticism of Hegel's philosophy of law, but the criticism did not make him return to the liberal position. Although Marx accepted Hegel's basic judgment about the separation of civil society and the political state, his understanding of this separation was not entirely the same as Hegel's. This led him to point his finger more at the bourgeois state order and the liberalism that defended it after criticizing Hegel. From the perspective of Marx, although the theoretical propositions of Hobbes and others are different, they are consistent in terms of methods, that is, they all understand and construct political society based on the abstract rights provisions of people. _x000D_
      According to this method, the ideal social state is one in which human natural rights are fully realized. Of course, according to some thinkers, natural rights still need to undergo some kind of transformation process. The essence of this method is to construct an abstract political society based on abstract people's abstract rights. In this model of constructing a common human lifestyle, people's real material life, that is, civil society, is not included in the scope of examination. For most natural rights theorists, a country that fully realizes human rights and freedoms is a just country. As for the status of individuals with complete rights and freedoms in the political sense in real life, it will logically not damage the perfection of the country, because this is outside the political field and is located in civil society. It is a social or personal matter that state power cannot interfere with. Marx's criticism of national and political issues begins with the criticism of this method of thinking and its conclusions. In fact, such a critical perspective was first opened by Hegel, and Marx's later thoughts were deeply influenced by this. It can also be said that Hegel formed the direct intermediary between Marx and the natural rights doctrine of the 17th and 18th centuries. Although Hegel thoroughly criticized the previous doctrine of natural rights, his own political philosophy still formed part of the doctrine of natural rights. Therefore, Marx's criticism of Hegel's philosophy of law can still be regarded as a criticism of the doctrine of natural rights, and it is precisely through Hegel's criticism of the doctrine of natural rights. Through Er's criticism and the criticism of the natural rights theory of the 17th and 18th centuries, Marx gradually developed his own methods and concepts, thereby proposing a new understanding model of the relationship between state and society. In a sense, it can be said that Marx's entire political theory is based on this. _x000D_
      This course will take Marx's theory of state as its theme. It will guide students to read representative texts of the modern theory of natural rights that constitute Marx's ideological background, Marx's own texts on state issues, and Engels and Lenin's discussions on the state, in order to have a systematic and comprehensive understanding and mastery of Marx's state theory. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Ethnic Studies
Introduction: Ethnic issues are major social and political issues worldwide. Since the opium war, China has long been at risk of national secession, with separatist forces present in Tibet and Xinjiang and strongly supported by anti-China forces abroad. The development of “Taiwan independence” “Hong Kong independence” is also notable. At the international level, following the break-up of the Soviet Union, Yugoslavia and the emergence of separatist movements in Canada, Spain and Scotland, it was necessary for university students in the North to systematically understand the basic trends in the development of ethnic relations at home and abroad, the major issues that existed, the theoretical and social contradictions associated with national separatism. The course will provide a systematic introduction to: (1) China's traditional group identity, including the basic concepts of “summer resolution” of “underworldism” “and the different” and the history of development formed by the Chinese nation; (2) the concept of nationalization from the West after the opium war, which was translated into Chinese “ethnicity”, the study and research of the theory of “ethnicity” during the late Chinese-Republican era; (3) the Chinese Government's official ethnic theory, nation-building and ethnic policy in 1949; (4) the new trends in the evolution of Chinese ethnic relations since the reform and opening up of the open world; (5) the discussion of “ethnicism” in Chinese academia since 2000; (6) the major topics currently being linked to the improvement of ethnic relations: regional autonomy, bilingual education, preferential policies, regional differences in development, etc., the course will be a shallow one that will provide an opportunity for fundamental and external theoretical evolution related to “ethnicity”, as well as a direct reflection and policy adjustment in the face of the current intense debate in society and academia. It is hoped that, on the basis of truth and reason, students will be able to learn about national theory and practice at home and abroad in a systematic manner, and that the Chinese National Community will be truly intellectually entrenched and that the correct national, historical and national perspectives will be developed.

Name: Selected Readings from Marx's Economic Manuscripts of 1857-1858

It is an ideological station from the "Communist Manifesto" to "Das Kapital". It is a "theoretical laboratory" that fully displays Marx's philosophical thinking process and research methods. It has a significant and far-reaching influence in the current international Marxist philosophy community. Through the study of the "Outline", this course will provide an in-depth understanding of Marx's ideological process and grasp of the logic of capital, master important concepts and basic principles in Marx's philosophy such as materialization, abstraction, labor force, and social form, and understand Marx's profound insights into modern society.

Name: Approaching German-Speaking Countries through Their Literature
Prerequisite: The language of the German-speaking country is closer to that of the German-speaking country, and students meet the European standard German A1
Introduction:
In response to the call of the Ministry of Education, the School of Foreign Languages ​​at Peking University has launched an experimental class for cultivating top-notch “multilingual international talents” students starting from September 2019. This project is aimed at top-notch students in various majors with excellent English proficiency, excellent professional academic performance, and sufficient learning ability to strengthen their second and third foreign languages. At the same time, they will consolidate their English proficiency and strive to reach the level of their mother tongue, so as to cultivate the outstanding talents of "one proficiency, multiple skills" and "one specialty, multiple abilities" that the country urgently needs. _x000D_
This course is the core course of the first semester of the German part of the program and is offered for the first time. _x000D_
Through this course, students should have a solid foundation in second foreign language language and literature, have a comprehensive understanding of the culture, history and political status quo of the country where they are learning the language, have good foreign language application skills, and be able to engage in professional foreign language teaching, international cultural exchanges and general scientific research. In addition, graduates of this major should have the ability to learn across majors and cultures. They should not only excel in the field of foreign language majors, but also become experts in various fields by virtue of the rigorous, systematic and formal theoretical and skill training they have received. _x000D_
In addition to achievements in culture and knowledge, students should also have the ability to learn and progress throughout their lives, possess high-quality thoughts and hearts, and have an ethical attitude toward life. At the same time, they should also be able to understand, accommodate, and appreciate various cultural differences, have a broad vision, and become outstanding talents who promote the harmonious development of society. _x000D_
In this course, by studying the original German textbooks, you will develop a more systematic understanding of the German language, acquire the basic abilities of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation, and lay a solid foundation for eventually reaching the intermediate German level according to European language standards.

Name: Approaching the Spanish-Speaking World through Its Language
Introduction: This course is the core course of the multilingual international talent experimental class. It is designed to allow students to have a preliminary understanding of Spanish, master the pronunciation and basic grammatical features of Spanish, and conduct elementary text reading.

Name: Approaching the Spanish-Speaking World through Its History
Introduction: This course is the core course of the multilingual international talent experimental class. It is designed to allow students to have a certain understanding of Spanish, master the grammatical features of Spanish, and perform elementary to intermediate text reading.

Name: Approaching the Spanish-Speaking World through Current Affairs
Introduction: This course is the core course of the multilingual international talent experimental class. It is designed to allow students to have a certain understanding of Spanish, master the grammatical features of Spanish, and perform elementary to intermediate text reading.

Name: Finance and Society
Introduction: This course introduces financial institutions and financial markets from a social and historical perspective, helping students understand the principles of the financial world and explore the deep connection between finance and social development. This course will review the development process of financial institutions and markets in the world and China, sort out the impact of contemporary finance on all aspects of society, and look forward to the future trends of financial and social development. This course will explore the financial problems that college students encounter in real life and use real-life examples to demonstrate financial principles.

This course is dedicated to carefully studying and analyzing medieval texts, reconstructing and reflecting on the philosophical arguments and insights in them, in order to gain a direct understanding of the general form of medieval philosophy. In various traditions of medieval philosophy, whether it is the Byzantine, Islamic, Jewish or Latin world, philosophical reflection and religious belief are inseparable, and Aquinas is no exception. Selecting the "Summa Theologiae", an introductory book written for medieval theological students, will help us understand the Christian background of Latin philosophy while also deeply grasping the relevant rational arguments and having a clear understanding of the power and limits of reason in revealed religion. _x000D_

Name: China and Africa: Diplomacy, Development and Migration
Prerequisite: This course is aimed at general education and is not subject to prior curriculum requirements. It is so stated.
Introduction: Over the past two decades, China ' s influence on the African continent has grown rapidly, triggering controversy in national and international academia, policy circles and the mass media. Will China “take over” Africa? Is China's practice in Africa called “new colonialism”? Is China a predator of African resources? How have African countries and the general public responded to the opportunities and challenges presented to them by China? Can China ' s development experience and development model apply to Africa and help it achieve substantial development? Are Chinese racists? These are very difficult and challenging issues. In order to help answer such questions, the course focuses on three different but interrelated topics of Central Africa ' s interaction and seeks to achieve a more complete and objective understanding of Central Africa ' s relations as a new phenomenon of historic importance in the globalization process. These three topics are diplomacy, development and migration. Further, by exploring these three topics, the course focuses on three different dimensions of Central African interaction, namely, the State (including large State enterprises), the private sector (especially small and medium-sized enterprises) and the general migrant population from the lower strata of society. Central African relations as a phenomenon are often misinterpreted. This misinterpretation is partly due to the fact that observers tend to interpret China or Africa unilaterally as a single actor, ignoring the complexities and diversity within “China” or “Africa” itself and the patterns of Central Africa's interaction resulting from such complexity and diversity. On the other hand, over the past two decades, the growing influence of China in Africa has raised the alert and even hostility of Western countries; at the same time, we have seen a marked lag in our perception of relations relative to their rapid development. As a result, there have been many distorted, false or even malicious reports and manifestations of Central African relations in the media and popular culture, with extremely negative political, social and cultural implications. In order to avoid misinterpretation of Central African relations and to enhance our understanding of China ' s rise and globalization, we will focus our study on the following four main areas: 1. History of Central African interaction and status of Central African relations Various “myths” and rumours about China in Africa Economic and social development effects of China on the African continent 4. The important role of migration and human interaction in Central African relations Through this course, students are expected to develop into better observers of international development and globalization. In this course, academic, media and video materials are used to present a comprehensive picture of developments and challenges in Central African relations and to torture such fundamental concepts as development, migration, race, gender, culture and capitalism. These insights and reflections will not only help students to learn the subject, but will also benefit students in their daily lives outside the academic sphere.

Name: China and International Law
Introduction:
International law and international relations are inseparable. The relationship between China and the international legal system is a core issue in understanding China's relationship with the world. Since the reform and opening up, China has signed and participated in the formulation of a number of international treaties and played an increasingly active role in international organizations. This is a key measure for China to join the world system and participate in the construction of the international legal system; the international legal system has also profoundly affected the development of China's political economy. With the rise of China's international status in recent years, international legal issues represented by the South China Sea arbitration case and the Sino-US trade war have become urgent challenges facing China's diplomacy. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is offered to non-law majors. It adopts the interdisciplinary perspective of international law and international relations and focuses on teaching the core concepts of international law, core elements of the international legal order, the complex interaction between international law and international relations, China and international trade law, the Belt and Road Initiative and international investment law, China and the International Court of Justice, and international legal issues in Sino-US relations. The course aims to help students become familiar with the core concepts of international law, establish an objective understanding of China's participation in the international legal system based on historical facts, and help students understand China's international legal practices and international legal challenges through specific case studies. _x000D_

Name: Criminal Procedure Case Studies
Introduction: This course will provide a comprehensive analysis of the typical criminal cases, such as the Dupei Wu case, the Zhao Shui Hai case, the Niehui Bin case and the Lee Wei case, and will analyse the problems in the application of the procedure and the evidence so that the values, functions, structure, basic principles, the judicial system, the system of evidence, the proceedings and the mechanisms of redress can be explored in depth so that students are more aware of the legal provisions and the basic spirit of the system of criminal proceedings and evidence.

Name: Studies in the Chinese Insurance Market
Introduction: The topic of China's insurance market is a classified elective course for insurance majors. This course provides special discussions on hot issues in China's insurance market and key issues encountered in the reform and development of the insurance industry. This course has two characteristics: first, it focuses on integrating theory with practice; second, the topic selection is timely. The purpose of this course is to guide students to use the professional theories they have learned to analyze representative issues in the Chinese insurance market and achieve the effect of applying what they have learned.

Name: Foreign Economic History
Introduction: The course, which focuses on industrialization and takes the world economy into consideration, describes the development processes and experiences of major modern economies from the pre-industrial era to the present and provides a historical perspective on understanding the global economy.

Name: Organizational Economics
Introduction: The course is an introduction to organizational economics for graduate/doctoral students and senior undergraduate students. In the course of this course, we will present both the classic literature in the field of organizational economics and the latest studies at home and abroad. The course covered topics such as formal and informal incentive contracts, empowerment and communication, organization of the internal labour market, enterprise boundaries, and the role of managers. The study and discussion sessions of this course are based on theoretical models, supplemented by presentations of relevant experiences or experimental studies.
