Name: Introduction to Industrial Production
Introduction: This course has an open system, integrates engineering, economy, and society, intersects technology and industry, is compatible with domestic and foreign situations, integrates epistemology and methodology into engineering examples, integrates ideological education and cultivation education into business content, and focuses on cultivating students' thinking atmosphere. The course covers major industrial sectors such as energy, metallurgy, chemical industry, machinery, automobiles, electronics and emerging technology industries. It takes the basic laws of system science as a clue and uses students' team participation in engineering practice as a carrier to develop understanding and learning of the industry. The course adopts an organically advanced teaching model at three levels: classroom lectures, case studies and practical operations to enhance the teaching effect. Teachers' classroom case teaching is the mainstay, student teamwork and inquiry-based learning is the main body, and small-class team hands-on practice is the supplement. Students are guided to listen to lectures with a discussion mentality, use the classroom as a guide to develop course content through reading, practice and cooperative inquiry, deepen their understanding of systematic scientific thinking, and cultivate students' team spirit, independent learning ability and innovative thinking.

Name: Public Organization Management
Introduction: The management of public organizations is the core basic course in international public administration, sociology, economics and so forth. It is a typical interdisciplinary field of research involving a multidisciplinary category of social sciences. The course will build on the international frontier and will systematically teach key elements of the structure of public organizations, incentives, leadership development and development, and decision-making. The course emphasizes the ability to train students to combine theoretical knowledge with empirical phenomena, requiring, on the one hand, that students be able to use the knowledge they have learned to explain empirical phenomena and, on the other hand, that students be able to abstract problems and theories from empirical phenomena. Through this course, students should have a solid theoretical foundation, a strong sense of logic and a high-quality empirical research.

Name: Cross-Cultural Communication
Introduction: With globalization, the Internet, and the general shrinking of time and space, cross-cultural communication has become a necessity in people's daily lives. This course is designed to explore different aspects of intercultural communication and cultural differences: family life, social relationships, workplace, government, education, gender, romance, and religion. In exploring these themes, we will strive for personal self-reflection, practical experience, and understanding of connections to larger social structures.

Name: Chinese Management (I)
Introduction: The goal of this course is to help you understand important management topics in a Chinese context or working with Chinese people. You will study concepts, theories, research findings and successful management examples relevant to this area. You will learn from lectures, your classmates, and your own exploratory learning activities. This course requires students' highly interactive classroom participation, as well as exploration outside the classroom.

Name: Management Science and Information Management
Introduction:
This course consists of two parts. The first section highlights the importance of information technology and information management in organizations. Part II focuses on data, models and decisions in organizations_x000D_
In the first part, we will focus on the unique characteristics and managerial implications of information technology and management, and how managers can use them to improve business processes (or create new business models), increase customer satisfaction, and gain strategic advantage over competitors. It is worth mentioning that with the rapid development of China's economy, China's infrastructure and application technology are also developing rapidly. In this course, we will introduce and discuss China's performance in information evolution. Examples include macro data and company cases, and will be compared with foreign cases. _x000D_
Part II: (1) enable students to master the basic principles and methods related to data, models, and decision-making in management science; (2) cultivate scientific management thinking ability; (3) skillfully use computers to manage data and solve models; (4) have the ability to solve decision-making problems faced in business management. This part will use EXCEL as a modeling tool to improve students' EXCEL skills. _x000D_

Name: Economic History
Introduction: Economic history is a branch of economics. This course focuses on the transformation of modern China, combines classic research and cutting-edge literature, and examines Chinese history from an economics perspective. The course content specifically includes two parts. First, it introduces the economic facts and systems of Chinese history, including per capita income levels, productivity, technological progress, fiscal systems, markets, monetary and financial systems, etc. Second, it discusses modern China’s response and economic performance under the impact of the West.

Name: Chinese Management (II)
Introduction: The goal of this course is to help you understand important management topics in a Chinese context or working with Chinese people. You will study concepts, theories, research findings and successful management examples relevant to this area. You will learn from lectures, your classmates, and your own exploratory learning activities. This course requires students' highly interactive classroom participation, as well as exploration outside the classroom.

Name: Business Ethics and Social Responsibility
Introduction: CSR and business ethics are a practice-oriented discussion course. Through reading and discussion, students will deepen their understanding of the complexity of the institutional and social environment in which enterprises operate. Understanding the underlying meaning of corporate social responsibility, evaluation systems, and how to integrate corporate social responsibility strategies with the development of corporate business. In addition, the course will include case studies to understand the basic content of business ethics, the principles of judgement and the basic ways of dealing with business ethics issues. Through course learning, students will have knowledge of (1) the basic categories of responsibility and ethical dilemmas that managers or senior managers will face; (2) an in-depth understanding of the content of these responsibilities and how to balance in practice the requirements of different responsibilities and the basis for ethical choices; (3) the responsibilities of enterprises and business managers towards different stakeholders (investors, customers, Governments, employees, society); and (4) how to use the basic knowledge they have learned to address ethical issues related to these responsibilities in practice.

Name: General Bengali (III)
Introduction: Bengali belongs to the Indian language family of the Indo-European language family. It is the official language of Bangladesh and the Indian states of West Bengal and Tripura. It is spoken by about 270 million people and is the seventh largest language in the world. Rabindranath Tagore, the famous Indian poet and writer, wrote literature in his native language, Bengali. One of the earliest documents in Bengali is the 10th-century Buddhist poem Chaliya Gita (Jorjabod). Bengali literature is splendid. In addition to Rabindranath Tagore, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature, famous Bengali writers include Panjim, Nazrul, Saurod and other literary greats. Learning Bengali is an important way to understand Bengali literature in Eastern literature.

Name: General Bengali (IV)
Introduction: Bengali belongs to the Indian language family of the Indo-European language family. It is the official language of Bangladesh and the Indian states of West Bengal and Tripura. It is spoken by about 270 million people and is the seventh largest language in the world. Rabindranath Tagore, the famous Indian poet and writer, wrote literature in his native language, Bengali. One of the earliest documents in Bengali is the 10th-century Buddhist poem Chaliya Gita (Jorjabod). Bengali literature is splendid. In addition to Rabindranath Tagore, who won the Nobel Prize for Literature, famous Bengali writers include Panjim, Nazrul, Saurod and other literary greats. Learning Bengali is an important way to understand Bengali literature in Eastern literature.

Name: Modern History of Asia, Africa and Latin America Exercises
Introduction: The course selects a number of original literature in English (which includes non-English translations) to guide and analyse major historical issues in the near-modern history of the non-Western and to guide students through history to learn the basics and research methods of the near-modern history of the non-Western.

Name: General History of China (Modern Period)
Introduction:
The content of this course mainly covers the history of the late Qing Dynasty (from the mid-Qing Dynasty to the Revolution of 1911). Lectures are given in the form of lectures, _x000D_
It uses more than a dozen special topics to summarize the entire history of the late Qing Dynasty and highlight the changing characteristics of Chinese society from tradition to modern times. _x000D_
Introduce the latest results of research on related issues to promote students' thinking about China's social development trends and their understanding of the people_x000D_
concern about the fate of the nation. Pay attention to knowledge, novelty and vividness.

Name: International Criminal Law
Introduction: International criminal law is a legal discipline that studies the norms of international criminal law. It is an interdisciplinary subject that not only involves knowledge of international law, criminal law and other legal disciplines, but also covers many aspects such as international politics and world history. International criminal jurisprudence covers the basic theory and practice of international criminal law. The main contents include "the foundation of international criminal jurisprudence", "general principles of international criminal law" and the types of international crimes stipulated in the Statute of the International Criminal Court such as genocide, crimes against humanity, war crimes and crimes of aggression. International criminal jurisprudence not only involves the knowledge of international law and criminal law, but also covers important views on international criminal jurisprudence in the world's major legal systems.

Name: Information Ethics and Privacy Protection
Introduction: Information ethics and privacy protection issues have become increasingly prominent in the era of big data and intelligence, such as racial discrimination hidden in data labels and classifications, the abuse of privacy by data profiling, the replacement and transcendence of people by intelligent systems, election manipulation in politics, and privacy violations involving the Internet of Things. This course will introduce students to various information ethics and privacy protection issues, and explore with students the possible business, political, social, and personal impacts of these issues. This course aims to train and improve students' independent thinking ability, so that students can master some critical thinking methods to consider information ethics and privacy protection issues in the era of big data and intelligence, so that students can think and reflect on these issues at a certain depth.

Name: Case Studies in Big Data Applications
Introduction:
Big data is widely used in various fields and has produced many successful cases. This course selects typical cases for in-depth analysis, and discusses the successful application and future development of big data in e-commerce, industrial manufacturing, intelligent transportation, urban management and services, public culture, scientific and technological information and other fields from the aspects of demand background, data resources, technical methods and functional applications_x000D_
This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduate students. _x000D_

Name: Management and Innovation of Knowledge Service Organizations
Prerequisite:
Need to begin with: information resource management base, library science overview
Better: Management principles, information services
Introduction: This course mainly teaches classic organizational management theories and innovation theories to senior undergraduates, and explores the development and interpretation of these theories in the context of public cultural institutions represented by libraries. It aims to guide students to understand management issues with strategic thinking and lay a certain theoretical foundation for students to engage in management work in organizations. The course mainly involves theories including four parts: organizational strategy, organizational structure, organizational capabilities and innovation management. The theoretical part of the teaching is completed by reading classic management literature, and focuses on discussing and analyzing the guiding significance of these theories to public cultural institutions. In addition, this course uses case studies to explore with students how to apply these theories in real scenarios of public cultural institutions, and to form more targeted new theories based on the particularities of public cultural institutions.

Name: Machine Learning
Prerequisite: Advanced mathematics, computational overview, Python program design
Introduction:
In April 2018, the "Artificial Intelligence Innovation Action Plan for Colleges and Universities" issued by the Ministry of Education clearly stated: "Accelerate research on core key technologies of new generation artificial intelligence such as machine learning." _x000D_
    This course is a core basic course for the big data management and application major. It mainly introduces the basic concepts of machine learning and commonly used machine learning technologies and methods, including: linear regression, cluster analysis, support vector machine, neural network, decision tree, Bayesian algorithm, ensemble learning, deep learning, etc. This course simultaneously plans a series of practical application cases corresponding to classic machine learning algorithms, which can train students' practical abilities. _x000D_
    There are three basic materials supporting this course: (1) Peking University MOOC course taught by the applicant: "Data Mining Algorithm and Practice"; (2) Textbook "Data Mining Algorithm and Practice" edited by the applicant, Peking University Press, September 2020 (to be published); (3) Case database in Peking University's "Big Data Analysis and Mining" training platform, for details, see: http://scielab.pku.edu.cn/datamining/

Name: Text Mining Techniques
Prerequisite: Linear algebra, probability statistics, data structure and algorithm, python data analysis
Introduction:
Papers, patents, reports, news, online reviews and other multi-source information are important sources and components of big data, playing an increasingly important role in data analysis and mining, and this information is mainly unstructured text. To analyze and mine this information, it is necessary to identify the characteristics of text information, establish a language computing model, use machine learning, especially deep learning, for training, identify text characteristics, and then analyze, understand and generate text. _x000D_
      This course takes unstructured text information as the main object, focusing on the technology, algorithms and platform tools of text analysis and mining. It specifically includes three modules. The first is the natural language processing module, including lexical analysis, syntactic analysis, and semantic analysis, focusing on language models, analysis processes and algorithms; the second is the text computing model, including text representation, deep learning language models, topic models, etc.; the third is text mining applications, including information extraction, text classification and clustering, network comment mining, etc. _x000D_
      This course is a required course for the "Big Data Management and Application" major and is also available as an elective course for students from other majors. This course is mainly offered to senior undergraduate students. _x000D_

Name: Data Visualization
Prerequisite: Python-related courses, or Python programming language
Introduction: Data visualization aims to convey and communicate information clearly and effectively through graphical means. This course teaches the principles of different data visualization methods, with special emphasis on choosing different visualization methods based on different data types. This course pays equal attention to theory and practice, and specifically includes three modules: (1) Theoretical and practical foundations of data visualization; (2) Visualization of different types of data; (3) Visual interaction and evaluation. In practice, this course mainly uses Python language to complete visualization tasks, and will also introduce a variety of visualization tools (software). This course is a required course for the "Big Data Management and Application" major, and is also a restricted elective course for other majors in the Department of Information Management. Students from other related majors are also welcome to take it as electives.

Name: Applied Quantitative Analysis
Prerequisite:
1. Advanced Mathematics D (low) or Probability Statistics, 2. Survey and Social Statistics
It's better to fix one and two at once.
Introduction:
Economic measurement is the most important and most common method in empirical research in social sciences. This approach can also be an important tool for empirical research in the area of information management. In the research tradition, however, the degree of application of this approach in the field of information management is still at a relatively early stage compared to other social science disciplines. The course therefore focuses on the specific application of econometric methods in research practice in the field of information management, in particular conceptual measurement, regression analysis and statistical extrapolation methods based on survey data, archival data or information measurement data, using an information management perspective.
Instead of focusing on basic theories and methods such as probability statistics, survey statistics, the course is based on a presentation of (1) the conceptualization of social sciences and its measurement issues, (2) the practical application of the meaning, principles and specific methods of regression analysis in the field of information management, in particular the practical application of the core issues of modelling, hypothetical testing, etc. (3) the five scenarios of regression analysis and the extension of each scenario in the practical application process, including non-linear models, internality issues, sample dependence issues, subvariant issues and longitudinal studies.
The course is intended for undergraduate students in the middle and upper grades of the studies and social statistics who have already been taught, and is conducted in a theoretical and practical combination. Theoretical part focuses on teacher lectures, supported by student discussions, and covers these core elements. The practice part is based on relevant data accumulated by teachers in the field of information management, with student analysis and practice dominated. The combination of the two can help students to master the methodology of applied measurement and analysis for information management.

Name: Basic English Listening
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is aimed at undergraduate students who have entered Module A in the English Placement Examination for Freshmen at Peking University. The textbooks used in the "Basic English Listening" course are the "New Edition of College English Listening and Listening Course" Second Edition Preparatory Level, and the "New Edition of College English Listening and Listening Course" Second Edition Volume 1. This course is designed to help undergraduates who have insufficient English listening training and weak English listening ability in high school to improve their English listening skills, master various listening skills, and consolidate the English skills learned in high school. It pays attention to both intensive listening and extensive listening, a two-pronged approach. Students are required to master about 2,000 listening vocabulary words in total and be able to understand English listening materials in different scenarios and topics at normal speaking speed. Also master some simple oral expressions. By studying this course, students can enhance their cross-cultural awareness and critical thinking ability, and at the same time cultivate students' independent learning habits, laying a solid foundation and preparation for entering the advanced stage of English learning. _x000D_
    Students are required to prepare before class and review after class according to the teaching arrangement, log in to the teaching platform for two hours of independent study every week, and complete the prescribed online listening exercises and homework on time; teachers supervise students' learning in class through listening training, intensive lectures, testing and other activities to improve students' English listening level. _x000D_

Name: Lecture Series on Topics in Anthropology
Introduction: This course is mainly lecture-based, supplemented by classroom discussions. The lectures are organized by inviting representative, original and pioneering scholars in the field of anthropology inside and outside the school to give lectures. Through the study of this course, freshmen undergraduates in anthropology can understand the basic characteristics of the discipline of anthropology, including some basic fields, topics, concepts and methods, understand the differences and commonalities between anthropology and other disciplines of social sciences, understand anthropology's research perspectives and research results on Chinese society and China's overseas perspectives, and lay the foundation for further systematic and in-depth study of anthropology.

Name: Visual Anthropology
Introduction: In 1939, Mr. Wu Wenzao established the "Yenjing University-Yunnan University Sociology Field Investigation Station" in Kunming. Later, due to the bombing of Kunming by Japanese military planes, it was moved to Kuixing Pavilion in Chenggong County, a suburb of Kunming, and was called "Kui Pavilion" by the academic circle. Later, outstanding scholars such as Fei Xiaotong, Tao Yunkui, Xu Xangguang, Shi Guoheng, Li Youyi, Tian Rukang, Gu Bao, Zhang Zongying, Hu Qingjun, Zhang Zhiyi, etc. all left their names in Kuige and completed a series of far-reaching research. Today, 80 years later, in order to continue the fine academic tradition and promote talent training and scientific research development and innovation; in order to promote interaction and complementation of advantages, the Department of Sociology of Peking University and the School of Ethnology and Sociology of Yunnan University decided to rebuild the "Yunda-Peking University Kuige Workstation". Through teaching and field practice workshops, they will focus on the theory, technology and practice of film and television anthropology, focus on borderland and ethnic construction, and enhance students' theoretical vision and field practice ability.

Name: Selected Readings in Marxist Anthropology
Introduction: To enable anthropology major students to understand the basic theories and perspectives of Marxist anthropology; they will select chapters that have important influence on anthropology from the original works of classic writers such as Marx and Engels, and will also read anthropological monographs in the Marxist tradition.

Name: Medical Anthropology
Introduction: This course is a professional-only elective course for undergraduate students majoring in anthropology. Aiming to expand relevant students' basic understanding of anthropology as a whole and related sub-disciplines, the course content is based on the introduction of the origin, historical development and different traditions of medical anthropology, supplemented by research examples, and combined with health, disease and medical issues in real society, guiding students to pay attention to the connection between society, culture and medical care, and grasp the main topics, theories and methods of medical anthropology.

Name: Fieldwork
Prerequisite:
Proposal to begin with “anthropological theory” and “anthropological methods”
Effective use of course information and the development of operational research programmes can only be achieved with a full understanding of the basic theory and research methods of anthropology
Introduction: This course is aimed at junior students majoring in anthropology. Through classroom lectures, reading reports and special discussions, students can understand and master the basic concepts and methods of anthropological fieldwork, initially form ideas for fieldwork and a practical research plan, and systematically formulate the number of readings and conduct a literature review based on the plan.

Name: Social Network Analysis
Prerequisite: None, but basic probabilities and simple regression analysis knowledge is required
Introduction:
Who are the key individuals in the group? How quickly do rumors spread on Weibo or WeChat? To what extent will the lockdown slow down the spread of COVID-19? How to understand "involution" from the perspective of social networks? Social network analysis has become a rapidly growing field of social science research and is increasingly attracting the interest of the general public and policy makers. With the advent of the Internet age, the popularity of online social networks, such as WeChat, Weibo, Facebook, Twitter, etc., has brought revolutionary changes to social network analysis. Whether it is interpersonal interactions in online communities, or interactions between offline and online social networks and their individual, organizational and social impacts, network analysis has increasingly become a basic perspective for understanding basic social issues such as social structure. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is an introductory course at the undergraduate level that emphasizes cross-discipline and aims to provide basic concepts and analysis techniques of social network analysis. In this course, students will learn 1) how to understand the basic concepts, theories and statistical models of social network analysis; 2) how to collect and analyze network data; 3) how to identify the basic network structure and understand and preliminary analyze the development and diffusion process of the network. Courses will incorporate examples from around us and important real-world issues. By studying this course, students will understand the basic concepts and models of networks, analyze social network data and interpret results, and conduct research using network analysis perspectives and techniques combined with real-life issues.

Name: Introduction to New Structural Economics (Part 2)
Introduction: This course mainly introduces systematically the program, principles and methods of new structural economics. The main content includes the structural paradigm revolution, theoretical system and practical application of new structural economics. The general outline of New Structural Economics teaches the structural revolution of neoclassical economics by New Structural Economics; the specific contents taught in the Introduction to New Structural Economics include: a brief economic history of China and the world and an overview of the diversity of economic structural arrangements and the complexity of economic systems, a brief history of economic thought and the ins and outs of New Structural Economics, the basic principles of New Structural Economics and the various subfields of New Structural Economics. The basic principles of new structural economics include: the supply principle of endowment structure, the demand principle of endowment structure, the relative price principle of endowment structure, the principle of optimal production structure (principle of comparative advantage), the supply and demand principle of production structure, the principle of cumulative causality of structural change cycle, the principle of viability, the principle of optimal transformation (reform), the principle of government taking advantage of the situation, and the principle of optimal government intervention. The contents of various fields of new structural economics include: new structural industrial economics, new structural finance, new structural labor economics, new structural spatial economics, new structural international economics, new structural business cycle theory, new structural environmental economics, and new structural institutional economics. The main contents taught in the practical part include: new structural economics applied research methodology and policy analysis tools, and their application in national development, regional development and enterprise development.

Name: Introduction to Classic Works of Lenin
Introduction: The course is based on the Lenin Selection as a teaching material, reading the basic works of Lenin in the areas of Marxist philosophy, political economics and scientific socialism.

Name: Developmental and Regenerative Biology
Prerequisite: Cell biology, molecular biology, human autopsy. Learn.
Introduction: Developmental and Regenerative Biology is based on cell/molecular biology and provides a detailed introduction to the basic knowledge of developmental and regenerative biology related to the regeneration of higher vertebrates. Developmental biology mainly introduces embryonic development, germ layer formation, body axis formation, and organ development; regenerative biology introduces the principles and latest progress of regenerative biology by organ.

Name: Nanomedicine
Introduction: Nanomedicine is an emerging edge discipline that uses the theories and methods of nanotechnology to carry out medical research and practice on the basis of traditional medicine and modern medicine. It is currently the most cutting-edge research and development hotspot in the field of biomedicine, with wide applications and clear industrialization prospects in the field of medicine and health. This course teaches and discusses the basic concepts and methods of nanomedicine as well as new developments and achievements in this field, including the preparation methods and clinical applications of nanomedicine carriers, nanodiagnosis (molecular diagnosis, nanoimaging), nanomaterials used in regenerative medicine and transplantation medicine, nanorobots for treatment, nanobiochips, nanobiosensors, nanobiocomputers. Characteristics and applications in biological analysis, especially in immunoanalysis, HIV detection, and applications in gene transport and genetic engineering.

Name: Empirical Strategy
Introduction: The objective of this course is to train students in empirical strategies used in economic research, with a focus on practical application of identification methods. This course will cover several identification issues. For each issue, the class will first briefly introduce the underlying theoretical problem, then detail on the empirical strategy, and finally look at some specific examples using this strategy. The empirical topics will span labor, health, education and program evaluation.

Name: The Civil Service System
Prerequisite: It is proposed to begin with the courses on " Principles of Administrative Sciences " and " The Government of China and Politics " , offered by the School of Government Administration.
Introduction:
Basic purpose: to enable students to understand the design principles of China’s civil service system, grasp the operation of the civil service system in real life and the direction of reform and development, and enhance students’ ability to analyze and explain human resource management phenomena in the public sector. _x000D_
_x000D_
Content introduction: This course is based on teaching the theoretical basis, main content and basic methods of China's civil service system. Through reading textbooks, expert lectures and classroom discussions, you can understand the basic knowledge of China's modern civil service system and the background and significance of my country's establishment of this system, and then analyze and explain the phenomenon of China's administrative activities, and deepen your understanding of personnel administration issues. Focus on introducing and discussing some core issues in the theory and practice of China's civil service system. In short, through the study of this course, students can have a more systematic understanding of the basic knowledge and basic theories of China's civil service system, and can more deeply summarize and grasp the development and management rules of the civil service system.

Name: Administrative Law Case Studies
Prerequisite: Administrative Law and Administrative Litigation Law
Introduction: The Study of Administrative Law Cases is an advanced subject of compulsory undergraduate studies on Administrative Law and Administrative Procedure, focusing on improving students ' understanding of the basics of administrative law through the study of practical judicial cases, while at the same time building their capacity to analyse and solve practical problems. The curriculum, while based on typical Chinese court cases, will appropriately integrate comparative law perspectives and provide some theoretical interpretation of cases.

Name: Introduction to E-Government
Introduction:
E-government is an interdisciplinary area of policy research. The rapid development of electronic information technology has not only profoundly changed the basic patterns of economic and social functioning, but has also given rise to the task and challenges of modern governance: on the one hand, responding positively to the new opportunities and problems presented by technology, and on the other hand, using information technology to improve and improve their own governance. As students in public administration and public policy, there is a need to understand and acquire basic knowledge of the use of new technologies in government governance to meet the challenges of the future society.
The curriculum is conducted in small classes, in a variety of forms such as teaching of knowledge, transfer of classes, practical research, etc. Includes two main modules.
i. Teaching of knowledge. It is structured around four knowledge points. First, the underlying theory and best practices of the use of information technology in government governance are discussed at the tool level. Second, government governance of information technology, especially in the frontier, is discussed at the client level. Third, a paradigm shift in governance in the context of informatization. Fourth, the application of information technology in governance and social science research.
II. Research practice. Each student may choose a specific or self-selected subject of digital field studies for research, and the teacher will mentor the student through a number of classroom discussions, which will lead to the completion of a study as a final thesis. In accordance with the actual conditions of each semester, teachers are sent to the relevant government departments or enterprises to study and study in order to increase students ' awareness of the situation.

Note: This course is intended for students in the public administration category and does not require a computer or related scientific and technical professional base.

Name: The Belt and Road Initiative: China's Original International Strategy
Introduction: The “Away the Way” initiative is China's long-term, original and important international strategy to realize the Chinese dream and the destiny of mankind. In the five years since President Xi Jinping's “One Way Forward” initiative, it has had a wide global impact. It will be an important strategy for China to provide international public goods and new forms of global leadership. The curriculum is designed to help students understand the essential nature of the “one-way” initiative, strategic decision-making processes, strategic implementation and strategic management. The course was divided into two main parts, the first focusing on the generation, development and content of the “one-way” initiative and the second on the implementation, evaluation and impact of the “one-way” initiative.

Name: The U.S. Constitution: How Lawyers Think through Case Law
Foundations of Modern Society: Culture and Civilization
Introduction: The concept of civilization and culture is the two key concepts that express the history of modern society, and the different research traditions of social theory have developed some important theoretical ideas and frameworks based on the interpretation of these concepts. The course will select a part of the key texts of both concepts in French-German social theory for study, lead students to an initial understanding of the content of the two concepts and the historical basis for their formation, based on theoretical research and discussion. The course also hopes to help students understand why the differences between the two have a strong resonance with China in recent times and why they continue in today ' s world.

Name: General Education First-Year Seminar: Political Reflections on the Modern State
Introduction: In all aspects of modern society, the "state" occupies an important position. But what is a modern state? How was it constructed historically? Why does the modern state have such a decisive power that cannot be ignored? This course aims to explore issues such as the constituent elements and driving forces of modern countries by reading modern and contemporary political philosophy works and combining them with empirical research results in social sciences, and on this basis, to gain a clearer understanding of the political development prospects of China and the world.

Name: Chinese Art and History through Along the River During the Qingming Festival
Introduction: This course begins with a famous Chinese painting and leads students to the art and Chinese culture. Understanding history by reading paintings.

Name: Principles of the University: Society and History
Introduction: The junior course at the Faculty of Pedagogical Studies, level 2018, is based on the literature of " The Evolution of Educational Thoughts " , based on the book " The Evolution of Educational Thoughts " , which is part of the literature on the conceptualization, institutional development, major historical transformation and contemporary issues of university education, discusses the relationship between education and religious, political and social evolution and reflects on the basic issues of university understanding of “humans” and their educational processes.

Name: Machiavelli: Modern Politics and Morality
Introduction: The junior course of class 2018 of the Institute of Pentecostal Studies on the relationship between modern politics and ethics through a comparative reading of political, historical and literary works in Makiavili

Name: Ancient Egyptian Language, Writing and Culture
Introduction: This course is an intermediate course in the classical form of the ancient Egyptian language, “Central Egyptian”, and a compulsory course in the literature of the ancient Egyptian culture. The course is divided into three parts, the first of which is general, beginning with an account of the history of the development of the ancient Egyptian language, its demise and the process of its reinterpretation, highlighting the value of research in the history of linguistic development as a 4,000-year-old ancient language, the importance of the ancient Egyptian language in understanding the history of the ancient Egyptian culture; and, secondly, an account of the academic history of the ancient Egyptian language studies, the important schools and their main contributions. The second part provides a systematic presentation of the basic structure of the Central Egyptian language, the main grammar phenomenon, the main ancient Egyptian literature and its related studies that have been discovered, and the major literature and representative writings for systematic evaluation of the main historical material. The third part is the interpretation of classic works, which, in addition to the grammatical assessment, are also interpreted in historical and literary terms.

Name: Images and Representations of the Spanish Civil War
Introduction:
This course takes a special war in the first half of the 20th century - the Spanish Civil War (July 17, 1936 - April 1, 1939) as a case study. Through careful reading and analysis of its film representation and historical narrative, it attempts to touch, understand and process the history and images of this "extreme era" of the 20th century. Through the discussion of image narrative - film medium, film language and film representation, we will show that similar films not only reproduce the special historical event of the Spanish Civil War, but as a sequence, they also become one of the beams of light that carries the spiritual history of the entire 20th century and the current social and cultural dilemma. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: First-Year Orientation and Adjustment Education
Prerequisite: It's an adaptation orientation course for fresh freshman students.
Introduction:
This course focuses on the typical psychological and behavioral processes of college freshmen during the admission process. The main purpose of this course is to explore effective methods to help college freshmen successfully complete their admission adjustment and career exploration, and gradually adapt to the requirements of college life through practice. This course is based on psychology-related theories, draws on the on-site intervention methods of new member organizations to adapt, and designs relevant courses around the four main aspects that affect the adaptation and academic performance of college freshmen: academic, life, social and career development. And through individual assignments and group discussions, students can initially grasp the rules of university life in action and form their own growth model. _x000D_
_x000D_
Part One Self-Awareness and Exploration_x000D_
Discover personal strengths. Through the discussion of self-understanding, we help college freshmen master the ability to explore and tap their own characteristics and advantages, and try to use their individual strengths to deal with more challenges and problems in college. _x000D_
Learning strategy construction. By analyzing and comparing the differences in performance of academic tasks between high school and college students. Know in advance the problems you may encounter in future studies and try to use the learned strategies to study and solve academic problems. _x000D_
_x000D_
Part 2 Academic Motivation and Creative Problem Solving_x000D_
Self-motivation and academic goal setting. By understanding and mastering the principles of goal setting and the five steps of goal management, you can learn to initially master effective methods of self-motivation and management. _x000D_
Decision-making skill development and problem solving. Understand the cognitive dissonance caused by decision-making, and deal with decision-making problems by learning the decision-making balance sheet, the six-step rational decision-making process, and the three-step dilemma method. _x000D_
_x000D_
Part 3 The development of social skills in college_x000D_
Improvement of social skills. By learning and building the skills of "speaking well" in general social interactions, we can improve the social confidence of college freshmen and master typical college social skills. _x000D_
Communication with university teachers. Learn relevant communication skills and methods by understanding the common issues and importance of communicating with university teachers. _x000D_
Communication with dormitory roommates. Predict the current situation of the dormitory in advance, learn the three-step method of dormitory communication, and deal with long-term problems in dormitory communication. _x000D_
_x000D_
Part 4 Personal Development and Initial Career Decision_x000D_
Time management in college. By learning time management tools such as the Pomodoro Technique and the Four Quadrants of Time, we help freshmen rationally arrange their college life. _x000D_
Cultivate self-control at Peking University. By understanding how “self” is developed and formed in the face of peer comparison and pressure. _x000D_
Stimulate personal development initiative. Focusing on the above topics learned, combined with their own individual advantages and problem-solving strategies, they can enhance college students' individual development initiative, thereby promoting psychological, social and emotional well-being, and helping individuals proactively cope with changes in various environmental demands and adapt to challenging situations. _x000D_

Name: Yue Fei: Methods and Practice of Historical Research
Introduction: As an example, the course will lead students to read and discuss, develop history resolution skills and awareness of problems, introduce basic tools and digital humanities tools, organize visits to the collections of the Department of Good Books of the National Library, and examine some of the historical monuments associated with the flight, with a view to obtaining a preliminary understanding of the basic research methods and practices of history.

Name: The International Political Economy of the Rise and Fall of Great Powers
Introduction: Taking the rise and fall of great powers in the international order as an entry point, this article introduces the subject development process and core academic logic of international political economics. Help students understand the evolution of the modern world system from the perspective of international political economics, gain access to relevant classic works, master interdisciplinary analysis methods, and have a preliminary understanding of international relations research ideas.

Name: Practical English: From Conversation to Public Speaking
College: Department of English Language and Literature
Introduction: The main purpose of the "Practical English: From Listening to Speaking" course is to help students gradually overcome hearing difficulties through planned, formal, strict and various forms of listening skills training, so that they can gradually master various English listening skills and understand listening materials of different genres and themes, thereby gradually improving students' listening comprehension level and cultivating students' ability to actually apply language. Through listening teaching, students can understand and master the oral expression forms and methods of common English genres and themes, correctly understand grammatical forms and material content, correctly understand the role and meaning of pronunciation, grammatical structures, and vocabulary in materials, and become familiar with typical language, commonly used vocabulary and expression forms that appear in common situations, thereby continuously improving their English listening and speaking levels, and further guiding students to use English. The ability to analyze problems critically, through the use of spoken English scenarios and English practice Analysis and research on combat abilities, guiding students to: 1) gradually master the breadth and depth of advanced spoken English; 2) cultivate students' high-level cross-cultural communication skills; 3) master the ability to express high-level topics with various complex English vocabulary; 4) and initially achieve the ability to use English for functional and practical public speeches, so that students can pass various exams containing English listening and speaking content during the school year, and lay a solid foundation for English expression for entering the workplace and entering society in the future.

Name: The Evolution of Wisdom
Introduction:
Wisdom is an advanced comprehensive ability of the biological nervous system, including perception, memory, knowledge, understanding, association and other functions. In the long history of biological evolution, the continuous complexity of the nervous system, the material basis, has endowed living organisms with increasingly complex and advanced forms of intelligence. So, what is wisdom? What is the difference between wisdom and intelligence? What kind of intelligence do animals have? How did intelligence evolve over hundreds of millions of years to develop into the complex forms we have today? At the individual level, how does wisdom develop and improve with growth? And, is it possible for us to create materialized intelligence based on artificial intelligence technology? _x000D_
With these questions in mind, this course will work with students who are interested in the topic of human and animal intelligence to study and discuss the evolution and development of intelligence, comparison of forms of intelligence among species, and the future of artificial intelligence development. As a freshman seminar class of Yuanpei College, this course will also lead students to read and discuss to cultivate critical thinking, train basic academic abilities, and form a preliminary understanding of the wisdom-related content of evolutionary and comparative psychology. _x000D_

Name: Structure and Properties: Reason and Intuition in Chemistry
Introduction: Chemistry is a discipline that studies the structure and properties of matter. The structure of matter determines its properties. Therefore, chemists often start their research by analyzing the structure of matter and obtain the properties of matter through reasonable reasoning, calculations and experiments. This course is based on the basic content of general chemistry, starting from the perspectives of atoms, molecules, crystals, intermolecular forces, solutions, chemical reactions, etc., leading students to read classic literature, thereby understanding the development history of chemistry, and cultivating students' ability to review literature. The focus of this course is to understand the thinking methods in scientific research through literature reading. The general chemistry content involved is relatively simple, and the thinking methods involved have a wide range of application fields, so it is also suitable for students with non-chemistry orientations.

Name: Freedom and Education: Rousseau's Emile
Introduction: This course led students to read and discuss the book " Amire " in Rousseau. Through careful reading and discussion of the text, teachers will try to guide their fellow students to understand the concepts of education and growth and reflect on the relationship between university education and self-development. The course will use a text-reading approach to help students to understand the book while training in reading and analysing the discussion of the classic text.

Name: Applications of Econometrics
Introduction:
Econometric methods are an indispensable tool for economic forecasting and decision-making, as well as modern economic management. Econometrics is also the most important part of the economics course_x000D_
_x000D_
This course introduces the econometric methods necessary to conduct empirical research in economics. It includes simple multiple regression, least squares method, instrumental variables, finite variable variable models, simultaneous equation models, time series, panel data processing and evaluation of policies and projects. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teach students how to use econometric special software (Stata) through economic examples, so that after students learn and understand the basic theories and basic methods of econometrics, they can skillfully use the software to perform parameter estimation, statistical testing, econometric testing of economic models, and further conduct economic structure analysis, economic forecasting and policy evaluation. Students can master the method of establishing econometric models to conduct empirical analysis of actual economic problems, improve their comprehensive analysis capabilities, broaden their knowledge horizons, and cultivate their ability to discover, analyze, and solve problems. _x000D_

Name: Classical Psychoanalysis: The Individual Life and Society in Case Histories
Introduction: This course is intended for the first year of the junior students of the Institute. The theme focused on psychiatric analysis and case studies in Freud. The course follows a system of discussion. The purpose of the course is to guide students to understand the basic lines and interests of classical psychoanalytical thinking. The course is structured according to the inner structure of the Freudian idea, with a shallow in-depth approach, which places its work in the history of European civilization, leading students to understand the theory of classical spiritual analysis from the standpoint of social and political theory.

Name: Physics Inquiry Based on the IYPT
Introduction: What is physics? Physicists believe that there are universal connections within nature, so they use a combination of experiments and theory to accumulate effective cognition of objective objects throughout nature. These cognitions must at least meet the requirements of falsifiability. Physicists' methods of cognition and the independent personality formed in the cognition process together constitute physical culture. Physics culture is a typical example of rational thinking and embodies an effective method of establishing cognition: it has a general significance that exceeds physics itself. One way to understand and learn about the culture of physics is to participate in physics inquiry. This course takes the topics in the International Young Physicists Championship (IYPT) as the research object, and guides students to form teams freely and complete the research process of 1-2 topics within one semester. By reading literature, designing and conducting experiments, communicating, discussing, and reporting, students can learn physical culture in practice and practice basic abilities such as reading, research, cooperation, and expression.

Name: The Physics of Life Processes: The Case of Bioelectricity
Introduction:
The life sciences are a frontier discipline with broad development prospects, with a wide cross-section of other areas. As two branches of natural science, life sciences and physics have long interacted and mutually reinforcingly played an indispensable role in human exploration of the world. Bioelectric research is a typical example of the intersection between life sciences and physics. The course demonstrates the wide application of physics methods in life sciences through lectures on bioelectric phenomena and their mechanisms. At the same time, the course sought to reflect the importance of experiments in life science research, in conjunction with the experiment “Measurement of Biotelecommunication”. In addition to the transfer of knowledge, the course is intended to give students a sense of common mental characteristics and research methods in the life sciences and physics, reflecting important trends in cross-cutting disciplines; and to learn about the “paths” of science.
The course consisted of six discussion sessions and one experimental course, which was offered to all students at the level 2018 of the Institute. Students interested in the cross-cutting integration of life sciences, physics or disciplines are welcome to study.

Name: Mechanics (Integrated Science)
Introduction: This course is based on the first volume of New Concept Mechanics and Feynman's Lectures on Physics, and teaches mechanics courses systematically. The difficulty level is between general physics courses for non-physics majors and mechanics courses for physics majors. It is mainly aimed at undergraduates in integrated science and interdisciplinary science.

Name: Foundations of Chemistry (Integrated Science)
Introduction: The course is divided into two parts: general chemistry and organic chemistry. The general chemistry section will introduce the basic concepts and methods of chemistry to freshmen in integrated science classes, including the basic laws of gases and liquids, chemical thermodynamics and chemical reaction directions, chemical equilibrium, molecular structure, crystal structure, coordination compounds and elemental chemistry. The organic chemistry section provides a comprehensive introduction to organic chemistry, allowing students to master the core knowledge of organic chemistry and understand the development history of organic chemistry and the development trends and application prospects in cutting-edge fields. Lay a solid foundation for subsequent study of biochemistry, physical chemistry, analytical chemistry and other related courses.

Name: Integrated Science Seminar
Introduction:
Teach and discuss different systems and methods of biological quantification to enhance students’ interest in quantitative biology;_x000D_
Cultivate interest in quantitative biology and establish a basic sense of biological quantification through the study and discussion of quantitative biology classics and interesting work.

Name: Integrated Thermodynamics
Introduction:
This course is the basic course for the second semester of the undergraduate course on integration of scientific experiments. The main content integrates thermal and chemical physics of physics.
Some preliminary introductions to the theoretical approach to statistical physics are also provided. This course requires students to better master the basics of thermodynamics and physicochemistry.
(c) Study, basic theory, basic knowledge and basic methods of thermodynamics and physico-chemistry to develop students ' capacity in scientific thinking and analysis of problems.
A combination of teaching content and biological system regulation mechanisms to sensitize students on the relationship between thermodynamics, physical chemistry and life sciences and to stimulate interest among students
And innovation.

Name: Quantitative Genetics
Introduction: Quantitative Cell Biology is a required course for second-year students majoring in Integrative Sciences. This course also welcomes students from other courses. Students will learn problem-solving and critical thinking skills in classical (Mendelian and quantitative) and modern (genomic and molecular) genetics. Students will learn through a combination of lectures, interactive problem solving, and computer programming.

Name: Integrated Quantum Mechanics and Molecular Spectroscopy
Prerequisite: Integration of thermodynamics, integration of chemistry
Introduction: A compulsory course in the science of integration at the Institute of Philosophy, which introduces the basis of quantum mechanics and molecular spectra.

Name: Fundamentals of Artificial and Brain-Inspired Intelligence
Introduction: The course will systematically introduce the basic knowledge of artificial intelligence and brain-inspired computing, and arrange corresponding computer practice. By studying this course, students will master basic knowledge of artificial neural networks, machine learning, neural computing modeling, etc., learn to use commonly used artificial intelligence algorithms, such as unsupervised learning, support vector machines, deep learning, reinforcement learning, etc., and understand commonly used brain-like computing models, such as spiking neural networks, attractor networks, library networks, etc., laying the foundation for future research in the intersection of artificial and brain-like intelligence.

Name: Natural Language and Data Science
Introduction:
Natural language processing is the cornerstone of the technology of the information age: on the one hand, we have used it extensively — search engines, advertising recommendations, spam processing, intelligent passenger service, machine translation... Nature language processing is everywhere in our lives. On the other hand, allowing machines to “understand” complex natural languages is also necessary for us to finally achieve strong artificial intelligence.
In this course, we will introduce some basic concepts in the processing of natural languages and some mathematical models behind natural languages and help you understand why natural languages are “calculable”. At the same time, the course will introduce cutting-edge studies on the processing of natural languages, in particular the application of in-depth learning techniques in the processing of natural languages.

Name: The English Novel Middlemarch: Text and Context
Introduction:
1. Through careful reading of the original text of the novel, become familiar with the basic framework, plot arrangement, and character design of British Victorian novels, and understand writing techniques such as metaphor, metonymy, irony, and quotation. _x000D_
2. Understand the historical background of novel creation and content, and be familiar with major historical, religious, and intellectual history knowledge of the 19th century. _x000D_
3 Understand George Eliot’s realistic writing techniques and the relationship between realism and moral construction. _x000D_
4. Preliminarily explore ideas and methods of academic discussion and academic writing. _x000D_

Name: Organic Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction:
Organic chemistry experiment is a compulsory basic course for undergraduates in the School of Chemistry and Yuanpei College. The arrangement of the organic chemistry experiment course focuses on cultivating students with a rigorous scientific attitude and good laboratory work style, who can master the basic operations, skills and methods of organic experiments, and become professionals who can adapt to the needs of future development. Cultivate students to develop the habit of questioning and thinking, the habit of persevering despite difficulties, the habit of timely summary and diligent communication, so that students have good abilities of observation, analysis, judgment, expression and evaluation. _x000D_
The teaching content of organic chemistry experimental courses includes: learning basic operating techniques; learning basic reaction devices, feeding methods, condition control, reaction post-processing, product purification and other synthesis methods. _x000D_

Name: Labor Economics
Introduction: This course describes the use of economics tools to analyse labour market behaviour.

Name: Organization and Management Seminar
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for undergraduates in the School of Business. It aims to help students understand the planning, organization, leadership, control and other functions involved in the organizational management process. Its positioning is: deepen understanding, discover interests, and improve abilities. There are eight sessions of two hours each. In the first part of each session, the instructor will briefly introduce the theoretical issues covered in the Organization and Management course. In the second part of each course, students will discuss distributed cases related to the course content under the guidance of the instructor. Deepen your understanding of course content and improve your ability to apply theory through case analysis.

Name: The Ocean and Climate Change
Introduction: Climate change is considered one of the biggest threats to the future of human existence, but what role does the ocean play in it? This course will introduce and discuss the scientific issues involving the ocean in climate change research from the perspective of the ocean's status in the evolution of the earth system and from a multidisciplinary perspective. It will cultivate students' interest in the earth's environment and their concern for the future environment of mankind, and enable students to understand the scientific issues involved. The lecturer will introduce relevant knowledge and scientific figures, guide students to read reference books and literature, and conduct micro-research and discussions on a number of classic and cutting-edge issues, as well as the current situation at home and abroad. Students with "professional intentions" in mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, geology, etc. who are interested in the ocean are welcome to actively participate. We will lead the students to understand the academic circle and explore the secrets of the ocean together!

Name: Psychology of Healthy Personality
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Healthy personality psychology is a popular science discipline that studies the basic characteristics of healthy personality and the laws of development and change. This course aims to explore students' potential and improve their quality of life and happiness. _x000D_
This course is developed on the basis of related disciplines such as personality psychology and clinical psychology. It helps students understand their own personality characteristics and their development rules through the introduction of classic theories on the development rules of healthy personality. Enable students to more comprehensively understand and accept others on the basis of self-understanding and self-acceptance. _x000D_

Name: German Lexicology
Prerequisite: This course requires students to have the four basic skills of listening, speaking, reading and writing after completing the German Intensive Reading Courses (1), (2), (3) and (4), have relatively systematic knowledge of grammar and text linguistics, and master a certain amount of vocabulary before they can participate in this course.
Introduction: Lexicology is an important part of the study of language, and the object of its study is the vocabulary of language. As a language student, you should have an understanding of the development and rules of the language and vocabulary you are learning. This course is mainly offered to third-year students in the German Department. The course content is divided into two parts. The first part teaches and learns the most basic knowledge of German vocabulary, that is, words as basic vocabulary units, word composition, word meaning, word classification, word combinations, and idioms that are closely related to vocabulary. The original works on vocabulary are relatively difficult. In view of the fact that third-year students are not yet able to read a lot of original German works, the course uses "German Vocabulary" written by Xu Zhier and self-edited handouts as the basic teaching materials. The content taught and studied in the second part of the course is German word formation. Since third-year students already have relatively systematic knowledge of grammar and mastered a certain amount of German vocabulary, they can more systematically understand and learn the methods and characteristics of modern German vocabulary formation. The teaching materials used include "Modern German Word Formation", "Wörter zur Wahl" and "Practical German Word Formation" as well as self-edited lecture notes.

Name: Linguistic Theories and Schools
Introduction: This course is an elective course for undergraduates majoring in German in the School of Foreign Languages. It is taught to undergraduates majoring in German. This course will systematically teach the overall development of modern (German) linguistics, systematically introduce linguistic schools and viewpoints in various periods, and enable students to master certain basic knowledge of modern linguistics theory and have a more comprehensive and in-depth understanding of the development process, latest research status and development trends of modern linguistics. At the same time, they will improve their German language ability and gain preliminary training in linguistic research methods. _x000D_

Name: Austrian Media
Introduction: Austrian media has some characteristics that differ from other German-speaking countries. Austrian films in recent years have achieved great influence both in the German-speaking area and around the world. For another example, the influence of some Austrian tabloids on Austrian politics and public life is worthy of discussion and analysis. This course looks at what makes Austrian media special. The course content includes analytical surveys, group discussions, reading influential media reviews, and watching movies, etc., so that students can understand the differences of Austrian media. In addition, students are required to analyze articles and films after class and make two class presentations on this each semester.

The series of courses on ancient writing aesthetics will introduce the basic knowledge of ancient writing materials such as oracle bone inscriptions, bronze inscriptions, and bamboo slips and their application in art, including copying and creation. _x000D_

1. Introduction to basic knowledge of Oracle_x000D_
2. Analysis of commonly used oracle bone characters_x000D_
3. Copying of exquisite oracle bone inscriptions_x000D_
4. Discussion on different calligraphy styles of oracle bone inscriptions_x000D_

Name: China's Energy and Environmental Challenges
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Prerequisite:
The chances are critical knowledge in chémistry, physics, and math at the high level level.

No prior course requirement.
Introduction:
As the world's second largest economy, China is the country with the largest coal consumption and the second largest oil consumption in the world. It also emits the largest amount of carbon dioxide. Economic development has brought tremendous pressure on the environment. Environmental issues, especially the frequent haze in recent years, have attracted high public attention. This course intends to look into China's energy structure from an interdisciplinary perspective, analyze the energy-related environmental issues that are prominent today, such as air pollution, and elaborate on the climate and health effects that these environmental issues may bring. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will discuss the important energy structure adjustments since the founding of the People's Republic of China, including the development of coal-related power generation, heating, oil use and transportation sources and their contribution to air pollution. It will comprehensively analyze the types and pros and cons of alternative clean energy in China, as well as the checks and balances between environmental protection and economic growth. By introducing the relationship between energy, pollution and climate in the context of China's compound pollution, we strive to guide students to scientifically understand the environmental problems that developing countries may encounter in the process of rapid economic development, and to think deeply about possible solutions. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will lead students on field trips to visit air quality observation sites, as well as new energy facilities such as pumped hydro, wind power, concentrated solar heating, and photovoltaic power generation around Beijing.

Name: Syrian Arabic
Introduction:
The Arab world includes 22 countries and a population of nearly 400 million, with both linguistic and cultural identity and diversity. The cultural identity and internal and external communication of Arab countries rely on a unified standard Arabic language, while the dialects of each country facilitate daily pragmatic use and contain multicultural factors. Among them, Egyptian dialect and Syrian dialect are one of the most important branches of Arabic dialects. _x000D_
The Syrian dialect is not only spoken in Syria, but is also the main tool for daily communication in the Sham region. _x000D_
The Syrian dialect course is, first of all, linking standard Arabic language with dialects to provide richer language tools for pragmatic communication in Arabic; secondly, it is to gain an in-depth understanding of the social culture of Syria and Al-Sham and enrich the cultural connotation in pragmatic communication; in addition, through the study of dialects, it is further promoted to understand and master the linguistic characteristics and structure of standard Arabic language. _x000D_

Introduction: It enables students to have a comprehensive understanding of Indonesia's basic national conditions, promotes the study of professional courses, and enables students to be competent in relevant jobs after graduation. This course comprehensively and systematically introduces the rich and colorful multiculturalism of Indonesia from multiple aspects and angles. Main content: Indonesian tribal culture, national psychology, literature, religion, language, education, media, folklore, geography, art, economic construction and tourism culture, etc. Understanding Indonesian culture will help you further understand Indonesian society and its history. Exploring its characteristics and development patterns will help cultural exchanges between countries. Teaching takes the form of lectures, discussions, term papers, etc.

Name: History of Indonesia (I)
Introduction:
The Indonesian nation, like the rest of the world, has been a primitive society for thousands of years.
Historic country. In the ancient Indonesian era, strong rural community remnants formed the basic features of the early Indonesian society. With the gradual decline of clanism, the increasing power of tribal chiefs, the transformation of military chiefs into the earliest self-governings, the emergence of institutions of power for class oppression, the radical transformation of society and the replacement of the ancient clan system by the State. This course focuses on the archaeological discoveries and major ancient kingdoms of Indonesia.

Name: History of Indonesia (II)
Introduction: Through classroom lectures, discussions, term papers, etc., students can gain a more comprehensive understanding of the major events and historical development context in Indonesia’s modern history. It also introduces the rise of the Indonesian national liberation movement, the activities of the Indonesian Communist Party, the process of Japan's occupation of Indonesia and the policies implemented in Indonesia, and the Indonesian people's resistance to Japanese rule and struggle for independence.

Name: Topics in Thai Studies
Prerequisite: General information on Thailand, cultural and social bases of Thai science.
Introduction:
This lesson focuses on introducing some important issues in the study of Thai literature and history, and combines previous research results to inspire students to think deeply. _x000D_
1. The discovery and interpretation history of the Ram Kamhaeng inscription and the debate surrounding the authenticity of the inscription, the origin, focus and progress of the debate; the different results of linguistic, philological and historical analysis and the positions indicated by these results; _x000D_
2. The origin of the Tai people: various views on the origin of the Tai people and their formation process, the criteria for judging scientific and non-scientific views, whether there is a substantial relationship between the origin of the Tai people and humans in ancient Thai history (Ban Chiang culture), the basic structure of the origin of the Tai people; _x000D_
3. Thailand and Siam: Discussion of the historical changes in local nationalities in Thailand and the formation process of the Thai nation; the historical and cultural significance of the change in the name of Thailand. _x000D_
4. The establishment process of the Sukhothai Dynasty and the story of Parang: What do the contradictions between historical records and folklore indicate? _x000D_
5. The establishment of the Ayutthaya Dynasty and the formation of the Thai national cultural tradition: the mystery of King Uthong’s origins and the history of the integration of the Thai and Mon ethnic groups, and the political, economic and cultural forms of Thailand during the Ayutthaya Dynasty; _x000D_
6. Imperial Language and the Formation of Imperial Language - Sociolinguistic Analysis: Imperial Language is not a language, but a language used by a special class; _x000D_
7. The historical origins of the Myanmar-Thailand War: the cultural origins and focus of conflicts between Myanmar and Thailand, and the causes and consequences of Thailand’s expansion; _x000D_
8. King Taksin and the history of Chinese migration into Thailand: the internal and external causes of Chinese migration to Southeast Asia, and why are Chinese able to gain a foothold in Thailand? _x000D_
9. Analysis of Chulalongkorn’s reforms: analysis of reform methods and processes: details determine success or failure; _x000D_
10. The influence of Chinese culture on Thailand: At what level is it appropriate to talk about this issue?
