Prerequisite: Portuguese heard (i), Portuguese heard (ii) Portuguese heard (iii)
Introduction:
This course is a professional basic course for the second semester of the Portuguese undergraduate major. It complements the intensive reading class and the oral class. It focuses on training students' listening comprehension skills and strengthening students' ability to communicate and express freely on specific topics. _x000D_
As a professional basic course, the materials selected for listening in the course have begun to change from conversations to short essays and articles, and the content involved has begun to change from daily life to professional. The materials selected for listening are comprehensive and extensive, and have a certain degree of professional involvement, such as economics, politics, culture, society, etc., to train students to master professional vocabulary, so that students can reach the B2 level of listening and speaking proficiency in the "European Union Common Framework of Reference for Languages". _x000D_

Name: Portuguese Reading (III)
Introduction: This course is for the next semester of the second year of Portuguese-speaking specialization and is based on self-generated materials. The purpose of this course is to develop the reading skills of students, to increase the speed of reading, to interact with the simultaneous Portuguese-language fine readings and the historical and cultural profile of Brazil, to select historical and cultural articles appropriate to the student level, to help students promote the learning of vocabulary and grammar and to enhance the understanding of Brazilian history and culture in reading.

Name: Physics for Non-Majors
Introduction: They are offered to students of university faculties without the need for mathematics and focus on understanding physics phenomena, basic patterns, ideas and methods, as well as the use of these ideas, methods and conclusions that have been obtained to analyse phenomena in everyday life and form judgement.

Name: The Global Sixties
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Global “sixties” — what kind of age is this? The age of shock? The turning age? Extraordinary times? The age of questioning authority? The era of revolution and liberation? A wake-up call? Welcome, gentlemen, to the new semester to discuss with me the global social, cultural and political issues of the Long Sixties. At the beginning of the semester, the teaching staff will provide a global overview, reflection and commentary for the 1960s. This will be followed by thematic presentations and discussions on the main social movements, cultural thoughts, the spirit of the times and political events of the 1960s in a number of focus countries and regions. Secondary school students made a presentation on topics of interest and delivered an original paper at the end. The course was delivered primarily by instructors, with relevant audio and video clips and classroom discussions.

Name: Organizational Behavior and Leadership
Introduction: This course is a basic course on organizational behaviour and leadership. Through this course, students will be able to acquire theoretical knowledge about the individual (personality, attitude, motivation, consciousness, etc.) in the organization, the group and team, as well as the organizational level and the relationship between the organization and the environment, to provide them with a knowledge base for future courses, and to provide the necessary preparation for the students to move to work.

Name: Introduction to Data Science
Introduction: Data science is a cross-cutting profession that explores the extraction of knowledge from data. The course is a major basic course in data management and application designed for the specializations in information management disciplines, with the aim of promoting data science applications in other fields, such as humanities and social sciences. The course will provide an in-depth introduction to the principles of data science and basic technologies and methods, and will be divided into five main modules based on the data science process, based on basic concepts, problem definition, data preparation, data modelling and results presentation. The course is aimed at students without an empirical basis, helping them to understand the concepts and processes of data science, focusing on the exploration of defined issues, building the sensitivity of data preparation, understanding the concept of data modelling techniques and demonstrating the results of analysis using data visualization thinking and methods.

Name: Information Representation and Knowledge Graphs
Prerequisite: Information organization; Data structure; Database system; Information storage and retrieval.
Introduction:
Information representation is the basis of information management. Knowledge graph is a semantic and conceptual representation of information to support intelligent operations such as reasoning, question answering, and semantic association. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course divides information management into four historical stages: paper document environment, digital information environment, network information environment and intelligent information environment. Traditional libraries, information retrieval systems/database systems, search engines, and knowledge graphs are regarded as information systems in the above information environments. This course analyzes the internal information processes of information systems by sorting out the methods of information representation, information organization and information operation in the above-mentioned types of information systems, so as to bridge the gap between the core courses of the Department of Information Management and consolidate and deepen the disciplinary foundation of information management. _x000D_
_x000D_
On this basis, learn basic knowledge about knowledge graph construction such as XML, RDF, and ontology, as well as methods to build semantic and intelligent information systems. _x000D_

Name: Big Data Application Practice (Part 1)
Prerequisite: Python data analysis, big data application case analysis
Introduction:
This course is a comprehensive application practice course for the major of big data management and application. It consists of several parallel comprehensive training modules for different application fields, including but not limited to one of the following application fields: scientific research big data, public culture big data, digital humanities big data, education big data, user behavior big data, government affairs big data, financial big data, health big data, etc. _x000D_
      For different application fields and data sources, the dimensions of comprehensive training include technical methods of big data collection and data preprocessing, main objects of data analysis, specific analysis indicators, modeling and analysis methods, visual tool software, typical application case analysis, etc. Work with industry mentors to guide students to complete the construction of a comprehensive big data application experimental platform that integrates multi-source heterogeneous data. _x000D_

Name: Data Analysis with Python
Prerequisite:
1. "Introduction to Data Science" or other related courses; _x000D_
2. "Introduction to Computation C" (original Liberal Arts Computer Fundamentals) and above or other related courses.
Introduction: The course teaches methods of data analysis and uses Python as a practical tool. The curriculum requires students to have the basic ability to use Python before starting. The course is divided into three modules: the first module (basic part) begins with a brief introduction and a review of the syntax of the Python program design, as well as a presentation of the basis for data analysis using Python, such as the use of Numpy, pandas, matplotlib and Seaborn; the second module (application part) presents multiple applications for data analysis using Python, such as exploratory data analysis, time series analysis, machine learning, social network analysis, image analysis, text mining, etc.; and the third module (summary part) will be presented by students at the classroom with group exercises and a final examination. The course is a compulsory course in the “Big Data Management and Applications” specialty and is also a limited subject in other specialties of the Department of Information Management, and is open to students from other relevant professions.

Name: Data Analysis with Python Computer Lab
Prerequisite: This course is devoted to the Python Data Analysis course, with reference to the Python Data Analysis course.
Introduction: This course is an on-board course for the Python Data Analysis course, which must be taken simultaneously with Python Data Analysis.

Name: The Literature and Life of Su Shi
Introduction: This course takes Su Shi as the subject of research and discussion. It starts with his literary works and life experiences, connects them with the general background of the time, and invites course participants to explore Su Zi's philosophy of life, worldly sentiments, and interest in life. The course has a total of 16 hours, divided into 8 lectures, and strives to be both interesting and academic, thereby helping freshmen deepen their understanding of Su Shi and establish systematic academic thinking.

Name: Selected Readings in the Professional Literature (I)
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for international undergraduate students of Guangxi College. It is an important basic course for successfully completing professional studies, improving professional learning abilities, and ultimately completing studies. Its purpose is: _x000D_
1. Improve the ability to study Chinese research literature through the selection and study of relevant professional literature, and lay a foundation for the study of other professional courses. _x000D_
2. Use relevant theories of international politics and diplomacy to interpret issues related to Chinese politics, diplomacy, and international relations from different perspectives, thereby increasing professional knowledge and improving the ability to understand historical and current Chinese and international issues. _x000D_
3. Improve professional expression and writing skills in Chinese. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in the Professional Literature (II)
Prerequisite: (i) History of International Relations of the People ' s Republic of China
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for international undergraduate students of Guangxi College. It is an important basic course for successfully completing professional studies, improving professional learning abilities, and ultimately completing studies. Its purpose is: _x000D_
1. Improve the ability to study Chinese research literature through the selection and study of relevant professional literature, and lay a foundation for the study of other professional courses. _x000D_
2. Use relevant theories of international politics and diplomacy to interpret issues related to Chinese politics, diplomacy, and international relations from different perspectives, thereby increasing professional knowledge and improving the ability to understand historical and current Chinese and international issues. _x000D_
3. Improve professional expression and writing skills in Chinese. _x000D_

Name: Innovation and Rapid Prototyping
Prerequisite: There are no prerequisite courses, and it is open to students in Yuanpei College’s majors (engineering, science, liberal arts, business, medicine, art...). If you have some foundations in engineering drawing, circuits, and programming courses, you can experience more creative fun in the course, but these foundations are not required.
Introduction: In the innovation process of students, the production of physical objects is often involved. This course uses a small project including model making, circuit construction, and programming to experience the practical operation and application of these three types of skills. The course provides basic project prototype templates, making it easier for students who have not learned the corresponding professional knowledge to complete the most basic settings. Students with certain professional knowledge and interest can achieve self-developed prototypes through various improvements, transformations, and customizations with greater freedom.

Name: Advanced Academic Writing in Chinese
Introduction: This course aims to cultivate the ability of international students at Yuanpei College to use Chinese for professional literature reading and academic writing. The course content mainly includes four parts: 1. Literature reading analysis, combined with Yuanpei teaching training plan and requirements, learn how to summarize or abbreviate professional papers. 2. Commonly used course paper writing training at Yuanpei undergraduate level, including reading reports, literature reviews, etc. 3. Training on common writing methods in Chinese academic papers. Four. Logical analysis of Chinese academic papers and writing training on the structure of academic papers, including introduction, argument, conclusion, abstract, etc.

Name: Investment Banking
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the theory and practice of investment banking from both the buyer and seller perspectives. The course is divided into six parts. The first part is an introduction to investment banking, understanding investment banking from the perspective of investment banking concept analysis and development process; the second part is based on the "broad asset securitization theory", mainly understanding investment banking from the perspective of financing entities; the third part understands investment banking from the perspective of trading venues; the fourth part understands investment banking from the perspective of capital suppliers, that is, in the investment process, individual investors are based on knowledge and the scarcity of information, entrusting institutional investors to make professional investments; the fifth part understands investment banks from the perspective of organizational restructuring. When enterprises are used as wealth carriers, economic entities will adjust the corporate structure around corporate control rights to obtain wealth maximization effects; the sixth part understands investment banks from a management perspective, including both self-management of investment banks and supervision from outside investment banks. The biggest feature of this course is the combination of theoretical explanation and case analysis.

Name: Practicum in Financial Markets and Institutions
Introduction: The course brings leading figures from the financial practice community to the classroom, where professionals teach them practical knowledge of the financial field and communicate with them in close proximity with a view to building bridges between theory and practice. The course mainly invites heads of departments or senior practitioners of large financial institutions to act as lecturers and to present and discuss issues of focus and interest in China ' s financial markets, covering the priority operations of financial institutions such as investment banks, commercial banks, funds, trusts, leases, venture capital, Internet finance, etc. For each type of institution, the course will provide detailed information on the pattern and development prospects of the sector, its internal organizational structure, business model, products and services, corresponding career opportunities, etc.

Name: Wang Ren Lecture Series in Mechanics (I)
Introduction: The course addresses front-line and hot-spot issues in the fields of mechanics, including fluids, solid mechanics, engineering structural analysis, biomechanicals and general mechanics and control, and invites highly accomplished experts and scholars, both national and foreign, to give lectures in the form of academic reports, and select students to ask questions and discuss the content of the lectures. The purpose of the course is to enhance academic exchange, broaden the perspective of students, develop new scientific thinking and promote cross-cutting and integration between the mechanics and disciplines. The subject is compulsory for master ' s and doctoral students in mechanics. Students are required to complete the course for two semesters (two credits) prior to graduation, and are required to sign at the site, with a attendance rate of not less than two thirds per semester, with a summary report at the end.

Name: Advanced Fluid Mechanics
Introduction: Fluid mechanics is one of the most important basic courses in our department. Based on the undergraduate fluid mechanics course, this course uses the decomposition and coupling of the basic processes of fluid motion to introduce several major sub-disciplines of fluid mechanics, clarifying their interconnections and their respective status and characteristics, and providing guidance for subsequent units (vorticity dynamics, flow stability and transition, turbulence, and waves) and for students to master the essential content of the entire fluid mechanics. Students are required to have mastered the basic concepts and methods of fluid mechanics.

Name: Advanced Applied Mathematics
Introduction: Systematic introduction to applied mathematical equations and analytical methods involved in mechanics and natural sciences, including Lagrange equations, quantum mechanical equations, distribution function equations, continuum equations, etc., especially the general principles contained in these equations that explain the laws of nature, and the application of these equations. Qualitative and approximate analysis methods, including scaling analysis methods, linear expansion methods, multi-scale progressive expansion methods, statistical analysis methods, scaling laws and fractals, combined with the ideas of system science, enable students to apply these methods to analyze and research complex phenomena in mechanics and related scientific fields.

Name: Organizational Mechanics
Introduction:
A comprehensive exploration of the applications of tissue mechanics in bioengineering, physiology, and medical sciences. The research methods for this course are as follows:_x000D_
  1. Study the morphology, anatomy, and histology of organisms to clarify the geometric structure of the biological tissue under study. _x000D_
  2. Determine the basic mechanical (or material) properties of biological tissues. _x000D_
  3. Based on the laws of physics, derive relevant differential and integral equations. _x000D_
  4. Determine the boundary conditions of biological tissues and organs. _x000D_
  5. Solve boundary value problems to clarify the mechanical properties within biological tissues and organs. _x000D_
  6. Implement physiological measurements to verify relevant theoretical prediction results. _x000D_
  7. Based on experimentally verified theories, further explore the application of tissue mechanics in bioengineering, physiology and medical science. _x000D_
This course combines theory and experiment to provide mechanical mechanism analysis and new methods and technologies for relevant clinical diagnosis and treatment.

Name: Computational Fluid Dynamics
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, high algebra, numeric algebra, numeric analysis, dichotomy equations, hydrodynamic inferences, computer program design, numeric equation values Break
Introduction:
The course ' s teaching content includes the basics of hydrodynamics, the hyperbolic-consistent method of high-resolution heat wave capture, the numerical method of compressable fluid equations and the numerical method of non-compressible fluid equations. The selection of teaching content is intended to be generic and novel, ranging from the numerical methods commonly used in the computation of hydrodynamics to some new advances and research results of recent studies in computing hydrodynamics. The course is based on the numerical solvency method of introducing the hydrodynamic equation group, but will also involve relevant mathematical theories and applications, narratives and justifications that are both shallow and rigorous.

The course may be aimed at master ' s degree students in various fields of science and technology, as well as at senior university students, doctoral students, mathematics practitioners and other science and technology personnel using computers for science and engineering.

Name: Advanced Computational Fluid Dynamics
Introduction: Through the study of this course, students will have a further understanding and mastery of the differential method, finite element method, finite volume method, boundary element method, finite spectrum method, grid generation method, etc. in computational fluid mechanics.

Name: Thermodynamic Analysis of Renewable Energy
Introduction: The thermodynamic analysis of renewable energy is based on environmental thermodynamics as a theoretical basis, and is a generalized thermodynamic analysis method that systematically defines, factors decomposes, hierarchical analysis and accounting evaluation, system simulation and scenario prediction of the entire energy conversion process of the renewable energy industry chain from various perspectives such as environmental impact, resource investment, social impact and policy analysis. As an alternative energy source to traditional fossil fuels, the research and application of renewable energy has received widespread attention around the world. This course is based on the rich knowledge background of renewable energy and the profound theoretical understanding of thermodynamics and systematic systems. Through a combination of classroom lectures and discussions, starting from the perspective of thermodynamics and focusing on different emphases, this course enables students to systematically master the thermodynamic analysis framework, methods and evaluation systems of various renewable energy sources, and understand the latest domestic and foreign development trends of renewable energy sources and the many challenges they face in their development. This course takes about 70% of classroom lecture time and 30% of student discussion time. Examination scores account for 60%, and attendance and class discussions account for 40%.

Name: Combustion Theory and Simulation
Introduction:
"Combustion Theory and Simulation" is the main technical basic course for the first-level disciplines of power engineering and engineering thermophysics, aerospace power, energy and environment. It is also an indispensable foundation for the development of high-tech technologies such as power devices in other industrial fields, and plays a core role in modern development. It is a specialized knowledge that studies the conversion of fossil fuel chemical energy into thermal energy. This course will use chemical fluid dynamics as the basis for analyzing combustion problems, and systematically explain the basic phenomena and laws of combustion, so that students can more systematically master the basic knowledge of combustion theory and simulation and their applications. This course starts from the latest cutting-edge developments, combines the elaboration of basic principles with new developments, new problems and new thinking, and uses intensive extracurricular literature reading and analysis to perfectly integrate the course and research work, which greatly enhances students' desire for innovation and promotes scientific research and subject development. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching method: Classroom teaching (mainly blackboard teaching, with appropriate use of multimedia teaching methods)_x000D_
_x000D_
Assessment method: 20% daily homework, 20% major homework, 20% reading report, 40% final oral examination_x000D_

Building on traditional algorithms and based on classical strategies, improving students ' ability to design new algorithms. Name: Fundamentals of Parallel and Distributed Computing
Introduction: Over the past decade, parallel and distributed computing has experienced explosive growth, moving from an elective course to a core component of undergraduate computing courses in data science. This course includes the basic concepts of computing model theory of parallel computing and distributed computing, as well as MPI programming technology on distributed memory architecture, OpenMP programming technology on shared memory architecture, and CUDA programming technology on GPU many-core architecture.

Name: Intelligent Bionic Machines
Introduction: The main task of this course is to introduce the basic knowledge and latest developments in the interdisciplinary field of intelligent bionic robots, improve students' understanding of robotics, and at the same time enable students to understand general research methods in interdisciplinary fields. The study of this course will help students comprehensively and systematically grasp the research status of this field, understand the academic frontier, expand scientific thinking, and cultivate students' ability to discover and solve problems.

Name: Advanced Thermodynamics
Introduction: Thermodynamics is one of the most widely applied and rich physics branches and is a subject that should be taught by my graduate students in the fields of hydrodynamics, environment and logistics. The course system presents modern theory and application of thermodynamics, the main elements of which include balancing thermodynamics, non-balanced thermodynamics and analytical (fire) theories that have received extensive attention in recent years. The course also provides for the necessary discussion of the formulation of basic concepts of thermodynamics. Students are required to master the basic concept of thermodynamics and have some knowledge of the modern development of thermodynamics.

Name: Computer-Aided Design of Control Systems
Introduction: "Computer-Aided Design of Control Systems" is a course that uses MATLAB high-level programming language as an auxiliary tool to study the analysis, design and simulation of control systems. The purpose of this undergraduate course is to enable students to initially master the basic skills of analysis, design and research of control systems using computers.

Name: Hyperbolic Equations
Prerequisite: Micro geometry or Lehman collection, real-life functions, generic analysis
Introduction: Over the past 40 years, the broad relativity of mathematics has generated widespread attention, thanks to significant findings in physical astronomicals (such as gravitational waves, black hole photographs, etc.) and, more importantly, based on a deeper mathematical understanding of the hyperbolic equation (Einstein equation) in the early 1980s. The purpose of this course is to present these developments and related frontier developments.

Name: Harmonic Analysis
Introduction:
This course introduces the analysis on Siegel fields and Heisenberg groups, as well as the analysis on SL(2,R) (or Poicare unit disk). _x000D_

Name: Advancing Together with My Country in the New Era
College: Peking University Committee of the Communist Youth League of China
Introduction:
This course is a patriotic-themed education course for all students participating in the phalanx of the 70th anniversary of the National Day. It has a total of 2 credits and 32 hours. Each student participating in the phalanx of the National Day will receive two credits after completing the course. _x000D_
This course closely focuses on the grand celebration of the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China. It combines the training of mass parades and the "My Motherland and Me" patriotic education activities, focusing on enhancing the sense of ceremony, participation, and gain, with the focus of the course on achieving the triple gains of strong bodies, well-trained, and firm minds for participating teachers and students to inspire students Patriotic sentiments, education guides students to strengthen their ideals and beliefs, cultivate patriotic enthusiasm, mobilize the enthusiasm and initiative of the majority of students, and create a strong atmosphere of active participation, thereby ensuring the successful holding of various activities of Peking University celebrating the 70th anniversary of the National Day. It also becomes a stage for Peking University students to show their high-spirited appearance to the motherland and express their patriotic voices. _x000D_
This course aims to transform the process of organizing teachers and students to participate in the 70th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China into a variety of vivid courses on patriotism education, effectively unifying ideas, boosting morale, and raising spirits, so that teachers and students can sublimate patriotic emotions while completing training tasks. The course content includes theoretical lectures with the theme of "Learning Patriotism". Experts are invited to conduct a series of lectures on themes such as the spirit of patriotism and serving the country through science and technology to guide the participating teachers and students to deeply understand the theme and purpose of the phalanx. Combined with the vivid patriotic practice of daily phalanx training, theory and practice are combined to achieve a two-pronged approach to truly establish It establishes teachers and students' belief in Marxism, belief in socialism with Chinese characteristics, and confidence in realizing the Chinese dream of the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation; at the same time, the course invites those who have witnessed the mass parades during the 35th, 50th, and 60th anniversary celebrations of the National Day to talk about their experiences in all aspects of the year, inspiring contemporary youth to carry forward the past and inherit patriotism into the future. Affectionate; in addition, the course organized a flag-raising ceremony with the theme of "Raising Patriotism" to fly high the red flag in the hearts of every teacher and student; organized sharing activities with the theme of "Speaking of Patriotism", recited and studied the General Secretary's speech, shared training experiences and growth experiences, and carried out criticism and self-criticism; organized "Patriotism Speaks" as the theme. The striving for excellence and innovation activities with the theme of "Compare", set up vanguard model posts for party members, carry out recommendation of outstanding candidates to join the party, and form a good atmosphere of "compare, learn, catch up and help"; organize interesting activities with the theme of "Patriotism, "Move", hold fun sports games, tug-of-war competitions, and singing activities, and build a display and exchange platform for teachers and students to express their patriotic enthusiasm.

The multiplication theory, the Pesin entropy formula, the Lyapunov index approach theory and the measurement approach theory, etc.

Name: Group Representation Theory
Prerequisite: High algebra, mathematical analysis, probabilistic theory, mathematical statistics, program design base
Introduction: Pattern recognition is a subject with rich content and wide application fields. This course will systematically introduce the basic concepts, basic theories and typical methods of pattern recognition. Specifically, we will focus on statistical decision-making theory and methods, estimation of parametric and non-parametric probability density functions, linear discriminant functions (including support vector machines), nonlinear discriminant functions (including feedforward neural networks), feature selection and extraction, and unsupervised pattern recognition methods. In addition, we will supplement the introduction of cutting-edge developments in some disciplines based on practical applications.

Name: Game Theory
Introduction:
1. Non-cooperative game theory. _x000D_

The sub-game is a perfect equilibrium. Stackelberg equilibrium. A game with a chance to move. Repeat the game. Folk theorem. Examples and exercises. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals and Applications of Nuclear Materials
Introduction: The name of this course is "Fundamentals and Applications of Nuclear Materials". This course is a professional basic course on nuclear materials for master's and doctoral students majoring in nuclear technology application in the School of Physics. It is mainly aimed at graduate students engaged in nuclear energy materials research in our school and the School of Physics. It is a course at the intersection of physics and materials. The teaching targets are doctoral students and master's students. The course is mainly taught in the classroom. Through teaching, master's students and doctoral students engaged in scientific research can master the basic knowledge of nuclear structural materials (nuclear materials) used in nuclear reactors, including material science and basics and their applications in nuclear energy materials (material crystal structure, diffusion, defect formation process, etc.); the basic process and evolution of defect formation in nuclear materials under ion irradiation conditions; nuclear material radiation effects (radiation hardening, swelling, creep, fracture, etc.). The course will introduce in detail the basic knowledge of materials, the interaction between ions and solids, the formation, development and evolution of defects under irradiation conditions, as well as the performance changes and mechanisms of nuclear materials under extreme service conditions. The course not only introduces the changes in the microstructure and macroscopic properties of materials under service conditions from a material perspective and the correlation between the two, but also explains and explains the basic mechanism of material changes under extreme service conditions from a physical perspective. At the same time, the course also combines the current characteristics of nuclear energy development to introduce the current opportunities and challenges faced by nuclear materials in our country, and stimulate students' scientific interest in studying nuclear materials. Through the study of this course, students will have a better understanding of nuclear materials and lay a solid foundation for future study and scientific research work.

Curriculum: This course includes the following experiments, which were made out of a combination of nine experiments in the original teaching material, with the addition of accelerator experiments: Measurement of the absorption and characterization spectrum of X-rays (including the teaching material experiment 6 "According and characterization of X-rays" and the experiment 11 "Active numerator"): the method used to master the positive numerator, using the sample characteristics X-ray spectrum to analyse the type and content and absorption factors. Name: Applications of Big Data Analysis Techniques
Introduction:
Course purpose:_x000D_
The "Big Data Analysis Technology Application" course teaches the key technologies of big data analysis. It aims at the practical application of big data analysis technology. It combines theory and cases to teach students the theoretical knowledge and application of big data analysis technology, so that students can understand and master the application of big data analysis technology and be able to apply the learned analysis technology knowledge in actual scientific research work. _x000D_
Basics of starting a course_x000D_
The research and application of big data is a research field that my country's natural sciences, humanities and social sciences attach great importance to. Generally speaking, big data refers to the structural form and scale of data; in addition, the meaning of big data also includes the structural form and scale of data, as well as the technology for processing data. At present, the key technologies of big data analysis include: genetic algorithm, neural network, data mining, data fusion, machine learning, network analysis, time series analysis and other research and analysis methods. _x000D_
Big data analysis applications can be implemented through numerous software carriers. This course uses R language as a carrier to implement big data analysis. R is a programming language and environment for statistical computing that is similar to the S language developed by Rick Becker, John Chambers, and Allan Wilks at AT&T Bell Laboratories. Depending on the operating system, the R language has UNIX versions, Windows versions, and Mac versions, and can run on computer systems of different architectures. All source code for the R language is freely available for inspection or exploitation. The open source nature, flexibility, and highly flexible database interface technology of R language make it particularly suitable for data analysis of large-scale problems. _x000D_
This course will include a brief introduction to key terms in the use of R language and is suitable for graduate students without any foundation in big data analysis. Therefore, students do not need to be familiar with computer programming knowledge to easily understand and master the R language big data analysis methods and cases introduced in this course. _x000D_
Teaching requirements_x000D_
(1) Understand and master the basic principles and steps of big data analysis methods_x000D_
(2) Understand and master R language data analysis methods_x000D_
(3) Understand and master R language to implement the application of big data analysis methods

Name: Lecture Series on Frontier Issues in Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Name: Semantic Analysis
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly teaches semantic research methods at the sentence level, and guides students to use these methods for practical operations through the analysis of examples in Chinese. The main content includes: derivation, presupposition, focus, function word semantics and other issues, and discusses related phenomena in Chinese. As a basis for discussing semantic issues, logical issues related to semantics will be introduced first. This course has daily homework, and the final exam is in the form of a research paper.

Name: Morphology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Terminology law is the linguistic arm of the internal structure rules of the study. Some of the basic concepts and theories of the introduction to the term law found that, in combination with material in different languages, different models of study of the term law were discussed, the interface between the analysis of the term and the voice and between the term and the term, and the study of the lexicon, with specific reference to the characteristics of the Chinese term. This course of study gives students an initial insight into the content of the study of the lexicon, the methodology of the study and the basic state of Chinese syntax research.
Terminology law is an important area of study in linguistics, but since Chinese grammatical research is weak, there has been no special subject in Chinese linguistic law. This course is intended to fill this gap in postgraduate teaching.
Teaching is primarily teaching and is discussed. Students are required to perform practical language analysis exercises in the course of the course and to read the relevant reference books after the course.

Name: Contemporary Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The course focuses on the basic linguistic theory and methods of study in contemporary linguistic studies such as structuralism, the generation of grammar, cognitive linguistics, and structural grammar.
Theoretical presentation of this course, combined with research cases, is designed to enable students to understand the background, theoretical framework and dynamics of the evolution of the various linguistic theories, to properly evaluate the theory from the perspective of linguistic history; to make students aware of the basic theory and methodology of linguistic studies and to learn to use them to explain the phenomenon in Chinese, ethnic English and English using the theories and methods learned.
This course is compulsory for Masters and Doctors in Linguistics and Applied Linguistics. It is also suitable for the selection of Masters and Doctors in Chinese Language.

Name: History of Foreign Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course examines the process of the development of Western language studies from the perspective of academic history and explores the historical roots of modern linguistic thinking. The course will present linguistic perspectives, research perspectives and intellectual results from different historical periods, and make the necessary analytical discussions on the historical transmission of ideas and their differences. The objective of the course is to develop a more comprehensive understanding and reflection of the development of Western linguistics, the characteristics of the study of ideas and materials in different languages, social history and macro-academic thinking through learning and discussion. The course is for postgraduate students in linguistics. The curriculum takes the form of a combination of teacher instruction and student reporting discussions.

Name: Historical Syntax
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Historical syntax is a branch of historical linguistics, which mainly studies the evolution of syntax and its laws. This course mainly introduces the following contents: the nature, characteristics and development history of historical syntax, types of syntactic evolution, research theories, research methods and research findings on syntactic evolution by different linguistic schools, mechanisms, motivations and research hot spots of syntactic evolution, etc. In class, materials on the evolution of Chinese syntax will be analyzed, as well as materials on the evolution of syntax in other languages. It is hoped that students who take this course will have some basic knowledge of syntax, historical linguistics and Chinese history. This course uses a combination of professor and student inquiry and reporting. The evaluation of the course is based on the final course paper and usual classroom performance.

Name: Linguistic Typology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Language typology is a discipline that has developed rapidly over the last 40 years, and its results are widely used in other aspects of linguistics, with an understanding of the theoretical methods of linguistic typology and an important reference for the study of Chinese. This course is a general course in linguistic typology, which focuses on basic theoretical ideas and research methods in linguistic typologies, so that students have a basic knowledge of linguistic typologies and can apply to Chinese research.

Name: Morphosyntax in Fieldwork
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course aims to equip students with key knowledge and investigation and analysis techniques to facilitate the investigation and analysis of language morphosyntax materials. The course introduces rich morphosyntactic phenomena of various Chinese and non-Chinese languages ​​in a step-by-step manner. After fully mastering the class content, students taking the course can gain a deeper understanding of Chinese grammar, broaden their horizons, and increase their systematic knowledge of human language structure and cognitive connotations. This course mainly consists of teacher lectures, textbook introduction, and discussion exercises, two hours per week. Students are required to read designated chapters every week, submit exercises, participate in class discussions, and write a small report each midterm and final.

Name: Pathological Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Language, as the most important communication tool for humans, is an important ability that distinguishes humans from other animals. Researchers have conducted a large amount of basic research on general language. The research object of general linguistics is the normal language itself that humans already have. Such research is not enough to reveal what kind of abilities humans need to have language abilities. The research object of patholinguistics is abnormal human language. It studies the basic conditions for human beings to be able to produce language by studying the relationship between the physiological or psychological defects of patients with speech disorders and the patients' missing language ability. _x000D_
Patholinguistics is an emerging discipline that spans linguistics, psychology, physiology, medicine and other disciplines. The study of patholinguistics will deepen our understanding of human language and further understand the causes of language disorders in patients with language disorders. It will play an important role in the diagnosis of patients with language disorders and the design of rehabilitation programs. It can relieve or reduce the pain of language-impaired people and their families, thereby reducing social pressure, improving and improving the quality of life, etc. _x000D_

Name: Selected Readings in a Single Classic Work
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The programme is run by a graduate teacher, who assigns students the task of reading books and writing book reports. Before selecting students, please confirm with their mentors.

Name: Historical Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The purpose of the course is to combine Chinese and Western theoretical linguistic studies, to conduct a comprehensive analysis, to study representative historical linguistic theoretical models developed since the end of the nineteenth century and to systematically develop students ' historical linguistic research capabilities. The curriculum is based on Xu Tongyu ' s Historic Linguistics, reading a series of classics of Chinese-language studies, and from a practical point of view in Chinese, in conjunction with the content of the literature reading course, systematically summing up the various models of history linguistics, evaluating the advantages and disadvantages of specific methods in Chinese-language research, enabling students to analyse materials with basic models, discover rules and, as far as possible, develop habits of new methods and principles through material observation and analysis. It covers core topics such as language classification, historical comparisons, structure and sound changes, and the Han Tibetan language system.

Name: Second Foreign Language: French (I)
Introduction: The course is a basic French-language course offered by a zero-basic graduate school and is open during the autumn semester.

Name: Contemporary Phonology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for master's degree majors in linguistics and applied linguistics, including theoretical linguistics (including teaching Chinese as a foreign language) and phonetics. It is also a professional elective course for master's and doctoral degrees in Chinese language and philology and doctoral degrees in linguistics. _x000D_
_x000D_
Phonology is the core subject of linguistics and the basic theoretical knowledge that language major students should possess. This course will lead students to understand the most basic core concepts of generative phonology, including phonemic analysis, distinctive features and natural sound sets, autonomous segments, non-linear syllable theory, morphological phoneme analysis methods, word rhythm, etc. The above knowledge is not only conceptually introduced, but also presented through rich real phonetic phenomena. Students must be familiar with and apply the learned concepts and methods to analyze the phonological changes of various world languages. At the end of the semester, some slightly more advanced phonology theories and methods will also be introduced, such as optimization theory, evolutionary phonology, acoustic foundations of phonology, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
Phonology comprises one of the core subfields of Linguistics; students majoring in Linguistics should therefore be equipped with the basic and crucial knowledge of this subfield. This course will cover the basic topics and theories in Phonology, including phonemic analysis, distinctive features and natural classes, autosegmental theory, syllabification, morphophonemic analysis, as well as word prosody. While learning about the above-mentioned theories and methods, we will also put the knowledge into use by analyzing sound patterns of many languages of the world. Toward the end of the semester, we will also progress a bit to more advanced phonological theories and methods, such as Optimality Theory, Evolutionary Phonology, and Phonetics-based Phonology.

Name: Historical Chinese Grammar (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory graduate course in Chinese and Chinese in Chinese and Chinese at Beijing University. The course is centred on the research of the Maastricht Book, surrounding the grammatical framework of Maastricht and its place in the history of Chinese. - The creation of the Marx and the ancient Mandarin. The Maastricht Institute has developed a complete grammatical system by taking into account the philosophy of Western grammar and observing the fact of the Qin and Han languages. In the course of this process, Ma is really faced with the rich linguistic reality of the Goohan language, focusing on the fundamental objective of the study of grammar, namely, the method of formation of the Chinese language, the law of structure, and not simply the introduction of an existing grammar system in the West and the inclusion of an example of Chinese. The study of the Marx Book will revolve around the following questions: [1] What are the concepts used by the Marx in the construction of the grammar system of the Goohan language? Why do you need these concepts? What is the logic of these concepts? In other words, what are the layers of these concepts? [2] How is the conceptual system set up by Ma to generalize and interpret the facts of the Goohan language? [3] What are the important grammatical realities analysed in the Marx Express? What kind of rules? What kind of trouble did he have in dealing with specific linguistic facts? How did it be solved? On the other hand, what was Ma's description of the Goohan grammatical fact was reasonable and successful? What is unreasonable or unsuccessful? What's the reason for this? The research of ancient Mandarin. Exhibition After more than a hundred years of Ma's Mandarin, several generations of scholars have been constantly exploring and modernizing ancient Chinese grammar studies. The more than 100-year-old Chinese grammar study has not been able to get rid of the full impact of the Marx Express, so it can be considered, to some extent, a history of adaptation and improvement of the grammar system created by Marx. So, what adjustments and improvements have been made to the Marion? What are the adjustments and improvements? More than a hundred years later, what are the real developments in the understanding, portrayal and interpretation of the grammatical features and rules of the Goohan language as compared to the Marx Express? Through a study of the Ma's Book, thinking about and trying to answer the above questions, the basic subjects of the ancient Chinese grammar study can be studied in depth, looking at the nature of the subjects, the value of the system, the current state of affairs, the problems and solutions from both the linguistic and the theoretical background.

Name: Studies in the Shuowen Jiezi (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a required course for majors in the history of Chinese language. The content includes: 1) An introduction to the basic situation of Xu Shen and "Shuowen Jiezi"; 2) Mainly explaining narrative examples, 540 radicals, and six book character examples; 3) Focusing on the characteristics of form-based interpretation of "Shuowen", emphasizing "Mingxing" (Mingguwen, seal style, Libian), "Distinguishing meaning" (distinguishing the original meaning, extended meaning, and borrowed meaning) and "Zhiyin" (knowing ancient sounds, rhymes, and tunes). Teaching adopts the method of explanation and discussion, using Duan Yucai's "Shuowen Jiezi Annotation" as the teaching material.

Name: Historical Chinese Phonology (Part 1)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: "Ancient Phonology" is a compulsory course for graduate students in the "History of Chinese Language" major in Chinese philology and an elective course for graduate students in other directions. It is divided into two sections: "upper" and "lower". The teaching goal is to require graduate students to have an in-depth understanding of the medieval Chinese phonology centered on the phonology of "Qie Yun" and the ancient Chinese phonology centered on the phonology of "The Book of Songs", to further become familiar with research materials on the history of Chinese phonetics, to comprehensively master research methods, and to have a clear understanding of the history of subject development, in order to strengthen the professional foundation and improve research capabilities. The teaching method is to allow students to intensively read various representative important monographs under the guidance of teachers, supplemented by classroom discussions, to deeply understand and summarize the research methods and main conclusions of past dynasties, and to integrate them with modern linguistic theories. This semester's "Ancient Phonology? Part 1" mainly reads "Qie Yun Kao" by Chen Li in the Qing Dynasty and Gu Yanwu's "Five Books on Phonology". Cross-reference "Qie Yun Kao" with modern research results to deepen the familiarity with the phonology of "Qie Yun". Through "Five Books on Phonology", we can understand the research foundation of ancient phonetics and the establishment process of ancient phonetics.

Name: Studies in Sound-Meaning Relationships
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The relationship between sound and meaning is the essential attribute of language symbols, and the study of the relationship between sound and meaning plays an undoubted fundamental role in the study of language and related disciplines. This course systematically teaches the relevant results of studying the relationship between sound and meaning in the history of Chinese language studies, the basic materials and methods for studying the relationship between sound and meaning, relevant theoretical and practical knowledge, as well as specific research topics that need further exploration in the future; combines ancient sound and meaning materials to teach Chinese phonetic meaning Various complex relationships and historical development between them, and the specific research status of Chinese word formation with changing sounds, changing rhymes, word formations with changing tones, and complex word formations with complex phonetic changes will be taught in sequence; the basic role of the study of Chinese phonetic and semantic relationships in promoting theoretical and practical research in Chinese and related disciplines will be discussed. The course focuses on cultivating students' practical abilities and laying a solid foundation for students to engage in future research related to the relationship between Chinese phonetics and meanings.

Name: Qing Dynasty Evidential Scholarship
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course begins with a cataloguing and presentation of the results of research related to fresh science, centred on 200 major reference and tool books for CES. A comprehensive analysis and discussion is then conducted, focusing on the reasons for the formation of the CSA, the methods and affiliations of the CSA, the key representatives of the CEA, the achievements and shortcomings of the CEA, etc., so as to provide students with an in-depth understanding of CEA and an understanding of its governance characteristics, and to provide a solid foundation for future learning and research. The course is conducted in a combination of classroom lectures and teacher-student discussions to produce academic papers relevant to the examination criteria to reflect the achievements of the course.

College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Name: Historical Chinese Phonology (Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course goes on to follow up on the subject of Anticothecology, which requires Masters Studies in Chinese History to continue their study of important literature books, such as the Classical Standard and the Six Phonograms, and to acquire a comprehensive and thorough knowledge of Chinese speech history and mastering research methods, after an excellent reading of the Mid-Cultural Phonography Department and the Kuinyinwu Five, which are centred on the Musical System, with a view to strengthening the professional base and improving research capabilities. The course has been in operation for many years and has become a compulsory postgraduate course in Chinese history, with a good teaching base and practical experience. The method of teaching is to enable students to read several representative monographs under the direction of the teacher, supplemented by classroom discussions, to understand and summarize the research methods and main conclusions of past generations and to integrate them with modern linguistic theory.

Name: Studies in the Shuowen Jiezi (Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a required course for postgraduate students (master's and doctoral students) majoring in the history of Chinese language. The content includes: 1) An introduction to the basic situation of Xu Shen and "Shuowen Jiezi"; 2) Mainly explaining narrative examples, 540 radicals, and six book character examples; 3) Focusing on the characteristics of form-based interpretation of "Shuowen", emphasizing "Mingxing" (Mingguwen, seal style, Libian), "Distinguishing meaning" (distinguishing the original meaning, extended meaning, and borrowed meaning) and "Zhiyin" (knowing ancient sounds, rhymes, and tunes). Teaching adopts the method of explanation and discussion, using Duan Yucai's "Shuowen Jiezi Annotation" as the main teaching material, supplemented by other relevant materials.

Name: Exegesis of Classical Chinese Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is an elective course in the history of Chinese language for graduate students majoring in Chinese language and philology in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature. This course is based on courses such as "Ancient Chinese", "Philology", and "Phonetics" and aims to further improve students' ability to read ancient books, while cultivating students' ability to discover and solve difficult problems in ancient books, and improve students' scientific research level and ability. _x000D_
Through the study of this course, we hope to achieve two goals: (1) To enable students to understand the basic content of traditional Chinese exegesis, including the exegetical styles contained in ancient Chinese classics, the exegetical terms commonly used in ancient books, the exegetical methods commonly used by ancients, and A brief history of Chinese exegesis, etc.; (2) Enable students to accurately understand the meaning of the original text and annotations in the process of studying ancient books and annotations, and use common exegetical methods to judge right and wrong, and solve various difficult problems in ancient book reading and ancient Chinese teaching.

Name: Lecture Series on Frontier Issues in Modern Chinese
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The "Lecture on Frontier Issues in Modern Chinese" postgraduate course is jointly taught by teachers from various research directions in the Modern Chinese Teaching and Research Office. The teachers' recent research results or research ideas are introduced in the form of lectures, and the academic value and significance of the research results are discussed. The purpose of this course is to help graduate students in the Modern Chinese Teaching and Research Section understand the latest developments in different research directions such as modern Chinese pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, dialects, teaching Chinese as a foreign language, and Chinese information processing, and understand the development trends of this discipline at home and abroad. Through lectures and discussions, graduate students can understand valuable new topics, new ideas, and new methods in the current academic world, strengthen graduate students' problem awareness, theoretical awareness, and method awareness, and inspire and encourage graduate students to choose cutting-edge research topics to carry out research work. _x000D_
  Assessment methods and requirements: Complete a course report. It is required to comment on the latest domestic and foreign research on a certain academic topic, and to analyze and discuss issues worthy of further research.

Name: Studies in Chinese Dialects
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for graduate students in the field of Chinese dialectology, and is also available as an elective course for graduate students in other fields. The prerequisite course is "Chinese Dialectology" for undergraduate students or "Introduction to Dialectology" for graduate students. This course covers dialect pronunciation, dialect vocabulary, dialect grammar, dialect division, dialect evolution, dialect contact, etc. Focusing on the analysis of several dialect phenomena, it introduces how to use the basic principles and methods of linguistics to study Chinese dialects, and also reviews and discusses some cutting-edge issues in Chinese dialectology. Students who choose the course should independently complete a related paper before the end of the semester.

Name: Overview of Research in Middle Chinese
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course provides an overview of the study in Chinese. Three issues of the “update” “modern” “modern” in the history of Chinese have been relatively independent and have achieved remarkable results. As an indispensable part of the history of Chinese, the Chinese language (in the East Han-Tang Tang section) is receiving increasing attention from the academic community, and it is imperative to conduct relatively independent research. This course will provide a detailed summary of the national and international studies on Chinese grammar, among others, by comparing them with the previous and recent times, and will be based on a careful assessment, drawing attention to the methods and priorities of research in Chinese in order to develop their research capacity in this field.

Name: Cognitive Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course teaches the basic concepts, basic principles, research methods and research content of cognitive linguistics, especially the basic methods and related topics of cognitive research on Chinese grammar. Contents include: (1) Prototype theory and the structure of categories, the prototype of grammatical categories, (2) Conceptual level and categorization level, basic level categories and partial productivity of language, (3) Concept metaphor and metonymy, physical experience and image schemas, (4) Figures and backgrounds, and the prominence principle of language expression, (5) Selective attention, conceptual framework and language construction, (6) Conceptual space and conceptual fusion, cognitive correlation and pragmatic reasoning, (7) The symbolic reality of language and the copying of syntax, (8) Chinese functional grammar based on cognition, (9) From cognitive research to computational analysis, (10) Cognitive linguistics and second language teaching.

Name: Studies in Old Chinese Phonology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will first introduce various materials for the study of ancient phonetics, mainly internal evidence materials, including the nature of the material, its role and limitations in the study of ancient phonetics, how to collect, organize, and utilize various materials, and how to discover ancient phonetic issues from the materials; then, focusing on the current cutting-edge and hot issues in the study of ancient phonetics, it will introduce existing research in Chinese and foreign academic circles and explain The speaker made necessary arguments for his systematic insights into ancient initial consonants, rhyme parts, finals, and tones, aiming to enable graduate students to systematically master some knowledge of ancient pronunciation, inspire them to think independently about ancient pronunciation issues, and deepen the research on ancient pronunciation; combined with the knowledge of ancient pronunciation that has been obtained, he explained the significance and value of ancient pronunciation knowledge in solving related subjects.

Name: The "Global Sixties" in Film
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will start with relevant film and documentary materials, and select the 1960s - an era that created a revolution in film aesthetics and recorded dramatic changes in the world through film, to reflect on and explore the deep imprint of highly inherent Eurocentrism in historical writing and social imagination. The starting point of this course is: discovering history in the third world. The speaker intends to enter from the concept and perspective of the "global sixties" and explore the significance, cultural heritage, ideological and theoretical value of the global sixties. Discuss the global changes after World War II and a series of major political events in third world countries, and try to outline the global picture of the 1960s. Through the turbulence and revolution of the 1960s, we sort out the ideological genealogy, historical and theoretical legacies and debts.

Name: Research Instrument Design
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to improve an important part of postgraduate thesis research ability, that is, the design and execution ability of research tools. Whether a data collection strategy based on qualitative means or a data collection strategy based on quantitative means is adopted, the appropriateness of the research tools determines the quality and usability of the data collected. Generally speaking, in research methods courses, students learn more about various specific methods of data collection. Few courses specifically focus on the design and execution of research tools. Therefore, this course will be an important supplement to general research methods courses. I have been teaching the postgraduate course "Empirical Research Cycle" for many years. Based on the four mainstream methods, I guide graduate students to choose appropriate topics and go through all stages of the entire research cycle during the course, which is very popular among students. During the teaching process, the students' training and level of how to produce appropriate research tools are seriously insufficient, especially the design of qualitative research tools. This is also an important driving force for me to offer this course. This course mainly focuses on the design of four main types of research tools: 1) Interview outline; 2) Participant observation tool; 3) Questionnaire; 4) Post-coding framework

Name: Business Demography
Introduction: The purpose of this course includes: first, focusing on introducing the basic concepts and principles of business demography and the main analytical methods of this emerging discipline; second, focusing on explaining how to use demographic research methods to make business planning decisions and provide theoretical basis for the layout of government public facilities. This course is intended for master's or doctoral students in sociology, demography, public administration and other majors.

Name: The Botany of Food
Introduction: "Food is the first necessity of the people" is a saying we have all heard since childhood. But do you know what our food is? How did our food evolve during the long development of human civilization? How to ensure nutritious, safe and stable food supply for all humans on earth in the future? The answers to these questions lie in the delicious and magical world of plants. Plants are the primary producers supporting the earth's biosphere and the most important source of human food. For thousands of years, the roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits, and seeds of plants have provided all seven nutrients needed by humans: water, protein, oil, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, and dietary fiber. The domestication of wild crops and vegetables is the beginning of all ancient civilizations, including the Chinese civilization. In recent centuries, the observation and study of plant life activities have greatly promoted the development of life sciences and natural sciences. More importantly, as the world's population grows and natural resources become increasingly stretched, each of us is a stakeholder in modern agriculture, because agriculture is related to personal health, social progress, and how humans can coexist harmoniously with nature and develop sustainably. This course will comprehensively demonstrate and explain knowledge related to food nutrition and safety from multiple aspects such as nutritional composition, plant classification and development, crop domestication, biotechnology, and agricultural big data. Plants are our wonderful neighbors and close partners, condensing our history and nurturing our future. If you love life and care about nature, you are welcome to take "Botany on the Tip of the Tongue" as an elective!

Name: Survey of China
Introduction:
This course is a public required course for international postgraduate students at Peking University, as well as students from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, on the development status, challenges and future prospects of contemporary China's economy, politics, society, culture, science and technology and other fields. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is taught 10 times, 3 hours each time, 8 of which are special report lectures. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is divided into two classes, namely the English-taught class and the Chinese-taught class. A student can only take one of these electives. _x000D_
_x000D_
The degree programs of the following departments (Yenjing Academy, School of Government, Law School, and National Development Institute) currently offer such courses. International students and students from Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan in these departments can complete the relevant courses specified in the training plan in this department without taking this course. _x000D_
_x000D_
In this course, the teacher will arrange basic reading materials in advance and ask questions for thinking. The lectures are mainly interactive, stimulating students' enthusiasm and curiosity to understand contemporary China, and inspiring students to understand and study Chinese issues. The content of teachers' lectures is problem-oriented, focusing on one or two issues in the field, rather than general content. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Gender, Marriage and Family
Introduction:
This course uses a gender perspective to think about the study of gender and marriage and family issues, breaks gender stereotypes, and advocates gender equality between marriage and family members. The course not only introduces Western theories, but also focuses on the research and discussion of Chinese issues. Key discussions: 1. Marriage and family in traditional Chinese gender culture; 2. Discussion of gender roles and gender expectations related to marriage and family in gender stereotypes; 3. Thinking about gender power relations in marriage and family; 4. Advocate for research on men’s participation in childcare and housework. 5. Emphasize the gender analysis of laws and public policies related to marriage and family. The course is divided into six parts, each part has 2-3 topics; each topic has two lectures. The course is mainly lecture and discussion. Examination method: 20% reading report; 30% small survey; 50% final paper _x000D_

Introduction:
This course introduces multivariate model analysis of variables at different levels. Its precursor courses are undergraduate "Social Statistics" and "Linear Algebra". _x000D_

Name: Anthropological Demography
Introduction: Demography and anthropology are social science disciplines that emerged in the nineteenth century, and they differ markedly in research methods. Demography focuses on quantitative and quantitative analysis, anthropological characterization, holisticity and cross-cultural comparative studies. Yet the concerns of both are often similar, such as human reproduction, death, family, marriage, etc. In today's international academic community, two disciplines have begun to interact, drawing on each other's theoretical interpretations of demographic phenomena, as well as unique research methods, and even emerging as cross-cutting subjects of “demographic anthropology” or “anthropology”. The former can be seen as a branch of demographic research in the field of anthropology, while the latter is an area of anthropological research in the demographic community. This course is a postgraduate course that brings the two closer together in depth. The purpose of the course is three: 1) to provide an overview of the anthropological development of the population and to identify the main anthropological links of the population, the leading figures, the contribution to population research and the lack of development of this anthropological branch of research. 2) Studies that specifically analyse the anthropological concerns of the population, including ethnic and data collection and analysis, application of demographic studies of anthropological research methods, major factors affecting fertility (including successful fertility, control of fertility, marriage or family forms, kinship systems, etc.), perceptions and treatment of death by different ethnic groups, and “soft” demographic anthropology in the study of population issues. 3) Increased communication between different disciplines, in particular anthropology and other social sciences (mainly demography). The course is expected to allow postgraduate students in different disciplines interested in population studies to interact with each other, to break down possible barriers between different disciplines, to appreciate each other ' s strengths and to further develop their research. At the same time, research methods and unique interpretation perspectives in demographic anthropology can inspire and drive individual research.

Name: Squash
Introduction:
At the beginning of the 19th century, in the center of London's old city, there was a "Fleet Prison", which was dedicated to detaining debtors and nobles who violated criminal laws and canonical rules. In order to pass the boring time in captivity, they entertained themselves by hitting small balls against the wall with a racket-like device. This can be said to be the earliest prototype of squash. _x000D_
      Squash in the true sense was invented by students of the famous aristocratic school - Harrow School, around 1830. Although the students were children of aristocrats, they lived a boring campus life like prisoners, so a sports game of hitting the ball against the wall was invented. It was named after the ball made a sound similar to the English "SQUASH" when it violently hit the wall, which is today's squash sport. Soon, this recreational fitness sport became popular in schools. In 1864, the first dedicated squash court was built in Harrow, which also became a symbol of the official establishment of the sport. With the British colonial expansion at the end of the 19th century, squash was brought to the Commonwealth countries by the British and spread rapidly around the world. _x000D_
      Entering the 20th century, squash has been widely popularized, with the emergence of a large number of outstanding players, and the unified authoritative management organization of the world squash world was born (1967). It was initiated and established by the then squash powers Australia, Canada, the United Kingdom, India, New Zealand, Pakistan, South Africa, the United States and the United Arab Emirates, and was named the International Squash Federation (ISRF). In 1992, it was renamed the World Squash Federation (WSF). Mainland China started the sport of squash relatively late, with the Chinese Squash Association (CSA) established in 1999. _x000D_
      Squash is a ball game in a venue with four walls. According to certain rules, a racket is used to hit the ball against the wall, and both players alternately hit the ball that bounces off the wall. _x000D_
      Squash is fast-paced, heavy-loaded, and highly entertaining. It is easy to learn, passionate and fashionable, charming and elegant, and has high fitness efficiency. It is a very good mass entertainment and fitness project, and it is also a competitive sports project with great appreciation value. _x000D_
      _x000D_
      This course aims to popularize the sport of squash and is aimed at teaching beginners with no basic knowledge. Mainly teaches the basic techniques, tactics, rules and court equipment of squash. _x000D_

Name: Python
Introduction:
This course is offered to students in MEM specialties, starting with python grammar and programming, and then learning about data acquisition, data processing, data analysis and the development of artificial intelligence applications in the machine learning library of python.
Through this course of study, students are able to understand Python ' s programming model (command programming, function programming) and master and are able to use Python operators, built-in functions and basic data types such as lists, metagroups, dictionaries, collections, vectors, matrices, etc. Proficiency in the design and use of Python branch structure, cycle structure, function design and classes, in the use of string methods, regular expressions, in the debugging of Python programs, and in the design of Python-oriented programs.
