Name: Business Data Mining and Analytics
Introduction: Systematic presentation of basic theories and techniques of data mining, knowledge systems and practical techniques to help students acquire data mining in the commercial sphere, and the development of skills and hands-on skills to solve business problems through data mining. The curriculum requires students to have a certain mathematical and computer base, including advanced mathematics, probabilistic theory and computer introduction. Through the study of the above-mentioned courses, students can learn about the associated mathematical concepts of probabilities, statistics, etc., and have a degree of abstract logic and ability to apply the relevant algorithms of the course using tool software.

Name: Case Studies in Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Introduction:
This course is a case analysis course in the field of innovation and entrepreneurship. It mainly conducts research on actual cases through special lectures by entrepreneurs and entrepreneurs, as well as field trips to companies, and conducts case analysis under the leadership of the course host. _x000D_
Through this course, students will become familiar with the practice of innovation and entrepreneurship, laying a solid foundation for students to engage in related work in the future. _x000D_

Introduction:

1. Learning to use physiology experimental instruments to develop physio-surgery skills, to exercise the student ' s ability to analyse problems and solve them, and basic design experiments.
In conjunction with the design of the course “Physiology” the relevant experimental content is used to observe and document physiology phenomena, to validate classical and basic physiology patterns and to consolidate the theoretical knowledge of physiology.

Executive summary
1. Fundamentals and methods of use of physiology experimental instruments; characterization of irritating signals.
Bioelectric properties and physiological function characteristics of the irritable tissue (neurological and muscular).
Bioelectric properties specific to the heart as a blood cycle “pump” and its connection to the physical function of the heart.
4. Regulation of the activity of the respiratory and cardiovascular systems in the nervous and endocrine systems.
5. Characteristics of neurodulgation of organs in the machine and factors regulating internal activity.

A group of students of one to three (based on different experiments) operate experiments on their own.

Name: Methods and Practice of Technological Innovation
Introduction: This course mainly uses various teaching methods such as lectures, discussions and experiences to enable students to become familiar with the development of science and technology, understand various innovative thinking methods, master technological innovation methods, and ultimately understand that technological innovation is a process of integrating science and technology and economy. The course first uses teaching organization modes such as teaching lectures and discussions to enable students to learn a variety of innovative methods, such as trial and error methods, brainstorming methods, etc. It focuses on introducing TRIZ theory, including engineering problems, innovation principles, contradiction matrix, separation rules, technical contradictions, physical contradictions, contradiction transformation and application, and evolutionary rules of technical systems. Secondly, practical teaching links are used to enable students to understand and master technological innovation as a multi-stage decision-making process that integrates market demand, ideological design implementation, key problem solving, and achievement protection and sharing.

Name: Ideological and Political Practice (Part 1)
College: Peking University Committee of the Communist Youth League of China
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for first-year undergraduate students. It aims to rely on the content of ideological and political theory courses and guide and organize students to participate in practical activities such as volunteer service and philanthropic teaching based on students’ growth and development needs, so as to cultivate and enhance the ideological and political literacy, patriotism, social cognition, sense of responsibility and dedication of young students at Peking University. _x000D_
This course is a 1-credit compulsory course for the whole school, and is divided into two modules: "Philharmonic Learning" and "Volunteer Service". After the first-year students' academic affairs system automatically selects courses, students can choose one of the above two modules as the learning direction of the "Ideological and Political Practice (Part 1)" course, and complete the necessary study plans according to the course requirements of the above two modules. After passing the department assessment, they will receive course credits. _x000D_
This course requires selected students to participate in corresponding theoretical courses, practical activities and achievement presentations, and submit written assignments such as insights, reports, and papers.

This course is a 1-credit compulsory course for the whole school, including a module of "Social Practice". Name: Selected Topics in the Theory of Functions of Several Complex Variables
Prerequisite: Basic courses for undergraduates and graduate students such as theory of functions of real variables, theory of functions of complex variables, functional analysis, abstract algebra, commutative algebra, differential manifolds, differential equations, algebraic topology, differential topology, etc.
Introduction: The course focuses on the basic methodology of the multi-variant function theory and discusses some recent developments.

Name: Introduction to Phenomenology
Introduction:
This course is an introductory course on the phenomenology of Husserl, the founder of phenomenology in the 20th century. The specific philosophical topics covered in this course are: issues of perception, embodiment, and intersubjectivity. By reading excerpts from three important philosophical texts by Husserl, this course attempts to help students clarify the main concepts and basic distinctions. _x000D_
_x000D_
Students who choose the course are required to read 20-30 pages of designated text before each course. The entire course revolves around the assigned reading text and is mainly conducted in the form of lectures. _x000D_
_x000D_
Students who choose the course are required to submit a final paper. The paper should rely primarily on Husserl's own philosophical texts and course notes. The main goal of the paper is to demonstrate that you have mastered the basic concepts and main distinctions in Husserl's philosophical texts. In addition, students can refer to the research works of other phenomenologists to draw philosophical conclusions or question some philosophical assumptions.

Name: Becoming a Better Self at Peking University
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is mainly to help freshmen integrate and adapt to university life as quickly as possible. The main content starts from guiding students to have a comprehensive and objective self-awareness, analyzing common major selection issues among students, helping them to objectively and correctly understand their majors, and to personally experience the relationship between majors, interests, abilities and life development through communication with teachers on campus. Then teach students some practical methods and strategies to improve self-management skills, as well as ways to communicate with others, make new friends, and maintain a positive and optimistic attitude. Finally, through off-campus inspections, students can understand society, establish a sense of responsibility, improve holistic education, and guide students to establish their university goals and life direction, and grow into better selves.

Name: Environmental Laboratory Safety
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction:
Environmental science and engineering is a more practical subject, and students in this direction need to be involved in experiments in water and soil gas and in field practice, and the safety of laboratories and field training is the primary responsibility and necessary knowledge. Sites of environmental experiments have some of the same safety requirements as traditional chemical, biological, physical laboratories, etc., and some of the specialties of the profession, covering both hazardous chemicals, high-temperature and high-pressure facilities, and risk factors such as water and electricity, as well as safety concerns such as biosafety, field practice processes, etc. Experiments therefore need to have solid laboratory and field safety knowledge and skills.
The teaching of environmental laboratory safety includes laboratory safety facilities, fire safety, pressure container safety, water electrical safety, chemical and agent configuration and disposal, disposal of hazardous chemicals and wastes, safety of ionizing and non-ionising radiation, biosafety, safety of field practice, etc., by focusing on safety examples in specialized and relevant types of experiments through teaching by teachers, on-site visits and hands-on exercises, directing students to enhance safety awareness and responsibility, learn safety knowledge, train safety skills and develop safety habits. It is essential that safety is a matter for you and me.

Name: Simulation Methods for Optimization and Learning
Introduction: This course explains the key points of dynamic stochastic model analysis and optimization using computer simulation. The focus of the course is on using discrete event dynamic systems to simulate stochastic systems, and on analyzing and improving the performance of their simulations through discrete event simulation. Applications of the course content are widely distributed in a variety of fields, from social networks to computer networks, and from financial engineering to business processes. This course will introduce students to the application of computer simulation in dynamic stochastic model analysis through simulation-based optimization and learning methods. The overarching question the course answers is how to use simulation to make better, more responsible decisions for real-life problems. In addition, the course will review the technological and mathematical theoretical advances we have witnessed in addressing the above issues. While actively designing simulation topics, the course will also take time to review the corresponding mathematical and technical models. That is to say, while learning practical technologies, the course encourages students to think about and summarize relevant scientific and technological development results.

Name: Introduction to Human Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The introduction to humanities and geography is an important basic course in human geography and urban and rural planning management and urban and rural planning.
The course seeks to introduce some changes in the traditional teaching philosophy of humanities and geography, with emphasis on stimulating interest among students, emphasizing both theory and practice, by combining theoretical knowledge of humanities and geography with the case studies of urban and rural planning and local development strategies, emphasizing the context and characteristics of rural and urban planning at Beijing University, and emphasizing the use of humanities and geography in national economic development, particularly in urban and rural planning practices. As a basic course of specialization, the above-mentioned teaching lines are adapted to the special characteristics of undergraduate students in the first and second grades of humanities and urban and rural planning, and are of interest to them in further study of the various branches of humanities and geography, to understand the specific uses and important mental characteristics of this subject, and to play an important role in the training of students in the scientific field of urban and rural planning and humanities and urban and rural planning management.
The course's companion material, Human Geography: Theory and Application, complements the teaching process, focusing in particular on the following three features: first, the shift from a purely “knowledge” focus to an emphasis on “interest”; secondly, a shift from a purely “theory” focus to a “theory and practice application”; and thirdly, a shift from a focus on “scientific orientation” to a “building the mindset of discipline”.

Name: Fundamentals of Engineering Fluid Mechanics
Prerequisite: calculus (I, II), high calculus, high algebra, constant differential equation, engineering mathematics (including compound function, mathematical physics equation), theoretical mechanics
Introduction: The Basics of Engineering Flow Mechanics are one of the main basic courses in the fields of thermal and power engineering, oil and gas and oil machinery, construction environment and equipment engineering, civil engineering, environmental engineering and light engineering. The purpose of the course is to provide the necessary basic theoretical and experimental skills for the study of professional subjects and for technical engineering work. The teaching of the curriculum focuses on the basic principles of hydrodynamics and on the engineering applications of hydrodynamics, including the basics of basics, hydrostatics, ideal hydrodynamics, the basics of visceral hydrodynamics, rotational and dynamic flows, and gastrodynamics.

Name: Signal Processing and Systems
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Signals and systems is an important course in electronics-related disciplines. It studies the basic concepts and basic analysis methods of signal and system theory, understands how to establish mathematical models, solve them through appropriate mathematical analysis, and provide physical explanations and physical meanings to the results obtained. This course "Signal Processing and Systems" is offered to students majoring in microelectronics, integrated circuits and other related majors. In addition to the basic content of time domain analysis, Fourier transform, Laplace transform, z-transform of continuous-time systems and discrete-time systems, it also strengthens the s-domain analysis methods and system functions of continuous systems for the subsequent learning and research needs of analog integrated circuits. Explanation and practice of zero-pole analysis of numbers, root locus method, system stability determination, establishment of system state equations and solution of state equations; for the direction of digital integrated circuits, based on z-transform and z-domain analysis of discrete systems, students can understand the preliminary content of digital signal processing such as discrete Fourier transform, fast Fourier transform, and digital filters. Due to the wide application of computer-aided design, this course will also provide a brief introduction to Matlab/SimuLink, an important tool, to reduce the hand calculation requirements for complex circuits. _x000D_
Because this course involves a lot of content, it is planned to downplay the mathematical derivation process and emphasize physical images and physical meanings. It is hoped that it can lay a better foundation for subsequent learning and research.

Name: Introduction to Spin and Superconducting Quantum Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: This course is mainly for second- and third-year undergraduate students in information science (electronics, microelectronics/integrated circuits, computers, artificial intelligence, etc.), physics, materials and other similar majors. There are no special prerequisites. But you need to have some basic knowledge of programming (such as Python/Matlab/Mathematica, etc.). It would be better if you have preliminary knowledge of linear algebra, quantum physics and other related courses.
Introduction: This course introduces basic concepts, device technology, circuits and algorithm applications in spintronics and quantum information science. The course includes classroom lectures and supplementary tutorials on hands-on learning of simulation tools. Students are expected to demonstrate through hands-on work (using simulation tools) the ability to apply fundamental principles to understand spintronics and superconducting quantum technologies. This course will be jointly taught by Professor Shao Qiming of the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.

Name: Approaching German-Speaking Countries through Their Language

Introduction:
In response to the call of the Ministry of Education, the School of Foreign Languages ​​at Peking University has launched an experimental class for cultivating top-notch “multilingual international talents” students starting from September 2019. This project is aimed at top-notch students in various majors with excellent English proficiency, excellent professional academic performance, and sufficient learning ability to strengthen their second and third foreign languages. At the same time, they will consolidate their English proficiency and strive to reach the level of their mother tongue, so as to cultivate the outstanding talents of "one proficiency, multiple skills" and "one specialty, multiple abilities" that the country urgently needs. _x000D_

In addition, graduates of this major should have the ability to learn across majors and cultures. They should not only excel in the field of foreign language majors, but also become experts in various fields by virtue of the rigorous, systematic and formal theoretical and skill training they have received. _x000D_

At the same time, they should also be able to understand, accommodate, and appreciate various cultural differences, have a broad vision, and become outstanding talents who promote the harmonious development of society. _x000D_
In this course, by studying the original German textbooks, you will develop a more systematic understanding of the German language, acquire the basic abilities of listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation, and lay a solid foundation for eventually reaching the intermediate German level according to European language standards.

Name: Intermediate Organic Chemistry Laboratory
College: College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering
Introduction: In intermediate organic chemistry experiments, students are required to use the theoretical knowledge and experimental techniques they have learned to identify and address problems encountered in relation to specific topics; to enhance knowledge of, and learning about, the basics of more recent studies in organic chemistry and to develop the capacity to recreate documentation methods, focusing on the research potential reflected in the experiments. Further develop good laboratory and research practices, including access to literature, data collection, analytical evaluation of results, complete reporting specifications, etc. The selected pilot projects are based on multi-step synthesis, with the subject matter of the experiment being of some relevance, operational difficulty, methodological characteristics and training in a comprehensive manner.

Name: Field Research in Health Economics
Introduction: Students in the field of health economics must not only learn the theoretical and empirical research methods in this field, but also obtain first-hand data through fieldwork is an important skill. On the other hand, it will comprehensively learn how to conduct scientific population health surveys from the dimensions of sampling methods, questionnaire design, and field execution, understand the data generation process, and master the quality control links, thereby laying the foundation for independently hosting scientific research projects in the future. At the same time, as a practical course, students will participate in a month-long field survey of the China Health and Retirement Tracking Survey (CHARLS) project throughout the summer, gain an in-depth understanding of people's livelihood through social practice, hone their will, exercise communication skills, cultivate the ability to observe, think and solve problems, and cultivate leadership and team spirit.

It is expected to cultivate a group of experts and scholars who can integrate Chinese civilization and world civilization and devote themselves to the future construction of Chinese culture.

Name: Advances in Experimental Atomic Physics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course is based on the seven famous Nobel Prizes in Physics in the history of atomic physics (Rabi's atomic beam magnetic resonance technology in 1944; Kastler's optical pumping technology in 1966; Paul and Dehmelt's ion trap technology in 1989, Ramsey's atomic interference technology; Chu, Cohen-Tannouji, and Phillips' laser cooling technology in 1997; Cornel, Weiman, and Ketterle's evaporative cooling and quantum gas technology in 2001; Hall and Haensch's optical comb generator and precision measurement technology in 2005) as the main line, describing the basic ideas, theories, methods of experimental atomic physics, and important applications and progress in quantum technology. Introduce the principles and applications of the main achievements of today's quantum technology: quantum metrology (high-precision cold atomic clocks, optical clocks, etc.), quantum sensing (cold atom interferometers, atomic magnetometers, etc.), quantum communications, quantum computing, quantum imaging, etc.

Introduction:
This course is an innovation and entrepreneurship methods course that introduces the basic principles of business models and technology commercialization methods. Available to students of all majors. _x000D_
The course helps students master the principles and methods of accelerating technology transfer and realizing social and economic value in the context of major technological changes. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Mesoscopic Optics
Introduction: This course introduces the basic principles, measurement techniques, and applications of mesoscopic optics. The first part introduces the development history, basic concepts, basic principles, theoretical analysis methods, applications, development frontiers, and interdisciplinary aspects of surface plasmons in metal micro-nano structures. The second part introduces the basic principles, implementation methods, and applications of photonic crystals in integrated photonic devices and other fields. The third part introduces the basic principles, implementation methods and important applications of high-quality factor optical microcavities, such as filtering, micro-nano lasers, microcavity QED, biosensing, etc. This course focuses on the close integration of basic knowledge and cutting-edge research, expands students' academic horizons, and helps students become familiar with the research frontiers in the field of mesoscopic optics as soon as possible.

Name: Linear Algebra A (I)
Introduction: This course will study linear equations, determinants, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues ​​and eigenvectors of matrices, quadratic forms, etc., so that students can initially master the basic theory, basic methods and basic skills of linear algebra, and cultivate students' scientific thinking and ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Linear Algebra A (I) Problem Session
Introduction: This course will study linear equations, determinants, matrices, vector spaces, eigenvalues ​​and eigenvectors of matrices, quadratic forms, etc., so that students can initially master the basic theory, basic methods and basic skills of linear algebra, and cultivate students' scientific thinking and ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Linear Algebra A (II)
Introduction: This course will study linear space, linear transformation, Euclidean space and unitary space, matrix analysis, tensor product, etc., so that students can initially master the basic theory, basic methods and basic skills of linear algebra, and cultivate students' scientific thinking and ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: Linear Algebra A (II) Problem Session
Introduction: This course will study linear space, linear transformation, Euclidean space and unitary space, matrix analysis, tensor product, etc., so that students can initially master the basic theory, basic methods and basic skills of linear algebra, and cultivate students' scientific thinking and ability to analyze and solve problems.

Name: General History of Technology
Introduction: The course outlines the course of technological development in the context of the history of human civilization. It does not focus on the appearance of a mechanical “year of invention” nor on the structural principles of technological instruments, but rather on the human face of technology, highlighting its interaction with social and cultural cultures. The course is an overview of the years, with the most representative technical cases of the time, and under each topic it is not limited to a single moment. For example, “Mechanical clocks” have emerged in the late mid-century of Europe, and this course will include a section on the theme “Medieval clocks” in the context of the medieval to the early days of recent times; instead of being limited to the late part of the European medieval century, the course will be devoted to modern atomic clocks from ancient time-calculations techniques and introduce Chinese time-calculations as a comparison with relevant cultural phenomena. Understanding the history of the clock and its socio-cultural implications for Western Europe in a broader perspective. The overall course is presented in more than a dozen presentations on representative technological innovations from different times, such as pottery, writing, mechanical clocks, steam machines, computers, etc.

Name: Quantitative Molecular Biology
Introduction: The quantitative molecular biology described in this course is a freshman in the field of integration for the Institute of Penitentiary Studies and is offered in the first semester. This course consists of studies on molecular biology base and four quantitative topics: (1) a dichotomy system; (2) random movement of organisms; (3) ratio equation; and (4) introduction to system biology. This course is aimed at new entrants, and the knowledge of mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology will be adequately supplemented, so there is no need for a first course. The greatest feature of the course is a superficial introduction to the concept of quantification for young people who have just entered the university and started systematic learning of life sciences. Quantitative research involves cross-cutting and cooperation in different fields, and is a major trend in scientific research, for which the North Congress has created a front-line intersection The Faculty of Sciences, where the teacher of the subject holds the position of a quantitative biology centre. Through the course, students are expected to learn and accept the idea of quantitative research from the outset of their studies at the university level, and to learn the glamour of cutting-edge cross-cutting subjects, which is the main purpose of the course. The subject is relatively easy to understand and provides a good basis for future systematic learning by students. In the molecular biology sector, an optional course is available in the future: (1) Molecular Biologic College of Life Sciences (College of Life Sciences); (2) College of Life Sciences (College of Life Science) of RNA biochemistry of Life Sciences; (3) Biochemistry (Integrated Science); (4) Courses such as Biophysical Chemistry College of Chemistry and Molecular Engineering continue to be developed. In the area of quantitative studies, further study is possible in the future through courses such as: (1) Physical Biologic of The Cell College of Life Sciences; and (2) Science of Mathematical Science. This course is the basis for the above-mentioned courses, does not conflict with them and can be well integrated

Name: General History of Science
Introduction: General History of Science is an introductory history of science course that introduces the panoramic historical picture of the five thousand years of human scientific development with clear clues. It tells both the history of Western science and the history of Chinese science; it pays attention to both the speculative tradition of philosophers and the technical tradition of craftsmen; it pays attention to both the logical development of scientific ideas and the social and cultural background of science; it involves both the mathematical and physical science traditions and the natural history tradition. The course consists of two blocks of 15 lectures. The first block (Lectures 1-6) tells the history of the development of science and technology in the four ancient civilizations, ancient Greece and Rome, Arabia, and the European Middle Ages in chronological order; the second block (Lectures 7-14) talks about the three major traditions of modern science, institutional construction, and their impact on the world landscape, social culture, and production methods by theme. The last lecture is the spread of Western science to China.

Name: Interpreting the World Economy
Introduction: This course is a sister course of "Special Topics on Chinese Economy". If the theory of new structural economics in "Special Topic on Chinese Economy" is used to analyze China's rise and fall and then from decline to prosperity, then this course "Interpreting the World Economy" is the application and test of the theory of new structural economics in analyzing the distribution of rich and poor in countries around the world and how to move towards common prosperity. The basic goal of the course is to use the least theoretical tools of new structural economics to gain the greatest understanding of the world economic structural change phenomena and policy options.

Name: Ancient Chinese Literature (Part 2)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is an elective course for non-Chinese majors in the Department of Humanities. The course will sort out the Chinese _x000D_ through the teaching of classic literary works of the past dynasties.

The formation process of ethos, revealing the interactive relationship between literature and external factors such as society, thought, politics, etc., and mastering reading, appreciation, and analysis of ancient literature_x000D_
Basic methods of studying works. This course consists of two semesters and is divided into four sections: (1) Literature of Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties; (2) Literature of Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties, Sui, Tang and Five Dynasties_x000D_
Studies; (3) Song and Yuan literature; (4) Ming and Qing modern literature. Taught by four teachers respectively. _x000D_

Name: Cell Culture Laboratory
Introduction: The content of this experimental course includes general knowledge of cell culture and basic principles of aseptic operation, basic experimental techniques such as primary culture and subculture of animal cells, recovery of cryopreserved cells, and cryopreservation of cells, as well as comprehensive experiments such as cell viability determination and cell transfection.

Name: Neural Basis of Learning and Memory
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the brain basis of learning and memory, helping students understand neuroscience research methods, the formation process of learning and memory, the role of different brain areas in the process of learning and memory, changes in brain structure and functional connections in learning and memory, the cellular and molecular basis of learning and memory, related brain diseases that affect learning and memory, and many other contents. Discuss the latest research progress in cutting-edge neurobiology related to learning and memory, and explain in detail the research background, research purpose, research process, results, discussion, references, etc. of each study.

Name: Fundamentals of Network Science and Systems Biology
Introduction: From the network of atomic interactions within molecules to the social networks that connect everyone and the air transportation networks that span the world, our lives today are surrounded by networks of varying scales and characteristics. The rapid development of cheap, high-throughput genomic technologies over the past two decades has brought life sciences into the era of big data, while also improving people's understanding of many biological networks. In addition to the unique properties of different types of networks, the study of the physical properties and generation mechanisms of unified complex network structures is crucial to the correct understanding and application of different complex networks. This course will cover the basic theory of complex systems, basic analysis algorithms of omics data, discussion of classic literature, and case analysis. The teaching of relevant software tools and computer practice are also an integral part of this course. As a key module of this course, the independent research project will provide students with a simulation experience covering the entire process of scientific research, including the conception of original scientific research ideas, actual research, pre-publication discussions, publication, and post-publication scientific communication. Through the research of independent projects, students will combine their own knowledge background and the knowledge and technology learned in this course to analyze network problems contained in the real experimental data provided by this course.

Name: Bioinformatics Laboratory
Introduction:
"Bioinformatics Experiment" is a main basic course for undergraduate students. By leading students to complete representative and advanced experiments in the field of bioinformatics, this course combines the experimental principles, design ideas and experimental techniques of bioinformatics experiments to help students master the basic methods of bioinformatics experiments and cultivate students' scientific research literacy. _x000D_

To this end, the course will adopt a "practice-driven, problem-oriented" practical model, combined with front-line scientific research topics or literature, to provide students with an environment and opportunities to apply the knowledge and skills they have learned in real scientific research data. The course lasts for one academic year and requires students to choose a practical laboratory and participate in scientific research under the guidance of course teachers and laboratory instructors. The final score will be comprehensively evaluated based on daily performance and scientific research progress.

This enables students to have a deep understanding and mastery of the content of Advanced Mathematics A (I).

Name: Primate Behavior, Society and Evolution
Introduction: Why has humankind evolved so successfully? Perhaps we can get some clues from our human cousins, the inhuman primates. The primates, the size of all things, are the more special category of mammals, and now number as many as 500. The behaviour of primates is diverse and highly socialized and is inextricably linked to human beings. Research into primate behaviour and society helps us to understand animal and human behaviour, its origins and evolution. The course will be based on (1) the system of characteristics, classification and behaviour of primates; (2) the history and diversity of the evolution of primates; (3) social behaviour and evolution; (4) reproductive behaviour and evolution; (5) dietary behaviour and nutrition; (6) female and male strategies; (7) personal investment and life history; (8) communication (face expression, voice, etc.) and perception; (9) cultural behaviour; (10) the intellectual and human origin of primates; (12) community ecology of primates, among other things, the protection of primates; and (12) the formation and evolution of the social fabric of behaviour and the exploration of the human origin of animals and human society by looking into the shadows of our ancestors and the mechanisms for the evolution of human society and behaviour.

Name: Introduction to Industrial Production (1)

Through the combination of theory and practice, students can achieve the effect of being exposed to engineering reality and gain industrial experience, which helps to sublimate engineering thinking and engineering methodology while learning industrial knowledge.

Name: A History of American Innovation
Introduction: A history of economic development in the United States is a history of innovative entrepreneurship among immigrants. The course seeks to provide students with an understanding of the characteristics of innovative entrepreneurship at all stages of the history of the United States, as well as the historical patterns of the country ' s flourishing, through teaching, research, reading and case analysis; and an insight into several examples of business growth in the United States that were typically based on youth, as well as the United States ' STI features at the time. It also provides an objective view of the phased differences in the NIS between China and the United States, analyses the uniqueness and commonality of the two countries and draws lessons from the American experience on China.

Name: Territorial Spatial Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: This course is a required professional basic course for urban and rural planning and related majors. On the basis of the urban and rural planning theory introduced in the prerequisite course "Principles of Urban Planning" and combined with the trend of my country's territorial spatial planning reform, the objectives, content, and important practical methods of territorial spatial planning as the research and practice outlet of urban and rural planning disciplines will be further taught. During the course teaching, students are guided to form an interest in in-depth professional learning and expanded research, and master the basic methods of in-depth learning and research. The purpose of this course is to cultivate students to establish a comprehensive and correct concept of ecological civilization and sustainable urban development, and to lay a foundation for students to carry out land and space planning and related practical operations in the future.

Name: Landscape Planning
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Prerequisite: It is recommended that students first learn basic cartographic skills and learn GIS before taking this course. The main prerequisite courses include: Art and Drawing, Introduction to Architecture, Urban Garden Green Space Planning, Urban Planning Principles, and GIS Principles and Applications.
Introduction:
What does the landscape mean? What's landscape planning? What is the context of landscape planning? What are the relationships and differences between landscape planning and urban planning? What kind of career is a landscape planners? What kind of work is it? How does landscape planning relate to neighbouring disciplines? What are the responsibilities and tasks of landscape planning in the context of contemporary Chinese identity?
In the context of these questions, the course will address these questions in conjunction with theoretical, practical design projects and cases. Through cross-scale analysis of urban landscape development processes and integration of the skills of landscape planning, student systems are equipped with the development history, related theories and methodologies of landscape planning.

Name: Historical Geography of Beijing
Introduction:
Beijing is the last capital city in the history of Chinese dynasties. It is still the capital of the country today and has a history of more than 860 years. The shape of Beijing has also changed several times in history, and its geographical space has very prominent characteristics. _x000D_
This course is a seminar class for freshmen from Yuanpei College in 2020. It mainly focuses on the two main lines of Beijing’s history and geography. Students who choose the course will fully appreciate the unique charm of Beijing’s history and geography through rich teaching methods, including regular classroom teaching, field visits, after-class readings, discussions and presentations, etc._x000D_

Name: Introduction to Geobiology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Earth biology is the science of studying the interactions between the biosphere and the environment, focusing on the evolution of the Earth ' s system and the formation of a liveable planet Earth. The course will systematically describe the concept of Earth systems, the main biogeochemical cycling processes on the Earth ' s surface, and the interactions between organisms and the environment in the geological history. In addition, the course will teach geochemical modelling and how to use numerical models to regulate biogeochemical processes.

Name: Digital Circuits and System Design (Honors Section)
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Circuit Analysis or Electronic Line Analysis and Design
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course in the electronic information undergraduate course system. The task of this course is to familiarize students with the principles and functions of the basic components of digital logic circuits (such as digital integrated circuits (SSI, MSI, MEMORY, AD/DA and programmable logic devices, etc.) through course study). And usage methods, master the analysis methods and design methods of digital logic circuits, basically have the ability to design, develop, debug and implement medium-scale digital systems, understand the latest progress in the industry, exercise the ability of digital innovation, and lay a solid foundation for subsequent course learning and future scientific research innovation. _x000D_
The goal of this course focuses on mastering the basic principles, analysis methods and design methods of digital logic circuits, and training the ability to design and apply digital systems. The course requires a team of two to complete a medium-scale digital system prototype design project based on an FPGA development board (such as the Brick Breaking game, electronic keyboard music, smart fan, smart photo frame, Amazon game, MDI controller, etc.) as shown in the picture below, and conduct acceptance through a demonstration report, thereby exercising system design capabilities and innovative design thinking. In addition, this course requires each student to complete a cutting-edge paper reading and sharing, a digital product disassembly and a course content summary. _x000D_
The course requires "Circuit Analysis" or "Electronic Circuit Analysis and Design" first. The total course duration is 80 hours (48+32), including 36 hours of theoretical lectures, 22 hours of small class discussions, and 16 hours of systematic experiments. _x000D_

Name: Appreciation of Chinese Cultural Relics
Introduction: Cultural objects are the material legacy of the various social activities of humankind, as well as the objects of spiritual civilization and the symbol of national cultural traditions. The course will be based on a systematic presentation of the Chinese cultural heritage and will focus on time, highlighting representative cultural objects of various ages in each of the various disciplines, so that the students selected for the course will have an initial knowledge of Chinese cultural heritage and related backgrounds.

Name: Integrated Circuit Logic Synthesis Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Logic synthesis is an important means for optimizing the design of digital integrated circuits. Logic synthesis realizes the mapping of digital designs to process libraries through the process of converting RTL source code into gate-level netlists. _x000D_
During the synthesis process, the optimization process completes the configuration and combination of library units so that the circuit can best meet the functional, timing and area requirements of the design. Logic synthesis is constraint driven, and the given constraints are the goals of synthesis. Constraints are generally obtained through timing analysis of the entire system, and synthesis tools will optimize the circuit to meet the constraints. _x000D_
This course arranges 10 experiments. Through the experimental content, students can learn and master the basic knowledge and practical operations of logic synthesis. Through course study, students can master the basic methods, tool usage, optimization techniques and other knowledge of logic synthesis. _x000D_
The prerequisite for this course is digital logic circuits. _x000D_
This course is an experimental class, and the class time is scheduled for two weeks. There are a total of 10 classes, each time on the computer for 4 hours. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Rural Education in China
Introduction:
The sustained growth and prosperity of our economy over the past three decades have been remarkable for the world. In large cities such as the North and the West, the buildings of high-rises are much larger, and modern infrastructure is no worse than any major city in the world. China ' s outward investment and trade policy is shaping a new pattern of the world economy. As education is fundamental to a country ' s long-term economic growth, the outstanding performance of Shanghai students in the international student assessment project has impressed the Western educational community.
However, many children have not been able to share prosperity in the poor rural areas of the country. Studies have shown that nearly one third of children in poor areas do not complete secondary school and only 7 per cent have access to university. These children will be our main workforce after 10-20 years. There is no doubt, however, that if these children are not provided with a good education, they will not be able to meet the demands of their jobs in the future and will eventually have an impact on our economic development and the upgrading of our industrial structures.
What prevents children in poor rural areas from moving forward? From the point of view of the productive function of education, the theme " Rural education " will lead students to explore ways of solving the problems of rural pre-school, basic and upper secondary education, based on large-scale survey data, from an economic development perspective, around how to improve the human capital of students in poor rural areas.

Name: IP-Based SoC Design Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Digital Logic Circuit, Digital Integrated Circuit Design
Introduction:
The design of integrated circuits has evolved from a single function dedicated to ASIC to a complex system, the system-level chip design (SOC) is based on IP design methods, and the Intellectual Production, also known as Virtual Component, Macro etc., is a reusable circuit module in SOC. Through relevant experimental content, the course learns basic knowledge and practical operation of IP-based SoC design.
The design of digital integrated circuits consists of a top-down design method and a bottom-up design method, in which the course will first learn the bottom-up design method and complete an IP hard core using customized methods; then learn the top-down design method and complete the system design using a semi-customed process; and finally complete the entire design and layout validation through an IP integration.

Through course learning, students can acquire knowledge of the custom and semi-customed design methods of integrated circuits, IP modelling and SOC design methods.

Name: Appreciation of Peking Opera Art
Prerequisite: Interest in traditional culture or the opera, and basic knowledge of the ancient and recent history of China.
Introduction: This course is an elective course for all students in the school. The course adopts a small class teaching mode and combines lectures by famous artists and teaching teachers with live performance demonstrations and discussions. The content covers the development process of Peking Opera art, Peking Opera profession and appreciation of famous pieces of Peking Opera performances. Enable students to appreciate the classics of Peking Opera art form, enhance their artistic aesthetic ability, and improve their cultural literacy.

Name: Physical Design of Integrated Circuits Laboratory
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Physical design is the design implementation process of digital integrated circuits, usually called Place-and-Route. By placing and routing the gate-level netlist and other processes, the digital design is mapped from the gate level to the physical layout. With the continuous development of integrated circuit technology, the physical design of deep sub-micron integrated circuits poses new challenges to designers, such as timing closure, voltage drop, crosstalk analysis and other design challenges. _x000D_
The input file of the physical design of the integrated circuit is the gate-level netlist after logic synthesis. After layout planning, layout, clock tree synthesis, wiring, layout inspection and other processes, layout data for semiconductor processing is output. _x000D_
Layout planning stage: Layout planning mainly includes chip size (area), input and output I/O unit planning, macro module planning and power supply planning, etc.; _x000D_
Layout stage: The layout task is mainly the layout of standard units and macro modules. In order to better achieve timing closure, a timing-driven layout method needs to be adopted. In addition, it also includes congestion analysis of the layout; _x000D_
Clock tree synthesis: The clock network has the largest load, the longest traces, and the most demanding requirements among all signal networks. Therefore, the quality of clock tree synthesis directly affects the performance of the chip. Clock tree synthesis includes settings, synthesis, optimization and other processes; _x000D_
Wiring stage: After the layout and clock tree are integrated, each module and unit needs to be connected through specific interconnection lines to complete the interconnection of all signals, so that the function of the chip can be realized. The specific implementation includes global wiring, detailed wiring and wiring correction. The effect of wiring depends on the layout plan and the algorithm of the tool itself. _x000D_
This course arranges 10 experiments. Through the experimental content, you can learn and master the basic knowledge and practical operations of integrated circuit physical design. Through course study, students can master the basic methods of layout and routing, tool usage, optimization techniques and other knowledge. _x000D_
The prerequisite for this course is digital logic circuits. _x000D_
This course is an experimental class, and the class time is scheduled for two weeks. There are a total of 10 classes, each time on the computer for 4 hours. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Aesthetic Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Aesthetics is the way of transcendence in life, and it accompanies human beings innately. Aesthetic culture is a summary of various aesthetic phenomena in human society. This course focuses on the discussion of works and texts in the field of aesthetic culture. It mainly includes the analysis and discussion of the materialized products (artworks) of aesthetic activities in ancient and modern China and the West, the conceptual system of aesthetic activities, classic documents, and aesthetic behaviors (creation, acceptance, etc.). By introducing a large number of ancient and modern Chinese and foreign aesthetic culture cases, such as various classic works of art, important aesthetic cases and ideological documents, students can fully understand the cultural attributes of aesthetic activities, thereby enhancing the consciousness of aesthetic activities and adding a touch of agility and depth to the bustling real life. _x000D_

Name: Topics in the Centennial History of the Party
Introduction: The main teachings were the 100-year struggles of the Communist Party of China and its experience, deepening the understanding of history and why the people chose Marxism, the Communist Party of China, socialism, reform and openness, and building “four self-confidence”.

Name: Controlled Ecological Experiment Field Practicum
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
This course is a practical course. _x000D_
_x000D_
On the basis of the basic theoretical study of "General Ecology I, II", through field practice, you will master the basic principles of ecological experimental design, understand the internationally advanced ecological control experimental facilities and operations on the spot, and practice the operation of field instruments and the collection process of experimental data. Through field internships and discussions, we are deeply involved in the main processes of ecological scientific experiments.

Name: Advanced Mathematics A (I)
Introduction:
In order to facilitate students in relevant majors to have a more comprehensive and down-to-earth understanding of "Advanced Mathematics A" (Mathematical Analysis for Science and Engineering), and to facilitate comparison with similar courses, here are some explanations about the course. _x000D_
 _x000D_
1.	Course Positioning: Advanced Mathematics A (also known as Mathematical Analysis for Science and Engineering, hereafter referred to as Advanced Mathematics A) is a very important basic course for students majoring in science and engineering who have very high requirements for mathematics. The "very high requirements" here refer to high requirements in terms of course structure, system, theory, concept, method, etc., which are second only to the standards of the mathematical analysis course of the School of Mathematics. In some aspects, such as applications and modeling, the requirements are no less than mathematical analysis.  The "very important basic course" here refers to the concepts, content and methods that a large number of subsequent courses are indispensable for. Mathematics courses closely related to this course include: probability and statistics, differential equations, differential geometry, complex variable functions, real variable functions, functional analysis, etc. Other professional courses such as: basic physics, theoretical mechanics, information, signal processing, data processing, econometrics, economics, chemistry, statistical mechanics, or emerging interdisciplinary and professional directions closely related to mathematics... _x000D_
_x000D_
2.	The position of Advanced Mathematics A in the difficulty chain of similar courses (calculus courses) (from difficult to easy): _x000D_
Mathematical Analysis (Mathematics) > Advanced Mathematics A (Mathematical Analysis of Science and Engineering) > Advanced Mathematics B _x000D_
Note: 1. "Mathematical Analysis for Science and Engineering" is a "simplified version" of mathematical analysis offered by some universities. _x000D_
        2. There is no strict definition of difficulty here. It is based on the common feelings of most students in many years of classroom teaching. No quantitative indicators are given. _x000D_
   Three.  Characteristics of Advanced Mathematics A, comparison with related courses, teaching purposes and requirements. _x000D_
  Advanced Mathematics A focuses on the cultivation and training of basic mathematical abilities and ways of thinking. It requires an overall understanding of the calculus system. It is required to correctly understand the basic concepts in calculus, improve logical derivation capabilities, master the basic methods of proof and calculation, understand the basic ideas of calculus, and skillfully use this knowledge to solve some basic problems. _x000D_
  Advanced Mathematics A is less difficult than mathematical analysis. Specifically, mathematical analysis focuses on the essence of definitions, the construction of systems and structures, the core ideas of the theory, and the connection with other courses. On the other hand, Advanced Mathematics A is slightly more difficult than Advanced Mathematics B. In layman's terms, advanced mathematics B replaces the words "understanding, mastering, understanding, proficiency..." in advanced mathematics A with "understand, understand, understand, know..." and the words related to mathematical analysis are "chew, analyze, dig deep, essence, promote..." _x000D_
The teaching purpose and basic requirements of Advanced Mathematics A: Through the study of this course, junior students in relevant majors will understand the overall framework of the calculus discipline: using real numbers as the platform (set), using limits as tools, and using one-variable functions as the research object, to study the three perspectives of functions: (meso) continuous, (micro) differentiable and (macro) integrable, and then expand the platform from real numbers to the platform Rn where multivariate functions are located. Therefore, the purpose of teaching should highlight the foundation in a univariate scenario and the richness in a pluralistic scenario. _x000D_
    High Mathematics A focuses on cultivating students' intuitive guessing ability, strict logical reasoning ability, abstract thinking ability, and the ability to use mathematical knowledge to solve practical problems, and cultivate and enhance students' rigorous mathematical thinking and scientific spirit of courage to explore. _x000D_

Name: Practice in Intelligent Manufacturing
Introduction: Intelligent manufacturing is an important component of China ' s manufacturing programme and one of the priority areas of science and technology supported by the State. The overall framework of the programme is defined as “Experience of smart manufacturing, consolidation of engineering culture”. The curriculum is defined as a generalization course, cross-grouping of students from multidisciplinary backgrounds such as arts, science and engineering. The course is part of the Theory + Basic Practice Training + Integrated Practice Training Classes, which follow the model of teaching organization for major classes + small seminars. The course, which is carried by the "Soft Cars" project of the National College of Higher Education Integrated Engineering Training Competition, is an in-depth experience of the entire product-making process: mechanical design (undercarnet, mechanical arm), manufacturing (laser cutting, 3D printing), electronic hardware design (sing machines, electric machines, steering machines, sensors), programming control, etc. Integrated project development by learning engineering-related theories (design thinking, engineering thinking and computing thinking), from basic manufacturing methods to the integration of theoretical knowledge and practical skills. The curriculum also allows students to think about the impact of advanced technology on human society and life in the context of current industrial contexts and social hotspots.

Name: Introduction to Environmental Mineralogy
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The ancient discipline of mineral science has focused on the understanding of mineral properties and the open use of mineral resources. With increasing environmental pollution and the widespread use of minerals in environmental governance, the early 1990s saw widespread attention to environmental mineralogy as an emerging discipline in the mineralic neighbourhood. Environmental mineralology is a science that studies the interactions between natural minerals and the various layers of the surface and reflects natural evolution, combating ecological damage, evaluating environmental quality, cleaning up environmental pollution and participating in biological processes. From an environmental perspective, the course introduces mineral types closely related to environmental change, as well as their mineralogical characteristics, presentation methods, environmental response mechanisms, etc., making students aware of the important role of minerals in reflecting environmental changes at different spatial scales, influencing and evaluating environmental ecological health, governance and restoring environmental pollution. Focusing on mechanisms for interaction of typical minerals in the terrestrial environment with the hydrosphere, the atmosphere and the biosphere, which are widespread in the environment, provides students with basic principles and research methods of mineral science and understanding how to use the characteristics of natural minerals to understand and address environmental problems.

Name: The Changing Earth
College: College of Environmental Sciences and Engineering
Introduction: The "Changing Earth" course is a professional basic elective course for undergraduate majors in environmental science. It introduces the multiple layers in the earth system, the interactions between the layers, and the disturbance and impact of human activities on the earth system, especially climate change. Understand the composition, formation and evolution of the atmosphere, lithosphere and hydrosphere in the Earth system, the evolution of the spheres over time, and the biogeochemical cycle of major elements such as carbon. Focus on environmental problems caused by human activities, including greenhouse gases and climate change, photochemical smog, ozone layer destruction and acid rain. This course aims to train students to master the basic theories of the atmosphere, ocean and earth sciences and to understand the common characteristics and interrelationships of each sphere, and to learn to use multidisciplinary methods to analyze various processes in the earth system, so as to have a comprehensive understanding of the impact of human activities on the earth system. This course covers some basic concepts in environmental science, including the composition and vertical structure of the atmosphere and seawater, the basic forms of atmospheric and seawater movement, air-sea interactions, and past, present, and future climate changes. The scope of teaching ranges from the composition, sources and transport of pollutants from urban and regional anthropogenic sources to global environmental issues. This course not only introduces the earth system and the impact of human activities on the system in detail, but also introduces some current important scientific research results in atmospheric science and oceanography.

Name: Systems and Computational Neuroscience
Introduction: Systems and computational neuroscience is one of the core contents of brain science research. It is a bridge between molecular neuroscience and cognitive neuroscience, and is also the basis for many applied research such as brain-computer interface, brain-like intelligence, neural regulation, and neurological rehabilitation. The research goal of systems and computational neuroscience is to understand the structure and function of the brain at the level of neural circuits and networks, reveal the neural mechanisms of human behavior and cognition, and inspire the development of the next generation of artificial intelligence systems. Systems and computational neuroscience comprehensively use scientific methods such as experiments, calculations, and theoretical modeling to solve complex and challenging problems in brain research. The course "Systems and Computational Neuroscience" will systematically introduce the basic research methods in this field, as well as the physiological basis, working principles and computational models of major nervous systems such as vision, hearing, touch, movement, language, learning and memory, and explore the intrinsic connections between these mechanisms and brain-computer interfaces, artificial intelligence, etc.

Name: Neurobiological Foundations of Cognition
Introduction: This course focuses on the neurobiological basis of cognition and learning activities. This course will start from the principles of cell biology of the nervous system, explain the newly acquired learning, cognition, maturity, aging and other new characteristics of neural networks composed of single cells, and embody the reductionist principle of modern neurobiological research. Classes are mainly lecture-based, and the main contents include nerve cell physiology, molecular mechanisms of neurophysiology, the composition and development of neural networks that perform related functions, neuromodulation mechanisms of physiological functions, molecular and circuit mechanisms of learning and memory, molecular and circuit mechanisms of nervous system diseases, neural signals and information processing within brain circuits.

Name: Advanced Mathematics (Type D, Foundation) Problem Session
Introduction: This course consolidates the content of the higher mathematics courses taught through lectures.

Name: Media and Chinese Society
Prerequisite: No first course is required. The students who choose classes should have a prior knowledge of the contemporary history of China.
Introduction: The course will help students to learn and understand the overall situation of journalism and communication in China (which encompasses mainland China and Hong Kong, Taiwan, etc.), as well as the evolution of China ' s information and communication policy and related factors. In addition, the course will analyse the development of various media in China, including print media, electronic media and emerging online media, and their interaction with Chinese society, and explore the influence of Chinese media abroad, as well as the situation of overseas media in China and its impact on Chinese society. The courses are delivered by teachers and related panel discussions/visits.

Name: Introduction to the Classics
Introduction: The course will select the classic literature of archaeological research, which will specifically guide students in their reading, understanding and initial academic training to lay the foundation for future academic writing.

Name: Introduction to Underwater Archaeology
Introduction: The course is devoted to underwater archaeology theory, methods and techniques, the process and practice of underwater archaeology investigation and excavation, preservation of underwater antiquities, and the law and regulations governing underwater cultural heritage and management of underwater sites, based on which the findings and research profiles of such thematic areas as the sea Silk Road, ancient navigational techniques and sea trade ceramics, which are closely related to underwater archaeology, are taught.

Name: Training in Economic Research
Prerequisite: Economics principles, middle microeconomics, middle macroeconomics
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to help students become familiar with economics research paradigms, understand research methods, and guide students in writing research plans. This course is taught through a combination of teacher lectures, classroom discussions, student reports, etc. to provide students with a good interactive learning environment. In the first two weeks of the course, teachers will explain a variety of empirical economics research methods and lead students to study classic papers. After the two-week course, students will have an understanding of how to conduct economic research and write papers in a standardized manner, and be able to initially establish their research interests. Next, students will spend one week independently completing a high-quality research proposal. The teacher will adjust part of the class time to the third week, and the selected students will present their research plans respectively, and the teacher will provide guidance.

Name: Introduction to the Philosophy of Biology
Prerequisite: Basic knowledge of secondary-school biology is required.
Introduction:
This undergraduate course introduces the main contents of philosophy of biology to two types of students: students in philosophy departments, and biology students interested in philosophical issues. Because this course will include a certain amount of philosophical background and biological background knowledge, students from other majors (as long as they have the most basic middle school biology knowledge) are also welcome to take the course. _x000D_
You may have read about some philosophical issues in biology from the news media, such as the debate between evolution and creationism, or the impact of genetic research on our understanding of human nature. These are the issues that philosophy of biology deals with. Philosophy of biology also includes topics such as: What is natural selection? Does natural selection act on individual organisms, genes, or populations of organisms? Can natural selection explain all the diversity and complexity we see in the living world? If all individual organisms are inherently selfish, how does altruism, or the act of sacrificing individuals for the good of the group, come about? Also, what is life? wait. _x000D_
In this course we will touch upon some of the major issues concerning the conceptual and philosophical foundations of the life sciences. Many of these issues are controversial (debates about them have been going on for centuries and are still going on), so we will also set aside time for open discussion. _x000D_

Name: Media and the Evolution of Education
Introduction:
This course takes the reading of a set of classic works on media environmental studies as the main line and leads students through five important development stages of media technology in human history, experiencing the impact of media technology on social evolution, knowledge production, and the development of education and teaching; and understanding the impact of the Internet on education, teaching, and personal development from the depth of history and the breadth of the knowledge industry. _x000D_
