Eisenstein's book, The Printing Press as a Cause of Change - Communication and Cultural Change in Early Modern Europe [M], analyzes and sorts out the development context of maps, theology, medicine, science, etc.; criticizes and analyzes the current examples of Internet + education.

Name: Introduction to the Chinese Economy
Prerequisite: A university-level introductory course in Economics (e.g. Principles of Economics).
Introduction: The course is offered in English.

Name: Religious Law and Religious Belief
Introduction: The purpose of the curriculum is: Religious law is the foundation for the existence of the Order, an important link between monks and believers, and an important guarantee of the maintenance of religious observance. Religious law is therefore an important subject of religious science research. Religious law studies are a key to understanding religious beliefs and to understanding them. At the same time, religious law and secular law are both common and different, and religious law often has various effects on secular society as a cultural tradition. Therefore, religious law research is also a key to understanding different religious backgrounds and national cultural traditions. The purpose of this course is to take advantage of the resources of teachers in the Department of Philosophy and Religions, with six teachers providing a comprehensive and systematic introduction of religious laws from a different religious perspective. (c) To direct students to an objective understanding of religious phenomena and of the many cultural factors underlying religious laws and laws. Summary of the modules: Module I: Catholicism (Professor Seo Yong Fei) It is understood that religious law is one of the manifestations of religious content, one of the manifestations of religious reason, and that, from the point of view of the Christian religion, particularly the Roman Episcopal Church, the Church has the power to legislate, and its powers are derived from a variety of sources, and its laws have the grounds and scope of application. On the other hand, from the point of view of the Christian religion, and in particular of the Roman Patriarchate, the State must also have its legislation and its laws governing relations between the State and the Church, such as religious organizations (note: these are two interrelated and different legal concepts) to regulate the conduct and powers, duties and obligations of the State and religious organizations (such as churches). Module II: Orthodox Church (Professor Xue Fenglin) I. The Status and Basic Composition of the Orthodox Church Statutes II. Source and history of the Holy Apostolic Code III. OVERVIEW OF THE CONTEXT OF THE STATE OF STATES (85 in total) Module III: Islam (Associate Professor Sha Zongping) Through classroom teaching and classroom discussions, it is hoped that the students will first grasp the flexible, interactive and pragmatic relationship between the Islamic faith and the Islamic Shari ' a, and articulate the Islamic heritage of the Arab traditional culture, as well as the social identity of the Shari ' a that serves Muslim societies and interests. Module IV: Buddhism (Associate Professor Wang Song) Buddhist law is very rich. The Buddhist monks have established strict legal norms in the self-resolved Garonni era. These laws, as one of the three collections of literature, have become the central part of the cultural resources of Buddhist thought. The Chinese monks began to seek justice in the times of the North and South, and many of the high monks, like Fahsi, were involved in their quest for justice. In the era of Kantang, the Handi Buddhist religion established a legal system with the quartet as the norm, followed by the emergence of the Zen Chong, which established rules unique to China. It is an important means of promoting Buddhist ideas and has an impact on Taoism and other cultural traditions. Module V: Taoism (Associate Professor Cheng Lo Song) There is a strict system of discipline in the church, which is closely associated with social life, and strict norms of behaviour are the basis for the religious faith and its effectiveness. In the course of history, there has been a proliferation of discipline, discipline and discipline, which has led to complex hierarchical systems. Different denominations have different types and content of discipline: on the one hand, it is a prerequisite for life-purification practices and, on the other, it guarantees the effectiveness of ritual services. The system of ceremonial life and the norms of conduct, as well as the ethical and faith principles that govern the practice of faith at home, are part of the law. Another function of science is to be the premise and foundation of the spirituality and the legacy of mystical technology, so that the religious science itself carries with it a sense of mysticalism. The Part of the Taoist Church discusses the jurisprudence of the Taoist faith, mainly from the two dimensions of history and practice of belief, and spectral discussions are conducted in conjunction with the behaviour and cultural taboos of ancient Chinese cultural traditions. Module VI: Confucianism (Professor Zheng Kai) Since ancient times, the Confucian family has been known for its ritualism. The etiquette holds a secular ethical, clan-blooded dimension and is also embedded in elements of sanctity. While the study of the secular ethics of comity has been rich, insufficient attention has been paid to the religious colours inherent in its sanctity. The course will discuss the relationship between Confucian courtesy and law and will be analysed using religious science as a means of broadening students ' multidimensional understanding of traditional culture.

Name: Guanghua First Course
Introduction: This course is a targeted course offered by Guanghua School of Management for freshmen. By inviting college leaders, senior professors, psychology experts, undergraduate academic tutors, class teachers, etc., through lectures on different themes, it goes in-depth from school history, college history, academic literacy, to psychological construction and other dimensions, so as to guide the outlook on life and values ​​of freshmen, so that students can complete the role change as soon as possible and start their university study life with full enthusiasm and correct attitude. This course will also serve as an important supplement to students’ ideological and political work.

Name: The College Experience and Student Development
Introduction: This course is designed for all undergraduate students in the school (especially junior students). This course is divided into 3 modules: [1] The development and evolution of higher education, [2] Related theories and empirical research on the influence of higher education and student development, [3] Independent research by student groups. The course first provides a basic theoretical thinking perspective and framework for scientific planning and design of one's own university study and life experience through the study of theoretical and empirical research on the development process and functions of higher education, the influence of higher education and student development. On this basis, the course will collect data on relevant topics through group research to form a group research report, use relevant theories to analyze the influencing mechanisms behind the cases, and provide important reference and inspiration for students to plan their future campus experiences.

Name: Classics in East Asian Humanities and Social Sciences
Introduction: This course starts from the perspective of East Asia, uses specific issues as clues, selects important figures and ideological texts that have played an important role in the historical evolution of East Asian countries, and studies and analyzes them to gain a deep understanding of the highly interconnected civilizations of East Asian countries and the reasons for the intersection and divergence of the historical paths of various countries in modern times, and to think about the future of the East Asian region on this basis. The course is jointly taught by teachers from multiple disciplines at Peking University and the University of Tokyo. It is divided into intensive teaching part and regular teaching part. It focuses on classroom discussion and paper writing guidance. It is taught in Chinese, Japanese and English flexibly according to the students' conditions and needs.

Name: Asia and the World: Issues and Methods
Prerequisite:
East Asian Classics in Humanities and Social Sciences (Starting from the perspective of East Asia, using specific issues as clues, selecting important figures and ideological texts that have played an important role in the historical evolution of East Asian countries, and studying and analyzing them to deeply understand the high correlation of civilizations in East Asia and the reasons for the intersection and divergence of historical paths in modern times, and to think about the future of the East Asian region on this basis.)_x000D_
_x000D_
This course is only open to students who have taken "East Asian Humanities and Social Classics".
Introduction:
Asia and the World: Problematics and Methods _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will deeply explore the position of Asian civilization and culture in the world, the significance of Asia to the world, and the organic connections within Asia, Asia and the outside world in social history, political economy, literature and art, thought and culture, etc. The course will start from various "problems" in Asia, select important figures, events and ideological texts related to Asia, and conduct detailed interpretation and discussion. During the course, teachers will fully demonstrate Asian cross-cultural research methodologies; during the learning process, students are expected to gain solid academic training in the fields of Asian and world studies and improve their theoretical analysis capabilities. _x000D_
_x000D_
Note: This course is only open to students in the Peking University-Tokyo University "East Asian Studies" joint program.

Name: The Contemporary World and China
Introduction: The course focuses on topical issues in the contemporary world and helps students build on China ' s open international perspective. The course began with an introduction to the current basic political, economic and security landscape of the international community and its sources. On this basis, the course provides a detailed analysis of the world's hotspots, their sources, key factors, progress, interaction between the countries concerned and the implications of the problem for China, China's response, etc. These include the DPRK nuclear issue, the Iraq war, terrorism, missile proliferation and missile defence, China's border issues, international resource relations, technical cooperation and control in outer space, international trade and WTO, and the financial crisis and its response. Through learning, students learn about the basic features of the contemporary world and the analysis of basic international issues.

Name: Selected Readings in Classic Works of Civil Law
Prerequisite: General principles of civil law and criminal law
Introduction: Classical programmes in law are offered to undergraduate students in law. The course is planned to devote one semester of time to a detailed reading of the book " Jurisprudence Methodology " by Carl Rarenz, German jurist. The curriculum combines teaching methods such as lectures by teachers, student discussions, after-school work, lectures, etc., with the aim of providing students with a clearer and deeper understanding of the history and current state, content and boundaries, functions and meaning of the philosophy of jurisprudence, on the basis of which case analysis is attempted.

Name: Roman Law
Introduction: In general, the system of human, material and procedural law teaches the concepts, principles and institutions of ancient Roman private law, as well as the general processes and patterns of their evolution, and is linked to the near-modern civil and commercial law, so that students can understand the origins of civil and Roman law and lay the foundation for learning about civil, commercial and economic law.

Name: Literary Classics and Opera Appreciation
Introduction:
This course is a thematic course that places equal emphasis on literary reading and music appreciation. Through the introduction and reading of classic Chinese and foreign literary works, we will enter into the classic opera works adapted from literary masterpieces in the history of Chinese and foreign operas, and sort out the intersection of the relationship between writers, dramatists and composers, the creative background of literature and opera, as well as the differences and sublimations of character design and narrative clues in different carriers. The interpretation of literary classics and the analysis of their representation in the form of operas in this course will help students more easily enter the world of opera derived or extended from literary classics. This elective course can be regarded as an upgrade of literary reading, or the experience of opera appreciation can be regarded as a shortcut to enter the world of opera through a literary dimension, a new attempt with introductory significance to opera. This course focuses on opera works based on literary masterpieces. The course hopes that readers who have read these literary masterpieces will gain an ear for listening to operas and discover the characters, character relationships, plot development, narrative style, theme and motivation presentation and metaphors in the masterpieces in the operas. _x000D_
In the history of music, literature has had a great influence on music, and literary masterpieces are the source of many musical creations. The classical music that is often performed and is the most popular in the world today is mainly concentrated in the 19th century. The music of the 19th century is characterized by romanticism and is "title music". The main forms of expression are operas and symphonies. The famous American musicologist Paul Henry Lang believed in his masterpiece "Music in Western Civilization" that the Romanticism movement in the 19th century was essentially a literary movement. In other words, the Romantic movement in the nineteenth century first started in the field of literary creation and then spread to the field of music. Based on this idea, this course carefully selects more than ten classic operas based on literary masterpieces. Through the interpretation of the relationship between the composer's opera creation process and the original literary works, a basic concept of opera appreciation is established, that is, "literary masterpieces in operas", or "perceiving opera through literature." _x000D_

Name: Introduction to the Comprehensive Mirror to Aid in Government
Introduction: Putting the Qualification of Resources in the context of the times, discussing its birth point, the characteristics of the text and its ideological content, and further exploring the essence of history.

Name: Topics in Rural Education in China
Introduction:
In order to achieve the comprehensive popularization of high school education and reduce the unemployment rate among young people, my country, like most countries, implements a "dual-track" education system in which high school education runs parallel to general education (general high school) and vocational education (secondary vocational education, referred to as "secondary vocational education"). The two types of education are very different in educational objectives and teaching content. By the end of 2020, my country will soon achieve the goal of achieving a gross enrollment rate of 90% in high school education, and secondary vocational school enrollment will account for about 40% of high school enrollment. Among them, rural students account for more than 80% of students in secondary vocational schools. The quality of talent training in secondary vocational schools is not only directly related to educational equity, but also has an important impact on the quality of the labor force and the stability of future society. _x000D_
It is worth noting that secondary vocational schools are generally considered to be “second-rate education” by students and parents in many countries (including my country). There are many reasons for this, including the limited career development prospects of secondary vocational graduates and the low quality of secondary vocational talent training. In the past decade or so, our country has increased investment in secondary vocational schools in order to improve the quality of vocational education talent training, but how effective are these policies? What experiences and lessons can past practices provide for future vocational education development decisions? Relevant empirical research at home and abroad is very lacking. _x000D_
The goal of this summer course is to help learners who are interested in vocational education research familiarize themselves with and master empirical research based on data and evidence while improving traditional speculative research, advocate the formation of a new empirical education research culture, enable educational research to better provide decision-making support for educational reform, and further expand the influence of my country's vocational education research in the international academic community.

Name: Introduction to Industrial Systems
Introduction: This course is the continuation of Introduction to Industrial Production (1). The entire course content integrates major industrial sectors such as energy, materials, chemicals, machinery, automobiles, electronics, light industry, and construction, as well as agriculture and service industries. It forms a complete system that develops the industrial system head-on, opening the door for students to absorb nutrients from engineering departments and engineering disciplines. This course has an open system, integrates engineering, economy, and society, intersects technology and industry, is compatible with domestic and foreign situations, integrates epistemology and methodology into engineering examples, integrates ideological education and cultivation education into business content, focuses on cultivating students' thinking atmosphere, and lays a good foundation for integrating different cultures to create new theories, products, and services. The course adopts a teaching model of three parallel lines of classroom case teaching, on-site inspections and online collaborative inquiry to enhance the teaching effect. Teachers’ classroom case teaching is the mainstay, students’ collaborative inquiry-based learning after class is the main body, and industrial visits and research practices are supplemented. Listening to lectures - reading - practice are closely linked; training - thinking - communication are deepened step by step. Guide students to listen to lectures with a discussion mentality, use the classroom as a guide to learn, and develop course content through reading, practice and cooperative inquiry.

Name: The Dynamic Earth
Introduction:
Maybe you've seen the fine drawings left by the ancient elves through the windows of the museum, and perhaps you've seen the giant bodies of the ancient beasts in crowded crowds. Perhaps you are familiar with the “Cirque of Cold War” and are as dear to the many creatures that flourish in the ancient seas, perhaps you are a fan of the natural sciences, a fan of observation and practice, of reading the book of nature, and perhaps you have just asked a lot of questions about “why”, and you have valuable curiosity about the world that is now alive and want to know the story of the past of this planet.
Vivid Earth - The junior discussion class at the Yuen Pedagogical Institute, 2019, represented by the cyanide outbreak and the cyanide dinosaur boom and extinction, in contrast to two field events, drew a graphic picture of life and the environment from a geological historical perspective, leading students to an understanding of the content of the disciplines and disciplines of Earth sciences and hoping to prepare them:
What? Interest in the field of Earth sciences
What? Concepts and basic methods of university studies
What? The ability to practice, observe, think logically and express ideas in the field
What? Capacity to create problem awareness in the natural sciences

Name: Introduction to Information Management
Introduction:
Course Chinese Introduction_x000D_
This course is an introductory course for information management and related disciplines. It aims to introduce the connotation and extension of information management to freshmen and deepen students' specific understanding of the discipline and major. Specific content includes: introduction to subject areas, major and course structure system, research areas, issues and methods of this subject, career development paths for graduates, etc. This enables students to have a preliminary understanding of the courses and related skills taught in this subject, and establish their own learning directions and goals. At the same time, through sharing with department friends and on-site inspections, we can gain an intuitive experience and understanding of the role of this major in social development. _x000D_
This course is a required course for majors. It is taught to freshmen, transfer freshmen, and double-degree students in the Department of Information Management. The teaching methods include interactive classroom teaching, sharing and discussion, and field trips.

Name: Contemporary World Economy and Politics
Introduction:
_x000D_
     Focusing on the two themes of prosperity and order, the course uses the classification of country types as an entry point to define the post-World War II world, that is, the contemporary world, and conducts in-depth and systematic analysis of a number of important issue areas such as economic growth, transformation, governance, democracy (democratization), etc., and explains the contemporary world economy and politics from the perspective of political science, with a special emphasis on the transfer and learning of the characteristics of different economic and political systems, with a view to understanding and discovering the world through political thinking and logic. _x000D_
    _x000D_
   As a course mainly taught to undergraduates, this course helps students form the habit of consciously paying attention to the world and thinking professionally, enriching their knowledge accumulation, expanding their academic horizons, and constructing a good knowledge structure. _x000D_

Name: Happiness: Research Methods in Psychology
Introduction: This course is one of Yuanpei College’s 2019 freshman seminar series. It will introduce some basic concepts and research methods of psychology in eight weeks, allowing students to understand how psychologists explore the mysteries of human psychology. It is hoped that students who take this course can better understand themselves and better adapt to the environment. We will tell you: What is psychology? How to study a person's psychology? Why are you different from others? How does culture affect individual psychology? How does psychology study positive emotions, such as happiness and well-being, and prosocial behaviors, such as empathy, altruism, and gratitude?

Name: Metamorphosis: The Transformation of the Human Image in Film
Introduction:
Introduction to courses:

The curriculum seeks to develop the following competencies:
Development of basic skills for film analysis
To understand the variable image of people in Western films and its significance
It's called philosophy, painting, literature and film.

Name: Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them: Demonic Beliefs and Imagery in Ancient Mesopotamia
Introduction: A discussion class for freshmen from Yuanpei College in 2019. Through comparative observation and case analysis of the complex and diverse images of "magical animals" presented in different contexts of ancient Mesopotamian civilization, the course guides students to explore a core issue of concern in art history research - that is, the connection between "form" and "meaning" at the historical, cultural, and social levels. The course is committed to introducing some basic research paths in the art history discipline into the teaching, that is, starting from visual materials, combining documentary records and archaeological materials, and exploring the unique civilizational forms and cultural traditions behind them through the viewing, reading and interpretation of "pictures" and "objects".

Name: Social Transformation
Introduction:
Course Introduction:_x000D_
    Observe social changes in the world and modern China from a macro-comparative perspective, and understand politics, economy, and society_x000D_
Modern issues arise in the fields of society, rules, concepts, etc., helping learners enhance their sense of history and experience. _x000D_
Each session is 100 minutes, with 80 minutes of lecture and 20 minutes of discussion, 1 credit. _x000D_

Name: Politics of the Ancient World: The History of the Peloponnesian War
Introduction:
A discussion class for freshmen of Yuanpei College in 2019. By reading Thucydides' "History of the Peloponnesian War", the course will help students understand the way the ancient world viewed war and politics, and help students think about issues related to politics and history. The course hopes to cultivate students' following abilities:_x000D_
a) The way of studying in university;_x000D_
b) Text reading method; _x000D_
c) Critical discussion and writing;_x000D_
d) The ability to think about contemporary issues with the help of classic texts. _x000D_

Name: The Logic behind Environmental Problems
Introduction:
Maybe you are a freshman who aspires to major in the environment and do not have a systematic understanding of the content you will learn in the environmental major; maybe you are a student who has a strong interest in environmental protection and want to have a relatively professional understanding of the environmental issues around you through a relaxed and enjoyable course; maybe you are just curious about real-life environmental issues and want to follow our footsteps and visit one after another interesting ecological and environmental protection internship bases..._x000D_
This course is an introductory course in environmental science for college students who are interested in environmental subjects. It is co-hosted by four teachers from different fields in the School of Environmental Science and Engineering. The course fully considers the different needs of students of different majors and levels. It mainly uses the teaching method of "case discussion-teacher explanation-field visit" to discuss classic cases in the fields of environment and economics, atmospheric environmental science, water pollution control, environment and health, etc., to inspire students to think deeply about the environment. Based on the students' interest in environmental issues, teachers teach the main issues and research paradigms in related fields on the basis of guiding students to actively participate in discussions; at the same time, they go out of the classroom and go to the field, through visits to two Beijing internship bases in the field of atmospheric and water environment, to deepen students' understanding of real-life environmental problems and their solutions. Finally, through the educational concept of "case appearance - problem discovery - layer-by-layer dissection - in-depth essence - improvement of abilities", students are made aware of the urgency and complexity of solving environmental problems, and improve their ability to systematically analyze environmental problems and integrate solutions to environmental problems, as well as their scientific literacy in comprehensive research. _x000D_

Name: The Legal Mind
Light and Shadow of the Enlightenment
Introduction: The Enlightenment, which took place in Europe in the eighteenth century, is one of the most far-reaching ideological movements in the history of humankind, with its resonance throughout the world for more than 200 years, and the debate on it remains intense today. Enlightened philosophies routinely compare their thoughts to “light”, in contrast to the “dark” that has gripped the European mind since the Middle Ages. However, it is increasingly pointed out that this statement is neither complete nor accurate: while breaking the authority and superstition, the enlightening critics believe that the enlightenment is inextricably linked to the many ills that characterize modern society; while the enlightening historians tend to emphasize the complex characteristics of the Enlightenment movement, especially the major differences between different countries and different schools of thought. In other words, even if we see the Enlightenment as a light, it does not seem to be able to escape the shadows that accompany it. In this course, we will seek to better understand and evaluate the nature of the Enlightenment movement by reading selected sections of the works of the Enlightened Zionists and the Enlightened Critics. Most of the philosophies' writings are well thought and well understood, and are therefore particularly suitable for introducing freshmen to some of the classic theories in humanities and social subjects. In addition to learning about these theories, it is hoped that the students selected will become familiar with some of the basic methods and more recent developments in the study of philosophical and intellectual history, thus providing a good basis for further learning and research.

Name: Engineering Science Methods and Robotics
Introduction: The course focuses on the field of robotics engineering and radiates to scientific methods and research models in engineering systems. It mainly uses the teaching model of "case discussion - explanation of knowledge and principles - hands-on practice" to guide students to understand the research paradigms and implementation approaches in the field of engineering science. By learning the basic knowledge of the intersection and system in the field of robotics engineering, as well as hands-on practice and creative design, students can improve their interest in engineering science, understand the mathematical and physical foundation required in the field of engineering science, and cultivate innovation, practical awareness and literacy in the field of engineering science.

Name: Introductory Seminar on Artificial Intelligence
Introduction: This course will introduce the core areas of artificial intelligence to undergraduates majoring in artificial intelligence with no basic knowledge in the form of popular science, including machine learning, computer vision, natural language processing, multi-agent, robotics and cognitive reasoning, etc., to facilitate students' preliminary understanding of the artificial intelligence subject, and encourage students to express their views and opinions, thereby stimulating students' interest in learning.

Name: International Competition Law and Policy
Prerequisite: Competition Act, General Economic Act, Intellectual Property Act
Introduction: This course aims to introduce students to the basic principles of international competition law so that students can have an in-depth understanding of the principles behind competition regulations and policies; in addition, English teaching can help students improve their legal English proficiency.

Name: Integrated Laboratory Course I
Introduction: This course lasts for one year and includes a total of 9 large-scale experimental trainings. It focuses on training students' hands-on experimental skills, basic experimental skills in physics, chemistry, electronics, and computer science, and focuses on the application of relevant knowledge in the study of classic problems in life sciences. Each large-scale experiment requires one day per week for 2-3 consecutive weeks to learn and operate. Students should carefully study relevant theoretical knowledge before class. Instructors are responsible for training students in basic experimental operation skills in experimental courses, inspiring and guiding experimental discussions, appropriately teaching background knowledge, and requiring students to write experimental reports. Contents covered in the course include: fluid mechanics and life phenomena at low Reynolds numbers, measuring yeast mutation rate, measuring simulated bacterial growth rate with a homemade photometer, measuring Avogadro's constant, Boltzmann's constant, biological motion and chemotaxis, radiation and random phenomena, cell mechanics, basic chemical synthesis, geometric optics and imaging basics. This course is a required course for the integrated science experiment class.

Name: Advanced Modal Logic
Prerequisite: First-class logic/digital logic, better model logic.
Introduction: Basic theory: models and frameworks, formal modal logic, canonical models and completeness; expressiveness and invariance: mutual simulation, correspondence theory; finite modelability and decidability; algebraic semantics: modal matrix and modal algebra, representation theorem, modal algebra and general framework; extension and application of modal logic: dynamic logic, dynamic cognitive logic, modal mu calculus, model checking; modal logic, games and automata, etc.

Name: Politics as a Way of Life: The World of Political Thought in the Analects
Introduction: Through a close reading of The Analects, this course inspires students to reflect on their common-sense views on politics that have been formed since middle school. Through careful reading of the text, explanation and discussion of key sentences, and personal experience of situations in The Analects, students are helped to understand how the thoughts on "politics" in the Analects were generated in the life world of Confucius, and then explore how Chinese classical political thought understands the relationship between politics and life. The course also conducts a comparative analysis of the political thought of The Analects and modern political science to help students reflect on the ideological limitations of modern politics. I hope that through studying the course, students can gradually understand how they can still live independently like Confucius when they face bizarre political phenomena.

Name: Introduction to Statistics: The Science and Art of Data Analysis
Introduction: In today's "big data" era, understanding the basic ideas of data analysis, mastering the basic methods of data analysis, and correctly interpreting the conclusions of data analysis have become basic qualities that every citizen should possess. As the most important pillar of data science, statistical ideas, theories, methods and techniques play an irreplaceable and important role in data analysis. Mastering statistics requires a comprehensive understanding at three levels: ideological methods, analytical techniques and practical applications. In the practice of statistical education in my country, due to complex historical reasons, there is often great emphasis on the specific "analytical techniques" in statistics, but not enough attention is often paid to the "ideological methods" and "practical applications" of statistics. This course will focus on introducing statistical ideas, aiming to demonstrate the application and impact of statistics on all levels of society. It will introduce statistical ideas, methods and cases in a simple and easy-to-understand manner, as well as how to implement practical applications through R software. If this course is used as the "first" statistics course for undergraduates, it will help students effectively establish correct statistical concepts and conceptual systems, laying a solid foundation for more in-depth study of statistical "technical methods" in the future; if used as the "last" statistics course for undergraduates, it will help students effectively establish correct statistical intuition and data thinking without involving specific details of "mathematical techniques", which will be of great benefit to their future study and work. The course will start with the history of statistics, gradually introduce the display and acquisition of data, statistical models and inference, data science, etc., and finally introduce some topics that are closely integrated with applications in different fields.

Name: Vision Science and the Visual Arts
Introduction: Why does the red sun in "Sunrise·Impression" have a sense of movement jumping out of the sea level? Why are Van Gogh's paintings dominated by yellow tones? Why does Mona Lisa give people the impression of smiling but not smiling? Why is one painting so appealing and another so off-putting? Answering these questions requires an understanding of the psychological processes behind art creation and art appreciation. This course combines visual psychology with visual art, aiming to enable students to understand the brain operating mechanisms behind various visual phenomena through teaching. Starting from the pathways of visual information processing, the course will introduce spatial vision, color vision, depth perception, motion perception, perceptual organization, object recognition, and the mechanisms of various visual illusions. The course content also includes attention, multi-sensory modal processing, and the role and impact of eye diseases and neurological diseases in the process of appreciating and creating visual art works. In addition, the course will also explore how to understand the aesthetic rules and mechanisms in art appreciation from the perspective of traditional experimental aesthetics and the neuroaesthetics that have emerged in recent years.

Name: Research-Based Learning Seminar: Mathematics, Modeling and Prediction
Introduction: The course is part of the 2020 series of discussions at the Institute of Pentecostal Studies. The course revolves around the creation of modern astronomy and describes how practical problems can be studied and resolved through the creation of mathematical models, while encouraging students to look for problems in their lives, build corresponding mathematical models and solve them, and extract knowledge from modelling practices.

Name: Hot Topics in Resources and the Environment from an Economic Perspective
Introduction:
From "sandstorms" to "PM2.5", from "water pollution" to "water shortages", from "desertification" to "soil heavy metal pollution", from "endangered wildlife" to "biological invasion", from "reducing wetland area" to "global climate change", these are the resource degradation and environmental pollution problems we are experiencing. _x000D_
_x000D_
How much natural resources can we leave for future generations? How to protect the environment while pursuing economic development? What role does economics play in solving resource and environmental issues? What economic tools can effectively deal with environmental problems? How much is a ladybug worth? Is the emissions trading system really effective? How much are global ecosystem services worth? Let us take these questions into "Resource and Environmental Hot Issues from an Economic Perspective". _x000D_
_x000D_
This course mainly interprets hot issues in the field of resource and environmental economics. It aims to inspire students to understand resource and environmental issues in real life from the perspective of economics and master the main economic tools for managing resource and environmental issues. The course materials come from cases in natural resource protection and environmental pollution control from countries around the world (especially my country). _x000D_

Name: Exploring the Mystery of the Intracranial "Black Box": Introduction to Brain Science
Introduction: ? ? ? ? ? The emergence of the brain was an important event in the evolution of biological "intelligence". However, because the brain structure itself is too complex, the current technical level of human beings is not high enough, and the theoretical research on complex systems is not in-depth enough, it can be said that human understanding of the brain is still in a "black box" state. We hope that by studying this course, students can understand the basic knowledge of brain science and even related neuroscience, as well as the methods and techniques used in related research, and have closer contact with brain research through lectures.

Name: Industrial Data Mining and Analysis
Introduction: Starting with the spring semester of 2016, the course on Industrial Data Excavation and Analysis will be significantly adjusted to focus on the relevant aspects of web-based product design and data analysis in response to the current rapid development of products in the Internet. The course will be designed from mobile Internet products to be a portal to the design and basic knowledge of web-based products and to inform the idea of using data mining and analysis to help us complete a good web-based product design. This course is intended primarily for future students who are interested in the design and development of web-based products, and is open to undergraduate and graduate students. Starting with the spring semester of 2018, this course is supported by the Microsoft Cloud Global Top30 Innovation Development Programme. Microsoft will select senior Internet product managers to share in product design. At the same time, the course will continue to invite 58 senior city product directors, Internet-based product supervisors and information product directors to share their ideas on the design of Internet products.

Name: Hebrew Audiovisual and Speaking (I)
Introduction: This course organizes and guides students to listen to daily life conversations, stories, short dramas, news, and watch relevant original recordings in Hebrew. The first semester starts with basic Hebrew conversation, consolidating the letters, words and simple sentences students have learned, and organizing students to practice listening and conversation.

Name: Hebrew (I)
Prerequisite: The material is from a zero starting point and is not subject to prior course requirements.
Introduction: This course is a major course for first- and second-year undergraduates majoring in Hebrew. It includes the teaching of basic language knowledge such as Hebrew pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar, as well as the cultivation of practical language skills such as listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation. It is specifically divided into two parts: pronunciation and text. The pronunciation stage mainly teaches the knowledge of Hebrew phonetics systematically and lasts for two months; the text stage mainly teaches basic grammar and basic vocabulary. This is a language practice class. While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: Hebrew Audiovisual and Speaking (II)
Introduction: Students are organized to conduct basic daily dialogue exercises in Hebrew and to improve their ability to read and read through listening to Hebrew stories, films, news, etc.

Name: A Brief History of the Jews
Introduction: This course teaches a brief history of the Jewish people, from biblical times to the founding of the modern state of Israel. The lectures are rich in content and span a wide time and space, covering important chapters in Jewish history. Through learning, students can have a basic understanding of the formation and development of the Jewish nation, and master certain historical learning methods, laying the foundation for further in-depth study and research on historical topics of interest.

This course is taught to students in the second semester of their first year of Hebrew language. _x000D_

While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: Modern History of Israel
Introduction: The modern history course of Israel introduces the history of Israel over the past 70 years since its founding in 1948, including the establishment of the country's political system to previous Middle East wars to the Palestinian-Israeli conflict and peace talks. This course will introduce the development of Israel since its founding, its achievements in politics, economy, military and other aspects, as well as the problems and challenges that Israel faces in the 21st century.

This course is the main course for Hebrew undergraduates in the second year of their studies. It covers the terminology of Hebrew, the teaching of basic languages such as grammar, and the development of the practical skills of listening, speaking, reading, writing and translating. It is divided into text and French. This is a language practice course, which, while teaching language knowledge, places particular emphasis on the training of basic language skills and on the development of basic skills.

Name: Israeli Society
Introduction: This course will provide a comprehensive introduction to Israeli society, including the basic situation of Israel's basic political, economic, military and educational systems, as well as all aspects of the deeper ideological field of Israeli society. Through systematic study, everyone will have a deeper understanding of the characteristics and nature of the Israeli state and society, and understand the contradictory forces that coexist in Israeli society (religion and secularity, Eastern and Western Jews, ethnic separation, Arab-Jewish conflict, etc.) and the impact of these contradictions on the development of Israeli society and history.

Name: Basic Vietnamese (I)
Introduction: This course is a major course for first-year Vietnamese undergraduates in the first semester. The content includes the teaching of basic language knowledge such as Vietnamese pronunciation, vocabulary, grammar, etc. It is divided into two parts: the pronunciation stage and the text stage. The pronunciation stage mainly teaches Vietnamese phonetic knowledge systematically and lasts for three months. Students are required to be proficient in spelling Vietnamese syllables after completing this stage of study. The text stage mainly teaches basic grammar knowledge and basic vocabulary. This is a language practice class. While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: National Conditions of Vietnam
Introduction: This course mainly introduces Vietnam’s physical geography, rich resources, administrative divisions, population, ethnic groups, folk festivals, language, religious beliefs, political system, military, economic innovation, transportation and tourism, foreign relations, education, science and technology, health, sports, press and publishing, etc. Understand the important events and figures in modern and contemporary Vietnamese society. It attempts to give students a general understanding and grasp of all aspects of Vietnam, so that they can have a preliminary and basic understanding of Vietnamese society in future language and culture studies, which will help them have a deeper understanding and research of Vietnamese language, literature, and culture.

Name: History of Vietnam
Introduction: This course mainly teaches the development process of Vietnamese history from ancient times to the reunification of northern and southern Vietnam in 1976. It focuses on introducing, analyzing, and discussing some historical phenomena, historical events, and historical figures that affect the historical development of Vietnam. It also briefly introduces the research status of Vietnamese history in Chinese and foreign historical circles.

Name: Vietnamese Conversation (Part 1)
Introduction: Simulation of different scenes of life in Viet Nam, identification of different themes, guidance for students to engage in dialogue exercises on topics of daily learning and life, in conjunction with the basics of Vietnamese that they have learned.

Name: Basic Vietnamese (II)
Introduction: This course is a major course for first-year undergraduates majoring in Vietnamese in the second semester. The content includes the teaching of basic language knowledge such as Vietnamese pronunciation, vocabulary, and grammar, as well as the cultivation of practical language skills such as listening, speaking, reading, writing, and translation. This semester focuses on teaching basic Vietnamese vocabulary and grammar knowledge. After completing this semester's teaching, students will be able to master about 3,000 common Vietnamese vocabulary and be able to conduct simple daily conversations in Vietnamese. This is a language practice class. While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: Vietnamese Conversation (Part 2)
Introduction: Simulate different scenarios of living in Vietnam, determine different themes, and guide students to combine the basic knowledge of Vietnamese they have learned to conduct conversation exercises on some topics in daily study and life, discuss some issues, and practice expressing simple thoughts and opinions in Vietnamese.

Name: Vietnamese Culture
Prerequisite: State of Viet Nam, history of Viet Nam
Introduction: This course is divided into several topics to briefly explain and introduce Vietnamese culture, especially Vietnamese traditional culture, which mainly includes Vietnam’s original culture, religious beliefs, customs, traditional arts, traditional festivals, etc. In addition, students are guided to read some relevant books outside class, conduct class discussions on designated topics or students’ chosen topics, and write term papers.

Name: Basic Vietnamese (III)
Introduction: This course is a major course for the first semester of the second-year undergraduate students majoring in Vietnamese. The content includes the teaching of basic language knowledge such as Vietnamese vocabulary and grammar, as well as the cultivation of practical language skills such as listening, speaking, reading, writing and translation. This is a language practice class. While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: History and Present Conditions of Southeast Asia
Introduction:
Southeast Asia is my country's close neighbor. With the expansion and deepening of exchanges between China and Southeast Asia, we need to have a better understanding of Southeast Asia. This course mainly teaches:_x000D_
1. Basic overview of Southeast Asian society;_x000D_
2. Similarities and unity among Southeast Asian countries;_x000D_
3. Connections between China and Southeast Asian countries;_x000D_
4. Real hot issues in Southeast Asia. _x000D_

Name: Extensive Vietnamese Reading (Part 1)
Introduction: Students are assigned to read Vietnamese articles about politics, economy, culture, life, education, science and technology, military, diplomacy and other fields after class. They answer questions in class and perform grammatical analysis of key sentences and translation exercises of key paragraphs. Students are required to master the reading skills and correctly understand the content of the article, especially the correct understanding of long and complex sentences in Vietnamese. _x000D_

Name: History of Vietnamese Literature
Prerequisite: History of Viet Nam, profile of Viet Nam, basic Vietnamese
Introduction: This course is an elective course for Vietnamese language students and is of major importance in the discipline system. Through teaching, students are made aware of the basic context of Vietnamese literature and its development, pupils are taught the face and artistic characteristics of Vietnamese literature by guiding them to read the respective author ' s work, students are initially trained in the appreciation of Vietnamese literary works, students ' knowledge of Vietnamese literature and culture is enhanced, students ' humanities are enriched, students ' cultural upbringing is enriched and their spiritual qualities are enhanced. At the same time, issues such as the rise and decline of Chinese and musk literature in Viet Nam and the process of modernization of Vietnamese literature have been explored in the context of Vietnamese history and culture, thus exploring the indigenous characteristics and external influences of Vietnamese literature.

Name: Basic Vietnamese (IV)
Introduction: This course is a major course for the second semester of the second-year undergraduate students majoring in Vietnamese. The content includes the teaching of basic language knowledge such as Vietnamese vocabulary and grammar, as well as the cultivation of practical language skills such as listening, speaking, reading, writing and translation. This is a language practice class. While imparting language knowledge, it pays special attention to the training of basic language skills and cultivates students' solid basic skills.

Name: Vietnamese Ethnicity and Society
Prerequisite: State of Viet Nam, Vietnamese history, Vietnamese culture
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the current situation of the Vietnamese nation, the traditions and contemporary cultural characteristics of Vietnamese society. By introducing the multi-ethnic culture and social life of Vietnam, the course presents the development process and cultural characteristics of the Vietnamese nation and society from tradition to modernity, and deeply explores the diversity and diversity of Vietnamese culture. The course designs different topics, focusing on teacher lectures and classroom discussions. Students read materials in advance before class, including Chinese, Vietnamese, and English multi-language literature and related audio and video materials. The course teaching language is mainly Vietnamese, supplemented by Chinese and English.

Name: Cognitive Neuroscience (B)
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Prerequisite: General psychology, experimental psychology (or cognitive psychology)
Introduction: Cognitive neuroscience is an emerging edge subject that is rapidly developing in the international academic field in recent years. It is the intersection between cognitive science and neuroscience. It is necessary to combine the basic theoretical concepts of cognitive science, including physical symbolism, semiotic theory, ecological phenomenology, and modular theory, with the technical achievements and theoretical progress of contemporary brain research, and conduct highly interdisciplinary research on the laws of intelligent activity and brain mechanisms of the human brain. After a general discussion of the two major discipline systems of cognitive science and neuroscience, this course focuses on teaching the principles, research methods, main results and existing problems of cognitive neuroscience branches such as cognitive psychophysiology, cognitive neuropsychology, cognitive physiological psychology, cognitive neurobiology and cognitive computational neuroscience. This course can enable students to have a new understanding of new research progress on the basis of biological brain and intelligence in contemporary high-tech theoretical and technical issues.

Name: Aviation Sports 1
Introduction: 1. Course Introduction 1. Physical fitness is a person's ability to engage in physical activities that require speed, endurance, strength and flexibility. The physical fitness course mainly teaches knowledge and methods related to healthy physical fitness and the role of physical activities in improving aerobic fitness, muscle strength and endurance, flexibility, and body composition. The teaching content mainly includes healthy physical fitness exercise methods, light equipment fitness methods and strength training methods. 2． Course requirements: (1) Wear suitable and lightweight sportswear. During the study period, you must master the safety knowledge of classroom equipment. While taking elective courses, you should continuously enhance your physical movement ability. (2) Students who suffer from chronic metabolic diseases, asthma, hypertension, heart disease and other diseases that are not suitable for high-intensity physical activity should take this course with caution. 2. Course tasks 1. Teach physical health and fitness exercise methods, light equipment fitness methods and strength training methods. 2. Cultivate students’ physical exercise habits, strong will and quality, and the ideology of “health first”. Understand the knowledge, skills, attitudes and behaviors that contribute to a physically active and healthy lifestyle, and achieve the goal of lifelong physical activity.

Name: Media and Chinese Society
Prerequisite: No initial courses are required, but read and familiarize themselves with the contemporary history of China
Introduction: This course helps students understand the development of China’s news media and its impact on Chinese society. The content covers different types of media, from traditional print media, radio and television to the latest online media development in China, as well as the exchange and interaction between China and the world in the field of news communication, and discusses the impact of the development of news communication media on Chinese society and culture.

Name: Ancient Egyptian Civilization
Introduction:
This course uses the major research topics of Egyptology as clues to introduce the development process and cultural achievements of ancient Egyptian civilization (3000 BC - 7th century AD). Analyze the characteristics of ancient Egyptian civilization from the aspects of language, mythology, royal concepts, artistic style, etc. And introduce the current status, latest research trends and future development trends of this subject. _x000D_
The ancient Egyptian civilization was characterized by its high degree of material development and the penetration of religion into various cultural fields. The former is reflected in long-term political unity and stability, a complete centralized system, the establishment and expansion of the empire, as well as the rich legacy of architecture and art, the high development of language and literature, etc. The latter is reflected in the close integration of political power and theocracy, the popularization and ritualization of religion, as well as unique architectural and artistic styles, lifestyles and customs, etc., which are also reflected in religious beliefs centered on the afterlife. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Industrial Systems
Introduction: Nature of the course: The course is positioned as a core basic course in cultural quality education, mainly for undergraduates in non-engineering majors such as liberal arts and sciences. It is a theoretical and practical course, and adopts a teaching organization model of large class lectures and small class discussions. Course Introduction: The overall framework of the course is determined as "engineering thinking, practice-oriented, and humanistic perspective." This course is guided by the description of industrial systems by famous experts, takes the basic laws of system science as a clue, and uses students' team participation in engineering practice as a carrier to develop content. Through the combination of theory and practice, students can experience engineering practice, understand engineering systems, strengthen engineering thinking, and feel industrial civilization. The course is 3 credits and is divided into three stages. The first stage: lectures by famous experts to understand industrial systems and improve engineering awareness; the second stage: analyze industrial cases and understand systems engineering thinking; the third stage: carry out team discussions and practice engineering projects.

Name: Major Trends in Global Politics
Introduction: This course aims to provide a broad international political and economic background knowledge for understanding international relations and global governance, including the theme of world politics, the world pattern after the Cold War, regional and national politics, analysis of hot issues along the Belt and Road, etc.

Name: Intermediate Financial Accounting
Introduction: Intermediate Financial Accounting

Name: Measure Theory
Introduction:
1. Chapter 1 Measurable Space (recommended hours: 4)_x000D_
    Set operations; various set classes; measurable spaces; monotonic class theorems; distance measurable spaces. _x000D_
2. Chapter 2 Measurement Space (recommended hours: 10)_x000D_
        The definition and properties of measures; external measures and their measurable sets; the expansion of measures on half fields (Corotheodory theorem); the relationship between measures on fields or half fields and their expansion measures; the completeness of measures and the completeness of extended measures on half fields; measures of distance spaces, especially the Lebesgue-Stieltjes measure on Rd. _x000D_
    3. Chapter 3 Measurable transformations and measurable functions (recommended hours: 8)_x000D_
    Measurable transformation; definition and operation of measurable functions; measurable functions are approximated by simple functions; typical methods apply to monotonic class theorems of functions; convergence almost everywhere and convergence based on probability. _x000D_
4. Chapter 4 Integral of measurable functions (recommended hours: 8)_x000D_
The definition process of the integral of measurable functions; the properties of the integral; taking the limit of the integral sign (monotone convergence, Fatou's lemma and controlled convergence; Lp space. _x000D_
5. Chapter 5 Testing and integration on product spaces (recommended hours: 10)_x000D_
        The product of finite or infinite measurable spaces; measurable functions on product spaces; measures of finite-dimensional product spaces generated by initial measures and transfer functions; finite-dimensional product measures and Fubini's theorem; generalization to divisible cases (limited to probability measures). _x000D_
6. Chapter 6 Symbolic Measurement (recommended hours: 10)_x000D_
    Definition, simple properties and examples - indefinite integrals; Hahn-Jordan decomposition, absolute continuity and singularity of symbolic measures; Radon-Nikodym derivatives; Lebesgue decomposition. _x000D_
7． Chapter 7 Basic concepts of probability theory (recommended hours: 4)_x000D_
    Probability space, events and probabilities; random variables and distribution functions; discrete random variables and continuous random variables; numerical characteristics of random variables and their calculation formulas; the definition and properties of conditional expectation and conditional probability.

Name: Graduate Academic English Writing
Introduction: The course is compulsory for Ph.D. studies in English (including direct and continuous studies)

Name: Thesis Writing Guidance
Introduction: The writing of master's and doctoral theses is the main work that master's and doctoral students have to complete. Due to the higher difficulty, longer writing cycle, and relatively high requirements in terms of innovation, writing standards, practical and theoretical significance, etc., the completion of master's and doctoral dissertations is generally quite difficult. A good master's or doctoral thesis is not only a good academic monograph, but also an academic exploration result with theoretical innovation value. Therefore, thesis writing guidance courses are specially set up to help masters and doctoral students successfully complete thesis writing.

Name: Models of Derivative Instruments
Introduction:
The purpose of this course is to learn and master the pricing methods of derivative securities, and to cultivate students' abilities in mathematical modeling, solution and analysis of derivative securities pricing problems. We will teach this course from two perspectives: focusing on the discrete model of derivative securities pricing using probabilistic methods - the binary tree model; focusing on using partial differential equations to analyze and numerically solve the continuous model of derivative securities pricing. _x000D_
The difference between this course and "Options, Futures, and Derivative Securities" is that the latter is an introduction to general theory, while this course emphasizes mathematical rigor. Having learned "Options, Futures and Derivative Securities", "Partial Differential Equations", "Numerical Solutions of Partial Differential Equations" and "Probability Theory" is beneficial to listening to this course, but it is not necessary. _x000D_

Name: Mathematical Methods of Risk Management
Introduction:
This course mainly introduces the latest research progress in risk management. Lectures mainly focus on current hot issues in financial risk management research. Divided into the following topics: _x000D_
(1) Bank risk management_x000D_

Name: Optimization Theory and Algorithms
Prerequisite: Mathematical analysis, upper algebra, numerical algebra
Introduction:
Optimization method is a discipline that studies the selection of optimal solutions among limited or infinite feasible solutions. It has a wide range of applications. With the development of computers, optimization methods have been widely used in engineering, design, scientific computing, finance, management, economics and other disciplines, and play an important role in these fields. _x000D_

Name: Machine Learning

The course requires students to be familiar with at least one programming language and have a basic understanding of machine learning. Coursework includes the application of deep learning models in computer vision and natural language processing.

Graph neural network has become an international research hotspot and a cutting-edge technology in the development of artificial intelligence. _x000D_
       The main goal of this course is to introduce the basic concepts, theoretical methods of graph neural networks and their applications and challenges in representative frontier fields, and guide students to understand and master the theoretical methods of graph neural networks, so that students have the ability to apply their development to their respective research directions. The course deepens students' understanding of the ideas and cutting-edge research of graph neural networks through classroom lectures, cutting-edge paper reading and project practice. _x000D_
       Students should have taken prerequisite courses such as advanced mathematics and linear algebra before taking this course. Through the study of this course, you can understand the basic ideas, theoretical methods and important issues of graph neural networks, and learn to apply graph neural networks to your respective research. _x000D_

Name: Network Representation Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Course background: Big data has become the new engine driving social development. As the most universal organization and representation form of data, network data widely exists in our daily lives, such as social networks, transportation networks, biological information networks, etc. Generally speaking, the complexity of a problem depends on the problem formulation, and the key to reducing the complexity of the problem is to choose an appropriate problem formulation. Therefore, how to represent data in a reasonable way is the key to network big data research and application. _x000D_
The main purposes of this course are: 1) To cultivate students' ability to model network data representation and solve practical problems, and to firmly master the current internationally mainstream technologies such as network embedding, graph neural networks, network data visualization, and the application of network representation in many application fields; 2) To improve students' scientific research capabilities It enables graduate students to have direct access to cutting-edge international network representation learning research results through the study of this course, and to be able to independently complete established scientific research training tasks, and even complete the production of scientific research results; 3) Enrich and support the construction of the school's curriculum system in the fields of artificial intelligence, big data and machine learning.

This course is a general school elective course for non-Korean language major students. Name: Biostatistics
Prerequisite: High algebra, calculus, mathematical statistics, probability theory
Introduction:
Thanks to the rapid development of modern science and technology, bioscientists can now produce large amounts of data in a short period of time. Name: Topics in Theoretical Machine Learning
Introduction: Designing and analyzing machine learning algorithms will involve the following basic issues: learnability, generalization, stability, scalability, and computational complexity. The theoretical basis of traditional statistical learning models, such as generalized additive models, support vector machines and kernel methods, is the statistical learning theory pioneered by Vapnik (Vapnik, 1998), which is widely used in other machine learning models. Relevant theoretical foundations and algorithm design, such as VC dimension, Rademacher complexity, PAC, PAC-Bayes, and online learning, are systematically summarized. Note that these statistical machine learning models are usually defined as a convex optimization problem, and their calculation and theory are widely studied on this basis. In recent years, deep learning has risen strongly. Although deep learning has made remarkable achievements at the application level, its theoretical foundation has been stagnant because the statistical theory and optimization algorithms developed based on convex optimization are not suitable for it. Researchers still know very little about the reasons behind the success of deep learning. Therefore, this course hopes to explore this area.

In addition, since Japanese political thought is closely related to Chinese and Western political thought, the various issues contained in it can not only deepen the understanding of Chinese and Western political thought, but also be helpful in exploring the problem awareness of Chinese and Western political thought research. Introduction: The main content of this course is to show the initiative of Wang Yangming's theory of mind in promoting the spirit through innovative interpretations, and at the same time absorb the strengths of other schools. Name: Chinese Shuttlecock (Jianzi)
Introduction:
Shuttlecock kicking was invented by the ancient Chinese. According to historical records such as "Historical Records of Su Qin" by Sima Qian, a famous historian in the Han Dynasty, the predecessor of shuttlecock kicking - the ancient Chinese Cuju movement - existed in the Qi State during the Warring States Period. The "Extended Biography of Eminent Monks" written by Shi Daoxuan in the Tang Dynasty is the earliest record of the shuttlecock kicking sport discovered so far. By the Song Dynasty, ancient Cuju developed to an unprecedented level After the prosperity of the Yuan, Ming and Qing Dynasties, ancient Cuju gradually declined. In the Qing Dynasty, the shuttlecock movement replaced Cuju and ushered in a period of prosperity and development. The shuttlecock movement evolved and developed along with the rise and fall of the nation. In practice, the shuttlecock skills and tactics have not only become one of the external manifestations of traditional culture, but also enriched the theoretical content of traditional culture, and are the pride of the Chinese nation's sports culture. _x000D_
This course aims to promote traditional sports and teach beginners with zero foundation. Teach the basic techniques of traditional figure kicking, some figure techniques, traditional collective kicking methods and introduce the rules of modern shuttlecock. Everyone is welcome to take electives!

The thoughts and practices of the landlord class reformers who attempted to develop the capitalist economy centered on military industry within the feudal body; 2. The thoughts of the early bourgeois reformists who attempted to develop the national economy centered on foreign trade; 3. One of the further deepening of the research on industrialization ideas during the Republic of China:. Name: Topics in Financial System Reform
Introduction: The experience of my country’s economic system reform over the past thirty years is that we always adhere to a path with Chinese characteristics and do not blindly copy the practices of other countries. Facts have proved that this is a very wise choice. As an important part of economic system reform, financial system reform has also made significant progress. The subprime mortgage crisis in the United States once again reminds us that the financial systems of other countries are not always the best model. To this end, we need to continue to explore a financial system reform model with Chinese characteristics. Against the background that problems in the Western financial system are constantly exposed and China's financial reform urgently needs to solve problems and clarify its direction, we need to reflect on the theory and practice of financial system reform from a higher perspective. In the past, we have always viewed mainstream foreign theories with a learning attitude. Now, China's economic growth has been recognized by the world. Facts have proved that China does not need to always put itself in the position of students. In the next few decades, as China rapidly becomes an economic power, building a financial system with Chinese characteristics and international competitiveness will be a far-reaching feat. To this end, we need to make bold breakthroughs in theory, not be constrained by the existing Western rules and regulations, and explore a path to reform the financial system that is suitable for China's national conditions. The topic of financial system reform is one of the elective courses for graduate students majoring in finance. This course strives to combine theory with practice to prepare students for forward-looking exploration of China's financial system reform. This course will analyze domestic and foreign financial system theories, lessons learned from the practice of financial system reform, existing problems in the Western financial system, and countermeasures and suggestions for my country's financial system reform. Specifically, it includes: financial structure theory, transaction costs, and information asymmetry; financial crisis theory and information asymmetry; financial intermediary organization theory; the ideological basis, historical background, and bottlenecks of the evolution of financial regulatory models; research on financial system reform ideas since the founding of the People's Republic of China; the optimal approach to my country's financial system reform and its theoretical basis; the latecomer advantage of China's financial system reform, etc. On the one hand, this course is based on cutting-edge theories in financial economics, and on the other hand, it focuses on the history of the theory and practice of financial system reform. Through the combination of historical and logical methods, we prepare rich materials and knowledge for students' research and provide clear research paths. Students are required to study under the guidance of teachers and be able to independently conduct in-depth and comprehensive analysis of specific financial system reform issues, combined with China's reality, and the use of contemporary financial and economic theories, and conduct in-depth and comprehensive analysis and research on the theoretical essence, solutions and practical operability of the issue. The basic content of this course is substantial. Since the 1960s, Western scholars have begun to study financial systems, and a large amount of valuable literature has been accumulated. At the same time, the practice of financial system reform at home and abroad in the past half century has provided a wealth of materials and cases for this course. This course is closely related to the practice of my country's economic reform and is highly integrated with the research work of the National Social Science Foundation, Natural Science Foundation, and the Ministry of Education that the lecturer himself applied for. This course requires students to learn to independently engage in meaningful academic research based on a full understanding of the literature and practical background, combining theory with the reality of my country's financial system reform, and using abstract logical methods and scientific research methods.

Introduction:

Its original motivation is to build a multi-level information processing model similar to the human brain by simulating the biological organization mechanism and information transmission and processing mechanism of the brain, conduct unsupervised feature extraction and analysis of a large amount of information, and form abstract high-level features by combining low-level features to discover valuable information, knowledge and abstract meaning hidden behind a large amount of data. _x000D_
_x000D_
Since 2006, deep learning has continued to heat up in academia. Stanford University, New York University, and the University of Montreal in Canada have become important centers for research on deep learning. In 2010, the U.S. Department of Defense's DARPA program funded a deep learning project for the first time, with participants including Stanford University, New York University, and NEC America Research Institute. An important basis for supporting deep learning is that the brain nervous system does have a rich hierarchical structure. One of the most famous examples is the Hubel-Wiesel model, which won the Nobel Prize in Medicine and Physiology for revealing the mechanism of the visual nerve. In addition to the perspective of bionics, the current theoretical research on deep learning is still basically in its infancy, but it has shown great power in the application field. Since 2011, speech recognition researchers from Microsoft Research and Google have successively used DNN technology to reduce the speech recognition error rate by 20% to 30%, which is the largest breakthrough in the field of speech recognition in more than ten years. In 2012, DNN technology achieved amazing results in the field of image recognition, reducing the error rate from 26% to 15% in the ImageNet evaluation. In this year, DNN was also applied to the drug activity prediction problem of pharmaceutical companies and achieved the best results in the world. Today, well-known high-tech companies with big data such as Google, Microsoft, and Baidu are vying to invest resources and occupy the technical commanding heights of deep learning, precisely because they all see the important role of more complex and powerful deep models in the era of big data. _x000D_
