Name: Linear Partial Differential Equations and Their Applications
Prerequisite: First courses are advanced mathematics and linear algebras.
Introduction: Linear partial differential equations are partial differential equations about an unknown function and all its derivatives are linear, such as the wave equation, Poisson's equation, and the heat conduction equation. Linear partial differential equations can be seen as the generalization of linear equations learned in linear algebra in infinite-dimensional vector spaces. It has important applications in many fields. In addition, learning the theory of linear partial differential equations is also very helpful for nonlinear equations, because the solution and analysis of nonlinear partial differential equations are often based on linearization. The content of the course selection for the basic part of partial differential equations is generally recognized to be the hyperbolic equation represented by the wave equation, the elliptic equation represented by the Poisson equation, and the heat conduction equation represented by the heat conduction equation. The emphasis is on the existence and uniqueness of classical solutions and the solving methods of analytical solutions, such as Green's function method, separation of variables method, etc. In many practical application problems, classical solutions to differential equations often do not exist, and problems need to be considered in a wider function class. In other words, the concept of classical solutions must be broadened. However, the advanced part of the course on partial differential equations involves knowledge from multiple disciplines such as topology, real variable functions, and functional analysis, which hinders many graduate students in applied disciplines from learning this part. As a quasi-advanced course on partial differential equations for applied science, I will introduce the theory and application of generalized solutions of linear partial differential equations that are closely related to applied science through analogy. The course does not require students to have previously studied topology, real variable functions and functional analysis. During the lecture, the basic knowledge of topology, real variable functions and functional analysis will be introduced by analogy with the knowledge of calculus and linear algebra that students have learned. The lecture content includes Soblev spaces and embedding theorems and trace theorems, the existence and uniqueness of weak solutions to boundary value problems of elliptic equations, compact operators and Fredholm operators, variational methods and their applications, generalized functions and their Fourier transformations, uniform continuous operator groups and strongly continuous operator semigroups and their applications in time development equations.

Name: Introduction to Contact Topology
Introduction: The tangent structure is a maximal non-integrable co-one-dimensional distribution on an odd-dimensional manifold, and is the odd-dimensional counterpart of the symplectic structure. Similar to symplectic structures, tangential structures are locally isomorphic to the unique standard model, which means that it only makes sense to consider the overall tangential structure. Tangential topology has developed greatly in recent decades and has a large number of connections and interactions with low-dimensional topology. For example, Kronheimer and Mrowka's tangent topology proved the Property P conjecture of knots; Hutchings defined embedded tangent homology for three-dimensional tangent manifolds. This theory was later proven to be isomorphic to Seiberg-Witten Floer homology. This course will provide a preliminary introduction to tangent topology.

Name: Morse Theory
Prerequisite: Simple fluid knowledge, simple algebra to expand knowledge.
Introduction: Morse theory is a mathematical theory developed since the 1930s. It examines the relationship between the analytical properties of the Morse function on a smooth manifold and the topology of the manifold. The Morse function is densely open in the C2 smooth function class, and the critical point of a Morse function is isolated. Therefore, the deformation of the manifold can be constructed through the negative gradient flow of the Morse function. However, when the flow passes a critical point, a strange phenomenon will occur, and a topological transformation will occur between level sets. The isothetic type of the transformation is determined by the cell dimension of the Morse function changing at this critical point, and the cell dimension is equal to the Morse index at this point. By studying stable or unstable manifolds, a smooth cellular decomposition of the manifold can be obtained. As an application, we can immediately get Morse's inequality. The weak Morse inequality gives a lower bound estimate of the Betti number of a manifold. In the early 1980s, Witten discovered a new method of constructing Morse complexes. The Morse-Witten-Smale complex can be obtained by using deformation theory, thereby converting the critical point information into the ground state information of the Schrödinger equation and obtaining the spectral gap decomposition. The discovery of the Morse-Witten-Smale complex led to some important applications, such as a new proof of the Reidemeister Torsion conjecture and application to the proof of the geometrization conjecture. Morse theory can also be extended to Novikov theory and Conley indicator theory for gradient-like flows. In recent years of research on symplectic geometry, Fukaya once again updated his understanding of Morse theory. By considering multiple Morse functions instead of a single Morse function, he obtained the Morse categorization theory. Infinite-dimensional Morse theory has become an important means of nonlinear analysis and is used in theories such as partial differential equations and geometric analysis. As a more classic application, we can use Morse theory to study the number of geodesics, Bott's periodicity theorem of classical Lie groups, combinations, many problems in algebraic geometry and applied mathematics. To sum up, Morse's theory has become an indispensable part of the foundation of modern mathematics.

The goal of this course is to close the distance between the basic courses of the subject and the scientific research practice and research frontiers of this subject, and to help graduate students majoring in nuclear physics and particle physics experiments to participate in actual research work as soon as possible.

Name: Frontiers of Nuclear Science Lecture Series
Introduction: This course aims to stimulate students' interest in nuclear physics and gain an understanding of nuclear science by introducing undergraduate students to relevant knowledge at the forefront of nuclear science. The content includes major discoveries, important applications, and major scientific projects in this field. Specifically, it includes high energy physics, particle physics, nuclear physics, nuclear technology, nuclear physics applications, accelerator physics, nuclear energy, etc.

Name: Density Functional Theory and Its Applications
Introduction: This course presents the main results of density function theory. Including Hartree-Fock molecular orbital theory, Kohn-Sham equation. Various approximations in the Kohn-Sham equation and their extensions (LDA, GGA, hybrid functionals,). Various basis sets used (atomic orbitals, plane waves, plus plane waves). Quasi-particle method to accurately calculate the energy gap - Green's function method and BSE equation. A preliminary introduction to the quantum transport method (non-equilibrium Green's function method) will also be given. At the same time, the use of Materials Studio calculation software is introduced, allowing students to use the software to construct various structures and optimize them. On this basis, they can calculate the electronic structure, phonon spectrum, total energy, binding energy, magnetic properties and optical properties.

Name: Theory of Solids
Introduction: Solid State Theory is a specialized course for graduate students majoring in condensed matter to learn the basic concepts, analytical methods and research overview in this field. The teaching objects are doctoral and master's students in condensed matter. This course focuses on key concepts and theoretical methods that are widely used and fundamental, such as the many-body problem and the energy band method for analyzing solid electronic structures. It also appropriately introduces some important research fields and current scientific research trends to lay a solid foundation for students to engage in scientific research.

Name: Solid State Structure
Introduction:
The course is mainly for doctoral and master students majoring in condensed matter physics, and teaches the structure, characterization methods and measurements of various solid materials (divided into crystal materials, amorphous materials and their defects according to the degree of order, and bulk materials, nanomaterials and thin film materials according to the material form). This course was originally hosted by Professor Zhu Xing, and in recent years it has been hosted by me. The requirements for students’ prior knowledge are not high. It is best to have studied "Group Theory", but it involves content in many fields such as crystallography, metal physics, X-ray science, neutron scattering, and microprobe technology. Studying this course has important guiding significance for students in the field of functional materials research to understand the intrinsic relationship between the structure and performance of materials, and then improve the performance of materials. _x000D_

Name: Semiconductor Photonics
Introduction: This course will lead students into the emerging intersection of semiconductors and photonics, and understand the important applications of semiconductor photonics in today's information society. Semiconductor photonics is developing rapidly, and many graduate students in the School of Physics: low-dimensional nanophysics, semiconductor optoelectronics, wide bandgap semiconductors, mesoscopic optics and other fields may need to focus on this course. This course focuses on teaching the basic methods of dealing with optical phenomena in semiconductors; the physical process of interaction between photons and electrons in semiconductors; and the basic principles of the operation of semiconductor lasers. It is required to use energy band theory to calculate the absorption and gain of semiconductor media. Use rate equations to derive laser threshold, population inversion, and modulation response characteristics. This course will also introduce the basic principles of typical semiconductor photonic device design, basic manufacturing processes and the latest progress in research in this field.

Name: Topological Electronics
Introduction: "Topological electronics" is a new electronics paradigm that takes advantage of new quantum degrees of freedom, including geometric phase (Berry phase), topological electronic states, energy valley degrees of freedom, and non-local coherence or entanglement. In topological electronics, the control and manipulation of topological quantum states will provide key technologies for future low-energy electronics and solid-state quantum information. The topological properties of quantum states and their interactions play a crucial role in spin-orbit interactions, topological insulators, topological semimetals, topological superconductivity and Majorana fermions, as well as non-local quantum correlation and quantum entanglement. In this course, we focus on teaching the topological properties of electronic energy bands in solids, quantum Hall effect and Chern insulators, Haldane model, Berry curvature and Berry curvature dipole, quantum spin Hall effect, Dirac equation and three-dimensional topological insulators, Weyl equation and topological semimetals, Majorana fermions and topological superconductors, and pay special attention to representative quantum phenomena in topological electronic systems and cutting-edge scientific research trends.

This course covers a wide range of knowledge and requires candidates to have taken advanced mathematics and general physics. It is suitable for graduate students interested in physics, chemistry, biology and other majors. _x000D_

Name: Modern Optics and Optoelectronics
Introduction: This course teaches modern optical content such as optical waveguides, nonlinear optics, laser spectroscopy, nanophotonics, and femtosecond light science. It also teaches optical and spectroscopic measurement technologies such as light modulation, optical radiation detection technology, laser spectroscopy technology, and femtosecond spectroscopy technology. This course focuses on basic knowledge and experimental techniques, while introducing cutting-edge research progress. It is an advanced optics course designed to further understand the theory and experimental methods in the field of optics after completing university optics. It also provides knowledge preparation for those who need to use optical or spectroscopic measurement technology in their work.

Name: Optical Theory
Prerequisite: Optical, electrodynamic, quantum mechanics, mathematical physics
Introduction: This course is a professional basic course for graduate students at the Institute of Modern Optics, School of Physics, Peking University. The course includes five parts: classical theory of light wave propagation, quantum properties of light fields, statistical properties of light fields, light wave radiation theory and theory of interaction between light and matter. Mainly studies the propagation characteristics, statistical characteristics and quantum properties of light and the interaction between light and matter. The theoretical methods used include classical theory, semi-classical theory, quantum theory and statistical theory. The basic knowledge involved in the tutorial includes the optical part of general physics, classical electrodynamics, quantum mechanics, and mathematical physics methods. The Institute of Modern Optics, School of Physics, Peking University offers two postgraduate courses, "Nonlinear Optics" and "Quantum Optics". Therefore, the part about the propagation of light in the "Optical Theory" course mainly discusses linear media, while the part about the interaction between light and matter mainly discusses semi-classical theory. _x000D_

Name: Topological Photonics
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Topological photonics is a cutting-edge branch of photonics that applies topological perspectives to the study of electromagnetic laws. The topological method focuses on the invariant characteristics of the system under continuous evolution, which provides a global perspective for understanding the general laws of photonics. On the one hand, topological photonics provides a high degree of abstraction for understanding the physical laws of devices, which is conducive to seeing the essence through phenomena; on the other hand, it provides an overall image for the design and optimization of photonic devices, which can avoid falling into local optimality, so it is a powerful supplement to traditional device design methods. In recent years, topological photonics has made great progress in the fields of new topological energy bands, topological insulators, new lasers, non-reciprocal devices, etc., which contains the possibility of constructing new photonic devices. The course is intended to be oriented to the frontiers of the discipline, integrating the cross-cutting backgrounds of multiple disciplines, introducing the basic knowledge, research methods and cutting-edge progress of topological photonics, and laying a foundation for graduate students interested in engaging in this field. This course is intended for master's and doctoral students majoring in optoelectronics, physics graduate students who are interested in research on optoelectronic devices, and senior undergraduate students. The course is planned to be taught bilingually in Chinese and English. _x000D_

Name: Frontiers of Atmospheric Science (I)
Introduction:
This course invites domestic and foreign experts and scholars to the department every week to give cutting-edge reports on various research directions in atmospheric science, so that students can understand the latest research trends in atmospheric science and broaden their horizons. _x000D_
This course is offered in the spring and autumn of each academic year. It is required to listen to reports at least 15 times in each semester during the two semesters (it is recommended to choose the first academic year unless there are special circumstances), which will be counted as 2 credits (students must sign in each time, and write down the report title, report location, time, etc. and submit it to the office of the Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences for record). On this basis, students are required to simulate writing a youth fund project application report (the format is formulated by the Atmospheric and Oceanic Science System and sent to the students), and then go on stage to defend the report about a week before the suspension of classes. The department (or subject point) will organize a review committee to review and give results. _x000D_
Assessment indicators: The number of lectures per semester is at least 15, and students listen to at least 30 reports in total; submit a project application; and defend the project application. _x000D_

Name: Physical Chemistry of Climate
Introduction: A required course for graduate students majoring in climate science, it introduces the Earth's climate system, its important physical and chemical mechanisms and feedback processes, and the concepts of climate models. Topics include Earth's climate history, climate time series and stochastic processes, the role of the atmosphere in the climate system, ocean carbon systems, atmospheric chemistry and climate, ocean physics and climate.

Name: Numerical Weather Prediction
Prerequisite: Atmospheric dynamics, mathematical physics equations, statistics, linear algebras
Introduction: Course content includes continuity equations, basic atmospheric fluctuations and filter approximations, numerical discretization, parameterization of physical processes, data assimilation, atmospheric predictability, and ensemble forecasting. The model operation topic of this course selects high-impact weather instances that occurred during the semester. They design experiments from different aspects of the model in groups to examine the sensitivity of the simulation effect of the same weather process to different setting conditions of each part of the model, such as different cumulus convection schemes, different cloud physics schemes, and different initial or boundary conditions. This effectively trains students in the practical application of theoretical knowledge and teamwork skills. Each part of the course explanation is accompanied by a Matlab graphic animation demonstration, which is of great help to students in understanding complex numerical forecasting concepts and methods.

Name: Fundamentals of Geophysical Fluid Dynamics
Introduction:
A required professional course for graduate students in the Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences, it teaches the most basic large-scale theory of geophysical fluid dynamics, from barotropic fluid to baroclinic fluid, from Kelvin waves to Rossby waves, from stable flow to unstable theory, etc._x000D_
_x000D_

1. The original name of this course is "Marine Geophysical Fluid Dynamics", and the course number is 00407774. This application is only to change the name to emphasize that this course pays more attention to the most basic dynamic processes in earth's fluid dynamics. _x000D_
2. This is a requirement of the latest curriculum planning for the Physical Ocean major of the Department of Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences. _x000D_

Name: Statistical Analysis and Applications
Introduction:
Statistical analysis is a very important means for atmospheric science, especially climatology. Climatology research, whether based on data or model simulations, is inseparable from statistical analysis. This course mainly teaches the simple basic theory of statistical analysis, main analysis methods and applications in the field of atmospheric science. The purpose is that through the study of this course, students will master the theoretical basis of probability theory and mathematical statistics of basic statistical analysis, and become familiar with relevant statistical analysis methods, especially statistical significance testing of various analysis methods. At the same time, you can skillfully apply relevant analysis methods in actual research, especially the latest analysis methods and their applications related to time series analysis. The specific teaching content is roughly divided into the following parts:_x000D_
Part 1 Basic process classification, including classification of deterministic processes and stochastic processes_x000D_
The second part introduces the basic basics of probability theory, including the distribution of random variables, different moments and their physical meanings, etc._x000D_
The third part is statistical principles, including parameter estimation, reliability testing, hypothesis testing, etc._x000D_
The fourth part begins with an introduction to various topics including autoregressive models and their parameter estimation and testing, single and multi-variable linear and nonlinear regression models and their parameter estimation and reliability testing, spectral analysis and parameter estimation and reliability testing, continuous process analysis methods and their parameter estimation and reliability testing, basic concepts and methods of nonlinear time series analysis and their parameter estimation and reliability testing, etc. For each topic, relevant application examples are prepared to specifically illustrate the application of analysis, with special attention being paid to the statistical testing of the corresponding process.

Name: Modern Atmospheric Sounding
Introduction:
This course is divided into two parts to introduce modern atmospheric detection technologies and methods. The first part focuses on the basic elements of the atmosphere detected by modern remote sensing methods. Through the study of this part, students can understand the detection principles, inversion methods and application frontiers of modern ground-based remote sensing equipment. The second part focuses on the physical characteristics of cloud detection by aircraft and the characteristics of atmospheric aerosols. Through this part of study, students can understand the advanced instruments, basic principles, data analysis methods, and applications of aircraft for field detection of atmospheric particles. Lay the foundation for subsequent courses and professional studies at the postgraduate level. _x000D_
Specific contents include: precipitation, wind field, water vapor, temperature remote sensing, trace gases, atmospheric aerosols, microphysical properties of clouds, sampling technology of aerosols and cloud particles, ground observation of aerosols, clouds and precipitation, etc.

Name: Physical Oceanography
Introduction:
This course aims to apply theoretical knowledge of fluid mechanics to understand the observed dynamic processes of the Earth's oceans. It is an introductory course for learning ocean circulation theory and wave theory. The course begins with an introduction to the basic forms of ocean circulation, starting from basic hydrodynamic equations, and gradually understanding the physical mechanisms of ocean wind-induced circulation and thermohaline circulation, the basic characteristics and theories of ocean fluctuations, the role of air-sea exchange in ocean circulation, tropical ocean processes and the El Niño phenomenon, the variability and mechanism of the Atlantic meridional circulation, thermocline theory, etc. Most of the theory will be introductory in nature and not comprehensive. In order to deepen the understanding of the theory, some simple numerical simulations of ideal experiments will be done using ocean models in the course. _x000D_
_x000D_
Students who choose the course need to have studied fluid mechanics, preferably geofluid mechanics, and do not need to know much about the ocean. The course assessment method is 40% of daily homework, 25% of midterm exam, and 35% of final exam. _x000D_

Name: Talent Development for International Organizations
Introduction:
In order to implement the "Global Governance Talents" training plan, the Graduate School, the Academic Affairs Department, the International Cooperation Department, the Student Employment Guidance Service Center and other departments jointly launched the first "Peking University International Organization Talent Training Summer Program" in July 2018. _x000D_
The teaching content is divided into four basic modules: basic courses, expert lectures, student group exchanges and discussions, and on-site visits and surveys. The basic course offers several modules such as overview of international organizations, international organizational law, theory and practice of international organizations, and global health governance. Mid-level and high-level practical experts from some international organizations are invited to the school to give special lectures and reports. In the practical inspection phase, we will arrange on-site visits and on-site teaching at international organizations in Beijing. _x000D_
Students who have completed all courses and teaching content and passed the assessment will be allowed to graduate. The Graduate School will issue a completion certificate for the "Peking University Talent Cultivation for International Organizations" certificate program. They will also receive 2 credits (elective courses), which will be recorded on their transcripts, and their grades will be recorded as passed (P). Course assessment includes comprehensive evaluation such as attendance, class participation and discussion exchanges, group work and discussion reports.

Name: Introduction to Reactor Physics and Engineering
Introduction:

 This course is offered to meet the needs of the development of the country's nuclear energy industry. The goal is to enable students to master the basic knowledge and basic principles of nuclear reactors and nuclear energy systems. The course content mainly covers the principles of reactor operation and control, including reactor structure and classification, nuclear physics knowledge related to reactor physics, neutron diffusion and moderation, reactor criticality theory, reactor/nuclear power plant engineering foundations, principles of next-generation nuclear energy systems, reactor safety, nuclear fuel/nuclear waste management, etc. This course involves many physical concepts and is closely related to engineering practice; studying this course is conducive to the cultivation of students' abilities and the improvement of their overall quality, and is conducive to students' development in nuclear energy-related fields.

Name: Global Change and Urban Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Global Change and Urban Ecology_x000D_
Human activities have greatly changed the earth system. These changes are what we usually call global changes, including changes in atmospheric composition (the most prominent of which is the increase in greenhouse gases), global and regional climate changes, land use changes and habitat destruction, increases in reactive nitrogen compounds, increases in species extinction rates, and increases in the number and impact of alien species. The global changes mentioned above are all reflected in urban ecosystems, such as a significant increase in urban CO2 concentration (urban CO2 domes); an obvious urban heat island effect; urbanization is the most drastic form of land use change; urban nitrogen deposition has increased significantly; urbanization is a major cause of species extinction, which reduces the species richness and evenness of most biological groups in cities, and because of the city's ecological footprint (Ecological footprint). footprint) far exceeds the boundaries of the city itself, so urbanization may lead to a reduction in local species diversity regionally and even globally; urbanization also provides a unique "niche opportunity" for alien species to gain a foothold, and many studies have found that along with urbanization, the number of alien species increases. Therefore, to a certain extent, urban ecosystems are a microcosm of future global changes and a "natural laboratory" for studying the interaction between global changes driven by human activities and terrestrial ecosystems. This course organically combines global change and urban ecology to illustrate the interactions and feedbacks between terrestrial ecosystems and environmental changes. The specific courseware outline is as follows:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Progress in Global Change Research_x000D_
2. Specific manifestations and cases of global change_x000D_
3. Global changes have promoted the development of urban ecology (traditional ecology often avoids urban ecology). The development process of urban ecology _x000D_
4. Two aspects of urbanization: urban population increase and urban area expansion_x000D_
5-8. Changes in urban physical environment (changes in urban land cover, urban climate, urban soil and urban hydrology)_x000D_
9-12. Urban biological changes (plants, animals, microorganisms and humans)_x000D_
13-16. Cities are social-ecological systems (Social-Ecological Systems: SESs) that couple human society and natural ecological systems; _x000D_
The global impact of urbanization on ecosystem services;_x000D_
People are an important component of urban ecology;_x000D_
Unique biogeochemical cycles. _x000D_
_x000D_
_x000D_
In addition, I learned that Mr. Li Dihua is teaching an undergraduate course on urban ecology. Let me briefly explain the complementarity and non-duplication of this proposed course with Mr. Li’s course: _x000D_
For urban ecology, relevant literature and researchers have two different interpretations. One is the so-called scientific definition (that is, from the perspective of ecology). Urban ecology refers to the study of the distribution, change, and interaction of organisms (including people) and the environment in cities and their surroundings, as well as the structure and function of urban systems and their changes. This is exactly the perspective of the course I propose. At the same time, combined with my own scientific research work, I use the urban ecosystem as a "natural laboratory" to systematically study the interaction and feedback between global changes and terrestrial ecosystems. It is a more suitable graduate course for graduate students with a certain knowledge base of ecology and geography. The other is the definition in urban planning. Urban ecology is the ecological standard in urban planning and design that makes the urban environment more comfortable for people, reduces the negative impact of urbanization on the environment, and emphasizes specific planning methods and goals. My personal understanding is the direction of Teacher Li's teaching. Taking courses in these two directions at the same time can enrich students' horizons and gain a more comprehensive understanding of urban ecology.

The purpose of this course is to improve the oral and written expression skills of postgraduate students majoring in geophysics. Name: Modern Analytical Techniques in Rock Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
1. Microscopic analysis technology: _x000D_
The main teaching content is electron probe microanalysis technology. Electron Probe Micro Analysis/Analyzer (EPMA, Electron Probe Micro Analysis/Analyzer) is a common instrumental analysis method in analytical chemistry (hereinafter referred to as electron probe). Its biggest advantage is that it can conduct qualitative and quantitative analysis of a small area (~ 1 μm) of the sample in-situ without causing obvious physical and chemical damage (injury). The world's first electron probe was designed and manufactured by the Frenchman Castaing in 1951 (Castaing and Guinier, 1949; Castaing, 1951). It was an inevitable product of the cross-fusion of electron optical technology and X-ray spectroscopic analysis technology (Moseley, 1913; Siegbahn, 1931). The electron probe uses a beam of high-energy accelerated electrons (5-30 kV) that can be focused to an infinitesimal size to bombard micro-areas of the sample, thereby stimulating different X-ray energies (photons), which are then captured by the detection system (spectrometer and probe) and later analyzed and processed by computer software to convert them into corresponding element type and content information. At the same time, under electron bombardment, there is also the release of other energy (backscattered electrons, secondary electrons, transmitted electrons, absorbed electrons, cathodoluminescence, etc.), which can provide corresponding electronic image information. Electron probe analysis can simultaneously obtain the morphology and composition image information of micro areas under very high spatial resolution (secondary electron image, 10 nm) without destroying the original structure of the sample. The analytical testing work it can complete is irreplaceable by other analytical chemistry instruments. Theoretically, the electron probe can analyze all elements from the 4th element beryllium (Be) to the 92nd element uranium (U), including almost most of the currently known elements. It is an important technical support for the development of modern science and technology and is widely used in physics, chemistry, chemical industry, geology, materials, metallurgy, machinery, environment, microelectronics, biomedicine and other fields (Xu Cuizhang, 1990). Electron probe analysis generally uses X-rays excited by electrons in the element's inner layer, so its analysis results are not affected by the valence state of the element. _x000D_

Name: Applied Paleontology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Microarchaeological fossils are important fossil materials in evolutionary and developmental biology (evo-devo) (such as embryonic fossils and three-dimensionally preserved soft body microfossils, namely Orsten-type fossils), and have extensive application value in the fields of plate tectonics, energy, environment, oceans, archaeology and other fields. The purpose of this course is to introduce students to the basic biological knowledge of some microarchaeological taxa (physiological and ecological characteristics, morphological structural characteristics, geological history and geographical distribution characteristics) and the latest progress in international research and their applications in geoscience, energy and global change research. The biological groups taught include conodonts (including conodonts), radiolaria, foraminifera, ostracods, embryonic fossils and three-dimensionally preserved soft body microfossils.

Name: Biogeochemistry and Biomineralization
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Biogeochemistry focuses on the study of chemical processes on the earth's surface and involves many branches of geochemistry and life sciences. Biomineralization is the process of mineral formation from living tissues, and biomineralization refers to the role played by organisms and the organic matter they produce in the formation of mineral deposits. They have an important influence on the earth's surface circulation and geological processes, and are one of the main geological processes in the formation of mineral resources. Through learning, students can understand the basic principles of biochemical cycles and the role of biomineralization in biochemical cycles, and master the principles of using geochemistry and sedimentology methods to restore earth system factors. The main teaching contents of this course include: the properties of the earth's outer layer; the geochemical cycle of life elements (carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulfur, phosphorus, etc.); the mechanism of biominerals and biomineralization; the environmental indication significance of biomineralization; and the mechanism and evolution of biomineralization.

Name: Sedimentary Cyclicity and Facies Analysis
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Sedimentary cycles are widely distributed in various sedimentary records in marine and continental basins. This course focuses on the analysis of sedimentary facies and sedimentary cycles, focusing on teaching the basic concepts, latest developments and working methods of interdisciplinary research on sedimentology and stratigraphy. The main teaching contents of this course include: sedimentary facies, sedimentary patterns and sedimentary environments; sedimentary cycle interfaces; types of sedimentary cycles (terrestrial sedimentary cycles, littoral and shallow marine clastic rocks, shallow marine carbonates, slopes and basins); sea level changes and sedimentary cycles; tectonism and sedimentary cycles; Milankovitch cycles and sedimentary cycles; sedimentary cycle analysis methods; mathematical models and sedimentary cycle research; application of biostratigraphy in sedimentary cycle research; sedimentary cycles and chronostratigraphy.

Name: The Evolution of Plants
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course begins by introducing and explaining the basic concepts of paleobotany, the preservation characteristics of paleobotanical fossils, research methods and the systematic classification of plants. Taking the main evolutionary events of the plant kingdom in the history of the earth as the main line, it teaches and discusses: the evolution and development of lower plants, including prokaryotic cells to eukaryotic cells. The evolution of cellular, multicellular metaphytes and algae; the development of plants from aquatic to terrestrial, the emergence of embryophytes; the evolutionary differentiation of vascular plants; the successful evolution of gymnosperms and seed traits from gymnosperms, lycophytes, euphytes, and the emergence of angiosperms on the earth. Changes in the global environment, including plate movement, climate zoning, and the evolution and development of the atmosphere and hydrosphere, will undoubtedly have an impact on the evolution of terrestrial ecosystems. This course also plans to discuss the interaction between terrestrial ecosystems, environmental evolution, and the evolution and differentiation of terrestrial plants in some chapters. Through the teaching of this course, we hope that students will have a deep understanding of the evolution and development of the plant world to guide their scientific practice.

Name: Remote Sensing Structural Analysis
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Remote sensing geology is a new discipline and a marginal interdisciplinary subject that combines remote sensing technology with earth science. Its theory is based on the electromagnetic radiation of geological bodies; while the technical methods are based on "multi" technologies, that is, multispectral, multi-platform, multi-temporal, multi-directional imaging, multi-polarization, multi-level enhancement processing, etc.; its research objects are various characteristics of electromagnetic radiation of the earth's surface and surface geology, and geological phenomena. Remote sensing geological structure analysis is to use technical means such as remote sensing's wide field of view, rich information, timed positioning observation, and computer processing to obtain high-definition, large-area coverage, and a large amount of geoscientific information beyond human vision. On this basis, relevant theories of structural geology are used to extract information on various geological structural phenomena, such as folds, faults, linear structures, annular structures, etc., to serve mineral resource exploration, regional geological surveys, environmental and hazard geological monitoring and other work.

It attempts to explain the mechanism of earth surface processes, surface mass transfer and material circulation, layer-circle interaction and balance, global change and geotectonics from a new academic perspective and from a multidisciplinary perspective. The scientific content involved in the course is a major issue at the forefront of the discipline, which is highly exploratory and has broad application significance. The course focuses on basic theories, basic skills, computational modeling, thinking expansion and interdisciplinary interdisciplinary development, and cultivates graduate students' in-depth data mining and fusion abilities.

Introduction: This course is a basic geology course on the theory of early earth evolution. It is multidisciplinary and takes into account early history and deep processes. Before taking this course, you should have a basic knowledge of geotectonics, petrology, isotope geochemistry and geochronology. This course is based on the basic geological composition of continental cratons, the earth's early geological evolution history, the accretion, stability, and amalgamation history of the world's ancient continents, the deep crustal structure and thermal evolution process, and the theoretical exploration of Precambrian plate tectonics. It comprehensively introduces the latest theories of early earth evolution and its practical applications. The main contents include: 1) Precambrian stage division and signs; 2) Basic geological composition of ancient cratons; 3) Structural-metamorphic evolution of granite-greenstone belts; 4) Structural-metamorphic evolution of advanced metamorphic areas; 5) Main orogenic belts and plate tectonic models in the Precambrian; 6) Continental lower crustal profiles and deep processes; 7) Aorogenic magmatic activity, basic dykes, rifts and early continental breakup; 8) Supercontinent cycles and ancient plate tectonic evolution. 9) Analysis of continental basement resources.

Name: Hydrogeology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The introduction mainly talks about the significance of learning "Hydrogeology" and the learning focus and learning methods of this course. Chapter 1 The Source, Distribution and Cycle of Water on the Earth (1 credit hour) Chapter 2 The Occurrence of Groundwater (2 credit hours) This chapter focuses on concepts, focusing on the concepts of aquifers, aquicludes and water-bearing systems. Chapter 3 Groundwater under different burial conditions (4 hours) This chapter is mainly conceptual, focusing on the concepts of phreatic water and confined water. Chapter 4 The Movement Rules of Groundwater (10 hours) This chapter mainly teaches the basic concepts of hydrodynamics, groundwater dynamic systems and Darcy's law. This is the focus of the hydrogeology chapter. Chapter 5 Chemical Composition of Groundwater (4 hours) This chapter focuses on the concepts of hardness and salinity of groundwater and the basic chemical composition of groundwater. Chapter 6 Groundwater in Different Interstitial Rock Formations (6 hours) This chapter focuses on teaching the concepts of three common types of groundwater and the geological conditions for enrichment. Chapter 7 Discussion of Groundwater Resources and Groundwater Environment Issues (3 hours) This chapter uses examples as clues to guide students to start classroom discussions and discuss the protection issues of groundwater resources and groundwater environment.

Name: Reservoir Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
The oil and gas reservoir is the direct target layer for oil exploration and development and the core of the oil and gas reservoir. The properties of reservoirs are closely related to oil and gas reserves, production and productivity. Reservoir geology mainly studies the macroscopic distribution characteristics, internal structural characteristics, reservoir parameter distribution characteristics, pore structure characteristics and dynamic change characteristics of the reservoir during the development of oil and gas fields, and serves the exploration and development of oil and gas fields.     The teaching content includes the following aspects: 1. Basic characteristics of reservoir rocks. Basic physical properties of reservoir rocks and basic geological characteristics of different types of reservoirs.   _x000D_
  2. Reservoir distribution model: Genetic type, distribution model, sand body structure and reservoir characteristics of reservoirs (focusing on clastic rock reservoirs and carbonate reservoirs).     _x000D_
3. Reservoir pore evolution model and controlling factors: Reservoir diagenetic evolution and pore evolution mechanism, pore evolution model and distribution rules.    _x000D_
 4. Reservoir pore structure: Reservoir pore and throat types and pore structure characteristics.     5. Reservoir fractures: The mechanical origin and geological origin mechanism of reservoir fractures, the distribution rules of fractures and the basic characteristics of fractured reservoirs.     6. Reservoir heterogeneity: the basic characteristics of heterogeneity and its influencing factors.     _x000D_
7. Reservoir geological model: the basic content of the reservoir geological model, model classification and classification, as well as deterministic modeling and stochastic modeling methods.     _x000D_
8. Reservoir evaluation technology and methods

Name: Sequence Stratigraphy
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Content summary: 1.	Sea-level changes and sequence stratigraphy: basics and key definitions of sequence stratigraphy; control of clastic sedimentation by global sea-level changes; concepts and applications of sequences and systems. 2.	Sea level changes in geological history: A comprehensive and systematic introduction to the research methods of sequence stratigraphy, including biological, sedimentary and chronological analysis processes. 3.	Sea level changes and applications in oil and gas exploration: the relationship between global sea level changes and sedimentary sequences; taking the relationship between the sequence stratigraphic framework of typical basins and the distribution of oil and gas reservoirs as an example, the application scope and prospects of sequence stratigraphy are introduced.

Name: Basin Dynamics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Abstract: Basin is the most important tectonic unit on the earth's surface, and it is also the main area for human survival and resource dependence. With the in-depth study of global basin exploration, basin research has entered the era of four-dimensional geological research, especially the advancement of seismic reflection technology, which provides extremely rich content and information for basin geological research. _x000D_
Starting from the big thinking of geodynamics and earth systems, this course classifies global basins structurally and systematically analyzes and dissects different types of typical basin structures. Based on modern new technologies and within the framework of ancient plate and supercontinent reconstruction, this course understands the dynamic origin and evolution of basins, especially the analysis and summary of seismic structural profiles at the basin scale. On the basis of basin structural evolution, this course understands the intracontinental plate tectonic dynamic processes and their control over resource enrichment. _x000D_
	_x000D_
The main teaching and seminar contents are as follows:_x000D_
1. Basin structure research technology and methods_x000D_
2. Global basin distribution and structural background_x000D_
3. Prototype basin dynamics type_x000D_
4. Structural anatomy of typical basin types_x000D_
5. Basin tectonic evolution, ancient continental reconstruction and deep processes_x000D_
6. Basin genetic model and formation mechanism_x000D_
7. Oil and gas enrichment patterns and structural mechanisms of important basin groups

Name: Advances in the Practice and Theory of China's Oil and Gas Exploration
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: It is undertaken by senior explorers and famous scholars such as Academician Jia Chengzao and Academician Ma Yongsheng, who are responsible for and organizing the significant progress in oil and gas exploration in my country in recent years. Taking the Kela 2 gas field in the Tarim Basin, the Puguang gas field in the Sichuan Basin, Daqing deep natural gas and other major overseas discoveries as examples, the system It comprehensively introduces the recent major progress and breakthroughs in oil and gas exploration in my country. On the basis of case analysis, it systematically understands the situation and dynamics of my country's oil and gas exploration, and then understands the frontiers of my country's oil and gas exploration and oil and gas geology theory, and promotes the close integration of subject development with major national needs.

Name: World Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:

Name: Petroleum Exploration Techniques and Methods
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: This course systematically introduces petroleum exploration technology and methods, focusing on petroleum seismic exploration data acquisition technology and methods, petroleum seismic exploration data processing technology and methods, petroleum seismic data interpretation technology and methods; it guides students to learn and use UNIX computer systems, seismic data processing software systems, and petroleum exploration data interpretation systems.

Name: Sedimentary Geochemistry
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
Sedimentary geochemistry is an emerging edge discipline resulting from the mutual penetration and combination of sedimentology and geochemistry. It takes sediments and sedimentary rocks as objects to study the migration, accumulation and distribution rules of elements and stable isotopes contained in them during the deposition and diagenesis process, and then determines the ancient environment and structural background when they were deposited. Through the study of this course, you will become familiar with the compositional characteristics of continental crust and seawater, and master the factors and processes that affect the chemical characteristics of sediments. On this basis, by recording the chemical characteristics retained in the sediments, and by obtaining effective discriminant parameters, you can determine the structural background and climatic environment when the sediments were formed, as well as the chemical evolution characteristics of sedimentary rocks in the geological historical period. _x000D_
I have been engaged in research on sedimentary geochemistry since I was studying for my PhD. I have not only systematically mastered the basic theories in this direction, but also am familiar with its cutting-edge trends. Students who choose this course should have a knowledge background in sedimentary petrology and geochemistry.

Name: Well-Logging Geology
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Mine geophysical logging is one of the important disciplines in the petroleum profession and is widely used in oil and gas exploration and development. Through the study of this course, graduate students can master the basic principles of well logging, learn to apply well logging data to carry out geological research, and master the basic methods and software applications of digital processing of well logging data. The teachers to be taught have long been engaged in scientific research and teaching in the oil field. They have been engaged in research in this professional field for more than 20 years. They are proficient in new theories and new technologies in related fields and have a good foundation for teaching courses. This course is 36 hours long and is recommended as a required course for petroleum geology majors and elective courses for other majors.

Name: Carbonate Rock Oil and Gas Exploration
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
1. Purpose of the course: To enable graduate students majoring in petroleum geology and related energy to systematically master the theory and latest research progress of carbonate oil and gas exploration, especially the knowledge of carbonate rock diagenesis mechanism, diagenesis types, diagenesis research methods, diagenesis control factors, diagenetic evolution history and its relationship with reservoir development. _x000D_
2. Basis for starting the course: Carbonate rocks contain abundant oil and gas resources. Basic geology and oil and gas exploration application research around carbonate rocks have been richly accumulated. A set of systematic theoretical knowledge and research methods have been formed, with complete teaching materials, research monographs and experimental support conditions. The teachers who start the course have profound theoretical foundations and rich practical experience, have made significant contributions in the field of carbonate rock research and exploration, and have many years of experience in training graduate students. _x000D_
3. Teaching requirements: Master the basic methods of carbonate rock petrology research, including the classification and naming principles of structural origin and sedimentary facies/microfacies identification, diagenesis types and diagenetic sequence analysis methods, etc., focusing on mastering carbonate rock thin section research and geochemical analysis methods, carbonate rock reservoir development mechanisms, etc. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence
Introduction: This course keeps up with the latest developments in the field of artificial intelligence, combines artificial intelligence with big data, and teaches the basic ideas, basic theories, basic methods and typical applications in the fields of artificial intelligence and big data in an easy-to-understand and easy-to-understand manner. The content of this course includes: overview of artificial intelligence and data engineering, frequent pattern mining and applications, cluster analysis and applications, neural networks and deep neural networks, basics of computer vision and natural language processing technology, etc. The basic goal of this course is to enable students to initially understand the basic principles of artificial intelligence, initially learn and master the basic methods of artificial intelligence, have a deeper understanding of big data and deep learning architecture, help students form a perceptual and rational understanding of artificial intelligence applications, and lay a technical foundation for students to engage in artificial intelligence application development in related fields in the future.

Name: Cloud Computing Technology and Applications
Introduction:
This course requires students to be familiar with basic computer courses, such as operating systems, data structures, databases, algorithm analysis and design, computer networks, software engineering, JAVA language, etc. By studying the above courses, students can understand important concepts such as "computing resources", "object-oriented", "virtualization" and "SOA", master the basic skills of using JAVA language to develop software, and have certain experience in network software development. _x000D_
By learning the relevant concepts, technologies and platforms of cloud computing, you can understand the basic ideas of cloud computing, master the relevant technologies of cloud computing, understand the trends of the cloud computing industry, and be able to develop cloud computing applications on open source cloud computing platforms. Specifically include: _x000D_
1. Basic ideas of cloud computing, understand the basic concepts, development history, causes and typical applications of cloud computing. _x000D_
2. Cloud computing architecture, understand the basic architecture of cloud computing, the basic principles of IAAS, PAAS and SAAS. _x000D_
3. Cloud computing related technologies, including concepts and knowledge of virtualization, distributed file storage and management, and parallel programming. _x000D_
4. Open source cloud computing platforms such as Openstack, Hadoop, etc. _x000D_
5. Typical applications of cloud computing and typical products in the industry. _x000D_

Name: Machine Learning
Introduction:
Mainly teaches the basic principles and methods of machine learning and its application in the fields of financial big data and modern management. The main content includes basic concepts of machine learning and commonly used learning methods. _x000D_
It mainly teaches commonly used learning methods and enables students to use their methods to solve big data-related problems in engineering management through engineering internships. _x000D_

Introduction:
The course will systematically introduce the basic theory and application of scientific and technological innovation management to students in management, finance or engineering, as well as introduce the basic knowledge of innovative technology and cutting-edge innovative technology_x000D_
This course leads students to systematically understand the field of innovation. The textbook content covers two parts, namely innovative strategic management and innovative science and technology. In the strategic management part of innovation, it mainly teaches innovation theory, innovation motivation, entry timing, innovation direction, strategic planning and implementation of scientific and technological innovation, etc. In the innovative science and technology part, it teaches the basic knowledge required for scientific and technological innovation, and introduces current and future cutting-edge innovative technologies. _x000D_

Name: Blockchain
Introduction: Understanding the origin, concept and status of the block chain; understanding the underlying algorithms, supporting techniques and key mechanisms of the block chain; understanding key block chain projects and major applications in the financial sector; understanding the issues of security privacy, relevant laws and regulations and regulatory controls involved in the block chain; and understanding the challenges and problems of the block chain and its future development.

Name: Financial Innovation
Introduction:
1. Teaching purpose:_x000D_
Enable students to master the basic concepts of innovation; learn to construct a knowledge system of financial innovation; summarize typical cases of financial innovation; and master the basic methods of financial innovation. _x000D_
2. Basic knowledge: _x000D_
Currency banking, financial intermediary, financial engineering, integration of industry and finance_x000D_
3. Teaching requirements: Students should improve their independent financial innovation skills on the basis of mastering basic content_x000D_

Name: Innovation Strategy Management
Introduction: Innovation strategic management is the most active field in management disciplines in recent years and is a core course in management. It is based on the latest trends in modern enterprise development and focuses on how China can achieve steady, sustained and confident economic growth through technological innovation. The course provides a systematic framework of innovation strategic management knowledge and methods by effectively organizing the theories and methods of innovation strategic management.

Name: General Education and Frontier Technologies
Introduction: Improve students' comprehensive quality and enable students to understand the cutting-edge science and technology of the subject; promote students' appreciation and understanding of Chinese civilization and world civilization, think and understand the development and changes of modern China and the world, and think about life and the meaning of life; improve students' language expression, communication and career planning abilities; cultivate students' strong physique and good temperament. The content design of this course includes 4 modules, namely cutting-edge technology, humanistic literacy, artistic literacy, and safety and health. Through literature reading, expert lectures, lecture practice, book clubs, special activities and other forms, students can gradually improve their ideological and moral quality on their own basis, understand and establish a correct world view and values, inspire their sense of innovation and the spirit of pursuing truth, promote a healthy body and mind, improve aesthetic ability and management communication skills, and achieve both unique personality and comprehensive development, both humanistic literacy and scientific spirit, both the independent thinking spirit of self-cultivation and family management, and the sense of historical mission of governing the country and bringing peace to the world.

Name: Computational Intelligence
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: This course systematically teaches the relevant theories, technologies and main applications of computational intelligence, and provides students with a comprehensive introduction to the cutting-edge fields and latest developments in computational intelligence research. Through the study of this course, students are required to systematically master the basic content and methods of computer intelligence and understand the main application fields of computational intelligence. Before studying this course, students are required to have taken elective courses such as "Advanced Mathematics", "Computer Fundamentals and Algorithms", "Artificial Intelligence Fundamentals" and "Pattern Recognition Fundamentals". The main contents of this course include: Introduction to Computational Intelligence, Artificial Neural Networks, Support Vector Machine Theory, Adaptive Boosting Algorithms, Evolutionary Computing and Genetic Algorithms, Simulated Annealing Algorithms, Swarm Intelligence Optimization Algorithms, Artificial Immunity, Fuzzy Sets and Fuzzy Information Processing, and the Future Development of Computational Intelligence.

Name: SQL and Data Analysis
Introduction:
The generation and exchange of information are core components of economic activity. The emergence and development of digital information technology in the twentieth century has had a profound impact on all industries. This is not only reflected in the improvement of production and service efficiency and the emergence of innovative business models, but more importantly, with the process of digitalization, data technology develops rapidly, and a large amount of information is collected, recorded and saved in the form of data. How to effectively manage data and mine knowledge from data is an important driving force for the further rapid development of various industries. Understanding the basic theories of databases and mastering data query and analysis tools are necessary skills for managers in the new era. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is mainly designed for students who have no database-related knowledge base. The course teaches the fundamentals of databases, structured query languages, and recent developments in big data tools. The course will combine business cases and sample data for practical teaching, guiding students to apply database knowledge to database design and data analysis, and cultivating students' abilities to access data, manage data, and analyze data. _x000D_

Name: Distributed Storage and Computing
Introduction:
In the era of big data, global digital data doubles every two years. Massive data gives data scientists a broader application space. Use rich data analysis tools to mine valuable information from data, make decisions more intelligent, and make life more convenient, which has greatly subverted people's traditional lifestyles and business models. At the same time, the arrival of the big data era has made people worry about not having data and not knowing where to get data, to being unable to start with such large-scale data and not knowing how to apply it. The Distributed Storage and Computing course is a required professional course for students with a master's degree in business analysis. Through the study of this course, students can master the distributed computing methods commonly used in the field of big data mining, deepen students' understanding of statistical distributed computing and the value of big data, and cultivate students' ability to use statistical methods under modern distributed architecture to deeply mine the data structure of big data and solve some practical problems. _x000D_
 	The teaching content of this course mainly includes ten modules such as big data distributed computing, Hadoop-based distributed and Hadoop database operations, big data value, etc. Each module is divided into three sections. Each part is the main content of this course. It strives to explain the profound things in a simple way and is guided by practical cases. It not only explains the processes and principles of various distributed computing, but also strengthens students' in-depth understanding of statistical distributed computing. The teaching method adopts a combination of slide classroom lectures and computer guidance practice. The first two sections of each module are taught by teachers plus cases, and the third section is conducted by students on computer practice. The computer-based practical part for students generally has classroom practice every two chapters. It includes the practice of teachers’ classroom cases and extended practice. Extended practice accounts for 50% of the total grade as usual grades. Students complete homework based on the teaching content in class. _x000D_

Name: Marketing Management and Customer Value
Introduction: In the big data age, more and more companies are aware of the need to use data to better exploit consumer values and optimize marketing strategies. This course responds to this need and is designed to build the capacity of students to complement marketing decisions through data analysis. The course presents important models in the field of marketing and demonstrates their practical application through data and examples. These include joint analysis, cluster analysis, product selection models, customer life value models, etc. These analytical methods and quantitative models will help decision makers to understand consumer needs, design new products, stratification and precision marketing, assess customer values, etc.

Name: Topics in Data Science
Introduction: This course is a data science course designed for non-computer majors. It mainly involves the basic concepts, principles, methods, and technologies of data science to establish basic abilities. It also conducts feasible applications and explorations based on the scientific field of the case. Students can also use this to think about the use of data science technology methods in their own fields for practice and experiment. The strict research boundaries of data science are not very clear, and it is an interdisciplinary discipline that explores the extraction of knowledge and wisdom from data through scientific methods and provides data insights. This introductory course will introduce the basic principles and process methods of data science from a simple to in-depth basis, and further explain the importance of analytical thinking and the basic principles of business analysis.

Name: Value Investing
Introduction:
This course consists of two parts. _x000D_
The first part focuses on the value investment theory of Graham and Dodd and will be developed through courses, cases and classroom discussions, including (1) assumptions and methods of value investment; (2) value assessment methods based on balance sheets and earnings; (3) construction of value-based risk control models; (4) design of search strategies for value investment opportunities; (5) supervision, investor protection, corporate governance and their impact on company value. _x000D_
The second part will allow students to immerse themselves in the specific practice of Graham and Dodd's investment principles. Through guest lectures and other forms, students will understand how to create an investment program that suits the investor's personality traits. The topics discussed by the guests include (1) search strategies; (2) valuation methods; (3) research methods; (4) investors’ risk management experience. _x000D_

He has proposed the concept of happiness of "peace of mind toward goodness" and the "one body, two wings" happiness education model. This course is planned to be based on the reading of Chinese and Western classics, through classroom teaching discussions on several major themes, as well as the design of daily cultivation and comprehensive practical activities, in order to understand reading and integrate knowledge and action, improve students' (preparatory teachers) ideological and moral understanding, and lay the foundation for their effective implementation of school moral education. _x000D_

Name: Educational Leadership and School Management
Introduction: Education Leadership and School Management programme Type of course: Selected postgraduate courses Teacher: Chiang Seong Office: Education College Room 307 Telephone: 6275 3568 E-mail: cjiang@gse.pku.edu.cn; Assistant teachers: School hours: 1-8 weeks in spring 2021, 2 hours per week, 16 hours Place of delivery: Introduction to the course: Education management is a more applied discipline in educational science and is important for improving educational management capacity and addressing problems that may arise in the management of education.
