Name: Reform and Practical Methods of Educational Evaluation
Introduction:
Educational measurement and evaluation are related to the direction of educational development. What kind of evaluation baton is there will be what kind of school-running orientation. In order to accelerate the modernization of education, build an educational power, and provide education that satisfies the people, in October 2020, the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council issued the "Overall Plan for Deepening the Reform of Education Evaluation in the New Era", which clearly proposed to improve the evaluation of primary and secondary schools, lead the professional development of teachers, improve the level of education and teaching, and create a harmonious education environment. What are educational measurement and educational evaluation? As educators and researchers, why do we need to study and research educational measurement and evaluation? What role does educational measurement and evaluation play in actual teaching work? What kind of educational measurement and evaluation is scientifically effective? How to improve? How do policy and scientific theories guide teaching practice? _x000D_
By trying to answer these questions, this course helps students understand the definition, functions, and basic theoretical models of educational measurement and evaluation, master the basic methods of analyzing and designing teaching evaluation and educational measurement, and become familiar with the scope and limitations of common evaluation methods. Be able to accurately understand my country’s existing educational evaluation, educational measurement methods, policies and reform directions, clarify the correlation and directionality between educational measurement and evaluation, educational teaching and educational management, and learn to apply measurement and evaluation methods in basic education teaching and school management. _x000D_
The teaching methods of this course are "question-based heuristic" and "inquiry-based teaching". Taking the problem as the guide, reading literature and research and discussion as the main method, and arranging a certain number of practical activities to help students master the thinking and theoretical framework and practical methods of analyzing real educational problems. _x000D_
This course is 1 credit, 8 teaching weeks. The assessment method is a mid-term paper and a final examination. The mid-term paper accounts for 30%, daily discussions account for 20%, and the final examination accounts for 50%.

Name: Designing Effective Instruction
Introduction:
Peking University senior or postgraduate teaching students whose subject knowledge has reached university graduation level are competent to teach high school courses in their majors. The teaching content of the volunteer teaching is determined (there are textbooks and teaching reference books), the test questions are basically determined (young teachers rarely create their own questions, they basically use or learn from them), and the teaching methods often adopt the practices of their own teachers. _x000D_
Challenges faced in supporting teaching: 1) High school students are under pressure to pass the college entrance examination. How to teach to improve students' academic performance? 2) How to correct students’ previous poor study habits? How to improve students' interest in learning? 3) What do some popular teaching reform terms, such as flipped classroom, cooperative learning, precision teaching, project learning, layered teaching, etc., mean? (This may be part of the education reform being carried out by the school)_x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching objectives_x000D_
At the end of the course, each student will be able to complete the following:_x000D_
1. Know how to design different teaching processes according to the type of knowledge to make subject knowledge easy to understand and ensure that learners are proficient in it. _x000D_
2. Understand the mechanism of various teaching strategies to promote learning and be able to use them appropriately to encourage students to develop a deep understanding of subject content and apply learned knowledge and skills in a meaningful way. _x000D_
3. It can effectively diagnose problems and their root causes in students' learning, build an inclusive learning environment, and allow each student to realize his or her potential. _x000D_
4. Ability to reflect on own teaching practice by applying reliable research methods, collecting teaching data and other evidence. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching Plan_x000D_
Four units, two lessons each. Use the method of connecting knowledge points and "situation description--guess--results revealed" to outline relevant teaching design knowledge. _x000D_
_x000D_
Unit 1 Psychological Foundations of Teaching and Learning_x000D_
Introduce behaviorism, cognitivism, constructivism, connectivism, and new behaviorism’s explanation of learning conditions, as well as examples of their application in teaching. For example, how behaviorism principles are used to reward and punish students’ behavior, how cognitivism learning principles help students remember, and why some students can solve the problems taught by the teacher but are unable to solve new problems, etc. _x000D_
Reference book_x000D_
Snowman, J., & McCown, R. (2011). Psychology applied to teaching. Nelson Education._x000D_
McDaniel, B. P. R. H., Brown, P. C., & Roediger III, H. L. (2014). Make it stick: The science of successful learning. Belknap Cambridge MA._x000D_
_x000D_
Unit 2 Overview of the Instructional Design Process_x000D_
Overview of the teaching design process, introduces how to write teaching objectives, how to use different teaching methods to teach facts, concepts, theorems, skills, and attitudes; how to design various examinations to test the achievement of teaching objectives based on the teaching objectives; how to reflect on the original teaching design based on student test data and use new teaching methods to revise it. _x000D_
Reference book_x000D_
Morrison, Gary R., et al. Designing effective instruction. John Wiley & Sons, 2019._x000D_
Bambrick-Santoyo, P. (2010). Driven by data: A practical guide to improve instruction. John Wiley & Sons._x000D_
_x000D_
Unit 3 Advanced Teaching Strategies_x000D_
What are the success mechanisms of various popular teaching methods? How to stimulate students' learning motivation? How to develop students' critical thinking? How to help students master knowledge from proficiency to proficiency? _x000D_
Reference book_x000D_
Ambrose, S. A., Bridges, M. W., DiPietro, M., Lovett, M. C., & Norman, M. K. (2010). How learning works: Seven research-based principles for smart teaching. John Wiley & Sons._x000D_
Dean, C. B., & Hubbell, E. R. (2012). Classroom instruction that works: Research-based strategies for increasing student achievement. ASCD._x000D_
_x000D_
Unit 4 Basic Teaching Methods_x000D_
How to give lectures most effectively? How to speak so students can learn? How do you ask students questions to learn better? _x000D_
Reference book_x000D_
Bligh, D. A. (1998). What's the Use of Lectures?. Intellect books._x000D_
Berger, W. (2014). A more beautiful question: The power of inquiry to spark breakthrough ideas. Bloomsbury Publishing USA._x000D_
Faber, A., & Mazlish, E. (2008). How to talk so kids can learn. Simon and Schuster._x000D_
_x000D_
Score Rating:_x000D_
10 minutes before the end of each class, test the content of the class (8*10 points) + the teaching design of one unit (20 points) _x000D_

Name: The Learning Sciences and the Future of Education
Introduction:
Learning Sciences is an interdisciplinary research field on teaching and learning developed internationally in the past thirty years, involving many disciplines such as education, brain science, cognitive science, and information science. R.K. Sawyer once pointed out, "The goal of learning science research is, firstly, to better understand cognitive and social processes to produce the most effective learning, and secondly, to use the knowledge of learning science to redesign our classrooms and other learning environments so that learners can learn more effectively and deeply." In short, learning science is mainly about research: "How do people learn, and how can we promote effective learning?" This course is mainly aimed at master's students at Peking University, hoping to give them a systematic understanding of the basic knowledge of learning science, which roughly includes: cognitive neuroscience, learning theory, learning technology and learning environment, learning analysis, teaching design based on learning science, etc. The specific arrangements are as follows:_x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 1 "The Origin and Development of Learning Science"_x000D_
Teach the ideological origin and development of learning science, including the three metaphors of learning science, the birth and development process of learning science, the core research content of learning science, the future development trend of learning science, etc. _x000D_
Requirements for this lecture: I hope students will have an overview of learning science. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 2 "Brain and Learning"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches the structure and function of the brain, brain mechanisms of basic cognition and advanced cognition, memory, retention and learning, etc. _x000D_
Requirements for this lecture: This lecture hopes that students will have a certain understanding of the structure and function of the brain, the main brain and cognitive outcomes, and be able to connect it with real classroom teaching. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 3 "Learning Psychology"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches the meaning and classification of learning, learning motivation, representation and organization of knowledge, the meaning and methods of problem solving, reasoning, decision-making, creativity, the difference between novices and experts, metacognition and cognitive strategies, etc. _x000D_
Requirements for this lecture: Students are expected to have a basic grasp of psychology and be able to master some of the most core concepts. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 4 "Learning Theory"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches basic learning theories such as behaviorism learning theory, cognitivism learning theory, constructivism learning theory, humanistic learning theory, and connectivism learning theory. _x000D_
This lecture requires students to master the most basic key points of learning theory. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 5 "Cognition and Learning Supported by Technology"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches the basic knowledge and basic theories of how technology promotes cognition and learning, including multimedia learning theory, cognitive load theory, embodied cognition theory, etc. _x000D_
This lecture requires students to understand how to promote cognition in a technological environment. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 6 "Learning Technology and Learning Environment"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches learning technologies and learning environments supported by new technologies, such as mobile learning, VR/AR, gamified learning, simulation, emulation, etc., and will analyze several classic cases. We will also teach about the currently popular learning space construction. _x000D_
This lecture hopes that students can understand how a new technology occurs, develops and dies in education. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 7 "Classroom Teaching Design Based on the Perspective of Learning Science"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches how to apply the knowledge and theories of learning science in classroom design, such as how to design exercises, how to ask questions, how to evaluate students, including how to apply various technologies in the classroom. _x000D_
This lecture hopes students to modify several teaching designs from the perspective of learning science. _x000D_
_x000D_
Lecture 8 "Learning Analysis and Learning Evaluation"_x000D_
This lecture mainly teaches how to analyze a large amount of learning behavior data based on artificial intelligence and big data technology to better evaluate and intervene in students' development. _x000D_
This lecture hopes that students can have an intuitive understanding of learning analysis and be able to apply some software for basic analysis. _x000D_
_x000D_

Introduce structure-development theory, self-direction theory and cases; help students understand the development stages and characteristics of self-realization, independent thinking and spiritual autonomy; understand the mutual influence between the environment and the self. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Educational Games
Introduction:
In recent years, the rapid development of online games has made educational games a new research hotspot in the field of technological research in education, while the rapid development of virtual reality technologies and the emergence of virtual societies have also given educational games (virtual learning) a vast and incalculable development perspective.
In order to help students learn about the development of educational games, master the design strategies of educational games and familiarize themselves with the study methods of educational games, the Northern University of Education and Technology has been running the subject of educational games since 2007.
The course will begin with a discussion of the current dynamic of online games, beginning with a discussion of the relationship between play and education from a traditional perspective, followed by a discussion of the theoretical and technical foundations of the development of educational games, a discussion of why people are so fond of games, and a systematic review of human research on the motivational theory of participation in games; a further examination of the value of the educational applications of games, the current state of development and the difficulties and obstacles they face, followed by a discussion of the design and development strategies of small educational games and situational education games, respectively, as well as the role of teachers in educational games; and a subsequent analysis of several educational game studies in turn, with a final look at the development prospects of virtual reality technologies and educational games.
Since there is no authoritative reference to the curriculum available for the course, the above may be adapted in the course of the course in the light of the latest developments in the study of educational games.

Name: Grassroots Governance
Introduction:
In order to further implement the fundamental mission of "cultivating people with moral integrity" and carry forward Peking University's family and country sentiments of "serving the west and contributing to the grassroots", the Graduate School has joined forces with the Department of Academic Affairs, the Student Employment Guidance Service Center, the Student Affairs Department, the School Youth League Committee, the Party Committee Organization Department and other departments to organize and implement the "Grassroots Governance" certificate project. It is hoped that the training of this project will further guide students in our school to pay attention to the grassroots, study the grassroots, and study the grassroots. In the future, more graduates will devote themselves to the grassroots, build the grassroots, and serve the grassroots. _x000D_
The teaching links of this project include basic courses, expert lectures, seminars and exchanges, inspections and surveys, and summer practice. It offers basic modules on grassroots public governance, social survey theories and methods, rural development and governance, grassroots party building and political power building, leadership and team building, innovation, entrepreneurship, and career development. Some experts from local government departments and alumni who have gone to the west and grassroots employment and entrepreneurship will be invited to give special reports or experience exchanges. Weekends and summer vacations will be used to participate in grassroots social practice and conduct research work under the guidance of teachers in relevant subject areas. _x000D_
Students who complete each link and pass the assessment will be issued a certificate project completion certificate, and will receive 2 credits and be recorded on their transcript.

Name: Quantitative Investment Strategies

These applications are mainly reflected in: 1) How investors make use of existing market anomalies to invest and adopt various investment Alpha and Beta strategies, such as Small vs Big, Value vs Growth, Price Momentum and Earnings Momentum. 2) How legal persons carry out trading portfolio management and high-frequency trading, including the measurement of transaction costs, and how to use trading strategies to reduce price impacts during transactions. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Frontier Issues of the Media
Introduction: This course is based on the hot spots and focus issues at the forefront of current media communication. The Internet era has brought about many new issues for mass communication, new changes, such as media integration, media transformation and innovation dissemination. The course will be based on communication science as a fundamental theory, looking at the theory and practice of disseminating business practices from a multi-dimensional interdisciplinary perspective and recognizing the growing and cross-border trends of communication. The theoretical basis of professional research is taught, the methods of research are developed and the academic research capacity of students to capture and analyse cutting-edge issues is developed.

Name: Research Methods in Communication
Introduction: Communication Research Methods is designed to provide students with a brief introduction to general methods of communication and social science research. It involves the basic concepts and nature of scientific research; the history of the development of communication research methods; important concepts related to research methods, and introduces several basic methods of communication research. Through the study of this course, students will understand and basically master how to design a research plan, conduct literature search and organization, collect information and data, and write a research report or paper on this basis.

Name: Studies in Communication Theory
Introduction: This course is mandatory for graduate students at the Institute of Journalism and Communication and is the first station in the theory of contact with communication systems. Communication is a discipline in the emerging social sciences of the mid-twentieth century and is characterized by a wealth of content, a multiplicity of theoretical sources and a strong interdisciplinary nature. The emergence of communication science provides a new perspective for interpreting social phenomena in new social conditions beyond the boundaries of traditional social sciences, rather than dividing new areas of social research. Therefore, the construction of communication theory has been a dynamic, multifaceted process to date. The parties have focused on the theoretical or research areas, and sometimes it is difficult to find intersections. The focus of the course is on the transformation of social institutions, economies and cultures that focus on the modern media and the development of modern media in their broader context, tracing the development of modern social theories and their interlinkages. It is important to provide new graduate students with a clear but open communications concept and a social focus. In this course, students should not only have an initial understanding of the core content of the important theory of communication, but also historical and critical perspectives and consciousness, attention to the dialogue and controversy between the various theories and their relationship to the historical conditions of society that they each produce. The main objectives of the course are the following: first, to give students a preliminary view of the important theoretical orientation of communication science, the setting of topics, the debate of views and their place in the history of communication science. Second, students are introduced to the basic themes of social theory, theoretical vocabulary, thinking methods and academic approaches for future theoretical research and dialogue. Third, students are given initial access to literature in a number of fields of communication and their historical status and theoretical contributions. Fourth, to help students enter the discourse of issues and arguments that will be involved in theoretical research and social life. Fifth, preliminary exploration of the introduction of communication theory, absorption and innovation in China.

Name: Studies in International Journalism and Communication
Introduction:
To provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the historical processes of international communication (as a practice and as a discipline) that arise, develop and evolve. In the logical order of subjects, means, audiences, effects, etc. of international communications, the case-by-case analysis is used to summarize the internal patterns and special requirements of international communications. It focuses on China ' s international dissemination practices and analyses, discusses and researches specific cases in order to guide students from the point of view and from the point of view of the phenomenon, so that they have a clear understanding of China ' s position in international communication, its role and future development.

Name: Media Operations and Management
