Introduction:
Through course learning, students are able to improve their practical abilities based on systematic knowledge of advertising theory and through case studies.
Students are required to have training in the dissemination of theory and methodology in science and basic knowledge of advertising and marketing.

Name: Independent Research in the Major
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to guide students to conduct practical research based on their different characteristics and specific projects, so that students can master the basic methods of communication research and improve their scientific research capabilities.

Name: Journalism and Communication Policy, Law and Ethics
Introduction:
Purpose of the course: Master's students majoring in journalism and communication should understand and even be familiar with the party and government's basic policies on media activities and media work, as well as the government's laws and regulations regulating the relationship between all aspects of media activities. This is the basis for cultivating a healthy professional awareness and mastering basic professional skills. For this reason, this compulsory course is specially designed for training. _x000D_
Basics for starting the course: Students are required to have studied the course "Media Ethics and Laws and Regulations" at the undergraduate level. _x000D_
Teaching requirements: During the learning process, pay attention to knowledge such as introduction to law. _x000D_

Name: Discourse Analysis of Communication
Introduction:
The most important feature of contemporary social practice and life practice is the prevalence of discourse practice. The production and negotiation of all meanings and the struggle for power all use "discourse", especially the "discourse" produced day and night by the mass media, as a weapon. Modern media has shown unprecedented power to express and construct reality. The content produced by the media becomes an absolutely powerful narrative and discourse. News, advertising, online blogs, etc., have all become a form of public discourse. The production and interpretation mechanisms of these discourses and their relationship with society have become very complex, and the struggle for meaning has become fierce. Almost all social actors, from political parties to heads of state to social public organizations and individuals, and even terrorists, have realized the prerequisite of discourse strategies for them to obtain practical benefits. Whether it is the self-use of discourse or the resolution of other parties' discourse, it has become an extremely conscious behavior. _x000D_
    In the face of the overwhelming "discourse communication", the central issue of "discourse analysis" is to unearth the hidden meanings and production and circulation mechanisms behind various popular discourses, and to place these discourses in the context of their production to gain insight into the secrets of power and discourse strategies implicit in them, in order to strive for more discourse and communication power, as well as the closely related freedom of movement.

Name: Journalism Case Studies
Introduction:
Based on the teaching purposes and characteristics of MJC, and adhering to the teaching purpose of combining theory and practice, this course chooses _x000D_
There are about 8-10 classic cases of contemporary journalism practice and development. The content basically covers all major aspects of journalism. In addition to in-depth analysis, research and discussion in class, appropriate extracurricular studies and field visits are also arranged, with a view to deepening students' theoretical foundation and greatly improving their practical abilities and skills. Course hosting and basic content teaching are undertaken by teachers in the school. In addition, most of the case studies are conducted by senior and accomplished professionals in the contemporary journalism industry. _x000D_

Name: Globalization and Communication
Introduction: Due to the deepening of globalization in recent years, almost all-round dramatic changes have been brought to our world. Therefore, this course will discuss globalization and the relationship between globalization and communication from an interdisciplinary perspective. This course consists of two parts. The first part analyzes the causes of globalization from the aspects of society, politics, economy, culture and communication. The second part comprehensively discusses the impact of globalization from the perspectives of political economy, sociology, and communication. Topics covered include: the theoretical basis of globalization, the evolution of companies and globalization, the evolution of capitalist society and globalization, the evolution of consumer culture in capitalist society, the role of media and globalization, capitalist alliances and the home and host countries of multinational corporations, globalization and the state, globalization and global cities, globalization and communication, etc.

Name: Studies in Chinese Society and Culture
Introduction:
The reasons why my country's economy and society have developed rapidly over the past 30 years of reform and opening up, as well as the difficulties and challenges it faces, all have a distinct brand of "Chinese characteristics." It is precisely because we persist in following our own development path that we have been able to avoid all kinds of interference at home and abroad and achieve great and remarkable achievements. So, what are “Chinese characteristics”? How to understand “Chinese characteristics”? From the perspective of cultural stratification theory, the country, as a survival system shared by groups, its economy, systems, and people's behaviors, etc., all belong to the category of explicit culture; and what has a long-term impact and restriction on this are implicit cultural connotations such as values, ways of thinking, religious beliefs, and aesthetic concepts. And any cultural system has the characteristics of history, continuity, universality and difference. Especially for a country like China with thousands of years of civilization, the "Chinese characteristics" present in many contemporary economic, social, political, and conceptual fields actually contain inevitable factors of history and culture. Therefore, starting from some eye-catching phenomena and issues in contemporary Chinese society, conducting in-depth cultural research and discussion is an indispensable perspective for understanding contemporary China and "Chinese characteristics." _x000D_
In summary, the theoretical value and practical significance of this lesson mainly include:_x000D_
1．	For the "seeking truth from facts" and "construction tools" that our party has proposed and adhered to since the reform and opening up,
"Socialism with Chinese Characteristics", "Scientific Outlook on Development" and a series of correct and effective political and theoretical lines are an argument from the perspective of national conditions and culture; _x000D_
2.	For graduate students in the School of Journalism and Communication, hope motivates them to build on their understanding of _x000D_
Understand China's national conditions and historical and cultural origins to comprehensively and deeply understand the many phenomena and problems of China's contemporary development, so that when engaging in news communication activities in the future, we can provide correct and effective guidance to the broad audience, so that our media can better play its due role in the overall development of China's economy and society. And based on this, we can combine criticism with "Chinese characteristics" and learn from foreign achievements, and then explore a news communication development path that suits China's needs. _x000D_
3.	The deep theoretical significance implicit in this study is from dialectical materialism and history_x000D_
From a materialist perspective, it supports the idea that multiple cultures should coexist and follow multiple development paths in today's world. _x000D_
To sum up, this course belongs to the intersection of national conditions research and cultural studies, and national conditions research is a focus that our party has paid considerable attention to in the field of theoretical propaganda and news communication in recent years. Therefore, this course has a certain cutting-edge nature, and it is also a gap in the college's discipline construction and graduate course teaching. And as far as I know, even within Peking University, there is currently no similar course. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Information Society
Introduction:
This course is a discussion of issues related to "information, technology, and society" in communication and media studies. The course requires students to theoretically understand the information society and think about the historical mutual construction relationship between technology and social, political, economic, and cultural forces. Students need to read literature, participate in discussions, and apply the theoretical tools learned in the course to conduct targeted and critical understanding and analysis of the current political and economic processes and cultural phenomena of information communication technology applications in daily life and related industries. _x000D_
_x000D_
Assessment method: _x000D_
Midterm book review. _x000D_
The final thesis is to apply the theories learned in the course to design a specific research plan related to the problem awareness of the information society, conduct a literature review in related fields, collect research materials, and obtain preliminary analysis and discussion.

Name: Methodology in Journalism and Journalism History Research
Introduction: This course focuses on many of the issues facing researchers in contemporary journalism and journalism history. The content includes reading, topic selection, collection of research materials, screening and sorting of historical materials, historical facts and historical perspectives, elaboration and development methods of arguments and arguments, etc., to improve students' interest in research in related fields and achieve the effect of teacher-student interaction. This course uses examples of essay writing as possible to illustrate the course, and encourages course candidates to actively participate in class discussions.

Name: New Media Studies
Introduction:
This course aims to conduct a comprehensive and in-depth observation of new media, with a view to analyzing what opportunities it creates for journalists and media operators, and what threats it poses. This course will analyze the operation and business aspects of new media at the same time, and sort out the key and strategic issues faced by new media. _x000D_
The Internet and related communications and network technology revolutions are driving media organizations to redefine their relationship with their audiences. To this end, this course will examine whether traditional economic principles and business strategies can still be applied in the network economy and online publishing, while refining the new rules generated by global digital networks. This course will also examine whether traditional journalism principles still apply, how the Internet has changed the way news and information are organized and expressed, and how online media builds brands and protects their credibility. _x000D_
At the end of this course, we will explore the theoretical basis for understanding the construction, consumption and consequences of new media, examine new media within the social ecosystem, analyze the interaction between digital technology and society, and clarify the relationship between technology and economy, culture and politics. _x000D_
The subject of this course, new media itself, is highly interactive. Therefore, the teaching will place great emphasis on the interactive design of the entire course. Students will be divided into different groups to analyze the differences between old and new media, the different types of online media companies, the changes in new media business models, the social impacts of media changes, etc.; then, teachers and students will discuss a series of issues faced by new media. _x000D_
This course will strive to achieve: theoretical foundations, real-life cases, and practical techniques of online media are carried out in the classroom at the same time. Students will learn three things from this course: what perspective to use to observe new media; how to grasp the latest development of new media; and what impact new media has on society. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Western Social Thought
Introduction:
This course uses a series of lectures to run through the brief history of changes in Western social thought, using core figures and schools as clues to provide a schematic introduction to the main social thoughts from Western classical to postmodern. There are two main teaching purposes:_x000D_
_x000D_
1. Improve students’ understanding of the ideological context of Western society_x000D_
2. Help students connect various schools of modern communication thought with historical clues of social thought_x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching method: Lecture_x000D_
Assessment: 1. Class participation and feedback; 2. Final paper

Name: Theory and Practice of Cultural Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Name: New Media Studies
Introduction: The purpose of the course is to enable students to understand the development trend of new media, its position in the media industry, and its impact on the media industry; to master the basic theories and laws of new media and network communication, to understand the characteristics of audience behavior, cultural phenomena, and social structures in the new media environment, and to be able to use communication, sociology, and The theories and methods of management and other disciplines can solve the practical problems of media development and information dissemination in the new media environment; understand news gathering, writing, editing, construction and operation of new media communication platforms, laws and regulations on network information dissemination in the new media environment, and have certain theoretical knowledge and practical ability.

Name: Film, Television and Cultural Studies
Introduction:
This course comprehensively and systematically teaches the theories and methods of film and television cultural research, presents the dialogue and mutual influence between film and television studies and cultural studies, displays different cultural theoretical contexts and practical methods, improves students' reading ability of theoretical documents, and masters the use of film and television cultural theories to interpret and analyze film and television texts. _x000D_
Course outline: Lecture 1 Introduction to Film, Television and Cultural Studies; Lecture 2 Classical Film Theory; Lecture 3 Structuralism, Semiotics and Narrative Criticism; Lecture 4 Frankfurt School and Cultural Industry Research; Lecture 5 Marxism and Ideological Criticism; Lecture 6 Psychoanalysis and Popular Culture; Lecture 7 Feminism and Gender Studies; Lecture 8 Discourse Analysis and Power Research; Lecture 9 Film and Television Culture and the Birmingham School; Lecture 10 Film and Television Culture and the Political Economy of Communication; Lecture 11. Film and television culture and audience research; Lecture 12, Film and television culture and industry research; Lecture 13, Film and television culture and modern experience; Lecture 14, Film and television culture and media research; Lecture 15, Film and television culture and new media; Lecture 16, Film and television culture and the digital turn.

Name: Introduction to Classic Studies in Advertising Research
Introduction: This course mainly introduces and organizes students to read and discuss classic literature in the field of advertising research, as well as recently published relevant works that have a wide impact or inspiration in academia or industry (including theoretical research and industry analysis, reports, etc.). The main purpose of the course is to strengthen students' professional literature foundation and theoretical literacy through reading and discussion. The course seminars have obvious characteristics and require small class teaching conditions (such as small classrooms, etc.).

Name: Transmedia Narrative and Communication
Introduction: High-tech developments such as AI, big data, and so forth, have brought about an all-inclusive dissemination dynamic that constantly generates and diminishes the meaning itself in cross-media narratives, while highlighting the power games behind the various media. If we are to answer questions about where the development of technology, such as AI, big data and so forth, we should go back to re-collating and understanding the media, narratives, narratives of the media, narratives of the media, narratives of the cross-media, social structures, etc., in social relations, the deconstruction and restructuring of social structures, which requires attention to the impact of cross-media narratives on self-dissemination, cognitive revolutions, social patterns, etc., in teaching and scientific research, and responding to the transformation of communication sciences and their adaptation to the integration of science and humanities. I have been offering courses on " Media and Society " , " Media and Social Change " to Ph.D. students and undergraduate students, with a wealth of theoretical and practical foundations. The pedagogical approach is based on theoretical teaching, supported by classroom discussions and case analysis; and the assessment approach, combining the regular appraisal with the final course paper.

Name: Radio and Television Case Studies
Introduction:
Through case analysis, masters have been given an accurate understanding of the nature of television broadcasting and the specificity of the audio-visual language, its disadvantages and advantages vis-à-vis the press, radio and electronic networks, as well as the characteristics of the various types of television programmes and their respective origins and historical causes of infiltration.
This course, which has been taught in eight of the six academic years at the North Bank HQ and Shenzhen Graduate School, is popular and has a long history of teaching, which has gradually resulted in improved teaching, PPT and related video materials.

Name: Theoretical Foundations of Journalism and Communication
Introduction: This course is a compulsory course for the professional master's degree in the School of Journalism and Communication. It is the first stop for graduate students to gain exposure to the systematic theory of journalism and communication. Communication studies is an emerging social science discipline in the mid-twentieth century. It is characterized by rich content, complex theoretical sources, and strong interdisciplinary nature. The emergence of communication studies does not so much divide a new field of social research as it provides a new perspective to explain social phenomena beyond the boundaries of traditional social sciences under new social conditions. Therefore, communication theory construction is a dynamic and diverse process. Each theory or research field has its own emphasis, and sometimes it is even difficult to find intersections. The focus of this course is to focus on modern media and the changes in social institutions, economy, and culture with the development of modern media as the background, and trace the history and development of communication theories as well as their interrelationships. Its importance lies in providing new graduate students with a clear-cut but open-boundary concept of communication and a perspective that focuses on social issues. In this course, students should not only have a preliminary understanding of the core content of important communication theories, but also have a historical and critical vision and awareness, pay attention to the dialogue and debate between various theories, and their relationship with the social and historical conditions in which they emerged. The main purposes of the course are as follows: First, to enable students to have a preliminary understanding of the important theoretical orientations, topic settings, viewpoint debates, and their positions in the history of communication studies. Second, introduce some basic propositions, theoretical vocabulary, thinking methods and academic methods of social theory to students to facilitate future theoretical research and dialogue. Third, it enables students to have initial exposure to some literature in the field of communication and understand their historical status and theoretical contributions. Fourth, help students enter the discourse environment of issues and debates involved in theoretical research and social life. Fifth, a preliminary discussion is given on the introduction, absorption and innovation of communication theory in China.

Name: Research Methods in Journalism and Communication
Introduction: Journalism and Communication Research Methods is a core compulsory course for the Master of Journalism and Communication (MJC). It focuses on introducing the concepts of basic journalism and communication research methods (including quantitative and qualitative methods), research hypotheses, research design, as well as research data collection, analysis, and research report writing. Teaching method: lecture + case teaching. By the end of this course, students should be able to establish an objective attitude and empirical spirit in news communication research, be able to flexibly use various research methods and techniques, independently propose research questions and hypotheses, design research frameworks, collect data, interpret and reason based on data analysis, and write research reports. Through these skills, we hope to effectively improve the scientific nature and professionalism of our work in the journalism practice process (such as understanding the communication process, testing the credibility of news materials, etc.) or in the academic research of news communication.

Name: Case Studies in Health Communication
Introduction: This course is aimed primarily at graduate students specializing in health communication, using the teaching and research of health communication cases, and is centred on the frontier development of health transmission, theoretical exploration, and research paradigms. It addresses the threshold of increased attention to health transmission in China. It explores the front-line topics of health communication in research and practice at the interpersonal, organizational, mass communication, and new media technologies.

Name: Professional Internship
Introduction: To cultivate applied high-level professionals with both ability and political integrity for socialist journalism and communication with Chinese characteristics. The master's degree in journalism and communication will carry out a large number of professional internships while theoretically cultivating, so as to further master the basic principles of news communication in practice, and have the professional qualities, skills and methods required to engage in news communication practice; in practice, students will cultivate good political and ideological qualities and professional ethics, have modern news communication concepts and international vision, and have an in-depth understanding of China's basic national conditions. Cultivate students into high-level, applied news communication professionals who are proficient in news communication skills and methods.

Name: Introduction to Medicine
Introduction:
The Medical Review, which is an entry point for common, multiple and serious diseases, introduces the basic pathology of diseases and their main mechanisms into clinical cases, while familiarizing students with the basic structure and physiological functions of the human body, a certain level of basic medical knowledge, and an understanding of the human, legal, group and national health development strategies related to the disease. A total of 16 courses of three hours each on 16 topics, of which two are taught in theoretical subjects and one is discussed. The course records achievements, which are evaluated in the form of regular performance and final papers. Of these, regular results are random class assessments (50 per cent) and final papers, after the end of the course, select any of the 16 topics of interest to submit a paper of no less than 3,000 words, with experience, feelings and suggestions for the course (50 per cent).
The curriculum teacher team, which is dominated by the College of Basic Medicine, has been widely appreciated in the relevant fields of teaching by the under-secretaries and senior teaching cadres of the Faculty, as well as by the participation of senior medical and clinical hospital specialists in an interdisciplinary and basic clinically integrated teaching team.

Name: Topics on the National Conditions of China
Introduction: National conditions education is a basic method for imparting basic knowledge of national conditions and understanding of national conditions to help students form a correct view of national conditions. The national conditions education curriculum design includes four major units: Chinese society, Chinese culture, China and the world, and Chinese reform, involving basic content such as population, agriculture, rural areas, and farmers, resources and environment, social security, and innovation capabilities. China is a developing country, a backward country in the process of modernization, and its national conditions are very special. National conditions education requires students to understand the long history and profoundness of Chinese culture through courses, experience the greatness and difficulty of the construction of the motherland, and feel the glory and pride of being Chinese. In the teaching process, we adhere to the principle of seeking truth from facts and cultivate students' ability to analyze problems objectively and dialectically by integrating theory with practice.

Name: Case Studies in New Media Innovation and Entrepreneurship
Introduction: "Internet Innovation and Entrepreneurship" is an important course that is practical and comprehensive. It mainly introduces how to use the Internet for innovation and entrepreneurship under the conditions of diversified and comprehensive development of informatization. How to prepare for starting a business, analyze conditions, start a business plan, find business financing, business opportunities, and the management and development of new ventures, etc. Through comprehensive methods such as teacher lectures, expert lectures, and research visits, the course enables students to master and understand the basic theories and basic knowledge of Internet innovation and entrepreneurship, enhance students' practical abilities, and enhance students' competitiveness in all aspects of future career selection, employment, and entrepreneurship.

Name: Selected Readings in Western Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This undergraduate course is a required course for graduate students majoring in literature and art. The course preparation focuses on the focus issues of Western literary theory and selects representative literary theory texts. Students who choose the course are required to participate in class discussions on the basis of careful study. The selected questions can be the same or changed each time the class starts. The purpose is to provide students with basic training in literary theory reading ability and theoretical thinking ability.

Name: Selected Basic Readings in the Aesthetics of Literature and Art
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Literary aesthetics is a new achievement of the discipline expansion of contemporary Chinese literature and art. It is closely integrated with reality and pays attention to interdisciplinarity in disciplinary positioning. Literary aesthetics is the product of reality and history, and has a long tradition of academic thought. Selected readings of basic literature on literary and artistic aesthetics is a professional skills course. It basically has two meanings: basic and important, so this course takes into account both knowledge and thought. This course emphasizes revisiting classics and integrating new knowledge, combining ideological context, text reading and meaning interpretation. It not only focuses on the in-depth understanding of Chinese and Western traditional literary and aesthetic classics, but also focuses on the ideological review of important documents on modern literary and aesthetics. Through the study of basic literature on literary and aesthetics, it improves the literature interpretation and critical reading abilities of graduate students majoring in literary and artistic aesthetics. This course is based on the tradition of academic history, and uses important basic documents from ancient and modern times, both at home and abroad, to deeply understand the historical context, problem awareness, and cultural spirit of literary and artistic aesthetics through careful reading, interpretation, discussion, etc., in order to develop students' good critical thinking and perception abilities, and also have a better promotion effect on students majoring in other literature and art.

Name: Academic Standards and Research Methods
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Through this curriculum, students are trained in academic ethics so that they can both adhere to academic norms and maintain a sense of innovation and breakthrough in their future research work.

Name: Introduction to Classical Western Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a supporting course for "20th Century Western Literary Theory". It focuses on the selection of 26 English-translated classic works by 14 representative writers from ancient Greece, Rome and the Middle Ages (5th century BC to 14th century BC). The content involves ancient Western poetics, rhetoric and hermeneutics. It explains key concepts while sorting out their origins and changes, so that students can have a preliminary understanding of ancient Western literary theory and prepare the foundation for further study of modern literary theory.

Name: Studies in Artistic Discourse
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Discourse theory is the most powerful academic thought since the late 20th century, and has profoundly and extensively affected the basic research landscape of the humanities. In this context, artistic discourse emerged. The core of artistic discourse is narrative (expression), which means that art is no longer a simple reflection activity, but a humanistic discourse-narrative construction process that includes value, spirit, and culture. This course takes discourse theory and narrative practice as the main line, sorting out the history of art discourse thought, and successively analyzes the basic connotation of art discourse, discourse ontology, value inquiry and art humanities, art narrative and art theory narrative, canonical narrative of art theory, art history narrative model and Chinese modernity, and art history diversity. Narrative and Western modernity, artistic stance and humanistic value, artistic identity and spiritual redemption, cultural identity and re-Chineseization, artistic discourse power and international status, spiritual capital and core competitiveness, contemporary value of Chinese artistic spirit, modernity dilemma and spiritual narrative, symbol system and global consensus, etc. A series of issues.

Name: Studies in the Works of Foucault
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Based on the selected works of French philosopher and intellectual history scholar Michel Foucault, we conduct in-depth reading and classroom discussion of Foucault's representative works to train graduate students' theoretical interpretation and thinking abilities.

Name: Topics in Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Special course on literary theory, the theme of discussion is aesthetic modernity and cultural community. _x000D_
The process of modernity itself is extremely dialectical. On the one hand, it aims to empower independent subjects, and on the other hand, it must prevent subjects from entering a state of complete disorder and atomization. Therefore, relying on categories such as common sense or sympathy, it attempts to construct a unity based on individual opposition for all subjects, that is, a sense of community. Since the publication of Schiller's Letters on Aesthetic Education and Kant's Critique of Judgment, aesthetics has been discussed as an important foundation for the modern cultural community. Since the discussion of the relationship between aesthetic modernity and cultural community often involves many core propositions in modernity theory such as body consciousness, political order, ethical consensus, literary value, etc., it is particularly important for the Chinese theoretical field where class consciousness has withdrawn since entering the new era and a new community consciousness is still being constructed. Understanding the relationship between aesthetic modernity and cultural community will definitely be beneficial to the contemporary construction of Chinese literary theory and literary creation.

Name: Aesthetics of Literature and Art
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course analyzes the aesthetic spirit of Chinese and Western modern literature and art from a new perspective, and examines the aesthetic core of various new artistic trends from a new aesthetic perspective. Paying attention to the spiritual heritage and resources of Chinese aesthetics, re-elaborating the concept groups such as "experience" and "artistic conception" of traditional Chinese art theory as the core, committed to integrating traditional Chinese literary aesthetic thoughts and modern Western literary aesthetics, focusing on elucidating and emphasizing the original significance of the unity of man and the world in literary and artistic activities, and the basic value of aesthetic experience in opening up individual living space and coordinating the relationship between individual and society, and man and the world. This makes the inheritance and rupture between the aesthetic categories of Chinese traditional literary and artistic aesthetics and the aesthetic categories of modern literary and artistic aesthetics come to the fore.

Name: Studies in The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: "Wen Xin Diao Long" is a work on writing style written by Liu Xie during the Qi and Liang Dynasties in the Southern Dynasties. Qing Dynasty scholar Zhang Xuecheng called it "big in style but considers Zhou". Modern scholars generally regard it as a classic of Chinese literary theory, comparable to Aristotle's "Poetics" in the West. This course is based on the academic background of the history of Chinese literary theory and criticism, and is connected with the actual literary creation in ancient and medieval times. It selects some important chapters of the book to guide students to accurately understand Liu Xie's literary theory thoughts and viewpoints, and make appropriate interpretations and evaluations. It guides students to deeply understand the development of ancient and medieval literature in connection with "The Literary Mind and the Carving of Dragons", cultivates students' thinking in Chinese literary theory, and guides students to think about the modern value of traditional literary theory. This course is suitable for master's and doctoral students majoring in literature and art and ancient Chinese literature.

Name: Topics in Modern Western Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course plans to select about 30 important monographs on the issue of "modernity", mainly focusing on central topics such as "the occurrence of modernity", "the concept of modernity" and "modernity and modern culture". It will conduct careful reading and lessons on these papers that have had a major impact on Western intellectual circles. Class discussions are held in order to enable students to have a preliminary understanding of the rich connotations of the concept of "modernity" in the original Western context and a series of concepts and issues involved, and to provide practical and concise guidance and signposts for further in-depth exploration of the "modernity" issue field and understanding of the modern society in which we live.

Name: History of the Development of Marxist Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The course is aimed primarily at graduate students in arts and arts. It focuses on the formation and development of the “Western Marxism” literature, analyses the nature, characteristics and methods of the “Western Marxism” literature, and provides insight into the artistic thinking and logic of Lucage, Gracie, Brecht, Adono, Habemas, Markuse, Lefever, Sart, Aldusse, Marshall, Goldman, Williams, Eagleton, Jameson and others.
Lectures were combined with discussions, within 20 persons.
Students are required to read the scriptures, to think about the methodological meaning of the ideologue, and to link theoretical learning with thinking about reality.

Name: Introduction to Hegel's Aesthetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course intends to read Hegel's "Aesthetics" (volumes 1-3) chapter by volume and conduct classroom discussions as much as possible, so that students can gain a deep understanding of Hegel's profound aesthetic thoughts and acquire the basic academic ability to analyze and think about literary theory and aesthetics. At the same time, it will lay the necessary solid foundation for expanding the understanding of the entire Western literary theory and aesthetic history and promoting the research of related important issues.

Name: Studies in Chinese Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is offered to graduate students (including senior undergraduates) in the Chinese Department of Literature and Art and related majors. It is a required course for graduate students in Literature and Art. _x000D_
  This course grasps Chinese literary theory from a macro and overall perspective, presents many issues inherent in Chinese literary theory in the form of a special topic, conducts comparative discussions and research, guides students to read classics, and establishes a consistent academic connection between classics and classics in ancient and modern times, cultivating the literary theory thinking of Tao Yi, Zhong Zhong, and the end. _x000D_
  The topics taught in this course include literature and literary theory, text language and literary theory, various meanings related to literary context (body, style, artistic conception, typical), review of the concept of "literary", literature and regional family dialects and eras, literary theory and academics, literary theory and translation, temperament theory and Chinese literary theory, literary narrative and Chinese culture Chinese literary theory, the lyrical tradition (emotional ontology) of Chinese literature, the subjectivity of Chinese literary theory, reception aesthetics of Chinese literary theory, hermeneutic tradition, "literary as teaching" and "entrepreneurship as a link", examples of Chinese literary theory research paradigms in the 20th century, and related research on Chinese literary theory and other categories of literature and art, etc. _x000D_
  This course is of a general nature, connecting ancient and modern times, and evaluating the relationship between literary theory and other academic issues. On the one hand, it is inherent in Chinese literary theory itself; on the other hand, it takes the perspective of larger literary theory. Explore the propositions that great literary thinkers in history have faced, the spiritual wisdom in solving problems, continue the spirit of literary theory, and pay attention to the present, and try to make new explorations and developments in literary theory research paradigms and results based on "ancient and modern, new and old".

Name: History of the Development of Marxist Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is mainly for graduate students majoring in literature and art, focusing on examining and sorting out the formation and development of "Western Marxist" literary theory, analyzing and studying the nature, characteristics, and methods of "Western Marxist literary theory, and through careful reading of the text of "Western Marxist" literary theory, in-depth understanding of Understand the literary and artistic thoughts and their internal logical relationships of Lukács, Gramsci, Brecht, Benjamin, Adorno, Habermas, Marcuse, Lefebvre, Sartre, Althusser, Macherey, Goldman, Williams, Eagleton, Jameson and others _x000D_
Combination of lectures and discussions, no more than 20 people. _x000D_
Students are required to read the original texts intensively, think about the methodological significance of the theorists' thoughts, and organically connect theoretical learning with thinking about practical issues.

Name: Academic Writing and Standards: The Case of Language and Human Complex Systems Research
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Academic writing and norms are not acquired in the abstract, but are traveled in specific research practices, and as the new age's methods of transmission of information develop rapidly and the boundaries between disciplines continue to break, how good academic writing habits and norms can be built into language research are important for the research of language scholars. Through the training of this course, we hope that students will both respect and absorb the research of others in their academic writings and clearly demonstrate their academic contributions. The course is written on the front-line topic of “Language and complex human systems research”. In introducing and understanding relevant research, the classical research of front-enders regulates our own research and writing. Words allow us to think beyond the limits of space and time, to imagine the possibilities and the impossible, and to constantly create a new and changing world for our brains. It is therefore necessary to study the complex relationships of linguistic, brain, cultural interaction, based on which the human nature is understood. Much progress has been made in this area at the beginning of the twentieth century. Since the end of the twentieth century, as a result of the breakthroughs in cognitive neuroscience, there have also been teams that have used different neuroimaging methods to study how culture affects brain growth, how the brain shows the functioning of the expression language, how language reflects the structure of culture, etc. The languages and cultures of dozens of peoples in China have very important characteristics and are rich in academic values. The objective of the study on this topic is to combine field work and brain experiments to study human nature in the field. The results of the study will give us a deeper understanding of the biological basis of language, help us understand language acquisition and learning, and further assist in the treatment of such disorders as loss of speech, loss of reading and degradation of older languages. In the context of specific cases of linguistic and human complex systems research, the course seeks to demonstrate how to write an academic overview, lay the context in the precept, structure the theoretical framework and concretize it in the context of actual phenomena, strengthen the logic and norms of academic writing through selected cases, and finally rationalize the expansion of the theory and draw appropriate conclusions.

Name: Topics in Discourse Functional Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Discourse functional linguistics has been one of the main academic schools in the field of linguistic research for half a century. _x000D_
The course will systematically introduce the theory, methods, main contributions and main achievements of discourse functional linguistics in Chinese studies. _x000D_
Students need to have a basic knowledge of general linguistics, Chinese grammar, and Chinese history courses, and be able to read English literature. _x000D_
The assessment is conducted in the form of short essays in the course. _x000D_

Name: Pragmatics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Based on the background of contemporary functionalist linguistics, it is connected with human speech communication behavior, systematically introduces the theories and methods of Western pragmatics, and combines the principles of general pragmatics with Chinese research and the relationship between pragmatics and Chinese structure. The research is divided into two major aspects. One is general pragmatics, which studies the general principles that govern the role of language communication. The main contents include the following seven aspects: 1. Pragmatics and linguistics; 2. Context: 3. Demonstrative words: 4. Conversational meaning: 5. Presupposition: 6. Speech act; 7. Conversation structure. The second is Chinese pragmatics, which uses Chinese as the material to study the relationship between human pragmatic abilities and core language knowledge. Study the structural laws of Chinese from the perspective of Chinese language use, especially the choices made by Chinese users, the constraints they receive in Chinese social interaction, and the impact of language use on other participants in letter delivery activities.

Name: Topics in Chinese Semantics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is an improvement course in semantic theory. Connect the history and current situation of Chinese semantic research, and describe the important theories and cutting-edge research methods of modern and contemporary semantics. Explore ways to combine Chinese and Western semantic research, focusing on the discussion of the relationship between semantics and Chinese structure, especially the study of the relationship between semantics and syntax. Based on this, we can summarize the general rules of semantic encoding, semantic combination rules and semantic evolution rules from Chinese semantic analysis. The main contents include the following aspects: 1. The issue of semantic concepts; 2. The issue of word meaning analysis; 3. The study of the relationship between semantics and syntax; 4. The analysis of discourse meaning; 5. The evolution of semantics; 6. The issue of formal expression of semantic knowledge.

Name: Introduction to Dialectology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is for graduate students who have not taken Chinese dialect studies as an undergraduate. It is best to take phonology first. The course mainly teaches the basic concepts and theories of dialectology, the basic methods of Chinese dialect investigation and the overview of Chinese dialects. During the teaching process, it focuses on training the following three basic skills: (1) the ability to use the International Phonetic Alphabet to record speech sounds; (2) the ability to use phonological theory to summarize phonology based on phonetic notation; (3) the ability to systematically record the sounds of characters based on the induction of phonology and use phonology knowledge to explore the laws of synchronic and diachronic phonetic correspondences. Students who choose the course should complete a phonology report in the designated dialect before the end of the semester and take a closed-book exam.

Name: General Spanish (I)
Introduction: Among graduate students in various departments, many students have the desire to learn Spanish because of professional needs. This course was initiated with the intention of providing these students with the opportunity to learn Spanish and to lay a foundation for further study in the future.

Name: Corpus Analysis in Linguistic Typology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The main purpose of the course is to introduce (the first two hours) the diversity specimen sampling issues of language typology, the diversity of morphosyntactic structures under functional commonality, implication commonality, the harmonious first and second patterns of word order (fixed order) and the explanation of the phenomenon of dominant word order and its competitive motivations, that is, economy and iconicity, grammatical levels and semantic mapping, the connected explanation of subject-object and communicative languages, etc. (Third hour) Practical exercises on typological analysis of ancient Tibetan corpus.

Name: Linguistics Seminar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: If the research results or important insights of linguistics master's students during their studies are considered by the instructor to be of innovative value, they will submit a report during the discussion. Master's students should report at least twice in seminars during their studies, and the instructor will give points based on the quality of the report.

Name: Studies in Chinese Prosodic Grammar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Comprehensive explanation of the phenomena, methods, theories and controversies in the study of Chinese prosodic grammar. By specifically discussing specific phenomena such as the prosodic pattern of Chinese syntactic structure, the prosodic pattern of compound words, the order changes of compound words, and the consonant tone changes in Mandarin and dialects, the application status of rhythmic phonology, prosodic word formation, and prosodic phonology in the study of Chinese prosody and grammar is explained, so that students can understand the cutting-edge issues and research of prosodic grammar, and be able to rationally view the gains and losses of cutting-edge theory in dealing with Chinese prosody and grammar issues, and can actually solve Chinese prosodic grammar issues.

Name: Speech Analysis and Programming
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is a speech analysis and Matlab programming course for PhDs and masters majoring in phonetics, linguistics, and vocal arts with a liberal arts background, and for masters and PhDs majoring in otolaryngology with a medical background. The course is divided into two aspects: the first aspect is speech analysis, which mainly teaches basic knowledge related to the physiological production of speech, the acoustic properties of speech, the physical meaning of speech, and the psychological perception and cognitive characteristics of speech, as well as the problems and research methods of modern speech research; the second aspect is the use of MatLab to realize parameter extraction and post-processing in speech analysis, mainly teaching the basic principles, physical properties of speech signals and basic algorithms for extracting main parameters. This course does not require advanced mathematics.

Name: Studies in Chinese Dialect Grammar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course examines the grammatical differences between northern and southern Chinese dialects from the perspectives of functional grammar and language typology, discusses the specific grammatical phenomena of specific dialects (including word order types, categorical phenomena, tense and aspect categories, and modal categories), and introduces language contact issues in dialect grammar. Through the observation of northern and southern dialects, many grammatical phenomena in Mandarin will also receive new interpretations.

Name: Grammatical Analysis
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly introduces the theories and methods related to grammatical analysis, and discusses some basic concepts, viewpoints, and methods of grammatical analysis. I hope it will be helpful to everyone in their grammar research. Some examples are also given, but the purpose is to explain the methods through the analysis of examples. By studying and discussing the relevant chapters of some important monographs in this area, we focus on discussing some core issues in the study of Chinese grammar, and at the same time discuss the methods and systems of Chinese grammar analysis.

Name: Introduction to Computational Linguistics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course has two main teaching objectives: first, to cultivate students' ability to think about linguistic issues and formally describe language knowledge using computers as the background; second, by studying this course, students can understand the basic theories of computational linguistics and commonly used models and algorithms in natural language processing, and initially have the ability to engage in research in the field of Chinese information processing. _x000D_
The teaching content of this course is divided into three parts: the first part is the basics, which introduces the general theories and methods of formalizing language knowledge; the second part is the algorithm part, which introduces some commonly used algorithms and models in automatic language analysis; the third part is the application part, which briefly introduces the application of computational linguistics theories and methods in actual information processing technology. The teaching time arrangement for the above three parts is roughly as follows: the basic part accounts for 60%, the algorithm part accounts for 30%, and the application part accounts for 10%. _x000D_
The assessment of this course includes 2 daily assignments and 1 final report. Daily homework accounts for 40% of the total grade, and the final report accounts for 60%.

Name: Studies in Phonetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course teaches the basic knowledge, basic research methods and classic theories of modern phonetics. The specific content is: 1. Research methods of phonetics; 2. Physiological and acoustic analysis of vowels and consonants; 3. Acoustic and perceptual research on tones; 4. Research on word stress; 5. Research on intonation; 6. Research on prosodic structure.

Name: Modern Chinese Seminar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
"Modern Chinese Discussion Class" conducts teaching activities in the form of tutors leading students to read professional literature and conducting seminars on special topics. There are three purposes: (1) Accurate classic research literature in this field; (2) Learn and master the research methods of classic research cases; (3) Understand current hot spots, cutting-edge research topics and trends. _x000D_
Students are required to complete reading of designated literature, report the content of the literature in detail, and make comments. Through exchanges and discussions between teachers and students, a reading report on a certain topic in this field is formed. _x000D_
Students generally must complete at least two reports to receive credit for this course. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Chinese Vocabulary and Word Meaning
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will combine the actual practice of Chinese vocabulary research and teach contemporary linguistic theories related to vocabulary research, covering the following topics: metaphor and metonymy, prototypes and categorization, vocabulary polysemy, image schema, corpus and vocabulary semantics, frame semantics, dictionary interpretation, etc. The main purpose of the course is to enable students to have a more comprehensive understanding of vocabulary research, especially the study of lexical semantics, through teaching (combined with students’ after-class reading and classroom discussions), and to enhance their ability to analyze and solve vocabulary problems, especially to enhance their ability to research Chinese vocabulary problems.

Name: English for Specific Purposes
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course aims to improve graduate students' academic English writing and speaking skills, so that they can write academic papers and engage in academic exchanges with professional vocabulary and expressions in international journal papers and international seminars. Under the guidance of teachers, students will understand academic terms, analyze the style and argumentative techniques of various academic papers, and at the same time apply what they have learned in various writing and speaking exercises, and gradually become familiar with expressing their own findings and insights in accurate and authentic professional English. With the accumulation of sample reading, not only the expression method can be improved, but the accuracy of reading comprehension can also be improved.

Name: Wang Li Memorial Academic Lecture Series
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Mr. Wang Li (1900-1986) is a well-known linguist and one of the founders of modern Chinese linguistics. Mr. Wang Li has devoted his whole life to research in Chinese and has published hundreds of thousands of words in academic literature. He has done excellent work in various fields, such as hymn, linguistic law, poetry, Chinese history, linguistic research history, linguistic origin, history dictionary and the construction of teaching materials in Guhan; he has also made important contributions in various fields, such as vocabulary, linguistic logic, editorial reform, the standardization of Chinese, the promotion of Mandarin and the dissemination of knowledge of languages. Mr. Wang Li, one of the most representative masters in the history of Chinese language, has developed a modern Chinese-language study. His academic philosophy has emphasized the importance of Chinese language as a fundamental factor in the history of ordinary languages. Mr. Wang Li was the oldest teacher at the Chinese Department of Beijing University (1954-1986) and the most significant contribution he made to the various branches of linguistics. It is incumbent upon us to summarize, inherit and promote Mr. Wang Li ' s academic thought and academic heritage, to study the spirit of Mr. Wang Li ' s humanism, thus comprehensively clearing the development of Chinese linguistics in the twentieth century and the lessons learned, and to explore the path of Chinese linguistic development in the new century. It will also be of great importance for the development of graduate students in Chinese history. On the basis of the above, we plan to start the course " Mr. Wang Li ' s Academic Lecture " in 2009. Mr. Wang Li ' s Academic Lecture is a compulsory postgraduate doctoral course in Chinese history. The content of the course is presented on a thematic basis on various aspects of Mr. Wang Li's academic thought and research, as well as on academic achievements guided by Mr. Wang Li's academic philosophy. Two credits per week for this course. It is proposed to take the form of academic lectures, each of which will be taught by experts in the relevant fields.

Name: Standards and Frontiers of Classical Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The course is offered by the Classical Platform of the Chinese Department of Beijing University. The curriculum is divided into two parts: general and separate. The general section describes the basic academic norms of classical research, the content of ancient Chinese and Western classicalism, how to build disciplines and systems in Chinese classical science, and the relevant theoretical and research methods of Chinese classical science. The segment describes the cutting edges of the fields of classical science-related specializations such as ancient Chinese, classical literature and classical literature and the methods of writing related academic papers. The curriculum is shared by teachers in the “Tripoli” specialties of the Chinese language.

Name: Theory and Practice of Ancient Text Compilation
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Through specific examples, we summarize the theories, methods and achievements of previous people in collating ancient books, and conduct a thematic analysis and discussion of the methods, processes and related knowledge of ancient book punctuation, collation, annotation, modern translation, compilation, forgery identification, cataloging, indexing, ancient book identification and protection, etc., so that graduate students will have an understanding of the history and current situation of ancient book collation and publishing, and initially have the basic knowledge and skills to engage in related work. _x000D_
The course will also cooperate with relevant institutions such as the National Library to organize teaching internships. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Bibliographic Treatise of the Book of Han
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The Han book, art literature, is China’s oldest collection of catalogues, not only in the West Han collection, but also in a comprehensive and systematic way reflecting the evolution of the Qin-Handei science, which has a profound impact on the development of later-life catalogues and the whole science. Han Ji is not only an indispensable study of the evolution of Qin-Handey, but also a search for ancient sources, basic references to the system, and its place in literature and in the history of science as a whole.
The curriculum is based on two sections of general and textual reading, from Liu Dynasty, Liu Dynasty and Sons The Seven Scrolls are a book-writing exercise, focusing on their disaggregated systems and features, the achievements of the catalogues and their impact on future generations, and the adaptation of the Seven Scrolls by the Hans. The text has been carefully read in the form of a sample of six art schematics, and a wide range of pre-humans have been interested in the interpretation, preparation and follow-up of the research, and have taken the initiative to lead students to study from the double-minded angles of cataloguing and learning history, thereby giving them a basic, holistic understanding of the shape, type, source, system and, more importantly, the path and methodology of healing.

Name: Historical Sources of Song Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course focuses on various historical materials that provide historical and cultural background and poetic biography, writing and Song poetry, as well as the value characteristics, potential problems and methods of utilization of various types of historical material, and leads students to study the flow, characteristics and ability to search for, process and use accurately the relevant historical material. The teaching method combines teaching with reading and discussion; the main subjects are Master ' s degree students in Song generation literature and classical literature, whose knowledge and methods are also relevant to other students engaged in ancient linguistic, literary and cultural studies.

Name: Studies in Overseas Chinese Texts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The study of overseas Chinese books is an emerging academic direction in recent years. The word "Hanji" comes from Japan and refers to "Guoshu" (or "Washu"), which refers to books written by Chinese in Chinese. For scholars who study ancient Chinese books, Han books are often used to specifically refer to ancient Chinese books. Due to various reasons, many ancient Chinese books flowed from mainland China to foreign countries through various channels, including old engravings, rare and secret books from the Song and Yuan Dynasties. From a regional perspective, among the Chinese books currently stored overseas, Japan has the largest collection in Asia, and the United States has the largest collection in Europe and the United States. The investigation, understanding and research on the storage status and value of overseas Chinese books are of extremely important significance to the in-depth development of the compilation and research of ancient books and other related fields. _x000D_
This course provides a comprehensive introduction and research on Chinese ancient books spread overseas, teaches the versions and academic value of important ancient books spread overseas, and conducts comparative research with ancient books preserved in China. Through study, students can have a more comprehensive understanding of the storage situation and value of overseas Chinese books, and pay attention to the use of overseas Chinese book resources in future study and research. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Book of Rites
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course will take the traditional Chinese classic "Book of Rites" as a case study. Through text collation and reading of unearthed documents and handed down documents, manuscript documents and engraving documents, and discussions on the interpretation of the past dynasties, the textual evolution and canonization process of the book will be sorted out, and the face of Chinese classical scholarship will be revealed accordingly. The course will be conducted through a combination of background lectures on academic history, classroom discussions and text review exercises, with the aim of enhancing students’ in-depth understanding of traditional Chinese classics and academic history. Main contents: 1. Introduction to "Book of Rites". Mainly teaches the classic status of "Book of Rites", its writing process, nature and content, annotated versions, and philological research reviews. 2. Intensive reading of "Quli". Intensive reading of the first chapter of "The Book of Rites", "Quli", and class discussion on the norms and connotations of Chinese ritual and music civilization. 3. Dual reading of "Zi Yi". Comparatively read the Guodian Chu slips, Shangbo Chu slips and the handed down version of "Zi Yi", and explore the textual similarities, differences, and textual changes between the unearthed documents and the handed down documents. 4. Dual reading of "Ai Gongwen". The question and answer between Duke Ai of Lu and Confucius can also be found in "The Analects of Confucius?" "Wei Zheng", "The Doctrine of the Mean", "Book of Rites"? "Confucianism", "Da Dai Li Ji", "Xunzi?" "Ai Gong" and "Confucius Family Language", this article will read the texts of each book side by side to explore the textual evolution and book formation of early Chinese documents. 5. The canonization of "Book of Rites". Study the scriptures, annotations, commentaries, and exegesis of the "Great Learning" chapter, and refer to "Hanshu?" "Yiwenzhi", "Sui Shu?" "Jing Ji Zhi", "Classic Interpretation?" "Preface" and "General Catalog of Sikuquanshu" are about the preface and categories of "Book of Rites", exploring the formation and interpretation of classics, as well as historical issues of Confucian classics. 6. Editing and revision of the "Book of Rites". Sort out the publication origin and edition system of "Book of Rites", select representative editions for collation practice, experience the actual situation of the text's evolution and corruption, and explore the significance of edition criticism. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Studies in the History of Chinese Classical Scholarship
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Learning is the core and foundation of traditional Chinese academia. For a long time, the Chinese Department of Beijing University has not offered a course on the history of Chinese science. The following features are to be highlighted in the course "China's history of learning": firstly, the integration of literature and academic history studies, with academic literature as an entry point and as a basis for building a system of academic literature; secondly, the integration of historical and indigenous literature with indigenous literature, with appropriate and efficient use of new materials such as indigenous literature and their inventions, with full understanding and mastery of the dictionary; thirdly, the emphasis on personal research and the incorporation of existing research results, and the incorporation of solid basic research, so that it can reflect the latest research findings and the overall level of research in the field of economic history research; and fourthly, the integration of indigenous studies and academic exchanges, based on indigenous edifice studies, with a view to the general environment, the larger background, the internal and external integration of the East Asian Confucian culture, and the creation of high houses, so that our research can be of a world nature.

Name: Studies in Ming Dynasty Documents and Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course combs through all the major links and main aspects of the development of literature in the Ming Dynasty (such as the various poetry schools from the early Ming Dynasty to the late Ming Dynasty) and main aspects (poems, operas, novels, literary theories, etc.), and examines the literature of the Ming Dynasty within the entire development history of ancient Chinese literature and the specific historical environment of the Ming Dynasty, trying to reveal its basic characteristics and historical status. At the same time, we briefly describe the main documents of Ming Dynasty literature and their characteristics and values, introduce the important results of research on Ming Dynasty literature at home and abroad, and explore possible ways to expand research on Ming Dynasty literature.

Name: Academic Standards and Thesis Writing
Introduction:
1) The use of commonly used Chinese and foreign reference books. 2) Preparation for writing the paper: including how to search for traditional Chinese documents, using the editions and collation knowledge of ancient books, searching for contemporary works, browsing domestic and foreign magazines and special issues, and tracking new archaeological discoveries. 3) How to write a paper. 4) How to write a book review. 5) Writing standards. 6) Comment style. 7) Translation exercises. _x000D_
	In this course, teachers describe the basic qualities and basic knowledge needed to engage in academic research based on issues that have arisen in recent graduate studies and thesis writing, and use vivid examples to illustrate the teaching content. In addition to lectures by faculty, this course also guides graduate students to do their own research, using documents, unearthed documents, archeology, images and other materials to study certain issues and do certain writing standard training. We also hope to lead students to visit the National Library and Peking University Library and introduce how to find and use professional books and magazines. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Four Books
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The "Four Books", ancient classic documents, reflect the core values ​​of Chinese traditional culture. The "Four Books" formed thereby is an important part of the history of Chinese academic and intellectual history. This course combs and studies the formation, development and evolution of the Four Books, and goes into a close reading of the text to show the profound correlation between the arrangement of ancient books and the development of thought and culture. _x000D_
    The teacher who started the course has studied the Four Books and Zhu Xi studies for many years, has a series of related research results, and has also taught related courses. I look forward to having in-depth discussions with my classmates in class and jointly promoting the development of Four Books. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Texts of the Manuscript Era
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: In recent years, with the in-depth study of unearthed documents and the rise of "manuscript" culture research in overseas sinological circles, the credibility and stability of handed down pre-Tang documents have attracted more and more attention from scholars. Traditional academic concepts and methods such as compilation, collation, and forgeries have also been challenged to varying degrees: Can we study pre-Qin literature based on pre-Qin documents compiled by Han people, and can we study Wei-Jin literature based on Wei-Jin documents compiled by Tang people? What are the possible problems? Are these problems possible to avoid? How much academic basis and value does this questioning itself have? Can a new research paradigm be constructed from this? To answer these questions, we first need to conduct a large number of case studies on texts from the note book era. This course intends to demonstrate the complexity of the process of early text generation and dissemination through case studies of several "heterogeneous texts" in the manuscript era, and then respond to the aforementioned issues. The course content mainly includes three aspects: (1) Introduction to the research theory of "writing culture"; (2) Introduction to the theory of "heterogeneous texts"; (3) Case study of "heterogeneous texts" in Han and Tang Dynasties. This course will be launched by combining teacher lectures with student discussions and reports, hoping to further improve students' basic ability to read text carefully.

Name: Studies in the General Catalogue of the Complete Library of the Four Treasuries
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for graduate students majoring in classical literature in the Department of Chinese Literature, and is also intended for majors in literature, history, philosophy, and humanities and social sciences. _x000D_
    "Sikuquanshu General Catalog" is a classic work of Chinese classical bibliography and academic and cultural history. This course teaches the compilation situation, specific content, academic influence and reference value of the "Sikuquanshu General Catalog" for related professional research, focusing on the summary of Siku and issues related to Siku. _x000D_
    This course requires graduate students to be familiar with the compilation process and academic content of "Sikuquanshu" and "Sikuquanshu General Catalog", carefully study various abstracts of "Sikuquanshu General Catalog", focus on mastering the research methods of Sikuquanshu officials and senior scholars, and internally understand Chinese classical bibliography and classical academic traditions, so as to lay a solid foundation for future academic research.

Name: Introduction to Textual Bibliography
Introduction: This course systematically introduces the basic knowledge of Chinese ancient book engraving, so that students can master the basic form and era characteristics of reading ancient Chinese engraving documents through the study of this course, understand the important role of ancient engraving knowledge in the study of ancient Chinese history and culture, and lay a good documentary foundation for further academic knowledge of ancient literature and history.

Name: Lecture Series on Frontiers in Classical Textual Scholarship
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is an introduction and evaluation of the current hot spots, concerns and latest achievements in the field of ancient Chinese literature. _x000D_

It includes several aspects of the organization, research, storage, and publication of Chinese ancient books, as well as issues such as the spread, storage, and return of ancient books overseas. Focus on the introduction and discussion of new fields and new methods of ancient book compilation and research. It involves the relevant research status of scholars in mainland China, Taiwan, and Hong Kong, as well as the relevant academic status of foreign countries such as Japan and the United States. _x000D_

The topics of planned lectures for this semester mainly include: the current situation and problems of the collection of domestic ancient books, the spread and return of overseas Chinese books (including the auction and repurchase of ancient books), the institutional and storage status of Song and Yuan editions of Chinese books collected in Japan and the United States, 201 The pros and cons of the 3-year edition of "Historical Records", Japanese scholars' comments on the study of "Historical Records", the current situation of ancient book publishing in China, the pros and cons of current compilation and research on Confucian classics (Confucianism), the compilation process and value of bamboo slips newly collected by Peking University and Tsinghua University, etc. _x000D_
