Name: Classical Philology Seminar
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This seminar is intended to guide students to jointly study professional classic documents and discuss new domestic and foreign achievements and new academic trends in this discipline, in order to gain a deeper understanding of the mysteries of classical philology, gain a broad academic vision, and lay a solid foundation for future academic research.

Name: Introduction to the Classics of Chinese Philology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is mainly based on books such as Yu Yue's "Examples of Doubts in Ancient Books" from the Qing Dynasty, Wang Niansun's "Guangya Shuzheng", Wang Yinzhi's "Jingyi Shuwen", Qian Daxin's "Shenglei", Wang Zhong's "Shu Xue" and other books. It refers to the research results of modern primary schools and is lectured and researched by teachers. Combined with postgraduate discussions, through extensive reading and analysis of primary school documents from the Qing Dynasty, postgraduate students can deepen and improve their mastery and understanding of characters, phonology, and exegetical knowledge, and be able to use this knowledge in practice to solve specific problems encountered.

Name: Studies in the Textual Sources of Classical Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The course consists of five parts: an inventory study of ancient novels, a study of ancient novel versions, a study of the history of ancient novels, a study of ancient novels and a study of ancient novels. Based on traditional classical literature, the curriculum is designed to streamline and construct novel literature that is in line with popular literature, focusing on the ability of students to combine theoretical and practical research, paper and physical knowledge.
Teaching methods: Teachers tell + student classroom reports.
Examination methods: Presentation of course papers at the end of the academic year.

Name: Studies in Classic Works of Japanese Sinology
Bamboo and Silk Manuscripts and the History of Scholarship
Prerequisite: China's General History (Cultural Part), Chinese History Selected
Introduction: Since the 1970s, buried ancient bamboo slips and silk materials from the Warring States, Qin and Han Dynasties have been continuously unearthed, which has had a profound impact on the fields of archeology, history, philology, linguistics, ideological and cultural history, etc., forming the emerging comprehensive frontier discipline of "Bamboo Silk Studies". In recent years, our school has collected two batches of bamboo slips from the Qin and Han dynasties, giving our school a unique advantage in developing research and teaching on "bamboo slips". This course will adopt the form of multimedia teaching to systematically introduce the basic situation of the discovery, arrangement and research of ancient books and bamboo slips and silk documents. The main contents include a brief history of bamboo slips and silk documents, important discoveries of bamboo slips and silk documents, the significance of bamboo slips and silk documents in "rewriting academic history", the form of bamboo slips and silk books, an introduction to the classification of bamboo slips and silk documents, and the practice of proofreading bamboo and silk documents, etc. Through classroom lectures, study practice and after-class papers, students can master the basic knowledge and research methods of "Bamboo Silk Studies", understand the evolution and development of academic thoughts in the Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties, and cultivate students' awareness and ability to use bamboo slips and silk documents in research.

Name: Sources on Song Dynasty Poet-Monks and Poetry Compilation
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: A problem-solving introduction is made to the literature about the poets and monks of the Song Dynasty. Combined with the scientific research topics compiled by the poets and monks of the Song Dynasty, the work, steps, formats and issues that need attention are introduced in the collection of monks' poems, and students are guided to carry out specific collection and arrangement of monks' poems.

Name: Topics in Oracle Bone Inscriptions and Shang History
Introduction: On the basis of teaching the basic theories and research methods of paleography, this course will select representative Yin Ruins oracle bone inscriptions for specific and exemplary introduction and analysis, so that students can understand and initially master the professional basic knowledge of oracle bone inscription interpretation, and understand the significance of oracle bone inscriptions. He realized the important value of historical materials in the study of Shang history, and realized how to use oracle bone inscriptions scientifically, combined with literature and archaeological data to deeply explore important issues in the study of Shang history, and laid the foundation for more in-depth research using oracle bone inscriptions and other ancient text materials in the future.

Name: Topics in Bronze Inscriptions and Shang-Zhou History
Introduction: Through the selection and explanation of Shang and Zhou bronze inscriptions into special topics according to their connotations, students can understand the important historical value of Shang and Zhou bronze inscriptions for the study of Shang and Zhou history. They will also learn how to combine with handed down documents based on the study of bronze chronology and scientifically use bronze inscriptions to conduct in-depth research on important Shang and Zhou history topics. In particular, it will point out the current problems and difficulties in using Shang and Zhou bronze inscriptions to study ancient history topics, inspiring students to study and think.

Name: Studies in the Compilation and Printing of Song Dynasty Collected Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course introduces the general situation of the Song Dynasty's collection of works of the Song Dynasty, and gives examples of the compilation and printing of the works of writers such as Ouyang Xiu and Dai Fuxu in the Song Dynasty and its circulation after the Song Dynasty, so that students can have a basic understanding of the existing editions of the Song Dynasty's works and their relationships. At the same time, internship assignments are assigned to investigate various versions of Song Dynasty's works, learn and master the basic methods of analyzing and identifying the origins of Song Dynasty's works, conduct class discussions, and submit relevant reading reports at the end of the semester. The students who choose the course are mainly graduate students in the Chinese Department.

Name: Seminar on the History of Song and Yuan Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The main purpose of this course is to enable graduate students in the Chinese Department to have a further understanding of the appearance and characteristics of Song and Yuan literature after receiving systematic undergraduate education. This course is divided into several topics such as family and literature, region and literature, daily life and literature, imperial examinations and literature, women and literature, politics and literature, religion and literature, etc., to reveal the deep texture of Song and Yuan literature from multiple aspects of literature, documents, and culture, so that students can initially master the ways and methods to enter the history of Song and Yuan literature and even the entire academic research.

Name: Studies in Tang Dynasty Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is taught by teachers for half a semester, accounting for 16 class hours, and then students who choose the course will give class reports and discussions, accounting for 16 class hours. _x000D_
The teacher's teaching part will focus on the concepts of novels in the Tang Dynasty, the reasons for the prosperity of novels in the Tang Dynasty, and the artistic characteristics of novels in the Tang Dynasty. The class reports and discussions of students who choose the course will be based on the teacher's designated portfolio. The teacher will provide 20 Tang Dynasty novel collections in advance for students to choose from as subjects for report and discussion.

Name: Topics in Ming, Qing and Modern Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is centered on the important writers, works and literary phenomena of Ming, Qing and modern literature. It combines the academic history and cutting-edge issues of related research, conducts in-depth analysis of the research object, pays attention to close reading of the text, takes into account the discussion of the relationship between social and cultural background and literature, reviews the collection and arrangement of relevant documents, introduces the theoretical methods of research, and strives to cultivate graduate students' research awareness and ability on specific topics through course study. The course adopts a combination of lecture and discussion. _x000D_
      The first semester of the 2016-2017 academic year focuses on various issues in the evolution of modern ancient literature. _x000D_
      After the Song and Yuan Dynasties, especially during the Ming and Qing Dynasties, literature showed many unprecedented features in both form and content. Commercialization and social intervention constitute a special external environment for literary creation; the two major ideological trends of secularization and collection guide the evolution of literature as a whole; the concepts of "elegant" and "vulgar" continue to form a situation of both opposition and integration in new ways; vernacular as a new literary language gradually matures, greatly improving the expressive power of Chinese; novels, Opera replaced traditional poetry and became the mainstream or highlight of literary development; the purpose of literature transcended the expression of personal emotions and the ideal of "economic development", swinging between the entertainment function and the exhortation function; literary societies and schools emerged in endlessly, giving the literary world a pattern full of contradictions; regional colors became increasingly rich based on the inherent distinction between north and south, and so on. The course will combine the actual practice of literary creation to explore the above-mentioned important literary phenomena and laws and the academic history of related research, thereby establishing the historical concepts and research ideas and methods of the development of modern literature. _x000D_
_x000D_

Name: Studies in Ming and Qing Vernacular Short Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course uses the history of the creation and publication of short vernacular novels in the Ming and Qing Dynasties as a clue to discuss its stylistic characteristics and development process. It uses the core issues of short vernacular novels in the Ming and Qing Dynasties as the main body to analyze some common phenomena in creation, combined with specific literary backgrounds and specific works. Investigation; focusing on the representative writers and special collections of short vernacular novels of the Ming and Qing Dynasties, exploring their different ideological styles and artistic pursuits; focusing on the texts of short vernacular novels of the Ming and Qing Dynasties, analyzing the origin, evolution, gains and losses of specific works in terms of subject matter, content, art, etc. Courses are conducted through a combination of lectures and discussions.

Name: Topics in Pre-Qin and Han Dynasty Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: In the form of special research, courses are offered in the fields of pre-Qin and Han literature, documents and related academic history. At present, it mainly focuses on the classics of the Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties, with special books such as "The Book of Songs", "Zuo Zhuan", "Chu Ci", "Historical Records", and "Selected Works", as well as research on the prose of pre-Qin scholars, research on the literati literature of the Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties, and research on the historical and biographical literature of the Pre-Qin and Han Dynasties. , Pre-Qin and Han literature and document research, Pre-Qin and Han literature and social history research, Ci Fu research, Han Yuefu research, Han and Wei ancient poetry research, unearthed document research, etc. The above different topics are established according to the actual research situation of the teacher's personal research. The purpose is to enable graduate students, under the guidance of teachers, to master the research methods of pre-Qin and Han literature and documents, strengthen their understanding of special books and documents, understand the characteristics of pre-Qin and Han literature and documents, understand the social, cultural and historical background of literature, grasp the development trajectory of academic history, cultivate and improve their reading and research abilities, lay a solid foundation, and expand their academic horizons.

Name: Seminar on Frontier Issues in Ancient Chinese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course mainly focuses on the major issues in the history of ancient Chinese literature and current research progress. It combines the latest achievements of the teaching teachers to introduce and commentate on new hot spots, new issues, new phenomena, and new works in the academic world. It pays special attention to the in-depth analysis of controversial academic issues, guides students to think and discuss, and helps students more consciously grasp the latest developments and research methods in academic research, thereby cultivating their academic frontier awareness. This course uses lecture notes compiled by teachers and is jointly taught by all teachers in the Ancient Literature Laboratory of the Department of Chinese Language and Literature.

Name: Studies in Yuan and Ming Zaju Drama
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The creation of Zaju in the Yuan and Ming dynasties was prosperous, and it evolved and developed in the exchange with the legend of Southern Opera. It left many excellent works for ancient Chinese literature, provided nourishment for the development of opera, and also reflected the characteristics of the times and the lives of literati. This course intends to grasp the characteristics of the creation of Yuan and Ming operas, examine the development of opera, and conduct a detailed review of this important component of ancient opera creation through lectures and discussions, based on the study of works.

Name: Topics in the Literary History of the Wei, Jin and Northern and Southern Dynasties
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Based on the important research results of teachers and famous scholars in the field, the course guides graduate students to conduct special research and classroom discussions on the literary history, literary styles and writers' works from the Wei, Jin, Southern and Northern Dynasties to the Sui, Tang and Five Dynasties from various angles. It guides students into cutting-edge academic fields, focuses on cultivating students' academic interests and enhances their awareness of issues, so that students can gradually master common academic methods and have one-stop academic abilities such as independent thinking, comprehensive research, and academic publishing. _x000D_
During the teaching process, students are required to preview according to the teaching plan before class, prepare class reports carefully, actively participate in discussions and speeches in class, and write course papers with their own opinions or new ideas after class. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Ming Dynasty Classical-Language Fiction
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
In the past, the research community on the classical Chinese novels of the Ming Dynasty was very inadequate, and their evaluation was not high and inaccurate. This course plans to select about fifteen Ming Dynasty classical Chinese novels for introduction and research, and explore their connections with previous generations of novels, their interrelationships, and their impact on Ming and Qing novels, so as to re-judge their artistic and cultural values, and examine their status in the history of novels. _x000D_
    Based on the teacher's lectures, this course will arrange for selected students to conduct a survey of novel literature and make class reports. _x000D_

Name: Literary History and Modern Textual Collation
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Compared to the methodological thinking of modern texts carried out by Western research in the twentieth century (Texturral Criticism), Chinese literature does not yet have its own independent methodological theory, the idea and methodology of which have largely been extended from an ancient survey to identify a definitive or good version of the author’s intentions. However, the multiplicity and uncertainty of the modern text are intrinsically balanced between the goals and methods of this traditional calibration. This course is intended to combine the theoretical reflections and criticisms of modern texts by Western scholars, re-examine the objectives and methods of modern Chinese texts from the point of view of the sociology of the text, and engage in a process of discussion and dialogue with existing literary history discourse through specific examples of contemporary literature.

The course is presented in a combination of lectures and discussions, requiring the active participation of graduate students in discussions, the selection of topics for classroom presentations and the submission of research papers related to the course at the end of the period.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Writers
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selectively studies the most representative and important writers in modern China, such as Lu Xun, Zhou Zuoren, Lao She, Shen Congwen, Hu Shi, Mao Dun, Cao Yu, etc. It focuses on exploring the spiritual journey, literary propositions, creative practices, cultural ideals, stylistic changes and aesthetic styles of modern writers from the perspective of writer theory, as well as their relationship with contemporaries, influence and interpretation by later generations, and the possibility of serving as ideological resources. The course involves internal research and external research, using a combination of explanation and discussion. As a compulsory course for graduate students, the purpose is to train research abilities and master the basic ideas of writers' research. It adopts a method that combines teacher lectures with graduate students' discussions and reading reports. It requires students to write papers as a course assessment, hoping to train students' ability to discover new research ideas.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: "Research on Modern Chinese Poetry" is an elective course for postgraduate students majoring in modern and contemporary literature in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature. The course takes as cases the poems of important poets in the century-old history of new poetry, such as Hu Shi, Guo Moruo, Xu Zhimo, Fei Ming, Lin Geng, Bian Zhilin, Mu Dan, Haizi, Zhang Zao, etc. In a specific historical context, it extracts relevant poetic issues and discusses the establishment of the legitimacy of new poetry, the tension of modernity, and the relationship between language consciousness and historical consciousness. On this basis, it explores new possibilities for the study of modern poetry.

Name: Modern Chinese Literature and Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course focuses on China's "literature and culture" in the 20th century, focusing on text analysis, as well as images and sounds. Topics discussed include "'Modern Literature' as Material Culture", "Reciting to the Heavens Beyond China", "Restaurants and Teahouses", "Little World of the Stage", "Good Times in Childhood", "Memories of War", "Reciting the Jia Biao Xian in War" ", "The Spring, Summer, Autumn and Winter in Beijing and the Streets of Shanghai", "Travel Pictures and Changing Clothing Notes", "'Food is the First Thing of the People' and 'There Are Tens of Thousands of Buildings'", "'Literature' from the Perspective of Folklore", etc.
_x000D_

Name: Forum on Topics in Modern Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for master's and doctoral students majoring in modern literature in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature, and is mainly aimed at newly admitted first-year students. The main contents are: 1. The latest research results of teachers; 2. Representative research results of teachers in this major; 3. Outstanding and cutting-edge achievements in the academic field; 4. Academic topics in this major; 5. Discussion of academic plans for master's and doctoral students. _x000D_
The main lecturer of this course presides over the course, during which other teachers in the major are invited to give special speeches. Course assessment mainly takes the form of students submitting their academic plans after discussion and revision.

Name: Studies in Genres of Modern Chinese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Genre research is an ancient method of literary criticism and literary research. In the West, it can be traced back to the emphasis on ritual (decorum) in the Greek classical period. In China, there is a long tradition of "distinguishing style and style". However, since the May 4th “Literary Revolution” advocated the epochal historical view of “literature from generation to generation”, the idea of ​​​​genre research has been relatively marginalized. This course attempts to restore the vitality of the concept of "genre" on the basis of communicating Chinese and Western literary theories, and re-explore the history of the formation of modern Chinese literature (forms and concepts, institutions and practices) from the perspective of genre history. _x000D_
This course is conducted in the form of a discussion class. It is planned to select about ten works (parts) on genre criticism and genre history research on Chinese literature since the late Qing Dynasty, such as Zhang Taiyan's "On Style", Wang Guowei's "History of Opera in the Song and Yuan Dynasties", Hu Shi's "On Short Stories", Lu Xun's "A Brief History of Chinese Novels", Zhou Zuoren's "Introduction to a Collection of Prose in the Chinese New Literature Series", Fei Ming's "Talking about New Poems", etc., combined with the development history of the relevant genres themselves, and studied under the leadership of the teacher. Graduate students are required to actively participate in discussions, make class reports on topics, and submit research papers related to this course at the end of the semester. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Zhou Brothers (Lu Xun and Zhou Zuoren)
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The Zhou brothers are important subjects that cannot be ignored in modern literature and cultural studies. Their common experiences and different paths are thought-provoking. Their huge influence has made them the research subjects of many scholars. In the history of the Chinese Department of Peking University, scholars of every generation have taken this as their main research field. _x000D_
This course covers the Zhou brothers’ various stages of experience, literary ideas and works, cultural ideals and practices, literary style and written language, relationships with contemporaries, later influences and interpretations, and the possibility of serving as ideological resources. The course involves internal research and external research, using a combination of explanation and discussion. The Zhou brothers have a huge topic and have achieved high-level research results. As a course for graduate students, the purpose is to train research abilities. Therefore, most of the specific lecture topics are decided by teachers and students through discussion. Students are also required to write papers as a course assessment, hoping to discover new research ideas. _x000D_

Name: Contemporary Literary Criticism
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Fiction Classics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
"Study on Classics of Modern Chinese Novels" selects for study and discussion the classic works of modern Chinese classic novelists between the May Fourth New Culture Movement and the founding of the People's Republic of China in 1949. In the process of interpreting and discussing novels, it attempts to strengthen graduate students' text analysis abilities, ability to draw on theories, and ability to creatively interpret literary works, thereby cultivating the consciousness of independent innovation. _x000D_
This course mainly takes the form of a discussion class. The teacher selects specific texts in advance, and students participating in the course focus on one text in each class. In each class, one to three students will give keynote speeches, and other students will participate in group discussions based on careful preparation. Each class consists of one class hour for teacher lectures and comments, and two class hours for student lectures and independent discussions. _x000D_

Name: History of Chinese Film Culture (III): 1979-Present
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The course History of Chinese Film Culture (1-3) not only aims to introduce students to the history of the occurrence, development, evolution and twists and turns of Chinese films, but also attempts to use film, the seventh art born at the end of the 19th century, as a mirror to show an important aspect of modern Chinese social culture. The lectures and discussions of the course not only share the detailed investigation and exploration of the history of Chinese film, but also try to use cultural studies methods to open up thinking and observation of different aspects of China's modern and contemporary cultural history through film. The course places emphasis on both "film facts" - the professional close reading of film texts - and on "film facts" - the study of the history of the film industry, technology and media. _x000D_
History of Chinese Film Culture (3): 1979-present. This book focuses on teaching the history of Chinese films since the new era and its observation and reflection on the radical changes in contemporary Chinese society through films. It is also a sharing of the process of film history, the raising and opening of cultural history issues, the study of cultural and art history, and the reflection on its problem setting and research methods_x000D_
This course has been offered in the Chinese Department of Peking University for 27 years and is a mature course. _x000D_
While taking the course, students are required to independently study important films from different periods and participate in discussions, and finally complete the final thesis.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Literary Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course discusses classic works in the history of modern literature, such as Lu Xun's "Scream", "Wandering", "Weeds", "New Stories", Zhou Zuoren's prose, Mao Dun's "Midnight", Ba Jin's "Home", Guo Moruo's "The Goddess", Shen Congwen's "The Long River", Fei Ming's "The Biography of Mr. Mo Xuyou", Qian Zhong Shu's "The Besieged City", Xiao Hong's "Hulan River Biography", Lu Ling's "The Rich Man's Sons and Daughters", Feng Zhi's "Collection of Fourteen Lines", etc., in the original historical context and on the basis of careful reading of the works, sort out previous research results, introduce new ideas and methods, and explore the possibilities of modern literary research.

Name: Interpreting Cultural Events in Taiwan
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Through the interpretation of Taiwanese cultural and literary events, this course guides students to find the trajectory of the evolution of Taiwanese literature and culture from the restoration and exploration of event phenomena and meanings, and cultivates students' ability to read, understand and interpret historical materials. Important contemporary Taiwanese cultural and literary events often become nodes in the evolution of Taiwanese society and literature. Exploring these events is of great significance to understanding Taiwan. The course selects and interprets important cultural and literary events such as the February 28th Incident, the Cultural Cleansing Movement, the Free China Incident, the Chinese Cultural Renaissance Movement, Modernist Criticism, the Vernacular Literature Movement, the Formosa Incident, the Aboriginal Movement, and the debates on Taiwanese literary history at the turn of the century in contemporary Taiwan. It sorts out the development of Taiwanese culture and literature from the point of view, starting from the events and their correlations, and enhances students' in-depth understanding of Taiwanese culture and literature. _x000D_
Teaching requirements: consult and carefully read historical materials about relevant cultural and literary events; elucidate meaning from events and their connections. _x000D_
Basic purpose: This course is positioned to deeply interpret Taiwanese cultural and literary phenomena from the perspective of cultural and literary events. In view of the relatively insufficient understanding of Taiwanese society and culture by mainland students, and the contradiction between the richness of Taiwanese literature and the limited classroom teaching, the course explores the ins and outs of the events and their status and significance in the development of Taiwanese culture and literature through the description, sorting, significance elucidation and mutual reflection of representative cultural events in contemporary Taiwan. These events are like texts, and the interpretation of the events is equivalent to close reading of the text, but with the addition of training in the cleaning and analysis of historical materials, it breaks through the relatively superficial narrative methods of phenomena in the past and can improve students' ability to deal with cultural phenomena from a case-by-case basis. The course pursues a deep and specific grasp rather than a superficial comprehensiveness. It relies on the investigation of the event itself and surrounding influences, as well as the interrelationship of each event, using the point to illustrate the situation, and using the small to see the big. It not only presents details and explores meaning, but also has a broad vision, making the understanding of Taiwanese culture and literature more concrete and perceptible. At the same time, the elucidation of the meaning of the event focuses on its correlation with literature, that is, highlighting the relationship between the event and literature and the impact of Taiwan's social and cultural evolution on the development of literature, providing a new way of thinking about Taiwanese literature. _x000D_
Content summary and credit hour allocation (36 credit hours in total)_x000D_
        The course selects and interprets important cultural and literary events such as the February 28th Incident, the Cultural Cleansing Movement, the Free China Incident, the Chinese Cultural Renaissance Movement, Modernism Criticism, the Native Literature Movement, the Formosa Incident, the Aboriginal Movement, and the Taiwanese literary history debate at the turn of the century. These events are all representative events that have influenced the development of contemporary Taiwanese society, culture, and literature. Their types and natures vary, including cultural and political events, sociocultural movements, literary movements and literary societies, literary criticism and literary debates, the establishment of literary institutions, etc. The progress of the course is arranged according to the chronological order of events, with specific emphasis on two aspects: the first is the presentation and explanation of events and historical facts; the second is the discussion of the impact of events, inspiring and guiding students to start with a close reading of the text of specific events and embark on a cognitive journey of Taiwanese culture and literature. _x000D_

Name: Historical Sources of Modern Chinese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is specially designed for graduate students in the Department of Chinese Literature at Peking University. It hopes to combine theory and practice. It mainly covers the following topics: the connotation, origin and form of "literary historiography"; the production, movement and interpretation of texts; the editions, compilation and criticism of new literature; the story of the "New Literature Department"; how to compile the "Complete Collection"; modern and contemporary Chinese works Collection of home materials; modern and contemporary Chinese newspapers and periodicals (comprehensive category); modern and contemporary Chinese newspapers and periodicals (literary category); editing, retrieval and reading of newspaper supplements; diaries, letters and chronicles; autobiography, memoirs and oral history; archives in public and private collections and their use; images, sounds and network resources; how "historical materials" promote "literary research", etc.

Name: Literature and Society in 1920s China
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course adopts the method of special seminars, selects several cases, and analyzes the modern function and position of literature in the complex historical context of China in the 1920s from the perspective of literary sociology. On this basis, it discusses the possibility of reconstructing the research space of modern literature.

Name: Selected Readings in Recent Decade Academic Papers
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects about fifteen academic papers with exemplary significance in the field of modern literature research at home and abroad in the past ten years for study and discussion. On the one hand, it enables students to understand domestic and foreign academic trends and trends, and on the other hand, it helps students learn and learn from professional academic paper writing methods.

Name: Studies in the Novel since the 1990s
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Course Introduction: Since the 1990s, Chinese contemporary literature has published numerous novels. Some of these novels are quite important and represent the artistic achievements of contemporary Chinese novels. How to evaluate these novels is how to evaluate contemporary Chinese literature. This is the literary knowledge and academic ability that students in the Chinese Department must understand and master. This course selects Chen Zhongshi's "White Deer Plain", Jia Pingwa's "Abandoned Capital", Mo Yan's "Big Breasts and Wide Hips", Yan Lianke's "Shouhuo", Liu Zhenyun's "One Sentence is Worth Ten Thousand Sentences", Tien Ning's "Stupid Flower", Su Tong's "River Bank", Zhang Wei's "Remembering Aya" and other works to study and discuss. Have an overall understanding of the literary trend since the 1990s and the achievements of Chinese literature.

Name: New Media Theory and Practice
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The advent of the cyber age has ushered in yet another landmark media revolution in human history. The transformation and transformation of existing cultural patterns through mobile Internet is taking place with a profound butterfly effect, and they highlight the fundamental issue that is at the forefront of academic attention around the world. Not only is there a unique landscape of online literature in China, but the use of indigenous social media, such as microblogging and Twitter, is also leading worldwide. The development of new media will profoundly affect human life patterns, as will profound changes in cultural patterns, including literary ones. The aim of this course is to create a teaching platform that combines theory and practice, while studying important theories of new media in the country and abroad, and to incorporate new media practices that are now taking place. This semester will focus on the model of Twitter, the transformation trajectory of social media (facebook, MSN, twitter) and the Chineseization process (Web for All, QQQ, Twitter). Students are encouraged to create micro-intellectual accounts, practice entry, and theoretical summary and innovation based on practice. The programme will be conducted in the form of a seminar, the recruitment of experts to report, the selection of students for the course will require independent reporting and related practice, and cooperation with other fellow students on practical projects.

Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Drama
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Taking the occurrence and development of modern Chinese drama as the main object of investigation, as well as traditional opera and other drama forms, it studies the multi-faceted aspects of drama art from the perspectives of scripts and performances. On this basis, it considers the local characteristics of Chinese drama and the way of dialogue with world drama art. It reviews key dramatists and drama masterpieces, summarizes the gains and losses of Chinese drama art over the past century, and conducts an essential exploration of the performing arts.

Name: Introduction to Cultural Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The rise of cultural theory is an important historical phenomenon since the 1960s and has had an important impact on Western/Chinese literary and cultural research. This course uses special book selections to introduce, analyze and comment on different aspects of cultural theory and classic works. The course is divided into seven topics, including literary studies and cultural theory, structural-poststructuralist theory, postmodernism theory, postcolonialism theory, cultural studies, Western Marxist theory, feminist theory, etc. Each topic includes two parts: an introduction to the overall outlook of different trends of thought and an intensive reading of the original classics. Students are required to participate in reading and discussion by delineating specific chapters or paragraphs. This course strives to enable students to grasp the basic development context and important ideas of cultural theory, and through the interpretation of classic original works, learn and explore new ideas for studying the history and current situation of Chinese literature/culture.

Name: Introduction to Classic Texts in Western Philosophy and Social Science
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects classic documents from great Western philosophy and social science scientists such as Plato, Aristotle, Thomas More, Hobbes, Locke, Adam Smith, Marx, Nietzsche, and Freud. It introduces the specific historical background of their creation, the issues they address, and their contributions to the formation of the tradition of philosophy and social sciences. It also elucidates the contemporary significance of these classic documents and seeks the enlightening role of these classic documents in building a philosophy and social science system with Chinese characteristics. At the same time, these documents will be compared, interpreted and studied with the classic documents of Chinese philosophy and social sciences since the Tang and Song Dynasties.

Name: Studies in Twenty-First-Century Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Nearly two decades have passed in the twenty-first century. In the past two decades, the form and development path of Chinese literature have undergone major and profound changes. These changes are reflected in all aspects of literature. On the one hand, this course theoretically analyzes the main trends and new trends and growth points of literary transformation since the new century, analyzes the overall form of current literature, and also sorts out the characteristics of literary development from the current situation of cultural development. On the other hand, we study important cases and some representative works of the development of literature in the new century, and clarify the context and historical trend of literature in the new century through sorting out individual cases. Combining theoretical analysis, trend research and close reading of texts to explore the characteristics and expressive methods of new century literature. Let students have a more specific understanding of the development of literature since the new century and discover more issues for in-depth research. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Contemporary Western Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is an introduction to contemporary Western literary theory that has had an important impact on the study of contemporary Chinese literature. Many Western scholars who have entered this course, including Foucault, Lacan, Roland Barthes, Deleuze, Auer Bach, Bakhtin, Lukács, Sean Watt, Benjamin, Butler, Schmidt, Jameson, Žižek, Henry Jenkins, etc., are all giants of thought who have appeared repeatedly in literary studies in the past half century. The thoughts of these modern scholars not only inherited the essence of Western classical humanities, but also made effective responses and reflections on the trend of human civilization and the state of modern thought in the 20th century. They provided a new horizon and method for humanities research, including literary research, and had a huge impact on the knowledge structure, problem awareness, and research paths of literary researchers. Although the theoretical works of these scholars have long been included in the required reading list for graduate students in many majors related to literary studies in the Chinese Department of Peking University, and have become important reference books for related examinations, including the doctoral qualification examination, there has been a lack of concentrated study and discussion of relevant content in the graduate courses of the Chinese Department. This course will be dedicated to filling this gap. Through the mutual reading of theory and practice, while helping students who choose the course enter the forefront of Western thought, it also opens a dialogue between Chinese literature and even cultural and political practice and contemporary Western theory. It not only helps graduate students form a methodological consciousness in academic research and lays a solid theoretical foundation for literary research, but also accumulates knowledge and experience for the generation of Chinese thought and the dialogue between Chinese and Western cultures and even civilizations.

Name: Topics in Literature of the 1950s-1970s
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is divided into 8 special topics to teach the works of classic writers and important literary issues in contemporary Chinese literature from the 1950s to the 1970s. Topic 1 discusses contemporary literary history and national forms; Topic 2 discusses Zhao Shuli, "Three Mile Bay" and folk forms; Topic 3 discusses Liang Bin, "Red Flag Pu" and local forms; Topic 4 discusses Zhou Libo, "Mountain and Countryside Great Changes" and personal style; Topic 5 discusses Liu Qing, "History of Entrepreneurship" and Sinicization; Topic 6 discusses revolutionary popular novels and old forms; Topic 7 discusses Mao Zedong's poetry and the relationship between ancient and modern times; Topic 8 discusses contemporary literature and Chinese narrative issues.

Name: The Art of the Novel
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The long-term neglect of attention and research on the art of novels has made China's novel creations seriously inadequate in terms of artistry. This course aims to change this reading and research pattern and lead the listeners back to texts, literature, and the art of novels.

Name: Topics in Contemporary European and American Critical Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to enable students to understand and master the historical origin, main principles and basic spirit of contemporary European and American critical theory, and to clarify the pluralistic values ​​and evaluation system of contemporary European and American critical theory. This course takes the representative figures and works of European and American critical theory since the 1960s as clues to study the historical background, main terms and viewpoints of various schools of critical theory with different orientations. The critical theorists selected in this course include the theorists of the Frankfurt School, Fannon, Althusser, Lyotard, Roland Barthes, Kristeva, Foucault, Said, Eagleton, De Certeau, Bourdieu, Deleuze and Guattari, Badiou, Rancière, Balibar, Kruger, Agamben, Danto, Groys, Negri, Jameson, Michael Hardt, Butler, Zizek and others. This semester, some of the above-mentioned students will be selected for key lectures. After studying this course, serious students are expected to become familiar with the cutting-edge disciplines of European and American critical theory and have a clear understanding of the macro-trend of world critical theory. _x000D_

Name: Contemporary Fiction and Film
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Starting from case studies and text interpretation, this course explores the adaptation of novels by Chinese films since the 1980s, and analyzes the impact of novels on the development of films. It also focuses on the role of film in the development of the novel. Analyze novel trends and the role of specific works in movies. This enables students to have an in-depth understanding of the similarities and differences in the expression methods of novels and movies, and to have a deeper understanding and understanding of cultural trends and trends since the 1980s.

Name: Film Theory and Critical Practice
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is planned to follow the clues of the history of film theory and use several key issues in film research throughout the organization and teaching of the course. The course starts with the theory and practice of the Soviet montage film school. Through the questioning of the ontology of film in the history of film theory, it enters into the occurrence and development of film semiotics, the theoretical position of psychoanalysis, ideological criticism and genre research, and then explores the discourse network of "post-theoretical theory" and the digital transformation of film. _x000D_
    The course focuses on teaching theoretical context, with occasional sharing and discussion of film criticism practices.

Name: Comparative Poetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Comparative Poetics course is a required course for graduate students majoring in Comparative Literature. This course mainly leads students to carefully read the original classics of Chinese poetry (such as "Wen Xin Diao Long", "Wen Fu", etc.) and their important English translations, and explore the possibility of dialogue between Chinese and Western poetics and the core issues involved in comparison and translation. Through this, on the one hand, it inspires students to think about the similarities and differences between Chinese and Western literary concepts, and on the other hand, it strives to place Chinese poetic thoughts in a larger cultural context for systematic examination. The course is conducted through a combination of teacher-led reading and class discussion. Each student is required to read the designated text in advance and make at least one topic report. Regular grades account for 40%. Submit a paper during the semester and at the end of the semester, each accounting for 30%.

Name: Studies in Twentieth-Century Sino-French Literary Relations
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will focus on the major works related to China in the history of French literature and culture in the 20th century, as well as the important events involved in Sino-French literature and cultural exchanges. For example, the content includes the poetry of Xie Gelan and others, the novels of Malraux and others, the literary theory of Barthes and others, and the sinology of Ai Tianpu and others. The focus is to sort out the impact of Chinese thought and culture on France and the world, and then form a clearer understanding of the phenomenon of "Eastern learning spreading to the West" in the cultural exchanges between East and West in the 20th century, and gain a more comprehensive understanding of our own literature and culture.

Name: Academic English: Comparative Literature and Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: Taught in English, this class will allow students to read and discuss certain fundamental texts in comparative literature and literary theory. Through class discussions, writing assignments and oral presentations, students can hope to achieve a better understanding of these disciplines, as well as improve their mastery of academic English. All reading materials and writing assignments are in English.

Name: Studies in Literature and Intellectual History
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Literature has never existed in isolation. It is not only the artistic expression of social existence, but also has an interdependent dialogue relationship with the development of intellectual history. This course attempts to expand the boundaries of literary research from the unique perspective of interdisciplinary interpretation of classic literary works and, to a certain extent, reconstruct the inherent quality of humanities that directly faces the entire world. We hope that through this effort, we can further demonstrate the irreplaceable role of poetry (literature) in the entire spiritual and political life, and help students understand poetry from a broader background and understand the rich and complex composition of the entire human ideological world from a poetic perspective. _x000D_
The course founder has been paying attention to this issue for many years and has published several works and translations. He is currently hosting a series of books on related topics. Students with a background in literary history and literary theory can take this course. During the teaching process, students and students will mainly read literature on some thinkers' interpretations of literary works, and on this basis, they will sort out issues that can be studied in depth. _x000D_

Name: Second Foreign Language: French (II)
Introduction: The course is a basic French-language course offered by a zero-basic graduate school, which is open during the spring semester.

Name: Marxism and Literary Criticism
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course will cover classic and contemporary Marxist literary and art criticism theories, as well as Marxist cultural and social theories. Topics that may be covered this semester include: literature, art, history and cultural theory (analysis of base and superstructure, reflection theory and typical theory, Walter Benjamin’s concept of dialectical imagery, Hu Feng and Zhou Yang’s debate on typical issues), literary art and ideological criticism, Raymond Williams theory of sensory structure, Bourdieu's "literary field" theory, Frederic Jameson's historical literary criticism, cultural sociology); the form and content of literature and art (Marx's dialectics of form and content, Marxism and formalism, Lukács and literary form, Freud Rideric Jameson's Poetics of Social Forms); literature as production; aesthetics and politics (aesthetics and historical perspectives in literary criticism, writers and tendencies, the politics of literature and the literature of politics, the debate between Benjamin, Adorno and Brecht on aesthetics and politics, Terry. Eagleton's theory of aesthetic ideology, Jacques Rancière's theory of dissension); Marxism and Chinese literature and art (the debate on the human nature and class nature of literature and art, the politicization, depoliticization and repoliticization of modern and contemporary Chinese literature, the Chinese form of Marxist literary criticism), etc. The purpose of this course is to expect students to have a clearer understanding of the theoretical characteristics, key propositions, development and critical methods of Marxist literary criticism based on careful reading and understanding of relevant classic texts. Teachers give lectures, students make a presentation on an issue of interest, and submit a paper at the end of the semester. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course is designed to introduce students to representative works of literary criticism among Marxist tradition in the West and East. The main objective of the course is to raise students` awareness and understanding of key concepts, main characteristics, methodologies, and debates in Marxist literary theory.

Name: Studies in Chinese Narrative Singing Arts
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
The art of rapping was born very early, but its research started late; it has been continued in life, but the research is not systematic and relatively weak. _x000D_
This course intends to explore the development of rap art since the Tang and Song Dynasties, the relationship between rap art and social economic and cultural customs, the relationship between rap art and popular literature, and the research on rap art since the 20th century, to inspire and guide students to have a deeper understanding and recognition of Chinese rap art and its research. Courses are conducted through a combination of lectures and discussions. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Folk Legends
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: As a major genre of folk literature, compared to myths and stories, folklore has relatively weak theoretical construction, but is rich in case studies and has considerable academic depth. On the basis of a systematic introduction to the theory and historical framework of legend studies, this course focuses on the cutting-edge trends in the field of legend research in recent years. Then, some of the most influential cases are selected for students to study and form reports respectively for class discussion. It is hoped that through one semester of teaching and seminars, students can fully enter the research field of legends and develop basic research literacy.

Name: Structuralist Mythology
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
Introduce and evaluate the mythological thought of French anthropologist Lévi-Strauss. Including Lévi-Strauss's life, sources of thought, views of structuralist linguistics, basic concepts and specific analysis methods of structuralist mythology, Lévi-Strauss's answers to classic questions such as wild thinking, myth and life, myth and ritual, myth and history, myth and music, and the death of myth. Finally, an example is given to illustrate how to use the structuralist method to analyze Chinese myths. _x000D_
The purpose of teaching is to enable students to broaden their horizons and master the basic viewpoints and methods of structuralist mythology. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Folklore Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course focuses on the representative theories and methods in the history of folklore theoretical research, including comparative mythology theory, myth-ritual theory, functionalism theory, psychoanalytic theory, structuralism theory, feminist theory, etc.

Name: Religious Law and Religious Belief
Introduction: The purpose of the curriculum is: Religious law is the foundation for the existence of the Order, an important link between monks and believers, and an important guarantee of the maintenance of religious observance. Religious law is therefore an important subject of religious science research. Religious law studies are a key to understanding religious beliefs and to understanding them. At the same time, religious law and secular law are both common and different, and religious law often has various effects on secular society as a cultural tradition. Therefore, religious law research is also a key to understanding different religious backgrounds and national cultural traditions. The purpose of this course is to take advantage of the resources of teachers in the Department of Philosophy and Religions, with six teachers providing a comprehensive and systematic introduction of religious laws from a different religious perspective. (c) To direct students to an objective understanding of religious phenomena and of the many cultural factors underlying religious laws and laws. Summary of the modules: Module I: Catholicism (Professor Seo Yong Fei) I. Brief description: It is understood that religious law is one of the manifestations of religious content, one of the manifestations of religious reason, and that, from the point of view of the Christian religion, particularly the Roman Episcopal Church, the Church has the power to legislate, and its powers are derived from a variety of sources, and its laws have the grounds and scope of application. On the other hand, from the point of view of the Christian religion, and in particular of the Roman Patriarchate, the State must also have its legislation and its laws governing relations between the State and the Church, such as religious organizations (note: these are two interrelated and different legal concepts) to regulate the conduct and powers, duties and obligations of the State and religious organizations (such as churches). ii. Course organization: (two weeks, 4 hours) 1. Foundations of church legislation, laws of churches (CIC) Examples of church law (e.g. “administrative law”, “marriage law”, “property administration law”), legal relations between the State and church References: Scowburn's Bible, CIC, GG Module II: Orthodox Church (Professor Xue Fenglin) I. The Status and Basic Composition of the Orthodox Church Statutes II. Source and history of the Holy Apostolic Code III. OVERVIEW OF THE CONTEXT OF THE STATE OF STATES (85 in total) Module III: Islam (Associate Professor Sha Zongping) I. Brief description: Through classroom teaching and classroom discussions, it is hoped that the students will first grasp the flexible, interactive and pragmatic relationship between the Islamic faith and the Islamic Shari ' a, and articulate the Islamic heritage of the Arab traditional culture, as well as the social identity of the Shari ' a that serves Muslim societies and interests. II. Curriculum (two weeks for a total of four lessons): The Holy Koran and the Islamic Shariah 2. The Holy Spirit and Islamic Shariah References: The Quran, Machen translation, China Social Sciences Press, 1981 edition, 1996 edition. “Buhari Sanctuary”, Beijing: Chinese Press for Social Sciences, 1981. " Sant'Zhui " , Ma Xian, Beijing: Religious Cultural Press, 2002. Encyclopedia of Holy Instructions in Bouhari, full volume, Portable translation, Hong Kong Foundation Publishing Ltd., 2007. Module IV: Buddhism (Associate Professor Wang Song) Introduction Buddhist law is very rich. The Buddhist monks have established strict legal norms in the self-resolved Garonni era. These laws, as one of the three collections of literature, have become the central part of the cultural resources of Buddhist thought. The Chinese monks began to seek justice in the times of the North and South, and many of the high monks, like Fahsi, were involved in their quest for justice. In the era of Kantang, the Handi Buddhist religion established a legal system with the quartet as the norm, followed by the emergence of the Zen Chong, which established rules unique to China. It is an important means of promoting Buddhist ideas and has an impact on Taoism and other cultural traditions. II. Curriculum (two weeks for a total of four lessons): The translation process in China 2. The development and inheritance of Indian precepts References: Third Book of Chinese Buddhism, Knowledge Publishing House, 1984. Sanctuary, Quarter. Module V: Taoism (Associate Professor Cheng Lo Song) I. Brief description: There is a strict system of discipline in the church, which is closely associated with social life, and strict norms of behaviour are the basis for the religious faith and its effectiveness. In the course of history, there has been a proliferation of discipline, discipline and discipline, which has led to complex hierarchical systems. Different denominations have different types and content of discipline: on the one hand, it is a prerequisite for life-purification practices and, on the other, it guarantees the effectiveness of ritual services. The system of ceremonial life and the norms of conduct, as well as the ethical and faith principles that govern the practice of faith at home, are part of the law. Another function of science is to be the premise and foundation of the spirituality and the legacy of mystical technology, so that the religious science itself carries with it a sense of mysticalism. The Part of the Taoist Church discusses the jurisprudence of the Taoist faith, mainly from the two dimensions of history and practice of belief, and spectral discussions are conducted in conjunction with the behaviour and cultural taboos of ancient Chinese cultural traditions. II. Curriculum (two weeks for a total of four lessons): 1. Science and fasting: action in the shaping of beliefs Cultural implications of discipline: from faith to life References: Chen Yooting: The Taoist Monument, Religious and Cultural Press, 2003. Module VI: Confucianism (Professor Zheng Kai) I. Brief description: Since ancient times, the Confucian family has been known for its ritualism. The etiquette holds a secular ethical, clan-blooded dimension and is also embedded in elements of sanctity. While the study of the secular ethics of comity has been rich, insufficient attention has been paid to the religious colours inherent in its sanctity. The course will discuss the relationship between Confucian courtesy and law and will be analysed using religious science as a means of broadening students ' multidimensional understanding of traditional culture. II. Curriculum (two weeks for a total of four lessons): 1. Religious dimensions of protocol Relationship between comity and law References: Zheng Zheng Zheng, Inter se, Triple Press, 2008.

Name: Selected Readings in Classic Works of Folklore Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The symbol and communication is one of the fundamental theories of folklore research, and the study of the subject gives students a preliminary understanding of the theory.

College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature

Executive summary:

Intangible cultural heritage issues

In order to change the current pattern of graduate studies and to broaden the professional horizons of students, it has been decided to invite, as far as possible, teachers from foreign departments and even from foreign schools to teach courses, to be freely available to invited scholars in the context of folk culture, and to gather the relevant works of the scholars on the basis of their lectures, so as to gain an understanding of the state of advanced research in the academic world and gradually become a member of the “preventive” community.

Name: Studies in Eastern Mythology
Introduction: This course mainly uses mythology theory to study and discuss the classical myths of the ancient East and the living myths of modern Eastern countries. The goal of the course is for doctoral students to become proficient in mythological theories and methods, and to comprehensively use anthropological and folklore theories to deeply analyze and interpret Eastern mythology. Doctoral students are required to have relatively systematic theoretical knowledge of oriental folk literature and general folk literature.

Name: Modern Academic History of Chinese Folk Literature Studies
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
It was only in the 20th century that Chinese folk literature and popular literature truly entered the academic field and became a humanities subject in the modern sense. Although its history is not long enough, it has achieved considerable results in this century or so due to the profound heritage of Chinese folk literature and popular literature as well as the discipline's efforts to track the world's academic frontiers since its inception. However, due to the vicissitudes of the twentieth century, its fate also experienced ups and downs, with its ups and downs and gains and losses, which can quite arouse the interest of academic history. _x000D_
This course will focus on the perspective of subject history, focus on the exploration of academic theories, and strive to get as close to history as possible, understand the specific background of its ins and outs, and grasp tradition more accurately on the basis of being close to tradition. _x000D_
The teaching method of this course is equal emphasis on teacher lectures and student reports and discussions. Students finally submit a paper to obtain grades.

Name: Marxist Literary Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is mainly for MJC’s professional master’s degree in creative writing. In the overall framework of the historical development and evolution of Marxism, we focus on examining theoretical propositions with contemporary issues, sorting out the historical extension of these basic issues in the formation, development and dissemination of Marxist literary theory, and through careful reading of the texts of Marxist literary and artistic discussions, we will gain an in-depth understanding of the literary and artistic thoughts and their internal logical relationships of important Marxist theorists such as Marx, Engels, Lenin, Mao Zedong and Lukács. _x000D_
Combination of lectures and discussions, no more than 50 people. _x000D_
Students are required to read the original classics intensively, think about the methodological significance of the theorist's thoughts, and organically connect theoretical learning with thinking about practical issues, so as to strengthen the construction of their Marxist worldview from the perspective of professional learning. _x000D_

Name: Introduction to Original Texts of Modern British and American Poetry
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course will lead students to read the original works of British and American modern poetry, allowing them to understand the history of the development of British and American modern poetry and improve their ability to read the original texts. The selection of poems begins with British Romanticism, and the main poets will include William Blake, William Wordsworth, W.B.Yeats from the UK, and Emily Dickenson and Robert Frost from the United States. Self-compiled teaching materials. Each poet's works will be selected more comprehensively, rather than just one poem per person, so that students can have a comprehensive grasp of them.

Name: Studies and Creative Writing in Classical Poetry and Prose
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
In view of the lack of basic knowledge of classical literary styles among graduate students studying ancient literature, especially in appreciation and criticism, some misunderstandings caused by unfamiliarity with ancient literary styles, and also because ancient Chinese literary styles, represented by poems, lyrics, tunes, and poems, still have a considerable degree of use value in contemporary literary creation, so this course is offered on the research and creation of ancient poetry. The main content of this course is training in the research and writing of ancient Chinese literary styles. The content mainly includes: 1. The study of stylistic theories of ancient Chinese rhyme prose styles such as poems, lyrics, tunes, fus, and couplets; 2. The writing training of poems, lyrics, tunes, fuses, couplets, and other ancient Chinese rhyme prose styles. The course is mainly divided into the following parts:_x000D_
1. Introduction to ancient literary styles and the application of ancient literary styles in contemporary times;_x000D_
2. The structure and rhythm of ancient and modern poetry;_x000D_
3. Essentials of ancient poetry theory—emotional theory, xingji theory, allegory theory, legal theory, etc.; _x000D_
4. Rhythm and filling method;_x000D_
5. Writing in "Fu" style, parallel prose and couplets. _x000D_
6. Five-law writing training; _x000D_
7. Seven-Law Writing Training; _x000D_
8. Five unique writing training; _x000D_
9. Qijue Writing Training; _x000D_
10. Word-writing training; _x000D_
11. Writing training in "Fu" style, parallel prose and couplets.

Name: Studies and Creative Writing in Modern Poetry and Prose
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is aimed at master's students majoring in creative writing in the Department of Chinese Language and Literature. On the basis of introducing the basic knowledge of modern poetry and criticism, it guides students to try the writing of modern poetry and related criticism practices. The course is conducted in the form of discussion and consists of two parts: First, select key poets' poems and critical documents, conduct a careful text reading in class, grasp the aesthetic style and language characteristics of modern poetry, and analyze different criticism strategies; second, students who choose the course take out their own poetry works, discuss and comment on them in class, further revise them after class, and finally submit them as coursework.

Name: Studies in Contemporary Foreign Novels
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course selects contemporary foreign novels with profound influence, novels by writers who have won the Nobel Prize, Booker Prize or other awards, such as Atwood's "The Blind Assassin", Oe Kenzaburo's "Water Death", Pamuk's "Snow", Philip Roth's "The Filth of Humanity" and "Ten Seconds from the Sun", "The Book of Wind", etc. The artistic expression methods of contemporary foreign novels, the variation of tradition and modernism in Western modern novels, the relationship between contemporary Western novels and Western ideological trends, the changes in Western novels in the 21st century, and the conditions and problems of all these foreign novels are compared with the problems we face in Chinese contemporary novels, especially novels, to reveal the changes in contemporary world literature and the possibility of Chinese novels, and to find a way for Chinese literature to enter the world and dialogue with the contemporary trends of world literature.

Name: Professional Internship
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: The professional master's degree in creative writing is based on the profound foundation of Chinese and foreign literature and culture, and emphasizes the cultivation of practical creative ability. To this end, students are required to go deep into relevant enterprises and institutions during the study period, such as news organizations, new media, writers associations, film and television companies, advertising and culture companies, etc. to conduct teaching internships, complete internship works, and receive internship appraisal opinions from the internship unit. The teacher in charge will comprehensively consider the student's internship works and the appraisal opinions issued by the internship unit, and give a qualified or unqualified evaluation. Specific requirements: 1. Internship time: no less than four weeks, and it needs to be a full-time internship; 2. Internship works should be related to the internship work and truly reflect the students' actual work ability. 3. Internship unit. The nature of the work in the internship unit needs to be the same as or close to the creative writing training direction and training goals. The internship unit can be a self-selected internship unit approved by the teacher, or an internship unit arranged by the teacher. 4. Internship results, internship report and internship appraisal opinions should be submitted within two weeks after the internship.

Name: Chinese Literature of the Last Three Decades of the Twentieth Century
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course is basically a macroscopic study. However, this kind of macroscopic research is based on microscopic interpretation and is based on the analysis of specific texts_x000D_
and the analysis of some important historical details to present the context of historical development. This course has the intention of helping students understand the 20th century_x000D_
The literature of this period in the last 30 years also enables students to perceive a research idea and a research method. _x000D_
While this course rationally explains a series of literary phenomena, it will also attach great importance to cultivating students' perceptual abilities. Because in the instructor's opinion_x000D_
, to grasp literature, rationality alone is not enough - overemphasis on rationality may even make it impossible to approach literature. In Scientism for Scholarship_x000D_
Today, in the mainstream of research, there are very serious problems in literary research. When living literature is studied with a kind of surgical dissection, we treat literature_x000D_
Learning has lost its proper artistic feeling. This course will promote an attitude towards studying literature: be a reader first, then an interpreter.

Name: Introduction to Western Literary Works
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course is mainly offered to graduate students majoring in creative writing. It selects several representative works of an important writer (specific selections are attached separately) to study them carefully with classmates, and jointly understand the "intention of writing" of excellent authors. While studying specific literary works, students are also recommended and guided to read some important works on literary reading by famous literary critics and writers (such as Auerbach, Bloom, Calvino, etc.). The course is mainly taught by teachers. Course tests are conducted during the semester, and students are required to write reading reports at the end of the semester. Regular grades account for 60%; final grades account for 40%.

Name: Contemporary Nature Poetics
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: This course takes the writing of natural landscapes by contemporary poets as the research horizon, and takes the rise of natural themes in the development of contemporary poetry as a clue. It focuses on the literary relationship between contemporary poetry and natural themes, the relationship between the writing of nature poetry and contemporary ecological culture, the attitude of contemporary poets towards landscape poetry, and the self-reshaping of the subjectivity of contemporary poetry reflected behind this change.

Name: Studies in Popular Culture
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:
This course intends to lead students to discuss important contemporary popular culture phenomena, and select phenomenal film and television works, online literature, animation games, etc. for discussion. It is planned to sort out the important ideological threads of cultural studies theory on the basis of textualization of phenomena, and learn and try to use these theories to deal with relevant social and cultural propositions. _x000D_
Students who choose the course are required to read all required theoretical books, submit two reading reports (more than 4,000 words), give a keynote speech and participate in all academic seminars.

Name: Research and Writing on Online Literature Theory
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction:

History of Museum Development
Introduction: This course teaches the history of museum construction in different regions and allows students to think about the functions of contemporary museums and the requirements of contemporary society for museums. Museums have always been regarded as a product of modern society and have undergone major changes in the past three hundred years: they have evolved from a treasure chest of European aristocrats to a museum shared by citizens; from a place of higher education to a visiting venue suitable for all ages; and from a learning center that imparts knowledge to a city landmark for interactive communication. The above changes directly affect the museum’s collection direction, exhibition content, display layout, promotion and marketing and other aspects of development. The course starts with the background of museums established in Europe in the early years, and then moves to the Americas, Asia and other countries.
