Name: Studies in Modern Chinese Social History
Introduction: The course is mainly targeted at postgraduate students majoring in modern Chinese history. The purpose is to basically master the methods and characteristics of social history research through the course, grasp the basic situation and content of modern Chinese social history research, and be able to use social history methods to conduct research on issues related to modern Chinese history. In the past ten years, the study of modern Chinese history has gradually attracted the attention of the academic community and has become an important and promising field in the discipline. It has broadened the research perspective and the materials available for use. A number of good research results have been published, and the use of its methodology has also received more and more attention. However, overall it is still relatively weak, and further research needs to be deepened to facilitate development. The course content covers the two periods of the Republic of China and the People's Republic of China. The teaching is divided into theoretical parts and research special topics. The special topics focus on social changes in China's rural areas, social stratification research, social power structure research, organization and unit research, social mobilization research, social behavior research, etc. Students are required to carefully read relevant reference works, combine lectures, write reports and discussions, and complete relevant short papers, striving to partially reach publication level and prepare for graduation thesis.

Name: Studies in the History of the Republic of China
Introduction:
This course attempts to be offered in the form of a "joint study class" (different from reading discussion classes). The theme "China in the 1920s" is chosen to allow students to directly participate in the research and practice of specific issues. Students are guided to select a specific topic, from data collection, literature retrieval, text interpretation, to problem analysis and theoretical refining, and finally to writing, to conduct a full-scale training in research skills. The initial plan is to complete a full program of training in two semesters. _x000D_
_x000D_
In China's nearly 100-year history, there have been several major transition years. The 1920s were not only a transitional period for the Republic of China from the Beijing government controlled by the Beiyang warlords (military rule) to the Nanjing government controlled by the Kuomintang (party rule), but also a critical period for the founding and rise of the Communist Party of China, and the cooperation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party to launch the national revolution. It was also an important transition period for China's diplomacy, economy, society, and culture. Since modern times, the pace of historical change has accelerated greatly. Introducing the perspective of "era" into the investigation of modern China can highlight this changing trend. Using "era" instead of "event" as a boundary marker is helpful for the observation of politics, economy, society, and culture. Generally speaking, it is a new attempt to explore the historical evolution and historical complexity within a short period of time in a more detailed manner with a "ten-year" period. _x000D_

The basic contents include: (1) Utilization of reference books. (2) Accumulation of old and new historical materials. (3) Review of existing research. (4) Utilization of database. (5) Topic selection of the paper. (6) Writing of thesis. (7) Writing of book reviews. (8) Technical specifications and annotation style. (9) Modification of the paper. (10) Publication of papers.

Name: Studies in Major Issues of the History of the CPC
Introduction: The main content of the course is to sort out a number of major issues in various periods in the history of the Communist Party of China, such as the establishment of the Communist Party of China, the cooperation between the Kuomintang and the Communist Party, the Long March issue, the Western Route Army issue, the Gao-Rao issue, the history of the Cultural Revolution, etc. Use detailed information to conduct detailed sorting and in-depth research on these issues, guide students to look at issues from a historical perspective, help students deeply understand and comprehensively grasp major issues in the history of the Communist Party of China, and enable students to become familiar with and master the basic historical issues and theoretical issues of the Communist Party of China, as well as the basic experience and basic laws of the Chinese revolution, construction and reform.

Name: Studies in the Theory and Sources of Modern Chinese Historiography
Introduction: This course is mainly for doctoral students in this major. Historical theory is the main thread that connects complex historical phenomena, historical methods are the basic means of historical research, and historical documents are the basis of historical research. Only the organic combination of the three can more deeply and accurately understand and grasp the inevitable laws of human historical development. This course is in the form of a special study, with China's modern history as the main object of analysis. Through the introduction and research of Eastern and Western traditional and modern historical theories, historical research methods, the purpose and form of historical compilation, the collection, arrangement, analysis, and application of historical documents, it strives to give students a correct and scientific view of history, understand and master the latest Eastern and Western historical theories and methods, and cultivate students' basic abilities and literacy in historical research.

Name: Studies in the History of Nazi Germany
Introduction: The course involves a series of important issues in the study of the history of Nazi Germany, such as: Did Hitler have a worldview? Why did the Nazis call themselves "national socialists" rather than "fascists"? What was the social basis of the Nazi movement? How do you evaluate the Nazi's economic, social and cultural policies? Why did the Nazis start the war? What are its war goals? Why did the Nazis massacre European Jews? What kind of postwar "New European Order" did the Nazis envision? How did the Nazi empire come to ruin? etc. While cultivating students' interest in learning German and European modern history, the course will also provide training and assistance in reading and analyzing historical materials according to specific needs. The course relies on the Internet and multimedia teaching equipment, focusing on the use of electronic maps and photos, as well as historical documentaries and teaching films. The course requires students to actively participate in class reports and discussions, and requires reading ability in English or German. Representative works of the lecturer: Li Wei: Deutsche Pl?ne zur europ?ischen wirtschaftlichen Neuordnung 1939-1945, Hamburg: Verlag Dr. Kovac, 2007. Chinese translation: Li Wei: "Nazi Germany's Plan for the "New European Economic Order" 1939-1945", Hamburg: Verlag Dr. Kovac, 2007.

Name: Topics in the History of American Foreign Relations
Research Methods and Thesis Writing in World History
Introduction:
This course is a required course for postgraduate students majoring in World History in the Department of History at Peking University. It aims to introduce and discuss the basic research objects and related methods of the world history discipline, and discuss the theories, norms, rules and methods of thesis writing in conjunction with the writing of master's and doctoral theses. The research methods section will be divided into three parts: ancient world history, European and American modern history, and Asian and African modern history. The focus is to highlight the characteristics of each major and pay attention to the integrity of world history research. The paper writing part will discuss the general writing characteristics of papers, understand the basic elements of academic papers, and focus on issues such as normative technical processing. _x000D_
_x000D_
   The course consists of multiple topics, including research methods on ancient world history, research methods on medieval world history, research methods on European and American modern history, research methods on Asian and African modern history, an overview of world history historical materials, language tools for world history, the generality of essay writing, the particularity of world history essays, knowledge structure and originality of essays, legal and moral issues of essays, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
   Course Features: Combining world history research methods with thesis writing, allowing students to realize that academic research is the basis for thesis writing. It not only introduces general essay writing methods, but also combines world history research and essay writing in various majors. Based on the dissertation requirements of Peking University, this paper analyzes the history and current situation of our department's dissertation, and specifically solves some problems and deficiencies in the writing of our department's world history dissertation. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Process of Global Modernization
Introduction to the History of Knowledge and the Book
Introduction:
The main purpose of this course is to introduce two historical fields that are still "new" to domestic academic circles - the history of knowledge and the history of books - by reading a number of pioneering or exemplary research works. In addition to the historical clues constituted by the knowledge content itself and the macro-political and social environment, the history of knowledge and books pay more attention to the basic, daily and instrumental practices (such as the accumulation of notes, the writing of footnotes, the compilation of indexes, the production of experimental instruments, etc.) and the carrying The material media of knowledge has, to a great extent, changed the scale and framework of traditional intellectual history, academic history, science history, literary history, and philology. It has formed a number of novel interdisciplinary topics and represents a development trend that cannot be ignored in the current international academic community. Its influence on the study of Chinese literature and history is also increasingly apparent. Regardless of whether they are graduate students in Chinese history or world history, it is helpful to have a more systematic understanding of the basic issues and research methods of intellectual history and book history based on their own interests, which will be helpful in broadening their horizons, enriching their ideas, and choosing research directions. _x000D_
        The reading list we have drawn up covers some influential works in the international academic community that have Chinese translations. The research objects of these works mainly focus on the changes in the production, circulation and organization of knowledge from the emergence of printed books to the formation of modern society. The topics include not only the origins of modern science and modern history in the West, but also the culture of scholars and imperial examination culture in China after the Song Dynasty. Concentrated and systematic reading of these works, followed by comparison, analysis and discussion under the guidance of teachers, will enable students to have a deeper understanding of issues and methods in the history of knowledge and books, and be able to learn from and apply them in their respective research work. _x000D_
        The course takes the form of a discussion class. The pace is based on the principle of reading and discussing one monograph every week. Depending on the length and difficulty of the book, you can select readings or supplement other materials as appropriate. Each student is required to submit a brief written response to the work they have read that week before each class, posing questions for discussion. In class, one or a group of students will give an oral report, introducing the book's ideas, arguments, author and academic background in more detail, and then other students will discuss based on the written responses and oral reports. Grading will be based on participation and contribution to discussions and the quality of oral presentations. There will be no final assignments or exams.

Name: Studies in Machiavelli
Introduction:
This course is a professional elective course for graduate students in the Department of History. It is taught to master's and doctoral students who are interested in Italian history, European history, and the history of European political thought. _x000D_
The basic idea of the course: Mainly based on the following considerations - Machiavelli is a thinker that universities in Western countries pay great attention to. Most universities offer courses about him, and "The Prince" is a must-read classic for college students. Chinese universities currently pay insufficient attention and must change this situation; Chinese academic circles pay more attention to Machiavelli, but less based on reading the complete works of Machiavelli, especially his original works in Italian. At the same time, they basically rely on the research results of the English academic community, and it is difficult to see the results of the Italian academic community. This course attempts to make up for this shortcoming; I have taught "Intensive Reading of Machiavelli "The Prince"" for 6 years, and I feel it is necessary to expand the comprehensive study of Machiavelli on this basis; my academic field is In the modern history of Italy, it has offered undergraduate and postgraduate courses such as "Italian Great Thinkers", "Italian History Special Topics", "Italian History Research", etc., and has a foundation for studying Machiavelli; through teaching Machiavelli, it cultivates students majoring in world history to have an understanding of the history of ideas. Interested in, especially attention to Italian thinkers, I hope young scholars will study the history of Italian thought; Machiavelli is a highly original thinker. Through studying him, you can appreciate the charm of original ways of thinking, which will help improve the quality of academic research. _x000D_
Course features: Examine Machiavelli from the perspective of the general history of Italy and the history of Western civilization, pay attention to the relationship between individuals and society, pay attention to the relationship between ideas, theories, methods, and historical materials, try to explore Machiavelli’s background and original ideas, and strive to introduce the latest research results of himself, Italy, and Western academia. _x000D_
Course content: Using a topic-based explanation method, 16 topics are designed on Machiavelli's 500-year research history, Machiavelli's life, political activities, works, thoughts, etc. One topic is taught in each course. _x000D_
Purpose of the course: Through studying this course, graduate students can comprehensively understand the relevant issues of this founder of Western political science and his important position in the history of Italian and Western thought; increase interest in the history of Italian thought and the history of Western thought and civilization by drawing parallels and connecting the past with the next; recognize the importance of original thinkers, which is conducive to the formation of original research habits; expand the scope of academic cognition and maintain an open academic mind. _x000D_
I have been engaged in the teaching and research of Italian history and modern history since 1996. I have a good understanding of Italian history research information at home and abroad. I have published some research results, taught many courses in Italian history and European history, and have good academic accumulation. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Postwar Japanese History
Introduction: Japan's post-war history refers to the history of Japan after 1945, and learning from that history can accurately capture the process of transformation of Japan's internal and external policies, the nature of society and its characteristics, from the defeat of war to the reform of occupation, from economic revival to rapid growth, from economic to political power, from pacifism, conservativeism, big-Powerism and nationalism. I have taught the general history of Japan in the past, as well as the history of Japan at different stages, and it is planned, on the basis of in-depth discussions in the classroom, not only to give listeners a sense of the history of a given country at a given stage, but also to make a comparative analysis of the history of the same stages of development in different countries of the world.

Name: Intellectual History of Japan's Warrior-Government Era
Introduction:
One of the striking features of Japan's historical development is that after the decline of the ancient dynastic state, the military group, or samurai, held power for a long time. This is particularly striking in East Asia, which was widely influenced by ancient Chinese civilization with Confucianism at its core. From the theory of bushido that was popular in Japan after World War II, we can see that Japan’s basic views on bushido constructed before the war still dominate Japanese people’s understanding of bushido to this day. It provides important ideological support for the continuation of Japanese political conservatism and the rise of new nationalism. Bushido is often generally regarded as a certain moral tradition of Japanese warriors. However, in the approximately eight hundred years of development history, the samurai experienced a huge transformation from leaders of local agricultural operations to parasites of the urban commodity economy. The form of combat also evolved from single-horse battles of military nobles to organized large-scale combat. Correspondingly, their moral concepts inevitably experienced profound changes. In order to gain a deeper understanding of how this characteristic of Japan's historical development came to be? What impact did the long-term existence of the samurai regime have on the historical development of Japan? This course will start from the perspective of intellectual history, in chronological order, select eight topics of great significance in each era, and explore the historical development of the Japanese samurai era. Name: History of Japanese Historiography
Introduction: On the whole, the research methods in Japanese history circles are mainly empirical, but with the changes of the times, their theories and methods have also changed significantly. This course explores the development and changes of Japanese history research in Japanese historical circles since the Meiji Restoration. On the basis of having a certain knowledge of Japanese history research, it provides an in-depth grasp of the theories and methods of Japanese history research in Japanese historical circles.

Name: Readings in Turkic and Uyghur Historical Sources
Introduction: In the class, ancient Turkic stone carvings and unearthed written materials related to the Second Turkic Khanate, the Uighur Khanate, the Xizhou Uighur Kingdom and the Gaochang Uighur era were selected to cultivate students' awareness and basic methods of using ancient Turkic historical materials. Combining records in Chinese and other written materials, we explore some interesting issues in the history of Turkic-speaking peoples in eastern Eurasia from the 8th to the 14th century. This course requires students to have basic knowledge of ancient Turkic language, have previously taken the course "Introduction to Uighur Literature in Ancient Turkic Language", or have a good grasp of one or more modern or medieval Turkic languages. Teachers distribute self-compiled handouts and other materials in class.

Name: Interpreting Japanese Historical Sources
Introduction: Chinese scholars engaged in Japanese studies are not good at reading historical materials in Houwen or Hanwenxundu style. This is because they do not know the grammar of ancient Japanese very well. This course first explains the principles of ancient Japanese and Chinese reading, and then interprets Japanese historical materials from ancient times to modern times. I hope that students can use their own abilities to analyze and solve problems in Japanese history.

Name: Studies in Postwar Japanese Political History
Introduction: The current political situation in Japan is in chaos, which has also had an impact on Sino-Japanese relations. Studying postwar Japanese political history can accurately grasp the background, process, characteristics, and end of the formation of the postwar Japanese political system (the so-called "55-year system"). At the same time, it can conduct in-depth analysis of postwar Japan's decision-making process, political process, national political participation, and the relationship between mass media and politics. I have taught the general history of Japan and Japanese history at different stages in the past, and plan to invite Japanese experts in this field to teach some chapters. Based on in-depth discussions in the classroom, not only will the listeners grasp the essence of Japanese politics, but also a comparative analysis of the politics of other countries around the world.

Name: Historical Transformations of Africa-Arab-Europe Relations from a Cross-Cultural Perspective
Introduction:
In view of Africa's long history of exchanges with the Arab world and Europe, Africans today bear a deep cultural imprint of Arab and European cultures, especially language and religious beliefs. How did Africans adopt Arab and European culture? What twists and turns or conflicts did you experience during this period? What problems are you currently facing? These questions require research and analysis of historical documents to answer. _x000D_
The circle of African historians has paid great attention to the relationship between Europe and Africa during the colonial period, but has not yet paid much attention to the relationship between Africa and Arabia in the early period. To this end, I applied for a research course on the history of African-Arab relations two years ago. During the teaching process of this course, I realized that the relationship between Africa and Arabs is inextricably linked with Europe, so it is necessary to introduce Europe, that is, to expand the original research on the history of African-Arab relations into the research on the history of African-Arab and European relations. _x000D_
This course will focus on North Africa, West Africa and East Africa where Africa, Arabia and Europe meet from a cross-cultural perspective. By reading relevant documents and materials, we will find the cultural connections therein. For example, in view of the current emergence of extremist forces in the name of Islam in North Africa, West Africa and the Horn of East Africa, and Islam was introduced by the Arabs of the Arabian Peninsula, it is necessary to study the development, changes and current situation of Islam in Africa. The historical changes of Islam in Africa reflect the relationship between Africa, Arabia and Europe. _x000D_
    This course is based on the field investigations conducted by the lecturer in Africa in recent years, the relevant materials collected, and the African studies direction of the graduate students, which is related to Arabic language or Arab culture, and European colonialism. The course is aimed at undergraduates, masters or doctoral students who are interested in this research direction. It aims to guide students to promote the breadth and depth of African history research, while understanding and mastering the historical changes in African-Arab-European relations and its importance to the current development of Africa. _x000D_
_x000D_
2. Course Setting_x000D_
This course will be divided into the following four units, each unit is four weeks and 12 credit hours: _x000D_
The first is the syllabus and general introduction, including the definition of culture and cross-cultural theory; an overview of the population and geography of Africa, Arabia and Europe); _x000D_
The second is the relationship between Africa and Arabia and its historical changes, including the arrival of the Arabs and their rule of North Africa; the spread of Islam in Africa and its conflict and integration with African culture; the rise and decline of the Trans-Saharan trade route and its role in Africa-Arab relations; _x000D_
The third is the relationship between Africa and Europe and its historical changes, including the classical era, the Middle Ages, the colonial period, and the cultural connections between African countries and Europe after independence;_x000D_
The fourth is to summarize and synthesize the historical changes in African-Arab-European relations, including comparative studies of the impact of Arab culture and European culture on Africa and their existing challenges, and attempts to enrich or correct existing cultural theories. _x000D_

Name: The Maritime Silk Road
Introduction:
In 2019, the "Historical and Cultural Research on the Maritime Silk Road and Zheng He's Voyages to the West" project of the Department of History was officially launched. This project is an important practice for the history discipline to serve the national “One Belt, One Road” initiative. At the same time, through this project, it will drive and strengthen the construction of related disciplines in the Department of History, further leverage the advantages of the department’s traditional disciplines, and plan for future discipline development and construction. _x000D_
As an important part of the implementation of this project, this course will be conducted by a number of experts from the Department of History who have research foundations on the Maritime Silk Road, as well as some experts from external units, to conduct special lectures and discussions on several major issues of the Maritime Silk Road in history, to cultivate the academic interest of graduate students and undergraduates in the Maritime Silk Road, and to cultivate reserve talents for the research on this topic.

Name: Topics in Latin American History
Introduction: Through thematic research on major issues in the history and modernization process of Latin America, we will deepen our understanding of the modern history of Asia and Africa, improve our theoretical level and ability to analyze problems, and lay the foundation for further research. It is required to conduct discussions and write papers with certain academic content on the basis of reading a wealth of Chinese and foreign literature.

Name: Introduction to the Literature on Nationalism (Part 1)
Introduction: Nationalism is an important phenomenon in the modern history of the world, and related issues such as ideology, political movements, and nation-state construction are important dimensions for us to understand the world we live in now. The study of nationalism is an important subject in history, sociology and political science, especially the study of nationalism in Asia and Africa. Because the particularity of the historical development process in these regions has not received enough attention, our disciplines and curriculum construction are also lagging behind. Most students are not familiar with some basic research literature, and there is no corresponding course to study these literatures. This course selects two important compilations of original documents on Asian and African nationalism compiled by Elie Kedourie and his wife, focusing on the analysis and critical re-examination of their long introductions. The content covers the nationalist movements in major regions and countries in the world's modern history, as well as the different national theories of bourgeoisie and Marxism and their influence, which is conducive to students' understanding and understanding of national issues in modern times. Students are required to have the ability to read English literature.

Name: Studies in Latin American Development Issues
Topics in Non-Western Modernization Studies
Introduction: Modernization studies emerged in the United States in the 1950s and 1960s, and were directly related to the rise of national democratic movements in the non-Western world after World War II. From the beginning, the focus of modernization research was not on developed countries but on development issues in the non-Western world. Although Latin America and East Asia have been the focus of Western academic circles, case and comparative studies of the development path of the entire non-Western world have gradually attracted the attention of domestic and foreign academic circles. As an important member of the developing non-Western world, China's path to modernization has attracted widespread attention. An in-depth discussion of the modernization path of the non-Western developing world not only has important academic value for the discipline construction of world history, especially the modern history of Asia and Africa, but also has practical significance for understanding the process of China's modernization in modern times. This course takes the form of special narration, guided reading, class discussion, writing book reports, etc. An in-depth discussion of the relevant theories of non-Western modernization and the modernization paths of major representative countries is designed to enable students to understand the main theories, methods and classic literature in this field, track the research trends in this field, broaden their horizons, find academic growth points, and improve their scientific research capabilities. _x000D_

Name: Visual Art in Text: Introduction to Modern French Literary Works
Introduction:
This course focuses on the representative classic works of modern French literature since the 18th century, combines text and image research and pictorial semiotics theory, and teaches new issues and new thinking brought about by visual arts (mainly paintings and sculptures) in terms of literary types, writing themes, narrative methods, rhetorical techniques, text structure and other aspects. By introducing the interdisciplinary knowledge background of literature and art and the theoretical background of semiotics, students can deepen their ability to read and understand French literary works and strengthen their ability to analyze and research literary texts. _x000D_
From 1759 to 1781, the philosopher Diderot wrote exhibition reviews for nine consecutive Paris "Salons of Painting and Sculpture". These works were collected and published as a review book "Salon" with more than 600 pages, announcing the birth of a new genre of "art criticism" and becoming an important part of Diderot's entire works. Baudelaire, Gautier and many other later writers were attracted by this form and wrote famous salon reviews. Balzac's "The Unknown Masterpiece" is a short story dedicated to the art of painting. It uses two great painters who actually existed in history, Poussin and Porbus, to set off a fictional character. This fictional character is the real creator and tragic hero in Balzac's eyes. He embodies the passion, mystery and eternal doubt of art. Proust's seven-volume "Reminiscence of Lost Time" mentions about 190 paintings. The paintings construct images, atmospheres and situations in the narrative of his novel, and also imply various implications and thoughts on artistic philosophy..._x000D_
From Baudelaire, Huysmans, Zola, and Claudel to Aragon, Yourcenar, Jean Genet, Perec, Bonnefour...the ubiquitous infiltration and integration of visual art constitutes an eye-catching landscape in French literature. This reflects French-style humanistic accomplishment, injects a different kind of aesthetic meaning into French literature, and opens up new possibilities for literary creation. The form of visual art inspires the space-time form of the text, and the text continues to deepen and broaden the understanding and thinking of art. _x000D_
The course divides modern French literary works related to visual arts into three major categories, which are the three main parts of the course. _x000D_
The first part is prose writing with works of art as the direct object of thinking and writing. Focus on reading "The Salon" by Diderot and "The Salon of 1846" and "The Salon of 1859" by Baudelaire. Typical works of this type include Stendhal's "History of Italian Painting", Claudel's "On Dutch Painting", Sartre's "Tintoretto: The Hidden Man in Venice", Genet's "Giacometti's Studio", Pascal Guignard's "Sexual Night", etc. In this part of the writing, the text describes and analyzes the artwork, transforming the visible into the readable, and presenting the process of coexistence and mutual care between the text and the image. _x000D_
The second part is a narrative work that integrates paintings and painter images into literary writing. Focus on reading the passages about the death of the writer Bergotte in Balzac's "Unknown Masterpieces" and Proust's "The Female Prisoner" in Volume 5 of "In Search of Lost Time". Typical works of this type include Balzac's "Sarrazin", Mérimée's "Le Beaux", Huysmans's "The God of Love", Zola's "Masterpiece", Aragon's "The Tempest of Holy Week", Perec's "The Mercenary Captain" and so on. In this part of writing, the artistic works are integrated into the narrative, which not only creates the image and atmosphere of the novel, but also promotes the development of the plot, and entrusts the writer's thinking on the essential issues of art, such as creativity, imitation, form and materials, and aesthetic spirituality. These issues run through poetry and painting, text and image, art and literature. _x000D_
The third part is a literary work that takes visual art as the starting point of the entire work, integrates the space art of modeling into the time art of language, and explores new narrative perspectives, narrative structures, and writing methods through visual art. Focus on reading "The Topology of a Ghost City" by Robbe-Grillet. Typical works of this type include Djebar's "The Algiers Woman in the Room" and Pierre Mison's "The Life of Joseph Rolland". In this type of works, the author has a high degree of formal consciousness, trying to make readable text visible, actively introducing visual art techniques into literary creation, and using perspective structure, image shaping, visual imagination, etc. to explore new possibilities in writing. _x000D_

Name: Studies in Paradigms of Ancient Chinese Architecture
Introduction: The Building Code, the Code of Engineering Practice, is an official official construction standard officially promulgated in the late and pre-qing phases of North Song, China, and is a historical text of great historical research value. Tang and Song are at the height of the development of traditional buildings in China, and the sunset of the construction of traditional Chinese buildings in Mingqing is of great historical, artistic and scientific value, in combination with historical literature, in the study of architectural paradigms and their evolution. Through a comprehensive comparison of the Building Code, the Code of Engineering Practices, and the examples of the construction of logs and imitation structures in different regions, various models of construction and their dissemination and circulation have been identified, forming temporal and spatial faults of time and geography, thus establishing a framework for the evolution of ancient building of wood in China, thus laying a solid foundation for further macrohistory research. Name: Archaeological Literature and Thesis Writing
Introduction:
In the nearly century-long development of modern archeology in China, a considerable amount of first-hand information has been accumulated. A large number of excavation reports have been published involving sites, tombs, various relics from different periods, and a large number of unearthed materials (including unearthed documents). For master's and doctoral students, how to master and use complex archaeological materials well and understand the corresponding academic research background as soon as possible is a foundation and prerequisite for professional research and writing. How to complete standardized thesis writing within the prescribed study period, and how to integrate with international standards in thesis writing, etc., are also issues that need to be solved urgently in the current postgraduate training process. These are the main purposes of this course. _x000D_
Starting from this goal, the course requires each postgraduate student to read a certain number of professional reports and research works intensively, and complete reviews of 1-2 archaeological reports in the current academic context. At the same time, he actively participates in class discussions around various problems existing in existing archaeological reports, and discusses the retrieval and application of archaeological data, the citation of documents, the construction of thesis topics and frameworks, and specific format specifications and other issues often encountered in graduate thesis writing. _x000D_

Introduction:
The study of the political system of the Song Dynasty has long been regarded as an academic difficulty by scholars at home and abroad, and at the same time it is an aspect in which domestic academic circles have comparative advantages on the world academic platform. Since the 1990s, many first-class scholars have successively contributed new insights and results. These collective achievements have a positive impact on the international scale. How to introduce these results into the teaching field in a timely manner, and then form a positive situation of interaction of research ideas, interaction of related disciplines, and interaction of teachers and students at home and abroad, so as to promote the actual and steady improvement of the overall research level, is an important task we face. _x000D_

It has long been famous for its refined and concentrated research on the history of political institutions. On this basis, if the "Special Topics in the History of Political Institutions of the Song Dynasty" course can be specifically offered, it will effectively bring students to the international academic frontier, significantly deepen collective learning and research, and significantly improve the teaching standards in related fields. _x000D_

Introduction: This course deals mainly with specialized issues in applied ethics, where the main topics of current interest are global justice, environmental ethics, bioethics and economic ethics.

Name: Reading and Writing (Part 1)

Name: Selected Primary Texts in Philosophy of Science

Name: Chinese Finance
Introduction: Over the past 40 years of reform and opening up, China's financial industry has made considerable progress. Its development path, organizational form, operation methods, risk accumulation and release characteristics, formal and informal rules, and interaction with the real economy are all different from other economies and have obvious Chinese characteristics. Existing finance textbooks are mostly based on Western markets and have obvious deficiencies in interpreting China's magnificent financial landscape and its tortuous and subtle historical evolution. This course will describe the institutional background of China's financial industry and sort out the historical context of China's financial development. On this basis, based on academic research and problem-oriented, it will reflect on the historical choices of key nodes in the reform and opening up of the financial industry, summarize the experience and lessons of the development of China's financial industry, concretize China's financial development model, contribute to the in-depth integration of financial theory and Chinese practice, and predict the future development direction of China's financial industry. It is hoped that after studying this course, students will be able to grasp the historical process of changes in China's financial system, understand what a "good financial system" is, and actively think about the key nodes of China's financial development in the future, as well as the correct choices we should make.

Name: Studies in Reform and Social Transformation in Ancient China
Introduction:
Since Hegel, the “Western-centered” view of history has prevailed in academic circles. According to this historical view, China during the imperial period (221 BC - 1840 AD) (especially after the Song Dynasty) is said to be a stagnant country with no inherent vitality. However, in recent decades, this "Western-centric" view of history has been continuously questioned and criticized. More and more scholars have drawn new views from different aspects, believing that China during the imperial period was a country that was constantly changing and developing, and that the main driving force for change and development came from within China. The purpose of this course is to sort out the main changes in Chinese society, economy and politics during the imperial period, so that students can better see these changes and their context.  _x000D_
In the history of the imperial period, China saw several major reform activities that were of far-reaching significance and led to major changes that can be called social transformation. These reforms and social transformations occurred in the Qin and Han Dynasties, the Tang and Song Dynasties, and the Ming Dynasty respectively, and each transformation resulted in different consequences. This course will conduct an in-depth discussion of the history of these major reforms and social transformations, analyze their characteristics and nature, compare the similarities and differences of these reforms and transformations, and examine them from the perspective of global history. _x000D_
Understanding social changes and transformations from a long-term and large-scale perspective is an important issue of concern to academic circles at home and abroad today. An in-depth study of this issue is of great significance for us to get rid of the "Western-centric" historical view and correctly understand traditional Chinese society.

Name: Microeconometric Theory
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to enable students to learn the theory and application of panel data models and other related econometric models, thereby benefiting master's and doctoral students in their academic research. This course was originally taught under the course "Advanced Econometric Topics" and was highly welcomed by students. It has the basis for starting the course (30 candidates in 2011 and 41 in 2012, and the number of observers is equal to the number of candidates). Teaching requires final exams and daily homework; after the semester, students are expected to have a solid understanding of panel data models and other related econometric models, and be able to apply software to analyze data.

Name: Advanced Techniques in Data Management
Introduction:
This course covers advanced statistical modeling and data management techniques that are fundamental for quantitative analysis of large data. Statistical topics include (but not limited to) models for categorical (logit/probit, multinomial,and orderded), count (poisson), and limited (censored, truncated, and sample selection) dependent variables, panel analysis, multilevel models, and survival analysis. Statistical methods will be discussed along with processing and handling of public firms data from China (e.g., CSMAR and WIND) and the US (e.g., Compustat & CaptitalIQ) to answer real research questions. Throughout the course, we will highlight the connections among statistics, data, theory, and intuition. Students completed this course are expected to develop a solid foundation of large data analysis and the ability of seeing through complex empirical data.

This is computing intensive course. Students are required to choose a research topic and a real dataset in the beginning and to go through of the entire process of a research project, from hypothesis development, data handling and transformation, data exploration and modeling, result reporting and interpretation, to manuscript writing. Our official statistical software is STATA, but students can free to use other softwares.

Name: Advanced Multivariate Statistical Analysis
Introduction:
Multivariate analysis refers to the statistical analysis method of multidimensional data. Our common data are multi-dimensional. Big data started in a few years has a higher data dimension. Multivariate analysis is a basic method of statistics. Currently, there is no course on multivariate analysis methods for graduate students in the statistics course systems of Guanghua and Peking University. With the widespread collection of multivariate data in more scientific and social science fields, it is urgent to open a relatively high-level multivariate analysis course at Peking University. This semester, I offered the course "Advanced Multivariate Statistical Analysis" under Statistics Topic 2. There were 22 students from Guanghua, School of Mathematics, and School of Big Data who chose the course, and there were also 10 undergraduates and students from other schools who were auditing. _x000D_
This course is open to senior undergraduate students. The second half of the content is currently the most cutting-edge methods and algorithms in the world. This course can be taught in English. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will cover statistical models and analytical algorithms for analyzing multidimensional (multivariate) statistical data, including very high-dimensional statistical data. Multivariate statistical methods can be directly applied to the statistical analysis of big data. This course will start with basic multivariate statistical models, covering multivariate normal distribution, ellipsoid and other height distributions; then Chapter 2 will talk about the Copula-based correlation measurement method and application of multivariate data, including: the famous Sklar theorem and commonly used connection functions such as Clayton and Ganbel copulae, copular non-parametric estimation methods, and the selection method of copula models in practical applications; Chapter 3 talks about the mean estimation and variance estimation methods of multi-dimensional and ultra-high-dimensional data: maximum likelihood estimation under parametric models; data estimation under non-parametric models; the consistency of mean and variance estimation in the case of low-dimensional data, and challenges and solutions in the case of high-dimensional data. Chapter 4 is about the mean test of two parent data: the Hotelling test for low-dimensional multivariate data, problems under high-dimensional data and how to improve it, including the Bai and Saranadasa correction method and Chen-Qin's improvement in ultra-high data, and the optimal test method based on the signal selection method. Chapter 5 covers the consistent estimation method of covariance of high-dimensional data, including: banding method and thresholding method, principal component method and factor analysis method under high-dimensional data, and testing method of high-dimensional covariance matrix. _x000D_

Name: Theory of Financial Derivatives Pricing
Introduction: This course describes the general pricing methods of derivative financial products and the practical application of various methods. General pricing methods include: (1) Blac-Scholes option pricing method (2) Equivalent martingale measure method (3) Binomial tree method. Applications of pricing methods include: pricing of futures, American and European options, exotic options, and interest rate derivatives; calculation methods for pricing derivative securities; and estimation of parameters.    The prerequisite courses for this course are: Probability and Statistics, Simple Stochastic Processes, and Investment.

Name: Macroeconomic Management
Introduction: This course provides master's students, especially finance master's students, with core theories and core models of macroeconomics, and emphasizes the application of these core models to real-life macro issues and policy analysis. The purpose is to cultivate students' ability to use macroeconomic theory and econometric statistical models, combined with real-life data, to analyze problems and policies. Students are required to have intermediate micro and preliminary quantitative knowledge. The course requires an understanding of core models, the ability to form research questions from reality, and the use of appropriate methods to analyze them.

Name: Applications of Financial Analysis
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to guide students to familiarize themselves with the application of financial analysis in financial investments. Specifically, this course will include enterprise value evaluation analysis based on financial analysis, debt and credit investment analysis based on financial analysis, and explore the financial analysis of financial derivatives. The basis of the course is basic accounting knowledge and basic financial product knowledge. Students are required to actively participate in course discussions and make financial analyzes in groups on the pricing and trading of listed companies, listed bonds, and listed derivatives.

Name: Financial Econometrics
Introduction:
This course is a required course for master's and doctoral students in finance. The main goal is to master the basic methods of empirical testing and analysis of various financial models through the study of this course. Systematically introduces relevant theories and methods for empirically testing the effectiveness of financial markets, introduces three types of random walk models and martingale models, and systematically provides testing methods for various models. The method of empirical testing of market efficiency and the statistical assumptions and statistics involved in the testing and that need to be paid attention to are discussed. By studying the price behavior of the market, we conduct various tests on whether the prices in the market can be predicted and find ways and opportunities to make profits. Another theme of financial econometrics research is the pricing of assets. The asset price given in the market is an estimate of the actual asset value. How to characterize the asset price under random interference through various financial econometric models constitutes the wonderful content of financial econometrics: present value model, capital asset pricing model, arbitrage pricing model or multi-factor model, etc. The course introduces the parameter estimation methods of the CAPM and APT models and various statistics for empirical testing of the model based on the estimated parameters of the model, as well as the differences in power between different test statistics and some empirical examples. The present value model that characterizes asset prices and the relationship between the stock price process and the dividend process are discussed. Detailed introduction to event research methods and implementation steps on the impact of various events in financial markets on asset prices. _x000D_

Name: Financial Markets and Institutions
Introduction: The rapid development of financial markets and financial institutions is one of the hot topics in today's society. This course is dedicated to understanding the overall operation of financial markets and financial institutions, and analyzing a large number of phenomena emerging in this field. The course is positioned as the midpoint between financial theory and market operations, focusing on using financial theory to analyze the organization and structure of financial markets and financial institutions, as well as various issues that arise in the development of this field. The financial institutions section will discuss depository financial institutions such as commercial banks, non-depository financial institutions such as investment funds, investment banks, and financial companies, as well as the functions of the central bank. The financial markets section will discuss the organization and microstructure of primary and secondary markets, focusing on equity markets and currency markets. Each part of the course starts with the analysis of general financial phenomena using the U.S. market as an example, and is supplemented by discussions on the development and issues of Chinese markets or institutions.

Name: Fixed Income Securities
Introduction: Fixed-income securities are a general term for a large class of important financial instruments, the main representatives of which are treasury bonds, corporate bonds, asset-backed securities, etc. Fixed income securities include default risk, interest rate risk, liquidity risk, tax risk and purchasing power risk. The avoidance of various risks is the fundamental reason why fixed income securities are constantly innovated. Although there are default risks and liquidity risks in fixed income securities, this course does not cover these two contents; the theory of interest rate term structure is an important content of the fixed income securities course, but this course only involves single-factor interest rate term structure models, not multi-factor interest rate term structure models. This course mainly teaches the pricing habits of fixed-income securities, zero-coupon bonds, coupon-bearing bonds, bond duration, convexity and time effects, bond investment interest rate risk management, interest rate term structure model, option bond pricing, interest rate futures, options, repos, swaps, housing loan-backed securities (MBS), etc.

Name: Financial Risk Management
Introduction: This course is an elective course for master's and doctoral students in finance. Systematically introduce various technical methods of financial risk management and discuss theoretical models related to financial risks. Risk is a basic element of financial activities. A basic function of the financial system is to effectively allocate risks. Most of the decisions of financial institutions are actually to realize the allocation and management of risks among different departments. Risk management technology is the core competitiveness of financial institutions. For this reason, in daily financial activities, how to identify and analyze risks, measure the impact of risks on asset values, and analyze and research ways to implement risk control and risk allocation have become an important aspect of both financial practice and financial research. This course will follow the Basel Committee's classification method of risk and separately introduce the four major types of risks involved in the risk management process of financial institutions: market risk, credit risk, operational risk and liquidity risk. It will systematically introduce the relevant knowledge and methods of various risks from the four links of risk identification, risk measurement, risk monitoring and risk management. Discuss the characteristics of various financial risks and introduce basic methods for modeling different risk types. For market risk, it mainly introduces VaR and related methods, and discusses methods to improve VaR; credit risk is discussed from two methods: external evaluation agencies and internal ratings; finally, operational risk and liquidity risk are briefly introduced. Combining some specific cases to demonstrate the role and functions of risk management technology, the management processes and basic elements of various risks are discussed. The course is mainly based on lectures and material reading, combined with some cases.

Name: Money and Banking

It requires careful reading of textbooks, writing course papers, and closed-book examinations.

This course uses actual data and cases as the background to teach practical analysis skills of R language, including data processing, description and visualization.

Name: Regression Analysis and Data Thinking
Introduction: It is said that this is an era of data, an era where data creates value. But what exactly is data? What is the simplest definition of data? From this simple definition, how can we see the characteristics of the times in data? Correspondingly, what is value? In what ways will the value of data be expressed? How should the value of data be measured and expressed? How to achieve the conversion from data to value? What is regression analysis? What is the relationship to the business value of data? Is regression analysis a mathematical model or an idea? What is the relationship to the business problem? How can such a concept be realized in the practice of China's data industry? All these questions will be answered systematically based on real cases.

Name: Time Series Analysis and Forecasting
Introduction: Time series analysis is a general term for the method of studying and analyzing time series data, that is, one or more sets of data sequentially in time. A large amount of common data in economics, finance, marketing and management science are time series data. Time series analysis aims to establish a time series model to describe the inherent dynamic laws of data, so as to explore and study the data generation mechanism and master the characteristics of data generated by various data generation mechanisms. On the other hand, based on data characteristics, we find appropriate and effective time series models to describe them. Through time series analysis, we can make rational predictions for the future based on past observations, study the relationship between multiple series, and so on. This method is widely used in many fields such as economics, finance, marketing, management, etc.

Name: Theory and Practice of Wealth Management in China
Introduction: This course is a new course mainly for master's and doctoral students that discusses hot and cutting-edge issues in China's wealth management. When it was first offered, it was initially considered to use half of the lectures by professors/guests and half of the students working in groups to do practical projects, so as to enhance students' understanding of key issues in the development of China's wealth management industry.

Name: Data, Planning and Decision Making
Introduction:
This course is dedicated to teaching students to solve management problems and make management decisions through scientific methods. Students will learn the core theories and methods of management science, and form a scientific perspective on methods through data to modeling to assisted decision-making. At the same time, computer skills are combined to assist in model solving. This course requires students to have basic mathematical knowledge and computer skills (especially EXCEL). During the teaching process, students are required to ensure attendance, actively use their brains, and combine management examples to analyze problems, build models, make decisions, and solve problems. _x000D_
The main teaching contents include: planning theory; graph theory and network optimization; decision analysis. _x000D_

Name: Integrated Practicum
Introduction:
Course purpose:_x000D_
The core purpose of this course is: after students have mastered basic regression analysis and machine learning methods, they can comprehensively apply them to actual practical problems. Improve students' comprehensive ability to deal with practical complex problems. _x000D_
Basics of starting the course:_x000D_
(1) Student base: This is a restricted course for majors in the business analysis direction of the Master of Finance at Guanghua School of Management. Target students include but are not limited to: master of finance, MBA, general master's and doctoral students. Therefore, students have a good foundation for course selection;_x000D_
(2) Professional foundation: Through the first year of study, students in the business analysis direction (and students in similar directions) have fully learned: programming languages ​​such as R and Python, learned basic courses such as regression analysis, machine learning, etc., and have the ability to comprehensively apply; _x000D_
(3) Case basis: This course requires real industrial cases. The relevant faculty and research team of this course have accumulated a wealth of practical cases in the past years of horizontal subject research and industrial consulting, which can become teaching materials. _x000D_
Teaching requirements:_x000D_
This course is a 2-credit course with 3 class hours per week for a total of 12 weeks. The entire 12 weeks is divided into three 4-week modules, and each module is designed through 8 specific tasks to complete a large project. Students' projects need to be completed independently by forming a project team. During the weekly class time (offline or online), the group progress report will be made. The instructor will make comments and propose key work progress points for the next week. _x000D_

Name: New Media Marketing and Targeted Advertising
Introduction: i. Brief description of the course (including the purpose, basis and teaching requirements, etc.): In today ' s era of Internet, social networking and mobile phone movements, marketing staff face many new opportunities and challenges in terms of customer communication, client access, advertising, etc. Traditional print media, such as newspapers, magazines, and so forth, are rapidly declining, television is gradually being replaced by streaming media video sites, and the rise of the Internet, mobile ends is an entirely new subject for traditional marketing channels. In addition to entirely new marketing channels, in the age of large data, data from individual users are becoming increasingly available, providing brand new perspectives and opportunities for marketing staff. It is very practical to use these data for user classification and precision advertising, thereby increasing the effectiveness of advertising. These issues are addressed in three parts of the course. The first part aims to create a conceptual framework for using input returns (ROI) to understand and quantify advertising effects. We describe how ROI is measured against experiments and natural experiments, and present in case form frequent errors in practice. In the second part, we present different advertising platforms and channels, including digital media advertisements, search engine advertisements, display advertisements, online video platform advertisements, social networking advertisements, and mobile advertisements. We highlight the uniqueness of different media, how they can be used and how they can be measured. In the third section, students choose a case that is taking place in the Chinese market and use the classroom framework for case presentation. It could be the current advertising model in China, or some new ideas. II. What are the areas of knowledge or skills that the curriculum complements for students? In terms of content, the curriculum gives students a basic understanding of the advertising industry, including innovations in the Internet and in the big data age advertising industry, multiple forms of advertising, measurement of the effects of advertising, etc., and students are prepared for content in the course in their future work, either as demanders for advertising (general enterprises) or as providers of advertising (advertising companies). In a way of thinking, the course emphasizes quantitative analysis, prepares students to use appropriate metrics, select suitable models, design suitable experiments, etc., and evaluate any business model with data and analysis. From the analytical tools, students will use Excel and R, respectively, to process different data, dig data, analyse and present results.

Name: Fundamentals and Applications of Financial Technology
Introduction:
This course is offered in response to the current impact of financial technology (Fintech) on financial markets and financial institutions. The content of the course is to introduce students to concepts related to Fintech, as well as various technological innovations, including artificial intelligence, blockchain and other financial applications. This course is a practical course and will invite industry experts in the field of financial technology to share the latest applications and developments of Fintech in the industry. _x000D_
_x000D_
The objectives of the course are twofold. One is in the quantitative direction, allowing students to learn and master the use of simple data analysis software for big data analysis and the operation of intelligent investment advisory. Understand the concept of machine learning; the second is to understand the Fintech market and understand the latest such as the cryptocurrency (Bitcoin) market, the concept of blockchain, and its latest applications in the financial field. _x000D_
_x000D_
The course content includes an introduction to Fintech; learning simple data analysis software and basic big data analysis; using data programming software to perform the most basic robo-advisory operations; the application of big data in inclusive finance; knowledge of Bitcoin and an introduction to the cryptocurrency market; using price differences in multiple cryptocurrency markets to find arbitrage opportunities; knowledge of blockchain; and discussion of several case studies of blockchain applications in the financial field. _x000D_
_x000D_
There are no closed-book exams in the course. Grading is divided into class participation and group project parts. Students will be divided into several groups and complete a Fintech-related application project in each group. Projects can be chosen from several topics, including completing a trading strategy design and programming for computer programming to trade stocks; completing a cross-market cryptocurrency arbitrage transaction; providing a plan for a blockchain application scenario; participating in an artificial intelligence machine learning project and completing a report. _x000D_

Name: Microeconomics in Industry Research
Introduction: This course is an applied economic theory course used to analyze real-life economic problems. This course will explore some classic theories and important issues in microeconomics and industrial economics, and combine it with business case teaching to help students apply it to industry research that is widespread in the financial industry. Through the study of this course, students will have an in-depth understanding of some important theories of microeconomics and the classic models and analytical frameworks of industrial economics; they will be able to use relevant economic knowledge to analyze actual industrial problems such as corporate behavior, market operations, and industrial structure evolution, and cultivate students' theoretical literacy and ability to solve practical problems. This course mainly includes a review of basic microeconomics content, classic models and applications of micro-industrial organizations, and corresponding industrial policies. It specifically includes industrial organization issues such as enterprise theory, market structure, competitive strategy, market performance, government regulation, and antitrust.

Name: Advanced Financial Accounting
Introduction: This course mainly covers content not covered in basic financial accounting, allowing students to have a complete understanding of the entire financial accounting knowledge system and fully understand the impact of company financial decisions on financial statements. The main contents include: recognition and measurement of financial assets; equity method accounting for company equity investments; accounting treatment for company mergers; preparation of consolidated statements; goodwill; application and disclosure of special purpose entities; processing of leasing business, etc. This course teaches students accounting knowledge about corporate mergers, financial assets, etc., cultivates students' basic qualities in finance and accounting subjects, and improves students' theoretical level; by mastering accounting processing methods in related fields, understanding the reflection of financial decisions in company statements, and training students' ability to understand company statements; through classroom discussions and group assignments, students develop their ability to analyze and solve problems, as well as communication, cooperation, and expression skills; by comparing international and domestic examples, students' international horizons are broadened. The professor who started the course has been engaged in teaching and researching financial accounting for a long time and has a good grasp of the research and practice in related fields.

Name: Statistical Computation and Data Analysis
Introduction: This course introduces students to a variety of techniques and considerations important in dealing with data analyses in management research. Students will be exposed to descriptive and inferential methods and learn about their underlying assumptions, correct usage, and proper interpretation.

Name: Psychological Foundations of Management
Introduction:
This course is one of the first doctoral-level seminars to students. Thus, it targets at a number of objectives:
1. You are expected to establish your mentality about scientific discovery, the career as a scholar, as well as facts about academia.
2. You will be actively involved in learning some most fundamental and important topics in micro-OB, and gain a basic understanding of selected individual-level theories and research paradigms in this field.
3. You are expected to develop your sense of academic inquiry in this field, and enhance your ability to formulate important organizational behavior research questions through the use of theoretical synthesis.

Name: Strategic Management Research: Theoretical Foundations and Phenomenon-Based Issues
Introduction: Strategic management research attempts to explain the differences in firm behaviors and outcomes by analyzing the effects of a variety of factors at multiple levels, including countries, industries, firms, teams, and individuals. This seminar focuses on phenomena and research topics in strategy research. It provides an overview of classic and current research topics including innovation and technology strategy, strategic alliances and networks, international strategy, product diversification, corporate governance, executive leadership, strategic decision processes, change and adaptation. Specific topics and phenomena will be examined from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. Overall, the intent of this seminar is to provide students a foundation for conducting and publishing original research in strategic management.

Name: Management Research Methods (1)
Introduction: This course is intended for Ph.D. students who are preparing to conduct empirical research in management. The course will discuss a variety of research designs and methods commonly used in the behavioural sciences in general and social psychology and organizational research in particular.

Name: Economic Foundations of Management
Introduction:
This course is a required course for doctoral programs in strategic management and organizational management, laying a solid foundation in economic theory for independent, high-level academic research. The main contents of this course include industrial economics and game theory, firm theory, transaction cost theory, complete and incomplete contract theory, information economics and platform economics. This course emphasizes the integration and comprehensive application of these theories to discover and analyze important issues in strategic management and organizational management. This course highlights the development and cutting-edge issues in related fields on the basis of highlighting the basic training of these economic theories. The implications of theoretical analysis for empirical research and its guiding significance for business practice will also be covered in the course. _x000D_
The goal of the course is to enable students to have a systematic understanding of corporate and industrial organizations, as well as the literature on organizational theory. Have a good grasp of cutting-edge issues and be able to use these economic theoretical frameworks, analytical tools and research methods to propose testable hypotheses in strategic management and organizational management.

Name: Sociological Foundations of Management
Introduction: This course is a new postgraduate course offered after the teaching reform of the Department of Organization and Strategic Management. The faculty of the Department of Organization and Strategic Management realize that in order to improve students' academic quality and lay a more solid foundation for the future academic development of graduate students, they must strengthen the education of basic theory in the training program. As far as management is concerned, the main theoretical resources are economics, psychology, and sociology. In previous training programs, the introduction of sociological theory was mainly conducted in the course "Organizational Theory Seminar". But this setting cannot reflect the breadth of sociological theory. In addition to organizational theory, research results in economic sociology, political sociology, social stratification and other fields have been used for reference by management researchers and have produced new theoretical perspectives. Therefore, the main improvement of this course is to further expand the breadth and depth of reading based on the original course. Further strengthen students' theoretical literacy. The teaching method of this course will be based on student reading and class discussion. The main contents include classic sociological theory, organizational ecology, institutional theory, resource dependence theory, the debate between structure and agency, institutional logic, organizational imprinting and change, embeddedness and social networks, state and economy and other topics. Students read about 100 pages of extracurricular reading per week, and the final examination is conducted in the form of a term paper.

Name: Frontier Topics in Organization and Strategic Management
Introduction:
This course is a cutting-edge seminar. On the basis of students being familiar with the background knowledge and related literature in the field of organization and strategy, the course allows students to understand the cutting-edge and characteristic research of faculty in the Department of Organization and Strategy, helps students discover their own research interests, and ultimately improves students' ability to conduct cutting-edge research on organizational management in the Chinese context by reading and understanding background literature, studying and commenting on faculty research, and proposing personal research plans. _x000D_
Class structure: For the first 10 times, the host teacher of each course assigns students 3 reading and analysis materials (2 background documents + 1 published or working paper by the teacher), and students and teachers study and discuss the paper materials; for the last 2 times, students report their research plans, and the course host makes comments, which are used as the basis for the final grade evaluation of the course. _x000D_
