Name: Entrepreneurship Research: An Integrative Perspective
Introduction: Strategic entrepreneurship (SE), as an area of research, borrows from, and integrates entrepreneurial and strategic theoretical perspectives in an attempt to explain competitive advantage and entrepreneurial activity. Discovering and exploiting opportunities is the cornerstone of the entrepreneurial challenge of (emerging) organizations, while strategic management is about advantage seeking actions of organizations. The combination of these perspectives and areas of research generates interesting new theoretical vistas and research questions for examining central organizational phenomena in China and worldwide.

Name: Philosophy of Management Research
Introduction:
Course purpose:_x000D_
This course mainly teaches the philosophy of science to doctoral students in management disciplines (including strategic management, organizational behavior, and marketing). The content involves the basic logic of natural and social scientists studying natural and social phenomena. The course aims to guide doctoral students to understand the thinking logic of scientific philosophy and initially form scientific thinking habits. The course explores some basic philosophical issues of science. For example: What is scientific logic? What are the unique challenges facing the social sciences? The process and development of scientific knowledge, etc. _x000D_
Basics of starting the course:_x000D_
This course is based on the understanding of the literature of this subject that doctoral students in management have already formed in the first year of their PhD, and helps students further understand the significance of scientific research (especially management scientific research) and the basic principles that should be followed. _x000D_

Name: Studies in International Business Operations
Introduction: This course presents a set of tools, concepts, and perspectives that help students to analyze the key issues in international business and management. After finishing this course, students should be able (1) to have a good understanding of the current literature on international business; (2) to identify important research questions in the field; (3) to carry out independent studies to address these questions.

Name: Multivariate Analysis and Structural Equation Modeling
Introduction: After the first semester basic statistical theoretical training, this semester's focus will be model based case studies. More specifically, different mostly commonly used statistical model will be introduced, its interpretation will be discussed, its software assisted implementation will be practiced, finally, real data case study will be presented for each discussion.

Name: Studies in Public Cultural Services
Introduction:
Part One: The concept, meaning, content, scope, and basic theoretical explanation of culture, public culture, public cultural services, and public cultural service systems. _x000D_
 Part Two: The origin and evolution of domestic and foreign public cultural concepts and ideas; the framework system and main contents of domestic and foreign public cultural policies and regulations. _x000D_
 Part Three: The five major subsystems of the public cultural service system: (1) Facility network coverage system; (2) Product and service function supply system; (3) Talent, capital and technical support system; (4) Organizational support system; (5) Evaluation system. _x000D_
 Part Four: my country’s cultural reform and development and the construction of public cultural service system.

Name: Lecture Series on Frontiers in Library Science
Introduction: This course is a required course for doctoral students in library science stipulated by the Ministry of Education. It is a series of lectures and is delivered by 15 domestic professors and experts from various branches of library science (including editing and publishing). The content includes research on basic theories of library science, information resource construction research, library management and legal research, information organization research, metadata research, library science history research, contemporary Chinese publishing and distribution research, philology research, library reader service research, publishing and social research, animation industry development research, foreign library science research trends, library evaluation research, public libraries and private libraries, library science research methods, etc. Through this series of lectures, we strive to enable doctoral students to quickly grasp the research frontiers in related fields and lay the foundation for subsequent study and research.

Name: Research Methods in Library Science
Introduction:
This course aims to cultivate the innovative consciousness, scientific research ability and academic standard literacy of graduate students majoring in library science. Through teaching, seminars, and internships, graduate students in this major can master scientific methods in topic selection and writing in scientific research, and improve their thesis writing skills in this major. _x000D_
In recent years, many doctoral supervisors have devoted considerable energy to guiding students in research methods, such as how to choose a topic, how to collect data, which empirical method to choose, how to cite literature, how to abide by academic regulations and prevent plagiarism, etc. Therefore, it is urgent to offer this course in the library science major. _x000D_
The teaching method of this course adopts a combination of model study, classroom lectures, special discussions, and essay writing. The assessment method is daily grades plus final examination scores (thesis writing). _x000D_

Name: Community Informatics
Introduction: Community informatics is an emerging research field that studies how local and traditional communities (communities) use information technology and communication technology to influence and improve the work, study and life of community members. This course will introduce students to the main concepts from English academic literature in this field, as well as the main principles when people use information technology and communication technology in public libraries or other community settings, so that students can better understand the current rapidly developing technological environment and make good use of these new technologies in work and research. In-class fieldwork research will give students the opportunity to practice the theoretical knowledge learned in the course. In order to equip students with the ability to conduct fieldwork research smoothly, students will also be introduced to several social science research methods in the course (for example, observation method, questionnaire method, interview method, group discussion method, etc.). Students will also be required to conduct literature research and review of relevant Chinese literature.

Name: Topic Planning and Publishing Editorial Practice
Introduction: The first part of this course will focus on theoretical research on Western books and periodicals, book topic selection, topic selection case analysis, and writing of publishing plans. The content includes how to select a topic, the types of topics to choose, the composition of a publishing plan, etc. The latter part of the time focuses on teaching topic selection and actual editing work for newspapers and periodicals. Through these studies and writing internship reports, it is hoped that students will have a preliminary understanding of the publishing house's topic selection planning and the actual work of book and newspaper editing, and will also strengthen students' ability to think about problems and do things.

Name: Special Topics in Information Resource Management
Introduction:
"Information Resource Management Monograph" is a basic compulsory course for master's students majoring in information science and library science. The main contents include: ① basic theories of information resource management, such as the meaning of information resources, basic concepts and theories of information management and knowledge management, and the construction of information management discipline system; ② enterprise informatization and information resource management, such as enterprise information competition strategy and information system construction, IT application cases, etc.; ③ government informatization and information resource management, such as government information disclosure system, etc.; ④ information service operation and information market competition, such as the management and operation of information enterprises, domestic and foreign information market competition situation and strategic research, etc. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching methods: lectures and special discussions Examination methods: closed book and homework

Name: Studies in Library Science Theory
Introduction:
Study the macro-realistic issues in the development of my country's librarianship, including: ① China's library development strategy; ② Library network organization and management; ③ The definition, characteristics, structure, technical basis of electronic libraries and their impact on traditional libraries; ④ Network Information resource organization and retrieval; ⑤ data storage, compression, conversion technology and methods; ⑥ library collaboration and document resource sharing; ⑦ information services and information industrialization; ⑧ information resource management and hot technologies; ⑨ The impact of information technology on the library science discipline system. _x000D_
_x000D_
Teaching method: mainly lectures, supplemented by discussion. Examination method: closed-book written examination, course paper

Name: Topics in Modern Library Management
Introduction: As one of the professional courses for postgraduate students in library science, this course mainly teaches modern library management theories and methods. The content includes: the basic concepts of modern library management; general principles, characteristics and methods of library management; domestic and foreign library management systems and the reform of my country's library management system; library planning and target management; principles, structures and management systems of library organizations; library human resources management; library decision-making and command, library evaluation and control, etc. Through the study of this course, students can initially master the management methods of macro-librarianship and micro-specific libraries.

Name: Studies in Philology
Introduction: ⑴ Introduction, the expansion from the field of classical philology research to the field of modern philology research; ⑵ Document ontology research; ⑶ Ideas and methods of document organization: from tradition to digitization; ⑷ Sub-disciplinary philology research; ⑸ Branch philology research; ⑹ Document value research; ⑺ Philology research materials, results and philologists

Name: Research Methods and Thesis Writing
Introduction: Scientific research methods and thesis writing are basic courses for first-year graduate students in the Department of Information Management (all majors). Its content mainly involves three major aspects: the philosophical principles of scientific methods, technical and normative issues in applying scientific methods in library and information science research, and thesis writing. This course is designed to help graduate students establish a scientific and systematic theoretical system of scientific research methods, understand the meaning and basic methods of scientific research, enable students to form standardized scientific research practices, and master the writing skills of different types of journal articles and dissertations, and be familiar with important Chinese and English journals and conferences in this field. The course is jointly designed and jointly offered by the Library Science Teaching and Research Office and the Information Science Teaching and Research Office, so that its content can better meet the common needs of the two disciplines, and the teaching of related content is closer to the needs of each major, and it is also more in line with the development trend of research methods in each major. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Reference and Consulting Services
Introduction:
Reference services play an important role in various library services. The library reference department is also an important department of the library. Studying the content and rules of reference services and new methods and new directions of reference services in the digital environment are important issues in the current field of library science research. _x000D_
This course aims to enable students to understand the basic content of library reference work, the characteristics and rules of contemporary reference work, master the distribution of library reference resources, understand the responsibilities of reference librarians in the new environment and the characteristics of users in the library reference service process. The course content involves new reference service models such as virtual reference services and online real-time reference services, as well as the specifications, quality control and evaluation systems of reference services. It focuses on the organization and management of digital reference services in the new information environment and technology environment, which will help students understand how libraries use modern information technology to carry out reference services.

Name: Progress Report
Introduction: This course aims to hope that master's students can master the origins and basic contents of classic works related to library science, information science, and editing and publishing research, cultivate the basic theoretical literacy of master's students, establish a solid theoretical foundation, learn to use scientific principles to analyze social reality issues involving the development of the library, information, and publishing industries, and train graduate students' induction and expression abilities. This course requires master's students to systematically read Chinese and foreign classics on library science, information science, and editing and publishing research under the guidance of their instructors. Based on the literature reading, students are required to publicly report their reading results. Students will communicate and discuss their learning experiences with each other, and write reading reports on this basis. This course is 2 credits, 1 credit per semester, and completed within one academic year.

Name: Studies in Public Libraries
Introduction:
Purpose of the course: Public librarianship has been a hot research topic in the library industry at home and abroad in recent years, but our department has not yet opened such related postgraduate courses. Public libraries are the most representative among the many types of libraries. They can fully reflect the significant contribution of librarianship to social development. They are also the basis for public understanding of librarianship and play a huge role in social development and the construction of a democratic society. Based on this, our department should offer relevant courses. Through course teaching, students can learn about public library governance, history, services, resources, facilities, the current development and practice of public libraries, and their harmony with community development. _x000D_
Basics of starting the course: The lecturer has a large amount of teaching materials that can be used for course teaching. We have maintained good academic exchange relationships with teachers of relevant courses from well-known foreign universities. At the same time, because I work part-time in domestic professional societies, I have visited a large number of domestic public libraries. With the help of international academic exchanges, I have also learned about and visited many public libraries in the United States, so I have a lot of perceptual understanding and rational thinking about domestic and foreign public libraries. _x000D_
Teaching requirements: Students must be able to read English literature proficiently and have a basic grasp of field research methods and data analysis skills. _x000D_

Name: Retrieval and Use of Electronic Resources
Introduction: Overview of electronic resources; reference database (1) - world-famous comprehensive search tool (English); reference database (2) - professional search tool (English); reference database (3) - Chinese search tool; use of full-text databases and full-text services; electronic journals; electronic books and newspapers; factual databases.

Name: Information Systems Planning and Construction
Introduction:
Traditionally, information systems mainly refer to management information systems applied in enterprises, and information system planning is the main issue in the practice of information systems in enterprises. But in the network information environment, the meaning of information system has expanded. In general, it includes three aspects: traditional management information system, Web information system and small information system running on various intelligent terminal devices. In other words, all types of Web applications can be considered as information systems in various forms. _x000D_
_x000D_
This course will break through the scope of traditional information systems, that is, it will include not only enterprise information systems, but also Web information systems and information products running on intelligent terminal devices. This course will transform and enrich the content of this course from the perspective of information science and based on the Web information environment. In other words, although the course content still includes the planning and construction of enterprise information systems, it is no longer the focus of the course. Based on the Web environment, various Web sites, Web information services, and various Web information products running on desktop computers and smart mobile terminal devices are currently the main information system objects used by the public. Although these information systems vary widely in form, they have some common characteristics.

Name: Lecture Series on Frontiers in Information Science
Introduction: Experts engaged in information science research and teaching, as well as well-known figures in the industry engaged in intelligence work, are invited to give special introductions to the current cutting-edge issues in the development of information science in the form of lectures, mainly including: domestic and foreign information science theory progress, domestic and foreign intelligence industry development trends, hot issues in information science and intelligence industry, challenges faced by information science and intelligence industry in the digital environment, etc.

Quantitative research is an important research method in social and humanities research, and statistical methods play an important role in quantitative research methods. With the continuous advancement of the digitalization process, more and more data about human behavior and social activities are accumulated, and more and more data can be analyzed. The application of statistical modeling methods in information research fields such as information retrieval, information systems, intelligence analysis, information user research, and big data research will become more and more widespread. _x000D_
The purpose of this course is to enable students to understand and master the basic methods of data analysis and use statistical methods to build statistical models, including graphic representation of data, attribute data analysis, parametric statistical analysis, non-parametric statistical analysis, single and multiple regression analysis, time series analysis, path analysis and structural equation modeling, etc. _x000D_

Name: Intelligence Analysis
Introduction:
Course introduction: (If the length is not enough, you can add pages)_x000D_
Content analysis method is an objective and systematic quantitative description research method for the content of literature. During World War II, Americans Harold Lasswell and others organized a work called "Wartime Communication Research" to conduct intelligence research on Germany using publicly published newspapers as the research object, showing the effectiveness of content analysis and forming a complete model in terms of methods. In the 1950s, Bernard Berelson's book "Content Analysis in Communication Research" established the status of content analysis. In the 1980s, John Naisbitt's world-renowned "Megatrends-Ten New Directions Changing Our Lives" made content analysis truly systematic in the field of prediction research. _x000D_
Content analysis often plays the role of an analytical tool in intelligence research during its development process. Intelligence research has also been able to open up new practice areas and complete more analysis and prediction tasks due to the continuous development of content analysis. An effective political psychological analysis tool in intelligence research is based on content analysis. The improvement of modern information resource conditions and the advancement of information measurement and calculation methods have also provided sufficient guarantee conditions for the application and development of content analysis in the field of intelligence research. Therefore, the status and role of content analysis in intelligence research have become increasingly prominent in the discipline system of information science. _x000D_
This course is aimed at master's students in information science. It is intended to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the content analysis method system and its application and development in information research through the teaching links of literature reading, special discussions and analysis practice. It requires students to master and understand relevant basic technical means to lay a foundation for engaging in analysis and prediction work in the future. _x000D_

In recent years, he has successively published works and research papers in related fields such as "Information Analysis and Decision-Making (Second Edition)", "Competitive Intelligence Methods", "On the Quality of Intelligence Research", "On Quality Control Methods of Information Analysis", "Network Econometric Analysis in Competitive Intelligence Research", "On Indicator Analysis in Intelligence Research". Name: Topics in Management Consulting
Introduction: Management consulting has long been regarded as a useful professional service that helps managers analyze and solve practical problems faced by their organizations, improve management effectiveness, and learn from the experiences of other managers and organizations. The purpose of this course is to understand contemporary management consulting practice, explore issues closely related to management consultants and clients, explore development trends in management consulting, and introduce methods that can increase the value of the services provided by management consultants. Since 1993, I have offered a limited elective course on "Counseling Theory and Practice" for postgraduate students majoring in library science and information science in the Department of Information Management of Peking University. In 2000, I published a monograph on "Counseling Theory and Practice". Since 2000, the limited elective course "Principles of Management" has been offered to undergraduates majoring in library science and information science in the Department of Information Management of Peking University. Through the study and discussion of this course, we hope that students can connect theory with practice, master management consulting skills and knowledge, and understand various management consulting perspectives and methods.

Name: Web Data Mining and Its Applications
Introduction: The rapid development of the Web has made it the largest public data source in the world. The goal of Web data mining is to explore useful information from Web hyperlinks, web page content and usage logs; to obtain implicit knowledge and patterns by analyzing massive Web data. Through the study of this course, students can master the basic concepts, methods and techniques of Web data mining, and be able to apply data mining tools and some open source software to analyze real Web data and interpret the mining results. Analyze the application research cases of Web mining in related fields, and focus on analyzing two typical cases in the field of graphics and information: "Knowledge discovery based on literature databases" and "Library user borrowing data analysis"; cultivate students' ability to conduct in-depth analysis of Web data.

Name: Topics in the Knowledge Economy
Introduction:
This course is a professional course for graduate students of various majors in the Department of Information Management. _x000D_
Knowledge is power, knowledge is capital, knowledge is the first factor of production and the most important resource. With the development of the era of knowledge economy, production factors, production processes, distribution, exchange, consumption, evaluation, etc. are all undergoing qualitative changes. The two trends of capitalization of knowledge and intellectualization of capital are converging, presenting a new form of social development. _x000D_
Knowledge economics is a hot issue of concern in the academic and business circles in the world today. It is a cutting-edge subject. In higher education in Western developed countries, it is considered an indispensable part of the field of management and is highly valued and welcomed by teachers and students. Knowledge economics is an interdisciplinary subject, including the research and discussion of technology, information, knowledge, process, people, and organizational culture. This subject is not a linear superposition of these research contents, which is where the complexity of knowledge economics lies. _x000D_
This course systematically introduces the basic concepts and research methods of knowledge economics, conducts relevant case analysis, and guides students to view problems in a new way, whether in traditional fields or emerging fields, and to have the ability to explore and solve problems, so that they can calmly cope with the challenges of the knowledge economy in the information age and have a sustainable competitive advantage. _x000D_

Name: Modern Information Retrieval Theory and Technology
Introduction: Mainly introduces and discusses the basic theory and latest technology of computer information retrieval. The main contents include: overview of field development, information retrieval system models (Boolean model, vector space model, probability model, extended Boolean model), basic principles and technologies of automatic indexing (word frequency weighting technology, word distinction value weighting technology, probability weighting technology, etc.), typical system and technology analysis (SMART, SI RE, AIR/PHIS, CAS full-text automatic indexing technology, Chinese document self-indexing research), international large-scale text retrieval system evaluation experiment (TREC), new areas of information retrieval research (retrieval technology on the Internet, intelligent retrieval technology, audiovisual information retrieval technology, cross-language retrieval technology, etc.).

Name: Social Network Analysis
Introduction:
Society is a huge network composed of a variety of relationships. Social network analysis is to quantitatively analyze the relationship network to reveal the structure of relationships and explain certain social phenomena. At present, social network analysis has become a very popular social science research method and has been successfully applied in many fields. For example, researchers in the field of information science use social network analysis methods to study various relationship networks in competitive intelligence, knowledge management, resource allocation of enterprises and institutions, subject hot spots, citation analysis, scientific researcher co-authorship, institutional cooperation, network links, blog networks, etc., and have achieved many novel research results. _x000D_
    This course explains the basic concepts, principles and methods of social network analysis; introduces typical application cases of this method in some key subject areas, especially application examples in information science and information management; introduces the use of major software tools for social network analysis such as Pajek and Ucinet. Cultivate students' ability to use social network analysis methods to solve practical problems. _x000D_

Name: Lecture Series on Frontiers of Editing and Publishing Studies
Introduction:
Content summary:_x000D_
This course is a required course for doctoral students in editing and publishing stipulated by the Ministry of Education. It is a series of lectures and is delivered by more than 10 domestic professors and experts in various branches of editing and publishing (including library science). The content includes research on basic theories of library science, history of library science, contemporary publishing and distribution research in China, literature research, library reader service research, publishing and social research, animation industry development research, foreign library science research trends, library evaluation research, public libraries and private libraries, library science research methods, etc. Through this series of lectures, we strive to enable doctoral students to quickly grasp the research frontiers in related fields and lay the foundation for subsequent study and research. _x000D_

Name: Studies in the Modern Publishing Industry
Introduction:
This course is a course that combines theory and reality. It mainly discusses the following issues:_x000D_
1. Traditional book publishing industry and modern publishing industry; 2. Summary of the history and experience of the new book publishing industry; 3. Publishing institutions and publication issues; 4. Publisher quality issues; 5. Publishing and copyright; 6. Publishing and reading, etc.

Name: Topics in the Publishing and Cultural Industries
Introduction:
The birth and development of the publishing industry have played an incomparable role in the development and inheritance of human civilization. The formation and development of the publishing industry in different countries or regions are closely related to the development of local politics, economy, culture, and education. Teaching the publishing industry and publishing culture as a whole will enable us to have a more comprehensive understanding of the development and evolution of the publishing industry and publishing culture as well as their mutual relationships. It will also have important practical significance for us to understand and understand the formation, characteristics, structure and development trends of the publishing industry. _x000D_
Students are required to read more relevant literature, conduct class discussions, write course papers, etc. _x000D_

Name: Media Operations and Management
Introduction:
This course is a compulsory course for postgraduate students in media management in the School of Journalism and Communication. The course uses industrial economics and business management as background knowledge, focusing on teaching the overview and characteristics of the media industry and media organizations, business management theory and practice, and integrating methods such as industry analysis, policy research, case studies, empirical research, and literature surveys to train students' problem awareness and research capabilities. The course focuses on comparison of domestic and foreign situations and historical development context, which helps students broaden their horizons and comprehensively master relevant knowledge and abilities. _x000D_
Course purpose:_x000D_
(1) Understand the overview and characteristics of the media industry and media organizations_x000D_
(2) Master the relevant theories and analytical models of Mojie industrial economy and Mojie management_x000D_
(3) Be familiar with hot issues in practice and research fields_x000D_
(4) Master important research methods and improve research capabilities_x000D_

Name: Studies in Publishing Culture
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to enable students to understand the connotation and relevance of publishing culture, recognize the urgency of publishing culture construction, understand the differences in publishing culture around the world, gain an in-depth understanding of Chinese publishing tradition, and cultivate the humanistic care of publishing culture. Publishing culture is an essential part of publishing research and publishing activities. It is a three-dimensional cultural system based on knowledge and information as the content, based on material technology, with the legal system as the intermediary, and guided by values. The content of this course mainly includes: introduction (main issues and tasks in publishing culture research), cultural aspects of publishing (the relationship between publishing and culture, essay culture), characteristics of publishing culture (regional, national, contemporary), best-sellers, reading culture, classics and recommended books, etc.

Name: Sociological Theory
Introduction:
Content summary:_x000D_
Domestic and foreign sociological theories are sorted out from a horizontal perspective, allowing students to have a relatively in-depth understanding of the main issues and existing results in sociological theoretical research. It mainly includes the following aspects:_x000D_
1. Micro-social analysis: Mainly studies the theories of domestic and foreign sociologists on social action, interaction and micro-social processes. _x000D_
2. Macro-social analysis: Mainly studies the theories of domestic and foreign sociologists on macro-social structure and social process. _x000D_
3. The connection between micro-social analysis and macro-social analysis: It mainly studies the various theoretical strategies of domestic and foreign sociologists on how to connect micro-social analysis and macro-social analysis. _x000D_
4. Analysis of social changes: Mainly studies the theories of domestic and foreign sociologists on social changes, modern society and post-modernity. _x000D_

Name: Topics in Historical Sociology
Introduction: This course is intended for graduate students who have a good theoretical foundation in Western sociology and have a certain understanding of historical social research (such as historical sociology, historical anthropology, and social history). It focuses on studying some schools of contemporary historical social research and pays equal attention to both theoretical paradigms and empirical research literature, so that the reflection on some core concepts of social theory and the summary and improvement of relevant empirical research can mutually promote each other. The teacher has taught 7 rounds of historical sociology, 2 rounds of oral history, and 1 round of developmental sociology for undergraduate students. He has presided over the historical sociology section of the "Introduction to Original Works on Sociology" of the Higher Education Society, the "Progress in Contemporary Western Historical Sociology" project of the National Fund for Returned Overseas Students, and has translated a variety of Western historical social research documents. This course pays equal attention to teacher lectures and classroom discussions, and requires a large amount of English reading. The final assessment will combine classroom discussions (40%) and research papers (60%).

Name: Sociological Methodology
Introduction:
1. The nature and development history of sociological methodology_x000D_
2. Main schools and basic issues of sociological methodology_x000D_
3. Subject-object relationship in sociological research_x000D_
4. Issues of scientificity and objectivity of sociological methods_x000D_
5. Localization and Diversification of Sociological Research_x000D_
6. Logical procedures and case analysis of sociological research_x000D_
7. Methodological issues in the process of theory testing and construction_x000D_
8. Methodological issues in data collection_x000D_
9. Models and mechanisms of data analysis and theoretical explanation_x000D_
The purpose of this course is to enable students to further understand the theoretical and logical foundations of sociological research methods. Improve the design, organization, evaluation, method application and innovation capabilities of practical research_x000D_

Name: Topics in Social Psychology
Introduction: Sort out the classic legacies of different intellectual traditions, systematically discuss the basic theoretical debates surrounding the progress of the discipline of social psychology, focus on important contemporary research themes and techniques: such as proceduralism, the influence of minorities, religious action, discourse analysis, etc., and try to construct a unified theory of social action, that is, social actors.

Name: Ethnic Sociology
Introduction: This course mainly conducts a systematic analysis and theoretical discussion of the relationships and influencing factors among each ethnic group in a multi-ethnic country from the aspects of sociology and demography. In the study, the analysis will be conducted in conjunction with topics such as national integration, modernization, multiculturalism, and socioeconomic development. In terms of theoretical and empirical materials, we will absorb the traditional thoughts and measures for dealing with ethnic relations in Chinese history, Marx's ethnic theory and practice, and ethnic theory and practice in Western society. Combined with the new development of ethnic issues in the current process of China's modernization and our field investigations and case studies, we will discuss how our country's ethnic groups can achieve modernization, achieve common prosperity, and maintain ethnic unity and the reunification of the motherland.

Name: Qualitative Research Methods
Introduction: Introduce students to the methodology, basic methods and specific research techniques of qualitative research, and help students design and implement their own qualitative research topics. Students are required to read a large amount of English literature, actively participate in class discussions, and independently complete a qualitative research project under the guidance of the teacher.

Name: Studies in China's Ethnic and Frontier Issues
Introduction:
This course is offered to master's and doctoral students who are academically interested in China's ethnic and border issues. It aims to observe issues related to ethnicity, ethnic groups and borders in Chinese history and contemporary society from a sociological perspective and method. The goal is to enable students to establish an awareness of the research on China's ethnic and border issues, grasp the main issues and academic context in related fields, and be able to conduct independent research in this field. _x000D_
This course will be conducted through a combination of teacher lectures and student discussions (each accounting for 50% of class time). Specific topics include but are not limited to: (1) the historical path of the formation of China's multi-ethnic country; (2) Chinese society's thoughts on "ethnic" issues during the late Qing Dynasty and the Republic of China. Want to communicate; (3) "ethnic identification" and ethnic policies after the founding of the People's Republic of China; (4) ethnic stratification in contemporary China; (5) institutional exploration and value debate on minority education in contemporary China; (6) development path of minority ethnic groups in the context of modernization.

Name: Religious and Ethnic Policy
Social Governance: Theory and Practice
Introduction:
Over the past thirty years, Chinese society has been undergoing unprecedented changes in history. Compared with the great achievements of economic growth, the problem of social lag has gradually become prominent: manifested in the increasing social conflicts, aggravated value differences, the decline of interpersonal trust, the increase in uncertainty in behavioral expectations, and the prominent politicization of social emotions. _x000D_
More and more people realize that although economic growth can provide a material foundation for social development, it will not directly lead to comprehensive social progress. A series of major challenges in social governance are coming one after another, but conceptual updates and knowledge preparation are still very limited. _x000D_
This course is a course that pays equal attention to basics and applications. It focuses on the history, concepts, theories, organizations, environment, practical experience and consequences of Chinese social governance, and explains the relevant characteristics from the perspectives of change and comparison. Course goal: To help students strengthen relevant training in applied policy research.

Name: Linear Regression and Its Applications
Introduction: This course is a basic course for academic master's students and professional master's students in "Social Survey and Policy Evaluation". By teaching the basic ideas of quantitative research and review of basic statistics, this course focuses on introducing regression analysis methods and applications, as well as concepts and methods such as selective bias, processing of missing data, diachronic longitudinal data, hierarchical linear models, and causal inference in quantitative research. Combining literature reading, class reports and discussions, practical operations, etc., students can basically understand and understand the basic ideas and advantages and disadvantages of quantitative research; master regression analysis methods and basic data processing procedures; and be able to ask questions on their own, use data (processing) and analysis methods to test and solve problems; and lay the foundation for future advanced statistical analysis methods and practical applications. At the same time, by introducing the basic operations and explanations of STATA software, students can basically master the basic methods and processes of data processing, and can use actual data to complete the corresponding software analysis process combined with the content in the course.

Name: Selected Readings in Marxist-Leninist Sociological Classics
Introduction:
Select the main works of Marxist classic writers on sociology for study and discussion, so that students can initially grasp the Marxist viewpoints, theories and methods of observing, analyzing and solving social problems_x000D_

Name: Studies in Foreign Sociological Theories
Introduction:
Study and research the theories and ideas of Western sociologists, including classic sociological theories and contemporary sociological theories, introduce, analyze and evaluate a representative work of major sociologists. It also introduces the academic background and social background of the main sociologists' theory formation, the process of theory formation, and the gains and losses of major theoretical perspectives. This enables students to have a clearer understanding of the entire development process of foreign sociology and to have an objective evaluation of the theories and representative works of major sociologists. Through students' own special research, they will gain a deeper understanding of the theories of major Western sociologists. _x000D_
The main contents include:_x000D_

2. Max. Weber and "Protestant Ethic and the Spirit of Capitalism"_x000D_
3. Robert. Merton and "Sociology of Ethical Theory"_x000D_
4. Lewis. Koser and "The Function of Social Conflict"_x000D_
5. Peter. Blau and "Exchange and Power in Social Life"_x000D_

Name: Labor Issues

Name: Topics in Contemporary Social Stratification Research
Introduction:
Course Description_x000D_
Social stratification is an important research field in sociology. Social stratification refers to the allocation of social members according to specific social categories/attributes into a status system with differential rewards. Social categories/attributes associated with stratification include class, occupation, gender, ethnicity, etc. These categories/attributes are common in different societies and have an important impact on social members' status acquisition, encounters, interactions, behaviors and attitudes. Research on social stratification mainly discusses the issues and mechanisms of status inequality and status acquisition processes. _x000D_
The content of this course will be based on the mainstream literature on contemporary social stratification research to provide in-depth explanations and organize discussions on five important issues in this field, including: occupational stratification, income inequality and poverty, educational inequality, gender inequality, marriage/family and stratification. In addition, this course also sets up a set of special topics on social stratification and inequality in China, focusing on the academic debates and related empirical research surrounding the formation of marketization and social stratification in China. Since this course is mainly for graduate students majoring in sociology, the teaching method will combine classroom lectures and student discussions. Compared with "Social Stratification and Mobility" for undergraduates, this course will focus more on training students' ability to think deeply about specific topics and their ability to appreciate and operate empirical research. _x000D_
_x000D_
Course Objectives_x000D_
By studying this course, reading relevant literature and participating in discussions, students can: 1. Understand the mainstream research directions and cutting-edge research topics in the field of social stratification, and have a basic understanding of the main mechanisms of status acquisition and social mobility. 2. In-depth understanding of classic propositions and important empirical research on issues such as occupational stratification, income inequality, educational inequality, gender inequality, marriage/family and stratification in contemporary Western stratification literature. 4. Learn from the research ideas and methods of Western social stratification/mobility research to study contemporary social stratification in China. _x000D_

Name: Mythology and Anthropology
Studies on Humanity's Ideal Political State
Introduction: The exploration and pursuit of ideal politics and ideal society is one of the basic activities in human history. It constitutes an important part of the history of human civilization and thought. Every great nation and every great civilization has its own imagination and thinking about an ideal society, especially ideal politics and an ideal country. From "Book of Rites" to "Book of Datong", from "Utopia" to "Utopia", almost all great thinkers at home and abroad, both ancient and modern, have paid attention to the ideal political state of mankind, and this strong concern has left a deep imprint on the development process of human society. Observing political ideals in different eras, different countries, and different civilization conditions is to observe the rich and colorful political life of mankind; exploring the roots and evolution of different political ideals is to explore the laws of human political development; looking forward to the ideal political state of mankind is to look forward to the trend and future of human political development. This course attempts to mainly teach the ideal political state pursued by thinkers from various countries throughout the ages, analyze the historical conditions and realistic background that produced these political ideals, and evaluate the gains, losses, and impact of these ideas. On this basis, teachers try to make their own analysis and predictions on ideal countries, ideal governments, ideal citizens, and ideal officials based on the current conditions of the times that mankind is living in, combined with political examples from ancient and modern times, both at home and abroad.

Introduction: The course is intended to focus on the concept of “article science”, which is inherent in China, and to address specific issues such as the contemporary flow of the ancient tradition, the main medium and late Qing generation literature, linguists, articles carriers (including collections, selected books, inks, scriptures, modern newspapers) and articles writings, as well as antiquarians, time and ancients, ethos and electives. The course is based on a “joint research” approach, which combines classroom teaching with text reading. It aims to build a knowledge framework that adequately introduces the more credible research findings of the academic community and provides guidance for postgraduate students in the relevant fields of literature. The subject of “Current articles” covered by this course is mainly in the following six areas: (i) Standards of accounting for “purity and elegance”. The political situation at the beginning of the year was influenced by the balance of science, and “purity and elegance” became the style norm in the cages of time, ancients and even poetry. This set of standards is a prerequisite for discussing new and emerging post-modern articles. (ii) The formation and reproduction of the ancient system of Kiryu City. In this process, not only have there been a series of important selections and points of appreciation, but a particularly far-reaching set of classical-centred articles and correctional practices has emerged. (iii) The emergence of texts and policy papers. With the advent of the Judas to bring down the world's thinking, the book has become increasingly popular and its content has shifted from a secondary-school economy to Western polity. The Qingqing Qing Qing Qi has changed the policy paper (China's political history, foreign political art policy, four books) to replace the production of art (four books) for a short period of time and become the centre of the general literary life. (iv) The shift in the volume of articles from the “text collection” to the “press” has been accompanied by a number of changes in the mindset of writing, reader pre-sets, structure, linguistics, etc. Compared to the “text collection”, the “press body” has become a new phenomenon in articles of great interest. (v) Interaction of new terms with the new body. Qingmingxi High School, followed by the trend of “Tung Si” (Japan Academic) and the influx of new terms from the Western Ocean and Japan. With the proliferation of translations of literature, particularly the rapid development of foreign literature, such as “and Manhan reading”, foreign terms, expressions and writings are rapidly found in newspaper articles and even in public and private literature, from terminological to grammar, completing the recent modernization of the body of literature. (vi) The introduction of neighbouring knowledge systems of literature, such as law and rhetoric, in the western language, affecting the extraction, practice and presentation of literature.

Introduction:
Course Description_x000D_
Course purpose:_x000D_
The "R Language Statistical Analysis Application" course teaches the basic concepts of statistical analysis, elementary and advanced statistical analysis techniques, and how to perform elementary and advanced statistical analysis with R language. The theory and cases are combined to teach students the theoretical knowledge of elementary and advanced statistical analysis techniques and case analysis, so that students can understand and master the R language, implement elementary and advanced statistical analysis techniques, and be able to apply the learned analytical technical knowledge in actual scientific research work. _x000D_
Basics of starting a course_x000D_
This course uses R language as a carrier to implement elementary and advanced statistical analysis. R is a programming language and environment for statistical computing that is similar to the S language developed by Rick Becker, John Chambers, and Allan Wilks at AT&T Bell Laboratories. Depending on the operating system, the R language has UNIX versions, Windows versions, and Mac versions, and can run on computer systems of different architectures. All source code for the R language is freely available for inspection or exploitation. The open source nature, flexibility, and highly flexible database interface technology of R language make it particularly suitable for data analysis. _x000D_
This course will include a brief introduction to key terms in the use of R language and is suitable for graduate students without any foundation in statistical data analysis. Therefore, students do not need to be familiar with the basics of computer programming knowledge to understand and master basic and advanced statistical analysis methods and cases of R language through the study of this course. _x000D_
Teaching requirements_x000D_
(1) Understand and master the basic concepts of statistical analysis_x000D_
(2) Understand and master basic and advanced statistical analysis techniques_x000D_
(3) Understand and master R language for primary and advanced statistical analysis_x000D_
(4) Implement primary and advanced statistical analysis applications through R language

Name: The Nation-State and Modern Education
Introduction: This course plans to lead students to systematically read the twentieth-century German and French intellectual circles on the role of universities in the process of civilization and nation-states, as well as the impact of issues such as epistemology and scientific genealogy on higher education. The course selects three works about Germany: 1) Elias’s Civilization Process explains the transformation from feudal society to a modern country, the civilization process driven by the etiquette of the court nobles in this process, and the debate about civilization and culture triggered by this. 2) Meinecke’s classic discussion on cosmopolitanism and nation-states sorted out how to describe the existence value of nation-states and their relationship with cosmopolitanism within the German intellectual tradition. His book focuses on Humboldt, the Romantics and Hegel's thinking on this issue, which leads to questions about the purpose of education and the role of universities. 3) Ringer’s writings further focus on German universities in the first half of the 20th century, tracing how German intellectuals (Mandarin), who were shaped by Enlightenment rationality and universalist concepts, were impacted by numerous cultural value conflicts such as nationalism, modernism, and scientism during this period. The transformation that universities and intellectuals must face in this process. The course also selects two works by French thinkers: 1) How to view Bourdieu's discussion of the state and the cultivation mechanism of elitism from the perspective of the process of civilization; 2) Foucault's Words and Things explores the epistemological basis of university departmental distinctions from a genealogical perspective, as well as the modern transformation of epistemological paradigms, that is, how language changes from grammar to linguistics, how organic life changes from the discussion of natural history to biology, and how the understanding of money changes from the science of wealth to modern economics.

Name: Topics in the Philosophy of Education
Introduction:
Content summary:_x000D_
Higher education has always been a field closely related to philosophy. Philosophy has always been a core course in medieval and modern universities. The university philosophy at that time was inextricably linked to the trend of philosophical thought. Since the 20th century, higher education has played an increasingly important role in national and social life, and higher education philosophy as a discipline has gradually moved from independence to maturity. Based on the basic principle of unity of logic and history, this course attempts to make a relatively comprehensive summary of the philosophical issues existing in the history and reality of higher education, and explores the possibility of establishing a localized higher education philosophy in China based on the actual situation of higher education in my country. This course condenses my experience in the research on the philosophy of higher education in recent years. While striving to have a solid theoretical foundation, some of the views and opinions expounded are intended to share some relatively new and unique things with everyone. I believe it will be beneficial to the topic selection and theoretical research of graduate students in higher education and other related majors. _x000D_
This course belongs to the "Special Research on Educational Philosophy" series and requires course candidates to have a foundation in studying "Educational Philosophy" courses. In addition, it also requires learners to have a knowledge background in higher education research, and it is best to organically combine course study with graduation thesis. _x000D_

Name: Fundamentals of Child Psychiatry
College: School of Psychological and Cognitive Sciences
Introduction:
Children and adolescents are susceptible to psychological disorders. The current prevalence of mental problems among children and adolescents in my country has exceeded the international average level of 15%-20%. Conduct disorders and juvenile delinquency are on the rise, and many childhood and adolescent diseases have poor prognosis and difficult treatment. Carrying out children's mental health has become a requirement of the development of the times, and the understanding of children's mental illness and mental health need to be developed urgently. _x000D_
Child psychiatry studies the causes, pathogenesis, symptoms and clinical patterns of childhood mental disorders, as well as related issues such as prevention, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation. It emerged later than general psychiatry. Child psychiatry was not accepted as a medical specialty until 1957. Our country has been gradually developing since the 1970s. Child psychiatry is closely related to abnormal psychology, developmental psychology, psychotherapy and other disciplines in clinical psychology, but also has differences in content and form. It also has strong clinical practical significance. It has a great assisting and promoting effect on the training of students majoring in clinical psychology and other related majors. It is also a very distinctive practical science. This course will be based on the 10th edition of the Classification and Diagnostic Criteria for Mental Disorders (ICD-10) published by the World Health Organization as a reference for the classification, nomenclature and diagnosis of mental disorders in children. The purpose of the lecture is to enable students to familiarize themselves with and master the basic theories, basic knowledge, and basic skills of child and adolescent psychiatry, as well as the latest developments in child and adolescent psychiatry at home and abroad. And various media forms and interactive methods such as video, recording, simulation, and acting can be used to inspire the audience to think actively. After explaining the clinical manifestations of a certain mental disorder, typical clinical cases will be presented, which can better help the audience understand and master relevant knowledge. _x000D_

Name: Taphonomy
Introduction: The concept of burial was introduced by paleontologists in the 1940s. It is a knowledge of the entire process of post-graduate objects changing from death, destruction, degeneration, handling, burial to burial. As a result, the concept was introduced into archaeological studies, which were closely linked to animal remnants and were used mainly to analyse the causes of, and changes in, the burial process of animal remnants in the sites, thus providing a more accurate analysis of their relationship to human activity. However, with the development of archaeology, the concept and research methods of burial are being updated and refined to give it a broader meaning and meaning: That is, the study of the various components of the site, the way and process of its composition, origin, accumulation and burial, as well as the changes that have taken place after its burial, in order to understand the process of its formation, the causes and characteristics of the burial of the various types of remains, on the basis of which the human activity information recorded by the site is more accurately and comprehensively judged and extracted. Sites are a key vehicle for archaeological research, with a clear understanding of the process of their formation and transformation, and of the types of sites, the causes of their remnant and the characteristics of their burial, which are prerequisites for our understanding of the context in which archaeological material originates; a prerequisite for our scientific analysis and accurate interpretation of the relationship between the remnants; a key to the creation of a reliable series of epochal years; and, above all, a necessary precondition for our accurate, objective and comprehensive recovery of prehistoric human activity. Burial science is therefore the basis for archaeological research. Based on traditional burials, the course will teach a wider and deeper scale of burials, taking into account the new methods and research perspectives of the international frontier, with the distinctive feature of combining macro- and micro-level perspectives and approaches to the process of the formation of sites, the legacy background and the manner in which human activities and sites are occupied. The main elements include (1) an analysis of the type, composition, sources and causes of accumulations of sites, based on the analysis of geological features and microstructures and mineral components, and an analysis of the burial environment and changes; and (2) a systematic analysis of animal and fire residues to interpret the burial and post-burial processes and to determine whether the remains are related to human activities and are influenced by other factors, reflecting human activities, the manner in which the sites are occupied, the intensity and change processes, and the local environmental context of human activities. In response to the above questions, I will teach basic concepts, knowledge, research methods in the field of burial science, such as soil microstructure, animal archaeology analysis, experimental archaeology, national archaeology, and lead students to take stock of the development of the study and to prepare them for a better understanding of archaeology and the practice and research of archaeological excavations, taking into account typical sites at home and abroad, as well as research hot spots and frontier discussions. The course will also lead students to explore sites and study field trips to deepen their understanding of the above issues and to promote their reflection through practice.

Name: Methods in Human Skeletal Archaeology

This course focuses on the commonly used methods in archaeological research on human bones, but does not include biochemical analysis of bones, molecular biology analysis, histological analysis and other research methods that require special equipment. Instead, it focuses on simple, economical and fast analysis methods of the general morphology of bones, and understands how to explore the evolution of human populations and their lifestyles through the general morphology of bones and teeth. Through practical operations in the course, students can have a solid and proficient grasp of the general morphology observation method of bones and understand its applicability, advantages and limitations. It is a corollary of the combination of "historical questions and critical or aesthetic thinking" and is an important expression of the theoretical depth and breadth of world literary research and an important way for national literature to move towards dialogue and communication. The course places particular emphasis on comparative studies of the cultural systems of countries as a whole, of literature and art, and of interpretation and literary theorists. It should be emphasized that comparative poetry is not a mere literary comparison. Its purpose is to find common issues of concern in cross-cultural references in order to achieve deeper communication and to find new issues in different cultural "and different" to grasp the universal pattern of literary development.

Name: Studies in Spanish-Language Narrative Literature
Introduction: The course is a Ph.D. post-graduate thematic discussion. In accordance with the direction of research or academic interest in doctoral dissertations, a representative group of writers or writers in the history of the development of narratives in the Spanish-speaking country is the subject of in-depth research on the subject matter of the work, its methodology, its internal structure, its philosophical content and its social orientation, taking into account the historical, social and cultural background of the work, the author ' s personal life experience and ideological orientation. At the same time, students are required to study in depth the theoretical development of narratives, to be able to apply one of the theories, to undertake text analysis and to prepare their papers.

Name: Topics in German Literature
Introduction: The presentation and analysis of the topics of focus at the various stages of the development of German literature provide students with a more comprehensive picture of the development of German literature based on an analysis of German literature trends, writers and works.

Name: Western Classical and Medieval Culture
Introduction: A more detailed presentation and discussion of the basic thinking patterns and images of Western literature, as well as of works of great significance in the creation of Western literary ideas, requires the active participation of students in understanding the basic trends of Western literature and culture from ancient Greek Rome to the Middle Ages in comparison with Chinese culture and literature, and has some insight into and insight into some classic author works.

Name: Academic Paper Writing
Introduction: In postgraduate education, the writing of academic thesis is crucial. The purpose of this course is to improve the writing skills of graduate students, deepen their professional awareness and develop their scientific capabilities. The contents of the teaching include: examination of subjects, collection of information, research methods, establishment of arguments, validation process, writing style, revision of dissertation, professional literature, foreign digests, writing formats, etc. The course requires postgraduate students to complete academic papers with a certain number of words before or at the same time.

Name: Topics in Taiwanese Literature
College: Department of Chinese Language and Literature
Introduction: I. Basic objectives The outstanding achievements of Taiwan literature since the twentieth century constitute a unique part of Chinese literature. As a result of colonial rule and the division of the Taiwan Straits, Taiwan society and literature have developed features that are both connected and distinct from the mainland. The recognition of this specialty has a direct impact on the understanding of Taiwan ' s culture and society, as well as on communication and communication between the two sides. This course will enable students to deepen their knowledge and understanding of Taiwan literature and culture, broaden their horizons and understand in many ways the impact of different regions and social situations on cultural phenomena and literature, starting with the interpretation of historical literature, social phenomena and literary texts, and integrate the theoretical and text analysis of cultural research. II. Executive summary and allocation of school hours (total 32 hours) The curriculum includes reading and analysis of Taiwan culture and Taiwan literature. Focusing on Taiwan ' s new literature in the twentieth century, and in the context of Taiwan ' s socio-cultural background, the study focused on the unique cultural and literary styles resulting from Taiwan ' s unique historical destiny and reality; the cultural character, identity and literary imagination of Taiwan during the colonial period; the literary writing, literary thought and literary production of Taiwan during the post-colonial period; the classic author ' s works and literary hotspot analysis. This course is part of the French language programme, which develops practical French reading skills and highlights text reading training for the literary profession. The selected reading materials include the classic texts of modern French-speaking world literature, which are not limited to French literature. Language teaching is accompanied by the teaching of the basics of French-language world literature and the enhancement of language understanding.
The course is offered to postgraduate students with a primary French-language basis.
