Name: Topics in Modern Eastern Literature
Introduction:
From the early nineteenth century to the present, Eastern countries have undergone a dramatic transition from traditional to modern societies. As a result of the transformation of Eastern culture, modern literature in the East has undergone intense renewal and transformation. An essential link has emerged in the chain of literature development in Eastern countries: the transition between tradition and modernity, and between traditional literature and modern new literature. In the course of the conflict and slow integration of East-West cultures, Eastern countries have introduced Western literature, adapted traditional literature, completed the alternation and transformation of old and new literature and built new systems of discourse. As Western literature enters the Eastern countries, the Eastern literature, although increasingly "Westernized", still seeks to explore the broader ways and paths of national literature in the context of traditional and modernity, the East and the West, and nations and the world. A group of writers with worldwide influence has emerged, with a worldwide cultural vision, with a spirit of "willings to transcend" and adherence to the spirit of national spirituality and to the aesthetic style of national aestheticism, and has broken the world pattern of the "European Centre for Literature" with unique creativity.
The purpose of the course, which combines the work of individual writers with a detailed reading of texts, is to provide an in-depth analysis of the meaning, role and impact of Eastern modern literature. The purpose of the course is to provide students with an understanding of the contribution of Eastern modern literature to bringing world literature into a new era of East-West dialogue, plural symbiotic life and universal ties of literature.

Name: General Bengali (I)
Introduction: After learning the basic characteristics of the Bengali language and having the initial ability to read and write, the texts are combined to teach the common vocabulary and basic grammar; ultimately, it is possible to communicate freely with Bangladeshis and to read and study the books in Bengali by means of dictionary.

Name: Relations between Eastern and Western Literature
Introduction: On the basis of a macro-presentation of the study of Oriental literature (e.g. the basis for the study of Oriental literature, the basic features of Oriental literature, the formation, development and interaction of the three main literary systems of the East, the history of research in China, etc.), the course focuses on exchanges and the influence of ancient, Chinese, near-modern East-West literature, the system of Oriental literature, the general development of world literature made up of East-West literature, and the analysis of the historical status and important impact of the various buried and important works in the East in the history of world literature. It seeks neither to lower Western literature to promote oriental literature nor simply to reject the “European centralism” as a purely academic view. Through teaching, students are made to realize that they cannot turn a blind eye to literature that has developed and prospered thousands of years in the East because of the near-modern centennial backwardness of Oriental literature; and that they are nurtured in their love of Oriental literature, Eastern civilization and Eastern culture, so that they can benefit and inspire from their studies and enhance their pride as an Easter.

Name: General Bengali (III)
Introduction: Bengali is an Indo-European-speaking Hindu language and is the official language of Bangladesh and India in West Bengal and Tripura, with a population of approximately 270 million and the seventh largest language in the world. The well-known Indian poet, Tegor, works in his native Bengali. One of the first books in Bengali was the 10th century Buddhist poem, Jhariyabood. Bangladesh’s linguistics are brilliant, and well-known Bangla writers, in addition to the Nobel Prize for Literature, include the literature of Bangim, Nazluor and Shorod. Learning Bengali is an important lesson in learning the Bengali language in Oriental literature

Name: Population Health Epidemiology
Introduction:
Epidemiology is both an applied discipline and a very logical scientific research method. Based on multidisciplinary knowledge, it investigates the disease and health status of social groups by means of observations and inquiries, describes the frequency and distribution, presents research assumptions by summarizing and analysing them, and then uses analytical studies to test research assumptions, which can eventually rise to theoretical heights and predict population disease or health status using mathematical models. Epidemiological research methods have therefore been extended to a wide range of diseases, state of health and social sciences and have become increasingly useful. Research in the field of population and health is also based on an epidemiological approach. The objective of this project is to introduce an epidemiological approach into the field of population health research, which will not only strengthen the development of a basic postgraduate degree course in the field of population health, but also serve as an important cross-cutting interdisciplinary programme in the area of population health and epidemiological research, which will also contribute to the development of postgraduate academic research and innovation.
The basics of the course are master ' s degree and doctoral studies at the Institute of Population Studies, and there is a need for postgraduate studies in gerontology, disability, population and health.
Teaching requirements: To be familiar with the type of epidemiological methods commonly used, to understand their characteristics, advantages and limitations, to learn about their correct choice and complete scientific design, to use epidemiological methods to solve problems in the area of population health, and to identify and prevent major biases in scientific research.

Name: Reading and Writing Research Papers
Introduction: This course is compulsory for postgraduate students and is designed to provide systematic orientation and guidance to both master ' s (academic and professional) and doctoral students in the entire process of writing scientific papers, from research design to the publication of the papers. This course will enable postgraduate students to feel the scientific atmosphere at the first stage of their studies, guide the reading of scientific papers and the knowledge of international literature, develop a systematic knowledge of the methods of writing scientific papers and lay the normative foundation for scientific research, thereby raising the academic awareness, scientific rigour, scientific innovation and scientific writing skills of highly qualified graduate students in the preparation of their dissertation and future research work, and developing more comprehensive and integrated scientific skills.

Name: Applied Regression Analysis
Introduction: The main elements of the course include the meaning of linear regression models, model assumptions, parameter estimates and parameter extrapolations, several different forms of non-linear regression models (Logistic, Probit, Ordered Probit, etc.), the meaning and characteristics of various models, parameter estimates and parameter extrapolations, and the diagnosis and revision of linear regression models and non-linear regression models. The course will also discuss the development of regression models with actual data and introduce the SPSS and STATA statistical software. The purpose of this course is to give students an understanding and mastery of the fundamentals of regression models, the correct use of models, rational interpretation of model parameters, and the ability to apply them in social science in a normative manner.

Name: Survival Analysis
Introduction: Survival analysis is the statistical analysis of the occurrence and duration of the event. The methodology was first applied in the study of death and was therefore designated survival analysis. In practice, this method can be applied in various fields, as long as it is an analysis of the duration of a given situation, it can be classified as a survival analysis, from marriage to divorce, from unemployment to re-employment, the duration of a disease, etc. In the field of medicine, it is generally called Survival Analysis; in sociology, it is called Even History Analysis; in engineering, it is known as Reliability Analysis; or in economics, it is called Duration Analysis or Transfer Analysis. The purpose of the course is to equip students of social sciences with the most advanced international statistical analysis methods and to apply them to research in social sciences. Multimedia classrooms are required.

Name: Social Science Research on Population and Reproductive Health
Mixed Models and Their Applications
Introduction: The hybrid model is a large statistical model for the analysis of non-independent, tiered or vertical data and is an extension of the generic fixed effect linear regression model and the addition of random effects. Mixing means a mixture of fixed and random effects. The traditional linear regression model is mainly based on an independent sample obtained from a simple random sample and assumes that the variable is a given constant. However, with the emergence of a large number of complex sampling and longitudinal survey data, traditional statistical models are no longer adapted to the analysis of such new data, whereas the analysis of such data is mainly based on such hybrid analytical methods. The course focuses not only on the general rationale of methods, but also on their application in stratification and vertical analysis, enabling students to master this advanced statistical methodology in both theory and practice.

Name: Quantitative Research Methods and Applications in Population Health
Introduction: Population health is an important scientific topic, and population health issues have also been the subject of special attention in many disciplines. In population health research, with the expansion of research subjects, broad participation in a wide range of disciplines and the increasing wealth of research data, postgraduate students need more systematic quantitative methodological knowledge and a pool of applied experience in order to adopt the right approach to achieving research on health issues of interest to the population. The course will integrate cross-disciplinary approaches from a problem-solving perspective, guided by the achievement of research objectives, the teaching of the main quantitative methods and their practical application in population health research, and the comprehensive upgrading of postgraduate capacity for autonomous scientific design and research in the application and data analysis of practical research methods.

Name: Social Security and Welfare for the Elderly
Human Behavior and the Social Environment
Economics and Health Systems
Introduction:
The course attempts to interpret the operating patterns of the health-care system using economic theory (mainly the price theory component), focusing on the broader “systems” and understanding the phenomena, behaviour patterns and role of the system in the health sector.
This discipline is a new field, an experiment, or economics of the health system. The shift in institutional economics from economics to institutional economics has been ignored by traditional economics, with many theories, modelling and the like, such as the assumption of complete information and the assumption of zero transaction costs.
The course on economics and health systems corresponds to health economics, which basically follows the economics approach, studying health and the demand for and provision of health services, largely following the traditional economics approach, which focuses on the unique institutional characteristics and operating patterns of health care, health, and uses the theories and concepts of traditional economics and systemic economics.

Name: Deep Reinforcement Learning and Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Learning through interaction may be the first learning course for humanity. Similarly, learning through interaction is a fundamental idea of almost all learning theories. This course will present an important approach to interactive learning - intensive learning. The course will teach intensive learning and multi-intellectual intensive learning. It will cover, inter alia, the basic theory of intensive learning, traditional intensive learning algorithms, in-depth enhanced learning algorithms and deep multi-intellectual enhanced learning algorithms. This course is for postgraduate students, assuming that students have acquired relevant knowledge such as probabilistic theory and machine learning bases. Students will learn from theory and practice to enhance learning, to equip them with the basic theory and key algorithms of enhanced learning and the ability to use it to solve application problems. The courses include classroom lectures, research on dissertation and algorithmic practice. The course examination consists of studies and course design. Of these, 40 per cent were studies and 60 per cent were curriculum design.

Name: Optimization Methods in Machine Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The course will present the optimization methods commonly used in machine learning, including, inter alia, the decline in coordinates, the decline in the (sub) gradient, the Frank-Wolfe algorithm, the LaGrandjjject series algorithm (the staggered orientation method, linear staggered orientation method, etc.), the puppet problem, the penalty function method, the Newton method, and advanced topics such as accelerator, the random gradient method, the KL condition, the helipad method, double-layer optimization, multi-purpose optimization, the optimization towards thinness and hypothylene, as a theoretical basis, the underlying concepts of the relevant mathematical analysis and condensing analysis will be taught in the preceding period. The reasoning and proof of representative theory and methodology will be explained. The purpose of the course is to equip graduate students with the most commonly used technology for machine learning and to reach out to the research frontier. Students who choose this subject need to have an advance knowledge of mathematics analysis, advanced algebra, and have higher requirements for mathematical competence.

Name: Data Visualization
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Visualization is an important element in the processing of large data analyses, and this course is intended for graduate students with certain requirements for data processing and covers basic methods and principles of visualization.

Name: Theory and Methods of Multimedia Information Retrieval
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Multimedia information retrieval has become the hotspot of research in the age of cyberdata explosion and is an important foundation for applications such as web-based multimedia search engines, multimedia big data analysis and processing, product image searches, and smart image recognition. The course will summarize and explain classical issues, models, theories and methods in multimedia information retrieval research and recent developments in the field. The presentations included: 1) an overview of multimedia information retrieval; 2) text-based image and video retrieval; 3) content-based image and video retrieval; and 4) recent developments in multimedia information retrieval. The course will focus on content-based image and video retrieval and will present relevant video feature extraction and learning algorithms, data index algorithms, machine learning algorithms, and reprocessing algorithms. The course is intended to provide students with basic questions, theories and methods for the retrieval of multimedia information and to stimulate their research interest in this area.

Name: Digital Image Processing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Teaching Practicum
Introduction: Postgraduate students interested in scientific teaching are able to combine their basic theory, basic skills, professional skills and pedagogical and psychological knowledge and gradually develop and develop the capacity to perform their educational work independently, offering an optional course on " Internships " , which takes place in conjunction with the actual situation of cross-cutting colleges, for an open period of time, for two grades in the autumn and spring.

Name: Cloud Computing and Big Data Platforms
Introduction: The course will present the three dimensions of the theory, technology and application of cloud computing and large data platforms, using a selection of real cases from the current state of the industry to present the current status of cloud computing and big data developments in the IT industry, as well as their values and challenges, focusing on key technologies such as cloud computing, automation of virtualization and management, cloud computing platform architecture; concepts related to big data, key technologies and large data platform architecture; and typical applications of cloud computing platforms and large data platforms. As a front-line professional course, the cloud computing and large data platform courses focus on building practical capacities for the theoretical integration of students. In addition to requiring students to be fully aware of basic principles and techniques such as distributed system architecture, cloud computing basics such as IaaS/PaaS/SaaS, virtualization techniques and packaging techniques, cloud computing key technologies such as management and service automation, distributive data computing framework (Hadoop), memory-based computing framework (SARK), real-time stream data-processing STORM-like data computing platform and distributed machine learning frameworks such as the key components of large data platforms such as Mahout or MLlib, it is hoped that the capacity of students to design, develop and apply cloud computing and large data platforms will be improved through practice. The knowledge points of this course, which mostly relate to current hotspot research issues, will be presented in each teaching unit on current trends in cloud computing and large data fields, and will organize discussions and analysis of representative academic research papers and their technical problems and potential research directions, in the hope that this will enable graduate students to master basic independent methods of scientific and technological research.

Name: Frontier Advances in Aerospace Information Engineering
Introduction: As a front-line course for post-graduate students, Advances in Space Information Engineering aims to provide students with an overview of advances in space information technology and the latest advances in space information systems in the country, to broaden their perspectives, broaden their thinking and deepen their understanding and understanding of space information engineering. The main sections of the Advances in Space Information Engineering are as follows: (a) First: an overview of the space-related information project, which presents the basic concepts of the space-related information project and a representative typical space-based information system; (b) Second: progress of the Space Information Control System (SCI), providing information on advances in technology in the instrumentation instrumentation of aerospace platforms, forward technology in the measurement and system control of aerospace systems; Thirdly, the progress of the satellite navigational positioning system, which describes the basic principles of satellite positioning, the latest developments in GPS, GLONSAA and Beidou navigational positioning; Fourth: GIS frontier technology, which introduces the basic concepts of GIS and the latest developments in GIS; Fifth: Front-line technology for satellite communication systems, which describes the basic principles of satellite communications and forward technology in the relevant directions of data encryption, transmission, reception, etc., in satellite communications; Sixth: Advances in the early warning system for aerospace reconnaissance, describing the composition of the early warning system for aerial detection, the rationale for radar detection, hidden technologies and recent research developments; Seventh presentation: progress of the Space Remote Sensing Information Access System, presentation of basic concepts of remote sensing and recent developments of the Remote Sensing Information Access System; Eighth session: Space Remote Sensing Information Processing and Applications Frontline Technologies, presenting the latest developments and frontier technologies in remote sensing data processing and applications; Ninth session: Space-borne remote sensing information dissemination and sharing of technological advances, forward-looking technologies and up-to-date systems in relevant directions, such as processing, distribution and sharing of remote sensing data; Tenth: progress of the Integrated Command and Control System for Space-Specific Information, providing an update on the latest developments in the Integrated Command and Control System for Space-Specific Systems and related front-line technologies; 11: Advances in communication counter-traffic technology, information counter-traffic technology in space communications, and forward technology in the direction of communications decryption, electromagnetic suppression, etc.; XII: Progress in the Integrated Management System for Space-related Information, presentation of progress in the Integrated Management System for Space-based Vehicles and forward technology in the direction of flight route management, status monitoring, etc.; (c) Thirteenth presentation: progress of the Integrated Ground-based Safeguards System, presentation of forward technology in the direction of ground-based radar detection systems, progress of automated landing systems and spacecraft launch recovery;

Name: Optimization Methods
Introduction: Learning about the basic nature of non-binding and binding solutions to smooth non-linear optimization, etc. Through this course of study, students are expected to acquire basic optimization methods, develop their initial abilities for theoretical analysis of algorithms, and develop their ability to solve problems through computer optimization. This course is open only to postgraduate students other than those in mathematics.

Name: Recommender System Algorithms and Applications
Introduction:
The course focuses on the various classical algorithms of the recommended system, forward algorithms and some typical applications. Through this course, students can learn not only about the ideas, principles and realization of the various classic recommended algorithms and forward algorithms, but also about the application of the various recommended algorithms and some typical application cases and the future direction of the recommended system.
Students are required to have basic statistical knowledge of linear algebra and probability.

Name: Management and Mining of Massive Graph Data
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Course content: With the development of information technology, there has been an increasing number of map-based data, such as biological network data, social network data, semantic network data, etc. Unlike traditional relationship-type data, which emphasize relationships between objects, queries for these data are usually structured on the basis of chart structure, such as path-based queries, subgraph matching queries, etc. The main elements of the course are: a summary of the main current research topics of the chart data, including: frequent subchart excavation algorithms; path search algorithms; subchart matching query algorithms; and keyword search methods on the map database. Also present are the applications of the Map Database in big XML file management, semantic web data management, data management in GIS, and biological network data management, and social network data management. Purpose of the course: 1. Several basic search and excavation algorithms for the map database 2. Understanding the application of graphic database technologies in different areas 3. Building the capacity of students to think independently and conduct research. Basis of the course: 1. Database Foundation or related courses 2. Foundation of Graphics or related courses 3. Data Structure and Algorithms or related courses Teaching requirements: Multimedia classrooms with projectors. 1. 54 school hours, 18 weeks Three to four courses (60 per cent of examinations), 3. Students are free to choose subjects related to the curriculum and to write reports on course studies (30 per cent of the examination). 4. 10 per cent of the examinations for performance in classes (including attendance and answers to questions during classes) The report of the course study consists of two forms, one being chosen by the student: 1) An overview of the literature: a description of the research background and related work on the subject. It also provides its own comments on the different research findings available. 2) Dissertational reports: students are encouraged to undertake innovative research on a particular subject and to write papers.

Name: Principles of Database and Knowledge Base Systems
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Technological Innovation and Entrepreneurship
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The programme is designed to foster innovative thinking among students, to familiarize them with basic entrepreneurial processes such as industrial analysis, demand management, product design, business plans, and entrepreneurial skills such as team building and leadership development.
The course, which focuses on students listening to lectures, invites a number of successful entrepreneurs to teach outstanding life lessons, with a large number of classroom discussions, supported by practical case analyses such as networking of goods, big enterprise data, artificial intelligence, high-tech industries, etc. The practice is driven by a team project in which students are personally involved in project research and development and experience the passion and hard work of technological entrepreneurship. Depending on the characteristics of the innovative projects proposed by the students themselves, a guest of instruction or leader of the relevant industry is arranged to interact and guide the various entrepreneurial teams under the curriculum and to develop students ' scientific and technical sensitivity and business smell.
Building on the successful implementation of the Career Planning and Leadership Development course for many years, a North Grand Duke's course on “Technology, Innovation and Entrepreneurship” was held in spring 2016. According to feedback from the first session, many graduate masters wish to be given the opportunity to choose a course, many graduate students have attended the course throughout the course in the absence of an option and have participated in the design of algorithm models and the development of prototype systems. This is an application for a class of graduate and doctoral students of the same name to develop the soft quality of innovative entrepreneurship and leadership and to lay a better foundation for future development.

Name: Principles of Machine Learning
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Prerequisite: Mathematical statistics, matrix theory, digital image processing, digital media technology base
Introduction:
Image video analysis processing is an important research direction in the area of artificial intelligence, and machine learning is key to image video analysis processing. The course focuses on the theory, methods and techniques of machine learning that are commonly used in different tasks of image and video analysis.
At the content level, the course is based on algorithms and techniques, course design and reporting, and is closely linked to the relevant frontier areas of research and application. It is a basic specialized course with a strong theoretical background and wide application. The topics included three modules: the introduction to machine learning; machine learning methods for image video analysis, including Bayes decision-making and classification, clustering, characterization and flow learning, nuclear methods and support vectors, in-depth learning, etc.; curriculum design, using machine learning knowledge to resolve 1-2 international and national algorithmic tasks in the area of image video analysis processing; or participation in the research and development of artificially intelligent open-source platforms.
The course requires more solid mathematical statistics, digital video processing basics and programming skills. The teaching objectives of the course are to emphasize the learning of basic theoretical knowledge, to encourage students to use machine science to address the challenging tasks of image video analysis processing and to lay the foundation for subsequent relevant research and development.

Name: Fracture Mechanics
Introduction: Fracture mechanics has long been a basic specialized course in solid mechanics, which is not available at the post-graduate course in Northern Grand Solid mechanics. To this end, it is proposed that this course be introduced from this year ' s autumn semester. The curriculum ' s interpretation of content is based on the concept of knowledge components, including the classic Griffith break theory, the analysis of linear elastic cracks, stress intensity factors and energy release rates, the opening shift of cracks, the concepts of plastic fractures, J credit points, HRR field, J resistance curves, etc., and thematic extension sections, including composite fractures, dynamic crack extensions, interface fractures, stretches of fatigue, numerical simulations of fractures and three-dimensional cracks. In addition, three hours of experimental classes are arranged to test the fracture resilience of metal materials.

Name: Dynamic Testing Techniques
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to enhance basic training in experiments by master ' s degree studies in solid mechanics in dynamic testing techniques related to solid mechanics. To this end, the curriculum includes the measurement of vibration, stress wave and dynamic break-up properties, as well as material dynamic mechanics, and experimental studies in conjunction with modern and commonly used electron and photometric experimental techniques. This course is based on a university course on experimental mechanics and extends to experimental studies on dynamic mechanics. In addition to the classroom, there are six basic teaching experiments, including general dynamic stress measurement, transient response measurement, dynamic stress wave transmission, dynamic fractures, vibrations, and modelling. The teaching requirements include teaching experiments, laboratory reports and final examinations.

Name: Microscopic Molecular Simulation
Introduction: Course introduction: The course is aimed at a Ph.D. post-graduate degree at the Institute of Engineering. It is designed to present the history of developments and the state of research in micromolecules simulations. It involves many simulations and practical applications of molecular dynamics and Monte Carlo methods, as well as some current development frontiers, such as the use of machine learning for molecular dynamics simulations. The course will focus on: (i) theoretical foundations of molecular dynamics; (ii) representative empirical fields based on classical molecular dynamics, with examples of systems that molecular dynamics can handle and the related physical and mechanical nature; and (iii) computational simulation methods based on quantum mechanics (simplified introduction), highlighting density general theory that is widely integrated with molecular dynamics, highlighting the characteristics that do not require predictability of empirical parameters. 4) Micromolecular simulation methods based on machine learning. The course is three credits. Students are required to have certain materials and basic knowledge of computing science. Through this course, students are required to master basic conceptual and applied areas of simulation such as molecular dynamics.

Name: Thermodynamics of Climate Change
Introduction: Climate change thermodynamics is the basic course for studying the mechanisms, impacts and coping strategies of climate change. From a thermodynamic point of view, the course introduces thermodynamic climate models, detailing the role of critical elements such as the water-gas cycle, greenhouse gases and landscapes in climate formation and change; and describes the application of input-output analysis models in climate change policymaking, enabling students to use the models to analyse key human activities leading to increased greenhouse gas concentrations and landscape change and to make feasible policy recommendations. Approximately 80 per cent of the time is spent in this course in the classroom and about 20 per cent of the time is spent in discussions. Examinations were 60 per cent successful and attendance and classroom discussions 40 per cent.

Name: Scientific and Technical Writing in English
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to present basic knowledge and techniques for writing and reporting scientific and technical papers in English. The content includes professional English, the basic structure of scientific and technical papers, the presentation of parts, contributions to the papers, and the preparation of academic reports and presentations. In addition to teaching by teachers, students are required to train in writing and speaking.

Name: Systems Ecology
Introduction: The broad ecosystem is a complex system that encompasses different dimensions, such as geography, nature and society, and the discipline on ecosystems and their sustainable development is a multidisciplinary and cross-cutting discipline with a high degree of complexity and complexity. Therefore, studies of ecology must master the thinking of systems science and analytical and modelling methods for systematic decision-making. The course is based on general theories of system science, such as system theory, informatics, dissipation structure theory, synergetics, and culpability, combining the basic theoretical foundations of eco-thermal science, using teaching, discussion and case studies, integrating basic theories and research methods of system ecology, enabling students to acquire basic knowledge of system science, basic principles of system ecology and modelling tools, and initial development of the systematic design and research skills required by students in practical work such as ecological planning.

Name: Mathematical Foundations of Materials Science
Introduction: Courses for master ' s degree students in materials from various professional backgrounds to acquire basic mathematical tools in materials science and engineering for relatively short periods of time. Basic mathematical methods of material science and engineering are mastered over a semester.

Name: Laboratory Safety
Introduction:
This course is offered to undergraduate and graduate students and to relevant laboratory research employees. The purpose of this course is to familiarize and familiarize students with general knowledge of laboratory safety and basic safety procedures.
The course will cover a number of safety issues, including physical and chemical safety, as well as the handling of hazardous waste, the safety of micro-organisms and biological and chemical materials, fire safety, safety in the workplace in human engineering, personal protective equipment and emergency procedures. At the same time, given the extensive use of nanotechnology in scientific research, teaching materials will provide basic nanotechnology safety awareness education. Furthermore, the course will address the importance of professional ethics and academic integrity and honesty in scientific research and preventive measures.

Name: Materials Analysis and Characterization Techniques
Introduction: For graduate students in material science and engineering, knowledge and mastery of material analysis and needle-raising techniques are essential. The course seeks to provide, over a semester, a comprehensive presentation of most of the commonly used analytical and testosterone techniques designed in material science and engineering research. Students are informed about the analysis of the entire material field.

Name: Advanced Materials Chemistry
Introduction:
(b) The chemical design of materials based on their nature. It also provides students with access to materials for use in nanotechnologies, open-mindedness and follow-up to the technological frontier.
Students have taken courses in basic chemistry, basic materials science and so on, on the basis of which they learn advanced materials chemistry, master the principles and methods for the design and preparation of materials and their basic applications.

Name: Modern Spectroscopic Techniques and Applications
Introduction: Spectrum technology is widely used in scientific research and applications such as materials, physics, chemistry, biology, electronic information, energy, etc. In recent years, with the development of material science and electronic information technology, the invention of new light sources, detection techniques, the significant increase in spectral capabilities in space, time and energy three-dimensional resolution, and the emergence of a series of advanced spectrograph techniques. Modern Spectroscopy Technology and Applications, which begins with basic knowledge of spectroscopy, provides an overview of spectroscopy principles and techniques, in particular their applications in the fields of material, physics, chemistry and electronic information. Through this course, students are familiarized with the technical and equipment design of spectroscopy detection, with the basic principles and knowledge of absorption, infrared, Laman, fluorescent, ultra-fast, near-field spectroscopy, and with the physico-chemical properties of materials analysed using spectral techniques. This course applies to postgraduate students in materials, physics and chemistry-related subjects.

Name: Energy Materials
Introduction:
The course is an optional specialized course for graduate students from the Faculty of Energy and Resource Engineering and the Faculty of Materials. It is sufficient to have an undergraduate learning base in the above two faculties.
The main elements are: traditional energy materials, solar cell materials, fuel cell materials, new secondary battery materials and nuclear energy materials.
Multimedia teaching is used to enrich the content of the teaching.

Name: Optoelectronic Functional Materials
Introduction:
Purpose: Systematic learning of functional materials that are widely used in the current field of high-tech technologies, using acquired basic physical knowledge, such as optical, electrical, magnetic, heat, together with material chemistry and condensation physics.
Basis: Basic chemical knowledge is required.

Name: Introduction to Materials Physics
Introduction:
The opening of the course: In line with the philosophy of the University of Materials and the main direction of research in the Faculty of Materials of the Institute of Engineering, it focuses on the physical aspects of material science, providing students with comprehensive learning and understanding of basic physical issues in the field of material science and laying the physical foundation for the next scientific research.
(c) Basics for the opening of classes: the teaching staff has many years of scientific experience in condensation physics and related disciplines, covering a wide range of areas such as low-dimensional material growth, surface analysis and physical identity studies. The faculty and the relevant co-operatives have certain experimental equipment conditions and research bases.
Teaching requirements: Provide students with comprehensive learning and understanding of fundamental physical issues in the field of material sciences, including, inter alia, the physical properties of materials and their micromechanicals, as well as progress on relevant modern topics (mechanical, thermal, electron, magnetic, optical, acoustic, functional).

Name: Biomedical Materials Science
Introduction: The purpose of the course is to provide students with an understanding and knowledge of the structure, performance, processing methods, clinical applications of various biomedical materials (metal materials, ceramics, high molecular materials, composite materials), the biological compatibility of biological medical materials and their methods of detection and evaluation, the chemical composition of the materials, their organizational structure, the relationship between the process process and their biological properties, problems in the application of biomedical materials and the direction of development. There are no special teaching bases and teaching requirements, and students with the basics of material, mechanics, physics, chemistry, medicine, etc. can understand the content of the course.

Name: Advanced Liquid Crystal Materials
Introduction: With the development of the information society, there is a higher demand for high performance of information carriers (e.g. display and storage), and traditional materials are difficult to meet the needs of low-carbon, environmentally friendly and green preparation processes. LCD display technology has become the dominant and developmental trend in the current tablet display area due to the orderly nature of both solid substances and liquid mobility and control, which can be organized in a structured manner with external effects such as electric fields, magnetic fields, etc. At the same time, LCD is characterized by self-assembling and synergy, which can automatically form an orderly structure at the supra-molecular and nanoscale levels, which has been widely applied to the development of the superior properties of advanced functional materials. In addition, dissolved liquid crystals are an important component of biological tissue (especially cells) and are important for metabolism of graduate objects. At present, LCD applications are not limited to display areas and are widely applied to optical switches, data storage, signal amplification, optical modems, high-intensity fibres, optical drives, etc. From liquid crystal displays to light-advanced functional materials and life sciences is a multi-century development. Our lives are also increasingly enjoying the convenience and speed of modern liquid crystal science and technology. LCD has become a cross-cutting discipline that cuts across chemical, material, physical and life sciences, and the science and technology associated with advanced LCDs have become closely linked to the technological, economic and military competitiveness of countries. The course will be conducted in the following areas. Part one, LCD Foundation. These include the whole picture of LCD science, the history of LCD research, the classification of LCD, the phase of LCD, the representation of LCD, and the chemistry and physics of LCD. Part II, Application of LCD display. Includes liquid crystal orientation methods, common liquid crystals, advanced flat crystals, flexible displays, polymer dispersed liquid crystals. Part III. Progress in research on LCD. These include nanoLine crystals, LCD polymers and photovoltaic materials, LCD rasters, LCD elastics, LCD energy materials, LCD semen polymers, LCD gels, plate-shaped LCDs, banana-type LCDs and handmade LCDs.

Name: New Energy Technology
Introduction:
New energy technologies, as representative technologies for energy and resource engineering, are critical to the future of national economic development and the improvement of people ' s living standards. Based on this teaching of the basic theory of new energy applications, the structure and rationale of new energy conversion devices and applied technology, the course informs students of the latest developments and trends in new energy technologies. The aim is to develop the skills and awareness of students in relevant areas such as the use of high-efficiency, upfront and new energy technologies.
The lecturers have been conducting research for many years in the field of technology for efficient use of new energy sources, such as advanced solar power generation technologies, solar thermal use technologies, solar seawater desalination and water treatment technologies, solar integrated hydrogen production technologies, hydrogen energy extraction, efficient geothermal use and low-temperature ocean energy generation (including academic papers and invention patents); and courses on clean energy such as Energy Conversion Technologies, where renewable energy conversion technologies are a major focus of instruction. The extensive research and teaching experience of instructors in the field of technology at the front end of new energy sources and the technological and latest developments in the science and technology of new energy disciplines provide a solid foundation for the introduction of this course.
The course uses a multimedia approach, combining classroom teaching with hands-on training, etc., to prepare students/sense students to understand and master new energy technologies and their latest trends.

Name: Photovoltaic Materials and Technology
Introduction: The course provides a comprehensive and systematic presentation of near-modern photovoltaic materials and technologies. The main subjects of research are photovoltaic processes and photovoltaic materials, which provide students with basic semiconductor physics knowledge from semiconductor physics and PN structures, and elaborate the working methods of solar cells; provide information on the basic representation of solar cells around the understanding of solar cell technology; and, in the face of the development of a series of photovoltaic materials, describe in detail the various types of solar battery materials and their mode of operation, their progression, and recent developments in the photovoltaic industry. Through the entire curriculum, students ' interest in clean energy can be generated, and the foundation laid for the development of optical technology talent, leading to the design of more efficient and less costly solar cells, and for good semiconductor physics, optical and semiconductor materials.

Name: Chemical Reaction Engineering
Introduction:
This course is intended for graduate students in the Department of Energy and Resource Engineering of the Institute of Engineering and offers a compulsory course in the field of process engineering related to energy, resources, environment, metallurgical chemicals, materials, biochemicals, etc.
The course, while maintaining the basic framework of chemical reaction engineering, is able to illustrate problems with maps, tables and Excel, minimizing cumbersome mathematical inferences and focusing on the accuracy of the interpretation of basic concepts, basic theory and calculation, and the applicability of basic analytical problem-solving skills. Strengthening links with curricula and production practices that have been studied, focusing on the development of engineering concepts for graduate students, theoretical linkages, and postgraduate studies in the field of energy and resource engineering, with a view to establishing a solid theoretical basis for chemical reaction engineering for future professional studies, scientific research and work.

Name: Low-Dimensional Functional Materials
Introduction: “Low-dimensional functional material” is an important optional course for graduate students in material science and engineering. The low-dimensional material here consists of two-dimensional, one-peacekeeping and zero-binami material. The geometric structure and physico-chemical properties of the material will show completely different characteristics from those of its macromaterials as the linearity of the material decreases. With the rapid development of computer hardware and software technology, computing simulation has become the third pillar of natural science and an important tool for the development and research of new materials. The course focused on: 1) how to describe low-dimensional materials from a micro-level perspective; 2) how to design and study zero-dimensional hyperatomic and hyperhalogenoid clusters using basic physical principles and computational simulation methods, 1-dimensional nanopipes, nanolined functional materials and 2-dimensional monoatomic materials, as well as 2-dimensional functional magnetic materials; 3) how to study the stability of low-dimensional materials, their electro-structure and magnetic properties and adsorption properties; and 4) how to reveal potential applications of new materials. The course focuses on the development of students ' capacities in the design and integrated analysis of problems; it requires students to have a basic knowledge of material sciences, quantum mechanics, solid physics and computing science. Through this course, students are required to master the basic features of low-dimensional functional materials and the basic methods of designing and carrying out physical analysis of new low-dimensional functional materials; and to improve the integration of simulation design and research into new materials. The course is intended for postgraduate students in the Faculty of Material Sciences and Engineering, and is attended by postgraduate students in the relevant fields. Type of course: Postgraduate course at the Faculty of Materials Course organization: multimedia delivery; number of candidates proposed 10-20 Course hours: 3 hours/week, total 48 hours. (class hours: Thursday 9-12) Examination arrangements: an overview of the literature (20 minutes) + oral report (20 minutes) + written report on end-of-cycle subject design [calculating simulation (20 minutes) + analysis of results (20) + functional application (20 minutes)) Teaching materials: self-programming Reference materials: 1.
