Name: Solar Photovoltaic Cells and Their Applications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The use of new, non-polluting renewable sources of energy has become the focus of research, with solar energy placing the highest priority on its large and clean reserves. The course focuses on the current state of energy in the world and China and on the development of new sources of energy, basic performance and methods of preparation of nanomaterials, history, structure and rationale for the development of solar cells, and some of the current daily use of solar energy.

Name: Functional Materials and Devices (Part 1)
Introduction:
Iron electrical material is an electronic function that displays certain important properties as a result of spontaneous polarization and has been extensively used for the development of a variety of electronic devices, including high-media capacitors, thermal electrical sensors, voltage acoustic exchange powerers, photovoltaics, heat-sensitive electrical resistance, iron electrical storage and recently developed magnetic composites and magnetic appliances. It can be said that in the area of modern electronics, iron and electronics play an essential role as well as semiconductor devices.
The course focuses on the basic theory and background of iron and electric materials, practical iron and electrical materials, physical properties of materials, general methods of material manufacture, various iron and electronic appliances, design and application of equipment, etc. This course requires some knowledge of solid physics and university mathematics. The subjects are mainly undergraduate and graduate students from the Faculty of Material Sciences and Engineering, the Faculty of Electronics and the Department of Physics. The course is designed to be 50-60 academic hours, with English-language teaching materials, which will be taught in multimedia classrooms.

Name: Advanced Heat and Mass Transfer
Introduction: This course, which is compulsory for postgraduate students in fluid mechanics in the Faculty of Mechanical and Space Technology of the Institute of Technology, focuses on the basic principles of heat transfer, fluid exchange, heat radiation and enhanced heat transmission from an mechanical perspective, focusing on the basic equations and methods of solving problems of mobility and heat exchange. The lectures included: Theoretically based on heat conductor (the theoretical basis, the basic law of heat conduct, the basic law of heat conduct, the law of heat conductivity based on the basic heat conductor and the constant law of energy conductor, the single value conditions of the heat conductor and the method of solving the heat conductor problems; multi-dimensional steady heat conductor heat (the straight-angle coordinates and the two-dimensional steady heat conductor resolution in the cylindrical coordinate system); non-stable heat conductor (the basic concept of non-stable heat conductor); the law of the Lapras and the Green function (the behaviour of the flow flow mass in the control of current fluids, the heat exchange and the Green function.); the approximation method of resolution (the approximation method, the accumulation method, the single value of the heat conductor, the single value of the heat conductor) (the method of one of the straight angle coordinates, the method of the flowr flow flow flow path, the method of the temperature exchanger and the flowover of the fluids to the inner stream. The course requires graduate students studying the course to master the basic concepts and theories of advanced heat transfer and to analyse more complex heat transfer problems. Emphasis is placed on basic concepts and on the development of analytical reasoning capacity. Upon completion of this course, the graduate students should be able to accurately grasp the physical volume of the heat transfer definitions and their scales; properly understand the basic concepts and basic patterns of the heat transport process; master the methodology for establishing mathematical models of the heat transfer phenomenon based on the constant law of energy maintenance and be able to analyse the problems involved in seeking resolution; and properly apply the basic theoretical knowledge of heat transfer and deal with the more complex practical heat transfer problems.

Name: Thermodynamics and Its Applications
Introduction:
This course is an optional specialized course aimed at the Department of Energy and Resource Engineering of the College of Engineering and some of the relevant graduate students. It is sufficient to have an undergraduate study base in disciplines such as chemistry, thermal energy, resources and materials.
The main elements are as follows: foundation of chemical thermal sciences; application of chemical thermal sciences in energy power; application of chemical thermal sciences in energy and environmental materials; application of chemical thermal sciences in resource use processes; and prospects for the development of chemical thermal sciences and their applications.
Multimedia teaching is used to enrich the content of the teaching.

Name: Natural Gas Hydrates
Introduction: Gas hydrates are considered a potential source of energy because of their large reserves in nature. In recent years, the study of natural gas hydrates has moved from the survey phase to the pilot development phase, following several tests of gas hydrates in the land and sea areas. The course seeks to provide students with a more in-depth understanding of the basic properties of gas hydrates, survey and evaluation methods, technology development, hydrates applications and recent developments in gas hydrates research. The lectures included: Gas Hydraulic Profiles, Physical Nature of Gas Hydraulics, Chemical Nature of Gas Hydraulics, Natural Gas Hydraulics Production in Nature, Gas Hydraulic Survey Methods, Gas Hydraulics Evaluation Methods, Gas Hydraulics Development Technologies, Gas Hydraulics Mobility Guarantee, Gas Hydraulics Application Technologies, Recent Progress in Gas Hydraulics Research, etc.

Name: Numerical Simulation of Multiphase Flow in Porous Media
Introduction: Through the teaching of this course, students are given basic skills in the principles, calculation methods and programming of numerical simulation of multi-hull flow problems in multi-pore media, techniques for the application of numerical simulations of oil reserves and applications for the development of numerical simulations of the use of water resources, and recent research progress and trends in this field. Increased capacity to integrate basic theory, expertise and computer-based tools for analysis to address energy and resource engineering.

Name: Statistics and Data Analysis
Introduction: Mathematic methods and tools for quantitative analysis are increasingly being applied in many engineering disciplines. The Institute of Engineering currently has a complex undergraduate background of a number of graduate students covering materials, chemistry, biomedicine and other engineering disciplines, and students have mixed mathematical training and bases that make it difficult to qualify for the statistical and data analysis requirements of complex, big data in new developments in modern engineering science. As a result, the development of the mathematical base and related methodological skills of the above-mentioned postgraduate students has also become an important topic of current postgraduate education, particularly in statistical and complex data analysis. The aim of this course is to provide good mathematics training to graduate students in these specialties, so that students can lay a solid and practical mathematical foundation for solving the problems of experimental design, quantitative modelling and data analysis in their field of specialization. It is mainly concerned with non-classical mathematical methods based on statistical analysis and quantitative modelling: (1) content arrangements with a comparative system, taking into account postgraduate studies from different academic backgrounds; and (2) statistical analytical methods based on data, presenting preliminary knowledge of model identification methods and focusing on their practical application.

Name: Aerospace Positioning and Navigation Technology
Introduction: Positioning navigation technologies are widely applied and important in the aviation and space fields, and almost all aviation and spacecraft have the technology and methods to locate their space. The course focuses on positioning navigation techniques and systems that are often applied in the field of aerospace technology, such as the Roland-C system, the Beidou Global Positioning System, astro-navigation, inertial navigation and geomagnetic navigation, from the radio positioning, satellite positioning and autonomous positioning plates. Through the course, students are enabled to master basic aerospace positioning navigation techniques and methods and, on that basis, to expand their knowledge appropriately to lay the foundation for future scientific research and engineering practices.

Name: Theory and Algorithms for Electromagnetic Big Data Processing
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: The course is devoted to theories and algorithms oriented towards electromagnetic large data processing, covering, inter alia, the following: Rare representation and measurement of electromagnetic data, compression senses, matrix filling, greedy algorithm (OMP, COSAMP, IHA), emulation base, gradient iterative algorithm, Bregman algorithm, linear and non-linear precipitation of data, random algorithms, online learning, relationship between the neural network and thin re-engineering, thin Bayesian analysis, dichotomy of Bayesian, Monte Carlo Bayesian, transmission of information, etc.

Name: Topics in Complex Systems Control
Introduction: Introduction of frontier areas of complex system control, introduction of new mathematical tools, analysis and control of dynamic behaviour of complex multi-model, uncertain, multilayered engineering systems. It provides a good basis for successful research for doctoral and master ' s students. Doctoral and master ' s students must be actively involved in the whole process of finding literature, reading literature, identifying problems, analysing problems and solving problems. Doctoral and master ' s students are required to complete an academic thesis at the end of the term and to present their findings in the classroom.

Name: Mathematical Foundations of Control
Introduction: Introduction of the basic research tool in the theory of system and control - matrix analysis, laying the foundation for the entry of Ph.D. students into science. Students are required to study more and practice more. The written examination was closed at the end of the interim period. Students are required to study linear algebras and advanced mathematics at universities in advance.

Name: Multi-Agent Technology
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science

Name: Control of Perturbed Systems
Introduction: The theory and method of control, including detailed descriptions of control design issues, basic problems of stability and balance of performance of rods, and graphic design methods suitable for re-routing of stable and minimal phase objects, are the following: model of signal, model number of system, input-output relationships, basic feedback loops, internal stability, closer tracking, performance, rod stability, rods performance, serenity, inter-mass decomposition, parameterization of controllers, proximate nature, strong and simultaneous tranquilization, algebraic restraints, decomposition constraints, re-routing, nevanlinna-Pick problem, model matching problem resolution, etc.

Name: Dynamic Analysis
Introduction: The basic concepts, methods and applications of Lyapunov ' s stability are presented mainly in the fields of mechanics and automatic control. Students are required to have a basis for better constant differential equations and linear algebra courses, in addition to basic concepts in theoretical mechanics and control theories. By learning the basic concept of the stability of Lyapunov, the algebra method of the stability of linear systems, the linear approach of non-linear systems and the direct method of Lyapunov, the concepts and methods can be correctly applied in combination with specific problems.

Name: Academic Writing in Dynamics and Control
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to introduce basic knowledge and methods such as the norms, requirements, etc. for writing and reporting scientific and technical papers in this field, to develop the academic skills of students in reading, outlining, writing and reporting scientific and technological papers, and to clarify academic ethics and norms. The course included reading and retrieval of literature, basic elements and structure of scientific and technical papers, presentation of parts, professional English characteristics, contribution to papers, and preparation of academic reports, lectures. In addition to teaching in the classroom, students are required to conduct writing and speech training.

Name: Introduction to Modern Biotechnology
Introduction: Research in modern biotechnology has moved rapidly to molecular levels, and the whole research methodology and detection methods are very different from traditional biotechnology, and these differences determine that the focus of the course is on the revolutionary changes that have taken place in various areas of biotechnology, so that students can fully understand the similarities between tradition and modern biotechnology. In addition, modern biotechnology is a highly technical discipline developed on the basis of disciplines such as molecular biology, biochemistry, microbiology and genetics, so the course will focus on examples of applications that present some of the patterns common to modern biotechnology applications and development, as well as the principles and methods common to some of the special circumstances, so that students can learn some of the solutions to problems, not just new technologies and new advances; and to learn from scientific thinking, thereby enhancing the capacity for independent thinking, independent judgement, which is the basic qualities of modern biotechnology research.

Name: Cancer: Mechanisms and Treatment
Introduction: The course is intended to enable students to understand and reveal the occurrence of cancer by reading important representative literature in cutting-edge academic and clinical research on cancer; to develop a systematic and in-depth understanding of the theory and practice of individualized target-to-pharmaceutical treatment of cancer, as well as to further understand the mechanisms and preventive measures resulting from the resistance (resistance) to chemotherapy; to understand and master the current state of research and development practices and clinical applications of modern target-to-cancer drugs, and to lay solid theoretical foundations for the development of new generation-to-cancer drugs and the application of “precision medicine”.

Name: Genomic Data Analysis
Introduction: Contemporary life sciences and medicine are moving towards a large data age represented by high-throughput sequencing. Modelling, analysing and interpreting large genomics data will determine whether we can quickly and accurately detect new biological phenomena and patterns and treat patients with precision. The course will present the types of data common in genomics, such as WGS, RNA-seq, Hi-C, single-cell sequencing, as well as statistical analysis and mapping methods commonly used in data analysis, including exploratory data analysis, linear regression, differential analysis, Bayesian models, data drop-down peacekeeping clusters. The genomic literature and data will be discussed in the course and data analysis and mapping exercises will be conducted using programming environments such as R. The course is offered simultaneously with the same undergraduate course.

Name: Introduction to Biomedical Engineering
Introduction:
Biomedicine Engineering General is a compulsory course in biomedical engineering. The purpose of the course is to introduce students to the basic points of view of the biomedical engineering profession, the main branches of application and their application background, current hot spots and future directions. It also enables students to learn about important ideas in a wide range of disciplines and basic ideas for solving biomedical engineering problems.

It involves bioelectric phenomena, signal collection and processing, biomedical sensors and equipment, biomedical materials, medical images, optical applications in biomedical science, classical models, rehabilitation engineering, biotechnology and organizational engineering.

Name: Post-Translational Modification of Proteins and Its Regulatory Functions
Introduction: Protein is translated and modified to play an important role in protein regulation. Modifiers that occur in the amino acid side chain include phosphoric acidization, glucosis, methylization, acetylization, paninization, paraphrasinization and fat acidification. Knowledge of the types of modifications, the principles of their operation and their regulatory effects will help us to gain insight into the biological functions of the protein studied. In this course, there will be a systematic presentation of the types of protein modifications that occur in general, such as phosphate, sugar cellation, methylization, nuclide, etc., the principles in which the modifications occur, and the role they play in the cytologically important signal routing and physiological processes, as well as a presentation of specific experiments in some of these methods. Students are not only made aware of the principles of protein modifications, but also help them in choosing specific experiments to solve scientific problems in the future. The course would also be useful for the research of students not only in biochemistry but also in other experimental subjects.

Name: Principles and Applications of Flow Cytometry
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to provide students with the basic theory and application of fluid cytology and to keep them up to date in the relevant fields. The content of this course includes the basic principles of fluid cellology, the operation and sampling of fluid cellology, the main applications of fluid cellology in biology and recent developments in the field of fluid cellology. Theoretical teaching of this course is combined with experiments to enable students to learn the ability to apply current cytology to solve related problems in biological research and to develop scientific thinking in the course of learning.

Name: Introduction to Neural Engineering
Introduction: In recent years, neural engineering has emerged as an emerging science and field, thanks to the close integration and development of cytology, experimental and clinical neuroscience, biotechnologies and biomedical engineering techniques. Through the course, which will present the basic principles and applications of neuro-engineering disciplines, students will be taught the relevant fundamentals, including neuro-biophysics foundations, brain interfaces, neuro-prosthesis, neuro-organism engineering and regeneration, their scope of application and current international front-line research. This course is suitable for students who have completed the accumulation of undergraduate knowledge in biomedical engineering, chemistry, physics, life sciences, one of which is sufficient, and will be taught mainly through classroom teaching, presentations, experimental internships, etc.

Name: Computation and Software Use in Quantitative Biology
Introduction: A variety of algorithms and tools are often used in the research work of graduate students at the Quantification Biology Centre, so there is a need for a course to teach them about algorithms, software, programming languages that are common in quantitative biology and theoretical biology, which are particularly important for graduate students in biological backgrounds. The course will focus on Linux Foundation, which will require students to master software development in the Linux system environment, to operate, to learn to use high-performance computers, to teach Matlab computing and use, to learn about Matlab's basic operation, to learn to calculate and simulate system biology-related biological systems using Matlab in mathematical modelling and bioinformatics. ... In addition, the course will require students to first master techniques such as structured graphic displays and simulations of biomolecules. Quantification biology centres and start-up teachers have many years of practical experience in quantitative biology computing and software use, and have a foundation for opening classes. The main teaching framework is: Week 1-2: Preparatory experiments, networking, Linux base Week 3-5: Linux program design, cluster use and queue management Week 6: Onboard. Classes Week 7-8: Matlab Foundation Week 9-10: Matlab numerical calculation, programming, drawing, network dynamics modelling and simulation, etc. Week 10-11: Matlab Application: Web Dynamics Modelling, Machine Learning, etc. Week 12:Adaptation Classes Week 13: Graphical software for molecules such as PYMOL, VMD Week 14: Molecular docking, virtual filtering Week 14: Comparative modelling, database knowledge profiles; Week 15: On the plane. Classes Week 16: Focus on questions, exams, etc. The Linux section, which requires students to develop software in the Linux environment, to run, to learn to use high-performance computers, the Matlab section, to learn about the basics of Matlab, to learn to calculate and simulate system biology-related biological systems using Matlab in mathematical modelling and bioinformatics. Structural biology requires students to have initial knowledge of techniques such as structured graphic displays and simulations of biomolecules, commonly used drug design techniques, and database storage and use techniques. The approach is based on the use of software, supported by the presentation of algorithms and software principles, with 30 per cent of test results at regular intervals and 70 per cent of on-board questions. This course requires two to three assistants because of the need to use a large amount of computer equipment, network wiring, etc. References: 1. Matlab practical course (second edition), by Holly Moore, Quakers et al., Electronic Industry Press, 2010 2. Linux program design (version 4), Neil Matthew Richard Stones, People ' s Post and Telecommunications Press, 2010 3. Modeling Molecular Interaction Networks with Nonlinear Ordinary Differical Agreements, Emery D. Conrad and John J. Tyson

Name: Fundamentals of Biology and Biomedicine
Introduction: Biomedical engineering focuses on the development of advanced engineering techniques for the prevention, diagnosis, treatment and rehabilitation of human diseases. With the development of biotechnology, biomedical and engineering technologies, future research in the field of biomedical engineering is becoming increasingly cross-cutting in disciplines. Both the development of therapeutic diagnostic instruments and the development of biological materials and biopharmaceuticals will be closely linked to the basic cell and molecular biology processes of organisms, and the acquisition of relevant knowledge will thus provide an important basis for long-term biomedical engineering research. The course will serve as a mandatory postgraduate course in biomedical engineering, and will address the background and needs of students in the biomedical engineering department, and will focus on, and systematic teaching of, the basics of biology and biomedical science around modern biological and biomedical research, integrating the disciplines of molecular biology, cell biology and pathology. It will also address the technical characteristics of the Department of Biomedicine Engineering, taking into account the dynamics of the frontier studies, and will introduce in each of its teaching chapters a description of the relevance and application of biomedical basics and engineering techniques.

Name: Fundamentals of Materials Engineering
Introduction: The material engineering base is an important basic course for graduate students in materials science and engineering, which focuses on the performance characteristics of the various engineering materials, such as power, electricity, heat, magnets and light, and their engineering applications. The course, which covers the disciplines of material physics, material chemistry and solid mechanics, will combine the microstructure and manufacturing processes of the materials with a description of the various behaviours and mechanisms inherent in the analysis of engineering materials. Further through examples of engineering applications, the fields and characteristics of applications of engineering materials and their contribution to economic and social development. Students are required to have a certain level of scientific basic knowledge and experimental competence in materials. The course focuses on the development of a comprehensive analysis of the problems of material engineering applications, giving students an understanding of the characteristics of material engineering and the general knowledge of the engineering applications of materials.

Name: Thesis Writing
Introduction:
With the rapid development of science and technology, science, technology and innovation have become engines and sources of socio-economic development. The theoretical analysis and summary of creative scientific thinking and research results are of great importance in the work of science and technology.
This course is compulsory for a Master ' s degree in science and technology, and will be based on scientific and technological innovation thinking and academic ethics, teaching basic features of scientific and technological thesis, the expression of scientific and technological ideas, the common structure of scientific and technological thesis, the general method of writing scientific and technological thesis and the significance of scientific and technical thesis. The objective of the course is to enhance the capacity of graduate students to articulate innovative science and technology ideas and to provide scientific overview and discourse on the results of technological research.

Name: Business Model Innovation
Introduction: Through classroom teaching and case sharing, the course will systematically present the traditional business models of enterprises and innovative mechanisms. To help students understand how to develop effective strategies and a well-planned organizational framework for innovative mechanisms; how to manage innovation successfully at all stages of innovation; how to manage corporate transformation; how to gain market insight and put it into sustainable business practices; how to position appropriate customer values in the development of new markets; and how to explore how innovations at the bottom of the pyramid can open new business opportunities while addressing social problems. The curriculum uses interactive teaching methods to stimulate positive thinking and breakthrough ideas among students through case discussions, group exercises and role-playing.

Name: Technology Analysis
Introduction: The aim of this course is to help students develop a technological horizon and to raise awareness and skills for cross-cutting subjects. The courses will include representative technologies with potential for market growth, the analysis of technical principles and applications, analysis of technical routes and advantages and disadvantages of mainstream products, and guidance to students on potential applications and future trends. The course will be taught by industry experts from different fields, covering the six main areas of machinery, materials and chemicals, electronic information, resources and environment, biomedical engineering and biomedicine.

Name: Product Management and Design I
Introduction:
The course is a basic course for interdisciplinary cooperation in product development and applies to graduate students in engineering from different technical and professional backgrounds, as well as in innovation entrepreneurship management.
The course teaches the basic theory and methodology of industrial design, aims at training graduate students in non-design professions to make a preliminary distinction between different levels of product design tools, technologies, methods and methodology, and understands that design thinking generates a pattern from specific to general, familiar with general operational processes, and has a certain degree of identification of new tools, new technologies and new methods for a variety of purposes, allowing for one-on-one-on-one and critical thinking. Among them, helping students to understand the position and reflection of industrial designers on their self-role is an integral part of design education, so the curriculum will also focus on the development of non-utilitarian ideological dimensions in social contexts, such as the concept of design for sustainability, the positive leadership that design can play in a commodity economy, the social mission of design, etc.
The curriculum will be taught in the form of seminars to encourage self-incentived promotion. Students are required to choose their own themes at the beginning of the school year, and in the course of teaching basic ideas and topics, students are required to identify their own topics for personal discussions in the middle of the school year, to report centrally at the end of the term and to write thesis for the school year as the main basis for scoring.

Name: Product Management and Design II
Introduction:
The course is a step-by-step course for interdisciplinary cooperation in product development and applies to graduate students in the fields of engineering and industrial design, as well as in the direction of innovative entrepreneurship management.
This course system introduces the rationale and methodology for product innovation management and improves the ability of students to plan and realize their products. Starting with product design thinking, the course describes the core elements and analytical methods of product definition in a wide range of practical cases, and ensures the effectiveness of innovation by providing students with the capacity to integrate the integrated products of markets, users, technology, design, production, channels, teams, supply chains and capital through concrete practices for product design, implementation and branding business planning, and to upgrade the systems capacity for innovative design and business design with market prospects. The courses focus on effective coverage of different product types, encompassing both consumer-type products that address the daily needs of the population and strategic products that support critical economic and social development and industry needs, with a focus on developing innovative product management and design talent with high-technology product design and implementation capabilities.

Name: Sensor Principles, Design and Application Development
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Through systematic teaching of the basics of sensory technology, the course provides students with an understanding of the basic concepts, basic structures, basic properties and basic principles and applications of various sensors (e.g. electrical resistance, capacitating, electrons, voltage, magnetics, photovoltaics, etc.) and as a basis for further learning about the application of sensory techniques in nanotechnology and intelligent sensory fields.

Name: History and Theory of Design
Introduction: The course focuses on two main components: first, a factual historical account of the basic questions surrounding “what is design” and “what is good design”, and second, an account of how the soil of the artistic and technological history of human beings feeds today's design culture and how designers learn nutrition from that culture. There is some flexibility in the pace of the course and further development of specific topics. Subject to the basic intellectual structure and methodology of the course, students may, on the basis of their own interests, concentrate on the particularly interested and well-intentioned part of the course and develop the results of the in-depth research in accordance with their sensitivity.

Name: Design Methodology
Introduction: The course will focus on two main components: an open “design approach” and a binding “design ethics”. The purpose of the course is to train postgraduate students in the design of a preliminary distinction between different levels of tools, techniques, methods and methodology, and to understand the pattern of design thinking from a concrete to a general one, both in terms of familiarity with general operational processes and with a certain degree of identification of new tools, technologies and methods for a wide variety of purposes, which can be considered in turn and critically. The designer ' s orientation and reflection on self-role is an integral part of the design education, so it is necessary to focus on the development of non-functional dimensions of thought in social contexts, such as the concept of design for sustainability, the positive direction that design can play in a commodity economy, the social mission of design, etc.

Name: Integrated Design Expression
Introduction: The course consists of two main components: first, the design of basic types of expression and communication; and, second, the development of basic evaluation methods for designing expression and communication. The course is designed to train graduate students in the professional background of design to have the ability to combine design ideas, design processes and design outputs in a variety of ways, using a “do-you-go” teaching approach, basic principles combined with practical case practice, to enable students to understand the complexity, systemic and social nature of design expressions, while improving general artistic maintenance and aesthetic skills, and to enable students to record, reproduce and express architecture, space, products and even abstract things and even affairs in a skilled manner.

Name: Product Development and User Research Design
Introduction: This course is a mandatory master ' s course in various professional directions within the industrial design disciplines. It is designed to provide students with an understanding of the system components of product development through teaching and design subject practice, to learn business environment analysis and user needs research, to develop skills and methods for user research to identify design opportunities, develop design concepts and develop the complete design of new products. Each student is required to complete the specified subject practice and prepare product development reports (including user studies and new product development design reports)

Name: Design Innovation Case Studies I
Introduction:
The course is primarily designed and managed for design students. Through systematic learning of the curriculum, students are better informed about the location of design in business and about the importance of design bringing creative value to an organization to enhance their ability to design and integrate business. The course focused on design management in enterprises, management elements in design projects and design strategies. Through the learning and practice of specific methods, students are trained in design management and their skills in teamwork and communication are enhanced.
The study was conducted on the subject of teachers, the relevant research and planning was completed, the writing of papers or thematic studies was completed and, at the end of the period, individual reports, project production, classroom presentations, etc. were reported and evaluated.

Name: Design Innovation Case Studies II
Introduction:
The course is a comprehensive practical course for professional students that combines design methods, user research methods, design thinking, etc., learned during the first and second semesters to complete the process of designing the project. The areas of design research based on teaching staff may identify selected topics in relevant subject areas, such as green design, service design, information design, sustainable design, etc., in order to improve students ' capacity to design integrated practices and to integrate the theoretical knowledge learned.
The curriculum consists mainly of tutorials for teachers, hands-on work for students and field spot reviews, which are carried out by students as part of the first semester, with the main content being done by students on their own initiative under the curriculum, each session reporting only to the teacher on progress and exchanging ideas, with the teacher conducting a tutorial point review.

Name: Design Engineering
Introduction:
This course, which is a basic course in engineering for design students, will present the relevant engineering knowledge of design in the course of implementation, as well as elements of human engineering. It will provide students with an understanding of the selection and handling of materials in the product design process, how they are processed, and of some electrical and circuital issues. It will give them a real insight into the realization of product design and the related constraints and flexibility to transport these knowledge to complete the design programme.
The curriculum is designed in a variety of forms, including teaching by teachers, hands-on work by students, factory visits and site assessment. Students complete the final master's programme in the first week and complete the programme in the tenth week and present their reports in the course of the course. The work is mainly oriented towards product design in terms of material selection, processing, coating or human engineering considerations.

Name: Information Technology Design
Introduction: The course is a course for design students on the frontier and design applications of information technology to enable design students to understand and master part of information technology and to create a basis for the application of information technology in product design. The course is divided into two main sections, one dealing mainly with the IT frontier theory and the other with the design of IT applications, which enhances the ability to design programmes using IT through field practice. The purpose of the course is not to provide students with too deep a programming capability, but to focus on the process of information technology realization in the design of the project in order to provide IT control and communication with engineers in real projects.

Name: Topics in Service Computing and Big Data Technology
Introduction: This course is an elective degree course for graduate students in engineering and engineering in software engineering subjects and completes teaching tasks in the first grade. Students are required to conduct an in-depth analysis of the status and trends of research in the field of computing services and big data technology, both domestically and internationally, by reading literature, listening to a series of lectures, panel discussions and writing of course reports, to broaden their horizons, grasp their forward-looking research and enhance their scientific capabilities

Name: Information Systems Research
Introduction: If you ask, which of the capital markets is the fastest growing? That must be IT-related business. If you ask: What can be a factor in the youthization of traditional industries? It must be a new business model brought about by the dominance of information technology. If you ask: What is the most effective means of social communication and public opinion? It is also natural to use information technology to build social networks and numerous Apps as end-up self-media. The Internet+ has become the national development strategy of our country, and various sectors have been and are trying to use information technology to increase efficiency, expand markets, strengthen services and connect. It can be said that information technology has never attracted the attention of society as a whole and has profoundly changed the way the economy operates, the way the macro-microeconomic management is managed, the way the production lifestyle is carried out, the way the investment is decided, and even the national security strategy. As a Ph.D. in the management science and information systems orientation of the Institute of Management, it will become important in the future to engage in academic studies in economic management, business management, capital market investment, master basic thinking and methods of information technology, and to study the latest developments in information technology. The “Information Systems Study”, which we have launched, addresses three types of issues: (1) Information Systems Development Strategy and Implementation Organization; (2) Information Systems Basic Technical Thoughts and Common System Architecture; and (3) Recent Developments in Information Systems, in order to gain insight into thinking and development in areas related to Information Systems. The teaching is divided into three modules, as follows: Part I, Information Systems Development Strategies and Implementing Organizations Study: The main areas of study are the relationship between information systems and business operations, business design, business re-engineering, and the organizational framework and operational thinking of information systems development, taking into account the experience of computerization of large financial enterprises. Part II: Research on the basic technical thinking of information systems and the common system architecture: main studies on the following issues: (1) basic technical thinking, such as database system technology, network technology, transaction security techniques such as digital signatures, object-oriented programming ideas; and (2) analysis of technical characteristics of common system architecture, such as two-layer, three-layer, N-layer systems, enterprise-level information systems, online banking prototype systems. Part III: Research on the latest developments in information systems: first, understanding the inherent logic of the rise and fall in capital markets through a Wall Street perspective; then gaining insight into recent developments in information systems such as cloud computing and applications, goods networking and applications, big data and their applications in commercial banks, prospects for the application of block chain technologies, artificial intelligence and machine learning.

Name: Advanced Robot Control
Introduction: Smart control is the result of the cross-fertilization of disciplines, such as artificial intelligence, control theory, computer science, and the development of innovation, while robots represent and validate artificial intelligence. This course focuses on the integration of sensory information on industrial and service robots, visual control, coordinated control theoretical approaches and applications, as well as on frontier research areas in robotics and related hotspot issues. Through this course, it is hoped that graduate students will have a more systematic understanding and mastery of the basic structures, modelling methods and control principles of industrial robotics and service robots, which will provide the basis for further research in the areas of intellectual robotic perception, control and teamwork.

Name: Convex Optimization Theory and Network Applications
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
Optimization is a recurring problem in many areas, including network planning, machine learning and engineering practices. As computer and multimedia network technologies develop, the optimal theory and technology play an increasing role in many areas, including multimedia and network optimization. This course will present the best theories, algorithms and applications from the perspective of computer applications. This course links the best theory to algorithm applications, is simple and easy to understand, and benefits can be derived from it regardless of the student ' s mathematical base.

The main objective of this course is to present the optimization methodology and its application. To guide students to knowledge, question description, Lagrange pairing; to solve the problem of optimisation, including gradient, Newton, punitive functions, etc.; to learn how to optimize the use of methods in combination with examples of applications in multimedia, computer network. This provides a sound knowledge base for research or application using optimized tools. The curriculum deepens students ' understanding of the optimization of basic theory and application through classroom teaching, front-line research and project experiments.

This course is intended for graduate students in the fields of science and engineering who need optimized tools, assuming that students already have visual knowledge of multimedia technologies and systems. Through this course, the main principles and methods of the optimized tool are available. At the same time, through more than a dozen classic papers selected for advanced studies, the capacity to optimize the application and practice of methods is being improved, good scientific practices are being developed and a good basis is being laid for subsequent research.

Name: Regulatory Systems for Medical and Health Products
Introduction:
The largest difference between pharmaceutical health products and their products is that they fall within the realm of strict regulation because of their direct safety effects on the human body. Regulation in this area not only has a clear mandate at the legal, regulatory and law enforcement levels, but also is based on administrative regulation based on the regulatory science, not simply administrative quality management. Products will be dominated by pharmaceuticals and biological products, as there is an internationally recognized mature regulatory system. Biomedical devices are supplemented and the products and foods are properly covered. Regulatory instruction is based on a science-based system of international regulation, taking into account relevant domestic legislation and industry guidelines, which are integrated into business practice. This course will provide the necessary regulatory scientific foundation for future personnel in the fields of research and development, production (services) and quality management of medicines, medical devices, biological products, functional foods and medical services, whether in government departments, enterprises or academic institutions. The course is also suitable for undergraduate students at both the Ministry and the Ministry of Medicine. Teaching in English. Most of the references are in English, but they also contain a great deal of information in Chinese.

The main elements of the curriculum include the following:
(1) Content and extension of the concept of regulation of pharmaceutical health products
(2) Regulation from a medical health perspective
(3) Regulation from the perspective of commodity commonality
# (4) Regulation from a regulatory point of view
? (5) Regulatory, innovation and industrialization policies
# (6) Global supply chain security
♪ (7) Field visits to businesses

Name: Advanced Topics in Computer Vision
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction:
The main content of the course is the latest technological advances in key subjects in the field of machine learning and computer visualization, such as time-series in-depth learning, visual-based autopilot technology, visual target detection, automatic image title generation, image style migration, etc.

Before taking this course, students should have studied first courses in mathematics, linear algebra, probability theory, digital image processing, computer vision, etc. The objectives of the course are to enable students to learn the course, to have a more in-depth knowledge and appreciation of the research frontier on important theoretical and important issues of machine learning and computer vision, and to have the initial ability to address applications such as visual detection and identification, image search, and to lay a solid foundation for subsequent research and development in the fields of machine learning, model recognition, computer vision and multimedia technology.

Advanced Operations Research

The main objective of the course is to equip students with a number of commonly used methods of preparation, including integer planning, network flow planning, dynamic planning and the common meta-inspired algorithms (including genetic algorithms, taboo searches, calculus algorithms, etc.). The study of this course will enable students to have a comprehensive and systematic grasp of the state of research in the direction of preparation, understanding of the academic frontier and broadening scientific thinking.

Name: Modeling and Simulation
Introduction: This course deals with phenomena that are of a stochastic (rather than deterministic) nature: that is, some aspects of the system under study are subject to random variations. Systems with a stochastic component include a wide range of applications such as inventory, reliability, computer, communication, production, and transportation systems. This course provides a unified approach to the modeling, analysis and simulation of stochastic systems. Analytical tools include the Poisson process, Markov chains and queueing theory. In parallel to the mathematical models, we develop the concept of discrete event simulation.

Name: Applied Stochastic Models
Introduction: This course is a basic course in random processes, and focuses on engineering applications of random processes and probabilities. The content of the course covers mainly the Bernouli process, the Markov process, the Persson process, the updating process and the basic queuing theory. The objective of the course is to further deepen the understanding of probabilistic models, help students discover the application of random models in engineering systems and introduce the mathematical tools necessary to address common random models

Name: Engineering Data Analysis
Introduction: Rapid developments in computing and information technology have resulted in large amounts of data generated in engineering fields such as advanced manufacturing, smart medicine and the networking of goods. Understanding and making full use of these data has become an important issue in the current direction of data science, the generation of which has also contributed to the development of new tools in the field of applied and engineering statistics and extended to new areas such as data mining and machine learning. The main objective of this course is to be able to provide students studying in the field of engineering with a number of commonly used statistical and machine learning tools in the context of the current “Big Industrial Data” and to guide students to scientific research in the scientific direction of engineering data.

Name: Fundamentals of Cell Biology
Introduction: The purpose of this course is to give students basic knowledge of cytology and preliminary knowledge of the results of front-line studies of cytology. The curriculum is based on the basic elements of cytology, molecular biology, cell cycle regulation, signal transfer, cell skeletons and cellular instruments, and gives an appropriate account of the current ideological methods, experimental techniques and important advances in front of cytology. The course consists of one semester, in a combination of classroom instruction and extra-curricular reading, the results of which are assessed by the examination.

The course addresses the formation and development of water resources management science, explores changes in water resources in the changing natural environment and human activities, as well as the assessment, planning, utilization and protection of water resources throughout the management of water resources, provides an overview of the main trends in water resources management, and usefully explores the theory and approach to integrated water resources management and its values, with a view to looking at key issues to be addressed in the future in the area of water resources management.
The course is offered to masters and doctoral students in geography, urban planning, environmental planning, etc.

Name: Climate Change Seminar
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Since the industrial revolution, a range of global environmental problems, such as global warming, nitrogen deposition, land use and land cover change, have profoundly affected human survival and development. Among them, climate change, marked by global warming, is considered one of the greatest challenges facing human society in the twenty-first century. Since its establishment in 1988, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has published five assessment reports, including a comprehensive and comprehensive review of the natural scientific basis of climate change; impacts, adaptation and vulnerability to climate change; and mitigation of climate change. The course will select the classic or high-citation literature from the IPCC report for discussion and will complement the literature on climate change following the IPCC Fifth Assessment Report 2013, with a view to building the capacity of graduate students to read literature, think independently, present scientific assumptions, research methods on climate change and write scientific and technical papers.

Name: Weather Analysis and Forecasting
Introduction:
The course will focus on basic principles and techniques for weather analysis and weather forecasting and on the integration of knowledge from other courses in atmospheric science, such as weather science, kinetic meteorology, atmospheric physics, satellite meteorology, radar meteorology, etc., to analyse and forecast the occurrence, development and evolution of weather systems.
The course will facilitate the learning of atmospheric science by postgraduate students specializing in non-atmospheric sciences. Students are not required to have taken other atmospheric science courses.

Name: Scientific and Technical Writing in English
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The development of scientific and technical English writing skills is an important component of post-graduate education and an important component of post-graduate academic literacy. In response to the general weakness in scientific and technological English writing skills of post-graduate students, the course systematically teaches basic knowledge and basic skills in science and technology English writing, learns from case studies in English and has extensive written training, especially anatomy and combat training for various parts of English scientific and technical thesis, so that students can master basic skills and basic requirements for writing English dissertations, and enhances post-graduate English writing and application.

Name: Integrated Ecosystem Assessment
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
Integrated ecosystem assessment, which refers to the status assessment and trend analysis of ecosystem structures and functions, is an important decision-making basis for ecosystem management and sustainable development. In recent years, there has been a proliferation of literature on ecological footprints, performance analysis, material flow accounting, assessment of ecosystem services functions and research on key elements of integrated ecosystem assessments, such as ecosystem health, ecological risk and ecological safety, with a number of outstanding results at the international/national level, which have become the hot spots of current macroecological research, but there is still a lack of systematization of linkages between the various branches. Based on the importance of integrated ecosystem assessments, it is necessary to educate the student system on the basic elements of integrated ecosystem assessments to enable students to gain an initial understanding of recent developments in integrated ecosystem assessments, master basic assessment methodologies, and to clarify logical linkages in related areas.
Students who choose this course should have an ecological basis. The course will be presented in a theoretical and practice-based way and will be accompanied by examples of relevant research by instructors and national and international scholars. As the study of integrated ecosystem assessments is extremely rich, it is unrealistic to attempt to cover all content over a school term, and this course is designed to provide the necessary foundation for further learning by teaching core content.

Name: Studies in Rural China
Introduction: The Rural China course is an elective course for masters and doctoral students from the Faculty of Economics and other faculties of Beijing University. Its purpose is to provide students with a systematic understanding of the history and current situation of rural and agricultural development in China and, in particular, of the transformation of the economic and social system of rural China since the establishment of the People ' s Republic of China. The course, in the form of a topic, addressed a wide range of key and topical issues in rural and agricultural development in China, such as the birth and evolution of the community system of rural people, the process and performance of responsible reform of rural households, the evolution and innovation of the rural financial system, the historical changes and recent developments of rural cooperative organizations, traditional rural governance and its modern transformation, the history and status of rural anti-poverty, and the past and future of agricultural civilization. These discussions provided the basis for a comprehensive and in-depth understanding of rural China, one of the most important components of understanding the history and current situation of China as a whole.

Name: Studies in Twenty Classic Papers from a Century of the AER
Introduction: The main course is a reading and discussion course for graduate students on the classic literature, focusing on 20 of the most influential papers in the 100-week history of AER, such as A Theory of Production, which is designed to train students in the methods and habits of studying the classic literature, to equip students with basic writing norms and the core underlying theory of mainstream economics, to develop the ability of students to extract the essence of the phenomenon and to link theory to reality, and to lay a solid foundation for economic research. The content of the course will involve more theoretical models and empirical analysis, and the selection of students will require a mathematical basis and pre-school preparation to familiarize themselves with the relevant papers, actively participate in classroom sharing and discussion, master the core content of the papers and eventually produce a full report of the course paper in the context of practical issues. At the same time, students interested in the relevant fields can further read the literature and prepare for master ' s and doctoral thesis.

Name: Industrial Strategy: Industrial Policy and Business Policy
Introduction: The essence of industrial policy is that it induces transactions between rents and business operations. The success or failure of industrial policy depends not only on the efficiency of the allocation of rents induced by policy, but also on the efficiency of their use. The existence of policy-inducing leases alters the external environment of the enterprise and has an impact on the business policy/strategy of the enterprise (business policy = business strategy), which is an important variable in determining the allocation and application efficiency of policies to induce leases. In this sense, the relationship between industrial policy and enterprise strategy determines the success of industrial policy and affects the competitive advantages of enterprises and countries. This logic applies not only to classical industrial policies based primarily on the theory of dynamic comparative advantage, but also to modern industrial policies based mainly on the theory of competitive advantage. The course aims to analyse the linkages between the production-based industrial policy view (producing-based industrial policy view) and the resource/operational enterprise strategy view (resource/operation-based strategy view). This course is mainly based on English literature. However, the same level of Japanese documentation will be provided to students who speak Japanese as the first foreign language. Broad industrial policy includes industrial structural policies, industrial organization policies, industrial technology policies, industrial trade policies, industrial layout policies and recessionary industrial aid policies. This course focuses on industrial structure policy as the main object of analysis.

Name: Topics in Applied Human Geography
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The main thrust of the course is to strengthen the theoretical orientation of human geography and the capacity of geographers to participate in practice.
The classroom lectures focus mainly on research on urban-rural segregation, population studies on urban master plans, industrial studies, regional positioning studies, urban system planning studies, development area studies, community studies, urban village studies, land-intensive use studies under “local integration”, studies on regional urbanization development models, planned public participation studies, social studies on urban planning topics, etc., and on models, problems and strategies in China's urban-rural development planning practices in the context of rapid urbanization, taking into account typical cases.
Classroom discussions lead students to focus on current research developments in the field of urban and rural development planning in China, requiring students to conduct analyses in relation to specific cases (preferably familiar or hot spots), to develop the capacity to summarize development models from typical cases and to improve the ability of students to apply the human geography theory to urban and rural development planning practices.

Name: Introduction to Spatial Econometrics
Introduction: The economics of spatial econometrics, an emerging branch of econometrics developed in the 1970s, is based mainly on space economic theory and geospatial data, with the establishment, testing and application of spatial metrology models at its core, and is the foundation of important disciplines in space economic research. The course will focus on the foundations and methods of spatial econometrics, with emphasis on the application of spatial metrology in spatial economic analysis. The objectives and tasks of the course are: 1) to inform students about basic concepts, models of spatial econometrics, their development processes, state of the art, etc.; 2) to equip students with basic analytical methods of spatial econometrics; and 3) to develop students ' capacity to conduct empirical research using spatial econometrics.

Name: Historical Geography of Cities
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: The historical geography of cities is a branch of historical geography, which focuses on the origins, development and evolution of cities, and the content of the course is based on the main elements of the historical geography of cities, which can be divided into five areas: the geographical conditions of urban sites and the factors of urban growth; changes in the spatial structure and functioning of cities; the shaping and evolution of urban patterns; changes in urban location and patterns of its growth and decline; and the relationship between the evolution of urban systems and regional development.

Name: Studies in Regional Environmental Change
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction:
The main focus of the regional environmental change study is on the interrelationship between human activities and the natural environment in the region and their evolution during the historical period, emphasizing the systematic study of the historical processes of human adaptation to the natural environment and its transformation from an integrated perspective of natural and social sciences, namely cultural ecology. The course is offered to Masters and Ph.D. students in the fields of History and Geography, Fourth Qualification and Geomorphology, Archaeology, History.
The Regional Environmental Change Study will systematically present and discuss the theory and methodology of historical and geographic research in the region at home and abroad. Through analysis and discussion of specific empirical research cases, students will be able to develop the scientific capacity to use historical and geographical cultural and ecological analysis methods for an integrated analysis of changes in human relationships during historical periods.
The course discussed the theory and methodology of cultural ecology, the study of cultural ecology of agricultural origin, the ecological basis of livestock origin, historical climate change, desertification in arid and semi-arid areas, changes in river and lake water systems in the vicinity of Beijing, changes in the west coast of the Bay, changes in vegetation on the yellow highlands, and changes in the yellow river during the historical period. Through the analysis of these specific issues, students are empowered to properly diagnose and use historical and archaeological literature. Environmental Change Research also focuses on the integration of historical geography with geomorphology, fourth-century environmentals, vegetation ecology and modern remote sensing technology, emphasizing multidisciplinary cross-cutting research and building the capacity of students for integrated analysis and research.

Name: Fundamentals of Epigenetics: From Chromatin to Human Disease
Introduction:
Although the extension of some concepts of epigenetics is still controversial, epigenetics is undoubtedly a rapidly developing field in modern life sciences. In recent years, with the breakthrough of new technologies and the establishment of new methods, rising research interest has promoted the rapid development of the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, and the regulatory mechanisms of important life processes using chromatin as carriers in eukaryotic cells have also been deeply explored. In particular, research on human health and disease has found that epigenetic regulation plays an increasingly prominent role in the diagnosis and treatment of diseases. This course starts with the research history of chromatin and epigenetics, and systematically introduces the basic concepts of chromatin and epigenetics. The course not only introduces landmark research in the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, but also introduces classic and modern research methods on chromatin. Focusing on the mechanism of epigenetic regulation in core issues such as cell fate determination and maintenance of genome stability, this course mainly introduces the dynamic changes of chromatin, focusing on the molecular mechanisms of epigenetic regulation (including nucleic acid modifications, histone modifications, and dynamic regulation of nucleosomes, etc., and in-depth discussion of the establishment and maintenance mechanisms of gene transcription silencing); finally, this course focuses on the relationship between chromatin and epigenetic regulation disorders and human diseases, including cancer, diabetes, and many neurological diseases. _x000D_
_x000D_
     This course is intended for upper-division undergraduate and graduate students interested in epigenetics and chromatin biology. In this course, 3/4 of the class time is generally spent on lectures, and 1/4 of the class time is devoted to student-led discussions of 2-3 research papers. At the end of the semester, each student writes a short research proposal based on one of the topics discussed in class. Through classroom training, students not only learn key concepts and current advances in the fields of chromatin and epigenetics, but also strengthen critical thinking and presentation skills, as well as research proposal writing. _x000D_

Name: Field Observation and Experimental Techniques in Ecology
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Ecology is an extremely practical discipline, based on field observations and data collection, with field observations and samples taken back for laboratory testing and analysis. For the graduate students who have been enrolled in the ecology profession in our institution for many years, the vast majority of students are not properly equipped with ecological field observation methods and experimental analytical techniques. The course focuses on ecological field sample surveys, field observation techniques, field survey instrument use, sample collection, large field research platform design and research project observations, biodiversity measurements, chemical metrology, laboratory sample analysis, etc.

Name: Applications of R in Ecological and Environmental Science
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Ecology and environmental science have received increasing attention in recent years as ecological civilizations have been built. With the development of observation techniques and field survey tools, these twin disciplines have ushered in a great data age. Data from both disciplines accumulate rapidly, and many are spatial or time series data. The analysis of these data characteristics makes it difficult for many of the traditional data tools to meet current data analysis needs. The R language is a language and environment for scientific computation and mapping. In recent years, the R language, with its many advantages of flexibility, openness, ease of command, proximity to human languages, and free of charge, has spread rapidly in the area of data analysis and has won the favour of a wide range of researchers. Most CSI research papers in the field of ecology and environmental science are currently available in R as a tool for data analysis. The New York Times published an editorial that R language brought about a new revolution in statistics. The reason for the widespread use of R is mainly because it can also be used by researchers who do not understand programming languages for complex analysis. The course will address the basic syntax of the R language, the development of R functions, the realization of commonly used statistical methods (relevance, regression, plural statistical analysis, hybrid linear models, structural equation models, etc.) and their statistical basis, advanced drawings of R languages, parallel calculations, string analysis and applications based on R language, spatial analysis and mapping, and methods of analysis of R-language ecology and environmental sciences (macro-evolution analysis, community ecology analysis, eco-zero models, species distribution modelling, data search and acquisition, climate and environmental data calculations, etc.). The goal is to equip students with the basis of R and to be able to use R language flexibly in personal studies. This course, which includes classroom teaching and on-board practice, will be taught in multimedia and students can also use their personal computers. Calculation of climate and environmental data

Name: Plants and the Environment
Introduction: After a long evolutionary history, the earth, our home, has a rich and diverse variety of plants. They perceive the world in their own way, adapt to and even change the world. The sunlight captured by plants through photosynthesis provides energy for the earth's ecosystem and a source of food and clothing for our lives. However, changes in the earth's environment caused by human activities over the last century have triggered a global ecological crisis, which requires us to pay more attention to the harmonious development of plants and the environment. "Plants and Environment" will present you with a world of plants that can be seen, heard, touched, and full of vitality. It will introduce the close relationship between plants and the living environment in simple and easy-to-understand terms, connect the research results of ancient and modern natural history, plant physiology, and modern molecular biology, unlock the unique life code of plants, feel the history of the development of plant scientific research, and grasp the frontiers and future development directions of modern science and technology.

Name: Theory of Biological Evolution
Introduction: The course consists of 12 chapters, which read as follows: Chapter I Biosphere and New Nature Perspectives: a biosphere-centric system of the Earth's surface; biosphere occurrence, development and future; and the rational circle. Chapter II The concept of evolution: the concept of evolution in a broad and narrow sense. Chapter III - Studying ways and means of biological evolution. Chapter IV. edifices: ancient natural philosophy and evolutionary thinking; religious philosophy and anti-evolutionary thinking; early chemistry; Darwinian literature; post-Dalvin evolution theory; recent debates in evolutionary chemistry; and chemical classification. Chapter V: Evolution: Chemical evolution of former life; evolution of cells and origin of real nuclear cells; origin of photosynthesis and optics; origin and early evolution of multicellular organisms; skeletalization and ancient marine environment; origin and early evolution of terrestrial piped plants; biosystem trees; fossils and geological records of evolutionary processes and major evolutionary events. Chapter VI. Evolution of the form: two trends in the evolution of the form; overlap and combination; specialization and differentiation; origin of new organs; summary of patterns of evolution. Chapter VII Small evolution: the concept of small evolution; basic units of evolution; changes in populations and gene frequency within stocks; natural selection; internal and external causes of evolution; determinants and randomism; summary. Chapter VIII: Large evolution: concepts of mega-evolution: formation of biological species and species; forms of evolution; gradual and intermittent balance; large-evolution rate; large-evolution trend; extinction. Chapter 9 Molecular evolution: concepts, evolutionary patterns at different levels of biological organization; evolutionary characteristics of large molecules; neutral theory of molecular evolution; molecular evolution versus surface evolution; molecular system trees and molecular clocks. Chapter X Evolution of ecosystems: concepts; evolution of species within ecosystems; evolution and coexistence; evolution; evolution of ecosystems in geological time. Chapter XI Human evolution: biology, human beings and societies; human biological characteristics; human biological evolution and cultural evolution. Chapter XII Evolution and society: evolution and social sciences; evolution and social practices; social biology and eugenics; the future of the community of reason and human civilization.

Name: Environmental Soil Chemistry
College: College of Urban and Environmental Sciences
Introduction: Basic purpose: Through the study of this course, students are expected to have a systematic understanding and understanding of the main elements involved in soil environmental chemistry, such as the structure of the soil and its environmental functions and properties, the basic patterns of soil pollution and the various transport processes in which pollutants occur in environmental systems and organisms, the environmental behaviour and effects of pollutants in the environment, the basic methods of environmental detection of pollutants and the theory and techniques of commonly used remediation methods. Executive summary: Soils are inextricably linked to green plants and human life. Thus, in a broad sense, environmental soil studies should target complex systems of soil-biological interactions. The system consists of three subsystems: the inorganic part of the soil, the organic part of the soil, and the flora and fauna. Soil-biosystems are the basic building blocks of the biosphere, the link between urban and rural ecosystems and the bridge between the environment and flora and fauna. But if it is contaminated, especially if the pollution load exceeds its capacity, the productivity of the organisms will decline or even be completely lost. Moreover, pollutants in the soil spread into the atmosphere and water, into plants and endanger human life and health through the food chain. Soil chemistry focuses on chemical phenomena and processes occurring in soil-fatal and animal environmental systems. Soil chemistry can be adjusted and improved using various methods. Research subjects often include the chemical composition of organic matter, composition of minerals and environmental functions, soil glue, soil solution, soil charge properties, soil adsorption properties, soil acidity, soil buffers, soil oxidation. Soil chemistry and chemical processes are one of the important factors influencing soil fertility levels. In addition to the direct impact of soil acidity and oxidation on plant growth, the chemical properties of the soil mainly indirectly affect plant growth through interventions in soil structure and nutrients. The composition of soil minerals, the amount and composition of organic matter, and the number and composition of soil exchange positive ions have had an impact on soil quality, soil structure up to soil moisture and bioactivity. The transformation and fate of pollutants entering the soil are also constrained by the chemical nature of the soil. The physical nature of the soil, such as soil mass, soil structure and soil moisture, has a clear impact on the amount and nature of soil glues, the electrical charge properties, the degree of oxidation and the composition of the soil solution; soil organisms, especially soil microorganisms, have an impact on processes such as the accumulation, decomposition and upgrading of soil organic matter and the formation of decay. Environmental soil chemistry is a multidisciplinary discipline that intersects environmental soil science with soil chemistry and environmental science. Its research is based on the theory of relevant disciplines, such as environmental soil science and soil chemistry, clarifying the composition and nature of the soil environment, its underlying characteristics, environmental functions, environmental significance and the chemical processes therein, studying the quality of the soil environment and its patterns of evolution, the relationship between the transport of soil pollutants and biological and human health, and exploring scientific principles and technical approaches to soil environmental protection and restoration.
