Name: International Trade
Introduction: This course is designed to provide students with basic concept and framework of international trade. Discussion of every topic covers three components: economic theory, case studies, and policy options. Classroom deliberation will be an important part of teaching.

Name: Leadership Development
Introduction: This course aims to deliver some key concepts and theories related to leadership and to train students to develop some leadership skills or capacity through real practices. 10 classroom lectures on different aspects of leadership such as building personal branding and influence, self-leadership and teamwork, organization, effective communication skills, self-recognition in a cross-cultural environment, public speaking, etc. will be offered in the fall semester by professors or practitioners in a specific area.

Name: China's Reform and Development
Introduction: This course is designed to provide students with the objectives, roadmap, and step of the reform of the Chinese economic system. Decision made to initiate the reform measures is introduced in the course, including agricultural and rural sector reform, state-owned enterprise (SOE) reform, diversification of the ownership structure, financial and fiscal reform, opening-up policy and social security system reforms.

Name: Chinese Diplomacy and Global Governance in the New Era
Introduction: It mainly tells Chinese diplomatic ideas, frame, practice and Chinese cultural quintessence since new century. In addition, it analyses the practices after China participates and leads Global Governance, the procedure of dealing with the challenges from all of the world as a core member of G20. So that people all over the world can understand China’s diplomacy and socialism from different views of politics, economy and culture.

Name: China's Regional Development and Strategy
Introduction: The objective of this course is to provide participants with a sense of economic location, regional industrial layout, regional industrial clusters, regional competitive advantages, regional innovation systems, regional industrial structure optimization, inter-regional division of labour collaborative development, regional development, regional development strategies and regional planning by focusing on the state, dynamics, characteristics and patterns of urban and regional development in China, understanding the basic patterns of industrialization and urbanization since the country ' s transformation and opening up, and understanding our strategies, policies and measures to achieve sustainable development of the urban and regional economy.

Name: International Development Cooperation and China
Introduction: This course starts by stock-taking the existing theories and practices in international development with a focus on economic development, which sets the background for the discussion on the role of China. It is followed by a concise review of China’s unique development path, in particular, on how China leveraged international aid to its advantage and what it means for the neoliberalism in international development.

Name: Solar Physics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The Sun is the source of everything on Earth, and its activities are the source of space weather and occupy a very important place in the study of the solar-terrestrial environment. Heliophysics is a core subject in space physics and astronomy-related professions. With the significant advance of international solar exploration in recent years, space weather disasters caused by solar storms have received increasing attention from major countries, including the Government of China. In addition, more than 20 graduate students in the North Great Space Physics specialisation are involved in research related to solar activity. It is therefore essential that special courses be offered to graduate students to systematically explain heliophysics. The proposed teacher Tanaka has been working on heliophysics for more than 10 years, has worked in Germany and the United States as a leading team of heliophysics and solar satellites, has been familiar with the physical processes on the Sun, has published more than 60 academic papers and is currently a researcher in the Youth Thousand Plan. The course will systematically describe the physical state and dynamics of the Sun at all levels, both inside the Sun and in the atmosphere, the phenomena of solar storms such as flares, coronal mass ejections and the genar outbreak, and the electromagnetic radiation of the Sun, particle radiation and the behaviour of the magnetic field and methods of detection. The course will also provide information on solar wind formation and the impact of solar storms on the solar-terrestrial space environment, human high-technology systems, meteorology and human daily life.

Name: Space Plasma Physics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: Space plasma physics is primarily taught about the basic principles of plasma physics and its application in solar-terrestrial space. The content consists mainly of the basic temporal and spatial scales of the plasma, the theory of single particle orbits (swinging, drifting, capture particles from the Earth's magnetic field, etc.), magnetic current mechanics (magnetic hydrodynamic equation group, magnetic current physical waves, magnetic current physical instabilities and heat waves) and the basis of kinetic theory (basic knowledge of kinetic theory, kinetic equations, electrostatic waves in the magnetic field plasma, and rodosni, etc.). In teaching, emphasis is placed on the relevance of the basic principles of plasma physics to phenomena in space physics, and efforts are made to equip students with the basic treatment of space plasma physics.

Name: Magnetospheric Physics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The Earth's magnetosphere is in many ways a unique plasma system. The dynamics of the magnetosphere determine the plasma environment of the Earth and control ionospheric physics. Magnetic storms and substorms create strong aurora, which can be observed at high-Earth magnetic latitudes. The magnetosphere is a very non-equilibrium and non-linear system in which physical changes in magnetic fields and plasmas take place at several levels. Satellites can conduct in situ measurements and can promote understanding of basic plasma physical processes. Typical characteristic scales range from hundreds of metres to hundreds of thousands of kilometres. Thus, the magnetosphere provides a great deal of information on microplasm physics processes, balanced distribution of bits, plasma instability, particle acceleration, highly non-linear non-linear explosive plasma processes and global dynamics, including interactions between various regions of the magnetosphere. Magnetic physics is therefore a key background for all areas of space physics. This course will present various aspects of magnetospheric physics, systematically discussing the structural foundations of the magnetosphere, their dynamics, and related plasma physics. This would involve fundamental aspects such as particle dynamics and equilibrium theory, and more complex concepts such as non-local instability processes and non-linear dynamics. This course will combine observations and related plasma physics and theory. The analysis theory has greater limitations in non-linear processes.

Name: Space High-Energy Particle Physics
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction:
High-energy particle physics in space is an important area of research in space physics, but no relevant courses have yet been offered in North China. In order to fill this gap, it is proposed to introduce this course. The course system describes the main observations of energy particles (above plasma energy) in the Sun and interplanetary space, as well as associated particle acceleration, transmission and radiation theory.
The instructors have been engaged in research and research in the field of space-energy particle physics for many years and have a solid theoretical basis. The basic conditions for opening classes are thus in place.
The teachings included solar quantum particle events, heat energy particle events, solar and interplanetary radiostorms, solar soft and hard X-ray storms, solar gamma ray storms, particle acceleration theory, particle interplanetary transfer theory, and prospects for space observations of future energy particles.

College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The system describes physical and photochemical processes occurring in the middle and upper atmosphere, describing the effects of solar-terrestrial physical events on the middle and upper atmosphere, the interaction of human activity with the middle and upper atmosphere. Name: Guidance on Scientific Writing and Academic Standards in Space Science
College: School of Earth and Space Sciences
Introduction: The field of space science is an area of very close international cooperation and exchange. The English-language scientific and technical thesis is one of the important ways in which academic thought is expressed and exchanged in space science research. One of the basic skills required for postgraduate students in each field of space physics is how to write a high-quality scientific and technical paper in English that adheres to basic academic ethics and norms, how to fully demonstrate their research findings in the international academic arena, and how to interact with their international counterparts. As a compulsory subject for the first year of postgraduate studies, this course will be presented to the student system in the form of a thematic report on how to write and publish scientific papers in English. The main elements of the course are: Introduction to the teaching plan (Instructor Investment 2): Basic processes in space science research, purpose of scientific writing and importance of academic norms. How to conduct scientific research effectively (How to Technically complete Your Research 4): how to choose the direction of research; how to obtain background knowledge - selective reading of research-related papers and literature reading techniques: fine reading and general reading; scientific literature search, classification and management. Name: Image Understanding
College: School of Electronics Engineering and Computer Science
Introduction: Image understanding is an important research direction in the field of intelligent information processing, which is to understand the nature of the objects in the images and the interrelationships between them, thus giving the inner semantic meaning of the images. Image understanding is an essential technical basis for applications such as intelligent image monitoring, retrieval, classification, etc., and has important research significance and broad application prospects. Images are understood as a comprehensive cross-cutting discipline involving many disciplines, including image processing, computer vision, machine learning, model recognition, artificial intelligence, brain and cognitive. In recent years, with the emergence and development of in-depth learning, the study of image understanding has evolved rapidly, e.g. in the areas of face recognition, image classification, etc., the level of manual processing has been reached or close, thus beginning to be applied to various areas such as image retrieval, identification, etc. This course will give a definition and framework for image understanding, guided by two main research lines in recent years (fixed features + classifier learning (traditional machine learning), feature + classifier-joint learning (in-depth learning)) and will progressively elaborate the underlying theory and methodology of image understanding. The course consists of five modules: basic knowledge, character extraction, cataloguing design, multi-perspective characterization integration, multi-object co-understanding. Basic knowledge modules present basic knowledge related to colour and perception, camera imaging and display, camera models, lighting models, object models, scenery models, motion models, etc. The focus is on camera and motion models, as well as sampling and filtering. The basic knowledge module provides the necessary, abridged basic knowledge for subsequent image understanding of theory and methodology. Basic knowledge modules are expected to last 6 hours in 2 weeks. The feature extraction unit describes the commonly used feature extraction methods, edge extraction, texture description, colour characterization, etc. The key to feature extraction lies in the unchanging nature of the feature, for example, a person ' s face and identity are usually accurately identified regardless of his or her pleasure or sadness, face or side. The reason for this is that the human brain accurately extracts constant facial features. This module focuses on hierarchical features resulting from local constant features SIFT, wordbag models and in-depth learning. Examples of relevant studies, such as fast-track quantification of SIFT characteristics, improved DIFT characterization extraction, attractive characterization methods, CNN volume neural network, etc. The feature extraction module is expected to last 6 hours in 2 weeks. The taxonomy design module describes classification and generation models, SVM cataloguers, graphic models, measurement learning, fluid learning, migration learning, in-depth learning, etc. The more the features remain constant, the lighter the burden of the classification and the heavier the opposite. This module focuses on the classification of SVM and CNN in-depth learning. Examples of relevant studies, such as AlexNet, GoogleNet, VGG, ResNet, Deep Neural Network of Deep DeepID, and the methods we have proposed for the CNNack approach, combined flow method, domain migration learning, measurement learning, object identification based on visibility, etc. The classification design module is expected to last four weeks for 12 hours. The multi-perspective characterization module introduces basic knowledge of stereovision, optical stereotyping, and applied algorithms such as three-dimensional object reconstruction, multi-perspective learning and multi-perspective in-depth learning. Images on different sides of the object may vary significantly, and three-dimensional expression is a necessary technical tool. This module focuses on multi-perspective and in-depth learning. Name: Topics in Russia's Political Transition
Introduction:
With the reform and opening up, our political science researchers have come to realize that there is no ready-made theory that can be replicated and that they must explore their own path of development and establish political science that is appropriate to China ' s circumstances. After the break-up of the Soviet Union, the bipolar pattern was broken, and the dichotomy and controversy between the European-American model and the Soviet model in the political science theory subsided. For our political science researchers, who used to be “Russian-led”, “Sioux-led”, fundamental changes must be made in values, perceptions and even mentalities. On the one hand, the collapse of the Soviet Union, which implied a multidimensional change in Russian politics, necessitated a comprehensive re-examination of the Russians ' awareness, expectations and objectives with regard to a range of issues, including their own country, government, political parties, regimes and constitutions; on the other hand, the collapse of the Soviet Union demonstrated the shortcomings of the Soviet Union ' s experience, so that a series of political theories of the Soviet academic community must also be re-examined to remove potential problems in the country ' s political development. Indeed, the political realities and experience of political development in Russia are also becoming two of the main concerns of our scholars in conducting political research in Russia.
The course is therefore an attempt to teach the political transition in Russia as a whole, offering students a new perspective and way of thinking, leading them away from the inherent political logic of Western development and thinking about the basic features, basic stages and basic logic of the transition process, using the historical background of Russia itself as a starting point.

Name: Environmental History of East Asia
Introduction: Environmental history was an emerging interdisciplinary field of research in the 1970s and an important branch of history, focusing on the historical interaction between people and the rest of the environment. In a narrow sense, it can complement the neglect of the environment in traditional history; in a broad sense, it can provide new thinking for historical research. East Asia is also one of the most dynamic and visible regions of the world. An in-depth study of its environmental history has emerged as a new trend in the international environmental history community, with the results of domestic studies of environmental history in East Asia accumulating. It can be said that the time is ripe for the “Environmental History of East Asia” course for undergraduate students. The East Asian environmental history course describes the history of the relationship between people and the environment in East Asia from time to time, from a regional and national perspective, land and oceans. Vertically, the history of the East Asian environment can be divided into three phases: The pre-era 1500 was an era of relative balance in the relationship between environmental culture, people and the environment in East Asia as a whole; the period 1500-1970 was a recent period, when Western environmental culture was introduced into East Asia and gradually assumed dominance, when human-environment relations were unbalanced, and when the environment was overused, transformed and destroyed; and the post-1970 period, when East Asia experienced environmental pain in the course of high-speed economic development, when it was in pain, when it gradually abandoned Western environmental culture and when it explored the re-establishment of a new environmental culture with East Asian cultural background. Horizontally, East Asia ' s environmental history focuses on four issues: The first is environmental change, mainly caused by human activities, from the natural environment to the man-made environment; the second is the relationship between the environment and human production activities, focusing on the relationship between improved human production technologies and increased use of the environment; the third is the relationship between the environment and political institutions, emphasizing changes in power relations and the expansion and contraction of resource boundaries; and the fourth is the perception and creation of the environment and its changes in East Asians. The historical and methodological aspects of East Asian environmental history studies will also be presented appropriately.
